reviews.comment: Summer online: Exams were open note, but even with every resource it was impossible to get a good grade because of the time limits. There is no time to check your work or to stop to think about anything, you have to rush so you can't show all of your work which you then will get marked down for. And then your exams are basically your whole grade.
This has been my second class with Professor McConnell. If you can avoid having her, I highly suggest.
Truly the goat! study hard and you will success.

She is a good professor, but she believes attendance is very important, and paying attention to lectures is too. Expect lots of clickers, and 2 achieves a week with a reflection due every Friday. If you keep up with the assignments and pay attention in class, it makes it easier to pass.
guys what is this achieve homework she just posted we didn't learn this and the exam is on wednesday and im scared. happy hunger games yall stay strong dr mcconnell is not showing us mercy

She does get a lot of hate, but I think for people who actually want to learn and understand chemistry her lectures are great. The course is very organized, and everything is exactly the same every week which is super helpful. Tests are hard but if you actually use all of the resources that she provides before the test you should be fine.

this is the 3rd term ive had mcconnell and her teaching style truly is not suited for a gen chem lecture. expects you to conform to her personal study habits, treats her class like high schoolers, and switches up how she administers midterms and finals with little warning. im sure she'd do great at a higher level but gen chem is just not for her

Dr. McConnell will explain concepts and problems in a way that is more confusing in her lectures. She does take attendance using iclicker questions which you get get extra credit for. We did in-class practice exams before tests, but it's not really that helpful. The tests can be hard but she replaces lowest midterm if you do better on the final.

Amber consistently showed up late to lectures and exams, when she did show up on time she would run 4-6 Iclicker questions within the first 2-3 minutes and that would be attendance for the day. She argues with students and doesn't seem to enjoy  teaching and certainly isn't passionate about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McConnell is super hardcore and I think she would work better with a smaller size class, but it's entirely possible to pass if you use the materials she provides and actually pay attention. Everybody hates on her but honestly, it's probably because they feel called out when she calls out the class for yapping during lecture. She doesn't mess around

Not a good professor. Doesn't properly teach any of the material, and then blames students when they don't perform well on exams. Exams are unfair, and try to trick you more than actually test your knowledge. Avoid at all costs, this is my third term with her, and thought it would get better at some point, but I was wrong.

I took her class as a senior and it was the worst structured college class. No grace given, no communication on her end since there's “so many students”. So much assigned and graded in a week. For discussion if you finished early, you had to stay bc there was attendance taken at the beginning & end. Take Adam Glasses class I thrived.

She puts a lot of effort into her class, easy to understand explanations, very organized canvas page, lecture notes always accessible ahead of time. You will only fail if you don't take advantage of the resources she gives you. Overall a wonderful professor! Wants students to succeed, sad to see low rating just because it's a difficult curriculum.

Don't overprepare for studying. I know the C looks bad, but genuinely, if you focus on the basics of chemistry, you will be fine. Go to her specific office hours, and really focus on clicker questions. Those written questions will trip you up, though. She lacks consistency in this class.

She's honestly amazing and will take your considerations and use them. Make sure to go to office hours if you can, she's super helpful, don't be afraid to ask her questions after class. She drops many assignments towards the end of the term, too.  STUDY with whatever she gives you, specifically (clicker too). All tests are usually multiple-choice.

Took for intro to chem and it was super easy. Had her again for gen chem 1 and her lectures don't go in depth with concepts that need more attention. Tests are hard. Lots of homework. Harsh grading. She gives extra credit but it doesn't do much.

Avoid at all costs if you're not a good test taker. Her exams are nothing like the homework or in-class problems. Gives decent study guides and that's it. I would HIGHLY recommend waiting another term if she's the only option. I've gotten stuck with her for three terms now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely dense and hard to follow, with concepts rushed and not clearly explained. The practice problems given in class don't reflect the difficulty or style of the exams at all, making it hard to prepare. Genuinely do not take this class with this professor, you will regret it.

if u need this course for your major i recommend you to wait another term, probably one of the worst professors at this school. if you end up having to take her good luck to you. if you don't have a religion get one and pray because that's the only thing that might be able to help.

If I am being honest this is one of the worst experiences I have ever had in a class. Her lectures teach you nothing you need on the exams. I would have to spend hours each week teaching myself content just to still do poorly on exams. GE's are extremely helpful and arguably better job teaching the class than she does. Avoid if possible.

Her tests are worth most your grade if you dont do well on them your graded is cooked. bad in lecture she doesnt care about her students if the GE's taught the class everyone would pass. the way she teaches is so bad she zooms through lecture homework doesnt really relate to tests
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not like this teacher. The homework is annoying and doesn't relate to any of the tests. Extremely annoying as well, and calls out people for whispering. Just overall not good

She just quickly goes through her slides and pertends everyone understands. The only reason I learned anything is because of the GEs office hours. Amber thinks this is a 20 person class and doesnt realize its a 500 person lecture. She uses the same 3 phrases every class 🤮. If someone breaths she calls them out for being disrespectful.

You can tell she cares about chemistry and wants you to care just as much, It will feel like you are doing chemistry every single day and not learning anything because nothing is explained in where I could understand it just off of lecture. Clicker questions every class too that is graded on correctness and participation.

This class was more difficult than it needed to be. Lectures were very surface levels in terms of learning material. She would only briefly go over topics in class. Midterms and final were incredibly hard. Expect to spend a lot of time teaching yourself outside of class, and make sure to take advantage of tutoring. I would not take her class again.

This class was fine. The topic is relatively easy. McConnell is okay, she sometimes makes things more confusing than they need to be. Encore helps A LOT so use that if youre struggling. I also took 222 with her and it was also fine.

Amazing teacher! Lecture-heavy class, lot of in-class questions and worksheets. Two to three assignments per week. Studying is the most time-consuming part of this course. She knows what she is talking about and is willing to help if you go to office hours. She wants everyone to understand the material, not just get As.

She honestly just does not teach at all. I had her for chem 111 and now chem 221 and I have had to teach myself all of the material outside of class. All she does is briefly brush over the material and then expects us to do a deep dive question about the subject which requires calculations and expects us to have the correct answer in 60 seconds.

this woman does not teach and her midterms are actually impossible. i got a 90 on the first one and we only had two weeks to prepare for the second and the class average was a 65 %. absolutely ridiculous, give us at least an extra couple days instead of assigning new topics two days before the exam.

simply does not know how to handle large lectures. lectures are very fast paced and she refuses to slow down when teaching. achieve (the homework program) is incredibly difficult to navigate, and is based off of the textbook, so sometimes topics in it don't align with the material you learned. questions on midterm were in unfamiliar formats.

She simply does not know to to teach large classes. She gets carried away when people are talking and makes up excuses when she forgets things like simple math, often saying 'it is hard to do math in front of lots of people'. Her tests do not reflect the lectures at all and the homework system is a complete nightmare. Impossible to reach by email.

I took her class last term and had lots of difficulty with understanding key topics. Lecture feels like an overview which left me and many of my peers confused. Lectures and homework don't match up at all often diving deeply into topics that were barely mentioned in class. You pretty much have to teach yourself how to do things to pass exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Heavy amount of homework that doesn't save your grade -- exams are 70% of your grade in gen chem! I think she does a good job at teaching but it's difficult for her to go through example problems as class time honestly isn't long enough. Weirdly, she definitely uses generative AI for some things like instructions.

No complaints. Large lecture hall but managed to increase participation and somewhat make the student feel more connected to the learning in a class full of 400 students. Many announcements because of students who had tech issues. Homework website can sometimes be difficult to manage, have to use certain browsers and stuff. Easy class for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I barely passed, and with no help from the class. I had to attend chem encores and office hours because the explanations sucked. The homework and midterms did not correlate either. I would do super super well on the acheives & Friday discussion worksheets, but bomb the midterms. She doesn't reply to emails either.

lexture are just a summary of the textbook and the textbook is really confusing, don't bother reading it. As long as you study the lecture notes you'll do good. Homework is easy and helps with understanding so actually do it. Pay attention to clicker questions cause she uses them on exams. Iclicker keeps history of the pulls you do so review them.

Very straight-forward and no-nonsense, other than that she is great. Typically 2 online homework assignments per week, with 2 midterms and a final making up most of the grade. Don't expect any extensions or late work. Discussion sections are useful, but definitely review a lot outside of class. Also posts beneficial study guides before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She definitely is not the best at explaining new concepts, but as long as you read the textbook, go to office hours, and take advantage of all the resources within the chemistry department you'll be fine.

Despite the bad reviews, she's really not that bad. I had her for 111 and am taking her again for gen chem. Attendance is required and she keeps you the full class time. Lectures are clear, but you have to check Canvas for the achieve homeworks cause she doesn't tell you about it. Study guides don't match the tests, so you need to study everything.
not very great

She's a very nice person but extremely strict policies. Half the topics on the homework she briefly goes over/doesn't teach at all, and Achieve is graded on accuracy. Most of the class I felt I taught myself even with perfect attendance.
Bad Professer

course felt extremely hard for literally the easiest chem class available. dr mcconnel has an incredibly strict attendence policy; not only do you lose points for not coming to class, its possible to attend class and STILL lose points if you miss an iclicker question. exams were hard but not impossible, but GEs are largely unhelpful.
She is awful

The class is fairly easy, but professor Mcconnel is the worst professor I have had in all my college classes. She's uncaring, poorly organized with her tests and assignments, and simply not empathetic. My friend had kidney failure during one of her exams and was given no makeup opportunities despite her providing a doctor's note. And exams 7-9pm!!!

She's nice but just not a very good teacher. You will absolutely have to study to pass and attendance is graded, unfortunately. If you even miss one day, it will impact your grade. But that isn't as bad as her tests being worth 70% of your grade. There has yet to be a single day in her class that people around me haven't been confused (and me too)

Horrible at teaching. No flexibility whatsoever with homework, even with doctor's notes. Achieve is horrible to use, and the AI tool was no help whatsoever. When I took her for 111 then 221, we switched homework websites, which was annoying and expensive.
Terrible and doesn't teach at all
was not good at teaching the material

I really liked how easy her lectures were to follow and how she prepared class notes prepared for all of us beforehand. The reason I rate her low is because of her awful, extremely harsh policies. No late work, even with a doctor's note. No extra credit. No flexibility or understanding.

Achieve is annoying to use, there is an ai there that is no help in explaining what is wrong with what your did and you can't turn it in unless you have answered the ENTIRE thing right so if you don't understand a concept you should give up on doing that weeks Achieve homework entirely
You have to go to every lecture or else it affects your grade. She just reads off the slides

Honestly, she is so hard to follow and really bad at making sense during lectures which is a little annoying because you NEED to go to basically every lecture as to not affect your grade so you have to go but yet literally leave and need to figure out everything then on your own once you are out of class. GEs have no idea what is happening ever.
Only actually had to go to 2 classes but they were enjoyable, good company.

She is not good at lecturing and it is extremely hard to follow. I studied for hours before the first midterm but still managed to fail a test which has never happened to me before. Her GE's are also extremely unhelpful. If you have a hard time with chem and math do not take her class you are setting yourself up for failure.

Too strict for the content of the class. Attendance is mandatory, but she closes the iclicker polls too fast. She has a weird attitude and expects too much for 8:30 in the morning. study guides are nothing like the tests. there is no late homework despite the textbook website that is used for it constantly glitching out.

Amber McConnell herself is very nice however a lot of averages on her tests were 50% and the study guides weren't like the actual exams. Also attendance is mandatory for every lecture and McConell skipped a lot of lectures letting us know with very little time in advance and still required us to do clicker questions even if she was not there.

She's nice, but is not a good lecturer and that's all she does. Her slides are confusing and unclear. Her i clickers are apart of your grade and if u get them wrong it brings your grade down. Her tests are really hard and worded weird and don't make sense. She gives homework every night and on fridays.

McConnell is a cool person but that is it. As a professor her lectures are too heavy with not enough time to digest everything due to how quickly she goes through all the material. The material, homework, and exams have nothing in common each of them are extremely different no matter how much your study and practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My biggest mistake was not dropping her as a professor when I got the chance. Her grading system is terrible, she relies too heavily on exams with unclear study guides that have nothing to do with the actual exams. There is little room for error with these exams and she zooms through the lecture cramming everything into one hoping it makes sense.
Lots of homework every single day and attendance is mandatory 5 days a week! Homework program is hard to deal with.

McConnell does a great job with her lectures, and she honestly does a really good job with "dumbing down" the content and walking us through it during lectures. If you pay attention to the content in class, it will be easy to go ahead in homework for the week, and tests will be a breeze. She's also pretty funny and super nice (imo).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While Amber was decent, her exams were WAY too difficult in comparison to any lecture and homework material. Her lectures get kind of boring after a while. She overall is a nice and funny person, but her teaching style isn't the best.

Dr. McConnell is a great professor who truly cares about her students. I took CH111 and CH221 with her  and got an A+ in both. If you are willing to lean in and put in work you will succeed with McConnell. She is extremely knowledgeable and really knows her stuff. If you are focused and put in effort you will learn so much, so fast.

Prof. McConnell is super caring and genuine, gen chem 1 is hard and I think she made it bearable. There are always detailed study guides and practice exams. There is homework Tuesday through Friday and 3 midterms and 1 final. Exams are 70% of your grade. She provides everything you need to succeed but you still have to put the work in.

I really enjoy Dr. McConnells lectures and I find her to be a really passionate and intelligent person. The midterms are worth a lot and I feel like they are not 100% based on the lectures. I took her for 111 and 221 and got an A in 111 and haven't got my grade back for 221 but assuming a B+/A- after whatever that final was. I'd take her again!
Amber gives exams that don't consists of material covered in lecture. Extremely incompetent and demeaning. Kinda of a nerd and loser. gave a midterm and final within one week.

I just thought she was ok as a professor, but def better than chem 111. She grades iclickers and sometimes when its not working, she will tell us what word to submit in a quiz for credit that day, just as an FYI.
i hope no one has to take a class with her

Although there is a LOT of homework and exams in one term, McConnell is a good prof. I had her for 111 and 221, and she has upped her game for 221. Be prepared to study hard for exams. Very lecture heavy and lots of material covered in a short amount of time. Lots of GEs and even concept help on Fridays. Difficult, but doable if you really try.

221 much better than 111 when she was new. Very passionate, funny and caring. Teaches at an advanced level that doesn't make sense until you have an initial understanding, I watch videos and read textbook to gain that, then it makes sense and I learn a lot. Good study guides and curve. Sometimes homework isn't quite synced with class content.
All she does is talk about how disrespectful her students are when people are talking. Very test heavy and grades hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had her for 111 and 221. 111 was kind of a train wreck because it was her first time teaching that course, but 221 was a lot better. Fridays are just for practice, which helps A TON. Lots of GE's/ PLA's. She is very kind and really wants to help. Just go to class and pay attention and you'll pass.

Does a good job explaining complicated material, and if you are struggling with anything there are plenty of ways to get more practice since she dedicates one class period per week to just doing example problems. Always good study guide for tests, as well as lots of GEs willing to help you out.

I had Dr. McConnell for CH 111 and CH 221. In both classes, she displayed a level of incompetence and ineptitude that left me wondering how she even had a PhD. She doesn't know how to teach simply put. Her explanations are always surface level, never elaborating on WHY things happen.

I loved Dr. McConnell for both Chem 111 and Chem 221. She is funny and genuinely cares about her students. She is a very strong and determined woman in Science and you can tell she is very intelligent and passionate about Chemistry. I would take her again any day.

She was great as long as you participate and do the homework. She assigned it early so I personally just did all of it early because I was familiar with the content, but it took me about 30 minutes to do each, and besides that there were the worksheets on Fridays due that night.

Genuinely cares about students — curved exams, good guided notes, and came across very kind. But her teaching is vague and unclear at times, and I felt that I did well partially because of prior familiarity with topics from high school chemistry. Average exam scores were around 60% before curve, and I could gauge classmates' confusion during class.
Has amazing guided notes and genuinely cares about us. Tests are hard and most of your grade but they are multiple choice. I recommend studying right from the jump, don't cram and you'll be fine.

Late to every single class, class wouldn't officially start till 15 minutes later. She teaches stuff good in class like 60/100, but that 40 you must learn yourself or through tutors/GE's to get a B at minimum. She made her exams so difficult that the class average were 60's (CURVED!). Exams take up 70 percent. Does NOT drop lowest or replace exam.

showed up late every single day. cancelled office hours and pushed them to zoom almost everytime. tests are 70% of your grade. she doesnt do a great job teaching, you have to do a lot of teaching yourself outside of class. class averages for both midterms were in the 50-60s..... overall, just a frustrating way of teaching students

Lectures are very surface level with little information on how to do actual problems. Therefore, homework and exams are very hard to do as the material covered in class is not nearly enough to be able to do these problems. Huge disconnect between what is taught in class and the difficulty in the homework and exams.

What I liked about this chem class is that it made me like my physics class more. 
Honestly I never had a good time here. The class average exam scores were about 55% (that's w/ a curve too), professor was difficult to reach via email, and I felt that the GEs helped the students more than the professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework doesn't impact your grade, you have to teach yourself a lot of the material. GE's weren't helpful. A lot of memorization

This professor put majority of the class onto the grad students without giving them very many tools to help the students succeed. Tests are weighted ~70% of your grade for the term, and the expectations leading up to the tests changed every day, even the day of. Due dates are always changing, making assignments confusing, iclicker rarely works
she's always late to class… loves to cancel as many office hours as she can and push them to zoom which is very annoying. Hard to retain what she teaches.. have fun!

I love her! She has been so helpful and validating when students struggle with work. I wish the class was smaller so I could speak with her on a more personal level, but that is not a reflection of her at all lol.

I had her for CH221. It was her first-year teaching so there were some bumps in the road, but she was overall really great! She tried to teach us in a way that we could relate to and understand. She curved the final exam and course grades. Super nice and willing to talk to you about anything! Don't be afraid to approach her if you have questions.

Only ever covers things at an extremely surface level, never explains why things work. Essentially just rephrases what she has on the slideshow before skipping to the next slide before giving enough time to take meaningful notes.

When taking her class last term for chem 221 it was horrible. She does not explain the concepts well, and whenever you try to ask her a question she never gives you a clear answer. Also, there are many examples that she uses in class. She also explains everything like you already know the material and are a chem professor yourself.

I had Dr. Mconnell for 221, and her lectures and explanation's of Chemistry were amazing! Because of her thorough and interesting explanations of Chem, I actually found that I really enjoyed chemistry, and ended up adding it as a minor! So I would definitely recommend her as a professor! :)

Amber explains things extremely clearly, and her lectures teach exactly what you need to know for exams. A lot of practice problems & walk throughs. Super caring and test review resources are fantastic. Lots of homework, but in manageable pieces. Exams were not craxy hard, but go to class as much as possible to do well. Taking her again for 222!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the best professor I've had at UO. Provides so many practice problems, recorded walkthroughs, and extra resources that are easily accessible. She genuinely seems to care about her students and is willing to answer questions during and outside class. If you can get her for chem, TAKE THE OPPORTUNITY. kisses amber, we love you

McConnell tries super hard to make sure everyone understands the material, she does lots of practice problems in lectures, goes over practice exams, and encourages students to join encore. I think she did a great job keeping students engaged, you can tell she loves chem and wants students to succeed. Love her and would take a class from her again.

99/100 students will tell you that Adam glass is the best Ochem prof, and they're not wrong. Adam is extremely knowledgeable and can answer literally any question you ask. Also, if you email him he will usually reply within 5 minutes so that's nice. Ochem is a hard class... there's no way around it, but Adam makes it easier if you invest in it.

I took his summer 2026 accelerated class. His tests can be pretty tricky but always fair. He's pretty engaging. The homework can sometimes feel like it goes beyond the scope of the lecture videos, but it can still be helpful for repetition. I definitely recommend taking this course with him.

I think this is literally one of the worst professors I've had. His tests are set up for you to fail. His first portion of all exams are " Nothing or all", With a, b, c, d, e, and they're all weird gray area questions. Then his " multiple choice", is A, B, C, D, A&B, or E, None of these. Oh just wait, You will SUFFER. Take it with someone else.

Dr Glass is AMAZING! He will set you up for everything perfectly!! Take advantage of his pre-lecture readings, the worksheets, and the practice exams; they help!  Dr Glass does everything he can for his students to succeed!

It feels like Dr. Glass wants you to fail. Despite my grade I dislike this man because he is intimidating to approach and he answers questions condescendingly. He is not forthcoming about expectations, and it feels like he wants to trick us on tests. 336 is easier than 331/336 but not thanks to him
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You literally have to get 100% to get an A+ in the class.
He has replied to my emails sometimes before the minute is even over. Best prof.

Dr. Glass is in a league of his own and is by far the best professor at UO. He is not only extremely knowledgable, but an excellent communicator and talented at making sure lectures are engaging. The energy he brings to class everyday is palpable and it ensures it's never boring. After taking him for 331 and 336, I truly can't recommend him enough.

I appreciate how Professor Glass wants students to understand the mechanisms behind chemistry, rather than just memorize stuff. He's accessible outside class and always welcomes questions. The content is hard, but Adam does a great job of providing resources/advice to help you learn. Class isn't mandatory, but I wouldn't skip if you wanna do well.

He is hands-down the best professor I have had at UO. I have him for CH 111, and his lectures are interesting and understandable, and he is always willing to answer any questions you may have. He posts worksheets that are based off lectures which are extremely helpful, and his practice tests are IDENTICAL to the midterms. I would 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great prof, had for chem 111 at 8-9:50 am. 1/2-2/3 of each class is engaging lecture, with pre posted notes, and after posted annotated notes. Midterms were exactly what the practice exams were. Exact format, and style. 2 15 question hourlong midterms. Ge wasn't in our classes but had office hours like every day. Strongly recommend. Super good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yo these reviews bugging. Prof Glass is so goated. Legit the best out there, he teaches in a way that could genuinely resurrect from the dead. Not boring but inspiring and you can tell he's got passion. Makes me have passion for studying. Much respect to prof Glass.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Glass is an amazing Lecturer. That being said, he can be quite condescending when you ask him a question during office hours and his multiple-choice-multiple-answer questions on his exams are pure evil (also all or nothing), so be prepared
He is condescending and his tests are hard. He does provide a lot of supplemental resources that are very helpful. BEWARE of the multiple choice section.
If you are taking ochem, just prepare that any professor you get is going to be hard because it is a hard class. Glass made it much easier than it could've been.

Great teacher, takes student questions seriously and answers them earnestly. Lectures are easy to follow, and office hours are always available. Definitely do the textbook reading and recommended problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I thought the grading for the test was rough (specifically section 1), but otherwise he's a good professor. Take detailed notes, like excessively so. Everything you learn at the start comes up again by the end.

I could not reccomend Dr. Glass highly enough. He is both very helpful and caring but also doesn't beat around the bush on pushing you on concepts and material that is IMPORTANT. I've had some great conversations with him in office hours this term, and I can say with confidence that he is truly a good dude. Only warning is to STUDY your gen chem.

Adam Glass' lectures are awesome, his tests are a bit tough with the multiple choice questions, but if you keep up his lectures and study enough you'll be good! He is very nice and is a cool professor.

His lectures move through very complicated ideas fast; it's hard to keep up. He also teaches as if everyone already understands the background behind what he's talking about. A lot of the examples and explanations he uses are things only students that has him for gen chem would understand so tons of students have an immediate advantage.

Prof. Glass is an awesome instructor. He covers things in a very visual way, which I found made it easier to understand. He is very open and nice when you ask questions, even if they seem stupid.  He does cover a few things that the book doesn't, so taking good notes is important. Overall not bad. 100% would take again, if I needed to.
Very condescending tone when you talk to him during office hours. Also refused to hear my side when the GE very clearly messed up my grading during lab, and no points were given back.
The absolute best person you'll ever meet

Adam Glass was a phenomenal lecturer and clear grader!! He didn't give much homework, just small assignments that covered essential concepts. He is obviously a talented chemist, and his passion really carries over in class. I am excited to take more of his courses in the future.

Generally (wink wink), he's a great professor with very clear lectures, and he gives active learning opportunities. However, some of his knowledge is based on things you should've learned in CH221, so review it before you come to class. His tests can be difficult, so do not skip studying; IClicker is mandatory. Overall a cool guy, great class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Glass is one of the best educators I've ever experienced. He is well-spoken in his lectures and is always happy to answer questions after class even if they go beyond the scope of the course. Multiple practice exams are given before the real thing so you know exactly what you need to study.
Very knowledgeable about anything chemistry-related and great lectures. The exams may be a bit difficult as there are questions that are meant to trip you up but if you study you'll be fine.

Dr. Glass is one of my favorite professors I've had at UO. His lectures are clear and example based making it easy to follow along and learn concepts. Minimal work required outside of class but ample opportunities to practice are provided. He is very accessible outside of lecture hours and eager to help students lear. 10/10 would recommend.
Very content heavy but his lecture style if very easy to follow and learn from

Adam Glass was the best STEM prof I've ever had. The class can be difficult but as long as you attend lecture and engage with the content often its not that bad. Tests often have trick questions so watch out.
Super great professor!
I love this guy. Rediscovered my love for science in part because of his knowledge and passion. Take his class!

He worked a lot of practice problems in class as he would cover topics, which was extremely helpful for the exams. I've honestly never learned more from a class through just the lecture than in this one, and as long as you go to the lectures, and workshops, you'll learn and practice all the content you'll tested on. He's a great professor :)
Dilffffffff

Adam is extremely knowledgable and really connects with his students. He wants to make sure everybody understands and he is really clear with his expectations for assignments. He also made ochem fun. Take this course with him because it will change your life for the better

Wow Adam Glass is one of the best professors I have had at the UO. I used to hate chemistry, but he made the subject really enjoyable and interesting. He has really engaging lectures and it seems like he really cares about the well being and success of his students. LOVE HIM!!

It is what it is! He knows his stuff and insists on your attendance yet rewards you for it. He encourages engagement in his class and would like participation which is part of the attendance grade. Overall, I'd take him again. Not the worst I've had in the sociology department, and believe me, there are some bad ones!
It's not just about the class; it's about the prof. He's way, way too impressed with his PhD.  Very sensitive to perceived criticism. Can't handle women who stand up for their views.

It's not about the class; it's about the prof. He's really hard to get along with. I've seen him in action outside the class. Way, way too impressed with himself and the fact that he teaches at a university level.

How in the world can anyone think that this class was difficult? Read the chapters (I mean, skim, come on), do the homework, attend class. That is literally all you have to do. Stop whining about having to do the most basic work ever, you are in college for god's sake. This class is a breeze, stop worrying.
This guy put on a good show.  Really seemed to care about his students and went out of his way to help them.  I would say that for a research methods course, this was a good class.
Very interesting class.  Used technology to make methods interesting.

Save yourself, and your GPA—do not take his class. Expectations are as clear as mud. Grading is about as “fair” as a carnival game. Mid-term is 20 multiple choice questions (no partial credit) and worth 20% of entire grade. Book is long and boring. Attendance is mandatory. Course is painful. Worst sociology class I've ever had.
Lectures are mandatory and incredible boring. Assignments lack structure and are unclear. Proposal project is very ambiguous and students typically receive low grades.
Very unclear about everything. Boring lectures, unclear about tests and what is on the test. Too much information about his own work.
Expectations are very unclear. Can't really talk to him about it or he'll accuse you of being the one with a problem not understanding
No Comments
Do not recommend stats with this prof. already an annoying class and it's not gonna be any more enjoyable here.

Aj is one of the best professors I've had the chance to encounter during my time at UO. He is very hands on, he goes out of his way to help his students, he's very accommodating, and his office hours help a lot. Would 100% take any of the math lectures he teaches.
He is genuinely so funny without even trying to be and you can tell how much he cares about his students. This was my favorite math class i have ever taken.
If you have the chance to take Math 111 with AJ, do it!! His lectures were well organized, and he explained things in a way that just made sense. He will also set you up to do well in calc.
best math teacher at uo
I WOULD NOT RECOMEND TAKING HIM IN THE MORNING. Overall, He was a nice professor but he teaches very fast so you definitely need to learn sometimes by yourself. Very test heavy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AJ is very kind, funny, provided a free online textbook (not required to read to pass), and made math easier for me considering I suck at math. Attendance isn't mandatory but gives extra credit (via Canvas attendance quizzes) which helped get me from an A- to an A. No calculators however, and there are 4-5 problem quizzes every Friday discussion.

The way Professor Rise teaches makes it very accessible for me to actually learn the material. I used to be pretty bad at math, but this class made it easy. Lectures aren't mandatory, but if you do go, you'll get extra credit for attending. Professor Rise is super fun and wants his students to learn!

Having taken his Math 111 class, Aj was extremely helpful and always willing to help. Being in a large lecture hall seemed really overwhelming to me at first as a freshman, but as soon as you attend his office hours it immediately feels like a smaller class. He truly wants to help you understand. He is also very passionate in what he teaches.

If you are bad at mental math good luck, had a C all throughout the term and bombed final ending with a D. You are not allowed to use any calculators on the exams or quizzes which was a really hard adjustment considering in hs every math class I taken I used a calculator, nice professor knows what he's saying but talks really fast.

AJ is super kind and genuinely cares about teaching. He explains concepts very thorough and is always checking to make sure the class is caught up with his explanations. Best math teacher I've ever had.

AJ is chill, but he wears the same shirt every day like it's part of the syllabus. The class itself is pretty laid-back, and there are 2 midterms and a final, which are 70% of ur grade, but he prepares you well for it. Just be warned, he makes you do dancing math functions at 8 a.m, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really good professor but homework is a lot easier than exams
Very good lecturer and good grading system. Periodically gets off track so we dont get enough examples for the actual important concepts. Other than that good guy and good enough class.
hes a cool teacher

Just awful, he goes way to fast and doesn't slow down for anything and you get quizzed on the same information on multiple midterms so if you don't understand the material on the first midterm then you're screwed because you're gonna get tested on it again.
Not very willing to work with students when situations come up. Overall made 243 a much larger headache than it needed to be.

AJ is an amazing instructor! He made stats easy to understand and truly wanted the best for all of his students. Despite it being a large lecture, he was always easy to reach for questions and additional office hours. STAT 243 is a time consuming course but if you put in the work and get help, you'll do well.
Doesn't give flexibility or much accomedati
Great teacher very clear with what he wants and expects from you. Only con is he is a little boring but the exams are reasonable and not too hard.

Well structured class and lectures were very helpful. Posted notes online right after class and gives lots of prep for midterm and final. You can tell that he genuinely cares about what he teaches and whats everyone in class to succeed. Sometimes he can go on long rants or class notes start a little alter in lecture, but overall great!

One of the best math classes I've taken at UO. Super well-structured, with lecture notes and study guides that are very similar to the tests. Attendance isn't required, There is alot of homework but its usually short. I've kept a good grade without going to class much or being great at math.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Aj is great! Exams are worth 65% of your grade but they aren't too bad and he gives you a very in depth study guide. I find his lectures to be fun and entertaining and its pretty easy to understand everything. There is a lot of homework but its online and better than webwork.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rise is a fantastic teacher. Lectures were clear, and he listened to his students. I struggled a lot due to mistakes in the written assignment answer keys, though. There are many GEs, but office hours often overlap with class times and are only an hour long, which is no time considering the number of students and complex problems. Still recommend.

class was pretty good and he was a good prof, math is hard for me so i took it pass/fail but i was able to pass with an 86% or something despite not doing great on some of the quizzes/tests. its a math class so big lecture and discussions almost every day, only things we were graded on were webwork and tests/quizzes.

AJ is so kind and really cares about his students. The textbook was optional (free and written by him). Weekly WebWorks that were only a few questions, 2 midterms, and a final that weren't that hard if you skimmed the study guide and went to the lectures.

I loved this class! AJ's lectures were very clear but efficient and he seemed very approachable. The WebWork was annoying but there wasn't a tremendous amount of it. There were weekly quizzes but we got one side of a 3x5 notecard and both sides of a notecard on the final exam. There were two midterms, also with notecards.

AJ was a great professor, sometimes could be a little boring but is for sure the best Math 111 professor. A quiz almost every week but tests and finals weren't insanely hard. If you do the homework you will succeed.

AJ is awesome and super funny. He makes things easy to understand and he just wants to support you. However I got stuck with a terrible GE for the discussion so just beware of that. Also attending the lectures you can get extra credit which is cool. This class is pretty easy!

I highly recommend taking a math course from AJ! He explains concepts very well and wants his students to succeed in his class. He is easy to access outside of class and willing to answer questions. As long as you go to lectures and complete the homework, you should be set for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: best math teacher ever. Makes difficult topics accessible. text book is free. The lectures are fast paced, but followable. he is passionate, and kind and very reachable. Midterms and quizzes are easy no curve balls, the tests are a big percent of your grade but its not bad, also your lowest midterm is replaced by ur final if its better.
AJ is super nice and explains math very well! Go to office hours! He is super helpful and gives you great feedback. Best math teacher!!

One of the best math professors out there. I really enjoyed math 101, and his lectures were easy to follow. We had time in class for homework every day, and I didn't even have to work on much outside of class. I would definitely take it again.

AJ completely changed my view of trigonometry! He explains concepts well, gives students a clear step-by-step process to follow when solving problems & cares about his students. The first time I enjoyed math in 2 years! Office hours were fun and very helpful. I appreciate how he uses humor to teach concepts, haha. An absolute pleasure to work with!
AJ is a good professor and a better dude. Put in a little effort and any class you take with him will be fun and you will get a good grade. I recommend anyone take a class with AJ.

Dr. Altman is very kind and wants you to do well, however, she is against giving 100% the high on every assignment was 0.5 away from 100%. This class was also just filled with busy work and redoing the same assignment. We also were assigned a group for a term long project, and that group makes or breaks you. She is accommodating and accessible!

Altman is a very smart and caring teacher. I've had two of her classes in the past and enjoyed both of them despite me not having a physical science background. Pay attention to readings and homeworks, as she is a pretty tough grader, but she is also accommodating if necessary.

Dr. Altman is amazing. I'm not a science person, but this class was still very accessible. She gives really good feedback, she is willing to go over things outside of class, and responds to emails very quickly. It's a lot of work but I think that is true of all 301 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Altman is such an amazing professor. She truly cares for each and everyone of her students. She makes science and her class accessible to anyone in any discipline. We spent the term constructing a research paper and the way she structured the class makes it so everything is done by finals. I took Beneath the Surface Science.
Amazing Proffesor. Learned a lot about science even as a business major.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Altman cares deeply about her students. She facilitated an intr

Dr. Altman is one of the sweetest women ever. She is clearly very intelligent in her field but also very willing to help her students. She definitely pushes you to do the best you can but overall a pleasure to have as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Science of Music with her and it was really informative. MUCH more math than the course description says: 5 weeks of math and physics before getting to biology and psychology. She is willing to help and answer questions. Clear expectations and group projects are pretty simple. Doesn't assign tons of reading, but it's complicated information.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She would make simple problems a lot longer/harder than what they need to be, and would erase all of her work on the screen after realizing she did it wrong. Didn't seem to know what she was talking about which made taking notes/understanding material extremely difficult. Talked in circles a lot. She's a sweet and lovely person though. Don't do it.

Professor Goering is great! She really cares about student feedback (asks for it A LOT like at least once a week...). The grading is very confusing at first, but you get used to it. Basically if you pass all the standards up until the final you are guaranteed a B+ or higher which is nice and makes the final less stressful.
She should not be advocating for the use of AI in class, even though she is.

do the homework and online quizzes = guaranteed B+. Grading is different but its easier to pass. Only thing in-person is the final. Final is hard and a bit confusing, she provides photos you need to use to answer questions but description to find the photo is vague and hard to determine which photo to use to answer question.
This is an amazing professor, the lectures were engaging and helpful. The assignments and projects were relatively easy. As long as you go to class and complete the work you will do well.

She's a good professor that had engaging lectures. Her grading criteria is different but makes it a lot easier for students to succeed. As long as you get at least an 80% on assignments/exams and complete the criteria for the 3 projects assigned throughout the term, you will get an A+.

Professor Goering grades by a different scale, and it really helps focus on actually learning. Dr. Goering is very open for students to receive help if needed, and she responds fast. Highly reccomend.

She is very passionate about astronomy and I appreciate the effort she puts in her class. However, the coursework was confusing and took me a while to get the hang of. I really didn't like that to find out your grade you have to calculate it yourself. This made it very difficult to track my grade and see whether I was passing or failing.

I have taken 121, 122, and 123 classes with her because I enjoy the subject. I really recommend taking her classes. The lectures are easy to understand, and her office hours are super helpful for homework. I'm bad at math, and I'm not a science major, but she is very knowledgeable and sweet. She wants to see students succeed.

Love Andrea! You get 3 "tokens" and can earn more if you talk with her and make a plan of success. Office hours helpful, especially if you go with friends and compare answers. Tests = digital, multiple choice, 2 attempts (higher score counts). First attempt on your own before class, second attempt do with friends in class. Final only helps you!

She's a very kind professor who makes sure that all assignments and expectations are clear and easy to understand. The homework is relatively easy and quick to finish, and the quizzes and projects are designed to help you learn while also allowing for revisions in order to up your grade.

Dr. Goering is a wonderful professor. She has a great personality. She is very approachable, and makes her students feel welcome. While many topics were not of my interest she makes an effort to keep her lectures engaging. She also makes a point to meet students where their at, and help them get the best possible grade in the class.
For ASTR123, a lot of reading but if you are genuinely interested in the class it'll all seem really fun and worth learning about.
Grading is weird as heck! Uses a mastery grade book based on mastery level for each topic so you don't know your grade until like the end of the term.

Andrea is a professor that legitimately cares that you do well. She's very approachable and willing to help out and communicate.
Her grading system is wack though

The class itself was not bad, she is really great professor, minimal homework, strictly group quizzes and one final project. But the grading system is impossible to keep track of/actually know what your current grade in the class is, since she uses learning standards instead of just inputting your grades into canvas.
She's a great professor! Textbook is free and online. There is 3 projects per term, but they are very easy. Tests and homework are hard, but you can work with people on your second attempt.

I took this class just to get a science credit and did not love the content (was harder than anticipated as a non-science student) but Dr.Andrea is such a wonderful professor. you can really tell she cares about her students and wants them to do well. She offers many opportunities to improve your grade on assignments and is very approachable.

Dr. Goering is the best. I'm not very good with science but I managed to get a good grade because of her grading system. It is VERY participation heavy, so show up to class and participate in iclicker to get a good grade. She has lots of extra credit opportunities and is very understanding. If you need a science credit, take her class!

Goering is a great professor. She explains topics very clearly, communicates her expectations, and makes success achievable. Group quizzes are a great part of the class. The final project required significant effort, but it never felt overwhelming. Highly recommend for any non-STEM majors who want to take an interesting science class.

Andrea was an awesome professor. I don't like science, but she made the class really great. For such an enormous class, her ability to make it interactive was wildly impressive. I will absolutely be on the lookout for more classes from her. She is talented, passionate, and very caring. Her passion is clear in her teaching.

I really loved this professor. Her grading system is really lenient which is nice. Also the readings are typically very short and the tests are easy as long as you know the major formulas and terms, she isn't the kind of teacher to throw in super niche difficult questions. I learned a lot from the lectures too.

Andrea's very sweet and caring about students and wants everyone to succeed, that's clear. Assignments are very consistent besides the 3 projects/peer reviews, and there are readings. Only a few quizzes throughout the term, final is similar to the quizzes and you're allowed a note sheet. Just show up to lectures and keep up with assignments.

Goering is an awesome professor. Her curriculum was meticulously thought out and structured online, and she always had so many opportunities to make up for failed attempts at homework and quizzes. She's also very down to Earth and had charming lectures.

Andrea is an excellent professor. She always has great lectures. Communication on upcoming work, projects, and exams is all excellent. Couldn't recommend her enough for any astronomy class to satisfy Core Ed science classes, especially 122 as I think this is the most interesting of the three (I took all three)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great personality, great grading system, & opportunities to pick yourself up if you get behind. You can tell she wants everyone to succeed. Readings were relevant and concise. Homework can be challenging and working together is encouraged. If you take good notes and understand most stuff the final isn't that bad (A note sheet is allowed.)
She let our weekly quizzes be open note so it's easy to get a good grade if you put effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a caring professor who I truly believe wants her students to succeed.  However, given the amount of kids in the class I can understand how it is difficult to reach out and check in with students.  That being said if you are struggling you have to go to her.  The grading system is pretty weird. Final was hard as well.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Does not use the traditional grading system unless you opt in to it. It is based on if you do assignments with a passing grade instead. I loved it! Amazing for people who are not great at science. She is very forgiving and you get many makeup opportunities.
Super sweet and seems interested in the topic but boring lectures and did not explain the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Andrea is pretty chill and passionate about what she teaches. I took this class for a science credit so I wasn't super into it but she's pretty engaging. She encourages group work, but if you don't like that she doesn't force it. There are lots of canvas homework quizzes every week, but none too hard. Final doesn't rly effect ur grade.

Barley teaches during class and the readings and lectures aren't super helpful for the activities and quizzes. You get to work with people in class for all the activities but then dont get to on the final. Final was a bunch of stuff that we barley learned and everyone did awful on it. Pretty easy besides the final but  too much work for a 100 level

Andrea is amazing! Go to her office hours, she's so helpful and kind and will walk you through homework if you need. Pretty much every assignment, quiz, and test has at least one opportunity to retake it, and she has additional resources on how to study and stuff. I don't need science for my major, but took another of her classes bc of her.

Do not take this class if you need a science credit. The professor explains things terribly and the textbook doesn't even help either. So much pointless homework that counts for 30% of your grade that is sometimes extremely difficult. There's a huge disconnect between the lectures, homework, and quizzes. Way too much for a 100-level class.

reviews.comment: Her class was easy enough because you could collaborate with classmates on some assignments and it was very easy up until the final. I did not feel she did a great job explaining astronomy. Despite going to all the classes, I did not learn very much.

Willing to work though issues with you. Quiz every other week, homework every week, in class activity every class. Unlimited tries on activities, retakes availiable. Two tries on quizes, one before class and one collaborative in class. Offers extra credit. She great and its a relatively easy class. Good class even if you're not a astronomy person.

Incredibly fast paced and Goering doesn't seem to understand that not everyone is just naturally good at science. She doesn't explain the concepts well, and will move on when its clear that most the class has no idea what she's talking about. Quizzes are difficult with weirdly worded questions. If you want an easy science credit, look elsewhere.

reviews.comment: Very caring professor who obviously wants her students to succeed, lots of options to retake tests, homework and extra credit. Also very nice. However SO fast paced, lectures move so quickly it's difficult to grasp any material. Too many topics covered much too fast, I wish this class had gone more in depth about less topics. Not easy.

Material is conveyed clearly and effectively. She is helpful in office hours as well as during class in answering questions on the material. She clearly articulates class expectations and there are plenty of resources available to help you succeed in the class.

Andrea is mindful & helpful 1 on 1. Just moves extremely fast & blames you if you can't keep up. Theres graded class work everytime & a homework once a week. Very aware of her teaching style but not willing to try & adapt to people who learn differently. Be prepared to learn little to nothing if you have a booked schedule. She makes work accessible

Professor Goering is so caring and sympathetic to all her students. The course material can be hard, however, Dr. Goering gives students many opportunities to receive extra help outside of class. She also offers extra credit throughout the term.

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you want to enjoy life. I worked really hard and got a 50% on the final. She makes this class impossible and does not do a good job explaining concepts during lectures. So much work and such a waste of time.

Andrea is a great teacher. She is very caring and passionate. However, the class can be a lot of work. By the end, you have to know a lot of information and if dont continually pay attention, its bad news. Lots of weekly homework but it improves your learning. I really liked Andrea and would love to have her again, but the workload is a little much

Andrea is a caring person and extremely passionate about physics, but for a lower level Astronomy class, it was incredibly hard. There is so much busy work and so much content it is overwhelming. She cares a lot, but this class has not been enjoyable for me personally. If you're looking for an easy science credit, look another way.

reviews.comment: All over the place—GEs grade poorly, and so does he. Criteria is never clear. You think you understand everything until you see your grade…I would avoid taking this class with him at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Singh is a good person and very friendly, but his teaching style was all over the place. Nothing was clear, and the class was very difficult! Get ready to put the work in!

I did not do good in his previous class (bi380) because i skipped- my midterm and final scores were like a D but this term i attended most lectures for BI390  and did way better on my exams (midterm -85). I actually took the time after class to understand the slides which helped me retain it better later on during the test. His GE was amazing!

Super kind and knowledgeable professor who does care for his students. Class has a fair amount of busy work, but helps to buffer exams which are harder than expected. Overall, content was semi-interesting, some was very boring, but I would def take a class with him in the future.

My third course with this professor, and I hope to keep taking courses with him. I love his lecture style, and as long as you show up the class isn't hard. Full sheet of paper allowed on each exam and one big project at the end of every course. He is very knowledgeable about what he teaches, and I enjoy his lectures.

Avinash is awesome. This was the only class I took during Winter term that didn't stress me out beyond belief. He's a really funny guy and he genuinely cares about the success of all of his students. The only hard part of this class were the exams.

I took Dr Avinash for BI399L (Animal Physiology). So far our exams have been quite difficult, his explanation of what will come up in exams are quite different from reality. He mentions that it should be "difficult" to fail his class yet his exams are filled with questions that have not been gone over in class and he rambles offtopic when lecturing
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is boring unless you're interested in Neurobiology - I found lectures super interesting. Avinash had some odd direction at time, and exams were harder than they probably should've been but I thought it was a great course
Boring. I learned next to nothing. Easy course to Ace.
Easy A. Awful course.
Don't take this course. Boring lectures. Grading criteria unclear. Singh was never available to talk. Avoid.
Nice guy and might even know what he is talking about but his lectures are boring and filled with trivia and useless details. Doesn't respond to emails. Exams are easy.
Very boring and confusing lectures. Not sure what to study on test. Asked us to use AI to write a paper. Not worth the time or effort.
Lectures were boring and disorganized. Tests were unclear. No help outside of class. Nice guy but would not take another class from him.

One of the most disappointing classes I've taken so far. Attendance was mandatory due to 3 assignments per lecture. Lectures themselves were confusing, overloaded with a lot of details that prof said we didn't need to know. Lectures were discrete and had no overarching theme. Difficult exams due to vague questions. Do not recommend.

reviews.comment: Very odd professor. Required the use of AI on the final paper, and marked down on students who did not use it because they didn't need to. On top of that, he gave very little feedback. His teaching of science communication was sub par at best. Overall, I do not recommend taking his classes.

Dr. Singh is the worst professor I have ever had at UO. He is highly disorganized and vague about grading. His version of neurobiology (BI 360) fell far below my expectations. His lectures were confusing and the course lacked serious organization. He had 3 graded assignments per lecture, and he gave only a single sentence of feedback on papers.

Lectures were clear and enjoyable, and he cracked some funny jokes sometimes in class. He was always helpful in office hours too. Exams weren't bad, and you get a note sheet. If you love animals, take bi390!

Avinash is a great professor! He is very kind and understanding, and humble too! Uses in class clicker questions as an easy quiz system and for participation. Two fairly graded exams are given. Lectures are slightly disorganized, but he makes up for it with his charm. Optional supplemental textbook readings.
Great professor!

Took over a 4 week course. Good labs (and fairly easy), lectures bit long but it was summer & a few hrs each day. Course is fast but manageable. Testing quizzes were a bit late fee but he grades fair. Do the assigned work and a 10 lecture for attendance points he graded on a curve. No dissecting!! Overall easier than I thought and would take again.
Takes attendance for lecture. Weekly readings for points. Boring lectures.
THE BEST. had him for developmental biology. made material interesting and attainable. so helpful and warm. one of my favorite classes at the UO, I learned so much

I took all three classes that BBH offered, and I can't recommend him enough. I took his 100-, 200-, and 400-level courses, and I loved all of them. He is one of the most knowledgeable, straightforward, funny, and engaging professors I've ever had. If you think you might want to go to law school, take his classes!

This was one of the best classes I've ever taken. He is an incredibly entertaining professor who ensures that the workload is never too heavy. There was minimal reading for this class, and lectures included a lot of discussions. His method of teaching is very engaging and entertaining. Also in LAW 202 with him, same notes.

Good class, but he lectures for 4 hours, from 8am-noon, but he only teaches one day a week. He has little to no homework and a presentation and final. I lowkey came to class at like 10 and he was fine with it. Smart and funny
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT ASSIGN YOUR PRESENTATION LAST you will be doing your final paper at the same time. Other than that, very straight forward, very attentive professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Brockman Hawes class in fall term and his lectures were overall engaging and I felt like after leaving every class I got something out of it and it would inspire me to do my own research. He was super funny and felt like he really cared about his students and their well being.

I took Law 202 with him, and he is my favorite professor at Oregon. The class consists of two major graded activities, but both are essential to actually understanding and getting a good grade. He does not want you to do badly, he wants you to try. No matter how long lectures are, they are incredibly entertaining and interesting.

I took Intro to International Law with Ben and it was an amazing class. He commutes, which is why most of his offered classes are one day a week. He is a great lecturer and has meaningful in class activities. There were no tests in this class, only a presentation and a final paper.

Ron is a great person, but maybe the worst professor I've ever had. This course is pretty much about environmental science, not much to do with Political Science at all. All lectures with little to no engagement, rambles, obsessed with AI. Do not recommend.
Its a 100 level poli-sci class why is it so hard? His TAs also grade so harshly too? You can follow all of his instructions and the highest grade you'll get on it is a C.

Very harsh grader. Tells the class everyday that even if we don't do anything, we'll at least get a 70% on assignments. After attending office hours and getting advice about a specific assignment that we had in class the next day, I only got a 75%. Really disappointed by his lack of empathy and inconsistency in grading.
Obsessed with ai and flagged multiple people when they didn't use ai. Harsh grader and him and his ta's don't give any good feedback. Highly suggest finding another class

He's overly fixated on AI usage in class and it just gets annoying when you're trying to focus on working on the actual assignments. He and the TA's grade way too harshly and don't provide good feedback. Essay prompts are hardly clear, and I've taken much easier upper level courses that are way more straight forward than this one
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For a 100-level course, the assignments and readings were intense. Weekly quizzes that include stuff from the readings, so you do have to do them. Professor is also obsessed with AI, and will try his best to catch you if you use it. I don't recommend this course, and I think you would be better off in any in-person poli sci class.

This is the worst professor I have ever had at UO. He is extremely overly obsessed with AI and will send you multiple messages/emails every day about AI and will even report many students to conduct for alleged AI usage. He is very rude and has no compassion for students. For a 100-level async course, this is harder than any upper-division course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mitchell is honestly an okay professor. His class instructions for the online course aren't incredibly clear, and it's hard to understand what you need to do for an assignment. His GEs grades are like theyre selecting from a random grader wheel instead of actually reading your assignments. Hes OBSESSED with AI, and it will be brought up in lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Largest issue I had was with the essay gradings, him and the TAs comments were very unhelpful, with some comments sounding like they didn't even read the essay or look at the sources I used. Super frustrating. Does not feel like a 102 class. I'm taking upper divisions in my final year here and those classe were easier.
Long and tedious readings assigned every week, shows up on the quizzes which is annoying. GEs are super nit picky when grading papers. I've had less work assigned for upper classes.

(Took 101, wasn't an option on here)
Prof. Mitchell is a very solid teacher. The class itself was so, so easy so if you have experience taking polisci classes (which I do) I wouldn't really recommend it. However, Mitchell was always extremely helpful and responded to emails quickly, which is awesome for someone with tons of questions like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have actually nothing to say about this guy because I didn't watch a single video lecture. Everyone says he's strict about AI but I used AI on every knowledge check, quiz and essay and ended up doing fine. I took this hoping to not have to do any real work and that proved to be true. Super easy class, would recommend if you need a filler class

only recommend this class for those who need to fill their social science core education. for a 100 level online class, there is an absurd amount of reading that was unnecessary to pass. GE's are strict graders and do not give helpful feedback. midterm and final are easy but the prompts have to be deciphered from poorly formatted prompts.

He's a passionate professor and lecturer, often using analogies and really drilling in key examples. He had a well organised canvas where all resources were accessable. He does get heated sometimes, like when I challenged the truth of a resource and criticised it a bit, he shut down stuff like that with anger. You must read all the sources to pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Irks me that he's not rated higher by current students. He teaches you to *really* be smart - not just have a bunch of knowledge. Nearly a decade later, I still refer to my notes and matrices from 205 and 320. Yup, he is one of the most challenging teachers you will ever have - that's because he actually cares and is not about lowering standards.

If you are looking for a class just to fill out your gen ed requirements then this is the perfect class for you! If you are a political science major or any affiliated fields and dont have to take this class then definitely dont. You dont actually end up learning anything useful in this class but its easy enough to pass with at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ron is a horrible professor the grading is super strict for this class and the lectures and readings are really unhelpful, time consuming and pointless. after the midterm I stopped watching them and the reading and still passed all the weekly quizzes and final using common sense. Avoid this guy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Avoid this class at all costs. The GE's grade extremely harshly and usually don't offer valuable feedback. The professor is so afraid of AI that he bans you from using grammarly. For a 100 level course this class felt like a 400 level.

This course felt extremely overdone for a 100-level. I'm passionate about social science research, but the harsh grading and overwhelming structure of this class lost me. I went to a GEs office hours and was marked down for following the exact suggestions that I was given. This course could've been extremely interesting if it wasn't trying so hard.
The GE's grade so harshly, instructions are very confusing and feedback is poor. So much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He makes a great effort to get to know all his students but assigns too much reading before each class. He requires us to include information from the readings in our essays and rambles in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oh my god. Avoid this class at all costs. He assigns WAY too much reading, is constantly spamming your inbox for random articles about AI, will *not* give you an A, even if you follow instructions to a T and lectures take up to an hour at times. I understand that AI is harmful, but he won't let you use GRAMMARLY! It just seems so ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor has a very strict grading system where the recent midterm the mean was only 78 on a 4 part essay for a 100 LEVEL CLASS. The GEs and Professor is committed to making sure nobody gets an A. One of the GEs gives me a 68% on one of the assignments and made sure to comment and grade it AFTER the due date so I cannot resubmit. Avoid this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ron seems terrified of the proverbial AI Boogeyman, spending 2/3 of the syllabus quiz, multiple papers, and more rattling off half-truths about AI. The final was focused almost entirely on remembering the generalities of examples to tease out if you watched the videos. Very nice guy, but no valuable information was delivered from hours of material.

i took this class online and he definitely had strict grading requirements for the papers, but there were lots of quizzes that could help bump your grade! he offered lots of support during office hours, through email, etc since it was an online class. highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was taken online, There were lots of readings and quizzes. I had a hard time finding what I needed to study due to it being unorganized. I really enjoyed this class though and it wasn't too hard.

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have ever had. He brags about students failing his classes and does not believe in giving A's.

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is a good professor overall. He's super good at responding to emails quickly and always has good responses/ advice. My experience was a little different because my class was online but overall the content was pretty entertaining for an online class. If you're taking this class online, get ready for a lot of reading/lecture videos
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took his class online. Weekly quizzes that focused on the lectures and reading so do them! Graded pretty easy. The midterm and final both had two parts, a short quiz and an essay. The lectures were really helpful, and as long as you watch the videos and do the readings you should understand most things. Encourages talking to him/office hours.

I do NOT recommend taking PS 102 w/ prof. Mitchell. Brilliant professor; however, it should be an upper-division class. The intensity of this course is similar to a 400-level course at UO. The Lectures are hard to follow, with disorganized slides and lots of rambling, vague rubrics and harsh grading. Take a different 100-level PS class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ron is nice enough and office hours are encouraged. He's a tough grader and the rubric is often unclear. The final paper represents most of the grade, and he is controlling of every step in the assignment. His lectures are unorganized, have little to do with the readings, and he does not care for student feedback/ideas. Too many emojis in canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm in the middle of a midterm for this class right now and it's FOUR PARTS LONG. This is a 100 level class and he's giving us the work of an upper division. Shouldn't even be under the poli sci tag, it is basically a humanities class. Many better lower div poli sci classes out there.
