Class itself is very boring and hardly relates to political science at all. Is entirely about methodology rather than politics, and is a super hard lecture to get through first thing in the morning. Ron himself is chill but his assignments are really boring and does not actually stimulate thoughts at all. Class is easy enough though.
He talks a lot during his lectures. Final is one 15 question quiz and an essay. There's multiple papers due throughout the term and there's daily attendance checks.

I actually really liked Dr. Mitchell! He is one of those teachers who will never give 100% on essays, but besides that, the class is pretty easy and straightforward. You have 2 weekly quizzes (5 questions each) and 4 essays/response papers due throughout the term 
Mitchell is very caring and shares a lot of real-world experience which I enjoy!
This class is not worth your time. The material is a mix of common sense and complete nonsense. If you take it prepare for a lot of reading and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very unorganized, the assignments make no sense whatsoever. He grade the class like its a 300/400 level class. He is overly obsessed with attendance, spends at least 10 minutes every class talking about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mitchell is a great professor/lecturer. The content is not at all dense or difficult, but his grading criteria is borderline insane. He ranks all the greenbook exams and then only gives As to the top %s regardless of effort. That said, you will learn a lot in his class and he is compassionate.

Ron is a character for sure. His lectures are great, although he sometimes says some weird stuff. (used "illiterate indonesian women" as an example of why sweatshops are sometimes the best option people have, but Indonesia has a higher literacy rate than America) Besides comments like that, my only compliant is the ungodly amount of reading.

Ron is great and he's famous in his field of work. He is pretty strict on paper but if you meet him you'll find that he's a sweetie. I was in two 400 lvl classes when I took PS102 and I worked harder in his class to maintain an A than I did in those other two combined. I'm pretty sure only a handful of students got As that term.
This is without a doubt the worst class I have ever taken in college.
The class content wasn't too bad, but the GEs can be tough graders. I'd recommend going to office hours because he genuinely is a good professor and is super passionate about the subjects.
Ron sets an 80 percent average for the papers in this class, making it nearly impossible to earn a good grade in the class. The material itself is interesting and he is a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ron is a great guy. Easily the best prof I've had. Sure, he grades a bit heavy but I STRONGLY RECOMMEND going to his office hours. You will have a friend for life.

I think the worst part about this class was the GEs, they didn't give any feedback at all or if they did it wasn't helpful just rude. Prof Mitchell is really nice and his lectures are short and easy to watch. For an intro course you have to work for it but it's not too bad!

Him and his GE's are pretty tough graders and don't give feedback on the assignments or explain the grade unless you go to office hours. His class had a reasonable amount of work though and his lectures were easy to watch. He also made weekly quizzes pretty easy. Overall just a tough grader, but funny and personable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have been taking college courses for 2 years and have never taken a class as awful as this. This is a 100 level class. Ron doesn't believe in A's (95 is the highest he will give) and the weekly writing assignments to test your understanding are impossible to get a good grade on. If you have grade anxiety, do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was by far the worst class I haven taken at UO so far. Ron is an extremely tough grader (doesn't believe in giving A's). Lot's of writing assignments that are impossible to do well on. He was never available to his students and seems to not care about being a professor at all. Do not take this class.

Some of the worst grading rubrics and policies out of any class. Took PS102 and exceeded difficulty of the classes I have taken at the 300 level. Impossible to get full credit on anything, even opinionated statements. Take another 100 level class that is appropriate for this difficulty. Unclear grading expectations. So much reading and lectures.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS RON TEACHES. First, Ron refuses to give A's ! He also believes that "all first years are dumb" and compares first years to senior students. He admitted during office hours that his class sucks. Ron does not grade a single assignment but, tells GE's to NEVER give full credit. Grades are based on what's missing in the rubric.

Professor Mitchell is extremely difficult. His class during COVID-19 online was nearly impossible to pass. I am a senior taking a freshman level psych class and he makes the curriculum as if it is a grad level psych class. He doesn't budge on grading and is a really tough grader.

Professor Mitchell can be a tough professor to take but if you pay attention you will do very well. Going to his office hours is crucial not only does it put a face to who he is grading it helps a ton with your final project. I recommend starting on final paper early I waited until two days before the 15 page final paper was due and it was hell!

Professor Mitchell is an engaging lecturer and provides an inclusive space to communicate ideas. However, be aware he's one of the more demanding political science professors and unless you're willing to study and prepare, I wouldn't recommend him. If you are serious about your academics, his class is very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is honestly a good teacher if you like the lecture style of class. If you don't like lecture classes, then I would not recommend him. Good class and good teacher overall though.

Smart professor and overall good guy but the lectures were really long, sometimes dry and content-heavy. Also a ton of readings expected in a short time. Assignments weren't too bad, I just made sure to check in with my GE about grading expectations. There were a few quizzes throughout the term but the big assignments were papers.

Prof. Mitchell means well, and the transition to remote classes probably was difficult. However, he often lost trains of thought and the lectures were a bit monotonous. The content wasn't all that exciting, which made it hard to go to lecture. A lot of writing as well. He cares about what he teaches, and he tried his best. Easy enough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good guy and means well, but his train of thought is all over the place. I feel like I get seizures trying to understand him.

Professor Mitchell's class was the worst class I've taken at the university. He was disorganized, said things that weren't politically correct often, and made a class I was so excited for insufferable. Would not recommend.
Ron is a really hands-on professor. Learning with him means you get a valuable opportunity to grow as a scholar.

He just clearly doesnt care about any of his students. I understand classes are tough right now with the coronavirus but thats not an excuse to be unnecessarily tough and rude. I cant judge how his class is in person but online and through zoom I would never take his class again.

The grading was almost solely done by 2 GE's who seemed to have arbitrary standards. The grading standards weren't clear, especially for the final paper. Biggest takeaway: form over content. Citations matter immensely. Format your paper the way the prof. seems to want it. There was a lot of objectionable material presented in the class.

This was probably the most engaging class I took in the economics department. I wouldn't say the material is hard. It's very intuitive. The workload, however, is heavy. You will spend a lot of time doing independent research to support your hypothesis on the final project. Maybe it's not a good idea to take this one when overloading on credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is a very educated, engaging lecturer. Hes a great professor and encourages you to make the most of your education. Dont take this class if you dont actually care about learning the material. He has great lectures and is interesting to listen to. However he offered extra credit that I did and never gave me the points for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ron Mitchell is one of the best professors that the University has to offer. He may seem tough and a hard grader (which he is), but is all in fairness and with the intent to push his students to get the most out of their education. Take this class if you have ample time to read and prepare as it is necessary. Love this professor!

The class is not super heavy on the workload, but make sure you complete the readings if you want to understand the lectures. Ron is a fantastic professor who relates every concept to real-life and teaches you how to think like a political scientist. His teaching methods are second-to-none and is extremely professional and fair. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not the easiest class. Used to be a 400-level. There's plenty of theoretical stuff if you're into that, but Mitchell's lectures are comprehensive and he provides plenty of materials to succeed in the class. It's difficult to ace the course, but if you at least review the slides and draft essays, you'll do well.

The course is no walk-in-the-park. Professor Mitchell takes a structured approach to teaching the Environmental Politics class and gives open-ended questions for the final paper. Exams and projects are difficult but he makes himself very available during office hours. I would personally take a class again with him.

Ron Mitchell is a captivating and engaging professor. Lectures are relatively comprehensive- it is necessary to glance over the readings and generally understand it, but reading every page is not needed. He covers lots of ground during lectures and incorporates critical thinking skills as he exposes students to international organization. Fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ron Mitchell is undoubtedly the best professor you will ever have at the U of O. He makes you work for your grade, yet doesn't make the class unreasonable. You won't have to do much on your own so long as you pay attention in lecture and listen to everything he says. That said it requires plenty of studying attentiveness to the topics.

Professor Mitchell truly cares about how politics affects the global environment. He will broaden the scope of your thinking and will challenge your beliefs about the world. He makes the class a hard-earned grade but its so rewarding.

Professor Mitchell is a highly intelligent man and will challenge your thinking immensely. That said, the class is extremely difficult to get an A in but don't beat yourself up for it. The learning experience in this course and Mitchell's candor is well-worth the time and effort and you'll leave the class knowing more than you would have otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ron Mitchell opens your eyes to the international realm in this course. The course is structured on three theories that often overlap and intertwine with one another depending on viewpoints, but they are also distinct. His lecture material was more than enough to be successful on tests and he is very accessible. The workload is high so be ready.

The class is a walk in the park until the final exam, which is incomprehensibly difficult. You are expected to write three substantially in-depth essays within the course of two hours. It just isn't enough time especially for freshman polisci students to have the capability to do this. That said Mitchell is an amazing professor and cares deeply.

Your grade is primarily based on the midterm and the final. The other assignments should be completed, but they're not really worth anything. He has unrealistic expectations for an introductory course, but you do absorb a lot of information and you learn well in this class. He is a very engaging professor and super intense and unfiltered.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing quality professor. He makes you work for your grade, but covers topics exceptionally well in class. Make sure to do your readings and you will be fine. He has lots of interesting things to say with regards to today's foreign policy. In terms of the class, he's a captivating lecturer and fair grader. He cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is the best professor that I have had at UO. You are definitely going to be challenged and there is a lot of work but he is willing to help and super easy to talk to. I would highly recommend taking one of his classes if you want to be challenged academically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: favorite professor at UO. extremely knowledgeable on the subject and clearly enjoys teaching the subject which is evident in his lectures. genuinely cares about his students and wants to see people learn and succeed. would highly encourage taking the time to go to his office hours.
My favorite professor I've ever had hands down. He truly cares about what he's teaching and really focuses on student development. Tough class, worth it.

Professor Mitchell is the most knowledgeable teacher I've had. His classes are very challenging but they're worth taking to learn from Mithell. He comes off intimidating but if you go into office hours he's really helpful and welcoming.

Professor Mitchell is by far my favorite teacher I've had so far. He is very knowledgable and passionate about what he does. He does come off a little intimidating but he is very approachable and really wants you to succeed

Professor Mitchell was the best professor I've ever had.  He expects a lot from his students, but trust me, you'll want to live up to those expectations out of respect for him alone.  Take his class, you won't regret it.  You won't get an A, you may not get a B, but you'll leave the class having your academic world rocked.

Mitchell's classes are hard, but they are incredibly rewarding. Taking this class has made me a more confident student. He sets high standards, but he wants you to do well. MITCHELL WILL HELP YOU! Taking his help will lead to your success. Respect the class, respect him, work hard, ask for help-and his class will change your academic life.

Professor Mitchell is an outstanding professor. He comes off as a bit intimidating, but he's passionate about what he teaches. This class isn't easy for an Intro, but you learn so much. He really sparked an interest for me in International Relations and Environmental Studies. In the end, he's a very likable professor, and it is an interesting class
Very informative, interesting professor. If you like writing, this class is for you. The whole course is structured around a 15-20 page paper, with a few supporting writing assignments.

Mitchell is the most passionate teacher I have ever had, he made me want to become a better person. This class is no walk in the park, but once you finish it, you feel great! I learned a ton, and he really got me pumped for more PS classes in my future! Take anything taught by Mitchell!

Ron Mitchel was a very good teacher. His lectures were interesting, and he was very interested in helping students succeed. This class also sparked my interest in International Relations. There was a lot of reading, but they were all useful and interesting. I strongly recommend taking this class.

Ron Mitchell is an incredible professor. He made lectures exciting with his sense of humor and interpretation of current events. This class is challenging, but well worth the time. Five stars for the class and the professor.

Ridiculous amounts of reading for a lower division class.  No visuals during lecture so it gets incredibly boring.  Too much focus on theory as opposed to current issues.  Insane exams that are basically all essays and complicated ones at that. I thought I was really interested in Intl Relations, thanks to this class, I've realized otherwise.

Great Professor. Lots of readings, but if you learn to skim its fine. Do the reading because he touches on other things in lecture, but it wont make sense unless you read. Lecture notes are online, which is super helpful because lectures can be hard to follow. He is very interested in his topics and so makes it interesting for the students

Class is alright, he posts lectures on Blackboard but has no power point or any visuals during lecture, you just listen the whole time which means you really have to listen and keep up.  It's easy to get restless this way but some of the material is interesting.  Lots of reading though.  Alright class overall I'd say.  Could be better.

I can't sing Professor Mitchell's praises enough.  He is intimidating at first, but as long as you apply yourself, ask questions when things are unclear, and do the work, you can learn four times as much from his class than any others.  He is also great at rewarding you for your hard work: with respect, mentorship, recommendations, and even jobs.

Be prepared to learn.  His courses are demanding, complex, and he expects you to set yourself apart from your peers.  One of the hardest and most rewarding classes I've ever taken.  Don't give up in his class, push yourself through it.  Also, sign up for office hours.
tons of busy work and abnormal amounts of reading. if you like essay tests take this class
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Mitchell is quite demanding and his classes require students' full attention. He expects a lot and is very helpful in office hours. Very friendly but TURN OFF YOUR CELLPHONE during class and when you visit him. He gets mad.

Billy's humor is not it, he doesn't reply to emails and smells strongly of cigarettes and coffee. But he wants you to understand. Yes, if you get a 4/5, it's "not met", and only if you get a 5/5 have you "met" a topic, but there are a lot of opportunities for you to "meet" on a topic. This class is not hard to pass if you make an effort.

Billy really wants everyone to do well in this class. He prioritizes understanding over short term memorizing concepts to be tested on once. The LO style of grading is a bit confusing at first but then incredibly helpful.
Convoluted grading scheme. Hard to reach outside of outside of class. Very sassy and condescending. Shouldn't be teaching at this university

Billy genuinely should retire, he doesn't know how to teach a college class. He not only ghosts students that email him, but even his TA's who are often left in the dark about certain questions. Additionally, on tests, you must get a 5/5 to "pass", as even a 4/5 is considered a "fail" in his exams. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Billy does not actually teach. He rambles about god knows what, genuinely speaking gibberish half of the time. On top of that, the exams are incredibly difficult when we have no clear criteria of what we need to be studying for. Not one question has been answered by this guy during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The one word I would use to describe this class in overcomplicated. I feel bad for the GE's that are in charge of grading. Nearly every lecture has an in-class worksheet that is submitted for credit, but class is only 50 minutes long, so the entire class is the worksheet instead of him actually teaching.

Imagine going on a treasure hunt everytime you want to find where your assignments are, nothing is populated in Canvas and he releases assignments each week with differing dates they were due than last week. He doesnt respond to emails and may just be the sassiest man of his generation. The whole course is a joke, but 203 truly is the cherry on top

He is a funny guy, and honestly, the class can ask some stupid questions so he is partly intitled to his sassy nature. The grading system is very bad. I got an A+ alongside many others, but really, the class is set up as Pass No Pass. It is a very challenging course until you realize all the test questions come from the textbook.

By the fourth time Billy asks the class the same clicker question, it'll suddenly dawn on you how your time would be better spent playing NYT games on your computer. A very sassy man with very poor teaching skills!
He's a nice guy but a terrible lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My #1 problem with his course is that he never uploaded the complete lecture slides, making it extremely hard to study efficiently to his standards. The bi-weekly pass/no pass assessments a lot of the time had ridiculously hard problems that didn't reflect the general course work. LOCK IN if you're a student who has to work a lot of hours for money
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really like Billy as a person but this course was definitely challenging. It is unlike all the other physics courses. Do not expect to pass without putting in the work. Graded on a standards based system with bi-weekly exams. Difficult exams but many makeup opportunities. If you stay on top of the textbook and office hours you can pass.

Goodluck is all I can say. I'm sure Billy cares for his students,but lecture made it difficult to believe so. He had passive aggressive answers to students, would talk about irrelevant things, and was just SO sassy. He made a very specific grading system with biweekly tests,but you do have a number of opportunities to pass each Learning Objective.

Hot take but I liked Billy as a teacher, but outside of his lecturing ability and his personality everything else in this class sucked. Horrible system of really hard bi-weekly tests, although pro tip: all of the questions came from the textbook. Re-grade requests will be your best friend because the GEs and Billy are so god awful at grading.

I would go so far as to say that his grading system is arbitrary and capricious. It's so convoluted and it's based on a P/NP system. I've never been so frustrated with the structure of a course. He doesn't give feedback, and he uses ai to grade the exams. I had to teach myself all of the material. Don't take 203 at UO.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall the class isn't difficult to get a good grade in; however, it takes a lot of work to get there and feels very overwhelming up until the end of the term having biweekly tests. Billy thinks very highly of himself and his grading system, if anything I felt like I learned less this way. Lectures are terrible Billy is not kind with questions.

He didn't post half of the lectures.The material itself isn't that hard, but his system is confusing. He didn't answer questions in a nice way, neither straight forward. The grading is P/NP. That's why only about 20-30% of students pass each LO on the first 2 tries combined. The grading is very slow. Exams(LOs) are bi-weekly on your tutorial time.

He doesn't respond to constructive criticism, is rude, & the entire class is Pass/Nopass, lets say u mess up by accidently putting the wrong units on an answer, you get 0% even if all the work up to that point is right. Previous courses got take home exams, but we had in person exams and yet class is worth the same credit, whole course is unfair.

Lectures were pretty unhelpful, pretty much did all of my learning for this course from the textbook (pro tip: all of the test questions were taken from the "problems" section of the textbook). Grading system was also incredibly complicated, but there were a decent amount of ways to make up missed learning outcomes. Billy is a sarcastic AH.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is one of the hardest I've taken at this university so far. He will answer questions sarcastically, slides are incomplete, and the grading system for the tests is P/NP with barely any students getting the questions right. If you can, take this course elsewhere for your pre-requisites. Be ready to teach yourself EVERYTHING and GOOD LUCK.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class has a lot going on and is honestly quite confusing. Lecture isn't useful, and the slides he posts are incomplete so good luck trying to use them to study. Test questions are incredibly challenging and P/NP format, with only about 10% of people getting most questions correct. If you can take online I highly recommend.

Pros: This course will force you to learn & retain so much information that your brain expands 10x bigger. Cons: Extremely difficult test questions, lots of work and super time-intensive (self-study, lab, tutorial, readings, office hours, pre-lecture questions). Can't find any answers to tutorials/activities/slides/past exams.

His grading system is both lenient & VERY strict. 14 LO's & u need 12 to get an A. Each goal is P/NP w/ bi-weekly exams, u get 3 chances & couple other opts, but u must be almost flawless to pass LO's, I missed 1 unit & got a 4.5/5 = 0% for that LO. Test Q's can be REALLY hard. Frustrating that tutorials and slides have 0 answers to Q's. Stressful.

Do not take the third term of physics here if you don't have to. The grading system is confusing and for the exams, he uses AI to grade them which is inconsistent between students. He also does not answer emails which makes it difficult to do revisions for these exam attempts. The class is very unorganized and he uses multiple homework platforms.

I loved the structure of lab, there was a pre-lab done at beginning of class, in class lab, and after class you annotate your pre-lab and complete a follow up quiz. You can always resubmit your work if you do not meet competency, making it easy to do well in the course. I would not have passed lecture without taking the lab.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Steven Beda, specifically his US Vietnam war class, DO IT. This class changed my life, because it made me really want to reengage in writing and reading again. The lectures were not even mandatory, but I showed up to every one because it was so interesting each class, especially w the vet speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor in many ways. Extremely engaging lectures and discussions, actually knows how to lead a class through learning in ways other than just assigning readings. Very fair grader. Excited to take more classes with Beda in the future.

While there was a lot of reading, this class is absolutely worth it. It's a seminar style class, where our focus was on PNW history. He is an excellent professor who gives solid feedback. When in doubt, go to his office hours. Would absolutely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Beda is the bomb dot com. This was my second course with him, and I cannot recommend him more. He cares deeply about your success in his class and will always find ways to support you where you're at, which is especially valuable in a class like 290 (very research heavy and dependent on one huge paper). TLDR; he's the goat.

My favorite professer, gives really good engaging lectures that are really easy to pay attention too. Does not grade papers on writing quality, just ideas. He also is really funny and understanding about extensions or extra help.

This class is fantastic, light work load outside of a few books, however the second book of the term is the best I've read in college by far and greatly changed my relationship with the university. The field trip is fantastic, and the lectures are very informative while being light and interactive. Easily one of the best classes you can take.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Classes were genuinely enjoyable and quite engaging. Highly recommend taking any class with Steve when the opportunity is there.

Really engaging and interesting lectures, the only assignments were the mid-term, final and term paper. He's a really fair grader and seemed to focus more on the overall quality and content of your work instead of nitpicking random details to take away points for like a lot of professors do.

Steven Beda is an amazing professor! He is passionate in lectures, and he is very funny and easy to talk to. He is very down to earth in office hours which makes things easy if you have a problem.The exams are short answer & one essay question, but you get a week to do it. There is also a research paper. History for the non-history student!
Steve is a super awesome guy with very insightful lectures. Majority of the class is graded off of the midterm, final, and research paper. All those are graded by a GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives interesting lectures, doesn't give much homework, easy to follow along even if you never had taken a history class

Amazing Professor and was the easiest to work with so far at the University of Oregon. Attendance isn't always mandatory, but a lot of the stuff for midterms and finals is always gonna be on the lecture slides.

Beda is one of my favorite professors I've had. Our only assignments were two midterm papers and one large, 8-10 page essay. I know what you're thinking, "Oh that's awful!", but in reality, it wasn't that bad and he gives tons of accommodations and leeway. His lectures are incredible, and he does a great job of keeping students entertained.

Steve is my favorite history professor by far. Graded on take-home exams and papers, and you need to read a few books throughout the term. Impossible to fail and he is super funny, involved, and nice. Very interesting lectures. 10/10 recommend this class and Steve.

This guy is super nice, and attendance is mandatory. There is a take home midterm and take home final with a ten page paper in between. The paper isn't bad honestly because its about someones you know. The tests take some time, but not that bad either. His classes are engaging and is genuinely a really good guy. GE was also super chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Beda is genuinely one of the only professors who has made me excited to go to a history class and learn. The way he structures his lectures is very engaging, entertaining, and timely. His GE's this term are awesome too! Overall great class and highly recommend.

Other than the 10-page research paper this class is a breeze. Absolutely would recommend taking this class. Despite its length, the research paper is also graded extremely leniently, so its hard to mess up in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: funny and nice guy. if you need to take history class TAKE HIM. i've done pretty bad in history classes before but prof. beda makes the lectures so interesting. i always looked forward to going to his class. tbh it was my fave class and im not a history major. not a lot of weekly homework so you really have time to digest information being taught

This was one of my favorite History classes I have taken in a while. I struggle to pay attention in lectures, but Beda makes it super engaging and interesting. The workload is light except for the 3 major writing assignments you have throughout the term. Basically, your entire grade depends on those essays, but grading is pretty chill.

Great teacher, amazing lecturer. Engaging lectures, makes difficult content understandable. Only issue is a lot of grade rides on 3 papers. One of which is very long, and I do bad with assignments that span the whole course. Otherwise, TAKE HIS CLASSES!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and funny guy. He loves to chat outside of class, or whenever he runs into students. He is very considerate with his students and wants everyone to pass. Highly rec taking him if you need to fill in your history credit. There is nothing hard about the class if you pay attention during the lectures. Weekly hw just consists of reading
cool guy. easy class. sometimes the instructions are mixed but he's so chill it doesn't really matter. ge's are also chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very nice and helpful outside of class. Lectures are not hard to follow and he makes them fun. If you do the section assignments and pay attention in class there is no reason you can't get an A!

I took two classes that aren't listed; HIST352 and HIST290, Steve is a great lecturer and is always engaging and funny. History majors should be excited when they get him for a class regardless of the topic. Definitely give your effort because his feedback and teaching will make it worth while.

One of the best teachers I've had so far, I've taken two of his classes now and loved both. Very lecture heavy but if you pay attention, take notes and go to class you'll do fine. He's very passionate about everything he teaches and will bend over backwards to help you succeed. HST 352 and 468 are both great, 10/10 would recommend.

I loved this class more than anything. Steve teaches with such passion and truly is such a smart man. His midterms and finals are very easy and stress-free. I highly recommend taking this class. I decided I wanted to do a history minor after taking this class.
Professor Beda gives super engaging lectures! I recommend him for any class, he cares about his students and has made me enjoy learning about history. Definitely take this class!

BEDA IS THE BEST PROF!! He really set the bar high for all other professors. He genuinely seems so passionate and cares about his students and any questions they may have. All quizzes and papers were easy if you just went to the lecture and took notes.
Says attendance isn't mandatory but I wouldn't miss lecture or sessions. They will help you on the exams. Beda is also passionate and thoughtful and his lectures are awesome to be in. Great prof.
Professor Beda gives amazing lectures and is very funny. This class helped push me to become a history major.
Made lectures interesting, and easy to follow. Super lecture heavy but if you show up and pay attention you'll pass. Midterm and final are both take home, only big project is a research paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good chill guy, super engaging lectures and very helpful outside of class too. Class has a few major assignments but honestly isn't very hard or that much work. 100% would reccomend.

Beda is an amazing professor but you will really only get something out of his classes if you are white. He addresses racial relations in a way that BIPOC already understand and have experienced. The class is 100% setup for white students who need a broader scope of historical white privilege.

Steven was both my history 202 professor and my FIG leader. He was a wonderful first introduction to the school. He is very lecture heavy and while attending class is not a requirement, you will struggle if you miss the majority of his lectures. Overall, professor Beda is an incredible history professor and I would take any of his classes offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took American Century hist with him and his lectures (they were recorded because it was all online) were always so fun, interesting, and full of info. The thing I liked most about this class was that it dug into parts of history that weren't discussed in my high school history class. Such a fun first-year class to satisfy gen requirements!

I took professor Beda for 2 classes this term, the most difficult of which being a required seminar for history majors where we had to write a HEFTY research paper. Throughout the term he has been nothing but an amazing professor, especially given the circumstances and the difficulty of writing this paper.

I loved the structure of this class and felt it provided for optimal learning. Weekly documentary, lecture, and reflection. Two novels read over the term, one for the midterm, one for the final. Lectures covered various interesting topics not addressed by the documentary. Take this class!
Professor Beda is probably my favorite Professor I've had at UO, he's very funny and caring and the class is a lot of interesting discussion.

Dr. Beda is one of the best profs I have ever had! He gives great lectures and is always there to help you. As long as you watch all the lectures and take notes, you will do great. Its mostly little weekly assignments and then a research paper, an essay-questions mid term and final.

Lectures are easy to follow and relatively interesting. Good communicator. Makes no effort to shield his political beliefs and grading criteria is not always completely clear. This class really only focused on a couple of elements of 20th century U.S. history when, to my knowledge, it was intended to be more of an overview of this time period.

Steve was amazing, even through the pandemic! I had so much fun in HIST203 because he was stilling engaging through pre-recorded lectures. Steve and his GEs (I had Adam Quinn) gave useful feedback. The lectures and assignments were sometimes long but never too tedious.

I cannot recommend Steven enough! He is incredibly kind and understanding towards his students, and I have learned so much through this class. The course material is incredibly relevant to today and the way that Steven teaches makes it easy to understand. Everybody should take this class!

I took History 203 my first term of college and am so happy I did. Your grade will mostly be determined by midterms and finals, but Dr. Beda prepares you well, so it goes smoothly. Take good notes on his lectures and you will pass with flying colors, as well as learn a great deal of important history along the way. Highly highly highly recommend!

This professor reminds me of the amazing, funny, and great history teacher we all had in high school. He is relatable, understanding of students, and makes lectures interesting. Even in an online world I have still enjoyed his class!! Would definitely take again and would love to take his class in person so I can get the full experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Beda is one of the best professors at the University of Oregon. His lectures are amazing, and his passion is clear. The workload of the class is manageable and he is always available outside of class. Would highly recommend.
I am not a history major, but he makes history fun and easy to learn!

Anyone who doesn't like Steve must have a dislike of genuinely funny, nice, intelligent and caring teachers. From his 203 and 388 courses, both had a low workload (as long as you attended class and kept up) with few-to-no readings. But I learned so much and declared a major in history. He is exceptionally engaging in both 1 on 1 and in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man made me love history and want to minor in it. His lectures are amazing. I had this class at the end of the day, from 4:00-5:50 i believe, which is late, and I got tired, but I looked forward to this class every time I had it. I genuinely feel like I learned something from this class and I actually had a passion for it, which got me an A.

Steven was easily the best professor I have ever had. He was super easy and open to talk to outside of class and he is super knowledgeable on all the topics he discusses. Highly recommend taking any of his classes

Steven was a solid teacher. He knew so much about the topics at hand, always allowed students to question or voice their opinions, and generally, seemed to be genuinely passionate about the class. Honestly, one of the best class and teacher combination you could hope for.

Steven is a caring professor, with interesting lectures. Lots of reading required, but most of it is interesting. The grade is made up of essays, not super challenging. You won't regret taking Steven's class.
Steven has the most entertaining lectures of any teacher I've had. The grade for this class is made up of essays, about assigned books. If you don't like writing a ton don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most passionate professors I've ever seen. Steve is amazing.

Steve is an incredible teacher. His lectures are fantastic, but get ready to take lots of notes. His mid-terms and finals are take-home, but focus heavily on themes from lectures and discussions. Read the books andd go to class, because he really enjoys teaching to an interactive group.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It was such a great class, the information was interesting, and his lectures weren't boring. You could tell he really wanted to be there teaching us. It was enjoyable to be in class. He wasn't a super hard grader, but he also gave great feedback. Midterm and Final were both take-home. AWESOME TEACHER! He is funny and keeps the lectures interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best history professor at U of O.  Lectures are really fund and really interesting.  I was always interested in what Prof Beda was talking about.  He's an easy grader and I actually liked the assignments.

Beda is a great professor.  His lectures are really interesting and he's funny.  He really encourages students to speak up and he really wants to know what students are thinking.  I'm not a history major but I definitely want to take more of his classes.

Very informational class. His lectures have a lot of information in them, but it's cool to see the progression of the media throughout time. Accessible outside of class and is a cool dude to talk to during his office hours. Take him if you can!

Two weekly quizzes directly from the lecture videos. The lecture videos are many years old, mixed with AI, and overall boring, long, and unhelpful for the most part. Two essays determine sixty percent of your entire grade with a super vague loose rubric. You will get marked down for random nonsense in your essay's. Take an in person over this.

Such a fun class to take, he makes the most fun and engaging slides I have ever seen from a professor. His creativity, wit, and humor are pretty unmatched when it comes to online courses, and this class is totally worth taking. Couldn't recommend enough!

I had Prof. Bivins for J305 ASYNC Media History* TAKE THIS CLASS WITH TOM! He is extremely silly and cares about his material, even making it fun when it can be boring at times. I wish so badly I could have taken this in person with him, but it's still great as an online class. Easy to follow lectures with open-note weekly quizzes + two papers.

Horrible professor. Lectures are 1-2 videos a week on canvas, they're just AI slop mixed with 5+ yo reused lectures. Prof. wont email you back, lazy, and manages to be condescending in an online class. 60% of your grade is 2 short papers, unclear and subjective grading, if you mess up one in the slightest there is no chance to recoup your grade.

For me, the lectures just being videos weren't helpful. I started to realize the content wasn't really helping me learn but the class itself is truly interesting. I enjoyed all the work that he has put into his lectures. Just get ready to watch 20+ minute videos (at least 2 a week) and 2 big assignments for your grade to be based upon.
Super nice guy. Puts in the work to make his lectures watchable, and it pays off. Essays can be a bit hard but the rest of the class is pretty easy.

No textbooks needed to buy, no attendance taken but you do best if you watch the lectures and take notes too. Only two big assignments besides the quizzes you after every lecture, which again are easy if you pay attention and take notes. He is SO kind and you can totally tell he cares so much about students even tho it's async and he's hilarious.
Absolutely amazing professor. I've taken a few classes with him and would take more if possible. He is so passionate about each topic and makes it easy for students to learn.

Professor Bivins is a little wacky but is so fun and engaging. All textbook info is linked in the module so no purchase is necessary! You have 1 quiz for each lecture (about 2 lectures each week), and then 2-3 case studies that allow you to actually apply the knowledge you've learned to real-life experiences! He's a great professor I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did poorly on his first case study and attended his next office hours for help. He explained everything I did wrong, read my answers for the second one, and advised me on what I could improve on. Seriously such a kind professor despite some things I see here. I think he's hilarious and I like his cartoons as they don't bore me like other classes.

The class is set up super clearly and is easy to complete. You have plenty of time to prepare for assignments. There are two weekly quizzes and two essays over the term. The lectures are interesting, and the modules are set up really well.

This dude is so lazy, it's WILD. It's spring of '23 and he's still using stuff from COVID for his online lectures. Also, he treats students like they're middle schoolers. His assignments are all just busy work, no help. His online lectures are full of horribly made cartoons that scream "I have too much free time." Avoid this POS at ALL costs!
Prof Bivins is literally the best professor ever! Theres 2 small quizzes each week and only 2 two page essays for the whole term. overall this class is super easy and he is just the best
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his online media ethics course and thought it was well set-up and easy to complete. Weekly there were two interactive and fun lectures, and two quick and easy quizzes. The case studies are the hardest part, but they're interesting and fun. I could reach him outside class just fine. I would take again!

Thomas is a great guy who creates creative lectures. The quizzes are questions right off the lectures, so those are pretty easy. His GEs are the tough ones. I gave pretty in-depth and detailed papers (3 of them), but I got Bs on all of them. The directions say, "there are no wrong answers," but the GEs think otherwise.

Bivins is overall the weirdest yet cool professor I have had. I love his vibe and even though all information is within his video lectures, it's entertaining. There is about 2 quizzes every week about the video lecture, but information can low-key be hard to find just how it's organized. There is no way you can fail if you do everything.

All in all, this class is super easy and professor Bivins is so sweet and helpful! You only have 2 (5 questions) weekly quizzes and a 3-page midterm and final essay - so super easy and manageable! You can tell he cares a lot about his job and his online class is pretty laxed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This guy. THIS GUY!! I love him so much. Who else does their best to engage students in lectures by making funny animations and voices? Never before this class have I looked forward to a lecture, but here we are. You can tell that he cares deeply about the subject hes teaching and that he wants everyone in the class to succeed.

Took this class during Covid, didn't know what to expect. By far the most profound and CARING professors at UO. Wow, if yall took J 387 during the winter, I cried throughout his last farewell video. This man puts so much effort into his lectures and makes it fun with the cute animations he does. So deserving and an honor to take his class. 10/10

He is a great professor who clearly loves what he does. He cares about what he's teaching, he cares about his students and you will walk away from his class looking at the world around you a little differently. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bivins is knowledgable about the subject matter. The required book he assigns is written by him, so it covers everything that he talks about in lecture, sometimes even word for word. He takes attendance and you are only allowed 3 absences. If you have the opportunity to take media ethics w/ a different prof, I would. Pretty boring class.

He definitely puts a lot of effort into his lectures. Very humorous, and always does his very best to explain concepts. Even though attendance is mandatory, he is accommodating. Tests require good amount of studying. I learned a lot in this class.

You can tell he puts effort into creating the lectures and is passionate about his subject. An understanding guy. I missed a final exam for no reason other than my own mistake and he let me make it up when I emailed him about it.

One of the worst professors. Extremely arrogant, thinks his humor adds to the class when in reality it only takes away from learning. His book, that he forces you to purchase, is poorly written and extremely redundant in regards to lectures. Cannot stand listening to this professor speak; his assumed self-worth has out-grown his ability to teach.
Makes class as interesting as possible. Class is not mandatory, but is helpful for some of the test questions.

He zips through slideshows like it's nobody's business, so don't expect to get all the notes you NEED in class. All the slideshows are online. Concepts seem simple when he explains them but an immense amount of studying won't even save you from the exams.

Bivins is a great professor. The trend among students who think he is horrible, is that they aren't great students. Yes he is mildly arrogant--but he has reason to be. If you show up and try, you will pass his classes.

Worst professor I've ever had at the university. His grading criteria is ridiculous. He calls students out for being late and texting which is a complete distraction to the whole lecture. I would recommend NOT taking a class from him. Not helpful and you can tell he hates his job.

I did not appreciate the professor's judgments and character. For an ethics teacher, he was arguably the most unethical and disrespectful instructor I have had at UO. His arrogance was also quite unpleasant and the way he regarded his GTFs was impolite and uncomfortable. Highly contemptuous.
not helpful and hard grading.
This professor is extremely arrogant, full of himself, and absolutely loves the fact that he has a captive audience for two hours.

This was my 2nd class w/Bivins. He is a sweet guy, he was always right on top of emailing students back outside of class. His test are EXTREMELY hard though & he does not curve & has no mercy on students w/test, but if you go to class everyday & make an effort he will pass you. He can be a bit silly but overall fun & a good teacher.

Arrogant. Expect to buy his book and be required to quote him in HW (one essay per night) or lose points. Arbitrarily canceled midterm and graded class based on rigorously examined homework. Calls out students for being tardy, takes attendance every class. Gets a huge kick out of himself, creates annoying following of minions in doing so.

He is smart (and yes, he does know it), but is extremely down-to-earth and helpful when asked. He may seem arrogant, but he's seen a lot of things, been a lot of places, and done a lot of stuff. He doesn't like to participate in office politics, and is no-nonsense.  The people offended by him are often a little overtly-PC. He gives what he gets.
Just make sure you go to class, even though he doesn't take attendence regularly. He will take attendence randomly and then screw you over for not being there.
I loved this class's material, but the professor was arrogant and self-centered when I approached him with my concerns.
Great teacher. Love his keynote slides!

There's a lot of homework, the equivelency of an essay per class. However, they aren't hard and as long as you write a lot and cite the text at least once you, he's a pretty easy grader. He's not as scary as people think. He's actually a really smart and helpful funny professor.

He wrote the textbook and it is used little. Assignments due with every class. Entertaining lectures. Only allows laptops in the first three rows. Hates myspace and videogames. Expect to spend as much time working on the class outside of it as you spend in it.
Average grade on the midterm was failing. The final was optional because the class grades were so bad. Only 15 people tops took the final. Lots of memorization. Could have been a better experience.
He's very enthusiastic about what he teaches, and it is very interesting. However, the midterm was way too difficult and there was SO much homework.

I thought he was a great teacher with a lot of knowledge.  I was scared of him at first with because of his strictness but I learned a lot.  Class teaches very valuable information for any journalist.  What seems like busy work(homework) was very helpful to me in understanding the content of the topic.
Likes to lecture just to hear himself speak. Cool powerpoint presentations though. Tries hard to be funny. Offends a lot of people.

very clear grading rubric, you basically choose your final grade based on how many assignments you complete (so if you wanted a C youd only have to do 70% of the work) very understanding format, very understanding teacher, genuinely a good class !
Amazing professor who is super nice and gives feedback to make you truly a better writer.

Bjorn is nice and responsive to his students' wants & needs. He is knowledgeable about debate and assigned interesting and challenging public speaking projects, including both speeches & debates. He uses labor-based grading which gives you a lot of control over your grade and is essentially just a measure of participation. Cool class!
Bjorn is a really caring professor and clearly keeps all his students wellbeing in mind. However the workload for this course is beyond heave, expect like 9 hours a week.
Was a very engaging professor with good class participation in our discussions. Creative classroom topics to discuss in relation to the material being reviewed.

Somewhat of a tough grader, and expectations are a little too much for a simple class like this. If there are options for other instructors I suggest looking into it. I feel like others might be far more easier and less work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A bit of a tough grader and class can be a little boring, but overall a cool guy and good professor. He gave us the opportunity for up to 4% extra credit which was great.

he is a bit of a tough grader with a caveat. That being you will be guaranteed a C as long as you turn in something that meets the assignments minimum recruitments. The only way you fail this class is if you dont turn anything in

Bjorn is an extremely personable guy and leads a consistently enjoyable class. He uses a labor based grading system that essentially just rewards completion with the option to do extra work for an "A". He definetly assigns a lot of writing but also helps improve your writing with peer review sessions and thoughtful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most work graded on completion.  Lectures tend to be a bit boring, but Bjorn is really flexible and willing to help with anything and everything.  Easy grader.  He cares a lot, he is willing to spend an hour individually going over your essays with you.  Really good feedback on writing.  Attendance mandatory, but he does hybrid zoom classes.

This course had the labor-based grading module therefore you could get a B if you just do the most basic work. That's nice because you can just write and not worry about the basics, which allows you to write better. The course itself is a little bland but not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy. Bjorn is both helpful and understanding. He helped me write a great cover letter for internships and the class did not take a lot of time, which was great considering my other CIS classes were really challenging at the time. I took the class in Winter 2020.

Bjorn is an interesting guy, his class is graded on labor so you literally just have to do the assignments plus 2 extra credit assignments for an A. His class lectures are incredibly boring so that is the one down side to the class but it definitely is an easy GPA booster!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bjorn is a wonderful person, but not the best instructor. Heavy on the writing and quizzes, but his class is very manageable if you use your time wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Bjorn really surprised me with his class. Not only does he show that he cares tremendously about his students and our futures. He acts like a student in the sense of how he gets along with his students and overall is just a splendid guy. Would absolutely recommend him if you are worried about writing classes in college.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Super nice guy and does labor based grading instead of grading on quality... Soo just make sure you complete all the requirements and you'll get an A. Super flexible and easy going.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Personable, funny, helpful, honest, understanding, and willing to help outside of class. He really made an effort to include everyone in discussions, and make students feel at home. If you can't handle being critiqued, you shouldn't be in college. His job is to help you improve your writing, and he does it well.
Bjorn was amazing! He went out of his way to help me succeed and was always available for extra help.  I am so glad I chose Bjorn and am hoping to take 122 from him as well!
Thought I would hate this class but Bjorn made discussions fun and was super helpful and understanding if necessary.

Strongly advise not taking his class. He gives horrible feedback! He told me to revise things that didn't even make sense.  He schedules peer reviews during midterms, which was extremely inconvenient. Makes you do a reading assignment on blackboard twice a week, it took up way to much unnecessary time and it didn't help with anything.
awesome

I got a good grade in the class. the teacher is honestly a rude grumpy man. He called multiple students out during class and tried to humiliate them. As a student listening to that, I was disgusted. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Fine enough professor. Participation is seemingly expected to align with his readings of texts + likes to go off on unrelated political tangents during lectures.
Overall he was a passionate professor that has fairly engaging lectures. The only downside is he was very passive aggressive in situations that weren't that deep.

Was distrustful of all students, went around the terms of the syllabus, and generally did a lot of petty things during lectures. Would often ask "open" questions during lecture while having a specific subjective answer in mind which could feel like ragebait, he then complained about engagement going down. My GE was great thankfully, s/o matt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steve if great if u like philosophy. The movies and readings we watched were interesting. Start of class question about the assigned material which is easy just have to prove you engaged with it in some way. In class essays were easy too if you kept up with the material and showed creativity. Lectures were sometimes boring but discussions were fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's actually really sweet, but you have to get on his good side because I can see how other people don't like him. it was a little frustrating that he didn't grade anything and would redirect you to the GE for questions but if you really need to talk, he will. I found him interesting but nice.

One of the worst electives I've taken. Attendance required, but lectures were confusing and mostly tangents. Brence ignored questions he didn't like, and even our GE knew he was crazy and had to reteach the material for us to understand every week. I rarely knew what he was talking about but maybe he didn't either.

I was terrified of Formal Logic but Dr. Brence made it make sense. Still a difficult class but if you apply yourself, you'll succeed. He is also very entertaining and has a good but dry sense of humor.

During the first half of first class all of the students were looking around confused if this teacher was real. Every single lecture we have, just wants to convince students that his negative thoughts and views are the correct and right way to think about things. He cuts students off to go on tangents to prove them wrong and is so pessimistic.

He says he loves class participation, but as soon as you disagree with him, you get shut down immediately. I was not a huge fan of this class, simply because he was super pessimistic about everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Brence is closed minded and ignores any opinion that negates his. He says he has a no-penalty absence policy of up to 4 days, but he grades based on attendance? If you don't turn in a reflection notecard at the beginning of class your grade legitimately drops 5 points, and he doesn't allow you to make them up. Loved my GE though S/O Kiley.
I can't really blame him for not liking his class, it's the people in the class that like to drone on.

Professor Brence was an amazing Formal Logic professor. I wouldn't want anyone else to teach it. While he does not take attendance, class is mandatory. You will be lost if you miss a single lecture as every concept is cumulative. He makes a daunting subject satisfying and challenging
Steven said that being creative is as difficult as giving birth.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures weren't engaging and made it hard to participate. He'd brush off comments that didn't match what he wanted. He expected us to respect his time but often went over class time without caring. The only thing that made this class bearable was my GE (shoutout Jonanthan). Attendance is mandatory.

Dr. Brence changes the syllabus and assignments throughout the quarter - he turned a paper into a test, makes you move your seats around and changed how he graded participation. He was unpredictable and not encouraging of students who disagreed with him. This class is very stressful and demanding for an introductory class in Philosophy.

His lectures were very dry and hard to sit through. He doesn't let you take notes on any electronic device and will call you out if he catches you using one. He also mandates that everyone sit in the first few rows of class to be counted for attendance. Overall, not the worst class but definitely would not recommend taking.
Horrible Boring lectures never listens to students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Brence just made me mad on occasion. He would ask the lecture hall a question expecting a certain answer, and he would then brush off a student's train of thought. He also shows one modern movie, but I think the class could benefit from a few more or even just a movie he doesn't like.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Light work load, there was assigned reading but you never had to do them, nor did you have to take any notes

Very enjoyable!
If you are interested in Philosophy, you must take him. Even if you're not, take him. 
He is passionate about what he teaches, its very refreshing. He cares very much and he is extremely funny and enjoyable to learn from. Do nottt pull out your phone in class or be stuck on your computer, he will call you out!

Expects his time to be respected when he can't respect his students time, constantly goes overtime and WILL call you out if you're on your phone/have headphones in. Close-minded, will expect people to share their views/thoughts, yet he diverts their views back to his. Do not take this class if you're new to philosophy, don't start with this guy.
This guy is the goat. such a funny fella. knows what hes teaching and teaches it well. He also drinks out of a mason jar.

Brence himself is a funny guy who slyly hints at his marxist belief system until we read marx. However, get ready for an all time snoozer. Always goes over time limit and repeatedly calls out those who are on any devices. Class consists of 3 easy papers and Brence being purposely overanalytical with 2-3 other philosophy geeks. Easy A nonetheless.
Class is kinda fun, pop culture critique and hating on bag chasers

Dr. Brence provides really interesting media sources for philosophical engagement and the essays and lectures are really insightful. And on top of all that, I was never not at least semi entertained and engaged by the lectures and material.

I personally did not enjoy this course. Lot of readings/movies to be completed outside of class along with discussions. The course is basically a criticism of pop culture which I was not expecting. I did not notice or experience the fighting with students that many other reviews mentioned. He's kind and it's an easy A if you're looking for that.

Class, Canvas page very well-organized. Very reachable if you need help or just wanna talk. The assigned reading is pretty interesting! His lectures were pretty easy to follow, but sometimes skips over some stuff. Grading was TA-run. First reading of class was the hardest. Doesn't fight w students, just introduces not-universally-accepted ideas.

I enjoyed this course more than I thought I would. It's definitely more "math-based" than philosophy (which I liked) so keep that in mind. The lectures closely follow the textbook, so reading the assigned section and doing the practice problems before lectures makes them easier to follow. Plus, the exams were open-textbook which was amazing.

I liked the material that Brence taught and it was a really eye-opening course. However, I wish we learned about the material before we had homework assigned. I don't like how we learn about it after we've done the work already. I also wish we could use technology in his class, but that's just based on my preference.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the most pessimistic man I have ever seen. His prompts reflect that for the essays which force you into siding with him. 3 essays over the semester and 2 paragraphs a week which are not harsh. The GEs are good. Added attendence midway which sucked.

Search up "pretentious philosopher". a portrait of him should be the first thing you see. 

easy class. theres only like 3 essays + 2 paragraphs per week as homework. but his lectures and essay prompts are terrible. he has you explain how HIS view is correct instead of letting you give your own.

overall, couldnt stand this man. loved my ge tho

He's smart and passionate, but I wouldn't recommend this class. Long lectures (no phones/laptops), repetitive discussions, lots of reading, and boring films. I skipped discussions (Socratic seminars) and used ChatGPT for Canvas posts. Easy A with short papers, but he started taking attendance randomly after not doing so earlier, which was annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Material was overall very easy but I have to say the class was complete bullsh*t. Although the course description says "pop culture" get ready to only talk about stuff from the early 1900's. Also his lectures are just him rambling about Trump.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very thorough and does a good job creating organization in the class. The only complaint I have is that he makes us do lecture specific assignments before class, and then the lecture is all just him discussing what we already learned in order to submit the assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had wanted to take this class since my freshman year and going into it, now as a junior, I was excited for this class. After having a mental health crisis this term, however, Dr Brence failed me for missing more than 5 classes. If you want a professor with human decency and understanding, it seems Steven Brence is not the one for you.

I personally really liked this class! The only issue would be the reading. There are 3 books that we read, & they are very dense/heavy. Some chapters are over 50 pages! Get ready to read! Easy grader. 3 papers & a reading response before every class. If you go to class & work hard you will be okay. Thinks his opinion is the only valid one though...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class wasn't all too hard but man this guy was bad, like real bad. The homework was always due at the weirdest time i.e. 9am on Monday and Friday morning... whats up with that prof. Worst part are the lectures though, he basically tries to get class discussion going and has crazy takes about these movies. Easy class but boring.

This professor is funny and engaging during his lectures, although, he sometimes allows the full class discussion derail the lecture, which can be annoying, if you are in lecture to get a better understanding of the material. He did have an incredibly well-organized canvas that is easy to navigate. beware, his essays are due middays on the weekends
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whole class is basically just an embarrassing argument between the teacher and students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's kinda condescending in lectures when students make comments, and he only posts the homework questions in class so if you're not there you're out of luck. The readings are really wordy, but that may apply to all philosophy classes. I think a lot depends on if you get a good GE for your discussion section

This is a good intro philosophy course. There are daily discussions on canvas that are short and easy but he posts the prompt in class so you either need to come to class or have someone send it to you. There are 3 essays that I found pretty easy but you definitely should take some time on them. No final either. Friday discussion was easy too.

As someone who loves pop culture, this class was not at all what I expected. The lectures were boring and I found that he belittled and beefed with students during his lectures. Essays were easy to write, some GEs will grade easy while others will take grading more seriously. I loved my GE though, Waldeck. He made the topics enjoyable to discuss.

For someone who makes a career of studying different interpretations of the world, he is impressively good at not listening to others' perspectives. In theory I would have loved the class, but his lectures took away all my interest in the topics. Class is also ridiculously easy, essays took no more than 2 hours and I only lost points for lateness.
great professor!

Steven is a genuine guy and knows most people in the class aren't philo majors. He will change your perspective on life if you really dig in to the class. The timing of assignments is odd but the workload is light. He comes off as rude but is often just pushing your thinking deeper. First class I've ever taken that changed how I think.

He's a nice guy but the only reason I have a low rating was that he said something about having a special connection to MLK because one of his post-grad/graduate advisors went to the same school as MLK which seemed kind of tone-deaf/fake activism. Other than that all good and an easy class with all the basics for business ethics.

Professor Brence is overall just a snobby person. He offended a different person in class probably every lecture. If you try to disagree with his logic or say something that he doesn't believe, he will simply tell you that you are wrong and embarras you in front of the whole class, by going on a tangent. Homework often doesn't make a lot of sense.

Overall good professor and interesting lectures. Some people may find him a bit mean because he is opinionated and will say if he disagrees with you, but personally, I don't think he is a rude person. I liked all the movies we watched.  

Most of your grade is based on two essays and weekly discussion posts. This class can be time-consuming.

I enjoyed most of the films he picked out, but boy is this guy arrogant. He babbles nonstop about his opinions and although you can raise your hand to participate, he often dismisses people who have different takes than him. His lectures are often rambling and get off-topic. Class is great if you like film and philosophy, the teacher not so much.

Clear on expectations, class structure is easy to follow. Brence is very opinionated, he could talk all day if you let him. Overall very amusing and gives interesting interpretations of the text, just have to sit through "teasers" of his political opinions first to get to the stuff you actually need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: 60% of the grade is on 3 essays. 20% is on canvas discussion posts that you get all the points by doing them. The other 20% is on participation by showing up and interacting in the discussion section of the classroom

Prof Brence was overall a good teacher and interesting lecturer. I liked the topics we discussed and the fact we watched two movies. There were 3 discussion posts a week and three essays. Grading depends on your GE but I liked mine. The annoying thing was that talking in class was intimidating and he sometimes kept us over time.
Confusing lectures that always go 3-5 minutes past the end of class, grades very hard for a 100 level class, 3 discussion posts & readings per week and very arrogant speaker at times.
This professor is just a really cool guy. He expects you to work hard but is very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have taken 2 of prof Brence's classes and they consist of 2 weekly discussion posts and 3 essays for the whole term. The essays are not very difficult, but each one is worth 20% of your grade. The discussion posts are another 20% and participation is the last 20%. Attendance is mandatory for discussion sections. Overall, he is nice & a good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class with professor Brence. He is very attentive and genuinely wants students to succeed. He always makes time to talk outside of class and is always down for a deep conversation. Class is definitely mandatory though and he values participation a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting and consisted of lectures, discussion board posts, papers, and a discussion section. The lectures were 1 hour and were easy to understand. 4 papers, three different activities relating to each. One final paper that wasn't too difficult. The overall class is easyish, just put in the work.

I would highly recommend taking a philosophy class with Prof Brence. He's extremely engaging and brings very relevant issues and topics to his lectures. I liked that our homework wasn't just solely reading and writing but also watching movies and listening to podcasts. I firmly believe that I'm coming out of his class with a different perspective.

Prof Brence is a really cool and engaging guy. Despite the challenges of online learning, he seems to be able to actually teach us something. There's a lot of readings but most of them are shorter than 15 pages and you can skim them just for a couple of details to put in your biweekly discussion post.

If you want a good grade in his class it's important to do the reading, it especially helps a lot with understanding the material and the exams (midterm/final) rely heavily on it. If you attempt the practice problems in the reading youll be so grateful (answers are in back of book) plus they help when doing the hw. Hes amazing, I def. recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This is was my first philosophy class, and it was definitely interesting. It is very clear that Steven loves teaching and loves philosophy, but for me it was hard to learn anything from someone who just gets philosophy in a way that I dont. I honestly learned more from YouTube summaries of readings sometimes.

I took Brence's logic class and really enjoyed it. He's a great lecturer, although the subject material is by nature somewhat dry. He has a relaxed grading policy; he let us replace our midterm grade with our score on that content on the final. Very accomodating.

Brence is a brilliant guy and explores philosophic ideas in a pretty unique way. That being said, you do have to pay close attention in order to follow what he's saying. If you're ready to do the readings and commit, being in his class will be very rewarding. Definitely take advantage of his office hours. Also talks about music and his cat a lot :)
