reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Brence is brilliant and cares deeply about helping students to understand the texts, which are difficult but enlightening. Do your reading, go to class, ask questions when you have them amd you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brence was super moody about people getting up and going to the bathroom. In a lecture of about 100 people? Just keep lecturing please. I never got up, even if I had to use the restroom. He also would continue to lecture after class was over and was moody (once again) if we packed our stuff up. Even if lecture was supposed to have ended. Lame.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steven himself is absolutely amazing, he feels kind of a sarcastic and judgey grandpa but who will still make you laugh in class. There's no textbook, just lots of articles and a few movies but i used free trials on amazon and didn't need to pay for anything ! quality class and i really enjoyed it
Great professor! Sometimes can get off topic but otherwise his lectures stayed very interesting due to his goofy humor. Make sure to attend class and do the readings/practice work and youll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I liked Steven (he sparked my interest in Philosophy), however sometimes he does get off topic and boring. The class itself was interesting if the discussion didn't go off on a tangent. The daily assignments he gives you are based on completion, but if you want to do well I would make sure you read as your more likely to do well on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Daily assignments but only graded on completion. Nice teacher.

Dr. Brence is very passionate about what he teaches. The readings are sometimes long and difficult, but lecture explains them very well. I would recommend taking a class with him, because he is willing to work over complicated notions with you. Overall, the course has 3 essays and while they can be a bit tricky, good grades are attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Brence doesn't want to teach you how to get a great job. He wants to teach you how to lose a terrible job. He wants you to care about your integrity. He wants you to question the status quo and the easy path. He wants you to actually consider your life's purpose or lack of purpose. This class will make you think, if you let it. Try it!

Awesome prof, very intelligent and knowledgable on a huge scope of topics. Choses readings and films strategically. You should attend class, and engage in discussion or you wont get much out of the course. He tends to rant and share is opinions widely. Not necessarily an issue. Overall such an engaging and manageable (work load) course.

Professor Brence is incredibly bright and cares a lot about philosophy. His class has a pseudo-required attendance because you are required to turn in a reading reflection each class. And he doesn't give you the reading prompt if you missed class. 3 Essays and one for the final. Essay prompts are wordy and very hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class, but it's a lot more rewarding if you actually participate in in-class discussions. Essay prompts give a lot of room to go whichever route you want to, which depending on how you feel about writing is either really good or really bad. There's no textbook, just PDFs, but you HAVE to do the readings.

Lectures were incredibly boring and his slides made no sense and didn't relate to the readings most of the time. The GTF's that he has are great and really help to clear anything up that was confusing (usually every lecture with Brence.) Good class, but will kill any interest in Philosophy for you and bore you to tears.
Very funny and pretty clear as far as philosophy teachers go. Really nice guy and great speaker.
Boring lectures with random side notes that did not pertain to the actual lecture.

He knows what he is talking about but does not always explain it in the easiest terms to understand. His GTF's help a ton though. The only thing I do not like about this course is how much printing and reading is required. I have wasted so much paper on things I will never look at again. Digital copies in class would be awesome.

Very intelligent teacher..Leads students by inquiry...Class participation is key, as is attendance and doing the readings...The theories of reality class is tough in regards to the abstract content, so you need to pay attention, but otherwise he only requires three papers over the course, no final save for the third paper.

The most interesting lecturer I've had as a professor. Very intelligent and knows what he's talking about. Not a very labor-intensive course (two 5 page essays and a final). A lot of readings but they're interesting.
Great teacher, really nice guy and fantastic at lecturing. I learned a lot in Philosophy of Film.
Provocative lectures, smart guy, can get a bit convoluted at times, but that is to be expected with most philosophy.
You need to be pretty good at writing a solid essay. If you can do that, you'll be fine.
Interesting prof. Hard class, but he made it lively. Good points but occasionally was hard to follow. Did make me want to take more philosophy classes!
Great teacher!
Excellent teacher, really cares about students and their learning.

I am somewhat taken aback and in truth, embarrassed by some of the presumptuous comments already made here at the expense of prof. Brence. His commitment to the philosophical practice and its cultivation among new minds is apparent for anyone who takes a meaningful interest in their own studies. Right on if not above par with U of O's phil. dep.

Prof. Brence likes to talk alot but goes out fo his way to make office hours and extra voluntary discussion sessions.  He is fair with grading papers and not opposed to adjusting the syllabus depending on how the class is going.
Brence is a great guy. Really funny, extremely passionate about his subject. I definitely suggest taking one of his courses.
Don't understand why others are bashing on him. He knows his stuff and does a good job digging at what philosophy is all about.

the above comments are definitely true, but the reason why i rate him low is because of the non-math or problem based discussions. he really asked us what we thought the origin of things was, without much elaboration, then made fun of us for not being good philosophers and responding. philsophy is discussion, not piping out answers meaninglessly.
Hes alright, kind of boring and not great at explaining the texts.

worst professor ever. doesn't know his material at all. attempts to use material from the book, but either explains or copies it wrong. will admit quickly to errors (even though the person correcting him may be wrong) because the probability that he made the error is so high that he's better off to admitting to it first. get Kaag for disc section

Very intelligent so he made the class harder thinking everyone is like him. Our midterm averages were dramatically lower than the other stats class this term and he didn't curve anything. Weekly discussions were all about excel for some reason even though you don't use excel on the tests. First midterm was pretty easy, second and final were harder.
He did not prepare us for the tests very well, the average for midterm 2 and the final were like 60%, his reviews were too easy. But he was nice and his lectures were decent.

Bownik is very dedicated, but you can tell it's his first time teaching stats; however, he offers a lot of extra credit with the iClicker to allow for any mistakes throughout class. The lectures can move fast, but he posts them after class. Overall, the class is mainly graded by the exams, which aren't too bad as you get a full page of notes.

Prof Bownik really cares about everyone but you can tell he hasn't taught a stats class in awhile. The tests are relatively easy but lectures can be extremely confusing, so if you are fine teaching yourself some of the material then this class won't be too bad. There's technically a textbook, but you don't really need it, its just extra problems.

Bownik is a nice guy, but the lectures are pretty confusing. The midterms are significantly different from the in-class review, and be prepared to memorize excel functions (even though you are not allowed to use excel on tests). Overall a helpful guy and there is only 3 homework assignments each week.

He was really confusing sometimes, and got calculations wrong in class. The extra credit was really useful though and the tests really weren't that hard. Take him if you want to go to lecture, get extra credit, get confused, and then go home and mostly teach yourself.

Professor Bownik gave a very clear syllabus with grade weights and material covered each week. He follows the textbook closely, and he gives practice exams that are extremely helpful for doing well on the real exams. There is also usually a 10% extra credit problem on the tests. Difficult but rewarding class.

Very confusing in lecture. Lecture was also 500 students large and math should be taught in a smaller classroom where its interactive. Quiz every week and tests are very difficult. would NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Teacher is fine. He is better personally than in the lecture hall. Though, he doesn't know how to teach a business class. He told us many times he's never worked with these business problems. The university just shoved in a mathematician to teach us a topic he doesn't truly seem to know either. Had to neglect my other 3 classes to maintain my D+.

This was the hardest and most frustrating class I've ever taken. I'm not sure it's entirely the professor's fault (he's a nice guy)- UO Math completely dropped the ball on 241. 500 students w/ 1 prof is NOT HOW YOU LEARN MATH. I spent so much time preparing for quizzes and tests only each week receiving the worst grades I've ever gotten. Awful...

His explanations could've been more simple, however, he made them more complicated than they should be. I stopped going to the lecture after the first week but attended all the discussion classes. I looked over the professors notes and also read the text book, but his notes weren't helpful when doing webwork or the exams.

The proofs in class are difficult. However, the  tests are not difficult and he is clear what will be on them. When I didn't understand something he did a great job of walking through concepts with me during office hours.

This is a math teacher I honestly can't say anything truly bad about; he was fun, clear, and direct.  He could've been a little more clear on his grading policy, but it was fair and consistent.  Kudos, prof.
GOOD

Prof. Bownik was a very nice guy who really wanted his students to learn the materials. As long as you do all the assigned readings and homework assignments seriously, you'll likely to do fine in his class.
Marcin is a very helpful teacher, but he expects a lot out of his students.  I would reccomend.
No Comments

I love Brendan, he is the best science prof I have had outside of lab. He is so kind and listened to us and our requests. He heard what we asked for to help us succeed and implemented it and then congratulated us on advocating for ourselves. His lectures are also very interesting!!

For being so experienced in his field (the hall to his office is covered with his lab's published research), Dr. Bohannan really makes topics easy to understand at our level. He seems to care a lot about the learning process and cherishes the curiosity in his students- he has that spark of passion for biology that makes discussions engaging.

He is an absolutely amazing instructor. Not only would I take a class of his again, but I would choose to take a class just because he is teaching it. He turns every question into a learning opportunity and cares about the students.
A really great teacher, I feel like I learned a lot from his classes. Experienced in his field and very knowledgeable.
He is kind of a big deal in his field but not stuck up.

Tina is very particular when grading writing assignments, and when people say she rarely gives A's, they are not kidding. I am usually a straight A-assignment-student, but it was very difficult to get above a B+ in her class. The group project lasts the entire term. Tina seems passionate about what she teaches, which makes the class more enjoyable.

Tina was a fun teacher who had a lot of energy. She very much disliked students on phones or computers, so you could not have one out during lecture. Overall the class was not challenging, I put in almost no effort other then joining the Encore and I got an A. The test scores were so low overall that there was a 4% curve to the entire class.
She makes lecture go fast and not boring at all. Be ready to work there are 3 home work assignments each lecture and exams are weighed very heavily.

Tina was a FANTASTIC BA 101 professor. Her lectures are very engaging, and it feels like she is talking directly to you. There is a decent amount of online homework, but very manageable. Her slides are very informative, and anything she puts on the slide will be on the exams. You can tell she is very passionate about her job, I would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tina is a good professor. Exams are moderately difficult but you can do well if you study. She is an engaging lecturer but goes through slides way too fast. She curves overall grades at the end of the term but not by much. Much of the content is terminology, so study that a lot for exams. Homework is a bit boring but not difficult.

Professor Tina speaks very clearly and keeps me engaged. Exams are moderately difficult, but you'll do well if you listen and review terms. She goes through material quick, so review chapters before lectures.
Easy class, fun professor and teaches the material pretty well. Only issues is she goes through the slides way too fast in class.

Requires iClickers for attendance credit which is a bit annoying due to the cost, but other than that she is a fantastic professor. Lectures are engaging, homework outside of class takes 20 minutes at most, and exams are easy if you study well.

Very fluid speaker and good stories. The professor puts a bunch of real world examples. The McGraw-Hill homework will take at least 15 minutes. If you understand mikesbikes at least a little, you can do very well in the competition.
Talks way too much about information that doesn't go with class material and gives random stories. Lectures are too high paced and easy to fall behind during these lectures.

I loved her class. Attendance is very important and be prepared to have an IClicker. Homework everyday after lectures, with mikesbikes. Her lectures go by very quick, definitely would review the slides. Midterms are fairly easy. Good class.

Boscha is good at including examples in her lectures, which makes them more entertaining and also easier to remember/understand. The only minor critique I have is that her slides are self-explanatory, and it can seem pointless to be in class just to hear her read them aloud. BUT overall, she's friendly, a great teacher, and I recommend her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tina is such a great and engaging professor. Her lectures are often fairly long but she makes sure to keep them entertaining. There are usually 2-3 short homework assignments per class, but you're able to work ahead.
She was a solid professor; classes did get boring, and lectures covered slideshows, which were very important. If you study the slideshows for a long time, you will get good test scores and do well.

Tina is very funny and relatable, and she definitely cares about her students. She is very easy to contact outside of class and prepares students well for tests. There is about 3 homework assignments per class but you can do them a week early to avoid getting overwhelmed. Absolutely no devices in her lecture hall..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I genuinely enjoyed going to her classes, they were engaging and she's an easygoing professor. Yes she's a tough grader, but her thoughts and opinions are really constructive! There is a lot of reading, but they're not as boring as it seems. I took this class spring 2025, so maybe the nice weather also had a positive impact on this overall class :P

Nice lady tries who make it interesting. Tests are almost your whole grade and the class average was usually C- or D which is pretty low for a BA101. she goes through slides SO quick and you have 3 things of homework each day of class. Lokey hard thought it would be a lot easier. Class got out 20-30 min early every day which was a +.
Very nice professor and a good lecturer. Tests matter a lot though she usually prepares us well. Homework heavy. Goes way to fast in class so notes must be taken outside of class.

Super amazing, funny and engaging lectures. I loved this class so much I switched my major to business. There is a lot of homework in a very short time frame. I-clickers are required and are exspensive. Loved this class! One of my favorites.

Tina tends to go very fast through slides so it was a common occurrence that I would have to take notes outside of class. Lectures were straightforward and easy to understand. She seems very passionate about what she teaches which is refreshing for a student. She uses iclickers to count attendance and exams are worth 60% of your grade

She is very nice, but the class was strictly no electronics, which is hard with the speed of her teaching. Exams make up 60% of your grade. The midterm average was like a 60%, and she told us it was disappointing and that we needed to do better. The slides are very hard to understand, vague, and are just recycled slides from every other teacher.

professor boscha is amazing. this was my first business class i've ever taken, and having her as my professor made it 10000x better. she's funny, smart, and super professional and talented. she's kind of strict and the midterms were pretty difficult, but if you put in the work, you'll do well. would 100% take again.

I don't think it's Tina's fault, I think BA308 just sucks. She was kind, but she was a very tough grader, but I've heard the other 308 profs are just as tough. She sort of seemed like she knew what she was doing, but her feedback wasn't the best. The entire class is 1 big group project, so you better hope you get good team members.
She is chill and a little corny, but her grading standards were unreasonably high. Take someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tina was a great professor who cared about the success of all her students even in big lecture halls. As long as you stay on top of the homework and study a normal amount for tests, it is not too difficult and the whole course was curved a bit at the end of the term. I'm not a business major but I am glad I took this class!

I think Tina was one of my favorite teachers at uo so far. She takes time to explain things well, even though she goes through the slides sort of fast. The midterm and finals all had very clear study guides and most of the tests were very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Boscha is a great professor especially for BA 101 shes fun and informative.

Tina was pretty good. She had long lectures, but was well respected. She is a very nice person and a kind soul, who wants the best for each of her students. For even though BA101 was fairly simple, I recommend taking the class encore because it helped me. But overall Tina was a pretty good professor and a nice grader. Just turn in your hw, on time.
Pretty straight-forward business class, you''ll have 3 midterms which results in no final -- Yay! Pretty easy homework every week, respectable and fun professor!
Her lectures are very hit and miss, some are very engaging while other will have you falling asleep. Showing up to class and taking some notes should guarantee a passing grade.

You need to be present for her lectures. its a big class and she goes through class slides very very quickly-- be good at taking notes. If you didnt get all the notes down, she posts the lectures on canvas. if you take good notes, and study for 2-4 hours on each midterm, you will pass. midterms are not hard at all if you just study.

I personally did not find Tina's lectures that helpful. I felt that she went over the slides way too fast, but still found a way to make the class at least an hour and a half. I had to go back and take most of the notes at a later date. It didn't help that attendance was mandatory, so I was just going to class without getting many notes down.
I can't say much because every BA101 class is literally the exact same but, attendance was mandatory, 3 midterms all were pretty difficult, good amount of homework, and studying is mandatory.
Chill and valid

Tina is a really cool professor. I had her class for almost 2 hours twice a week, but I always enjoyed being there. The weekly homework load was quite tolerable, and was very correlated to the in class lecture. She does not accept late work at all, so that can be a little tricky, but I never found it too hard to get the work done on time.

Tina runs a pretty tight ship, but it's understandable as it's a class of about 300. She doesn't seem particularly knowledgeable on the content and often defers to asking her colleagues when students ask deeper questions. The midterms (of which there are three) were pretty easy. Homework was a bit excessive in volume, not in difficulty though.

Honestly, Tina was a decent prof. However, her grading was so difficult to the point 99% of people have a D letter grade until week 9/10 and then jump and stay around a B. She has only given 1 group of 5/6 members an A letter grade in her career as a professor. Other BA 308 professors are more fair graders for sure.

Tina is an often cringe yet nice person, but her demeanor is not what makes her a poor professor. Her class is specially set up for you to leave with a B-/B. Rubrics are bare but her critiques of group work are extensive. Additionally, she doesn't even give her whole edits in the rough draft process so she can critique these unbeknownst edits later
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: It was an easy class, I spent at most 4 hours a week on work. I would recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hard grader, but wants to help you improve. It'll be hard to get an A in the class. Basically you need to hope you get paired with a good team as most of your grade is based on team assingments.

Tina is a very nice person and very engaging as a person, you can tell she cares. With that being said, she is an extremely tough grader claiming she doesn't want to simply hand out good grades. But, I don't think making it nearly impossible to achieve an A grade in this class along with the great density of work motivates students.

Tina is a really kind person and you can tell she cares a lot about her class but she's definitely the toughest grader out of all the professors that teach BA308. Very nit picky when it comes to grading written assignments. She also gives a lot of assignments the last 3 weeks of the term so be mentally prepared. Attendance is mandatory.

Tina is a good person, but not the best professor for BA 308. The guidelines for assignments are very vague, and if you do not adhere to exactly what she wants for assignments you will lose significant points. She will not tell you exactly what she wants though, you have to spend the term figuring it out. Her canvas website is IMPOSSIBLE to use.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reflections every week, besides that, big group project/presentation. She is a tough grader, but really nice. Just wish she would be more lenient on her grading

Ridiculous grading system in comparison to the rest of the teachers that teach BA308. Really self-centered and claims to have given 3 "A"s in her career. Considerably more work / readings than other BA308 classes. Avoid this professor at all costs in this course

I took online and there's a final paper that you start around week 7. Due to the fast pace of the course, she wasn't able to always give timely comments. Example: you pick a final topic week 7 and she tells you it's bad week 9, when it's too late to change it. She is also a pretty tough grader if you are aiming for A's. A nice person though

Truly one of the worst professors I have ever had. She has no business experience and has the most ridiculous grading structure. While this may not all be her fault, she does not prepare you for anything. She talks about herself all class. I have never put in more effort to an assignment, only to receive a terrible grade. DON'T BELIEVE THE 4.9!

Ms. Boscha is a great teacher because she has so much energy. She always comes in to teach, which is a good trait. Honestly, everyone in the class gets Bs, which she tells you at the beginning of the term. The only problem I experienced was that her grading was very subjective. You work long hours to get a B kind of sucks.

The first few assignments are skewed in the C-D range to scare you in the beginning. As long as you complete everything after that "well" the grades even out in weeks 8-10 of the term. I personally did not find Tina to be the right fit for a business course, or this course concept as a whole... Beware this whole class is one group project/prez.

Tina is AWESOME. You can't get an A, but that's just bc Lundquist wants to try to scare you. Can get a B+ pretty easily tho. Tina is easily the most involved teacher I've had at UO. So nice, easy to talk to, and always positive. This class demands constant participation and a hard group project, but the challenges will make you better. Participate!

Tina seems like a genuinely kind person, yet for someone teaching a class on communication she seems to lack in that area. Rarely gives effective or useful feedback, and it all seems very nitpicked, yet deducts a chunk of points from your assignments. There are not a lot of points available in this class, so don't skip any assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was one of those "If you do all the required work, you will receive a B, if you want an A, you need to do extra work" classes. Most of the writing assignments and discussion posts for this class were shorter than other professors' assignments which made this class a bit easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Tina was an amazing online professor. She did a great job making content available and providing everyone a chance to earn an A if they worked for it. She made her grading policies very clear and never once did I earn a grade I had questions about. She gives wonderful feedback and makes everyone feel apart of a great writing community.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tina Boscha is one of the best professors I've ever had. She gives stellar presentations each class and overall she has a really nice, caring, and fun personality. Thanks to her, I've grown immensely as a writer, team player, speaker, and leader. Tough class, but worth every penny. She's def one of my top three fav professors. Thank you!

Incredibly tough grader and should not be teaching an upper level business course, especially since she is brand new to it. Does not have the expertise or professionalism that you would want out of a teacher.

Understandable that this class wasn't the most fluid given it was Tina's first time teaching the course. However, that is no excuse for tanking the students grades as a result. By the end of the term, a small handful of students had a B-, everybody else had less than that. Class average on most assignments was a C-. Love the class but not the prof
Very engaging. Tough grader but just keep working at it and will pay off. Go to class!!

I absolutely loved her, a great class to take when you are worried about your workload as it's graded on an effort basis. You are guaranteed a B if you do all the work and can bring it up with a few extra assignments. I only put in 2ish hours or less a week and still did fairly well.

I loved having her as my professor virtually during Spring term. She was really accommodating, and I felt like she cared that all of her students did well in the course. If you want an A, I recommend doing the readings and submitting any extra work she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Tina is AMAZING. She is so friendly and very funny. She is incredibly understanding and I actually have fun in her class. Would definitely recommend taking one of her classes.
Great teacher!

LOVE LOVE LOVE TINA! If you have the chance take this class with her. She is such an amazing teacher with so much energy and truly cares about helping students become better writers. Wish every professor taught the way she does.
Tina's class was one of my favorites of freshman year. She's engaging and easy going and always seems to be excited to teach.
She is such a great teacher, I am so glad that I was able to have such a great experience in my first college class. I would recommend her to any student!
She really know what she is talking about, helpful and very funny. Come to class prepare to read.

Tina boscha seriously is such an amazing teacher. I feel like I would of failed WR121 if it wasn't for her. She comes to class excited, she's hilarious, and does exercises in class that really makes you understand what she wants you to write. Class was enjoyable and definitely my favorite class I had all semester. Take it!
She's the best writing teacher I've ever had! Definitely recommend taking her class. I really wish she taught WR 122!
Boscha's class was really interesting and she was an amazing professor. REALLY wish she was also teaching WR 122.

Super nice, great at teaching, AND funny! That's a rare find in a professor. She was always willing to listen to concerns and help clear up confusion. She actually offered HELPFUL feedback on assignments, too. Class wasn't very difficult, but there was an assignment due almost every day. It was manageable, though. I highly recommend this class.

Tina is an AMAZING teacher! Fun and welcoming personality, interested in what students have to say, and very encouraging. She is very open minded and encourages an awesome classroom atmosphere. I would recommend taking anything you can from her, especially Eng. 199!
Very helpful and clear!

Tina is an amazing teacher. She really makes class fun and has amazing ideas. She really wants her students to do better and I applaud her for that. Surprisingly she is really funny and I have really enjoyed this class as I was nervous going into it. Don't hesitate to sign up for her class as you will not regret it.

Tina was one of the best teachers I've ever had. She keeps students paying attention and interested. She really wants her students learn and succeed. She is amazingly kind and extremely helpful. She is great at keeping in touch outside of the classroom. I could not have asked for a better writing teacher.
I'm so happy I got have her for WR 121. I was not looking forward to taking the course, but Tina definetly made it bearable! She was so nice and very helpful. Wish she taught WR 121!

I had this class at 8:30 in the morning and regretted until I went to her class.  She made every single class fun and I have never been a good writer but she helped me improve so much!  Highly recommend!!!!!!
Tina was a great teacher for me. Originally I hated writing but her lectures were interesting and she kept me engaged. She isn't that hard of a grader either as long as you're improving.
Tina is great! She is super helpful and her lectures are actually interesting.

Tina is a very fun teacher.  I do not feel like I learned much beyond the first week or two.  However, I did enjoy coming to class every morning to hear what she had to say.  She focused a bit too much on group activities than how to write.  I would recommend her to anyone taking WR 121.
Great teacher. Very cheerful and helpful. The workload was ok.

Tina is an AMAZING instructor! She is very knowledgeable and extremely dedicated. She stimulates class discussions and keeps the students engaged. She is always more than happy to help in her office hours and gives great feedback about the essays! I loved her class! She grades a little hard but gives you great feedback! Easy A if youre dedicated.
She is very attractive and also helpful. Very easy class and it was a good time.

She is absolutely amazing! Take from her if you need a writing credit. She's not super difficult but definitely challenges you as a writer and she wants her students to learn. She's a huge help in and out of class. She takes time to meet with every single student and is a great person to get to know for Letters of Rec.

I'm not sure how much actual teaching of writing she did in class (beyond enythmeme emphasis) and she could be a bit disorganized/unclear, but she was more than willing to give useful help in any way. Reasonable workload, allows for creativity, extremely personable and encouraging (of individuals and of class discussions). Definitely recommended
If you ever have the chance to take a class from her, do it! She has been, by far, the most helpful and interesting professor to have. She is truly interested in her students and cares deeply.

She is a great teacher!! She is trying to make everyone fair in the classroom, and as long as you try your best and show the improvement to her. She gives you a good grade.One thing i dont like it's the vocab quizes :( overall i have learned a lots in this class.
She is the nicest teacher I have had at Oregon, highly recommended. Plus she doesn't really require you to write just like her.
I learned a lot about myself in this class, if you had a chance to take Ms.Boscha as your writing professor, you should do so.
i love this lady! shes amazing! shes a great teacher and shes really helpful! i go into her office hours just to kick it with her. but really... i do! shes awsome, take her class!
Extremely helpful, great personality- made class bearable.  Easy!!!
Take her class. You won't regret it. The topics she uses are very broad and you decide what you want to write your essay on.  Very fair teacher who listens to everyone.  Good humor too.
No Comments

By far the best professor I've ever had. Tina made writing fun for me, a subject I hadn't enjoyed in the past. She was made everything energetic and lively. Even though class was in the morning she still managed to be funny and put a smile on my face. She was extremely helpful and overall wonderful. TAKE HER CLASS!

Could care less about the success of students. He sucks so bad at his job. I literally felt myself losing brain cells listening to this guy talk. You wanna fail calculus and waste 11 weeks of your life? take this class. PS, I flipped majors solely bc of this class

I should have listened to the reviews here. I spend 5 hrs/week in personal one-on-one tutoring with a previous professor for this class on top of the homework, lectures, and office hours. He took points off for my zeros because I put a slash in them. Avoid at all costs. I'll be retaking with another teacher.

Head my warning. I should have listened to the reviews here. I spend 5 hrs/week in personal one-on-one tutoring with a previous professor for this class on top of the homework, lectures, and office hours. Im still failing. He took points off for my zeros because I put a slash in them. Avoid at all costs. I'll be retaking with another teacher.

He is passionate about math, but at the same time he's tech illiterate. He also grades incredibly harsh. It's either you get the answer right or you get a flat zero (whether its a worksheet, hw, or exam), with no partial credit. His handwriting is also very hard to read, and I learned more from watching online videos than his lectures.

I kid you not, he's afraid of Google and all its technology. Theres no way to email him, questions must be asked after class or during office hours. Homework was assigned over WebWork, however there were frequently difficulty's accessing assignments as he's technically illiterate.

He has no people skills or idea how to teach to modern generations.

Take this class if you enjoy frequent headaches, suffering through confusing lessons, and want to question your self-worth. Have never met a teacher with such harsh grading compared to a very limited lesson plan and don't know one person succeeding in this class. Don't take this class if you want to be taught or pass Calculus.

I have never had a professor/teacher like him. No credit for late work, even if sick. Both classes are failing. Doesn't explain problems or completes them. Unorganized, even with AEC accommodations. Harsh grader- he took points off because he didn't like the way I wrote my zeros...yeah. If you are a student he remembers, he might be generous. GL!

Avoid taking his class at all costs. Very minuscule details he will dock off major points for. When you ask him for help, he'll give little to no help. I asked him for help with specific problem, as I had absolutely no idea what to do, in which he proceeded to ask me "Write me the first step." after I already told him I had no idea what to do.

Do not take him if you are not a good text/exam taker. Has a terrible grading system. Assigns irrelevant homework problems to things we haven't even learned about. Has homework due at random times (i.e Webwork due at 2pm, 9pm, 11:59pm, 12pm, 11am). Extremely unorganized. Gives no genuine feeback and expects his students to know everything.

Do not recommend this professor at all. He is extremely unorganized, often leaves every student confused. Rushes through lecture and gives no explanations or definitions. Has a terrible grading system and does not update canvas, rather has a sketchy website he made. Makes things harder than they are.

Not sure how he got hired to teach. From what I've heard most students are failing or have already dropped. Doesn't explain anything very well and just a very awkward guy. Will often ask a question and just stare at class in silence for at least a minute. Would not recommend.

The professor often spends too much time on basic concepts, while rushing through more complex material. His examples can be confusing, and will stare in silence for an uncomfortable amount of time. Additionally, grading lacks clarity, leaving students uncertain about expectations. Doesn't use canvas, uses a random poorly made website.

Hasn't taught since 2017 and did so l this year 2025. Both 9am and 11am class are FAILING. Handwriting: unreadable. Hard at explaining things. Don't expect him to give you any sort of hint of what's on the test as he will just say it's everything we covered so far. Has office hours. SUPER HARD GRADER. notation is his thing. Good luck passing

He is the worst professor. I'm taking this class during the pandemic, so everything is online. I honestly feel like he is too old and can't keep up with the technology anymore. Also, his homework due date is so confusing, some of them due at 8:00 pm while others due at 12:00 am (ie. 12:00 am 5/5/2021 - it will instantly lock after 5/4/2021 11:59pm)

It could be that he is not used to teaching online classes, but he was by far the worst professor I've had for online learning. his lecture heavy class may be good for some, but he talks much too slowly to hold my attention. when I expressed my concern and asked to do group work in class he refused. I do not recommen if you have attention problems
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very awkward guy, VERY awkward. He had weird guidelines for emailing him, which made it so I never did. The midterms weren't bad if you did all the written homework and sample tests beforehand. I wouldn't recommend him, but he wasn't too bad.
Not helpful in the slightest. Very awkward man in general, and his teachings don't provide any clarity. I spent the entire term struggling to even get a D. Wouldn't recommend anyone take his class.

If you've never had calculus, this class is going to be very hard. It was my first clac class and he just assumes you already know the basic concepts about derivatives and such, and all he does are examples in class. I ended up teaching myself through YouTube videos. All the learning happens outside of class.

I'm not one to complain about teachers. If your a student who can learn math via powerpoint this is the guy for you. But don't expect to understand half the material because he doesn't teach everything and your responsible to know the rest on your own.I got a better understanding of statistics taking a computer science class in the business school
Awesome prof. Great at explaining things, has good office hour times, I would not hesitate to take any math class taught by him. I am seriously considering trying to get him as my thesis advisor.

The previous entries show what is wrong with the students in this country, they are too lazy to do their own work.  So sad that these people are allowed to be students at a university.  I guesss they will have quite an education, while serving coffee to people that understand what work is.
Plan on reading the textbook on your own, he doesn't explain the concept right, and the office hour doesn't help what so ever. Definitely avoid his class if all possible.

Very award teacher, doesn't explain the material clearly. Expect us to know something that isn't pre-req. Gives very hard tests and the office hour definitely doesn't help, word of advice:unless you are a self learner, DO NOT take class from him.

This prof does give a good lecture.  However, the grading on exams is abhorrent.  Somehow, in the midst of his advanced research, he has become convinced that PhD = God.  He was intentionally misleading on an exam in order to mark points off.  I suggest (strongly) that all students take their statistics from another department like Psych or Soc.

Plan on reading the book and doing lots of learning on your own because only about 1/2 of the material is covered in lecture. Grading is not fair because there is very little partial credit. Tests are very hard and there is not enough time to take them. Overall, the class is just "OK", not that great but not that bad either.

I loved Professor Cortez. He wants his students to succeed and if you care and ask questions he will help figure out the best way to support you. GE's were also great and were quick and clear with their grading. Would recommend taking this class especially if you enjoy in class discussions!

Diego is one of the most hardworking instructors I have had! He genuinely wants everyone to succeed and is always available to help anyone out if asked. He and the GEs were pretty strict when it came to the formatting of assignments, but as long as you show up, participate, and show care, you'll succeed!

Cortes is a nice and smart guy but this course is bad. Mandatory attendance with iclicker questions throughout lecture which are not graded, not just participation. The readings are very dense and you have a few essays for the term. I would take it online if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There's been a lot of issues in this class. He's a nice guy but his instruction is very confusing, he is a very hard grader even though his slides are sooo messy. I don't have time to talk about all the little things but they stacked up really fast. He shows so many YT videos and doesn't even lecture that much. It's an easy participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take this class. take JCOM305 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If Professor Cortes is going to show so many YouTube videos instead of teaching, he should at least get a Premium subscription. Does little to no teaching himself. Class is incredibly boring. Assignments must be formatted correctly or you receive an F, but the necessary formatting is never fully explained or found on Canvas. Truly awful professor.

Perhaps the worst professor and organize course I have ever taken. iClicker questions provide nothing and the format of read the reading, discuss the reading, youtube video, and iClicker question on repeat is mind numbing. Worst professor at UO and its not close. Made me dread waking up Monday and Wednesday knowing 2 hours of my day is gone.
A rating can not capture the disasterclass that is the daily iClicker tests.

This is the worst and most boring class I have ever taken at UO. The professor takes 15 minutes to make a single point when that same point is common sense...complete and utter waste of time. Attendance is based off iclicker questions and you have to get them correct to get attendance opposed to simply answering them. Worst professor at UO by FAR.

Grade is heavily dependent on I-clicker, but grading criteria for assignments isn't clear. None of the feedback I've received is beneficial, and the only thing we do is watch YouTube videos and then answer I-clicker questions based on those. Global comms should be informational, but I am learning nothing from this professor.

Don't listen to the two other reviews, Cortes was an amazing professor. He cares about his students and is easy to talk to outside of class. I don't get why people complain about a person just because of what they believe in, shouldn't be the case.

Grade relies heavily on iclicker questions and ability to answer correctly. The whole class is spent watching videos or reading articles he posts on canvas.  Spends 5-10 mins for each question and uses the whole class time, which is not needed and could easily be avoided if he taught the lecture rather than relying on severely dated media content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: All we did was watch YouTube videos then answer clicker questions. This class is heavily dependent on clickers and each class the grade is based on the amount of iclicker questions you get right - not participation. Showed many triggering videos and photos with no warning and in a term with stress about election talked about his support for Trump

Why a grad student was allowed to teach a 520 person lecture? I have no idea. This was hands down the most boring class I have ever taken in all of my 14 years of schooling. She read directly off slides and explained the same thing over and over, often creating more confusion. I did better once I stopped attending the lecture. Avoid at all costs.

Kirkaldie is a grad student and with all due respect, was not ready to teach a big lecture. The slides were confusing, and her notes often contained admittedly wrong work. Nothing was ever explained besides the slides, and I did better studying on my own instead of lecture. The class is easy but the prof made it more difficult than it needed to be.

Not a super hard class but she was the worst teacher I've ever had, didn't know what she was doing at all and lectures were in a massive room. First midterm she told us after that she put 5 problems on it that she knew people wouldn't get right. Maybe would be an ok teacher for a 25-person high school class but avoid her if possible.
Her lectures were VERY disengaging and she never explained things well. Do NOT take her class, worst ten weeks ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great professor, first midterm was really bad and she intentionally put questions she knew we would get wrong, midterm 2 and final were better tho. Her lectures are not helpful whatsoever and she was passive aggressive at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst lecturer you will EVER find. Reads the slides off word for word. You might as well teach yourself lowkey. Started doing better after the first midterm when I just stopped even trying to take notes. Like genuinely the most dry person ever. Lectures looked like a 2023 Oakland Atheltics home game iykyk.

SHE'S A GRAD STUDENT. Half the class failed the midterm and both the GEs i've talked to seem to think his teaching and work load are ridiculous. My GE continuously apologizes for his teaching technique and how hes making it more of a 300 level instead of 100.

This class was awful. The work load and content covered was closer to a 300 level class. There is excessive weekly readings and a quiz at the end of each week. The quiz questions are unclear and difficult to find the answers to considering there are multiple interpretations of each story. This class is way to difficult to be a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He heavily curved the midterm for this class. There are weekly, online quizzes that are super easy if you take the time to look for the answers (they are open note). Although a lot of people failed tests, I felt that it was all very clear. If you read and attend class and discussion you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor is treasure for the university. He is challenging but those who commit themselves to his classes will be rewarded by his brilliant teaching.

The work load he expects from students for a 200 level class is ridiculous, he asks that you read for 3 hours everyday for his class imagine if all of your classes did that. Also terrible with grades, its the day before the final and I still dont have a grade for 4 quizzes and a midterm entered. Lecture is very boring and doesnt keep you engaged

Prof. Chamberlain means well, but the man teaches the course like everyone in the room is a classics major; which in my personal opinion does not work for those that aren't classics majors. His course info is overloaded, his structure askew, and generally creates tests and quizzes meant to screw you up than test you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He tries to be funny in lectures but dont buy into it. He is a secretly very and doesnt really care about how hard you work. He gives two midterms in this class, the first was challenging and fun and the second was just ridicules. He isnt testing your knowledge just your ability to figure out what he is asking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor. Lectures contained a lot of information and were not always easy to follow, but prof's humor & enthusiasm kept me engaged the whole class. Expect a TON of reading. Weekly quizzes and 2 midterms as well, but all are open book and not super difficult. Love the subject, but class had a bit too much info for one term.

Professor Chamberlain is very knowledgeable and explains complex grammar in a way that is easy to understand. He makes difficult and seemingly boring readings seem fun, interesting, and enjoyable. His classes are not the easiest, but if you put in the effort, his grades are always fair.

David Chamberlain is an awesome, professor. I have had him for a few language courses and I highly recommend him. He is very intelligent, but also accessible; he will help you pretty much whenever you need it; and he asks tough questions of you in class, but also helps you out if he can see if you're trying.
Very unorganized

Chamberlain is a fantastic teacher. He's witty, hilarious  and always comes in with a warm personality. Maybe this is because i had him early in the morning after his cup of coffeetea; either was he always excites. He does require a bit of reading, but it was understandable given the class. He may also quiz you on dates so beware!

Hard class with a hard professor. It's obvious that he knows what he's talking about, but his class is completely centered on him. He's a tough grader and the midterms and final are SO hard and take SO long. You better love this topic and love to read. If you're a business major like I am just trying to fulfill global context req, DO NOT TAKE THIS.

This teacher likes to listen to himself. Although the course is slightly interesting to me, there is a lot of expectation to know all the information he gives you beforehand. Along with this, the cumulative final is a test of the amount of knowledge you have at the end of the term, not as much your analysis of the books you read.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. He's smart but is SO DISORGANIZED. His tests are IMPOSSIBLE and there's a 10 page paper. His instructions are horrible and I never know what he expects from me I just know it's a LOT. There's a ton of reading. I'm a Physics major and was NOT interested in this class so keep that in mind. Worst Prof ever though. DO NOT TAKE

A lot of your grade will be based on participation yet many students never or almost never showed up and seemed to get off fine. Also, the class is dominated by him and usually a couple opinionated people. Very long lectures, some boring, some bearable. Not the easiest class. Overall a very cool guy teaching a class I didn't like much.
I've taken several classes with him and he's my absolute favorite. He's brilliant and anyone who doesn't see that is a moron.

Got a 97% but not an +A, annoying since a 93 would lower my GPA. Bob is a very good teacher, The class itself was just whatever, however Bob is the type of person you want as a teacher because he listens, is flexible, and is caring. I would recommend classes with him, it's very easy. Try and meet people early so you get a good group.

This is one of many classes I've taken with Bob, He is a wonderful and personable professor, he really tries to bridge the gap with students. There are many activities that are fun in the course and grading and feedback was detailed and fair

Bob is the best. I took this class as an "elective" as I needed some filler credits. The topic was not my favorite, but not bad at all. You take this class for the teacher not the lesson, great human, understanding, and genuinely cares about his students.

It was an easy class. Bob is nice and he provides a pdf of the textbook. Attendance is mandatory in the way that he does random attendance quizzes. I don't have any complaints about this class I just found myself being bored sometimes but you do learn a lot about nonprofits.
Bob is super funny and you can tell he really cares about what he's teaching as well as his students. There are about two assignments per week but they are pretty quick and easy.

Bob's a sweet guy and clearly enjoys his job. I will say: you're gonna have to be really interested in nonprofits to really enjoy this class. Material is pretty dry and lectures are slow. Your participation in discussion will be where you learn the most, so show up. Overall painless experience and PPPM students def need this information.
Extremely biased and goes on political tangents every class that are entirely unrelated ot the course.

This is for PPPM 445 Green Cities. This was Bobs first time teaching this course and very early on he was open to how the course should be structured and what we should be graded on. The grading is done on a point scale that totals 140 total points through various assignments but you only need 100 to get an A. Lots of field trips which was awesome!
Course content is super interesting and Prof. Choquette does a great job at engaging the class.

Bob is a down-to-earth professor who genuinely cares about the wellbeing of his students. His teaching style is pretty laid back and he's very informative and passionate about nonprofits and bettering the global community. Final project is pretty time-consuming but engaging, group presentation in discussions. Lots of great guest speakers.

Bob is a really casual and honest instructor - it teaches it how it is, making sure to teach and aknowledge systemic inequalities in the nonprofit sector. The assignments are all very relevant and encourage you to engage and connect the course content to your life. The final project is very heavy, but understandable. Grading was very fair.

Bob is lovely. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him take it! No tests in this class, mostly short writing assignments. There is a choice between a 4-5 page essay where volunteer work is necessary or a 8-10 page research essay for the final. Both options are manageable! There is a small group project as well. The GE was great as well
Great professor. Genuinely cares about his students. Lots of fun activities and discussions.

Absolutely great person who deeply cares about project management.  The class is very flexible and you can chose to do a group project or induvial project.  He is an easy grader, but expects lots of creativity.

Best prof I have ever had, he really works to engage with his students and learn to know them on a personal level even though it is a big lecture. I also took PPPM 201 and loved him which is the only reason why I took 280 and enjoyed the class even more

BOB IS THE BEST!!! He is so fun & really cares for his students. No exams and easy assignments. He really engages the class to discuss important and interesting issues. He brought in guest speakers who were cool. Free textbook. I would recommend anyone to take him!
One of the best teachers ever. I have taken his PPPM class multiple times because I love his teaching so much. He is hilarious and really cares about his students.

I LOVE BOB!!! If he was my only professor I know I would be set for success. He is so caring and understanding for any student's needs. I would recommend him for any class honestly, he's just an overall amazing professor and person. The homework was easily doable, and the finals are not intimidating in the slightest, offering multiple options

The world does not deserve Bob Choquette!!! He is caring far beyond expectations. He is down to earth and treats others like they really matter to him. The textbook is free. The class consists of a lecture with discussion and field trips/class guests. Homework is writing assignments & two straightforward projects. Attendance is graded but nominal.

Best teacher I have ever had. He makes all of his students feel like they are cared about and he is incredibly understanding and will adjust for his students needs. The work was very simple and not too hard at all. Very fair grader as well. Bob clearly loves his job and makes sure that his students enjoy it as well. Sweetest man ever!

I LOVE BOB CHOQUETTE. I would honestly die for this guy. I highly recommend Bob to anyone. I have taken a number of his classes so far and will continue to do so. Just such a caring, down to earth, and funny person. This class was his project management class, and it was lecture heavy with a weekly reflection, two papers, and a final project.

Overall positive experience in class. The first part of the course zooms through the book and then it becomes more of a student led about policy we are interested in. He makes content applicable to real world situations. The only critique is lectures can sometimes be dry and boring but that is probably just the nature of intro policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Bob is a super sweet professor and makes the content interesting. He actually cares about what he's teaching and his students. He always offered to go to coffee with us after class so we could ask him questions in a less intimidating environment than office hours.
Such a good professor. Very inclusive!

I LOVE BOB CHOQUETTE. Bob was great this term, he really cared about his lectures and put a lot of effort into making them worthwhile. Pretty easy class, there was a decent amount of reading and writing, but overall not too bad. Getting a decent grade was pretty simple, strongly recommend this class. Bob was a great sport and made the class fun.

Bob cares about his students and their feedback. Lectures often included discussion of current events and contextualizing class content. Weekly homework includes reflection of class material and a summary of textbook chapter - so there is busy work but it is easy enough. I learned a ton from this class which is most important to me!
Reasonable and engaging. I think anyone would benefit from a professor like him. Personally, I liked the way he structured his class and I feel like Ive actually been learning.

Bob Choquette is a great professor and really cares about his students and what he is teaching. This was my first PPPM class and I enjoyed it so much that I will definitely be taking more of these classes next term. He is very easy to talk to so participation in class comes easily. Great prof, I reccomend
Bob was an awesome Professor! This was my first PPPM class and it inspired me to double major in it!!! Take one of Bob's classes!!

Bob is such a kind professor. Never had a class like this one before in where the students run how the class is and Bob guides the discussion. Not my favorite class, but seriously one of my favorite professors and human beings. Highly recommend anyone to take a course from him given the opportunity.

Bob was an amazing professor. Everything is group based and there is no final. There are short individual presentations and group presentations. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and it's definitely an easy A if you put in a little bit of effort.
yea

I never received any of my grades back so although I believed I earned an A I got a B. Never knew how I did on my presentation which was week 6. Never updated blackboard with grades. Although he is a great guy and teacher he never gave feedback on assignments.

Bob is a great teacher. Although, he has a tendency to get side track and his assignment requirements are so ambiguous it's hard to know what he is exactly looking for. There are no midterms in this class but expect to write a weekly blog entry that is 1-2 pages long and based of of weekly reading assignments.
Great professor. Very passionate about the nonprofit sector and provokes a lot of class debate. I learned a great amount from this course and hope I'll one day work within the nonprofit sector
Great class - get a lot out of it.
lagit
Bob is a nice guy. Easy to get along with. Good material to take with me and use on the job anywhere I go.
The easiest class I have ever taken.

Professor Choquette was one of the only prof's in 3PM that actually taught anything useful. Interesting since it is supposed to be a professional school. Obviously the person who rated prior hasn't ever had a real job otherwise they would appreciate his courses. I found him very approachable and willing to take extra time with students.

I feel very grateful to have taken Latin with Dr. Calhoon. She is very caring & wants everyone to succeed. She always encourages students to ask questions & doesn't make them feel bad for having them. While grading is mostly based on the exams, the daily homework adequately prepares you for her tests. A lot of studying, but it was very rewarding.

Professor Calhoon was very kind and helped any student struggling as much as possible. She truly cares and wants you to succeed; however, I know her teaching methods don't work for me. She grades only on tests and attendance. There was daily homework that did nothing but give practice. Latin was incredibly difficult, and I regret taking it.

Only grades came from exams, which were essay and short answer style written tests, and graded pretty harshly meaning you have to remember specific details, storylines, names, etc from lecture (which she spends spiraling on confusing tales)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Calhoon cares about her students; that much is clear. But the organization of the class can be a detriment. You have daily homework you must do, not for a grade, but it's half of the class every day. The tests can be really difficult, and the preparation sometimes unclear. If you want to learn a language for fun, look somewhere else.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Calhoon's first language is Italian, and perhaps there is a language barrier. I ask a simple question, and she expands about the full translation being done. Not my question Christina! Overall, she is friendly, fairly ruthless, (comedically) and will absolutely cold call anyone and everybody, especially when you don't do the homework.

Great teacher. No complaints. Heavy on in class participation/answering when going over the homework. Tests were graded kind of harsh imo. Lots of work/vocab/grammar so be ready for that. Homework everyday

I loved CLAS101; I would definitely take it again. Professor Calhoon is a great lecturer. With that being said, the tests are hard, but if you really study hard, passing should be easy. I would say she doesn't really communicate with students, more with the GEs, and then the GEs tell us. Take if you like all kinds of myths, not just Greek and Roman
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a nice professor, and is always willing to help you when needed, but the entire grade is based off of 4 tests. These tests are very hard, and so is the material. Requires TONS of studying to pass, and there is homework every night for participation, but nothing else. Professor is very very nice though.

Professor Calhoon is not the teacher you want if you are going for an easy A. We had 4 tests each worth 20% +Participation at 20%. However all of the grading is very subjective and they did not put in grade until the last day. Calhoon can be straightforward at times but gets off topic or rambles often, making the class difficult. Wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A perfectly nice lady but a terribly boring professor. Lectures were only 50 minutes but felt much longer. The tests were pretty easy and very intuitive but the material gone over in class was organized in a confusing way. I wouldn't take another class with her, it was hard to attend class and even harder to stay engaged.

Must go to class! Her lecture slides are just notes to herself rather than notes for students to look back on. She explains the concepts pretty well in person, but if you miss class you could miss quite a bit. Sweet professor though and cares a lot about what she teaches!. Grade is cumulation of 4 tests, nothing else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: took this class for arts and letters requirement. one of the most challenging classes i have taken. final grade is 4 test and 20% attendance. GE's are hard graders. lectures were hard to follow, to much information given to learn in 10 weeks. did not feel like an intro class. i would not recommend this class AT ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To start, Professor Calhoon is not a history professor, and she is tasked with fitting all of Roman history into ten weeks. This is simply not feasible, and it felt like we never got our feet under us. However, she is obviously passionate, caring, and funny! Interesting lecture style and course content, but dont expect to actually gain too much.

I loved Dr. Calhoon! She knows the material and adds humor to the topics. The grade is based on four exams, but I would say her study guides for them were great resources for the exams. I would love to take her class again, though this history class was through the lens of classics. We read Livy and Tacitus, many pages a week, so there is that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor Calhoon is both knowledgeable and smart but she is not a history instructor.

This was the worst organized class I have ever taken. The grading is incomprehensible and seemingly random. There are four in-class tests and together they amount to 90% of the course grade. Expect to need to know the smallest details.

I do not recommend 414.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor Calhoon is obviously both incredibly smart and incredibly knowledgeable about her field of study - classics. Her Ancient Rome class is presented through the lens of a classics lens and a majority of reading assigned is an ancient source.

This was the worst organized class i
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
My favorite teacher at UO so far! Funny, genuine, and she really cares about each and every student. Someone in my class even nicknamed her "Beautiful Christina" because she has such a beautiful personality. 

She will know your name. She'll know what you're struggling with. Very accepting of incorrect answers in class, as long as you're trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is funny, engaging, and she cares about her students and their understanding of the course material. She was able to make even latin class enjoyable and she took the time to answer every single question that anyone asked about the material.

Lots of interest in what she teaches. Lecture outlines are hard to follow so showing up to class is your best bet. 3 classes a week was a little heinous but we were only graded on tests and discussion attendance. The tests were nice because they let you pick the prompts that you responded to, which helps in terms of writing about strong subjects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Calhoon is great - the lectures are interesting and you can tell she loves teaching it. Her lecture outlines are set up in a way that they don't make much sense unless you attend class and hear her talk about the subject, so you must attend each lecture. The tests are nice because they are paragraph-length responses - easy for full credit
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was lucky I had a good GE

I don't get her bad reviews. Maybe she's changed her teaching style, but she was very straightforward on how she tested us. She could be a tiny bit disorganized with hw, but not enough to cause problems. She wanted us to succeed, and set us up the best she could. Very accommodating to me needing extra time before I got AEC accommodations.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She goes above and beyond to offer accommodations for students. Hand typed fantastic lecture overviews during covid containing all she'd test on, allowed at home typed tests... She isn't the best with tech, but she keeps to simple documents to make it easy to understand. Excellent professor, interesting lectures, answers questions wholeheartedly.

Professor Calhoon was the coolest professor I have had in a while. Classics 314 Gender and Sex in Antiquity was my favorite class this term and I would 100% recommend it to anyone who is interested in classics. I found her lectures to be hilarious and entertaining. she only grades on attendance and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COST! She was so bad that I did not take Latin 102 and literally changed languages for my BA requirement because she is the only latin prof at UO. She literally failed me after I worked SO hard and destroyed my mental health over this class. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Latin is tough no question but Calhoon does a good job teaching the material without overwhelming you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I thought she was a very unfair grader and also refused to answer most questions. Everything was pretty much graded on exams which never had anything to do with the study guides, and had vocab never brought up before. Take with someone else if you can.

Professor Calhoon is a genuine professor. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. We mainly correct the homework during class, which is really helpful for catching your mistakes and building a greater understanding of the material. She isn't a tough grader so if you at least try and attend class you should be fine.
horrible teacher, would never take this class again. bad at lectures and ge are bad at explaining stuff.

Dr. Calhoon is extremely caring and definitely wants her students to succeed. I want to give her the benefit of the doubt as this in an online class, but I often find the lectures to be unorganized, and much of class is spent correcting homework rather than actually learning Latin. Still, I think that she does a pretty good job overall.
Tests are fairly easy. Lectures are posted online but attendance counts for grade

Calhoon is a solid choice for a CLAS professor. Her notes are fairly sparse so pay attention and take notes on what she says as anything she says could be on the exam. I also recommend printing out images from her slides and studying them; that really helped me for Image ID on tests. Readings aren't really necessary. Really doable class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Christina is the best. Super kind and caring, and really REAL when you visit her office hours. A sunflower of the Classics department to make things a little better there. Had to rate her when I saw that she hadn't been done justice.

The lectures the professor gives does very well to keep attention. She's pretty funny and easy to get a hold of outside of class. If you stay on top of your readings, you can follow along to her somewhat sparse lecture notes with no problem otherwise. Tests are not as intimidating as it seems. I'm taking another one of her class again next term!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: LOVE this professor. I've taken two Latin courses with her and she is probably the best teacher I've had at UO. She's approachable, caring, and so funny. She makes class enjoyable, I definitely recommend!

CLAS 110 was by far the easiest class I've taken and I'm a marine bio major so no mythological background. Passed every exam by following the study guides and keeping up of the readings. If you aren't lazy, you'll get an A easily. Barely had to study the material and got 100% on the final.

Went into this class thinking it was going to be a INTRO level class & left thinking  I wish I had had more a background before taking it. The lectures were boring, she's a very dry speaker, attendance is mandatory, and the tests are 100% writing: Passage or term identification, T/F (must fix if false) & essay (all in 50 minutes). Not recommended.

Lectures are very boring, and the notes she uses to outline her lectures have no structure. The reading rather dull, and you almost need to have a previous knowledge of the gods if you don't want to be confused the entire time.

I have had Professor Calhoon for three terms of Latin now (101, 103 & 302) and she has easily been one of my favorite Professors at the University. Her grading criteria is clear, she is very helpful inside and outside of class, and she is pretty funny sometimes too. Knows the subject very well, she is head of the classics department.

Probably one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. Super easy tests if you follow the study guide. Don't buy the book, all the same information (that you don't really need) is available online. All that being said, this was also the most boring class I've ever taken. Please find another easy A class besides this one if you can!!

One of the worst lecturers I've had.  She was not excited or energetic while lecturing and it caused not only myself but a majority of the other students to lose interest during the lecture.  Her notes are incomplete and very scattered,  making it difficult to study by yourself.

Prof. Calhoon is a very clear and precise in her teaching and I feel like I not only began to learn Latin, but love it as well.  You have 3 exams, a midterm, and a final, one every 2 weeks or so. You can ace them if you have proper study habits, such as memorizing each chapter's vocabulary, which is very important, since they will be on the exams

This class was very easy, especially if you actually show up to class and actually do the work. Taking notes is also a good thing in this class. She gets into what she teaches, and she teaches it well. Her accent is no hindrance. The tests are also very easy, as long as you keep up on the notes/reading. Just don't be lazy.

She's nice, and also smart. She likes the people in her class and if you can keep up with what she talks about, it's cool. She's really an okay teacher and the class shouldn't be hard, especially if you get a kind GTF. No real homework but her tests are tricky.

Her tests are extremely difficult. She'll mention something in lecture really quick and expect you to know it. Her lectures are scattered all over the place and difficult to follow. You have to spend hours reading to even understand any topics being taught. DO NOT take this class if you have no background in mythology, definitely not a intro class.

Good Professor. She's witty and funny, with a great accent! She makes the lectures very interesting, but her tests are hard and you have to keep up with the reading in the book. Sometimes things aren't quite clear, but she's friendly and helpful.

Loved this class/teacher. The style she teaches in is like listening to a storyteller, which makes subjects like the classics all the more interesting to learn. She is very engaged and excited about the topics she teaches and passes that enthusiam on to her students. I have taken multiple classes with her and enjoyed each one.
Awesome teacher!  She did a great job with taking Latin grammar and making it enjoyable.

She's a hard teacher. Her notes are very incomplete (a headache to read) and attendance is mandatory.
