I'm very grateful to have been able to take a class with her because it has made my senior year so much better. Take any class you can with her if you are able. Hands down the best professor I have had at UO.

Sarah is an amazing professor, she cares about her students and wants them to do well. She is very easy to reach outside of class, there are few homework assignments that are fairly easy. The content of this class isn't very interesting but Sarah does her best to keep attention. The test are fairly easy if you study and can apply the knowledge.

She's so great and super funny. Content is interesting and we learn a lot. Assignments and exams are not stressful at all as she gives us plenty of time to do them. Exams are take-home and really fun; we apply moral psych theories to famous real-life cases!

The best professor at University of Oregon, hands DOWN. Her lectures are  very informative and all of the exams are on a study guide that she gives before the test. You're also allowed a study flash card during tests! Genuinely cares about her students and their success! I took 301, 306, and 302, and would take any other class she's offered

Sarah answers questions, responds to emails milliseconds after they're sent, and has clear expectations. It really feels like she wants you to succeed. She also said that her moms probably the only one that reads these reviews LOL.
2nd class with her and I love her!!! For 302 being not a fun class to take, she makes it way more enjoyable. Attendance counts but it's on iclicker. Highly recommend!

Very funny and kind. Loved her class.
Very clear on grading criteria and expectations. Truly wants people to succeed and makes time for students outside of class. Explains topics clearly and doesn't mind questions.
She deserves to be a full time hire! not just pro-tem :(

Sarah really wants her students to succeed! She is clear about what concepts students need to understand for the exams, and the lecture and homework materials and topics translate very clearly over to the topics on the exam. I would quite literally take any class that she teaches because her lectures are so straightforward and engaging!
Super kind, funny, objective, and passionate about the subject! She is also really accessible outside of class and is always willing to help if you have questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she is amazing! so glad I was able to experience her class and UO is lucky to have her.
Such an understanding professor and great, engaging lectures.
Dimakis is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students and the content she lectures on. She keeps everything interesting/clear and the assignments are pretty minimal. Overall top tier

My favorite professor of all time. I will literally take any class she teaches. Her lectures are engaging and hilarious, and she somehow even makes the homework interesting (never thought I'd enjoy writing a discussion post).
I love sarah, shes so funny and a really good professor overall. I can tell she really cares about her students learning. 2 midterms and one final, pretty good class. Definitely recommend

Genuinely the best psych class I have taken at UO, have never had this much fun learning and have retained all of the content super easily. The exams are take home and are fun, providing unique challenges that are very rewarding. The lectures are super engaging and some of the examples are hilarious, making it easy to stay engaged + fun discussions

Sarah is funny af. The homework is minimal and the only big assignments are 3 exams. There's a discussion board every week and some weeks there are video quizzes instead of the discussions. The lectures are entertaining and she keeps people engaged easily. I would literally die for Sarah she's such a great professor!
Sarah is awesome by far my favorite professor at uo, I don't even normally write reviews for professors but did it bc she was that cool
I've had Sarah for 2 terms in a row this year and she has set me up well as a psych major. I'm very grateful for her 301 class; I've had a good time in her 306 class!
I love her more than anything she literally gives answers to the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love her! She is an amazing teacher, she makes the material interesting and fun to learn. I come away from class retaining the information. Highly recommend any of her classes.
Sarah is my favorite person ever. She is so funny and her lectures are incredible. I wish I could take her class every term.

Sarah is so funny and always makes class enjoyable. She is super easy to talk to and is always willing to help with assignments or answer any questions you may have. If you have the chance to take her class I would definitely recommend it!!

Sarah was great, she was a really fun professor to learn from. Her lectures were probably one of the most engaging I've had. Sure, sometimes it would be a bit dull just to get through the material. But whenever she had a chance she made it super fun and interactive. Also very easy to reach outside of class. TAKE HER IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE!!!!

Took social psych with Sarah and it was amazing. The lectures were structured so well and easy to follow. Her examples and activities are fun and engaging. The exams were not too difficult, if you study you'll do great and you get to use a notecard. Highly highly recommend

Sarah is such an amazing professor, it really shows since she hasn't been teaching long that she has a real knack for it. She lays out a predetermined lecture schedule so you'll know exactly what to expect for each class, and actually won't want to miss them! (Unless you take an 8:30 like I did) She gives great feedback, overall great experience.

Sarah is a amazing professor and is very authentic when it comes to teaching. She is more on the monotone side, however it adds to her charm. She is easy to understand and will explain things differently if you don't understand. She cares for her students and is willing to work with you. Keep in mind her lectures are slide based and easy to follow.

Great professor! Her class is organized so you know everything you will do ahead of time, and there is very little homework assignments. You are allowed to use a flashcard for exams, but they aren't that hard! Loves ot engage with students, and truly listens to them! I would definitely take her class again!

Sarah is one of the best psych professors I have come across. Her slides are clear and she gives real world examples, which makes the content easier to understand. You are graded on 3 exams, which you are allowed a notecard on, discussion posts, 3 reflections, and attendance. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

Sarah is such a great professor, she is super engaging and makes class really easy to follow and understand. Assignments are not super hard but they're engaging. She makes you want to come to class because she is funny and makes up interesting discussions. I've taken multiple classes with her and all have been great!

Despite being her first term teaching, Dimakis excels in making the courses concise, interesting, and relevant. The lectures and slides were straightforward but interactive. Assignments were easy enough not to overwhelm me but challenging enough to make me engage with the material. I always looked forward to her classes. Highly suggested!

Took two courses with Sarah and was beyond impressed. Material was easy to understand because of the way she skillfully broke it down. She applied clear and interesting examples to the concepts given and was extremely open to helping when something is unclear. Super big fan and would recommend to all types of students.

My favorite professor I've had at UO by far. Lectures are easy to understand and easy to focus on, homeworks aren't hard, and neither are tests (especially since you get a notecard.) Dimakis is chill, funny and engaging as well as flexible. It feels like she's on your side and wants you to learn. She knows so much about her topic and clearly cares.

Professor Sarah Dimakis is totally awesome. I actually looked foward to going to class to listen to her lectures. She does a really good job at connecting things were learning in class to the outside world, making what we were learning way more engaging than the average lecture.

Overall a really good professor and gives clear and easy to track lectures. Slides are also concise and useful for studying. Homework and exams were reasonable as well. Would absolutely take her class again.

She is very clear in her lectures, and there are a few homework assignments over the term but nothing too difficult or too much. Participation matters, and iClickers are required, but overall it is not a difficult course at all.

We got a notecard on the exam so immediate yes 
Very chill and understanding of unfortunate circumstances, definitely a professor who will work with you

Honestly, the class is decently easy as long as you pay attention during the lectures. Her voice is a little monotone which can make the lectures feel a little long. But overall, like she's really great with resources for the exams and everything within her class is super accessible. She's also lowkey really funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LOVE LOVE LOVE! shes so sweet and the best psych professor its her first term teaching and shes doing AMAZING. The grading is balanced on many categories from essays, quizzes and 3 tests. She makes it very easy to engage with the material and it directly applies to exams!
10/10 cutest human ever
Professor dimakis is very clear and has great lecutres. slides are easy to follow and expectations are very clear. a funny prof and im taking her again next term!
Take her classes, I love sarah!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is amazing.

Sarah is my favorite teacher in the PSY department. She is funny, kind, and always willing to answer questions. She provides study guides, lets tests have notecards, and allows music if it helps you. Her slides are always clear and easy to read. She regularly dismisses class early. She is passionate about her lectures and genuinely cares about you.

Honestly this class was perfect in the middle of not too hard but like you feel as though you genuinely are learning something. The lectures are a little boring, but overall have all the content you need for the exams etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very kind professor. Her voice is monotone which kind of me sleepy and become bored of the lectures, but her lecture's were very good and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for psych 309, I really enjoyed this class, she has a monotone voice, but besides that, she is an amazing teacher. She is very passionate about the subject and knowledgeable about the topics. She makes the lectures fun and engaging and changes them based on world events. She is a great teacher, I would definitely take her class again.

She speaks dryly but is still engaging and her slides are very organized and easy to follow. Going to lectures is important to understand the material but if you can't make it you can rely on the slides and the reading will go just be a more in-depth version of those slides. I'll take her social psychology course (306) this winter.
She is so funny and relatable, I 100% would take her class again, the workload is really not that bad and she is willing to help you if you're struggling.
One of the best professors I've had at the U of O!

Hands down the best professor Ive ever had! Ive come to expect that most prof show up, grade you, and help only if you want it. Dimakis makes this notion completely false. Not only does she EXCELL in giving you help outside/ inside the class, she intensely reads your work and gives thorough feedback that actually helps. She WANTS you to succeed!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I loved both terms of German that I took with Daniel. He provided a very conversational atmosphere, and with the homework it created an environment where I felt I learned a lot. He genuinely cares about his students and tries to cater the class to their wants and needs as much as possible. He is very accessible via office hours and email as well.
Excellent class! I was having a hast time last term with German, however with this class, I got a lot of motivation again. I highly recommend.

"I really enjoyed Daniel's class! He was very attentive and his class was entertaining. This class gave me a lot of motivation to learn German. Being an economics major, I was always looking for a class like this, since my other classes were boring and not very engaging. Viele Dank!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, genuinely cares about you learning the language, and is a super lenient grader and almost always offers extra credit on quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Daniel's class was thoughtfully organized and he has a good understanding of the learning process (clear in the assignments and quizzes). He can be funny and offers good explanations for anything. A class someone who cares to learn German, rather than put a language course on their transcript.

I had Daniel for GER223: Germany: A Multicultural Society, in spring 2025. This was my favorite class of the year. It was a chill and supportive classroom environment, and Daniel is a very knowledgeable and relatable instructor. I was excited to come to class each day and encourage you to take this class if Daniel is your instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Although I wanted to stay with my GER101 teacher, I was happy that my schedule conflict led me to take GER102 with Daniel. He is a very nice instructor who seems very passionate about teaching. It was my favorite class this term! The atmosphere in the class was great, which helped relieve a lot of the pressure when being called on. Totallyrecommend
I love Daniel

I really enjoyed having Daniel as a professor. He was attentive to his students and very engaging. It was a bit intimidating to be called on at first, but he just wants to make sure you are involved in the class and actually learn the language. He is will help as much as he can to make sure you succeed in his class. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was really fun and interesting, and Daniel is really receptive to any feedback about homework and other assignments being too much. Like some of the other reviews said, yes he speaks a lot of German but it's a German language class and he'll always explain in English if people don't understand.

He spoke mostly in German, which I really liked. But I simply did not understand his instructions. My classmates and I only guessed what he could possibly mean. The whole class seemed confusing and irritating sometimes, I didn't know what to do or how to respond to Daniel's questions.

I took German in high school and was expecting this class to be similar but I really enjoyed having Daniel as my professor! He is great and his classes are fun. He really cares about his students' success and is also very approachable. There is sometimes a lot of homework but it's manageable. Go to class, do your assignments and get an easy A.

He is nice, young, and high-energy. Instructed using almost exclusively in German, which led to a lot of guessing between me and my classmates. We were typically confused about the instructions for the group participation exercises, which occurred at least 3x a lecture. 
I do not feel prepared for Ger. 102.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not a particularly good course. I didn't really learn German. The exercises seemed ineffective and often difficult to understand. He tried to be very popular.

This teacher was very focused on being liked.  The activities were entertaining but not effective for learning.  There was a lot of homework and group work, but it didn't set me up well for the next course in the sequence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Wrote an earlier review on here and wanted to come back and correct it. The first several days of the course were tricky to get the hang of, but if you do the homework outside of the course it starts to make more sense by the fourth day in class. While he sometimes puts you on the spot with questions, it's never intended to demean or embarrass.

I have ADHD & Autism, and so far the class is a nightmare for me. Instructions are pretty much only given in German despite this being a 101 class, and given that I already struggle with instructions in plain English, I don't have any effective way of knowing whats going on, and I took German online prior to this class.

I had a horrible experience taking this class. I was struggling with depression, was diagnosed with ADHD six weeks into the term, and I also got COVID during week 3. These health challenges made it very difficult for me to keep up with the work and Daniel didn't seem all that sympathetic. Taking this class actively worsened my mental health.

Loved Daniel as my professor! I had taken a break, but he made jumping back into learning German much less anxiety-inducing. Unlike previous German professors, he didn't continuously press on you when you didn't know the answer. He is funny and a great teacher! I learned more in one term than ever before.

His class was super fun! We were able to learn a lot of German throughout the quarter as he actively engaged his students, but he made sure to be kind/caring when giving feedback. The class had a fair amount of homework but it was not very stressful and he is fairly lenient with grading so that students are encouraged to keep learning German.

His classes are fun. He asks everyone questions during class in order to make you speak in German what can be at first intimidating but he never tries to put you on the spot in a negative way. There is a lot of homework but I think it's a fair amount if you really want to learn the language.

Dreiling is awesome, hes clearly very passionate and cares more about sharing the content than exams or hw. His lectures are interesting, and attendance matters because there aren't many assignments. He offers loads of extra credit. Super kind and funny guy. Discussion attendance also matters a lot and is a great way to engage in the content.

This class is not worth the time/money, I've learned nothing. His lecture slides are text heavy and he doesn't even lecture based off of them. He stands at the front of the class yelling and making himself upset about politics. He's extremely closed minded, makes backhanded comments, and talks in circles. Overall disappointing, content seemed cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He yells at us, and he doesn't release our canvas exams on time so you never really know when you have to do an exam. He is so close minded and you have to think how he does to get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy overall, but not the best lecturer especially when it's 2 hours long and a 500-person class. I got bored and many students around me tuned out as well. Tests are online and questions are from class slides and the textbook. Just take it for the general ed credit. Thumbs up for moving the 8am in-person final exam to Canvas though!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He really cares about sociology and what he is teaching however at times his lectures will get confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Learned more in my high school sociology class. Our last paper was about climate change, and he didn't even relate it to sociology. He forces his political views onto you. 10/10 would not recommend taking this class. Grading rubric for discussions don't make much sense.
This guy is a joke. Small minded. Thinks the world is ending. Avoid him.

Michael gets side tracked very easily and will call people out in the middle of class if they appear to not be listening. But he is a great professor and is very passionate about Sociology. Attendance is not mandatory, 2 midterms (both online) and one final (also online). Highly recommend.
His class was alright. Lectures were long and he tends to rant a lot. I appreciate how in a 400 student lecture hall he encourages people to share their opinion. Be prepared for a lot of reading.
He tends to rant and get way behind schedule, but he gave us 3% of extra credit added to our grade if we missed no more than 1 class all term. Fairly easy course

Amazing Professor, great class. 3 Tests, 1 paper. Easy/short homework, 1 assignment a week. Last 2 tests were online/open book. You get the final essay prompt in advance and have a couple weeks to do it. Even if this class wasn't super easy I would recommend it, one of the best classes Ive had. Only sucky thing was the massive amounts of reading.
His tests are really hard and the lectures are extremely confusing, you dont know what is important

Michael is a very cool professor but he also doesn't hold back with his opinions about things going on. He's very liberal and teaches at a very liberal school but sometimes he says things that could be uncomfortable for some. But besides that he is a very motivated professor.
Awesome, funny, enthusiastic! Definitely would take another class from him!

He is easily one of the best professors you can take. He is passionate about what he is teaching you and you will learn a lot. His lectures are entertaining. This quarter has been pretty easy. Our first mid-term was in the class, the second one was online, and now our final is online or in-class. I would recommend him to anyone. You'll learn a lot.

Dreiling is AMAZING! He is so engaged with his students in lecture. Having his SOC 204 class last every TuesThurs, my day always ended better than it began. I would recommend him to ANYONE. He cares about his students learning, not getting an A. Therefore, it is a pretty easy class if you put in some effort. Attendence in Discussion is required.
Entertaining. Dreiling definitely knows how to get the attention of everyone during his lectures.
Class is interesting and not hard to go to and Dreiling usually has pretty entertaining lectures.
Top notch!

I have an adult-crush on Michael Dreiling. Not an actual crush, but he's just a really extremely cool dude. He's really passionate about what he teaches (I took an intro Soc class with him, and American Society), which makes class fun to be in and entertaining. He really loves talking about this subject with you, and is really engaging and fun.
Professor Dreiling is a very engaging lecturer and knows his material well. Will inspire you to do better for the world. I would take another class with him.
Fantastic teacher! I highly recommend any class he teachers. He is understanding and very interesting. I learned so much.

Best professor I have gotten at the U of O thus far. You can tell he is passionate about what he teachers; very intelligent. He cares so much about he students: for example, he made the midterm and final online just because a student raised her hand and asked him to in class. I would recommend this teacher to anyone and everyone.

Professor Dreiling is a great teacher. He sometimes is a little biased is in his opinion but I don't think he does it on purpose. If you have your own opinion you should speak out because he loves to hear about what people think about his topic. If you do the one page journals, attend class and do the online stuff you should be good. GREAT TEACHER!

He tends to rant in class, which makes it difficult to know what he deems as important from the textbook. His first test came straight from the book, but the second test was online. It's not that hard of material, but he's very detailed in his questions about it.

An amazing instructor, by far the most passionate I have ever had. Made me think critically and re-examine things that I had long taken for granted. It's true he is extremely liberal and conservatives likely will not enjoy him, but it is undeniable that he is incredibly intelligent and well-read; doesn't regurgitate media BS. Strongly recommend him
Would be a good class if he didn't allow his personal opinions to interfere with his lectures. So unless you're a radical liberal as he is, prepare to be offended by his rude left wing comments

I was really not a fan. His lectures consisted of the same kind of rant over and over, making it hard to tell what he actually wanted us to know. As a person, he was a nice guy, but I didn't like his teaching style.

LOVED this professor! Extremely engaging lectures with lots of information. He's a very liberal thinker and breaks a lot of social norms in lecture. He draws his test info mostly from lectures and key phrases from the textbook. Discussion sections are mandatory though. Loved this class and professor! I am planning on taking many classes from him.

This class really opens your eyes to a lot of things. I highly recommend taking this class from Professor Dreiling. He is very, very smart, but also funny and explains things very well. The assignments are easy but require thought. I learned a lot and although I will never take another sociology class I loved this one.

he makes the class. teaching style is unique but his lecture style is very captivating. he's liberal but he'll clearly separate opinion from facts. keep an open mind, it's sociology. much of the topics are the problems in society but so relevant. if you dont get his points, youre probably conservative, in denial, or dont care about social issues

He definitely gets a little rant-oriented at times, but he's a really cool guy. He's hilarious and admirably intelligent. Class is manageable and pretty interesting too. Probably my favorite professor I've encountered here so far.
He's a cool, energetic guy and gives little homework and some take home exams.  It was either boring or controversial issues were brought up, but overall good class.

Very energetic and knowledgeable about sociology, makes you want to attend class. Some classes can be controversial if you were brought up very conservatively, but his opinions are based on facts! Great professor, I plan on taking another one of his classes.

Michael Dreiling is such a great teacher. He's very knowledgeable about sociology and you can tell he's had a lot of experience. He really cares about the issues we talk  about in class and his lectures are always energetic and interesting. He always sticks around after lectures just to chat. He's really made me want to pursue sociology.

This guy really knows his stuff. Its easy to tell he has done his research on the subject and is not simply spitting out what he reads in the textbook. He doesn't necessarily care about your grade (in fact on quizes he even will tell the whole class some answers) but what he truely wants is for you to understand the material. I recommend him

He is very energetic. His lecture is more about his opinions rather than our ideas or teaching materials. He checks class attendence frequentely. So if you need points to level up your grade, you probably may not miss his class. Many films are shown and the information would be on the exam. Those films made me want to pursuit a sociology major.

He was very energetic in class and he was fun to listen to. I found the subject very interesting, and though he has his own strong opinions, I didn't find them too imposing. Very nice guy. Gave extra credit just for coming to class at the end of the semester and the class was pretty easy. Online final and not even that necessary to read the text.

He doesnt reply to emails. You will have to rely on your GTF for questions. I agree with the comment below mine, he doesnt listen to apposing views in class... His class isnt that hard, he just makes me not really want to be there... I had high hopes after his first lecture but it has kinda let me down since.

He is very biased and not willing to listen to other students that oppose his point of view in class. He completely ignored them and cut them off. Very rude and not a good professor. His tests were filled with statistics that even my GTF didn't quite understand when I asked her about them. Don't take this section of SOC 204 from him!
super chill guy, easy to listen to and makes lectures not too boring.  lectures can get boring sometimes but he is very lenient in grading and overall pretty cool

Hard to follow lectures. Classes were too long for such a off topic teacher. I did  not go to class on the longer day because I just could not stand to sit through lecture. The topic was so interesting, but it was hard to pull out what he was going to test you on from his lecture. The only good thing was the online final, thats how I managed an A.

He had very biased opinions that he ranted about in class.  I learned nothing really, and his tests were pretty ridiculous.  The only time I was happy in that class was when he told us there was an online final.

He is continuously interrupts students when they have a point to make and he rambles on thinking that what he says is somehow more profound than everything we read in the book. Not good, maybe funny at times, but quite honestly I am surprised he was hired.

He's my favorite teacher so far, and the only class that I never fell asleep in.  I found him very approachable when I had a problem and it got sorted right away.  Plus the final he gave us was only 4 multiple choice questions that you could take online.  Easiest final ever.  Nice, interesting teacher.

This was probably my favorite class that I've taken so far in school. Dreiling was an amazing Professor, I wish I could have him for all my sociology classes. This class made me seriously consider majoring in Sociology.

This is the best sociology class I have ever taken. I STRONGLY recommend taking this class, even if you are not interested in sociology. He's such a great teacher and really cares about the things he teaches.

Dreiling is an amazing professor. He incorporates current and past issues and sparks further interest about many subjects.  I recommend his class!  You will learn something if you care about the world today.

Lectures were pointless, his power point slides were exactly from the book.  Dreiling kept lectures interesting, but he's very intimidating.  When I went to his office hours, I just felt stupid.  Tests are all multiple choice, not hard, but you need to study for them.

Great class.  Would recommend him strongly.  Do the reading and pay attention to his lectures and you will do great in the class.  Book choices left a little to be desired, but the additional readings made up for it.

He's really passionate about what he teaches, although, unfortunately, this means he usually has taken a side on an issue.  I'm pretty moderate, politically, and I think conservatives would have a hard time getting a good grade, as most of the quiz/essay questions are slanted from the start.  He presents interesting perspectives on a lot of issues.

Many would do well to apply what Professor Dreilling has to say in class. He doesn't just teach terms, he applies them for himself and expects you too as well. Unfortunately I don't think many people go into the class looking to broaden their horizons; yet, he still tries to dumb down the material for just those people.

I thought the class was very informative and that he was very organized with the information. I liked the lectures, and he was always helpful when I went to office hours. If you've been sheltered in Oregon or you're not a sociology major, yes, you may think he's too liberal.

His classes were so boring that he had to bribe kids to come to class by randomly giving out extra credit points to kids who came. The kids who came for the extra credit points just played on their laptops the whole time. I don't think I learned a single thing from this class that I did not already know. He bored the class with star trek references
very informative, always willing to help students

I thought this teacher made class kind of corny and although he didn't upset me personally, he did upset a couple of my friends because he seemed to be one sided on certain issues. However, the information of the class was interesting.
Interesting prof.
The material he covers in soc 204 is stuff a lot of us already know, but he teaches it in a really good way. Although the class is rather boring, its easy and interesting.
Winded, boring, tricky, spiteful if you skip class
No Comments

This is a great class to take because he gives out lots of A+s. Everybody I know got an A and never even studied. I had about an 85% in his class and got a 4.3! He is late every day, so you don't have to be on time either. He doesn't control the classroom much, so you can chat with friends during the lecture.
Dreiling is pretty boring but the class is easy

I thought he focused too much on poverty in other countries and too much on inequality. Although those are very important things, sociology is so muh more than that, and that's coming from a socialist (me). I do like that on the last two days he PROVES that he is a Marxist.

Gives a good lecture, but he's late sometimes. Show up to his class and you don't even have to study all the reading material (which is good, because there is a lot of it). Professor is very smart and energetic--fun to listen to. His TA is uptight about grading essay questions, so use lots of terms rather than concepts.

Prof. Dreiling is definitely opinionated...and does use lecture time to talk about his beliefs. However, I don't feel there's anything wrong with it: he does research on these topics, so he's just sharing what he's worked on. Also, he's open to any student opinions, despite what some people may have you believe. Overall, interesting and friendly!

Professor Dreiling does not use class time efficiently and does not cover the amount of material that he could because he spends most of the time on preaching his political beliefs.  Nothing is gained from the lectures, he continually falls behind on the schedule, but still tests on all the material.  Overall, very unprofessional and rude.
he made us watch fahrenheit 9/11, which had no relevance, for an hour before our midterm. i am a liberal student but i can't stand it when teachers try to push their views on you.

VERY opinionated. Tries to push views and beliefs on students. Doesn't cite graphs and figures posted on lecture slides. Not wholly bad though. He seems to know his stuff, and enjoys lecturing. Spends alot of time talking about social inequality, multinational corporations, free trade, and the big bad US Government.
awesome

He is the most unapolegetically biased professor I have ever come into contact with.  I respect it when professors have their own opinions, but I think that he should show a little more respect for his students by not forcing his own opinions down their throats
He's gota lota knowledge. AAAnd will give you a work-out! We did a "union-made", "no sweat[shop]zone" project.--awesome

Listens with empathy to the feelings and believes of others.  Has never shut someone off in the 4 classes I took from him.  A great prof let's you do creative projects and alternative grading plans so you don't have to do the tests.
No Comments
Awesome guy, awesome professor.
No Comments

Ok for all you raters out there, you need to keep in mind that sociology professors are always biased. I personally admire the kind of passion Mr. Dreiling has and I learned quite a bit from him. 4 out of 5.
Couldn't stand the class, it was horrible. His views were right and everyone else was wrong - ALWAYS! I think he even made a guy cry.
This man was very opinionated, and very very biased with his lectures. He only looked at one side of issues and was full of rage at just about everything!
He went off on a lot of tangents, a little boring.
Really nice and an interesting class. Not sure if that is the number but its called American Societies.

Great professor. In the beginning I was a bit nervous about taking this class after hearing how research heavy it can be but her explanation made it easy and fun throughout the term. She is a great professor I highly recommend.
Professor Simnitt was very kind and clearly wants each student to succeed. While things could be disorganized at times, it never got in the way of learning in the class.

Any of my issues with this course do not stem from the professor; Simnitt is amazing! She cares deeply for her students, and she wants her students to learn. She offers extra credit regularly throughout the term, and she is very understanding. Classes can be a bit boring, but I would nonetheless reccomend taking Professor Simnitt.

Dr. Emily is very personable, she is reasonable in her requests and clearly outlines how to be successful in her class. Her expectations are that you show up and do the work. There are extra assignments requirements for an A, but they aren't meant to be hard. If you complete them with an open mind you will learn something about yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Simnitt is clearly very knowledgable in her field. She's kind and flexible, but overall I found the course difficult to navigate. The assignments themselves are not that challenging, but the instructions leaped around quite a bit, making it difficult to understand exactly what she was looking for. She was quick to respond to messages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The grading system was if you turn everything in, regardless of quality you will get a B. So if you write an amazing paper or if you just check off all the requirements, it doesn't matter. Prof. Simnitt was a nice lady but she didn't actually teach anything. She seemed a little scattered and I often felt like showing up to class was a waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is overall a really nice lady, but I found her class to be disengaging. Hard to follow along with what she is saying and cant get her point across. Lots of reading and writing and you have to do extra work to recieve an A. Definitely on the easier side but the way she explains assignments is so confusing and I never know exactly what to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Because Emily Simnitt is new to the University of Oregon, this class was largely experimental. I wouldn't have taken the class if I had originally knew this, but the class was okay and enjoyable at times. Professor Simnitt has a tendency to ramble and it can get boring but it's an easy A if you just show up and do the class work! She is very nice.
Not too challenging of a class given the content-dense nature of an introductory course. Prof. Gade is super kind and very enthusiastic to help out students!! Highly recommend

Not too challenging of a class given content-dense nature of an introductory course, and Prof. Gade is super nice and is always enthusiastic to help out her students when you talk to her!! Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is very easy to reach, and I can tell she genuinely cares for her students. Classes are very slide-heavy, but it's not bad. Beware of pop quizzes! Attendence isn't mandatory, but there are occasional easy quizzes (a few are dropped tho). Also, be prepared to use Perusall a LOT. Overall, Emily was great, but I didn't like my GE....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Gade is a great professor. Be prepared to have mandatory readings, she uses software that tracks engagement and annotations with reading. There is around 1-2 hours of reading per class. Outside of that there is a final exam, no midterm and two in small in-class presentations. Attendance is not mandatory. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire class is going over a series of different economic models that pertain to different political topics. The lectures go over the math and derivations behind the models, but the tests are just on intuition/explanations. If you show up to class, or just really try to learn the intuition, the tests are straightforward, and no homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 exams make up entire grade but there is so much practice material and the questions are all on things taught very explicitly in class. There is no math on the tests. The "textbook" is one he wrote but didn't complete, it is essentially a packet of very clear, relevant, and helpful notes. Come to class and you will easily pass if not get an A.

Teaches out of his failed attempt at a textbook for the last 20 years. Two midterms and a final, very harsh grading. Class average was around a 75%, maybe a tad lower. Does not curve or offer extra credit. If you take for an elective class prepare for lots of studying on your own, he is not much help.

Has been teaching out of his unfinished textbook for 20 years now. Kind of funny but mostly dry, boring, and extremely disorganized lectures despite teaching the same thing 20 years straight. Felt like I had answered certain questions word for word to the definition and docked a point or two for no reason. 2 Midterms worth 50% and Final worth 50%.

Listen to intuition and use past exams to practice. The derivations he shows are for grad students so undergrads that's the time for your bathroom break lol. Ask questions especially before the final because he won't upload the answers he expects you to attempt it yourself and ask him questions about what you saw. Major case of senioritis (same).

I would never take another one of his classes again. Ellis didn't show up for class three times and didn't even email us to cancel. He rarely replied to emails and it would take forever to get back to the other students and me. He wasn't very friendly, his lectures were dry, and he gave little to no instructions for the case studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was taking his EC440 in Fall2021, he is definitely a tough grader and our average is around 70 percent which is a C-. He has no curve even with such a low average. What is more important is he hasn't replied to any email even your it is polite to him. Also, practice mid-term and finals haven't answered. The lecture recording is unreadable.

Professor Ellis class was entertaining albeit confusing at times. He definitely knows what hes talking about but uses a ton of math for a class that tests mainly on written intuition. Despite these factors, the class was enjoyable, Ellis is really funny, and its graded on a curve so youre likely to do well as long as you put in a solid effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor, keeps things engaging, even when the subject matter gets a little dry. Encourages debate/participation instead of just droning at you.

Chris's class is math-heavy, which could be why students are reviewing him poorly. I personally grasped the material well. Take extensive notes during class, don't be afraid to ask questions and spend time outside of class studying the mathmatical explanation behind the economic models he presents. He doesn't hold hands. I learned a good deal.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chris is a nice professor, if you don't know the answer for practice questions, just ask, he is always sitting in his office in office hour and waiting for students who is ready to ask questions. Things learned in his class are many and you cannot just memorize things because you need to understand the materials.

The text is first four chapters of a textbook he attempted to write several years ago: YOU ARE LITERALLY STUDYING OUT OF HIS FAILED ATTEMPT OF A TEXTBOOK. Lectures and text cover the math behind the theories, but you're only tested on the intuition/explanations. Tests are vague and if you don't write a page long, super specific answer, you'll fail.

STAY AWAY. Ellis is a terrible teacher. He was terrible in office hours, would make things even more confusing and it wont help. Expects you to learn everything from the book or in his very vague slides. Tests were on stuff we didn't learn and grading was difficult. Look elsewhere for teachers.

Took his Public Econ class over summer '12. Interesting lectures, no textbook, math heavy but he never tests you on the math except for extra credit points. Clear in what he expects you to know, if you go to class and keep up on studying your notes there's no reason to not get a good grade in Ellis' classes. Recommended for serious students

It was pretty obvious that he did not prepare for lectures and just goes off the top of his head. He had no homeworks: 25% participation, 50% final, 25% midterm...intensive scale for tests. Class was pretty fun though. He is not too concerned with teaching, much more so his consulting and research.

He is a nice guy, but tends to clarify aspects of the course through mathematics loosing some of the students. There is no official text for this course except the one he has written which of course is strongly based upon math. In short, take the time to learn the math and use it to explain the intuition of the course.

Tests are on subject matter other then that learned in class or read in book. He can't answer questions form students about test material, even though HE wrote the test. would never take another class from this guy. His sense of humor might get people that haven't taken his class to think he's great. DON'T BE FOOLED!!
Chris is one of the best proffessors ive had keeps the class interesting by using real world examples and occasional humor.. very good class. the tests are difficult though
Tests are poorly written and class notes seem worthless in preparing for them.

Chris is an awsome guy.  Had him for two classes as an econ undergrad.  Always avalible and clear.  Watch out for his tests though.  Sometimes, you won't be prepared for the tests by simply taking notes.  READ the book assigned for the class even if it doesn't direclty tie into the class.  He sometimes likes to take test questions from the reading.  Also check with him befor buying the book, he usually has copies in his offoce which he will check out to students.
This class was fun.  Chris Ellis does a great job of teachin his material in a masterful, yet entertaining and approachable way.  He's laid back, and very fun to listen to.

Professor Ellis is by far the most approachable, helpful, and fun teacher in the Economics department.  His lectures are paced perfectly and the content is presented clearly and with light-hearted humor, which actually made the class (dare I say it) fun!
Fun class, good lectures. Final was ok too, but what was he thinking with that midterm?
No Comments

Tests are what you expect and mostly easy but the grading is kind of random, although he is always happy to address concerns-or just to chat. Very nice and knows his stuff and makes it interesting. He is unclear when graphing and drawing conclusions from them S/Times but sincerely encourages questio
Best class ever.  I love game theory and I love Chris Ellis!

would rather drag my cooter on hot steaming gravel for a mile than take another class with her. thank god she is retiring because for a mental health class she sure made a lot of people depressed and cry in class.
She doesn't actually care that much about attendance, she is nice and is clearly very good at her job, but she is a little dismissive
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty easy prof as long as you pay attention and do the readings. Doesn't always seem to know what she's talking about and tries to have GEs answer most of the questions in class. Pretty much everything is graded by the GEs so if you have a strict GE, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Canvas was hard to navigate, and hard to find course materials.

This class overall was ok. There is not many things graded which means you need to do good on the midterm and final. The lectures are long, but the textbook is free which I appreciated. The GE's are helpful, and Professor Replogle responds to emails quickly. If you enjoy sociology, I would reccomend this class and this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All you will be doing is reading A LOT and writing A LOT. Lectures are hard to stay focused on. 1 midterm, 1 final exam, 6 discussion papers, and dis attendance...that's all you will be graded on, so one horrible test/paper expect that grade to dropppp. Overall the discussions with the GE were the best part of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elaine has zero media literacy for a professor who teaches Sociology of Mass Media. First there was the JD Vance textbook in her Soc of Poverty class, and then the paper on Homer's Phobia, the simpsons episode, claiming the simpsons was homophobic when the whole point of the episode was homophobia bad. Most of her readings are equally as low brow.

Elaine has SUPER interesting lectures and is a very likable person. However, I think I've read more for this class than any other class at UO. It's possible to succeed once you get the hang of the writing style she prefers, but you'll have to take some hits to your grade to figure that out. Study the authors and who said what b/c she tests on that.

I enjoyed Elaine very much. Her lectures were super interesting and I liked having time to discuss topics in class. There is a textbook and the two midterms for the class have a lot of material from it so you do need to get it. The exams weren't too difficult, but although attendance was not required I would highly recommend not skipping lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Was for Soc399 - Sociology of Mental Health. Shes a good teacher at times but can also not be at times so this isnt an easy class. You need to read A LOT (I read 529pgs). The content is interesting but the grading is not great. Tests are hard, Paper is long and hard. Shes very nice but doesnt exactly realize that we have lives and other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SOC 399: Great class with many interesting topics. Overall she does give many readings, but they are pretty easy to read and get through. Participation and turning in assignments will help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SOC 399: Honestly, I'm so disappointed! I was looking forward to this class yet it is SO MUCH WORK and it is so hard to succeed. We have frequent class discussions that the participation criteria is unclear for and don't get me started on the tests! The questions are on which author said what, not even the content. It's like everything is a trick!

Professor Replogle is a good professor and she is kind. There aren't too many assignments, but lectures are heavy, and there were many dense textbook readings (average 4 chapters a week). There are 3 exams (60% of grade total) so studying is a must! Although attendance is not graded, you probably will not pass if you miss more than a few classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super intriguing class, lectures kept me entertained. Great professor, super genuine, and really cares. Work is straight forward, class is structured well. Great! 10/10
Super generous and cares about what she does. Would ABSOLUTELY take again, 10/10.

Professor Scott is an incredibly passionate professor, it is very clear she cares about what she is teaching. Online lectures are engaging and intriguing. I really enjoyed the material and even the readings. The discussion section also produced great conversation. The class is organized very well, and easy to navigate. Would highly recommend!

I absolutely adore Professor Scott! She is one of the most caring professors @ UO and really tries to support her students in any way possible. I have taken 3 or 4 classes with her, and I love her. If she asked to adopt me, I would say yes. Take a class with her if you can!
I loved this class! Professor and GE were both very kind and caring. Discussions were interesting and engaging. Lots of homework assignments each week but they dont take long. Two big papers.

I didn't have a problem with the professor herself, but the discussion section I was in was simply terrible. Instead of talking as a class, we mostly talked in partners or small groups, and most of the students in the class were very exclusionary toward people who were clearly different from them. Funny, considering it's a social inequality class.

I loved Ellen. I took her SOC 410 class and it is definitely one of my favorite classes I have taken. Ellen is so kind, caring and joyful. I look forward to going to her class. We read a lot of books, and discussed them in class. I felt like I learned a lot about all the inequalities in society. All the books we read were super interesting.

The best professor I have had so far. If you are interested in the course, you will love it. She is so thoughtful, funny, and smart. TAKE HER 410 CLASS! I do not understand why her rating is low. Reading 410 is heavy on reading (duh), and as someone who hates reading, I found them so interesting and easy to get through.

I really enjoyed SOC 207! My class was online but as long as you keep up with the work you will be fine. On average there are about 3 assignments a week and usually a quiz per week. I really enjoyed learning about the concepts that are covered in this class. There weren't any final exams, only 2 papers that weren't too challenging to write.

Genuinely one of the easiest yet most interesting classes I've taken. Prof Scott makes it very clear what to do every week, and assignments are easy. 5 question quiz at the end of all assignments every week, but it's easy if you just do the readings and watch the lecture. No huge exams/finals either, just 2 main papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Easiest class I have taken. It is a lot of reflections and summary’s of the assigned readings. Discussions with Christine were enjoyable, although I don’t feel as though I learned a lot from the course itself. It touched upon many subjects, but not necessarily in depth
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is pretty easy and relatively low participation. I wish that we went more in depth with the sociological topics. I don't feel like I learned a lot, but it wasn't a bad class.

Most caring and thoughtful professor I've ever had. She works with each student individually to ensure you succeed, even if you're behind on readings or assignments. She was flexible when I was dealing with home issues, even going out of her way to help me find solutions. Amazing professor, as long as you try your best she will treat you right!

Sociology as a whole is super interesting, but this class wasn't very engaging. Don't be worried if this is your last option though. The tests are almost entirely based on lecture material, so it's not really necessary to read the textbook. I would recommend attending class because there were a couple films shown that test questions were based on.

Boring lectures filled with common knowledge. I learned nothing. She skews VERY liberal. I didn't disagree with her, but I can see why someone might. SO much reading, none of it ends up being helpful. One test, two essays, and a take-home final you have 3 days to complete that you have to write 2500 words for. A little ridiculous.
Actually the worst professor I have ever had. She doesn't care about teaching us and only shows data that has really now relevance to the class. Avoid at all everything.

Ellen Scott is by far the worst professor I have ever had. She does not care about actually helping us learn, she never seems prepared for class, and only presents data and videos in class, never actually teaching. The tests are super tricky and unfair, with really long and hard to read questions and answers. Avoid this class at all costs!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ellen is an ok professor. Shes nice and approachable, but isnt very good at actually teaching material. She has powerpoints that seem useless, but most info is common sense. 2 essays, 1 in-class multiple choice (average was a 75%), take home short answer final. Discussions are mandatory. Show up & comprehend & youre guaranteed an A-B range grade

Lectures for the entire hour and 20 minutes without cracking a joke or having "discussion time." She's a nice person but class is poorly set up. Assigned seating and no electronics use in a 300 person class. If you miss 1 discussion class, your grade goes down 2.5%. Essay criteria not very clear. I got above a 93% in the class and still got an A-.

Ellen wasn't bad at the beginning of the term for Spring 2018, but around half way though the term, she got lazy with lecture structure. Often she wouldn't give enough time to take notes on slides, seem unprepared at times, and had guest speakers that felt irrelevant to the current topics covered in class. Not a bad person, but not a great prof.
Ellen Scott should not be a lecture teacher. She clearly does not care about making her classes engaging, and quite frankly I did not learn much that I didn't already know.

Shes disorganized, not enthusiastic, really opinionated and her lecture slides aren't helpful. I felt as though her opinions and beliefs shaped the class material. I often felt I had to think or pretend to believe a certain thing in order to understand or even agree with what was being taught. Find a different SOC teacher especially for gen ed.

Ellen Scott is NOT a good lecture teacher. She does not care about keeping the class engaged and wastes time with figuring out the technology, constant guest lectures, videos, and asking the lecture class questions. She does not keep the class interesting in any way and does not seem approachable or caring. Her class lectures are useless.

Ellen Scott is terrible. She finds any excuse not to teach by showing movies, bringing in guest lecturers, fiddling with her laptop etc. Class is 1.5 hrs, and she comes with only 10 or so slides. The lectures were pretty much useless and she gave us extensive reading in the textbook every day instead of teaching us anything. She obv hates teaching.

Class was very easy- as long as you kept up with readings and took down notes in class, tests and papers were fairly easy. Professor Scott can be repetitive, but it helps you learn the material. I would recommend this class to somebody looking for an easy and interesting class.

This class was not what I expected. Prof. Scott's exams were extremely hard and the essays were graded unfairly. The mult. choice questions were also worded poorly and unclearly. Her lectures were extremely boring and she repeated the book every class time. Her GTF's are HORRID and don't seem to understand the material either.
She's a very enthusiastic teacher, much better than the other ones I've had this year. She can be entertaining, and is respectful of the students.
She relates readings to lectures.
This class is about as repetitive as it gets, and liberal.  Not saying it's bad but it can get boring.  She loves what she does which makes lectures bearable. KEEP up on reading and all is well.

The movies Prof. Scott shows are very interesting, but her lecure material can be a little repetitive and boring at times. But she is very clear, easy to understand, and makes great study sheets for the tests.

Save yourself the effort and just read the wikipedia page for northern renaissance art. Her lectures were boring and uninsightful, and we spent the entire term at least a week behind in content. This class was actually the bane of my existence, and the exams are unnecessarily long and complicated. She does care a lot about her students though.

ARH 211: The other ratings weren't joking about the "ums" during lecture but I feel like it really isn't that big of a deal. She still gives very goo dlectures and the class was really amazing. No busy work which I appreciate and you really only need to read two readings. Only 6 assignments, plus attendence grade.

Ehrlich is honestly the best art history teacher I've had--not only in she incredibly knowledgeable and can answer pretty much any questions you have, her classes are genuinely such an easy A if you show up and take notes -- both midterm and final are online. Lecture heavy but she's super sweet and willing to help with anything. Love her
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures are disorganized, but her merit within the discipline of art history is esteemed; she knows a ton and can answer any questions you have. I'd say that the lectures make or break this class. if youre unable to parse through a fair few tangents or if prose often interrupted by yeahs, buts, and uhs, then you shouldnt take this class.

Ehrlich's lectures are soooooooo boring I was falling asleep in class half the time and so was half the class. She needs to find a better way to keep people engaged other than just showing photos on slides and yapping. She passes an attendance sheet around every single class as well like girl be fr.

You can tell she is passionate about the subjects she teaches, and expects you to put the work in. Don't expect an easy A just because it's an Art History course. As long as you pay attention in lectures and take notes, you should be fine. The midterm and final are both online through Canvas, and she was always available outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took 211 (not 205) with Ehrlich and she is the worst lecturer I have ever listened to. I can never follow her and she says uhm every third word which makes it almost unlistenable. I came in thinking this would be another relatively simple art history course but don't take this class with her and you'll thank me later.

Ehrlich, while a nice person, is not made for lecturing. She reads verbatim from a packet of notes and frequently loses her place, hits you with a volley of loud "ums" and "uhs", gets in a fight with her slideshow, then rapid fire throws artists and movements at you. Be ready to take a lot of notes as her slideshows have no words.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very technologically challenged to the point where it is insufferable and affects learning as well as grades. She is always lost in her lectures and lecture slides, so every other word from her mouth is um. Someone in class counted the number of times she said um in an hour and 20 minutes, and it was a hundred and thirty-six. Never take this

Ehrlich is a super awesome professor, and cares a lot about the success of her students! Her lectures can definitely be pretty information heavy, and you will be seeing a lot of the content on the midterm and final, so make sure to take good notes! Two essays and two reflections, pretty simple and straight-forward if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful lecturer, but her lectures can be quick and not very interactive. They are interesting, and you can feel her passion, which I appreciate. There are only four papers and two exams for the entire term. The papers all relate to each other and are straightforward. However, this also means that the grading can be make or break.

Victoria is the queen of the world, shes hilarious, knowledgable and ready to help at any moment. Her class was pretty lecture focused, with readings being class preparation. Her canvas is a little hard to navigate, but she makes it all worth it. Graded by a couple reflections, a comparison essay and online midterm/final exam. Take Victoria!

Don't get me wrong, Ehrlich is very sweet and understand but her class standard for an entry level art history course is pretty unrealistic. We are sped through lectures and expected to have prior art history knowledge..more specifically religious historical context that the average person may not know. But if you put in the work, you'll be okay.

Easily my favorite professor at UO. She is SO kind. Her lectures are super engaging+she's genuinely excited(and very knowledgeable)about what she teaches.Her classes are lecture heavy for sure but as long as you take good notes you're set! Midterms can be hard bc of limited time but not a harsh grader and always wants her students to succeed.
sometimes lectures are really boring because the slides are not engaging, just a picture of an artifact. I liked the papers we did, not a tough grader in my opinion

Professor Ehrlich may get a bad reputation from students who are not expecting to take Art History for an easy A and then get the presentation of an Art History class, but she is an extremely caring and understanding professor if you put in effort. I have also taken her ARH 407/507 course. She is an incredible professor and person outside of class.
Not engaging, so many readings, and not considerate of AAC, this was the worst class Ive taken at UO so far :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor. Cares about her students

She is nice, but do not take this class for an easy A. There is tons of reading, many papers to write, and the midterm and final were EXTREMELY hard. Her canvas is extremely confusing with different due dates for everything, plus her slideshows are hard to follow. You're expected to be an art history genius prior, so it's hard to learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Terrible class and unfair expectations of her students. You are expected to use the slideshows to study for exams (which have questions about terms time periods etc.) and the slideshows only have pictures of artworks and the dates they were created. She switched the date of the final the night before it was originally going to happen for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ehrlich is a nice person but doesn't really teach, just puts pictures on a screen and expects you to know everything. Plus, LOTS of reading. Which leads to lots of papers to write, which are the only assignments you do in that class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Victoria is super nice but this survey class is way harder than it should be. GE's expect you to know this that they have been studying for years. The class is hard to follow sometimes and then lectures are hard to keep engaged in. Tests were hard and too hard to study for. Don't take for an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Ehrlich! Her lectures are interesting and engaging and a little bit of participation in her class goes a long way. As long as you share your opinion even a little she'll love you. The topics were super interesting, and her grading is super fair. Definitely an underrated professor and her classes are definitely worth taking.

This class is very reading and writing heavy and it is made even more difficult due to a poor canvas setup. Due dates are at odd times of the week and you have to dig through canvas to find info about them. I would not recommend this class unless you have prior knowledge about medieval art or are great at memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class is full of boring and confusing lectures. Get ready to memorize everything on the slides (with only photos and minimal notes to guide you) in order to pass exams. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class takes all of the fun out of art by making students write like 8 papers on art throughout the term. If you dont like writing essays, do not take this class. This class feels like its going at a faster pace than it should be. Dont take it if your looking for a easy A. Also the way the professor organizes her canvas page is confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures were always interesting. Very enjoyable course, you will actually like the readings. Tests are tough so take time to review and take good notes in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BA169 is my favorite class I've ever taken. Erik was an excellent teacher who definitely cared about everyone who was there and made sure the concepts of the class were drilled down so everybody understood.

I absolutely loved having Erik Ford as my professor this term, he is incredibly caring and amazing at teaching. You can tell he really wants each and every student to succeed, and he's definitely been my favorite teacher so far at UO. I highly recommend taking his class.
You can tell professor Ford loves teaching. He is such a sweet guy, his class is very fun and easy material as well as grading standards.
Ba169 was one of my favorite classes.
Erik the goat

Class was easy if you did the weekly work, which didn't always need to be done in class. He didn't care how you did your work as long as it was done, and the class was very clearly organized. Very easy to keep up with and fairly engaging if you did go to classes in person. Attendance was through a form posted online at end of class every day.

The man, the myth, the legend. Erik Ford. Somehow turns a normal class into a full-blown experience. You walk in thinking it's just another day, and leave like you just witnessed something. Keeps everyone awake, on their toes, and occasionally questioning reality. 10/10 would take again

Passionate and caring professor. Very clear that he wanted students to succeed. A bit on the higher end in terms of workload, but if you attempt almost all assignments it is an easy pass. 100% recommend.

Even though this class was online, you still can feel just how caring and invested Erik is in your success. Definitely plan on taking more business classes with him in the future. Not really much else I can say, he's every bit as good as people say.
Called the goat for a reason. He's so nice and so clearly cares about all of his students.
Eugene is nicknamed the Big E because Erik Ford resides here. G.O.A.T.
Live, Laugh, Love Erik Ford.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, class was pass/no pass, and with it being pretty easy made it a low cortisol experience.
We need a statue of this guy on campus.
Genuinely great professor, will answer all your questions as best as he can

The class was taken as pass or no pass and it is very easy to pass. The only reason I rated the difficulty as a 2 was because there is a good amount of work that you have to do each week. If you can focus for 1.5-2 hours twice a week for the online lectures than you will definitely pass. Overall, he's a very good professor and I would recommend.

Really enthusiastic professor and you can tell he genuinely enjoys teaching. Nice guy and the class is super easy, a fair amount of work but not difficult if you pay attention in class. Major con for me: he preaches AI usage every class and even tells us to use it sometimes for assignments which felt unproductive.
This guy is seriously the GOAT. Online class but felt his awesomeness through the screen. Class and content was pretty chill also.
Awesome guy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Erik Ford has been my favorite professor so far as a second-term freshman. He clearly enjoys teaching this class and wants students to be prepared for the future both at UO and outwards. Lovely guy to listen during lectures (though he will remind you to pay attention), and the most organized coursework and Canvas page I have ever used. G.O.A.T.

Literally the goat for a reason. I really enjoyed his lectures. McGraw-Hill and MikesBikes rounds due the days you had class (11:59pm), but not the worst thing. He's very clear and helpful if you have questions. Physical iClicker + McGraw-Hill textbook and MikesBikes bundle needed. Truly recommend him!
He is so chill and always ends class early!
what a god

Erik is a great professor; he is super passionate about business. There are weekly homework assignments, including MikesBikes and Connect. He gives study tips and is pretty straightforward about what will be on the test. I've never taken notes; I just make quizlets off of his class slides, and I've gotten A's on every midterm. Small class curve
Goat. An awesome class and professor, made me consider switching majors. Perfectly structured online course and perfect amount of work.
Super fun dude, loves what he teaches, gotta be at lecture but he makes it fun

I came into this class thinking everyone was glazing him, but now I've joined them. When I tell you he is the BEST professor, I mean it. You can tell her truly cares about his students and their success. His lectures are great, I look forward to class each week. Class is chill and easy, but Ford really makes it so special. I LOVE HIM and that's all

How do we clone Erik Ford to fill up the entire business department with him? He is the best professor I've had. He gets me pumped up to do the most mundane tasks because he's so full of energy and spirit. If you read the whole book chapters, not just the highlighted portions, it should be a pretty easy A too. Tests were generally fair.
THE GOAT, best teacher I have ever had. I was always excited for class.

As long as you attend class, do the homework, and do decent on your labs, you'll have an amazing grade in this class. For BA169z (formerly known as BA240), the class will be pass/fail, and you only need an 82 or above to pass, so it is super doable. Just lecture-heavy and homework-heavy.
GOAT. Same class as BA240 just renamed. Great professor, super knowledgeable class is easy and super useful and helpful. He is always available and wants to see his students succeed.

Erik Ford is the GOAT for a reason. I took his BA 101Z class online this term and he was an absolute gem to work with. The lectures are interesting and he is very knowledgeable. He is easily reachable outside of class and always has a smile on his face when talking to you! If you can, take one of his classes. Doesn't matter if it is online or not.
Such a good lecturer really cares, homework after each class but it's so easy if you go to class and do all the demos!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The online course is easy, as long as you follow the videos. He talks kind of slowly so I recommend to put the speed on the videos to 2x to speed up the assignments. There are about three big assignments each week that take an hour each and then an "exam" each week. But the exam is almost easier than the homework. Also a career fundamentals class.

THE ONLINE CLASS HAS 3 IN PERSON PROCTORED EXAMS AT THE UNIVERSITIES TESTING CENTER. The average score in each one of the exams was around 70%. Prof Ford is an excellent hilarious guy but some of the material on the exams made little to no sense. However at the end of the term he boosted everyone's grade by 5%
He's super chill, works through each formula step-by-step, and honestly I'd take the class again for fun!

loved this class so much. definitely was time consuming, 4ish hours a week on projects and homework. he makes it super easy to understand and is super easy to reach out to if you need any help. overall best class ive taken so far at UO

I have never had a professor at the university of Oregon better than Erik Ford. He genuinly cares so much about your well being and success in his classes. Not only that, but he's an amazing lecturer, super passionate, energetic, and engaging! Highly recommend any class you can take with him, you'll remember it forever.
Lectures super clear but often get very repetitive. Very good lecturer but if you understand the material then can get boring. Easy A if you focus and pay attention.
best professor ever. i loved this class and the material and everything was super clear.

The goat. Everyone loves him for a reason, 2nd business class i've taken with him this year and such a fan. I preferred taking BA240 online, made it more simple to follow in my personal opinion. Easy class, P/NP so just do the work and you're fine. Can sometimes pile up and be a lot but get ahead and just do it and you'll be fine.

Content was really interesting and he obviously cares about his students a lot. Only needed to contact him one time outside of class, and he was very helpful and responded quickly. Lots of hands on work for a non-graded class, but all useful and relevant.
Truly the goat. Easy, monotonous class made not boring by Erik Ford himself. The career aspects are helpful too. Passed easily
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took his online class, easy to do at my own pace and still know the information. Lots of lecture videos but they are all at the most 10-12 minutes long with short and easy quizzes after each one.
Still the Goat. Couldn't explain the class any better. Pass/No Pass class you would have to try to fail.

Erik ford is the best. BA 240 online is so easy to follow and he makes it his priority to make sure you pass his class. Even though there are exams every week he prepares you extra well and is hilarious during his lectures. Highly recommend.
