reviews.comment:
I think the biggest drawback to MTH252 is the assignments. The Achieve & Recitation have virtually no connection to tests or in-class work. Idk a single person who doesn't chatgpt the entire thing.

As for Prof Gyde, she's nice, but definitely on the spectrum (like most profs). Her work is sloppy and after a couple weeks I stopped going to lecture.

Nina is very kind, but in all honesty I do not believe her strengths stand in being a math professor. She often has been unsure of the processes she was actively teaching us and has several times given incorrect answers during in class lectures. If you have the choice, I don't recommend taking a course with her, though I will say she is very sweet.

Awful professor, a huge class and yet doesn't use the microphone provided with the classroom, if you're in the back of the class just leave the classroom you won't be able to understand a single thing she says, awful teaching and doesn't even know the answers to the questions most of the time and awful management during exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I cannot express how awful this professor is in words, they do not exist .This professor should not under any circumstances ever teach any math class again, she seems to have a tentative grasp of math itself. I'll list the bads, doesn't understand what she teaches, doesn't know the curriculum, can't teach or answer questions. Avoid this trainwreck!

Worst class Ive ever taken. Do not expect to learn anything in lectures. You will just sit and watch 4-6 problems get done over an hour by someone who does not seem like they know what they're doing. Don't expect to get clear answers about questions or have any idea what will be on tests. You will be on your own.

I'm 5 weeks in and HAD to warn u guys. Unless u love a self-guided learning journey do NOT take this class. I'm studying 3 hours/day. She acts like she doesn't know what she's teaching, ends every sentence with "i don't know," + forgets her materials @ home. So unorganized. I stopped going to class and am somehow doing BETTER on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is one of the worst professors I've ever taken. Be ready to teach yourself the material and fake it till you make it. SO much busy work that contributes absolutely nothing to your learning. I wanted to drop the class but she is the only professor that teaches this course for ecampus so I'm just SOL, but if you have a choice go to ANYONE ELSE.

She is completely absent! Does not answer questions, no clear guidelines. I'm a 3.9 GPA junior and after the first 2 weeks with this professor, I dropped so I can take this class with basically anyone else. Deadlines are wrong so 30+people are late on discussion posts because Canvas says one thing and the text says something else. Horrible 0/10.
Brace yourself for a self-guided learning experience as you take on the role of your own educator.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! If you have to take a math, make sure it is NOT with Nina Gyde. She would straight up admit to not knowing the material in class. Her slides if you miss lecture were NOT helpful and gave no answers to the practice problems. I had to learn the material on my own time and STRUGGLED.
worst professor ever. "flipped classroom" is complete hooey and you will learn nothing from her.

If you want to actually be taught don't take her. If you like it when teachers use their class time to teach, don't take her. If you have any difficulties with math this is not the class for you. However, if you know everything already it should be a breeze. If you don't, you are simply on your own.

The class started with a video saying the class would be a flipped classroom because "data shows students learned better and scores improve." That data may be true if it were being implemented correctly. Students must rely on a TA to find some material. The instructor is misguided. I can't believe I paid for this. Take the class elsewhere!

Nina was an okay professor. The content was difficult and the lectures were boring. The in-class problems were hard to follow as the professor kept changing how you solve the problem. The TA was great and I learned more form him then I did the actual professor.

Nina Gyde was okay; she made many mistakes in her math skills and seemed to always make the math seem harder than it actually was. I have taken this course in high school before so I knew the math but if I have never taken this course before it would be quite difficult.
Nina is mediocre at best. The class seems to lag behind whenever she lectures. Practice problems during class are not applicable to test material.

I'm not a fan of math, but have always done well in it (A's 110 and 111) and I barely passed this one. Her class was hard to follow in lecture, even harder to get help and near impossible to succeed in. I would assume it was own issue, but most of the class struggled as well. Try a different professor if you can or be prepared to pay for tutoring.
plain and simply just and aweful teacher

I was extremely disappointed with this professor. Her class was hard to get an A in simply because of her inability to give real help and lack of understanding for students needs. I got the impression she simply didn't care about any of her students learning or succeeding. Math is a beneficial subject, but try not to take her class!!!

She had clear notes and they helped with the homework and quizzes, but I spend most of the time questioning whether my success was from her or from taking calculus in high school the year before because most of the people in class were failing. If you don't understand the material from the lecture then you're screwed. Not helpful with specific ?'s.

Worst math teacher ever. I thought my high school math teacher was a joke until I took a class with her.... Does not teach at all. Does not help at all. And is a useless waste of my time, no point in attending class. USELESS. DO NOT TAKE her class. What are you thinking? Perhaps, "she cannot be that bad...". Let me just say this, you are WRONG.

Gyde is the worst teacher I have ever had. It is so sad that the university hired someone so unbelievably bad at teaching. After this teacher i have a somewhat negative outlook at the university for letting us students waste our money on such a waste of time. Do whatever it takes to not get this "teacher", youd be better off learning from your dog.
umm let me just say that i hate this ****ing teacher. she is useless and teach for herself, to make herself feel good. she doesn't care about how her students are doing at all.

Failed this class, and I am actually good at math. Not willing to help, when you go in for office hours... only gives you the first step at most of how to do a problem if you need help. Overall, nice person, but i feel like she wants you to fail. Out of a class of 40... only about 10 showed for the final. Take from another professor if possible!
I really believe she does not care for her students at all, if you start doing poorly in class, don't expect her to help you do any better. Her grading criteria is very poor and unreasonable.

Very unclear, does not care if you pass or not, gives recommended problems from book and makes them all even problems so you cant check your answers even tho your not turning them in. does not grade on a curve. does not answer questions clearly, she wants you to fail the most failed class at oregon
Not clear, unwilling to help students, do not recommend this teacher.
a lot of homework in math95
No Comments

She is a wonderful professor and cares about her students very much. This class is very heavy on group work but the assignments aren't very difficult. Her lectures are engaging and she includes a lot of discussion and student participation. If you go to class and pay attention you will likely do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very heavy on group work and there are a few assignments your team will have to do together. There are weekly quizzes but there are not many big assignments. Khonika is kind and funny, she values student success and wants to make the class fun and engaging for her students.

Great professor. Super funny and always brings energy to her lectures. Course content is extremely relevant and valuable. Group project is fun. Class is clearly meant to be enjoyable and informative, not to be a headache for her students.

Great business elective class if you're able to take it! Khonika is kind, funny, and values students being interactive during the course for participation. There is a fair amount of group work, so be prepared and okay with that, but it's not meant to be overly difficult.

Professor Gope is one of my favorite professors I have had here at UO, she is very kind to every student and wants to see everyone succeed. As long as you put in the work, you will succeed in this course.

She is a very good teacher and is funny but her grading structure is completely messed up and will leave you questioning what your true grade is. I have a B+ in the gradebook right now and she gave me a C as my final grade.

Fun class loved the jokes and team projects! That said, I didn't learn anything about entrepreneurship even with perfect attendance. The content was very basic, which was a bit disappointing given the cost of this university. Still, Gope is hilarious and made it an enjoyable experience!

This was one of the best electives I have ever taken! Prof Gope is kindhearted, humourous and highly knowledgeable about entreprenership. The class is always engaging and the projects are fun and useful! The instructions and grading criteria are clear and easy to folow. Her feedback is always useful for future improvements. Best prof at the UO!

Professor Khonika Gope is fantastic! Her Management 335 class is fun, engaging, and supportive. She cares deeply about her students and loves teaching. Attendance and participation are key, to sparking your interest in entrepreneurship. She's very nice and accommodating. Highly recommend!

Professor Gope is an extremely kind and encouraging instructor. She is extremely engaging and provides very thorough feedback on where you missed marks and what you did well. Through group projects and discussions you will learn a lot!

Professor Gope is one of the most engaging professors I have had. She consistently encourages the class and does NOT show favoritism towards any students. MGMT 335 is a group project centered course. Assignments are graded with some leniency but the criticisms given are always fair.

I would recommend fellow students to take this professor.

Wonderful professor one group project with side projects for basically the whole term. Makes the class fun and engaging. Has guest speakers. Overall fun class where you get to come up with a startup and see it come to life! 100/10 recommend!

Some of the new reviews are a bit biased. Prof. Gope directly called out her RMP and it got some help.

Class is heavy on reading and presentations. Grades are simple. Make sure to find a good group, otherwise, it will bite you in the ass later. Her cultural difference makes her indirectly funny and her personality will grow on you.

Recommended.
One of the best professors I have been able to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You never really know what to expect with Khonika's class, however, I am honored that I was able to take this entrepreneurship class with her and be one of her first students teaching in America. I received lots of insight into the world of entrepreneurship and starting a venture and loved this class. Be ready to participate in lectures.

Khonika is very intelligent and humorous. Lectures are packed with information but are often lighthearted. 10/10 would take this professor again! First class taught at UO and in the US and she was awesome!

One of the most unintentionally hilarious professors I've ever had. Super kind-hearted and happy to accommodate your needs. Class is pretty easy to earn a high grade and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a business elective
I thought Khonika was an excellent professor who made the class enjoyable and fun. The whole class is a group project, but the project is fun and enjoyable.

This class was very enjoyable, it was her first time ever teaching in the US and she made the class fun and engaging with her humor and teaching style. The class is one overall group project that is broken down into three short presentations. If you follow the rubrics and include everything she is looking for you will receive a good grade.
one of my favorite professors at the school. Prof. Gope made class enjoyable every day
Khonika was an incredible professor. She created a classroom environment that was enjoyable to be in day in day out. overall she has been one of my favorite professors at the school.

Very easy class that anyone could take in the business school for easy credit. She makes class enjoyable and is very funny. If you cannot take a joke then do not take this class. The project is very easy if you follow the guidelines I am normally a B student (3.17 GPA) and got an A.

Amazing class! She's so funny and engaging with the class. She cares about what she teaches and the students. I definitely recommend taking this class. In a genuine and truthful way, this class is great. Ignore the bad comments posted because they are not true.
Professor Gope is awesome. She tries super hard to connect to her students and always has very fun guest speakers or activities for the class.
Super nice lady, makes class fun and gives quality, meaningful feedback on your work. Genuinely one of the most enjoyable classes I've taken here and it was largely due to her teaching.
Great teacher very nice and very easy course
Great professor and very funny person. Class was very easy.

MGMT 335 was the best class that I have taken here. From the first day of lectures I knew that this class was going to be different. Prof Gope cultivated a community feeling in her class while still trying to push education and understanding. This class is heavily focused on group projects to push the importance of group diversity and collaboration

I have no clue why Khonika is getting all of this hate. She is a very nice person and wants to see you succeed. Although there are some cultural barriers and I think it was her first time teaching this course she did a really good job. Khonika is funny and lighthearted and keeps class entertaining and fun.
It's a conversational course which makes it very engaging. She makes the class enjoyable through the lectures and is an elementary grader. Would definitely take a class with her again
Class was actually super easy and fun. Easy grader so long as you show up and participate in class. Does make some questionable comments but class itself is easy.

I'm disappointed at the way this class is being taught. The in-class discussions do help your learning and participating is a big part of your grade. However, the directions for assignments are not clear and group projects are the main part of your grade. She also cuts people off when they raise their hand and doesn't validate your ideas.

FIN311 has long lectures and Garrett kept them very engaging. Lectures are not mandatory but you should go to them or you will fall behind. The curve was good and he gave out extra credit opportunities. In terms of difficulty, the course was not extremely difficult topics but you should be studying a good amount before the midterm and final.

Dude is amazing. Best lectures I've had besides Mary savage (the goat), and he's always trying to make it easier for students to understand the material. UO please pay this man. He gives a lot of good extra credit opportunities. Good curve and material on tests isn't out of left field. This guy actually cares about his students and their futures.
Garrett is an amazing professor and made this class as interesting as possible. He gives out a lot of extra credit over the year and cares about all of his students.
Goat teach

Garrett is an extremely kind and caring professor. Haven't ever had a professor as down to earth as him. Lectures are engaging and it seems like he genuinely cares about each student. Come to class and you'll succeed. Easily my favorite teacher at UO. Cant recommend enough.
Very funny and down to earth guy. Lectures are engaging and hands on. Coursework is not hard at all if you come to class and participate. Would 1000% take again
The material for this class sucks but Garrett is a really good professor and takes notice if you go to class and try.

Garrett is the GOAT. FIN311 is the driest and most brutal material you could have to teach in the business school, and yet he makes it interesting and funny. The class is difficult and the material is dense, but Garrett is a good teacher who legit cares. ELECTRIC LECTURER + ABSOLUTE LEGEND.

(BA315) Garret is amazing, a deeply fun lecturer who makes boring content less boring. Go to class even though attendance isn't mandatory. Garret is a G. Go to class don't be a bot, pay attention and you'll enjoy him and the material.

(BA315) Garrett was wonderful. Class is lecture-based and a lot of content pretty quickly, so while attendance isn't technically mandatory, it'd be easy to fall behind. I really enjoyed the style of teaching; he's clear and gives good examples and answers questions in a very productive way. Also just very funny and makes long lectures interesting.

(FIN 311) Garrett is a great guy who cares deeply about economics and genuinely wants his students to succeed. The class itself is pretty difficult and requires a lot of extra practice and studying to master. Exams are 60% of your grade. He is always open to meeting with students to help them out and overall did a good job as a new professor.

Garrett has a great personality, but he tends to ramble a lot and doesn't get straight to the point. When explaining definitions there's always an easier way to explain it, but somehow he makes it harder to understand. The hw is lengthy but doable. The midterm and final is hard and can make a dent if you don't study well.

An extremely friendly person who is genuinely enthusiastic about Environmental Economics. He helped me out all the time outside of class and is extremely approachable. The lectures were simple and relevant, and there were very few homeworks throughout the term. The overall grade is heavily determined by large projects and the midterm and final.

All the lectures provided were from his colleague and there's two websites for the homework. Only one extra credit assignment worth up to 10% of grade. Lectures were not helpful in exams and exams are proctored. I mainly learned from the homework and not the prof himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stanford is not yet a full-on professor, just something to keep in mind. Course is well-structured, workload was about right in my opinion. Coursework is relatively easy but tests were difficult and students tended to score somewhat poorly. Textbook was easier to learn from than lectures. Discussion sections were not helpful.

This class is pass/no pass, it just wasn't an option so I selected A. (I passed). Easy class, homework is light. She clearly cares and if you simply talk to her she will be flexible with scheduling/due dates. Rubrics are clear, like extremely clear. She will catch you on the small details, but its also mentioned in the rubric. Gives good feedback.

I took this two credit class and it was honestly so much work. Not a full prof, but acts like her class is the most important in your schedule. Her favorite phrase is 'you risk a no pass!', which she said in an email to me after the term was over, forcing me to resubmit an assignment over break (the only thing wrong was header font sizes).

Professor Gatlin loves PPPM so much, and she provides her students with important resources. There was a lot of valuable knowledge gained from this class, but the guidance and advice she gives can feel condescending at times. She has high expectations and enforces them clearly.
Really good at teaching this course and supporting students. Great office hours, was a super helpful class.

This lady has consistently prayed on my downfall for so long. She threatened to fail me for submitting an assignment with double spacing instead of 1.25 spacing on the part where I write my name and date on a rough draft assignment unless I changed it that day. That is just one of many examples, other ones being worse. She makes it hard to succeed.
Katie is lovely! She's cares about her students a lot, and she is super supportive! She is a pretty slow grader, but she's fair. Assignments are pretty straight forward.

She is so bubbly and so energetic. Very caring PPPM professor but kinda extra with assignments. She cares about students and LOVES PPPM, and she really wants everyone to succeed. Attendance is mandatory, slow grader, and you have to make appointments for office hours.
Relatively easy class, but she's a really slow grader and requires you to read a book as part of a book club which was difficult if you have a lot of classes. Lectures can be boring.

The class material itself was interesting, but we had so many readings, and ig its fine, but we would never really have a good discussion in classes, we would just read in class instead of discussing. We had to do like 7 essays, and it would have been helpful if he had graded and given us feedback, but he never did. He only graded the first one
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Pedro is the kind of professor you take once and wonder if it was worth it. So far, we've read so many secondary sources that my brain starts to turn to mush, and half of the time, we never discuss them. Please beware of the lack of organization in this course. If you cannot time manage, DO NOT GO HERE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'll start by saying this course was three hours long, once a week. I can tell Pedro has a kind heart, but he was not organized with Canvas until at least week 3. There are a lot of readings outside of class though, so come prepared. The one thing he does value a lot is student feedback- especially after class if you don't understand concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pedro is extremely knowledgable on the topic but it seems like he comes to class with absolutely no plan of what he's going to lecture about. He doesn't use a Powerpoint most of the time so his lecturing is often hard to follow. Students will try to speak in class, but he will take what they are saying and go on a ten minute tangent.

Pedro Garcia is an amazing person. Pedro doesn't believe in late homework, however, what does that teach me? I don't have self-discipline. He's truly amazing, there have been moments when I would stay after class and speak more about the class discussion we had. Although there were papers and many readings, I enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor is very knowledgable on the topic of Latin American studies, and easy to connect with (especially helpful while learning online). If you have a genuine interest and passion for the study of Latin America, this is the class for you. Be prepared to read a lot, think deeply, and actually learn.

Pedro is deeply knowledgeable in his field. However, that does not make him a good teacher. He lacks organizational skills. He does not follow his own syllabus. Assignments are frequently posted last-minute. Some readings are never posted at all. I liked him as a person, but as a professor, he was deeply frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Pedro is an expert on Latin America. He's always willing to help students and gives good feedback on essays. There are tons of readings and films outside of class; class time is lecture. You must do readings, watch films, and take notes to succeed. This class was much work but I'm glad I took it; I'm better at essays, researching, and learned lots.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable about the material, and really helpful in office hours (I'd recommend going even if you're a good writer just to get more bibliographic ideas). It's true that he sent out some assignments at the last minute, and he can seem intimidating, but I think he appreciates it when you at least try to participate and seem engaged.

Pedro is very knowledgeable and highly qualified. However, he is arrogant and often assigns last minute things (ie an email at 10pm telling you do an assignment for the next morning). He can also be condescending. He might be better for a smaller class, but I did not like him for a lecture.

His accent is very clear, and is pretty nice. Very well-spoken and professional. The class is pretty tough, although most survey courses are. There are a lot of readings, some very hard to comprehend. Participation/attendance is mandatory to pass.

Other teachers should use Pedro as an example.  His class is challenging and highly interesting and that is how a college course should be.  Most people who do not like them feel so because they were unable to keep up.  If you are interested in actually learning Spanish and Latin American history, he is the man for the job.

Pedro is a really nice guy. He's funny, super knowledgable about his subjects and his lectures are interesting. He's a fair grader and is willing to help any way, he even changed a reading assignment to match student interest! All in all a really good class. There IS a lot of reading, but it's not hard reading and he does go over it in detail.
Insane amount of reading, but you can get by skimming it--he goes over most of the important parts. A lot of work, but he's not a very hard grader.

Pedro is a good teacher. It's a lot of material in a lot of time, but I figure many people that have trouble in this class shouldn't be studying a foreign language, anyway. Pedro will, on occasion, throw in a dirty joke here and there when he thinks no one is listening (and few are). I'd recommend this class to a competent person.

Pedro is amazingly knowledgeable and expects a great deal from students, so those who do not have a proficient level of Spanish should take other courses first. However, he is amazing. I learned so much about myself as a part of a repressed culture and also about other subaltern cultures from him. One critique is that he is sometimes unorganized.
I don't understand why he got into teaching when he is terrible.

Pedro doesn't answer emails. He gives us a syllabus with assignments but then when we get to class the assignment that was assigned wasn't what we were supposed to do. He's really knowledgable about the subject, but seems to think students are on the same level as him which makes it ridiculously hard for everyone in the class.
Great Teacher. Extremely knowledgeable and in-depth in his teaching. Likes to slip in jokes when no one is listening. Pretty fair grader too.

He is a very intelligent and inspiring teacher. His knowledge about the subject is AMAZING! However, be prepared to do an immense amount of reading and writing in his class. You would definitely be challenged!

This class was only graded by three assignments. The day one of the assignments was due my family member passed away. She agreed to give me an extension, but when the assignment was graded she marked me down for being late, even though she agreed to give me the extension. Her class was disorganized and her videos had such bad sound quality
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have such mixed emotions about this class! The topics were relevant, and Nathalia is a super knowledgeable and caring professor. However, it was PAINFULLY disorganized--we were given the most confusing & broad instructions for exams and homework (which would be up to 40 pages of reading). Your entire grade is based only on 3 exams & attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hernandez-Vidal is amazing! Take her class.
I love her dearly. Taught important topics and was super understanding and flexible with students. Took her twice and wasn't even a sociology major. Importante en la comunidad latina.

Professor Nathalia implied that attendance would not be mandatory for the class on the first day. It is mandatory. There is no way to make up for a missed in-class assignment, which is all of the assignments. The class itself is relatively easy, but the professor can be difficult to understand and tends to ramble. I wouldn't recommend.

She is very helpful teacher, and gives out lecture guides to fill in every unit to ensure you can easily follow along with the work she is doing on the board. She is a tough grader (I never got an assignment that didn't get a point taken off), and there is a lot of homework. Overall, she is very helpful and I would recommend taking a class with her

Nice professor and she teaches really organized and at a nice pace. If you have questions she'll answer and really make sure you understand. Homework was a little tedious ngl but other than that pretty good! She also drops lowest quiz, hw, and if u do better on final she'll replace a bad midterm grade

Super fast paced class that relies on skills from lower level courses, weekly quizzes, she does give partial credit when grading but doesn't do a good job leaving feedback at all. No curve on any exams or grades, and multiple be assignments every week. Overall work heavy and test heavy, with a lot of assignments and 3 exams. She was just okay.

I used to love math and through some of the professors I've experienced at UO I began to hate it, but Prof Fisher actually lectures in a way that I can understand. She considers explaining even the things most people would know but I love that. I hadn't taken math in about 2 years, but I was able to learn everything I missed in 2 weeks bc of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the best math profs Ive had. Lectures are fast and sometimes hard to follow if you get lost, but ask questions and she will help. Ive always had a hard time in math but the way she taught made it easy to understand.
Recommend not skipping the class, I missed some days, and it was hard to catch up on. But go to her office hours because that really helped.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the best math teacher ive had. Practice test are very simliar to the real midterm, and expect quiz weekly/hw/webwork. But overall pretty chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Fisher is very kind, but the class itself has flaws. The class is very test heavy, midterms worth 40% and final worth 30%, everything else is homework and quizzes. She does not post lectures, slides, or notes after class so you need to show up or else you are screwed. She is hard to follow along with and went fast in lecture, very hard class.
Cassandra took the time to make sure her students understood the material. I was nervous about the material at first, but she explained it very well. Overall, I would take her class again.

she is amazing i love her! super caring and helpful, easy to reach outside of class, and her lectures actually make sense. first math class ive enjoyed since middle school and i feel like im actually learning/understanding content. weekly homework/worksheets/quizzes but they arent hard and you get a notecard for tests/exams

Cassandra was amazing, she was caring and always explained topics well, especially if there were questions. There where 2 midterms and a final with weekly quizzes on Friday. Attendance is not mandatory Mon-wed but is on Friday, go to class -she does not post notes or lectures. Overall, I really enjoyed this class because of her teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ms. Fisher is very nice and helpful but pretty sure she is a Trump supporter

Prof Fisher was one of the best professors I've had at the UO. Expect a weekly, one-page quiz and weekly homework assignments. Prof. Fisher is very understanding and easy to talk to, and is very fair in giving partial credit on quizzes/ exams. As long as you put in effort and attend lectures, you'll be fine.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, one of the WORST profs I've ever had. I did good on the homework assignments but her quizzes and exams are an actual joke, final exam was a literal joke. Went to her office hours, she was so rude and passive aggressive. She WILL mark you down for the smallest mistakes and not say why. Retaking this class, but NOT with her.

I really liked her as well as this class, as long as you go to class you will be good. She explains things well and clearly and gives out extra credit everyday in class with the iclicker. Attendance is graded, but if you get the extra credit points it covers you.

this professor grades very hard, she marks you down many points for one mistake. She makes the quizzes very heavily affect to your grade. She also isn't very helpful when asking questions. She did about 14 units in 10 weeks, that's less than a week to even learn an entirely new topic which is nearly impossible.

While very math-savvy, Prof. Fisher often comes across as rude and tends to talk down to students. I would not have passed this class if not for my WONDERFUL GE and Class Encore leader who helped me understand the material instead of just reading it to me and solving it in class. Overall a very frustrating experience and I am glad it's over.
As long as you show up to office hours and take notes in class, you will do fine.

If you show up to lectures and try to learn you'll do great in Business Calc. It's not a crazy class and I was pretty nervous going into it. Fisher's lectures are super clear and break things down really nicely. Just don't miss class or you'll fall behind. Also go to tutoring and office hours as soon as you need help cause stuff piles up fast.

I would generally say every criterion matches to be an adequate professor. The course is formatted similarly to every math class I've previously taken, just at a bigger scale. I think it's just a basic math class, just like every other math class, so everything is fair.

Professor Fisher was great at explaining the content; however, the exams were way more difficult than exams of previous 241 classes. Attendance is required with iclicker questions and exam reviews tend to be way easier than the actual exams.

Such a difficult teacher, did not at all make lectures engaging and would get incredibly frustrated if someone just as much coughed during lecture. She seemed to hate her job and take it out on us, could not finish out the term with her because of how unhelpful she was

You can't miss a single class if you want to be caught up, if you miss one you fall so far behind and it's hard to catch up. Study guides and other related materials do not prepare you for exams, which always seem to be made as hard as possible. The class average on the final was below a passing grade.

This class is not easy, but Cassandra explains everything so clearly! She talks to us like kindergarteners, but sometimes that's exactly what we need. If you don't have calc experience, you'll struggle. Pay attention in every lecture, ACTUALLY do the webwork/homework and this class will be a breeze. Sign up for encore if you can.
My experience in this class was very frustrating. Despite making every effort to do well (Go to class or you will not pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think she was generally a good professor, I just didn't have a good time because I don't enjoy math at all. She was very helpful throughout the term and I definitely would've gotten a worse grade if I had a different professor lol.

I love ms. Fisher. I had her for both trig and calc for the bio sciences 1 and i'm going to taker her next term for calc for the bio sciences 2. She is really helpful and approachable during office hours and she prints out worksheets and notes packets for you and gives them to you at the start of class so you are not on your own.

She was a great lecturer and really cared about your success in the class. Go to her office hours, it really helps and she is very helpful when she is able to help you. Grading is very clear; study well and pay good attention in class and you'll be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Truly enjoyed her math teaching. Very clear explanations and walks you through every step of the way! I LOVED her lecture guides; really were useful to have! Webwork and practice exams are usually tougher than the actual exam itself! Overall really loved her!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fisher made this class interesting; she always used real-life examples, which helped me keep focus. I would 100% recommend her as a math teacher.

Professor Fisher is a great, flexible professor if you prefer high-school-style classes. Color coding and all. Grading is fair and fast, awarding partial credit often. Weekly quizzes, 2 midterms, and 1 final, which can improve midterm scores. Homework roughly twice a week on webwork. She also gave the entire class a massive grade bump after finals.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fisher teaches lectures at a reasonable pace, notes are clear and easy to understand. I recommend printing out the lectures, making it easier to look back on. There are weekly homework assignments and a quiz at the end of the week. DO the practice reviews for exams plus you're allowed to have a notecard. Overall she's a great math professor!

Fisher teaches in very cryptic ways if you do not have access to a printer. Without her lecture guides in your hands, it can be difficult to understand the concepts. I took high-level math in high school and still had difficulty learning from her.

Professor Fisher lectures are clear, well spoken and taught at a reasonable pace. She teaches content in a digestible way making concepts clear and simple. She is kind and willing to help if reached out too. All assignments for this class are helpful in preparing you for the tests.

Casandra makes the lessons easier by writing in different colored pens, so you know how she did the problem. she has weekly quizzes on Fridays with her GEs, Joe was the best GE out of all of them. Her study guides for the midterms didn't match.

Professor Fisher is a great math teacher. If you go to class, take notes, and pay attention to the material, you should have no difficulty getting at least a B. She makes things almost too simple at times. Extra credit is possible through clicker questions.

Professor Fisher is a great math professor and someone who I hope to be in another class with. Her lectures are a little fast paced, but she is very willing to go back and repeat herself if needed. She is incredibly flexible and understanding, which is great for a student like me, who struggles with due dates and generally dislikes math. 5/5
Fisher is very straight forward with her teaching style and isn't afraid to go back and repeat herself when needed. Her guidelines of grading is also much more clear than most math classes.

I thought this class was easy and the lectures were clear. It's important to print her lecture guides to follow what she's doing in class, or through a tablet. Although I thought the class was easy, I know many students who struggled. I never went to her office hours but those who did said she was not very helpful.

Dr. Fisher is a great math professor! She made concepts super easy to understand and posted lecture guides (blank and fully filled out) on Canvas in case you miss class or need more time to focus on an example. I really like how she color-codes her work so you can see where she's getting all of her numbers from.
Professor Fisher was amazing! She is so sweet and this class is relatively easy. Consists of webwork assignments, 1 midterm and 1 final. She was an amazing teacher!

At first, I thought there was a lot of homework for this course, but the concepts were fairly easy to learn and the homework never took too long. She explained things in a way that made sense and posted the notes from lectures online.

Ms. Fisher was a great professor and her lectures were easy to understand. She provides lecture guides before class and posts all of her notes on canvas. You have 1-2 weekly homework assignments, 1 weekly discussion worksheet, weekly quizzes, 1 midterm and 1 final. She gives you more than enough time to complete all of it. She is the best!

Cassandra is such a smart, thoughtful instructor. She does not complicate things as much as it is said here. The things are helpful if you pay attention. I would not recommend skipping this class as you will miss A LOT of info and its difficult to catch back up. Her grading/assignments are very well organized and she was great at explaining math!

I'm seeing all of these poor reviews, but they seem to wrong! I'm someone who isn't really the smartest person, but this class felt fairly easy, as she explained everything thoroughly and well. Some reviews talk about how she complicates her lectures, but it's only to give the students a better understanding of the material. She's great!

I love her! She makes the class really easy and her teaching is very straightforward. Attendance in lectures is not mediatory but in discussions it is. Her tests are straightforward as well. She is easy to get a hold of and offers lots of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fisher is an excellent lecturer and a fair and considerate professor. Her office hours are extremely useful and I would definitely recommend going to them if you're at all having difficult with a topic. Her tests and quizzes are reasonable and she prepares us well for them, I would definitely recommend taking her.

Cassandra Fisher completely changed how I view calculus. I consistently got Ds on tests in high school and was crying over my homework each night. The way that she teaches the material just works so well for me. I got As on every test! It was insane how she managed to make such a difficult topic so approachable. Love u P. Fisher !

This was my first calc class ever and she helped make it less difficult as I had imagined. She gives a quiz and like 2 homework sets a week but it's webwork. Lectures could be better but at least she covers what's gonna be on the exam. Office hours were definitely beneficial but she treats you as if you were still in hs which is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Fisher offers a lot of extra credit for just participating with iClicker and she is great at explaining problems during the lecture slowly and thoroughly. Her course is structured very well and if you are willing to put in decent effort, I recommend taking this class.

she was an ok person, overcomplicates the lectures and uses iclickers to take attendance. she acted like a high school teacher though, as soon as people started talking she did the "ill wait" bit which was really annoying.
DROP THE CLASS PLEASE!!!!!!!!!

Fisher was a good professor. I think she overcomplicates things but overall is clear and thorough in her lectures. Weekly quizzes and homework were honestly good to keep me on track. reviews.comment: Good professor for lecturing, arguably goes too slow and sometimes overcomplicates/explains problems. Good teacher, very difficult course.

reviews.comment: WORST TEACHER EVER I was struggling with the class and sent a kind email to her asking where I could find resources to help. reviews.comment: I was afraid to take her class after seeing the reviews here, but after taking her class I can confidently say that the reviews are not at all similar to my experience. She explained everything thoroughly, was eager to help, and offered lots of extra credit. She made calculus feel easy. Only con - sometimes treats students like they are still in hs

Best math teacher I've had in years. Hard weekly quiz/Midterms killed my grade, but I honestly feel I learned a lot, Fisher truly cares about the good of the class. Her office hours are super helpful and she is always happy to give more problems/explanations. Recommend to anyone needing Calc. Take good notes her lectures are super helpful

This class is really easy and all review if you paid attention in high school math, but if you don't know your algebra you will struggle. Professor moves fast through content because it should all be review of high school algebra but very helpful and patient during office hours. Extra credit for attendance and drops low quizzes. Notecard for exam.

Cassandra was an amazing math teacher. I got a lower grade because I didn't apply myself as well as I should have but she is very concise with the way she explains concepts. She really wants you to do well and as far as math goes she is really great professor. If you want to do well in her class, if you apply yourself you will do great.

Calculus is definitely a tough subject but Professor Fisher made the material easy to understand and helped it seem very relevant to biological topics! reviews.comment: Professor Fisher grades incredibly rough and gives immense amounts of homework. Good luck with this professor.

I could probably learn more in an hour and twenty minutes of silence than I could in the hour and twenty minutes that I am stuck in the lecture hall during her lectures. She is genuinely one of the worst math professors I have ever had. She overcomplicates every topic and explains everything at a pace which makes it near impossible to keep up.

This is a hard class in general so I think she tries her best to make the material easy to understand. Her follow along notes help make lectures easy to follow. Calculus was so confusing for me in high school! I took Calculus for the Bio Sciences 246 and 247 with Prof. Fisher and she made calculus SO straightforward for me! Great teacher, shows respect for students, provides a manageable amount of work.

reviews.comment: Good teacher, notes were clear and easy to understand. She posts lecture guides after class so you dont have to pay a TON of attention in lecture.

If you are someone that struggles with math and are unable to teach it to yourself then I do not recommend Cassandra. She does the math examples during lecture but does not explain at all how or why it should be done that way. There are quizzes every week and no extra credit, retakes, or curve on test. Overall, not a good class.

Fisher is good, don't skip lectures or you won't understand what's going on, and don't be afraid to ask questions. Weekly homework packets and twice weekly WebWork. The weekly quizzes and packets aren't bad if you go to lecture, the webwork is challenging. I would recommend this class just make sure to not fall behind.

She takes her time in lecture to make sure the content is clear and understandable. You get extra credit when you get iClicker questions right, so make sure you pay attention and you'' do well in the class. Quizzes every week, but honestly they kept me on track to I didn't mind them.

If you can teach yourself math or math comes easy this class will be fine. But if your someone who struggles with math and or needs extra help I would not take this class. No extra credit, no retakes, very strict, and lack of care for students.

Professor Fisher is one of my favorite professors this term. She is really understanding about make ups and she is good at explaining the content. Sometimes the textbook homework is a lot more difficult than what we do in class but if you go to office hours she explains it well and helps walk you through it.

Her organization is all over the place. Wayyyy too much work and she doesn't give you enough time to process it. Find a new professor if you can. You'll learn much more from Khan Academy than you will from her.

Cassie was my favorite professor this term. She's clear about her expectations and directions. She's very clear on her explanations of problems and leaves a lot of class for if you have questions. Cassandra is a very nice woman who does a good job of explaining the content. Not her fault math is the worst. She does a really nice printed note format that is extremely organized, helpful, and easy to follow along to.

gives clicker extra credit for getting all the questions right in class. math homework takes about 3 hours every time due to different terminology and some stuff not being taught in class. kinda mean to be honest. felt a little dumb sometimes. sometimes felt like she was talking to me as if i was in 2nd grade but she is def a greatlecturer

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Clear requirements. Better than the other professor for math 246.

reviews.comment: Cassandra has been my favorite math teacher/professor I've had. She can be a tough grader on some things, but she makes math really clear. I like her note style a lot and she's easy to reach out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fisher takes the complexities of calculus and makes it easy to understand. I've never her seen her have a bad day, and she's always ready to help (i.e. doing homework questions at the beginning of class). She is very welcoming and I was never afraid to talk to her. There were quizzes each week but they made it easy to understand the material.
Professor Fisher is a great teacher. She explains content thoroughly and gives lots of examples. She is easier to understand and seems caring. I'm math challenged and I was able to pass her class.

There are only 2 tests and both are worth 35% of your grade. There is weekly homework that is due during discussion but there isn't much of an option to get help with it. It was very frustrating going to office hours and not getting the help that I so desperately needed. Overall the material makes since, but you need to go to class in order to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She doesn't let you have note cards for any of her exams or her midterms so expect to memorize a lot of calculus stuff.

Cassandra is a good math teacher but she isn't really good at working with students. Our HW is assigned on Monday around 2 pm, and it's due Thursday at 12pm, which means we rush through it. She isn't flexible with it either. Not having HW on the weekends sucks. She also assigns lots of even numbers which means you can't check your answers.

She grades hard and off of weird unnecessary criteria. Example: if you are given an equation where you have to simplify, put f(x) in-front of every step because you're going to be marked down 50% on that question even if you did everything right. She marks off a ton if you do something correctly but not the way she wanted even if she didn't say so.
One of the better math professors Ive had. They were able to explain things very well on a one on one level when I went to office hours. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's alright but unless you know how to read math through the textbooks its hard to get help for her class. She doesn't curve grades so what ever you get is what you get. She is helpful during office hours and is very respectful and kind. Not entirely clear on how she gets her answers (this is subject to whoever is taking her class though
She has a way of teaching that makes everything really understandable. Really takes the time to make sure that everyone is understanding the material. She was my favorite professor.

Expect lots of homework and quizzes weekly. Despite large homework load I would recommend her simply because she is a really good teacher. You might have to spend more time on the class with her as the teacher but you'll leave it extremely knowledgeable.
really clear communication.

Professor Fisher is the best math instructor I have had in college. This course was extremely organized and her instructing pace never felt rushed nor slow. She makes an effort to know each of her 150 students understand. Tests were reasonably hard, but she allows a half sheet of notes. Wish I could take her for 106.

I took Cassandra Fisher this summer ('15) for Math 105 and she absolutely made my summer term. I struggle with math but she somehow she laid it out there and made it so simple. I have an 85% going into the final and this is my first math class at a university. She expects HW but its due the exact same day each week. TAKE CASSANDRA FISHER FOR MATH!!

She is a horrible speaker and talks to you like she's hosting a game show and it is the weirdest thing. The examples she does in class are pretty easy but then the worksheets, quizzestests and homework are a lot more difficult. She also assigns a lot of online homework which is frustrating.

Great prof. Prof. Hopkins is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, and that motivated me to do well in this course. Tough course, very lecture heavy. Honestly a miracle I came out with an A. Definitely would take classes with this professor again

Professor Hopkin's lectures are boring and hard to follow, and paired with unhelpful assignments to be completed in the ladder half of class. Most of the class is rogue memorization, the GEs are smart but clearly not given info pre-class, and Professor Hopkin's answers to questions were unhelpful.

This class is unrealistic. The in-class mandatory assignments barely connect to anything you are tested on and are on the tail-end of an hour long of straight lecture at you. This class would be far better if the concepts were usefully connected and not just straight memorization of terms.

Before this class, I thought I was interested in paleontology, but not anymore. The lectures are hard to follow, sporadic, and boring. Attendance is graded with bad assignments, with terribly written questions and multiple pages; half the class would never finish on time. No study guides, cumulative exams, GE's have no idea what's going on.

Professor Hopkins clearly cares about the topic, but the organization of the class doesn't work. You work in groups, and her answers to any questions are unclear and difficult to understand, along with GEs who seem just as confused as the students at times. The lectures are boring and difficult to pay attention to.
She is very disorganized. Never replies to your emails. She plays favorites.
Hopkins clearly cares about teaching and her students but she is definitely one of the toughest graders I've had, and majority of my grade was determined by a few essays. Also, participation matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really like Hopkins as a person, but wow-- she literally never grades anything. Nothing but three reading quizzes were graded until the end of week 10 (we took quizzes every day). This was hugely disappointing because she expected a lot out of us (including peer-grading) but never graded anything herself. It was extremely stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite teacher at the UO/CHC. Clearly passionate about student success, very knowledgeable, very down-to-earth and approachable. She has high expectations but is very clear about what you need to do to meet them, and often it isn't hard to rise to the occasion because she gives you all the necessary tools to do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Hopkins is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She's tough, and she makes you work your butt off, but you learn a lot and really respect her for it. I would totally take her class again, just because I got so much out of it. You learn something, and it's not an easy A, but it's totally worth it.
Sometimes gets behind on grading, but she's willing to admit it.

William is a very good professor. He is engaging in class, and happy to discuss assignments or concepts further outside of class. He can be a bit hard to reach by email sometimes, but he would always get back to me eventually. Participate in class and he will like you.

William is a great guy at heart, but with his unorganized lectures and heavy African accent, it's hard to comprehend really anything he teaches. Most students were playing games or scrolling in his class. He has readings, lecture slides, and a midterm/final that are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: William is one of my favorite professors I've taken in my two years at this school! He is such an interesting person and is able to use his own life story in relation to global development. All exams and papers in class are fairly easy, and attendance is not mandatory, but he refuses to post slides, so be wary!

This class is very interesting, and he is kind but isn't organized. Homework is readings or documentaries with weekly and unit quizzes. Attendance not mandatory but no lecture slides posted. A lot of the options on the quizzes are very similar so it can get confusing. Have to submit final paper outline too early on, in the first few weeks.

This class is definitely lecture heavy but he makes it interesting. Theres new subjects with readings and quizzes each week but its easy. Although attendance is not mandatory if you dont come to class he will not post the lecture slides so go at your own risk. He is very accessible and so sweet!
He's super sweet and willing to give extensions if needed. Only have to do weeekly quizzes on the lectures and write three papers. It's the easiest class I've taken so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material was interesting to learn, I personally enjoyed it. Yes, there are a lot of readings, but It's a Global Studies class, so that's to be expected. There are weekly quizzes, but they are not bad at all. Just show up, do your work, pay attention and you will be just fine!

I know that this is William's second term at UO, but wow, he is a bad professor. The lectures are unorganized and mostly consist of him just reading off the slides verbatim/showing us YouTube videos, and the quizzes are all on Canvas and lazy. The paper assignments also make no sense. Easy A, but don't expect anything else from GLBL 101 or William.

He'll test you every week, but the answers to the test wont be correct. It'll be correct based off of someone's experiences or one of the 30 weekly readings. I dean needs to audit this class, its terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It is very hard to be engaged in this class. It is extremely lecture heavy and the lectures consist of the professor reading off of the slides. The slides have entire paragraphs of information on them that students are then expected to remember for the weekly and unit quizzes. The slides are also not posted on canvas making it more difficult.
I think reading a book thats upside down in a foreign language would make more sense than this class and its assignments

Joseph is a great professor. He is very knowledgeable and straight forward. It is only graded by two exams and case summaries, but he does offer extra credit. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't go to class you will likely get lost. I found the content very engaging and easy to follow along with.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joseph is such an amazing professor! Lecture topics always super interesting. Does cold call but goes off a list so you know what day you will be called on. Case load kind of heavy first 6 weeks but all the work is easy. Midterm and Final both graded on slight curve and offers extra credit to boost grade up a letter (A to A+, B- to B, etc.).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very informational and passionate about the law, and allows gives room for discussion and opinions in class. homework consists of case studys before each class, and a midterm and final, so pretty laid back if you can be organized. He does cold call so be prepared with course material

Amazing teacher, knows exactly what he is talking about. You will succeed if you go to class and do the homework. He cold calls, super helpful for anyone looking at law school but can be intimidating to be called on in class.
One of my favorite professors, went into a lot the practical side of criminal investigations from the DOJ side.
such a fun and cool class.
Chill guy, hard tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's such a great professor and knows so much about his profession. Case heavy but only for a couple of week, but he mainly wants you to focus on application and understanding rules. Not a harsh grader at all, but don't take advantage of the non-mandatory class attendance, you can get lost easy.

Professor Huynh is an amazing professor. Lectures are two hours, and they usually contain a guest speaker. All of the speakers have experience relating to criminal investigation and are very interesting. Beginning half of the class is contains homework that does require time/effort, but later half of the class has no homework which is super nice.

Professor Huynh was an amazing teacher.  I often find it difficult to stay engaged in long lectures but for a almost 2 hour lecture period I was almost always engaged.  Attendance is not mandatory but you will understand the topics a lot better if you do attend.

Lectures were super engaging because he calls on students, which is stressful at first but you get used to it. There is homework for every class and I got burned out pretty quick, but the lectures make up for it. He brings in lots of guest speakers that work in different fields of law, and learning about what they do was super interesting.

Joseph is my favorite professor that I have had so far at UO. This class is very lecture heavy but he makes the lectures interesting and is interactive with his students. The midterm was pretty hard and the final was a take-home project that took me over 20 hours to complete. If you are interested in law take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's just a great professor. He clearly enjoys teaching, and despite being a law class, he makes it fun and engaging. Attendance isn't exactly mandatory, but going will make getting good grades on the midterm and final a lot easier as he explains the content well in his lectures. Lots of good guest speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joseph is a great professor. The lectures are super interesting and he always brings great guest speakers. There is a good amount of reading for the first half of the term, but the workload was light after. As long as you pay attention in class you should do fine on the tests.

Love this professor. Very accessible and accommodating if you talk to him. Lots of reading judicial opinions and summarizing but worth it. Always has great guest speakers and amazing personal experiences as a federal prosecutor. Not much goes in the grade book so study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher and has great first hand information to give you as well as an absurd amount of connections in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher, super knowledgeable and has so many guest speakers. Very nice, way overqualified for the job (he's a federal prosecutor). Tests were hard but the only things that were graded. Pay attention in class and you will do well. Overall amazing experience!

Lots of guest speakers and only two assignments, plus one extra credit assignment. The midterm was definitely difficult and required a lot of studying. Same goes for the final, I spent well over 10 hours working on the final alone. The class was extremely worth it if you are interested in criminal law, if not I would not recommend taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an overall great professor, he seems interested in what he's talking about, and is hilarious. However, there were only 2 things in the grade book for the whole term: the final and midterm. But if you show up to lecture, and take good notes you should be fine. He did a good curve and offered extra credit.
He has the coolest guest speakers, and you need to do a bit of reading before every class. awesome class
Super fun and investing class. Very well taught and enjoyable content. Prof Huynh is a really good teacher and funny as well. One of my favorite classes this term!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Hokanson is one of the most caring professors I've met and is super kind when you reach out with any questions. She's super passionate about the material which makes lectures enjoyable and engaging. The assignments are very easy if you do the readings and she always goes over everything in class. Highly recommend COLT232 as an elective
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor and human! Katya is so educated on her subjects and picks really engaging Russian books and poetry to read. I am a STEM major and loved her class. If you actually read the books, the class is extremely easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My opinion has soured recently. Prof felt disrespected about attendance and would wait to hand out the sign in sheet until the end of class, keeping us late. It is Friday of finals week and we have not had an upgraded grade in over a month. Every other class is finalized but I do not know a result of a quiz we took in February. Actual class was ok
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: TONS of reading, with readings discussed in every class. Assignments and quizzes are easy as long as you understand the reading, and Katya is an extremely generous grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tons of reading in RUSS204, but honestly I didn't do any of it on time. As long as you read the materials before the few quizzes in class you should be fine. Katya is passionate about what she teaches and is very open for interpretation from students. Class size is small and feels like a community. Overall good experience but get ready to READ!

Professor Hokanson is very kind and understanding! She is clearly passionate about what she teaches and puts a lot of effort in. She is not a harsh grader, so as long as you show up, participate, and do the work it should not be a difficult class. I had a lot of fun taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The lectures were long and sometimes boring, but it's clear that she's passionate about the subject. She is also open to students interpretations of the material, which was very nice. It's easy to fall behind on the required readings and films, but you won't feel completely lost and should be able to catch up.

I've taken her two of her classes and would take more if I could. Very respectful of different interpretations of course content, always interested in what you have to say. You have to buy some books, but she tries to find free versions as much as possible. Paper prompts and quizzes are consistent with lectures. Highly recommend her classes.

Professor Hokanson is very educated and passionate about Russian culture, and that shines through in her lectures. The workload is significant, and you will be expected to help lead discussions in class at some point. However, the actual assignments and quizzes are fairly easy and Katya is always willing to lend a hand.

This class isn't very hard, there's a good amount of reading but they're decently interesting texts and many of them are pretty short. Professor Hokanson is a good lecturer and discussion leader, and she knows a ton about the subject so if you're really curious about it then she'd be a great resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was a decent class, but the writing prompts were so vague that it actually made the class harder. I think that she was trying to give us as much freedom as possible, but these were some of the most difficult papers I've written since there was no clear prompt. Also did not give out "perfect" scores (not a criticism, just a heads up).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was the easiest class I've ever taken. She's a very sweet lady, and you can tell she's passionate about the material. Very few assignments, usually bi-weekly, and they were very easy. I had to write 4 papers, but they weren't required to be that long and the topics were relatively easy to write about. Super easy Arts & Letters credit!

Katya is fantastic. You're taking a Russian Literature class, so you will be reading a decent amount, but it's pretty manageable and I can't imagine why you'd take this if you didn't want to be reading. Not too many papers and they are graded pretty generously, you don't have to completely memorize every plot detail. Absolutely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Katya's class a lot. It's a LOT of reading, but if you can get past that, this is a really insightful class into Russian literature and lifestyle. Katya is also really friendly and responds to emails fast. If you read about half-3/4ths of the time, and you show up to most classes, a B or B+ should be pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Such a fun class to take. Just do the readings and show up for class and you'll get an easy A. She's super knowledgeable about the subject, and is also kind and personable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Her knowledge was intimidating at first, but then I realized she was kind of my fairy godmother. Always responds to messages right away and provides great feedback. Take her classes.
I loved her russian lit 204 class in the fall term. She was an amazing prof that real inspired the interest of russian culture already.  All the readings were pretty interesting too

This  was one of the most enjoyable classes I've taken. You don't need any background at all in Russian, as long as you enjoy reading you'll like the course. Grading is very straightforward and fair, if you do all of the reading and put in the effort you'll easily get an A. I'd highly recommend this class, Katya is an amazing prof who really cares!

Katya's love of literature, especially Tolstoy is very evident when you take her class. She is always open to discuss the books you read and knows a lot about her subject. She's a bit tough in the beginning but once you get to know her she is very nice and supportive of her students.

Katya Hokanson is a very motivated instructor and really cares about the subject and how discussions are going. Very well prepared for each class, with lots of visual aids and additional material on the topic. Keeps her students' interest up. An easy yet well deserved A is quaranteed as long as you read, participate, turn in papers on time. Cute!

I would undoubtedly say best professor at REESC. Hokanson most certainly excels at a seminar level, although maybe this isn't the case in the lower level courses, I can't say. If she is in a class with people that genuinely know Russian literature and have a background, then she is amazing. If you ask her for help she really goes above and beyond.
This professor is not very nice. She puts people down when they don't think the same way as her, and it makes students not want to add to discussion. Very strong opinions.
Very intelligent but has trouble getting engaging discussions going.
Easy class. Just keep up on the reading and you'll get an easy A. She's very nice and easy going too

Habib is literally amazing. No one in my class was a dance major but we all had so much fun. Best GPA booster class you could take. He does make us dance every week but do not be intimidated, he makes everyone feel so comfortable and its truly so easy and so much fun, take it with a friend if you can!

I took this class as a last option and I am so thankful I did. While it was out of my comfort zone I still had so much fun. He describes his class as a GPA booster. He is so knowledgeable and kind. I highly recommend even though you have to dance, you get used to it after 1 class.

Habib is one of the chillest prof i've ever had. All he asked was that you attended class and the lectures are pretty interesting, and majority of the time he let us out 30 minutes early or if it was nice out. Great guy too, I definitely recommend if you need the GP credit too.

Habib is literally the best teacher on campus. Even if you don't like to dance or are scared to dance, I promise this class is amazing. I was really nervous to dance in front of other people but that feeling goes away so quickly. PLEASE take a class with Habib if you can

I really liked the class and Professor Hendrix is really chill as long as you show up to class and participate. There is a lottery system but as long as you try thats all that matters. Grading isnt harsh at all either which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very passionate about what he teaches and gives very interesting lectures. The class is set up a little odd and hard to know what your grade is ahead of time.

I have taken 3 classes with him all have gotten A's. Very easy willing to help you in office hours and super nice guy. Passionate about his classes normally a essay or 2 and then some reading response questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class, he was clearly very knowledgeable on the subject matter.  Grade was based on 3 larger consecutive papers that built to the final 3rd paper, as well as weekly response papers and participation.  3 free absences, 6 total before an automatic 0 on participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Decent professor, but for a class in the morning, his ramblings were mind-numbing. Would often go on long tangents and rush through slides too quickly. Cold-called in class, and even if you got the question remotely right, he would still say you were wrong and not count you present. Has yet to release any grades after W10 and no final study guide
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you want to know what your grade is before week ten, do not take this class. Going into finals week, we still do not have class grades. I get that grading takes a long time, but this is a little ridiculous. I could be fully failing this class and have no idea and no way to fix my grade.

I really enjoyed Hendrix, especially considering I took the class at 8 a.m. He was always engaging. The only critique I have is that it is a lottery system for participation/ answering questions, which was stressful, but I will say it was effective. His tests were green book but fairly easy as long as you studied and remembered the vocabulary.

Professor Hendrix is super passionate about what he teaches and cares about his students and our role in the future of the U.S. The lectures are just slideshows and notes, so if you aren't super interested in this topic then you will get bored very easily.... Hendrix is easy to talk to, responds to emails, and is very knowledgeable. GOAT PROF!!!

He is a nice professor, but his lectures were not very engaging. It felt like a lot of rambling, and it was hard to feel engaged. You are only graded on a couple of things. There are 4 papers just a half page long, a midterm, an essay, and a final. For poli sci majors, take this class as opposed to an upper-division theory course. Boring but easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't understand why people love this guy so much- his lectures are rambling, repetitive, sometimes incoherent, to the point where I feel like he failed to get across the main points. He genuinely annoyed me to no end. For someone not well acquainted with political science, I can't imagine how confusing this class would be. Would not take again.

Really great lecturer. Not the most personable (he teaches massive classes) but extremely knowledgable about the subject matter. Participate as much as possible. Assigns lots of readings, but you don't need to do all of them to write the essays. No midterm or final tests. Great class to take if you want to sound smart at parties.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hendrix is so amazing, in every single class I was completely engaged and interested. he is such a supportive professor and I always felt like I could come to him if I needed help.

I loved how Professor Hendrix organized his lecture slides, as his related lectures made it easy to create helpful notes. 

There are 7 response papers that only have to be half a page and two big 2 essays.

Class participation is required. If you raise your hand but do not get called on, he still marks you down for participation for that day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall okay professor, the one bad thing about this class is grading is a bit tough and there is not much making up your final grade; term paper, midterm, final and then just some small percentage for attendance and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things
