reviews.comment: Participation was a bit rough and the lectures can be a bit boring at times, but overall a good professor and a really nice guy. As long as you put in the effort for the essays you will be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Incredible professor, probably the best in the Political Science department at UO. The material is interesting, and he lectures in a way that makes the material easy to understand without being condescending towards students. 

Grade was mostly based on essays, which were graded somewhat strictly, but not unreasonable for a an upper division class.

Very good lecturer and engaging guy. He seems to have a fundamental grasp of the material in his fingertips, and he really knows what he's doing when teaching it. He also does a good job of being impartial in teaching, and furthermore can be funny in his lectures. Good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting readings and lectures/class activities were helpful for understanding, but there were only two papers that went into the grade book that were very difficult to get a good grade on
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and he is smart. GROUP WORK for ALMOST EVERY CLASS, and he cold calls EVERY CLASS. The readings are at times hard, but manageable. Interesting class about Athens and Rome. There are 2 essays, response papers, and attendance grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not a great professor. You don't learn anything from him. He mumbles, does the work for the problems to go over in class BEFORE he gets to class, and constantly asks if things make sense when everything is so unclear. When asked to explain again, he reiterates what he already said. I learned more from youtube. Avoid taking with him if possible.

it was for STATS and it did not feel like he was actually teaching but more like we were watching him do math. he would just do the worksheet and would not really answer questions. it was somewhat difficult to understand him but the teaching itself was the main difficulty. if its possible to take someone do but if you cant youll survive

This guy does not speak English very well and is difficult to understand. It's hard when its already a difficult subject and it just gets harder. The exams are SO similar to the practice exams tho so just study those up and you'll be good.

MATH 341 - Lectures were very organized and he stayed close to the textbook. Was always super kind... one day he literally caught up to me on the sidewalk after class to explain a question I asked. Exams exactly like practice exams. Put in the work and you'll be fine. He offered extra credit for picking up exams at OH/cares about your feedback.

Clearly knows and understands what he teaches, but isn't great at communicating it. He tends to skip over most of the work during example problems, which wasn't the greatest. It doesn't feel like he understands that students are learning things for the first time, and what seems easy to him might not he easy for them
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: MATH 251 Not a good lecturer at all. Mumbles and doesn't even explain steps to solve equations, just goes up to the boards and solves it, expecting everyone to understand what he does. Do not take a class with him unless you can teach yourself and actually understand what is supposed to be taught because you will not retain much with him.

This professor is by god the worst lecturer I have ever seen, mumbles half the time and has very hard to read handwriting. he also seems to just be showing up to lecture and winging it from the textbook as he goes. Quite frankly, in his class, you are pretty much better off just reading the textbook and only showing up only for the exams.
Professor Hollenberg is a nice guy and always asks his Muslim students for input, which I think is really nice. Offers a lot of extra credit too. Great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very kind, caring, and knowledgeable professor. The only thing I struggled with is that I feel like he sometimes makes understanding content harder than it should be just due to his teaching style. But overall he is a great professor. Just don't be afraid to ask questions and try not to stress if you are confused.
He's a great professor who is clearly EXTREMELY knowledgeable on the sub
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class but still educational. Graded on only two quizzes and a paper and they're all easy as long as you are keeping up and paying attention. Wish there was a greater focus on modern history, but what is covered is gone into with a good amount of depth. Recommended as either a gen ed course  or for relevant majors.

Good teacher, especially for the subject, he is very smart and knows what he's talking about. I was extremely bored because I am an accounting major, but this was a good class, if you pay attention and attend class you don't have to stress about anything else. There is no structure to the course, so it was confusing, but not necessarily hard.
Dr. Hollenberg is incredibly knowledgeable in the areas of Arabic and Islam. He teaches the class very well, and keeps everyone engaged. I would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken two advanced Arabic classes with Professor Hollenberg, and he is an incredible educator and mentor. He is a fountain of knowledge and cares a lot about the success of his students. I found his classes challenging but worth it. Gender and Sexuality in Early Islam (410) remains one of my favorite courses taken throughout my three years.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: David cared so deeply about teaching this class and seeing what students struggle with when first learning arabic. While arabic is a tough language, he provided a lot of materials to aid us. He was an understanding grader and gave as many points as possible.

He's accessible outside of class and is willing to help you during office hours. Promptly replies to emails and gives you good feedback. His course material is interesting and he's well read and knows a lot about professional focus area.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good course.  A bit heavy on the Arabic terms.

Islam is a truly fascinating religion/belief system. Although I guess it would have been more interesting to learn from a Muslim per say (to ask about personal experiences), Mr.Hollenberg did an 'okay job'. This class has left me wanting to learn more about Islam, looking forward to taking future Religious/Islamic study classes!
Good class.

His teaching is pretty scattered-- Everywhere.  But the material is pretty relevant and kind of interesting-- eventho. his lectures can be really dry. You have to learn the arabic alphabet which is insane if you don't have an interest in it... But if you're going to class and taking notes-- it's a pretty sure A.  I'd recommend it for a GenEd.

He's just not good at all, really boring. knows alot about the subject but doesnt explain it, just tells you and expects you to memorize it. oh and his notes he puts on the board are almost impossible to read.

His lectures can be a bit dry and boring at some times, but the material is still interesting and very relevant.  He teaches a bit scattered, but it was mainly because it is a gened, and 9/10 of the students don't know a thing about the subject material beforehand, but he tells you exactly what is on the tests and quizzes, so it should be an easy A
completely confused, but somehow doing well enough.  unclear what he really wants, what the goal of the course is.
i would just like to point out that his name is hollenberg, not hollinberg, and he is really good if you pay attention and let him do his thing.

The guy is a stud.  Just study for quizzes, they are a 1/3 of your grade.  Talk to him after class, the subject material is interesting, and don't be afraid of being wierd. Just talk to the man.  He'll appreciate you reaching out and in turn you'll learn more and earn a better grade.

Kind of stumbles over explaining the material. Ask a lot of questions to get what he is saying. Lots of reading but most is on blackboard. A couple of tests and a few papers (4-5pages). Not a bad class at all. Very interesting material. No attendance policy. Only hard part was all the reading, Papers are pretty easy and he's a fair grader.

So many people dropped the class in the beginning, but I stuck it out and I think I'm doing fine. He is very intelligent and you can tell he know a ton, but he isn't great at relaying the info. You really can't miss a class.

Class with Hollenberg is anything but excitement, but that doesn't mean the topic itself isn't. Quizes and Tests really aren't too difficult, you can basically BS essays on tests (with sufficient amount of accurate information), and mult choices are hit or miss. Take the 50 min one I took that one and felt any longer would kill my mind with boredom

i took islamic civilization. subject matter is to die for, really interesting. i think everyone, with todays issues should take this class to gain a better understanding about the history behind who we're fighting. he's kind of boring at times, can ramble, but if you focus on how interesting the topic is, you'll do fine. take the 50 min. one.

he's a pretty nice guy...make sure you get a 50 min class because anything other than that and you'll die of boredom. DEFINTITELY read his study guides they are very helpful for whats going to be on the quiz or test. but tests are way more difficult than quizzes.
I had him for Islamic Civilizations, and it was really interesting. Plus, I LOVE the way he dresses! Definitely take him.

He is so funny.  The first few days of class, he pretends the class will be hard, but the only difficult part is reading all of the stuff he puts on blackboard.  He says that there is a participation grade, but as long as you answer his questions when he calls on you, you'll be fine.

Such a caring professor. She really shows that she cares about her students. Participation is required but you can also make it up and get your points back. Highly recommended I wish she could teach all my classes!

Indy was one of the best teachers I have had so far at UO. She is super warm and caring and very understanding. I was having some personal issues, and she accommodated my needs perfectly! She is very knowledgeable and passionate about her class. I would 100% have her as my prof again.
She's so amazing! the sweetest prof I've had!

Indy Recker is an angel on the planet earth, being one of the nicest professors I have ever had in college. On the flip side, the class she teaches is so unbelievably boring and easy, I feel like I already did every one of the activities in 10th and 11th grade. But, again, Indy is amazing and I love her but be ready to snooze through all the class.
Best professor at Oregon

Indy is one of those teachers where you know she's here for YOU. She wants YOU to succeed and pass the class. She is a relentless ray of sunshine even if your class is a graveyard. The bar is very low for all of the assignments (in WR 123) cuz she knows it's a class we all have to get over with. You're in good hands with Indy Recker! :)
Best English class I've taken at college. Very easy and chill. The workload won't interfere with your other classes. Extremely understanding and flexible.

I had Indy for ENG105Z. Incredible teacher, incredible person. Easy grader, accepts late work with no penalty, extra credit opportunities, genuinely cares about you and if you are willing to do the work, you can easily get an A.

Indy was very laidback in most everything regarding her classes: everything had a due date but she encourages turning something in late for better quality. Easy to make up attendance, also really cares for her students and can bring the energy to a tired 4pm writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a BLESSING. (I took writing 122 not 123 but I couldn't change it) She is literally the nicest and most caring professor ever. Theres weekly journals (only one paragraph) + two essays and a portfolio at the end. She grades quickly and easily, mostly based on completion! I'm at week 9 right now and I literally have 100% in the class.

She was absolutely one of the better professors ive had. She is very kind and she cares about the workload for class. Very straight forward work. Weekly one paragraph reflection that is on a completion basis. The big assignments for the class are well constructed and she gives plenty of time for you to do them. Great professor. 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing Teacher! Easy to reach outside of class, and timely response! Gives good feedback on writing, what works and what doesn't. Even if you are late still counts as attendance, and you get 2 absences. Stretches due dates for students if needed. only 4 writing assignments, taking into consideration that students have other work.
I didn't appreciate some comments made in this class and lack of tolerance for contradictory opinions.

Professor Gassama is extremely knowledgeable and provides a lot of insight to the text. He applies it to real-world current events, and makes class extremely enjoyable. I took International Law with him as an undergrad course, but I'm sure his other classes as just as good.
Great professor.  Funny and engaging in class.  The book he uses lays out the basics of torts in a clear and helpful manner.

Hmm... If you like to laugh, you will enjoy attending this class.  Overall I appreciate him, however he gave no A's or A-'s.  To all the gunners out there that will drive you mad.  He has implied this will not be so in the second semester.
Didn't give any As or A+s.  Really screwed our section over with the grades.

Very entertaining, very intelligent Professor, but he didn't seem that interested in teaching the subject.  I really like him a lot on a personal level and he is probably an outstanding professor in a course he is passionate about, but Torts doesn't seem to be the subject that inspires his best teaching.  Grading seemed arbitrary.
Did I learn enough about tort law?  Probably not.  Really entertaining, wonderfully self-contradictory (honest) about his ideology, and very laid back in his teaching style.
I learned a lot from him. Like how much he loves coffee
You will learn more about his daughter than about the class... but very entertaining.
No Comments
Huh?  What did he say?

Miller is a tough grader and not the most organized, but one thing he cares about is his students and their success. If you have interest in being published he'll help you. Also the effort you put in Miller matches, so if you give up he won't help you. He's passionate about the SOJC, give him a chance.

He is a great storyteller with a clear passion for his career. Unfortunately, his teaching style was a bit too unorganized for my liking, and I felt like I was in a raft without a paddle. Overall, I enjoyed the class and Professor Millers positive spirit. However, the class felt rushed and had unclear expectations. I think he is new to the UO, GL!

What a teacher should be. He truly cares for his students success, and will be the reason the SOJC sees positive change at UO. He will push you to improve your writing, so don't be discouraged if your first grade isn't amazing, he will show you exactly what you need to do in order to improve.

Ivan has not provided anything unique to my educational experience at the SOJC. The class is mostly just him talking in circles about his life. I just feel like I'm not gaining anything from this experience, it's just the same assignments that I already did in Reporting 1. He's nice, but definitely not a professor I'd take again.- jcom332

Ivan Miller is going to save the SOJC. He is committed to helping students in & outside class, and is so willing to help and be flexible. He wants his students to be good and helps them get there. He wants you to put in the work, but he backs you up every step of the way, and is always encouraging you to "swing for the fences." Take his classes!
She is the most kind, loving prof in the whole world. She actually cares about her students rather than their grades and scores. Very down to earth, professional, informative and smart.

Class was async with weekly Canvas quizzes about the lecture material. Weekly discussions were mandatory and mainly talked about the week's lecture. Very easy class if you know anything about sociology. Boring if you've taken other SOC classes. 4 required activities throughout term. No tests, easy final project. Lots of reflecting on life in HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The main lecture is online in which you just watch a video, do the reading, and we have a weekly quiz. The quizzes are super easy, and you'll get 100% no matter what. The discussions are on person, and the difficulty will depend on your GE/TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One in person 50min meeting per week, mandatory. Weekly quizzes and biweekly essay's, along with a long essay final. She offers a 5% extra credit assignment, honestly one of the easiest classes you can take for credit. Just do every assignment, skim the reading & lectures, and put in effort for your papers and it will be a no brainer A+.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's very enthusiastic about the course material during lectures and makes assignments very easy to understand. Her course really gets people thinking about sociology.

Straight up, if you don't like reading and writing, you will not like the work in this class. You end up engaging with the GE way more than Jill herself, but that's also because I took it as an online class. Very easy overall, not hard to get an A on the papers and you get multiple chances on quizzes. Shoutout JY, they're a great GE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: We had essays every other week as our classwork and the prompts were pretty confusing and wordy. The class itself was easy I only ever watched the lectures and didn't do any of the reading and got 100% on all the essays. I only realized this might be an issue till the final. Very flexible final!

The assignments were very easy, but prompts were sometimes confusing. No exams and short quizzes to show you watched lectures. I got by without doing many of the readings because the lectures were pretty much what you read about anyway. She is engaging and a good professor to visit during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: easy credit, papers every odd week but they are all fairly easy. the course is relevant but a little boring. if  you dont do the lectures dont stress, the GEs will most likely summarize the week during the discussions.

Jill was a very sweet and caring professor. I think she would do better with smaller class sizes because she is decently shy. However, this class was a really nice intro class and did not require much work, but allowed you to engage with the material more. There was required reading, but it was only $8 in total and really helped with definitions.

The class itself was the easiest class I've taken. The "hardest" part was remembering concepts that needed to be applied to tests + assignments. I rarely thought of this class besides when we had our test week in our sections (3 tests). I think Jill would be a great professor in a smaller class. She always reminded us of due dates and was flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Harrison was amazing. As long as you pay attention to lecture slides (attendance isn't mandatory) that are posted and do the assignments on time with effort the class should be an easy A. Her GE's are nice too. She provides many extra credit opportunities to raise your grade, optional final paper to raise your grade.
This is a chill class to get a requirement over and done with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is extremely easy. Liberal group think brainwashing. If you are right wing be prepared to write against your own views if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Instead of tests, you can do short essays and the average scores were always A's. You also get multiple extra credit opportunities. Not the most fun class but super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Harrison! She is so helpful & kind. There is an in person midterm & final, but she provides you w/ a study sheet that you can bring to the final & midterm. The power points are posted & she does a very good job w/ getting back to you. She gives bonus questions on the finals & midterms too. If you pay attention you'll be okay!

Professor Harrison is very sweet and cares for her students! Unfortunately, the lecture material can be somewhat boring causing many students to never come to class, but at least the coursework is easy. I would definitely recommend taking this course!
soooo easy, reading is interesting. stopped going to class halfway through and easy peasy. graded on 3 assessments or papers + other mini assignments.

Jill was an okay professor. Her lectures felt long and boring. She sounds nervous half of the time. There is two papers, one midterm and one final. There is also one weekly assignment but it's easy. There is also an attendance sheet. The overall class is easy but she almost unbearable to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jill Harrison was one of my favorite teachers. Her class was straight forward, with reasonable deadlines. She was easy to listen to during class, and gave good feedback on all of the papers we submitted. If you need a good sociology credit class, this is it,
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jill Harrison was an awesome professor. SOC 447 Organizations is probably the most interesting and practical sociology course I've taken. The business elements are a PLUS. I'm glad this class isn't under the school of business bc they would ruin it. Interesting content, readings, and assignments. This class def changed the way I look at things

Pretty good Professor, great lectures, little reading, 2 papers due, 1 midterm and a final, the only negative of this course were the discussion sections. Felt like a waste of time, GE that graded our papers left us no feedback and wasn't helpful at all.

She is a solid prof. Attendance sheet every class, one final research paper, a midterm, some assignments for homework and in-class, and a book report. Lectures are boring but so is the class topic. She is nice and caring, but this is about as normal as a college class as you can get. Nothing special or extraordinary but no being caught off guard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: She doesn't make lectures boring, but the subject itself is one that everyone already knows which is why students say they find it boring. She is a great lecturer, but the class doesn't want to interact with her or answer questions. I definitely recommend taking a class with Professor Harrison.

Extremely boring lectures with attendance sheets at the very end of class. You can miss up to 6 classes before being dropped. She is a nice person, but lacks lecturing skills, and the class feels pointless even though it's easy credits. Topics are gender, homosexuality, labor unions, worker's rights, social movements. Two essays, 1 midterm, 1 final

Interesting class with many interesting concepts that I mostly already knew. Lecture's were really boring and basically straight out of the textbook but overall, it was a straightforward, and relatively easy class. She's a very nice and helpful professor, but I would just suggest for her to brush up on her lectures and lecturing skills.

Jill is an amazing teacher who is passionate about what she teaches. If your truly into Sociology, some of her work will inspire you. Jill has a great teaching style, makes sure that the information is explained clearly, and gives no surprises in class. If you just show up, you wont do great in the class. However, if  you give it effort, its an A.

This class is a breeze. Show up, sign the attendance sheet, 2% extra credit at the end of the term. She posts a study guide a week before any test, and all of the answers are found on the slides. The test only consists of things given to you on the study guide. This is my third class with Prof. Harrison and I highly recommend if you want an easy A

She is very nice and you can tell she is passionate about the subject. Lectures are kinda boring but she does make an effort to mix it up. Easy class, I never read and hardly went to class and I got an A-.

Boring delivery. She reads from her notes. Changes the syllabus which is not very precise in the first place. Doesn't post grades so you never get any feedback on how you are progressing. Overall, She is a nice woman but a poor professor. Not very charismatic and rather dull and droll.
Not bad. I rarely went to class, because the tests were based completely off of lectures. I missed out on the in-class writings, but overall it was a pretty easy class.

Recommended Class! I learn a lot about work and occupation from this class. The only way to earn extra credits is to have 90% class attendance. But relax, her GTF is fair grader. And she is really approachable. Visit her office hours and you will learn more beyond lectures.

Fairly easy class. However, lectures were very boring and I found myself getting up and leaving early because I was so bored. She is helpful with SOC as a whole but I dont know if social psych was her thing. I would recommend if you want an easy class

Very knowledgeable.  She shows a keen interest in the subject matter.  There is a lot of information to process in such a short period and her tests are not easy, but it is rewarding if you have the time to process and digest large quantities of information in a short time frame. She is also very attractive.

Favorite professor thus far. Very helpful with students both about her course and life outside college. Tries very hard to engage students without making them feel uncomfortable. Really wants students to succeed not only in her class, but also once they graduate. Visit her office hours and she will help you all she can. AMAZING professor! :)

I am writing this comment in week six of a ten week term, in order to critique more fairly. Overall I enjoy the class, however I feel like the professor is sometimes rude to people who are not familiar with Sociology or politics. This attitude, makes it very uncomfortable to participate in lecture's.
Nice guy and obviously cares but I have a tough time understanding and seems to second guess himself a lot. Test score heavy and pop quiz every class..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor does not explain things, rather he just gives examples and expects you to figure it out on the weekly worksheet he gives you. His teaching strategy is not the best and I would not reccomend him to anyone.

He reads off the slides for 20 minuets and calls it a lecture, then has you work for the rest of the 2 hours and is very unhelpful when you do have any questions. there is a quiz every class with 3-6 pages of homework. fi you don't already know how to do the stuff he is very badly attempting to teach then you're not going to do good in this class.

This class was an extreme struggle from the start. He is a nice guy, and grades easy, but is not helpful in any way, shape, or form. The answer key for the final and midterm reviews had 6 WRONG answers, and my friends and I relied on learning at the math tutoring department. I would not recommend this professor unless you can teach yourself easily.

Ivanov is a nice guy and a generous grader but he is a poor teacher. It's clear that he cares about his students but none of that helps the fact that he cannot communicate the math. Answer keys are often full of mistakes. The two-hour class is 10 minutes of lecturing, and nothing else. If you have trouble teaching yourself, do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He explains the concepts like he isn't sure what he's talking about...he also usually just reads off the slides without explaining the text on them further. Sometimes his answers to my questions leave me with just more questions.

This guy sucks so much, your “lectures” will be 8 slides and him talking nonsense, you have a quiz every class and a homework packet usually around 5 pages. His midterm review and homework consistently have errors. He doesn't tell you about important dates so you feel consistently unprepared. Do not take this class.
Solid professor, fun to talk to, nice and gives fun projects. Not too difficult.
Isami is super nice and funny. He is always willing to sit down with you and help you on the projects. I think his assignments have the perfect balance of guidelines, but freedom to do what you want.

Isami is an epic king. Animation is really difficult and he understands that, so he's always there to support you and troubleshoot issues. A typical class is usually a demo of strategies and techniques, then work time on projects. Class is well organized, the information he gives is useful, and it's a lot of work but I didn't feel rushed.

Isami is willing to work with you on your projects and is very easy to approach during and outside of class. My issue with him is that he doesn't provide a lot of criticism, which makes it hard to know what to improve on moving forward. He also didn't grade any assignments til the end of the term which was not ideal for a project based class

Maybe the Art/Design ARC just didn't click for me but I found myself often getting bored during these classes. As the semester went on I got a bit more interested and he is very nice to everyone so I still respect him regardless. Although most people will likely have a strong connection with him, he might not click with everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken multiple classes with him and he's easily one of my favorite professors at UO! The course content was challenging enough to be fulfilling but still doable. Isami is really good at explaining things if you need help. A very stress-free class experience!
A very funny, interesting guy! Nothing really else to say other than attendance is required and graded. Work days are a little boring.

Isami is my favorite instructor at UO! I've taken so many art and design classes at UO and in my experience the critiques aren't helpful, but Isami is wonderful with guiding you in the right direction with what you want to do. He is kind and truly a great instructor
Animation with Isami is a must. You will not regret it. Super nice dude, fun to joke around with, and he'll pretty much leave you completely alone for the quarter if you don't need help.

Isami is great- he's really there for the students. What makes him such a great teacher is his ability to work so cohesively with different types of students. If you need space-he gives it, however if you want feedback he's great with that
He made 8 am so easy! Love it!

Isami is essentially the greatest and if I could take all of my classes with him I would. He makes the course material approachable instead of intimidating and if you ask for help he will meet you more than halfway. He made the class so enjoyable that I found myself forward to going to my 8 a.m.'s for once.
Cool guy - cool class.
Great professor in general. Pretty much let you explore your own art as well as helping you to stay in a direction of the class goals.
Funny guy, cares a lot.

Isami's a really chill guy. He's funny, laidback, and personable. He has a tendency to be kinda vague when describing assignments at first, but he's helpful if you ask him questions. He only assigns things verbally, there are no project sheets or anything. He knows his stuff and gives good personal attention to his students.
Will work with you. Funny and chill.

Isabel is my favorite prof so far. She's funny, genuine, and really cares that students succeed in her class. She is very flexible with due dates and often gives extensions. There are 2 main projects in the class with a few scaffolding assignments that go with them. 2 weeks out of the term are cancelled and revision meetings are held instead.

Isabel is my favorite prof so far. She's funny and genuine and really cares that you succeed in the class. She gives extensions and is very flexible with work and due dates. The workload is also very light in this course. There are two big projects and a few scaffolding assignments for them. She also has revision weeks where class is cancelled.

I LOVE MRS. BRINEGAR!! She's an absolute gem for this class and she'll make you have the inspiration to write! She's very lenient on assignments and extensions are very much possible as long as you communicate with her. Feedback is very helpful to improve your writing! By far the most fun, chill, and worthwhile professor you'll find here!!

Ms. Brinegar's class was one of my favorite this term. She has a very engaging and enthusiastic approach to her class and will often provide extensions if they are needed. Her feedback on the papers you write in the class is very helpful and as long as you fix whatever you discuss in your conference you should be able to pass the class very easily.

I have taken classes with this professor twice now, and while readings were heavy, they were necessary and comparable to other 400 level sociology courses. I learned a lot in her courses as she uses active learning practices. Not to mention these are important and meaningful topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her class very very good and insightful. There is more reading than average but the readings tend to be  quite accessible and interesting. Overall good class
Y'all need to find religion when she's your professor. She did not take feedback from myself or others about how her class was failing us. At least 200 pages of reading every night btw.

LOVED THIS CLASS! Super friendly and felt more like a discussion among peers compared to the normal professor talking down to and at you. The readings weren't too bad (maybe an hour per class, which is posted at the beginning of the week). The midterm is manageable if you understand the topics, and the class is mostly focused on the group project.

I LOVED Professor Colaiacovo! This class is very class discussion and group project heavy, and there's lots of reading you'll have to do outside of class; BUT, this class is so much fun and so interesting! It was super engaging and Colaiacovo was the perfect professor to teach it. I highly recommend taking her class, even if it's for an elective,

I absolutely loved this class. Colaiacovo is absolutely amazing, she pushes her students to do the best they can. Participation matters and there's lots of group work. I looked forward to class everyday and felt challenged and motivated to do my best. 10/10 take this class. shoutout 4pm, such a fun time!

I loved having her so much! She is an extremely tough grader, but you can tell she cares a lot about her students. If you write something for her, make sure it matches the rubric 100% and does not go over the word count. Going to her office hours really makes a difference and she explains things really well. She is really funny in lectures too!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun professor who is easy to communicate with. She's a tough grader, but she also gives her students all the information and teaching to succeed at a high level—one of my favorite professors I have had in college.

She is amazing! Classes are actually interesting, I never dreaded coming to class. She is a tough grader for sure but she offers so much one on one support. She is very clear on what she is looking for and gives you the resources. I def recommend. Just make sure you actually talk to her and go to OH and you will be more than fine!

Definitely an interesting class if you're an entrepreneur. I am not. She's a pretty tough grader but is very enthusiastic and clearly knowledgeable about what she's teaching. Be careful on the first midterm and go all out on your project, she's not messing around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Professor Colaiacovo's first term at UO and she was amazing! I felt that the material covered in class was engaging and applicable to the real world. She offers thorough feedback on assignments and is encouraging. There is a group project, but as long as you communicate with her about how to improve you will be fine.

This was Professor Colaiacovo's first term being a professor here at UO and knocked it out of the ball park. She came into every class engaged and ready to teach. She was a tough grader but gave amazing feedback. Second half of class is group work, be picky about your group! I had an amazing term with her, wish I could take another class with her!
Amazing teacher! Grades projects and tests a little hard but would take a class with her again she's amazing!

Great energy, such a fun class even if you don't like entrepreneurship. Wish I could take again!
Thanks Prof C, - noon class W24

She's not clear on what she wants from us on assignments. Unclear rubric and instructions. Attendance heavy: even missing once or twice will mess up your grade, which is completely unreasonable. Very long readings that sometimes don't or barely get discussed. Would not recommend.
She talks constantly during class as well as the graded projects are out of hand. Very unorganized and attendance heavy.

She's a nice lady but doesn't run her class very well. Very unclear about grading criteria and does not respond to her email in a timely manner. Lots of long readings that feel unnecessary by how little we discuss them. Seems like an easy A at first, but there's a lot of work and the class is harder than a K-pop class should be.

A little confused on other comments because if you take a class it's pretty normal to make sure that you go to your classes. I would compare it to your average high school teacher on attendance strictness. Great teacher, very nice, beware of long readings although the actual content is manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is very kind! Definitely very reading heavy and strict on attendance but she is very passionate and a great teacher. Will say she is less understanding about accommodations and not the most lenient, but great professor for those interested in Korean studies.

I would not recommend taking a class with her, as she is not understanding of students. Even when students express concerns, she dismisses them and shows little to no respect. Her assigned readings are excessively long and do not contribute effectively to my learning. A very disrespectful professor who I don't will change.

While the class was fairly easy, the professor was very disrespectful in emails to me. I had a tough time communicating with her, and she was never transparent about grading criteria. Attendance credit makes no sense, if you show up 5 minutes late you might not get credit at all! There is no need to be disrespectful with students, just be kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is a difficult person to get ahold of. The class is supposed to touch on Language and Culture but is more based on Language and is more of a linguistic class then anything else. Her policies are very unclear, grading is all over place. She is a nice person, don't get me wrong, but she is the worst professor i have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is overall really kind. However, her grading criteria aren't clear. She was difficult to get ahold of over email, as I've sent multiple emails and have yet to receive word back. Her lectures are long and information-heavy but not terrible. There are so many readings, so prepare to read 20-50 pages every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were long but definitely not the worst. Her instructions for grading were not very clear, but she was very accessible by email or office hours! There are readings/music videos/TV episodes for each class, but there was only a few papers, so that was nice.

I took Professor Kims Korean pop Culture and Transnationalism class, I enjoy K-pop and Korean culture in general so the class wasn't too awful but my god there was so much required reading. We did analyze a few episodes of K-Dramas and K-pop music videos so that was fun. She's a pretty hard essay grader and the final was a bit long and tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Req textbook(s), but you can find them free online. GE does most of the grading. Group project and final exam. Prof Kim is very nice and always willing to talk. Grading criteria is a little unclear so it's difficult to understand what she wants, but if you just put in enough work you will get a good score. Depends on GE but often toughish grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At first I thought I was crazy for not understanding the point to any of her lectures and how they related to the course material, but it turns out every other classmate I talked to felt the same way. Tons of reading every week and she would not clearly explain the relation to course material and then expect you to write in depth essays about it.

Professor Kim as an online teacher made the class hard for everyone! She did not have clear instructions (we didn't know what she expected) or an organization and got upset when we didn't understand. Assigned irrelevant readings, and her feedback was never on the content. Would never take any other of her classes it is NOT worth the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is so hard but passable if you show up to class every day. Super caring professor and understanding when I forgot my calculator for the final.
Im gonna be real I couldn't understand half of his lecture with the accent and difference in logic. I did my own work and had to go into office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! Super helpful outside of class. Homework and practice exam are extremely useful for exams. He will prepare you well for both homework and exams. 110% recommend!
Great professor. 11/10 recommend

Ioannis is an amazing prof and really wants students to do well. Always goes over homework questions in class before they are due, and exams are relatively similar to homeworks. He also posts zooms of lectures if you can't make it, and very helpful outside of class. Highly recommend this prof, very knowledgable and caring,

Ioannis was an awesome professor. He is very passionate about finance and makes finance understandable for everyone. Lectures can be boring sometimes, but Ioannis does his best to make it engaging. He goes over HW questions in class and gives bonus questions that can help on the midterm and final. Ioannis is the GOAT.

Branikas is a truly passionate professor who wants his students to succeed. His lectures are genuinely interesting and the tests arent that hard bc he gives amazing formula sheets. I recommend taking FIN316 with him if you want a fun, low workload class. This guy is awesome

Ioannis is so sweet and funny in his lectures. He goes off track frequently but always goes over homework and is very engaging with the class. He always cracks jokes and makes learning about finance more entertaining. The class is only based on 5 HW and midterm, final. He gives bonus opportunities for the homework and curved the tests.
Branikas is the goat.
Best finance professor. Engaging lectures and easy tests. He cracks jokes and makes class entertaining
Awesome teacher who makes me laugh every time im there. Cares about the material and his students.Would love to take every finance class with this teacher. Take him!!

Ioannis is a great professor, and his class allows you to get a pretty solid foundation in finance. He is a funny guy and really likes to engage his class in lectures. He does have a bit of an accent but I didn't really find it too challenging. Manageable weekly HW's and two exams (formula sheet provided).

Such a great young professor. Strong Greek accent but you'll get used to it. Pretty lecture heavy but that's expected, and he is good at lightening the mood and cracking jokes. Super nice guy that's clearly passionate about teaching. He says publicly that he wants to make sure nobody fails. Tests aren't too bad. Take Ioannis!!

He knows the material and teaches it in a way to understand the concepts of FIN 316. He talks fast and is sometimes hard to understand. However, if you do all your homework, there always an option for extra credit, these help when studying for tests.

He has a thick accent and talks fast, but constantly goes over things. He really cares about his students' success. All homework had a 10% extra credit option, and he goes over almost every problem in class almost completely. The midterm and final both have practice tests, formula sheets, and he tells exactly what slides to study before the tests.
Nicest professor ever, genuinely cares so much about the material and the students. Wants you to succeed. Take this class.
Awesome dude! Take his class! Easy A!
The homework is more difficult than test questions. Provided formula sheet for all exams which was incredibly helpful. Very passionate about teaching, makes lectures more enjoyable.

Professor Branikas is a professor who does not leave you to wonder if he is passionate for education. Very enthusiastic and gives one on one help when requested. Will grant extensions if reasonable and communicated, and makes it known what content will be on tests and homework.

Overall great professor, very caring and he explains concepts very thoroughly so that they are easier to understand. He makes sure that there is a lot of optional material so that you can prepare for tests and the tests are heavily based off of problems done in class so if you go to class you will do great!

Ioannis is an overall alright professor. He talks over and over about how students should not cheat in his class, and when one or two students do, the entire class is punished. The final was barely curved even though the average was a 68%. He made the material easy to understand, but his tests were overall too long, with very little time to finish.

Great Professor. Always willing to help. lectures are very informative. He likes to break down concepts, which helps when you dont understand the topic. The only issue I can see is that if you have trouble understanding accents, you will have trouble understanding him. Otherwise, if you get a change definetely take a class from him.
The rating says it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She grades till the last minute. She's super unresponsive when emailing. The homework schedule she makes is very unfair and in class work are pointless. sometimes it helps towards the homework but most of the time is pointless.

A very fun lecturer though the class feels more like doing projects for the sake of doing projects than learning anything. Despite that I would take the class again, it was enjoyable and gave me opportunity to learn about things I was interested for projects.
She hardly ever showed up on time, if at all. If she did, she was usually unprepared, but could lead a discussion well. Better way to spend my tuition money.
Very easy to get along with and does a lot of good group work. Gets the class working together well. Good conversation topics, Uses very nice modern material.

Jiesha is nice and the class was easy but I felt I would have learned with a more involved teacher. She was consistently late and at the end gave EVERYONE a 100% on the Final Project and Participation so it felt like she didn't really try. Course topic is open ended so she focused on black cinema which was great topic and gave lots of good convos.

She is nice and flexible. She genuinely cares and wants her students to learn. But she can be disorganized with classwork and changes outlines of assignments frequently and last minute. Also shows up 5-15 minutes late to 90% of classes which isn't the end of the world but a little frustrating. Overall, she's good and its truly an interesting class.

Love the material, time, and fresh new take on teaching. She lets us have a say in how we want our learning to look, and it is super chill and understanding. It's clear that Stephens cares about what we take away from the material and wants us to enjoy the experience.

Jiesha truly cares about her students. This class explored black cinema. We had weekly discussion posts, one film review essay for a midterm, and a final creative project with a short artist statement. She's also very flexible with deadlines and not a tough grader! I highly recommend her for any course, she's an amazing professor and person.
She's a gem!! One of the best profs I've ever had! Engages with students and actually cares.

I was not a huge fan of his teaching style. It felt like he rushed through every lecture and ended up skipping over a lot of material in his slides. Despite this class having more to do with my career, I actually preferred my PSY 201 class more simply because I didn't really these lectures.

The only bad thing I can say about this class is the Inquizitive. Other than that, Dr. Pennefather's lectures are engaging and the other assignments are not difficult. Even though attendance is not required, go to class if you want to do well on the exams.

307 is taught like a 25 year old man just did shrooms for the first time and learned how life works. If you're conscious at all and already have the ability to think do not take this class. Unless you need something easy that you dont need to show up to. But get ready to learn absolutely nothing -- and do inquizitve.

Overall good psych professor. As long as you study for the midterm/final you'll be fine. They both only account for 20% of your grade. Passionate instructor, and super chill. As long as you do the work an ego to class you'll be fine.

Although I did not favor the textbook used for the course, more specifically, the quizzes, his lectures helped clarify information that I was unable to understand. Thinking assignments are the hardest part of the course if you are lost on how to apply the information learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about the subjects, but its very memorization heavy. The inquizitives are really annoying and most of the homework seems like busy work, but you can get 100% almost all of the time. But as long as you show up for participation points and do the homework, you'll be fine.

Overall, this class was great and it ultimately makes it much easier if you actually attend class. There is a bit of busy work but 2 of the weekly assignments are done in class and half the time we ended up skipping questions on them. 1 midterm and 1 final (70 questions) and 1 essay made up most of the grade and all were straightforward and simple
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His test are really hard and is solely focused on the textbook which doesn't make sense because you don't have a clear understanding on what to study. His essay for this was is very unclear and he doesn't give you a rubric. He is not very understanding when you try to talk to him about clarifying questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Second class with Jordan, and genuinely the worst professor I've had at UO by so far. Class was taught by 2 GEs and Jordan and they were all on different pages about material. My all-Honors kids class was LOST- sent an announcement that said "Office Hours is not to discuss the homework".. what. Literally avoid at all costs. Was harder than Ochem

Pennefather is a great teacher and knows what he is doing. It is a 400-level class so be prepared, but the prof is great. He is very straightforward about the content, teaches it well and is clear about what you need to do to learn well and get a good grade. I would def. recommend, but only if you are prepared to work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer, textbook wasn't too bad but the tests were pretty hard. If you're good at memorization and go to class, you'll be fine. He has like no office hours available so reach out to GEs. Very interesting content but not the easiest grade.

The amount of work is unnecessary, the  midterm and final both had 70 questions on top of a final paper. The lectures felt uninteresting. I have had this professor prior and the class was not that bad but 307 was the absolute worst. Additionally, if you work multiple jobs or are dealing with extenuating circumstances, he does not care.

The class was okay. Same with the professor. He really does care about the materials and likes to get the class involved in the lectures. His tests are annoying because there are multiple correct answers to one answer. The homework can get to be a lot, and the discussions are useless. But overall i have learned a lot in his class.

I am personally not a fan of this professor and is methods. I have had several classes with him. For this class, he gives an ungodly amount of busy work, and the midterm was 70 multiple choice questions which was outrageous. He also assigned a full paper, 2 collaboration assignments, 2 inquizitives, and a reading response all in one week.

Cultural psych could be an interesting class if it was taught by someone else. The grading instructions are unclear, with grading of the tests being based on how he would have worded the answers. Professor doesn't know the answers to his own study guide. Avoid if you can.

Had him for PSY306, and was great. I have him for 459, and this is the worst class I've taken at UO. Lectures are just a recite of information, test was completely what he thought was "the most right," and upon asking him, received no feedback. One of the profs that things are only right if they're "his way" and is petty if you question it. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are willing to put in the effort, this class is a breeze. The lectures aren't the most exciting, but if you're willing to attend they are super helpful. His teaching criteria and grading is clear, only gives one midterm and one final.
I've had this prof for multiple classes and he is great. Pretty straightforward guy who makes assignments clear. Coursework may be challenging but he prepares you for it

I also had Dr. Pennefather for PSY 306, I have had a good experience with him. His lectures, although they go fast, are interesting, and the slides are very well organized and pair well with the textbook reading. The study guides are helpful for the exams and the essay criteria is clear, I definitely would take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a G, very good lectures, made math simple!

Overall a good professor just very slow to listen to. For PSY 202, the reading was what was on the midterm and final and there was very little of the information actually talked about during the lectures.

Dr. Pennefather is a good guy and teacher. However, the class had a pretty heavy workload and was stressful at times. Lectures are not mandatory, but I absolutely recommend attending them. The material is covered quickly and it is easy to miss a lot in one day, plus they are usually interesting (depends on your interest in research methods).
Not very helpful when asking questions, didn't give feedback on paper. Lectures make 0 sense. Don't take his class!
Unfair grader. Unclear lectures. Avoid.

Jordan is a great professor! I found his lectures to be very interesting and engaging. There isn't too much homework and the tests may be a little difficult, but as long as you study you'd be fine. I definitely recommend taking this class.

I was slightly worried when taking this class with him, but it was actually pretty nice. Was doing well in the class until the midterm, but I think that was more of a me issue than his teaching. He is slightly intimidating when I went to office hours, but other than that, I haven't had any issues. Just study well for the midterm and final.

This is the first time I had Pennefather as a professor and I have to say he is one of my favorite PSY professors I have had. He is engaged during class and makes lecture's something that is easy to listen to. I think it it also helpful that he uses examples to teach. Overall good teacher for PSY 306. As long as you study for tests you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jordan is excited about statistics and this shows in his teaching style. He does often go through lecture slides very quickly, though, and new concepts were thrown at the class in almost every lecture (after the basic review). The labs were super helpful for assignments, but expect to spend quite a bit of time on homework for this class every week.

Prof. Pennefather had really great lectures that were clear and had all the necessary information to do well in the class. The content of the course was pretty hard, but there were usually curves on all of the tests that helped everyone's scores. I would take his class again!

One of the worst profs I have ever had, his lectures make absolutely no sense, he goes through slides so fast and whenever someone asks a question it seems to be an inconvenience. His GE's are really nice but even they do not know how to interpret his lectures and the way he teaches. Legit take any other professor for this class pls
The class is organized very well and as long as you pay attention and do the homework, you will get a good grade. Go to lab, it really helps!

The rudest professor I've had at UO. Makes you feel so stupid for not understanding SUPER hard material. Literally publicly embarrasses you in front of the class for asking a question by being so condescending and rude. Does not care at all about students. Don't take him if you're looking to be taught by a nice, understanding teacher.

Pennefather is definately one of the WORSE professors I've had, almost changed my major. He goes really fast through slides and is passive aggressive and condencending when you ask questions. You're better off asking the GEs, going to tutoring thats offered or forming a study group. If you wanna understand any of the material.

Cold, and does indeed make you feel very unintelligent if you ask clarifying questions. Recommend taking anyone else for 302. Rely on your GEs as much as you can. Do not bother asking him questions directly, he will get obviously annoyed and it was off-putting. Lab hardly applies to lecture, APA style will hardly be covered, so ask GEs for APA help

Pennefather is cold, condescending and unhelpful if you ask him questions. I am really confused and have tried to get help but he didn't help at all and makes you feel stupid. Attendance isn't required which is nice but you will fall behind so quickly. This is def the hardest class I have taken at the UO

JUST DONT TAKE PSY301 IF U DONT HAVE TO. as a gen-ed, NO. such boring material istg. quizzes & tests worded TERRIBLY tbh. questions could be so much more straightforward. the avg score for the midterm was 75%. that says enough. also hardest essay to write just cuz of how boring it was to do. he rly tried his best, but bro.... :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great professor. He made an 8:30 lecture as entertaining as he could, and I would definitely take this class again. Super communicative. Grading standards and expectations in the class were very clear.

This is my second time taking a class with him and I love it. His grading expectations are super clear and his assignments are easy to complete and follow through. He gives a reasonable amount of time to complete the research papers and all the other assignments as well. I also loved the weekly discussions cause the topics were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Instead of taking the time to thoroughly explain difficult concepts, he let's us out earlier, which, although it makes it easier on him to teach, it makes it harder on kids to learn. Always acts like you're bugging him when your confused or have a question about the material, my least favorite teacher at U of O so far.

Even though the class was web, I could tell he's a kind and very understandable teacher. Most of the assignments are ZAPS and INQUIZITIVE which were super easy as long as you read the instructions and read the readings/materials in the textbook beforehand. Definitely recommend the online textbook to search up keywords. Super easy class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: PSY was just boring; the lectures were not engaging. He often used them from Youtube. The study guide is very long, and the tests and quiz questions were quite difficult; you must do the readings to understand the FULL material that will be on the test. I didn't do any reading...I just skimmed and got C- on both of my tests...

Dr. Pennefather is amazing. While there were a lot of lectures, they were easy to follow and not difficult to understand. The exams weren't tough, but you do need to study. There were only 2-3 assignments per week: a textbook assignment, sometimes a lab, and a discussion post. He's a great communicator and has very clear expectations.

Very organized, responds quickly, and gives great lectures. Handled the transition to online because of COVID-19 very well and succeeded in keeping the class very interesting. He has clear expectations and is very nice and helpful. Super easy A if you do the work and keep up on reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Pennefather for social psych. The class was super interesting and applicable to every part of life, which was super cool. Final wasn't cumulative and midterm and final were both very fair and mostly had lecture stuff on them (but I'd still read the textbook). He also gave really clear expectations for the essay which wasn't bad.

His Personality class was great! Definitely an easy A as far as upper divisions go. Lectures were interesting enough and the exams were very fair. There's one paper that has super easy to follow instructions and like 8 short response homework assignments and that's it. He's kind, laidback, and very respectful of questions. Would recommend!

Really kind with clear lectures and expectations. Midterm and final are somewhat hard with some tricky questions, make sure to read the textbook because not all midterm and final questions are covered in lecture, which he is open about. Still, engaging and very funny, and passionate about his field. Would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The midterm and final were honestly incredibly tough but since the class has many other things that factor into the final grade it is not too difficult to get a decent grade in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pennefather is the kind of person who makes you wonder why he went into teaching. He acts like every question is a stupid one and every student is a delinquent. He can't admit when he's wrong and will get defensive instead; he also doesn't seem to feel he should be accountable to students for guaranteeing fair and consistent grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jordan seems like a good guy which makes this review harder but overall I thought he was a very poor professor. Having two midterms, one final, two papers, seven reading quizzes, and required attendance is extremely excessive for a class with fairly simple content. His lectures also seem disorganized and unproductive.

Jordan is a GREAT lecturer but otherwise fell flat. During office hours he was rude and brusque. He enjoys trick questions designed to trip you up rather than test your knowledge. He took FOREVER to grade things, to the point where you have to almost finish Paper B before receiving feedback on Paper A, so you have no frame of reference for success.

A lot of work for an online course. Every week there are 4 lecture videos, each about 15 mins long and BORING, a quiz, 2 discussion posts, and 1-2 extra assignments. There is no clear rubric for the essay. Midterm and final are long but pretty straight forward. DOES NOT CURVE the class or any tests AT ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Pennefather is a good teacher. He is enjoyable to listen too and trys to make lectures more intersting. However, the lectures are very long and tend to get boring. Midterm and Final is pretty hard so be ready to study and pay attention.

Great guy. Easily one of the best professors i've had. The lectures are very long and do get boring but he does his best to keep the class interesting. Midterm and final are very lengthy so you will need to study but they're also very straightforward. Overall, very easy class.
The lectures are pretty boring and he uses the whole hour and 50 minutes, but he is nice. STUDY for the exams, they are nothing like his lectures. Homework is easy and lab is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's a big class so it mainly relies on lecture, he keeps it engaging and quick. As long as you do the homework and remember the main points for the tests you can pass fairly easily.

He's one of the best professors I've had in my college experience. I loved his lectures, they kept me engaged and helped me remember terms just by the lecture being so memorable. Really recommend this teacher. His grading criteria are well defined too, so writing papers for him goes a lot smoother than other professors make it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken his PSY 202, 307, and 306 and he is awesome! His lectures are upbeat and passionate, which makes them fun and interesting, and almost every other psychology student that I know loves him. His tests are usually long (60 multiple choice questions) but fair game, with material coming mostly from his lectures

I've taken 2 courses with him so far (202 and 302) and athough he is a good professor, his classes feel like a waste of time because he spends way too much time letting you work on problems in class with groups, grades on iclicker attendance, and then tests on more way harder versions of what you learned. it's not a very intense lecture. Go to lab!

Long two-hour lectures which are usually boring but make sure to take notes on the slides for the midterm and test. The tests are multiple choice and are pretty straightforward. The iClicker questions are useful for the test and are graded on participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Slides is barely related to exam.... No study guide... Only have midterm and final but they are extremely hard!!!!!

I have taken two classes with Professor Pennefather and he is one of the best psych teachers I have ever had. He cares about the students and incorporates funny examples so information is more relatable. He's really funny and answers questions well and responds quickly to emails and gives great advice about grad school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is also good at teaching for Non-native Speaker.

Jordan is a great professor. For it being a 2 hour lecture class, he tries to make the class as lively and active as possible. Clicker questions are also not graded on correctness, only for participation. GO TO CLASS! Participation is 15% of your grade so go! But he will not curve or bump. I ended the class with a 89.9 and he didn't give me the A-.

I had Jordan last term for PSY 202 and I thought he was a really awesome professor! Miraculously, I ended up getting 105% in the course after the midterm and final were curved down! I have him for PSY 302 now and he's really knowledgeable with Statistics. Funny guy and definitely really helpful!

Pretty easy class. Show up too class and you will easily pass. Barely cracked the book open and didnt really study and ended up with a solid grade. Rack up your points with all the homework, quizzes and participation since there are only 2 tests and he curves them. Overall, good professor, but the lectures are way too long, but its an easy class.

He's lecture is boring, boring, and boring. You have to stay there for 2 hours just for your participation points. No break between 2 hour lecture literally killing me. However, it is easy to get a good grade in his class as long as you did the homework and prepared for  the test. Thats' it.
Easy A
Jordan is a clear and sufficient prof. He's not exceedingly charismatic or funny, but he explains the course concepts well. Jordan is a safe bet as a prof for this course.

Pennefather was interactive and gave a variety of material in lectures. He presented data, graphs, excerpts from different sources like interviews, videos and more. This is a larger class but he worked with it the best he could. I would recommend going to lectures and reading. He was also very responsive to questions in class and email.

Jordan is a great professor, I have also taken psy 302 with him. His lectures are very straight forward, posts slides online. Study guides are pretty long but very useful and his tests are not cumulative. Very nice and easy going. As long as you study and go to class with some frequency you should do fine.

Jordan is a fantastic professor. He makes his lectures interesting by engaging with his students. He stops after the end of each section in the lecture to ask if anyone has any questions. He is very humorous and has a great overall teaching quality.

The class was a great intro to psych and the professor was fantastic. The lectures were long but the professor has a good sense of humor and really tried to engage students. The class was also very consistent for students that like that. I always went to class knowing exactly what we would be doing that day. Overall a great professor!

I like Jordan. He keeps lectures interesting with videos and media clips that pertain to what we are learning. He is organized and is a very fair grader. Gives random points out for showing up to class. MT and Final-not cumulative. Go to class and you will be fine. Nice guy.
Very, straight foward. Homework is more difficult than tests.

He's alright but lectures were basically repeat of what was in the textbook. If you take a class from him, take social psych, not cultural psych, because he's more interested in that. Study guides are misleading so just study everything, not just what's in the guide. He's not very personable nor mean, just kinda neutral
He is funny and organized.

He is a great professor. Frequently uses videos and examples to facilitate teaching. Keeps class engaged by doing mini-social psychology experiments on them. Great in office hours and very nice. Easily one of the best psych teachers at the school
He is nice and somewhat entertaining. Pretty easy if you stay on top of all the due dates.

Jordan was an awesome professor! He really keeps you interested in the lecture and speaks the same jargon as most college students. Although attendance wasn't mandatory, it was much needed (and interesting). Very highly recommend this professor!

I really enjoyed this class and the way professor McGee structured it. The material consisted of readings and videos that were very engaging. The course drastically improved my writing skills as well. Would 100% recommend both professor McGee and this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor McGee is pretty good. There were only 4 assignments - 2 journals & 2 papers, so you have to do well on each to do well in the class. However, if you do the readings and at least show up to class, you should be relatively okay. Its pretty fast paced and he doesnt really use slides (or post when he does) so you gotta take notes fast!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You're only graded by 2 journals and 2 take home exams but if you read the articles and books it's not bad at all. One of the easiest classes I've taken at UO, I only went to class once. He said he makes it so you can do everything online. Highly recommend!

Professor McGee is truly one of the best professors I had at UO. His lectures are fast paced but very engaging because he is so passionate about what he teaches. The content is relevant and thought provoking. I learned so much from his class and he's the type of professor you remember even when you're far out of college.
Great professor. Very knowledgable. Fast talker. Loves questions.
He was very kind, cares a lot about what he is teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's a total of 4 assignments, 2 journals, a midterm, and a final. The majority of the percentage comes from the journals which are easy to fill out when you attend the lecture. But even if you don't go, you can talk about the online readings. Overall, amazing teacher, really smart, and most importantly, understanding.

Prof. McGee is extremely smart and is passionate about his subject. There are very few assignments, 2 journals and 2 essay exams, (1 Final essay if taking 516). His lectures are more talk at you rather than slides or even notes. It is discussion based but he does most of the talking. There are several readings to do each week but not needed to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class only has four assignments, two of those being the midterm and final. I sometimes found myself zoning out during the lectures because he often talks without a projection to take notes from. His passion is very clear though and the topic was very engaging because of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is amazing! His class is super easy but so interesting! 100% would recommend taking his class.

He is passionate and his lectures are very interesting. He has 2 exams (40%) and 2 journals (60%) that you are graded on. You have a week to work on the exams, they are open note and he allows you to work with others. I would highly recommend taking this class. The topics are also very very interesting!

John Park is great. supportive, passionate, and genuinely caring. However, the Art and Technology program itself does not prepare students for the job market. The skills taught are niche, experimental, and rarely applicable to most real-world roles. Students seeking career-ready, industry-relevant skills should look elsewhere or heavily self-teach.

I had John Park for 251, 252, and 370. The classes can be a lot of work, especially 370, but so incredibly rewarding. John is so kind and communicative, and even though I'm not the biggest fan of coding, he revived that passion in me. Could not recommend him more :-)

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! John is the reason that I switched into Art & Tech. Smart, kind, & wants his students to succeed. If you show up & give 100% you will not only pass, but actually learn valuable skills. I hope everyone can have one professor like John. I came into college not knowing any code, & now I can say that it is one of my fav mediums.

Lectures are very interesting and fun to listen to, I actually enjoyed going to them. Class basically consists of going to lab and following along with the TA for most assignments. 3 projects for the whole time and they are interesting but time consuming. As long as you put forth the effort you'll get an A, basically if you turn it in you get an A.

Hands down best professor I've had at Oregon. John is a great guy who understands how college aged people learn and engage in projects. If you show up, you will succeed. When instructing, he will take time to make sure everyone is caught up no matter how advanced the material is. John's classes are the reason I go to class actually excited to learn
John Park was an amazing professor! His lectures were engaging and interesting. I would take his class again.
FAVORITE professor at UO! I created this account because I wanted to get his rating up. Do yourself a favor and take one of his classes!
John is a fantastic professor with relevant topics that connect to the course material. The assignments and projects were fun to do and easy when it came to grading.

John Park is awesome!! His lectures are super interesting and involve relevant information. I loved going to his lectures and really enjoyed the class. Explains information perfectly and is understanding in terms of classwork. I highly recommend his class and would love to give him a huge-thanks, as he inspired me to get into more coding based Art.
