John is the coolest professor ever. Dude knows his stuff, is kind, patient, and always willing to help you. If you ever aren't sure about coding, " tech " stuff; definitely be communicative with him and he'll have your back. I took three of his courses and he was AMAZING. 11/10 recommend if you can take his class, DO IT.
Whoever said John park didn’t make it needs to stop projecting their own issues cuz he’s bomb and a hunk

His classes are probably the only organized art and tech classes in the program. Great programmer , but can also teach programming to an idiot. Everyone in the class does well and works hard. peaceful dude overall.

Amazing teacher, explains everything very well and down to the simplest concept. You must show up to office hours if you don't understand something, but as long as you pay attention and follow along, you will pass. Super interesting lecture videos as well. John was one of the best professors I've had, true goat material.

John Park is probably the most genuinely nice person I have ever met. He is super caring and will go out of his way to help you succeed. In his classes, your time and effort are valued. If you are willing to work hard, he will always meet you in the middle.

I've taken a few classes with Park and have come to this:  Get ready to learn.  Relevant, fresh, inspirational content. He's a genius and the programs he knows, he knows inside and out. Puts his whole heart into teaching.  Does not put his whole heart into students/work/personally. Painfully attractive.  Amazing human being. Best teacher at UO.

Loved this class! Lectures are super boring but it is only once a week. Projects are most important, there is 3. Just do the best to your ability and you'll get an A. They do not grade on how great the projects are but on how much effort you put in. Follow all the guidelines! Reading Responses are a waste of time though.

J Park is an awesome teacher. He caters his lectures to what interests the students, and he offers specific workshops (wiimote, xbox video hacking, arduino) for those who actually want to learn it. He really cares about helping students grow and follow their interest. This is the only lecture class ive beenexcited to go. Best teacher at UO

John is the epitome of "if you can't make it, teach". The weekly lectures are nothing more than TED talks. That's fine and all, but the lecture has nothing to do with the homework or labs. If it weren't for his occasional attendance, I wouldn't have gone to the lecture class.
doesn't do a lot of teaching, kind of talks about random stuff. most of the computer skills you just have to teach yourself.

He is very good at teaching how to, and he makes tutorials for each section and those are amazingly helpful. His example in the lecture is fun and very spicy too. Always there is new inspiration of creativity.....and he is very cute<3 haha

His examples are always clear, and he hosted a lot of excellent labs (including a wiiMote hack!) Very easygoing, and his projects challenge you to be creative. He's why the UO Digital Arts dept is so good!
He's great. Who DOESN'T like John Park? He can be kind of vague but he makes class enjoyable and he uses time well.

Very entertaining and engaging lectures. Fun projects, but require time and concentration if you are not used to certain computer programs. He is really, really attractive and nerdy at the same time! Wonderful class.
He's really knowledgeable and enthusiastic, as well as nerdy and adorable. Super cute and makes the class  exponentially more amusing and enjoyable.
Favorite teach by far! Lectures were very informative and entertainnig at the same time. Showed really cool videos and shared interesting websites.

Hey always showed us entertaining videos in class and was always willing to help you and answer questions. He gives lots of good examples before we start on a project. Not to mention he is absolutely gorgeous. ha ha
Absolutely awesome teacher. Totally easy-going, and covers an interesting variety of material, brings a fresh and youthful vibe to the subject. Definitely convinced me to major in Digital Arts.

Professor McCole is amazing. He was always willing and happy to discuss things further outside of class, and he genuinely cares about the intellectual development of his students. There is a good amount of reading and the concepts can be challenging, and there is an in-class graded midterm. Otherwise, the class was not too hard.
German Intellectual History was a phenomenal class to take, with moving themes woven into every lecture. I would highly recommend it to anybody interested in Marxism and the rise of fascism.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man is a treasure. Very knowledgeable and remains passionate about his areas of study. I loved his old school approach to daily lectures and long essay assignments though I have spoken to (younger) classmates who did not prefer his style. Weekly quiz answers easily found in slides and texts. Attendance is mandatory ~once/week for discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very Good, take his classes

John McCole is my favorite professor by far, however, tough grader! He gives great lectures, and they're crucial to understanding the course material. Participation in class bumped my final grade up, so try to prep for discussions and raise your hand when you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McCole was so nice, and I found that he really knew how to give a lecture! He uses language that is easy to understand and EXPLAINS history, not just by reading slides to us. There were no tests, and the midterm and final were just as the study guide. His essay and book review were given plenty of time to complete. I definitely would recommend it!

Half discussion, half lecture. Discussion questions are tough and the readings are long and dense, so the discussion days can be painful. The midterm and final are super straightforward, he gives you a study guide. The essay is time-consuming but he grades it fairly. Lectures are sorta dry, but he cares about the material a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McCole is probably one of my favorite history professors at UO. During this term I was extremely sick, and McCole not only showed compassion but allowed for flexibility within the course that I greatly appreciated. Overall his lectures were engaging and interesting even though it was a topic that I didn't initially think I would enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Good teacher, packs lots of info into short lectures so be ready to take notes. Quizzes weekly that are very easy if you attend class. Midterm and Final cover the material from about the previous 2-3 weeks and aren't bad. Term paper is a book review 6-8 pages in length and was very easy to complete. Overall a good teacher, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was set up to be half lecture, half discussion days. He explained things thoroughly in lecture and checked in with us often. The readings can be dense, but his reading questions help guide you. 2 exams and 2 papers (4-5 pgs), just make sure you take good notes. He clearly cares about what he teaches and the students' experiences in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McCole made the study of modern European history very fascinating. His lectures are never dry and he always encourages participation amongst the students. There were two 4-5 page papers to write along with a midterm and final exam. He graded fairly, but there is certainly a lot of reading to keep up on (70-100 pages a week).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I first want to mention that I took McCole's course during quarantine. As an online teacher, it's extremely evident that he puts effort in with his students. His lectures are extremely interesting and informative, although there are a lot of them. He's dedicated to what he does, kind to his students, and cares about our learning experience. 11/10

OMG i love this guy! I met with him out of class and he totally loves if you come to see him like brownie points! Does require lots of reading but he's super understanding, the finals aren't TOO bad but definitely prepare for them. His lectures are great and he's very passionate. Taking another class with him because I love him!

If you don't like dense reading, don't take the class.  McCole is an awesome teacher and clearly cares about the material, but I was not prepared for the amount of reading he assigned and the amount of information he tested us on.  Readings are so important and the class definitely requires a lot of outside studying to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the subject. Clearly wants to be there and helpeducate students. Not much to the course itself, just study hard for the exams (provides study guides) and work hard on the papers. Papers are a bit more confusing as sometimes they are either not relating to lecture material. Great course overall. Would recommend.

I recently took history 303 and 410 with McCole and although parts of the classes were challenging,they were intrigueing, and he used the class time well.There wasn't much homework, but the tests are somewhat challenging.McCole is an excellent professor and is always willing to help students. I highly recommend him.
I really enjoyed his teaching style, his interest in his students, and the clarity of his lectures

McCole is amazing, and probably one of the best dressed professors at Oregon. But in all seriousness he knows his stuff and explains it so well that everyone understands,. I did hardly any of the reading and got a B. The GTF for the class was a chill bone too,
good, funny teacher. makes information easy to understand. extremely helpful when you go to his office hours for help

A very good lecturer who uses powerpoint. The textbook that he used in history 301 was short, precise, and excellent. Additional readings were a bit hairy and long. I got an A- in the class and can tell you that you have to do all of the reading in the textbook and 80% of the additional readings to do well.

Very knowledgable professor, has the ability to make the difficult material interesting and accessible.  He is always willing to talk outside of class in office hours, and always works to help the student understand the material.  I reccomend this taking a class from McCole.
A nice guy, really knows the subject, the reading can be a little dense, but his classes are worth it.  Interesting and very educational.
Doesnt use Canvas but instead runs everything through his own third party website. Is disrespectful in emails and unhelpful to students with question about his course or the work within the course.

You do not really do anything. Currently he is suffering from medical issues and commonly doesn't hold class. I assume he is retiring soon, so these issues will persist in any classes he teaches moving forward. You dont learn much in class, kinda felt like we got robbed of a course that should have been educational.
It's an easy class, but the professor is very mean in emails and not helpful at all. Every email I sent professionally, I was responded to with a one-line just blatantly mean response.
Very online class, but also very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The negative reviews are COMPLETELY unwarranted. The professor has a genuine love for astronomy which is VERY clear in lecture. The lecture notes contain lots of information to help with the quizzes and exams. The complaints about his website are simply wrong. It is incredibly easy to navigate and not hard to track. Fun jokes, and an amazing class.

DO NOT. Take this mans classes if you can help it. He uses a completely different, janky website for literally everything; lectures are unfathomably long, drawn out, and go on rambles that dont mean anything; says there is no textbook required, but all test/quiz material pulls from the book instead of lectures.

I went into this class thinking it was going to be awful because of what people said about him on here. He doesn't waste time and often lets us out early. I really enjoyed it and I intentionally chose him as my professor again for my next term of astronomy because I like his teaching style so much. He was also very funny.

DO NOT; he doesn't care for his students, does not have in-person office hours, and will reject you if you go up to him and ask him about the material in the class. He gives the bare minimum effort in person and can't even take the time to spell-check his tests and exams. The weekly tests have NOTHING to do with the exams.
Do NOT take this course, lectures did not correlate with quizzes or exams. He had no office hours and didn't use Canvas. Please just take another course!!!

He is unaccommodating towards students and doesn't care about your success in the class. When people emailed him about missing the quizzes, he got annoyed, and he threatened that the next person to email him would drop a percentage of a letter grade. Said he wouldn't believe our "excuses" for missing the quizzes. Overall, super rude and unfunny.

Schombert is a bitter professor who is unwilling to work with students based on their needs. His website is not connected to Canvas making the course extremely difficult to keep up with and stay organized in. His communication was aggressive and unsympathetic. As an ASTR prof., he should know best that the world does not revolve around him!

Schombert has some of the worst communication skills I have seen from any professor I've had at the UO in 3 years. He teaches from his own website with minimal connection to Canvas which is super frustrating. When you miss one of the quizzes (which there are no reminders set for) he is very harsh about the consequences. Not an enjoyable class.

This was probably the weirdest physics class that I've taken thus far at UO. Grading was just decided off of the homework assignments, but there weren't really deadlines or specific grading criteria (the questions were decently hard but he would help with them). Nice guy, has a lot of interesting knowledge, but the class is mostly in the homework.
This professor is0/10, would never EVER take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had the worst experience in this class, even when I put in the effort the quizzes and the lectures didn't match at all. He had no office hours and was very unapproachable. The grading system is really weird and I wasted a P/F when I had a B+. Save yourself the stress and take another class.

When registering for Schombert's class I was extremely worried due to the overwhelmingly negative reviews he seems to have, but I absolutely adored the HC 441 class I took with Schombert. He is truly a very funny guy (some jokes are on the fence of being okay and I hope he changes that at some point). His lectures were fascinating and inspiring

Prof Schombert is a great teacher who is enthusiastic about astronomy and has taken the time to break difficult topics down to supermarket math. Attending lectures and doing the homework should be enough to ace the tests. Also offered me guidance that ended up landing me a job.
Extremely unsympathetic when communicating and was not flexible. Class was extremely difficult and taught on a separate page that was built in the dark ages

The lectures were COMPLETELY unrelated to the quizzes. He was rude, and I had to drop the class because there was no way to study for the midterm. The material and lectures given NEVER related to the quizzes! He also doesn't hold office hours to get help if you need it (which you would because nothing makes sense). DO NOT take this class.
Terrible communication skills with students and the design of the class is horrendous. The class is still run off an abyss blog from what looks like 2005.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this as an online course and lectures were vague at best and don't prepare you for quizzes and assignments at all. Quizzes are way more detailed than what he lectures about including a lot amount of calculations. For an intro level course, it's quite difficult and spend more time working on this class than upper division chem and math classes

For an online, asynchronous course this was horrible. He did not provide any office hours. There are about 2-4 quizzes a week and 3 tests over the term. Look for quizlets to help with the quizzes and then just hope for the best for those tests. There are better professors for astronomy. Do not put yourself through it. Not worth it.
Take it if you want depression

I am here to warn anyone away from ever taking this man's class. By no means, ever, should one subject themselves to this. The material is tough, but what makes his class hard is the complete unwillingness to help from Schombert himself. No office hours, and the most you get in an email is to look at the lecture again. Save yourselves as I can't.
Tests are NOTHING like the quizzes given
Horrible. He's rude and condescending. Well taught class but I do not like him as a person. He there to get paid not to help out the student.

He grades on a curve. I got a gross f and a net b. If that doesnt tell you how hard the class is, I dont know what will. The subject material is very broad and challenging. It includes everything from chemistry to quantum physics. That said, Schombert is extremely smart and interesting. Dont go into the class expecting to ace every test though!

He is a brilliant astronomer but is terrible at teaching it to beginning students. This is an intro class and he spoke to us as if we are in a 400 level class. His class is so broad and his test have such specific questions. They are IMPOSSIBLE to study for. He does 100 multiple choice question tests. I failed all of them. Most people feel the same
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! This is the hardest class I have ever taken. I read the reviews before taking the class and I thought I could do it. I thought that the people that found his class hard were lying. It turns out that they were right this class is so hard. I have put many hours into the class and I am still failing the class.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. I went into this course interested in learning about space. The teacher gives out the hardest exams I have ever seen and I HIGHLY recommend to never take a course taught by Mr. Schombert.

This teacher is amazing. I currently have an A in the class and even if my grade drops by that time I am still confident in saying he is one of the best teachers I've had. The material is challenging and invaluable to any individual who takes science seriously. I've spent more time on the material in his class than I have in any other class. 10/10.

This professor is obviously a highly intelligent person, but his intellect does not translate into teaching ability. Instead, Dr. Schombert airs on the side of expecting students taking an introductory level astronomy class to dedicate themselves to his material, regardless of its relevancy to any other aspect of life or study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The dude cant even respond to an email without being snarky and rude. Dont put yourself through this. Id give him a zero if I could.

The 100 question exams are impossible to study for as you are just thrown random information at you and there is no way to memorize it all. I scored a 47, 52, and 50 on each exam and got a B in the class because I found the answers for the quizzes and it was curved so hard. There is no point in showing up. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS- seriously, this is by far the worst class I have ever taken. I am a straight-A student but this class is set up to ensure you fail. The quizzes contain math he never talks about, the tests are unreasonably hard- I have failed every single test like every other student yet he has to curve it 40% so some students will pass.

Worst person ever. In all my years of school I have never had a professor who hated teaching. Doesn't actually go over what is on his lectures. Doesn't use canvas probably because he thinks it is beneath him. RATES his students after the first exam so that if you are the worst in the class you will know it. Very arrogant. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES.

His online course is ridiculous. He says any edition of the book works, but we must check the lec. and topic line up (when we won't know what the topic is). His tests are barely relevant to the material and he won't use Canvas. His lectures are 10 min and extremely vague. Resources are not clear on what to use them for or when they are needed.

This is the WORST class and professor I have ever with in all my years of education. Rude, stubborn, and arrogant don't even begin to explain his attitude any time you approach him personally to ask a question. He refuses to use Canvas, a system which I PAY for through my tuition. He consistently tests on content that is much too difficult fr a 100

I did not like this professor or his class at all. He is late most classes, just reads off lecture slide, doesn't take the time to talk to students, and when you do reach out, he is rude and belittling. Would not recommend to any students looking for an easy A or an interesting prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I hate this professor. I took ASTR 123 my freshman year and he stressed me out so much. This class was useless because he just read the content of his website and then handed us 100 question tests 3x throughout the term. Also had quizzes every week, just about the reading (which was just stuff that he would read to us from his website in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I have never been more frustrated with a professor in my life. This class is set up to have people fail. This teacher doesnt care about his students and every interaction ive had with him he has almost dismissed me and made me feel like my questions were not important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hes probably the worst teacher on campus. Went to his office hours first week for him to explain a concept to me and he basically dismissed me as if I was an inferior wasting his time. NEVER TAKE A CLASS HE TEACHES

Understood the lectures, but the quizzes and tests were extremely hard and most of the lecture slides had nothing to do with the quizzes. My mother, who is a college instructor, even she said the class is not worth the money to take and we are quite literally set up to fail. Hes a nice guy and very funny, but the tests are hard to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This professor is quite literally the worst, he has a reputation at the university for being difficult. He doesn't care about students and will not even give you the time of day if you ask him. I appreciate his honesty but his lack of care for his students is astounding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The fact that his class is graded so heavily speaks to how difficult the class is. He has 100 question tests that are supposed to be finished in 50 minutes. This only gave me 30 seconds per question, which isn't enough to actually think critically about what the answer is. Also starts the tests at different times than class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His tests are absolutely insane, and he gave NO information about what would be on the tests prior to taking them. His lecture slides are incredibly dense, and it's literally impossible to memorize everything he expects you to know for the test. In my class a D curved to an A, which shows just how little help or guidance he extends to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor makes class unreasonably difficult. His tests are 100 questions long, but he only gives 50 minutes to accomplish them, which is obviously not enough time to think critically about the questions at all. He also starts the tests 30 mins before class starts, which is unfair to students with class beforehand. Gives ZERO test prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: this teacher is such a jerk, he uses his own rating system for class and accuses every student of cheating if they do well on all of the online quizzes. he uses an outside website and only reads from the website when in class, so prepare to get very bored and space out. after taking the test he gives you a placement number in his class.

He doesn't let you know when big exams are and I missed the final because he didn't tell us it wouldn't be on the finals schedule. It was before finals and I didn't know because the dates were online on his stupid website. Also the fact he has to curve the exams 40% shows the students don't know anything from his teaching.

If you think this is going to be an easy class, you shouldn't take it. The class was very interesting to me and I did well in it because I paid attention in class, studied, and put in a good amount of effort. Every class is a lecture but he knows the subject well enough to just talk about it. Difficult class but worth it if you like science
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The worst and most boring teacher I have ever had in my life. I engaged with him twice throughout the term and both times he kind of just shrugged me off. The whole class he paces back and forth with his hands behind his back reading the lecture off the big screen. If there was a stereotypical "I know everything and you don't" professor it'd be him
The tests are hard and don't pay for study blue to help you with the quizzes that are online.

This teacher is really arrogant. I went to his office hours to ask for guidance and he basically told me to leave. He doesn't teach the subject well enough to grasp the material he expects you to know. If you are not scientifically minded, take another class to satisfy that general ed credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: As long as you go to class as much as possible and keep up on the weekly quizzes from the reading (with the curve) you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Please, never take a class with Schombert. He manages to make the most interesting subject extremely boring. He just stands at the front of class and talks for two hours, never engaging the students. The subject matter is confusing and he clearly knows quite a bit about it, but is so awful at teaching it. I have never failed a class but this one.

This professor is horrible. He is stubborn and arrogant. When I approached him to talk about my testing accommodations through the university, he said he didn't know and didn't care. That is more than an attitude adjustment, it is against the law. I dropped the class and talked to the department head and reported his behaviour.

There are 3 extremely difficult exams, each comprised of 100 questions. You do not get to use notes. I did the recommended reading, read the lecture slides, got decent (A-B) on the online quizzes, and went to most classes. Yet I still averaged 40100 on the exams. Hardest class I've taken here at the UO. It's essential Astro Physics. I warned you!
Lectures are just old powerpoints and not very clear.

Only take this class if you want to fail. Tests are super hard and have nothing to do with what you read in the book, the tests are NOT open book and are 100 questions long. The grade average for the class is a D. He pretty much tells you in the beginning of the term that half the class won't pass, so there's that.

The material was hard to keep up with and the math was hard to follow. He will say it once then that's it, if you don't ask. He's really funny, but it's hard. Attendance is mandatory ONLY if you want to pass. Everything is on a curve.

I think Dr. Schombert does a great job teaching this class. His tests are difficult, but he grades on a curve which makes it pretty easy to pass. I like how difficult the class is, it makes me feel like I'm getting more for my money and I know that I will have a better understanding of Astronomy. He is funny and incredibly intelligent.
This is by far the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He is so god awful at teaching he has to curve each of the exams 30% to get people to pass.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
I love Schombert. He is single handedly the greatest man and mind alive. Class is like watching Discovery Channel everyday. Do you like joke? do youlike getting your mind blown? James is your man.

Pay attention in class and this course is super easy. All quiz questions are open book, and lectures are put online. The quiz answers are pulled straight from the lectures. Tests are long, but not that difficult. Plus, he's hilarious!

DO NOT I am serious, DO NOT take this class, it is literally impossible to get a good grade, or merely pass the class, Schombert does not teach and his lectures have nothing to do with the quizzes or 100 question exams that are incredibly difficult. If you want science credit, get it somewhere else, by far worst professor and hardest class.

Professor Schombert is an awesome guy. People will say he is rude, condescending, arrogant, and whatever else. But he is just a very smart guy who is hilarious that does not put up with stupidity. He knows the material very well and teaches it well. The giant curve makes the class very manageable. I will definitely be taking another class with him.

He is a really smart guy and teaches the class well. HUGE curve on everything, so just put a little effort into the quizzes and exams and you can easily pull off at least a B. He is very condescending at times, but he is hilarious as long as you don't act stupid and ask terrible questions.

Schombert is awesome. Don't expect to skate by in this class and receive a decent grade. His class is heavily curved, if you're willing to put in the hard work, you'll do fine. Just don't take this class if you are an entitled princess or unintelligent.

Schombert is amazing.  The class is difficult so don't expect it to be easy.  He knows what he is talking about.  He will act like he knows more then you because he does.  If you don't want a snide remark to a dumb question then either don't take the course or don't ask them.

Not a very good professor. He acted like he didn't really care about the subject, and his tests were all over 100 questions each, and some of the questions weren't even related to Astronomy. His homework sets were ridiculous, and almost impossible to get all the questions correct. Although attendance isn't mandatory, it's necessary.

Schombert is awesome and hilarious.  If you think he's condescending, you either have stupid questions or the emotional fragility of an overweight girl on her first day in high school.  Suck it up.  Test/quizzes are hard, but that's what a curve is for.

Awful man. NEVER sign up for a class being taught by him. Extremely contradictory and his quizes have irrelevant material in them. When you ask him for help he makes you feel incredibly stupid and will not even answer your question.

haha... this guy has the most ridiculous quizzes.  Can't read the math that he writes on the board, which is crucial to know for quizzes. Class was 80 math based, not what I expected. Rude, and incorrect about many of his answers on the quizzes. don't ever be taught by this human being. being in class was a pain in the ass but you need to be there.
Very unhelpful when asking for help in the class. Has the idea that he is better than everyone else.
Boring, Boring, Boring teacher.  Beware!  Not what I expected.  Received a C in the Class and was so glad when it was over!
Not good
He's got an interesting sense of humor but his lectures never seem to help with the tests nor do the readings.

NO BOOK. I took a class on astrophysics with schombert, and found him to be rude and unconcerned with his students. His personal website talks about what a well educated man he is and how you should feel small due to his knowledge. He was also condescending to his students, and made painfully sarcastic remarks when they left class early.

Great professor. Interesting lectures. Funny and witty. I suppose he can be a little condescending if you can't handle that type of stuff. Tests were difficult and made you think about the concepts instead of just repeating facts. Tests had large curves.

lectures completely unorganized, extremely rude and disrespectful in personal interaction, and made me feel like an idiot just for asking for help. i failed one of his tests and going in to get help he basically told me I should drop out of school, citing problems on my transcript. also made fun of me for having attended comm. college.

This class was the biggest disappointment. I was way excited about History of Spaceflight, and the fact that is was a freshman seminar was cool. But this class isn't really structured for freshman, it would be better for Sophomores and up. The lecture notes are online and the grade is based on a midterm, final, and term paper.

Very difficult if you are just looking for a science requirement. You must work hard to do well in this class. The Professor was not helpful in answering my questions outside of class. He is condescending and makes you feel stupid for trying to learn his material. Homework Quizzes do NOT reflect material in lectures, notes, or textbook.
No Comments

Schombert is the best teacher I have ever had, hands down.  His style is definitely different and his students can't expect to breeze by without lots of hard work and THINKING.  He teaches students how to think and learn - those who prefer high school style Q & A probably shouldn't take Schombert unless ready to make a huge change.

This teacher is very interesting. If you like dry humor, then he is the man. If you are whiny, annoying, or argumentative, then do not take his class. If you are dedicated to work and seek out his office hours, he is exceptionally helpful. Most of the poor reviews are because of poor students who didn't do well. Welcome to college. Its hard.

Awful. I'm not afraid of hard work, but this class just doesn't make sense because the answers to quizzes aren't in the lecture notes, the book, or his verbal lectures.  Schombert is an ok teacher, he's really into the class, but this was ridiculous. Your grade goes down while you attempt to learn these things. Bad idea if you're not a math wiz.
Fun professor, lots of great jokes. Learned a lot. I agree with all these previous comments - you have to be quick and work hard, but it's worth it.
No Comments

James Schombert is a great teacher, and his classes are amazing.  As far as any negative reviews are concerned you should really question the source.  The only reason I can think of for anyone to truly hate Schombert is if they're just too slow to keep up.

Amazing professor. Took the honors college Cosmology class with him and it was everything I hoped. The tests are straightforward and directly from the notes. He is sarcastic and hilarious in class. You just have to be willing to do the work to get the grade...

Great teacher, brought me into the World of Astronomy ever since I have taken his ASTR121. Challenging Online Quizzes. Long but easy exams, 100 Multiple Choice questions is all he has for you for Midterm and Finals.

People who don't like his classes didn't pay any attention. He gives away the answers to the online quizzes in class, and you only need to get a 60% on his tests to get an A. Funny guy who really knows the material. His class is based on the online quizzes which are automatically graded at 12 on Sunday night, if you miss them you miss them, don't.

Openly insults undergrads. Utilizes a confusing curve that handed more than half the class (50+) below a C on the midterm (average score was a 40). Mandatory quizzes have material that is sometimes not covered in class until AFTER quiz due date. Overall seems to have a smarmy attitude toward his class.
No Comments
Bad teacher, not helpful, lots of math

If you are expecting ASTR 121 to be easy, its not. It is more of a physics class with an astronomy setting to the questions. Schombert is boring but occasionally dryly funny. He is condescending when answering questions and explains the math horribly. I'd recommend something else for a science credit if that's what you need.

Schombert truly knows the material. Very knowledgeable and conveys lecture material well. He is always willing to answer questions in class during his lecture. This class consisted of 26 online quizzes and 3 exams. Math is only on the online quizzes.  Exams are difficult, but there is a fairly big curve, so you can still do well.
He Rocks
I took his honors astronomy course, and it was the most educational science class I've ever taken.  Go out of your way to take this guy, he's great!
Funny guy.  He smells like hotdogs.

Very interesting guy.  Always has something to say in class and it never gets boring.  Can be a little bit tough, but hey.  What is wrong with a little bit of work.  If you really enjoy Astronomy, this guy is great.

boring, i fell asleep a lot in this class. but everything was online and he goes over most of the quiz's in class and the mid-terms arrant that hard. the short online quiz's are the only time you need to do any math at all, and he walks the class through the math.
Everything is on-line. The class is too much into the details of astronomy. I DO think he's qualified to teach though, and I did like his ever so dry humour.

yo only gake this class if you are really into the chemical compostion of stars.  I thought this was supposed to be a cake walk, boy was i wrong.  There is hard math and chemistry in this.  Needless to say i wasted a pass no pass.  oh and he sounds like the dry eyes guy.

Proffessor schombert isn't qualified to teach elementary school astronomy, much less a course at U of O. He shafted me more times than any one person has ever shafted me before, I've never hated a teacher, but that was before THE SCHOMBERT came into my lif
This guy is the worst F'n teacher I have ever had, pathetic!

I love Mr. Schombert!  He was endlessly kind, helpful, and interesting.  I took his classes several years ago, but he is hands down my favorite teacher ever...I wish I lived in Eugene so I could say hi to him!

That was not a hard class as what others have described. Curving is the main thing for this class, so it is guaranteed that someone can get an A in the class. Quizzes are hard and sometimes doesn't have the answer on the online notes. But overall, it is a great class. funny and informative.
Funny guy.
Hard to get an A but he will help you if you go in to his office hours. He is just kind of mean.
The least caring, least helpful prof I have ever had.

Makes it easy to pass by giving a HUGE curve--in his large lectures, anyway. He's funny, but HAS NO PATIENCE FOR WHINY STUDENTS. That's sortaimportant. If you feel entitled to an A, he'll probably make fun of you. If you try to learn from him, the class will be awesome. i mean, he worked for NASA!

he knows a lot about what he's teaching, and is a good resource.  he must just work better with smaller classes (only 8 students were in mine).  great if you're interested in science but don't want to go through the technical background.
Awful teacher. The average for the final was a 35%. Quiz questions are biased and often make no sense. Grab a pillow if you decide to go to class, but there's no point because everything is online.
I thought Schombert was great!  He is very knowledgeable in the fields of space flight and astronomy.  His lectures are a little unorganized, but very informational.
Very Knowledgable, but lacks the ability to clearly transfer the needed information.
No Comments
Expect to sleep through his class; his lectures are boring
big headed
Mr. Shombert is a very knowledgable professor, in large classes lacks interest.
No Comments
funny
No Comments

473 is one of the topic courses offered from time to time. I had Sports Brand Rep with Kelli. We talked a lot about how sports brands now have an obligation to be ethical and responsible with their practices. Very informative and fun class. Final project included a group project of us creating a potential campaign for a sports brand of our choosing

I had her for 476* I agree with the other reviews of Kelli. Her projects and course materials are interesting, but she is very unorganized, doesn't know how to use Canvas and seems generally unprepared to teach lectures half the time. She doesn't have anything in the gradebook until week 8, and grades are based on only a handful of things.
I'm her son, I think she's amazing :)

Kelli is the most disorganized professor I have ever had in my four years at UO. She does not know how to use Canvas and we did not have grades until WEEK 8. It's clear she prioritizes her professional career over being an instructor. She is also VERY snarky and not clear in her communication. Somehow sucked the fun out of social media.

Class projects and class topics were interesting. The class itself is hard to follow. There are no modules, and everything is put into announcements. Grading is unclear, and the grading does not reflect what is said during class. Rubrics and instructions for assignments are in the announcements and not on the assignments. No grades until week 9.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kelli doesn't grade until the week 9, which makes it difficult for students to grow and learn from feedback throughout the term. Her assignment instructions are incredibly unclear and are recycled from previous courses that are no longer relevant. She's not the absolute worst, but I wouldn't recommend taking a class from her if you can help it.

Her lectures were engaging and kept it real with everyone. She didn't make lectures 2 hours long full of random content. In class she is very kind and always has time to answer questions or even just chat after class. Canvas was very easy to navigate. She offered lots of extra credit! I would definitely recommend her!

Honestly I really liked Kelli!! Weve had barely any HW, everything is graded SUPER easy and fairly and her lectures aren't boring. I've emailed her a couple times and she always gets back to me within the day. I would definitely take a class with her again and recommend her for J350!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor ghosted me for months during a summer course and didn't send me the syllabus until 2 months in. She's supposed to be the summer SOJC advisor but refuses to answer any emails

Not sure why everyone raves. She talks in depth with few students. Is very passive aggressive & talks down to others. Only talks about her outside agency work & says that is why we do the huge group project because it replicates what she does, but she never grades them so not sure how we were supposed to learn from it. Also would cancel randomly.

She doesn't know how to work canvas so there are no modules. You have to search through announcements to find anything. She takes weeeeks to grade and grades very hard. Her lectures are decently interesting but the assignments are unclear and frustrating.

Kelli is an amazing professor, currently enrolled in her course and she's very accessible to reach. Her lectures and classes are structured well to serve the best learning environment for students. Overall great experience, would definitely take her class again.

Kelli Matthews is a great a professor who deserves a higher rating on rate my professor. She is extremely accessible she answers emails quickly and also gives out her phone number to her students. The class is engaging and includes a lot of student participation. I highly recommend you take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kelli is a great professor! She is extremely helpful and accessible outside of class and always provides clear feedback about what she is looking for. She is great for learning about working in the PR world.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was excited to take Kellis class because of her reputation in the SOJC. However, my experience was nothing but frustrating. Kelli constantly prioritized her outside projects over teaching our class. Assignments were WAY too much to handle and assigned through Canvas announcements + grades werent given until AT LEAST 3 weeks after the due date.

Kelli simply does not know how to manage her time. She boasts about the various projects she is involved in, yet is absent as a teacher. She waits until the week after finals to grade homework, yet expects students to work on homework proactively. It is a double standard. She does not live up to the reputation she attempts to create in the SOJC.

Okay, listen closely. It's a no go. Period. The class was super confusing to navigate when it came to canvas. Absolutely no organization too. Assignments had no description or instructions. Literally, the worst experience ever. It's a no go my luvs... It's a no go...
Worst professor ever! She is unorganized, horrible communicator (which is ironic), and seems not to care about the success of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Matthews sure has a great reputation for being well connected in the industry, but she is not a good teaching figure. She was way too adventurous with the course without being responsible for it. Grading was more than three weeks behind and classes were canceled cause other work commitments came first. We felt like a side gig.

Kelli is hands down the worst professor I've had in my years at the UO. She is extremely unorganized and she resists adapting to a majority of her student's needs. She refuses to use modules to organize her courses. She adds way too many things to her personal plate that affect her performance as a professor. She is behind on posting assignments.

She is extremely unorganized and does not care that it impacts her students. She refuses to organize canvas like a normal teacher and assigns assignments/projects through announcements. It almost impossible to know when anything is due. Students have complained many times to her and she simply does not care. Do not take a class with Kelli

Kelli is probably one of the worst professors I've had during my time at the UO, and one of worst professors in the SOJC. The entire class was extremely unorganized and her Canvas page was even worse. She rarely puts any due dates on assignments and it takes forever to find directions on how to do an assignment properly. Don't take her classes.

Took Mrs. Matthews sports communications class my first term here at the school and she rocks. She's super nice and a sports fanatic which makes for easy conversation. You can tell she is just a genuine good person and she deserves a better rating on here. I'd definitely take another class of hers.

Kelli is nice, but she didnt care about this class at all. We were gonna have a final but she cancelled it because she didnt actually teach us anything. The GTF did all the work when it wasnt just guest speakers. And i absolutely do not want to show up to a 9AM on friday to listen to a guest speaker.

Kelli is an engaging and funny professor, and practicing PR professional. She provides a lot of opportunities for extra credit, so make sure to utilize those. There is a lot of participation outside class, but it isn't difficult as long as you do them. Not a class you can forget about when you leave lecture, but fun and engaging.

I worked with Kelli as a graduate teaching fellow. Although I wasn't a student in the class, I was lucky to have a chance to observe such an engaging and dedicated professor. Her classes aren't easy but she cares about her students and works hard to prepare them for careers in strategic communication industries.

Kelli is the most pretentious teacher at the University of Oregon. She thinks she is the know all of all things social media, but the reality is just because you tweet a lot doesn't make you a social media expert. She is judgmental and picks favorites. Her class is a popularity contest.

OHHHHH. Kelli is really smart& respected. But she lost sight of why she was hired. Her 2 little kids are such a distraction in class - they run the class! She is total disconnected from the basics she needs to provide: ignores emails, no advance notice on deadlines, & disorganized. Students pay $$$ to learn so please stop with the in-class daycare.

Kelli is Great! Understanding if conflicts come up. She is super busy and not always fast w/ emails but she is super cool and stays behind after class if you have questions.  She is sassy and can be sort of a harda$$ on assignments as far as what she expects out of you but she is one of the nicest profs I have had at UO.

Kelli is a great lecturer  But as a professor she isn't organized. She "misplaced" a few of our midterms and graded them for us the week before finals. She posted rubrics for things a week or two days before they were due and if you aren't one of her favorite PR students don't expect a lot from her. She is flaky with emailing back students.
Kelli is a great educator.  Always relevant and interesting to listen to.  Highly recommend taking a class from her.  She is not a push-over though so do your work!

Mullen's is one of the most caring professors in the econ department and I would heavy recommend meeting her outside of class. I think the move from 2 midterms to 1 midterm (and a retake)was a beneficial choice for the class. As much as I enjoyed getting out early, her lectures are really fast and if you don't have strong statistics skills its hard

shes very nice and wants you to succeed, but she reads right off the slides extremely fast and skips over a lot of stuff, and does annotations on the chalkboard, so she cant upload any annotated slides for later. Your best bet is to come to class, take extremely detailed notes, and hope for the best. Avg on tests are 70%.

I used to walk in the middle of the road on my way to class and hope that I got hit. I spent my entire semester on this class and somehow always scored terribly. Slides make no sense, most of the things that come out of her mouth do not make sense. When you ask her a question she freaks out and gives incorrect information. Do not take this class.

She teaches the whole class of the slides she made, but she doesn't even know what the slides mean. All the slides are word based and explain the math through words, not examples, and then gives homework on these problems without showing how to solve. She was snarky when a student would ask her to explain or elaborate. Rude and can't teach.

In no offensive regard, Dr. Mullen is not a good lecturer whatsoever. Her logic and intuition is confusing and she manages to make simple concepts much harder than they need to be. She confuses herself often when teaching and her lectures tend to be empty word salads that have little substance.
Professor Mullen is a very nice lady; however, her lectures are fast-paced and can be hard to follow at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice but not a great instructor. The tests are extremely difficult and long. The lectures lack examples and the slides make formulas and important concepts unclear. She assigns entire homework assignments in R with no instruction on how to use it. I don't think she has bad intentions though.

She is nice and will work with you; however, she is always scatterbrained and disorganized. She will take half of class time for students to work on 1 question together. Instead of just going over the material herself. Makes exams insanely long. Unless you go to office hours each week, dont bother taking her class.

I like Professor Mullen and she is certainly a nice professor. The lectures are pretty fast paced and convoluted and can get hard to keep up with at times. Also, I wish we had done more R in the class. But not a bad professor by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thankfully I got to experience Karrie's lectures before she left! She was by far my favorite professor ever. Lectures are always engaging, she seems excited to teach what she knows, students feel comfortable chipping in, and her GE was always timely. In class group work was relevant and all assignments were easily manageable. HIRE MORE OF HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Karrie Walters is the best professor I have ever had; she genuinely cares about her students and the work she does. She never fails to check up on her students or ensure that everyone understands the material. I am sad to see her go, but excited to see what she will do next!

This was the best FHS class I've ever taken! LOVE Karrie so much, she cares a lot about the development of her students as human service professionals and gives great feedback on assignments. Her lectures are engaging and fun!

BEST FHS professor hands down. She clearly cares about her students and gives extensions when the whole class needs. The class itself is super interesting, and you get to apply the skills you learn in class in practice client sessions. Lectures are interesting and she doesn't just read from the slides. 10/10 would take again.
Best professor I've ever had
Professor Walters is a great professor. I had her for FHS 215 during Summer 2024 and currently have her for FHS 330. Her lectures can be a bit information heavy, but they're very informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I love professor Walters! She is an amazing teacher!

Karrie Walters is the best. If you have the chance to take her, I definitely suggest that you do! Definitely my favorite professor within the FHS department, especially since the Muruthi family left. She's very well-respected and gives very engaging and funny lectures, while making sure to cover content thoroughly. 12/10

I love Karrie, I've had her for multiple classes and I hope to have her again! Her lectures are always fun and very engaging, and she really cares about her students. She's passionate and interactive with her students and allows students to learn at their own pace

Karrie is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. She's funny and engaging and always helping students who ask for help. She helps you look at career paths if you want which I found really helpful. This class was very group oriented and there's only so much time to practice the skills. I didn't like the GE but Karrie is definitely one of my fav

Karrie is the best. She's so fun and always passionate about what she's teaching. It's never a dull moment in Karrie's classes. They might be on the easier side, but it really is you put in what you want to get out. If you just want an easy A, then this class can give that to you. But if you want to learn and engage, you'll get a lot more out of it

I have taken a handful of Karrie's classes and I love the class every time! She's very interactive and understanding of her students and understands that the FHS major can get emotionally draining at times. She has experience in the field and really uses that to your advantage. In my opinion, she is the best instructor within the FHS major!
She is an amazing teacher. I highly recommend taking her class. She is so inspirational and cares deeply about her students and their wellbeing!!

Dr. Walters is one of my favorite professors I've ever had at UO. She is extremely knowledgeable of her field and integrates real life examples from her years of work into lectures. Her animated and encouraging teaching style always kept me engaged. I took both FHS 329 and 330. Not the easiest classes but I got a B+ in both and learned a ton.

Dr. Walters has a ton of experience in the FHS field and knows exactly what she's talking about; her readings are wordy, but they're current and accurate in a fast-paced field. Beware: sometimes extremely hard to contact outside of class. Chase her down after lecture or hound the GE's instead.

I've had walters a few times, mixed results 329, 330, 493. 330 sucked bc her ge sucked. This term (3298, 493) is great, she is super covid understanding, she keeps her online lectures interesting, her ge's are great, she is super knowledgeable, no complaints!

Good Instructor, although lengthy lectures. GE grades everything and she's tough. Dr. Walters doesn't have clear criteria for papers and the information from her contradicts what the GE does. So beware. Ask questions, use email for proof. Few things are graded: forums, a few papers, and she doesn't give exams.

Not clear on assignment specifications. Got an A on every assignment and only missed class twice yet got a B for my final overall grade because on a day I was absent they apparently showed rough drafts to show prove they started (this was graded). So because I was not there to show my rough draft I got a B (even though on that final I got an A.

Probably one of the greatest human beings on this planet. She really goes into depth about FHS as a major and career. She applies information into real life situations and has guest speakers from local organizations to speak about their field. love herrrrr

Probably one of the greatest human beings on this planet. She really goes into depth about FHS as a major and career. She applies information into real life situations and has guest speakers from local organizations to speak about their field.

Professor Walters is a fascinating lady and an amazing teacher. She handles her giant class size very well and keeps me engaged all class. She has real-world experience in the field which makes her stories and opinions very valuable. overall, great class.

This teacher was not very clear with what she expected on assignments.  I found myself always having to clarify her instructions.  Communication through email was also poor, it would take days to get a response and then always the same answer (to come see her).  Ruth Bichel who co-taught this class with her is AWESOME.  I wish Ruth taught it all.

Karrie is such a great professor. She is super passionate about this subject and makes you super engaged. She is a great person. Only downside about the class is, IT'S A LOT OF WORK! There are tons of tedious things to get done. There are 3 BIG projects with 1000 plus words and a 350 to 500 word blog every week.
Loved this class & Karrie! She is very knowledgable about the course content/passionate/excited to teach.  Quizzes were easy, graded easy on midterm!

Karrie is so awesome.  She always keeps the students engaged with her energetic personality, class activities, and group discussions.  I absolutely loved taking this class. Make time for the readings because they are novels that are actually interesting.  She is such a wonferful teacher and person!!!!

This was easily the best class I've taken at the UO. She is an incredible professor. She has a very encouraging, hopeful attitude that pushes all of her students to strive to be the best they can be. Her lectures were diverse and interesting. I suggest all students take this class whether they are FHS majors or not.
Awesome...loved her class. she's awesome. class was semi easy..lots of writing

Karrie is truly a wonderful person which made her class very intriguing. The subject matter was not always riveting but her lecturing abilities and her use of guest speakers and movies made the class always interesting to go to. She is someone who clearly has a great heart and is a very inspiring person. Easy A if you do the work and can write well
Engaging instructor.  Passionate about the subject matter.  Super flexible and accommodating to students with disabilities.  Overall a very nice person.

Lots of passion and a good teacher.  I had no idea how much people had to struggle through in this country until I took this class.  Karrie helped me recognize that I needed to think beyond "I like helping people" to really seeing that I have a responsibility to make a change in the system as well.

GREAT teacher.  But textbook is boring and hard to read.  Quizzes are hard, but there are no big papers.  The final was take home.  I thought I put a lot of work into it but only got a B.  Worth taking, though. Karrie made class interesting and uses good examples.  She has a sense of humor and was always willing to give extra time to students

Karrie's one of the best and most engaging teachers I've had as an undergraduate.  I like pace and variety - lectures, activities, large and small group discussion.  She encourages a variety of views and pushes you to think past your first initial responses to things.  I know I've grown a lot in the class.  The final is really hard, though.
Karrie is one of the nicest people I've ever met! She gives great, clear lectures that are informative. Her FHS 215 class is great!
She is very laid back but still very informative. I really enjoyed her class as well as her teaching style she is definitely worth taking.
She really made me think about stuff I hadn't before.  Plus, she's really passionate about the subject, which gives the lectures energy.

The easiest college class possible all lectures are word for word power point and super easy quizzes and assignments.  There is a schedule of when quizzes are so showing up to those classes are the only ones that are realy necessary to get an A in the class.  Since it is so easy it is inceridbly boring and if you go to class bring a laptop for fun.
Karrie is very sweet and good natured. Her FSH215 class is interesting and not extremely challenging.

Karrie is an AMAZING teacher! She is very good at leading discussions and getting people interested. She also uses great, fun examples to get the point across. She teaches us interesting information that we need to know, and she is just an all-around great teacher!

Truly one of my favorite professors, she's so kind and genuine. She's very understanding of circumstances and just wants everyone to succeed. Her passion about archaeology definitely rubbed off on me.

Prof. McDonough is one of my favorite professors at UO! She's amazing and sweet both inside and outside of class. She encourages questions and will often do her own research and get back to you next class with an answer. I learned a ton in this class but the workload was kept very manageable. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER IF YOU CAN SHES THE BEST!!!!!!!
Loved her class, she was definitely passionate about her work and it made everything a lot more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor McDonough is one of the best professors I have had in my 4 years at UO. She does a good job making lectures engaging and brings in interesting guest speakers. For this class there were biweekly quizzes, a couple short essays and a few participation assignments (so pretty easy overall) I would highly recommend taking a class with her!

Very easy class, most take it for easy science credit but if you're generally interested in archaeology then you'll love it. All assignments are online including exams. Half of classes have attendance that counts for grade, and you're not told ahead of time. Very equitable professor.
Katelyn gave really engaging lectures that made the labs quick and easy to understand. Very easy mindless science credit that was enjoyable.

Absolutely love her, also this class is incredibly easy. Labs are simple, lecture attendance is random participation days and there are 5 scattered throughout the course so you don't know when a day will be for attendance. Very easy for a science credit and she is so passionate and kind. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Icon. She is very passionate about her studies, and you will hear her talking about all of her personal work as well, but it's so fun and interesting! This class is very easy, but I think Dr. McDonough does that on purpose because she cares about her students' success.

If you're thinking abt taking a class with her DO IT! I just took anth 145 for a science credit but she makes it so interesting while not being too much work! Just one inquizative a week + small discussion group work, and the midterm and final are online. She's also just so nice and fun!!

Literally the best professor I've had so far. So caring and passionate about what she's teaching and her students. I'm not an anthro student but I want to take more of her classes. Couldn't recommend more, you'll learn so much and actually want to go to class.

Jump at any chance to take a class with her! She is so funny and kind, and her course organization is fantastic! She's very accessible outside of class, and provides all the resources/readings you will need. As long as you read the papers(of which there are many) and attend the lectures(which are fun) you will do great!!
Love her so much! She answers every question thoughtfully and provides great feedback on assignments! Participation is important in her class, but it is always beneficial to learning.
I love her! She is passionate, which makes class fun and engaging. She makes an effort to bring guest speakers and keep labs engaging. I loved archaeology!

Dr. McDonough is amazing! I'm very glad I had her for my intro to archaeology. She is super enthusiastic about what she teaches, and she helped me realize my love of archaeology as well. There were only 2 tests, both online and open note + book, so as long as you attended lectures and labs, it should be pretty easy.

Great professor! Very organized and easy to reach. She is clear on expectations and content. The only qualm I have is that the quizzes are a bit difficult even when thoroughly read the readings right before. I would definitely take this class again.

Super nice and enthusiastic! Always comes to class excited to present her lecture. I've found all lectures very interesting, it's a great class to learn the techniques of archaeologists. Exams are open book as well.

Dr. McDonough is a wonderful example of how archaeology can be accessible to anyone with the right teacher. She is extremely effective at lecturing and focusing on the big picture. Classs is relatively easy - 2 papers, 6 quizzes, 3 annotated readings, and one field trip. Willing to give feedback on papers ahead of time, but inflexible on deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the most useful ANTH class I've taken at UO and I'd highly recommend it to other ANTH majors. Professor McDonough gives amazing feedback and knowledge, brings in professionals in the field to speak on their experience, and offers to help students with career-oriented advice. Pretty easy class for the most part, but really valuable.

Professor McDonough is an amazing professor. I had her for Oregon Archaeology, and she's extremely passionate and knowledgeable about the her field. She made class interesting, and the material in her lectures was always very concise and straightforward. McDonough is very approchable and always does a good job helping students out if they need it.

One of my favorite professors ever! She is so enthusiastic and eager to help students who are really interested in archaeology and will go above and beyond to share resources/opportunities in the field. The knowledge she provides is not only academic but practical.

Took Game Art. He is a very chill, funny guy. He knows his gaming stuff and always tries to help you out. The final project is making a game or a game-related thing, just so you know. Overall, an amazing class if you love games, and the instructor is also chill.

This class is great if you're into experimentation. Definitely not an Illustrator class. The projects are pretty unique and open-ended, so you get to explore your own ideas in formats you probably wouldn't in other classes. There is some step-by-step guidance, but the material can still be challenging. It's rewarding if you put in the work though.

Took his Vsynth class spring term of 2025 and absolutely loved it. He is incredibly knowledgeable and an excellent teacher. Honestly, someone who has inspired me inside and outside of the classroom, I wish I could take this class again. Its pretty awesome UO has him as a professor and I hope to take his classes in the future!
Mad cool professor! Classes were great, and we did a full-dome AV concert at the Eugene Science Center Planetarium with our own work. By far one of the coolest things I've done in school!
Kevin is the best ARTD professor I have had. He is very caring, a fair grader, engaging, and just fun to listen to in class. I would recommend any of his classes to anyone interested!

I learned a ton in Kevin's class. He really pushed us to step out of our comfort zones, and I ended up using Photoshop and Illustrator in ways I never thought of. Get ready to mess around with a pen-plotter and experiment with making drawings from sound!

very easy peasy class! learned a lot and had very little homework!! went up to him after class after something he said really angered me during a lecture and we worked it out over a very civil conversation where he ended up admitting he was wrong ! idk I feel like thats really rare for a professor to do, very understanding guy:)

Jeff is a great professor and always gives it to you straight. He is clear and direct in teaching and the material, which leads to very minimal confusion. That being said, the lectures are very mundane and hard to sit through at times. A lot of the test material comes from the readings and slides. he is charitable with extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Measelle is one of the smartest professors I've ever had, and this is very evident in his lectures. He's very engaging, but it is still hard to focus when the entire class is just lectures. He's reachable outside of class but is not the friendliest over email. Other than that, he's great, and I'd definitely take his class again!

Measelle is a great professor and is super straightforward. I took this class because I had him for 202 and liked him. Lectures are always fun and he basically just yaps and we take notes. There's very simple weekly quizzes (like 3-6 questions) or a 250-300 word written response. There's a midterm & final as well.

Chill professor that definitely knows what he's talking about. Practically only graded by the weekly InQuizitives and the 2 midterms, but very interesting class. Would take him again, just not in Straub 156.

Really interesting class. Prof Measelle is very understanding and listens to his students and their needs. He is super funny and does a good job at keeping the class engaged. The exams are pretty difficult. In the winter term, everyone did so badly on the first midterm that he had to give every person in the class 7 extra points.
Follow the study guide and find someone to study with. Go to the office hours to learn more about the topics there isn't enough time in class to move past the surface level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graded pretty much on two midterms. No retakes. Not the best lecturer, a lot of memorization on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this professor and his receptiveness to feedback and drive for student success. When the first midterm didn't go super well, he gave out extra points and made a much better study guide for the second midterm. Only critique is that most class content is identical to the required reading, but it's a good refresher, I guess. Overall, great.
Too much homework for my blood, but it's an introductory course, so I get it. A great lecturer would recommend.

1 midterm was open book an other was canceled. 3 unique projects fairly easy and clear on requirements. I took 399 longevity and it was a good time. I can't say I was engrossed in the content as I played clash alot but it was decently interesting. I'm kinda a bum of a student in fairness

Jeff is an engaging person, but a bad professor. His approach to psychology is philosophical like which is strange for a science course. He rambles in lectures and has you critique theories. His exams are 80% long essay based which is tedious. He is unclear about the guidelines for his exam responses and nitpicks the smallest inaccuracies.
1000000/10 best professor and class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jeff is great and his lecture style made the class interesting even to someone who doesn't care much about psychology. There were 2 midterms and no final which were both online. Go to lecture and do the HW and its an easy A class.

Jeff's lectures are so good, they make you actually understand the material. Weekly Inquizitives and attendance taken by iclicker. Midterms were multiple choice but weighted pretty heavily so make sure you do well on those. Some Qs were directly from study guide so that helped. Definitely would take him again he is so funny and passionate!!

Loved this class. He's super chill n funny. Some iclicker questions throughout lecture for credit. Only work is Inquisitives, 4.5 research participation credits, 2 midterms. Labs r just discussions, so chill but attendance taken. This has been the only class I've been truly interested in so far. Tests r open note/book and online super easy.

professor measelle is a super charismatic, friendly teacher. he doesn't just read off the slides and has a good sense of humor. his tests in psy202 are pretty difficult despite being open note, but if you prepare well enough, you'll do fine. overall great professor!

this guy is awesome. lectures are engaging, he always ends 20-30 mins early, and there's very few assignments. his tests are HARD though so be sure to really go into detail with the study guide. other than that this guy is an awesome prof

Such a great professor. Slides are easy to follow and understand, along with the lecture that goes with them. Get out early often times. Exams are super, super simple and easy to take. Would honestly take this professor again.
Amazing professor! I felt like he really cared about what he taught and it was inspiring. Not many classes leave me feeling that way, but highly recommend!
Amazing class and amazing prof. Super funny, caring, and open to student input. The only assignments are weekly reading quizzes, a midterm and final, and a final paper. Highly highly recommend!
lectures were interesting and usually ended early! the tests were on canvas and open note, open textbook.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far at UO. Kind, funny, personable and makes it very easy to learn psych. GEs were easy to talk to, and he always answered emails quickly and helpfully. Highly recommend this class!

One of the best profs ever...lets you out early, online midterms, and attendance is mandatory, but you get 4 skips. Lectures are ok (he is funny but psych is so long and can get boring).  Labs are just older students trying to get a quick overview of what you learned that week. If you can TAKE ONE OF HIS CLASSES!

Dr. Measelle is so awesome! One of my favorite professors. He is hilarious and so much fun, and I was bummed I wasn't able to get into PSY 308 with him next term. He makes the lectures fun and always ends early because. He takes attendance with iClicker everyday, and there are only 2 tests, open book + note.

Super good class, if you pay attention you will learn a lot, he makes lectures interesting. Every single classes ended short, only 2 tests and both were online + open note. Easy, fun class and good teacher.

Really great and funny professor. He knows what he's talking about and isn't boring, keeps you interested even though the lectures are long. iClicker is used for lecture attendance. Class is super easy and laid back. Weekly inquizitive and 2 midterms, both online.

Jeff was one of the first professors I had during the first term of my freshman year. He is also one of the most memorable. He was clever/hilarious, and a great speaker. His lectures are pretty comprehensive, so you don't need to read; although, you should do the practice questions he gives you before the tests as many of them are verbatim.

Jeff was a really good teacher. Hes very supportive of students and always puts them first. He cares about psychology and inspires the students. Hes also pretty funny, I would definitely like to have him as a teacher again.

Jeff was so great. Class was 4-5:50 but he always made sure to let us out at 5:30 or before. He is such a great lecturer I was never bored because he talks so well and the topic of the class was super interesting. There are clicker questions so you need to go to class but you can miss 4 without penalty

Jeff is such a great prof! Very knowledgeable & funny during class. Lots of reading in the textbook & weekly quizzes on InQuisitive which were pretty easy. 1 midterm & 1 final which I found to be more difficult than expected. Also required to participate in research studies throughout the term. Overall really enjoyed the prof despite the workload!

Great professor, very funny and engaging lectures. Professor Measelle is honestly the best professor that I've had here so far. You are graded on attendance by using iClickers and the work is relatively easy. Midterms are on the harder side but you should be fine as long as you stay consistent with the other work.
Great professor, funny, very knowledgeable. Class has not a lot of work but the midterms can be kind of hard. Make sure you do the study guide and read the important parts of the textbook.

Professor Measelle gave good lectures and all of our tests were online for the course. He also curved the class a little bit too! Hes really clear with grading and assignments and answers emails fast! He makes the large class feel small and always will answer questions!
