Jeff is an absolute joy to have as a teacher. His lectures are comprehensive, engaging, and wonderfully hilarious. The slides do a great job of covering the readings. You don't have to read the book for exams besides for the inquizitives which are annoying. The 2 exams are pretty simple - multiple choice w/ sample questions often verbatim. 4/5.

This class was super interesting. We had some lectures and videos to watch every week, and then a straightforward weekly multiple choice quiz (quizzes could be done by getting info directly from the textbook). I also really enjoyed raising my virtual child in the simulation. We also had one paper which was fine. Jeff really cares about students!

Jeff is so far my favorite PSY professor. He is funny and so chill. The first 2 weeks are a little boring if you have taken 201 already because it is the same topic. Overall, If you are questioning who to take PSY 202 with, please don't hesitate to go with Jeff because he is awesome!!! 10/10

This class was really fun and relatively easy for me. The textbook is the same as PSY201 and there's a little bit of overlap in the first two weeks but then it the class takes off on its own course. I would recommend taking this class instead of PSY201 unless you need a <3 science group satisfying course because I found this prof's class better.

Jeff makes a 520-person lecture feel small. He's always excited and cracked jokes a lot. His slides are very good at conveying the textbook material, though he tends to speed through them quickly. Your grade is based off of 10 online quizzes, attendance, research participation, a midterm, and a final. The final is not cumulative.

The class was super interesting, but I felt that the structure of the class was not so great. His lectures were interesting, but I felt that they were compiled of so much information that was never used on the exam. The exam was super confusing as it was super short, but the average was low on a faulty grading system (he does allow you to make up)

Jeff was an awesome guy. His class is really interesting, just lulls on a bit! There was a midterm and a final, but you had to go outside of class to participate in psych research. All in all, if you come to class and study for the tests you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and goes too quickly during slideshow presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Jeff was extremely insightful for his general psychology class. He goes more in-depth into the topics than most professors were and sparks peoples' interests in psychology. He encourages participation and makes the learning experience less painful. Midterms are easy though they require some studying.

My favorite prof! I have taken a few classes from him and every class I have taken from him has been my favorite class. Amazing lecturer with humor and extreme intelligence. I have learned so much from him and am completely engaged. Not an easy class but that the respect I have for him and the subject motivated me to do the work.

Jeff has a magnetic, funny personality and is an engaging speaker. He manages to keep (almost) everyone's attention for the lengthy 2-hour lectures with 500 students packed in an intro-level course. His tests are quite difficult though, so make sure you pay attention in class and read the textbook. Definitely review lecture slides before exams!!!

Dr. Measelle is an excellent and captivating lecturer. Lectures are interesting and usually never boring. Attendance is by iClicker, though it doesn't count for much of your grade. InQuizitives can be long and annoying, but the two Midterm exams are not difficult. Take the practice exam, most of the questions are verbatim. You will learn so much!

Nice guy, was obvious he was passionate and knowledgable about psych. The class was huge and completely lecture based, which was tedious. Attendance is taken through IClickers. Inquisitive's are long and the book is necessary to finish them quickly. Labs for this class were pointless and dull but mandatory and are led by students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jeff was by far my favorite professor for fall term. He's a super funny guy and he makes the long lecture go by really quick. He's one of the few professors that can actually make a lecture really interesting. He's a super engaging lecturer and knows a lot about psychology. The class does entail a lot of reading in order to do well on the midterms.

Measelle is hilarious and makes a 300-person class feel way smaller. He's a cool guy that wants students to do well, and he knows his stuff! iClickers were attendance. LOTS of reading, and midterms are hard; just make sure you study/read hard.  I got bad grades on the midterms, but with other points I still got a B. Definitely would recommend him!

Jeff know what he is talking about when it comes to psychology. His lecture are very interesting but covers lots of information. You think you don't need to know every detail he covers in lecture, but YOU DO! He threw questions at us on the exams that the class would not of expected. Tests are fairly difficult.

This class was very enjoyable! The thing that I would recommend, is to read the textbook thoroughly, and to pay attention to the definitions in the book. To prepare well for the exams, make sure you review the lecture slides carefully, as well as the big concepts from the book. All in all, the prof. is very humorous and caring for his students.
Really interesting, great class

Hilarious professor that keeps long lectures interesting and engaging. Provides good study guides for tests so if you attend lecture and study the 2 midterms (not cumulative) won't be a problem. Would definitely recommend taking a class from him!!

He was funny and respectable, but left out HUGE parts of the lecture that we had to finish on our own. The work load is do-able and the tests were okay but classes always got out early when there was so much more that needed to be covered.

Great professor. Classes are usually composed of lectures, activities where he makes us engage with the material (often debates or asks us how we would approach this real life scenario). Loves questions and makes us think about it first instead of automatically feeding us answers. Class size was really small so it felt more personal.

Dr. Measelle is an awesome professor. Gives great lectures and does an excellent job engaging a large hall full of students. He seems very busy, he hands off most of his administrative duties to the GTFs. Very knowledgeable about psychology and thoughtfully answers questions; he clearly respects his students. Study guides will be your best friend.
Super funny and very knowledgable. In terms of grading you have 2 midterms and no final and they're not cumulative so you're chilling.

LOVE this guy. lectures are long but he makes them entertaining and funny. would take another class from him, you do have to study hard for the tests though, but theres only two. I clickers are used in classes for participation.

Great professor. I am taking two of his classes. PSY 202 is a huge lecture class of 500 people and it still makes you feel connected. He is hilarious, real, and you get out of it what you put in. Make an effort to get to know him and I am sure you won't be disappointed. He is the most interesting man, with many connections! Love him!
Just an all around good guy. One of those teachers you want to go visit after you have taken his class. If you get the chance please take one of his classes!
Jeff isn't one of those teachers who tries to be cool. He just is.
Super interesting class but the tests are really hard
Jeff is a really nice guy and a very knowledgable teacher

He is awesome because he's super funny and chill but he's also just a good teacher! He took the material and made it interesting and easy to follow even when the concepts were complex. Reading is very important, but if you keep up nothing is a surprise or difficult. Figured that out when I actually started halfway through.

The tests are absolutely ridiculous. The tests are pretty much like taking a psych analysis. The only nice thing is that the grades are curved at the end of the class. We have weekly quizzes that are pretty difficult as well.

Jeff is very knowledgeable about the field and expects an appropriate amount of work from his students. I'm not complaining about the reading because it's impossible to cover everything in the lectures. See him at his office hours, ask him questions, get to know him. He has a lot of students.

He is a funny professor, and really makes class fun and enjoyable. One thing I do not like about this professor, is that he is a very tough grader, and makes his tests very hard to even get a C. I would take him if you like reading, but if you don't like reading, don't take him. The only way to get at least a C in this class, is by reading the text
He never responds to emails. He is too into being funny and liked. He uses online tools because the class is otherwise too large for him to handle.
Class is overall very interesting and he is entertaining. The tests are very very hard. Last midterm 75% of the class got a C or below. Need to read the textbook!

Jeff is very fond not only about what he teaches but of his students as well. He has experience in the research field and loves discussing that with students. His exams are as much textbook based as they are lecture based. He obviously wants to inspire students and brought in a multitude of great guest speakers. Loved the class over all!

Professor Measelle is the best of the best. His classes are fun, engaging and appropriately challenging. Additionally, he is a sweet guy and likes helping and relating to his students. I highly recommend him as a professor and a great resource at the UO.

Would not recommend. Material is interesting, but tests are impossible. Harder than online, open book check-ups. 87% was the high score. And he MIGHT curve our final grades. I dropped because I didn't want to spend the majority of my time trying to barely pass. He may be funny, and show cool videos, but something's wrong when no one gets an A.

8am killed me. What he taught, I learned in my basic high school class, but it was still interesting. He was funny. If you didn't take a high school class, I'd take it. It's easy and hard at the same time. You really have to think and know everything, but the answers are common sense almost. I liked the class overall.
GREAT TEACHER. HILARIOUS.

No use in going to class, everything is on blackboard. He covers material that he is personally interested in, and skips 90% of the information in the chapters assigned. Yes its an easy class, but boring.
He is really funny and shows interesting youtube videos in class to help you comprehend the information.  Really intelligent and knowledgeable in this field.

Very funny guy. Lectures are very informative, but not mandatory. Course grade consists of exams (including final), research (participating in lab experiments), and completing reviews of the researches. The exams are primarily made up of questions from the study guides (questions are identical in exam).
A terribly easy class. Waste of time.
Great teacher. Makes the material very comprehensive. I loved the class and would say take any class he teaches!
hes way chill, shows lots of you tube videos. test are completely off the study guides.
Very good teacher, easy but a good speaker and very experienced in his field.
He is one of the most entertaining teachers I have ever had. He keeps this large lecture hall interesting and fun, with a few laughs here and there. I would strongly recommend Jeff Measelle.

Jeff Measelle is a joke professor. I felt like I wasted so much time and money on this class. He posts all of his lectures online; test and quiz questions are posted online prior to the actual text but the questions are impossible to answer and don't match up with what we're learning at all. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.
He is funny and we really like the short clips he pulls off youtube. They make the class more fun. I like him but his studyguides are so difficult

he posted all the questions for the quizzes online as "practice questions."  also all the lecture notes were posted so it was more or less pointless to attend. (plus he was never there) however he screwed everyone over with the completely unexpected backwards curve at the end... so just cuz its easy, def dont slack off

I thought he was an okay teacher, but not the best. Psychology is my major so I loved the information, but I found myself bored most of the time, especially when there were guest speakers. Also, I was confused about the grading becuae.

This class was interesting, but not too challenging intellectually.  Professor Measelle did not make clear his grading policy at the beginning of the term, so I ended up with a 91.5 thinking I got an A.  Then he changed the grading curve giving me a B.  It pissed me off majorly.  At least he could tell us at the beginning of the term!
sweet

The class was relatively boring...but decent.  His lectures are posted online, so you don't HAVE to attend for a decent grade. Unfortunately, we had a lot of guest lecturers who were more dull than him.  And his curve on the final is horrible.  I earned a 92% and got a B+, which was highly irritating, especially when you're on academic scholarship.

He reverse curved the final grade in the class so my 93% only earned me a B+.  A huge lecture and this teacher had to have substitute teachers about half the classes because he was absent for personal reasons.
Really easy class if you study the test question pools. Prof. Measelle is nice, but his lectues are some what dull.

WOW. I only showed up for the midterm and the final, and got an A. This class was such a joke, and the discussion sections were worthless too. I opened my book all of three times. PSY 202 overlaps WAAAAAAY too much with PSY 201, it's like 201 dumbed down.

Poor attendance for his lectures...has been there for 2 or 3 the entire term. Questions on midterm and test do not match up with lectures. Requires a lot of book reading. Cool, funny guy...time demanding class
This class is great! Dr. Measelle is a really interesting lecturer. He makes learning great fun! His tests and quizes are really easy as long as you use the study questions.
awesome teacher, makes lectures fun and interesting. shows funny video clips, and tests are super easy if u do the practice questions. the tests took me 15 minutes each and i did really well.
Awesome prof. He is funny and is willing to explain anything you need help with! Awesome guy! Tests are super easy as long as you do the practice questions!
No Comments

All the assignments are made and graded by Ai the ExEc program is annnoying and makes it feel like he didn't even put any effort into designing the class. Maybe he's better in person but do not take online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: really suportive and understanding

I took MGMT 225 which is an intro to entrepreneurship class. He is a good lecturer, and engaging however the class could have been shortened from 2 hours to 1 hour 20 minutes. He also grades really harshly. I got marked down on an assignment because "my names weren't creative enough". He is passionate about the class but the assignments were subpar

Honestly Nathan was an amazing professor. He kept lectures engaging and was super funny. This class might be an introverts worst nightmare because he calls on people randomly throughout lectures. The group project could have been better. Tests are the EXACT same as the practice tests so take those as many times as you can and memorize. great class

I wish Nathan taught something other than MGMT 311. While the material is important to learn it's pretty much teaching you how to work in corporate America, Thrilling! He's very sharp and the tests are easy, but classes are very long and lecture heavy. If you ask me most of the information taught in this class is very half baked. He can do better

He is a caring and thoughtful professor. Very nice guy and he is interesting to listen to but that being said, he is an awful teacher. His teaching style is that you have to read the textbook to get any course content at all. Gives 2 hour lectures and rarely mentions any course content and he assigns busy work. Mandatory waste of time lectures. FIO

Nathan is a nice guy and means well. He does have engaging lectures but be prepared to participate as he is not afraid to put you on the spot. I know it is in good spirit but for some people it can cause stress when you're suddenly asked to define a term you've never even heard of…overall good guy though.

Nathan was a great professor, he made what could have been a very boring class, engaging and easy to pay attention to. He's an interesting and smart guy, if you have a chance to take a class with him, take it! MGMT 311 with him is pretty chill and he didn't grade too hard.
Nathan is the best. I hate being a business major and he made this class enjoyable. He is so unserious and makes everyone feel comfortable and welcome in class.

Nathan is a great professor. He give good feedback and appreciates students who care about their contribution to the course. Yes there is a lot of busy work, however it mostly beneficial and is not very time consuming. I learned a lot even though it was online. I would definitely recommend.

Probably one of the worst classes I have every taken at the University of Oregon. For a completely online course you would think he would have lecture videos, panopto recordings, or SOMETHING. But no. This guy literally just uses other colleges resources and has none of his own material. He gives no expectations of what he wants from you.

Nathan is a typical undergrad professor. He gives out a lot of busy work (weekly discussion posts, case study assignments, final presentation and a final written assignment) and even makes peer grading difficult. Nathan is not the best professor for a grad course and needs to understand that assignments for grad students are quality over quantity.
Super caring and passionate professor!

Professor Ulibarri is the reason why I've become so interested in Anthropology. His class not only caught my interest but he just wants everyone to succeed and truly cares about his students. Highly suggest taking his class!
Amazing and caring professor, love his sound effects! Makes learning interesting and exciting

his lectures are important to go to especially lab but attendance isnt manditory. he clearly cares about his students and wants them to do well. labs are manditory and will effect your grade if you dont go. he posts all his lectures on canvas.

He is so fun and passionate about his work and does a lot of kahoots and it is so cute. but make sure you study for the labs because you think you know but you actually don't and you will be in trouble..

Larry has always been a favorite professor, makes learning tough topics really fun and easy. He's always supportive and thrives to mold the course into something that helps every student as much as possible. Studying and memorization is a must for the topics, but as long as you participate in assignments and lectures then it's a super fun class :)

Professor Ulibarri clearly cares about what he teaches, and it shows in his lectures where he takes chances to add humor and fun in between informative slides.
Additionally, he was willing to work with me when I missed an exam, and is one of the few professors I've had to let you in the door of an exam even if you're late, saving you from disaster.

I've taken two classes with Professor Ulibarri. His lectures are very engaging and he seems to care a lot about the content and the students. This course has four 1,000 word discussion posts, so if you are not fond of writing I do not recommend. Overall, he is a great professor no matter what the content is.

I found some parts of the course content interesting, but I also got bored at times. Ulibarri is a great guy, but it's a lot of work for just a science credit as a business major. I would recommend finding another course if that's why you might take it. There are 4 essay-length discussion posts, 4 quizzes, and 3 documentaries with questions.
4 discussion posts the length of an essay and you have to use all the readings so they are time consuming. The grading is pretty harsh don't expect this to be an easy A.

One of the best professors in my opinion. He really cares about his students and their success and wellbeing. He reads off slides in lecture then submits it on Canvas, so if you miss class, it's not a huge deal. Labs are graded for completion not correct answers, which is a huge relief. If you're on the fence of taking his class or not, do it.
Content proposes a challenge but Larry is the best!! Love forensics and want to go into the field and Larry just motivated me even more. Highly recommend :)

Larry is such a good prof who is so invested in his students and passionate about the material. The material is not easy but if you go to lectures and acc pay attention it will be so much easier. Labs r super easy, graded for completion. my rec is to draw the bones/features for studying, will make it 100x easier when tests roll around

He seems like a really genuine and cool guy! As a design student, this was a straightforward science credit that didn't overwhelm me. Only complaint is the discussion post assignments were hard, and I felt like there was one to many of them. The quiz answers were often direct quotes from lectures. My GE was a really picky grader

Very love hate relationship with this course. The content is decent and the professor himself is super sweet and accessible, but coming from a straight A student, the GEs are sooooo insanely knit picky on assignments, I chose to drop the course because I got graded down for the most minimal things that werent on the rubric.

For an online course, Ulibarri is easy to learn from because you can tell he is passionate about what he's talking about. It's important to take notes on the slides and listen carefully, because the quizzes usually had what he said word for word. He's a teacher that will make you chuckle.

Larry was an amazing professor, but was lecture heavy. Not too many assignments but in the later half the class the workload increases as you have to do a group presentation and write a 10-page essay. Are weekly quizzes, but they are open everything. Would take his class again, he gives great feedback, is funny, and easy to talk to after class

Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy A 100-level class. This was one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken, despite being an introductory class. The majority of the class is just memorizing bones and every little feature on them. This was so, so hard. The lectures were also kinda boring. Larry is a nice guy, though!

easy class to fulfill science gen ed, grades a bit slow, one thing that sucked was there was a total of 4 1000+ word "disscusion posts", which i feel shoud have been more labeled as an essay because it was misleading before reading further in the instructions, otherwise really easy class and very intresting!
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, gives great advice, and is very kind. Made our textbooks all free and was a very engaging lecturer. The class was pretty hard because I had to memorize most of the bones in the body, but he provided all the resources you would need and had some good Google slides.

Dr. Ulibarri is by far the best professor I have ever taken a class with at this university. I have now taken two classes taught by him and he cares about his students so deeply and you can tell how passionate he is about his work. He is an easy grader and assignment criteria is very easy to follow. He is super kind and very approachable.

As a non-Anthro major, this class was very informative and interesting. The lecture slides were very put together and intentional and are very important for both the midterm and final. Professor is very nice and engaging. Attendance not mandatory except for once-a-week labs. Definitely read all the slides and attend the labs and you will be good.

The best lectures I've experienced. He uses sound effects and relevant stories to make engaging content. Grading is two exams and labs, labs are graded on completion and extensive study guides are provided. I'm a poli sci major hoping to be in his class again. His final lecture of the class is one that every student should hear at least once.
Larry was a very nice professor and I am glad I took this class. It was pretty straight forward you just have to essentially write four essays but they are only 1000 words long each.

Larry Ulibarri is an awesome professor. I unexpectedly enjoyed his class. The lectures are interesting, and the workload is minimal—just four essays, four easy tests, and three video documentaries, all graded fairly. I'd definitely take another class with him.

Larry is amazing, I have had 3 classes with him. His classes are not hard but you have to put effort into your assignments. He gives great feedback on your writing, and is very quick to respond to emails. He sneaks extra credit into the lecture videos if you watch them! Assignments are not hard, but do take a lot of time, stay on top of deadlines!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Larry was an amazing professor; I was in the FIG, and he made it even more interesting. He da bone man for sure!! I love the Kahoot's we played sometimes at the end of class. The labs are very relevant to the weekly material and the lectures are easy to follow.

Professor Ulibarri is one of the best professors I've had at UO, and I'm sad I won't have him again. His classes aren't tough, and I came with no background knowledge of the subject at all, but they are still very interesting, and have a good mix of lecture and discussion. He is very caring, very passionate, and very knowledgable.

This is a very memorization-heavy course, and going to lectures and labs is very important if you want a good grade. His lectures were super helpful because of the weekly Kahoots, which I would use to study for the midterm and final. I never ended up getting the textbook so I don't think it's necessary to pass the course.

Dr. Ulibarri is an extremely engaging lecturer, his course content is interesting and he always tells relevant stories. He is very communicative and cares about every students success. Class is graded by a midterm, a final and labs so studying is important! I highly recommend any class taught by Dr. Ulibarri!
It's clear he is very passionate about his work, making this class especially engaging.

Really good lecturer, although I feel like the lectures are kind of drawn out. Easy to do the lectures at home if you miss class. Labs are really easy but attendance is mandatory and if you miss a lab the makeup assignment is super long. Overall, good prof, would take again.

Larry was fine. Pretty average lab science class - lots of memorization and reading. Grades are based on 2 exams, weekly lab reports, and a lab exam. Labs are very easy and he's very charismatic in lecture. Super willing to be flexible (I missed the midterm because I was sick and he was willing to reschedule for me).

I absolutely loved this class and this professor. It is clear that he cares a lot about his students and is passionate about the subject that he teaches which helped to make this a really good class. I would take this class again and currently, I am taking another class he teaches as well.

Dr. Ulibarri is a fantastic professor! He truly loves what he does, making the lectures very interesting/engaging. He is a kind-hearted person, who is dedicated to his work and students. The course can be difficult, but he makes the material fun to learn by making jokes and doing Kahoots. I highly recommend taking any class with Larry!!

This course is a lot of memorization and very content heavy but super worth it. The labs and lectures are super interesting. Having Dr. Ulibarri as a professor is such a privilege, his lectures are well taught, clear, and super engaging. This course was my favorite this term, just be prepared to study!!

Wonderful professor. He is very flexible and understands every kind of situation sometimes the material can get hard but he always has room for questions and time to help in anything you might be stuck on. Grading is harsh but there is a lot of feedback given and opportunities to bring your grade back up. overall he is a great professor.
Very flexible very easy to engage with

Prof Ulibarri is a great professor! He is extremely well-spoken and his lectures are very easy to follow. Though I found his exams hard, he is really respectful and caring with his students. As a trans student, he touched on the subject a bit and everything he said was extremely educated and made me feel seen. Very kind professor, highly recommend
He is one of the most caring professors who is passionate about what he teaches, and his classes are interesting to take!  He definitely cares about students, just a great guy.

Larry is a fantastic professor! It is obvious that he loves his field and the classes he teaches. Grading was very straightforward and a lot of info was provided to help study for exams. Everything comes from content covered in lecture, so as long as you go to class reading the textbook is unnecessary. GE's were also super knowledgeable!

I enjoyed this class and professor Ulibarri. He cares about the subject, and his lectures are clear. Attendance for lectures is not mandatory and the slides are posted online. You will only be graded on lab assignments (which require attendance), tests (midterm and final), and the final project. Lab assignments are graded tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best teacher I've ever had. Sometimes his lectures were long and boring but he always did his best to make things interactive. He's brought candy and other interesting treats to help us understand concepts. He is super caring and will help you reach out to other professors to get extra opportunities. Not a hard grader either.

I have taken something like 4 classes with Dr. Ulibarri. Larry truly puts his heart and soul into everything he does. This man clearly loves what he does and loves his students. There aren't enough kind words that I could fit into this review to properly express how great this professor is. His classes will challenge you and you will love it.

He is the sweetest man who is so passionate about what he teaches I will take any class he offers to have him again.  Participation was not necessary but I always went because he put so much love and effort into his course.  Even if you are not interested in the material he will captivate you.

Larry is a great professor but teaches this class like it is a 400 level. Be prepared to memorize a million things. Your grade is made up basically only by huge tests which makes this class super challenging. Awesome professor but don't take this class if you're not prepared for something extremely challenging.

I had Professor Ulibarri for my HC241 Top Primates class and I absolutely loved it. I was unsure about the class as the study of primates was new to me. Professor Ulibarri was so welcoming and passionate about the topics he taught us in class that it was hard not to feel the same. He really does care about his students. Take his classes!

I waited three terms to get into Larry's course and it certainly did not disappoint. His lecture's were really easy to follow and were wordy enough for you to understand the material in case you missed lecture. He also is wonderful to talk to outside of class whether it be about future career goals and advising or otherwise.

Loved his lectures and beginning of the week videos! I had his summer async course, there were hidden easter eggs for extra credit in his lectures and readings. The lectures were very long (40-60 min x 6) for a 4-week course, but the option to do an art project as a final was great. I enjoyed his caring personality and the class content. Loved him!
AMAZING lectures. you can tell he really cares about everything he talks about. he takes his time going over the material and is very thorough when answering questions.
I really liked his class, lots of reading but super interesting and he is very kind. Highly recommend. I am not a science major so I was nervous but this guy made the material highly accessible.

This was my second class with Professor Ulibarri. His lectures are great and the material is very interesting. The four quizzes are easy and open note. The discussion posts require more time and thought but are not difficult if you closely follow the guidelines/examples. Same with the final project. Great class highly recommend

Please take Animals & People with Larry!! He's the most caring prof I've ever had at UO. The class is super fun and you learn so much about animals. There aren't any exams, just some discussion posts, four easy quizzes (if you've taken lecture notes) and a final project in a format of your choosing. Lectures are great and so is this class!
This was a really interesting course that I took for my food studies minor but I think anyone could enjoy how applicable it is
Great teacher and super nice guy. This class was extremely interesting and taught well but you do need to attend in order to do good in the class.

As an HC class, it should be discussion-based, instead he lectured EVERY DAY (he is very kind and passionate though). LOTS of readings (provided) but interesting concepts/material. Weekly quizzes start easy and get harder when group lectures begin. You'll lead a 30-60 min lecture w/ other students from the class. Final project is a bit of a doozy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ulibarri is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. The class was easy for me, I got over 100% in it, but the material was so fascinating. Ulibarri put so much time into his lectures, his selected readings, and everything about the class. The discussion essays were enjoyable to write, which is rare for a college class. Take his classes!

I learned so much in this class and it was really interesting and useful information about nutrition. Definitely feels like hes trying to convince you to be vegetarian though. The quizzes were easy and straightforward but the discussion posts are really like 4 papers and one TA graded much harder than the other.

Mr. Ulibarri is super awesome and you can tell he really cares about teaching! There's 4 quizzes (which aren't the easiest but they're not terrible) and 2 big discussion posts and responses that you need to do! Overall really simple class and he doesn't give you too much work!

I love Prof Ulibarri! He's super nice and willing to help you get a good grade. I had late work which was not counted and a 60% in the class the week before the term ended, and I met with him and he was perfectly willing to meet with me and change my grade. He wants the best for his students. Also, the content of the course is super interesting!

Probably the most caring person I've ever met, he is truly a gem. You will never be bored with his lectures because he's so passionate. I can't emphasize enough how amazing he is - by far the kindest soul that I've met at the university. I would take many more classes with him if I could. Keep being you, professor Ulibarri!

Ulibarri was a fun professor! Class consists of lectures that you need to watch for the bi-weekly quizzes. In our specific course, we didn't have to get the textbook due to COVID. 2 big ongoing discussion boards, quizzes and video worksheets make up your grade. Pretty easy class and also very informative!! (Lectures posted on Youtube- hefty!!)

Ulibarri is an amazing instructor. This course would be beneficial to any student as it encourages all to become environmentally conscious and critical of our own effects on the world and its animals. Ulibarri is so passionate and his message is impactful even through online lectures. He truly cares about what he teaches and he makes me care too.

Larry is an amazing instructor. Even with an unexpected fully online course, I still learned so much. He's incredibly passionate about what he teaches and is a very caring guy. There are a couple of assignments every week but they're straightforward and aren't incredibly difficult. I've also become more environmentally conscious from his teachings.

Ulibarri is the best, by far the most passionate professor I have ever met. His online lecture videos are easy to understand & if you take detailed notes, what he says is word for word on quizzes. Discussion posts can be difficult but if you adhere to the instructions you will get a good grade (at least I did). I highly recommend Ulibarri & 369.

I love Larry! He is an amazing person. He inspired me to go vegetarian and he really cares about his students. I am not a science major but I really enjoyed listening to what Larry had to say. Thank you Larry. You are such a kind soul and I hope you have a great summer.

Larry is wonderful. Hes very passionate about the subject and teaching. He can get a bit off track sometimes in lectures on tangents about monkeys but the class is about monkeys so theyre interesting. The readings were a bit boring, but the tests are manageable and you get to watch squirrels for the final paper so overall great class and prof

Professor Ulibarri is awesome! I've taken multiple classes from him because I really like his teaching style. He knows that the subjects he teaches can be difficult so he takes the time to make sure you succeed. He responds to emails immediately with helpful details and doesn't make you nervous to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really invested in his work and students. Cares about his teachings, and has experience to back the knowledge! He offers easy, fun extra credit. If you attend class and pay moderate attention you can pass with a solid B. Take notes, and you're aceing his class. I recommend !

Great guy and teacher, really cares about getting the knowledge across. Attendance is not mandatory but you will get extra credit sometimes for showing up. You only need the textbook a few times but if you're not really into biology, definitely get it.

Larry is one of the best professors at UO. He doesn't give busy work, and the readings he does assign are thought provoking and relatively short. He does give "pop quizzes" in class, but sometimes that is as much as signing a paper saying that you were there.  His lectures are really funny and make you rethink your consumer habits! Take his class!
Lectures were long and often redundant, but assignments were fairly easy. If you need to take this class for credit, Patricia is a good professor for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She doesn't understand situations that happen with people and is open to helping out on a deadline even though its a complete online class with no lectures required to attend. Takes it way to serious for a simple online class. RUN
Get ready to actually do the work that she expects of you, but she is very clear with the expectations and makes projects very clear. Interesting topics covered. She is very nice.

Professor Lambert reads off of the slides entirely, and none of the information in the lectures was on the actual exams, only textbook material. Grade is 4 exams, which contained 50 multiple-choice questions and anywhere between 3-5 essay questions, one of which had to be 10-12 sentences. These had to be done between Fridays and Mondays at noon.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Lambert gives amazing, well thought out lectures, grading criteria is very well put together, and she is very upfront about the expectations for the course. She is a little bit of a tough grader, but she gives great feedback. This class is lecture heavy but she moves through content quickly and in an interesting way. Would highly recommend

I had a bad experience with those in the group project, I explained, gave her my paperwork and she was just surprised that it happened, but didn't budge on my grade. Nice person but assignments and grades are set in stone, heads up.

Professor Lambert is a bit of a tough grader but gives clear critiques for improvement down the line. I love her lectures. She puts a lot of time and effort into her talks and I appreciate that. You will learn a lot, and I appreciate how much she cares about her students.

Shes a good professor and does care about her students. The workload for her 300 levels is very heavy, which she discusses in the first day of class, so if thats an issue for you refrain from her classes. You do learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Lambert is god awful. In the middle of the COVID pandemic when all other professors tended to be more lenient, she graded harder, with average paper scores of B- (often lower), and papers make up about 60% of your grade. Two 5 page papers during finals week. Absolutely no mercy or concept of how much work students receive in other classes.

Worst class I've taken at this University by far. She is enthusiastic about marketing, and I don't think she's a bad lecturer, however, if her goal is to encourage critical thinking and understanding it does not necessitate hours of busy work and research "by design". My overall contention with this class is the workload and unclear instructions.

This course is unnecessarily difficult. The online mandatory lectures take 3hrs+ on average if you take notes/ watch them fully. First midterm has questions that are framed in a difficult fashion to even understand. Many poorly worded questions in the 62 problem midterm. It was hard to understand the information they were even trying to give you.

The worst class I have taken at UO. She does not care if her students succeed or fail. All she wants to do is catch people for plagiarism, which has happened to several people I know when they were able to prove otherwise. I have no other words than absolutely not.

Most responsive professor I've ever had. After 5pm and I have a question? I would Teams message her and she would respond within the hour 90% of the time. She wants students to succeed so she is willing to help in any way she is able, within reason. Her recorded lectures were fun and the course content was relevant to current pop culture.

I took this class online and she said at the beginning of the class that students would spend 12-15 hours a week on this class if they wanted to succeed. She, unfortunately, was not kidding. There is an intense amount of work and honestly I think that was because it was online. I am guessing it would be easier to take her class in person.

Dr. S is so kind and helpful, genuinely wants to see students succeed. She answers emails with miraculous speed. That being said, it's a TON of work, truly. You have to work hard for an A in this class, but it isn't impossible. Lots of work, super high ethical standards, if that doesn't sound like you, I'd advise against this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's nice and willing to support. Class isn't hard at all it's truly just REALLY TIME CONSUMING. Takes her video lectures and no use of AI SUPER serious. Overall the class is fine and manageable but her class takes up more time than any in person class I have ever taken my 4 years. Definitely not an “easy” online class for credit workload wise.

Her online class has a good amount of work, but not overwhelming. Clear instructions and responsive/kind if you ask for help. Lecture videos longish but I felt like I got a lot out of them. Just stay on top of your work, overall not a hard class and a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr S provides very clear, explicit instructions for assignments and deliverables. She's extremely responsive if you have any questions or want any feedback on course material. Even though the courseload is intimidating, she is dedicated to helping students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this class
no. just dont do it.
SAVE YOURSELF, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IN PERSON OR ONLINE!
Says this class will prepare you for the real world and then holds your hand in group projects and tells everyone how to play nice. Skip this lady if possible.

Genuinely one of the worst professors and people I have ever encountered. She has zero regard for her students, seems like she just wants to flag everyone for plagiarism. Do not waste your time being in her presence with this class.

Dr. S is not by any means a bad professor, as some have reported in the past. Yes, she does assign a lot of work, but it is very doable if you actually spend the time to sit down and do it. If you listen to her lectures, the projects are very easy and are genuinely fun. She also responds very quickly, so easy to get your questions answered.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Literally one of the nicest teachers ever and so helpful. Will help you any time of the day with anything you need. There is a lot of homework though and the lectures are super long, if you stay on top of it you will be completely fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seriously out of touch with reality. The lecture quizzes that ruin the course. Each one has about 2 hours of lecture content that she can see if you watched, if you skipped maybe 15 minutes you'd lose tons of credit , despite much of what her saying being unimportant and despite your accuracy on the quiz. Will take these things personally as well.

Honestly one of the worst professors I've had, period. The formats of the quizzes don't allow you to go back to previous questions,which makes no sense. She is also not pleasant to communicate with and her assignments require an excessive amount of meticulous information and researching/reading. Try to avoid if possible.

Very nice person, bad teacher. Would avoid taking her class if possible, she is picky about small things such as not watching 30 seconds of lecture videos, very picky grader, and expects communication even when it isn't necessary. Love her passion for the topic but don't love the format of the class

Beware biased reviews. This class was homework and lecture intensive, but the teacher is caring, helpful, and ultimately wants you to do well! She replies very quickly and offers great feedback.

-5 major homework assignments on weekly marketing topics/application (be ready to research)
-2 part group project
-Lengthy lectures (watch @ 2x speed)

I hope to never take a class with Professor Schneider ever again. I gave an ok rating for quality because she is very responsive and will give you any feedback you need. Other than that, I found the assignments and project instructions to be extremely word heavy and convoluted. It completely defeats the purpose of instructions if you can'tbeconcise

Dr. S is a very nice person who cares about her students a lot. But the course is a ton of work, and the professor can be picky when grading. The team project is way longer than it needs to be. Exams were pretty straightforward and easy. I would only recommend this course if you are ready to put in the work; if not, just take a different professor.

So understanding, fantastic professor. If you put in the effort you'll do fine and she wants you to do well. Responds so fast at all hours of the day and gives lots of feedback and grades last. Content is great and if you pay attention it's fairly similar to tests. Course seems scary at first but once you get in it and stay on top of it it's fine
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was by far the worst course I've taken at UO. BA317 was ridiculously jam packed with busy work and confusing combinations of assignments and needlessly long lectures, and every single assignment managed to have a novel's worth of writing to explain basic concepts. Would not take this again even if I had been paid to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Actually a horrible professor. Had an online class with her where she literally time stamped and reported anyone to the conduct board if they didn't watch lecture videos all the way through or were suspected of using AI. Would actually avoid this professor at all costs. Trust me. You will hate your life if you have a class with her.

This class is very difficult, but if you take it seriously, you will learn so much. The professor is so helpful and so accessible. She responds to emails in less than five minutes, no matter the day or time. If you reach out to her, she will help you. If you put in effort and work closely with Dr. Schneider, you'll get an A.

These ratings for Dr. S are not entirely accurate. Yes, there is a LOT of work. But you should plan in advance on how to get it all done. She gives plenty of time in advance to plan accordingly. Her Canvas page is full of information and tells you exactly what she expects on each assignment. Just put some actual effort in and you'll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is the worst teacher I have ever had. By far the worst experience I have ever had with a teacher or faculty of a school. She is by far obssesed with criticizing students work. She never says anyhting positive, doesn't help with assignemnts, and is striaght up rude. Never take her class, I hope she gets fired.

I thought an online class would be enjoyable, nope, she managed to make it insufferable. She is not understanding or compassionate to students. She believes her class should be the center of your life and takes it very personal when she feels you are not putting enough time in. The homework takes very long to complete and contains long instructions
Awful, mean women boring teacher, do not take!

She clearly is overly obsessed with her course. Exhibited signs of OCD in how she teaches and grades. Possibly one of the worst professors I have ever had. Save yourself and your sanity. Do not take this class.

Attendance was mandatory, if you arrived even 30 seconds late the assignment that is due before every class was deducted half of its points. She was serious about using AI and or plagiarizing and will deduct you a letter grade and give you a 0 on the assignment. DO NOT take her class.

Leah makes you waste hours a week watching her long-winded online lectures, which are graded. If you watch them at 1.25x or 1.5x speed, you will get a 0. If you answer the lecture questions with a word that she did not use in her lectures to describe a concept (i.e. mention a term from another marketing class), you will get a 0. Avoid this lady.

By far the worst experience I've had at the University of Oregon. Worst professor I've had in any UO department. Unhelpful and not understanding. PLEASE do yourself a favor and avoid at all costs. She will happily tank your GPA. Lectures are long, and full of mostly unhelpful info. Group project rubric is unnecessarily confusing. Waste of time.

Professor will give long winded lectures that take up a lot of your time. She fails to break down the concepts and make it easy to understand. Thus, the lectures are time consuming and have no real value. Group project is a good concept, but it is tainted with LONG instructions that are hard to follow, that she exploits to give bad grades. FAIL.

Dr. S is super easy to get a hold of— and you WILL need to reach out at some point because this class is so confusing. The lectures are long-winded, take hours to complete, but are full of good info. The group project instructions are super confusing, and no examples to reference. Nice teacher, awful class, lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It would be in your best interest to avoid this professor at all cost, the course material itself isn't difficult but this professor may have been the most harsh I have come across in all of my years at the school.

Absolutely awful professor. She provides no guidance for the team project, which is worth a large part of your grade, and is extremely unclear on expectations for assignments. Marks you tardy if you are more than a minute late to class, and only gives one excused absence. Worst business professor at UO stay away from her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall Dr. S is a nice person, but not a very nice teacher. Lots of unhelpful busy work, like writing 1-2 pages of research before each class. STRICT attendance, can't be 30 seconds late, one free absence a term. Midterm and final exams, also a major group paper/presentation that determines most of your grade. Avoid in person if possible.
Overall a good class but a ton of work. She is super nice and cares about her students. Exams are super long and kind of hard to study for.

Truly a wonderful person and she shows that she cares, but a lot of the assignments don't help in understanding what marketing is. There is a lot of unnecessary busy work, she grade you harshly for attendance, and lastly gives you exams that have more than 50 questions with each question having a large paragraph for you to read.
Absolutely horrible. Ridiculous amount of work and tests are nothing like the lectures. Stay away at all costs

Honestly the sad reviews for Dr. S makes me sad. She's a really great professor that is super passionate and caring. She's very accessible outside of class and her lectures are fun and informative. Yes she is harsh about attendance but follows the university guidelines she is required to. She cares about her students so reach out if you need help!

Feels more like a class where she parents and disciplines her students. Overall a nice person, but very harsh on assignments, attendance, exams. Docks you points for showing up two minutes late to class, but then holds the class for multiple minutes after class is over.
Nice teacher overall, however, very tough grader, hard exams. Hold's class the day before Thanksgiving. Don't take her; you will regret it.
Horrible professor. Do not take this class online. She hasn't updated her lecture videos in over 5 years.
Outdated work and very harsh in grading. Expectations are unreal!
Worst teacher I've ever had

Dr Schneider defiantly knows her material, but this is a very heavy workload class. You have to spend a lot of time doing HW and group projects. The discussions are the worst part, and they are extremely harshly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not worth it. Material is easy but assignments are very tedious and graded super harshly. I wrote over 1000 words on a discussion and she still said to elaborate. She isn't gracious and her feedback isn't helpful.
She has extremely hard expectations. Even if you spend hours and hours on an assignment she will grade you down or accuse you of cheating. Avoid her if you can.

Took as an elective, the most time-consuming class I've taken at this school. Spend AT LEAST 15 hours per week on homework for this course and a ton of group work. Weekly quizes, long and tedious writing assignments. The material isn't difficult, but she's an EXTREMELY HARD grade. Wouldn't recommend this class as an elective based on the workload.

Leah is by far one of the best professors I have had in the LCB at UO. It is a heavy course full of assignments, presentations, and activities. However, I learned more than I have ever learned in any other marketing class at UO. She gives great feedback that can help guide you in your projects and steer you in the right direction.

I love Leah! Always accessible through teams and she's genuinely just a sweet girl. Class is based off group project (paper and presentation) and lecture video quizzes. You can text her at any time and she's happy to go over quizzes and give points back. only con: sometimes grading is a little unclear. 
textbook is available for free on libgen ;)

I believe that Schneider is a good person. However, she assigns an unholy amount of homework but the issue here is that the homework consist of incredible amount of writing without any objectives (Company Questions assignments). Also, she is paranoid of her tests being posted and the quizzes are structured tediously. Doable, but if you can avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: While she is a nice person, her class is structured terribly. She assigns an unholy amount of busy work every week, which contribute little to your overall learning. Lecture videos are 4+ years old, there is little engagement with students, and grading is harsh for trivial assignments.

Leah was an overall good teacher! Her lectures and assignments are very tedious and if you don't follow the directions precisely she will mark you down - but overall the class is very doable and easy! She has answered all of my team's messages within 5 minutes and is super caring and wants to see everyone succeed.

Dr. S was honestly one of my favorite profs. Her lectures are quite heavy but if you take time to watch them (1.5x speed), then the exams are easy. The group work sucks but she's accommodating if you give her notice and are nice about it. She sends out a lot of announcements to remind you about assignments too

The *bad* reviews about Leah are insensitive. She is a super responsive, caring professor who truly gives you everything you need to succeed. Yes, she kinda gives a lot of homework, but we are in college what do you expect! The homework she gives is seriously simple if you just set aside some time to sit down and complete it. She's actually great.

She is awful. One of the worst teachers I have ever had. Insane amount of busy work for no reason. Also her online lectures are from multiple years ago yet she had the audacity to assign and critique assignments so harshly. Avoid her at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible horrible horrible.  Very tough grader, unrealistic expectations, lectures are wordy and any feedback is wordy but no matter what you do your grade is harsh.  Worried of possibly failing.  Group project graded harshly.  She really should help students pass her class vs setting them up for failure.

There is a fine line between pushing your students and setting them up for failure, and Dr S. plays jump rope with this line. Do not take her class, she has IMPOSSIBLE standards and will not only screw you on individual grades, but team projects as well. Will not make any exceptions for anyone, and gives a TON of homework. AVOID AVOID AVOID

Dr. Schneider really is one of the better teachers at Lundquist. She is responsive outside of class, and although she is a harsh grader, it is not hard to receive good grades in her class with a little bit of effort. She is super understanding and helpful when concepts don't make sense, so don't be afraid to ask questions!

If possible avoid her classes, overcomplicates assignments. Lacks social awareness, and provides poor instructions, yet grades extremely harsh. Besides her grading, you feel no excitement, no real value in learning from her. Simply, don't take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her expectations are too high, especially on "communication activity" assignments. I averaged 1,200+ words for each discussion post, which was with concise wording, and she expected me to "expand my answer more." She has no understanding of business writing and expects nothing less than a dissertation for discussion post assignments and quizzes.
She just sucks no nicer way to say it but lots of worse ways I would describe her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was a heavy workload. However she didn't give exceptions to anything. I worked full time while taking a full course load and I was given no sympathy. On the final project we were marked down for our gif's not being animated. We sent her three emails clarifying that they didn't work after the file was downloaded. She never responded. F.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Junior - 4.0 student. Assignments were not matched to the time required & Professor was so unforgiving about missing assignments due to poor communication on her part. Canvas page listed the wrong due date and despite submitting at 6 am on Saturday (supposed to be due Friday at midnight), I received an F that dragged my entire grade down. Avoid.

Please do yourself a favor and avoid this person. She will show how motivated she is to take away your points without any particular pattern. Avoid her and her outdated teaching style (and sometimes aggressive and rude behavior) . Avoid, Avoid, Avoid at all costs. Coming from an A average student.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely high yet unclear expectations. Avoid this class if you hate group projects. We worked so hard as a team but still got bad grades. WAY harder than all other 300-level classes and even most of the 400-levels.

One of the worst teachers I have had, not going to lie. She is an incredibly hard grader and leaves no room for mistakes. If you accidentally miss an assignment bc of real life, she does not care. Her tests are super long with paragraph long questions and super hard. For a minor level business class she makes it miserable. don't do it.

Too hard on students, esp. during COVID. No leeway if assignments missed. Big group projects, which wouldn't be a problem except the amt of homework and the way the tests are made is wild for a 300 level class. Also, we're not allowed to discuss even just opinions about the tests with others, or we risk a zero. Prob against the rules. Bad vibes.

Ridiculous discussion boards every week which are pretty much essays. Final was pretty difficult for a course that could be much simpler. Purchased the book and opened it maybe twice. Not great experience work load was ridiculous given how time consuming discussion boards were alone. Group project was fine, had to record presentation together.

Professor Schneider is a good person and I have to admit it. The final worth 30% of the total grade, and individual assignments that took me dozens of hours to do only worth 18%. The questions on the final are so confusing, seems like she was meant to do it. Last warning, if you have no passion for it, then skip it because you won't get an A anyway

AVOID. Very unclear on grading criteria and getting full points on assignments is practically impossible since she refuses to give clear examples of whats good and what isnt. Lectures were boring and she was more worried about the integrity of the class than she was people succeeding. If you take her, be ready to do way more than necessary.
Dont recommend taking her class. Very tough grader and not much feedbacks.

Leah is very passionate and cares a lot for her students' well-beings. The coursework was very straight-forward and she provided clear guidelines and expectations for her grading scale. Lectures are a little long, but she did a great job at being engaged in the classroom and providing real life application to the material. Highly recommend.

She has a lot of energy in class. Tests and projects are fairly straightforward as long as you stay consistent with your workload. Interesting lectures and gives good feedback when you ask for help. Overall, I enjoyed her class a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very enthusiastic and cares about her students. Tests are difficult and participation matters but if you go to class and do well on your final project, you're all good.

Very enthusiastic professor who makes the lectures interesting. However like a lot of the business core classes its a lot of group work. She expects a lot in the papers and presentations. Almost no one is a marketing major, but she expects us to be that motived.

If you are an international student, skip her class! you won't learn anything from her class only paper paper paper! If you have no friends with you in the same group, then your team members are your biggest enemy(pay attention to peer evaluation).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really fun professor with a lot of love for the subject. It's more work than I expected but she makes it worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult, even having done all the reading and homework assignments. She makes you work the hardest you've ever worked and then gives little back in reward. She's very enthusiastic for lectures, but she expects you to be just as enthusiastic about the class. Lot of work for a Minor Degree class. Be leery when signing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very strict and a pretty rude attitude in class. She's enthusiastic and gives interactive lectures, so that helps. But she really demands a lot without being very clear on what she wants exactly.

Great professor! Leah is very enthusiastic about lectures and cares about the students she teaches. She expects A LOT from her students, but you will learn a lot! Grading criteria was clear, lectures were engaging, projects and tests were focused and helpful to learning the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a tough grader but I don't know how fair that is,,  u never really know why u get a B+ as opposed to an A  for example. Those little differences add up and it can be nerve-racking especially if ur aiming high and trying ur best always other than that she is very helpful and its true what everyone said, she's very enthusiastic about marketing.

She is very into marketing. She is a very tough grader. Expect to have a 20 page paper that has to be very in depth in your company. She cold calls during class so you have to read. She knows everyone's name even if you do not think she knows who you are. With this being said you have to show up to class.

Participation is mandatory, so is showing up to class. She wants you to know every single detail in the textbook to the point it's almost impossible to memorize everything. She is REALLY  into marketing and you need to also be to make it through.
Awesome, show up to class, participate, optional final, great teacher overall

Your grade in this class is only based on the two midterms and a final, although he gives you the exam questions a week before you take the test which was helpful. His lectures were fine, but hard to focus on and lengthy. There are a ton of readings and you have to take a lot of notes. It wasn't a bad class, but I wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have previously taken his PS205 class. I have the same gripes. Lecture and reading-heavy, and he's not very good at explaining economics to beginners. There are only 3-4 assignments that make up your entire grade. He makes comments that are a bit demeaning if you don't have knowledge about certain concepts. He's nice, just not a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good at explaining econ concepts to non-econ majors. Made otherwise boring material seem fun and interesting. Strongly recommend his International Political Economy class, but every class I took with him was great

I loved Professor Skalnes' class. He is very knowledgeable and interactive during lectures, and you can tell he really likes to teach. His grading is tough but fair. You need to do all the readings and attend most of the lectures if you want a shot at a good grade. He's very approachable and happy to answer any questions you have. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Skalnes is a great lecturer. He makes class interesting, and the readings, while helpful, are usually covered in-class so not always needed. However, his classes have a tight gradebook (1 essay, 2 exams) and messing one up tanks your chances for a good grade in class. Still, content is interesting and worthwhile.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lecture attendance wasn't mandatory but discussion sections were. I never bought the textbook and was fine. Goes through slides very fast. Only grades 4 things, midterm, final, one essay, and discussion attendance. Nice guy, extremely smart. Great GEs too.

Grade was based off of three assignments.  While it is a little difficult to understand professor skalnes he knows his stuff.  The midterm and final are both 35% of your grade so study hard for those.  I made a mistake when studying for the midterm and emailed him about retaking it and he let me.  If he hadn't I would have failed the class

Pretty easy if you put in the work. Take notes, READ and do the study guide IN DEPTH (start early) bc the test is the EXACT same. I will say, I would recommend taking macro econ beforehand because it definitely does help, it's totally doable without it (I didn't take it) but you'll have to put in more work to understand some of the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy and extremely knowledgeable, but the entire term there's only 3 assignments that you're graded on and you're pretty much screwed if you don't do well on them. He also doesn't believe in giving A's, first class he'll tell you in his many years of teaching he's only given 2 As. He asks you to buy 2 textbooks and we did not use them at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only graded by a few things which was difficult

Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but heavily encouraged to understand the material. Keep up with reading assignments and you should do just fine. Only grades you on 3 assignments: written midterm exam, written final exam, and a paper at the end of the term. With 30+ years teaching IR, he is very passionate about this subject and his students.

kinda really boring at the beginning but if you do the readings and go to lectures and get engaged in class discussion then it will be more fun. mostly just do the readings, take good notes on them, and go to discussion and you'll probably get an A. Also, the tests are exactly like the study guides which is so nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lars is an interesting professor who loves to go on rants, and who is obviously passionate about the subject. Very few grades so make sure to pour your heart into each one. The lectures are interesting but definitely not needed to get a good grade in the class. Participation in the section is very important for grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Skalnes solely relies on lectures but only barely explains the theories he's talking about. There were only 3 assignments, a midterm, a final and a paper. He said he would hand out the topics for the final paper a month before it was due, but he only handed it out 1 week before. There is no rubric for anything and he doesn't clarify
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Skalnes is one of my favorite teacher at the UO. He is always willing to help students who seek help. He doesn't give you much assignments, but listening to his lectures and skimming through the reading helps you to understand the material. Not only that, he is passionate about what he's teaching. Would love to take his other classes!

I absolutely loved his class. He was always willing to meet students who want help. He did assign heavy reading, but skimming through is enough to get the gist. Lectures may not be mandatory, but attending lectures HELPS A LOT. His tests are basically the same as the study guide; so just go through the study guide seriously and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this class. The material is so scattered and the professor doesn't explain when he moves to another topic. He doesn't tell the GE's anything and the quizzes have material on them that is not talked about in lecture or in the readings. This course is extremely frustrating, again I do not recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class relies on 3 assignments. Two are in-class exams. However, he doesn't give much advance notice as to the content on those exams. You can try to guess. And he does provide some semblance of a study guide. But it's vague and covers everything. If you don't read the assigned material or have some background in IR/Int'l Econ, you might fail.

I would give a 0 if I could. Professor does not communicate with GE's and misinforms students about what is on the quizzes. Behind on lecture slides, by 2-3 weeks. Also grades midterm and final, not by a rubric and answering correctly, but in comparison to other students, so the student that goes above and beyond sets the standard for the question.
An incredibly smart professor. His insights into international relations are consistently well spelled out. Lectures can get dry, but generally, he maintains an interesting path and keeps me engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher Ive ever had. So unorganized. So uncaring. Currently, we are 4 lectures behind. The grading is uneven between students because he doesnt communicate with this GEs. Were so behind because he spends his whole class off topic (sometimes only going through 2-4 slides). GEs tell us to study topics not on tests. Take online.
The class isn't too difficult, however lectures are hard to listen to because any time you try to answer a question he interrupts you and goes on his own tangent.

Lars' class was just fine. He can get off topic really easily in lectures and expects you to have background knowledge of current and past world events, but he grades pretty easily for how difficult the material can be.

For such long lectures, it's unusual how unecessary attending them is to understand the material. Were it not for a participation grade, it would be possible to succeed without them. Lars seems opinionated in his grading. You might score higher if you appeal to his perspective. I feel like I wasted more time than was required to learn.

While Lars is an extremely knowledgeable man when it comes to IR, the course grading rubric is non-existent. He essentially has the ability to decide your grade based on any arbitrary standard. After receiving a C+ (class average) on the midterm, I spent over double the time studying, only to get a C+ on the final with no comments...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Thoroughly enjoyed his lecture, but there is a very large amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Skalnes is very informed and delivers his lectures well. He is easy to follow in class and explains the material fully. He assigns a lot of readings so it's key to keep up with them, especially because your class grade is just a midterm, take-home essay question, and a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: What a great guy
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lars assigns an insane amount of reading including an entire book, however, if you have any interest in international relations you will enjoy your class. He is an extremely knowledgeable man and while he can be tough during in-class discussion it is to help you learn the material. He is a very easy grader on tests if you have read the material.

His lectures are really dry and monotoned. I didn't bother to go to class for 3 weeks but ended up with an 84 on the midterm. Anyways, all the lecture slides are posted online so you could teach yourself the material like I did. Your grade will rest on 3 components, 40% of your grade rest on your midterm, 40% on the final, 20% on "participation".
Great professor. Very knowledgeable and willing to help out students. Cared about students learning the material, and was always there for questions. Would definitely recommend him.

Prof Skalnes sometimes connected with students, but overall I felt he did not do a particularly good job of instructing. He quickly fell behind in material that his syllabus dictated would be addressed, his lectures were 80 minutes of him speaking in a rather monotone voice, and lost students' interest quite quickly. Would not recommend.
Readings are easy but his slides aren't good. His organization and timeline are hard to follow.
engaging class.
Not engaging at all.

The class is basically him lecturing the whole 80 minutes day after day. Quizzes are all unannounced "pop" quizzes and the essay questions are always weeks old and irrelevant to current subjects. Studying for them are just dumb. His textbook reading list is unorganized and sporadic. Take home essay prompt was very unclear and grading was punitive.
i love how much he cares and respects his students opinions, this class was interesting and an easy A

This is for Soc 458 - Cultural Sociology. Professor Light is super nice and he totally knows what he is talking about. He highly encourages participation and rarely forces it. You should definitely take him. There were 3 in-class papers but we ended up only doing 2. And there were 2 papers but they were fun. He is honestly a fun, cool guy.

Had Prof Light for SOC 310 social theory this past spring, loved his class and personality. His lectures were super entertaining and he grades relatively fairly. He knows his stuff but you have to come to class to pass. Would love to have him again
