reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Light is passionate about what he teaches and it comes through in his lectures. Occasionally he talks in circles, but thats sociology for you. Just come to class, do your essays and you will get a good grade.

Prof. Light is a good professor however his lectures are very boring. His class overall is very easy if you pay attention and are good at writing essays. There are 10 short exercises throughout the class and three long essays along with a final at the end. Reading is encouraged although you can get by without doing it. Overall good but very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Light is by far one of my favorite professors at UO! He engages with the class and really takes time to address social issues going on in the world. His class was very easy, only essays, no tests. He thoroughly explains each topic and goes into detail about them, giving examples. I would absolutely take another class with him!

Professor light is a good professor who tries to make the class interesting. He was reasonable about grading and things like late work and honestly just wanted people to learn. If you do the work this class is very manageable.

He is enthusiastic about the topic and does an excellent job relating it to contemporary examples. Overall super interesting and is super respectful towards his students. Im used to checking out and doing my work, but he made me want to really engage. Fav prof thus far.
Do the reading, try best to write the essay; not easy to be good, but show passion and the best try ever you could.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Light is a super nice guy. He's a family man and knows what he's talking about. One problem with this class is his use of vocabulary. He constructs these obscenely complex and difficult to understand sentences which makes it really hard to follow his lectures. I spent more time trying to decifer his lectures than I did on the work itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The readings are boring but that's bc the course is classical theories. Ryans lectures make it all very interesting tho! He tries (and succeeds) to be down to earth and relatable. I loved his lectures on bureaucracy and capitalism. His sup materials where all very interesting. I did not love his/his GE's grading however.

Great class, nice/funny prof. Class time was always used effectively. The lectures are plentiful, but helpful and you learn a lot. Be sure to do the assigned reading, though. Class discussions are excellent when people actually read and participate. Occasional partner and group discussions, quizzes, and a couple tests. Totally doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ryan Light is a great professor. He is funny, kind and his lectures are super interesting. Theory is a tough subject to break down, but his lectures and power points make it much easier. His class can be a bit boring, as the material is quite boring, but if you don't go you won't pass. He has pop-quizzes, so make sure you go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: one of the hardest and worst teachers I have ever had. Uses language nobody understands and you're only right when you answer the way he thinks and wants you to. reading is horrendous and the tests are super hard. STAY AWAY
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Light is a really good teacher. He is good and conveying what needs to be learned and what he will be testing you on. I think I did well because we had good GEs, though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ryan, like his wife, is extremely passionate about Sociology. He has a clear understanding of the theorists and how they fit into Sociology. His passion is to allow students to understand the material and strives for your success. He presents material clearly and breaks it down for understanding. Do expect reading, essays, and pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took SOC410 Science & Society. The class ended up only having around 10 people in it.  This was my second class with Ryan. He is a good professor. I hope to take more classes with him before I graduate.
top five professors I've ever had. he's the shiznit. he is ridiculously talented at teaching dense material and motivates students to think on their own. he challenges and inspires. five stars!

The last comment was spot on haha. Ryan is hard to listen to at times due to the "grandiloquence." When he's not trying so hard, its a great class. Beware that most soc classes are in that crummy building.

Ryan is one of the best professors I have studied under within the Sociology Department at UO. His lectures are informative. He encouraged seminar style participation. Don't miss class because attendance is required and if you miss too many classes he will automatically give you a failing grade.
Professor Light is great at explaining dense material and he is an extremely fair grader.

I love Professor Light! Yes, the readings and theories can be difficult to understand but you're in a 400 level class! Don't come into it expecting easy readings and content. He makes funny jokes and loves for students to give their opinions in class. Very helpful! Make sure to attend class, they pass around a sign-in sheet.

Professor light continues to be one of my favorite professors. His classes are a challenge but the amount of knowledge gained is invaluable. He really gets students to engage in the material. He is clear in his teachings and passionate about his study. He is a fair grader  and makes himself available to all students.

Light was a really nice professor and does a great job at breaking down theories... The only downside is the subject which would probably be boring no matter who taught it. I think he would be a great professor in a different class where he would be able to teach a more interesting topic

He is a terrific professor! Easy-going and knowledgeable. Visit his office hour and you will have a better understanding of those complex sociological theories! He replies e-mail in details. Definitely recommend his class!
Very approachable and easy to talk to.  Had a keen interest in the subject matter and helping people to succeed as long as they had a mutual interest in learning.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Great Great Great!! I am new to Sociology and in a huge ridiculous classroom Ryan Light provides a great learning environment. Ideas are respected and discussed with ease.

Ryan is an amazing teacher! He uses a textbook that is so practical and inline with what he is teaching.  He is great about responding to emails and is really helpful if you go to officehours.  He made a class that could have been painful really interesting and worthwhile.  Try to take him for 311 if you can! The challenge is worth it.

Ryan has become my favorite prof. at Oregon after 3 classes. Class attendance is crucial to your grade but this is because you don't want to miss what he teaches. A good amount of reading is required for the 410 classes but it is well worth it and interesting. He is very friendly and conversational and will be happy to help. highly RECOMMEND!

I have had Ryan for two terms now. He does assign a fair amount of reading but I have never once found it necessary to complete in fact I have received two great grades and haven't touched a book. Fair amount of writing but an easy grader.
Requires just way too much work for one quarter. So much reading and writing to do, it's ridiculous. Don't miss one class, or you're screwed.

She baked the entire class cookies twice and they were great. I was trying to figure out how one person even bakes that many cookies at a time. They had an infusion of caramel that really added a unique twist to the generic cookie formula you often see. The lectures prepared us very well for each exam, important because of their heavy grade weight.

Overall one of my favorite professors She keeps the lectures engaging, focused, and interactive. I think she explains things very well and there are a lot of resources if you do need additional help. The three tests do take up a considerable portion of the grade but they are very similar to the practice problems/test and not cumulative.

Laura Wellman has by far been the best professor I have ever had with my time at University of Oregon. She is the reason I pay for college. She teaches like she knows exactly what shes talking about, never stopping or saying "uhms". Her canvas is set up perfectly to follow and do reviews, as well as her videos are super helpful to go back and learn

A normally difficult class, made easy by a great professor. It was always clear exactly what needed to be studied and while the concepts could be confusing sometimes, once you had everything studied you could be confident you would do good every time. One of the most well put together courses I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's really sweet and baked us cookies. Lectures are dense and fast, and you really have to try to keep up. She gives plenty of resources to help you succeed though.

Professor Wellman is an absolute goat. She made cookies for our entire 200 person lecture TWICE and they were delicious. There is one homework assignment a week, usually only having between 5-7 questions, midterms are non-cumulative and aren't too challenging.
I was out for a couple of weeks, and she took the time to help me catch up on work. Very supportive when I had questions.
Extremely supportive professor. She offers many ways for students to stay on track with material and get good grades. She's also just very sweet and welcoming.
Prof. Wellman is the kindest teacher I have encountered. Taking her class has been a breath of fresh air, learnings form her has been such a joy.

Went to review session today. She had us try problems on our own, then she went through solutions. There were also a couple of bonus questions. She finished a bit early, but then let us stay and study/ask additional questions. Awesome!
Canvas page is great. Also meets one on one outside of class to review exam.

Adored Laura! She obviously cares about us. She provides videos of the lectures, reminds us where to get extra help, and is also willing to meet outside of class when WE can meet. She sets us up for success. It is a tough class to do well in, at least for me, but I appreciated Laura's patience and kindness. Wish she taught more classes.
She is good at her job
Prof. Wellman is very helpful at answering my questions and takes time during class to see if anyone has questions. Constantly checking in.
I really appreciate Laura's extra review sessions, and practice exams/study resources. She provides all the resources that I need.
Very organized! Lots of reminders! The Laura!
I always felt that Prof. Wellman cares for her students. She wants us to understand the course and do as best as we can.
Tests are most of the points, but she provides lots of study material/opportunities to practice. I highly suggest taking advantage of review materials!
She keeps the students engaged, easy to ask questions, and offers different ways to describe if unclear. Great lectures.

I personally didn't love Wellman's style of teaching but I did appreciate all of the resources she offered. There are online lectures, study guides, practice quizzes, etc you can use to study for exams. She took the student survey's to heart and made changes accordingly, she definitely cares about helping students succeed.
Would recommend. Helpful professor. Minimal homework. Was a given ample study material for tests. Tests were straightforward.
Great professor. Tough content, but she is so helpful. Highly recommend.
Very accommodating and helpful. Always found time to help me outside of class.

I had to take this class twice because I didn't put in the time. I didn't use any of the practice material the first time around. Second time around, I used practice questions, attended review sessions, tons of stuff.
Professor Wellman is awesome! She puts so much into her materials. Honestly, just show up and follow along, do the work. You'll be fine.
She posts vidoes of all lectures and review sessions. So easy to review before tests.
Tests are challenging, but so many practice problems posted on Canvas. Show up and do the work and you'll be fine. Prof. Wellman's review session are also a big help.

One of the best professors ive ever had here. She truly cares about the success of students and constantly askes during lecture if she needs to repeat or rephrase anything. She posts all of her lectures/course material answers and doesnt require attendance. Tests were hard but practice tests were accurate and she provided lots of prep material.
I always have at least a few questions after lecture. She always patiently walks me through step by step. Much appreciated. She is awesome.
Really enjoyed having this professor, she was very well organized, providing handout for easy follow along notes for the lectures. She answers emails relatively quick and always open for questions.
I wish Professor Wellman taught more classes! Great professor!
Solid Canvas page, lots of resources. Content is a little dry, but I'm not sure there is much she can do about that.
great quater! thx prof. wellman!
She baked 500 cookies for the entire lecture and if that doesn't show that she actually cares then I don't know what does.
I have taken ACTG 213 3 times, this is the first with Laura. Laura is way better. I'm actually going to pass the class this time.

She actually listens! I left a mid-quarter review and Prof. Wellman took my comment to heart and adjusted. It was a simple request to print the student handouts differently, but she came through. Thank you Professor Wellman!

It's obvious Laura genuinely cares about her students' wellbeing and success in the course. Her lectures are clear, move at a reasonable pace, and she constantly asks if anyone needs her to slow down or clarify anything. She even offered a review session every week led by her where she goes over the week's concepts/problem. Definitely recommend her
Review session was great. Cleared up so much for me.
I was unable to attend review session, prof generously recorded for me. thanks!
Pre-records all lectures. Highly recommend watching before class! Made it is easy to follow along.
Wasn't sure if I should take online or in person. Def take in person if you can.
Prof posts everything in advance. Class already laid out. Review sessions every Friday a plus.
Super helpful, very organized. Little dry, but clear.
Not good bruv
I have really enjoyed this class. I didnt do as well as I had hoped in yerms of my grade, but I truly have learned a lot, and I feel a lot more confident with accounting.
Thanks for the great class! Have an awesome summer!
The videos are very straightforward and I like how she explains the material! Some stuff was a bit confusing but that isn't entirely her fault, accounting can be tough but she makes it bearable
Loved the class and the professor. Class is run very well.
The modules were pretty straightforward each week. I learned the most from the homework assignments.
I really liked how this course was organized and it felt like things built off of each other without being overwhelming
Laura was very concise when explaining content and was always willing to slow down or re-explain concepts if necessary.
I think Professor Wellman does a good job communicating the material in a way that makes sense.
Great Module, very organized, easy to find materials!
I have really enjoyed this course! Prof. Wellman is a fantastic instructor.

The course page is very well organized and having the files available to the student at any time was incredibly useful. The course slides were always available to print or review and in general the openness for files and reference/example made this course very accessible.
the questions practice is very helpful.

Prof. Wellman has clearly given a lot of thought to the way she presents material and explains topics. While accounting is not my
strong suit, I feel that I have a good grasp of the course materials and really appreciate her efforts.
gets paid as if she's actually teaching a class (nope, it's just McGraw hill connect.) but doesn't respond to emails. nice!
This class was not that hard Laura did well to teach and offer in class examples. Just do the homework and use the practice tests and you will do fine.
Very monotone, tries to trick you on tests

Easily the worst professor I've had. She makes it clear she doesn't want to be teaching. She treats this course as an online class and she doesn't provide any support. I sat in the front row and she would make jokes with her student teachers about students questions. She was bad at explaining the concepts. I'd recommend avoiding this professor.
Not very accommodating. Lectures feel read straight from the slides and they are not at all engaging. Honestly, would not recommend. Class median on final was 67 percent.

The only way I passes this class and didn't get a C was from having a private tutor. The lectures were no help, the practice quizzes are nothing like the exams(expect the exam to be 10x harder). There is no extra credit, Hw and labs count for very little. The exams make up around 70 percent of your grade if you do bad on one you won't recover.

3 tests a term. She puts 2 many long questions on the tests with 2 short of time to complete. She makes u use a scantron which wastes more time & she always starts her tests late.
She only gives 6-7 multiple choice practice problems before each test. Only 7!
Students have asked her 2 give more in the past, yet she still won't. Don't take her class

Provides additional lecture videos that are helpful when studying later, lectures go over examples in follow along note taking packets, Practice Quizzes were great study material, practice tests were poorly written and too short. She tries to help if you ask. Overall just ok, do not want to take her again though.
I really appreciate Professor Wellman's clear and comprehensive teaching style.

Prof Wellman is very thorough in presenting the course content but expects students to watch videos and print out long packets prior to class. Goes over one long example to explain content which made understanding new concepts overly complicated. Not a fan of her lecture style, very disengaging. Midterms require lots of studying and practice!!

Laura Wellman is extremely hard to understand during lectures. She is scattered and hard to follow. She explains the lecture through confusing examples. I have to rewatch her videos because I come out of class feeling so lost. So just be prepared for that. 

Also, the GE's are not helpful at all.

Good luck!

Professor Wellman puts up a well organized course. Everything is posted at the start and is clear. My guess is that some of the bad reviews are from students that aren't putting in the work. Lots of resources and Laura is great at answering questions and explaining concepts whenever I ask.

I think Professor Wellman is a great professor. She is engaging and provides many extra materials to help you succeed. Although she goes over her lecture slides quickly in class, she has videos posted on Canvas going over the lecture slides, which you should watch before class. She is also helpful in explaining concepts if you need help.

Do not recommend this Professor. She doesn't teach the class, just goes over examples the whole time at a pace no one can keep up with. Many students find her lectures as a waste of time as she plans lectures horribly.

I think Professor Wellman is good. Although lectures tend to be fast at times, she is very patient and explains things thoroughly. If you missed a few things in lecture, she also gives a lot of helpful resources and videos for you to review on. Overall, if you show up to lectures, do the hw, and practice, you'll be fine.

She has no clue how to teach. Expects you to print out 20 page packets before class and just has you do examples on your own. She treats like an online class expecting you to watch videos and understand everything before going to class so she doesn't have to teach. Talks way too fast and just is not good at explaining things.

She gives incredibly boring lectures and it's very difficult to pay attention to her. Overall, she does not know how to teach the material. Do yourself a favor and take someone else. I've never disliked a teacher this much in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She talks way too fast during lecture. It feels like she expects you to know everything and just gives u examples to work on. I feel like i learned more doing the homework and lab assignments than during her lectures.

She is a very rude professor and seems like she does not want her students to succeed. In class one day, a student asked for more study materials for exams and she was very unwilling to do so. If I were you I would take a class with anyone else but her by far the worst professor I have ever had.

this class is a super boring subject to teach so I understand it is hard to keep students engaged, but he teaching style just is not for me. It is so hard to retain any of the information and anything that we learned in lecture. She does provide lots of materials and those are super helpful for when studying for the midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Laura was my favorite accounting professor. She is so authentic in her teaching and has a clear and straightforward approach. She proves resources and is more than happy to help. I'm so grateful to have taken her class!

Laura was super sweet. Accounting is a very hard subject and she did amazing teaching it. Anyone who didn't do well simply didn't pay attention or skipped classes, and the exams are fair. She has a dry humor which is super entertaining during lectures. I love her style, shoutout Laura Wellman!
Doesn't teach just tells.

I absolutely loved Laura Wellman; was a great teacher and very comforting. Posts all of her lectures online, so if you want to review, it's super convenient. Exams are fair and based on what you do in class. It's accounting, so you have to put in work ofc. Overall, Laura was genuinely caring and wanted her students to succeed, I recommend her!!

I don't know what everyone is on about, but this class is fine. She is a good teacher and if you do the work and takes notes, you will be fine. It's a boring subject, but she teaches the class well and is very nice.
She is straightforward but comes across as quite harsh and strict.
Obviously very knowledgeable but has a tendency to talk down to her students and come across as rude. Frequently interrupts herself to say “No talking!” during her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her during her first term at UO, and she was super clear/organized with her content. She is always willing to re-explain a topic during lectures or say it in a different way which was helpful. Overall, an easy class to follow as long as you do pre-reading and try the practice problems she provides.

Lectures are very fast! Luckily everything is online which is probably what saved me. I would say the third exam was the trickiest with the wording of the questions. I used Edspira on YouTube since he was a little more lively about accounting. It's a very bland topic so maybe if she was a bit more enthusiastic it would help keep people interested.

Solid teacher with ok lectures. Pretty mid class. Content sucks and is super boring. Test questions are worded totally different from the actual homework which was frustrating. Luckily the course was curved, I had a C+ then it curved to a B. Overall an ok teacher and a crappy subject.

Professor Wellman was good. Very nice lady, but just not very enthusiastic about what she teaches. (I wouldn't be either if I were an accounting teacher) Its hard to catch up if you miss class because the concepts build off of each other. Overall just an OK class.
She is an okay teacher, the class is not difficult, you just are better off teaching yourself because there is no incentive to attend class, she posts everything on canvas.

Laura is super nice but talks insanely fast throughout her lectures. You end up focusing on trying to write the numbers she's saying down more than the actual content. She does record the lecturers which are accessible in canvas which are super helpful and provides notes to follow along with the lecture. Not a lot of final/midterm study material.

She really cares about her students understanding what she teaches. She posts online videos of her lectures, and other videos to help with tough topics. She is always open to "repeat, reword, or explaining" anything she just said in lectures with kindness and patience. Extremely understanding of missed tests. Supports her students a lot.

One of the worst profs I have ever had at UO. Better off just watching a YouTube video because her lectures are so monotone and boring. Overall the classwork is not bad but she is super robotic and the class could be taught a lot better. Would avoid if possible.

New professor here, joined Oregon for research opportunities. Cares about her students but seems like she doesn't really know how to teach. But she is very receptive to feedback - after we told her she was going too fast, she took it to heart and even filmed review videos of the entire daily lessons for us to study with. Just stay on top of things.
Very caring and kind professor that genuinely cares about your success. I don't have any reasons to take any more Anthropology classes, but I kind of wish I did so I could take her other classes.

Dr. Mostafavi is a super supportive professor who grades gently and offers plenty of extra credit. Attendance is super helpful, tests are mini and you can make them up for extra credit after you take them. The lectures are about interesting and important topics. Really enjoyed this class and would definitely take this professor again.

I took ANTH161 with Professor Mostafavi, and it was an easy and engaging class if this topic is right for you. Attendance was not mandatory, but for the discussions, it was. There was no midterm or final, just a straightforward final project. Quizzes were biweekly and open-note. It made for a nice quarter in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall this was a really easy class. The only assignments were small quizzes with pretty straightforward content and a basic paper at the end. I honestly rarely went to class but when I did Professor Mostafavi was engaging and knowledgeable. This class was extremely easy and I would recommend it to anyone interested in anthropology or seeking an A

I will say, this class was pretty left-leaning, and could have been a tad more objective. However, Dr. Mostafavi is very caring and kind, and flexible with deadlines and assignments- she cares a lot about her student's well-being. Course wasn't too hard and generous grading. ANTH 322
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very engaging lecturer that clearly cares about what she she is talking about.

I took ANTH 322 with her, and she is a great lecturer who really cares about what she teaches and cares about her students a lot! Prof. Mostafavi was always available and gave great feedback on every assignment. Amazing professor I would highly recommend taking any class with her if you get the chance!
She is very kind and has very interesting and engaging lectures.
Great lecturer, offers lots of extra credit opportunities. Definitely worth stopping by to chat with her during office hours.

Easy class (5 assignments total, 2 tests 2 hw 1 project) not very challenging he's just not always clear with what the assignment is/what a question is expecting us to put (only a couple times, didn't impact my grade much). No zooms, textbooks, or mandatory readings, just lecture videos. Was a good summer class, I'd take again.

Great guy, clearly cares about student success and wants you to learn. Very knowledgeable and pauses often for questions. Matt was super kind, more than willing to help answer any question you have and go through it thoroughly to make sure you understand. If you like ecology and evolution plus have a little stats background you'll love the class.

I had Matt for Ecological Genetics, he is an excellent professor that is very knowledgable about the subject matter. Read over his slides and do the assigned readings, and you will have no trouble keeping up with the course material and will gain vast insight into the field of ecological genetics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Matt is a nice guy who cares about his students, however he isn't the most gifted lecturer so class can drag on. The material isn't too difficult, but the test questions are very specific so you definitely need to know your stuff. I didn't love this class but I didn't hate it.
He seems impatience not a bad teacher when talking about easy materials but when it comes to the more advanced ones... he makes it harder than it should be (complicating things)

Not terribly difficult material, but Matt isn't a gifted lecturer, and people were often very confused about topics. He doesn't seem to like answering questions very much, and he gets a bit of an arrogant attitude when someone asks for help. I did go to his office hours several times, but I can see why a lot of students avoided asking for help.
Michael is great. I've taken 3 classes with him. If you like creating and you're able to take feedback you'll be fine. The university is lucky to have him teaching here.

Took ARTP281 with Michael. Overall, it was an amazing class, he really cares about your progression as an artist and the work you're making. Critiques were one-on-one rather than as a group, which was nice because they didn't take 3 hours. Would definitely recommend taking one of his classes.
such a great professor. super helpful and makes the work fun and hes super easy to talk to.

This class was only graded by three assignments. The day one of the assignments was due my family member passed away. She agreed to give me an extension, but when the assignment was graded  she marked me down for being late, even though she agreed to give me the extension. Her class was disorganized and her videos had such bad sound quality
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think if you have a difficult time understanding how institutions impact people (even though you are a sociology major) this will probably be a difficult class for you. She brings prospectives that many professors on campus don't provide or go in depth. I think if you actually want to get your money/educations worth you should take her class.

Dr.Vidal isn't for you if you have a fixed capitalist mindset or need extensive structure instead of working on growing your creativity & fluid learning- though she will provide if you simply ask. She is extraordinarily knowledgeable and teaches concepts that'll open your brain up to vital & powerful world perspectives. heavy on concept connections
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching is extremely disorganized and frustrating. No technology is allowed in the class, she'll call you out if you try to use it. All readings need to be printed and brought to class, keep in mind this is an environmental sociology class. She posts readings late, doesn't prepare for quizzes and assignments. A nice thing is theres no homework
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: 5/5!!!!! Overall, I wouldn't recommend taking a class with Professor Vidal again. Her lack of empathy, rigid structure, and resistance to adapting her teaching style made the course more frustrating than enriching. I would actively avoid taking another class with her in the future. The subject alone was a great class concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 4/? What made this more frustrating was the fact that her graduate teaching assistant (GE) was clearly the one who carried the course in terms of delivering content, engaging with students, and providing actual support. It felt like the GE, not Professor Vidal, was the one truly running the class and making the learning experience worthwhile.

It wasn't about wanting things to be “easier,” but rather about recognizing that learning looks different for everyone. Much of the course content could have easily been adapted to Canvas or other online tools, but instead, it felt like she was unwilling to consider any approach outside of her own. The course was uncoordinated, feeling difficult.

2/? While maintaining structure is important, it was disappointing to see such a lack of empathy, especially in a discipline centered around understanding human experiences.
She has a strict no-technology policy, which made it difficult for many students to engage with the material in ways that work best for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 1/? Professor Vidal is clearly knowledgeable in sociology, but unfortunately, her approach to teaching lacks the compassion and flexibility you'd expect from someone in her field. Throughout the course, she repeatedly emphasized that there would be no exceptions or accommodations for students, no matter the circumstance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vidal is my favorite instructor, and the courses I have taken with her have genuinely changed how I think. Her courses are structured similarly: No exams and writing assessments are taken home. If you talk in class, you will likely succeed. She doesn't teach in a traditional Western style, which may be why others like her class.

Professor Vidal's course is disorganized and stressful, with unclear grading criteria and poor communication. Assignments are often posted at the last minute, leaving little preparation time. Few graded tasks mean high stakes and minimal room for error, creating a frustrating and challenging learning environment.

Rambles a lot, her lectures rarely have much important information and is mainly just reviewing the readings and asking for student's thoughts on the matter. Incredibly unclear grading criteria, takes 1+ month to grade assignments of which there are a total of 3 for SOC 313. If you take this class, go to office hours and have them check your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most chill professors I've had. I highly recommend stopping by films and other events for extra credit. Casual yet engaging course.

I took PS 201 with Nick. I'm not a political science major so I was unsure how much I was going to like this class. And to my surprise I really enjoyed it and loved Nick as a professor. Nick is a very funny guy that makes lectures very interesting with personal insights, stories, and jokes. As far as the assignments they weren't too bad.

Nick is a genuine guy and it shows in everything he does. The course had plenty of extra credit, 1 essay 2 greenbook tests, and 1 chill presentation. He never rambles in lectures, and I learned all the content through them (no reading checks). He provides all the reading for free. He's accessible all hours and holds optional review sessions. Goat.

Nick is not only a great teacher, but an all-around great guy. I've had him for both PS326 and PS455. I hope to take more classes with him when I get the chance. He works hard, is super understanding of his student's needs-- and genuinely cares about your success.

Take any PS class with him, and you'll walk away a happier student.

Nick even as a GE instructor was amazing. He made you want to come to class and his lectures were clear and easy to follow. He also made sure to be available outside of class and hosted study sessions on off days for both his midterm and the final exam. I plan on taking any class I can with him in the future.
Professor Squires was amazing. He hosted extended office hours and study sessions for the mid term and final. His ability to make lectures fun and connect current events to readings really helped me

Every time I tried to take notes in his class, it was almost impossible. His lectures and Canvas are extremely unstructured---and he knows it. Passionate lecturer but he made it so hard for me to learn the subject.

One of the worst professors ive had at UO. his quizzes are fine but he adds questions that were never taught before in class. Hes super passionate about the subject but his slides are so vague that the only way you understand the information is by going to class. 5 quizzes throughout the term, 3 case assignments which are graded pretty easily.

Actually the worst professor i have had at UO. 5 quizzes throughout the term, one midterm, one final. Midterm was actually excruciating, final hopefully is easier, its in 1 week. He adds problems to the midterm and quizzes that you've never seen before in your life and expects you to reason with them. Slides are vague

Does he go on irrelevant tangents during his lectures? Yes. But what people don't normally catch is how unintentionally funny Nagesh is. One time he asked a group how many people in the group (5 people) were in class that day. Two people raised their hand which caused Nagesh to say "oh my god" like he had just saw a great tragedy.

I hope you like teaching yourself, lectures for 2 hours with 0 in class participation, refers to maybe 5 slides the entire lecture 7 if your lucky. Homework is ungraded but is necessary if you want to do well on the tests. Cant stay on topic to save his life, tough grader and unclear what will be on tests/quizzes. "whats going on rn?"
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nagesh is clearly very knowledgable in his field but is unable to effectively communicate information to students. Tends to ramble on and never gets to the point. Had to rely heavily on the textbook to learn the material. Says that exams will be straightforward but are actually very difficult. Group projects and exams make up most of grade.
Talks for the whole class period every single time and goes on tangets for long periods of time. Very hard to learn anything from him and tests are nothing like what he talks about in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very engaging professor, but prone to tangents. Focus on textbook and homework, that's where most of test material is from anyway. Some test questions were straight copied HW problems. Take advantage of all his extra credit! Very helpful office hours. I went to office hours to review midterm and he gave me 2 extra test points just for showing up.

He knows what he is talking about but he CANNOT TEACH. He copy and pastes stuff straight from the textbook. There is no clear progression to the class and jumps around to different topics. He will talk way too fast and get through a couple slides in the 2 hours. A headache for sure
Would drop the class but he teaches both sections. Dont take if possible

Professor Murthy knows his content very thoroughly. He lacks structure in his lectures. He gets through 3 slides in 2 hours. Not forgiving for missed quizzes even for extraneous health concerns. It would be better to take this class with another professor. He claims his tests are easy, but they are not. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagesh is definitely a very smart guy but has no idea how to lecture effectively. He often goes off-topic and can be extremely hard to follow. The course lacks much structure and often students are confused about what they are learning. He only uses a couple of slides per lecture and has no relevant information for students to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Crazy hard for this class. He asked you to finish a bunch of graphs in just 2 hr of test. Took this class remotely and it is so hard. You definitely would learn some things, but just go to the classes that teach graph. Other lecture are useless. He spent 50% of the time talking non-lecture-related stuff.

Nagesh is super passionate about the class, but he foes on tangents, and the material are all over the place. He stressed that all you had to do was come to class and do the homework but it's not that easy. He was very understanding but not super helpful and HW wasn't mandatory so there were very few grades.

Nagesh is a really smart guy and you can tell he is very knowledgeable about the material but he really struggles to lecture effectively. Most of the lecture time is spent going in circles and you never end up covering much at all. He provides lots of opportunities for extra credit and the assignments aren't terribly difficult so that helps out.

Good professor who is passionate about the material. Tends to go on slight tangents and uses LOTS of sports references which can be annoying. Everything before midterm is pretty easy but lots of content after week 6.

Murthy was an enthusiastic professor, but had confusing lectures and tested us on things never covered in class. His tests were unpredictable and inconsistently graded and not as "easy" as he said they would be. He is very accessible and eager to try and help, but won't help with the homework. Most of this class was learned independently.

A very smart professor, but not the most effective at communicating through lectures or projects. You will learn a lot in his classes, but expect to work throughout the term. He isn't a bad professor, he just likes to give you a few slides and some lecture material and expects you to figure the rest out yourself.
Read the textbook carefully because his lectures aren't very helpful. His quizzes are on content he doesn't cover.
Uses class time very inefficiently. Content overlapped with pre-requisite courses.

Nagesh's class is very hard but I guarantee you will learn a lot. He makes sure his coursework is super relevant and not just trying to get concepts out there. You will gain some good skills if you put the work in. I worked really hard but learned a lot from him.

Nagesh is the best professor in the LCB.  He makes it super easy to come to class every morning with his enthusiasm for the subject.  He has a lot of connections and provides awesome out-of-class opportunities.  Very approachable as well.
Nagesh is the man; he made DSC easy for me to understand and he is very passionate about making sure his students learn.

This was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Lance is a great instructor, he's very knowledgeable and the class material is engaging and relevant. As a STEM major, his weekly assignments and quizzes were easy to keep up with and didn't feel like busy work. The exams are very straightforward and he offers practice exams and a study guide.

I found this class very difficult to stay engaged in. Most lectures involved reading directly from dense slides, which made the two-hour class feel long and hard to retain information from. The quizzes and midterms did not seem closely connected to the lectures, and I did not feel like I learned much from the course.

Just beware that you will really struggle with grading. There's absolutely no way to tell what you are going to get on an assignment, and even if you try super hard and go by the rubric, you won't get appropriately graded. I haven't seen a single person get a 100 on anything. He is checked out and gives up in the middle of the lecture too

This class was a lot of effort. I expected it to be less work than it was. There were hours worth of lecture material and reading every week, and some assignments were very lengthy. Exams were straightforward as long as you completed the readings and lectures. Takes a long time to grade, which isn't ideal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class material is easy to understand but Lance truly is the most confusing grader. He grades based on a "moving target" - this means that "each assignment is graded relative to what other peers turned in, so it's hard to explain what I'm looking for". This is so impossible to work with, and results in bad grades for hard work.

Asks you to respond to detailed prompts on essays/finals but expects you to answer the question in very few words. You'll get marked down for not being specific enough, but if you try to be more specific you go over the word count and get marked down anyways. He just a terrible grader for essays.

Final exam is tomorrow and he has not graded any assignment since our midterm exam, including the paper worth 30%... good luck figuring out where you stand in this class. I did like that he recorded video lectures and instructions to assignments. Not the friendliest or most helpful when reaching out over email though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class online, and I would say it feels very disconnected. Things are graded almost 2 weeks after you have done it, as I have taken the midterm about 1.5 weeks ago, and it's still not graded. He grades very hard on certain assignments that I felt met the criteria and more. Hard exam is not like the practice at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

Class follows the same format every time, which is fine because for the most part the material is engaging. Lance is a very nice professor who is also accommodating of his students needs.

Grading material is highly subjective, choice answer questions will have have similar answers without much clarity on which is correct with certainty. Took MGMT 250 but that wasn't an option for course code. He clearly did not want to be there. Tough grader for in class writing assignments and discussion questions while unclear with his feedback for improvement.

This course has a decent workload but nothing out of the ordinary for an upper division class. Professor Gabrielsen provides in depth feedback and is willing to work with you when you want to improve. He wants to see you succeed! Setting up meetings over teams with him was simple.

Lance clearly cares about the subject matter, and it's an important topic to understand in depth. However, the online course structure leaves little flexibility to move through the material quickly. Lance was a cool guy. He was funny and engaging in lectures while delivering really important information about sustainability. He even watched an instagram reel about sustainability each class to get us going. Super caring and supportive dude.

Lance is a great professor and is passionate about what he is teaching which makes it a lot easier to learn. I think that the readings can be a bit long but other than that straight forward class.

Lance is a very nice and caring professor. Very lecture/homework heavy though, so be ready to spend a lot of time working for this class. Tests/Quizzes could use some refining/clarification as well, half the time I couldn't understand what the question was asking.

He is clearly passionate about what he's teaching which inspires his students to be as well. This dude knows what he's talking about. Also great mustache, super well kept.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Forster was a really engaging professor to work with! His lectures were incredibly thought provoking and made you consider things important to life outside of class. He wants the best for his students and encourages being present and doing your best.

Conversations with her in studio were rushed and ineffective, often interjected with snide comments about irrelevant personal details. She expects personal workflow to perfectly follow her program with no leeway or personal gain for students. She's started to heavily push the importance of Gen AI but simultaneously clearly knows nothing about it.

Shes kind but incredibly scattered, on desk crits you end up more confused than before. She is very unclear on what she wants you to improve on and doesn't help you get there. She only gives feedback on a specific week's subject, even if your project isn't there yet. (Unhelpful). Other ratings are not reviews, they're warnings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's super scatterbrained, disorganized, and a workaholic and expects students to be the same. She gives students meaningless and time-consuming homework to keep a "record" of their progress which doesn't help develop our design (we have mandatory desk crits to show her our progress anyways). I do not recommend her.

She is horribly unorganized, gives an overwhelming amount of assignments that have nothing to do with students actual projects and ultimately wastes valuable time. She paces class in a way that sets up students for failure unless they are great at managing themselves. DO NOT TAKE HER STUDIO NO MATTER WHAT unless you are ready to feel angry 24/7

Overall the class and professor were not easy to understand because of the disorganization. The professor was not good at giving lectures and teaching us about rhino/grasshopper, the readings were not helpful in helping us develop our design. Also the extra add-ons we had to download on Rhino was ridiculous, confusing, and in my opinion, useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: she is always scattered and unclear which makes he very unhelpful. first class i ever took that made me want to ask for my money back. she has unrealistic standards for students which she won't communicate with you. lacks people skills and teaching skills which makes it difficult to learn from her. her classes are very appealing but don't be fooled
horrible teacher. unclear, disorganized, and out of touch with the world

Amazingly scattered, has no clear picture of how to teach a studio class.  Does a shotgun approach with guest speakers and field trips taking up all the class time.  Very disappointing for a graduate level studio.

Had Nancy for Architecture studio as well as Environmental Control Systems I & II (ARCH 491, 492).  Challenging, knowledgeable instructor with real-world experience and a real desire to push students to perform at their highest level.  Unlike many studio instructors, she strives to get you to explore your OWN ideas and develop them, not hers.

Nancy's class topics (design, computers, co-housing, etc) are fantastic and she does bring a fresh perspective to the department.  However, I don't think anyone is breaking down her door to take her classes because she is complete scattered and incomprehensible.  Nancy has a hard time keeping focused and her lectures often spiral out of control.

Professor Cheng significantly lacks in people skills and in my opinion, is the worst professor on the faculty.  She may bring in research money but when dealing with students she is cold, political, and unwilling to inconvenience herself.   She jarringly contrasts with the Oregon culture and I would avoid any interaction with her like the plauge.
Scattered and at time rambling.  The online documents were helpful but were relied on a little too much as teaching tools.  Unwiling to work with Macintosh users.
not good at interacting with students... makes it a point to get on youre case if you screw up once. my studio was unfulfilling and i think we wasted a lot of time doing stuff that was irrelavent.
No Comments

I do not recommend at all. Dosent respond to emails, Shows up late, Very disorganized lectures, Dosent post anything on canvas or gives us heads up about midterms. Took him 7 weeks to grade a midterm. Not good at explaining things. Nice guy, but disorganized and you will learn nothing.

Cool guy, but not an effective professor. The course is very disorganized, and materials are never posted on Canvas, which makes it hard to keep up if you miss class. Lectures are rushed, unplanned and lack clear structure, and feedback on assignments is nonexistent. Communication is also an issue, as he just doesn't check his email.

Have you ever wondered how Helen Keller felt? Take this class, then, because you will not be seen, heard, or given any form of communication. Bad at teaching, forgets about quizzes, gives problems never even touched in class. Slightly condescending when you're confused and expects you to just know everything. Nice guy, but avoid for your sanity.
Great class

reviews.comment: I took 262, and there's only 5 assignments the entire term. He doesn't put words on lecture slides so if you need to take notes and miss something, you're screwed. Your homework for the week are egregiously long readings, which are used for two quizzes worth like 5% of your grade. Some of the GE's are harsh graders so be aware of that too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I actually took him for HIST262, and as my first history class in college, it was pretty difficult. He doesn't put words on slides so going to lectures is pretty important, but overall he's a really chill guy who is fun to listen to. The GEs graded all my work and they were EVIL though just a heads up.

Ocean Howell is a great professor. This course was incredibly tight and thematically coherent. He repeatedly mentioned that he is dyslexic, so that's why the slides have no words. Anyone who thought they didn't need to take notes on the lectures were very mistaken. Pay attention and interpret what you hear and read and you'll be fine.

Ocean is a great guy and very passionate about what hes teaching. Class was relatively easy, as well as assignments. Lectures are him describing images, so notes rarely need to be taken. Great class and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if ur not a history major. Have no idea what's going on, and my only guides are the 100-200 page dense readings or VERY vague lectures. Slides are literally just pictures, so if you attend all the classes and miss something/ hear something wrong, good luck. Expectations for assignments/exams are also not very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades stuff hard, got confused on what we were learning the whole course I couldnt tell a single thing on what I learned

Ocean is a great guy I just personally would not take the class again its very tough im typically a 4.0 student and im scared of failing this class tbh, VERY VERY tough grader and the midterm and final are pretty rough im ngl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An incredibly uninteresting class in which I feel like I did not learn a single thing of importance. And I went to every single lecture and did all the homework. Extremely tough grader, do not expect to get an A in this course. Review slides are atrocious before exams; it will be 100+ pages of images with no accompanying notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging and connects the subjects to relevancy to our personal lives. Walks you through the expected essay as well as the mapping project. Sources for the paper could be harder to find than usual history papers so don't get caught behind on that.

Professor Howell was a very cool guy. Enjoyed the class because he is very passionate about the subject and was interesting content. That being said, hard to follow lectures sometimes and the take home exams are graded very tough. I also ended with an 87.5 and got a B instead of a B+. Super harsh no tech policy during class whatsoever.

Professor Howell is passionate about his subjects and knows a lot. There are lots of tedious assignments and he grades them toughly so prepare yourself to be unhappy with some grades. I did learn a lot from his class.

Interesting professor, his lectures were entertaining, and I learned about a historical map database that is very interesting and will potentially be useful to me in the future. He was instructing a history class, but it was obvious that he was honestly only interested in the architecture related to the location the class was focused on.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cant describe in 350 characters why u shouldn't take his classes, exams rely on info from lectures but slides are just pics & hold no informational value at all, gives no context to the topic of his courses, assigns 150pgs to read a week to answer a question in >300 words taken two of his classes so far, feel like I learned nothing even with a B&A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Ocean! He has always been so helpful in both classes I have taken with him. His courses are reading heavy, but the reading feels needed for the content. Papers are lengthy but he provides lots of help throughout!

Definitely one of the best professors I've had, he really cares about what he's teaching and even though it was a zoom lecture it felt like a real class. I would 100% recommend taking one of his classes. There are two big papers that are kinda challenging but he gives you the prompt early and you have room to explore whatever interests you most.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is such a cool dude. Hes so easy going and really really understandable and good to his students! Probably one of the easiest professors to talk to and it is def worth getting to know him. Hes very understanding and very fun to learn from. He also just genuinely wants his students to thrive! There is a term paper but he will help you!

Incredibly intelligent human. His ARH 410 class was informative but, I felt, very poorly organized. Tons of reading that we discussed weekly, yet received no feedback for assignments. Class structure was monotonous; same thing every week, and no designated time to work on our huge term papers. Very chilled man but has high expectations, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is so approachable and smart. He will assign you a lot of reading but it will all ultimately help you in the end with your papers for the term. Wish more professors were like him. He grades hard, but he grades well; an important distinction.

HUGE amounts of reading, but gives lots of feedback on essays. Only 2 essays/ term, which is great. Isn't clear on the rubric he uses to dock points on essays, but gives fantastic qualitative commentary. Also, incredibly good-looking with a great sense of humor- meaning he tolerates joking around in discussion as long as it's relevant to the topic.
Capturing and Entertaining Professor. Classes are primarily discussion based as opposed to lecture. Be prepared to read, a lot.

A whole lot of reading, but this guy legitimately wants to teach you the material and is very passionate about his subject. He is very hard when he grades his essays. As long as you follow the prompt, you should be fine.
Chill guy who obviously is interested in what he teaches.  Lots of reading, and a fair amount of writing.  If you go to class expecting him to skateboard in on the first day, you'll be disappointed.
Cool guy with a chill attitude. A LOT of reading but lectures are pretty interesting. Ask him about his ex pro-skateboarding career.
Not very good at commenting on papers, which is what the class is based on.  Just grades it on how he feels about it without proper feedback on the docking of points.

Ocean is a really chill guy, but he didn't grade assignments until the end of the term, making it hard to know how you were progressing in the class. He knows and loves his subject, and can seem a little intimidating - but he is approachable. However, the class was really difficult and set up like "your first term at graduate school" - verbatim.
awesome professor! he really knows his stuff! there is a HUGE amount of reading and the class requires time and effort, but the professor makes it rewarding!
Take 411. Trust.

Professor Ostler is the reason I fell in love with history. His lecture style is engaging and I ended up taking every history class I could from him. He can be a tough grader and you'll really need to know your stuff for the exams.

I love this guy so much. He is so smart and funny and his class was so informative. If you have the chance, take HIST 411 Founding of America. It's a great way to learn and honestly one of the funnest classes I have ever taken. I would gladly take all of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeff Ostler is a great instructor. Lectures can be a little slow at times but the care of the material and of the ideas is clear and apparent. Very responsive and you can tell he cares about educating his students. Made our class laugh out loud many times. Hilarious.
Lectures were great, you will mainly be doing assignments with the GEs rather than the professor. You're only graded on 2 tests and a paper. Make sure you take notes and read the assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Ostler is approachable and helpful, but this class had unreasonably high expectations. If you have limited historical knowledge, dont take his classes. He provides little background information and relies on largely student-led class discussions. There was no textbook, leaving a lot of gaps in material that werent otherwise filled.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good teacher, average lectures (somewhat long and boring), really easy to get off task on computer. Really tough grader, need to provide tons of details on tests and essay but is fair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher with great, organized lectures. Will push you to think and challenge your mental, but is very good at explaining and engaging. No homework, but there is some reading for discussion. Only a midterm and final which are term identification and an essay but they are not hard if you study. Gives you the essay prompts to study before.

Professor Ostler only does lectures and group discussions during class. This class had the most reading I've ever had for a single course (last term of college). The final was incredibly challenging and specific. There are also pop quizzes so you won't succeed without showing up to class. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He relied purely on group work and was not good at giving background information. Do not rate.

I've taken two classes with this professor and he is one of the best in the history department at UO. Very passionate and interesting lectures. He communicates well with students and has clear expectations.
I have taken a multitude of classes from professor Ostler over the four years I have been here. Absolutely my favorite US history professor. If you haven't taken a class from him you are missing out!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ostler is the only professor you should take HIST 202 with. Very, very passionate about US History. Lectures are very organized and easy to take notes from. Clear grading criteria. Would take again. Go to class, take notes, attend discussion, study solidly for the exams, and you will get an A.
Extremely passionate about history and recognizes that it can be boring. He always makes jokes and loves the University of Oregon.

Professor Ostler is a great professor! He seems to genuinely care about the students and what they take from the class. The workload isn't overwhelming, but the reading is important. He is very down to earth and doesn't have the holier-than-thou attitude many professors can have.
Such a great teacher and so enthusiastic about history. Literally a walking encyclopedia. Lectures were organized very well and it made note taking super easy.

Wonderful person and professor! He is genuinely interested in your well-being and wants everyone to do well.  He even took my whole class out to pizza at Track Town! If you can, get Ostler as a professor, it's impossible not to love him!

One of the best professors I've had so far at UO. His lectures are interesting, and he makes snarky, sarcastic side comments that are great. Just go to lecture, take decent notes and you'll do fine in the class!

He is the best history teacher I have had, his lectures are well organized and if you go to class and listen to him talk there is no way you can do bad in the class.  He has such passion with what he is talking about that it makes you want to listen, the only down side is that the GTFs grade the exames and some of them are hard graders.
Great professor. The lectures were sometimes boring but they were always very organized. Not too much reading.
D.C ostler is a awesome professor. He is very kind and easy to touch. And also he is so pleased if you ask him questions. I am sure you will not want to miss the opportunity to attend his class.

Oslter is awesome. He is very funny and engaging. He is also very easy to approach and ask for help. He has also been doing this for a while so he knows what he is talking about and knows how to teach that class.

Ostler is a great teacher. He really knows what he's talking about and makes even most boring lectures fun. He recites history accurately but at the same time makes it engaging & funny & he's always up for questions and reponds fast to emails. Only boring part in his class was when he wasn't lecturing and some guest lecturer came. Great professor!
Hilarious
Ostler was really clear in his lectures and had a clear outline for every lecture.  The only problem was that there was a lot of information to write down, but the professor was good.
great professor.

I enjoyed his course.  He knew what he was talking about and made the lecture's easy to follow with cohesive transitions and stories, even some "historical reenactments".  He tries his best to engage students to participate in lecture, and didn't tolerate those who were disruptive.  Personally, easy to talk to and even at times pretty funny.
No Comments
felt very uncomfortable in her classes, don't reccomend
can't talk to anyone during class, zero devices, will be humiliated for talking, laughing, etc… pretends like she's chill but is actually the opposite

reviews.comment: You can't speak a word to your neighbor in this class without public shaming. Also if you thought you were allowed your phone, ipad, or a laptop, you're wrong and she will call you by name in front of everyone to put it away. Hundreds of pages of reading and so lecture heavy. Extremely strict about everything. I would avoid this GE if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was brutal. One of those classes where you can't say a single word to the person next to you without her stopping the entire thing. Not one grade is shown until 9 days after your final class, and the grading itself is laughably brutal… avoid at all costs. Most unfunny and unlikable personality I've ever seen.
Avoid at all costs

I don't know what Kimmy is trying to prove, but it's almost like she degrades her students in order to gain respect from her superiors, as the other reviews suggest. I honestly don't know how people like Kimmy get the position to teach and lead students.
Insufferable personality. None of the teachers or GE's seem to like her either. Annoyingly laughs at everything and enjoys putting students down.
Fair grader but disliked by many students. As the other person sortof said, she takes her job very seriously

No one likes her. She is insufferable to the point where everyone in class looks at each other like "is she serious right now." HARSH grader. Treats & disrespects students as if they are children who must obey the rules. She'll do ANYTHING to get her higher ups to like her (like laugh hard during class) but could care less about the actual students
As with most writing professors shes tough on the grading scale but a really nice person and reciprocates any effort to form a good student-professor relationship. Easy class and easy content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Be ready for a teacher that makes a 100 level writing class not seem like a 100 level writing class. Her class is certainly entertaining and thought provoking but she makes the class far to difficult and is extremely stingy as a grader as well as there being 1-2 papers every week. She is not at all willing to work with her students on the direction

Professor Olivar is an extremely caring professor who gives great feedback. As expected there are a ton of writing assignments but she takes a lot of time to individually read each paper in depth and leave helpful comments. She makes the classroom environment fun and I honestly looked forward to going. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

Clearly understands concepts innately, and expects you to as well before any instruction. Doesn't matter how well you understand reading, if you do not grasp nuance he hints at but won't explain, too bad. Pushes students but does not allow questions without mockery. Takes no time to explain difficult concepts in general terms before nuance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and very kind. People talk poorly about him because they are sensitive and misery loves company. Don't give into the fear mongering and negativity. He wants to help and wants people to ask questions. He is super smart and cares.
Very good professor and masterful at explaining constitutional concepts.

Shocked at the positive reviews. I find Raban's lectures both dry and lacking in content. He just goes in circles the entire class and glosses over a lot of the readings. I am very unsure what is and isn't important, and if you ask him questions he just laughs and goes "no, that's not quite true". Plus, he's very off-putting (you'll hear about it).

This is an absolutely phenomenal professor. The most dense, content-heavy class I've ever taken, but he made it fascinating. He's a tough dude, and he makes you work for it, but he tries very hard to make the material relatable and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Raban is extremely unforgiving if you cannot answer his questions. He will not help you out and is not afraid to embarrass students. Do the reading and be ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brilliant man. Totally willing to make sure we understand the material, but will take silence as acceptance.  He teaches jurisprudence from a place of wanting to help us understand what is this practice of law to which we aspire.
Always be prepared for class. He asks tough questions. He is an excellent lecturer and if you do the reading and pay attention in class you will be prepared for the final. His exams are fair.
Super sweet professor and genuinely wants her students to succeed. Class is a take out what you put in.

Absolutely take this course with her!! She is so easy-going and helpful. There are group projects with presentations, but they aren't bad and you get to select who you work with. One midterm, but no final. The midterm is really easy as long as you've paid attention to her lectures. She uses the entire class period, so be ready!

She's an excellent professor. She's ridiculously smart and understands the way a student thinks. She's a little soft spoken so it can be hard to hear her but she's more than happy to clarify. She's attentive to emails and gives the best feedback I have ever seen a professor give. She's very educated on the subject and enjoys answering questions.

She is an amazing professor and you should absolutely take MGMT 335 with her if you can. Her background from Stanford is very impressive and is very qualified to be teaching this course. The class itself is relatively laid back, there are a couple of presentations and a group project at the end, but that replaces the final.

Professor Overmeyer is super sweet and cares about what she is teaching.  She was super understanding of everything and made sure all her students were happy with the course.  There was only one reading that we had to buy, but it was around $10.  I definitely recommend taking her class.

Professor Overmeyer is amazing! The content covered in the class is relevant, super interesting, and easy to process. She does not require attendance but you can only miss so many classes before it affects your professionalism grade. There are a few group projects that are fun as well.
Probably my favorite professor I've ever had here at UO. I'm so thankful I randomly added her class on a whim this quarter.

Natasha is awesome. She is incredibly knowledgeable and one of the most pleasant professors I have had at UO. She leads some pretty interesting discussions during class, and she's super accommodating. Her educational background is also super impressive, and she's a great resource on campus.

I am currently taking this class and it has been awesome. She always gives us a break during class it's 2-3:50, and she takes lectures at a good pace so you aren't overwhelmed. She is very kind and coming from such a highly educated background she knows what she's talking about. There is a good amount of projects, but no final exam.

Natasha Overmeyer is amazing. You can tell she is highly educated, inspiring, and kind. She's a super nice person and is very approachable. The class I had with her was very discussion-heavy and has a decent amount of reading but it's definitely doable. All the feedback I got was very constructive and thoughtful. Definitely recommend!!

Professor Overmeyer is an amazing teacher. Her background explains why she is so good. Graduating from Harvard and then attending Stanford for a Masters is incredible. I am currently in her class and I absolutely love it. She explains everything very well. We just had a midterm and there were no suprises on it, she prepared us very well. Thank you!

Very knowledgeable about what she teaches, but doesn't really make an effort to connect with students. Discussion based lectures, and you can get away with not reading the textbook. Pretty easy and mangle class with not too much homework. Definitely recommend!

Attendance is mandatory. Class is very discussion-based and the lectures are not structured the best. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the class content. Caring and helpful if you reach out.

Professor Ok is very knowledgeable in her field and is very deliberate with the films she shows in her class. You should be fine if you make some effort to engage with the content and complete the work as instructed. She's one of those professors that "rarely gives an A" though. Overall, she's a great professor, and I would take her class again.

Professor Ok is very knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches. Her lectures are interesting and she cultivates engaging class discussion through the materials and questions she presents. She is a fair grader and overall an enjoyable professor.

Her accident at times can be hard to understand, but other then that she is a good teacher. I did minimal readings and just showed to class and in the end did great. 6 movies shown in class. Most of the class is based off writing, so as long as you can make 2 good essays and 6 screening notes based off the movies you'll do great.

Ok was a very respectable prof which engaged with her students, but the class its self could be set up differently. A lot of the lectures are repetitive if you actually read the textbook, it is almost word for word the same as her lectures. This made it hard to stay focused/engaged in class. Great screenings and super accessible outside of class.

Lecture heavy with no breaks once a week, second day was film- but can barely see subtitles. Once a week film notes which are easy if you watch film and read the one article or whatever is required for a question. Passionate about her work, and interesting topic. Essays are long (1500-2k words), but don't require a extreme amount of readings.

Dr. Ok is a fairly nice and is very kind, however when you do not attend class you will not get a participation grade. I had participated in this class and had attended many classes but if you miss one you will drop your grade. The essays are difficult and her lectures go over the films the readings, so I figured I should not go, yet you need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures, explains thing really well, weakly screenings were interesting and the note taking was easy. Learned a lot. The Final was simple and follows the same style as the note taking. Quizzes were easy if you read the textbook ( which was a really interesting textbook) and joined the lectures.

The worst class I've taken at UO. You are quizzed on the lecture before she teaches which is a useless strategy and her lectures are boring and repetitive. The assignments are simple but she grades for specific things that she does not clarify. Would never take her classes again, I do not recommend them.

Good lecturer. Do the work and abide by her rules and you'll be ok. Little to no flexibility in things such as late work, attendance, etc. Strict and formal class dynamic which in my experience makes it hard to learn. You will learn a lot of information but I would not take a class from her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good lecturer and good at communicating information. Do the work and abide by her rules and you'll be ok. Little to no flexibility in things such as late work, attendance, etc. Strict and formal class dynamic which in my experience makes it hard to learn. You will learn a lot of information but I would not take a class from her again.
