I have no problem understand Professor Ok's English. All of her class is not very hard, as long as you put in the effort she expect. I even got an A+ in one of her class, just saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable of what she teaches, and very kind to all students. The topic she covers is very interesting and modern. Also, I had no problem with understanding her English at all. For those of you who are complaining about her accent, I hope you think through if you were making that judgment based on your linguistic bias or not.

Professor Ok's class was one of the more boring classes I've ever taken. Lectures are impossible to get through without getting bored. It's hard to pay attention because she talks slowly, softly, isn't very animated and has an accent. Tests were hard. I got 12/20 on the first exam, one of the worst grades I've ever had on an exam.

She is a very enthusiastic and nice lecturer and she is very passionate about her work. The clear difficulty with her is that is nearly to impossible to understand her english. Additionally, it is quite difficult to keep up with her pace with the lecture slides.

This is the worst class I have ever taken after being at the school for 4 years. The class isn't difficult because the course material is hard to understand or a difficult topic to teach. It's difficult because grading is inconsistent, you're not given clear instructions to complete the assignments, and the course is disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class. The comments on the guidelines are true, just pay attention during class and reference the syllabus over the term. Otherwise, fantastic class, super interesting and covered so much breadth in a focused yet easily manageable way. I don't get the bad rep this site gives her. Reach out if you're confused, she's so nice

I did not enjoy this class. She expects you to know a lot about literature even though the class has no pre-reqs. She's mildly racist, says weird things about "transgenderism", and doesn't agree with your answers unless they're the ones she has in mind. Would not recommend taking any of her classes.

kind and knows her stuff but can't handle teaching a class. gets off topic and goes on long tangents every class. canvas page is a nightmare with half not working URL links. grading makes zero sense. asked class to grade ourselves for participation since she didn't yet and put it in as the first grade of the class already after half of the quarter
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Slides are never posted. Attendance is mandatory. Instructions are unclear. She's hard to understand. Assignments are unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Widely disorganized and confusing class. Agree Dorothee's kind and knows her info, but she is constantly losing track when talking (MANY tangents), canvas organization is extremely confusing, constant cold-calling but won't call it correct unless it's what she's thinking. 2 weeks and still no grades, just class participation she deems worthy or not

She is very passionate about her work, but wildly disorganized. The grading for the assignments were unclear and felt very subjective. She remade the syllabus six different times and it was still different than what she assigned in class. I had perfect participation and she still removed a point because I didn't sound "confident enough."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unorganized but engaging professor. Demanded a lot of participation and preparation. Clarity of the assignments was not very apparent, and students were often confused. I would take her class again solely for her energy and passion for the subject(s).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The most confusing and un-organized class ever. It wasn't hard she made it so that none of the students cared about the course material or even knew. what we were supposed to be learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dorothee knows her stuff and is always delighted to share it. She's occasionally hard to understand, but she's more than willing to help you and be more concise if you ask, she's not trying to trip you up or confuse you. Very sweet.

She gives A LOT of readings. She needs to focus on specific tales iin detail. We moved through many tales, but we needed to have more focus on a few tales; to better grasp concepts. Many people seemed to be confused about exactly what she wanted, in terms of Essay papers.

The class content would have been fun if the structure was better. The professor often went off on long tangents and did not explain directions clearly. Students had no idea what to do. I wasn't told how to do my assignments until week 6, so I received an F in that class when I had straight A's otherwise. A GPA ruiner, would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class design could be cool,it's a history class that was designed like a D&D game. Sadly the professor completely butchered the class. Her assignments were confusing and disorganized. When you ask for help all she ends up doing is bashing you as a student. She personally insulted me more than once. I would never suggest this teacher to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Extremely boring professor who just wants you to regurgitate information on her exams. Not the toughest class, but definitely one of the least interesting.

Seemed to teach personal interpretations as fact and could be really demanding of critical thought and Biblical knowledge (and participation). Was also not the clearest on assignment expectations, and had a hard time relating to the class. Nice lady though, knew her stuff and was interested in open literary discourse.. very willing to help.

She is a very intelligent woman and knows the content of the class very well. However, she's kinda kooky and doesn't make sense all of the time. Also, when she says she wants participation, she doesn't just mean attending class. She means raising your hand and sharing, despite it being a 300 person lecture class. Not fair and she doesn't know ppl.
Great teacher, interesting lectures/discussions.

She knows what she's talking about and is here to teach. which makes her course challenging. However she's understanding, intelligent and very german. I would recommend her if you're looking for a moderately challenging course, different kind of course because we spent alot of time discussing and reading sweet stories.
No Comments

shes lovely when talking to her directly but can be a bit strict when it comes to attendance and participation on assignments. the majority of the questions on quizzes and tests are created by the students of the class which is very helpful
Trish is so sweet and kind!! Child Language seemed like it would be a really fun class, but it was kinda boring. Mandatory attendance with 2 free absences and a group project at the end.
She was such an amazing teacher and is truly passionate about what she does. Every time I reached out to her she was quick to respond and was super helpful and caring.
Thought this would be a low maintenance online class but no! One small discussion, written assignment, canvas quizzes, and additionally exams due on Saturdays weekly.

Worst class i've taken in college. not a LING major, but genuinely think she was teaching us incorrect information because her answers wouldn't match with the dictionaries SHE recommends! a LOT of exercises with these errors, many things due throughout the week and no late work accepted. content will be easy one minute and impossible the next.

I have asked for clarification on assignments and simply get a response let me ask the GE and then the GEs response makes no answer or sense. She had no idea what she is teaching and frankly she doesn't care. AWFUL professor online maybe in person she is better but RUN don't take her class. You will be so confused and she doesn't have office hours.

LOVE Trish! Gives you access to free textbook. Just do the quizzes and projects as the rubric says and you'll do well. Super fun and engaging, never really a boring moment in class. She really knows her stuff and is eager to share with the class.

I loved this class. She created a very calm learning environment and is fabulous at explaining the material. Weekly readings along with a quiz to follow to make sure you understood the material. There are a few larger assignments, but they arent bad at all. As long as you show up and pay attention you are fine! Would recommended taking her class!

Trish is very passionate about what she does and it shows. Class is a smooth ride as long as you do the short readings and quizzes before class. Very few large assignments - but they allow you to really apply your learning to real life. Definitely recommend!
honestly the class was easy the professor just treated us like middle schoolers

She is a very kind professor and cares a lot. Attendance is taken in every class and discussion. She grades very accurately to the rubrics so just follow those very well. A couple of projects and tests but they were easy if you pay attention. would take again1

Jeremy is a really nice professor to talk to and ask questions. His midterms and Final are the one's worth a lot of your grade so if you don't study for one it could cause a toll to your grade. He doesn't let you have a notecard so ensure your good at memorizing formulas and terms

Jeremy was a very good professor and the midterms we're not too bad. He also gives a nice curve at the end of the year. His lectures can be somewhat dull and repetitive but overall he is passionate about Macro.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty boring and he uploads all the slides to Canvas, so there really isn't a reason to go. He's super chill though.

The lectures for this class did not help me so I did not attend them after week 2. However, I did do class encore and that was way more helpful than the lectures. Not really much homework for this class which is nice. Tests are not that difficult if you study the material which is not too complicated.

Professor Piger is a great teacher, and I really enjoyed his class. He explains every concept thoroughly, and for tests he tells you exactly what terms to study and gives a practice exam. He also curves the tests. I would definitely recommend taking his class because you'll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeremy is a very kind professor who understand the material very well. He provides clear office hours and hosted study sessions the days before the exams. Regardless, this is not an easy class and requires out of class work to perform well. However, Jeremy is the 100% the professor I would recommend for this course. No attendance but lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He takes a lot of time to explain new concepts, which makes learning intuitive.

Professor Piger is an incredibly simple teacher, which I find very beneficial. Attendance is never required, but DEFINITELY go to lectures. He also provides ample study material prior to tests which makes them a lot easier. Overall, great teacher, would be glad to have him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of info, but easy if you pay attention. Piger is a great guy.

Great! I found Jeremy to be easier to understand than my last econ professor, you can tell he cares, lecture heavy and only graded by 2 midterms and a final with daily quizzes and reading which are easy, study practice questions he posts bc they help for the tests, I recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you attend lectures and discussions this class should be pretty easy. Make sure you study and understand the material as the only graded things are quizzes, 2 midterms, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his class fall term 2022. I didn't appreciate him as much until I've taken classes with other faculty in the ECON department at UO. His lectures are at the right speed and very organized, explains things clearly and is very professional. Grading is hard in this class, but the curve is around 5%-10%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Piger is a great lecturer. He speaks slowly and repeats concepts to make sure everyone understands. This is very important since this class is the foundation for EC 421 and other classes. He is is very helpful in office hour. If you do the optional homework he assigns, you will be ready for exams.
Very nice and explained things well. It is important to do the homework because it definitely solidifies the concepts even though it's technically optional. Be sure to study and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 95% of the grade in this class is based of 2 midterms and a final. There is a discussion class that wasn't helpful to me and I found myself having trouble staying focused in class because he repeats himself a lot.

Lectures are a bit dry but he's a cool guy and tells you on the first day that you don't have to come to class if you don't gain anything from it. Grades are based solely on 2 midterms and final but the exams are written very clearly and are easy to follow along. Everything in the exams is in the lecture slides and he also posts practice questions
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, even though its a very dry subject. Very accessible outside of class, was able to answer complicated questions for me when I was not able to attend his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy, good at explaining the material, it's just boring material and hard to stay focused on. Your grade is basically made up of 3 tests, homework/labs are like 5%. Attendance isn't important at all, the lectures are on Canvas and he just reads from them. Homework takes 20-30 mins each week and is due every Monday. Be prepared for every exam
He is great. And super hot, sit in front.

Very average class, I thought his lectures were pretty dry but he seemed nice/helpful in office hours. The whole class is graded basically on 3 exams. Wish there were more opportunities to improve one's grade.

Lectures are very clear. The material is dry but nothing you can do about that. Know your statistics well! Math-based course but not cryptic or purposefully confusing. 2 quizzes, midterm, final, and 8 homework assignments. Labs were helpful. Tests are super tough but plenty of study material is given. Grading is fair. Nice guy. Go to class!
Class are pit dry and very poring, he only reads though the slides which he post in the B/B. Exams are m/c and predictable. Straight forward exams, and nice professor. I recommend him.
Great professor, extremely clear and helpful.  Very useful during office hours

The professor could improve his public speaking skills by omitting "OK" at the end of each paragraph and "SO" at the beginning of each new one. The numbers for natural employment rate were inconsistent, some slides were showing 5% for 90-es, some higher. Professor did not provide explanation on why that was the case.

Jeremy is a very easy instructor to follow along with, he makes attending class fun and interesting! Explained the material very clear and used slides that contained all the information you need to know for the tests.
His class is so boring. I only attended about 5 times, and I think it wasted my time. His class is very easy. I only looked the slides before exams and got an A.

Attendance isn't mandatory because he follows slides but going to class always helps b/c he is great at explaining things and understanding any questions you may have. Made econometrics seem like an elementary school math class, very easyy
Cool guy. Made Econometrics (which is pretty boring stuff) seem mildly interesting.

Really boring class, he follows the powerpoint completely, there's no homework, only some quizzes and the midterms, the quizzes are easy, the tests are hard because he doesn't explain how or what to study, and you don't need the book unless you like having the book to go off of.
Not a hard class but honestly the most boring professor I have ever had. Do yourself a favor and don't go to class, its hard to keep your eyes open.

This guy is totally boring,He follow his lecture slides point by point which are posted on blackboard. He will make you fall asleep in a matter of 10-20 minutes of starting the class. Just skip, follow the lecture slides and read the book and this class should be a easy A.

Jeremy is a brilliant and caring professor.  He is always available to students and takes time to explain things so people understand.  The class material is really dry but he tries to keep things light.  His tests are somewhat hard but he gives you a full page of notes.

Easy class. Skipped most of the time, but lectures related to reality were interesting when I did go...exams modeled after homework, piece of cake if you do homework (or just figure out how to do it before exams).

Professor Piger is extremely intelligent.  The book is completely unnecessary, so don't buy it.  Just go to class and take notes--he always follows his powerpoints (which are very clear).  This class is ridiculously easy!  He's a really nice guy, too.

Eh, hard to stay awake. He has obvious knowledge of material, but class test averages in the 60s made it quite clear that I was not the only one who wasn't comprehending the material. He just reads his slides word for word and is pretty monotone. Oh yeah, multiple choice on tests are next to impossible.
umm i hold no interest in economics, or really competance for that matter, but thanks to the curve, i received a A-...
No Comments
No Comments
Good, fair teacher. Assignments were fairly straight forward. Test questions were all from the class notes.

Genuinely the easiest class I've ever taken in my life. He tells you at the beginning that the minimum score he will give is full credit, so every assignment was literally over 100% as long as you did it. I went to two classes the entire term and finished with 117% in the course.

This class was easy, with very few assignments or real work you have to do, but it was impossible to follow the professor. He either can't stay on topic or will go on a 20 minute confusing tangent about something that makes no sense. Overall very nice guy but would not take a class from him again.

I'm a sophomore and so far I've had 3 of his classes. (Blurbs, 315, and 380) His classes are nice if you're really busy and don't want a lot of work to do. All the assignments are quick writing ones (a few sentences r good), and the finals super easy. Goes on tangets sometimes, fun to listen to. Attendance not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I see what Prof. Miller is trying to do, but he does not do it well. Lectures are all over the place and it's hard to distinguish what's important and what's just a tangent. He taught on Blurbs and we were graded on 5 writing assignments. Went to maybe 3 classes total because attendance wasn't mandatory and I didn't learn anything from him.

Quinn was extremely nice, but I wouldn't recommend taking one of his classes unless you are okay with a classroom without any structure. It was interesting some days just to come to class and listen to him ramble about whatever he wanted, but other days the lack of actual structured discussion was frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Women Writers in Vinyl was the easiest class I have ever taken. He just kind of vibes and says whatever interests him during lectures, but fear not- attendance was not even required! He gave random extra credit on the three essays, so basically everyone got an A. Easiest class, chillest prof.

I've been extremely disappointed with this class. I'm all for trying new forms of pedagogy, as it is something that many traditional classes need, but this was just a mess. It felt like they were just winging it and were not able to really get the class to participate, as it was so confusing. I couldn't tell you what we really learned, honestly.

I'm extremely disappointed with the quality of this course. The entire class is unstructured, awkward and hard to follow (much like Miller's speech). Miller hardly talked about cinematography, which is the whole reason I took this class. The classwork was easy but I'll never get my money and time back :(
Miller is sooo laid back. Just stay up to date with the few assignments he gives and youll pass with flying colors. Hes an easy grader and is super flexible about due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Most classes will not ask you to access your emotions, to question the stories you tell yourself, or to do any mental work in class other than copying down lecture slides. Quinn Millers will if you accept that his class is not like most classes. Wake up from your pudding-brain daze of academia. Pay attention to the way he thinks.

Probably one of my least favorite professors Ive ever had. He barely taught me anything about media aesthetics, and hes often off topic in lecture, so good luck following along. He rarely gives feedback on papers/tests so you cant really learn from your mistakes either. Definitely dont recommend taking a class with him.

Very passionate and educated bur should not be a teacher. Very confusing material, quizzes, test. More passionate about gender and sexuality than about media aesthetics. Hard grader and very unclear assignments and projects. Reading was very unrelated to to the course and hard to follow. I would not reccommend taking the media aesthetics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Really amazing professor. Can sometimes be hard to follow but if you show up for class and stay engaged he'll be one of the greatest teachers ever. Challenges you to think in new ways and engage media critically, and is receptive to feedback and willing to help you out. One of my favorite professors and I definitely plan on taking more from him

His class was completely unorganized and he didn't provide any guidelines for his assignments and then made you feel stupid when you didnt know what he expects from you.  He lectures off of a piece of paper and it was impossible to differentiate what information was important and what was his own opinion. Awful professor and even worse class.

Quinn is so unprofessional with teaching with random pictures he would find on Tumblr. No slides or notes are pointed out for you, if you ask for information you are directed to a Tumblr page. Unorganized to the point his students have to ask what the test are going to be about.  Worst teacher for cinema Studies major required classes.

Quinn Miller is the worst professor I have had in my entire college career. He is so scattered and makes NO sense, yet somehow still manages to be incredibly pretentious and demeaning towards his students. Its hard to exactly put into words how bad of a professor he is... there was no prereq for the class, yet  I (and everyone else) felt SO lost.

Attend class regularly and take notes during the movies and the tests are relatively simple.  The Short answers questions were ridiculous in my opinion and the class would benefit students more if there wasn't such a substantial emphasis on these questions.  But you get to watch a few good movies, at the price of sometimes gouging your eyes out.
I think everyone on campus should be exposed to the critical thinking this class offers. The professor implores you to think of the world in a completely different way.

I love Quinn Miller and I had to review him when I saw how negative the feedback on here was. He makes you think about TV and film in ways that are different, and occasionally far-fetched. Only thing is he sees B's as A's, and A's as brilliant, so that may be a detraction.

Pretentious. That is the only word I can use to describe this guy. Full of himself and intimidating. Grades like this is a 400 level cinema studies class. It's obvious he teaches a queer studies course; he adds elements of gender discrimination into every aspect of every film we watch. Very confusing, hard grader, no structure. Avoid his classes.

His class is entirely unorganized. He lectures with Tumblr (whaaat?) and speaks off a paper. Expects us to discuss films like we're film experts (it's 267), and cares more about expressing his opinion about films than hearing yours. As long as you watch the movies and go to discussion you'll survive. Do not recommend the class if he's teaching it.

dr miller can be a little difficult to understand and follow at first, but if you stick with him, it's so worth it. he totally changed the way i thought about television. i learned so much from him. plus he's really funny and a great dresser.
Way too engrossed in his work. He knows what he is talking about but doesn't care that you don't.

Qusheng was very scatterbrained, he lectured about random topics half the time. He is really funny and cares about his students deeply. The class was pretty easy, online midterm, and a final that was optional. Labs were very disorganized, and he gave random pop quizzes which you couldn't make up if you missed. Overall pretty good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students, and goes over homeworks in class, so it is easier to complete the assingments if you attend the lectures. There were group research projects that were fairly open-ended, so it was cool to learn more about a topic I was interested in.

Qusheng is very helpful and goes over homeworks in class, the assignments are definitely easier to do with the class because sometimes the instructions are a little difficult to understand without him there to explain in person. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Sometimes the classwork was a little confusing, if you weren't in class when he assigned the homework it was difficult to tell what the questions were asking when trying to do the assignments at home. Overall super caring guy, he really tries to connect with his students, and is very helpful if you ask questions.

The final focused on information that was glossed over and he asked for very detailed answers because it was based on his own research. It was very specific and he did not teach us anything about hydrology. The final was graded as if it were an advanced class after he spent the term being overly accommodating and saying he wouldn't do that.

Lectures were interactive and never boring. Qusheng was so helpful and encouraging, taking time to make sure I understood the material and fully answering questions. He also spent a considerable amount of class time preparing students for careers after college (via field trips, intro to industry software and techniques, etc). Favorite class ever!

Qusheng Jin is an excellent professor with a firm and clear command of the course content. He is very patient and understanding during class, and he explains the topics exceptionally well. Professor Jin does a wonderful job making sure all the students are understanding the class content. His was my favorite class of the term.

With him, sit up front, dont text or talk, ask questions, and never, ever walk out of a lecture. He is hard to understand and he can be all over the place with notes. But he means well. For a 100 level class there are a lot of people who don't care and that is his biggest pet peeve. He gives mini lectures on respect if people break class rules.

Couldn't understand his accent, didn't curve the class, told students to shutup, yelled at students for literally looking down because he thought they had a phone, most terrible professor I've ever experienced. Did not at all respect his students. Horrid.
The only thing harder to understand than him are his GTFs.  Extremely frustrating class, first C in college because of him

Really confusing to listen to lecture.  Lab and lecture were like taking two completely different classes.  Gave ridiculously hard final exam and didn't curve the final or the class.  Horrible teacher.  Avoid.

Seems super intimidating but is just plain weird. Easy class - all the in class assignments and lab worksheets are easy points. Lectures can be somewhat boring, especially since you can't talk/text or he will through you out if caught, but tests require some studying as there is a lot of info. Easy way to get your science requirement done with.

This guy is intense when he's in a bad mood and straight goofy when he's in a good mood. DO NOT talk, laugh, text, or have your laptop open while in lecture or he will throw you out. Lectures are boring but his endless amount of memorable/weird quotes will keep you going. Also, a little hard to understand.
This guy was lame.  He is kinda funny but you can't understand anything he is saying.  It was a pretty interesting class and it wasn't too hard but lectures were boring.  Labs made it interesting.
kicks you out of a 200 person lecture if he sees you talking or playing with your phone. Boring class, but easy way to get your science requirement out of the way.
Dude is a trip. He kicks people out of class for talking so just don't talk and you'll be good.  He is one goofy dude.

He made class interesting the only thing that might annoy you would be his accent, however he is funny and takes a topic that can be easily taught in a boring fashion and makes you want to go to class. Grading isn't very hard and testing is easy if you read the material.
Fantastic person. He made geology fun and interesting. He himself is worth taking the class alone. A great, easy way to get a science credit

QinTao is a great professor. Lectures are helpful and engaging. All quizzes are open note. Midterm and final are not, but if you have been paying attention, doing the homework, and understanding the quizzes, they are quite doable. People who struggle or don't like her don't pay attention. Make sure you understand the topics and ask questions
Nice teacher and seems like she cares but lectures are not helpful at all for tests. You basically have to teach yourself all the topics. Good luck getting a decent grade

Qintao is a good professor with fair grading, especially compared to other upper-division accounting classes. The majority of the grade is made up of one midterm, a cumulative final, homework, and cases (graded by completion). She truly cares about what she teaches, though some topics can be boring at times. Fair warning, homework takes 4-6 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Keep in mind that ACTG 360 is going to be a tough class, regardless of who is teaching it. That being said, Professor Fann is incredible at making cost accounting concepts digestible. As long as you read the chapter before the lecture and generally stay engaged, you're going to be fine.

The professor clearly cares a lot about the class and her students. ACTG 360 will be brutal regardless of who's teaching, but she makes the topics easier to understand with helpful in-class exercises and mini-cases. Highly recommend!

Awesome professor who really cares about making the class interesting and useful. Lectures are clear, insightful, and connected to real-life examples. You can tell she puts a ton of effort into teaching!

Professor Quigley is so sweet and really cares about his students and their success! I've taken 2 of his classes now and passed both with A's. He's super responsive over email and always gives you positive feedback. There are no tests, just two weekly discussions and an essay due at the end of the term. Only negative thing is it's reading-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do the work and it's an easy A. He's an easy, fair grader, and he teaches about important topics. I've taken several classes with Mark and have always got over 100% because he offers 7 extra credit points max for the whole term and they're really easy to obtain. If you need to bring up your GPA & also want to learn about global literature take him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't waste the money on his classes you will regret it. Uninspiring, unoriginal, and unprofessional. It was already bad enough for his class to be the same boring curriculum that he has reused for years but for him to also be rude and speak down to me (for something that should have gotten that reaction) was icing on the cake.

It is not the complexity of the words he uses that makes him hard to understand, but the time it takes him to find them. Incessant use of um? True. And also, he uses repeated iterations of this word to give himself time to string together highly academic words. These huge words become islands from the rest of the sentences meaning..
Tough grader, but lectures were really quite amazing. Got the feeling he really listened to what was said by each student, and tried to push each commenter to really say what they were trying to.

Said "uh" or "um" 237 times in 20 minutes. Don't take him unless you absolutely have to. Overloaded with texts and readings and then discuss barely anything. The tests try to trick you and a lot of his questions aren't even English related it's history. Doesn't care about the students and didn't engage the class at all.

I am going to sum this up in a few words. He umms, he focuses way to much on historical content, skipped over major writers, and his main point make little to no sense. If you have to take the class for the major, make sure you get Paul B as your GTF, he is a God send!

Quigley is terrible. If you love hearing "uh" "uhm" and "uh hem" then this class is for you! But other than that, avoid this guy. He gets lost in what he's saying, his slides are dull, and lectures are terribly boring. If you HAVE to take this, get Paul B. for a GTF; that'd help.

It's only been 2 weeks, and I'm already annoyed. If you share my pet peeve for those who constantly break up their sentences with "ums" and "uhs," prepare yourself! Unless he is personally interested in the material, there will be many "ums" and "uhs" He is a smart person, knows his stuff, but he is not a lecturer, that much is evident.
Nice guy. He knows the subject matter but his lectures make it seem dull when it's not. Not every intelligent person makes for a great teacher.

Very difficult teacher. Nice guy who is approachable, but ultimately uses language that many will find difficult to follow. Doesn't prepare for lectures very well and as a result, lectures include MANY "ums" and "uhs."

Quigley is great. I can see how he would not be a good fit for some. This guy is a pretty serious intellectual. He is challenging but he is also very supportive and invested in his students. His lectures are incredibly insightful and often pretty funny too. However, as other posts have mentioned, I think this guy is for serious students only.

Prof. Quigley is a generally likable guy and his insights are meaningful and interesting. The BIG problem is his ability as a lecturer. I have never had a professor who was this boring. During one lecture, I tallied 127 "umms" and "uhhhs." Very difficult to stay engaged with this quality of lecture.
Quigley is an excellent professor that any serious English major should take. His lectures were very insightful both in close-reading and in providing strong broader claims about the material.

Quigley is a great teacher. He is extremely intelligent and witty. I took two classes with him and felt challenged and excited with each one. He knows his stuff and is passionate about literature, you can't ask for more in a great professor.

Quiqley is an awesome teacher. Screw these other posts. Any English major who would criticize his/her professor for using "big words" is an ignoramus. Why wouldn't you want your professor of ENGLISH to have a good vocabulary? His lectures are dense, but he also jokes a lot, which balances the class. He's only boring to the dull-minded. Thumbs up.

I loved Quiqley. He has a really good sense of humor. Those who criticize him for being boring or self-involved merely because he uses an advanced vocabulary totally misunderstand why they are in college. He's not pretentious at all, and those who think so are probably the non-serious English majors looking to breeze through college. Take Quiqley!

Ignore these other posts. Quiqley is the man. Unlike most English professors, he delves deeply into history AND literary theory to give background for the texts he assigns. His discussions are also "BS-free" as he'll politely correct students who make uninformed or poorly-articulated comments. Those who want a serious English class, take Quiqley.
I can't stand this guy. His lectures are so boring, and he has no personality. One of the worst English professors I've ever had, and I'm only in week 3. :(

THE WORST. Boring, self-involved, completely unengaged with the class. When students asks questions, he totally shuts them down every time. He showed up almost 20 minutes late to the final! I understand that survey classes are usually pretty awful, but this was unbearable.

He made the class very difficult to enjoy. His teaching style is basically "look how brillant Mark Quigley is" He's all about lecture and takes great offence if he sees you looking sleepy or if you come in late, and WILL call you out in front of everyone. He expects everyone to be involved at his level and can make people feel stupid sometimes.
boring

He's not always the most engaging lecturer, but he's very flexible and helpful when it comes to assignments.  He also seems aware of his boring lectures and appreciative of class involvement.  If you're bored, raise your hand.  This guy knows his stuff.

worst prof I've ever had. Half the class was spent trying to stay awake during really awful class power point presentations, the other half was spent sleeping through monotonous lectures on subject matter that I actually had a passion for, BEFORE I took this class. He killed it.

Mark is the worst teacher I have ever had, I am a junior and thought I would take an english class for fun, all this guy is interested in is hearing the sound of his own voice, he spends the entire class rambling on about nothing that has to do with the class. If you can get around it I would stay clear of his class!

He helps a lot during office hours- really makes sure you understand the material when you reach out for extra help. The quizzes are taken from homework problems and the exams are adopted from these questions as well. Overall, great lecturer and professor.

Best prof I've had in math. I took Calc 2 in winter 2023. Rather than giving crazy problems on tests, he made students demonstrate they knew the steps and principles needed to solve problems. The Webwork was heavy and long, but they were more difficult than the actual tests. He takes student feedback and explains things really well in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class content is hard but he does his best to give good examples and pause to see if anyone has questions. I think the homework is tough but will help you with your learning. There is weekly quizzes but they are only 5% of your grade. I wish he would curve, but at least I feel confident going to the next part of calculus after this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He goes over proofs for formulas as if it is an upper division math class which takes time away from what could be spent doing more examples. He does a basic example in class and then the Homework problems are way harder than any of the examples we did. Makes it super hard to get good practice in because the numbers are so hard I can't practice

You are responsible for understanding the concepts just like any other class. His accent may be rough to start out with, but it gets easier to understand. His tests were reasonable and easy to get 100 percent. You get multiple tries on each.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is a lovable character. He isn't the best at explaining concepts, in fact he neglected to define what a determinate was until a week after usage, so just be prepared to ask a lot of clarifying questions -- he won't hesitate to answer them. If you study the practice exams, you'll get an A on the tests.

He is very different to understand due to his accent and average english, and he also changes some english words which can be very confusing. Lectures are not well organized, and the pace of the class can vary rapidly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Be prepared to get cold called in class. She does NOT give in on her late work policy for any reason. Her lectures are okay but she does lots of in class group work towards the second half of the course, these give little time to prepare for and as a socially awkward person I felt uncomfortable not knowing when it's happening.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Weissler is the best instructor I have ever had, she has extremely relevant content and encourages class discussions that welcome all types of questions. Her late policy was almost too forgiving, and she made herself constantly available to help students with any and all assignments, and has lots of departmental connections.

She is really fun to listen to and I loved going to her lectures. I'm not even interested in linguistics but I want to talk her class again next year on another topic. There are 3 major papers we did, but she accepts late work until the end of the term so it's easy to take your time on it. Also, very relatable and explains her slides well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Weissler's LING 201 Language and Power class for equity course credit. Dr. Weissler is very considerate of her students and has a great late work policy. The lectures are informative and fun. Great memes as well. Although it wasn't a difficult class I would recommend her based on the student-professor relationship she tries to build.

Prof. Quarles is genuinely a great professor who had us discussing a ton of different topics. She pushes peoples' thinking, especially when it comes to stereotypes or biases that we have, but is patient about it. Tons of reading, but if you participate in class and listen to what other people have to say, it's really easy.

After several classes with Heather, she works hard and therefore expects you to as well. It pays off, as I have learned more Spanish in her classes than with any others at the UO. She has passion and vitality and will keep it real with you, she isn't phony. She also responds to feedback and makes changes if you bring up an issue with the workload.

Heather was the best spanish professor I've ever had. Kind, caring, and highly intelligent. She puts a lot of work into her course and it shows. Loved how much interaction there was in class. Truly, I could not recommend her more. The expectations are high and that's what helps students to succeed. I loved the class and her.

You can tell that she is passionate about the subject which is respectable.But I think that the amount of workload is inconsiderate of the outside life of an average college student. Class met 4 days a week and every day you need to complete a preparation which at times, were time consuming. Very strict about grading and often interrupts students.

She is so easy to talk to, well-organized class structure, and super enthusiastic about her field of work. The class is very easy, but I might be biased as a heritage Spanish speaker. Her midterm was pretty straightforward and you are assigned about 2-3 hours of weekly homework. You also get in-class writing assignments and a group project.

She's approachable, caring, and accessible, prioritizing student well-being and active participation. Roughly 2-3 hours of homework 2x week, 2 projects (one is a group project). While grading is strict, she offers valuable feedback. Her flexibility decreases with repeated tardiness and attendance is mandatory.

Quarles cares about the class a lot but is not the best teacher. If we even show up 1 minute late it's an absence and she interrupts people a lot. She is a tough grader and is not that understanding about making points up if you misunderstand something. She also often just makes questions to ask them so the homework is a lot of repetitive work.

I can't believe I never rated Heather, she was AMAZING. I learned a lot more about Spanish, and I am a native speaker so that says a lot. She is very caring and is very open. Her class was very much participation based but I always felt comfortable speaking up and participating.

Highly recommended
Shes a good person and will always answer questions if youre having trouble but homework takes hours to complete and she grades them harshly.

This is my second class I have taken with Prof. Quarles and she is great! Most of your grade is calculated based on homework, so this is not a test heavy class. She's very understanding when life happens and is definitely willing to work with you. She also assigns interesting material so it's hard to get bored in one of her classes. I recommend her

Professor Quarles is a great instructor, she provides very specific feedback that helps you improve your grade and she is very flexible and understanding about any personal situations. This course is very interesting but will be very time-consuming as the homeworks are very lengthy, expect to spend at least 2-3 hours on each.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Quarles is a sweet lady but she gives lots of homework (40% of our grade). I do appreciate that she spends a lot of time giving you good feedback so go back and read what she says! If you get a bad grade on something go to her office hours and understand why (she added points to my grade for doing so).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very great professor, just gives a lot of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework is worth 40% of the grade, work hard on it. The homework is heavy, takes about 2-3 hours and due before each class. The lowest 2 homework assignments are dropped. Study for midterm and final and you will do well on them. Class is engaging; a combination of lectures, individual projects, discussion of homework and videos. Heather is nice ��
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting but the amount of time it took to complete each homework assignment was a lot. Heather assigned homeworks each week, a couple projects throughout the term, and a midterm & final. The class is interesting, but get ready to do a lot of homework that is usually repeated during the class lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This person is a nice human being, but she is not a good "teacher". Her class can be very boring, her accent is not good and she assigns more homework than it makes sense. I've taken 500-level classes that have less homework than her class does. The amount of papers is really the hardest thing about her class.

Nice person who seems to really enjoy teaching the class, but assigns far too much homework. Most assignments are busywork that get convoluted very quickly, and weekly course loads normally take 4+ hours just to earn a B. You'll definitely learn new things but it probably won't be enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great class, great professor. Definitely a bit difficult, but overall not too hard if you put in the work, and really try to understand the material.

Literally such a good class and such a good professor. She is so kind and helpful. The homework is all very doable and if you email her with questions or concerns she replies super quickly and is very kind.

Heather is incredibly insightful and aims to show you additional world views for you to consider in her class She did struggle with finding a reasonable work load while moving online, but even struggling students could sit down and do her work in a day. And the fact that the content is so interesting helps you get through the homework and lectures.

Tons of homework. She "cut down" some of the work midterm week, because too many students complained about it. It went from extremely absurd to absurd. Tough grader-even when you've spent 3hrs trying to do all the weekly assignments. Avoid this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heather is really caring and knows her subject matter and really loves spanish. She's generally flexible, understanding and nice . If you show up and complete the homework you can pass with a B or more. Cons are that she doesn't give enough time for discussion, her instructions are obscure/too detailed and her accent is hard to listen to sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I've taken a good slew of professors in the Spanish department at UO and Heather was definitely a favorite. Make sure you go in ready to participate and show her you care and she'll help you along the way. She made the class relatively interesting too, coming from someone who doesn't know a ton about art.
Really cares about her students. Very talented and is willing to work with you/patient with you if you come to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is one of the best spanish teachers I have had at UO. I have taken multiple spanish classes and she is always willing to help you and super easy to talk to.  She is a tough grader, but you really learn a lot.

Super friendly and knowledgeable professor. Class conducted entirely in Spanish, but professor speaks with clarity and is understanding when students make mistakes with their Spanish. She is a fair grader and an understanding professor.  Homework is frequent, but very easy and takes about 10 min to complete. Excited for SPAN 203 w/ her next term!
I was definitely over my head in the class, and she took the time to help me out. She can be a tough grader, but overall I think she is a wonderful teacher.

You're lucky if you find yourself in Heather's class, especially if it's your first year learning Spanish. She is incredibly passionate about the subject and extremely eager to assist students. I learned more in one week than I did in two years of high school Spanish. You'll have online homework most nights. I'm sorry I can't take her class again.

She makes you work for the good grade, but it's the kind of pressure I expect for language.  She forces the practice in order to help you get better.  Her feedback is great and she's always eager to assist.  You can't slack on homework, but if everyone is feeling like it's too much, speak up.  She listens.  You'll be better for taking her class.

Heather is one of the BEST professors I have ever had. I took her for the SPAN 111,  and made sure I had her AGAIN for 112. She is always there for you and flexible if that means you will succeed. She speaks clearly and always makes sure you understand what is going on. Beyond happy to answer your questions and keeps things upbeat and fun (:

I had Heather for both SPA 218 and 228, and she is fantastic. She is passionate, especially in the heritage program. There is a heavy workload, however, if you complete it all to the best of your ability you'll do fine. It's heavily discussion based, so be prepared to actually be present up to class. She's awesome - would definitely recommend!
Heather is awesome I would recomend her to anyone taking the 111,112 sequence. She is there for all her students, and she is passionate about Spanish. LOVE HER!

Heather is an amazing teacher; she is very clear, knowledgeable, fun, and helpful. She is very fair with her grading which means as long as you perform the assignment correctly, you will receive a great grade. She ignited my passion for Spanish; prior to the class I wasn't interested but, thanks to her, I've declared a minor. Highly recommend her.

Heather is a great teacher. I like that she is not a native speaker per se so it is much easier to understand her spanish. She is very helpful and taught me a lot. Her assignments and tests are straight forward. Although there is a lot of homework, none of it is busy work. She incoorporates many different teaching techniques. I recommend her x1000!

Heather is a brilliant teacher.  She is very knowledgeable on the Spanish language and she is very easy to understand. She takes the time to explain difficult grammatical lessons and will go out of her way to make sure  the class is understanding. I would recommend her classes to anyone
Very good teacher, very understanding. If you do the work you'll get a good grade.

I had Heather for two terms and she was truly an excellent teacher. She was clear and patient. She clearly knew what she was talking about and cared about what we gained from the class. She is very helpful during class as well as office hours.

Heather is an exceptional teacher. This class was well structured, creative and fun. She has an excellent way of directing the course while still allowing the atmosphere to be student-centered.Her style is clear and organized. She is also clearly passionate about the subject matter and that is contagious!
Heather is a great teacher. She s helpful and extremely knowledgeable. She grades fairly, and is very personable. Her classes are a piece of cake if you show up and pay attention.

I took 303-expresiones artisticas with Heather this term. I have really learned a lot in her class and her examples for the different types of art were great! She has been so helpful with all my questions and I have learned a lot. I would take another one of her classes
Heather is a great teacher to those who are willing to work, and tackle learning a new language. She is clear in her expectations, and is a very fair grader.

She is horrible, a hard grader and it seems as if she decides what grade you will get from the beginning and grades all your assignments accordingly. When she is talking she does not use the correct grammar or verb conjugations but grades solely on your grammar and not on the material/thoughts/quality you put into your work AND crazy amount of hw.

Heather is a great teacher. She is very personable and it shows. All of her first year students returned the second year, myself included. She is a very tough grader, but her teaching method is well worth all of the effort. Came out of her class knowing more than other students who had taken Spanish from other instructors.

Heather is a GREAT professor! I had the wrong impression of her in the beginning. She makes it clear that in order to succeed, you need to study and be engaged. She isn't going to hold your hand through a college level course. She is very clear with her expectations and overall teaching. Nice, Fun, articulate. I declared Spanish because of her.:)

Heather was a horrible teacher and I feel like my ability to speak Spanish actually was reduced in her class. Aside from the fact that she is a tough grader, she makes it very obvious if she doesn't like you. She uses words that are not found in ANY dictionary and forms questions that make no sense whatsoever.

Heather is a great teacher.  She is fair and fun at the same time. She definitely has a sense of humor which makes class more interesting. She is not that hard of a grader, just do your work and it will pay off.
No Comments

I thought she was cool in the beginning but turned out rude. She likes to cut people off when there talking and she holds grudges. If she doesn't like you she will make you pay for it. I have heard horrible stories about her. Also she is a very hard grader. Seems like she just learned Spanish and  a experienced student can talk better than her.
Heather is very enthusiastic, happy, and encouraging. She explains the criteria in detail so that even confusing concepts are very easy to learn

She thinks very highly of her underdeveloped language skills.  Her vocabulary is all wrong, one word she says means something is different in the dictionary. She is a hard grader and her quizzes make no sense to someone attending everyday. Would NEVER recommend her.
Heather is great, she is funny and helps you alot. If you need help she is there. She keeps her class fun but you learn alot, it is very fast but if you keep up she is a great teacher.

she is definitely a nice teacher but extremely hard and intimidating at times. you will learn a lot in the class if you can keep up. not too much of a work overload, just doesn't go into much detail about difficult concepts
Heather is awesome!  Smart, helpful, serious and fun.  She has a real cute accent and the cutest freckles!!!!
Loved this class! The behavioral endocrinology field needs some work and he promoted criticism against study's methods and effect sizes.  Bell was understanding when I needed extensions.

Not the best lecturer. I've taken stats before in high school and college, yet left confused and uninspired. He is not helpful when you ask a question, he answers vaguely and with a condescending tone. When you ask how many questions on the midterm/final, he says he doesn't know.

Reuse of lecture materials meant that the content was unclear, disorganized, and occasionally incorrect. The midterm 2 study guide had questions for a topic that wasn't being taught until after the test. For that reason the study guide was not really helpful. The Canvas was also disorganized and often wrong. Class got out early every time though.

Very nice guy, lectures are pretty entertaining. The one objection I have is how unclear he is about projects and assignments. Questions are framed in a way that could have endless responses, which can make exams stressful.

I really enjoyed this professor. The class was very lecture heavy and there were multiple presentations. I do not like presenting in front of the class, but I still think this prof was great and he is very open to helping his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you read the chapters before coming to class. Once in class he will summarize the main points but the deeper examples are always found in the textbook. Find study partners and you'll do well!

His lectures are super boring and make you want to sleep. He is good at explaining the material, so it is worth it to go. Don't get the textbook, just take notes in class and review his slides before the tests (2 midterms and a final).

Teaches like a dad. He always had reddit open and a cup of coffee. LOL. he was a good teacher; I just dont know if he sounded that passionate. that's probably why he has bad reviews. He was pretty disorganized, but overall his class was enjoyable. I liked him a lot and will be taking his class again.

Extremely boring professor and often doesn't know what he's talking about. Didn't even know when our final was and didn't print enough finals.... That being said, his class was extremely easy. Cognition is pretty self explanatory and his study guides are very useful.

Professor Bell is an okay teacher. He knows what he is talking about and teaches that fairly well. One downside is that he can be a little demotivating but he's a great teacher other than that. Class was lecture heavy and textbook optional (I recommend), and graded by 3 tests but as long as you study the study guides, you are set.

Immediately no. The only reason I gave him 2 stars instead of one is because this class was hilariously easy. Incredibly disorganized, boring, and inaccessible by email. He teaches a class next term that I need to graduate and I will be waiting to take it until someone else is teaching.

By far the most useless class I have taken. It was a flipped class so "lectures" were done at home using online crash course videos and in class he just talked and we sometimes did a worksheet. He was very hard to engage with as he rambled during class. I constantly felt he had no idea what was going on, or when any due dates or tests were.

Very confusing and did not even know the large group assignment he was going to give us by the 8th-week of a 10-week term. Always had reddit open at the beginning of class. Used multiple presentations and often repeated himself more than once a lecture. Overall, very unprofessional and disorganized.

Horrible professor, if you enjoy any semblance of organization. I am currently in his PSY 302 class and had him for PSY 301 as well. 

He informed me personally that an exam was on a different day of the week. I was surprised to find the exam was on an earlier date than I expected. When I confronted him on this, he told me to check the syllabus.

There are two assignments a week but the majority of your grade is determined by the two midterms, final exam, and final paper. While the lectures could get boring, the material is fairly easy to grasp. I found the exams to be easy because I would study by testing myself through the textbooks Inquizitive.

If you are considering taking this course through Professor Bell, simply do not. 
The coursework is light, but there are three exams, which are awful(poorly worded, and misleading) and are worth far too much of the grade. There is also a research paper due week before finals, it was silly. Overall avoid the course it's painfully borning
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ted is one of the most laid back professors I've had. Evolutionary psychology was the first 400 level course I've taken in person, and I was really worried. But, with Ted being so chill, relatable, and funny, combined with his simple and matter-of-fact teaching style, I felt a relaxed energy all the way through the course. Would take him again!

This is a very dry subject, but Bell makes it so much harder than it needs to be. Lectures are confusing and repetitive. 2 exams and a cumulative final, but you do not have access to your previous exams so you cannot see where you need improvement. I have never bombed an exam until this class. Please pick a different professor.

This is the second time I have had Bell as a professor and is someone I really enjoy learning from. His grading is clear, as well as tests and he is interesting to learn from. I  think he cares about his students, and wants everyone to succeed. I would suggest Bell for any PSY class if he is an option.

Bell was one of my favorite professors by far! He was super caring and passionate about what he taught. He was always willing to explain concepts further and as long as you attend the lectures the exams (which are online) are pretty straightforward.

Prof. Bell did his very best with a quite dry subject. You could tell he is passionate about the psychology field and has a lot of experience under his belt. Integrated recent news and events into his lectures and assignments which was interesting. Super light workload and easy to manage. If you follow assignment instructions you'll do well.

Psych 301 is kind of a useless course, but it's not Professor Bell's fault. He tries to make the content as interesting as possible. If you do the assignments, you'll be fine. Everything is really straightforward and Bell is super helpful if you are struggling.

Caring teacher and the grading expectations is clear and he respects students feedback. His assignments are super easy, if you participate and go to lectures and do the readings. The assignments are really easy and he gives a reasonable amount of time until the due date and honestly wants no stress and the best for you. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice professor, lectures are very slow and often easy to follow so it is easy to lose motivation. Tests are veryyyy long and free response and are graded very specifically. The most annoying part of this class imo were the labs, but still easy to pass the class as long as you are doing the basics. You can still bomb the tests and be ok.

Content is not difficult, but exams are very long for only a 50-minute class. Exams are mostly short frq but graded very strictly by the key, if your answers miss anything from the key you will be docked. A little unreasonable with grading.
Content is very applicable, professor communicates well. Lab adds a lot of work, but it's not overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and passionate about his subject, but takes a long time to grade and has required in-class assignments. Exams are weighted towards short answer rather than multiple choice, which I preferred since he would often give credit as long as you understood mechanisms of ecology. Would reccommend!

I cannot write all because of the word limit.Tests are god awful; extremely long, long answer, enough to not be able to finish is the allotted 50 minutes. Is inconsistent with his grading rubric from class-class. Week 10 he decides to shift the canvas to what your real grade is (wasn't calculating the exams correctly) half the class is now failing.

Professor Policha cares about the work he does. The lecture quiz questions and exam (2 midterms, 1 final) questions are NOT similar. In order to do well on exams definitely do study guide and review all of the practice problems because some are exact same. Some exam questions have crazy point totals (ex: 26 points) so be prepared. No note sheet.

His exams were sometimes too long, and him and the GE's were nitpicky about giving specific explanations on exams. Also, he sometimes has lecture quizzes or practice exam questions from previous years that don't match what we learn. However, overall he's a good guy, decent lecturer, and relatively simple concepts that are certainly manageable.

I really like Tobias. He's extremely friendly, accessible, and easy to talk to. Lectures are short and not super heavy content wise. Labs are in line with the lecture material. His tests are pretty lengthy, but doable if you study. My only gripe is how nitpicky the GEs are with grading. Other than that, they were helpful.

Policha has the energy of a middle school theater teacher, which was a fun change of pace from the other BI200-level courses. The course was not too tricky, there were a couple of hiccups here and there that I wish he would have communicated better about though. GE's were super helpful and the lab and lecture were very inline content-wise!

No complaints about Policha or 213. The class and labs are straightforward and clear. The exams are long but adequately represent class and practice exam material. This class is very conceptual and, in my opinion, easier than 212 concepts. Additionally, there 2 Midterms and 1 Final, with the lowest dropped (go for M1, M2 success to avoid final).

It is obvious Tobias cares about his work. He is friendly and encourages you to try your hardest and really understand the material. He assigns readings but they're not necessary as long as you go to class. My only complaint is that he goes through lectures fast but is willing to re-explain if you ask.

prof. Policha has amazing lectures but he moves through them very quickly and doesn't publish them soon enough. He engages the class very well though. The class is very test + quiz heavy, but the assignments are pretty quick and the labs are really easy. Just be on track, and study hard. He's very nice, but he is a hard grader. Overall not bad.

Tobias is a pretty good professor. His lectures are informative and they make reading the textbook unnecessary. The class has many easy, simple assignments that make getting a good grade fairly straightforward. Labs were usually quick and painless.

Lots of plants that you have to memorize the family, genus and species by the latin language and the spelling is counted during the quizzes and exams. Tough field trips and tough grader for only international students.
great teacher, I took his class at lane for bio 104. he is a down to earth guy and easy to understand and his tests reflect what is taught in class.

Lecture heavy. Talks in circles when he lectures us and doesn't explain our labs very well. Would not take his course if you don't want to read the textbook since he is extremely unclear with his explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Tobias a summer lab prof.  He was super friendly and I really appreciated how accessible he was to the class.  He was always willing to help break down problems with the students.  He is also a quick grader which is also a plus!

He's a really nice guy but the class was very difficult and not well taught. The class is mostly labs but you don't turn them in, so you don't get credit for them. The tests are insanely hard and cover material we did not talk about. Quizzes are much the same, and there's no study guide for them. Would not recommend unless you're REALLY into plants
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Way too hard for an intro class.  Very unclear and tests were much too difficult for a 100 level course.  Unless you've had a lot of biology back ground this class will confuse you and make you never want to take a Bio class.  Would strongly not recommend.

Tobias was nice as a teacher and I enjoyed going to his lectures but his class was very difficult. We got absolutely no feedback on our paper and the two midterms that we had were hard even if you studied. The class average was a 66% on the first midterm. Unless you are an ecology major do not take this class.

Do not take this class if your not actually in to ecology. I took it because I thought it would be an easy biology class, it was unbelievably hard with unclear expectations, long boring lectures, and extremely hard exams. Tobias is nice enough but he expects way too much out of a 100 level biology class!

AMAZING professor, he really cares for the students and he will do anything to help you pass. He gave THREE extra credit chances that really improved my grade! Two midterms that are oddly very difficult compared to the lectures and homework; he does give study guides, which I studied, but still I didn't do the best on the tests.

He was not a bad guy but by far the worst professor I have ever had at university of oregon. I am literally graduated as a psych major and he was by far the worst I ever had. I normally get A or A plus and this was my first c. Do not take this class.

The amount of information and the difficulty of the midterm and final felt unreasonable for a 101 class. It's clear that Alan is very passionate and knowledgeable about geology but for such a big lecture covering so much different material, the lectures were unengaging. Labs=hands on. There are very specific questions on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: oh my god. for this being a 100 course this was the worst class in my schedule. midterm/final average was a fail, studied for hours for both but barely paid off, impossible to study for. attendance is a quiz every class for points not just checking to make sure you were there. sweet guy and likes rocks but poor teaching style

Please DO NOT take this course. So lecture heavy, his slides are organized so poorly, and lectures are impossible to pay attention in. The class quizzes have nothing to do with the slides and are always confusing. Midterm and final is extremely hard, almost impossible to study for. Please do not take this there are so many better science credits

reviews.comment: This sucks to say because I think he's nice and intelligent. The average for midterm was a fail. Lectures were long, impossible to remember, and the tests were completely unlike the practice final and study guide- with extremely specific questions. Studying for hours got me nowhere. and this is my interest. There was a good curve though.

Do NOT take this class. This is a 101 class, yet it felt like a 400 level class. It was extremely difficult because his lectures were confusing, unhelpful, and never clear. I felt like I had to teach myself the whole course before the midterm and final. Again, do NOTTT take this class unless you are seriously passionate about the earth science.

He seems like really knows what he's talking about and is a smart guy. But, this class was horrible. Going to class felt pointless but required. I studied for both the midterm and final a ton, but especially for the final, a lot of the questions felt like the came from nowhere and a lot of people failed. The class feels unnecessarily complicated.

I created an account just to say how much I don't recommend taking this class. None of the labs are relevant beyond "the topic" for the lectures, and don't get me started on the lectures. It's like Chinese water torture with words. I studied 9 hours for the final, and there were still questions that technically don't exist in this universe on it.
