reviews.comment: this class was terrible I would never in a million years take it again. every class is incredibly boring, he quite literally just repeats everything he wrote down on the slideshow. TA's barely do anything in the labs and half the class failed the midterm which he seemed to blame on us. his study guides dont even prepare you for the exams. DONT TAKE

Holy this class was TERRIBLE. I wanted to cry every lecture because they were so unbelievably boring. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The average for the midterm and final were failing. The professor is one of the bottom tier teachers at Oregon. I got an A in the class and I still DONT recommend. I would NOT take this class again if I got paid $1000.

This class was very boring for a 101 class. Long periods with no break in talking. Taking notes is hard because of the brief overview of the topics. In labs, the correlation to the lectures is unheard of. The tests are ultra-specific, and without hours of studying, you won't understand whats going on.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken, Labs were horrible and had zero relation to the class and the topics we were studying the labs also had no clear directions and i got 50 percent on all of them. Lectures are unbearable and extremely boring if you want a science credit DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS Has no regard for students his emails back suck

This class is the opposite of an intro to earth sciences class. Lectures have you falling asleep and material is not even close to what you do in labs (which are difficult). He then gives a terrible study guide with the broadest topics and then tests are hyper specific. Do not think that because this is a 101 class it will be a good time.
Lectures are super boring kinda just drones on. impossible to pay attention. Final worth 40% and theres like no preperation in class. No homework so grade all on final. Sucks

If you think this is a straightforward science class to fulfill your core ed requirements, YOUR WRONG. If you pass you are blessed by a higher being. The average on the midterm was below 60%, and he then proceeds to preach that we should not worry the curve (which tends to be 2%) will save us all. He wants his students to fail.

The entire class failed the midterm and final. Lectures are super boring and he spirals into things that aren't important to the topic. Labs have no instruction. Class is every man for himself. Do NOT take if you have other options
Super harsh grader and will not be understanding if you have issues or need help. Lectures are unbearable and so poorly made. Average grade in the class was a low C.

if you are wanting to take an easy earth credit, THIS IS NOT THE COURSE FOR YOU. class is fine, boring, but fine. labs are literally so confusing and the ge's are little help because they don't know whats happening in the labs either. Midterms and finals are very hard and have fialing averages around 55 or 60

I can tell Alan knows what he's talking about and cares a lot about geology. His lectures are very boring and fast paced and it's easy to get lost. I went to his office hours and he's a really cool guy, I just can't stand the coursework. I think he would be great in smaller high level class, not a large 101 lecture. Avoid if you can.
Does not want students to do well

He teaches this course with a heavier emphasis on math, which I did enjoy. Though a decent amount of the math did go over my head, I thought it was cool to see how certain processes can be defined by mathematical equations. Passionate professor and nice guy.
Goes through lecture slides way to quick and has no study material besides lecture slides for the exams, which are worth half the grade.
He spent the entirety of class time deriving complicated differential equations in an intro earth science class. Avoid at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The average for the midterm and final were around 26/40 including the 5 bonus questions. The labs were not terrible, but not always relevant to the material we were learning in class. I recommend to use the slides to study for the exams.

If you can avoid this class for science credit, do it. The lectures are not engaging at all and he goes through the slides way too quickly. No set study guide and the questions on the exams are unpredictable or extremely specific. Everyone fails the midterm and final as well. Easy to pass though because of steep curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was not good, but not awful. If you do not need to take it, avoid it. The tests are difficult and most people do not do well in them. The labs are not very hard, neither is the weekly homework. The lectures are confusing and tangential often.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rempel is a very kind man who knows the topic very well. That being said, his lectures are very boring and difficult to follow along with. Taking notes is difficult because he goes through the slides too fast. The class is an incredibly easy pass, but if you want a high B or A, you'll have to teach yourself quite a bit. AVOID IF POSSIBLE.

Had to take this class for my major, but avoid it if you can. Lectures were so incredibly boring, and I honestly learned better by going through the lecture slides by myself outside of class. You can tell he cares about the material, but honestly some people should just not be teachers.

Genuinely the worst midterm tests I've ever taken. And this is my major and this is a 101 class, the questions were the most specific random topics that were brought up on slides 1 of 120 I studied for 6 hours and memorized over 90 Quizlet terms perfectly and not a single one of my Quizlet terms was on the actual test because they were so specific.

I had Alan for Glaciology. He is a nice guy and clearly super smart. He has trouble bringing his teaching down to his students level. The lectures are him deriving super complicated equations and not explaining what they are used for or what variables mean. The hw is more math problems that are vaguely related to the equations he shows in class.

Least favorite class I have taken at UO. He went through slides very quickly and they were super text heavy. The average for the midterm and final were both a failing grade. I had to take this class for my major but if you are taking it for a science class, there are easier science classes to take.

It is telling when the entire class fails the midterm and the final. He grades on a pretty steep curve so it's pretty easy to pass if you need to take this class but if you don't need this credit do not take this class. His lectures were fast and confusing and he condescends when he answers questions

Goes through slides really fast in class. Lecture quizzes every week - not bad if u payed attention. Labs have absolutely nothing to do with what was learned in class. Homework is about textbook. Midterm and final were failed by the whole class, 40% of your grade. There is a curve but I suggest not taking this class unless you need to.

If you're taking this class for basic science credit, just don't do it. Midterm & final averages were 60% and 50% (so failing) and both are worth 20% aka 40% total. Labs don't apply to course content and will leave you feeling confused and frustrated. The class has to be graded on such a huge curve because everyone fails. Prof is very smart tho.

The lectures will be boring if you're not interested in the subject, they aren't totally necessary to go to but they will help your understanding. Some of the lab assignments are hard but take advantage of your lab leader they will answer a lot of questions. I didn't work very hard in this class and I did fine so I would recommend.

He does not go over any of the information that are in the labs and the section leaders for the labs do not help they just grade. Tests are difficult as well even if you study all the information on the slides Almost like twists the words he teaches for questions so you want to cry when you see the test. Good luck on lab assignments!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Professor Rempel is not as bad as people make him out to be. He is passionate about his class and does a good job at helping people understand the course. He does go through slides relatively quickly but if you sum it up you can get most if not all of it down. He posts slides online as well. The homework is based on a small reading and takes 20 min

reviews.comment: If ya actually show up and do the work he's not as bad as people say.

reviews.comment: Way too difficult for an introductory course. Alan does a very poor job differentiating between what are actually critical facts and what are just tidbits he inserts into his lectures. He speeds through the slides and doesn't give enough time to properly digest them, all while he uses very difficult and unfamiliar terminology. Would not recommend.

This is one of those classes where you should not be lazy and go to as many office hours as you can. Ask questions during lecture even if you think they sound dumb. There's a lot of concepts and vocabulary to understand so I recommend giving the effort to do so. He expects this of you which is why the tests are a little difficult.

Really says something about his teaching methods. I couldnt understand his lectures because he went so fast. Refused to give us a study guide, and sent a 99 page document as a study guide.

reviews.comment: I'll get right to the point here: 90% of our class (which was over 200 people) received a D or lower on our midterm. The average grade on our final was 26/80. Lectures are long and make no sense. I spoke to quite a few other students in the class and they all reassured me that they didn't know what was going on either. 0/10 would not recommend.

Alan is easily the worst teacher of any sort I have ever had. He gives tests that are way to difficult. He gave one to his GE that obtained their Undergrad at Harvard and are now in UOs maters program and he could only get a 60% on the midterm. OBVIOUSLY that is an issue. The average grade on the midterm was below 50%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Alan is by far the WORST professor I have had at Oregon so far. His lectures are incredibly disorganized, he is condescending to his students, and his tests are ridiculously difficult. His tests expand so much more on what we ever learn in lecture, so the tests are hard to pass. In fact, the midterm average was 46%. Do not take a class with Alan!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Rough to have a professor like this after excelling in all other geology courses I have enrolled in. He means well and is incredibly intelligent and qualified, but cannot teach intro geologic concepts. Midterm avg was 46%. Refuses to give study guides or any direction on studying for the test. Sent out a 99-page pdf to study for a GEOL 101 final.

Honestly the worst professor I've had here at the UO. He cannot teach to save his life and his tests are ridiculously hard (they cover material way beyond what we learn in lab and lecture) and he gives no advice on how to prepare for them. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!

reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He grades clicker questions each class and the class average for the midterm was a 46% and he wouldn't give the class a study guide for it. The lab sections are hard and make up the biggest portion of your final grade. NOT at ALL a 101 level-seeming class. A quote from him is that most final grades will be high C's or low B's.

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but he sets his students up to fail. His lectures are very long and boring. He does not provide a study guide and all of the questions on the tests are extremely specific things about broader concepts that he might of mentioned briefly in lecture. Avoid taking his classes if possible.

Alan is a great teacher who actually makes a very boring subject, interesting. But his grading is very very hard. The midterm was 5 pages front & back fill in the blank and the final was 11 pages front & back fill in the blank. Study a lot and go to his office hours and he will try to help.

Alan is fantastically smart, and you can tell by the way he teaches. He can be hard to follow sometimes, but you learn a lot in his class. I like that he doesn't just hold your hand and really helps you learn to think scientifically on your own. Highly recommend taking him.

I think people are rating Alan based more on the subject than his teaching methods...his class is like any other lecture, except the subject is really, really boring. Alan is a nice guy though, give him some credit!
Nice guy, does his best to interest students in a boring subject. Lectures are a little dry, but again, not really his fault.
Nice guy. He's not boring, the subject is.

Lame. Never have him, if you can help it. Well, i suppose it's like a free period, all he does is read exactly what he has previously written from a powerpoint.... which he posts on blackboard. The tests were super easy, only multiple choice, and the same questions off the weekly quizzes....
He is a good guy. Does his best to try and make the class interesting by showing videos. Not his fault the subject is so boring, he tried to make it interesting for all.

I think he's cute, so that's the only reason to go to class. Otherwise all of the notes are online, No reason to go to class, other than just to look at him. He is too good looking and too smart to be stuck with this boring subject. He would be better at teaching something else. the tests are a little hard, only 50 multiple choice questions.
This had to be the biggest waste of time in my life.  Stay at home and read the book, you'll get MORE out of it.
anything is better than sitting in his class, snoozeeee fest. boooooo
I thought that he did a good job of trying to make a very boring subject interesting.  He has a good sense of humor, and is a very laid-back type of guy.
Boring!!!

Tests are hard, slides are sometimes wrong, and she gets confused a lot, but there are a lot of generous ways to make up grades. It's possible to do well, but it's definitely more individual effort than should be necessary.
Tests were unkind, and most tests had Key-errors. For what it's worth, she is a decent lecturer.

Teresa Rapp was the only teach/prof I've had who made me doubt my ability to learn chemistry. I read every textbook chapter, studied for hours, went to office hours, did all the homework, but it was never enough. I only got a good grade because of all the xtra credit, but a professor shouldn't have to give that much xtra credit for students to pass

Compared to the past two profs, she makes everything incomprehensible. She does not teach the material, but only does practice problems that are riddled with mistakes and much easier than on the quizzes, The mean quiz scores are 20% lower than in past quarters with the same students. Most are relying on added extra credit and a curve to pass.

Good luck if you have this professor. I have read the textbook, done all the practice problems, the extra credit, homework, everything and first off my average quiz score is a 78 and I spent all day and all morning in a study room before the final and went over everything she gave us to study and the textbook- final was nothing like any of it

reviews.comment: This Professor makes this class nearly impossible. first of all each quiz is over 10% of your grade (5 quizzes worth 50% but one is dropped) and these quizzes by the way have basically nothing to do with the lecture. she never shows up our poor TA basically taught the class. this class is honestly terrible and is def the hardest part of gen chem.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Dr. Rapp had a passion for the research in her lab and was personable outside of class, I unfortunately cannot say the same about her class. Worksheets, quizzes, and homework sheets consistently had typos and errors in them, which often made decerning what information was accurate very challenging. I don't recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was in Rapps first class and I have a lot of compassion for her position. This class was a challenge. I am a good student with strong study habits but I could not possibly prepare for her tests full of typos and inconsistencies. She did not have a strong grasp of the material and often seemed confused about her own worksheets and quizzes.

I am so glad this class is over; this class will be difficult most of the time. Prof. Vu is a nice guy overall, but the participation credit is so inconvenient, and everyone is just fighting to talk to get the credit. Lecture slides are insanely bare, and the tests rely mainly on your own knowledge of world events, so many theories as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance and engagement were worth 30% of our grade, and in a large class that was not conducive to our learning. Every student is trying to get their points up which results in super long discussions that often lead into irrelevant topics. Nice guy overall but lectures were painful.

Attendance is mandatory. He also requires everyone to ask a question (75 person class) to get full attendance credit. This system leads to a painfully slow class as every student is trying to blurt out questions that they don't even really want to know in order to get their credit. The last quarter of every lecture gets cut off almost every time
Very nice guy and engages with students well. he only grades off of the midterm and final though but is a relatively nice grader. The only thing is he requires attendance.
Using misguided information

I enjoyed Professor Vu's lectures and his particular experiences having lived and traveled to multiple Southeast Asian countries. He's a kind and surprisingly funny individual. The content of his exams was concise and the material for the class was digestible. I wish I could take another PS class with him.
I'm honestly surprised this is the guy who is head of the political science department.

reviews.comment: He acts like he doesn't care about his students and wants to finish his class as soon as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've had to take

He knows a lot about what he's talking about. And the subject matter isn't necessarily for the faint of heart. Nonetheless, he talks AT students. And, of course, attendance is mandatory. Participation is graded, too, and he will yell at you if he doesn't like a question you ask. 3 assignments in nice, but his GE is a very harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: he's old school. impossibly tough grader and kind of abrasive as a personality. if you have the option to take literally any other course, do it. his grading policies were excessively stringent compared to the shallowness of the information provided in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's stern about the no-cellphone policy. But he also relies essentially only on three graded assignments throughout the term. Two of those assignments are fairly open-ended, subjective exams that primarily focus on questions asked and answered in class discussions. Think critically, support your answers, and show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I feel that Professor Vu has been misrepresented on Rate My Professor so far. Professor Vu is very knowledgeable and provides you with all the material required to pass his courses. He may be a tough grader, but that's just because he has high standards for his students. If you do the work, and do it well, you'll be fine.
He knows what he's talking about but he'll do most of the talking, which contradicts the fact that he grades participation hard enough to lower your grade a full letter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor needs to learn how to speak English better and learn have have a bit more communication and be engaged with his students. He made the class more difficult than it should have been because he is not easy to understand and acts like he does not want to teach.

The subject matter in Professor Vu's "Southeast Asian Politics" class was interesting, but not particularly in-depth. Prospective students should be warned that Vu is a tough grader, and all quizes are in short-essay form with a 30 minute time crunch (which makes it difficult even for those of us who did the readings to articulate our thoughts).
Prof Vu is the best. Put effort in and you will do well. He's really blunt but always helpful
HORRIBLE! His lectures were disorganized and the texts he chose for his class were bland.

Absolutely no reason to go to class, lectures are posted online and he's very boring. To get a good grade have to simply read the text book thoroughly and get a little lucky since he chooses random topics for essay questions on tests.

Not a lot of students attended regularly, but participation is a must. If he can put a name to the face then you get a great participation grade. All exams were essay based. If you attended class and studied then the exams aren't terribly hard.

Even if you went to class, took notes, studied, and read, the test was still really hard. There were a lot of random questions that weren't taught and students were expected to write two four page essays on the exam. Also, the only thing that counts for your grade in this class are the TWO midterms and the final.
Tries to keep the class entertaining with movies and other materials. You will get the most of this class if you sit up close to the front and ask a lot of questions.
A very boring lecture that is hard to understand. Not difficult material though and he post his slides online. so no reason to attend class

This is by far the best professor I've had at UO. Prod Tiwari very clearly cares about students and their success. He is also very very knowledgeable about a wide range of topics and is very impassioned when lecturing. His class was one of the only ones I've actually looked forwards to attending each week.

I have had a lot of great professors at the UO, but Professor Tiwari is by far my favorite! He is extremely well educated, and his passion for what he teaches is evident in every lecture, which makes them much more engaging. However, I wouldn't recommend taking a course with him if you have an issue with swearing, as he curses quite a bit!

Avinash is one of the best professors I have had yet. He actually cares about his students wellbeing and prioritizes getting to know you as a human. I loved his classes and he was always very thought provoking. The first couple days are intimidating because he monologues, but stick it through. Also very understanding and lenient with assignments.

I would take Tiwari's class again if I needed to. I have heard others in the class complain about how he is lecture heavy, but if you would just listen to what he is saying, and be engaged, his class is awesome. I was never bored in lecture as he is so thought provoking.

I would take any class with him! So passionate about education and his students and very knowledgable on SOOO much. Attendance isn't mandatory but I skipping isn't something you'll want to do as every lecture is full of thought provoking information and ideas.

Very engaging professor with very interesting lectures because his class is centered around conspiracy theories, which is fun. Only three assignments: a discussion post, an annotated bibliography, and an essay or other form of final project depending on what you choose. Overall a very light and easy class I highly recommend!

Avinnash was the most inspiring kind teacher I have had at UO. He really cares about setting you up for success and getting to know your personal interests. For this class, I had the opportunity to explore a topic I truely cared about because he gave us the freedom to do so and that made me excited about learning and happy to go to class.

Professor Tiwari is one of the best I've ever had. He puts real passion and effort into his lectures instead of just reading off of slides and he is a very engaging speaker. He is also extremely understanding about late work and attendance. Plus, there's no high stakes tests. You should be able to get an A as long as you pay attention.

Overall Amazing Professor, He knows so much and Has a great way of teaching. Additionally, He doesn't leave a lot of work, but all the work ties in greatly, and definitely helps with the final project.

He's a smart guy, but he has a lot of anti-science views. He's talked about the inefficiency of vaccines and masks, he says some incorrect stuff about math and science, and he's very pro-alternative medicine. Sometimes I come out of his class angry at how dumb some of the stuff he says is.

He was amazing! It is a very lecture-heavy class, he gives a lot of good context and background for authors. Wants to hear students' thoughts, and tailors class to students. There is quite a bit of reading, but it is very interesting. There were 4 discussion posts which as long as you put effort into will get an A.

Such a great guy. He has an endless wealth of knowledge about Black Studies and every topic related to it. His lectures are pretty much freeform, but everything he says is interesting and relevant. Lots of readings, but he doesn't mind if you only have time to skim them, as long as you do your best. Very easy grader. Great for non-English majors.

I had him over the summer online, he wanted to make sure we had time for summer and relaxing so he changed a few assignments. He isn't afraid to say what is on his mind and he is passionate in what he talks about, he cares for his students and it shows. He treats you like an adult and he's pretty down to earth. 10/10 would take his class again

Easily one of the best professors Ive had at UO so far. He is very wise, caring, and understanding. His lectures encourage you to think deeply about important topics that come up in our everyday lives. There was a discussion post and response every week but very manageable.

Has a lot of respect for his students. Attendance is not mandatory and he accepts late work without any penalty. Came across as harsh in the beginning but turned out to be super cool and understanding.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!! Took this class as a senior because I needed one more A+L and I wish I took more of his classes sooner. Avinnash is beyond qualified, the readings are interesting and he is an easy grader. I am not an English or Writing major but I found this class fun + interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to class helps with hw.

Avinnash is one of the best instructors I have had in any class ever. He will give you hard work, but you will feel inspired to work hard. Get ready to expand your thinking and become a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best writing teacher ever. Very caring and kind. His lectures are absolutely amazing. He is so knowledgeable and has so many interesting stories that make class very enjoyable. I have learned so much and love going to class. I can't say enough how much I recommend Prof. Tiwari, you will NOT regret taking a class from him.
This professor seriously cares about his students and wants them all to succeed and will go the extra mile for you if you show you are ready to work.
My favorite professor of all time. Seriously brilliant, caring, eager to help his students flourish. Respect for this man is off the charts.
Awesome guy, awesome teacher. Take him and you will not regret it.

Second time with this incredible professor. He is really caring and kind and has a class structure that is loose and focuses on what the students want to be working on and learning. He is super accessible and gives clear grading criteria. He isn't a fan of the grading system which makes him an easy A and he is flexible with deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Best writing teacher at the UO, period.

Mr. Tiwari is going to make you a better writer. He really cares about his students and is always ready and eager to help with the writing process. He is easily one of my favorite teachers at UO despite teaching a class I was not ecstatic about having to be in. I took WR 121 with him and waited to take 123 until he was teaching it.
If you choose this professor, you realize that he is the best professor ever.

Professor Tiwari is a great professor. His readings are a little challenging but he only requires your interpretation of what you read. The workload is fair, nothing too crazy or time-consuming, expect 2 hours a week for homework. Go to class if you want to have an intellectual/inspiring discussion though it is not necessary to get a good grade.

Professor Tiwari was the best professor I have ever had. His lectures were amazing and inspirational. He is easily accessible outside of class, and is willing to sit down and give you honest feedback and just chat. His classes are loosely structured and he has a very easy going vibe. If you have a chance to take his class, DO IT!

BEST PROFESSOR AT UO! he is SO intelligent and respect all of his students. he truly wants his students to succeed. he's super chill too but at the same time uses his class time wisely. would recommend to everyone to take any of his classes!!!!!!

Professor Tiwari is by far my favorite professor I've had at UO (im a junior). He is a respected yet easy going professor who truly loves what he does. His lectures are not mandatory but you will surprisingly go to most of them regardless due to his teaching style. 10/10 i'd recommend

The best professor you will ever meet in any University around here. He motivates you. He just loves and is excellent at what he does. He picks out latest news as his lectures. On top of teaching you how to write, he keeps you on top of everything. Take him.
He is very intellectual so he can talk and talk for the whole class period and sometimes it's hard to follow but he has one of those voices that is just very pleasing to listen to.

The best professor ever. He is so inspiring, and really makes you think about what you are writing about. As long as you follow  his guidelines and put some effort into your work, you will do great- and trust me,  in his class, you will be eager to put work into it. If you have the option to take his class, TAKE IT!
Most inspirational and best professor I have ever had! He is very helpful, and treats all ideas with respect.

He is probably one of the best teachers I will ever have in any level of education. He is so direct that it motivates you to do well in his class. If you try, he will help you until you deserve the grade you aim for. It requires work but its so valuable
Prof. Tiwari is an amazing teacher. He is very inspiring and incredibly intelligent. He treats everyone's ideas with respect and truly helps students better understand the concept of his courses.

Avinnash Tiwari was the best writing teacher I have ever had. His ability to communicate what he expects and wants you to learn is superb. He brings contemporary issues into play into his lectures which really are just discussions so he never really talks at you. He treats you as an equal and respects everyone's ideas. Fantastic teacher all around.

she is really nice and genuinely cares about her students and will help you succeed, she is bad at responding to emails and overall the fact that this class is weirdly hard and confusing is not her fault. if you are struggling office hours will be your best friend.

Tricia is the best professor I've ever had at UO. She's extremely caring and really wants her students to succeed. She's not afraid to admit she did something wrong or messed something up and makes students feel that mistakes are part of learning and good. I wish every math class I've taken was with her. Just an amazing person at her core.

Professor Bevans was a great professor! She was very open to help students, often encouraged it, and she wasn't that difficult of a grader. The only issue I had was the course materials itself. It is a lot of information that is being thrown at you at once, and because of that it made lectures feel very intense.

She has the purest soul, and what a great teacher! I've never understood math more than when I took her class. She has a daughter that goes here too and she's so cool and attractive from what I've seen.

this class shouldn't even be difficult, YET SHE MAKES IT DIFFICULT. doesn't reply to emails. office hours are always adjusted or canceled. GE's don't help. lectures don't match homework whatsoever. doesn't take attendance but randomly picks days to give credit for attending, and also tracks in-class participation online. BEWARE.
genuinely sucks at teaching. homework assignments are confusing. you either need to already know everything or go to office hours and ask for help because the lectures don't help.

Avoid her like the plague. I have never taken a worse math class in my entire education career. Her teaching style is abstract, unclear, and confusing to say the least. Good luck trying to go back and review the notes she writes during lecture as they are completely unorganized and all over the place. Don't even try reaching her, she won't respond

for a math106 class the class average on the first exam was around 50%. She is nice materrial for lecture and tests was inconsistent as for the formula sheets for each exam some of the problems didn't show up. There is one project where it felt confusing and just added more to it as it is three stages. Office hours got moved a good amount of times

This math course has caused so much anxiety and tears, mainly based on the fact that her tests are so vague and every exam has to be curved, and even after the curve the average is in the 50%'s. There is little to no support outside of class, since the office hours are constantly being canceled or moved. If you want sanity, do not take this prof!!!

Honestly terrible. It's not even that the content of the class is hard, it is  the way she teaches it. Does not reply to emails. Attendance isn't mandatory but tracks attendance through questions?? My biggest issue is her lecture  notes and in class notes do not match the webwork
Took pictures on her personal phone of students while we took a test without consent, and would create random attendance questions while claiming a "no attendance required" policy.

I took math 105 and 106 with Tricia. The material was difficult, but she is a wonderful and dedicated teacher. If you attend every lecture and go to office hours, you will pass. Tricia cares deeply about conceptual and foundational learning. She knows people's names and encourages group discussion about tricky topics. Yes, it's hard, just show up.

DO NOT take. Mean for the first exam was a 54% curved. Stated in the syllabus, the best way to reach her is by email. She didn't respond for three weeks until I sent a follow up. Was late for our meeting, causing me to miss work, admitted that if she met with me sooner, I would've been able to improve my grade. Passed by the skin of my teeth

She was very helpful for a hard math class. The first test was the hardest so study the most for that one. Tricia's office hours were accesible and she was always there in the morning to help and was very useful for homework and tests. Her review sessions were great and the math was explained well. The LAs are rarely at the library when scheduled
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bevans is great. You don't NEED to come to lectures, but you SHOULD. Also, sit in the front if possible. She's quiet compared to other professors, but she knows the content, admits when she makes errors, and is good at explaining it. Her tests are harder than the homework, and they will test your knowledge. Prepare some, and you'll be ok

DO NOT TAKE!!! In my math 106 class everyone I know is currently failing. The content from the lectures is vague and hardly relevant to the confusing fast paced material. It's impossible to get in contact with Tricia and she expects us to learn from our classmates more than her.
She is so nice and understanding. There is a lot of homework but she makes up for it with her comprehensive lectures that are highly interactive.

MATH106: Tricia Bevans is a horrible math teacher. The school must reevaluate her as a teacher as almost everyone I know is failing her class. Extremely heavy workload of content that she barely teaches us in lectures. Classmates of mine have cried, gotten upset with her teaching, and no one seems to know what going on. Avoid her class at all costs

Tricia is a lovely teacher. Class has a lot of participation. Is happy to explain topics over and over again, and never makes you feel stupid. Math classes are always a bit difficult, but Tricia is trying her hardest to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was easy and she was very frequently available to answer questions outside of class.

Professor Bevans is truly amazing. Her availability to help outside of class made me feel like it was okay to ask questions and be confused, which encouraged me to learn the material more effectively.

She's ok. Nice, but her explanations seem to focus less on actual mathematic formula and more on abstract applications in real world contexts. It works for some people, but it can definitely be confusing. 
Required group work in and OUTSIDE of class. Emphasis on attendance and group work reminded me of a high school teacher, which I didn't like.

takes some time to come around. After being in her class for a while the material was easy but not straightforward. focus on the subjects gets a little lost but realize she's mainly doing reinforcement+trying to make us think deeply I appreciate.will feel bad and curve for the whole class if you're a good student who comes to class + participates.

Second time taking this class because my last professor sucked. We went through Desmos Classroom with her and in groups everyday so it was really interactive. She has set office hours and separate tutoring. We did have to complete ALECKS. She was really patient and caring. Absolutely loved her class.

I enjoyed Tricias class as she used active participation such as the daily demos work where we did the lectures with her. Ive struggled a lot in math classes in the past but i actually did well in her class and actually learned well. She also didn't discourage wrong answers or different thinking processes which I enjoyed a lot.

Bevans is a very kind person. However, the way she taught this course was extremely abstract, then left little to no explanation for the actual math portion. She has a lovely personality, but because the lack of in class instruction, her office hours are always busy. I would choose a different prof.

I'm not sure why Tricia has bad ratings honestly. I've taken 3 of her classes, even throughout covid, & she's very understanding& flexible. She's always open to talk to students & give extra help. I think the material is hard, but she does a great job teaching it. Tricia is the best teacher for the 211-213 sequence by far! Even tho Its early in am

The tests in this class were ridiculously hard and the material was confusing. She did not explain it well. A really hard math class, which is crazy because it's a 100 level class. Take a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: For some reason, math 107 was harder than the two hundred level classes Ive taken, and thats because of Tricia. Shes incompetent to say the least. She doesnt know how to teach, and when she does teach it doesnt make any sense. Her tests are way to hard for the class, she just doesnt get it.
It seems like she really does not know what she is doing. The exams are short, so if you miss 1-2, your grade will not be great. I just do not recommend it at all.
Tricia has been one of the best professors I have had at UO. If you go to her office hours, and get help she is super willing to help you and work with you.
The material could be very confusing at times but she was very accessible outside of class and super helpful! She was always very positive and made me excited to learn the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ms. Bevans is super nice! Her teaching style is a little all over the place, so it can be hard to actually learn stuff. But there are lots of assignments that can help get your grade up - so it isn't too bad. But overall she is super sweet and really cares about us students

Great prof and is genuinely invested in seeing her students succeed. So wonderful with online classes and I highly recommend her if you struggle with math and want to build a solid foundation of understanding the basics. All around lovely person!

Probably one of the better math teachers I've had. Class is fairly easy but, be prepared to constantly work in groups. She genuinely cares about her students and is very much willing to help you in any way possible. If you're ever confused or stuck just email her and she will likely respond quickly and be quite helpful.

Tricia has been hands down one of my favorite teachers at UO. She is really easy to talk to and cares a lot about her students. She makes you work hard but she wants her students to succeed so she is very approachable when asking for help. I have loved taking class with her and was adamant that I wanted to continue this math sequence with her!

I love Tricia. She is the sweetest. I recommend taking the sequence with her. She's very kind and really cares about her students. She has office hours everyday where she explains everything over and helps with the homework. She's honestly so caring and very helpful. 100% would take the sequence again with her.

If you didn't take her class fall term, you are left to figure out everything on your own because she doesn't explain it in later terms. Lots of homework. Tests based loosely off in-class work. Final Portfolio is worth 60% of your grade and usually drops student's grades an entire letter. Would not recommend this course with this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tricia is a nice person but she is super unorganized and puts grades in slowly. The only reason the class wasn't horrible was because it was easy content and she is nice (had her for math 101). I probably would not take her for a high level math class, but for low level classes that will not challenge you you should be completely fine.

This sequence w/ Trish is very sink or swim. Some do well, others struggle. Prof is available outside of class. LOTS of homework. Final portfolio  60% of grade/her teaching style takes time to adjust to. Trish is a tough love kind of person and the math sequence with her were the most stressful classes I've had. Weekly quizzes/class participation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tricia teaches by giving worksheets and letting students figure it out on their own. The courses are work-heavy, especially at the end. She is kind and patient, but do not expect her to ever give you the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tricia was very unorganized and basically made it so 60% of you grade is determined on the last day of class. The final portfolio had little direction and was insanely hard and she was a very tough grader. She was really kind and tried hard but did a poor job explaining things. The only reason the class wasn't horrible was because the math was easy

During this class time, she changed her grading policies and began grading based off a final portfolio project that she did not create in the first place. the directions are unclear and the learning outcomes vague and misleading. maybe it was just this term or maybe it is all the time, but frequently She was not able to use technology.
I took her Math 212 last spring term and I really like it. Students can re-do the homework and get higher scores, she is very nice.
Awesome person and professor

Reuse of lecture materials meant that the content was unclear, disorganized, and occasionally incorrect. The midterm 2 study guide had questions for a topic that wasn't being taught until after the test. For that reason the study guide was not really helpful. The Canvas was also disorganized and often wrong. Class got out early every time though.

Basically reads of the slides for the entire lecture and is very monotone, but goes so fast that you cant even keep up to take notes. He also doesn't assign a textbook, but claims that in order to pass the exams you will need to read a textbook. There were 2 midterms, final, and an unnecessary critique paper which just added stress before finals.

lecture is sooo boring and he talks so quiet you can't hear him in the back of the room. assignments are easy and the tests so far are too but its just very very boring. he's nice and pretty chill but yeah boring is the only word ive got
take his classes if you like autonomy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken 301 and 302 with Dr Bell, and I think he is a pretty good lecturer. He's interactive with students in the classroom which I find to make the material easier to understand. There were assignments for every class but as long as you show up you should be fine. Labs were also super helpful for understanding the material.
really cool guy and had not-too-bad lectures. i would definitely reccomend.

Dr. Bell did a great job of teaching an overall boring class. This class is almost impossible to make more exciting but it was clear that he tried. The exams make up for most of the grade but are not difficult if you study. Attendance is not mandatory since most of the learning is within the homework. I would definitely take a class with him again.

I've had Ted for a few classes now, and he's a decent professor. He has experience in the field, and tells them during lectures. Doesn't have any super hard assignments or tests. He likes people to participate and uses examples given by students to explain the topics. Overall, all his classes have been pretty easy to get through.
Lectures are mind numbingly boring. Hard to say attention and stay focused. Lots of information but he does not do well explaining it.

All around a very average teacher. None of the tags do an accurate job of describing him. I didn't really attend zooms outside of the first couple of weeks because I realized that they were kinda pointless. He had us teach most of the content to ourselves. He seems like a very nice guy but was disorganized in the last few weeks which was a problem.

I have taken 3 classes with him and liked his teaching style, his lectures are dense and some classes are fast paced. If you are not interested in the course content then the classes will probably be boring. You must keep up with the readings to do well in the class.

Took Hormones & Behavior with Ted during COVID. It was a pretty laid-back class, and average grades were really high on mostly everything. There is a project, paper, and three exams along with some discussion activities. Overall, lectures were short, didn't go very in-depth, and pretty dry (he just read the slides, basically).

303 a hard class, sure, but its mandatory for psych majors. He is pretty good at giving timely feedback on the papers and genuinely wants us to perform well in the class. He is passionate about cognition.

Honestly if it wasn't for our GE in discussion every week I would have been pretty lost, even though I finished with an A. Lectures were convoluted and befuddling, and he went way too fast. He wasn't very receptive to questions and seemed grumpy and uninterested, but keeping a high grade wasn't tough either - lots of points for busy work stuff.
He takes 4 days to email you back

The lectures are really boring, but the attendance isn't mandatory and he reads off the slides so you don't need to go to class. If you can answer all the questions on his study guide then you'll probably get an A. Class average for midterm was 92% and the low was 70%. He says the readings are required, but you can get by without reading.

Personally, I enjoyed him. He can be a little dry or a lull at times, but I genuinely think he's a great and funny guy. The course itself feels repetitive, but he does that to hit hard at the important bits of the content. I was lucky and was taking stats at the same time as this class so my experience was made 100x easier based off that alone.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst science class I've ever taken. Nothing is clear. Everything has multiple possible answers but you have to "choose the answer that fits best" -- for everything. Content is extremely dry.

Ted is pretty laid back, and the class is an easy A if you've taken Stats before. But, if you didn't take Stats as the prereq, good luck passing the class or understanding anything in lecture based on his quality of teaching. He made everything confusing, read off slides, and was bad at explaining when students asked questions.

Easy class. He was a good professor. Lectures were repetitive but easy to understand. Worst part of the class were the in class exercises, but they were helpful for the homework assignments. Go to class and you will have no problem with the tests.

A good teacher, he is really kind and tries his best to explain everything. I went to all the lectures and found them a bit boring, but helpful when I could stay focused. I didn't once read out of the textbook because it was a bit too dense for me, and I still did ok. The final is optional and is used to boost one of your midterm grades.

Ok- so he isn't the most entertaining guy out there but he is very passionate and knows what he is talking about. Short quizzes every Thursday on the readings- 2 Midterms, that are all very easy if you just make flashcards. Optional Final which is nice. One group poster project with ability to get extra credit

He's a very great teacher! Very funny and very clear at explaining. He's also very clear with his expectations from the students. Although there are regular quizzes every week but these quizzes really help my overall grade. Quizzes and midterms are cumulative. There's homework every week as well but overall I would definitely take his class again!

Tobin is delightful. He is super supportive and forgiving of late work. He does this thing called "best by" deadlines, meaning "submit without penalty for a generously long time." He also gives tons of grace for people doing creative theses and lets them modify assignments when they need to. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Tobin is my favorite professor in the CHC. He is VERY passionate about what he teaches and genuinely wants his students to succeed. The classes are ENTIRELY discussion, so if you don't like word-heavy lectures, he is NOT the professor for you. The readings are sometimes long, but he puts so much effort in that you automatically want to do the same.

He clearly cares a lot about his students and is very passionate about the subject. There is a decent amount of reading/writing, but it is incredibly easy to get an A. My only complaint was that a disproportionate number of the readings in the class were about masculinity (the class was care and intimacy), with less focus given to women in general.
Give this man an award

Tobin is such a kind professor, he really makes you feel heard and respected. He put a lot of time into materials for this class, and I really appreciated his eagerness to give feedback and help us grow as students. I highly recommend taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Best teacher/professor I have had ever in my time learning. Tobin cares deeply about his students and the stuff he teaches. 100% recommend him to any student. Could go on forever!

First of all, Tobin is one of the most empathic people you will ever meet. He provides so much flexibility with due dates, via the "best by" dates as opposed to hard deadlines (besides the readings, you have to do them... and the responses the night before). 

You will be spending 12 hours a week on this class,so get ready to time manage.

Professor Hansen is very passionate about his work and it shows in class. The deportation class did a great job discussing historical contexts, relevant political conversations, and theories of open borders and human rights/belonging. After taking this course, I have a significant understanding of deportation in the U.S.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never rated any of my professors but I had to bc he is absolutely fantastic! Tobin is by far the best professor I've ever had at UO and I'd take his class a million times if I could. He's genuinely the sweetest guy and truly cares about his students.

Tobin is my goat, he cares so much about his students and was willing to go deep into topics we found interesting. He is often available for office hours and gives such great advice. He even wrote me a letter of rec after only teaching me fall semester of freshman year. I would die for him, take his classes if you're a strong reader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Tobin Hansen was one of the most caring people ever and his first priority is to support his students and make sure they are happy. He does sadly give a lot of homework and picky about terminology in essays. I saw him outside of class where he said hi and was friendly.

i love this guy, super nice and compassionate, 10/10. easy A. will admit, the class is very reading dependent. he makes you read 20-40 pages on average for every class, but it's not difficult. minimal writing: two 2-page essays + one 2-3-page final essay. recommend taking class with friends.

I really enjoyed Professor Hansen's class, it was super informative. We learned about the nuances of the U.S-Mexico border in an engaging manner, and he was a very good speaker and had great availability outside of class. The class is reading heavy but he gives great feedback. I would recommend his class highly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: *took HC 444 with Tobin. Wow, I've never had such a caring professor who's love for his students shines through from day 1 onwards. He has so much grace built into the syllabus, with "best by" dates instead of hard deadlines. He's so understanding while challenging his students to think deeply and produce some awesome ideas and work! Take his class

Professor Hansen cares about his students and is very passionate about his work. He's very well informed about what he's teaching and is able to connect with students about it. Get ready to read and discuss in class. The grading is straightforward and he gives great feedback on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Tobin is a great professor that obviously cares a lot about all of his students. He's a very sweet and caring guy who will help you to engage with the material, but also be there to listen to you if you need it. For his HC 101 class, it was definitely reading heavy, with weekly summaries of the reading due as well as some papers and presentation.

Tobin is a wonderful human being and a good professor. The class itself was a bit of a disappointment: pretty much all we did during class was discuss the readings (which were long and jargon heavy). My favorite part of the class was the discussion facilitation presentation. No due dates - I turned in all my essays during week 10 for full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: High expectations for work submitted but is flexible about deadlines. Dr.Hansen is a very caring person and integrated writing workshops in addition to the content we were working on, which was very beneficial with writing projects/papers in the course. I specifically took his HC231 on Care and the topics were super interesting and insightful too.

Best professor and educator I've ever met. Tobin really cares about his students and tries to get to know us personally. Late work is accepted without point reduction and resubmissions are allowed for all assignments. His personal research is so inspiring and his passion for his class topics clearly shows. 10/10 I got no complains.

Dr. Hansen is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students and is highly knowledgeable, approachable, and all around, an amazing professor.  Lot of reading and writing, and the hc231 class is very writing intensive, but well worth it.  Gives great feedback and can rewrite any paper for a better grade if you want to.

Tobin is the nicest professor I have ever had. I joined his HC 101 without any experience on the topic. There is a lot of reading and group projects, but he is understanding about everything. He will grade easily if you participate. 10/10 recommend this class to anyone as Tobin is one of the most genuine and kind teachers ever.

If you want a fast pace class, this isn't the teacher for you :)
Tobin is so kind and understanding of everything, and if you do the reading you will be totally fine. He is super forgiving about deadlines and grading, and I have never once felt stressed for any of his assignments. He is very passionate about his work and will go on tangents a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Tobin for my HC101 Class. He's incredibly knowledgeable. Expect a lot of class discussions and group work. Also, lots of homework and readings outside of class, but as long as you're engaging with the material, I felt like grading was very easy. He truly cares about helping students succeed, and is always willing to talk. Very caring teacher.

Very good professor. The class is reading intensive, but all the readings are done online. Professor Hansen is very accommodating and gives great feedback. The class is for the most part very easy, expect to spend 3 hours for this class a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Tobin is an amazing professor and I would recommend that anyone take a course from him. The actual class was almost entirely focused around discussion, but you will never be penalized for not participating or forced to participate. Easy grader and gives detailed feedback on all assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tobin Hansen is the best professor I've had at the UofO. He is so caring and understanding. Very passionate about his job. The class was very easy as long as you submit the assignment you'll get an A.

Be prepared to discuss a lot- and if your class doesn't like discussing, prepare for the discussions to suck. If you don't like to think and talk at least a little bit in the morning, maybe don't take this class at 8:30. All readings are online, which is nice.
Really sweet professor. A bit more work than my other classes but he also grades easier to make up for that.

Absolutely loved taking Tobin's class. He was super knowledgeable and very kind and understanding. The assignments were difficult but reasonable and there was a lot of reading, but I usually just skimmed them and I never had an issue. Classes were mostly discussion, and they were super engaging and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tobin was probably the most laid back professor I had last term. He is very chill during class and doesn't force you to participate in class discussions. I can't say that I was a fan of his "reading responses," which were required for every reading that was assigned. Overall, pretty easy professor as long as you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Hansen is very passionate about the subject matter and it carries over into instruction. His class was challenging but he is very understanding and easy to reach outside of class. Highly recommend.

He is a very understanding professor and a fairly easy grader. You only have to turn in 3 5-paragraph essays and a research paper for the final. Every class you have to submit a reading response which is super easy and self graded. I literally turned in every single essay the final day of the term (sorry Tobin) and received a B+ in class.

Reading heavy but honestly not too bad because all of class is essentially dedicated to the readings. Easy grader if you do the work well you'll get an A. SUPER understanding and will always give an extension if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: (HC101 US-Mexico Borderlands) Dr. Hansen assigns a lot of reading, & classes are formed around the readings. Super discussion based & participation matters, so come with things to say. He's somewhat of a hard grader on essays, but also super accommodating and truly cares about his students. I learned a lot and the topic of class is super important!

Very, very nice guy. Relies heavily on discussion, so come in with opinions. Great at making your questions feel valid. Clearly cares deeply about the subject and his students. Super flexible with deadlines and generally an easy grader. Prompts aren't always clear, but he's receptive to questions and feedback. I've mastered skimming long readings.

Tobin is amazing. He genuinely cares about your learning and facilitating a good discussion even if it veers from the reading. He cares about what is going on in the world and acknowledges the effect it can have on students. Some days can be pretty reading heavy but it is interesting. Can build a genuine relationship with him. Very enjoyable class!
He encourages discussion and I learned so much, but he really expects way too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tobin is the best. He is truly so understanding, and gave extensions on practically everything if needed. He truly is a professor you can have a relationship with outside of just class and he wants to get to know you. There is a lot of reading, but honestly I skimmed most of it and got through with an A!
Best prof I've had at UO, really cares about students and checks in often. Class topic was really interesting, lectures were engaging, tons of reading but interesting articles.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tobin is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic which created a great atmosphere, even online. Readings are from all over with a global perspective. They give us lots of feedback and freedom to pick our research topic. I would strongly recommend taking ANTH 365 to have a better understanding of food access in the world and to rethink systems of power.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Deportation in America was an amazing class. Prof. Hansen was very passionate about what he taught, and that made the class really enjoyable. There is A LOT of reading you have to do, but the actual assignments are pretty manageable. The class environment is very welcoming and intimate. The topics are heavy, but the experience is eyeopening.

Mr. Hansen was one of the best teachers I've ever had. Homework wasn't bad, and he was a fair grader, as long as you're specific and don't spell things wrong you should be fine. To do well you have to go to class though, lots of in-class activities and a lot of test questions are on what is discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Alright so the good things: easy class even if you do little to none of the reading. The bad: presents blatantly sexist and offensive ideas. Extreme amounts of reading for a 100 level class most of which is extremely outdated and irrelevant to today's views on any of the topics. Probably the worst humanities class I've taken in my life.

He is a blunt man who does not shade his language to protect your feelings. If you are sensitive do not take his class. He is trying to make you a better writer. I loved Dr. C. He's funny, and intelligent. However, if you decide to hate him, he will make it very easy for you.

An intelligent, interesting guy for sure but our classes were pure discussion with no engaging material or interesting in-class work. Prof. C was a fair grader and seemed understanding but the hours of crime movies and readings we had to do each class made me despise the noir genre.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I genuinely don't know if Dr. C has done some major reforming or has read these reviews but this is not him at all! He has sincerely changed and is truly an amazing professor and this class specifically is so so so interesting!!! He is kind, understands grades can be stressful for students and is truly so funny and treats all his students well.

He declines to provide explanations and is unavailable outside of class, unresponsive to emails. Within the classroom, his demeanor is often brusque and uncomfortable, with participation from students typically falling below fifty percent.

Really disliked writing in general prior to taking Ulrick's class but he introduced us to the reasons he personally is passionate about writing - the pursuit of conveying precisely and artfully exactly what you intend to say.

Dr. C is my least favorite style of professor, he got into teaching to be listened to. He does a bad job at providing feedback on pieces, informing students on when assignments are due and generally displays some pretty serious signs of narcissism. I would not and will not be recommending Ulrick Casimir to anyone. Steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most egotistical professors ever. He heavily favored male students, asking them about sports during feedback sessions while telling female students they were bad at writing or to drop out of the honors college. Papers due every saturday at noon. 2 group hour long presentations. His opinion was correct and anyone who disagreed was wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He will not give clear grading instructions even after prompted by multiple students in the class. He also will give 1 on 1 feedback and it is never constructive, with me and my classmates being told things like "just do better" and "your writing is subpar" and when asked for clarification he will not offer any. Very egotistical, very misogynistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Okay like the class isn't absolutely terrible. There is a good amount of work, but not too much to handle. The problem in the class comes with the professor. He is rude, and very condescending. I reached out to him through email and he would be late on important things, would talk to me like a child and refer me to incorrect information.

Do not take any classes from this teacher. He has very little time to respond to any students and will mock you for turning any assignments in late no matter the reason. He has also personally mocked me for having accommodations in his class due to an illness out of my control. He is extremely egotistical and rude. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Raise your hand and be curious about the content. Try to make connections across readings and check your understanding with him in class. He is very knowledgeable, but you have to do the work to show up and ask questions. He grades the social annotations on participation, not content. If short on time just scan the piece and say a few words.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Where do I start. Every lecture was essentially talking about his life/student's weekends with very little ACTUAL LECTURE MATERIAL. This was an advanced Shakespeare class and we read virtually none of his work. Taught it like a cinema class which was beyond confusing and prof was very egotistical, extremely defensive, and unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man is so difficult it's not even funny. So many papers. SO lecture heavy. You read 3 novels, annotate 80 excerpts, and write so much. Very much a "write what he wants to hear and you'll pass" rubric, too. He is rude, self-righteous, INACCESSIBLE, and inconsiderate. So much homework. I promise you don't want to pay him for his lectures at all.

So egotistical, not at all accessible, constantly claims professors are more overworked than students. We had to read 3 200-page books, write essays, complete an in-depth research project (consulting librarians, reading MORE BOOKS), annotate 2-4 readings every week, several 30-minute presentations. THIS PROF IS AWFUL! AVOID AVOID AVOID!

SUCH a difficult professor. Brilliant guy who clearly knows his stuff, but there is so much more homework than there should be, even in an upper divison class. Papers are due at noon on SATURDAY, no late work accepted. Also very vague about assignments, so I never know what I should be doing. Way too much work for an undergrad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was so unnecessarily difficult, mainly due to the fact there were essays due basically every week. It was a never-ending stream of work. The professor has a somewhat cold manner and does not come off as someone who is easily approachable; he is clearly very intelligent but his arrogance cancels that out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Way more homework than you would expect, tough grader, never give useful feedback, ask to write an essay that we would never able to do if we take another class other than his. JUST DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

Follow the rubric and turn in your work on time. The only way to get a bad grade is a lack of effort, most of the work is graded on good effort. Go to office hours or talk to Dr.C in person for feedback on your drafts, he’ll give you all the advice you need to excel. I hope to take one the honors classes with him in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, I know Dr. C cares about his work, I just wish he would go about caring about his students the same way. It was really difficult to learn and feel comfortable in his class when I received such harsh and personal feedback. It also felt like he was trying to prove that he was smarter than us. Is he? Absolutely. Reminder not needed, lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't let the good reviews fool you. He's egotistical and literally doesn't teach anything in class (just makes terrible jokes the whole time.) He critiques hard yet will give you no advice, never tells you when a paper is coming up (check upcoming assignments or you WON'T do well), & the essays are the main grade so there's no room for slip-ups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do yourself a favor and avoid this professor. His ego is out of this world. Gives way too many homework while also being a hard grader.

Had a significant paper/assignment due every week... at noon... on Saturdays... during a pandemic... need I say more? Was very strict about late work yet seemed easy-going in class which just made me distrust him. If he doesn't have the sympathy to have flexible deadlines during a pandemic, I doubt he'll be understanding any other time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This is the most homework I think I've ever done for a single class, but you can tell Dr. C is passionate about the material and most of it is quite interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He probably shouldn't be teaching at two different schools because it's obvious he doesn't have any time for his students. He's rude and hard to reach.

He is very critical of his students and simultaneously attempts to make jokes that land poorly. Does he know how to write? Yes. Is he self-absorbed? Also yes. Don't recommend if you don't want your questions answered in a ridiculously roundabout way and don't want to be talked down to.

This is possibly one of the most egotistical professors i've had at the University of Oregon. His lack of sympathy combined with his ridiculous deadlines make for an unnecessarily difficult required writing class. If he let go of his ego and became more sympathetic hed have a chance at being a decent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: super knowledgeable man, very funny, makes the class fun, very easy going and approachable. you luck out if you him, highly reccommed his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great person and even better teacher. Can be tough sometimes but in general has great idea and lectures.

For an online teacher he leaves A LOT to be desired. Took over two weeks to grade a paper and does not give specifics when asked a question. I am not looking for the answer but have given what I have done and only get a comment to look at a certain page in the required book!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. C is my favorite Professor at the UO.  He finds new ways to make class engaging and is super flexible. He always makes sure that his students are doing their best work and really listens to the needs of his class. Gives the best feedback and help. He transformed my writing and made me interested in literature.

Professor is incredibly knowledgeable and has a great grasp of the course that he is teaching. He is definitely very critical when it comes to writing and citing but there is a great reason behind it. Definitely cares about your success.  Also read the stuff he gives you a lot of it is not only good for the class but just great material to have

Taking Dr. C's "Revenge & Retribution" course has restored my hopes for the Clark Honors College and my passion for learning. Never before has an instructor so clearly invested such time and effort into a class, and I feel so fortunate to be able to learn from him! This class requires a lot of thought, but has been my favorite UO class yet- 10/10!
Great Professor.

Professor Casimir is my favorite professor I've ever had! The topics of his courses are very interesting, and he gets really into the material. There is a lot of work for the course: I think I spent about 6 hours a week writing responses and reading (as watching) all of the materials. However, the work isn't tedious since it's fun. Take his class!
Great class!
Callous, arrogant, rude, self-centered, selfish and sarcastic. Argues just for fun and treats every student in class as if they are children. He ruined my and many others' semester.
Favorite teacher at the UO! He chooses material that is very interesting and enjoyable to read. He sets clear expectations and is very helpful and knowledgable about the material.
The best teacher I've had so far at UO. If you ever get the chance to take him, please do. His lectures are amazing. As long as you show up to class and pay attention, this class will be fine.
Pretty awesome. Only reason this class isn't boring is because Nash is good at making it interesting and relevant. "Bout his biddness" is the best way to describe him. Fire guy.

Genuinely one of my favorite teachers yet. I love this class, everything you need for the exams is in the lectures. The lectures are extremely interesting, and I can't explain to you how good a class this was. Highly recommend.

Great professor, very good at lecturing. Breaks material into very easy to understand slides. Class is test heavy and 75% of the final grade for PSY 305 is test scores. Exams are difficult but if you go to class and take notes you should be fine, he's funny and a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Good lecturer. Kind and straightforward. Doesn't waste student time.
Very test heavy course. Only 3 tests and 1 paper graded. Study hard!
Likes student questions. Accessible for students who need extra support (like getting slides early).
Attendance not graded but necessary for learning material. Topics not difficult to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Unsworth is likeable & charismatic but his course is exponentially and unnecessarily difficult. Attendance is not required, but the slides are not posted until a week before the exam and there is no study guide. Class moves so quickly that notes are not always helpful as they are incomplete. Tests are quite content heavy even with this.

Nash is an amazing professor. This class is lecture heavy, but he makes the content clear and simple. You're graded on 3 exams, one paper, and participation on short demo experiments. Exams are pretty simple as long as you attend class and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer and seems passionate. I found the material very interesting; Easy to stay engaged. Grade is basically based off of two midterms and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Prof Unsworth's teaching style. He made concepts feel easy by connecting them to our day to day life. His examples were extremely helpful and I loved the topics we learned. Only assignments were demos of some experiments, 1 research paper, and 3 exams. Exams are 75% of the grade, but if you study and listen in lecture they're very simple.
