Nash is a great professor. Class consists of lectures, 3 exams, 2 article summaries, and 3 demos. He explains everything very clearly and is very to the point, makes difficult concepts easy. Show up to class, take notes and study for the exams and you will succeed. He only posts the lectures a week before the exams so it's best to attend regularly.
305 is a great class. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should go because the lectures are important. There's almost no homework so pay attention in lecture so you do well on the tests.

Nash is goated. Cool guy, bout his bidness right when class starts, efficient lectures usually only an hour. Extremely interesting and relevant material. Really enjoyed learning about memory. Lectures, 3 exams, and 2 article summaries. Good class.

Professor Unsworth has been one of my favorite professors in the psych department. He really knows the material and makes the lectures extremely clear and easy to understand. I am so grateful to have taken this class. He always lets us out 20 minutes early and emphasizes exactly what you need to study when it comes to the exams!
mocks any term for psychology that indicates what it means by the name.  says "does that make sense" after nearly every lecture slide and it gets old fast.
One of the best psych professors I've had. Super helpful and knowledgeable. An enjoyable class

Love this guy. He's funny and engaging and a great teacher. Seems to actually enjoy what he does. PAY ATTENTION TO AND COME TO LECTURES if you want to do well. He covers a lot quickly but he covers everything in one spot.
Showing up is important & hes really straightforward which is nice
He talks really fast.

I loved Nash for PSY 305 Cognition. The class consisted of two video lectures a week with slides that cover everything so you don't need to do the readings. He was a bit dry, but no-nonsense and very articulate. There were two noncumulative mid-term exams and two Article Summaries due at the end of the term. Class is an easy A.

Also took 306 online with Unsworth- also awesome. The material is super clear in video lectures posted each week. Small participation assignments and clear, open note tests make it a super accessible class. Two of the best classes I've taken + they build off of each other really well. Expectations are so clear, it'll be your least stressful class.

Professor Unsworth has done the absolute most for students during COVID. Open note/book tests, uploads online book for free, no zoom meetings just lecture recordings. Minimal participation. Lectures are informative and you can learn without the typical stress of online classes.

Amazing professor! He really cares about students' wellbeing, especially during COVID. There was zero busywork for this class--only a few article summaries and two midterms and the final (none are cumulative). Super straightforward tests and the lectures were pre-recorded and easy to follow. This class was super interesting and I recommend it!

Dr. Unsworth is the BEST. We didnt have any live lectures this term but his recorded ones were great and he was so caring. He only assigned mandatory assignments, no busy work, so the class was not a huge time commitment. A lot of material fit into each lecture, but he was very clear. Lovely professor and so understanding during the pandemic

Definitely the best professor I've ever had. Clear and gets straight to the point, while also managing to be extremely engaging (for a topic that I assumed would be very dry). Show up, listen and take good notes, review your notes/class slides before tests, and you 'll get a solid grade. That's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class relies a lot on tests, and only one final term paper. comparing my workload from this class to others, this class was a breeze. no textbook required, all the materials are actually covered in class so you should definitely go to class even though attendance isn't mandatory. He is also great in class, wastes no time and easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The heckin' bomb of a professor. Super clear in his lectures, doesn't try to confuse you with information he won't test you on. Two midterms, a final, and some kind of paper seem to be pretty standard for these classes. The tests are all noncumulative, and fairly easy to do well on. Would take Nash again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super straightforward person, very easy to understand. He understands students very well, and really enjoyed his class. He gives you all you need, not more, not less. He is clear, concise, and doesn't give you confusing statements. I personally struggle in exams, but his were clear that I didn't struggle.

Prof Unsworth has easy to understand lectures and is very straight forward with his expectations for the class. Midterms and the final exam aren't cumulative and he assigns two article summaries throughout the term, but there's no weekly homework. He doesn't take attendance but only posts lectures a week before each exam.

I enjoyed this class but it was very difficult for me. I feel like I really don't have the mind for memory, part of it maybe that I was about 8 years older than everyone in the class. There are so few things that you are graded on that it can be hard to do well. I ended up with a "B-"(unusual for me) but he rounded me up to a "B" which was nice.
His class was ok. really
Really great lectures, easy to understand slides, makes the subject interesting and is very funny. One of the best professors I've ever had

Nash is by far the best psych prof I have had, it's too bad I didn't take him until my last term here.  He is very strait forward and it's impossible to bad on his exams if you go to class every day.  The paper is really easy - I got 100% on it!  No cumulative exams!

Nash is a great teacher! He knows his stuff too. This was one of the most interesting classes I've taken and I thought it would suck. His tests are fair, paper is easy, and he is funny and keeps the material relevant to us. Definitely recommend this course!
Great professor definitely knows what he is talking about.
One of my favorite instructors at the university. No readings required at all and he is very entertaining and helpful.

I absolutely loved his lecture style. He is clear, gives great examples and applies everything he knows to the class. He utilizes all necessary class time wisely and lets you out early majority of the time. I'd definitely take another one of his courses.

Cool guy. He speaks with amazing clarity and he really knows what he's teaching. Outside of class he is very helpful. He gives 3 exams and a final paper. No textbook--just PowerPoint. Plus, he makes the content very interesting. I would most definitely take another class with him.
The best professor anyone has ever had

Prof. Unno is very knowledgeable about religious topics, but lecture is so incredibly boring. There is no structure to lecture, and he just talks for the entire 2 hour period. You get two absences through the term. 2 easy online exams and 2 papers. I wouldn't recommend this class if you're looking for easy credits, simply because of the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Unno is undoubtedly extremely knowledgeable about eastern religion, but fails at structuring an engaging class. The lectures are boring with little indication of what information in important or superfluous, and not nearly enough background/context is given for the readings to fully understand them.

Professor Unno is kind, charming, and lenient about grading. Clearly knowledgeable about theology and life in general.

My one main complaint is that the first half of the term had very few papers, but then almost every week after midterms had a paper due; it wasn't too many papers overall, just too many in a row.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class mainly has papers and two exams. Fairly easy and doable. Lectures can get super boring and are hard to get through. Overall not a bad class just not engaging or interesting, so it's hard to stay focused and productive.

Dr. Unno is very passionate about what he teachers, but I never felt as engaged during the lectures compared to other religion profs that I had. 4 essays, 2 exams, and 1 presentation which were quite a lot, but graded by GEs. So just hope that the GE is fair and easy grader.

Professor Unno is an incredibly kind and funny lecturer. He makes participating in class welcoming and encouraging. He talks a lot about his experiences in his life, which I enjoy, but sometimes doesn't address the course materials thoroughly. If you want to meet with Unno, you won't get a chance unless you go to his office hours.

One of the best lecturers ever, but not too much else going on in class. Thumbs up for humor.
I was assigned 4 essays over a term so it's not too bad but he only grades on that, attendance, and like 2 tests that felt kind of meaningless. GEs grade essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures felt up to interpretation and It was so hard to pay attention, it didn't feel retainable/concise. I don't feel like I learned much which is frustrating bc I really wanted to like it. Maybe if u don't have ADHD you'd enjoy this class more than me, but I felt consistently confused and like I was not given tools to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was SO philosophical and the teachings weren't very concrete. Everything felt open to interpretation which made it hard to follow along with the concepts. My GE graded hard too and I hated the GE discussions because it was so dry. I like Mark Unno, he's really funny and passionate about learning, but I wouldn't recommend the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You are graded on 3 papers and 2 exams. Plus a discussion grade that theres no criteria for so it seems like he just makes up a random grade. An extremely particular grader and takes off half points for no reason. so hard to maintain an overall A with such little assignments, no rubrics, and random harsh grading. I was excited but now disappointed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Unno is a really caring guy, but his lectures tend to be all over the place and just summarize the readings. Your grade comes pretty much only from the papers which are graded by your GE. The class is VERY PHILOSOPHICAL which I wish I had known. You also get a grade for showing up to your discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance is required for discussion, grading is done by GE, graded by just a few things so it's difficult to raise your grade a lot bc the GE grades hard. Prof always willing to answer questions. Can pass without doing a majority of the readings and attending dis. More papers/essays than tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Unno is a very kind man and was always a pleasure to talk to in lecture. There is a fair amount of reading but most isn't tested on, it's more useful for writing the short papers. I would recommend this course to anyone interested in learning more about Asian religions.

I signed up to take a class for the Dark Self, east/west comparative religion. Instead what I got were unrelated books and movies that half one sentence each that could be interoperated as "the dark self". In reality, these were just a list of things he liked. His lectures were 60% him just telling stories of his life and laughing at himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class because I've heard really good things about it. We read about a book(200-300pg) a week plus 15-30pm excepts. Tests are easy, but it was not as great as I expected. He focuses a lot on punctuation and grammar which was about half of the first exam. And he doesn't use canvas so we never know our grades.

Horrible presentations. He's a fun guy who seems really into what he's teaching, but it is impossible to follow his lectures. Instead of power points or slide shows he puts a few notes in a html document and open his computers note pad to write down extra notes while he lectures. You can see it on his website. Also a very hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is the best class I have taken at U of O so far. It gives incredible insight into the dark side of self in religion just like the title suggests. Beyond that, it really teaches you a lot about yourself, I started my journey of self-discovery, which is something I did not think I would be saying. It is an amazing class, I highly recommend it.

Guys. Take this class. I have learned more about myself through learning about the dark self than at any other point in my life. Not to mention Mark is one of the funniest, nicest and most intellectual professors I have ever had, and never have I been bummed when the hour and fifty minutes is up and I have to wait to go to class again. Amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Unno is a top-quality educator. His passion for the subject is apparent in the way through which he presents the material. Incredibly knowledgeable and entertaining. I do recommend that you keep up with the reading, but if you get a little behind Professor Unno will cover the material thoroughly in class. Highly recommended!

Professor Unno gives amazing lectures but at times they can be confusing or he gets off track. He has a clear grading criteria but is picky in how he wants things done. Overall he is a kind professor who genuinely cares about his students and what he is talking about. He is very knowledgeable and I would recommend him.

Mark Unno is an amazing profesor. He's hilarious and the amount of work you have to do is really reasonable. There's 2 short tests and a few papers. The readings are pretty basic, too. I'm by no means a 4.0 person but this class is very doable.

Too hard of a grader for a 101 class. GE grades, but follows Unno's guidelines and it's a bit ridiculous. I'm no straight A student, but I do well on essays and I got a grade I wasn't expecting. My GE later said it's hard to receive an A on essays in this class. Essays are a good part of the class. First test also included Q's about grammar? Why?
He's really funny if your class is well behaved. He really likes teaching. It's not a super fun class,  but he makes it fun.

Interesting, engaging lectures.  He's a cool guy that always has interesting stories to help you understand.  A lot of papers and a couple tests, and a ton of reading, but the whole class is fairly laid-back and interesting so it doesn't feel like a big workload.
Great teacher with interesting experience and a delightful sense of humor. You'll learn a lot in his classes!

Probably the greatest teacher I have ever had. Taking his class actually changed my outlook on religion and life. You must go to class and listen!! He is an amazing lecturer and is extremely knowledgable. He makes all his philosophical points easy to understand, often using his cats as examples, haha, or ice cream. Highly recommended. Amazing Prof.

Greatest, funniest, more intelligent teacher I've ever had. Incredible. Very philosophical but used incredible analogies to help the class understand what he was talking about. Absolutely hilarious in lecture. Extremely knowledgeable about his field. I have profound respect for Mark Unno and look forward to taking more of his classes in the future.

Unno was the leader of my fig and he made it quite interesting. While the lectures seemed long sometimes, he was able to mix music such as Miles Davis with philosophy and make it totally mindboggling. Unno KNOWS how to give a good thoughtout speech.
Probably the best teacher I've ever had. He just makes the whole class interesting. He's easy to understand and is very funny.

Amazing teacher! I've taken two classes from him and he's always very insightful and understandable. readings were excellent and the class was easy because he makes it so engaging! Take a class from him! Take seven! You wont regret it!

I thought that taking an Asian religions course would be semi interesting, but Professor Unno made this class a pain to go to. I couldnt really understand what he was saying because he says everything in a philosophical sort of way and didnt really get straight to the point. Make sure you do all of the readings!!

I thought it would be easy so didnt work as hard as I should have. He teaches in stories but is somewhat interesting. You have to pay attention. Easy class but make sure you are not sidetracked and actually try to listen or you will have to re-learn everything he says before the tests.

Unno is an amazing teacher. I took Medieval Japanese Buddhism with him this past winter. He is the funniest teacher I have ever met, very down to Earth, very real, personable, intelligent, and very eloquent in his lectures. Everybody take one of his classes; hell, the University should just fire everybody else and let Mark Unno teach everything.
A very funny and entertaining teacher, with somewhat lack luster lecture material.

this guy took me a while to figure out, but after a few weeks i was completely sold.  his classes and wisdom actually helped me in my personal life and a lot of the reading he assigned is some of my favorite literature now.  he is the kind of professor that makes me feel better about paying a gajillion dollars a term in tuition.
One of the best professors I have had at the university of oregon.  Very helpful. : )

Unno's lectures are very graceful. He punctuates long stretches of class material with personal stories pertinent to the subject matter. When reading passages, he always does voices for the characters. Tells a lot of jokes, proceeds to laugh at his own jokes. Definitely reccommend this professor.

He is very knowledgable about the subject and he's pretty funny, but he's a little unorganized about how he presents the information. He writes an outline for the lecture and talks a lot. You must listen very carefully to every single thing he says, otherwise you'll miss something and be completely lost!
Eastern Philosophy with Mark was a lot of fun. He makes lectures interesting, and has a sensible approach to otherwise complicated material.  He's very funny in class...gotta love the jokes.

Very very funny. Long lectures but always lets out early. Easy policies. Nice guy. I got sick and it was not a big deal. 1 thing: 1st quiz half of it is on grammer! so study even though it has nothing to do with the class.
I dont remember the number, but it was eastern philosophy. He is very smart and funny. He made me feel like I grew up around eastern thinking (4 part dialectic!) instead of western.
Eastern Philosophy.. Probly the best class i've ever taken... ever...
An engaging teacher with a thoughtful approach-well worth taking his classes
Such a funny guy, great storyteller, well-knowledged
Unno is the best. Has great stories and really seems to have a passion for teaching. Wears the same pants every day. Likes turtlenecks. Great guy. Ask him about his cats and the mango.
I love Mark Unno!  He is soooo funny!!!
Good survey of Chinese religions - somewhat heavier emphasis on Buddhism.

Rude, whether absent or there, passing or failing. If nobody answers a question we sit in silence. Nobody wants to anwer questions because she will straight up tell you "no", even if you're making a guess. The canvas site is a mess and hard to follow. Expects you to know what she knows. Very knowledgeable in what she is teaches however. Would avoid
WR 121** Forgot to rate this when I took the class a couple terms ago but sometimes I still think about how this was one of the worst instructors I've ever had at my time

This professor was incredibly rude to students and responded with attitude when students asked questions. The articles you read to debrief the stories are long and complicated, and you're expected to understand everything instantly. I got no feedback on any of the essays or exam. She's impossible to work with, and I would not recommend this class.

This professor is unbelievably difficult to work with. She is one of those professors who says there are no wrong answers but will shut you down if you say anything. She is really rude when you ask for clarification on anything, people stop raising their hands and showing up. If you don't talk or write like her, you won't do well.

This class isn't very hard if you show up and do all the readings, but you will probably be very lost if you have to miss class, she is not very accommodating of that. She goes off on a lot of rants, and you can tell she has a lot of knowledge but she isn't great at answering questions and overcomplicates explanations beyond just giving an answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is so rude and condescending to any student who asks her questions. Coursework is extremely heavy, and when you ask her for clarification on things she simply over-explains with huge words to the point where you can't even tell what she's talking about. Everyone I have talked to in this class dislikes this professor and this course.

I have a lot of respect for this woman. She will push and assist you to be a better student! You will know if/ when she disagrees with you because she will read you down nasty- somehow remaining very polite about it. If you respect her and the class, she will respect you. The best way to pass is just putting in the effort. Untara Rayeesa slays

Dr. Lawrence Ulibarri is very passionate about forensic anthropology which makes it easy to follow along in class. First four weeks was honestly like a light version of anatomy. Be prepared to start memorizing everything for exams. The Lab practical was not that and our classes midterm was curved 10 points! I got both over 90%.
Easy online class to take for a science requirement, he just grades harshly on the final project (at least for me)

Lawrence seems like a chill guy and interested in what he teaches. However, I found his online lectures pretty boring. The documentaries that we watched were interesting and I learned a lot from the sources he provided. Some of the assignments are very laborious, but he gives you a week to complete them. Easy course if you don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved the class, and as long as you go to lectures and labs you'll be fine. The course grade is mostly the lab reports, so make sure you do them. He clearly cares about the subject and is happy when students are interested.

I was nervous about finding classes to fulfill my science requirement, but I'm so glad I took Professor Ulibarri's class! He provides plenty of fun opportunities for extra credit and is clearly passionate about what he's teaching. Lecture videos can be long but have been super interesting. Tests and assignments are straightforward :-)
Great teacher. He explains things well and is very caring. Extra Credit is offered for the class as well. So far average difficulty. Would take him again for sure.

I've taken a few classes with him and he is absolutely an amazing professor and he really cares about his students and the subject. This was definitely a more test-heavy course, but as long as you study what he puts on the lecture slides you should do good on the tests.

Professor Ulibarri is an incredible lecturer: clearly knowledgable and passionate, and does a great job connecting with students. Class can be tough-- there's alot of background knowledge that can be helpful that I didn't really have, but homework isn't crazy and I think he's a fair grader. Really fun to pick his brain outside of class, as well.
Larry is an AMAZING professor. He makes the classroom fun to be in. very engaging and caring.

Really great professor. I'm glad I took this class and recommend him for any anthropology course. It does take a lot of studying and work, but the content is interesting and he's great at lecturing. I emailed him a few times and went to office hours for help and he was very patient and helpful.

Professor Ulibarri is a great lecturer and makes his class interesting and relevant to current events. He also cares a lot about his students and is very easy to talk to. You definitely have to study for the midterm and final and also attendance is required for labs and a good chunk of your grade. There is also a final presentation but is easy.

Mr. Ulibarri really cares about this class and Anthropology as a whole. Not only Anth but also his students and making sure the class has relevant and interesting stories/information. His lectures don't feel long but he does pack in a good chunk of terms and can go fast sometimes. Really you only get graded on your weekly labs and midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super passionate and engaging but difficult course. It is interesting, but you have to do a lot of studying terms and anatomy. the midterm, practical, and final exam is basically your grade besides the lab.

Loved his lectures and beginning of the week videos! I had his summer async course, there were hidden easter eggs for extra credit in his lectures and readings. The lectures were very long (40-60 min x 6) for a 4-week course, but the option to do an art project as a final was great. I enjoyed his caring personality and the class content. Loved him!

Omg I love Ulibarri. I took ANTH 220 & had to have him again for 274 (both online recorded lectures). These were just for science credit but I want to take all the Anth courses taught by him. He also loves the arts. He is incredibly passionate & I learned sooo much. I actually even have a better relationship with food now bc of Nutritional Anth.

(This prof has another page under "Larry Ulibarri") He's really excited to talk about forensic anthropology, and his energy is very engaging. This class involves memorizing a LOT of osteology & it is not something you can just cram last-second. Previous experience with anatomy will help you a lot in this class. You get to handle real bones in lab!

Ulibarri is an excellent professor, just know that this class is HARD! If you are interested in forensics this class is amazing, providing tons of information, case studies, and labs that are super applicable. Do not take this class if you don't want a challenge, because it is a lot of information and a lot to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor's passion for this subject made me switch my minor to Forensic Anth. This isn't an easy A, you need to study the material to do well, but that should be expected for any college course. Don't take it for a science credit, only if you're interested in learning this subject, or you will just be in hell studying. If you are, take him!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Was terrified to take such a hard course and indeed it was very hard. But I have never felt like school was rewarding until now. He is an amazing professor that wants you to succeed. He is VERY clear in what he wants to see from you. I emailed him so many times (lol) but he always answered fast and clearly. A great man that was meant to teacher!

At first glance, the material felt daunting and overwhelming. I struggled for the first several weeks bc I have a difficult time with remote classes, but after meeting with Mr. Ulibarri my learning and ability to complete this course greatly improved. He is the kindest man who has an honest love for animals. I highly recommend his courses.

Took this to satisfy science requirement. I loved the class so much more than expected. ANTH 274 is about such an interesting topic. There's a lot of freedom with what you write your discussions and final project on. Lectures are long (3 hours weekly) but quizzes are on lecture and article material. Gonna take another class from him! Take this!

He is definitely very passionate about the subject! I spoke with him outside of class once and we just chatted about it for a while after he answered my questions. A good combination of current news and history. Lectures were a bit dry and long but understandable. Provided info about the final project in the first week & gave us freedom with it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ulibarri is an amazing professor and totally worth your time! He's my advisor and I am continuing on with his courses.

On my canvas page and realized he had 4 video lectures up for every week. I thought this had to be a mistake because each video was almost an hour long. Along with this there are extremely lengthy readings that no one in their right mind would spend their time doing . This is the strucutre every week for 5 weeks. I dropped as soon as possible...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No papers, just a final group project. Labs are simple and graded mostly for attendance. Lecture slides are heavily detailed and he goes kind of quickly for how much information he wants us to absorb. Wouldn't take the class again but you can tell he's passionate about the subject and gives students opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Ulibarri is so sweet and so approachable. He's kind of like that really sweet, cute, older guy you wish were your uncle or your grandpa. He's clearly very passionate about what he teaches, and he gives a lot of "easter eggs" (easy answers to test questions) if you come to class.

Lecture can seem boring because it's fairly long, but he's super funny and is passionate about what he teaches. There's not many assignments before the midterm, but study a lot for it. It's mostly written which was a surprise, I was shook when I saw how much writing it had. If you memorize the basic stuff early on you're set.

This was the first anthropology class that I've taken, and I'm so glad that I took it with Professor Ulibarri.  It's not an easy class, and you have to study to do well on his tests, but he is incredibly kind and accommodating to each student's needs.  The labs are easy and fun as well!  Would definitely take him again.

Larry made the online class interesting and exciting. He incorporated relevant news items whenever possible! Provided great in depth feedback on most assignments and was dedicated to getting to know all his students.

Professor Ulibarri was awesome! He's so knowledgable about bioanthropology and it definitely shows. That being said, his class is definitely tough and he expects a lot out of you. I had to study and it was a lot of heavy memorization but I highly recommend the course!

Professor Ulibarri has be one of my favorite professors at the University of Oregon. He is so passionate about his subject, and it really shows in his lectures. Although, his lectures can drone on, but he's sweet enough to where you want to show up to class. Tests have a lot of material on it, but the study guides are very helpful.

Professor Ulibarri is fantastic. His lectures are so interesting, the reading load is manageable (about 1 textbook chapter per class), and there are three tests. He frequently gives extra credit for showing up to class. He is kind to his students, clearly demonstrates his intelligence on human anthropology, and was a pleasure to have as a professor
As long as you take notes and pay attention, the tests will be pretty easy.

Dr. Ulibarri is one of my favorite professors at UO. His class was so interesting, he was well organized and everything was perfectly clear. I think he was fairly easy for intro level classes. Would totally recommend his class!!

Came into the university as an International Studies major, but Dr. Ulibarri's Biological Anthropology 270 course made me reconsider my major! Few assignments, so the midterm and final are what your grade will be (along with your lab & some extra credit for attending lecture. Difficult but interserting!

Very nice teacher, makes the lectures interesting because he cares about the subject. You need to be at the lectures, but he was understanding if students missed one or two. I had a lot of fun in this class. Labs were easy, but taught you practical skills. Be prepared to do your own research paper. Difficult, but you have a lot of time to do it.

Not sure how useful this review is since he wont be teaching econ anymore, but Mike is easily the best of the lower-level professors in the department. The class was way easier than expected and you can tell he really cares about everyone's success. However, he does ramble a lot and lectures don't have a natural flow to them, which is distracting.
What a great teacher, but what an amazing person. Professor Urbancic (or Mike as he prefers) is one of the greats. A true GOAT of Economics!!! LOVE LOVE LOVE!

He's chill overall, but definitely keeps things interesting. Don't be surprised if he's suddenly standing on a chair mid-lecture. He'll call you out if you're not paying attention, but it's usually in a way that keeps the class awake. Never a boring day, and honestly a solid teacher.
office hours are peak and he's a chiller
Decent but boring lectures and would get mad at people talking in class every day and waste time because of it. Midterms were easy but final was pretty hard.

The resources he provides don't really prepare you for the midterms and final difficulty. Study guides are easy and don't compare to the actual test and homework did not benefit to learning the content. He tends to ramble a lot but just focus on the lecture slides and worksheets he provides every lecture and you should be okay. Bit of a crash out.

He's okay but the way he structured the class made it much harder than it needed to be. Homework was chill but did not contribute to my learning at all and his tests are weird and don't reflect what he says will be on them. The concepts of this class were not challenging, but he taught it in such a weird way that made it hard for me to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was okay. Rambles a lot and explains things in the most difficult way possible. Average was a C-C+ on the midterms. Only graded on 2 midterms and a final.
He is a good professor just off topic a lot and rambles a lot. As a few minor crash outs here and there.

Mike is awesome! Please take his class if you can! I took macro before micro and was worried but its actually been totally good. There is not a lot of homework, and the content is fairly straight forward. Also the math is basic if you are worried.

A good amount of your grade comes from your work in fairly easy discussion sections, but apart from that, there's not much going for him. The lectures drag on, and he gets pressed and condescending when people are slightly whispering, and on a few occasions has lectured from the balcony of Straub because he's gotten so upset.

Mike's course is graded mostly on tests and participation in discussion sections. Attendence in lectures is not mandatory but instead is offered as extra credit. He can ramble but overall lectures are organized and he has detailed slides that help if you miss a lecture and can be useful to study. Tests are relatively easy and note card is allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't enjoy this course because it was hard to understand Mr Mike. He rambles and mumbles but he does get his point across, even if it takes a while. His slides have a lot going on and aren't very engaging, but he does try his best. Overall it's hard to pay attention, but the workload is manageable. Tests are hard, but you do get a note card.

Lectures they were not engaging and frustrating. He gives you no time to talk to classmates as it is "distracting the whole class", so he would rather have you sit in silence listening to his non-engaging lectures and will stop class to wait for it to be entirely silent. Test heavy on 2 midterms and a final. Rest of work is easy, weekly hw/quiz.
Hard to pay attention to. He mumbles and rambles on about things not pertaining to his slides which makes the lectures hard to focus on. Other than that, easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is pretty difficult, with lots of different assignments going into your final letter grade. Lectures are not mandatory, but discussions are. Grading is odd, with every assignment being around 4% of your grade. Exams are also very difficult, with questions in Midterm 2 going back to one video in the first discussion section.
Great professor, cares a lot about the subject. Puts a lot of effort into his lectures too. Tests are as manageable as econ tests can be. Great guy overall.

Very chill professor, barely payed attention during class and was able to pass. Everything on the tests is in the slides/lectures so it's super easy to go back studying, Definitely recommend if you are looking for easy A class for prerequisite requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mike is very chill and this class is quite easy with posted materials, weekly understanding checks, practice tests, and notecard cheatsheets allowed. He is also available outside of class. Lectures can be meandering sometimes, but it's kind of endearing and never a problem. With some effort this class is easy to succeed in and Mike is very helpful.

Good professor, is very passionate about his subject material. Lectures tended to drag on a bit occasionally, and he sometimes gets a little caught up in explaining something and loses/confuses everyone as a result. Moderately light assignments and exams, just make sure you do the reading and practice midterms. 3x5 notecard allowed.

Would stop in the middle of the lecture and walk to the back towards talking students and tell them that they should be talking on discord instead. Also walks around the entire hall for the entirety of the lecture which is distracting. Midterms are quite easy and you can use a 3x5 notecard. Gives worksheets that follow lectures but still boring

Everything that is needed to ace the exams is fully on the slides which he posts on canvas. The worksheets handed out every class are also helpful too. Light homework readings on perusall and discussion worksheets. On both midterms I have gotten over 90%
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: missed midterm because i got the timing wrong, didnt hesitate to go out of his way and make a time for me to make up the midterm! would recommend.
Clear grading criteria but test and lecture heavy. Lectures are not very engaging.
Mike was an amazing EC202 professor. How abhorrent of the University to lay him off—he will be greatly missed.

Mike is an incredible professor - an inspiration to thousands of students. Interesting that the UO can afford all of these new buildings and advertising, but they can't afford to keep someone who has been a real treasure for the university for over a decade. His passion for Economics and teaching will be missed.

not a ton of HW. tests are difficult but manageable despite the class average being in the 50-60s on the tests. generous curve implemented at end. i personally didn't take to Mikes lecture style but his knowledge of economics is apparent.
Just bad, that's all. Don't take him if you don't have to.

Mike is very passionate about macroeconomics, but his teaching style ruins the class and makes it very difficult to follow and stay engaged. The class is heavily weighted on exams, which questions are highly specific and niche. It's hard to do well in the class, even if you study the entire unit! The exam will cover the most niche and odd questions
Amazing teacher and really cares about economics and his students. Please pay attention during his lectures, he puts a lot of effort into his presentations.

His lectures can be a little boring, but he does give worksheets to follow along with. These worksheets highlight the important things from the slides which is nice. By doing the IClicker students can get extra credit. Exams can be easy if you study.

Don't take Urbancic unless you have to. Everyone does poorly on the exam, and the curve is nowhere near sufficient enough to bring your grade back up, so nearly nobody has an A. Homework is easy and his tests are simply what ruin the class.

Very Very dull. Slides have little to no information. No study guide, what is going to be on the test is very unclear. Class try's to be interactive, but is not. Would rather have had any other teacher maybe one that knows about the subject and stays on topic better.

Urbancic makes it clear how to study for his exams, and most of it comes from the lectures, which consist of him rambling about topics in the slides for a long time. Although, I appreciated how he stretched out concepts for macro in lectures compared to the opposite for micro, but you have to be very focused to take in what he's saying

I found his lectures to be very hard to follow, but the class was easy to navigate outside of lectures. There were very clear expectations and guidelines for all assignments and exams, which was very helpful. He curved each exam and the overall class grade, as well as dropped lower scores on assignments. I recommend heavy self-studying for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor. Coursework consisted of weekly readings (online, free), going over material in class, and then a discussion at the end of the week. He curves tests, gives extra credit (ATTEND LECTURE), and late work can be turned in for partial credit. As long as you attend the lecture and do the assigned material outside of class, you'll be fine.

I've taken both EC 201 and 202 this was much more difficult. The wasn't difficult but there was a lot of homework that was irrelevant to the lectures and the tests. It felt extremely redundant and just an unnecessary class. I never knew that to study on tests and found the lectures were confusing and irrelevant.

Passed the class with an A because of the curves and extra credit!! His tests are hard, but he makes up for it by giving curves on every test and giving out lots of extra credit. Very friendly and if you go to his office hours, the concepts will make a lot more sense. If you like to push yourself and want to learn more about econ, try this class.

There's really no homework, but you must compensate the time with studying. As mentioned prior, the exams often include very specific models that may have been mentioned in lecture for a brief moment, which makes you regard them as insignificant. If you're genuinely interested in macroeconomics, you'll love this class. Go to office hours!

Professor Mike is a good person that cares about his students, but he often gets off topic during his lectures. His tests are hard with the average being a 50-60%. The tests contain very specific details in the readings or videos that he assigns that you'd think wouldn't be on the test. Only take this class if you're willing to study A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor ever. He puts questions on exams about a specific part of a video shown in a lecture from week 2 and backs it by saying to study just review every slideshow and video posted in the 10-week course. Do not take his class.

Nice person and clearly cares about his students. He promotes his office hours every week, gives out extra credit for coming to class, and gives out weekly reminders about when things that are due. His tests are hard and so I wished he would give out a practice test before each midterm and final. Take advantage of his office hours.

Guys, if you're reading this...find a different professor for economics. The term "the professor makes or breaks the class" has never been more true. The class itself, along with the information you're required to learn isn't to crazy. But he is AWEFUL at teaching. His Mean score for his midterms where F's... I shall say no more.

No notes on any test, and a ridiculous amount of information to be memorized. Tests have a lot of 
"multiple-choice multiple-response" questions and if you get one wrong the whole thing is wrong. He also led the Palestine protests outside of Lilis. Dude is weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take him. He barely gets on topic in class and rambles over and over about stuff that has the smallest correlation. In addition his work each week isn't that bad just super busy work and with extracurriculars it sucks. Also his exams are so specific it's a joke. Would not take him again, only because is required.

Mike is the worst professor I've ever had. Do not take his class. He rambles on and on about irrelevant topics in his lectures and leaves the entire class confused. I am a student who really cares about my grades, and because of the lackluster lectures and missing structure, I have absolutely no clue what to even study before his tests.

Mike's lectures can be dry, but with Unstuck ai and the textbook, you can succeed. Assignments don't prepare you for exams, but staying engaged in class makes a difference. Expect a challenge, but a manageable one.

This professor was god awful. He tried to be funny and make lectures entertaining, so I credit him for that. But his midterms and finals averaged 50%. I only passed the class because he handed out extra credit like crazy in the final week. His test questions came out of nowhere and had the most niche details without focusing on general concepts. NO

Mike is a great guy and a good professor. His lectures get a bit boring but he does his best by handing out free money and snacks at times. Some fun games to keep the class engaged. Tests are very difficult but he curves and can get you back a few percentages. The book and book quizzes we had were very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I might as well have taken an alien linguistics class because this class made absolutely 0 sense

Inaccessible outside of class, rambles in lectures to the point that people begin to talk, a TON of work per week between readings and discussion readings. The mini-exams are just midterms and there's four. You're tested on pretty specific content from the readings just as often as economic theory if not more. Too many assignments. Take Waddell
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mike seems like a really good guy, but his class was far too difficult. I wasn't expecting an easy A, but the online tests were way too difficult. One of the questions even had every answer correct. Needs to learn how to write a multiple-choice test.

Tests are online, he bases half of the questions on random articles and 30-minute-long videos instead of being more focused on concepts. His lectures aren't the most engaging and I feel like you could learn way more just by reading the textbook. Tests are worth over 50% of the grade and have  zero curve even when test performances are poor.

urbancic makes an amazing effort to get students to engage and understand. uses funny memes and tweets to get his points across and is overall very caring. tests are a little unclear sometimes on what exactly you're being tested on but provides lots of resources to understand class topics

Tests are really frustrating. He gives basically zero study materials aside from just saying to read over the slides. Additionally, the course assignments - annotated readings and discussion sections - do literally nothing to prepare you for the type of questions that will be on the exams.

Nice guy, but most boring lectures ever. Never once got through his entire slideshow or activity sheets. Never seen a professor grade you worse on an exam for getting something wrong than not answering at all. The class average was around 74 despite the simple material. Took over 2 months to grade the discussion responses. Prepare to be frustrated.

Some of the most boring lectures I have gone to. He rambles about unrelated topics for about 90% of the lecture. Average grade of the Midterm was a 18/32 and instead of thinking about changing up the class format or reflecting on his teaching style he said "study harder" and did not curve it or anything. I got a good grade but I dont recommend mike

I enjoyed this class but I flunked the mid-term. If I hadn't been bedridden I probably would have passed the class with an easy A. The hybrid class structure worked well but the lectures were necessary to get that extra insight on the week's topic. He is very entertaining and insightful in every lecture. If you have any interest in econ, its solid.

Mike is a very supportive and understanding teacher. While he doesn't give a lot of feedback on assignments, he provides lots of help, resources, and reminders that I didn't expect a college prof to give. He uses memes and tweets in his lectures and is very engaged during said lectures - you can tell he really wants to connect with students.

This class was very easy, but I think that is partly because it is a 101 and also because Mike is such a great teacher. We had a lot of reading, especially from weeks 2-4 but it ended up all being worth it. If I take another econ class I will definitely try to take it with Mike
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have never had to work this hard for an A-. There is an excessive amount of work in this class. Most Econ classes will just have a midterm and a final. Mike forces you to read every page and the 4 exams were very difficult. The final was awful. It sounds like he used to be nicer, but he takes his job way too seriously now. Take with anyone else.

Mike was fine, but he just rambles a lot which is hard for someone like me to pay attention to. He would constantly talk about hypothetical scenarios in order "prove his teaching point", but I never really understood it. The tests didn't really pertain to the lectures. He's average.

He is a great professor and is the better out of the econ 202/201 profs. You have opportunities to get good grades other than just exams but the exams are hard. Weekly online discussion posts (very easy) and you have to annotate the online textbook. Attendance is mandatory with worksheets and extra credit is given through iclicker participation.

Mike teaches EC 101, EC 201, and EC 202 in order all year. I strongly recommend taking them all in order with him, because he's a fantastic lecturer and a fairer grader than the Econ professors my friends have. That said, don't expect it to be easy if you're not super familiar with graphs. Many of the mini-exam questions can be very convoluted.

This is NOT a difficult class. Mike gives you all of the materials you need to succeed, all you have to do is halfway pay attention. I browsed the internet for every course, never studied, and finished with a 97. The lectures are long and can be really painful, but this is legitimately one of the easiest college courses I have ever taken. Gpa Boost

Mike is a great professor/lecturer and a nice guy, but he needs to work on the wording on his exams. The four mini-exams and final were extremely difficult even though I did all my reading and studied his lectures. The vast majority of your grade is the exams, so if you don't do well on them, you can't get the grade you want in the class. Very hard

Mike is a great prof for Econ 201; while you have to work hard to get an A, his class is easy to keep up with and get points. We have required activity sheets and clicker points for every lecture, so attendance and participation matter if you are going to succeed. We have four mini-exams and a final online. I recommend him for the class.

He is very kind n approachable,he will always be there to help n answer questions however his workload is heavy n the exams are HARD n graded heavy which is frustrating since we have 3 separate assignment every week n extra credit but its still not enough.I wish he would as least drop one of the exam scores especially since he has to curve them all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is an amazing professor who actually cares about his students and their understanding of the material. Exams are online and open note, and he uses a free online textbook. Keeps students engaged in class, even offering up money and prizes to make economic examples. Overall a great professor, can't wait to take EC202 from him next term!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very nice and funny guy. He does a really good jobs at keeping the lectures engaging. Grades are based on a few different things not just test and quizzes. The textbook is online and free which is also nice. The only negative thing I would say is that the mini quizzes can be pretty challenging. Mike slays
Really chill professor. Not too difficult of a grader, but lecture content could be a bit dry. Mike on the other hand is pretty funny and seems like a nice guy.
Lectures are pretty boring and drawn out, Mike is definitely a rambler. It's not too difficult of a class though, other than the moderately tough mini-exams every 2 weeks. I'm neutral about Mike.

MIKE ROCKS!!! Econ is kind of boring and hard but he made the lectures bearable and interactive. Sometimes gave out donuts or cash to make a point. Extra credit is given for showing up and using an I clicker as well as for going to section and midterm/final taken open note online. He is so nice and supportive and responds to emails quick.

He is always really positive and seems like he actually wants to be there teaching you. The lectures aren't mandatory which is nice but he makes them interesting. He's always responded to emails quickly and seems understanding to whatever's going on and is ready to help

Honestly, he's the best professor I've ever had. He makes sure to make every lecture fun and special. Genuinely invested in your wellbeing and success, and really interesting to talk to. The homework is easy - there's not a lot of it and it takes minimal time. You can get up to 28 points of extra credit. Everyone should take his class!

overall, mike's great! he does 4 mini exams instead of a midterm which are online but still difficult- these are my biggest complaint but still better than a big exam. lectures are good and he makes it worth it to go in person. also love his extensive extra credit system! homework load was enough but not too much.

Mike was great! If you truly put in the work you can get a good grade, but the "mini-exams" were very difficult, and I was not at a capacity to truly put my 100% effort forth, hence why I didn't do very good. However, this has nothing to do with Mike, as he truly did all he could to prepare us, and I truly felt he cared a lot for each of us.

Mike is the best! Genuinely cares about students + passionate about the subject. Goes above and beyond by sending reminders when things aren't turned in. So welcoming during office hours. Lots of extra credit, open note tests, and lectures are manageable even if Econ is not your best subject. I wish I could have Mike as a professor for every class!

Mike is a good person however his lectures do not help prepare for the 4 "mini exams" throughout the term. These mini exams are more like full on midterms with over 20 questions struggling to finish within an hour each time with a few short answers that have wording that lead you to overthink and mess up the mini exams.

Urbanic cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. His grading setup is simple, each week there is an Inquisitive, Discussion post, and worksheet due so you can't really forget what is due each week. The mini-exams are weighted pretty heavily. He offers extra credit on homework and for participating in class and discussion section.
Made the class so fun. Gives a perfect amount of homework that you are forced to understand material but it isn't busy work. Literally the best

Mike was an amazing professor to take for the first term of college. Even though his lectures werent mandatory he made them so entertaining that I always wanted to go. Some of the concepts can be confusing but he explains things very well, and using great analogies to make you understand it. Really nice guy, highly recommend.

Fairly dry class, but if you keep up with all the assignments you'll do fine. Weekly discussion board and reading quizzes make up a good amount of your grade, with a midterm, final, and final report. I wouldn't use his activity sheets and would suggest taking your own notes if you take notes.

Mike is super funny and I always looked forward to his class. The homework is pretty light, but don't let how well you do on that determine your readiness for the midterm & final. STUDY HARD FOR THOSE EXAMS. The "textbook" was just a book we spent 2.5 weeks reading then wrote a short report on. He is easy to reach out to, helpful, & transparent.

Mike Urbancic is a great professor. As an Economics Major I took Econ 101 my first semester at UO. This is a great class after I move on to the 200 levels. Also he is so good there is so much extra-credit opportunities and there is a curve at the end of the semester. For example, my final grade was an 85.33% but the letter grade is a B+. Mike

I love Mike's teaching style, and his lectures were super helpful for understanding the content. All of the tests were open note which was super nice. There was a fair amount of homework, but the same format every week so it's easy to plan out your time. I would 100% take his class again and definitely recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best econ profs I have had. His lectures are fun and entertaining. He is very organized and makes econ fun. In EC202 I had 4 mini exams each worth 10% of your grade and a final that was 20%.

Mike is such an awesome guy! I'm never bored in lectures since he's constantly running around and is very entertaining and funny. We have about a disc board post, 5-7 pg HW sheet, and one inquisitive due each week so it's really not that hard. He also explains everything super well so it's not the hardest thing to understand.
Generally heavy workload but course is administered well and the difficulty of assignments and tests is reasonable. Amount of start-up work at the beginning of the term is excessive in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mike was a great professor for macroeconomics, he is clearly passionate about what he teaches. There were a lot of little things to do throughout the week which was sometimes bothersome but overall it gave a lot of opportunities to solidify the course concepts. I found tests to be a lot harder than hw but lots of easy points to help balance it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is a great professor and he cares heavily about economics and his students. He's also relatable and funny which helps. The exams are stupidly hard though and its a real stretch to get anything above a 90 on the exams.
Good professor who gives easy assignments, but the tests are quite difficult in comparison to everything else.

One of the best lecturers the UO has to offer and all-around a great guy. That said, his exams are next to impossible and it doesn't matter how much you study. Practice tests are utterly worthless and you can ace everything but if you get bad test grades, you won't pass with anything above a C.
this guys a boss

He is a good teacher and amazing to explain concepts and make them fun. But this class is weird, It is good to know about the probability, but it goes way too far to the point where I will never use that in my daily life. Come on

3 tests & they are beyond hard. You can't really study the lectures/the textbook to pass. You have to be able to break down the concepts & apply it. MC but also a couple of written questions. I had 100% on quizzes & problem sets so iClickers didn't help my grade. 70% of your grade is the tests. If you suck at tests (cumulative, no notes) don't take

Mike is friendly and it's clear that he wants his students to learn and do well in his class. There are reading quizzes before every class but they're easy and iClicker points can make up for lost quiz points. Gives clear lectures with real world examples. Has some office hours in EMU to be more accessible.

Mike is probably one of the most meh professors Ive experienced. Not totally awful and not totally amazing. Lectures were kinda boring but he always tried to make it enjoyable which was appreciated. Work load wasnt too tough. I recommend going to office hours with GEs because theyll work through all the problems on assignments with you.

Pretty straightforward class. Couple problem sets due throughout the term but not much HW. Weekly reading quizzes only 5pts each. Reading assignments can be a lot sometimes but manageable. If you read through his slides and go to class for iClicker you should be fine. Some people found the class difficult but I thought it wasn't too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First class I've ever dropped. Completely incompetent in giving a coherent lecture that accurately portrays what will be on the exams. Discussions are extremely dull and irrelevant, and a complete waste of time. Take this class online or with another professor cause Urbancic needs to seriously check himself
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most poorly organized 100 level classes currently offered by the UO. Exams make up about 70% of your grade, and they question how well you know very specific examples of homework assignments, rather than concepts presented within the class itself. Attendance is required for iclickers, but lecture is usually just wasted time. Take BA101
Pretty awesome dude who tries to make economics fun. He is always upbeat and energetic and it helped me stay engaged in the class the whole time.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Finals and Midterms are extremely difficult and Urbancic did a very poor job of preparing us for them. Find any other medium to take this course if you can. This class expects way more than just economics from you if you want to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Urbanic gives great lectures and the assignments and quizzes before each class is fairly easy as long as you read. The class is cumulative so you really have to understand the information for each chapter because they all add up. GO to lectures and discussions because the handouts are valuable for studying
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: pros - awesome guy, easy short quizzes before each lecture, he makes lectures interesting cons - the content on the tests were so much more harder and complicated than what we learn in class and in the readings. Like super hard. he did a curve on 2 of are 3 tests which helped a little, but overall the average for the class was pretty bad
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy, fun to talk to. The course is textbook heavy, so make sure you read, and also there is a quiz everyday online before class. The lectures are very powerpoint heavy, which I am not a fan of, BUT Mike makes up for it by being available to answer your questions and trying to make a boring subject as fun as interesting as you possible can.
Lectures are very basic compare to the content on the exams. Discussion class is also very basic compare to the content on the problem sets.

Mike is a great lecturer and he makes his lectures interesting so it's easy to pay attention. As an econ major I'm biased, but I found the coursework very interesting and easy to study. As long as you do the required reading and pay attention to the lectures it shouldn't be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike's lectures are very thorough and pretty entertaining for an econ class. There are online quizzes before every lectures, some of which cover an entire 20 page chapter. The midterm and final are a big piece of your grade, but it's doable, and Mike is very approachable when you have problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I like Mike as a teacher. He is fun and interesting. The tests were really hard, and we had very low class averages on the tests, one of which he did not curve. There are two quizzes a week on the reading, a problem set to do every few weeks, and lots of reading. When I talked to him about not getting one of my tests back, he was kind of rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took his econ101 class, which was kind of hard in some sections, but mostly easy. The class is very test heavy, with about 32% of your grade being the final, which seemed like a lot for a 101 class. His lectures are funny though, and the homework is easy. The essays are also pretty straightforward. Overall not a hard class to get a B in.
Does not cover material clearly. Tests are extremely difficult and the practice tests did not reflect what was on the actual exam in any shape or form. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Mike is an awesome person and professor. He is super laid back and a great teacher. His lectures are engaging and he had iClicker questions for extra credit. He was great for Econ 202, bit I hated Econ 101. Seriously do not take Econ 101 unless you have to. It wasn't because of his teaching, its just a bad class. But Mike is great himself!

My favorite professor. He is one of the many reasons I changed my major to economics last year. He wants his students to succeed and gives many extra credit opportunities in the form of clicker questions (up to 5% bonus credit). Would recommend
Mike is a great lecturer, every lecture was entertaining and interesting, extremely helpful in office hours and is extremely approachable

You're in for a treat if you have Mike for an Economics class. He condenses information into lectures well. There are quizzes before every lecture, but they're straightforward. Problem sets are great opportunities to learn material before tests. Lectures are fun and engaging. It's evident he cares deeply. Large amounts of extra credit. Awesome!

I 100% recommend Mike. He's a great professor and actually cares about teaching you. He always comes prepared to class. Attendance is not mandatory but I recommend going because you will actually learn. There is a chapter quiz before class but that's not even bad its only five questions. He's a funny guy, very approachable and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Mike's lectures are interesting, but not comprehensive enough. It's hard to cover everything in Principles of Macroeconomics in ten weeks. Discussion sections, worksheets, and lecture activity sheets are very helpful for the midterms. That's not to say the midterms are still extremely hard. Extra credit is provided via iClicker. Good professor.

Mike's a passionate teacher. He uses real world examples and lots of in-class volunteer participation to demonstrate concepts. He's also very accessible and easy to talk to outside of class. A good amount of test questions come from lectures and the readings he posts on Canvas.

Mike's lectures are the best that I've experienced in college because he's funny, he uses real world events to convey the material, and he keeps the class engaged. Academically very helpful and not too difficult.

Mike is one of the best professors I've ever had. He's enthusiastic about the material and genuinely cares.  The material wasn't too hard, as long as you pay attention in lectures and do the worksheets in class you'll be fine.  Game Theory is the 3rd class I'v taken with him, and it was by far my favorite. Would highly recommend!
Great prof

Great teacher, super funny. Makes it really clear what he expects and has quizzes before each class. VOLUNTEER! It's a chance to win money! One of the best teachers at U of O, study lectures and problem sets for exams, but overall an easy to pass class if you do the work, since iClicker points help you out.

Be prepared to do lots of problem sets and have reading and a quiz before every lecture. His lectures were fun to attend and you get a lot of information from them, but his tests were very word and confusing. If you attend class, his review sessions, and office hours you will do very well in this class.

Best teacher I've ever had at UofO. I thought the class was interesting and he made the concepts easy to understand. I would 100% take another class taught by him. He also makes the tests similar to practice problems so you know whats coming.

Basis economics. Going to class nets you extra credit via iclicker. Mike was a very cool guy and had great references in lecture. There was a large amount of reading per class. Unfortunately towards the week 4 mark economics went out the window and the Democratic Agenda took over. Talking about climate change, Brexit as well as "trigger warnings."
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: EC 330 is definitely the easiest econ class I've taken. Mike is one of my favorite professors. He makes the grading criteria extremely clear, offers extra credit for attending lecture and answering iClicker Q's, and is extremely helpful & accessible for office hours. I highly recommend this class!

I was nervous about taking Econ even though it's required for my major. He made the topics easy to understand through a variety of examples. Going to discussion really helped me grasp the topic and the math involved. He gives extra credit for attending class through iClicker questions.

My favorite Econ professor. Attendance isn't required, but you get extra credit for showing up and answering iclicker questions. Everything is very straight forward and easy and he makes lectures entertaining and worth going to!
Great lecture giver. Made Econ fun!

Get ready for some good jokes.  This guy is awesome and very knowledgeable of macroeconomics.  If you ever get a chance you need to ask him why he chose economics as his major and he is sure to crack a couple good ones.
Very rambly professor. Lectures were a little tortuous because the material was so dry, but thats not his fault. MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK or you will fail the course.

Mike was a great professor.  Econ is a boring subject, but it is clear he cares about the topic and wants his students to succeed.  He is constantly available for his students!  The midterms and final are tough, but go over the lectures and PLEASE GO TO DISCUSSION.  It is so useful.  Also all iclicker questions are counted as extra credit!

Urbancic is a knowledgeable professor. If you do the work- readings, homework and attend lecture, it is pretty easy and feasible to get an A. Sometimes his lectures can get a little long and seem boring, but overall very straightforward class.

Mike is one of the nicest professors I've had and he teaches incredibly well. Lectures are interesting and he graded our work within a day or two of turning it in. His explanations on material are easy to understand and he makes students want to participate.

Journalism majors, this is the Econ professor you want! Mike focusses on conceptual learning rather than on a lot of math, which makes the class doable and honestly more interesting. He's a great guy and has a good sense of humor. You get extra credit just for attending class, and tests aren't easy, but they're fair.

Mike assigns current-day readings that relate to Economics in a relatable way, and make the homework reading interesting and exciting. The lectures are informative, with great examples and his sense of humor makes them enjoyable and he even has the tendency to do some crazy (and fun) activities that get students involved.

Mike is an amazing professor and is very lively in his lectures. You can tell he knows a lot about what he is teaching and he is enthusiastic about it, as well. And, he is incredibly helpful in office hours! Would recommend him to anyone!! :-)

Listin carefully, RUN FOR YOUR LIFE!!! Believe me very tough exams, the questions from book, vedios, problem sets, sections, and slides. So you need to read a lot, wich takes a lot of time. I will say it again RUN FOR YOUR LIFE!  You will regret taking this class if he is your instructor.

Urbancic makes everything 10x more confusing than it needs to be. The material is not that complicated but he words his tests poorly which makes every question confusing. The homework is also worded poorly. Tests would be easy if he knew how to write a question properly. Lectures are also super boring.

Really good lecturer. Assigns 5 question multiple choice quizzes before each class which is actually really helpful because it forces you to read and you come into the lecture with a good understanding, then he fills in the holes. Would highly recommend taking a class taught by him. Also gives lots of chances for extra credit.
Class is hard, although he explains things well.

Mike is an amazing professor. Every time I've gone to office hours he's been extremely helpful and personable. Economics is a pretty dry subject but he helps out big time by giving practice exams before midterms and the final.

Smart dude, but his knowledge doesn't reflect well when he communicates during lecture. I found his lectures to be confusing & even random at times. Although his tests are difficult & take time to study for, he provides study guides and lecture slides online. Quizzes before every lecture are online & he gives a couple opportunies for extra credit

Mike is super engaging and tries to make a subject like economics as interactive as possible - however his tests are very hard. The tests require long short-answer portions and often contain material we've never learned. His students disrespect him as he never stands up for himself. Attendance is mandatory via iClickernotecards in lecture.

I've never met a professor who was more available and ready to help students. He offered more office hours than anyone I've heard of, and was always prompt with e-mail responses. The class was a little dry, but it catered to many different majors and couldn't go too much into the actual data. Terrific, dedicated professor.

Mike is a great guy who makes himself very available during the term. He made study guides, which are helpful. His classes are very dry, and most of the class is pretty frivolous. The class is pretty difficult and you need to stay on top of your stuff.

I only used the textbook to reference to every once in a while. Mike offered a lot of office hours and answered all my questions. He's funny and witty. Lectures are kinda boring but bearable. Not an easy course, ask for help, go to office hours, and stay on top of things.

I don't understand how this guy gets low ratings. Econ is NOT an easy subject, but Mike does the best he can with it. The material is relevant, his lectures are upbeat, and he always has extra office hours before tests. He goes a little fast on slides, but they're always online. Just show up most of the time, do the readings, and you'll be fine.

Honestly, he has to be one of the worst professors i've ever had. I never once walked out of that class feeling like I learned anything useful even after spending all class taking notes. I can't believe anyone in this class found him helpful. I think he made my interest in Economics go from low to lower. Major waste of class time and money, he was.
Terrible teacher, very pompous and makes things way more confusing than they need to be.
Best Econ professor ever! He knows what he's talking about and everything learned in class was relevant to the exams. Willing to help, and I learned a lot from him.
My favorite class this term. Honestly, this class has made me way more interested in economics. He's a fun teacher. Really easy class. Take it.

Mike is a grate professor. I am a journalism student, and an so excited that he is now teaching 202, all Journalism students Do Not Fear Econ! I took him for 330 in the summer; so I had him for 3 week. I look forward to taking more classes with him. His lectures were Cristal clear. Homework is hard but go to his office hours. Tests are fair.

I took his course in an extremely condensed 3 week term and it was awesome.  He is very helpful and is 100% willing to meet with you and go over any questions you have outside of lecture.  He is engaging and funny during class and keeps the topics interesting.  If you're going to take an Econ class I highly recommend him.
Very reasonable on homework and tests, very fun, intelligent, and makes class interesting. If you need a good econ teacher, this is the guy. I highly recommend him.

If you need to take an ECON class at the UO, this is the prof you need to take. Really gets students engage in lecture, even in a class size of 200+. Energetic, keeps material interesting, very clear about new material. Homework is simple, weekly quizzes are easy if you were in lecture, creates practice tests to help out studying a lot.
Cool guy, funny in lecture when he wants to be, and personally favorite professor on campus.
Good professor, interesting and funny during his lectures when he wants to be. Good orator with interesting things to say about economics. Makes complex topics fairly simple.
Wonderful class. Thank you Dr. Vallega-Neu!

Too much is going on in this course. She jumps around with assignments and in-class attendance. There is a near-pointless test and then an essay. Overall, be prepared to do three essays, several in-class assignments, reading guides, and an end-of-quarter test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extremely intelligent professor, expect a lot of reading.
