She's a good teacher. There were a few hilarious moments in class. Her class is well structured which is maybe why I liked it. If you do everything you'll be fine. Main thing would be to be aware of how she wants information presented in the take home exams, but if you learn the format it is not bad. I had a great GE so that might be part of it.

She genuinely enjoys teaching, but she has high expectations where we have to read and understand the reading the day prior when she talks about it in the lecture. Some of the concepts that are explained are simple and just a single lecture was enough for me to understand, but others have left me confused even after studying it for the finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Topic of class has no relation to real world aspects. lots of reading and too much pointless information gets crammed into lectures. Professor is harsh grader and teaches information that does not relate to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think she is so funny and genuinely one of the smartest people ive ever met. I think she is so knowledgable and is not afraid to not have an answer to strong philosophical questions.

Requires a LOT of reading, prof. has high standards but teaches well. She's always willing to answer questions, and clearly really cares about her job and what she's teaching, takes it very seriously. DONT take this class as an "easy A" I made that mistake... Def try to find a study friend in this class.
This professor allows zero technology.
Very nice lady with a charming accent. Always willing to answer questions to make sure you really understand the general ideas. Weekly readings with assignments but they all help towards the final.

Professor Vallega Neu teaches a very conceptual class that most certainly is not for everybody's taste. Concepts can be very abstract, and so if you don't like reading and hearing about super difficult abstract ideas, her classes will probably not be for you. Be ready to thoroughly engage with the readings Professor Vallega-Neu provides.

Overall this professor wasn't the best in my opinion. Took forever to grade exams & assignments. Never posted any study guides or practice exams. Frequently had questions on exams that did not reflect what was taught. Lectures were hard to comprehend, so you'll most likely end up teaching yourself most of the work.

No such thing as partial credit, very tough to understand what he is saying, and does not really explain much. Everything I learned was on my own, and every single class, he would lecture and write down complex math and not explain it very much at all, and then would expect mastery of it the next day. Tough grader.
Can be a little bit hard to understand at times but does a very in depth job of teaching all the material. Grades easily and most things are curved, homework wasn't bad and workload was light.

Arkady was not a good professor I would have been better off just reading the book and watching YouTube videos. He is also very difficult to reach outside of class I would have to email him three times in a row just to get a reply. Was snappy with students made it difficult to ask questions in class. Yet his grading system was his saving grace

This class is tough, and I don't think Arkady is the best fit to teach it. He's hard to understand and doesn't explain the material well—I relied on YouTube and the book. Grading and feedback are harsh, but he curves generously, which helps. He's funny and clearly knows his math, but that doesn't always translate into effective teaching.

Vaintrob is fine, but I think I definitely taught myself 95% of the course material. He has a thick accent, and his handwriting is really really difficult to read, so lectures were tough. He also doesn't really explain concepts... he will just write a problem on the board, solve it, and then move on. Other than that he was an easy grader so not bad

He is the best teacher I've had at UO. His lectures are very engaging and he encourages questions and clarifications. His quizes and exams are fair and they strongly cover the assigned homeworks and class material (Also gives generous curves). You can tell he is passionate about math/teaching and wants his students to succeed. I also took 342.

This class was quite challenging. Lectures are tough to follow and the writing on the board is tough to make sense of. Oddly, however, I would take this professor again. The tests were tough, but usually curved. He allows you to swap lowest midterm with the final. Overall, a generous grading structure made this class tolerable and less stressful.
Tough, but fair. One of the few professors who truly cares about what he teaches. Could explain the reason behind anything and passionately talk for hours about math.

After taking about a dozen classes in the math department here at UO, I can confidently say Prof Vaintrob is by far the worst instructor I've ever had. No textbook for reference, cold calls students during class, assigns very difficult HW with no help, and belittles his students when they ask questions. Avoid at all costs.

Worst professor I've ever had. He makes students feel intimidated to answer questions. He interrupts students when they do answer. His accent is very heavy, and it's usually nearly impossible to understand him since he usually mumbles. DO NOT TAKE HIM! Don't say I didn't warn you.

Vaintrob is a great prof! Super easy to talk to and ask questions, especially since he often asks the class questions. He often has funny/quirky sayings and stories. Exams/quizzes are fair. He does sometimes mumble and his boardwork/handwriting isn't the greatest, but asking for clarification helps. He also takes a long time returning graded work.

Vaintrob was difficult to understand, and his handwriting was unintelligible. Although he is knowledgeable, he cannot express what he wants to teach the students coherently. I had to resort to teaching myself out of the textbook instead of trying to learn from his lectures.

While Vaintrob is intelligent, he is a very poor professor . Thick accent, he complicates this by writing in illegible chalk and moving at an incredibly fast pace. Doesn't explain himself at all, answers questions poorly, not helpful in or out of class. I took this class in place of Merchant's because it was later, and it was a very bad mistake.

Arkady is a very difficult professor, but not in a normal way. He is difficult in that it can be almost impossible to learn from him. I've spent more time out of class teaching myself concepts, than in class because he does not explain well. Very hard to hear and does not explain concepts well. Just goes over examples a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Completely unintelligible. Handwriting is impossible to read. Shuts down students who ask questions. The class is totally disorganized and he does not keep you informed of upcoming events in class. The material was made infinitely more difficult by a lack of coherent instruction. Myriad errors on board, leave with incorrect notes, makes no sense.

Vaintrob is one of the best math professors I've learned from. His style of teaching is very methodical and everything feels planned, which makes the flow of content through the class very smooth. He is also very persistent and makes sure people understand before building on the ideas presented.

Sometimes intimidating, but never mean spirited.  There comes a time in higher mathematics where a student transitions from following endless examples to participating in the process of problem solving.  If this is the kind of math you have a passion for, then Arkady is recommended.  He strives to provide context for every subject.

Dr. Vaintrob is one of the rare professors who can explain advanced math concepts in a funny and intuitive way. That being said, I found his class to be quite disorganized. His proofs were often hand-wavy, his board work was abysmal, and he did not follow any textbook closely. He was helpful in office hour, though.
Great guy, good teacher, knows what he's talking about and gives lots of examples. However, I found it a bit tough to get in touch with him outside of class.
I loved him.  Great teacher.
Arkady was a really fun teacher but his accent and method of explaining things were a bit tough to follow.
This professor is brilliant, however he is extremely difficult to understand due to a heavy russian accent, so sit up front! Grading system is very reasonable and i had an awesome GTF, Peter Dolan!

The quizzes are so helpful, Great material, Awesome Professor. 
Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 60% of the grade was based on 8 MC quizzes that were poorly worded and confusing (as many as 8-10 possible answers, 20 minutes to complete, and a class average of D or less). He curves grades after the final. He's nice enough, but it was hard to get him to explain concepts w/out condescension or defensiveness. YouTube will be your friend.

Dr Mayr has an accent which definitely isnt an issue, however, sometimes he doesn't know the correct word to use and uses the wrong word and makes it confusing. He speaks to you as if you have a PhD and thinks things should be obvious. Extremely test heavy, bad communication. Hes a sweet man but a tough prof. Tests had an overall 60% passing rate
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy who can be funny. He has an accent but their is no trouble understanding what he says. Don't sit in the first section of COL 150 cause he's always walking around. His quiz questions come straight from the clicker questions. As long as you show up you should get an A. I enjoyed this class and learned some cool stuff.

Great teacher, knows his stuff. Has an accent so he is a bit hard to understand at times, but the class is pretty straightforward. Quizzes every two weeks which can be tricky but if you attend class you should fine. Many of the questions are based off of his iClicker questions. I didn't study much and pulled away with a B in his class.

This class is relatively easy as long as you attend lectures and write down all of the clicker questions. If you don't do this you will struggle. Don't buy the textbook! You'll never use it and 80-90% of the quizzes come from clicker questions and lecture topics. Ulrich's a great guy, sometimes difficult to understand, but not impossible.

Wonderful personality, interesting lectures. Exam questions can be a little wordy and hard to understand, but it's nothing the curve won't compensate for. Highly recommended, take him if you can. He definitely knows the material.

Second time taking his class. Hated him the first time, really like him the second. The difference is reading the text!!! He's very intelligent, a good teacher, but his powerpoints suck and his quizzes are awkwardly worded. Just make sure you write the clicker question answers down, b/c that ends up being 90% of the quizzes. He's pretty funny too
He's a really great professor who knows what he's talking about. However, his accent can make it difficult to understand sometimes, and his tests are not worded very clearly.

Dr. Mayr is a good instructor that KNOWS his stuff and is always able to answer questions in lecture and office hours. His accent enhances the lecture if anything. Read and attend class and it's not that hard of a course.

Nice guy, loves to talk and you can tell he knows a lot. It's just hard to understand his thick accent and his lectures are long and boring. The iClicker questions were helpful for tests and the curve definitely helped in the end.

I love Ulrich, I found his lectures to be very interesting, his tests were easy if you paid attention and although at times his accent is a little hard to understand, he is very helpful if you are having trouble and overall easy to understand.

Professor Mayer is a nice guy but gives extremely boring lectures! The tests are nearly impossible if you don't fully understand everything from lecture. Don't waste you're time ready the book because it doesn't help much. His tests are hard but overall the curve helps in the end. Not a terrible teacher but definitely not my first choice.
So hard to understand! I love psychology and usually pick it up quickly... Not with him.

Would not recommend. He is hard to understand sometimes with his accent, does not clearly explain things, and his powerpoints are AWFUL. You would learn more psychology by just reading the book rather than listening to him drone.

Mayr a.k.a. Pimp G is a fabulous professor who's class may be difficult for those who do not attend lecture. I thought he was straightforward and his tests were fairly easy. I recommend taking a Psychology class from him at least once in your lifetime :)

Mayr is an interesting guy. He had trouble keeping my attention but he definitely knew what he was talking about and seemed really passionate about psychology. He put funny jokes in his slides if you paid attention. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND reading the book and attending the lectures! You cannot succeed in this class without listening to his lectures!
He had said at the beginning of the class that there would be no final during finals week. Even though the last quiz of the class is the monday of finals week at 8 am. Thank you for the lies
really difficult tests. my class averages at 7 out of 15... he grades on a curve though which is helpful.
Professor Mayr is a fabulous teacher. Can't recommend him enough. And what's this about difficult tests? (Read the text, anyone?) An inspirational fellow. More professors like this, please!

You have to read the text to get an A in this class. I read the book, I got an A. Dr. Mayr is a very good teacher, answers email quickly and is always available for office hours. Most of the people who didn't do well in the class tried to pass by just attending lectures and reading the notes; not possible with this material. You must read the text.

Worst teacher I have ever had. Was foreign so hard to understand, tests were ridiculous, lectures were boring. I am a psych major and he made the subject extremely boring and makes me want to quit my major. He was unfair, and I DO NOT recommend him to anyone. Waste of a term waste of my time.

Ulrich is a super nice guy. His lectures are informational, which is nice cuz i hate sitting in a class full of tangents. His tests are fairly easy, and my psych201 was a fairly entertaining class considering i have no interest in the subject. I would definitely recommend him. And its doesnt hurt if you miss class really either.

Not a fan... He is a head of the psych. department and HAS to teach a class, he prefers to soley work on experiments/write, so he really doesn't care much about teaching and that sucks. I hated it, never went to lectures, did fine, but was not a fan. Such a dull class, made me wanna change my major.
He was okay. He does not know how to spell. You can hardly understand him. His tests though are easy because he curves them all. Even the final!
Tough class when you don't do reading. Hard to go to lecture when its so early in the morning and all you hear is what he reads off the slides. I do not recommend hkm

He was an average teacher. Gets his words mixed up every once in  a while, which could be either funny or annoying depending on the situation. He speaks English pretty well for the most part. Quizes are hard, but he curves them. Keep up with the reading or else.
very boring class because it's all pretty much the same thing every time and nothing really stands out

"Hilarious and German." His expectations are clear. If you go to class, do some light reading and study for midterms you'll be fine. He shoots kids down in class when they have wrong answers. It's hilarious.
Ulrich is hilarious and German.  His tests may be difficult, but he's easy on the eyes.
nice guy
Okay professor but never have I been so bored in a class.  Lectures are very similar to the text.
very quirky and intriguing prof.
No Comments
pretty easy; whoever says the quizzes are too hard obviously never bothered to read the book and pratice on blackboard. not too much gained from actually going to lecture except review of the text.

this guy sucks.  you can't understand a single thing he says but at least everything he goes over is in the book.  you don't need to attend class except to take the quizzes.  do the online quiz preparation thing, it helps.  your grade also depends on which gtf you have for lab.

Not very interesting. I recall a specific event where i left for work 20 minutes early, and he ****ed at me and lazer pointed me...I would reccomend choosing another teacher, its basically just straight from the text so if you want to a more profound understanding...go elsewhere

i thought the class wasnt bad, you have to keep up with the reading but if you do, the quizzes are easy.  i worked with ulrich in his lab and he is a pretty cool guy, hard to understand sometimes because hes german.
Horrible teacher. No point to study for quiz's because the questions are way too hard, but he curves the grade pretty good. If you want to learn anything from this class dont take this teacher.
he was cool, kind of hard to understand, but his weekly quizzes were easy if you went to lecture.
No Comments

ulrich is the shiznit!  i got an A+ in his class, then he gave me a job in his lab, he is really cool and my friends think he's hot i guess, and whenever i say "hey whats up?" he never knows what to say because he doesnt understand slang, it
german

I took Yosa for SPAN 201, 202, and 203 and absolutely love her. She is by far my favorite professor at UO and I looked forward to class everyday! She is so kind, passionate, intelligent and understanding. She inspired me to continue on and minor in Spanish. Her grading is very lenient and clear. Take a class with her!!!
I love Professor Vidal. Grades super lenient and is super kind and passionate about teaching Spanish! Going to class everyday and studying a little for the exams will get you an A easily.
She is very kind and understanding, and she grades so easily. Quizzes I should not have gotten an A on, I received an A despite plenty of marks on things I did wrong.
my favorite teacher at UO!! learning spanish is hard but Yosa really puts you at ease, and her feedback is great. Take spanish with her!!

Yosa is so lovely! She's a great Spanish prof because she's very patient & encouraging. She's also super passionate and knowledgeable about art and history (especially in Chile). I had her for 200-level Spanish, which is well-structured, as well as her 300-level art history-type course, which was more casual. Definitely take a class from Yosa!!

I loved having Yosa as a Spanish professor! She will push you to make sure you learn, but she's super friendly and will help when you're struggling, and I never felt discouraged by her even when I made mistakes. There was also homework due almost every day there was class, but they were online assignments and I could finish them really quickly.

Yosa is a great Spanish teacher, and you can easily tell how much she cares about everything she's teaching. I had her for 303, and it was clearly a curriculum based on her own interests. She gives really interesting lectures and there's a lot of class participation. Her canvas is super disorganized, but just regularly check her syllabus.
Yosa is my favorite Spanish teacher i've ever had! She was always so nice and caring, and never made people feel dumb if they didn't know something. Great professor!

I LOVE YOSA. She is one of those professors who genuinely care about their students and know that the grade they give you impacts you. She is also very encouraging and gives great feedback. When I finished SPAN 201, I wanted to drop my BA because I hated it so much, but then I had her, and now I show up to every class with confidence and a smile.

Yosa is the best teacher that I have had at UO. Took her for Span201, 202, and 203. Takes lots of time of feedback, and she focuses on being sure you are learning how to speak spanish, rather than trying to grill you on tests. While there are lots of exams, they are not hard and she is very flexible and helpful if you miss a test.

THE goat. Had her for 201, 202, and 203. Wouldn't take a Spanish class if it wasn't her. Bright personality and cares about her students. Also knowledgable and is passionate about the content. Feedback is great and she's a loose grader. Those two negative comments about Yosa are insane and also inaccurate. She's the goat. Take Yosa.

Yosa is by far my favorite professor I´ve had so far at UO. She is incredibly kind, and her passion for teaching makes her classes very engaging. She likes to cold call a lot, which can be a bit intimidating, but it´s clear she wants everyone to do well. If you get the chance to be in Yosa´s class, definitely take it!

Did not set up the students for success in the tests. The tests were often not relevant to Spanish learning rather a test on some sort of film. She hardly taught relevant useful information lecture. Overall not a great professor.

Goes above and beyond. Teaches practical aspects of Spanish like how to sound more authentic in addition to the course requirements. Good feedbacks on tests. She believes in you in a way rarely seen since elementary school. Very encouraging teacher.
I love her so so much this was one of my favorite classes of my college career. I am starting a Yosa Vidal fan club
I really love Yosa! She is a great teacher and lovely person and this has been my favorite Spanish class I've ever taken. Super fair grader and if you put in the work you'll do well.
Had the time of my life my first semester in Span 201. Collados' was a class to look forward to at 9am and I felt confident I could make it through the whole time because of her detailed feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great experience overall experience even thought the class is challenging. Learning outside of the class is the main part which can be difficult but rewarding
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The entirety of the Spanish 201 program is structured the same, but I feel Yosa really made this course beneficial to me. She spends extra time during lectures making sure the class actually comprehends the material. Textbook is expensive, but it is used through the 201/202/203 sequence.

Decent teacher, but really tough grader. If it says write 50 words, and you wrote 45, she will count the words and take points off. If it says talk for 5 minutes, and her stop watch says 3 minutes, that's 30% off. If she thinks your reading for an oral assignment, that's 30% off. And don't use google translate, she knows. Not as easy as the others.

Yossa is very supportive and her teaching style is great, she of course gives corrections but she also gives very positive feedback which made it easier to participate in class. She was so helpful and adjusted curriculum to fit the needs of the class when necessary. Plus she's so cute, you can't not like her.

Gives really good feedback on Blogs and Trabajo Escritos. She's learning English but makes it fun. Very patient with students and will go over even the small things with you. I really appreciated her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yossa is very nice and wants her students to understand the assignments. It was occasionally difficult to understand her as she is still learning English. All in all she's a good professor who makes the overly-structured 200-level class decent.
The best teacher I have ever had. Beautiful and funny and smart. Absolutely perfect.
Yossa was a great teacher.  Her class was definitely more interesting than other spanish classes at UO. She was very nice and helpful.
best spanish prof I've had so far.
she is a great teacher! very helpful, funny and makes coming to class fun.
No Comments
Very nice teacher. Young and pretty. Is still learning English.
Game theory is a tough subject, but Van Kolpin makes it really interesting and engaging if you are there to learn.

He really cares about his students, and he is sweet and receptive to questions. His lecture slides were kind of hard if you didn't read the material beforehand, and honestly it would be borderline unfeasible to do good on the exams without reading the book. Fair grader, and good study guides for the exams.
Would often get lost on his lecture slides because it just looks like a bunch of gibberish on the board. tests are kinda hard but gives easy homework and quizzes to help your grade.

Van cares about the students and teaching. Tests are of average difficulty and he gives a lot of practice exam material that reflects the problems you face in the exams. He's very fair and easy going. The slides are quite unhelpful (no concept hierarchy, too many words) and he does ramble frequently, but his attitude & friendliness make up for it

He rambles a lot, and is occasionally unclear on the board, but overall is a solid professor. He leaves the last part of class open for questions which you should take advantage of if you are struggling. He is also a very fair grader on exams.

(law econ) His notes on the board are EXTREMELY hard to follow. He takes too much time with jibberish in answering student questions. W/ that being said he still gives out great practice exams to outline what will be asked on real exams, so those are helpful, he isn't

He will spend a lot of time on topics he considers valuable. At times its quick and overwhelming, but great for the most part. Homework is difficult and requires time. Tests are well outlined ahead of time.
No Comments

Tori lectures make sense when you can rewatch them and pause and rewind. In class though it is straight gibberish. No one understands what's going on and she doesn't care that students are lost, she will acknowledge it and continue teaching. Exams are evilly written, expect averages in the high 60s. Lab carriers your grade so prioritize doing well.
The tests are unnecessarily hard and tricky; even if you know the content, you can slip up with her weird wording of questions.

Tori is nice and clearly very knowledgeable but can get lost in the details when lecturing. Her teaching style can be pretty boring but she does work through a lot of helpful practice problems. The HW is hard, but you can/should go to office hours with Laurel or a GE to work through it each week.

It is obvious Tori has a lot of knowledge on the subject she teaches. She tries her best to explain concepts in a way that is not patronizing but still informative. She's easy to understand if you pay attention in lecture. My only complaint is that Tori's exam questions can be wordy and difficult to understand.
tests suck for this class, try to take this class a diff term with an easier prof..

Tory has very high expectations and her exams are extremely hard. She goes into extreme detail in some things in lecture but glosses over others they end of being on exams. Shes very unhelpful in office hours and no matter how much time was put into studying for exams, it never seemed to match what was covered in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tory is a very dull, boring lecturer which makes it hard to focus in class. Exams are not a huge percent of your grade thankfully, and no study guide or practice exam is provided. LOTS of hw for this class, but its helpful to boost your grade. overall hard to learn in this class, feel like i have to teach myself everything

Tori's lectures are fast-paced and might leave you behind sometimes. But her careful course design and problem solving-based approach result in superb comprehension of the course material. Expectations are exceedingly clear, it's just a matter of putting in enough work to meet them. Overall one of the best professors I've ever had.

Tori teaches everything with the expectation that you already understand the basics. For some concepts its very straight forward. For others you will sit there and have no idea what she is talking about. She fails to take the time to explain basic concepts before going onto more complicated subjects.

Tory is a very intelligent professor, but you can definitely tell she only lectures because she has to in order to do research. She is nice, but she can be intimidating to approach and hard to follow. Definitely meet with GTFs as much as possible whenever you don't understand what is going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tori's lectures are really clear and easy-to-follow, and I thought that she made the material really interesting. Her tests are just about right difficulty-wise.
Lecture notes are posted online. They help explain topics that may appear to difficult or simple in lecture. Tori is a good, honest teacher.
The class is difficult and the concepts are hard to master. But Tory is helpful and approachable.  Her typed lecture notes are a must read.
GLBL 431 was a great class. Amazing guy, kind and understanding. Interesting topics. Would take again. Field assignments and final were easy to complete.

Vogel is a great professor, this would be a great class if the field assignments weren't so annoying. U have to write 1k words about a topic that could be explored in 500, so u end up rambling and going into excess detail that doesn't help. Grading is weirdly strict but doesn't explain why u dont get full points. also the final is fried.
Matthias is a goat. Great introduction to german.

Cool guy, interacted with students lots and made sure everyone knew what was going on. Super good on communication, did not make the class feel impossible but still felt like I learned a lot from the class.
lots of reading outside of class but if you just skim before class it was fine, quizzes were easy, loved hearing him talk
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took GER 221 but this wasn't an option on the survey. Vogel is a great professor and the class is enjoyable and not too hard. Pay attention in the lectures and do the assigned films/books and you'll get an A fr.

Vogel is a rly good teacher, gives many opportunities if you bomb a quiz to go to office hours to get more credit. Had for GER221 and is acc rly interesting if you are into learning about WWII. He is an easy grader, just make sure to read/watch all the media he assigns bc that will be on quizzes + midterm/final

I took postwar Germany 221,wasn't an option to select above.Really nice guy who cares a lot about his class. Interesting for the most part, do pay attention because we had a quiz almost every Wednesday. You have to watch German movies outside class and then are quizzed on them. No homework really accept for 3 papers spread out through the semester.
He is a great professor, the ARC class was just too much work for only 1 credit.
Professor Vogel is a very kind man. Loved the Global Engagement Arc -- some of the assignments are very confusing, but worth the learning in the end.

Matthias is very caring, engaging, and passionate. His lecturesYou definitely have to come to class prepared and having done the readings. Every class you answer questions about the readings in groups and turn those in for credit. Throughout the term you have to do two group presentations on the readings that usually end up being an hour each.

German for Business was a very easy class! Engaging and super friendly, quizzes and tests were graded very graciously. Had homework every other week, I'd say the most work I've done in this class is takes notes -- which were optional.

Would 100% recommend this class if you are wanting to learn german without it being a hassle.

I took Ger 221. There were quite a few readings/films, 2 essays, a few quizzes and group projects. This class isn't hard and the work is pretty manageable. The only thing is be prepared to sit for the entire class listening to him lecture. I did really like him and the class though so definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Excellent experience with German cinema

I'm a huge fan of Professor Vogel! I've interacted with him many times through the German department and in classes. He's very straightforward with assignments and grades, which can be intimidating. He assigns things for a reason and expects them to be done! With this in mind, he really knows his stuff and you can tell he wants you to succeed.

Matthias is an amazing Teacher. If you put in the effort to listen to his lectures and understand the readings all of his classes are fun and engaging. You can end up with an A just talking to him and participating in class. everything in papers and tests is based on what you read and talk about in class.

I took German cinema over the summer and LOVED it. Matthias really cares about his students and has very interesting lectures. The films are really good and the assignments are engaging. One of my favorite classes I have taken by far, and I hope to take one of his classes again.

If you ever have the chance to take a class from Professor Vogel, please do. I took this German cinema course from him, and had him as a substitute for German 101, and both times he was absolutely wonderful. He teaches to help you learn and understand, and really opens your mind to seeing things. 11/10.

The Global Engagement ARC class w Professor Vogel is interesting - I do recommend it. You have great guest speakers, good conversations, but few assignments, grades and deadlines are kinda unclear. You just have to be ok with going with the flow, not over stressing the class. Matthias is a great person! so initiate conversations fun with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Matthias is a gem of a professor. I have taken 3 classes of his. Unlike a lot of professors, Matthias is extremely knowledgeable AND excels at teaching. His classes are always enjoyable, although he does expect you to read a lot. Highly recommend.
Despite lot of reading homework, he is easily the best professor I have had at UO thus far!

Matthias is one of my favorite professors at the U of O. This class, while being one of the more reading intensive 200 level classes I have taken, manages to keep moving and not get bogged down. Each text truly brings something important to the realm of Holocaust narratives. He does not give busy work and the discussions are deep and engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Matthias is an amazing professor! I have take multiple classes with him including German Language, Voices of Dissent, German Culture and others. He really cares about his students and is very accessible. I cannot reccomend him enough. He is a great person and has written me recommendation letters for scholarships and jobs.

Matthias is an amazing professor! I have take multiple classes with him including German Language, Voices of Dissent, German Culture and others. He really cares about his students and is very accessible. I cannot reccomend him enough. He is a great person and has written me recommendation letters for scholarships and jobs. He is a great connection
Lots of reading, three papers, discussion and history quiz. Throughout lecture he  is engaged and small group discussions brake up lectures. Ifyou do the reading, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Even at 9 AM a fun class. Matthias makes it hard but if you need help he lets you text him for feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The worst person I have ever met in my whole life. If you are the international student, he won't understand your English even though everyone else can understand it. I went to the TLC to fix my grammar and he still doesn't understand my English.  If you don't speak or write like a native English speaker, don't take any of his class.

Matthias cares about his students and the material he teaches. There was way too much reading and lectures were so long because he just read off his notes. It was difficult for him to involve the class because many people don't do the readings because there are too many. The lectures were terrible.

This class was more stressful than it should've been. There is 1 quiz and 3 essays, and a lot of reading. His teaching and paper expectations are unclear. He goes on tangents where even the GTFs didn't understand what he was talking about. He tends to take the overly dramatic approach, even to the most irrelevant things, such as skipping class.

Only had one test and three essays. However, I wouldn't recommend this class because it was pretty unclear and overall a stressful experience. I felt like there was almost too much reading to keep up with, and confusing group work that he makes you present in front of the class. Overall a good person, but an intimidating professor.
Matthias is a great teacher who cares about his students. He is very enthusiastic about German, life, and basically everything and is an awesome guy. I would recommend any class he teaches.

Great teacher in general! He's willing to help you out if you ask. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable in German. It's great to have a professor who's fluent in the language you're studying. He knows a lot about the culture and is a great teacher in general!
Great teacher!
Great teacher.

TAKE THIS CLASS! I absolutely loved it. He is a fabulous professor who is very knowledgeable, eloquent, and interesting to listen to. He is such a nice person who is very willing to help you outside of class. The class is three papers and participation in discussion. The book are interesting and the videos are moving. I highly recommend this class!
Sometimes a little vague in his explanations and a bit disorganized, but otherwise always there for the students, fun and easy going.

Matthias is a good teacher. Sometimes his lectures move a little fast, but if you stay awake and take notes you should do fine. He is always willing to help people, and really cares about his students. I also liked how his class had no tests: it was all based off attendance, a couple short quizes, and 3 papers.

I've taken 2 classes with Matthias and gotten an A in both. He is a fantastic teacher and genuinely cares about his students, if you put an effort into the course. He is incredibly understanding with any personal issues you may have, and is accommodating even going far outside his syllabus rules. He also has a great sense of humor.
i thought he was a good teacher, very entertaining in class and friendly. i've taken a few classes w/him, he's sort of hard, but you do learn stuff. i'd recommend him.
great teacher!!!! learned alot and had fun!
Matthias makes every class fun and he is always prepared and totally helpful.
Very helpful and enthusiastic about teaching.  Always available and willing to help students outside of the class.

I loved matthias! i thought he was funny and was very knowledgeable on the subjects studied. however, hwk was not always clear, the syllabus was not always followed and we got behind in it....so the hwk or assignments were not always clear. He's good at emails and will help you in office hours.  I very much enjoyed GER 259 and his other courses
Mattias pretends to be a professor but he's NOT. He is only ABD. What a poser! He thinks he's so great, but really he is only interested in making himself look good.
He can even make German interesting... Dresses really classy every day

Matthias is very nice, very funny, and knows his stuff, obviously, but he is very flaky and sometimes no one knows what the homework is or has any idea what to expect on a test.  Just be very diligent about asking what's expected.
No Comments

His classes are by no means easy however you learn a lot in them. He is also very willing to help any student who asks and is very friendly. I enjoyed being in class and stressed over the tests but everything turned out good in the end.
Marty genuinely cares about students' success. If you make the effort to communicate with him, he will be very understanding.

Marty is awesome! While lectures can be boring at times he uses his own experience and with everyday examples to help students explore topics relating to social change. The class is very group work heavy which I personally enjoyed. Pick your group wisely! He is funny and allows you to have extensions if need be. Highly recommend this class!

Amazing professor made everything really easy if you communicate with him unlike other people here that are rating him majority of class is group work which can be fun if you got a good group that works and communicates I feel I've learned a lot and was able to take everything in 10/10 would recommend.

The class was relatively easy.  Pretty much every assignment is group work so if you do not like group work I would not recommend this class.  The overall class was pretty boring during the lectures it was very hard to pay attention for almost 2 hours.  Some of the material applies to the course but a good chunk of it is hard to connect back.

Great prof! The course was heavy on group projects and group work, which was nice as it made the workload more manageable. Prof. Wilde cares about his students and is open to help you improve if you ask! Enjoyed his class a lot!
Marty is a great professor who cares about his students!

He was very respectful, understanding, and an easy grader. Just like many other professors, attendance was mandatory. However, this class was disorganized and did not have a clear layout of what to expect but it was also his first time teaching this class so it is understandable. He made it clear that he was trying to improve it for the future.

Marty like is not an actual professor, hes changed the syllabus maybe 5 times and doesn't teach coherently. The class is fully group work and yet we have no time to work in groups in class time. All he talks about is how no one comes to class and resorts to playing tricks to get students to come. We should not be learning about proper nouns in law.

He believes everything he says is correct and anything a student says is incorrect even if it makes complete sense. I don't think one student in his class liked him. He also belives that this class is a weed out course and uses language like "if you continue in journalism" but his class really isnt that hard. The material in this class is great tho

Long boring lectures that you'll be penalized for missing, a lot of field work, and clear your schedule outside of class. Avoid him if you can. Grading is harsh and inconsistent, and your grade point will be destroyed by late submissions.

Professor is decent, but when it comes to the structure of the course sometimes it felt like he wanted one thing from and another. Class is a lot going out in the field, sometimes when you have an interesting idea, to him to doesn't. His grading from my view can be inconsistent, and felt like stressed tying to appeal to him then feeling comfortable

I don't think he's worth the time or cost. Nice guy, but a lot of his materials are outdated, and the way he teaches is confusing and ineffective. I definitely blame the SOJC program for making many professors look bad, and I believe it is designed to fail them, but with Yurman it was pretty bad. Take it if you have to, but avoid it if you can.

Will Yurman has a unique teaching style. Get ready to sit in mind-numbing lectures. Also, every assignment is due at Sunday's at 10 pm. No exceptions, if it's late, one letter grade off. His feedback is unhelpful and ends up contradicting the techniques you'd learn from class. I didn't learn anything useful, typical SOJC. AVOID THIS CLASS

Will Yurman is the unskippable cutscene of teachers at the SOJC. His content is super outdated (lots of listening to mind-numbing NPR stories). His feedback will contradict previous remarks so much to the point where you genuinely won't understand what he expects of you. The class feels like a chore that you will be counting down the days to end.

JCOM Writing as a Practice: I do not recommend. Longest two hours of my life and lectures were repetitive. He contradicts himself when giving feedback and is very confusing. If I went into office hours for help I left more confused than before. He is nice and clearly enjoys journalism, but has no passion for being a professor.

I had Will for JCOM 203 and he was great. Attendance is required and his feedback can be a little harsh. He gives you a lot of feedback on every assignment and truly cares about his students. He always responds to emails and is available to meet. He is a smart and caring teacher and always helps his students. Would take again.
