The teacher does not explain the class concepts well. The tests and quizzes are a lot harder than the in class problems. A lot of answer keys had the wrong answers.

Xuanyu is probably one of the most unorganized instructors I have ever had. Practice sets and in class examples often have typos or are completely incorrect, quizzes are completely unpredictable in terms of difficulty, the lectures can be hard to follow due to her speed, and she overall looks way in over her head. Do not take her finance course.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard quizzes and doesn't explain things well. Uses excel to write out the examples rather than using the whiteboard and actually identifying the pieces of a problem. Not a good instructor and shouldn't be teaching this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xuanyu gives extremely difficult quizzes on new information that wasn't taught well. She gives answers to homework that are incorrect and extremely misleading to the whole class. Absolutely do not take her course. She's unorganized and never teaches class content in a way where information is applicable to quizzes and exams
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xuanyu is nice but far too specialized in her field to be a professor. The weekly problem sets are helpful but the quizzes are 100x harder than the problem sets. I have never been in a classroom where every student collectively deep sighs right when they read the first quiz question because they have never seen the content before. It's defeating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xanyu decided that she a PHD student is better than all other finance professors at this University and runs her class in an entirely different format than all of the other courses. With high value incredibly difficult quizzes.  On top of confusing unhelpful lectures with no homework to reference. Do Not Take.

She's very lovely and super helpful. If confused in class you can always go to her and she'll be so much help. Even if you don't regularly attend the class it's easy to pass since the subject matter is pretty easy even if Linguistics isn't your major.

Just a very hard to listen to lecture. Nothing to engage the students and often caused more confusion in lecture than I had before. Just read the book. Or don’t take this class is my recommendation. Especially if you don’t want to go into this field because the subject matter is awful.

She just read off her slides and went over them too fast. Overall she's not the best at teaching, and the class was "difficult" for a 100-level with her. Many quizzes, weekly online tutorials, and reading the book to teach yourself concepts  crucial. Xuan is also not the best at replying to messages fast. She's an okay prof. Extra credit offered!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most of your grade is based on your midterms and final. You don't even need to do the homework if you do the tests well because they are so highly graded. Grades don't go in for worksheets/hw until after the midterms, so you have no clue whether you are answering the questions right or not. I do not recommend taking this class.

Real analysis is a tough course, but Prof. Xu makes it at least bearable. He is a great lecturer and is helpful in office hours if you get confused (which is likely) Really emphasized the concept of limit and was def heavy. His TA was extremely tough grading HW (class avg. was a D or F on most), but he curved test and quiz grades to help you pass.
A terrible professor. his exam and quiz are really hard. Although he is a smart guy, he is unhelpful

He is really knowledgable and helpful. There are weekly quizzes and homework, but this is a really useful way to study for the exams. He also is spending a week and a half reviewing everything from the term, because he wants to make sure students really understand the material.

He was very helpful when you went to office hours.  The homework almost always had answers to the questions so you knew if you were doing the problem correctly. His handwriting was pretty bad, but he always said what he was writing, and would clarify anything if asked. A little intimidating at first, but very approachable.

Most people have complained about this professors english I noted from other comments, but I did not find that to be that big of an issue, The class is hard no matter you is teaching it. The instructor is enthused but is not very helpful at office hours. Once he told me my problem was I didn't understand Taylor series well enough and didn't help me

His lectures were little too fast, but they're usually clear and organized (and his accent didn't bother me at all). He could have been a bit more helpful on homework, instead of telling us to read the text. Analysis is a hard class, and I certainly wasn't mature enough to take this class, but if you have that maturity, you'll learn a lot from him.
VERY HARD to understand.  Speaks very broken english.  He also skips steps in math.  That's not a good combination for teaching a calculus class... my advice: get another teacher for math.
As long as your mind is at least comparable to  that of the average simian, you will find this class enjoyable, and not at all difficult to pass.

Super hard class.  Instructor difficult to follow, but does his best.  Hard to understand at first.  Proofs suck anyways!  Curves grades; if you can stick the class out to the end, you will most likely pass (big "if", though).
If you can understand a word he says maybe you will have a chance. Come on  you have been in this country for years at least you can learn our language.

He has contempt for his students.  Easy class but he put a lot of the grade on homework and does NOT curve tests.  He only maybe will curve the whole class.  That is great if you did badly but for the average slacker that gets A+ test grades it is pain.
He is a really nice guy and although his lectures can slow down at times I still think this class is worth taking. There is a weekly essay but the grading is very relaxed.

If you need an easy class do this one. Your grade is an open-note canvas quiz and a 500-word essay, both due on Saturday each week, and both take under an hour max. The discussions are trash but its fine. Xiaobo is super nice, and although his accent is impossible to understand and his lectures put half the class to sleep, he is still the GOAT.

I am honestly shocked by the reviews because I did not find Xiaobo to be very helpful at all. In office hours and over email he would be a tad condescending like it is a huge interruption to his day to answer clarifying questions, hence why I've only ever emailed him once or attended one office hour session. Easy class however!

Xiaobo is the best professor I had this term. He is so nice and seems like a great guy. class is pretty easy, just have to do the weekly quizzes and map interpts. Grading is light, lecture can be a bit boring but he tries to make it interesting with music at the start and during a break and discuss with the person next to you questions.

Grade mostly depends on weekly quizzes and map interpretation essays, plus a museum visit essay and a final paper. The weekly essays aren't graded strictly on formatting, just read the rubric. Readings are dense. He made lectures more engaging with slido and group work. Good professor overall. If you find geography interesting you'll like it.

Xiaobo is such a fun professor, the classes aren't too difficult, but they are interesting because he likes to have participation in the class and his got this website that he uses for us to put in answers which can be anything. I fw with Xiaobo heavy.

This was a very attainable class. Professor Su does spend a lot of time lecturing and sometimes it can be  confusing but between the discussion and office hours, it's easy. There is a wiki page every 2 weeks but they were kind of fun to learn more about a topic you like as well as two discussion posts every week which were summarizing the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Su is nice, but his teaching style is not conducive to meaningful learning. The content was very elementary in this course, and it can hard to pay attention in lecture because its monotony. His accent ISN'T a problem, but he often talks in circles and loses his audience. He was slow to reply to email and his syllabus had many missing elements.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xiaobo is my favorite professor. He is so cute and truly cares about what he's teaching. The biggest impact on your grade is the weekly quizzes and the 4 wiki pages. He provides an example at the beginning of of the year and if you stick to that format you are good for the wiki page. Quizzes are open note but they are somehow still difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Xiaobo is such a caring professor. Truly one of the best I've had at UO. He is extremely understanding and is so sweet. He really values participation but it was easy because of how interesting the class was. Assignments were fun to do and he gives credit if you showed you put in the effort by simply doing the assignment.

Xiaobo is one of the most caring professors I've had. Truly wants you to learn and get a good grade in his class, and he obviously loves his job. Very personable and tries to make a sometimes boring subject interesting.

Xiaobo is probably my favourite professor that I had this term. His lectures can be a bit boring at times, but he does try to engage you by having "music time" where he plays a song recommended by a student or "map time" where you can share a map that is related to the lecture topic for very easy participation credit. Overall, he is a good dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I can't believe this is supposed to be an upper division class. It is the most basic topics of society that only goes to surface level. Also, the grading is all over the place with inconsistencies. Somehow even though I was there more often than half the class, I'm getting a below average grade on my attendance? How does that make any sense?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can't believe how much I hated this course. Lectures were incredibly boring and monotonous. There are only a few assignments throughout the term and your grade mostly relies on the four pop quizzes that are given. And worst of all, nothing is passed out to help study for the midterm or final exams. Overall, I'd avoid this class like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. Very good lectures very approachable and laid back. keep up on the readings and you will not have a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I can't get over how difficult it is to understand him. I thought I would get used to his accent, but I honestly didn't have a clue what he was saying 80% of the time.  Class is boring and a waste of time. I love geography, but this class could have ruined the subject for me if I hadn't take other classes before. He also never replies to emails...

Xiaobo is hard to understand but even if you cut through the accent often times he is still talking in circles. The lectures are on subject matter that any college student should consider common sense. This class was the easiest 300 level that I have and probably will take, as well as the most boring and worthless. He does try but it's not enough

This class is basically intro to sociology, you can't understand anything he says and he generalizes everything. When students question his claims he acts like they are ignorant and moves on. Told me I was getting an A- in the class and somehow my grade is B, emailed him and he said he'd change it but yet nothing. Useless class, avoid it.

Really nice and funny guy. Readings suck but you can get by with skimming. I enjoyed the topics and assignments. It is a little difficult to understand him at first because he is Chinese and speaks with an accent.

Easy class for a 300 level. Doing all the reading is not at all necessary if you are reasonably intelligent and come to class. I kept mistaking this for a sociology class when it was a geography class though. Slightly disappointing. Also disappointing was the majority of the material was centered around American society only.
Hard to understand him sometimes as he is Asian. Class was fun and interesting and made it entertaining with a variety of teaching methods and activities.
He is just not a good teacher. He has no idea what he is doing and is genuinely corrected every single lecture. If you can avoid him, save yourself the frustration.

He's too smart and can't teach from an undergraduate level. Intro to proof but had a hard time explaining proofs for an intro class. He didn't structure the term well and got lost in his own schedule and changed the course schedule frequently.

232 with him is not very hard if you go to lectures, I was a dumbass and barely ever went to lecture and I struggled but thankfully was able to get an A because I read the recommended textbook and reviewed the hws before tests. He also does the lectures on a chalkboard so have fun being that kid that asks others for lecture notes 24/7 (aka me)

Lectures are amazing. Hard HW questions which make you think, but it's good practice. Very friendly, and very accommodating. However, HW times were a little sporadic (HW was given late sometimes but due date was never rushed) and he wasn't on top of things as I would have liked. Exams were take home, so more or less like HW questions.

Ben Young was the best experience I've had personally in the UO math department. He gave out good study material before tests, and we worked on helpful worksheets. The WebWork was often tedious and not all that helpful, but his tests are straightforward. Students also get rewarded for attending lectures, and he gave out a ton of extra credit points

Nice guy but seems like hes still figuring things out. Made some unpopular decisions regarding hw but really wasnt that big of a deal. Makes some mistakes during lectures but much better with explanations during office hours. I highly recommend going to office hours with any math class (saved my ass for tests) Overall thought he did a decent job

Benjamin Young was an interesting professor. He was a really nice guy but he made a lot of mistakes during the lectures, which made him fumble more. His tests are difficult but going to class is a must or you'll get lost really fast. Webwork 3 times a week, but only 5 probs. Worksheets every week to. I dont think he was a great instructor overall

Professor Young is a super nice guy, and very willing to help during office hours. His tests are pretty challenging and he focuses a lot on abstract concepts and proofs, but other than that his class was great and he's a fabulous professor.

He was useless in helping during office hours. He also wasn't very accommodating for students with disabilities. It was bad to the point where it got attention from Accessible Education and also my academic adviser, who even stated that he gave me bad advice on certain accommodations that I had a right to have.

After taking this class, everyone in the class is switching majors. He has poor time management, we spent the last few classes going over material from the whole term even though no one knew what he was talking about.

Never taking any of his classes again. We took discrete math, which is required for all computer science majors and math majors. After this class, my entire friend network in the class is switching majors. He has poor time management, we spent the last 5 classes speeding through material and he snapped if you didn't understand something.

This guy is the man. He is very smart, and understands the material well which allows him to teach it well. I took him for Discrete Math, which is actually connected to his research so he cares about it. He has a knack for making it interesting. Great professor, definitely recommend. Tests are hard though.

Great math professors are so rare, but Ben Young is truly one of the best I've ever had. He's very polite, patient, and able to explain concepts many different ways to accommodate students. He used a neat note-taking program on his tablet so all class notes were available on BB. Tests and homework were hard, but the class was quite interesting.
My favorite teacher and class ever!

Amazing prof! Very kind, intelligent, and supportive. Taking Neuroanatomy - super interesting class with an extremely fun lab. She prepares students for lecture exams quite well. Lab is difficult but rewarding. Love her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Made anatomy and physiology easy to understand with clear slide layout and extra time spend in lecture discussing the topics. Friendly and engaging, includes important topics in the class that are much needed to be discussed. Exams are medium-level difficulty, but if you study lecture material and go over quizzes you should be fine

TAKE ONLINE HPHY211! It was so easy and so awesome, the class is asynchronous, and the assignments for the whole term are posted day 1, so just get them done by your deadlines and you're golden. In-person oral exams were super helpful, and the test averages were always fine, there's so many office hours if you need them. Top 5 class I've taken fs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yasen's slides were clear with consistent formatting, would block out days in the term to dedicate lots of time to difficult concepts. She was also consistently at her office hours answering questions. Study from day one, trying to catch up when tests come will be difficult.

HPHY211. Professor Yasen was a clear lecturer and took time in class to actively engage students and answer their questions. Course requires a decent amount of preparation outside of class but lectures are simple and easy to follow along with. Attendance policy is strict but allows for some absences.

Extremely egotistical about her supposed subject matter knowledge. Has no respect or empathy towards students and makes no effort to teach as she reads off a slideshow every lecture that she didn't even write. Very passive aggressive. I believe all the positive reviews on this site are written by herself. I highly recommend Robin Hopkins instead.

Lectures were great, exams were very fair. Easily accessible through teams as needed. Alia is a strict professor; sticks closely to UO/department guidelines, she outlines this in syllabus and is transparent about it at the beginning of the term, doesn't play games or try to switch up on you. Honestly a breath of fresh air compared to Jon.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alia is possibly the most self centered teacher in existence. In both HPHY 212 and 211 she has a history of accusing students for cheating and then threatening to report them to the dean if they try to stand up for themselves. Alia also sets extremely strict grading and attendance policies which she claims the UO forced her to put in place.

Dr. Yasen is an incredible professor. She is so easy to work with and learn from and possibly one of the best professors at UO. Her lectures and grading are super clear and helpful in the long run. I'd recommend her to anyone that has to take a HPHY course. She's who made me enjoy my major again!

Get ready to hear "mhmm" every 3 words, treated like a classroom of toddlers and listening to her talk about her previous researching job 24/7. Hardest part of the class is forcing yourself to go to lecture as she has insane attendance points. Best of luck.

Best professor I've had at UO so far! It helps that I love the subject but I found the lectures to be really engaging and interesting, the slides are well written and are super easy to understand and take notes on. It's also very clear what's going to be on the exams and what you'll need to study for, which makes it a lot less stressful.

If you know Robin Hopkins, Alia teaches the same as Robin but carbon copy that over to anatomy. Super nice, and explains things clearly but not to the extent of Jon. Lecture slides were near perfect to what you needed to know for the exams. The exams were super fair game. One of the best instructors at UO by far.

Dr. Yasen is definitely the most helpful hphy professor I've had so far at UO. Her lectures are thorough and she always presents content in a way that is clear and makes sense. She is very good with answering all questions and connecting them in engaging ways to course material. Clear and consistent with grading and course policies from day one.

One of the most organized professors I've had at UO. I always knew what was expected of me for HW. She makes things easy to understand and encourages in-class discussion and questions. She can be a little intense sometimes with how rigorous some policies are but overall if you show up and put in effort the class goes fluidly.

I've had her twice for two different classes. This teacher has never once failed to falsely report students of cheating as well as targeting students who raise suspicions about the lost points. Her ENTIRE course is run by students and GEs she doesn't even write her own lecture slides or grade her own material. Expect threats of reporting you todean

Alia was maybe my favorite Human Physiology professor I've had at the UO. Her lectures were extremely fluid and very easy to follow. Her demonstration of knowledge is impressive. She made very complicated pathways and concepts easily digestible. Highly recommend taking any course with her.

Would take her if you can learn the material outside of the class. Work load is pretty light. Tests align with material taught. HW: 6-9 pages (whole week) but each has max 3 questions on it. Weekly quizzes, reading assignments (really easy), tests are not tremendously challenging, practice exams, flexible "office hours", kind, helpful.

Discrete Math is a difficult class in general, but Arya is good at teaching many ways to understand how to solve a given problem. Taking the time to read the textbook is highly recommended and if you can help it, try not to miss class. It's not mandatory, but you will be behind if you do not show up, even if material is confusing the first time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THE BEST!!! She was my TA my first year and I still go to her office hours, just for help. She is so patient, and offers to explain difficult concepts in multiple ways until you understand. She's hilarious and actually cares about her students' comprehension.

Arya was such a kind educator! Some basic coding applications introduced. Extra credit given out on exams. 
Concepts could be explained more clearly, but that's just the nature of the calc3 beast. Canvas feedback was eh, so utilize office hours. There's a free textbook, and I watched lots of YT to keep up. Class gets much harder around week 7.

Arya is very kind, caring, and funny. While the teaching was decent, the grading was very unclear and frustrating as the questions on homework (though there wasn't too much of it) were much harder than the practice we would do in class and what would be on quizzes/tests, making actual learning a challenge. Using outside resources is a must.
If you want whats best for yourself, you would take her

Very kind (probably the kindest professor in the math department), cares about students, and helpful during office hours. She will meet outside if her times don't work for you. If I could take another course with her I would 100%.

Arya is so incredibly kind and all around a good professor. Her style of lecturing is occasionally difficult to follow but she's more than happy to answer any questions. OFFICE HOURS ARE A MUST!! She is so so so helpful in her office hours and will take time to patiently explain to you any concept you don't understand. She's funny too!

Arya made math more enjoyable for me. Her lectures can be a bit disorganized, but she is very accommodating and kind, you can tell she is truly passionate about math! Office hours are a must if you take her class, she is very helpful and you will learn better by attending them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very accommodating and flexible. Will let you do what you want (with a reason) as long as you do the assignments at some point. Great drawings, and wasn't too fast paced despite being a summer course.

Arya is an EXTREMELY kind, accommodating, and caring lady. She draws great pictures, which are good for some of the tricky visualization aspects of Calc II. However, her ability to actually explain things is poor. This made tests/quizzes very difficult, and her review sessions/materials didn't rlly end up helping me on the tests either.

Ms. Yae is one of the better teachers in the department and I would highly recommend her. Her lectures focus on the important topics for the class and she is willing to further explain problems/concepts or meet up outside of class. Homework was done via Webwork, with the quizzes and exams being more challenging but curves given when necessary.
I did not learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found Ms. Yae to be very kind and willing to explain concepts and answer questions both in class and regarding homework. However, I struggled with her teaching style, which felt a bit disorganized and unpolished. I would recommend her to those with an intuitive grasp of math and an interest in a deeper understanding, but not otherwise.

Arya really cares that you know the material and is clear on her expectations. She's super easy to get ahold of and her tests are always fair with no surprises. The homework and the quizzes are probably the hardest part of the class; just go to office hours and ask questions - she's always happy to help and will often steer you in the right path.

Did a very poor job of communicating the information to the class, did not curve anything despite the fact the majority of the class failed the midterms. Often made mistakes when doing problems on the board and assigned problems that she couldn't solve herself. DO NOT TAKE!!

Dr. Yang is very nice and knowledgeable, but not a very engaging lecturer (they are a slog). She can give feedback ahead of the due date, then you can resubmit by the due date which is very useful. She is pretty responsive to emails. Get a head start on the 2nd project because it's very tedious. Readings can be skimmed for the participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice person, terrible teacher. Does not know how to teach and every class moves at a slow pace that feels so repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super sweet to talk to and very interesting class but her lectures and slides were incredibly long and rambling and she never once responded to my emails. The assignments were also very unclear and confusing.

This professor doesn't respond to emails. I emailed at least twice a week for the eleven week I had her as a professor and did not get a single reply. Doesn't show up to zoom meetings. All of her instructions are difficult to understand from either being horribly misspelled or missing steps.
Asynch class. unclear instructions. send help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was my least favorite class I've taken at UO. It was my first PPPM class and def my last. Yizhao would never answer emails, would grade hard, and was terrible at explaining assignments. She also waited to grade most work until the day before grades were due on duckweb. Would not recommend if you are just taking for major/minor elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took PPPM 440 and she made me hate the subject I love. Her lectures are hard to follow and she will never answer an email. There were many group projects that were unorganized and will completely mess up your grade. I tried to contact her for 2 weeks and she never answered any of my emails. I recommend never taking a class from her.

I took Yizaho's GIS class, but I was taught by a secondary professor. Yizhao's class is not organized well. Tough to get in touch with emails about missing material/grades. Her lecture recordings are very low quality and tough to understand. GIS was a fun application to learn, and a good skill to have but had to learn a lot on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took PPPM442 during COVID. Dr. Yang's lecture slides are only text, incredibly hard to read, and she speaks so softly it can be difficult to understand what she's saying. She takes FOREVER to grade, I am talking like do not expect assignments that are due in Jan to be graded before March or until the VERY END of the term. Would not recommend :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yang seems like a nice person overall, but as a professor she's not the best. She takes 5+ weeks to grade assignments, and provides very minimal feedback. She also speaks very quietly in lectures and does not provide engaging material. She will not respond to emails. If you have questions, it's better if you ask them in person.

Professor Yang seems like a very nice person. However, she is very bad at teaching. She is way to quiet and does not make the topic interesting. Large amount of text on slides but goes through them too quickly. Never responds to her email and does not have clear instructions for her assignments. You will be frustrated by her constantly. Do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super chill and easy grader, felt bad for him though as nobody really participated in class.

I would say that Professor Endalew was a very easy grader; he only gave two major assignments, and they were easy to complete. I was able to get most of my assignments done days in advance. Very low stress. He's very soft-spoken, but in my opinion, it's not a big problem. I would definitely take this class again with him.

(Took WR121, wasn't an option on here)
Prof. Endalew is super sweet and is clearly passionate about writing/literature. The class was super, super easy so you're not going to have a very hard time getting a good grade. You only really have two big assignments which are both essays, but there's little assignments here and there. Lovely overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Endalew is kind and considerate to his students. He makes effort to make the readings and the class engaging, but sometimes there is too much information. Overall, one can tell he knows his material well and def recommend!

Professor Endalew doesn't seem to be a confident lecturer; he tends to mumble and trail off. Lectures tend to get into the geopolitical history of Zimbabwe more than literary compositions of African texts. Despite this, the class was extremely easy. I didn't read either of the assigned novels and passed with a high A.

I took Prof. Endalew for Colt 101, his lectures are very long; however, the work was not bad. We learned about African folklore, you could tell he is very passionate about his teachings. He was also nice and helpful, and it was easy to get an A in the class. He cares about his students, just talks a lot. Overall good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took COLT 211 and wouldn't recommend him. Does not facilitate class engagement well, very soft spoken, don't feel like I gained much from the class. Lots of reading (a novel almost every week), and the way it's broken up in the syllabus does not match how he teaches it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There were only 6 homework assignments worth a total of 58 points, the midterm worth 100, and the final worth 100...so if you do poorly on the tests, you have absolutely no cushion. I think the final grade was curved, though, which was nice. Jane is difficult to understand and she talks very fast. The way she solves the math is also very confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, but not the best at teaching. Her methods are confusing and she just writes equations all over the chalkboard. She is extremely approachable, and I highly recommend you go to her office hours to understand the content a bit better.

She was a very chill grader which was nice because the content is a bit complicated. Grades mostly on work and less on the correct answer. She's super nice and clearly very confident in what she's teaching which can be a bit hard at times. She is so confident however, that she moves very quickly and isn't the best at elaborating.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is extremely caring and always eager to help, especially if you meet with her in office hours. She provides great in-class examples and there's lots of opportunities to practice the content in class. The course is structured well and she grades the tests and quizzes very fairly.

Professor is very nice and always willing to help. The class had essentially no homework which was nice, but it left me very unprepared for exams. She gives a lot of partial credit which is also helpful. Exams aren't similar to in class examples, so it was hard to prepare. Super kind professor, but the class structure is hard to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would recommend taking FIN316 with Jane if you can. She is very approachable and always willing to help out. It is math heavy, but she makes it easy to understand and does lots of practice problems. She is lenient with partial credit on quizzes and exams as long as you show effort and understanding. If you show up to class you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jane is a wonderful professor who cares a lot about her students and their learning. The course is laid out well with very little homework and she gives lots of partial points on quizzes and exams. The content is very math based, but Jane does a great job breaking down the formulas so we can understand them. I would highly recommend this professor!
Easy A. Jane is awesome. Learned a lot from her class.

Don't be afraid of Jane's class. I was in her fall term FIN316 class. Showing up and giving 70% effort was all I needed to get an A. Straightforward midterm, even MORE straightforward final, with a decent weight on homework. It's really not that bad if you put the effort it.

To preface: I'm an A student and a teacher's pet. I love school. Total nerd. 

Great course, horrific teaching. Like the other 1 star review said, we spent first few weeks of fall term explaining to her how to do your job, ie, explain when someone gets a math problem wrong. It's not an interpretive class, it's a calc class. Accuracy is key.
She is a really kind and caring professor, very enthusiastic and full of energy. Her explanations make the material easy to understand, and she's always willing to help. I recommend taking her class!

We spent the first few weeks of the term trying to teach her how to do her job. She doesn't explain example problems or literally anything. Went thru the first 8 topics of 17 in 2 weeks. I know nothing from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Asmatey was absolutely wonderful to have as an honors professor. She is so passionate and full of knowledge and resources, and I highly recommend taking her classes. I feel like I learned so much from her. I took HC231 Medicine Health & Storytelling, which was incredible. I also highly recommend this class for any pre-med/pre-health students.

She is an amazing professor and a truly great person as well. Even if you are not pre-health, I highly recommend the class because she really cares about her students and helping them become compassionate human beings. The environment of her class is great, and she encourages students to participate and get to know one another.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Provides good feedback, is very understanding, and clearly really cares about all her students. The class is engaging and interesting, really well thought out and organized.
I could not recommend a class more than this one!
She is incredible. An definitely A is in every one of her students' reaches, you just have to put in the work and show her that you care.
Super duper chill and very understanding. You could tell that she is truly passionate about the subjects she is teaching.
she is a god-send.

I feel much more prepared for my thesis and confident in it after taking this class. It's so clear that Yalda wants her students to succeed and the class is literally set up for that, some assignments are meeting with advisors and a person in your career field of interest. The class is easy and low-stress, I was able to take 5 classes with this one

Dr. Asmatey is a gamechanger. When she enters a classroom, it becomes a place of community and welcome. She brilliantly fights with care for her students. She will challenge you to face reality (even when dark) and enlighten it, making something beautiful, profound, ever-growing, delicious, or even funny out of this world and the task ahead of you.

Such a good professor, really inspirational and caring, but still tough. She knows just how to encourage students and push them to do their best without causing burnout. Easily one of my favorite CHC profs.

I like Yalda, but she stressed me out a little bit. I really wanted to do well because I respected her so much, but I never knew how I was actually doing since she gave everyone the same grade on Canvas. But I seriously would recommend her; she deserves the hype and respect she gets. #badasswomen

Absolutely LOVE Yalda. By far the best professor I have ever had. She so deeply cares about every single one of her students and will always take time in her classes to address what is going on in our crazy world. Her office hours get busy but she will always try her best to make time for every student. She is incredible.

She is kind, she is encouraging, she is supportive! She never once assigned any busy work, and it never felt like a waste of time. She intentionally makes the effort to get to know each and every one of her students individually, and she provides feedback that is very clear and honest, while still being useful. Easily top 3 HC professors I've had.
Great prof. She really cares about everyone getting something out of her class and fostering a unique environment. Super easy 101 but other classes are probably harder.

She is the best professor I have ever had. She worked with me through a family emergency and never made me feel guilty for needing to miss a class. She is incredibly inspirational and cares deeply for her students. I can't wait to take more classes from her!
Yalda creates a welcoming community. She is very passionate about what she is teaching and her lectures always made me think beyond my limits. The class was super fun.

Professor Asmatey is the best teacher I've ever had at the UO. She's so so caring and passionate, you can tell she really loves teaching, and everything we did in class felt like it had a purpose bigger than just the class itself. Workload was very manageable, if you turn things in and show that you care then you don't have to worry about grades.

Professor Asmatey might genuinely be one of the most powerful speakers I've had the pleasure to hear-- even in a lecture format. Her classes force you to engage with heavy, powerful, real, yet important topics. The class was not structured in any way except to make you learn-- it would be very difficult to fail unless you were determined to do so.

I never leave ratings, but Dr. Asmatey absolutely blew me away with how inspiring, genuinely caring, and considerate she was. She has a way of capturing every students' attention and care in a way I have never seen before. She changed my perspective on life, and left me still thinking of her and what she taught me even a year later.
Prof. Asmatey is the best professor I've had so far at UO.

Yalda is by far the best prof I've ever had. She has an incredible way with words and genuinely cares about each and every one of her students. She's not afraid to voice her opinions and talk about things that other profs typically avoid. She's super accessible through office hours and is always down for chat.

Dr. Asmatey is easily the most thought-provoking, inspirational, and genuine teacher I have ever had. Yalda emphasized a connection between what we were learning and how it applied to our own lives, making the coursework not just easy, but meaningful and gratifying. I am grateful for the perspective Dr. Asmatey showed me and her genuine effort.

greatest professor I've ever had. I actually took HC101 by her and she's the most wonderful, passionate, inspirational, empathetic, and honestly just has a way with words. I was excited for every class. Bc it was a 101 course the homework was extremely manageable and she was flexible with turn ins. I've heard this isn't the case w her other classes

Dr. Asmatey is my favorite professor thus far. It is clear she cares deeply about each and every one of her students. She creates a safe space where everyone feels included, welcomed, appreciated, and highly encouraged to participate. She provides excellent feedback and expects highly of each and every one of her students, but is a fair grader.

Dr. Asmatey is a great professor! She is caring and passionate and really gets to know each student in the class. She is very accessible outside of class and gives great advice regarding the thesis project. I would definitely take her class again!!

Taken this professor twice and regretted it each time. He somehow did not even care enough to format an easy to use canvas cite. He says no attendance but then gives you bad grades if you do not use content from class lectures in your essays. Hee is incredibly pretentious and thinks he's miles smarter than everyone.

Zaman was a great professor. Attendance wasn't mandatory but the lectures and content were so interesting and engaging that I actually wanted to go to class. He added humor and real life scenarios into all lectures which helped a lot. I loved the class and felt like it was a great elective for my minor!!!
Zaman is fantastic. Incredible lectures; you can tell how knowledgeable and experienced he is. He also gave me great career advice.

He is an amazing professor. His lectures are engaging and he cracks some good jokes from time to time. You don't really need the textbook, just take good notes and review his slides very every weekly quiz. Going to lecture is not required but if you want an A you should go.

Prof Zaman is intense but overall a good guy. Classes are discussion heavy, so recommend attending even though it's not mandatory. He hates AI with a PASSION, to the point of where he created an in person final just to keep people from using AI for everything (he used to not give finals at all). He's decently flexible if you built rapport with him.

professor is very good at speaking with the class rather AT them. this makes for a better learing experience and engaing class that is well within the popular interest in mental disorders. if youre heavy into AI, he does use his quizzes that test for AI answers. class is fun to go to and so far my favorite to attend.

This PSY309 class has been one of my favorite classes here at UO. He deeply cares, is incredibly knowledgeable in his field, and is a pleasure to learn from. I could not recommend this class and professor enough.

Zaman's lectures are very engaging. Every week, you will learn about one or two different disorders. There is a lot of lively in-class discussion. Zaman is very willing to answer questions or provide help and resources in and outside of class.

Dr. Zaman is such an amazing professor, definitely not one of those teachers who doesn't know what they're doing. His lectures are engaging and heavily oriented towards audience participating which can be good or bad, but where he stands out is in office hours. He's super helpful for career and personal help. Please take his class!

Prof Z really challenges his students—not only in his tough grading, but the way he challenges our thoughts and perspectives. His style may come off as argumentative. But I would argue that he is trying hard to let you come into class with an open mind. He is supportive and engaging. Work hard, engage, and you will get so much out of this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Lectures are an hour and twenty minutes of boring slides, which he reads. He encourages raised hands, but just tells students they are wrong and how he is right. I am not learning anything, yet there are 40+ slides per day. I do not recommend it.
AI policy is very strict, and is brought up often to scare students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is very discussion heavy, not that it's graded, but prepare yourself for lots of questions from the prof and discussions with the people around you. He is a very engaging lecturer and the content is super interesting. His AI policy is very strict just to note.

Just no need to even take this course as nothing is genuinely taught. Do not waste your time. Take 480 instead - goes much more in depth & has active learning practices. Zaman is also rude & does not consider that nobody wants to sit through black and white slides for an hour with no break. Avoid.

This class is probably harder than a 3/5 if you do not have an interest in the law. If you're taking it just for the credits, it will probably be difficult. That said, if you are interested in the intersection between psychology and the law, this class is incredible. Dr. Zaman is incredibly qualified and passionate about his field of study.

Nice teacher. All quizes are online but be warned chatgpt will get some questions wrong. 3 short essay are alot of ur grade and somewhat harshly graded make sure to review you ideas or go to office hrs and review with him in order to make sure you get a decent grade.

Prof. Zaman is one of my goats. The attendance to his class was not mandatory so I would rock up 30min late if I slept in late and just yap with him after every class cause I had the time to. Being able to pick his brain on different diagnosis criteria was awesome. His office hours were easily accessible and he gave me good career changing advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The course content is informative, but the difficulty comes from the instructor's condescending communication style. If you struggle and advocate for yourself, be prepared to be referred to the Dean of Students under the guise of concern. It felt more like deflection than actual support.

Accessible teacher, attendance not mandatory. He is very kind and understanding if life problems come up. Makes material interesting and the tests aren't too hard if you study. All projects/tests are relevant to course material and helping students learn.
just a great professor, I highly recommend him to both psychology majors/minors or people just looking to fill credits

I love Dr. Zaman!!! I took Psychopathology and Forensic Psychology and both were incredible classes (especially forensic!). He is a great lecturer and human being who is fun to talk to outside of class. Attendance is not mandatory but PLEASE go to class and read the textbook, what he says in class is what is on exams, not necessarily slides.

I would recommend Dr. Zaman's classes to anyone I know, even outside of psychology students. The courses I have taken with him have been the most engaging, interesting classes I have ever taken (genuinely), and his teaching has been inspirational in terms of my futureprospects and interests. I truly feel that he is one of the best professors at UO.
Zaman's classes are graded by mostly straightforward assignments and he has a lot of knowledge of the subjects he lectures on. However GE grading sucked and was often unclear, so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice teacher who is genuinely interested in the topic he is teaching. Didn't really show up to class after week 5 and still got an A. Had to write 3 essays, but grading was self-explanatory and the last essay was literally about yourself. Would take a class with him again.

He is so passionate about what he is teaching. He wants his students to fully understand and be genuinely interested in it. he makes his lectures a conversation in the best way. Work load was very manageable. Made me WANT to come to class regardless of no attendance. Not just memorizing content like most lectures.

Dr. Zaman was a great lecturer. Attendance was not necessary and there was only 3 essays due for the whole course. There was weekly discussion boards and 5 canvas quizzes (open book/note). The course was very easy and he makes lectures engaging and interesting. As long as you come to the lectures you will do well in the class.

Dr. Zaman was a great professor to have. You can tell that he genuinely cares for all of his students and wants them to do well. He answers questions well and holds engaging in-class discussions. I would definitely recommend this professor.

Ahmar is incredibly caring about the subject and his students. Although attendance is not mandatory, I would HIGHLY recommend going to lecture. His class is discussion based, and Ahmar has wonderful personal examples and interesting case studies for every pathology he presents. 10/10 would reccomend

Professor Zaman really appreciates participation. He hosts two classes where students describe a person and their interaction with others and the rest of the class tries to diagnose them. I thought the essay prompts were very useful for the grade I received.

Zaman clearly cares about his students and is very interested in what he is teaching. Welcomes questions during and outside of class time. Good resource to talk to about future plans/grad school. I loved taking this course.
Great lectures and interesting information. Dr. Zaman is very knowledgeable, and cares about his students. Not necessary to read the textbook if you pay attention to lectures

Dude is mad chill. In general gives very short essays and there isn't a final. Being said I actually found myself looking forward to lectures even though I didn't do any readings. He's so good. This class more than any other class changed my world perspective and got me thinking differently about the people in my life. Must take class

Not a pysch major but one of favorite classes I have taken at Oregon. Very interesting and engaging lectures and I loved the structure of the class. Professor Zaman wants you to succeed. Late work is not accepted even for partial credit so turn things in on time.

Dr. Zaman is one of the best professors I have ever had. I took him for 309 and 410. He loves class discussions and helping students learn actively. He cares about his students sucess and is extremely helpful and kind. 100% would take again I HIGHLY RECOMMEND DR.ZAMAN HE IS AMAZING!!

My favorite professor at UO! Dr.Zaman does his best to keep even the driest of lectures entertaining and engaging. Lots of class discussion which also keeps you engaged. Lowest quiz and discussion grades dropped and all the quizzes are multiple choice. Definitely take a class with Dr.Zaman if you have the chance.

Dr. Zaman is the absolute best. He's super helpful both in and out of class, and genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed. He also is super invested in helping students beyond the course-- he loves to chat about grad school and stuff like that & gives great advice. If you get the opportunity to take a class with him you absolutely should.

Genuinely has interesting lectures and adds commentary off of his slides instead of just reading word by word. Very kind, soft, approachable and is always willing to help. As someone who doesn't really go out of my way to talk with professors, his aura made me comfortable enough to do so. You can tell he cares about his students. Recommend.
I love this man. He is amazing. So helpful, so calm, so intelligent, makes lectures interesting and fun. Overall, he is a wonderful professor and person. Highly recommend him.

Helpful in and outside of class, with class related questions and general guidance. Overall very laid back, could've been more direct on what exactly was needed in the writing assignments in order to receive full credit. Included writing assignments that encourage you to engage with the material on a deeper level. wish he taught more classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaman is an amazing professor who really cares about the success of his student!  He is super knowledgable about Forensic Psychology and grad school for those who are interested. The tests were pretty hard, so definitely understand the material (not just memorize).

Most people like him but I'm honestly not the biggest fan. He read off the slides, and while most of the assignments/quizzes were fairly easy, some of the questions were unnecessarily confusing and poorly written. He also talked about his political views during the class which i feel like isn't his place at all for a class about mental disorders.

The reviews really aren't lying. This is one of the best professors there is, and the class somehow manages to be really fun, engaging, easy, and yet also incredibly informative. You could easily learn the most from this class than any other single one without studying, which speaks to the effectiveness of having a relaxed, discussion-based class.

I took his 410 class and it was so awesome. There is technically a textbook but if you attend lectures and pay attention and take good notes then you probably don't have to read the text. I think there was the perfect amount of assignments. No study guides for tests but he gives you an idea which concepts are important you just have to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved this professor! lectures full of so much information and on canvas 30 mins before the class. Online quizzes every other week are super easy and open notes/textbook. No homework but 3 short essay assignments that are about 500 words and no final. In-class group discussions almost every lecture but they're super useful and he makes them fun
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Zaman is a fantastic professor and person! I really enjoyed his class even though the material itself tends to be a bit dry, Zaman made lectures interactive and thought-provoking. The workload was very chill and attendance was optional, I would love to take another class with him!

Zaman is one of the best professors I have ever had at the University of Oregon. He is super interactive with his lectures, and emphasizes the importance of group discussions. He is tech savvy, so I rarely ever ran into any technical issues throughout the class. Would love to take this class again if I was given the opportunity.

Dr. Zaman is a great professor! His lectures are generally pretty dry, but he usually always incorporates class discussions and does activities to help everyone understand the topics. In office hours, he is ready to give information on the professional side of psychology and grad school options. Definitely take his class!

One of the most passionate and caring professor's I've had. Really open to one on one discussions and encouraging class discussions and asking questions which is essential for psychopathology. If you're looking to get inspired just by the shear amount that someone else cares deeply about a subject; this is the guy.
Best professor I have taken at UO so far. There are 3 essays and quizzes nothing hard. He is so passionate about the subject and answers all your questions. I 100% recommend taking this course.

Ahmar is super cool. He made psychopathology so interesting. I've gone to class a handful of times and still have a 99. He doesn't do any midterms or finals, only quizzes and essays that are 500 words max. He's very funny. I would take him again in a heartbeat!

Gloria was very turbulent in her emotions and seemed to take her personal life out on her students. She was never clear about instructions especially about notecards and the exams. Gloria also missed class multiple times and was very flaky when it came to office hours or times for our orals.

Gloria is one of the worst professors I've had. She was constantly late to class throughout the term. If she asks you a question in Spanish in class and you don't answer it the way she wants, she's very passive aggressive about it. She expects a lot and doesn't help you learn AT ALL. She also threw a chair across the room bc she was upset.

Gloria wants the best for her students, but she is incredibly disorganized and can be rude if she's in a bad mood. She came into class late every day the entire term. She talks fast both in English and Spanish, making it difficult to learn. She constantly interrupts during oral exams and gives vauge, illegable feedback on written exams.

She's just disorganized and late to class almost every day. She's nice and wants to help students succeed but idk I felt like I was teaching myself most of the course and just hoping for the best on tests and stuff. Feedback on written tests is completely illegible and if you ask what she wrote, chances are she won't be able to decipher it herself

I had her for Span 201, and it was probably the hardest Spanish I have ever been for me. Spanish doesn't come easily to me, but Gloria did not make it accessible or easy to learn from your mistakes. I continuously tried to show up to office hours, though she was always late. I do not recommend taking her unless you like to teach yourself.
She just seemed disorganized
good teacher and good person, a little disorganized at times but wants students to succeed and gives good feedback. classes are also very easygoing and funny with her.

I loved Prof. Zabala! If you are someone who likes to engage in class you will definitely have a good time in hers. Her class has a fun, relaxed vibe & I found her very easy to understand when she spoke Spanish. Not sure why others have struggled with her. She does cold call, but if you pay attention to the material you'll be fine.

Prof. Zabala's classes were not engaging and she's generally a very tense person. She can be passive-aggressive at times and personally being in her class always gives me anxiety. She's very critical of your work and not an easy grader. It's good in the sense that it acts as a challenge and pushes you but does not look good on the transcript.

Mrs. Zabala is awesome. She is very funny and gives good advice and wants the best for her students. You do a creative project to end the term which makes the end of the term much less stressful than it could have been. Not sure why people diss on her tbh, she's lit

Her classes are not for the faint-hearted. You get tested multiple times a week in addition to homework. She talks very fast and is NOT receptive to questions. She can be frustrating and is not afraid to cold call. She is also funny and personable, as long as you can keep up.

I took both Span 202 and 203 from Gloria because she was so engaging while teaching. You will definitely laugh each class if you are lucky enough to land her as your professor. She cares about her students and focuses on individual improvement throughout the term. Projects are fun and pretty open ended so you will have lots of choice in what you do

The low ratings for Ms. Zabala are crazy, I am shocked people had such bad experiences. I have taken her for three different courses now and every time I love her class. She is so kind, connects with all of her students on a personal level, and is very clear when teaching. Wish I could give her a higher rating, 100% take her class.
This teacher assigns ridiculous amounts of homework. The class itself is not hard, but I have wasted countless hours outside of class doing redundant and monotonous homework assignments.

The assignments are unclear and tests have a ton of errors. She is not receptive to students reaching out and her zoom classes are the equivalent of attending a class with a Spanish substitute. She is a nice lady but she cannot teach remote courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Huiliang is very sweet! Yes, she has an accent, but if you listen, you can understand. If you ask questions, she will answer. The midterm was difficult for me, but I could have prepared more. This class is unfortunately very test-heavy, but they're not hard if you study. However, the study guide does need to be more accurate. I really do like her.

If I'm paying tens of thousands of dollars to get an education here, I expect the university would hire teachers that are able to teach in English considering we are in the United States and help students properly learn. But nope! I couldn't understand a word she said all term and basically had to teach myself everything

She's extremely hard to understand. It's not her fault I don't think the university should have hired to teach English students' math. That being said she's very sweet and understanding if you meet with her outside of class. Just pay super attention and sit in the front because she writes messy and small.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is impossible to understand, for the midterm she made a review with everything you need, then I take the midterm and fail it! I reach out and ask why she had the last question as the highest point question and didn't put anything like that on the review and she admitted to not adding it in the review. I do not recommend this teacher.
Lots of extra credit and exams were easy

Maybe the best lecturer at the entire school. Extremely caring about the subject if you want to dive deep, but also an easy A even if you don't. Assignments were light, well-defined, and enjoyable to complete. Exams are in person with a notes sheet and require a bit of studying, but nothing too challenging.

This class bangs I loved everything about it. Theres a weekly quiz, 5 questions, online super easy. The GE I had wasn't super helpful but the class itself is crazy easy. Everything on the tests is on the slides and readings. There's hardly any work but the work is graded on effort so it's really light. I found new songs everyday and he's a fun guy.

Very engaging, especially since the class was not something I was initially interested in, was just taking it for the music credit. Knows how to get the class involved and makes every class fun and interesting. Cares a lot about the topics he teaches, making it feel like it's worth your time and money. Would recommend to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult because we weren't graded on anything until week 7, and then it was insanely hard and weighted from there. The final is a 10-15 page paper analyzing a movie and the midterm and final tests are difficult. The GE was a hard grader and feedback and responses from them were minimal. This class could have been a lot better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was not a fan, There were tons of little assignments that didn't make sense are you didn't know about until they were due. The projects themselves were fine, but I would not take again. She's not very helpful and the grading is super super weird. Especially when it came to missing assignments she was not helpful and kind of condescending.

I think she's changed her way of teaching because these reviews don't align with the course I just took this quarter. As long as you keep up with your work, ask her questions, and do assignments like you're supposed to, you'll get what you expect out of this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Every assignment is difficult to find and the instructions are unclear. At multiple points, I had to email her to correct/add something in her course. I also had to fight back on a grade and prove how I followed the rubric when I had. I hated all of the essays I wrote due to her topics, and there are so many essays. I wasted my time and money.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She might be the worst professor I've ever had. One of the toughest graders, and the instructions on any assignment are challenging to follow. You might only pass this class by doing her extra credit assignments. You'll be doing a scavenger hunt trying to find all the assignments, and you have to do a peer review on every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I am currently in her 122 class and I do not understand all the negativity. Maybe she changed from previous years but she was great in my online class. Her grading can be strict when it comes to rough drafts however if you fix your essay using her recommendations along with peer recs your all set. She is very accessible, I met with her often!

I've been in this class for a total of 2 weeks. Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. Be prepared to call ur parents crying about this class. canvas is set up terribly, ridiculous amount of assignments every week, no late work, and incredibly unclear with every single assignment. Don't take this class if u care about ur grades or sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: So much busy work. Instructions are terrible, unclear, and hard to follow. Totally unorganized canvas page. She disables your grade so you don't know your score until week 5 and the end. In order to get an A you have to do a ton of "extra credit" assignments. Very harsh grader as well. And just annoying. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor was extremely unorganized and the Canvas page seemed as if it was copied & pasted from a completely different year and term. The assignment pages were inaccurate, unclear, and difficult to understand. Each time I met with the professor I would leave feeling terrible about my writing abilities. I haven't learned one useful thing.

The canvas page is a nightmare there are at least 5 new daily notifications for some random assignment that she needs you to complete. You get lost in the notifications and will have missed a deadline by then. She wants to help but when you go to office hours she fails so fantastically and seems upset at you.

Do not take this class if you care about your general well-being, it is the hardest gen-ed class you will ever take. This class had no business being this time-consuming, and to get above a B, the only thing you can do is extra credit essays. If you get below a C, there is nothing you can do. She sets you up for failure from the start.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She was outright rude and passive aggressive the single time I had met with her. She made rude comments about my work after I had scheduled a one-on-one conference that she was LATE and unprepared for. Do NOT take this course, even if you think it'll be fine. She expects for this to be your only class with the amount of work she assigns as well.

Pick any other professor! She assigns so much work with unreasonable expectations. If you don't have a life, take her class. She also provided no support and always left me feeling discouraged.
