reviews.comment: This class was by far the hardest sociology class I have ever taken. If I did it in person maybe it would of been easier, but the professor was not that friendly and would comment mean responses to my homework. I reached out to him a couple of times for help but he was very helpful and was rude instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This course is easy for the first and even second week, but it's terrible for the last two weeks. Lots of quizzes and handout. He respond to the question really fast.

A really nice, down to earth prof. I am god awful at statistics and math and the like, but I attended class and put in a good effort and got a B+. Go to his office hours and he will help you with the quizzes. I really don't think I could have passed this class with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Aaron is a really great sociology professor.   60% of the class is online quizzes (he drops the lowest 2) and the other 15% is participation.  The quizzes are pretty simple, he shows you how to do most of them in his lecture slides online.  The course sounds scary, but it really isn't.  You use a program to do all the calculations.  Awesome teach

absolute great human being. always available to lend a hand. he's a very smart professor, in fact smarter than most other professors. he's the director of grad students and sometimes he forgets that undergrads aren't on his level and he occasionally leaves students behind, but HONESTLY just say "hey" and he will repeat it in normal english undergra
He puts me to sleep, the papers are easy but the midtermis tough. He grades on a curve because his questions are so bad.

He's a nice guy, doesn't make eye contact when lecturing making me feel like he's constantly nervous about messing up. DO NOT TAKE THIS DURING SUMMER. IT IS NOT AN EASY CLASS. In the beginning he made it sound like it's a breeze! There's a ton of analyzing to do for the tests and with just 4 weeks to learn all of this material is crazy.
Class was simple and painless a few essay like 2-3 pages. Not a super inspiring guy but does his job. Really takes a long time to get grades back.
Very easy if you do the work. As long as you attempt the homework you will do fine. He does anonymous clicker questions just to see if people are confused. Easy class, nice professor

He's the kind of professor that passes back your graded essay, then spends the last 30 minutes of class going over the real instructions/expectations of said essay. if you're into hidden expectations, boring lectures, balding, purple shirt wearing professors, this prof is for you!

Probably the best experience I have had during my time getting my B.S. in Art from the UO writing this review years after taking his class but I wanted to leave this note for anyone considering taking his class. Do it. If you love painting take this course and thrive it will be a life memory you will look back on fondly.
Can be abrasive, Older generation makes offensive jokes unintentionally, you either hit it off with him or you don't (i didn't). Great professor, drove me crazy, likely couldn't handle him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not patient. Burned out on teaching. Unapproachable. Talks for a long time about nothing. Unclear syllabus assignments.
Ron is an amazing teacher. Essentially, he's  honest. He knows what's up.

Ron was the best painting teach I have have ever had. He probably doesn't remember me but  he made a huge impact so it doesn' t really matter. He is just honest and it makes people like him.  Essentially he's just a good guy who knows what's up.

Straightforward art instruction.  One of the few drawing instructors at UofO that inspired me to really push myself to improve.  Ron Graff is an easy-going professor, but he will make a hard working student work even harder.  People wanting an easy A seem to drop out by the second week, or face some pretty honest critiques.

I had Ron Graff for 5 years at U of O.  He is fiesty, helpful, knowledgeable, and an incredibly great painter. He isn't there to compliment you, he'll help guide you.  If you want to have someone stroke your ego - forget it.  He'll push you.
Mr. Graff understands oil paint and its application like a successful farmer fertilizes soil and grows food.
Ron, friend, mentor, jedi I weep for the fact that we met in my last term at the university.
Ron's teaching will become a part of your biography.

Hella yeah! Imagine getting to rate a professor who scared the sh*t out of me when I was a young girl in the '70s. I took a drawing class from him at the U of I. He scared all of us. He was profane, outrageously critical, outright mean at times, even diabolical. I survived the class. He liked my stuff. Kept one of my drawings. I wish I had it back.
He is burnt out. Comes across as bitter. Seems to be competitive with the more talented students.
Forget your "art"

Prof Graff is one of the best art teachers, nationwide.  He has a hell of a reputation, and if you can get into his class, you're very lucky.  But remember, his job is NOT to tell you he likes your work, and he won't.  Very blunt, but that's what students need.  I've seen him make a student cry with his critique, but he was absolutely fair, correct
ron's ok but seems maybe burned out on teaching at this point.

He is absolutely my favorite instructor EVER.  He's a skilled artist in his own right, brilliant, sincere, blunt, and funnier than most comedians.  Warning - he's not shy about giving you his honest opinion/critique about something.  Don't take it personally.
No Comments
Ron is wonderfully patient and extremely good at both painting and teaching.

Most passionate teacher willing to look at things from your perspective as long as you are willing to look from his. He is also hilarious and incredibly talented and knowledgeable about all aspects of art. He was by far my favorite teacher ever.
Best painting instructor, ever.

Doesn't give clear guidelines for large projects and tells people they are on the right track and then gives them a bad grade with no explanation. Does not have a textbook and the tests are all essays.

Ron covers interesting topics and provides time to try out the techniques that we have learnt, which is really helpful in understanding the concepts. However, if you do not or are unable to follow closely, it is easy to feel overwhelmed and lost.

Spent class time telling stories about his life &doesn't cover class’s materials except @end of class time.Not clear with his guidelines nor evaluations grading is subjective b/c he doesn't provide reasons 4grading.U don't know where u stands til the end of term. F u r taking the class 2satisfy IBC Program bear in mind its not certificated from UO
Fantastic teacher

This is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. I'm surprised to see him teaches at UO. Very rude to the students, have zero knowledge, very demanding. Class is suppose to be easy but he makes is very hard! If he likes you, you will have a good grade which is unethical behavior. I DON'T Recommend this teacher EVER> Seriously AVOID !
Exceptional professor with many interesting stories from his past. Class is interesting as well. Takes attendance.Take this class if you need an upper elective.

Ron's a great teacher, and more importantly a great human being. I am more confident of my negotiating ability because of this class. However, I will leave you a few words of advice. Don't leave your annotated bibliography until the last minute like I did haha!
Great teacher!

Ron is awesome! He was one of the most clear and interesting professors I've had. He is very willing to help if you don't understand something and puts a lot of emphasis on effort. Since this class is for international negotiations, he tries to learn everyone's background and gives very useful tips on negotiations! I would definitely recommend him!
Such great lectures, very engaging and passionate. Recommended even if you aren't an architecture major. All around good time

The lecture's were mind blowing, unlike any other class I have ever taken. He really likes to see creativity in your projects and with having open guidelines on projects he has specifics on what he looks for so make sure to ask after lectures. Projects are really easy and lectures are very interesting with the use of hundreds of pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgeable and friendly professor. Lectures are long, but were interesting and not difficult to grasp, plus he usually gave the class a 5-minute break at the halfway point. He was extremely passionate about his subject; lectures were genuinely inspiring. Assignments weren't difficult and were fun to do, & the one exam was fairly easy!

He's an interesting guy with a lot of great ideas, but his lectures get boring after a while. His class is easy. All the concepts are broad and easy to grasp. There's basically no homework, and the three projects assigned over the term take only a couple hours of work each.
Hes a passionate prof, who sounds IDENTICAL to Jack Nicholson. Reasonably difficult, but as long as you take notes, you'll do great
Ron is awesome

Lovinger is one of the worst professors I've ever had.  His ego, personal life, sexual impulses, and favoritism completely prevent him from being an effective teacher.  Given the number of complaints the University has received about this man's behavior, he should have been removed years ago, and "passion" doesn't excuse his behavior
Seemed to be only interested in teaching the students who were going with him to Japan.  The others in his Japanese Landscapes class got the shaft.

He is extemely enthusiastic and loves what he teaches.  He paints a nice picture in your head of the places you need to know for the one exam that he gives. The class does, however, get a little repetitive. Many gardens are similar.  The three projects are fun to create.. if you have any sort of creative bone your body.

What a challenge; Ron's an easy teacher to please if you take notes, throw in "juxtaposition" on your exams, and take an interest in the topic. However, as female students may agree, he can be a challenging professor to deal with.
No Comments
Great lectures, very structured teaching style and very experienced in the field of landscape architecture.
This guy knows how to get you interested! He has a lot of experience in landscapes and I had so much fun listening to his lectures.

Best professor I've had at UConn. Can't say enough great things about him. Really respects students and has appropriate and fair expectations. Class assignments are very clear and straightforward. He is extremely helpful and always willing to help you. Definitely take any class you can with Beghetto
Phenomenal Professor! Super enthusiastic, funny, intelligent and has great advice for teachers. I hope to one day teach like Beghetto. Learned lots in this class.

Dr. Beghetto is a phenomenal instructor, who exudes creativity. I found his course to be an amazing (and rare) space to develop ideas and theory and to present and test that theory to my colleagues. I really think he is the single most talented and inspiring teacher that I have had in 17 years of undergraduate and graduate education. Amazing.

Beghetto was an awesome and inspiring teacher who really pushed you to understand the content. Autobiography of Schooling was both interesting and informative and made you want to learn more. I can't wait to be in his class again in the Spring!
awesome class
I took his Assessment class in the summer of 2008 and it was the only class that made me want to come to campus. His passion for teaching is contagious!
he's a cool professor
Beghetto is AMAZING! I would take any class he teaches. He is fun and can keep you involved during a long lecture class!

Excellent teacher - very engaging and respectable. Good sense of humor. Class is easy as long as you do the work on time.  Allows extensions on all assignments regardless of reason.  Only two papers and one group project.  Made me want to explore teaching as a career.

This teacher is amazing.  He has given me so many ideas on how to be a successful teacher in the future.  All of the information taught in class was so easy to learn because he used so many real life examples.  I learned so much from this class and I never didn't want to attend class.  The work load was very managable and he allowed extensions.
Very good teacher . Didn't need to show to class to do well but did just because the class was interesting.

This was a great class. He is such an amazing professor, he is so into what he teaches and is so energized about what he is teaching and it is such a joy to be in the class. Take this class even if you are not an ed major you will learn things that will help you.

dr. beghetto is one of my favorite teachers, as he knows how to turn a tired evening class lively. he's a very kind, caring guy and is passionate about what he does and it shows! it's not very often a professor with a huge class will take the time to learn names. great professor!
GREAT PROf!!! I love taking his class. My all time favorite. I would encouage everyone to take his class, even if you are not a education major. Very funny guy.

AMAZING! He made me want to go into teaching even more than i did. I wish he taught more than one class! He is my ALL time favorite teacher.. and he LOVES what he does, you can feel it. He's funny, he's charming, and he makes you want to learn more. LOVE HIM!

Beghetto is one of the best Professors I have had at the UofO so far. His lectures are always engaging and he never wastes your time in class and his stories are always super funny. He is very clear about what he expects and grades accordingly. I wish I could take all my EDST classes from him he was GREAT!
great teacher. very engaging. has fun during a long class. knows what he is talking about!
AMAZING PROFESSOR!! I loved his class so much, he is  so awesome! Best teacher I have ever had. and so cute ;-)

He knows how to make a boring class interesting.  He gives extensions on everything...he teaches in a clear manner.  He's funny, will give you good reccommendations, and is the best teacher I have ever had!  Take this class!
Fantastically engaging.  Hilarious.  Helpful.  Take his classes.

Great class!! My favorite so far here at UO. Amazing teacher, really helpful and really approachable. He helps you beyond the classroom with anything you need. He is a great guy, funny as hell, and he makes the class really interesting! I'd take the class even if it wasn't my major! Awesome guy!!!!
My favorite college teacher of all time
Awesome guy.  He learns everyone's name even though it is a huge lecture class, and he is very funny.  He is open to suggestions and questions, and the class is interesting.
He is so freakin funny. I went to every class and didn't fall asleep once.  I highly reccomend this cat.
He is really motivating and makes learning fun.
Beghetto is a GREAT professor. He is so inspiring! I learned SO much
He makes a potentially boring class as exciting as it could be.
Great teacher! He is such a great guy, so many interesting stories. He also makes it a point to learn everyone's name! Great guy!
No Comments
No Comments
Great experience! COntinue teaching with your amazing style.
No Comments
Phenominal professor, great entertaining lectures and you get a lot out of his classes!
Super Teacher
great teacher, he is hilarious, makes class very interesting all the time.  I loved his stories about his childhood.  Take classes from him
He is the greatest teacher! Take him...
No Comments
I loved his class.  I would definitely take more of his classes.
very good teacher. my favorite so far. take him.
No Comments
Listen to the reviews. Save yourself the stress and DON't take this class. Theres a reason why so many seats are open in this class
Worst prof I've had at UO

Don't trust the bad reviews! Dr. Ablow is great. Her expectations are clear. She gives examples for all assignments, clear rubrics, and assignment descriptions. She deeply cares about infant research. She quickly replies to emails. She gave helpful feedback on every assignment. The project requires work, but she openly warns students on day one.

While the material was awesome and worth learning, pretty much everything else sucked. The tests are easy if you take good notes, the lectures are fine, but oh boy was the group project poorly managed. The grading criteria makes no sense, the instructions are unclear, direction is minimal, and it feels impossible to get through to her.

Overall the worst professor I have had at Oregon. She is unclear, and does not work towards her students best interests. When she is unclear, she punishes the student by taking away points rather than understanding their confusion. A lot of work, and boring lectures. Not worth the 4 credits, highly do not recommend! Find another course if you can.
Had an exam and paper due the same work. Not willing to listen to feedback. Was not flexible when I had a traveling issue
z

This was the worst psych class I have taken. The assignment instructions were so unclear and the group project was terribly organized. The lectures also felt very scripted. I would not take this class again.

I thought her lectures were very informative. She answered emails quickly and was very understanding of a late assignment due to my work schedule. Tests were well written and I agreed with the grading standards.

Prof. Ablow is a good professor and is very accessible outside of class. She helps us by scanning the textbook for free. Slides are easy and digestible. Zoom tests are with camera on and closed notes however.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ms. Ablow references theories as facts, is unclear when trying to explain the details about these theories, and has unhelpful expectations about the assigned reading summaries. When I expressed concern about how the format of the reading summaries she simply slapped a word count on top of the other limitations on this assignment and called it good

Prof Ablow had the most confusing guidelines for class papers I've ever seen. We had a paper which at the beginning of the term was 3-5 pgs. She changed it to 5 without telling us, then graded us on whether it was 5-7. I emailed her and she pretended it was that from the beginning but multiple students saw the original requirements.

She is the worst professor at this school. She is unclear and unfocused. Her lectures are no help, and somehow her study guides are 40 pages long even though we've only had two weeks of information. Do not take her class. Seriously do not take it, wait for another psych course to open up.

The lectures are extremely interesting as is the virtual child aspect of the class. the down fall is that the tests are nearly impossible due to the copious amounts of material and the lecture slides being almost useless. She tells you Johnny has 4 apples and 3 grapes and then asks you on the test how many aliens are in the barber shop.

Tests are extremely difficult.  For the midterm, she gave out a 5 page, single spaced, "study guide."  Basically, read the entire text book and hope you get lucky.  Studied for hours and I might have well as circled the answers randomly.  The class is very interesting though which is a shame.

Jennifer seems to be expecting that you are only taking her class with the amount of work she requires. Textbook reading alone was ridiculous. I emailed her and almost 2 weeks later still haven't heard back. She speaks in monotone and boredom is inevitable. I do not suggest taking Dr Ablow's classes

The subject matter is very interesting to me and has been for a very long time but some how this professor has made is painfully boring to the point that I dropped her class.  The work load is giant and the clarity on the assignments is just not there. I tried to contact Dr. Ablow and she still has yet to reply to me...2 weeks later.

Currently enrolled in her class, will rate again after. 1st exam with her soon, I have a sinking feeling that she will be a teacher who gives almost impossible exams. Her lectures are interesting and I love her speaking voice/mild accent. She is extremely knowledgeable in this field and it shows. Hoping she enables my hard work to pay off though.

This class has a 12 pg syllabus. Required to make 2 presentations and you will only use 1 of them-her choosing (night b4 presentation)lots of group work. Expectations and guidelines are unclear. There is an obscene amount of reading for this class and unnecessary busy work. Nice person but terrible instructor. Don't take her classes.

Prof. Ablow is very rude. Tried reaching her several times with no response, had to go above her head at which point I finally received help. Never actually met her, but I knew I would rather drop her course than be stuck with a professor so inconsiderate all term.

Hands down the most awful professor in the psych department. Expectations are very unclear, has no respect for students, hypocritical of her own standards. Extremely frustrating course. I cannot emphasize her awfulness enough.
Very hard class. Really interesting class but for some reason she makes it very boring and her tests are extremely hard!

I do not suggest taking this instructor. Her lectures are very monotone, as well as all of her communications with students. She has a huge work load with lots of group work, and is very unclear in her expectations. One of the worst courses I took at the U of O.

Professor Alblow seems to be quite new to to the college teaching seen. By no means does this make her a poor instructor, instead I see her as having tons of potential to one day be a great instructor if she keeps working hard at it. Lectures are pretty clear and well-paced. Many times her lectures are too heavily dependent upon the text book.

Abby was a fantastic teacher, she was very funny and gave very clear instructions on projects. Didn't give much busy work and while the lectures are based on a textbook, she does a great job adding relevant news and going beyond just what the textbook would have said. As for the class, tests are open notes so take detailed notes in class.
Abby is a great teacher, and is very understanding.
Abby is an awesome professor, always giving clear instructions on projects, great feedback, light workload, fun lectures, and a generous grader! If you have the opportunity to take her class, do it!

GOAT. Hilarious, caring, and engaging. Learning from a younger professor was very refreshing, as Abby understands how to communicate information to a younger audience. Would take her class again in a heartbeat.

She's cool, if you care about marketing, this class is easy. She is switching the tests to Scantron so that isn't chill. I was focusing on other classes, but this class really isn't that hard if you put a little time into it.

Abby is super understanding and easy to work with! The class was well structured and lectures were interesting. She gave lots of time to do group work, prioritized not making groups meet outside of class.

Abby is an amazing professor! Super chill and understanding. Like BA 308 you'll have to work with a team throughout the term. Unlike BA 308, the team projects will be easier. As long as you have a good team and put in the effort getting an A will be easy.

Abby is a great professor. She is extremely enthusiastic and eager to help each student. She is super approachable and creates connections with students. Her lectures are enjoyable and do not drag out. I would definitely recommend taking her class!

Abby is a terrific professor. She is enthusiastic and clearly cares about every single student. She makes an effort to know them so she can cater to each one and ensure their success. Highly recommend
Approachable professor who makes class genuinely enjoyable while still making sure students understand the lecture material

I can tell that Dr. Cullen is very smart and cares a lot about her students, but her lectures are hard to follow and the assignments are extremely tedious with vague instruction. Her tests are way more difficult than what was discussed in class, and it sometimes feels like she doesn't even know what she's talking about.

Professor Cullen is very nice and she really cares about her students. However, her class was hard to follow at times and the assignments were confusing and time consuming. The statistics part of the class was particularly hard to follow as it wasn't always explained well. Deadlines are strict and attendance is required for IClicker participation.

Abby is so kind and relatable which was the nicest part about this course. This was her first term teaching a larger class style so she was trying to find her footing. Lectures were poorly explained and confusing and the final was 10x harder than any other practice we had in class. Overall the general assignments were easy.

This course was truly abysmal. The GEs and the professor were on complete opposite planets the whole term. Grading criteria is horrifically vague, but the deadlines are SOOO strict. I felt like I was constantly drowning in the course, and when going to GE office hours, they were often never there. PLSSS research professors before taking this course

Really good math professor. He doesn't use WebWork, and the homework is pretty easy. Weekly quizzes and multiple exams allow for a lot of different grading criteria. He actually shows how the math works with examples. Not a very traditional teaching style, but it works well if your open to it! Overall, the greatest math teacher I've ever had.
Didn't grade my work till like week 8, lied about being an easy grader, was late to our exam, never posted any notes, was hostile when discussing grading, no calculators, overall just a rough teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall good professor. He's behind on grading and doesn't release solutions to the weeks of work until the last days leading up to a test. Grading is frustrating but lectures are impactful.

Even though he has a heavy accent, he is more than willing to repeat himself. He is the best math instructor I've had in my academic career. He not only explains things in their definitive mathematic definition, but also in laymen's terms which are easy to follow. He takes his time at grading, but honestly it's not a big deal. Hands down brilliant.

Consistently shows up few minutes late to class, never grades any homework-took both midterms before receiving a grade for the first one. Examples he writes on the board are either written extremely small, with sloppy writing, or just on an odd spot of the whiteboard that offers limited visibility to certain spots in the classroom. Don't recommend.

Really kind and understanding. Very bubbly and fun energy. Will drop lowest homework grade, and will drop midterm grade if you do better on the final. There's a lot of hw but it's helpful and good for review. I highly recommend taking this class :)
Ahhilash takes a lot of time to explain new concepts, and rather than just writing equations on the board, he does complex math to show students how we got the equation. I would recommend him 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Abhilash is very passionate about the subject he teaches. He is very willing to give help and work with those who ask for it although explanations are not always clear. Class is graded off of webwork, weekly quizzes, a midterm and a final. Extra credit is offered through very helpful practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class and fair grader
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super inspirational
Professor Abia-Smith is super chill!

This is just about the easiest class I have ever taken. Professor Abia-Smith is very kind and cares a lot about her students. Most of the assignments are just busy work that as long as you complete it, you get 100%. I NEVER went to the discussions and only went to about half the lectures and still got a 95%.... take this for an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The easiest class I ever took I absolutely loved it. It was also a really fun class. There was some busy work but oh well the class was easy. No tests so you didn't have to pay attention in lectures but they were still fun lectures and attendance was not mandatory. She was also caring and really nice. She doesn't give A+ though.

This class was by far one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. It was a nice little break away from my other lecture based classes because you get to sit down, draw, and listen to music.Lisa is very nice and personable, and the assignments allow you to be creative.

If you need an easy Arts and Letters - TAKE PPPM250! It was probably the easiest class I have taken in my time here. No exams and only a few major assignments as a midterm and final, but they are pretty easy. Lisa is also really nice and understanding, as was her GE Ashly. I'm not super into Arts, but if you are, TAKE THIS CLASS!

She made getting an arts and letters credit interesting. I wasn't sure if I would enjoy this course, but the way she has taught us to be creative and not grading on art ability has been something I enjoy. Very kind woman, take her class if you can!

Assigns at least 3 readings a week, minimum. Never refers to the discussion posts she talks about, also not traditional discussion posts. Is often late and doesn't give clear instructions on what is expected and expects 2 -4 pages for every discussion board but there is no discussion in class in work off of because she never does it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lisa is the best!! Her classes are relaxed and 100% art-oriented. I've learned so much about contemporary art and the art/museum industry. She teaches a few classes, I recommend all of them.
Lisa is a great prof who really gets to know the students. She will put in the effort if you do too.

Lisa is an awesome professor that teaches such an enjoyable class. She is so easy-going and the content relates well to the course. Homework load is pretty light (a few lesson plans submitted electronically throughout the term), and no exams which is a bonus. I was introduced on the importance of Art in elementary education.
Best teacher, she really cares about her students, she is great for career and internship opportunities and advice.

Lisa is the best teacher I have ever had. She is the sweetest person at this university and is very understanding. There were no tests in my class, only essays, and she is very helpful and understanding with her feedback. If you write a bad essay all it takes is a quick email and she will explain how to do it better, and give you a second chance.
Great Women, so sweet so helpful. Truly loved teaching her class
I'v never met such a nice professor.
She is the best professor I'v ever met, her class is very interesting, and you can get an easy A.
SHE IS THE BEST !!!!
Makes you buy $80 textbook & tells you to bring it to class everyday; never refers to it again.

Course depends mostly on GEs, Prof Abbott does a good job on teaching the class but you only meet with him 1x a week so most of the learning and assignments are done with the GEs. There are also way too many assignments you have to worry about for a 2 credit class however it really helps.

Tyler Abbott is a professor who clearly knows what he's talking about, but can't for the life of him teach it to the class. Aural skills at the UO were by far the worst music classes I have ever taken. The hw is boring, repetitive, and annoying, and the lecture where he actually teaches does a better job at confusing students than it does teaching.
The worst experience ....
The worst professor I met ever!! As a Aural skill professor, never have student to sing melody in lecture.
While overall nice, requires us to stand for long periods of time in class. This can be very hard for disabled students and students with health issues.

Abbott taught my first 3 terms of aural skills, and the experience/grade varied each time depending on which GE I had; find one you like, stick with them. What was a D in one lab section would be an A- in another. One also graded really slow, but when someone emailed Abbott he fixed that. Kind of a "weed out" class- aural skills 4-5 went smoother
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher. He makes this class super straight forward and you always know what needs to be completed when. The material is hard, but he wants you to succeed and is very experienced in giving perfect tips to make you succeed if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had him for my aural skills class. Really good at teaching. I would say my singing and melody dictation had improved a lot after taking his classes. His class is really fun too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Having taken both Aural Skills and Lessons, I can say that Tyler Abbott has the best in mind for his students. He expects you to do the work necessary to learn, but is incredibly helpful and patient. I've grown as a musician more than I could have expected with his help. Class is always a blast, he really makes it enjoyable. Monster bassist, too.

Professor Abbot was great! Super nice & flexible if you gave him a reason. You work mostly with the GTFs but he's always to help. He tends to get into really fine details and lose track of time but you ALWAYS know what he expects from you. Class has the same routine every week. Practice the exercises regularly. You CAN'T walk in blind to quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Abbot is incredibly well intentioned, but really scattered/rambling in his lectures. Due to the nature of my class (Aural Skills), the lectures didn't really matter, but I could see it being a big issue in other classes. Outside of lectures, he's very willing to work with any students that need help, and a really nice guy!

Hadil is by far the best honors professor I've had. She clearly loves what she teaches, and her lecture topics and examples are very current to today's media. She replies extremely fast to emails and isn't afraid to offer all the help she can. I would recommend taking her; she's amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is super nice and flexible with the class. If you contact her before, she will always be super nice and reasonable. The class content is straightforward, and she is super passionate about her content.

Hadil is very kind and amazing. Go to class it's a big part of your grade. She is a tough grader on the midterm and final but lax with everything else so don't get caught of guard when the midterm comes around. We had 1 group presentation - 30 mins, 1 paper, and a final project. Then weekly discussion board post of the course reading.

Hadil is truly such an amazing professor and this course was very interesting. She did a very good job on not only being available but being relational with her students and open to bending assignments to create a more equitable community in her course.

Hadil is such a great professor and person. She is very responsive and understanding regarding deadlines. Her lectures are so interesting and the class has a good balance of discussion, lectures, and projects. I have loved her class on Arab Cinema so much and would highly recommend taking a class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you want to be a better filmmaker/producer and seek out office hours with Jesse, you will see the results. Jesse will respect you honestly if you respect honestly him.
Jesse is definitely an intimidating professor, to say the least. I don't have anything bad to say about him but I wouldn't say he's a professor that wow'd me either.

Jesse was awesome in Gateway. If you get to know him outside of lecture he always offers help and advice on assignments. Lectures could get a little boring, but he always had some good advice or a tip to make your assignments better. Gateway assignments are graded by GE's beware, assignments are subjective and they like to grade it by opinion.

I had him and Dan for Gateway to Media and they weren't very good. He grades too harshly, doesn't have his GE's give good enough feedback, and doesn't clearly explain what is necessary from assignments. He overexplains subjects that are easy and underexplains ones that are crucial to our success. Too hard for a 200 level class.
I don't know if Jesse is a good prof because I've only had him for a couple weeks but I just wanted to leave this review to say he's sexy

I imagine in-class Jesse would be easier to learn from. But remotely- my only interactions with him are through the harsh feedback he leaves on all the assignments and extremely dry recordings he posts for lecture. It's obvious he's intelligent, but I would have a hard time approaching him if I had to. He comes off as arrogant, wasn't a fan

I had Jesse for Reporting 1 and my Gateway sequence. I would definitely take another one of his classes. He knows his stuff and you will improve so much in his classes. You will feel like there is a lot of homework, but that's only because it's a J class and the articles take a lot of preparation and revision. There's really only 3-4 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jesse's a really good guy who tries to make students' documentary videos the absolute best they can be. You get to make your own documentary in his Doc. Production class, so know that's no easy task- be prepared to really care about this course and pour everything you can into it. Listen to Jesse's feedback if you can and don't take it personally.

Not very approachable or friendly for a professor that works in the Journalism field. I have been to office hours, and left feeling interrogated instead of professionally critiqued. He makes you feel like assignments are incredibly intimidating, when you are more than capable of doing a good job.

If it he wasn't for his tough grading, I wouldn't feel as confident in my writing as I do now. He pushes you, and will continue bashing you with criticism on assignments. It's important to not take it personally. Improve your writing with his comments and integrate suggestions he makes. He may come off as stand-offish, but is a very personable man.

Grading is tough - he'll tear apart your papers and leave plenty of comments. He does mark down your papers if your opinion or view is different from his. You have to really work for your grades and even then they're not going to be that great. Lots of homework - I mean every night. It's exhausting. Nice enough guy I guess.

Jesse is a very knowledgeable. He has plenty of expertise in the field and gives great feedback. His lectures are helpful and funny. If you want to be a filmmaker or broadcaster, Jesse is one of the best people to talk to in the SOJC.
lectures are sooo boring and she talks extremely slow, but assignments are easy enough
nestly, this class is 50/50 for me. It has a lot of opportunity to be a really good class, but overall, the day-to-day lectures are incredibly boring. However, the guest lectures are really enjoyable

I have really enjoyed this class &honestly disappointed in a lot of these reviews. Prof Cebere showcases artists that a lot of professors would gloss over &readings, videos, guest lectures she curates really are thought provoking. I noticed not many ppl that take this are art majors or seem interested. Every computer has poker or some movie on.

You have to attend every lecture to do any assignments. However they are monotone and last forever, she talks so much about nothing and has no idea what word she is going to say next. I wish I could've put her in 2x speed. Assignments are busy work hates summaries only wants your thoughts then will be upset if you don't reference the reading enough

Genuinely so painful to sit through her lectures. She speaks at the rate of a tortoise and very little of the material is actually interesting. You have to stay the entire class period because there is a quiz on the iclicker website at the very end. The homework is easy but essentially busy work (300-word assignments on Mondays and Fridays).
Overall boring although some of the guest lectures were cool/entertaining. Very easy class just to fulfill another arts and letters credit. If you didn't get an A in this class... that is beyond me
Very boring lectures to sit through. Assignments are long, but straight forward. Attendance is mandatory which is the only reason anyone shows up. Good class to get other work done in though.
Ridiculously boring and poor public speaker for such a large lecture. Seems vindictive of people taking her class for random credit.. it's Art 101 what do you expect from freshmen and seniors
The most boring professor ever. She is so monotone. The class is very easy and you don't really need to listen to her lectures and just do the assignments. Attendance is taken and mandatory.

Friendly and easy to talk to, no problems there. She has a way of speaking about a single bullet point for 5 minutes without actually saying anything. Talks very slow, and spends way too much time on very simple concepts. An easy class to take for credits, but patronizingly simple if you're actually interested in learning about contemporary art.

The class is really easy, but extremely attendance-dependent. There is an initial count of attendance and a quiz at the end of the class that covers the material in that lecture. It was hard staying awake and pay attention to the lectures, but the quizzes and assignments are not hard at all.

Very lecture heavy class, you cannot skip class because your weekly assignment are based on the lectures entirely. There isn't really a final so it's worth paying attention in class and those assignment are majority of your grade.

Agnese overall seems like a kind person, but is obviously very new to teaching in a lecture hall. The grade is made up of reading reflections and one other project per week which alternates between evaluating exhibitions and responding to a guest lecture. They are not difficult, but time consuming and are due on mondays and fridays which is asinine
Great lab instructor! Very communicative and concise when teaching. Talented artist as well

She is a great professor and really cares about her students. She really likes when you go to office hours before an exam. Homework assignments are on VHL and there are a few exams during the semester. Attendance is mandatory and participation is very important. I would 100% take this course again she is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Profe Boyero made Spanish class fun again. Her genuine nature and care for students created a safe learning environment with opportunities for rich discussion and expansion of class material. Although her time at the UO may be coming to an end, I highly recommend her courses to anyone who is looking to learn upper-division Spanish courses.

I had a horrible experience in this class. The professor was not approachable and graded tests with markdowns for every minor mistake, which is not helpful when learning a new language and trying to grasp the whole picture. I was advised by the professor not to continue studying Spanish, but instead studied abroad and minored in it, graduated 2022.

This was one of the hardest classes I have taken in the major, she requires critical analysis and deep thinking, and has a high standard for student achievement. However, she is personable, kind, and funny, and if you really dig in and work hard she is willing to help out and wants to see you succeed. NOT an easy A, but a great experience!

Lara is very willing to help and very patient. She is dedicated to helping you learn and is clearly passionate about what she is teaching. However, the grading could be a bit harsh for the class and she was not always very clear on what she wanted from assignments. But, overall she was well-prepared and a fun professor to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Lara is an amazing professor. Her class is engaging and fun. It was the best Spanish class/ class in general that I've taken. Lara really cares about her student's learning and understanding. She is always willing to help, and will go out of her way to do so. I always felt comfortable speaking in her class because she is so helpful and nice.

She has a lot of patience which is definitely important for a language teacher. She is very good at explaining the material in a straightforward and comprehensive manner, individually AND when instructing the whole class. She makes class incredibly fun by shaping it into an interactive learning environment where we are always conversing.

She is super passionate about Spanish and an incredible teacher HOWEVER grades wayyyy too hard for a 200 level class and out of all the classes I'ver ever taken she's the hardest grader. Sucks because she's so nice and easy to meet outside of class but its very disheartening

I took it during the summer and it was freaking great! She knows A LOT about grammar and her classes are fun because she uses games to get us engaged. I had a fantastic experience and I totally recommend her classes. She's dope.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you make any little mistakes she fails your assignments. Shes horrible. Doesnt help with feedback. I will never take spanish with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Had her for FR 201/202. Hands down, best French teacher at UO. Homework is helpful and not busy work. Her lessons are engaging and sometimes there is no class on Fridays. She's a fair grader and gives good feedback. Always willing to answer questions, is super nice and, very intelligent. Speaks mostly in French but helps with comprehension.

Sarah is amazing! The class itself is pretty tough but shes always there when you need help. Sometimes when I was confused I emailed her about setting up a time and she would always respond quickly and was very flexible about when she could meet. I would really recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected

reviews.comment: Sarah puts in more effort than two other UO professors combined. She knows how to help students in class while not making them feel stupid, and she gives tons of feedback on everything you do. Her lectures are a good speed, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sarah is the best Spanish professor I have ever had. She truly cares for her students and wants all of her students to succeed. She gives amazing feedback on all of the diarios and discussions and is always willing to help outside of class hours. She is probably the most generous profesor I have ever had in my two years in college.

Professor Agou is so relaxed and kind. She responds to emails in minutes most of the time. She always makes class enjoyable. Even the most unengaged students she seems to manage to keep engaged. You learn a lot in her class but it doesnt seem grueling like most spanish classes. Theres a decent amount of homework but none of it is difficult. A+

Naomi is awesome. Really easy to relate to, obviously very smart. She's really good at teaching and keeps the class interesting. For a stats class, she made it really enjoyable. I appreciated everything she did to make it engaging. She's a great teacher!! I wish I had an opportunity to take another class with her.
She was awesome teacher. Her TA's brought the class down, due to the very hard grading. I would take her again if I could. She drops lowest homework and test, if you follow her guidelines.

Naomi is a fun teacher that makes Psychology, let alone statistical psychology, very interesting and engaging. She does a very good job explaining the material, and the quizes are not to hard, but informative enough that you learn something, no final, 5th quiz is make up, as well is the last HW. Awesome teacher, if you make an effort, it's fun!

He is very passionate about what he does. He is a sweetheart and enjoys what he does. He loves to ask iclicker question for attendance and participation so show up. I loved being in class and the way he had us applying what we were learning to our assignments. I am an IARC major and this class reassured me in what path i'm going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty passionate about his career, talks quietly, so you should pay attention. 5 total assignments with an extra credit opportunity. I would recommend this class to anyone, not just in the college of design, good info to know. The only tests are the midterm and final.

Professor Kyu-Ho Ahn seems to have little interest in teaching. His lecture slides are dense, lengthy, and monotonous. Be prepared for the midterm—it's taken directly from the slides and is not open-note. The class average for the midterm was 34, with no apparent curve. Computers aren't allowed, which is fine, but be ready to do a lot of writing.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mandatory attendance for horrible monotone rambling lectures (with iclicker questions), slow grading GE's, worthless assignments, easy midterm and final (open note), required textbook but I didn't use. Maybe the worst class I've taken. If I was an IARC major I would change after this class. Very narcissistic, and he has NEVER practiced.

Professor is very nice and knowledgable. However, if you are not an ARCH major, this course may be somewhat confusing as he never really goes over the assignments in class. GO TO THE HELP SESSIONS - you get extra credit and they teach you how to do the assignments. There are only 5 assignments and two tests. As long as you study, you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IARC 204 wasn't a hard class to pass, and the professor isn't bad. Though I felt the lectures were hard to be intrigued in, potentially because it was 8 am and his voice never changes. PS mckenzie hall stinks sometimes. GE's will grade all your work, and help sessions get you extra credit so go to them.

While this class is really easy because there is no homework and only consists of projects. The midterm and final have absolutely nothing to do with the class or topics we learned. I took good notes every single class and when I took the final that was open note there was nothing that had anything to do with my notes. I do not recommend.

Professor Ahn is a fine professor, he's clearly passionate about design and you will learn a lot in his class. However, he can a bit hard to understand sometimes, so make sure you pay attention to the lecture slides and take notes. All of your work will be graded by his GEs. Works consists of two exams, 5 assignments, and a good amount of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kyu-Ho is a fine professor, that's it. He is most certainly not one of the greats, but if you are an IARC major he's the head of the department, so you're going to have to deal with him. The midterm was overwhelmingly hard with an average of a D, which cemented my distaste for him. Yes, I got an A+, but the class made me angry, and so did Kyu-Ho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: it is a nice n easy intro class to interior Architecture. The grading rubric for assignments are clear and easy to follow. He gives a good amount of time for you to complete the assignments. Also many opportunities to earn extra credit. yes textbook, but his lecture covered like 99% of what you need to know to pass the class already hhh.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The first half of the term was good, but the second half... I fell asleep every class. It was so hard to pay attention because his lectures are hard to follow and he has a monotone voice. Thank god for projects and extra credit though, because it would have been a tough class to pass.

Khu-ho is a great teacher. Super knowledgable, caring, funny, clear, patient + inspiring. He offers plenty of opportunities for help outside of class with projects + really sets you up to succeed if you're present + paying attention.

His lectures can be difficult to follow because of his thick accent. Sometimes he has difficulty explaining himself but the help sessions with the GTFs make the class quite easy. Projects are fun & not hard to get good grades on. Midterm is easy if you take good notes. Kyu Ho can be very funny and is definitely passionate about what he teaches.
Can't understand professors speaking.  Doesn't explain topic clearly and teaching irrelative content to the course.

Kyuho's Performing Art Center studio was my first IARC studio (as an ARCH major). He is very enthusiastic, passionate about design, and excels in his specialty (universal design). He is very thoughtful and put together an excellent and engaging field trip to San Francisco. I felt as though the term was relatively front loaded, but very manageable.

Lectures felt super boring and long, Kyu-Ho is sometimes hard to understand which makes it easier to zone out. Tests weren't too hard, projects made up most of the overall grade. Grading depends on your GTF, mine graded pretty fair and understood that this was our first time doing architecture for most of us.

Test's are as hard as advertised and prof. Ahn can be a little hard to understand when he's explaining assignments.  When it comes to lecture, he's allot easier to understand plus he's actually pretty funny, and clearly passionate about what he teaches.  For those that suck at test (like myself) the projects are a bulk of the grade.

Although somewhat difficult to understand in lectures, he is a really nice person and very understanding. Grades fairly harshly but no different than most professors. Has a good sense of humor and would definitely take a class from him again!
Kyu-Ho is so awesome. He's so excited about architecture, and he's inspiring. He does some amazing hand-renderings.

Really boring lectures and really difficult to understand. Projects are easy, but tests are very difficult. His English skills need some serious work, especially when it comes to writing up assignments.
Worst class and teacher I have ever had.
Grades very hard. I had no architecture experience before taking this class so it was hard to earn a good grade. Kyuho is a good teacher but hard to understand.

As long as you aren't on your phone all class and actually pay attention you'll get a good grade. Ahmad is clearly passionate about teaching, and I always felt like I learned something in his classes. Really nice guy, great to talk to in office hours or after class.

I was worried to take this class as I read that he was a hard grader. That really isn't the case - if you follow instructions and read the rubric you will get 100%. The group presentations kinda suck but as long as you answer the question you will get a good grade. Lectures were long and boring at times but I actually learned.

With engaging course material and lectures, Ahmad is one of my favorite instructors in the CINE program at UO. He is involved in the courses he teaches, no matter what it may be. As long as you keep up with the materials and reach out to him and your peers in class, you will not only do well, but learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ahmad is extremely passionate about teaching and specifically about film. This passion helped me be more interested in the class and the films. He cares about his students and how online learning is affecting them. You get out what you put into this class; watch the movies, go to class, take notes and you will be fine. Highly recommend!

This professor is such a hard grader for absolutely no reason. His grading scale makes absolutely no sense and is not logical. Overall the coursework should be simple but he can not explain things in simple terms and overcomplicates everything. Lacks communication and is rude in any communication he provides.
Great stats prof!!!

Avoid Ahern if you can. Test material doesn't exactly line up with homework material. You pretty much have to teach yourself the lessons because he does not go through lessons in any systematic way. Try to get tutoring for his course if you end up taking him. He will offer little to not help and office hours/emails are lacking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I go to class everyday and still dont understand the material. Very confused during lectures and makes you buy the textbook but doesnt really use the textbook. He is not clear on what to study and when he gives you practice midterms just expect there to be nothing similar to the problems given.

He is not good at teaching and does not fully explain the course material. The stuff he puts on the tests are not even stuff we learned in class. The textbook sucks and he does not even work on it. He does not provide really any study material for the midterms and never responds to his emails.

Does not teach the subject well at all. Messes up constantly in class. Gives homework and quizzes on material he did not cover. Does not project himself while teaching. seems nervous.  I recommended not taking this class.

This class was super interesting. His lectures are easy to follow and slides are good. There are 4 quizzes and 2 exams and that is all you are graded on but if you take good notes and at least skim the readings you will be fine. Having a baseline knowledge/interest in professional soccer will definitely make this class more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was great but the grading is a little rough. Only exams are graded and not engagement so be careful about that.

This class is great but the BIGGEST ISSUE is his GE that helps him grade. He doesn't seem to VALUE any of your engagement work and only depends on his student helper for grading. I feel ashamed for this class because his GE is the WORST grader. Don't take this class if you're Latino and and your Latino professor doesn't back up your work! JUST SAD!

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. the professor is AMAZING BUT he doesn't grade any of your homework! His GE grades all the work and is the WORST GRADER EVER and a POS. She is completely bias with all grading and has a tendency of giving you the same grade ever single time. BEWARE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a good professor and good class. Professor Aguirre is extremely knowledgeable on the information he teaches and it shows, however I wish there was room for more engagement from the class to be encouraged to actually think about the material rather than just write it all down to remember. Only graded on 4 quizzes and 2 exams so beware.

Professor Aguirre is a history legend. He knows his stuff left and right, but he teaches the info in an approachable way. He is very knowledgeable yet very humble. Make sure to attend class, look at the PowerPoints on Canvas (that's where quiz questions come from), and don't use your phone in class! Great man, 100% recommend HIST 382 with Aguirre.

This is a class that desperately needs a discussion section added. There is essentially no room to engage with the material and get a better understanding of it, and the best moment of the class so far has been when a guest lecturer came in and taught who actually prompted us to think about the material rather than just memorize and regurgitate it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was already getting a bad vibe from this professor on the first day after he responded to the class not being away of a current event by asking why we hadn't seen it on tiktok. He treats the class like children but demands respect and full attention at all times. I really regret signing up for his class, and will be careful not to in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carlos is passionate about the topic and knowledgeable. The class is lecture and reading heavy but it's not bad if you space out the reading. Assignments were clear although not much feedback on the assignments given back but that was the GE grading. Focused on major themes and examples of the time and region not memorizing dates and names.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Aguirres' grading policies are no joke, with little to no feedback on an assignment. It also took a long time for assignments to be graded given that only 5 assignments plus participation made up the class. I attended class at 8:30 am every single time and asked lots of questions. I even showed up on my birthday. I got a low grade for it. Boo.

Carlos is a very passionate and intelligent man. Despite this, I found this class to be difficult. It might be the GE's fault but the grading on assignments was literally just a number, no feedback for you to improve on whatsoever. Readings were manageable, but I didn't agree with the teaching methods. Just felt like rote memorization at times.

Keeps class interesting. Had 3 book reports and a midterm and final. Fair grader, but I would have liked a study guide for the midterm (it was only two essay questions). Would recommend this class for someone interested in really learning about latin american revolutions and is ready to put in some work for a grade!

Probably one of the top 5 professors at the University of Oregon. If you are a history major, or just like history, and have an interest in Latin American American Studies, Carlos is the professor to take. He is extremely knowledgeable, witty, and has personal knowledge about most every topic. And he is a great writer. He Cares about students!
This is my favorite professor at the university. If you are lucky enough to get a class with him, be thankful!

Carlos is great! He knows the material so well and is so nice. He is very approachable and understanding of students. Although it was a lot of work, he was a pretty easy grader. I would definitely recommend him.

Carlos is extremely knowledgeable in his area and keeps lectures interesting. He has straight forward notes, however he does not post them online. I did not always keep up on the reading. As long as you pay attention in class that is what matters most. I learned an incredible amount in his class and would recommend him as a teacher to anyone.
Prof Aguirre made the history of modern Latin America one of the most interesing classses I've ever taken.

Carlos is a great professor! His lectures were very interesting, and if you paid attention, took notes and at least skimmed the books you were fine on the quizzes, midterm and final. I would recommend his classes to anyone!

Carlos is a great teacher! I attended most classes, didn't always read, but pulled off the class with a B. The lectures are good (a lot of notes though) and the extra credit movies are a blast. If you do miss class, however, be sure to get notes from a classmate. Review them for quizes and tests. Carlos is VERY knowlegable in his area of expertise
exemplary prof. organized power points, answers in class questions well. friendly. one downfall: assumbed in lecture, that students knew a lot of stuff coming into class that i didn't know
Carlos is the best history teacher at the university of oregon. His lectures are incredibly engaging and very conducive to note-taking. Take a class from Carlos!

Carlos is the man. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. I walked out gaining a ton of knowledge and got a good grade out of it. His lectures were very good, and he made me want to go to class. He even made me think about switching my major to History. My only problem with Carlos was his all essay question final.
Study for the quizes off of the notes he gives you, I never read the book past the first quiz.  THe midterm and final are cake.
Good teacher.  Be ready to take some notes and read a few books, overall, enjoyable class (hist 380)
Incredibly nice man. Good teacher, very patient. Knows his stuff and is passionate about it.
Great teacher!!!

Dr. Aguirre is an excellent teacher with a great sense of humor. His lectures were outstanding and the assignments/quizzes were really easy; he even allowed for a make-up exam and early final. Definitely one of my favorite classes all year.

Carlos Aguirre is one of the most interesting and engaging professors in the History Department.  He's Peruvian by birth and this reflects in, although does not by any means dominate, his world view.  He is also the head of the Latin American Studies Minor Program.  It's worth looking into.
He talks alot about Latin American Politics and rambles more often than not. He once put a lecture topic up on the board and didn't get to it for 50 min in a hour and twenty minute class
No Comments
He was one of my favorites and he was my advisor.
Aguirre is one of the best professors at the UO.  He is passionate about what he teaches, and his passion lights the way for his students.
he is a the real deal-holyfield. He is hella nice, and is excited about anyone who is interested in latin american studies. Real Coo dude!
Gets off track on notes and goes into long side stories.
Great teacher, tough at times but very fair.
No Comments
Great Teacher

No Comments
Amazing lecturer with passionate views. Would reccomend Latin American history to anyone.
No Comments

No Comments
Great teacher.  Be prepared to do a lot of reading and write some papers, but also to get a lot out of this class.

this class assaulted my GPA after getting a low grade for no apparent reason. not sure if it was the GTF's or him, but if you are a 3.5+ student then be very cautious taking these classes. I had A's on all the work but received a B in the course, and he refused to change final grade. LAME policy
great teacher. not that accessible outside of class, but i learned much from the 3 classes i took with him.

Unexpectedbly tough grading for how large the class was (over 200 students). He makes an effort to destroy slackers grades by 'surprising' them with material that could be easily overlooked - so if you want a good grade it's not a good casual class or GPA pumper.
Aguirre is fascinating.  Talk to him after class for the real goods on Latin American politics.  One of the best profs I had at the U of O.

A very good teacher with a clear and truthful view of the world. He is one who will notice if you are smart in class, and appreciates it by calling on you. Seems to give a normal amount of feedback on papers. Term= 2 tests and 1 paper.

Carlos, is a great teacher, he is the type of teacher that covers most of what you will need to know in lecture, so books arn't really required to do well in his class.  I put forth a C effort and got a B+ in his class.
What can I say. Where else can I write a 1800's version of the Communist Manifesto and get 100%! This man is a very good teacher.
No Comments
Professor Aguirre is an excellent professor, and I suggest you all take one of his courses on Latin American history if you can. He's a must see for all of us raging lefties in Eugene.

Dr. Ahland's the raddest. He's kind and is immensely helpful. You have five homework assignments, a midterm, a final, and a research paper. He makes the topic fun and is never not available to help. Definitely take him!
Super interesting and helpful. Learned a lot from his discussion section in LING 301. He makes you want to know everything there is about linguistics!
He's nice
I had him as the GTF, and he made me want to take more LING classes, he was great! had a ton of interesting stories to tell, made class fun. he's one of my favorite LING GTF's by far
He is the bomb!
He knows his stuff.  He is sensitive to student needs and willing to clarify whenever needed.  Very open to student questions and comments.
GTF for this class, teaching the discussion section. very helpful, gives extra info that Payne doesn't teach. Go to the discussions, it does help. Very smart guy and interesting.
No Comments
No Comments
Enthusiastic and knowledgeable, very friendly. Class involves a LOT of memorization, and he has tests every friday. If you really like thirsty thursday, taking a mwf of this class isn't for you.

Fine. The class content and lectures aren't very well organized, and despite being an ENVS 410, I would not recommend it if you aren't environmental science, as its surprisingly very chemistry focused. I haven't found this class super hard, but I never really understand what the main points we're supposed to take away are, so I'm always kinda lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Aoki was a delightful professor! This was her first class and she did a wonderful job. She was flexible with scheduling because around a family emergency and empathetic. In my opinion, the class seems easier for people with more of a Biology/Environmental Science background rather than those with a environmental studies background

Lillian was great! I took coastal ecology with her. This was her first class ever so at times she talked really fast. 7 short answers, 2 group presentations, a term paper, and the final. The class content wasn't "hard" but at times it could be a lot. Attendance is encouraged not mandated. Highly recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Unfair grading for final assessment. had an A+ all term and graded my final project an F unfairly. would not take a class with her again

If you get the opportunity to take an art history class from Akiko Walley, it is a MUST. She is so passionate about her work and gives great lectures about interesting topics. I especially loved the Art History of Japanese Tea Ceremony class I took from here where we made a tea exhibit for the museum! I wish her canvas was better organized.

ARH 350 was the most interesting ARH class ever. You can tell that Walley is deeply knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. The work load though was a bit much and it was hard to understand what the teacher/ TA expected of you. The midterm and finals were split into multiple sections and I honestly think it was too much for the given time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Professor Walley for History of Manga and she was awesome! She lays out the week-to-week workload very clearly, making it easy to plan ahead. Most of our grades were based on the midterm and final but the test questions felt fair and relevant to what we learned in class.

Ms. Walley was a great lecturer who made the class very interesting. Make sure to attend or you will fail but she is a wonderful teacher, very helpful. She also provides extra credit opportunites and gives you a chance to go inside the art museum!

Fantastic lecturer, helpful outside of class. Took her for a 400 level ARH class. Clear deadlines, grading and organization. Complex source material was made easy to understand, and we were graded mostly through the parts of the material that we found the most engaging, comprehensive understanding, and level of work, not just memorization of facts

Akiko Walley's class was different from what I expected, but in a good way. I never got to interact with her in person since the lectures were prerecorded and our discussions were with the GE's. She's easily understood and the material is pretty interesting. However, I feel like the midterm and final outlines were harder than they should've been.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Very intelligent, knowledgeable, and gives organized and interesting lectures. Expect to do work and study, but this should be expected in any college course. Very helpful and willing to meet with you even with over 100 other students in her class.
She makes sure to give you valuable feedback on everything you turn in. There is a bit of writing required for every assignment, but you'll do well if you put effort into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great class!

If you are not interested in art history like me it is a very dry/boring lecture. It literally puts you to sleep. You need to go to lecture since you can use your notes on the final. The final was very tough, you need to know a lot of small details which is tough. Build up your points so you can afford to do poor on the final Would never take again

I loved her class! I highly recommend. Tons of neat information in the lectures and I highly recommend you print the exam slides and take notes on them. Pay attention to everything she's saying, including the descriptions of the objects. It's very important.

This teacher has no respect for her students. I have personally asked her questions and she makes me feel stupid by responding with "I don't understand how you don't get it" and using capital letters or saying that she doesn't believe I did my readings. I took the class for fun and left with no respect for this teacher.

I personally did not really enjoy this class, but I think it was mostly because I really don't enjoy Art History as I found out this term. She's a nice professor, but did not think she was very clear or very interesting.

Lovely instructor who is very knowledgeable and eager to teach. Very quick and clear with responses to questions, and the coursework was very engaging. If you do the work to the best of your ability and listen to her advice/feedback, you should have no difficulty with the course.
Boring class, but the teacher knows her stuff. Sometimes hard to understand but for the most part the assignments are clear and not very difficult.
Good teacher and enjoyable class, but its HAIR DUE, not HAIR DOUGH. DUE not DOUGH. If you've taken a class with her you will know what I'm talking about.

She spends a lot time going over Japanese history. Sometimes her accent is hard to understand, but she is always willing to clarify and she usually writes down any key terms or dates that are not already on the hand-out. Test are essay format and open note. All of the readings this year were online.

She cares a lot about her subject, and is very excited to be teaching. Unfortunately her excitement or accent makes it difficult to understand some key dates and names she mentions. Textbook readings are assigned in a way that it's difficult to get a clear timeline. Midterm and Final are essay-format, must remember specific dates and names.

The best professor at UO ive had so far. Honestly keeping me in the music program here. Amazing lectures that actually make you think and inspire you. The kind of class that will have you doing research outside of class and far beyond the terms end. TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Akiko gives amazing lectures and cares about your success.

Akiko's lectures and knowldege inspired me to join the music technology program at UO despite me originally taking the class as and arts and letters credit. learning the history behind so much of the music I grew up listening to and understanding the context gave me a better appreciation of it. T

It was such a privilege to be able to take MUS227 with Professor Hatakeyama! She is extremely knowledgeable and her lecture slides are engaging and include things that are really hard to find just surfing the internet. I took this class to fulfill an AL requirement and learn more about Elec Music and was not disappointed.

Prof. Hatakeyama is great! She is well-versed in the course topic and eases students into the world of electronic music very well. Reading was very easy, as were quizzes and discussions. The projects were fun while also being educational. She has very bubbly energy and is fun and easy to talk to outside of class. Would highly recommend!

Professor Hatakeyama was a fantastic teacher for MUS 227.  She let us drop our lowest score out of the 2 midterms and the final. There was minimal homework and she provided a lot of of time to complete it. Although we did use an iclicker for attendance points she allows you to miss a couple of classes. Highly recommend taking her class.

Prof. Hatakeyama was great! The tests were a bit difficult, but the lowest of 3 test scores was dropped. 3 excused absences before your attendance wasn't perfect. Perfect attendance = 3% added to your final grade, but absences won't hurt your grade. Audio effects projects were super easy and well explained. Easy arts and letters

I loved Professor Hatakeyama. She was incredibly nice and caring during the COVID situation. She just posted lecture videos twice a week and we could watch them whenever. There were short lecture quizzes, and the midterms weren't bad at all. She even canceled our final and gave us all extra credit. Really nice, interesting material. I recommend!

Akiko is a great professor. She really cares about her students and the material. The tests are just the lecture slides and she gives extra credit for doing the clicker questions. Everyone can get an A in this course. I also found some great new music to listen to from this class.

Very good professor. Extra credit for good attendance. At times a little boring but she really cares about her field and her students. You have a chance to show off the music you've been working on to the class.

Easy class (just show up to lecture & get participation, plus everything in lecture is directly on the midterms). Akiko clearly loves the course topic and it shows in her lectures, she's super nice too. Would recommend
