Prof. Akhtari was amazing this term! Although I am not a stem major, nor do I consider myself particularly good at math, Prof. Akhtari structured this course in a way that was easy to understand, didn't involve any large specific concepts, and dare I say interesting.

Akhatari is the best! She's very reachable, encourages you to make mistakes, and doesn't judge. This class was very small, but it make the class feel homey, and it felt more like we were doing math for fun instead of for a grade. It was fun to learn a different approach to math! Take HC241 Math of Choice if you still need a 241!!

Professor Akhtari is a godsend. She honestly listens to her students' feedback, and curtails her curriculum to the needs of said students. She is very knowledgeable and tries her best to help guide you , rather than force you, through proofs and logic. She always answers emails and was very understanding during COVID learning. Take her class.

Akhtari is great! She is also really understanding and gives great hints during office hours on homework questions, although she'll make you work for it. She's really knowledgeable and validates students' mathematical ideas. Exams were sort of long, but fair!

makes it obvious when you ask a question that you shouldn't have making you feel dumb. Bad format in going through chapters. Bad communication. Very smart, but doesn't explain like a teacher should. Feel like grader does more than the professor. Tests/quizzes are difficult and graded hard. Hw is easy
Shabnam is really awesome! She is so sweet! I could tell she really cared about the class, and was really enthusiastic for the subject! I loved her class! If you get the chance, take her class! :)
Lucia is a very fair and intelligent instructor. Always positive and extremely enjoyable to be around. She has traveled the world and shares stories about her travels. Would recommend her for WR90.

She has a certain aesthetic that I do not agree with, however, learning against her style improved my own.  My writing became stronger through her tutelage, culminating in winning an award at the U of O. She was very helpful, somewhat forgetful, has an excellent sweater collection, and her opinion is valuable, moreso since we differ in poetic taste
She's nice, intelligent, a wonderful teacher, well dressed, and most of all a good person.
She's very smart, conscientious, lovely, willing to help, and knows here****!
ugh. hate her grading. no helpful comments. tries very hard to be funny in class and wastes time talking about her personal life.
Aziza is great. She's always willing and available to help you when you need it, and she explains concepts very clearly. She also grades fairly.

Avoid at all costs. without a doubt the worst class i have ever taken. no redeeming qualities. boring lecture, uninformative lecture, stupidly hard final. i essentially taught myself econ because she was unable. i feel bad for her until i think about how horrible the class was then those feeling vanish.
Discussions are optional... which is nice. basically taking notes is pointless because she posts the powerpoints on blackboard.  Midterms are sneaky tough, but the final is not cumulative.

I would definitely nor recommend her class. She is not a good teacher at all. She stutters like 70 times in a span of 5 min. sayings things like "uhhhh", "umm", and "like". Whenever she is asked an intellectual question , she has a typical response of "I'll look that up for you", which means that she teacher.

I feel bad for her, she is trying but clearly has no experience. Reads the powerpoint and doesnt interact at all. Very hard to learn from her. Pretty much better off reading the textbook. She does curve very nicely and drops a quiz score so you still get a good grade even though you have no idea what you learned.
No Comments

She is very nice professor, definitely an upgrade from Mark. You don't get to keep your old exams and only have one lab to review post exam which makes studying difficult (imo). The assignments don't reflect the difficulty of the exams, but reviewing the pre-lecture videos does help a bit.

Such a refreshing professor to have after 212. Only thing is that lectures are reverse classroom which makes motivation to go to class difficult at times. Opportunities for extra credit are decent to make up points on exams/pre-lab "pop" quizzes. Super friendly professor as well!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor, but the content in the lecture does not match the assignments or test difficulty. In class, questions and quizzes were easy, but worksheets and exams gave questions that were of much higher difficulty than what we learned in class. The lab is slightly boring, but it was good for learning concepts that were taught in lecture.

Dr. Connolly truly made me love learning again. I started to hate bio after Mark but she and Tobias from 213 made me love bio again. She is extremely caring and such a good professor to learn from. I would totally take another class with her again.

Amy is really sweet and smart, but frankly not very good at lecturing. Lectures are long and boring, and she posts videos covering the content before so they're kind of pointless. There are so many assignments it's difficult to keep track of them if you're a self studier like me. The two midterm exams + final aren't bad, your lowest is dropped

she's super sporadic when she talks and not very well spoken. lectures are pointless since she uses videos recorded from covid as her way of lecturing. labs are boring and she's overall just not a well spoken professor

Any general biology class is pretty tough, but Amy was the best professor out of all of the terms I have taken and was a great professor to end the sequence with. She was way more down to earth and understanding towards students, and really gave time for you to ask questions and figure out practice problems during the lectures.

Amy is great at explaining topics and cares for her students. She has two grading options: take the 3 exams and have your lowest exam grade dropped or do well on the first two midterms and you can skip the final. Do the practice sets she posts! They prepare you very well for the exams (and sometimes questions in the problem sets are on the exam).

Amy is the best. She tries to learn as many names as possible and she really tries to get to know her students, especially during her office hours. There are lots of opportunities to increase your grade with assignments, and she is happy to help you through them.

Never have I had a prof. who asked each student for their name and tried to remember them. She is the sweetest human being and I loved the way her class was structured. Lecture videos were straightforward, and in class she goes over problems to deepen comprehension. Though the labs felt unnecessary aside from the last two.

Amy is such a great professor and takes her time to really make sure that her students understand a concept. The class itself is very rigorous but her pre lec videos help a lot and it is nice that you have two attempts on the quizzes which you go over in class. She drops lowest grades and does what she can to help your average. Very test heavy too

Best online class I've had after spending all of 2020 online.  Lectures are clear and informative and go at a reasonable pace.  If you pay attention to all the videos and take notes then exams and quizzes are simple.  Overall a nice person.

Loved her. The class is really what you make of it with lots of office hours and optional (but you should really study them) practice problem sets. Lectures are very clear and organized with only the content from the last "unit" feeling a little throwaway. The best part though is that if you study a lot for and do well on the two midterms, no final

I am currently taking BI 214 online. I have met Dr. Connolly multiple times in person and I think she is a very kind person (this might sway the way I feel about her as a teacher). Generally, she is organized and the class is set up in a way that each way is similar. I know when things are due and where to get help. Great teacher, interesting class

I have taken this class twice by Dr. Connolly. Last term when I took it, it was really rough because of how difficult the exams are compared to the lecture material. Now during this term you'd think I would do better since I've already taken it, but the average test scores are always below a 70% and it sucks that A students are now getting Cs/Ds.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. C was maybe one of the best STEM profs I've had at UO. She had clear and concise lectures & lots of practice problems and office hours. She showed us that she cared, and didn't want to set us up for failure, as is the case in certain classes. Always willing to explain concepts. If you put in the work, practice, and attend OH, you will do well.

You'll be able to pass if you do everything due and work on the practice worksheets. We were only graded on labs, quizzes, and two exams. Prof. Connolly is super nice and made things very simple to understand. We were able to go back to exam questions. This class was easier than BI212, and if you know some ochem is pretty easy.

Not the best class, not the worst class. I would rather have taken this course from another professor. Most of the grade was from the tests. If you're an anxious test taker, this is not helpful. She was not accommodating around covid. I got very sick and asked for an extension. She got back a week later to say she can't. Very bad at communicating

I've seen a lot of bad things about Connolly from last term, but she must've listened to the complaints, because she's way better this term. The tests are reasonable and similar to the labs/lectures (you can go back to questions). She seems really sweet and her lectures provide a good level of depth without being too confusing.

I felt like she was very unaccommodating during COVID (multiple students complained about being unable to go back to previous questions on the tests). Tests had things we hadn't seen before on them. Don't take this online. I thought I had a B- at the end but she changed the grading cutoffs immensely without telling us so I got a C+, so frustrating.

Professor Connolly was very unaccommodating during the Covid-19 situation. We were unable to go back and check our answers during an exam on Canvas. I experienced some technical difficulties during the course, but these were not taken into account in the final grade. I don't recommend anyone taking BI214 online.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biology 214 is a tough class and the material is challenging. Dr Connolly presents the material in clear and concise lectures. I appreciated the time she took to understand my questions and explain the answers. She is very approachable and knowledgeable. You can see that she cares about her students' success in this class and on the mcat.

Dr. Connolly seems like a great person, and very smart, but does not teach in high enough standard to how hard her tests are. Lectures are a bit all over the place, and we are only graded on tests, and quizzes, and reports. No grade for attendance, no grade for homework, no extra credit, no way to make up being an anxious test taker really.

Prof Cononolly is very smart and cares about her students but the way in which she goes about teaching is not ideal to learning whatsoever. Teaches in a very simplistic manner and proceeds to give ridiculous test question. Does not provide good practice for problems that are complex as on her tests. Great person not the best teacher.

Prof Connolly is obviously entirely infatuated with the process of learning. She is clearly the most knowledgable person in the classroom, but she considers all new contributions made by students significant. I took History of the Natural Sciences in the Western World and it was most definitely my favorite class that term. A gem of a prof!!!

She's kind of a hot mess and all over the place. Quizzes didn't get graded until week ten, so that's how long it took to get a vibe for our grade. Her rubrics not super clear, and she has to get emailed like 7 different times to post the notes, 2 weeks after the lecture and a day before the exam. The class is super freaking easy; just kinda a mess.
super passionate and knowledgeable, really awesome professor. Kinda of a messy canvas but super flexible and amazing class.

Stasiewicz is a great lecturer, who's passion and knowhow shines through in her lectures. Unfortunately, disorganization of the course and the final exam put a really bad taste in my mouth, and I wouldn't be able to recommend. She said the final would take 2.5 hours, took me 7 and a friend in the class spent 10, no feedback or grades were given.

Very accommodating and accessible outside of class but this class is really quantity over quality in terms of assignments. So many big projects, weekly discussion/responses that are all expected to be well researched and cited (including responses) and the final is super tedious. Clear rubrics and reasonable grading but assignments take forever.

I really like her as a lecturer and person but she is definitely disorganized. There's a lot of confusion about what exactly the assignments are asking for but she is very accessible and responds to questions pretty well. Very interesting class about fire policy though, as long as you ask questions and get clarifications the work isn't hard.

She cares about her students (easy to contact/nice), but was EXTREMELY disorganized. The class calendar was often incorrect and she would not alert the class of errors unless someone asked in class. She announced  quiz dates and then posted weeks late. My friend emailed multiple times to clarify calendar. However, class is easy and she is so sweet

Not great, she cancels/ends class randomly, and abruptly stopped teaching the class altogether. She communicated her leave with strange cryptic messages sent in the middle of the night. Multiple subs taught in her place, and another woman from COLT department permanently stepped in fro the remaining 4-5 weeks.

Amanda's lectures were indecipherable and unprepared, and we lacked any course concepts. I enjoyed the assignments, until our 16-page midterm on "AI bad." She was hospitalized and replaced partway through the term but still sent delirious emails telling us we'd have no more assignments (lie) and to "go out and enjoy the sunshine"???

This is worst class I've ever taken in college. Amanda averaged 30 minutes minutes late to class, dressed unprofessionally (leggings and sweatshirts), and never had a lesson plan. The syllabus changed on a weekly basis, due dates were changed with no notice, and class was cancelled with only 10 minutes to the start time. A waste of time and money.

This is the worst class I've ever taken at UO. She was late to class every day, the syllabus was unclear and kept changing, and we did not discuss the books we read at all in class. When we did discuss concepts, it was primarily her sharing obscure, vague thoughts, never letting the students participate. I'm disappointed I paid for this course.

She often changed due dates for assignments with little to no notice. She was late to class several times with no notice and does not excuse absences. If you don't show up, you probably won't pass. She also rarely updates grades. I think this professor has potential, but is too unorganized at this point to be beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amy is very kind and cares about her students. One of my quizzes had been regraded on accident and she was responsive and able to change it back quickly. There is a few homework assignments during the week, then a quiz and discussion board for the weekend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: shes amazing. take her if you can

Had her for SPAN203 Online (summer 2025). Professor Costales is one of the best professors I've had in the Spanish program - hands down. She tailored the material in the online class to her and the students interest - creating interesting assignments that make you want to do them - and learn as well. Was very accessible and would reach out as well.

This was the first in-person Spanish class I've had here at the U of O, and she's amazing! Professor Costales is thoughtful to many of the students in the class, and having it take place in a small class size helps it even more. She has homework daily, but outside of that, there isn't much given out, and a lot of the work is pretty open-ended.

Not a hard class, but has way more homework than any both 300 level Spanish class I have had. The class is very unorganized and due dates were changed often. Assignments were posted late sometimes and weren't graded for weeks at a time. Amy is a very caring teacher and very flexible, but the class was so unorganized it made very frustrating.

Dude she's an awesome teacher, really caring, nice and reallly flexible. I had fun in her class, her lectures are really niche topics but easy to understand. She does a hell of a job of getting to know you and understand you as not just her student but as a person. Disregard the person that rated her a 1, they js dont understand her frfr

The most disorganized class I have ever taken. Nothing was graded until week 10. Homework was due right before class, but sometimes not released until late the night before. No syllabus, so I didn't know if we had homework, quizzes, or finals. The course was nothing like what the description said it would be about.

Profe Costales is amazing and cares a lot about her students:) She is super passionate about what she teaches and I learned so much in her class that I know would not be taught in other classes. Homework and exams are straightforward if you pay attention in class (which is never boring).
Profe Costales is hilarious, caring, and easy going. The class and content of the class was very interesting. Lots of reading and homework. Be prepared to share in class.

Loved Profesora Costales' class. She really genuinely cares about each of her students and experiences. She's very funny and very passionate about her lectures, and the 50 minute class period always flew by.

I loved her class she is a great professor in my opinion, lot's of fun and super supportive. She does talk fast but I  still was able to understand she was talking about, her class can be a bit disorganized but I think if you are a adjustable learner you could easily understand what is going on. Overall, I would take her class again.

This class has too much homework. It is draining on my mental health. The class asked if we could have less homework each week and it appears we only got more. Nearly impossible to manage with a full schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amy wants to get to know everyone and cares about each student. She asked me why I was talking in class less frequently than I used to and allows you to turn in an assignment late if you need to. She has a chaotic energy, cusses, and is not the most organized but I found these all to make the class more interesting and fun. Was not difficult.

literally my queeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeen ive taken 2 classes with her i honestly don't even know if i took span308 with her they were just heritage classes and she is so accommodating and so sweet i think she made me cry like 3 times she's just to sweet and caring please take a class with her if you can also she's hilarious

So amazing! She teaches super interesting and relevant material that kept us engaged. The class is fairly reliant on participation. She is also very understanding of people's circumstances in these hard times, which is so nice. Very nice and funny as well!

Best professor I've had yet and she's SUPER passionate. I really appreciated the way the class was structured, and how her goal was to make you a more critical thinker. I learned about social constructs and hierarchies that I'd never thought before. I would 11/10 recommend this class. The conversations are also rich and engaging!

Amy is a great professor and person in general. Her class was very well thought out and insightful. The only thing I would say is that she would often not post things on canvas until later in the week, making you have to do it over the weekend even if you had time to do it prior. Overall, awesome prof.

Professor Costales teaches with passion and genuinely acknowledges the limitations of her students. When I struggled to keep up in her immersive approach, she allowed me to write poems in Spanish instead of essays, and praised me when I spoke up in class. I looked to Costales as not just a professor, but a mother figure in my first year from home.

I love Amy! She is passionate about what she teaches and it shows through her lessons. I appreciated that she was candid, she kept it real when she talked about her life and things going on in the world, it made me look forward to going to class. The only thing is that she will call on you unexpectedly, but she's so amazing it's worth it!
Best Spanish Teacher I've Had!!!!! Love the women. Enlightens me with history of Latinx culture, while learning Spanish.

Professor Costales did a great job of connecting various aspects of linguistic history and current interactions of language in contact in the bilingual linguistics class I took from her. She tells her own stories and asks students to share their stories if they're comfortable. She is not a harsh grader, just assigns quite a bit of readings.

She is by far one of my favorite professors at the U of O. She is friendly and easy to talk to. She truly cares about her students! She inspired me to maybe become a Spanish teacher myself. I hope to take more classes with her before I graduate. I wish more teachers were as dedicated as she is. She is respectful to her students and considerate.
Amy is a fantastic teacher. She is interested in what she is teaching and passionate about heritage speakers.

Amy is my favorite teacher so far this year. I really enjoyed her class and the topics we learned were very interesting. She is a teacher and a person that you can easily get a long with. But one down side she may have is that she sometimes isn't really specific about when or how projects are due.

Amy is probably the most ideal perfect professor you could get. She is so nice and gets to know all of her students on a personal level and it is awesome. The class is super easy, do the webwork (maybe 10 min max a night) and other assignments on time and get an A. Amy is the BEST
Amy is the by far the best Spanish professor you could get she helps tremendously and will do everything she can so you understand the material. She's also really funny and a good person in general

By far my favorite teacher at UO. She is hilarious and interesting and you can tell she really cares about her students. She does challenge her students but is very fair with grading. If you want to learn a lot and have a fun, hilarious teacher, take a class with Amy! You will not regret it.

AMY IS AWESOME! I wish she was still my teacher. SHE CLARIFIES THINGS IN ENGLISH! She calls on you (which I HATE, but she never makes you feel stupid or bad when you butcher things so it's actually very helpful) If you have the chance to take her class, DO IT
She is nice! But you have to study outside of class.

Amy is one of the best, most creative, and most effective teachers I have ever had. She has a way of making students feel comfortable and confident attempting to speak a new language! Class was a blast, and I learned more from Amy than with any of my other three Spanish professors!

If you want to get an easy A, take this class with Amy. If you want to learn spanish, find another instructor! She is fun, outgoing and makes having a full course load less stressful; however, she is extremely unorganized and sometimes wouldn't even show up for class. Luckily I had some prior spanish knowledge before taking her class.

Absolutely fantastic professor. She's super laid back, but doesn't make learning spanish feel like a chore. You'll find studying is hardly necessary because you learn so much in class and it comes so easy! TAKE THIS CLASS.
I took Amy's class Fall term. I think she is a good professor and is a fair grader. If you are passionate about Spanish and/or Latin America then you will enjoy this class

Amy is truly an awesome teacher. She is clear and concise, nothing's a surprise; which is especially true for tests, she does a great job preparing the class for them. A very animated and outgoing person. She will call on you, but if you mess up, it's no big deal- she'll help you get it right. Great availability outside of class and a fair grader.

If you have the chance to take a Spanish class from Amy, DO IT. Honestly, don't even think about it. Just click "register". She really understands how to teach a language and she makes the class easy to wake up for.

I hadn't taken Spanish in 4 years and hated the language before this class because of my last teacher. Amy got me to love it again and is a great teacher. Because of her I have considered making Spanish a bigger part of my college degree and Im going abroad. She is absolutely wonderful. Best teacher Ive had at the University.

She is energetic, fun, and a great professor. She is always available out of class to help, and it's almost impossible to fail her class. Had a lot of fun learning Spanish, and improved a lot as well.

I love Amy, but I don't feel she was prepared to teach a 300-level class. It is possible that her lack of organization stemmed from the fact that this was the first time this class had been taught, but it was still annoying. Having said that, she is hilarious and extremely passionate about her subject. I hope the class is better in the future.

She is extremely energetic and makes you excited about spanish. It helps that she is so passionate about it and also that she grew up learning it. She isn't so strict about the technical ways, as much as the conversational(like slang). She is always really positive with her comments, she really wants the students to be confident spanish speakers.

Amy is amazing. She is realy energetic and happy to be teaching. She is a crack up in class, and really gets the students engaged. She doesn't go too fast and is totally availible for help. She even helps you with stud tips for the tests. Which arent hard, and she's pretty leniant. Overall I loved the class, and she was a great professor (:

She's a pretty good professor and definitely helped me improve my Spanish. One plus is that she's Latino herself so she knows about the culture. But, because of this, she often is very opinionated when discussing Hispanic countries' history. Also, it seems she's not too much of a blonde fan either.
Wonderful teacher, very engaging and helpful.

Amy is a fun spanish teacher. She tries really hard to engage her students. At times she can be overwhelming and in your face but she has good intentions. She is an easy grader and always available to help her students.
Amy is a great Spanish teacher for beginners. She will use english on occasion, especially if she sees that youre struggling. She is generally easy-going and a lot of fun.

Exams which are long and very tough make up 80% of your grade. The other 20% is almost guaranteed if you complete homeworks and attend discussion. Cook's office hours are often more confusing than needed and make students feel degraded for not being up to her standards. She blames students and refuses to make exams easier when the average is a 55%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cook is a good professor but she makes you work very hard for a good grade. Lectures are packed with content and I honestly have never seen a faster writer than Cook. Grades are very test heavy making up 75% of the final grade, but the other 25% is almost guaranteed if you show up to discussion and complete the HW.

This class was very challenging. The homework and discussion work was always a bit confusing and I always had to go to office hours to work it out. The textbook didn't really allign with anything we did so all of the material was coming straight from the lectures. Cook was pretty fair and was really informative if you went to her office hours.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. The topics are very hard and she does a great job of making it very clear of what we're supposed to learn and how it makes sense. I don't think I would have done as well in this class if it was any other professor. She also gives advice on how to study- use it!

Dr. Cook is a tough professor with very tough, long, and mechanism-focused tests. Some questions on the final were worth way more points than others, with one of the questions being worth 30 points. However, she also grades fairly and has helpful lecture notes. If you take this class, I recommend following along in the textbook and practicing a lot

Professor Cook gives really tough tests. She expects you to have a LOT of information memorized. Skipping class will definitely set you up for disaster. Discussion sections are very helpful and are crucial to doing well in this class.
Dr. Cook makes you work for it. Her exams are tough and the averages tend to be low but she curves generously. I learned A TON and I am definitely a better organic chemist after taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the second term of o-chem (for majors) with Amanda. She regurgitates the book and fails to explain why reactions happen. We were left to attempt memorizing reactions, reactants, and products. She gave us minimal practice with synthesis and tests only have synthesis questions. Avg test scores: 62% & 49%. A reflection of her teaching ability.

Never gave extensions even for family emergencies. Homework was due before the entire chapter was finished, so you are required to go read the entire chapter to do the homework, but most of the chapter isn't useful. Exams are different from any practice problems or reviews done. And you have homework due at 10am following an exam till 8pm yesterday
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took second term O Chem with her, and she was organized and new the material well. It is a difficult concept and there are a lot of synthesis problems, which may be difficult unless you have practiced until it clicks. She is more than happy to schedule individual office hours and is here to help the students learn. Only used text to review.

Took African Dance Aesthetics, super easy class as long as you show up and at least skim the readings (enough to comprehend most of it), few quizzes, one discussion presentation, and one final dance project with peers which is super fun. highly recommend. Amy is very understanding and asks for feedback to make sure we're doing alr with the workload
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overly critical grading. Preaches how all dance must be viewed and reviewed diffrently but penalizes it in grading. Preaches valuing all forms of dance equally, but spends the majority of the course talking about modern and postmodern dance.

This class is a great way to satisfy an Arts and Letters credit if you have any interest in dance at all! There is a substantial amount of reading assigned for the class, and it is essential that you keep up with it. That being said, if you complete the readings and take notes, the class should be fairly light. Super caring professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing class that mixes history with dancing! I'm a buisness major that had no prior dance experience, but this class accepts students of any skill level including beginner. I had a lot of fun and learned lots and I reccomend taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Tachine is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had, she genuinely cares for her students and their success. I really enjoyed taking this class with her. She made the lectures and discussions extremely engaging and interesting, and I took away so much from this class.

Dr. Tachine was by far my favorite professor during Winter Term. Even though the class was at 8:30 am, she made the class so interesting and exciting that it made you actually want to go to the class. She makes a point to connect with all of her students and has a very clear teaching style.

Dr. Tachine is the sweetest person ever, and even though the class was at 8:30 am, she was so energetic and made the class fun that you didn't even notice how tired you were. I highly recommend this class!! It was also extremely interesting.

She is the sweetest, kindest soul you will ever meet. She is an amazing, engaging lecturer who truly cares about her students. Her attention to every person in the room is moving and impressive. I loved her and would feel honored to take another one of her classes.

Prof. Tachine is one of my favorite professors here at UO. She is new this term but did a fantastic job teaching and being interesting. As long as you do the work you will succeed and she will help you with whatever you need. Highly recommend!

Amy is a great professor, and really cares about her students and teaching. However, the tests can seem harder than you would expect in an Intro to Management class, and they are worded not as directly as you may expect. Understanding the material and how its seen in the real world through scenarios is more important than knowing a definition.

Amy is in my opinion the best teachers at LCB. She is so engaging while lecturing and really cares about your professional success and development (thus the class and her methods reflect this heavily). Professionalism is HUGELY IMPORTANT in this class and work diligently on your group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amy is probably the best professor for MGMT311. She's pretty nice, though her lectures are hard to stay attentive during. I thought the exams were hard to study for, as her slides are more visual than informative. I don't recommend her if you want to cut corners in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amy is so nice! She is definitely a tough grader, and it will be almost impossible to get a good grade with her unless you go to her office hours. That said, her feedback is very helpful. She is an engaging lecturer, and you can tell she does care about her students.

Amy has been a great professor and is super personable with students. Her lectures in BA308 are very informative and she tries to get students out of their comfort zone in a constructive and positive way by having the class work in a group setting. She's very particular about grading, so be prepared to include extra relevant details in assignments.

Amazing professor with easy assignments. Similar to BA 308 you'll have a team to work with and complete assignments but their easier than what BA 308 required. You also don't need to do a end of the term presentation!

This class is the sole reason why business majors get bad reps. The most pointless class you will ever take. 2 group projects can easily be Bsed and the textbook is necessary to do HW. Attendance is mandatory except for 3 excused absences.

Amy is a professor who cares a lot about her students. She is a harsh but fair grader and will mark you down for being late/on your phone. If you contribute to class discussions and og to office hours, you will get along very well with her. Make sure to hand homework in on time as well as there is no late homework allowed.

Amy is my favorite teacher. This class is group project-based. Go to her office hours frequently, participate in class discussions, and meet with your group often. Amy is a hard grader so I would meet with her for feedback. Don't be late to class or be on your phone because she'll mark you down for that at the end of the term!
The best teacher I've ever had. She can be a tough grader and has high expectations but if you ask quesitons and use her office hours it is much easier.

Amy is a great person and professor but she grades surprisingly harsh. very nit-picky and often too much. likes it better when you lie on assignments and write a ton than speaking the truth concisely. super accessible outside of class and always around to help.

Amy was an amazing professor to have, she really took her time to make sure everyone was on the same page and that you understand the topic at hand. All the midterms are online and take home open book/Note. I took her for Management: Value through People BA 316. Overall I think Amy is the best professor in the school of business.

Has a fun engaging energy. Clearly cares about her students and their learning. She does nitpick a bit when it comes to grading and class policies but is willing to have a dialogue with students and if you can make your point effectively she will be willing to change her mind. I do believe she is some of the best UO business school has to offer.

As long as your put in the effort for Amy's class, you'll get a good grade. Plan to participate in class discussions (raise your hands) and visit her during office hours twice a week (as a group or individual). When you're able to get feedback on your work several times before actually submitting the assignment, take advantage of it!

Although BA 308 will be difficult, you want to take it with Amy. If you follow examples provided in class, closely adhere to the rubric, and put in time and effort, you will do just fine. Amy is super funny and really cares about your success. She is practical and made 2-hour classes enjoyable. Friends w/ other teachers struggled way more!!!!

Took BA199 pass/no pass for the BizARC, and I am so glad to have gotten to know Amy. Take the time to get to know her, she just wants to see her students succeed. After talking with her during class for a term, she has already gone out of her way to recommend me for internship opportunities. Easy, unnecessary class, but glad to do it with Amy.

Amy is an amazing teacher and really knows how to work the room- found myself actually listening to her lectures. This class just genuinely sucks, lots of business writing, whole class is basically a group project with a final presentation at the end. if you get a good group its easy. if you can, take amy for ba308.

VERY tough grader! She's a nice person but the class just sucks. BA308 made me change my major. It's a big group project and a ton of work outside of class. Still, Amy is a solid teacher and was very helpful and responsive when I missed the last week of class due to a family emergency. If you have to take this awful class, Amy is a decent choice.

I LOVED Professor Nuetzman. She was clear, fair, and flexible when life happened. She even wrote me a letter of recommendation for an upcoming job interview. She is a tough grader, but you actually respect her more for it, and she makes you a better businessperson by the end of her course. If you do your share of the group project, you will pass:)

The course page (on Canvas) is not well put-together. The grading criteria, while stated for each assignment, is NOT CLEAR. Mandatory attendance for every class. Do NOT buy class materials before course begins. I don't like Amy personally due to her behavior towards me for missing a class (w excused absence), but she's an okay teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: BA 308 is mainly focused on group work. Although you do get individual assignments. Although she can grade tough, if you put in effort, you'll do fine. Class is mandatory and some of the lessons may feel useless, however she is the prof you want to take this class with (heard other profs are very strict and even tougher with grading). Overall great

BA 308 is one big group project. Attendance is mandatory but we do not even do anything helpful in class and we never get time to work on our group project. She grades incredibly hard; Ive never seen anyone get full points on canvas averages. When my group went to her for help, she literally said "No!" with a smile. so rude and expects so much
She is a really nice person but one of the harshest graders I have ever seen. She will never give you full points for anything. she expects wayy too much from her students. Prepare to get a B max.

They are a very nice professor but the class is basically based on a group project. If you have a bad group, well good luck. If you dont show up to class your group will most likely be upset and might recent you UNLESS YOU COMMUNICATE! Have a good group relationship for a good term.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Overall, I really enjoyed Professor Nuetzman. She definitely has high expectations and will make you work hard for a good grade. She is really approachable and gives a lot of feedback which is helpful. Get ready to do group projects and do a lot of writing if you take BA 308. I would recommend her for sure!

Excessive amount of homework (15-20 hrs a week), weekly group projects, extremely hard grader (no one gets above a B, docks points for EVERYTHING, considers a 90% to be perfect). I hate everything about this class but it is required. Good communication and interesting lectures, but the class requirements are horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The best teacher I have ever had. Very clear explanations, great discussions around the questions asked. Students are very comfortable and not afraid ask questions. Knowledge & skills I learned are very valuable for the current university education, & will also be extremely valuable for the rest of my life. Would love to have her as a teacher again

Amy was extremely helpful and passionate about what she was teaching. In class she presented interesting material and our assignments out of the class actually improved our learning habits. Also, extremely sweet and nice!!
Great teacher. Highly recommended!
Critical Reading was a very helpful class. There is a reading every week and one assignment due every week. There are not tests but an in-class writing every week. Great teacher, very helpful.
Amy is the BEST instructor at the UO! She expects alot from you in her classes but in return you learn alot. She is highly recommended.

Nicest teacher I think I have ever had. Always so pleasant and understanding. I learned so much useful information in her class. This is the best class that I have taken by far. Especially recommend to anyone having difficulty writing papers, taking tests, etc. Provides many strategies and useful information that is extremely helpful. Love her.

Amy gives a lot of very useful skills that really do help you read a lot faster. Since there's a lot of practice that you have to do in class and out of class, you really get to practice the skills a lot. She's also very nice and extremely good at names, which makes you feel included.
If you have a chance to take a class with McGuffie DO IT. She is so amazing and you will learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures are hands-on with group discussions and very informative. She knows her stuff and will give clear feedback on assignments.

CINE 112 - beware if you wanted to take this course for an easy extra class or elective, she required 30 hours per week. it is so much work for a 100 level course, so if you have a job or are taking other summer courses i would suggest not taking this.

Mrs.McGuffie is an amazing and incredibly thought-provoking teacher, as someone who is not majoring/minoring in Cinema, this class was very insightful and interesting. Class material and theories are complex and can be hard to fully understand at times, being it is a higher level class, she puts a lot of effort into making sure everyone understands

Professor McGuffie really cares about her students and their well-being. She is a phenomenal professor here at UO and I recommend every student and major take one of her courses. She does require lots of work to be done before in person class and lectures, however it is helpful to understanding what's going on in class. She's amazing!

McGuffie integrates extremely far-fetched and downright NONSENSICAL claims into her ENG 381 lectures. She theorized that the strobe lights in the 20th Century Fox theme are "representative of phallocentrism" given their shape... also said the same regarding the barrels of guns in a superhero movie scene?? Very irrational, could not take seriously.

One of the best professors I've ever had. So understanding of life outside of school, great and interesting lectures. Really changes the way I watch films now. Literally one of the sweetest professors ever. Clear grading criteria, lots of in-class discussions. I really wanna take more classes with her! I can't recommend her enough!

Dr. McGuffie is definitely one of the most passionate and caring professors I've encountered at UO. Her lectures were insightful, and opened my eyes and changed the way I watch films. She consistently made sure to check up on her students and remained flexible if circumstances arose. I have the utmost respect for her!

Trans* & Cinema is my fav CHC class I've taken so far. 11/10 recommend it. She is an incredibly passionate professor and made every class fun. The material was rich and eye opening, and it was a breath of fresh air to take a film class. It taught me a lot about not just film and media but about trans/enby/gnc life and I appreciate that the most!
Loved this class and Prof McGuffie is awesome!

Professor McGuffies CINE381 class has radically changed my perspective on the world. Concepts that seemed too alien to comprehend came far easier with the aid of Cinema and her guidance. Incredibly understanding of the chaos of being a student. Has the highest emphasis on actual learning that will carry with you far beyond the class.

AMAZING- he is a great teacher. Some hefty reading assigned for a few of the weeks, but in general the work is gonna be manageable and interesting. Like others, agree that participation is a big part of the class, so def do the readings, try to be active. Had interesting guest speakers from europe come to talk with us.

Professor langstaff is wonderful, some of the best class discussions ive had! A lot of history mixed with recent articles and things from the news. I think this was a really reasonable amount of work. Not too many readings for the requirements it fulfills.
A great teacher and lecturer. He is clearly passionate about what he does. Also wrote my rec letters and helped me with grad school even though I only took this one class of his. Would recommend!

As a teacher, he is great. His lectures are interesting, and he is passionate about what he teaches. Organizationally, however, he is awful. Due dates are random and sometimes inconvenient. His class feels disorganized at times, so just be cognizant of that before signing up. His lectures for 410 were also discussion based, so be prepared to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The due dates were pretty inconsistent and random, but other than that I really liked all of his lectures and felt like the class was engaging and relevant to lots of different majors/interests. There's a few quizzes and they're super easy because he gives you a study guide with the quiz questions on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The courses discussion format was a fresh air for me as a soon to be senior. I enjoyed how he challenged us every class and didn't see any answer as wrong. I learned so much and felt like it made me more passionate about my area of study. After reading his reviews, I def think he should stick to teaching upper div courses that are more interactive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring & lack relevancy. He gives random group assignments to be done in class and then is the first person to leave the classroom while students stay working. Evident that GEs can't stand him/understand his teaching. He has assignments due on Sunday at 9am or 5pm or Sunday. If this was my 1st glbl class, I would've changed my major.

This was one of the most unorganized classes I have ever taken. He really does not know what he is doing  The GEs basically run the class but they aren't that great. Due dates are all over the place. There is no info on his lecture slides making them hard to follow and he didn't post the syllabus until week 4. Avoid him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Alex Langstaff is the best professor I ever had, coming from NYU shows how smart this man is he cared so much about us during his class, took time to meet with students outside of class and helped me out through times when I was struggling 100/10.

Alex Langstaff is a new professor, and it shows. He has lectures both days that his class takes place, and he has quizzes every Monday. His slides can be difficult to take notes from, so beware of that. He has weird due dates for homework (examples include Friday- 9am, Thursday-6pm, Friday- 11 am) and he will assign homework over fall break.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Langstaff is a very nice person that is well in tune with the life of a college student. He is a young, relatively new professor. Lectures werent particularly engaging but important material. Weekly quiz accompanied by a helpful study guide. Look over and fill it out or you wont do well. Cancelled class during Thanksgiving that was nice!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: WAYYYY to much busy work and cases for a simple class and her GEs lack communication skills

Interesting concepts were discussed in this class but for a simple 100 class that's online-- there was far too much work. I understand that it's important to have live/weekly engagement for a class but that defeats the point of taking an asynchronous class. It was doable but very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Gash seems passionate about the topic and the lectures are interesting, however, for an online 100 course, the amount of work required is astounding. Weekly required engagement activities felt like a waste of time. Papers are 50% of the grade but are graded incredibly harshly (the highest was a 94). Quizzes are subjective and ultra-specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class off the bat was way too much work for an intro class. The assignments were hard to understand. The quizzes were subjective to answer based on the Professor's opinion and if you disagreed you got the answer wrong. The class was the most time-consuming class I took this term. Personally this class is one of the worst classes at the U of O.

The class content itself was interesting and informative. The assignments, tests, and essays are far too complicated and take so much time to figure out with bad grading criteria. Rubrics are filled with unfamiliar terms to an almost intro course. 2 weeks there was a 4-5 page essay, a 500 word paper, a one page paper, and a quiz due within 2 days.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loved this class, and Dr. Gash seemed so interested and passionate about everything she talked about. It is reading heavy, but it is about important and very interesting topics.

A shame I couldn't have her class in person. She is very knowledgeable and I enjoyed her video lectures. She made an effort to connect with us with weekly zoom meetings which I appreciated. However, her instructions and grading criteria were unclear, and she assigned a lot of unnecessary readings. If I ever have her again I will be more prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--So many papers--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Although the GE I got for my section proved to be an extraordinarily hard grader, Professor Gash is a truly inspiring and understated professor. This course was taken solely online and required no more than a 1-2 hour weekly commitment to complete everything needed for the class, something truly sought out in COVID.

The workload for this class was pretty heavy. The readings and lectures are long, but most were engaging/interesting. I wish the class was not online. Dr. Gash was really interesting though. I enjoyed going to her engagements activities! She assigns a lot of work but is fun to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Gash is very knowledgeable and a great person to learn from about these subjects, my only problem with the class is that many of her quiz questions seemed like common sense but were based on statistics so you have to really pay attention to lectures. Also, many of her online lectures were reused, I'd only recommend her for in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gash is super intelligent and DEFINITELY knows what she's talking about. That being said, a lot of Canvas was from last year, so it wasn't updated. I get that she has a bunch of classes, but sometimes it felt like she was too stressed to talk with me about assignments or email me back. A BUNCH of work and tests were actually very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ok so this class was probably one of the hardest I have ever taken. BUT it was a great class and I learned a lot from Dr. Gash. All classes were really engaging and we had great discussions. Reading was a bit overboard and we never got to talk about it all. The final exam and paper were insanely difficult though. I ended up taking P/NP
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was in Gash's 275 and 106 course in fall. She is great. I wish I could take more classes with her. Also, I think the number listed as the average on RCP is wrong. It says 3.9 but looking through she has mostly 5s. Average should be more like 4.3 by my calc.

Professor Gash is super accessible to her students. It seems like she is always on her computer and responds to emails on weekends. It feels like she cares. Gash's lectures are inspiring. I learned a lot, even on zoom. I also love that she connects us with alums. Lot's of work tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gash is a great prof. You should take her classes even the ones online. She's tough but really smart.

This was an online class. Professor Gash is a great lecturer. I'm used to having her in person which is even better but the video lectures are super interesting. Loads of work. But a good mix of news articles. Definitely take this class.

Dr. Gash is an incredibly inspiring person and knows her stuff when it comes to political science. She comes off a bit intimidating at first but you will come to learn that she is one of the most thoughtful and intelligent people youll ever meet. Do the extra credit and study well for your quizzes and you will pass. Would recommend to anyone.

Professor Gash is amazing and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. It was a WEB class and definitely felt a little unorganized at times, but the work load was totally manageable. She gives a lot of extra credit and lets you retake one quiz per term. 100% recommend taking this class, it was very informative and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Gash was phenomenal for PS-106. I didn't have any issue keeping up with the homework, or the minimal participation requirements. Professor Gash had no hesitation to give extensions for papers, which was especially kind during an overwhelmingly awful year. The lectures were incredibly interesting, and I would recommend this class!

She is a good person, but she forgets that she has to grade and see how her students are doing. She is more lecture orientated and does not reply to emails. Don't get me wrong, she is a nice person, but when it comes to grading, you must read what feels like 20 articles per week to pass the exams. Her feedback, though, is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Gash but she made PS106 a pretty hard class and it takes a ton of time if you want to do all the lectures, readings, and assignments. I would recommend this class to anyone passionate about inequality, but do not expect it to be easy and you'll have to set aside a ton of time to be successful.

High expectations but seriously one of the best professors I've had, she made me interested in US politics more than I already was. Explains everything in a way that makes sense. The weekly quizzes have some weird wording intended to make you read closely. There's a group project which was kind of rough due to being online but nothing too bad.

Took this class online during covid. There are 4 quizzes, an essay, a group project, and a few extra credit assignments. The lectures were prerecorded thank god because she can talk really fast. I didn't do most of the reading after the first few weeks. Take down everything on her slides and more of what she's saying and you'll do fine of the quiz.
She was really nice. She let me make-up assignments and responded to my emails. I learned a lot about the court system from her video lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her video lectures are cool, not boring at all like some online classes. The writing assignments are fun but there are a lot. And the group project is kind of a pain to organize. But she is really good about listening to students and getting back to them. Even at night.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Gash is great but the course has too much loaded into 4 weeks. It should be a longer course over the summer. She gives great lectures and most of the reading is about things happening right now. Liked the cases and the videos.
Great lectures. Ton of reading but pretty easy to read. You get to read cases which is cool if you want to go to law school. Writing-heavy but you can choose essays to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was really good at breaking down tough ideas so I could understand them in the lectures. The group project was hard and a couple people didn't do their stuff. Dr. Gash did let us give feedback on how hard everybody in the group worked, so that made it more fair.

275 worked my butt off but I really liked it. The lectures are pretty interesting and the topic is important. Especially if you want to go to law school. Like the other comments say the class has a lot of work.

This class is great if you want to know more about American Law. You should know that it focuses only on US law. The teacher is great. Cool and brief lectures. Theres a lot of work but most of it is easy. Mostly quizzes and essays.

Gash is a great lecturer. There's a lot of work and I had to start really early to get stuff done. Definitely don't take this class if you have other stuff going on over the summer. She expects a lot. But it's definitely worth it if you have the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gash is an amazing professor. Her online PS275 was interesting and she wasn't that hard of a grader, but the work in this 200 level class made it feel like it was a 300/400 level class. There's a group project which isn't a good idea for online classes. Only take this class if you plan on doing a lot of work.

This was a very interesting class and really helpful for understanding what is going on right now. There was a lot of material but if you begin the work at the beginning of the term and follow her schedule it is totally doable. She includes some really interesting videos with the readings. Definitely take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved professor Gash, she makes me proud to be a woman. She is very captivating in her lectures and is always willing to talk. As long as you pay attention to her lectures and stay on top of the course work you can pass easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For a 200 course she made it seem like we were taking a 500 course. I took it online. The amount of material and lectures that she did was way to much and her quiz's were so detailed it was hard to remember everything. She has a clean grading rubric. She barely replies to emails and if she does it's day's later. She was unorganized and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher!! I would take her again and again!!

Professor Gash is passionate about what se teaches, but she seems to spread herself thin. This was a 100 level class and I felt like she just did not give much time or effort into this class. Her lectures slides were pretty useless, and she just seemed unorganized. There were three short quizzes and three 4-5 page papers and thats it.

Dr. Gash is amazing. This was the first poli sci class I took and it has convinced me to minor in the subject. The class is not too hard, do the readings and pay attention to the lectures and you will do well on quizzes. If you want to do well on papers, consult your GTF as they grade them. Take this class you will learn a lot!

I think this was the first time this class was offered.  If she teaches it again, take it.  It was the most useful course I have taken in political science.  Now every time I see a fact I question it.  Really interesting subject. Very timely.  Liked that she used current examples.

Professor Gash seems intimidating but is actually very approachable. She is extraordinarily knowledgable in law and poli sci and her lectures are fun and engaging. Yes, she grades tough. Also takes a while to grade. Her office hours are very helpful!  You have to take her at least once if you're a PS major. Worth the challenge!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: No grade scale, didn't get any assignments graded until week 9. She defintely cares about what she's teaching, but needs better organization. Wouldn't take another class with her. Very vague assignment instruction/grading criteria

This is my third political science class. First one from this professor.  She is really great.  I have learned a lot about inequality. I felt like I came in knowing a lot about inequality but now that I am taking this course with Professor Gash I realized that I had a lot to learn. She is a great lecturer! Take this class!

I really liked this class. The professor is a great lecturer. She tries to mix in real statistics with more general topics--so you actually learn something useful.  The course covers A LOT but she uploads her lectures so it is easier to track.  Reading load is pretty manageable.  I will definitely take more classes from her--one of my favorites so
Totally loved her lectures. She cares a lot about her students, and is always there to help. One of my favorite professors. I would take another one of her classes in a heartbeat.

If you're not into talking about power inequality and civil rights issues in United States - don't take 106. This is more of a discussion class for freshmen to inspire them on their way through next 4 years of college. Skipped lectures and discussion sections - got an A. Beware of some false statistics, and specific agenda. Books are NOT required

She's a very fun professor. Bi-weekly quizzes aren't difficult at all and she seems to really care about her students. Don't buy the books, because you will not need them. She assigns a lot of articles, but hardly any readings from the book. Overall, pretty good Prof.

Very good professor. Very easy class. If you are looking for an easy A well here it is. DO NOT buy the 2 books. I bought them and didnt open them once. They were not on the test so i would stay away from them unless you like to read for fun. A lot of article readings, but you can skim them. Quizzes are kinda tough but just read the powerpoints.

As a 100 level course, this class was pretty easy for me. A lot of readings but I honestly just skimmed most of the stuff and got along just fine. Gash is really cool, I like her style. Lots of small quizzes, but she does a super good job preparing you for them, so they are not hard.
Take any class from this prof.  She is great.  Really interesting topics and readings that are about real-world policies.  Lots of in-class debates.  You will learn a lot and you won't be bored.

This professor is amazing! Doesn't matter which class you take with her, lectures are interesting and engaging. She expects her students to put in the work but she is fair in grading and is always available for questions. Rarely does she not know the answer to a question and if she doesn't she looks it up on the spot! Love this class and the prof.

You have to work, but you'll learn a lot.  It relates to the real world, which I liked.   It's not all writing.  There are also classroom debates, which are fun and make it much easier to understand what's going on.  She's one of the best profs I've had.
I would recommend this class. Prof Gash knows her stuff and does a great job explaining it.

TAKE THIS CLASS! BI weekly quizzes are not too tough just do the reading and be there for lectures. You will want to come to class because Prof. Gash is so amazing and knows what she is talking about. She expects high quality papers but tells you exactly how to write them. I have taken 3 classes with her and you will not find a better professor :)
Great prof.  Great class.  Lots of work. Don't take it if you don't want to work.  Highly recommend.
If I could go back in time and change one thing it would be taking this class.

Was a really interesting class. Freedom to do the final research paper on any supreme court case we chose. Gash provided an in depth look into the judicial system including all of its strengths AND shortcomings. I imagine it would be really interesting to take with recent current events and scrutiny of the judicial system
Dr. Gash can be really challenging.  Lots of readings, but she always reviews in lectures.  She's very approachable and knows her sh%$*.

Also took PS 399 from Professor Gash, and it was great. She is consistent about her teaching style, and is super helpful if your confused, there are definitely no curveballs. She is upfront about expectations, and workload. They were both challenging classes but well worth it.

I wish it was made clearer that instead of a final she expects you to write a 15 page paper.Mine was on a landmark supreme court case and had the opportunity to have two law professors review my work and I still received a B- on the paper.Quizzes are frantic writing nightmares and lectures are as boring as the 900 page book assigned (American Law)
Lots of reading, but awesome class if you're up for it
Had Legal Process with her last fall. Quite heavy on the reading and workload (for a 200-level class), though she was very helpful and very thorough with her expectations.

She seems very dedicated to our learning.  The course was hard with a lot of reading, but she was always available to help and had a way of explaining things that made even the most difficult subjects make sense.

This class had a pretty heavy workload, lots of dense reading. She definitely challenges her students but also is very approachable and great at explaining things in depth if you don't get it right away. Makes you think critically but cares about keeping students interested. She's by far one of the best teachers I've had at UO.

I LOVE YOU DR. PETE. PLEASE TEACH MORE CLASSES. WE ALL MISS YOU. PLEASE. (We yearn for dr. Pete to teach CINE 267. We beg). It was the best of times, now it's the worse of times, Dr. Pete, our lord and savor, save us from this calamity we are facing.

Dr. Pete is the best lecturer on the University of Oregon's campus. He's very kind, his lectures are incredibly engaging, and he's very knowledgeable. The screenings are fun, and I could always tell that he put a lot of effort into what he picked to show. My only complaint with him is that he doesn't teach the other two parts of the sequence.
Lectures were boring but interesting and movies he chose were good. the ge's for the class are really bad though.

Each project is based on whether you completed all the criteria (miss one thing, and you'll receive no credit for it). Personally, I didn't mind this unique system, but was disappointed we never once used the pricey textbook in class. However, Peter clearly cares about his students, and I loved his slides. (Take notes cause slides are not posted!)
Love him down like he's perfect!!!
Honestly really chill guy I only wouldn't take his class again due to his GE's that's were the tough grading comes in
Go to class to take a couple of notes and don't miss out on the viewings!!! He's very funny and inspirational. Really great professor who cares about his students :)

Dr. Pete is easily one of my favorite professors I have had. His lectures are engaging and so easy to pay attention. There's plenty of heads up on assignments and the exams are not difficult at all if you pay attention and take notes during the lectures. He makes the class very fun in general and has a lot of interactive sections of his lectures.
One of the best professors I've ever had, would definitely take his other classes

Incredibly seasoned orator, with powerpoints as polished as a ted talk. For someone self-described as "the porn professor" he's wildly passionate, worldly, and one of the only cinema profs who LOVES movies beyond a shadow of a doubt. Minor legal disputes from 1932 will feel like a goddamn marvel movie the way he paints their intricacies with verve.

Dr.Pete is easily my fav prof. Every lecture is hilarious, and they each dive deep into topics that are easy to understand. However, as others have said, there are only 100 points per term, so it can be challenging to get your grade up if you mess up on just a few assignments. Three papers throughout the term that aren't that useful.

I want to be best friends with him. Most amazing lectures ever and you can tell he cares so deeply about what he is teaching and is so intelligent about the topics he discusses. 10000/10 recommend him and I will be looking out every term to take literally anything he is teaching.
I'm sure other people have said what I'll say. Fun class with an amazing professor. You won't regret taking this class unless it dosen't help your degree and even then I don't think you'll regret it.

Dr. Pete is by far the best professor I have had at UO. His lectures are content heavy, but amazing. You can tell he cares so much about the class content and his love for it makes you even more interested in it. There are lots of readings but its prevalent to the course. His feedback on assignments is good. Open to discussion/ questions in class.

Overall the best class I've ever taken at the University of Oregon. Great lectures where I am actually excited to attend! GO TO THE LECTURES he does not post his slides  and the exams are very lecture heavy.

Dr. Pete is outstanding. I took 266, 410, and 490. I definitely recommend his higher level courses. Fascinating. He expects a higher caliber of work and will grade accordingly, but he gives good feedback and helps you push yourself. It is so refreshing to see someone who actually cares about teaching and is passionate about the material they teach

Professor Alilunas is incredibly funny, and his lectures are very engaging and enjoyable. The class workload is quite small, however the assignments are very well thought out. I highly recommend this professor if you want a simple class that is a great time.

INCREDIBLE LECTURER! I loved going to this class every day. However, the grading scale is extremely difficult to get an A with, so you've got to mentally prepare yourself for a B or worse when taking this class. 10/10 would recommend Dr. Pete

Dr. Pete is one of the best professors I've had at UO, he is amazing. His lectures were really interesting and entertaining while giving important information to the class. He is really passionate about this class and is incredibly knowledgeable. He is a super nice guy, I would love to take another class from him in the future.

How could you not love Dr Pete?! Best prof at uo hands down. I have learned more in this class (cin490) than any other class in my life & with 0 stress. Hilarious. Engaging. Genuine. doesn't give a shit about stuff that doesn't matter. deeply cares about students and learning. unpretentious but wildly intelligent. would take every term if i could!

Great teacher. He's really passionate and that transfers to great lectures. Online lectures was just his videos that we were able to watch. Grading was clear, and his weekly organization was great for learning.

His lectures are interesting and I can tell he is very passionate about the subject. However, there is only a total of 100 points you can earn in this class. I already missed a few points on the midterm and I don't expect to do perfect on the final so I'll probably end with a B. This class is not as easy as you might think.

One of the best classes I have taken so far. He was super funny and engaging. Although the class was three hours he was so interesting time flew by. I strongly encourage this class! It is very easy and the midterm and finals are online.

If you have the opportunity, take a class with Dr. Alilunas!!! He is probably the best lecturer I have ever had in my three years here at the U of O. His lectures are hilarious and never bland. I promise that you won't regret taking a class with Dr. Alilunas!

Professor Alilunas is the best professor I have had so far at UO. His lectures are fun, engaging, and useful. I enjoyed coming to class, but the movies we had to watch were very odd and boring. Overall it was a fun class, but the cumulative research took a lot of work.
hes funny and nice but not very forgiving

Ok, so... Alilunas is one of the best lecturers I've ever had and he's super funny and makes the class seem shorter than it is. However, the dude doesn't EVER post his slides so you HAVE to go to class or read the textbook if you want to pass. Also, you research all term for a paper you never end up having to write... kinda odd and tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Incredible! Best professor I've ever had and his slideshows are amazing, never seen anything like them!

I love Peter! I am not a morning person, so obviously taking a 8:30 class for my first term of college was not ideal, however, Dr Alilunas made me want to come. He is a very friendly, hilarious, and genuine guy that gives vivacious lectures that will leave your head spinning. Class was easy and fun, textbook not needed as long as you come to class.

One of the best profs Ive had at UO. Lectures are really interesting and he makes them fun. Attendance isnt mandatory but he doesnt post slides so if you miss class make sure you have someone you can get notes from. Quizzes every week, lowest one is dropped. 2 midterms, no final. He just taught his last term of J201 but take any class of his!
Go to class and study the main ideas and you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Peter had some of the most interesting lectures ever! He made lecture super engaging and I actually looked forward to going to class everyday. His power points are some of the best Ive ever seen! He is hilarious and genuinely cares about students! If you can take a class by Prof. Alilunas I 100% recommend doing so.
The best professor! Would take j 201 again and again! Some of the best lectures!

Peter was one of my favorite professors at UO. He had the most impressive lecture slides I have ever seen in my life. His class was so engaging I actually looked forward to going to class everyday. He's super funny and cares a ton about his students and engaging everyone. Grading is easy and lots of extra credit opportunities.
one of the most interactive, engaging, informative lecture classes ive ever taken. Remains relevant to students without powerpoints laced with memes like most other classes on this campus....

Alilunas made it clear the first day that the only way to get information from his lectures would be by attending his lectures, though the lectures are so entertaining/interesting I didn't skip any & ol' Peter somehow made 8am's fun. The class is overall easy but the concepts can be a little hard to grasp. It def changed the way I view the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Would take again

reviews.comment: Alilunas is the bomb. He's an awesome dude to talk to and gives boss lectures. I guess if you understand what you're reading you don't have to show up to class but I never read and just went to class. All you have to do is get the key concepts, my advice is don't think too hard, just think how it applies. If you don't get it, go talk to him. Trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Alilunas for my FIG & J201 & he is one of the best profs I've ever had. He genuinely cares about what his students have to say. J201 is just a huge lecture so you don't actually have to go if you don't want to but he makes the class so interesting that you'll want to go to his 8 am even if it's freezing outside.

Peter Alilunus is one of the most loved professors at the University of Oregon. He gives really engaging and refined lectures and knows how to connect with our generation. Alilunas does not focus on harsh testing as much as making sure we can apply the ideas from class to our own lives and the part we play in society. Overall, amazing professor!
