Tests were easy, he prepares you very well for them. His class was very relaxed. As long as you go and do the homework you shouldnt have any problems!

Rafael is the best Spanish professor I have had! He was very clear in his expectations and he was always there to answer questions.  He really wants to see his students succeed and that is evident in the way he runs his class.  If you go to class and put minimal effort into your assignments, you will do well.

Rafael is honestly the best Spanish professor I've had at the U of O. He is a native speaker, so he speaks almost solely in Spanish, which really helps you learn. H speaks slowly and clearly and is very easy to understand. He grades really easily and wants his students to learn. I HIGHLY recommend taking a Spanish class from him.

Really great teacher and hoping somebody will drop him as his professor for registration next term because I love him as a professor so much! Really helpful, fairly easy grader as long as you put the work and time in, and as long as you do the class work and study it's all good!

Definitely my favorite professor in my first term of college. He is always very helpful if you ask him a question and the tests are easy as long as you do the work. He is a nice guy and grades fairly easily as well! Just show that you care a little bit and your grade will be fine.
Very easy, just go to class and turn in the assignments and you're golden.
Very helpful and truly understood the students. Was always willing to move things around to aid a student if there were issues with time. Highly recommended.
Rafael is a great teacher, he's very helpful and encouraging. I would definitely recommend his class!
Amazing teacher! Take his classes!!

Asbury really cares about his students and really wants to see us do well in the class. easily one of the easiest-to-approach professors I've ever met who really understands a student's life and what we battle on a daily.
Steven is such a design mecca. He gives the best advice and my improvement this term has been INSANE. He also is so funny.

Professor Asbury is one of the best professors at the SOJC! His lectures and assignments are meant to make us better! Very inspirational and easy to talk to. He truly cares about his students. I took JCOM 408, it was very beneficial and an important class for advertising students.

I'm currently taking J 460 Brand Development (Design & Production) with Steven and he is AMAZING. We spend most of our time talking about typography, graphic design, and working with InDesign, and he knows what he's talking about because he has his own agency in Eugene. Our class was 6-8:50 but he never kept us the whole time which was so nice.
HE IS THE BEST TEACHER. He is really caring and very inclusive. His class is engaging and fun. I 100% recommend. If I could take this class again, I would.

I think Asbury is the hidden gem of the J school. He really cares about his student but isn't afraid to push your buttons. He owns a company as well so he has real world experience rather than some professors who have only taught their whole life. His design classes are amazing even if you aren't a designer!

Asbury is extremely talented and very fun to be around. He really makes an effort to connect with students during class time. Lectures are simple and easy to follow. If you like design, this is a great class. If you realize halfway through that you were never meant to be a designer, it will still be fun but very challenging.

Awesome teacher! He is really engaging and always available if you need any extra help. Such a fun class if you like design. Lectures are really interesting. Projects are time consuming but fun. Quizzes are easy if you do the reading.

Dr. Angulo was a fairly easy grader, however, her instructions within all assignments were vague and had limited information. You often don't know what she expects of you based on length of assignment responses, content and use of vocabulary. Her midterm was incredibly difficult and the questions were often grammatically incorrect or illiterate.

She only responds every 1-3 days, all of the assignments are so confusing no one knows whats going on especially in the first few weeks so hard to navigate her course. Assignments are easy but for group projects if you have bad people you're screwed if not you'll be totally fine and easy.

While some of the course content is interesting, it's disappointing that the class doesn't feel beneficial to my education due to the instructor's structure and interactions. Assignment expectations and feedback are vague, and Dr. A often leaves questions unanswered or posts them to the entire group. For a required course, this is frustrating.

Do you like vague feedback that doesn't help you? Do you enjoy condescending lectures filmed during COVID and recycled year after year? Do you like confusing criteria for assignments? If so, take Professor Angulo! This is one of the worst, if not THE worst, classes I have taken. Organized badly, graded vaguely, and zero substance in the work.

The class isn't to bad, she just has very vague instructions. So when you get a low grade on a project assignment you are left confused. The other assignments are pretty easy. She also talks to you like your are a 5 year old in her COVID lectures that she still reuses.

She is a crazy tough grader, and makes things due at 8pm/10pm but NEVER 11:59. Just a huge group project and a couple individual assignments each week. Basic marketing class, pretty easy but didn't get anything amazing out of Ashley as she often took 3+ days to respond to my emails. I wouldn't take this class.

She seems like a very sweet person, but this is easily the most disorganized online class (MKTG 490) that I've ever taken. Slides and lecture videos don't line up, the discussion post is due on Mondays but will use content from a week that hasn't been covered yet, won't reply back to emails with questions, and it's easy to get lost within the class

This is for MKTG 390 async. DO NOT TAKE!!! Lectures are short and confusing followed by long assignments with little to no guidelines on how to do them. Also if you want every example to be explained to you like you are a caveman this is your class. This course lead me to the decision that marketing probably isn't for me
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor is probably the most irritating professor I have ever had at this school. While she is not mean and her lectures aren't unbearable, she is just so annoying. Her guidelines for any sort of assignment are so unclear and her feedback is either nonexistent or just so unhelpful. She also treats us like 3rd graders.
This chick was pretty chill, very clear, had alot of fun with the topics, I only wish I could take another one of her classes...I also think she smokes weed...but im not saying its a bad thing.
my favorite teacher this year, very fun during class, easily engages students in topics. overall cool person as well.

Ashley is a cool person but a bad teacher. She was scattered and disorganized from day 1, which continued on until the last day. We barely had any helpful discussions on actually writing an essay, except for the last week of class, which was completely not helpful. A cool person, but not a teacher I would recommend.

She is a great professor, and I learned so much from her class that I will take with me in my future career as a teacher. She truly cares about her students success, is clear about instructions, and is always there to help if needed. I appreciated how she made class fun and enjoyable, i always looked forward to coming to this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Super caring professor. Knows what she is teaching about, and will answer any questions. I learned so much from her classes, I would take her again if I could. She has a no technology policy in her classes, which is an adjustment at first, but I found it so beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Unclear grading criteria and rubrics, will not change scores and often agrees with hostile grading practices/choices, a questionable professor in an otherwise sea of passionate Teacher's-Teacher's. Do better.

No tech/low tech policy, which is fine, but she has a holier-than-thou attitude about it. Super strict about grading, will get points off on anything. Make sure you stay within the word count or get marked down, but you'll probably be marked down for not going into enough detail.

Love Autumn! She was very sweet and understanding. Most of class time was devoted to our projects (~4 of them) and she basically showed us what to do for a lot of the research and qualtrics based stuff. As long as you pay attention in class and follow along with her, you'll be good to go. She also loves to chat with her students, which is very nice

I love Autumn, she's one of the best teachers at the SOJC. For JCOM 371 she does a flipped classroom so we watch lectures at home (and the lecture quizzes are open note) and then we have group work time in class. She really cares about her students and makes everything really easy to understand. I really enjoyed taking her class!
Pretty chill class. All group work. Only one homework assignment a week (watching lecture video with a quiz after). Best teacher for this course.

**JCOM 470** Autumn is my favorite professor I've ever had. Her class is structured to help you learn as much as possible without the workload being overwhelming at all. The entire course is group projects, but she makes it fun even if you don't know anybody. I have never liked research before and I loved this entire class.

Autumn is one of the best professors I've had at UO. Her class is super informative, and I have learned so much this term. I genuinely enjoyed going to JCOM 470 every day because of how Autumn structured the class and her passion as a teacher. Take this class with Autumn!

Autumn is one of the best profs I've had in the J school. The group projects were fun and applicable to real life. Did a flipped classroom so you never had to meet with your group outside of class time. Offered SO MUCH extra credit and was extremely helpful and kind. Cannot recommend her enough.
One of my favorite profersors. Group projects and informative lectures

Most informative class I've taken for PR. She teaches actionable things I will take into the real world. Very upbeat, kind, intelligent professor. You can tell she is passionate about what she does. Very understanding about life situations. HIGHLY recommend

This class was a lot of work, but Autumn was great. She really cares about her students. She is really into what she teaches, so you know that she cares about you understanding the material and succeeding. Definitely take class with Autumn, she is wonderful.
The lectures can be a bit dull but overall, she's a great teacher who loves what she does. The class is graded easily. Would recommend.

She speaks softly so sit on the front. The dates on syllabus are only suggestions to when the assignments and exams actually happen, but she will specify when they are due around a week in advance. If you love history, I suggest you take her class, but if you are doing it only for the credit search for a different professor. Different experience.

Loved her and her class, the information was super interesting and she does a good job communicating it. She talks very quietly and her voice is super soft so it's very easy to fall asleep in her class. Attendance is mandatory and if you want to do well on the quizzes, you'll want to go. Not too much reading and the quizzes are easy if you study
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assigns textbook readings but they're completely unnecessary. Speaks in a soft voice so be sure to sit near the front. Very accessible outside of class and happy to help out with more than just course materials. Clearly cares about student success. Tests on detail recall and the research paper is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most people would say Dr. Asim's lectures are boring, but if you're interested in the subject like I am I find her explanations to be engaging and digestible (although slow). She's really nice and excited to talk about the subject if you ask her more questions about it.

Every class I had in High School was harder than this class. Lectures are so boring and are useless, same with the textbook. Just look at the canvas notes and you'll be fine. 2 easy tests, 3 easy papers, and 1 easy final report. If you can sit through the boring lectures to get attendance credit, and just read the canvas notes then you'll be fine.
The lectures were very long, boring, and disengaging. You also couldn't see your grade until the quarter was over (from my experience).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She's just mean. There was like no feedback for several weeks. Then I guess she asked a bunch of students to drop the class. 

Don't ask her questions if you don't want to be on her bad side. She will snap at you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Daily ranted about completely irrelevant topics for the first 20-30 min of a 90 min class. No feedback whatsoever on any grades. This was a 300+ level class, and she wasted over half a class explaining how to format an essay, including what a bibliography was.

The class is ridiculously easy, if you have the patience for her long and boring lectures. The assignments and tests are graded fairly loosely, but the lectures are the sleepiest things ever. The format of the tests are strange. There are several subjects you have to review for the test, but you receive a test with only three questions.

Easily the most boring class I have ever taken. The content is fun to learn but Professor Asim will lecture for two hours every day. She talks nonstop and will go on tangents about random things that do not correlate. She teaches the class as if everyone knows the basics of early China but this is an intro course. Easy B or A if you can stay awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's no doubt that this professor knows her stuff, my main issues with her is that 1) her lectures are incredibly long winded and offers little to no engagement, 2) she doesn't use the canvas grading system, 3) talking to her after class for clarification or help is draining, she's very rude.
honestly shes just mean

We received 0 graded assignments until week 5. And in week 6 she made 6 students drop after the first assignment. There are only 5 graded assignments, so they matter a lot. The books are irrelevant, memorize canvas modules for the quizzes. Most of the time is spent enduring her long winded lectures, and you can't skip.  Avoid this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is easy. Lectures are a slog. My 10th grade APUSH class was ten times as engaging, my 12th grade history class twenty. She goes on tangents, and is repetitive and monotone. No gaps to ask questions unless you interrupt. Lectures are her reading off her bullet point notes, which are unorganized and near incomprehensible to everyone else.

She does seem passionate, but her methods of teaching are too traditional. When conducting an online class she expects students to be 100% engaged, which isn't really realistic when on zoom. Worst thing was that she emailed the whole class a list of students names who did not turn in their paper yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is super unprofessional. She goes on so many tangents, talking about topics which have nothing to do with the class at all. Also when we gave our final presentations at the end of the term, she constantly interrupted and criticized us DURING our presentation. Also she can be kinda snobbish and condescending when you ask her a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Tough grader--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring class!!!!!!! The teacher didn't respect students. She gave a lot of reading stuff and it's hard to understand!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly the most boring class I have taken in 4 years of college. Rather than focusing on important historical developments, she goes on tangents about random inventions and art. I did not sign up for an art history class. She ended up being 3 weeks behind our syllabus and never sent out emails to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She has a thick accent that makes it hard to understand her, and she wasn't very interesting. she was enthusiastic, but i was not feeling this teacher at all. i do not recommend this class.
AH this was the worst class, she was kind of hard to understand and monotonous, it wasn't interesting at all. But she knows her asian history
Lady knows her stuff but speaks in montone and you want to kill yourself every class...avoid taking her at all costs, unless the cost is your life, and then i guess i'd take her
she was one of the best profesors i have ever had!
No Comments

She was a little dul, but she mos deff knows her stuff on China.  I enjoyed her class and would take a class of her's again.  She is an easy teacher if that helps....study session the day of the quiz type stuff.   Just take her class.

Not good for lower classmen who haven't experienced discussion/research/indepedence in the classroom. Very knowledgable on asian studies, great teacher if you want freedom to study or research something that already interests you involving asia. I would recommend if you have an interest in the subject matter, not a survey teacher.
TERRIBLE professor. Is not clear whatsoever, and I was NOT interested in the slightest. Do NOT take her classes unless you want to be bored...

Excellent teacher and a complete and total expert on Asia and China. Ask and she knows. Not a typical lecture style of teaching, it's more like shes discussing with the class even if its mostly her talking. Expect to give a presentation in her classes. She rewards good students with good grades, pay attention and perform and you'll be rewarded.

Audrey is very nice but a hard grader. You don't think she will be because she is pretty chill but she grades hard. However, if you write a draft she will tell you everything you need to fix to get a better grade so that is cool.
audrey was great, office hours were super helpful & she really cares about your success
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Audrey is super nice. She grades hard but helps you if you go to office hours. I liked her class.
amazing person, will help you out throughout the entire course if needed and will have the patience to guide you step by step!

Amazing class to take if you're interested in solving math like puzzles. Audrey is really amazing when teaching this class, she's always making sure everyone understand the material before moving on in class. She is also very receptive when asked to explain more in detail, etc.. She is an amazing professor and I would recommend this class!
I took Audrey for logic and she was very nice. The class and material was hard but if you go to office hours she will help you and work through problems.

I have had Audrey a few times now as a GE, and she's always been awesome. She's extremely caring and understanding and definitely has a passion for philosophy. Her passion shows and has always helped me have a better understanding of the material. We could have just read the most boring piece and Audrey will find a way to make it interesting.

Audrey is really nice. She has office hours where she will work on your paper with you and is pretty understanding of most situations. She requires participation but allows for different methods so everyone feels comfortable.
He was fine, just seemed pretentious and insecure. A bit exhausting to be in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Appeared to be passionate about his work, he's very knowledgable, and it's a damn shame he is moving! He did a great job of cultivating a higher level class discussion. His feedback on my work was the best of any professor I've had.

Professor Augustine's class was a very pleasant surprise. He knew so much about the topic, knew what to say to prompt discussion, wrote thoughtful comments on papers, and didn't overwhelm the class with the workload. My favorite assignment was an essay with a barfight between two authors. And it doesn't hurt that he's cute. ;)

I have had the pleasure of taking two classes from professor Augustine, and I have to honestly say, the man is a genius. He holds heavy discussion-based classes that are incredibly intellectually stimulating, often changing your entire perception of something. He is relaxed, funny, and incredibly passionate about his studies. A must-have professor.

Augustine is a pretty cool person, but he doesn't always seem to have practical expectations. Sometimes his discussion-intense method of teaching worked really well, but more often than not, our 8:30 AM class was awkwardly silent. Having said that, he's a very knowledgeable person, and if literature is your life, he's a good professor for you.

Matt was all about class participation. If you like to talk in class, then he's the right teacher for you. He can get into some very detailed analyses if he thinks the group can handle it. He's laid back to the point of being a little hard to read--I was never sure where I stood with him. All in all, not a bad teacher, but not my fav.

Prof. Vander Wel initially seems laid-back and chill, but he assigns far more work and grades far tougher than other professors at the same level, especially on busy work assignments.  However, it's not hard to do well in the course as long as you are a competent Spanish student.  Likes to cold call, so be prepared to participate.

The curriculum is set by Georgetown, so Prof. Vander Wel wasn't able to design the course. He does grade tough. The class has a lot of homework, mostly busy-work, and is especially busy at the end of the semester. He is organized and accessible by email. Only offered one office hour a week. Brought lots of energy and passion to 8am Spanish.
I loved learning from Austin! He's an excellent professor and truly cares about his students' progress. His office hours are also super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Austin was supportive in my learning of the Spanish language. He obviously loves his job bc he made learning it a fun & funny experience. He will answer all questions (even the dumb ones) as if they were great questions & you will not be able to hide in the back bc he encourages participation. If you have trouble, just talk to him. Grades are fair.

Really cares about his students and the material. He is kind, passionate, and considerate. I have taken two courses with him so far and registered for a third. Would highly recommend. Do your work, ask questions, and be interested.

Prof. Vander Wel is so caring! He really does care about his students, and he's a very good professor. He's super nice. Also, he makes sure to check in with everyone to see if they understand the topic or not before moving on  he really wants to make sure that everyone in the class can follow along and not just waste away in the back of the class.

Austin is a very easygoing and helpful professor. He makes learning a second language a pleasant experience, and inspires us to keep pushing ourselves to get better. The grading criteria is very clear; the textbook seems expensive ($240) but it is for 3 Spanish classes so it's really a bargain. Definitely recommend this professor!

She missed almost 50% of the lectures. Horrible attitude and no respect for students. Didn't know how to explain things clearly. Majority of the class petitioned for a refund at the end of the term. Our GTFs (who were amazing and taught us more than she did) ended up giving us our final grades. She may be better now after that first term.

a lot of students complained about this class because it wasn't what they thought it was supposed to be. Personally- really I enjoyed this class and learned a lot. Prof. Aucoin could be a bit clearer on some things, but she is always willing to clarify. I think she is a new professor, but she is knowledgeable and funny and will help you if you ask.

Lindsay will tell you like it is. At first that can seem harsh but she knows what she's talking about and she really will help you LEARN SOMETHING if you are can take honest criticism which is what being an artist is all about. Thanks Lindsay!!

LOVED this class. I never thought about digital imaging being more than output methods & PS techniques I have no use for. This class was cool. Conceptual. More about what it means to make a image. Lindsay encourages outside-the-box thinking while insisting on a firm grasp of "basic visual principles of art." (: No tolerance for BS. Know your stuff.

Very easy as long as you show up. No midterms or finals, just easy multiple choice quizzes and one final paper. Lectures can be boring, he just reads power points, but taking notes is therefore easy. Certainly a good choice if you need an easy A in upper division history. Nice and informal in class.
Prof Kaiser knows ALOT about British history.  lectures are usually interesting but sometimes he does get boring.  You write one big paper for the class.  He's also pretty funny.
Strict but fair.  Extremely knowledgeable and interesting lecturer.  Funny, but slightly intimidating.  If you do the work, you'll get a good grade.

She was an okay professor. She seemed really sweet and caring towards her students but the course and assignments were really unorganized and confusing. I think this might have been because it was completely online and she wasn't used to that. There is a lot of group work which wasn't the best for me but that depends more on who you get put with.

Irene is so caring and helpful. You work the majority of this class in one group, but all of your assignments are group project besides one midterm, so if you have a good group of people it's not bad at all. I would definitely recommend taking a class with Irene.

She replies to emails pretty quick, but her and her GE's can be a little sassy sometimes. Expect a lot of discussion posts, unneeded lectures, and little to no homework in J201. It was an average class and professor, didn't love and didn't hate.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Irene is so sweet and loves her students! The assignments and weekly lectures were very great tools to learn the content; she is a bit of a tough grader, but gives so many opportunities to improve. Anyone would be lucky to take WGS 101 with Irene! She gives very valuable perspectives and leads amazing discussions throughout the term.

Irene is a sweet lady. You can tell that she's really passionate about what she teaches and sincerely cares about you on a personal level. The work can become a bit monotonous but each week, we're learning something new so it evens out. She's strict on plagiarism though so be mindful of that when writing or you'll get graded down. Solid choice tho.

I took Intro to Finance because I don't know anything about it, but want to go into the finance world. He immediately started the course using terms that I didn't know, and basically started teaching as if we already had financial knowledge, and were expanding on those topics. I was lost halfway through the first lecture. Poor explanations too.
Very inspired.

okay here is the deal... he knows the material more than anyone else... very smart...however he doesnt know how to teach...midterm was easy...final was very looong..if you want to understand the material dont take it with him period.

Amazing class, super easy if you want to learn Python coding. She has a lot of built-in leniency policies in her syllabus (i.e., dropped assignments, etc.). You get lots of practice through in-class activities, easy exit quizzes, formative quizzes, and the projects aren't too bad or time-consuming. Her lectures go at a nice pace. Highly recommend!
Professor Thuzar is an excellenet teacher and person.  She provided very clear and thorough lectures, fun engaging projects, accessible help outside of class, and has a very clear teaching style.

The midterm and final are in person and are collectively worth 50%. Everything else is online and coding, which is very manageable. She does her best to help, especially if you go to office hours and ask questions.

I'll be honest, I didn't apply myself as much as I should have in Aye's class. Despite this, I still thought I learned a good amount and that she was a good and available professor to the class. She had drop-in office hours after class that were very helpful if something didn't make sense, and was always happy to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Thuzar was great. I really enjoyed this class and the way she teaches is very clear and easy to follow. I definitely recommend her for CS111.

I loved Aye she was great at going over assignments in class and was very helpful when things got a little confusing, she also helps you study for the midterms and final and gives you plenty of resources to succeed in her class.

Professor Thuzar is an amazing professor that genuinely loves teaching computer science. I loved being in this class because it was challenging yet engaging. She's very good at answering questions and her lectures are pretty clear. There are a lot of projects and they can get a little stressful, but I enjoyed it. Would take again!

She is a great teacher for introducing people to Python when they come in knowing nothing. She is very clear, provides great answers, and offers many ways to communicate. I honestly looked forward to this class because the structure of the class made learning coding exciting, which I cannot say about many courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Aye was very sweet, her lectures were clear and she answered questions well. She moves really fast through her lectures, and sometimes it's hard to keep up. This class has a lot of work, we had 4 projects and 4 tests and daily exit quizzes as well that counted for attendance. I wouldn't reccomend taking this class as your first CS class at UO.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've had at UO. She truly cares about her students and their success. She has office hours every day of the week, and is very helpful and very good at explaining. 10/10 recommend.
Disorganized lecturer, homework problems were chosen carelessly however he's a nice guy and is very helpful at office hours so he gets an OK from me.

Professor Aycock is so nice but his lectures are a bit disorganized. However, his office hours are very helpful. He'll re-explain a concept if asked and he'll go over homework and quiz questions. He also gives a reasonable amount of homework for a calculus class per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is a quiz every week which could be a good or bad thing. The lectures are really confusing and I never knew what to study for or what to expect on tests. The content he teaches is really disorganized and unless you have time to go to office hours you are screwed.

He did a lot of examples when teaching this class. A big downside to this class is that you can't get a lot of help at the Fenton math library, however Jon's office hours can really help when it come to working on the homework. Definitely go to office hours!
I was lost in all the classes

He can be pretty disorganized during class, but his office hours are pretty good and he'll explain an entire homework problem to you. He gives a good amount of homework but is sometimes flexible about grading. His class can be confusing but be sure to go to office hours because he's a lot better at explaining one-on-one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is honestly such a great teacher! He's always available for help hours and really wants his students to succeed. I would definitely recommend taking his class! His lectures are short but they cover a lot of material. Tests are simple enough if you've been keeping up with the homework. Overall a really fun teacher and class!

Made this class more difficult than it should have been. Spent the entire class going through example problems, but never taught the concept or explained how he would get answers. Extremely disorganized, got necessary papers and study guides to us last minute, and does not know how to help his students succeed. Not enough time for tests. Switch out

This class is definitely too hard for a 100 level class. I am a senior taking mostly upper division courses and this was still my hardest class. Lets just say if I was a freshman walking into this class, I would be terrified. The prof is good at his job and communicating concepts, but the quizzes are way too hard.

Ayres is a great professor. This course does feel like it should be higher than 100 level. I am taking other 300/400 level courses and this one is harder than them. It is valuable material, but it was challenging and time consuming. Other than that, I recommend taking a class from him.

Must read the textbook to succeed in this class, but the textbook is very very enjoyable and funny, while also being engaging and thought provoking. One paper and quiz a week, which can be long and tedious. Midterm and final exam require thorough studying, and the final is cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures sometimes were a bit long, but the weekly written assignments were simple as long as you did the reading. The quizzes, however, were really tough and were hard to learn their "format". What bothered me is that he would sometimes not respond to emails or be blunt in his comments on our work. It's an ok online class...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class and great material it is a fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was an awful online class. He is not reachable through email or canvas. He does not grade any of the assignments, the GTF does all of the work. There's no use asking questions about grading becuase the GTF refers you to the professor who does not answer. His questions are both tricky and convoluted. His grading is not apparent and confusing.

I took his online anth 145 class. My website for the midterm ended up crashing and i was able to get screenshots for it and he gave me full credit. He is very respectful, and cares a lot about how his students do. The online class is very clear and i highly reccomend taking it.

Dr. Ayres' GTF did most of the work for this class.  He graded a few things, but the GTF did most of the grading.  And they graded things differently.  Grading and feedback came weeks after submitting assignments, which made it hard to apply the feedback to current assignments.

This professor is a nice person, I can tell. He just does not know how to engage a class at 8:30 in the morning. He does know a lot, but the organization of the class is scattered, too random, with no narrowed down structure. Being an archaeology class, sites and dates are important. But lectures are scattered and filled with irrelevant detail. :

Idk why the reviews for her are so bad. I would consider myself someone who puts in little effort but has high expectations for my grades, which is bad, ik. Anyways, I did not study a lot for this class and was able to score very well on the homeworks and tests because I had good notes from class. Giver her a shot, guarantee there are worse profs
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures are long, but all her quiz's are based on what she says in class. As much as it sucks WRITE DOWN EVERY WORD SHE SAYS. You will not regret it. There's a lot of notes and weekly quiz's but ayesha states everything how it is. Loud and clear!
Just not a good teacher. Literally the most boring lectures and she handwrites them all. Also studying the review doesn't help for the tests to much.

The most boring lecture you will ever go to. For a college professor she really has the worst grammar and she uses numbers like "1200 billion". All she does is read definitions and write them on a paper that she projects onto a screen. She doesn't engage the class unless she tells you to stop talking. Review is NOTHING like the midterms/exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easily the laziest teacher I've ever had. Her lectures consisted of her literally saying the material and then proceeding to write it down on a piece of paper under a doc cam which was projected onto the giant screen. None of the material was reinforced and examples weren't provided at all. No HW but there were online quizzes every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is caring and loves what she teaches but the class is harder than other Span 203. I would not recommend if you a looking for an easy language teacher. She lets no English into the classroom. She will not help you if you speak English. Be prepared to work for grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tough grader even on native speakers. All she does is talk and never allows students to talk. She is very rude and will ridicule you in front of the whole class. Definitely would NEVER recommend taking a class with her.

This is the worst class I have taken in college. 1/4th of our class dropped before week 8. Olga is an incredibly hard grader and has very little compassion if you're not fluent and don't understand everything she says she gets mad. However, somehow most of the class passed with an A even though we all thought we were going to fail, hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olga speaks very quickly and does not pause for questions, which makes it difficult to understand what she wants from the students. We had in class presentations and afterwards told each student what they did wrong. She is not sympathetic to excuses and she corrects students in a condescending way.

Unclear grading rubrics. Strict about attendance, if you are more than 5 minutes late you are counted as absent. Tough grader. Criticizes your presentation in front of the entire class. Interesting material but very stressful amount of homework.

She's super sweet and loves what she's teaching. There's homework every night but it isn't hard. Lots of opportunities to increase your grade because of the different presentations we do throughout the term.

I did not enjoy this class at all. The topics were interesting but she wasn't engaging. She constantly goes over the syllabus  but doesn't follow it herself. Grading rubric is a mystery and is not clear about due dates. PICK A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR.

She really wants her students to work for the grade they earn. This class was difficult for me because I am not a native spanish speaker. If you pay attention during class discussions, do all the readings, and participate in class you will do very well in this class. Do not take this class with Olga if you are looking for an easy class.

It all depends on what you're looking for in a Spanish class. She is a super hard grader who gives very unclear instructions and talks very fast. If you want a serious challenge/are a native speaker, this is probably the teacher you want. If you're looking to enjoy a class and don't have the best grasp on Spanish yet, don't take from her.

I've taken two other Spanish classes at UO under the same curriculum. None have been as difficult as when under her instruction. She is a native speaker, so it is hard to understand her dialect. She never spoke in English and ridiculed me during my presentation even though I met all the criteria. She hardly ever speaks in English, and grades hard.

She is a tougher teacher, but I respect that. The only thing that frustrated me in this class was that she could be unclear about due dates or grading criteria. How helpful she is depends a little on the type of day she's having and her mood, definitely go to office hours because it's a no - go in class.

I have mixed feelings about this professor. On one hand, she spoke quickly, as she is a native Spanish speaker, which helped improve my Spanish, and she was a fair grader on exams and assignments. On the other hand, her class felt very impersonal, and she generally wasn't that understanding if a student was struggling with a deadline. No phones.

I have mixed feelings about this professor. On one hand, she spoke quickly, as she is a native Spanish speaker, which helped improve my Spanish quite a bit, and she was a fair grader on exams and assignments. On the other hand, her class felt very impersonal, and she generally wasn't that understanding if a student was struggling with a deadline.
Olga is by far the best Spanish teacher I have had. She is willing to work with students who need extra help or clarity. She keeps the class light and fun and is a fair grader.

For a class where most people just finished the basic Spanish requirements, she expects a lot from students and gives terrible feedback.  I went into office hours multiple times begging for guidance, and she refused to assist. The readings are very difficult and overly advanced. Such a hard class, definitely do not recommend taking her.

DO. NOT. TAKE. HER. CLASS. Hardest Spanish class I've ever taken. She speaks extremely fast, doesn't post her lectures online, and does not give clear instructions for the many assignments she gives you. I've taken higher level Spanish classes easier than this one. She gives pop quizzes and will assign extra work if you have a long weekend.
She is very understanding. Cares about the students and is a sweet lady. Good overall professor!!!

One of the worst classes I have ever taken.  Professor lost my homework (made me re-do it and blamed it on me), entered my grades wrong and only when I looked at her spread sheet myself I found the errors, not clear in what she expects of class leading to multiple F's on assignments that she expects you to figure out. Demeaning towards speakers

Class is taught entirely in Spanish, she has a thick Peruvian accent and speaks quickly so you have to make sure and pay attention. The material was interesting and the amount of work she asked of us was fair. My difficulty in the class lay in the fact that she wants everything a certain way and if you misinterpret, you will fail miserably.

Olga is awesome!  She is very knowledgable and has a lot to say about her subject.  This class will not be a walk in the park and if you won't want to work, don't take it from Olga.  However, if you put in the time, do the readings, and participate in class you will get a ton out of it. I took this as a first term freshman and loved it.

This class is not going to be extremely easy, because there are a lot of readings and her class is entirely taught in Spanish, but I learned a lot. I think she is a fair grader. On quizzes and tests if you wrote a lot and did your best she would give you a good grade. Her accent is kind of hard to understand, but just keep up with hw

I'm guessing she was nicer/an easier grader for those in lower classes, but her 305 class was literally hell. Don't take it. She was so unreasonable with grading, so strict and nit picky about everything, and she chose favorites in the class and gave people bad grades simply for not liking them. Her emails were unhelpful and she was just rude.
She's a pretty easy grader, but has quizzes constantly that you're bound to fail! Also, there is an obscene amount of homework. Expect at least an hour every night.

Olga speaks entirely in Spanish during class, but she will definitely speak English with you outside of class if you have a question or want help. Great at explaining grammar & other things in Spanish; I would recommend her.

Olga is an amazing professor.  She makes learning Spanish real; she teaches more than trivial conversational Spanish.  However, she does talk ALL in Spanish-but don't let that scare you.  She is great!

She's cheerful and pleasant but very hard to understand and doesn't make sure everyone understands clearly. You usually have to search to make sure all the homework was completed the right way. Its also the only language class I've taken with VERY little oral practice.
I love Olga, she has great enthusiasm and input to every thing in the course. Willing to help and absolutely amazing.

Her class destroyed me, maybe I just don't have a knack for languages, but I didn't find her very friendly either.  She also talked faster than I can understand people in English, there was no way I could understand her in Spanish.  If you have any difficulty with Spanish I'd stay away from her class.  Most of my class dropped out.
such an amazing professor
Olga is a wonderful professor.  Her energy and enthusiasm make the time fly, plus she is very fair with tests and assignments.

She is a great person with a very fun and nice personality. She talks pretty fast, but she explains things well. She doesn't like it when people speak English in the classroom, but she will speak with you in English outside of the classroom.
Talks extremely fast, difficult to understand.
No Comments
She is a wonderful teacher!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
very enjoyable, chilean accent

Olga is a good teacher. She's from Peru, so don't let the Russian name fool you. She's an easy grader, and since she's been teaching for 20 years, so is really good at explaining things in spanish in ways that everyone can understand. She's not too difficult of a teacher. Overall, she's great!

Worst teacher I've ever taken at Baruch, he doesn't care about his students. One of the group projects all 19 out of 19 groups received the minimum grade on a little field labs simulation, even the control group that did nothing out-preformed everyone. The class average after the curve was a C+. I've been getting straight A/A- and this was my 1st B

This is the worst professor I have ever taken at Baruch. I received an F in the class after repeatedly going to the professor to tell him I was lost. He does not care about students. Like everyone else's complaints: he gives an enourmous amount of work for 7 weeks, the exam is impossible, and he refused to curve.  I had a 61.7%. He is AWFUL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about students, piles on the work. RUN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This guys was easily the worst professor that I have had at Baruch.  He speeds through the lectures, doesn't actually teach concepts, and doesn't connect with students at all.  His exams were difficult.  Avoid at all costs!!!

He's tough, but fair and if you are willing to put the time in you will pass.  The class is challenging and the workload is intense.  He makes himself available which shows that he cares.   You will learn whether you like it or not and believe me, the work shows up in the classes that follow.  He sets a great foundation for Operations Mgmt Majors.

Worst professor I have ever taken. No one had a clue what was going on in this class. He does curve a lot because I got a 40 and still got a B- in the class. Half your grade is based off group work so you are screwed if you are in a bad group. My recommendation is avoid this professor at all costs!

He's a tough grader (10 pts off for a math mistake!) but you will learn alot. Final was HARD with too many questions and not enough time. Form a strong team and you will do fine. Group problem set's, group paper, group game, individual report on "The Goal" and then final. He cares about students so reach out to him for help.

Avoid him if you can. Runs through the material to quickly. Would be helpful if he provided practice problems so you are not at a lost when it comes to the HW and exam. Always goes over the class time because there is to much material to cover.
Runs through important material, smiles and then gives more work then any 3 credit class. Sleazy, GPA killer Professor-- Avoid at all costs.

New prof to Baruch trying to prove himself which sucks for the students. He will not release the answers to textbook problems nor give you extra problems or do a Final review. Average grade on final was 56%. You work harder than any other class for a 1.5 credit and you're lucky if you get a B. Avoid at all costs.
Poses as a nice guy, but beware. Beyond difficult and very rigid--avoid.
Horrible learning experience. Won't flex a bit to try and accomodate.

Look, whether or not he was told that this is a 1.5 credit class, this work load is just plain stupid. Not even 3 credit classes have workloads like this. If the goal of teaching is to help students learn something, I think this class fails miserably; there's no time to learn anything due to the sheer load of assignments. Take this class alone.
Horrible, avoid him if possible. 1.5 credit class and a work overload. He doesn't always respond to e-mails and you have no idea what he is talking about half the time in class.

Horrible professor. Like some of the other comments said, he gives way too much work for a 1.5 credit class and gives no leniency in his grading. He expects too much from students and his lectures are very confusing. Avoid him.
Horrible teacher. I have no idea what is going on and have not learned anything. Amount of work is ridiculous. Another poor job by Baruch hiring this guy. Avoid if you can.

One of the worst classes I've taken in my MBA career. The class is a 1.5 credit (1.25 hrs/week), but is run as if it were a 3 credit course. Lectures heavily, and forces students to refer to his PPT. As others said, he gets off on being the "smartest" in the room and requires students to regurgitate his words back to him for full credit.

This guy is the worst. He loves being the smartest guy in the room. No one knows wtf is going on. He gets off on being arrogant. The concepts are ignored. There is no discussion, no questions, no encouragement, nothing. This is 1.5 credits  and is more work than my other 3 credit classes combined. I wish I never took this class. He is a bad teacher

Absolutely Aweful. Do not take this course unless you are prepared to devote all your time to it. Expectations for a 1.5 credit course is completely out of line. His grading is unfair and sloppy. I wish I never took this course with this professor.

I have no clue what this guy is talking about, ever. He speaks way to fast and doesn't do a great job in organizing/simplifying the material. Way too much work for a 1.5 credit course. I would not recommend, unless you have a really good understanding of the material to begin with.

Professor cares deeply about the topic and makes himself available outside of class time but he assigns way too much work for a 1.5 credit class and his grading is unfair: he is looking for his type of answer rather than whether you understand the material. Do not take assuming  the workload is anything less than a full size class.
Impossible. Avoid like the plague. Average on the final is 46%. no one learned anything. get a good group they will save you.
Very challenging... he makes you study very hard. In return, you learn all OM concepts in details. Find a good support group....

This class is challenging but there is a pretty big curve for the overall grade. You can tell he cares about the operations management because he is willing to offer as much help as he can. One of the better professors I've had.

Tolga was great, a really good guy. He always wears one of four sweaters...Anyway, there is a midterm and a final, but everyone fails it. The curve it huge, so even if you tank the tests your group work can pull it up. A dry, challenging class, but make sure you take the class with people you know!Its a necessity in this class.
This class is intnense. Hopefully you have a good group because half of the entire grade is with your group. The final is comprehensive, so study plenty.

Class is difficult especially if you end up with a poor group; a majority of the assignments are group assigned. Individual assignments can compensate for a poor group, though, if you do well. No midterm & 1 final. Not too difficult if you study and take notes.

I am so upset. Studied so much for his class and I have an F. Completely unfair for me. His class is entertaining but test questions are super confusing. He seems like a cool guy but I wish he would curve it if he want's to give out these type of tests. I deserve a B for all the effort I put in this class. This sucks.

Best professor I've ever had. I enjoyed his lectures every time, and definitely took a lot away from them. His classes aren't mandatory, but if you go, you'll understand his slides a lot more. Tests are difficult, but at the end of the class, he dropped our lowest test grade. I really enjoyed his class and wish he could teach every psy course.

If you want a GPA booster do not take this class! The class average is about a C+ and the class is almost entirely based on tests. Shariff is an awesome guy and has great lectures, but his tests are so hard that they almost cancel out.
Azim is a great professor, don't get me wrong. But the exams are SO hard. If you are anything but a pro test taker, I wouldn't take his class.

Azim is an amazing teacher that gives really good and interesting lectures. However, the class is pretty good (he admits this). I believe that he said last term the average was a C+. This is a very independent class. The effort you put in is the grade you get back.
One mistake to my last comment, I took psychology 202 with him, not 201. Besides that, hes still awesome

Azim Shariff is one of the nicest professors I have had at this University! He is really knowledgable about this subject and that shows during his lectures. Having said that, the tests are REALLY TOUGH. He makes it so the average test score of about 75% with a class of about 300 plus students. If you take this class with him, he's awesome but tough

This class is pretty interesting. He tries to tie in real life examples in his lectures but his tests are way too tough. If you are not majoring in psychology and are looking for a social science to take DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. tests are way too tough

The class is very interesting and Prof. Shariff always has funny things to add to each class. He uses all the time he has and only let us out early once. Tests are 80% of your grade and are very hard. He does curve tests and curves the final grade, he wants all his students to pass.

Azim is an amazing teacher. His lectures are interesting, funny, and thought-provoking. The tests are 80% of your grade and are very difficult, but as long as you go to class and read the material you'll be fine. Aside from being extremely nice to look at, he did a great job at keeping me engaged and interested in the topics.

Azim is amazing - best professor I've ever had. He is funny and engaging and presents the material really well. I was never bored in class and I actually wanted to go to every lecture. I don't know what else I can say; I would definitely recommend taking a class with him. The only thing is he is attractive so that can be a little distracting.

Amazing Professor. Couldn't recommend him enough. His lectures are very engaging and well thought out. He takes the time to make sure humor, learning, and excitement are a part of his class everyday. I never read the book and passed with a B. Take his class!

I cannot recommend Prof. Shariff enough. He is interesting and intelligent, funny and engaged. This class was the best class I've ever taken at UO and it made me consider majoring in Psychology. He also allowed our class to boycott the midterm, giving us all 100%. No lie. It is clear he puts a lot of time into the power points and is very helpful.

Professor Azim was very clear in explaining the topics and explained things with an authentic interest, which made the class more interesting. He was also helpful when going over the tests during office hours.

Loved this dude. His lectures are very energetic and fun while also being extremely informative and interesting. He's very helpful and encourages his students to ask questions. Excellent teacher. I would love to take another one of his classes

Very funny guy, makes class fun while still learning the material. Tests are difficult but if you do the reading and study you should be okay wit the curve, plus the online labs and psych studies are easy points for your grade. Highly recommend.

Shariff is an excellent professor. Lectures are always interesting and informative. Very funny/witty guy, you'll actually want to go to class. Don't worry if your exam grades are not what you usually get, the curve will take care of it. He just wants to make you work hard and learn the material.

Love this man, I went into the class fully expecting to be royally annoyed and bored, but Prof. Shariff got me genuinely interested in psychology. Lectures were extremely interesting, so interesting that I haven't missed one all term. Tests were difficult, but his grades are fair, and the homework wasn't very difficult at all. Read the textbook!
Very Hard tests, but great teacher, very funny, knows what hes doing, makes class entertaining and fun
Poor grading rubric,very tough grading of exams and papers.Friendly and approachable guy,but too much emphasis on evidence in correlational studies.This class showed me how arrogant Evopsych is.
I really enjoy this class. Professor Shariff is funny, smart, and makes us think in unconventional ways. The discussions are also really interesting.

I love Professor Shariff! He's very passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about his students. His class was by far my favorite this year. The loaded discussion questions, interesting lectures, and occasional jokes makes this professor well worth having.

This is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He made the information interesting and easy to understand. The only downfall was that our grade was based on 3 assignments. Also, he is really gorgeous and funny. This class was great.
Funny and really informative. I enjoyed, and learned the most from, his class despite it being 8am and outside my major.

This prof. chose to structure grading based on e 3 assignments: a 2 pg paper, a term paper and a final exam. I am fine with the limited graded assignments, but he was quick to critique and gave little constructive feedback. For the 1 exam, provided us little/no guidance regarding what may/not appear on the exam-and was considerably rude when asked

Its hard to concentrate in this class because the professor is absolutely gorgeous. You can hear the giggles of the other girls when he says something that is only slightly funny. Every girl in class is daydreaming instead of learning. But! the class is great and he is fun and the discussions are engaging!

Every time I entered her class I was actually scared for my life. She acts like she hates her students and is occasionally rude. Her lectures have pretty much nothing to do with the class and the only assignments you do are in discussion. Actually the worst class I've ever taken do NOT take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her class. Gives little instruction on the few assignments that determine your grade, then grades harshly on not delivering what she expected. Lack of student engagement was an issue but she only made the problem worse with outbursts and public shaming. Despite course concepts and materials being interesting, I dreaded every aspect
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Instructor is rude attendance is mandatory, assignments sometimes show up and have no grade or relevance to the course. Exams and big assignments are extremely harshly graded as averages are around a C- on every assignment if not lower. Do not take.

Actually worst professor I have ever had. The class was by no means difficult but little to no of our assignments where posted on canvas nor discussed before they where due (we were expected to have completed assignments by class time which none of us knew existed). Projects that COULD be interesting are forced out of quality by strict time limits.

COLT:232 Cultural Studies was a tad unfocused and I think that came out in the teaching. Mrs. Balbuena demonstrates a very deep albeit sporadic knowledge of world cultures. She does not interact with Canvas, but a tech does. Which can cause issues when referring to an assignment on canvas. Assignments are discussion forums, readings, and a pwrpoint
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with this professor. It's the most unorganized class I've experienced in three years. Most sessions are led by guest speakers, and when the professor IS teaching, she's confused. Her lesson plans are outdated, she struggles with Canvas, doesn't respond to emails, and fails to explain assignments. Worst professor award goes to...
Rough. Just don't bother.
DO NOT take a class with this professor

Read the books, watch the movies and participate in the lectures and you will be fine. Her assignments are unclear and when I tried asking her for help she was basically just rude. I do find her funny though. If this is the only class that fits your schedule don't stress you will be okay. It's just not heavily focused on film and is disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PLEASE do not take her class. Thankfully it is an easy A, but she is so rude. The lectures are just a bunch of busy work and the worksheets aren't even graded. No one participates in class which leads to pop quizzes. She doesn't even know how to answer questions about her own assignments... that she created...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is pointless, lectures are pointless. Takes forever to grade just don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly this class isn't too bad if you just do the readings... most people don't and she will give pop quizzes if she's upset about that. Class feels useless sometimes but it really isn't that hard to get a decent grade. Grading takes forever though so maybe I'm lying about that, still waiting on an essay grade. Do the readings, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Balbuena is extremely disorganized and her poor teaching made this class frustrating & unenjoyable. Even the GE who moderates our (completely useless) weekly discussions told us that we should have listened to the reviews on here and dropped the class. Nobody takes the assigned readings/movies seriously so no real discussion ever happens.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She does not teach in this class. Class always ends up being a pointless lecture on history. She doesn't teach any film or technical language, techniques, or applications. Everything you use is based on your prior knowledge and she expects you to use advanced technical and film language in her creative assignments without teaching you anything.

reviews.comment: Idk why everyone says shes bad... This class is an easy A. I haven't had one quiz. The lady barely knows how to work Canvas. If you want an easy A take this class. I didn't even read the book and I'm doing fine lmao

She complains when students don't participate but when they do she treats them poorly. Professor Balbuena has the right idea when conducting her Literature and Film course, however, what she truly lacks is sympathy and kindness towards her students. Never have this woman as professor, actually you don't have to worry about it she is getting fired.
Avoid this professor, unorganized and just so rude.
Non responsive to emails, does not leave feedback, and without a doubt the most unorganized professor I have ever had.

Professor Balbuena was completely unorganized. Her class was heavily discussion focused and the entire class led up to one large final project but she provided little direction until quite late in the term. Grading was harsh and was very closed off when asking for clarification.

This class was confusing and Professor Balbuena does not know how to interact with students. Does not grade anything. Does not give clear instructions, is confusing.

Really sweet and funny, but online was difficult. If you need structure in an online class then it will definitely be a struggle. Grading takes a long time and assignments lack clarity. Again, super sweet, but online is not her forte, I really wish I had her in person instead. Making a group chat with your classmates helps A LOT.
The class was so open ended we had no idea what was due when, what the expectations were or anything. She is such a sweet person, she's just entirely unorganized so this class was a headache.

reviews.comment: Nothing about this class matters. She is very happy and eccentric but has no awareness of what is interesting to students. Goes on tangents. Grades down for disagreeing with essays and not on the argument / quality. Do not recommend.

Personally, I really did not enjoy my experience with Professor Balbuena. It was extremely difficult to know what she expected from you, and she would grade you on standards that she never told you about. We had one cumulative assignment that I spent hours on, and she ended up not even grading it. I would not take a class with her again.

Kind of unclear in not only her expectations of you in class, but also in assignments. Her organization was nonexistant, and you could really see that on how she organized the Canvas website. Very, very poetry heavy. She's passionate about both poetry and the study of language, so prepare for translated poetry Ll term.

Prof. Balbuena is such an arrogant person. Though she has a vast domain in her topics, she does not consider the potential that a student may have. She is extremely rude sometimes and does not seem to be happy teaching. Also, she is the most  disorganized person I have ever met at the CHC.

Professor Balbuena's HC Lit class was hardly challenging but fun to take. She is an incredibly smart woman and speaks more than a handful of languages so a god portion of the class has to do with linguistics, regardless of the topic being studied. I recommend her classes, she is a passionate teacher with a lot to offer.

Never had issues getting a good grade. The self-directed nature of the research term works in her favor. Discussions were fine but nothing special. Won't do the work for you, but if you put in the time before seeking help she will lead you to success. Not the best prof, but not as bad as people make her out to be. I grew a lot from taking her.
Don't let her name confuse you. There is nothing "buena" about this class or the teaching style. The surprise quizzes are as frustrating as the way she grades your writing.

She is vague with what she wants in your papers but then grades harshly and without explanations.  Set an appointment to come into speak with her about my grade and the final research paper and she failed to show up.  This happened to other people as well.  No rubric and poor communication skills

Terrible Professor. She launches into spanish for absolutely no reason, she is totally disorganized, and does not provide good feedback on your work. Takes forever to grade anything, and her grades have little basis in any sort of scale. Does little actual teaching, just tests you knowledge in what she sees as important.

The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Interesting material, nice lady, but her teaching skills leave a lot to be desired. Didn't follow the syllabus, didn't give good feedback on essays, and rarely returned work.

Granted she is Brazilian, but this woman is a nightmare! She is NOT organized whatsoever, which makes the class very difficult. Due to her disorganization, we were not able to cover half the things that the syllabus said. When it came time to take the final we felt we were unprepared for the final that she administered. Don't take a class from her!
really interesting and stimulating material and discussions
not well organized but I learned a lot.
No Comments

At first, she appears to be fun and interesting.  After week 3, you realize that there are no themes to her discussions.  After you turn in your essays, you never get them back until week 9.  When you ask her for help on your essays, she does not provide ANY comments - she simply looks at the paper and shrugs her shoulders.  Balbuena = ****.

When in came to writing my evaluation for school I was bewildered. She is fun, funny, and even had the class over for dinner, but she puts you on the spot, and is intense! In retrospect, I am thrilled that I took the class and I think she was a great teacher!
I do not recommend this professor.  Period.
smart lady, no concept of teaching... i would NOT recommend her classes
Monique is so interesting and fun, but she expects a lot!
No Comments
His introduction classes were super easy, and he explained the readings and assignments well.

Bassem is amazing -- so kind, caring, and sweet. He has a LOT of energy and goes quick, so you need to stay on your toes! You have to show up to every class and come ready to participate, but it is so worth it. He is super funny and engaging. One of my favorite professors at the UO.

He quite obviously cares deeply about his students and their success, and he's really knowledgeable on the subjects he teaches, but he's just not an excellent teacher. He has a very aggressive teaching style, and will call you out if you don't partipate enthusiastically. He expects FAST learning, little to no review.Also, not good at using canvas.
One of my favorite teachers at UO. If you are looking to take Hebrew, he is a very funny and kind guy that cares about his students.
