reviews.comment: Baseem Hosny has to be one of the worst professors I have had at Oregon. Firstly he has a net total of 6 assignments that will make up your grade. 3 papers (easy), 1 group project that he provides little to no details about (not even a rubric!), 1 attendance grade, and 1 participation grade that is extremely biased. Also illiterate in canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible! He completely changed the content of this course and by the time i realized this it was too late to drop. All you do is read a book and then he yells at the class to discuss but doesn't actually teach us anything. It is an EASY class but absolutely not interesting or fun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Baseem is an awesome professor. He is nice and has a great sense of humor.  He does expect you to participate by sharing your thoughts but will never shame you if you are wrong. The course follows reading of "Scenes from the village life" by Amos oz, where every class is reading from the short stories and have a discussion. Essays are short & easy.

Taken several of his courses at Linfield. He is very passionate and caring. 
We have very different political beliefs but he often encouraged other viewpoints.  He also actively works to prevent his own political views from being taught in class, which is unfortunately uncommon in political science, and higher education. Overall great prof and guy!

Robin gives great lectures and cares about his students and the material. Attendance is mandatory, but missing class won't impact your grade if you participate. Lectures are super helpful where reading the text isn't even necessary. He grades super fairly and gives great feedback on exams and essays. Makes really hard topics interesting and fun.

Professor Barklis is a great professor. His classes are very lecture heavy but you get a break in the middle of class, and he throws in some jokes to bring you back into focus. His class is graded on two "take-home" exams and 1 essay (which he will give feedback on in advance), it is a very easy class if you take notes and review before the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Robin is an exceptional instructor overall, but his lectures are especially fantastic. He's approachable, down-to-earth, funny, uber-knowledgeable, and willing to go the extra mile for even just a chance at helping a student connect to the material. He'll make a great professor, he's one of the best instructors I've had so far at university. 10/10.

There were a lot of readings, but as long as you show up to class, you shouldn't have a problem just skimming the readings. Daily journal assignments were very up to interpretation and write about whatever you wanted for the most part. Book report was fun. Had to present in front of class multiple times
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her memoirs class, Dr. B makes meaning out of everything and genuinely adores teaching and connecting. Assignments aren't difficult, expect poetry and prose and writing authentically about personal things (& you will be sharing these to the class). She is understanding and can be confusing on what is due when, but just ask. Highly recommend

A sweet lady with infectious positive energy. Not a difficult grader, but expects you to be thoughtful and present. Sometimes her instructions can be confusing, but if you take the class at her pace, don't overthink anything, and reach out when you're unsure of instructions, it will be a fulfilling experience.

Dr. B is knowledgeable, devoted, and inspiring. However, her communication in all respects is incredibly confusing. Her syllabus is 30 pages long, and that's just a testament to how convoluted the information she offers is. Cool concepts and ideas for assignments, but very repetitive. She's a bit batty but impossible not to love.

Dr. Mossberg is an amazing woman who will teach you valuable lessons within and outside academia. She speaks beautifully as if she is constantly talking in rhythmic poetry and she is an inspirational genius. She will see beauty and genius in you no matter who you are and genuinely wants you to succeed.

Dr. B is a very nice, caring woman. Her classes are interesting, but she is terrible at communication and being clear. She also expected us multiple times to read a full book, write a 1-2 paper about it, and make a presentation with a partner, all by next class. Oftentimes ran over expected class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take this class!! Dr. B is one of the most lovely teachers you will ever have, and is really sweet and caring. If you're looking for a more manageable honors college class where you can be whimsical on the assignments this is the one for you. She can be unclear and a little sporadic with assignments sometimes but is very lenient.

Dr. B's superpower is her ability to teach students how to believe in their interests and passions on a foundational level. If you are a word nerd, or any kind of nerd, you will enjoy her classes. She will teach you what authentic interdisciplinary learning is, and the value of this is irreversible.

She really is the most caring teacher I have ever had! However, for those who have severe anxiety like me, she requires presentations every week and for me that was a lot to try and get through so just a warning. Her classes are heavy on participation so expect to have to do group projects/presentations and expect to read aloud often.

Regardless of the subject, take any opportunity to be in a class with Dr. B. She will be one of your greatest allies in the Honors College going forward. I took her HC 101 and 221 classes, and in both I laughed, cried, and sang with her, and I left each one feeling so sad it was over. I still have a card she wrote to me on my desk.

All I can say is that if there is a God, he sent down Dr. B. This woman deserves everything. Going to class was the highlight of my week, because I knew I was going to learn and have a good time while doing it. She teaches you how to write a strong thesis, while also being a teacher you can rely on. She may break out into song from time to time!

I took Dr.B's HC221 class! If you have the chance to take a class from her, DO IT! She is a poetic genius, and anyone would benefit from her teaching. The only complaint is that she struggles with canvas a little bit but do not let that scare you away. She is so caring and understanding, and she will work with you no matter what. LOVE DR. B!!

Dr. B is a real queen. She truly cares about her students and the material she is teaching. I would honestly take any class that she teaches. Can be a bit scatter brained but is very flexible and understanding.

If you truly lock in, complete all the assignments and go to class, you'll pass this class. HOWEVER, there was not one moment in the entire term where I was confident in anything I was doing and the lectures were incredibly confusing. I suggest you find people to study with.

Most confusing class ever, lectures never made any sense, he was rude and defensive when asked any questions, etc. No one I talked to in this class ever knew what was going on, and the professor was never any help. The only grace he gave us was making the final and curve "easy," as to not fail the entire class, but do not take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures were long and confusing, doesn't answer questions very well, i feel less smart after taking the course

I imagine everyone taking this class feels collectively defeated. Jori clearly knows what he's talking about but information is presented in a way that is obscure and unclear, hard to follow. Do not recommend this class if you want to learn anything.

I will give Jori the benefit of the doubt and at least offer that he is clearly very knowledgeable about his economic niche in a more corporate sense. However, that doesn't change the fact that his class was a living nightmare. I don't mean to be harsh but I really don't know why he's decided take up teaching. Avoid at all costs. (GE was also rude)

The worst professor I have had at UO by a wide margin. Has no grasp of where the class is at, deflects and outright refuses to answer Q's that are necessary to complete assignments. The professor really struggled to communicate with the students.

reviews.comment: Prof Barash is still developing as a professor. When teaching basic matrix concepts, his explanations were clumsy, giving incorrect notation, and a very unintuitive explanation of matrix multiplication. I've taken the lin alebra sequence already for context. I assume these teaching issues extends to the economics content which compounds difficulty.

Don't believe everything negative about Jori. He needs some more time. Teaching methods leave a lot to be desired, overcomplicates things often. If you have him for Econometrics or a related subject, the class will be a circle of hell-- and one of the deeper ones. That being said, he's super accomodating, brilliant and genuinely *tries*
Difficult, but if you work outside of class and go to his office you can obtain a decent understanding of the material.

lecture heavy. didnt slow down lecture pace when asked to do so. often brushed aside student questions. teaching style was monotonous. extremely difficult tests; averages for mid and final were sub 40%. practice test and lectures somewhat prepared me for exams. there is a significant curve that compensates for difficultly. avoid prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jori told us he is new at teaching (it showed) plus 311 is a hard class. But Jori tried to make the class better for us, helped in office hours and gave a generous curve. My classmates basically revolted when he announced the average despite the curve and they joked about review bombing him. Most of these comments are just sus and overblown.

Early in the course I went to office hours, I was struggling. Instead of helping me work through the problem, he said, quote, "Not to diagnose you or anything, but are you dyslexic?" Then asked me how I even got into the class and that I should drop. I still passed. This is the worst prof I have had. No desire to help students succeed. Power trip.

Jori Barash is probably the most unhelpful professor I've ever had. This class is hard as is, but with Jori as your professor it will be the most difficult class you've ever taken. I have absolutely no idea how I got a B in this class with a 64% pre-final but that curve alone should tell you how insanely difficult this class is.

Overall just a terrible professor. Doesn't care about the students at all and doesn't consider their feedback. Gives us one practice exam and the exam doesn't correlate one bit on the actual exam. Very monotone when he gives lectures and expects you to know every concept like you already have a phd in econ. Bouta call up UO and let em know wsp.

Prof was not great at explaining material and often overcomplicated a lot of it. Exams are much more challenging than problems given in class or on homework. I was in tutoring twice a week, attended class and still had a hard time on exams because he never taught us the material to that caliber, and would also include topics he never even taught.

The midterm score was an average of a 17 out of 45 which is less than 50%. He made the final exactly the same way and maybe made two problems slightly a bit easier but thats it. He doesnt have the personality of a caring teacher and I really think he should rethink his career. He doesnt like questions or things not going his way so…

If I could give negative ratings, I would. Worst Professor I have ever encountered. I don't know how Oregon hired him. Jori alone makes me want to transfer schools. I cannot tell you one thing I have learned from this class, and I have attended every class. I have gotten a 4.0 every term at this school and ended with barely passing from Jori
He was a very bad “teacher”

He has no clue what he's doing the entire class. I have no idea how this guy has a degree or has a job. Get this guy at a McDonalds, he belongs no where near a college campus. I hated every single class he taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The rating speaks for itself. He thought it would be a brilliant idea to have us retake the midterm to which the average was a 35% for extra credit. Someone asked if it would be graded on accuracy he smiled & said "I don't know". His handwriting is not legible, his ipad constantly unplugs pausing lecture, he kept making mistakes, overall terrible.

Worst professor I have had! He reads off slides for 2 hours every class and is annoyed when students ask questions. He teaches the class like we are all economics experts and gets confused himself when teaching. Tests are also extremely difficult (the midterm had an average below 40%), making it very difficult to get a decent grade in the class.

Adding to what others have said, he is very monotone and only reads off of slides. His lectures make little to no sense, and is not able to articulate a hard concept in a way students can understand. Handwriting is completely illegible and he will go through slides and concepts incredibly quickly. Does not take student suggestions into account.

When lecturing, he messes up his own problems... that's how hard he tries to make this course. After most of the class failed the exam, he still has not fixed anything and will probably make the exam just as hard or even harder. He is by far the worst professor I have ever had, and I seriously think he should rethink being a teacher.

Does not change any methods of teaching after receiving countless words of feedback from students. Handwriting is extremely hard to read during algebra examples and even messes up his own examples multiple times, throwing me off while trying to follow along. Does not set up class encore tutoring sessions either

Worst lectures in the world. Horrible handwriting you can't even tell what's he's writing. doesn't explain anything just does it. expects us to know everything like it isn't a super hard course. the most boring monotone teacher that teaches like someone is forcing him. doesn't care about students. the worst at answering in class questions

Imagine a teacher explaining economics to you as if he were talking to another economics professor...well you dont have to imagine it just take Jori's class. Just awful the midterm average was a 40 percent and he blamed it on the students and how we study??? How insane is that, if that doesnt tell you something about your teaching idk what does...

This is by far the worst professor at the U of O. The class avg for the midterm was below a 50% and then he proceeds to make it harder for the final by saying we cant put practice final questions on our one page cheat sheet he gives us. Do not take him you will fail and have to withdraw. Will make you feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: extremely lecture heavy. very dense material, 90-110 mins of pure slideshows every class. wouldn't adjust to classroom feedback asking him to slow down the pace of lectures. substantial curve though, which makes sense given the midterm average was sub 40%. manageable class, but not enjoyable. avoid if possible.

This man is genuinely the worst teacher I've ever had. Lectures were confusing and pointless. He has an over-inflated ego and ignores feedback, blames students, and makes the course miserable. He does not care about his students AT ALL. Avoid him at all costs. I hope UO does the right thing and makes sure he doesn't step foot in any Econ classroom.

Really boring but he gives out a huge curve attendence is not mandetory but your entire grade is based on the tests. As long as you get a 8/40 on midterm and final youll pass, assuming you did all the hw as well.

I have never been more frustrated in a class since being in this class, We have given feedback to him how he lectures too much content and confuses students in lecture. Tries to help but at the end of the day doesn't alter plans and is still teaching us a class or so before the final (midterm avg was under 40% btw)
Just don't take it if you do you'll regret and you'll hate yourself an Economics!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible Professor

This was hands down the worst professor I've had in college. He doesn't teach, he just reads word for word off the slides for two hours like a robot. When the class is confused (which is basically all the time), he gets annoyed and blames us for being behind. He acts like asking questions is an inconvenience. He doesn't care whether students learn.
Has extreme trouble explaining any concept. Not helpful when you ask questions

Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. He is unclear in his grading, his lectures are all over the place (and half the time he confuses himself on the material then is unclear when trying to explain it), and he does not care about any of his students. You will spend hours and hours studying just to fail all tests. Avoid him at all costs.

She was absent for 10/20 classes. Lectures consisted entirely of mindlessly reading off the slides with no added input or analysis. Class discussions happened in the first 2 weeks of class and then disappeared entirely. Little to no feedback given on assignments. Extremely disappointing for 400 level class. She's also a GE and not a real prof.

The grading for assignments was unclear and despite there being a rubric, she never actually provided the point break down on your assignments. They would sometimes provide feedback but it was one sentence and on other assignments I would have to email for feedback on my grades. I would recommend avoiding this class if you want to keep your sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're taking this class because you need it or it fits I wouldn't stress. As long as you do the work you'll be fine! However, I did find this class repetitive, boring and an excessive amount of reading. I was not a big fan of the reading guides they are time consuming and in my opinion it can actually make it harder for the material to stick.

This class was not challenging, however the lack of feedback and clear instructions made it more difficult than it needed to be. The content is very surface level and examines all types of inequality in U.S. systems. There were 2 relatively big projects, and long weekly reading quizzes plus one-page reflections.

Elaina Barker isn't even a prof, she's a GE with no experience in Poli Sci. She never gave any input for HW and you had to contact your GE for help 24.7. Reading guides every week are impossible to get almost 100% on, and required a weekly page of reflections that were a single participation point. For a 100-level class, it's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Would not recommend this class or this professor. The content is pretty interesting, but the grading makes it all not worth it. Your grade depends on 2 projects and reading guide quizzes. For being reading guides they're not easy to follow and I end up getting most questions wrong. You have to do page long reflections for a completion grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was taken based on one consistent book that we would read throughout the term, with a quiz every class for attendance and homework. I found it difficult to succeed in her course (as it is ENG101) due to the harsh expectations with grading and lack of consistent communication on assignments, especially with the coursework seeming easy.

I am so happy this class is offered and it is a wonderful idea, however, I wish it was taught by literally anyone else. Pretends to be nice, is actually incredibly rude and condescending. For every assignment and test, she has expressed how open ended things are and how it is hard to mess up, and then sends out an email about how everyone messed up

She assigns context dependent texts without giving context. Then asks students to interpret it just to call them out/insult them in front of the class as if to put herself above them. She is a bully with a privileged view on history not a teacher. I do not recommend this professor, instead take black studies (very similar texts)  - A black student
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She can be very abrasive when delivering feedback to students. She often encourages you to figure things out on your own; however, she is extremely unforgiving and unhelpful when you make a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her policy of calling people out in front of the class is incredibly subjective in what she decides to call out. There were students with good intentions who were publicly humiliated for minor things like slightly misusing a term. She doesn't allow students to defend themselves at all. Participation is important but most students are afraid to talk

If any professor in the English department deserves tenure, it's Professor Barter. Very intentional, approachable, and kind. Incredibly supportive, and sets students up for success in and out of the classroom. She's helped me apply for research opportunities and written me stellar letters of rec. Really cares about students.

Doctor Barter changed my life. She taught me the importance of how language should be used when referring to enslaved individuals and teaches topics such as slavery or racism with kindness, truth, and wisdom. She is one of the smartest people I have ever met in my entire life. She truly is my greatest inspiration in my academic career.
A really great professor. Class is interesting and she obviously cares a lot about her students.

While it is nice that there is no final essay, pieces of creative work are assigned instead. Thus the amount of time you spent for this class is not as predictable, since artistic creativity isn't consistent. Because of that, points given or deducted could seem arbitrary. Participation is very important.

I learned so much from Dr. Barter! She puts a lot of effort into giving feedback. She takes her black-centered space seriously so she will shut some comments/topics down sternly. This causes some anxiety but it's because she cares a lot. Once I got more comfortable in the class I participated a lot without fear. Just don't say anything tone-deaf.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: informative classes but if you have social anxiety you might want to avoid taking this class. 2 presentations. participation is a big part of your grade and you will not know your participation grade until end of term. she pretty much grades how many times you raise your hand. feedback is in form of 10 min voice memo. very constructive feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof.Barter is an amazing Professor. She is beyond passionate about her topics and fully changed the way I read books, and analyze text. I would not take this class if you aren't a English major, as it is reading heavy (1 book every 2 weeks). There are no tests or full length essays, and her grading is super clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Was looking forward to this class. However, most of the students in my class, including me, do not want to participate. If you say anything wrong about the topic, she will cancel you in front of the whole class in an embarrassing, humiliating way. This is ironic because participation is a huge part of your grade. So much for a safe space
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Barter is a great teacher but she is a harsh grader and participation really matters for your grade. The reading workload is also quite intense and I found myself spending hours on her class every night. That being said, I learned a lot from her lectures and she organizes her content in a really intentional way.
Dr. Barter is an amazing professor! Shes really helpful and accessible. Although her readings that she assigns can get lengthy. This is the second time I've taken her and her quality is consistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly rec this class with Dr. Barter!! Literally was the only class I looked forward to this year - class discussions were actually substantive and the readings were interesting. Also, she provides great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: this past year was a nightmare for a lot of reasons, but prof barters class was one of the only classes i actually enjoyed. i felt like my writing/thinking legit improved, which says a lot for me rn. we read some kinda charged stuff but she always made us feel safe discussing it. i wanna take her other class if i can.

This is my favorite prof in the English dept. I cannot say enough nice things about her. Amazing teacher, caring human, extremely smart thinker. She's the bomb! Take her upper division courses too. They will change the way you think.
Dr. Barter is a real gem. She cares, she's understanding, and she's fair with her grading. She give great lectures and holds class discussions effortlessly. It's never an awkward silence.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was the one class that I actually looked forward to going to! Prof Barter actually cares what we think but also does good lectures. She also cracks me up. I actually think this class helped me become a better writer in my other classes. Keep in mind, you have to actually show up, but it's genuinely worth it. Recommend a hundred percent.
There were 5 fairly difficult labs over 8 weeks. 2 field trips, which were fun. Lots of work in Google Earth pro. She is very specific about the criteria. She was a great professor.

Professor Dorsey is very kind and passionate about teaching earth science. The course was very fast-paced for 10 weeks, but if you attend the lecture it will benefit you. online, open-note exams, so take good notes! She is always willing to answer your questions and have engaging conversations with you, I would take her again if I could.

She is super passionate and knowledgeable about the subject, the lectures were engaging and there was a fun class trip to the coast. She is quite a hard grader, but once you know her expectations it gets easier.
Becky is a phenomenal teacher. She is very enthused, but very specific, which can make her out to be intimidating. Don't fall for it! She is very willing to help, but you have to work for it!
Great teacher, really loves the material.  Wants her students to love the material to.  She is extremely nit-picky, but she wants her students to be the best they can be!
Plays favorites, reduced interest in subject, nit-picky beyond belief

You're basically going to be sitting through a ted talk for every single class and attendance is required. She's nice enough to give you a rewrite on one assignment. But is you write what she wants to hear on every assignment you won't need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ben-Natan's Modern Isr*el/P*lestine (RMP forbids spelling out😐) was a great opportunity to study the historical roots and modern seeds of the crisis. She maintained really good discussions, assigned strong textbook materials, and could always answer any question. Her lecture slides were subdivided into sections that were easy to understand!.

Missing one assignment in this course will drop your grade for the rest of the term. The final paper is 2,000 words, difficult, and the prompt is released 3 days before the due date. She's definitely knowledgeable about the subject, but that doesn't make the class enjoyable.

I was often penalized on assignments for things not listed in the rubric or grading criteria. She is not very accommodating if you have an extenuating circumstance. She was not personable and lectures are long and boring.
She seems confused when she teaches. grading criteria is slim to none. she did not have any intentions to get to know students

Lots of reading is assigned and often needs to be used in the weekly paper and purposefully didn't make grading criteria clear (a GE told me), many students got punished for things not listed in instructions. Mainly referenced Israeli sources (including friends) which struck me as odd considering the current political climate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Computational Physics is a great class, very informative, you just need to actually pay attention during the lecture. If you tune out early on and try to focus later, you will not be able to follow along. Go to class, follow along, and you will do good. Most of the homeworks and midterm/final projects have the bulk of the content done in class.

He's a good professor that made lectures fun through his demos. There's quite a few things that you're graded on, so doing well on those assignments and retaking them if needed makes it easy to succeed.

Lectures were so interesting and engaging! This class is super manageable, come to class and finish the in-class activities, there's a bit of reading/annotating each week and one homework quiz per week.

Lectures were interesting and you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. Weekly quizzes and homework but they're all online and you're given unlimited tries on the activities and 2 tries on the homework so it's very doable. If you want an easy science credit and are even a little interested in astronomy take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Astronomy 122 is a interesting class, and professor Farr taught it well. He often includes activities, demonstrations, and questions as he lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is unable to properly lecture to her students. Not only do her study guides not follow her exams, the questions on the exam are worded to purposely confuse you. I could not tell you a single thing I retained from her lectures and I have taken two of her classes so far. I would AVOID taking her classes at all costs.
Made us purchase every subscription possible, which did not help my learning process effectively, making it a waste of time and money.

I wish I liked Dr. Bala because she is such a kind person, but she just not a good professor. Her flipped class style requires students to spend twice as much time on this course for the same amount of credit. Her lectures are rambling, make no sense, and are rarely relevant to course learning objectives. Be ready to teach yourself everything.

A helpful way to succeed in this class is by using flashcards and making connections between the material and real-world situations. The exams emphasize understanding and application rather than simple memorization of the textbook or slides. I also appreciated that the lowest test score is dropped, since it helps reduce pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Transcribe the notes into your own and read the textbook. Going to class is silly but attendance matters for your grade. She adds 2% at the end if you meet specific criteria.

The lecture is directly from the online textbook. If I didn't read the book I probably would've failed. The book is a must to get a good grade. The book taught me more about how to think than the psych professor. Kind of sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's very sweet but has no idea how to lecture. I've learned nothing from this class. Especially considering it's one of the first classes you take as a psych major it should be taught better. Literally changed my major because of her
please do not take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jagdeep is a wonderful person and about the worst professor you could find. She does not know how to lecture, and her lectures rarely are on topic for what is on the test. Beaware that you will have a test every other week. Super nice to talk to, but she doesn't know how to lecture.

Overall, you will have to google terms during lectures. The exams are material from every activity and homework assignment combined. The syllabus changes but you have to rely in it because not all assignments show up on canvas. She does drop your worst test score of the 4 midterms. Would not recommend for people who haven't taken a psych course.

Genuinely what the actual are we even talking about in this class. I don't know. she doesn't know how to teach I fear. no hate or shade to her, she knows what she's doing but doesn't know how to apply it to her lectures and it is very frustrating. Im writing this during her lecture.

She definitely is harped on too hard here! Lot of issues for sure: tons of weekly work compared to any other intro class, video lectures pile onto the hours already spent on this class, and the tests might as well be from a different class. But she wants students to succeed and has given several extra points of credit to everyone which helps!

Not a good teacher at all, very nice person but can't teach at all. Even paying attention in class isn't helpful because her slides make no sense and have nothing to do with the tests. Canvas is not organized at all and it's very hard to find things. She doesn't teach this class as an introductory class.

She does not teach like it is an introductory class. I know many people who have dropped the psych major because of this class. It is very hard to understand her lectures and the way she runs her canvas is horribly messy. Her slides are jumbled and confusing and are way too scientific for an intro class.

I think professor Bala has way too many opps on this website. She is considerate, passionate about psych and genuinely wants her students to succeed. The material is not too challenging (especially if you've taken psych classes before this one) but moves very quickly and can be hard to keep up with. Biggest complaint is waiting for test scores.

This Prof is smart but not a good teacher her lectures were not helpful at all on the tests and her tests were harder then they should be for an intro psychology class. If I could go back in time and not take this class I would. Prof. Bala is personable and nice as a human but is not a great educator.
The way she goes about lecturing is horrible. It's like she's talking to you for 2 hours NOT TEACHING. I felt like I learned nothing each class and the

How to pass the tests: ignore her nonsense outdated slides and lectures, study the textbook chapter's vocabulary+summaries, redo the inquizitives, google anything else you don't know on the study guides, and PRAY.
A waste to have an awful prof making an intro course so difficult and ruining psychology for others. 
If you can, AVOID TAKING HER CLASS

This class is extremely lecture heavy and the tests were very difficult. Lectures are very hard to follow and the slides are so confusing. It feels like she is teaching to an audience that is already supposed to understand the material even though it is an introductory class. Felt very hard to study for and get good grades.

very nice lady but was very inconsistent with releasing study guides and assignments (usually before the day they were due or a couple days before an exam). Slides are all over the place and do not correlate. She has a awesome passion for psychology and is really smart but does not know how to teach.

LONG boring lectures, she'll be on one slide for 10 minutes and just go on tangents. Tests are hard but if you study for multiple hours, you will be fine. Homework load is okay. I would only take this class if you have to. Your only going to get an A if you really have a love for Psychology.

Prof was utterly useless when it came to this class. ended up teaching myself the material, my other classmates & I relied on each other heavily for study material as she gives NO HELP for study guides. the lectures are all over the place, and you have to figure out how to pass an exam with info on it that you have not been taught. DO NOT TAKE!
telling me she's taught for 10 years but doesn't know how to dismiss a class after a test? I waited 30 minutes just tryna turn it in, represents the class as a whole. don't pmo...

Lectures are so hard to follow because she talks about nonesense for the entire two hours and you have to teach yourself the material. The exams are incredibly hard and only focus on random niche information instead of material covering the entire textbook. Avoid this professor at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly one of the most awful classes I have taken. I am still currently in the class and just waiting for the day I never have to take a class by this professor again. Your grade is majority test dependent, the study guides are awful and even say they may not help. Inquiz is given 1 day before it's due and must be a score of 1500. Lectures mandatory
flipped class, slides don't correlate.

The workload wasn't hard, but the tests were terrible. It's 40 question multiple choice exams every two weeks, but the study guide includes over 120 concepts, so you don't know which ones to focus on. Most of the questions are aimed to confuse you by having 4 correct answers but you have to choose the rightest answer. At least she's nice?

I went into this class thinking it would be easier since it's an introductory class, but I was so wrong. The lectures are so boring and she usually just goes on a long tangent taking up extra unnecessary time. The exam was nothing like the study guide. Her slides are so hard to make sense of and the exam itself was way harder than it needed to be.
She's nice but oh my god what is she talking about 99% of the time. I have a 4.2 gpa and I'm a psych major and I have no clue what's ever going on in her lectures.

Dr. Bala is a knowledgeable professor, but her lectures can move quickly. To succeed, read the textbook, take detailed notes, and use resources like Unstuck AI for study prep. The class requires effort, but is interesting if you engage with the material.

Dr. Bala is a very intelligent psych professor, but she went pretty quickly through slides and the tests were difficult. I am a little surprised at the bad reviews because despite her faults, she was very knowledgable and straight-forward.

Good professor strict. Goes through lectures quick and it can be hard to learn from them but if you read the chapter for each lecture before going to class you will understand SO MUCH MORE. Along with that, to effectively learn, read through and take deep notes on the chapters. The class requires a lot of effort but is very interesting.

I enjoyed my psych 201 class. It wasn't anything extraordinary. It was about what I expected from a 400 person lecture based class. Professor Bala is not the most responsive with emails, but if you go to her office hours or go up to her after class she will eagerly answer any questions you have. If you took AP Psych then the class will be easy.

The lectures are long and boring. The homework was not bad, just labs that took max 15 min. and then chapter reviews that do take a while, but I found them helpful for the exams. She takes forever to respond to emails/won't respond. Easy class if you took AP Psych.

Not only did she repeatedly not follow my accommodations, to the point I had to report her to the school, Dr. Bala curved my A DOWN to a B+ after final grades were due. She has horrific communication skills; never responds to emails and is very inaccessible outside of class. Lecture and textbook content is irrelevant to what is asked on exams.

Bala was ok. She wasn't terrible but she wasn't great. To pass the class you have to be willing to teach yourself (lectures are pretty much useless). Grading was clear, but beware 60% of your grade is from 3/4 exams given. Exams are multiple choice, so not horrible but still suck. Try to find a different professor, but if you can't you'll be ok.
test heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't think she was as bad as some others do, but I understand the low ratings. reviews.comment: shes not very straightforward. She can be difficult at explaining things. Tests are hard. She can be forgiving at times but its rare.
She is funny, but lectures are not very interesting. She skims over topics pretty quickly, which makes it difficult sometimes.
Not a great experience. Test heavy and study materials dont help with the tests.

reviews.comment: Bala is a great professor in my opinion. She will challenge you, hence a lot of the bad reviews, but if youre willing to study and put in the work, her class is absolutely worth it. I learned so much from her and would 100% retake the class.

reviews.comment: She does not explain concepts in depth and words questions to try to confuse people. Overall my least favorite professor I have ever had.

Heavily weighted online multiple choice exams that are instantly graded automatically would not appear in the gradebook for at least a week if not longer. Avoid this teacher if possible.
lectures are really boring, but if you take notes you'll probably be ok

So terrible. Lectures are a massive waste of time, 90% of it won't be on the exams. Terrible teacher; slides are impossible to follow, reading the textbook is way more useful. Takes as long as possible to grade tests; It has been 10 days and she still has not graded a multiple choice final, while most of my other teachers graded their short answer tests in a day or two.

In my opinion, Bala is an abominable professor, degrading students, bumbling on about comically irrelevant information, etc. On an open-note/book 50-question exam, there was NOT ONE QUESTION FROM CLASS MATERIAL! I Ctrl F'd every question. You'd learn more from staring at a doorknob. Avoid this class at all costs.
Everyone overreacts, she is so sweet and understanding to your needs, everyone is a jealous hater giving 1's
Goes so fast in lectures and is so hard to follow, unwilling to work with peoples accommodations, discouraging in class.
Bad. Bad. Bad. AVOID.

This is easily the worst class ive ever taken at UO. She NEVER responded to emails regardless of the content. The exams are nothing like the study guide and include subjects we didn't learn in class OR is in the book. So disappointed.

She is neither effective nor enjoyable. Test questions unrelated to what she's taught and worded awfully. Doesn't respond to emails. Seems too busy to care about the class. Assignments were irrelevant busy work graded by TAs. The course was unorganized and confusing. Not nice to students. Lecture slides don't make sense. Doesn't support students.

This is the worst class I have ever taken with the worst Professor I have ever had. She has single-handedly made me hate being a psych major. She does not respond to emails. Every person believed they had failed the midterm despite studying. She doesn't respond to her emails. Group projects. Not a well-structured course.

By far the most discouraging experience I have had in my collegiate career. Does not reply to ANY emails, is down right rude to students, and unprofessional overall. Lectures are from years ago and are explained in a difficult way. Reminds me of a teacher that I would have encountered in high school, not at a University where we pay top-dollar.

By far the most unprofessional and disrespectful professor in the entire state of Oregon. Her lectures make no sense and are recorded from 7-10 years ago. If you unfortunately have to take this course by her, reading the textbook is more helpful than lectures.

Worst professor Ive ever had. Spare yourself the trouble and avoid Dr. Bala at all costs. She is horrible at responding to emails and is quite unprofessional. I believe this course would have been much less difficult had she not been the instructor.

I found this class to be unnecessarily difficult. My biggest complaint is that her recorded lectures (which were from 3-7 years ago as of 2021 and sometimes were recorded "guest" lecturers) usually didn't make sense given what we had read in the textbook. reviews.comment: Literally take any other teacher possible. I could go on for hours but I'll leave it at that.

Her lectures and teaching style are hard to follow and make little sense, just stick with the book. Also be prepared to experience disrespect and gaslighting if you email her or ask questions during lecture. Take another prof if you can.

Her lectures barely make sense, the material is super old and she complicates things so much that it is much easier to just teach yourself from the book. Trying to get an email response from her is like pulling teeth, not mention she will lie about getting them and gaslight you. Her demeanor during lecture was horrid, disrespectful to students.

Professor Bala denied my AEC accommodations, claiming she never received an email from the AEC about them (I know she did because I was CCed on the email). If you use AEC accommodations I would avoid taking her class.

This was my least favorite class. The subject is a very interesting but the teaching was lacking. The material she presented was not complimentary to the tests given. The class itself was pretty easy and straightforward, my biggest issue was the midterm & final which account for 45% of your grade. She is so unresponsive and her remote learning class is boring and unorganized.

reviews.comment: She uses lecture videos from 2014. So much information on the screen and she uses words that she expects us to know but gives no background information on. She is disorganized, doesn't answer emails, and is an extremely hard grader. She also gives pop and reading quizzes which are really tough, even if you read!! UGH. reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was an 8-week summer class taken online, and it really wasn't that bad. Kind of a lot of little assignments and average-length lectures but they were fine. Jag as a person is nice and funny, but as a professor she is disorganized and has difficult exams and quizzes. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

She forgot our FINAL EXAMS so we had to waste 45 mins of our final. She makes EASY concepts IMPOSSIBLE to understand. And she blames everything on us and doesn't acknowledge her own mistakes.

This professor was a nightmare. Not only are her classes poorly structured, but she makes simple concepts feel so much more difficult. She makes you contradict yourself (all because it's a teaching moment in congestion), and patronizes her students when they try to answer in discussion. If you like psych, avoid her classes at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lecture videos were often impossible to understand and full of glitches and audio issues. The tests are worded in ways that make this feel a bit like an sat that you didn't prepare for and that's after studying hard. Tough Class

I have never taken a more confusing and downright disorganized class. I never knew what was due, the emails that were sent out were always out of date, and the amount of mistakes through the lectures, study guide, and test were insane. This is the absolute worst class I have taken (and I took the General Chem sequence)

Professor Bala is by far the worst instructor I've ever had at the University of Oregon. Her lectures are nearly incomprehensible. She spends too much time on things that don't matter, and not enough on things that do, making it hard to tell what she was even talking about in the first place. Tests are full of grammatical errors and poor wording.

I admire that Professor Bala is very passionate about Psychology. But, the course was pretty tough for me. It was very heavy on memorization which is something I am not good at. Lectures were very long and she would often speed through some slides. Exams were very detailed and it was hard for me to pass them. I am unsure if I would take her again.

This professor interjects little bits of her arrogance into the lectures weekly. Mentioned she "knows four languages" multiple times and likes to brag about her accomplishments. We are here to learn, not to fuel her ego. Class was moderately challenging, but A is possible with effort. Lots of quizzes, and there is a lot of group work as well.

The class seems somewhat fine until her weekly quizzes become SUPER hard, I expected to get a C or worse on most of them. As for the midterm, the best score I heard of was a 75% and most people fell in the 50s or below. She reuses lecture videos from past classes. VERY hard to succeed, hardly learned much. Very degrading class and she didnt care.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her quizzes and exams are very unclear. The material is not too difficult to understand, but she makes the questions unnecessarily difficult and confusing. She takes forever to respond to emails or flat out ignores them. She took an interesting class and ruined it with horrible tests questions.

She is the rudest professor I have ever have and will never have again. She is so unpleasant if you come to office hours and makes you feel like you are wasting her time. If shes not interested in answering an email, she won't. Class is unreasonably hard when compared to the same class taught by other professors. Hard tests and HORRIBLE powerpoints
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really did not like this class. I took extensive notes for every class. I got a B- in the class after struggling through each midterm, quiz, and the final. This class made me lose faith in myself. I was trying everything and studied all the time and still felt like a failure. Do not recommend. She makes tests really hard and not lecture based.

I will not take a class with this professor again. This class could be really interesting but she doesn't care about teaching at all. She's rude to students and seems super annoyed when people ask questions. It's incredibly difficult to know what's important information to know. Her slides are paragraphs of random bullet points. Super frustrating.

Her teaching style consists of dimming the lights to go over super dry content and explain things poorly. All her classes are  the same: 6 MC quizzes (drops lowest 2), 2 midterms, and a final plus an easy research paper. Basically just memorize what she says and it's easy, because she just  throws facts at you without the context of modern research

While the professor is funny and tries to bring fun into the classes, the exams are unclear and worth over 50% of the final grade, but on the final, the average was below 50%. I, myself, managed to get roughly 95% in every other aspect of the class, the exams really brought my grade down. They were poorly written and very confusing.

Professor Bala was a hard grader, but very personable. Her lectures were slightly above average and her personality and willingness to work with students is phenomenal. The subject-matter was inherently difficult due to a the large amount of vocabulary retention required for the course, but she did great. Her study guides were great, also.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I have never rated a professor before but came to save people from making the mistake of taking a class from Jagdeep. She doesn't answer emails, her tests are the hardest I've ever taken, her grading is strict, she is rude to students, doesn't speak english too well, her slides are convoluted and cluttered and littered with grammatical errors.
Love her lectures! Very fair and helpful. Tough tests but study guides are helpful.

Her lecture slides are novels. Way too confusing and too much information on the slides, you can barely even read it. She is not very helpful at all and often makes you feel dumb if you don't know what she is talking about.  Highly recommend avoiding a class with her.  She is a great person/ also a great advisor but not a great teacher.

I had a class at 8:30am and only showed up for quiz days (attendance2% of final grade). For her tests and quizzes, I just reviewed the material (slides+textbook) and I was able to pull off a B. If you aren't going to go to class, go for quiz days so you know where you stand grade wise. A lot of material isn't fairly new if you have prior psy knowl

NOT APPROACHABLE. She makes fun of her students in class constantly. I actually don't understand- I think she's trying to be funny but it's at the expense of her students intelligence.  This class was hard, but I was too scared to approach her with questions because she is such a bully.
has she ever answered an e-mail in her life? students from her classes 4 years ago are still waiting for a simple response.

There is so much material in this class which can be confusing. She has weekly quizzes, so read and go through lecture slides. She gives 15 pages long study guides and would only use a small portion of it on the exam, which i found frustrating. Do all the extra credits, and participate.

She is a solid professor. Do the assignments, show up to class, read and you should be good. She has weekly quizzes, but they are fairly easy if you've paid attention. Her test were medium in difficulty, but if you study smartly you'll be good (she gives study guides though-vague ones).  Interesting class, who doesn't want to learn about drugs?

No not the one. She is nice, and class are fun and interesting, but the exams are very very specific and detailed which makes it hard, its m/c exams very tricky. I say find another if you want to get a good grade. But she does offer extra credits which helped me rise my grade.
Very funny and nice. Her tests are kind of hard, but gives a TON of extra credit, so you can pretty much get an A or B without ever studying. I would highly recommend her!

Her class is really really easy to do well in. I got C's on all the tests but did good on the easy weekly lab quizzes and slid by with an A-. Her lecture notes are all over the place, so just do your reading and its best to do it before the class so you go in knowing what she's talking about.
She's hilarious and easy to talk to.

Jagdeep is an amazing instructor and she wants you to understand the material and will help anyway she can. She also gives extra credit and if she makes a mistake she will fix it. This class was extremely difficult but fun and interesting. I suggest you refresh brain regions before taking this class.

If you believe that college is a place where you pay money to read a book at you than this is your prof. She has absolutely no presence during class, her slides are very, very wordy. Cannot engage a class of this size, I'd learn better reading the slides on my own in my spare time then being required to come to this boring, molasses-like class.

Good professor overall. Nice, respects students opinions and allows everyone to speak, no matter their view. Dr. Jagdeep is an extremely smart individual who knows exactly what she is talking about, but she does expect quite a bit from her students.

There are weekly labs which are only 4 questions, pretty easy. She is a pretty funny teacher for it being a really long class. If you read the textbook you will probably get a really good grade (and go to lecture). It is really basic, not that hard.
Funny
Hard class. Lots of material most of which is only in the reading NOT covered in class. Also this class moves at a very fast pace with lots of material to cover,
Wonderful lady, cares about students, clear, extra credit, if you go to office hours you will get a good grade. LOVED HER

DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CLASS unless you are willing to put in a good 20 hour a week commitment.  Good teacher, had her for Psychoactive Drugs. This class MUCH harder, tests insanely hard.  Not sure exactly what she wanted to had to know EVERYTHING.  Very comprehensive and in-depth material.
Jagdeep teaches the material well. She also clear and reasonable expectations.

Great teacher! She is clear about what she wants from her students and grades very fairly. Lectures are interesting and very informative. Dr. Bala also gives numerous opportunities for extra credit. Highly recommended!
Good teacher!

She is an amazing professor!  She is so enthusiastic about what she is teaching it makes you want to pay attention!  Even at 8:30 in the morning I am excited to go to class! She gives extra credit during classes when students are sparce. All her lecture slides are from the book so if you miss a class just read the chapter.

She is great! Knows her stuff and keeps the class fun with her sense of humor. She doesn't drill you on the boring details, and doesn't expect you to remember them either. Everything that is on the tests is covered in class lectures. She makes lectures fun and gives many extra credit opportunities. I highly recommend her!

She was awesome, funny, and spunky. I would definitely recommend her to anyone. She was very helpful but the midterm and final were a little difficult but her class has plenty of extra credit opportunities as long as you go to class.

Her exams can be hard, but are not impossible if you study hard! She is a fun professor in class as well, and knows way too much! Its almost intimidating. But anyway, I highly recommend her! Just be prepared to work for your grade.

Jagdeep is a really nice lady and a good professor. I am taking Psychoactive Drugs from her, and she really knows her stuff, is down to earth, easy to talk to and willing to help. Definitely recommend taking 383 from her. Makes class fun, and even at 8:30 in the morning.

All her slides are online, a repetition of the book, but she has mandatory attendance with the Iclicker and sometimes when not that many students show up she gives out EC. As long as you read, you'll be fine on the tests; I got an A+. But warning, you want to kill yourself it's so boring.

One word: HORRIBLE! Her lectures were boring and hard to follow. Her study guides weren't consistent with what was on the exam. Her exams had some ridiculous questions, asking things that we barely went over in class. I have gotten mostly A's in all my psychology classes and I got my worst grade so far in her class. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS!

I would not recommend this professor.  Lectures were extremely boring and hard to understand.  The tests were also extremely difficult, especially if you struggle with multiple choice.  She also said she was going to curve our grades, and in the end chose not to which hurt a lot of people's grades.
Great teacher! She covers a lot of material but makes it really interesting. She is extremely fair but requires high attendance and you have to keep up with reading.
She is extremely boring, I am actually about to fall asleep in her class right now. gnight

Very nice lady.  Terrible teacher.  The material is not present well at all.  Very confusing flow.  Text book is terrible as well.  It is all very hard to follow and there is really no flow.  I would not recommend this class unless you are prepared to be very, very focused and dedicated.
Hard class. Good, fair prof.

At times she was a little overwhelmed with the summer time frame being so fast, but she made fair adjustments when she realized that there were certain aspects of biopsychology that we just couldn't learn in that period.  She is a humble and friendly person whose teaching is above average.
She has to cover a lot of material in a fairly short amount of time so it is fast paced. You really do have to do the reading and prep to keep up. If you do, it is a very interesting class.
Very nice, very smart, helpful if you go to office hours. Moves really fast and can be hard to keep up with. Good idea to review notes ahead of class to avoid being totally lost.
She is amazing!
Please don't take a class from this teacher! She is very smart but a bad teacher.

She is a nice teacher. Her lectures are simple and covers most stuff from the textbook. I like her lecture slides since its not only words but also pictures. Exam is little difficult but study guide really helps!
Really interesting class, not especially difficult as long as you can deal with multiple choice. Do the reading, go to office hours if you need help, don't miss any discussions.
No Comments

He's the most relatable professor I've had here. He's funny, he will cut lecture short if he feels like we've gone through enough for the day, his tests are exactly like what we go through in class. Overall, good experience and would recommend him.
If you take Fin 316, he is your best choice!

Great finance professor with real life experience and clear instructions. Textbook "required" but he managed to explain all the concepts through slides. Lectures made finance interesting. Come to lectures to get examples and cases explained.
Awesome professor who relates to students and is amazing at braking down tough concepts. One of the best professors I will ever have

Good professor, really smart guy having gone to Northwestern & Stanford. Really no complaints about the guy. Hw was tough and tests were challenging but everything was fair. If you end up in his class, you won't have any complaints about him or his teaching style

Nice and likeable guy, but makes homework very challenging.  Sometimes he tweaks it from what he teaches in class and when you ask him he say's he wants you to think outside the box... WE have shown homework to tutors and they had no clue how to solve it.  The tests are very difficult but at least he grades on a curve.  YOu need it!

Vineet was a very clear teacher. He did try to use some humor in the class but often times it was sarcasm which wasn't fun. For the teaching part I was able to keep up with what he was saying rather easy with all the formulas and what not. If you are not good at math this class might not be easy for you. Lots of equations.

Robert Binder is the most caring, respectful, and engaging professor I've had. His real-world projects are fascinating, and I credit him with helping me build the skills that led to my first full-time job. His discussions challenge our thinking and broaden our perspective. Ask him about Europe—he's the GOAT!

Dr. Robert Binder is the most caring, respectful, and engaging professor I've had. His real-world projects are fascinating, and I credit him with helping me build the skills that led to my first full-time job. His discussions challenge our thinking and broaden our perspective. Ask him about Europe—he's the GOAT!

You might not like it if you're just taking his classes as electives or you aren't into transport or planning, but if this is your area of study you'll love Robert. Very experienced, very kind helpful and understanding, fun assignments, grading is easy to understand. Disorganized at times but still attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Disorganized. Doesn't challenge you or care if you learn anything. All a big joke really.

Given that this was my first PPPM class here as a senior in another major, I was incredibly nervous before taking this class, given the unknown. I have never had a professor as kind, understanding, and supportive as Robert Binder. He was able to make everything super digestible and understandable, and was always willing to talk. He's the goat.

Honestly this is the worst class I have ever taken. The material you learn will be amazing but she doesn't teach it to you, you teach it to yourself through her many assigned readings and videos. It's obvious she loves to hear herself talk and thinks of herself highly. Lectures are boring bc she doesn't have anything new to say. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Prof. Beck's class. She very clearly knows what she's doing and I found her lectures very fascinating and easy to follow. There is a lot of homework, but I felt like the assignments she gave helped deepen my understanding of the topic and helped me perform better on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Beck clearly knows what she's doing; her lectures are well thought out and easy to understand. Although I found the material dull, I learned a lot. SO MUCH HOMEWORK but at least her late policy is somewhat forgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked her until I was a little late to class and she didn't give me credit for being there. I also emailed her multiple times with no response. She gives way too much work and the questions in the quizzes don't really match up with the reading. She is quite funny but I don't think the GEs for her class are very good.

Prof Beck uses a flipped classroom model, in which students do 95% of the work that would otherwise be her job. She stumbles through lecture slides in class reiterating what she said in the outdated lecture videos from 2020. I think her class would be better if lectures were given in class and participation was higher for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very textbook/homework heavy class. There's an expectation that no technology is used in the classroom which is a tad annoying because basically everything taught was in the textbook. If you listen in the lecture the tests will be fine. She tries not to be too political but is clearly liberal if you care. Would take again and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Beck is very knowledgeable and cares a ton about her students. Her class was engaging but had a heavy workload. She expects about 6-8 hr dedicated to homework a week and there is punishment for late work. Tests are free-response questions and were easy to BS when I didn't know the answer. Only take if you are interested in the Poli Sci.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof requires everyone to be fully engaged with no laptops or phones. However, I honestly thought this enhanced the class environment. She really cares about the topics she's teaching and made an intro level class interesting and engaging. I plan on taking more of her classes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors and classes at UO. Learned a lot of important stuff about Latin America and interconnected global policies.
Dr. Beck gives great lectures with mandatory attendance. Great professor, but expect tons of homework. Tests are all in essay format.

Dr. Beck is the person who inspired me to declare Political Science as my major. She's an amazing lecturer and has very clear grading criteria for assignments. There is a ridiculous amount of homework, but I've learned more in this class than any other at UO. If you do the homework, you barely even have to take notes in lecture. HIGHLY recommend.
its a reading heavy course, but she makes it very enjoyable and is an engaging lecturer with a lot of knowledge on the topics she is teaching.

Dr. Beck is one of my favorite professors at the university. Though she uses a flipped classroom that is reading and lecture heavy, this ensures you learn the content really well. I would recommend her classes to anyone who is serious about learning the content of the courses beyond just an easy A (which is not hard to get if you do the work).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't let the reviews stop you from taking one of her courses. There is a lot of work for her courses and she expects a lot out of but welcome to an upper division course. She is extremely helpful and willing to guide students through the course. She makes herself available outside of class and has extremely clear guidelines for all assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I only took this class because it was necessary for me to take other PS courses. If this class wasn't required I would have never joined in the first place. I believe she thinks this is the most important course and fails to acknowledge the workload students receive from other courses.

Amazing teacher, Homework is a lot and the readings take time but the structure of her classes really helps you learn. All essays for exams but it's all stuff covered in lecture. Very easy to get extensions, really cares about her students and well beings. Would highly recommend taking class with her if your passionate about political science.

I have so much respect for Prof. Beck because she is knowledgeable and responsive. We participated in discussion every class. The workload requires lectures, readings, and quizzes before each class. The midterm is 3 little essays and one bigger in a week. However, i still reference the content because I was so invested. A class for passionate ppl.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved taking Professor Beck's class. A lot of the class material stuck with me and was eye-opening. This class does require a lot of time and dedication but it is 100% worth it! The class was structured with online video lectures and then in-person lecture time was more for clarification and questions. Would totally recommend this class!!!

Genuinely the best poli sci professor i've ever had. Yes you're gonna have to do work sorry you're in college. Lectures are super interesting and you will learn a ton from her class. She is very charismatic and funny, but also extremely passionate about the subject. Lots of opportunities for extra credit if you want to put in the work.

Prof Beck does expect you to do a fair amount of work but if you care about what she teaches it doesn't really matter. She is funny and likeable and cares about her students. She is well educated and is good at explaining the subjects she teaches. I really enjoyed taking her classes.

Uses quotas for grading tells GE's to lower grades so class GPA is not too high. Only gives out a small number of A's. So if you are not at the top 1% of class do not expect to get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content: interesting! However the biweekly quizzes were the bane of my existence. Questions like "which percentage: 1%,2%,4%,6%" to find in 20ish pages of reading- quizzed on highly frivolous aspects of the reading. 3 thought papers were fun, but the midterm and final were ridiculous, 4 papers in 7 days?? Doable, but quite unideal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Beck is an amazing teacher and I would definitely take one of her classes again. She is funny and usually cheerful, but can also be serious no-nonsense. She assigns a lot of work and expects a lot from her students, but she's very open to discussing/answering questions and you'll learn a lot taking a class with her if you apply yourself.

Was afraid to take her class due to RMP reviews, but so glad I did! Lectures are interesting, and she really cares about what she teaches. Lots of discussion in class. Participation points are part of your grade, so speak up! There are also lots of opportunities for extra credit which is great. Lots of readings, but they are quite fascinating
Awful professor, if you can even call her that. This teacher should be in another department and not teaching classes that students require for their PS degree.

Beck can be kind of scary but you will definitely learn a lot in her class if you have the time. The class sets you up to succeed but it is a TON of work. I took multiple classes of hers because of interesting topics and her GE's are the best. She is also more flexible than you'd expect about due dates, extra credit, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: In a 100-level class named "Intro to Political Science," I was not anticipating a professor to come out and demand 30 hours per week of dedicated time to her class. This is an absurd amount of time dedication, and comes close to jobs I have worked in the past. This class should not be a full time job, but the time requirement is insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beck was the professor for my first PS class, and she made me love it! While the course was quite rigorous and demanding for a 100 level, if you keep up to date with assignments and readings, it's not that bad. Beck is highly intelligible and very helpful if you reach out. I have PS380 with her next term and can't wait!

Dr. Beck is the BEST prof I've had at UO. She can be strict but only because she doesn't put up with attitude and demands the respect she deserves. Attendance is mandatory but her lectures are so fascinating that you'll want to go, plus she's not going to test you on things she doesn't put in lectures. Take her class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is tough, there is a lot of readings and quizzes to go with every reading/lecture. There are no tricks in this class and if you do the readings you will be able to pass the class easily, the tests are based around questions she gives you in lectures. Go to her office hours she is a brilliant and kind professor and knows her stuff!

Professor Beck is a truly amazing teacher. Her lectures are so informative, and although she assigns a lot of work, everything is super valuable-no busy work. This was the most organized class I have taken during COVID, and she utilizes canvas so well so you always know what to do for the week. I learned so much from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a really smart woman and clearly knows what she's talking about, but she's for some reason decided to make an intro level class 100x harder than it needs to be. Homework due at 5pm, can't do it out of order, and in order to take notes you have to listen to exactly what she says b/c there are no slides with words. If you have her for PS111, GL
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she is very smart and truly makes one understand PS the course isn't too bad it's the workload! an average week would be 60 pages of reading at least 4 lectures, pulse 3 videos with quizzes after everything, along with two 300-word discussion posts every other week, and then on the weeks with no discussion post there is a 1000+ word exam 4 in total
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really passionate about political science and covers material well. THERE IS A LOT OF HOMEWORK (around 12-15+ hours every week) and requires a lot of time and attention. Also a fair amount of textbook reading. Easy to fall behind. Really interesting class but extremely time consuming.
You better have a lot more time on your hands if you want to pass this class with a decent grade. I wouldn't take her again because she makes the class way more difficult than it actually should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Way too much work for a 100 level class. I wouldn't even bother communicating with her because she gives off the vibe it's either my way or the highway!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class might be a bit different when taken in person, but I kinda enjoyed the online format. Lots of videos were assigned and there was a quiz for each video. I liked being able to have the quiz open while watching the video because it forced me to pay attention. A hefty amount of work was assigned each week and the textbook was quite boring.

Do not take this class if already have a large workload from other courses or even a part-time job. This class demands 12 hours of work a week. It honestly feels like she forgot we are taking other classes or she is greatly underestimating the difficulty of her own assignments. I did all of my work and understand the content of the class but...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Beck is an amazing teacher that made me proud to major in Political Science. It is a ver heavy course with 12+ hours of work a week. I recommend working with friends, office hours and becoming close with GE's (as they grade you). It is a hard course but very rewarding, if you manage time wisely. She is very accommodating, if you communicate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am a PS major, and Intro to PS w/ Professor Beck was the hardest PS class I have ever taken (hardest meaning most time-consuming). She is intelligent & organized, which I always admire; I do not look for easy. But, this is so ridiculous since this is supposed to be an introduction class. I definitely do not plan on taking a class of hers again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 12+ hours of work per week in an intro to poli sci class. Unbelievable. Tons of busywork that is semi unrelated and if the coursework was only her lectures it would be more manageable. Class is doable but you must have the time to devote to it. DO NOT TAKE if your schedule is loaded or if you have a job. It would be nearly impossible to do well.
Terrible

You have to set aside plenty of time for this class, so beware. If your schedule doesn't allow for literal hours of work, you should probably drop it. Kind of ridiculous for a 100-level. However I learned SO much, and you can tell she genuinely cares about her students. If you put the time in you will get a lot out of it.

I am a sophomore taking this class, I held off taking any Polysci classes until the election would roll around because I thought we would at least be talking a bit about the election.
