This class however was filled with so much material that it was difficult for someone who isn't a geology major to understand. He definitely makes you work for your grade and I even had to go to multiple extra credit opportunities to keep my A.

This class was nearly impossible. I took it as a fun class, and ended up stressed about passing the entire term. Prof Blackwell is not understanding and grades assignments extremely hard. He claims his tests are fair even though they are literally the hardest thing I have ever done. Do not take this professor. You will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Blackwell is an awesome person to get to know. He's super friendly, your average granola, outdoors dude and is a great person to know. But, his tests are very difficult. Very. Difficult. His class has to be a major priority. Be at every single one of his office hours.
I have taken many lasses from him and I love geology now. I am getting a minor in Earth Sciences now! Take as many classes as you can from him and go on the affordable field trips.

He is a super nice guy and the way he talks about his love for geology and his family is so wholesome and sweet. Just what one needs in this death trap we call school. His lectures, hw, and weekly article summaries are all straightforward The tests are easy if you do the HW and go to class.

Lectures were heavy with lot of material. Homework assignments were handed out without notice, quizzes were given every Friday. Tests were the hardest I've ever taken in college! There were two labs due a week and we had to spend a lot of time outside of scheduled lab time finishing them. Spent too much time focused on the workload to learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is an excellent teacher and always willing to explain things and has office hours regularly and very willing to accommodate odd hours. If you show up and do your work you will pass, but if you don't show up to class you won't do well. You get the grade you have earned and if you don't go to class why bother going to college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Not sure if it was the class or the professor but this dudes tests were insanely hard and impossible to prepare for. The average on the final was a 60 and the class wasn't curved at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He really knows what he is talking about and gets so passionate about our earth. Its awesome! Cares when you care so if you show effort and try, passing should be a breeze.

Dave Blackwell should not be teaching introductory geology. He is extremely passionate about the subject and very knowledgeable but has no idea how to teach it to first years or beginners. This is a fault he is willing to admit as he himself said he would struggle to teach the course on the very first day. Made geol 103 the hardest class I've taken

He is the best teacher I ever had in UO. He has tons of homework, lab work and etc, however, you will earn a good grade if you memory the graph. He also give 8 points curve. He also provide field trips in UO which is so fun to join it. It is a fun class,but also can learn a lot. I highly suggest to take is course once you have times.

For a beginners class, this was ridiculous. The tests were so hard and his study guides don't help at all. Dave is passionate about geology, but that doesn't help you understand the material any better. Probably one of the hardest classes I've ever taken at Oregon. Definitely avoid him if you're not a major.

Geology 103 was honestly the most boring class I ever had... The teacher has somewhat of an attitude, the tests are ridiculously hard for a 100 level course, and attendance is MANDATORY.... Do not take this class if you are not in the major...

Ridiculously and unnecessarily hard tests. Review sheet is useless. Power points were put together rushed and  unorganized, making it hard to follow the course.  It is very obvious he did not put much effort into the structure of the class. Some labs are too long to finish in the allotted time. He is very knowledgeable and the field trips are fun.

I had him as a teacher for a beginners geology class and the material covered didn't feel like it was meant for beginners. If you are a visual learner Dave is not for you, as a lot of his teaching is through his words instead of his power points. As someone who is not a geology major, I will not be taking a class of his again.

Though Blackwell knows his material that he teaches very well, his teaching doesn't seem to convey very well to the students. His PowerPoints are "bare" so-to-say meaning that you have to take notes in order to get a good grade. There is a daily assignment in class everyday of lecture. Homework should be expected every week, even week 10.

daily quizzes, but offers two grading systems (one w an essay and lower weighted midterm and final) and extra credit movies every week (up to 4% on grade in class e.c.) Contents kinda difficult but pay attention and you can pass easily

Dave is a great instructor with a true passion for geology. He want you to succeed, but also makes sure that you work hard. Skipping class is a bad idea, because of daily graded in-class assignments, and the topics move very fast so it's not worth missing lecture. He provides print out notes which are helpful, but annotate them if you want to pass.

Guy was rude, boring as heck, and didn't explain things thoroughly.  The class was 2 and a half hours long twice a week...soooo hard to concentrate. He's a really hard grader and his multiple choice questions are frustrating.  He also accused a few of us of copying on hw, which was completely false. You can only write a correct answer so many ways!

Super passionate about his job and sets it up so easy for anyone to succeed in this class! [I only opened my textbook once and that time wasnt even necessary.] Uses great analogies and examples that easily make concepts 'click'. I strongly recommend taking a class taught by Dave Blackwell.

Cute in the old man kind of way--reminded me of Santa Claus. Kind of rambles, but uses interesting visual presentations like silly putty. But for reals, Geology 101 is like top 5 hardest classes I've ever taken, which sounds sad but it's very detail oriented and a LOT of information.

This guy is great. He plays with silly putty, twigs, blocks, and ropes to demonstrate earthquakes. He gives 5-point quizzes every day (basically attendance). He does a good job, it's not his fault geol is boring.

I have never been so bored in my  life. He's very intelligent, very well-informed, and completely mind-numbing. Who knew it was possible to make learning about earthquakes and volcanos less interesting than watching paint dry?

I couldn't stand this guy.  The way he lectures is awful, I just get the sense of a really obnoxious attitude and he is difficult to follow.  People did not get a good grade in this class, largely I think because he is so hard to listen to in lecture and understand what he's trying to say, and largely because his tests are very focused on minutia
Excellent teacher. Cool dude. Pay attention and respect the class and you'll do great.

Although he isn't the most interesting teacher to listen to, he is willing to spend a lot of time helping you in and outside of class.  He also provides extra credit and the in-class assignments and homework help your grade a lot. If you want to learn something, he will teach you a lot!

A LOT of material, so attendance is a must. Also, you have to turn in in-class assignments and one-page homework at the beginning of the week. If you aren't there, you'll get docked 50% when you DO turn it in. He's really nice though and does interesting field trips. I recommend Blackwell, he really is interested in the material and

Great professor- always willing to help students and gives a lot of extra credit opportunity. Also, allows students to write a term paper- which then lowers the weight of the final exam. It is a difficult 100 level class, but you will definitely learn alot!

Dr. Blackwell is Awesome. Knowledgeable, helpful, and passionate about geology. He explains concepts clearly and his lectures reflect the test well. Interesting course if you're into geology, not so much if you're looking for an easy science credit.

Offers lots of extra credit. A little snappy and hates it when people leave class during lecture. Tests contain a lot of material, but not necessarily difficult. Lectures are somewhat monotone. And on a side note... he says "in there" at the end of every other sentence -- 71 times in one lecture!
geology 101

The amount of material in this class is ridiculous. I refilled my printer TWICE in a quarter for this class/professor. For a 100 level class, this was far too difficult. If you are an upperclassmen looking to take an easy science, don't take this one. Ya, he offers extra credit. So what? The tests are weighted and extremely difficult. stay away.
Gives tons of Extra Credit opportunities. The tests were difficult.

Dave definitely knows what he is talking about although lectures can get extremely boring but are still filled with a lot of notes and important information.  He offers a lot of extra credit which is nice because the midterm is pretty hard.
Really knows what he is talking about and the class and labs are very interesting.  Love the ec movie nights as well. However the midterm was way harder than expected.
so boring you have no idea, struggle to get through the class every single day. Would rather try to run away from LaMichael than go back to that class again. skeet

Dave is awesome. He knows his stuff and is excited about it, which makes the class itself exciting. He makes himself very available to students which is really helpful. Sometime the lectures can drag on, but that only seemed to be because they were 2 hours. Great guy and great teacher.
Very very knowledgeable and excited about the subject. Is a an amazing and fun tour guide on the field trips.

Dave is THE MOST dedicated teacher ever! He spends so much time coming up w/lectures and is willing to help @ all hrs of the day. There should be no reason as to why U can fail his course. He gives LOTS of EC+ opportunities and works hard with you. Dave knows his materials inside and out, curves class, guide lines.ect. He is a great! Take his class

I was amazed at the night and day difference between this and the other class that I have taken with Blackwell. I wonder if he is going senile. Extremely harsh on the grading even though he was vauge at best when explaining his expectations. The ONLY thing that he actually taught us was how to use a brunton compass. Time to retire!

Blackwell really puts his students first and goes out of his way to make himself available. He is also genuinely excited about rocks, which can help with the dryness factor. Overall, he's a great professor.

well he didn't know my name lol. he's  a good guy but i personally didn't like his teaching style and no extra credit in this class. his instructions weren't as clear as i had hoped. fairy good teacher. hard grader maybe it's just his style for 300 level classes?

Dave Blackwell is an amazing teacher. He knows you by name, is willing to give extra credit, is very helpful during office hours (check out his rockin' album collection and ask about the shows he has seen with his son) and will make geology even more exciting than it already is. Dave is a good teacher and a great guy. Review notes for tests!!!

Absolutely loved this class.  Took it in the summer - got to interact personally with the professor, taking field trips to the coast and cascades.  Labs were fun.  Lectures were interesting.  You can tell he is passionate.  Made me love geology!  I can't wait to take another class with him!  Attend class & stay on top of work & you'll do well.

Hey is really passionate about his work and stays very organized. He gives lots of extra credit, and you will need it. His tests are super hard. Attending class isn't mandatory but is extremely useful if you do.
blackwell is the man. just be prepared to take notes and remember to being you packet because his writing is a little messy. he is easy to talk to and more than willing to help you.

He seemed like a great guy.  He knew my name despite the fact that I had never spoken to him individually.  There is enough extra credit available so that some kids earned 120%.  But... his lectures are terrible.  They are all over the map... a mixture of hand drawn overheads and old slides.  I could hardly keep my eyes open.

Blackwell is a cool guy, I'd like to have a beer with him and have him tell me more about how crazy nature is. Overall the testing is straightforward, but the final was noticably harder than the other two midterms. No worries though, provided you've done well and showed up to lab, you'll end up with a B.

He was a great professor, engaging, clear that he cares. The class was interesting, and he made it easy to participate even if you didn't do the readings before every class. He took role with in-class attendance quizzes, which just tracked engagement. No other difficult tests. Lots of in-class discussions that helped me grasp the topic.

Very knowledgeable professor! While the class itself was mostly guest lectures, most of them were pretty interesting! Go to his office hours! Helped me out a lot! Sometimes certain grading criteria or instructions weren't super clear, but a quick email or drop-in for office hours can easily fix that!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were mostly guest prof. Assigned material is expected to be done before class (not difficult, max 15 pages total) and there's a small quiz at the beginning of class. This class was not difficult, and the textbook is offered online for free. Isn't a difficult grader either. Go to class, do the readings, and takes notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really kind and very knowledgable.

This class is quite enjoyable, I dont get the negative reviews for this specific class because the GEs for this term have been very lenient and have given full credit if you do what the assignments ask. Gives the final prompt out early so you can start on it early. The only issue I had was I forgot to turn in 1 assignment so I got a 0 on it.
This class had heavy readings for some of the units and lighter ones for others. Overall this was a fairly easy class for credit and the assignments aren't graded harshly.

The grading was left entirely to the GE's and they didn't grade fairly. They just flat out marked me down for no reason. When I reached out the the GE's I was ignored, so I emailed the professor who also ignored me. The instructions on assignments were very confusing and unspecific. This class is NOT worth your time or money.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor has clear guidelines for his class and the material is relatively easy to follow as you go along with the course. However this professor shows a lack of professionalism by not answering attempts to communicate with him about his course. In addition his method of grading is not there and his GEs do all of it and leave no feedback.

Similarly to the other posts, I had a difficult time with this professor. There was a lot of reading and lectures. Grading policies were extremely vague and assignment instructions and were even worse from a clarity perspective. Also, he never responded to my emails. I would not take this class, or any class with him, frankly.

Lectures were hard to understand, emails were confusing, & assignment instructions were hard to read & incomprehensible, when I emailed for help the responses were equally as incomprehensible. Weekly lectures were 30-40 min and my GE graded extremely harshly on what "qualified" as a sufficient comment on someone else's discussion post. NOT WORTH IT

I agree with the only other post made specifically for LING296 about Professor Bosire. He is a very tough grader  and has unclear instructions on assignments. There are few assignments so grade is heavily affected by any amount of points taken off.

Decent professor with a very informative class. The midterm was super easy if you've been taking the class seriously. One flaw is that he didn't look at any emails I sent to him throughout the term so you'll have to email the advisor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: HANDS DOWN BEST PROFESSOR AT THIS UNIVERSITY. Take any of his classes. He is one of the funniest, smartest, and kindest humans on the entire planet.
Awesome. Take Swahili. You won't regret it. Mokaya is the best professor ever and he'll make you feel so welcome in the class.

He is an amazing professor who is very caring and attentive in class. Sometimes he can respond slowly to emails but will respond within a few days. He is not the most clear assignment giver but if you ask he will either fix the problem or make it clearer. Highly recommend taking a class with him :)

Not available for assistance,  was not willing to help on questions and guidance in course.   Difficult grader on papers.   Assignments did not provide clear directions so would consistently receive points off.   Rude responses and unhelpful in email.

Professor Bosire is very specific when he grades. He assigns weekly homework with a 1-page length, and I would get points knocked off for not going into enough detail. I would explain everything, but to go into more detail, I would need at least 2 pages in length. His midterm and final were tough on grading too. His grading is frustrating
Professor Bosire is an all-around great person. He shows that he really cares about the subject he teaches.

I absolutely love Professor Bosire. I was super nervous about taking Swahili because it is such a new language to me, but Prof Bosire is super helpful, understanding, and overall a great teacher. He makes class entertaining with his witty banter and students begin to develop a close relationship with him through participation. I highly recommend!!

Mokaya is a great guy and HILARIOUS!! Class is based off of weekly reading responses and two five page papers. It's an easy A but also a really interesting class. I would recommend this class to anyone looking for a fun arts and letters. One of the best classes offered and you'll be lucky to be one of the few who take it in a term!
Bosire is a great Professor and is a fair grader. He is very passionate and is kind about hearing others opinions. Definitely would take again.
solid prof. fun class, pretty engaging even if you're not interested in subject. clear instructions and grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mokaya is great and this class was a lot of fun. Had weekly responses to the readings but they were short. I enjoyed the readings and the class atmosphere was enjoyable. I recommend if you are looking for arts and letters credits. This class is easy to keep up with. Just don't half ass your essay cuz that's what I did and I landed an A-.
Sweet man, passionate about Swahili, linguistics, and equitable development.

In this class Mokaya is less of a teacher and more of a guide. The class is structured around guest lectures but he does a good job of discussion on the topics. Easy grader, got 100% on the midterm and an A on the book report I wrote the day it was due without reading the book. It did take about 5 weeks to get the papers back but gives good feedbac
Great professor who clearly loves his job. Would most definitely take again and would highly recommend this class to others. It's the one of the best classes I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors! He is amazing and I would take any class he teaches. Very fair grader with clear grading criteria and gives you plenty of chances to receive an A. He makes you want to go to class everyday and you learn so much!
The first week is daunting, but it's amazing past that.

I believe he is unqualified for this position because when a student asked him to explain a homework problem he didn't know how to solve it at all. I wish the professor would prepare more before class and try to help his students

when students ask questions he answers very rudely and doesn't answers what students are actually asking. he makes students feel dumb for even asking and grades very inaccurately. doesn't teach well just does math on the board while talking, no explaining of what he is doing. pretty unorganized and very hard to read what he writes on the board.

Despite other reviews, this professor and class wasn't too hard. All you need to do is take notes and go to every class. This professor does move fast during lectures so be prepared for that but he will slow down if you ask. He is also a bit sassy at first but extremely helpful if you just ask questions or go to office hours. The tests were so easy

I think Holt was a good person but not an amazing professor. He teaches really fast and is not super clear when answering questions. He also has a terrible tone and makes me feel kinda dumb when he answers my questions. He did figure it out halfway through the term that he was teaching too fast when my peers and I were not doing well in the class.

Decent knowledge of calculus but he goes way too fast in lecture and you will often fin yourself writing as fast as you can to keep up. Tests are too long for the time constraint, homework has questions not from class. His biggest flaw as a prof though is that he flames kids for asking questions, which is why people don't go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has a good sense of humor but also destroys you for asking questions in front of the class, low-key humiliating. just writes equations on the board and doesn't explain them but everyone's scared to ask questions so no one understands anything. very condescending but as a person he's funny and I like him, just as a teacher not so much.

Hes so unorganized, one time he came to discussion with his sweater inside out. He smells awful and looks like he doesnt shower. Hes been wearing the same black pants that have chalk stains on them from week 1. Hes so rude and makes you feel stupid for asking questions. Dont take any class where hes the GE.

Holt is the type of person that you just need to give time to grow on you. At first he comes off as intimidating and rude but overtime he eases up. He is a very knowledgeable person. After attending tutoring hours with holt, you can see his true personality and he's honestly a chill, laid back dude thats pretty funny haha. He grades for accuracy!!

Holt is very knowledgable and over qualified for the math he's teaching, but he lacks in the "teaching" part...I think it's just his personality, but he comes off very rude and condescending. Doesn't try to make class fun and honestly I could not bring myself to class some days. Lots of teaching myself outside of class becuase he lacks explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Holt Bodish is very unorganized. He once wrote a quiz on the board because he hadnt made us a printed version that week. He is incredibly condescending. Very rude and makes you feel stupid for not understanding something. His teaching style has no structure, so I constantly had to teach myself things outside of class. Terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doesnt help students at all. Walks around and answers questions in a condescending and rude way. Doesnt seem to care at all about the class or students
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is a VERY EASY class. You just come in every week with a rebrand for an existing brand and don't turn anything in except for the simple final 3 brands, 6 executions per brand. However, his laissez-faire approach to teaching often led to misunderstandings about what we were supposed to do. I would take his class again though.

Bob makes you want to do good work. His course isn't very structured, but you get out of it what you put in. Listen to his feedback and talk to him- pretty much everything he says should be jotted down in a notebook or plastered on a billboard. This whole class is group projects, but that's ad for you anyway. It's a lot of hours, but so worth it.

Bob really cares about his students and he has a lot of insight. He gives really good advice and tell us tips and tricks on working in the industry. His entire class (ideasmithing) is based off of group work and every class youre just getting feedback on those group projects. I would recommend this class to anyone its my favorite ad skills class

Bob is great. Don't let these few bad reviews sway you from not taking his classes. Ideasmithing is a course that AD programs DREAM of teaching. Bob is honest and gives fair feedback to your work because he truly wants you to succeed. His course is designed for students to produce great work and give feedback all in collaboration.

Bob has that mindset where he feels as though his own thoughts and words will be sufficient for a course. I respect him as a person and can see him completely flourishing as a leader for his agency work, but I seriously could not handle the group work throughout the term and very unclear directions sometimes. A Canvas assignment is hardly there
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Bob is just a great guy! He meets you at a colleague-to-colleague level and treats you as such. He makes you feel like you are already in the Advertising business and he's just helping you perfect your ad-making craft. His classes are very relaxed and he creates a nice group environment to produce the best work and even better feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bob is a very passionate and dedicated teacher; he really cares about bettering his students and provides a phenomenal amount of valuable feedback. His teaching method works better in small classrooms but not so much in big classrooms. The lecture time is very inconvenient and long. The entire term is constant group work and Bob demands a lot.

Frustratingly difficult just because of the grading rather than difficulty in content. Instructions are vague enough that it was really hard to get full credit. She graded the tests and essays uncharacteristically easily, which was good. Lectures drone on, answers questions in a scattered and unhelpful manner, but the class is survivable.

A nice enough person, but personally was not a fan of her teaching style. Classes are extremely lecture-heavy, and the amount of reading assigned is abysmal. Asks obscure questions in class to fish around for the answers she's looking for, which 80% of the time are things that no one who doesn't have a significant background in classics would know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Normally I really enjoy when professors know a lot about their subject and go on passionate tangents, but she just reads from her TEXT HEAVY powerpoint and then goes on 20 minute side rants about something unrelated that we won't need again. Also has marked me down for having a different interpretation than hers on Ancient Greek literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You will be inspired by her.

Professor Bowditch turned one of my favorite subjects into a complete bore. Her lectures were extremely monotonous and uninteresting, which is a real shame because I normally love Roman history and literature. The class itself isn't super hard, and professor Bowditch is very kind, but her teaching style was just boring and uninspired for me.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you LOVE reading about ancient literature. You have to read the most boring books each week and have a weekly paper on what you read. Her exams are really hard if you're not interested in the class. She is passionate about humanities so she knows what she is talking about. I do not recommend the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: All she does is read the powerpoint and stutter. I read Sparknotes occasionally and I have a B in the class. I know she knows stuff, but she sure doesn't know how to talk about it.

This was one of my most interesting classes this term and I think it was largely due to her lectures. The topic are very entertaining and intriguing. However, this class comes with a big course load with heavy reading. If you want to do well you have to actually work.

I love Professor Bowditch! She is very knowledgable about Greek and Roman culture, especially relating to gender. The class itself is lecture-based with some discussion and there is a lot of reading but it's not overwhelming by any means. Grade is based on reading responses a midterm and a paper.
Professor Bowditch has an endless supply of knowledge when it comes to the Humanities. Her lectures can be hard to follow, but generally she is a good professor.
I thought she was a really good professor, and i credit most of my enjoyment in the class to her teaching. It really wasn't that hard of a class overall.
No Comments
Hard work, but very interesting.

Professor Bowditch was a pretty solid instructor. If you're into Greek Literature and the Humanities, then she would be a good one to take. I, myself, wasn't too interested in the topic, however, I didn't mind the readings or the work, and ended up getting an A.

He could've stood to grade and provide feedback quicker, but was plenty helpful if you asked for it. Often goes into Logic Pro to demonstrate concepts which is very helpful. Generously takes the time to accommodate for other DAWs as well. I preferred Dr. Bellona's DAW class to his; lectures were boring at times, but otherwise he's decent.
Genuinely a very easy class just for a GPA boost, nothing much to it.

Professor Boyt is very nice. Totally go to his office hours if you are confused with anything. This class was very straightforward grading wise and there are three "finals" with your lowest score being dropped. As long as you do all the work, which is not hard, you will be fine. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is extra credit.

Super easy class. Most boring lectures of all time, teacher has no presence and most monotone voice. Can drown him out in one second and fall asleep instead. Has a super annoying policy where you can't earn an A+, even with a perfect grade. Class is really easy, just a really boring guy with bad policies.

super nice guy who clearly wants you to succeed. weekly work is super minimal and all exams are take-home and open book/note. lectures are interesting, but attendance isn't mandatory and all slides are posted on canvas. nice guy and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy and was very kind to me during a difficult situation. However, very dry and monotone when giving lectures. It is hard to pay attention without falling asleep. He tends to cut class early and is overall just a boring, nice guy.
Class is very dry. His voice is very monotone and it's very hard to stay interested in what he talks about in class.
Life changing class lowk
She was a very good lecturer and facilitated class discussions really good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, funny, and intelligent professor. Do the readings assigned and you will be fine but they are thick! If you don't like reading it could be tough. Her lectures are thought provoking, engaging, and highly entertaining. She does not post slides so lectures are mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think the class is a great fit for those who really want to dive deep into the idea of love. You do learn a lot. My only issue with the class is the grading which is god awful. Literally attendance will make or break your grade. I find it a little unfair that attendance is 40% of the total grade. You do all the work, miss a few and are screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bonnie Mans lectures were engaging. She was very funny and I truly enjoyed her class. There's 4 written essay exams, everything after unit 1 is light however they don't tell you the prompts before hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 3 reading quizzes a week on average but they were pretty light after the first unit. We also did surveys that were fun and we compared scores. The content is so interesting and not as freaky as I thought it'd be. She's very funny and really cool. No final, only an in class essay exam each unit.

Dr. Mann is a great professor. Does her best to involve the class in discussion even with a 300+ person lecture. Not a philosophy person but she makes it fun and interesting. Very fun class and she can be pretty funny too. 
Only bad thing is that she doesn't tell you the prompts to the timed written tests in advance and you only get a quote sheet.
awesome professor

Very good professor, material is pretty interesting so the lectures aren't boring. Attendance is mandatory. There is a lot of reading but it's all very doable with and the reading quizzes are super easy. Tests are easy and graded lightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great at introducing philosophical concepts to people who haven't read philosophy before. Participation in lectures is required. Very introspective class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far one of the best lecturers I have ever had. While the assigned seating and hand taken notes were an adjustment, the classes and topics covered are by far worth it. The readings and quizzes are pretty easy and will only take up maybe 30-45 minutes of time. The discussions we have in a 300 person lecture hall are very interesting and worth it.

While the assigned seating and hand taken notes took some adjusting to, the lectures made them worth the hassle. By far one of the best lecturers I have had and I always look forward to her class along with the readings. The amount assigned is really pretty minimal and easy to get through, and the quizzes take maybe 10 minutes max.

I very much enjoyed this class, Bonnie Mann is a great professor and if you are interested in productive feminist discussion take this class. This would not be an easy credit or class to sign up for and forget about. Bonnie allows note taking on computers in her higher level classes.

I think Mann is a great professor. I think she presents topics in an open and honest way. Though she does say her perspective on points that you may not agree on I believe that is a part of philosophy. I think she provides space to figure out your own interpretation and the essay structures are great. Lots of reading tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Doctor Mann is overall a good teacher. However, she can be very forward which can come off as rude. The class requires a lot of reading and some participation but there are only 4 short essays with no final. AND the material and concepts you learn are very good and applicable. Highly recommend the class if you actually want to learn and try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: May seem difficult at first but you'll see by the end of the term she's tough because she wants to create real, critical thinkers. She's honest and shares a lot about herself. Quizzes are easy if you have the reading open with the quiz and look for the answers. She finishes the course with a lecture that will make you very emotional. Worth taking.

I admire Dr. Mann as I have taken a few courses with her. That said, she does not seem to understand that 100-lvl classes should not be as difficult as 300 lvl courses. Philosophy of Love and Sex is not a joke, despite its subject matter. Be aware that you will do plenty of writing (3 separate essay exams) and participation matters.

I loved this class and professor Mann. Participation is a huge portion of the grade but lectures are interesting and engaging. There is a lot of readings that can be challenging but are overall interesting. Lots of great topics discussed and essays are short and easy. Great Arts and Letters credit!

worst class ever. save your time and take literally anything else this class is beyond frustrating and the style of teaching is outdated and makes for an insane amount of homework. literally my biggest mistake was taking this
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class you will end up wanting off yourself,
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SO many boring and tedious readings, along with a quiz, are assigned everyday you have this class. You are forced to take notes by hand but she goes through all the slides so fast that you can never write down all the information you need. This 100 level class is so much harder than any 300 level class I have taken. Don't even waste your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mann should not be teaching a course with such heavy material such as sexual assault. She is insensitive and unemotional. Worst professor.

Dr. Mann gives great lectures explaining the material in depth. She does weight well-thought out participation highly, so make sure you do the readings and come prepared to talk! Only one essay was nice, mostly reflection journals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mann was great, a solid teacher overall, her lectures were very informational and made sense of the assigned readings. I enjoyed how transparent she is with her students.

Bonnie is an incredible lecturer and explains the readings so well that you don't really have to do them. That said, there are some pretty hefty assignments and she expects a lot. There is a reading response essay, a midterm essay exam with 2 prompts, and an 8-10 page final paper. Grading was easy because the GE was a joke.

This professor does not care about her students' learning or understanding of the material. She failed to adjust the course to coincide with the extreme adaptations students were forced to endure with remote learning. She was inflexible and uninspiring.

This is the HARDEST 100 level course Ive ever taken. Incredibly interesting, and very important lessons. I would still recommend this class, HOWEVER, you will need to dedicate a lot of time. I spent easily twice the time on this class than I did on my 300 level courses this term, reading and rereading and studying. GEs are told to grade HARD

Bonnie Mann seems like a great professor through her lectures. It is an immense amount of reading. but the topics are cool. PHIL170 is easy to get overwhelmed in, but getting good grades is do-able. I would recommend this class and this professor if you like reading and writing papers.

Prof Mann's teaching style isn't very engaging. The course was organized, however, I found myself dreading the lectures. She's very knowledgable and course content in itself could be interesting but the way it's delivered ruins it. Participation is huge and she doesn't give you your participation grade until the last day of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hands down the best philosophy professor at Oregon. She offers an extremely intellectually challenging Intro to Feminist Philosophy course. She's super inclusive, and though her expectations are high and workload at times overwhelming, you will find her courses to be a rewarding experience. I also recommend her 170 Love and Sex class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bonnie is brilliant. I find it amusing that so many reviews of her 100 level course (love and sex) are negative, as it's clear that these students are not interested in genuine philosophical inquiry. If you take philosophy seriously and actually want to learn and not just get an easy A, take an upper division with Bonnie, she won't disappoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Sooooo political. Dead wrong about so many things. Class was exhausting. Avoid.

This is the most unorganized course I have ever taken, first, off you are forbidden from using technology which really is a disadvantage because she moves really fast through lecture slides which makes it hard to keep up when your handwriting. The GE's are uncoordinated, attendance is mandatory but the grade never went toward my overall score.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mann was one of the best professors I've ever had, hands down. The class itself is incredibly challenging but in a way that makes you be more personally responsible for readings, surveys, etc. In a 300 person room, she's able to make lectures seem less boring as she adds an eccentric twist to everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Mann was great at giving engaging, informing lectures and it was clear that she cared deeply about the topics she talked about. Attendance was a huge part of the grade and the papers were pretty easy so it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Mann is equally intimidating and amazing. I took an author course with her and it remains one of the best classes I've ever taken. Be ready to participate, she can smell fear so make sure you've at least skimmed the readings before coming to class. The lectures themselves are fascinating, 15/10 would take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It was easy to understand what was happening throughout majority of the class. The tons of readings are "required" in a sense but I never read anything besides skimming through papers while writing midterms and I passed easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Plenty of participation grading to get you the grade you want in this class - so long as you attend and are engaged. Her lectures could be paced a little better. She struggles with rushing through slides and spending too much time on others. That said, structure of the class is clear and grading is precise. Good feedback and worthwhile course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Bonnie Mann is a privilege to have as your professor for this class. She will impact your thinking and approaches to love and sex and change your perspective on gender and sexuality - even if you agree with her. The readings she picked are well-suited to the curriculum and take-home tests are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I've ever taken, partly because I found the readings to be very interesting, and partly because Bonnie Mann is an amazing teacher. She made a 300-person lecture hall feel so intimate, and even though it's been a year since I've sat in that class, her words still resonate with me. Highly recommend this course

This course isn't difficult by any means. That said, she makes every aspect of the course as painful as possible. Makes her GEs take attendance, readings are collected. Will not use the projector because of an Accessible Education Requirement. Lectures pointless, not really a philosophy course. People whine about society's perceptions basically.

Bonnie tries to spark interest in philosophy but fails at doing this. Not only does she force you to print all the readings and bring them to class instead of creating a purchasable course packet, but she makes her TAs collect the readings to make sure you've annotated them. Her lectures are superficial at best and the amount of reading is insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bonnie Mann is one of the best professors I've ever had! I loved this class, it was super interesting and she makes it really relevant to today's society. There is a lot of reading and the couple of essays they assign take a while to do, but this class is 100% worth it. It's by far one of my favorite classes I have taken at UO.

in order to do well in this class you MUST READ. but the readings are interesting if philosophy is your thing. I absolutely loved this professor, it's so obvious how much she cares for her students. definitely recommend this course, i really enjoyed it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mann is definitely one of those professors who thinks that her class is more important than any other class you're taking. Material is interesting and there is no textbook, but be ready to do a lot of reading (approx 40 pages that you have to deeply read, annotate and print yourself). There are 4 tests over the term. They're take home on weekends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good teacher, good lecturer. Interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing and life-changing, highly recommend. It's a lot of work but it's worth it. Don't skip class. Take this class seriously and you'll really enjoy it. No textbook, only print outs.
There is a lot of reading, but I found a lot of it to be really interesting. It was a difficult class, but I would take it again.

this was the first philosophy class i ever took and i was pretty excited but honestly taking this class made me resent the idea of love. Bonnie is kinda pretentious, i hated this class. i didnt do much reading at all and passed with a C but i dont think thats usually the case. discussion attendance is the most important

Philosophy of Love and Sex has been hands down one of the best classes I have taken at UO. But beware, it is A LOT of reading, and all tests are essays, but overall it is a very rewarding class that is a big eye opener. To this day I still reference that class and the things I learned from it. There is no textbook requirement either.

I have taken a huge lecture class with her (philosophy of love and sex) and a tiny authors course with her. I think she is a fantastic professor. She is very intelligent, and takes the difficult texts of philosophical works and makes them much easier to understand for you. There is a lot of reading, but so are all philosophy classes. Highly recomm.

I took this class as a freshman and wasn't sure what I was getting myself into at first by taking a 300 level philosophy class but Mann makes the class enjoyable and more than worthwhile. This class inspired me to minor in philosophy! The small class size was definitely a plus and made discussions a lot easier. I highly recommend taking this class!

Bonnie Mann is amazing professor!!! This was the best class I have EVER taken!! My money was well spent!! You have to read the texts to do well in this class. Attend discussion sections and lectures and take good notes. They will come in handy when writing the three essays. Bonnie goes over topics and is incredibly thorough. Take her class!!!

Bonnie is a fabulous professor and very fair when it comes to readings, exams, and papers. She does NOT assign too much reading. Anyone who does not like her teaching style depends too much on lectures and probably doesn't read. She's the best professor I've ever had.

Her class had a lot of content that you needed to know, but as long as you read and do the study guides you will do just fine! Everyone needs to stop there ****in' about this class, really really interesting and worth your time!
Dr. Mann does a very good job re-capping and summarizing the author's viewpoints, only to the extent that it is complementary if you already read the readings in advance.

Excellent class, excellent professor. People are right, the content is difficult and the readings are a bit long. But she really does care about her subject, and if you're willing to put in the work, you'll get so much out of a class with her. Prof. Mann has high expectations, but she truly is a quality professor.
Best class I've ever taken at this school, I loved it,  changed my life. Learned more than in any other class. Take this!

Terrible class. Prof. Mann is very open-minded and is nice, but the amount of required reading is ridiculous for a 100 level class. During lecture, she goes through slides way too fast to take good notes and doesn't post power points online. And, most of the content from the slides are super long quotations from the readings. Wasn't a fun class!!
Love and sex is a great class, but the exams are very difficult for a 100 level class. The reading is a bit much, but she's a fantastic teacher who keeps you engaged during lecture.

Love and Sex is one of the BEST classes I've taken in my years here. Dr. Mann is open-minded, humorous, and is easy to understand. She is fun and makes class interesting. Lots of reading! Exams.. fairly hard.. but the class is totally worth it.

I can't fathom why anyone would say she does not listen to views.Quite the contrary, she encourages the entire class of 300+ students to engage in discussion. She does not express her own views, she thoroughly explains views of the authors we read. I learned SO much!
Possibly the first "real" philosophy class at UO. If you've had a 200 level philosophy class before, you'll be fine, but if not, be prepared to think.

Have had Dr. Mann for multiple classes.  She is by far the best professor at the University.  She is extremely intelligent and a fantastic teacher.  She never wastes your time and expects you not to waste hers.  The material in her classes are challenging, but only because she wants you to get the most out of your time.

Mann certainly knew what she was talking about. However, this is the hardest class I've taken-should NOT be a 100 class. There is SOOOO much reading-so be prepared for it. The tests are a lot of writing and depending on your GTF, graded hard. But, I really did enjoy this class...it was just difficult. Mann also goes over slides Fast-so be ready.

Love and Sex is an excellent class!! Bonnie is a really engaging teacher who really knows what she is talking about and likes to involve the 350+ class in somewhat of a lecture discussion... and she is good at answering any questions.
WOW please stop being a teacher. She goes way to fast and is not helpful with her slides. She does not give enough time for our midterms. :( i might fail
Don't take this teacher

The class is hard with too many readings for a 100 level class.  I did not find the quizzes/papers to be graded harshly at all (your GTF graded you) but I agree the workload is a lot for students who have never studied philo.  And she DID listen to other views in class if they were made. Do not take unless well motivated-you'll be over your head.

Hated that class. Her slides never made any sense and it was pointless.  Shes a crazy feminist and wont listen to people who do not agree with her.  Papers are graded super hand as well as some of her quizzes.
Interesting class. She's a tough grader but a good teacher, really cares about student opinions. I can see how non-feminists would dislike her, but that's just too bad for them.

She does have strong opinions, but is open to disagreement even if just for the benefit of class discussion. She is very well prepared for class, when she strays it is good, open discussion. There is a lot of reading, but it is well chosen and you learn quite a bit. She grades hard and grades better for those she agrees with. Overall, great prof.

I would say that this class was the best I've had at UO. Bonnie Mann is 1000x better then I expected. What really got me was actually how open she was to dessent and how non-judgemental. She never countered anything by shutting someone down, but listened and honestly considered it. You could say ANYTHING! %100 you will learn something in her class.
i had no idea that a philosophy class could be so useless
I thought she was awesome; she only challenged people to make them think about what they were saying.  I thought she was very understanding and this was one of my favorite classes i've ever taken
Class and assignments very straight forward. Professor was clear and interesting.
Excellent teacher! Encouraged people to speak and kept her own opinions out of the class.

I thought she was very willing and able to listen to people's opinions. People call her a hypocritical liberal feminist because she asked questions. She tried to get people to explain their viewpoints and they most often couldn't.
No Comments

Total hypocrite, always encouraged students to respect opposing points of view, but if you disagreed with her she treated you like you were the stupidest person on the planet.  If you aren't a ultra liberal, feminist, you will NOT enjoy this class.
Worst prof., worst class.  You can't conduct a classs of 300 people like a class of 30.  Huge waste of time.  Almost destroyed my interest in phil.

She's a biased feminist who had many blatantly dumb viewpoints in my class, and students often challenged her on it and proved her wrong.  Her class isn't very hard but I hated putting up with her, even two days a week.
No Comments

DO NOT TAKE!!! By far the worst professor I have ever had.  She is very biased and loves to hear her own voice.  If your viewpoints conflict with hers you should drop the class.  Our final was multiple choice and each questoin could have up to three right answers. If you did not get all it was wrong
Outstanding professor. One of the department's best.

She is definitely my favorite professor.  Does an excellent job of explaining very complex concepts and expanding on the readings.  Really well prepared classes. I know multiple people with very different opinions than the instructor's, and they have done well in her courses; she is very fair.
No Comments
Excellent class. Encourages opposing viewpoints. She is ideologically honest. She has crafty ways of getting you to come to every class, such as mandatory in-class writings. Great professor.

I enjoyed this class a lot.  The reading was difficult, but not unbearable.  The materials were interesting.  She was definitely opinionated, but encouraged alternate points of view to be expressed.  Great class, I reccomend it.
I thought she was great.  Very knowledgable and passionate about what she was teaching.
Not too hard of a class, very organized.  I followed her lectures, even if they were tedious at times.  Overall, recommended.
UGH... boring boring boring... very biased viewpoint... can't stand that voice
boring, confusing, and pointless
very boring... the first week there the whole class was full with lots of students trying to get into the class, now only 1/3 of the class remains.. and for a 100 level class, it is HARD!!

Lectured about random stuff most of the time, prepping us for stuff that wasn't even on the exams. Class wasn't difficult, but he made it way harder than it should've been. I'd seriously recommend taking anyone else if you can.

I think he is a very nice guy but the lectures could be very difficult to follow along with. I found it more beneficial to just study and learn on my own time using resources other than the lecture. The tests progressively get more difficult but the curves were very generous at times.

Homework was not related to class and test questions. Homework questions were always way too hard for what we were learning or comically easy. I spent a minimum of 5 hours a week in tutoring for homework help and support. Notesheets are allowed on tests and your lowest score will be dropped. Would make mistakes during lecture and explain wrong.

This class has no structure whatsoever so you will have to teach yourself some of the content in this course. He rambles quite a bit on problems that aren't that helpful to learning the content. However his tests are quite easy and you get a notecard to use as well as the curves are generous.

He's funny, but the lectures are boring. He overcomplicates example problems and rarely gives partial credit if part (a) of a question is wrong (depending on the question). He's helpful and caring. Exams are worth 79% of overall grade in the class.

One of the worst lectures I have sat through. He often didnt have a solid structure to his lecture. Instead of really teaching us through steps, he would give us the definition of a concept, then do 1 MAYBE 2 example problems which were extremely difficult and he usually messed up several times per problem. Would not show steps and overall bad.
He was okay. Explains concepts in a really confusing way so I had to go teach myself. Curves every quiz by a good chunk because the average is so low. You get a notecard every time which is nice.

I found this class to be challenging, and his teaching confused me. He often would mess up problems halfway through, making it easy to get lost. That being said, don't panic if you have to take a class with him. He is a nice teacher and genuinely wants everyone to pass; he is an easy grader, and his tests are not too hard with huge curves.

Such confusing lectures. He overcomplicates the material and often gets problems wrong while he's working on them. There are a lot of resources to get help for this class, but he's not one of them. He made this class so much harder than it needs to be.

He's nice guy, but absolutely the most confusing math teacher I've ever had. I am better off opting out of his lectures and teaching myself because he makes no sense at all. He often dives deeply into things that are irrelevant to what we are required to know, and writes tests that don't match with review material. So difficult (4.0+ student btw)
Nice guy, good attitude, but I felt his teaching style was a bit messy. Got confused so quickly in class

Class has entirely no structure to encourage students to learn. He freestyles on his iPad everyday with no lecture framework, and explains things so confusingly he consistently messes his own work up. Good person just no conducive to your success. YouTube and Tutoring center will be lifelines in order to pass this course. GOOD LUCK.

Nice person, but explains things in such a confusing way and nobody ever understands what's going on in class. To pass this class you will have to be in the tutor center and learn things from YouTube.

Extremely unorganized lectures, spends most of his time going over examples that will never show up on any testing or homework. You will have to spend lots of time outside of class understanding the material, as during class you will only have unrealistic examples.

Teacher was nice, knowledgeable, and pretty funny. Tests however, were too difficult and I felt like lecture material was being covered too quickly. Expect a lot of self-learning, more than usual. HWs were also very difficult. Although this helped with exams, the exams were just as difficult so even with studying, it was too difficult.

Jon is very knowledgeable & kind, but lecture material is covered too quickly and some content is irrelevant or so difficult & never used again that it actively makes us more confused. For 231, HW helped with exams. For 232 this term, HW & review not nearly as helpful for exams. Exams are too difficult and I wish Jon wouldn't write such hard exams.

Jon is a great guy, he's very humble, easy to talk to, and give good feedback. The only thing about his lectures is that he has pretty terrible handwriting and he's hard to understand at times, so taking notes is quite difficult. He gives study guides/review problems for the exams, and they cover a good amount of what's on the exam.

The homework is quite difficult but leaves you well-prepared for the midterm, however, HW is a large part of your grade (50%). Jon made it clear attending lectures is the best method of preparation. If the long lectures were broken up among shorter periods throughout the week, the material would likely be far easier to grasp.

Decent and nice professor. Lectures are very in-depth and quick-paced but learning-wise it's too fast and scattered. HW is plentiful, online and written HW takes 2-8 hrs/wk. I recommend going to office hours or else it'll be easy to get lost. Grading scale is in your favor (85=A-). 2 midterms and a final, it REQUIRES studying, but HW prepares well.
His lectures aren't boring, and although he can tend to go on tangents, he usually only tests on material that is heavily covered in class or lab. Study and take decent notes and you'll do great.

Rude and unhelpful. He was nice in class, but when I went to office hours he was not helpful at all. He said to me "why do you have to make things so complicated". Also, he made us do graded coding in a math class with no required programming experience. He taught all out of order with no textbook, making it hard to self-teach.

He is a nice person but is a terrible teacher. Math 231 is confusing as it is and he isn't very good at explaining what he is talking about. Be prepared to spend a lot of time watching youtube videos and teaching yourself 3/4 of the materials he goes over through the term.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bro I have never done this poorly in a class in my life. The homeworks are unrelated to the class lectures, and the tests aren't related to the homework or the lectures! I feel as if my grade in my other classes faltered because of how much time I spent on trying to figure this class and I'm still not even sure I'll pass. Good luck :/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Yo, the fact that you are taking discreet math shows you've already made some poor choices. I don't believe Jon is a horrible professor because I believe every professor teaches in their own language and understanding of the curriculum. However, I did not understand his and basically spent multiple hours a week teaching myself through youtube vids.

Brundan made his 341 Class his own class. A third of the HW problems are his own theoretical made up problems not covered in lecture that were graded randomly by the GE. They were challenging problems that he wasn't always able to answer in class or office hours. He's not a big fan of partial credit for carrying a mistake through in exams.

Jon had tons of office hours which was helpful. He delved into a lot of proofs which was cool but also confusing. He curved the class 15%, HW up to 20%, and tests 2-3%. Compared to the other 241 lecturers I've had (failed), this is EXTREMELY generous. UO still needs to dedicate a teacher to 241 and 242 though. Classes shouldn't be curved 20+%.

MATH241! Do not take him for this class! He does not care about you, he acts like it but then gives you tests with info you've never been taught. He teaches simplistic stuff in class and takes SO much time to show you proofs (which don't pertain) and not enough time showing you how to tackle difficult problems. I got a 83 and a 51 on the midterms
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was nervous about Math 241, but with him it's been easier despite some hard material. He always comes well prepared for lectures and reviews things before moving onto the new subject. If I had one complaint, it's that the webwork and exams have material we haven't learned, but luckily he implements a huge curve to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Brundan makes the challenge of 242 a little better with his teaching. His accent keeps me entertained in class but sometimes it can put me to sleep. Beware, sometimes he can go too in-depth into something and it can be extremely confusing.

Explains things thoroughly and clearly which is needed for discrete mathematics. He makes lectures enjoyable with his accent and British sayings. Absolutely would have him as a professor class again in the future if i can.

Amazing mathematician! Math is language, and he speaks it fluently. Most mathematician need a little time to think about how to put things in mathematical terms, but he doesn't. It's tough to keep up sometimes, but he is just awe inspiring!

Very concise and clear on what he expects from you on midterms and the final. The class is extremely difficult to begin with so its nice that he makes it as painless as possible. You just need to make sure you keep up, or you're doomed. One of the best maths teachers at the math department by far.
Lots of great professors in the math department, but Jon takes the cake. Wish I would have taken more classes from him.

I decided to retake Calc after a bad experience with a horrible AP Calc teacher in high school. I was glad I did. Brundan's class was challenging but so fascinating and enjoyable. He's a fairly lenient grader, he helps out a lot in office hours and he doesn't assume students understand complex stuff like other math teachers do. Plus, hello, HOT!
Very challenging. Surprise questions on midterms and final. Gives enjoyable lectures. Prefers not to be bothered during office hours. Students are expected to do a lot of learning on their own.
Brundan does not care about this class AT ALL. he goes extremely fast and explains nothing. homework is extremely hard
Very bright, very quick.  Makes math fun to learn, he is a joy to watch.

Not an easy class. his not so good, but i think he is the best available in UO. He like to do proves. Doesn't do example. I think it is easy to get 'A'.                             Has a good accent.  He likes to call him "Harry Potter".
If you can take a class from Brunden do. He only teaches Fall and Winter terms and takes the Spring off, just so you know.
Best math teacher at UO, if not the best teacher. I'm wish all my math classes were taught by him.
Fun accent. His lectures were dynamic and interesting, even to someone who is not a fan of math.  His tests seemed reasonable and appropriate for the material.
The class was pretty difficult to me and it didnt seem like he helped make it any clearer for me. I thought he was ok.
Very intelligent professor. One of the best math professors if not the best I have had at the University. 231 is a tough class but he does a good job.
Jon Brundan is absolutely brilliant.  His excitement about math is very inspiring, and amusing!  Also, I'd take another course from him just to listen to that hot British accent...

He's very helpful and clear, make sure to go to Office Hours because a lot of the problems (at least for 261) are really difficult and need a certain trick which isn't always obvious. If anything's foggy, he's the AC that'll clear it right up.

Jon Brundan is an Amazing instructor with the best teaching techniques! He approaches advanced subjects with caution that not everything will be "obvious" to everyone.  He is both entertaining and motivating. Highly recommended...
No Comments

I was at the UO years ago as a math major and can tell you that Brundan was one of the absolute best! He made the class not only entertaining but truly helped you see the beauty in abstract algebra. You couldn't ask for a better teacher.

I had Jon as a substitute for several lectures during Julia Pevtsova's MATH 341 - Linear Algebra class.  All I can say is Jon is THE BEST Math teacher at UO, and if you can get a class with him, you are not only lucky, but in for a treat.  It's true that he is the spitting image of Harry Potter :)
Looks like Harry Potter.
Greatest teacher ever!!! This guy is great I recommend everyone at UO to take a class from him. Just fantastic.

Because of Carrie's enthusiasm & genuinely caring personality, I looked forward to Spanish every day and made progress fast. I'm amazed at some of these reviews. I assume they are from students who didn't want to do the work. She's a natural educator, always accessible and did many kind things for students behind the scenes.

Carrie was the most disrespectful professor I have had at the University. She does not understand the proper boundaries between professor and student and puts several students in uncomfortable situations in and outside of the classroom. Overall I learned a good amount in the class but I would highly recommend taking 101 from a Latin professor.

SPAN 103. She is nice and genuinely will try to get to know you. This class is the same difficulty as any other Spanish class so as long as you do your homework and a small amount of studying you will be fine. To get an A and above you gotta study a little harder which I was too lazy for but it's totally achievable.

I personally had an outstanding experience in Professor Reilly's class. Her passion and love for the language is contagious and massively influenced the success of my studies. I would recommend her class to all other students interested in the Spanish language and culture.

I spent so long asking her for help and doing what I could to stay on track (even going as far as getting a 2nd tutor) so I could take the midterm very disappointing that my effort didn't matter she didn't let me take the midterm told me straight up that I was going to fail anyway.

Did not teach the class then would punish and blame students publicly for not understanding. Me and a couple of other classmates tried to ask for help, but she would act like we were the problem and only give attention to those who had taken span before and didn't need help. Her behavior is unprofessional point blank.

After many attempts to talk with Reilly about my confusion and needed help she continuously brushed me off then would gaslight me into thinking it was my fault for being behind and "not" doing the work. After connecting with another prof who easily helped and answered my questions I realized that the behavior exhibited was toxic and unprofessional

It seems like she means well and genuinely cares about her students but lacks social awareness and will often ask students personal questions in front of the class. There were several times when she made uncomfortable comments about my and other students appearances or personalities. For any feedback on tests she requires you to go to office hours.

If you put in the work and participate you will do well in this class. She is very sweet and caring and has a good sense of humor. I like showing up to class because she is always welcoming and kind. Not a super harsh grader either.

Mrs. Reilly is a very helpful and informative Spanish teacher at UO, in my opinion, she is the best one here! If you just show up to class, you will learn the required material, the VHL can be a bit much, but everything else about the class is amazing!

I switched from taking UO Spanish to going to LCC after this teacher. I would visit her after class every class to discuss topics I was struggling with, instead of helping me she would say i "needed to stop struggling with the language so much" and made me feel stupid (asking what my grades were in other classes).

Carrie teaches a good class, but she honestly is really rude to the whole class except a few. I learned a lot, but I've there are other professors that will guide you in a much better direction.

Carrie showed that she cared about her students starting on the first day of class and never stopped. She takes the time to learn everybody's name and level of Spanish and caters to the individual in a very specific way. She will call on random students if nobody raises their hand, but don't let that scare you.
Professor Reilly was very caring, but she doesn't excuse any absences and passing the class depends heavily on showing up.

She is very sweet and understanding and takes your problems into account. She is willing to work with you. Also, the people calling her an anti-masker need to get over it. She was trying to let us understand her better and so she could speak louder, which I appreciated.

Carrie is so caring and absolutely a great teacher! She was super understanding and helpful and her class was a lot of fun. She taught things clearly and concisely. She's super flexible and puts her students first. Wish I could take her again!

Everyone bashing carrie obviously just didnt do good in the class. I have never met a teacher who cared sp much for her students and did her best to ensure they all passed. For all calling her an anti masker for pulling her mask down 6 feet away from other students to speak louder so they can hear? Get a grip. Shes great

it doesn't really feel like she teaches anything. the professor goes off of the homework you learned the night before but doesn't do a great job explaining it thoroughly. she straight up told me to my face that I wouldn't pass her class. she doesn't respect boundaries and is very anti-mask

The class was an easy A but she doesnt really teach you. You really just have to teach yourself every night from the $180 textbook you have to buy. Carrie is a sweetie. Make sure she gets to know you early in the class.

Carrie is really awesome. I would highly recommend taking her class. I had never taken Spanish before and she was very patient with me. Her passion for teaching is obvious and really shows in her work. She genuinely wants students to do their best. Nightly homework, but it's quick and easy.

Read the Tribal Alliance Against Frauds report on this professor.

Brian is unlike many other teachers at UO, he actually cares about the topics he covers, is open to hearing other peoples viewpoint and is funny. I honestly looked forward to his class twice a week. reviews.comment: Pretty good

His class was enjoyable, as well as informational. He is passionate about Native American studies,  funny, and pretty personable. Gives good feedback on tests and papers, and expects a fair amount of work out of his students. Overall, his class is an enjoyable experience.

Grades hard on the papers, which are all your grade. Does not give enough points in the class to improve. There were a lot of cool videos though, cool teacher but class could definitely be more interesting.

Every time I raised my hand in this class he immediately shot down whatever I had to say - even if someone else said the exact same thing afterward and he agreed. I felt a blatant discrimination and favoritism. He never lectured and structured the entire class around small group work (not one day of not being in groups).
He is very educated on the topic, and seems very passionate. He is a little monotone, but the class is totally do-able, and he posts the lecture slides online!

He can be somewhat monotone but he used a microphone in my class to make up for it. Easy to pay attention if you are interested in the subject. Very easy to approach him and ask questions. I recommend the class because it is not only easy but interesting.

i've had several classes w/prof. klopotek...and over several years he's gotten much better at communicating w/the class.  love the topics, love the lessons, love the way he challenges you to critically think.  very understanding prof if you go to office hours and talk with him. not many teachers have the same kind of passion for their topics.
his teaching style people have to get use to it but is very informative. I greatly appreciate his teaching

as a consiencious student, i find his disinterest in students and their goal of learning offensive. He is a procrastinator who cares little or nothing for students' opinions,ethic,grade,or success. Agree with him or risk failing. He perpetuates stereotyping, and has poor attitude toward fellow man.Don't try figuring him out.
class was very dry, but interesting stuff
Lectures would be really good if he seemed like he were into what he was saying.  interesting but monotone.
I only had this guy for one day, and then I dropped his class because he was too monotone for me to stay awake on the first day! He seems really nice, but he's a bad lecturer.

Brent Walth is a tremendous journalist with some major accolades to back it up. With that being said, his class is by far the most difficult in the SOJC, and I felt really accomplished to pass.
