Brent is a tough grader and gives a lot of feedback, but it's because he wants to see your writing improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Brent is one of the most helpful professors I've had. He has helped set me up to do my very best in and outside of class. He may come off intimidating, but he truly wants the very best from each of his students. He won't let you get by with mediocre work. He will push you, but for me, it showed that he actually cared and believed in my work.
Brent cares about students and journalism. Do the work, take notes, don't use AI, go to office hours. He'll launch your skills and careers like he's done so many others. He's hard but in a good way.

Prof. Walth is the most legitimate journalist the UO SOJC currently has. He knows it. He is a powerful influence in the school, and upholds extremely high standards. Lesson only takes an hour 20? He'll find something to lecture about for the remaining 30 minutes (glancing at the clock to ensure not a second goes wasted)

Professor Walth is extremely difficult and can come across very intimidating but he truly cares. If you put in the work he will reciprocate it. He is there to constantly support his students though he holds extremely high expectations and will push you to the max. If you want to be pushed to grow as a journalist take a class with him.

Brent was by far the worst I've had while attending the UO. I actually had anxiety speaking to him because of his cold, narcissistic nature. Unfortunately, many of my classmates left the class with a bad grade, and worse, a crushed spirit. DO NOT TAKE. He does NOT care about your future and WILL negatively impact your GPA. Do better, Brent. Booooo.

This professor and class is not for the weak. The material is extremely hard, he grades very harsh, and you will question your worth and existence by saying anything. Every assignment is impossible. Good luck, many people will fail this class. But he will try to help.

Brent Walth possesses an arrogant and narrow-minded attitude toward learning, which is incredibly reductive in a discipline as creative and versatile as journalism. His grading systems and course instructions are highly confusing and undetailed, and his criticisms of writing are extremely unconstructive, belittling, and accusatory.
He pushed me to be a better journalist. The UO SOJC has its problems and I don't learn that much in most of my other J classes. Not the ones he teaches.

I had him for Solutions Journalism. He told me that my topic for the paper was good and had a solid foundation during our meeting in week three. I submitted the weekly check ins without any rebuttal. Week 7 he changed his mind and I had to change everything. He belittled me and made me feel stupid the whole time. I got a 102 but he doesnt give A+

Walth is an amazing professor. He knows what he's doing and is very good at explaining projects thoroughly. This course is hard in its nature, and he can be a "tough love" professor sometimes, but he offers multiple revisions if necessary and is very understanding of peoples' circumstances. The real-life applications of his class are amazing!

Not only is Brent terrible at communication, but it's your fault because he won a pulitzer. I understand and respect his pedigree but strongly dislike him as a person and teacher. He is great for you if you have an inflated sense of your own worth and the worth of investigative journalism.

Brent won a Pulitzer Prize, so he's not a bad journalist. He expects a lot of you, but you'll learn a lot if you keep up. Do NOT leave work to the last minute. If he sees potential, he'll push you hard. Act professionally in class, and do your research on your projects beforehand. Act like a professional journalist, but he is also fun to joke with.

Brent is one of the best professors I've ever had. His classes are hard, but he motivates you to be the best reporter possible for society. He is readily available and helpful- always helping improve students' skills and grade. He's got lots of knowledge in reporting, especially investigative, and is always engaging with his stories and lectures.

I had Brent for Reporting II and it was by far the most challenging hands on class I had at the J school. That being said, I learned A LOT from him, especially for writing and reporting big stories. He assigns a lot of work and you can't procrastinate, but if you give it your all and go to him for help, he will be happy to guide you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Brent's class isn't a cake walk like most of the J school, but it's extremely worthwhile. He gave detailed feedback for each written assignment. I suggest avoiding his classes if you can. He piles on the work load as if his class is the only one you're taking. His class focuses more on investigative journalism so if you like then he's a good choice.  Grades very harsh but offers guidance if you ask. You will have to do weekend assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

Great class. I had with him HIST 325 too, and both classes were outstanding. OK, there is a lot to read (and understand!), a lot to write, but this Professor will help you a lot.

Passionate about each class he teaches and willing to help you. Recognizes hard work and takes it into account when helping you. He isinvested in your success and will go out of his way to help you succeed.
Professor Buck was alright, the lectures aren't too bad to watch and the content is relevant to the homework. However, there is an unreasonable amount of reading to do in this class.

This class has five professors and professor Buck teaches the unit on China. The lectures are heavy and have regular information on China rather than the book for professor Bucks section. The paper was difficult because the prompt(s) were bland.

This course is required for Asian Studies majors, there is no getting passed not taking this. Overall there is a ton of reading weekly and per class. Professor Buck is nice. His lectures are informative, and if you want to learn youll do the readings. However, the GE that he had for the spring term was a harsh grader. Buck is doing the best he can online. I really enjoy how accessible is and how nice he is while also being very informational.

This class can be taken online because all Prof. Buck does is goes through his lectures that don't really make sense. reviews.comment: love him and hopefully take his class again! Smart and nice professor!

reviews.comment: Very intelligent professor that knows his stuff! I've never written a ratemyprofessor review but this prof. was so helpful and kind I would feel bad not writing a positive review for him. If you go to class you should definitely pass with at least a B since he clearly goes over the important details that he tests students on. Learned a lot!!

This class, Geography of food was so awful I had to drop it. Total waste of time & money. Prof is rude, only calls on you if he thinks you don't have an answer, then if you want to talk, interrupts or says you're wrong.
Overall not a bad professor, however I would not take another class with him. 90% of the class focused solely on two books, I would have preferred a little more variety.

Expectations are very high, randomly calls on people during full-lecture discussions who he doesn't think will know the right answer, assigns difficult 4 and 7 page papers based on two 300+ page novels, does not tell you what will be on exams. Do not take this class unless you are willing to work harder than you should have to.

One of the last remaining PROFESSORS at the university.  Knows his stuff, cars about the subject, available for office hours, and expects students to be students.  Wasn't that interested in the class when I signed up, but he presented the material so well I got excited.  Show up for class and do the readings and you'll do fine.
Very fun class. Lessons can be somewhat disorganized but overall a great experience. Ten-page term paper seems a bit frivolous but he was able to make it a tolerable experience.
He uses a mike now for lectures, you can hear everything. Enjoyable class and I learned a lot.

Better class than others at 200 level. Slides and lectures match well, but you can't just get the slides off Blackboard and understand everything. You have to attend lectures too. He uses a mike now in class so you can hear everything he says. Great content! Tests not to hard if you keep up and study.

What? I can't believe these other comments. Exciting class, learned more than most classes. Crystal clear expectations, exciting lectures, great discussions. Telling all my friends to take his classes.
Great class!

He seemed like a really nice guy, really intelligent but didn't present the material very well. Tests were extremely hard to prepare for because he didn't give any study guide. He just told us to know everything.
Good prof. If your going to complain about profs reading from slides, you should think for a second about how THEY MAKE THE SLIDES.

He is extremely boring. He legitamentally just goes through slides the entire timed no discussion about the topics just reads off facts. So hard to pay attention because he is soo quiet and boring. The discussion are useful in preparing for exams.
Super smart, super cute.
Not bad for a giant lecture intro class. I'm not majoring in Geography, but it's interesting enough I'd consider it for a minor.

Extremely quiet teacher. Almost impossible to hear from just feet away. Gets insulted when asked to be louder. Not helpful, random and extremely awkward. He takes pauses in his lecture where he just stares in silence for literally minutes. Overall a terrible teacher.

Really good, challenging teacher. Forces students to learn themselves versus simply memorizing what the teacher is telling them. Caution: you must be able to discern what is and what isn't important in the lectures, because he isn't very forthcoming about the test material.
very quite and hard to hear.  Not helpful with upcoming assignments. rarely posts lectures online. Does not tell you what will be on tests.
No Comments
Would not recommend this course. Many of her lectures went on tangents about unrelated material and she enjoyed berating students.

The lectures did connect to the assigned homework, and she spent the majority of her lectures tearing us down as a generation because of the involvement of AI in society. One of the easiest classes I've taken. Assignments were direct and clear and graded leniently. Lectures could be kinda tedious, but readings were mostly interesting. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

Spent most of the lectures complaining. grades unreasonably hard. lectures do not connect to the assignments AT ALL. got angry at students for asking questions and would respond with a rude tone but then is horrible at explaining assignments. genuinely don't take this class.

The lectures were pointless to the course content, essays every other week and a short assignment the next. The workload was moderate in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory/graded, but nobody pays attention to what she has to say. The readings are not needed, just focus on the assignment at the end of the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found the class quite easy, however I did fall asleep multiple times doing the assigned readings. While sometimes the material is boring, she clearly has a passion for teaching and wants to help kids learn which I appreciate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going into this class, I was excited because I do love reading and writing. However, Burkert is extremely unengaging and oftentimes lets her poor mood dictate how she treats and speaks to her students. She goes on tangents negatively and spends lots of time complaining about how lazy students have become. The class is pretty easy though.
Terrible teacher very demeaning. Nobody liked her and she had a super creepy vibe. Least favorite professor I've ever had at U of O.

I really wanted to like her. Unfortunately, she ruined the class for me by being lazy when it comes to academic conduct. I worked really hard in this class was proud of my work, so when she reported me to the student misconduct team instead of emailing me or asking about it first, I was so discouraged and did not want to do anything for her class.

Dr. Burkert's behavior as a teacher is concerning - take this as a serious warning. She is prone to bouts of unrelated ranting and when confronted with an issue, victimizes herself and blames the class for their failure to uphold her expectations. reviews.comment: The actual work for the course was very easy. The lectures were entirely unnecessary though. Attendance is mandatory but the lectures were relatively unrelated to assignments. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Project-based course. It was very interesting, and Professor Burkett is kind and helpful, and passionate about her work. Be prepared to be engaged and cooperative with the other people in the class. She has high standards but genuinely wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor B was nice...at first. A few times throughout the term, she came into class and spent most of the lecture time ranting at us. These instances were extremely unprofessional and seemed targeted at us as students and our abilities. Do not miss a single class or you'll fall behind very quickly. Beware, assignment prompts aren't very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Charlie Butler is an amazing professor, took him Winter 2026 Reporting and Interviewing 1. Class is 8 credits it is time consuming but he wants you to be successful. Go to his office hours he is funny and teaches s you feel understand and feel comfortable. Class you will off campus to the City Hall and other spots for different assignments.

Take Charlie Butler for JCOM331 reporting and interviewing. He wants you to be successful; his feedback is clear, and willing to go over the feedback if you have questions. Overall, he is willing to push back assignments if need be. 
The class is a 8 credit, not hard, but a lot. Multiple assignments you on/off campus to report and interview,

Charlie Butler is AMAZING. I am taking his Reporting / Interviewing class and wish I had him before my senior year so I could take all his classes. Everyone needs a professor like him! Class is fun, he talks to everyone and goes out of his way to know YOU. He has been my favorite professor all 4 years.

Take whatever class he teaches. Charlie is legit and knows what he is talking about. I took his reporting and interviewing class, JCOM 331, and I am very happy and satisfied that I had the opportunity to learn from him.

No offense, but it's such a shame that Charlie's no longer leading the media ARC bc this is who should be helping journalism students figure out what they want to do. Fantastic prof, fantastic content. Can be tough but just bc he cares and wants you to actually produce good work.

I had friends take this class with a different professor (Justin Francese) and they complained about how boring J212 was. This was not my experience with Charlie. This class was extremely fun and engaging, which is oftentimes hard to do in a class talking about words and grammar. If you can take any class with Professor Butler, do it.

Charlie Butler is a fantastic professor. He brings energy to every class, and gets students involved in a way that doesn't feel forced or intimidating. He has well organized, conversational lectures, and consistently addresses all of the subjects students need to focus on. He is probably the best professor I've had at UO -- highly highly recommend!

I LOVE Charlie. The GE's on the other hand... not so much. Charlie was very engaging with the class and really cared about his students doing well. I ended up getting a terrible GE and that made the course harder than it should be. 3 major writing assignments, 1 test, and all online quizzes get full credit as long as you do them.
so boring and basically the same class as J100 or 101, I forget which is the grammar one.

Charlie Butler is such a great professor! He truly cares about our writing. I visited him during office hours several times. He was quite accommodating when it came to the assignments we completed in class. He gave a lot of helpful insight and tips on how to make our writing stand out. I would highly recommend him.

I took J213 during winter term and there was a hybrid option for those who wanted it. It was a super fun class, Charlie presented the material in a very easy way to learn. The tests were super easy (he gives you two attempts and all the questions ahead of time) and there are only 2 papers!

This class really frustrated me because our writing assignments were limited to 350 words at most, with a sentence count of 2-3 sentences in each paragraph. There was also a max word count of 20-25 words in each sentence. I can't understand how I am supposed to write a story that's worthy of a good grade with all of these writing restrictions.

Charlie is not just one of my favorite professors Ive taken, but one of my favorite people Ive met. Hes extremely supportive of his students and truly wants you to succeed, not just in his class but in life. Hes really helped me grow in my writing and in my confidence as a writer. Please PLEASE take one of his classes before you graduate!!

Charlie is a super likable professor and easy to communicate with. Attendance was mandatory, and you take password protected quiz each lecture. He used real-world examples so it felt like I was learning things that were relevant. Also, we played Kahoot and Jeopardy to win prizes before due dates. A sweet professor who wants you to do well!

Charlie has been one of my absolute favorite professors at the SOJC. Although some of his assignments can be challenging, he explains everything clearly to make sure his students feel comfortable. Highly recommend taking a class with him

Professor Butler rocks! He wants to help his students and you can tell he genuinely cares. There is never an overwhelming amount of work due, and he explains assignments well. I hope to take another class with him.

Professor Butler rocks. He gives incredible feedback and I've learned so much from this class that will benefit me down the line. I hope I can take another class with him before I graduate. 10/10 professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are kinda entertaining but your GE basically does everything. Don't get an 8am lab time.
Charlie is an absolute gem! He goes above and beyond for his students and is an amazing mentor. He truly cares about your work and gives excellent feedback.

Please just take this professor before you graduate. Ive now taken him in multiple courses and I want to take him in more. He thoroughly cares so much about his students and makes class actually enjoyable. He is not at all a tough grader and the amount of feedback he gives you is unbelievable. Hes my favorite professor Ive ever taken in school.
Charlie is the best journalism professor I've ever had, but he's an incredibly tough grader. Write as much as you want, you'll hardly get anything better than B+

I had Charlie for Gateway and everyone loved him. He's the nicest guy and would love to help his students learn and improve. A lot of people complain about Gateway being hard, but the hardest thing about it is that attendance is mandatory. Would highly recommend Charlie as a professor. He has a lot of real-world experience and he loves his job.

Charlie was an amazing professor. He was very kind and always went out of his way to make sure students understood the material. He was very comical and had a good grasp of the topics we learned about. He made the class enjoyable and I would definitely recommend him.

Prof. Budd is an amazing person and amazing professor. She cares a ton about how her students are doing and is always available. Her lectures are super interesting and she's extremely organized. She loves constructive criticism and actually applies this to the classroom. Class is super light and interactive. Would 100% take another class with her!!
(FHS 492) This was a chill easy class it just sucks because it's 2 hours long.
I took FHS 492 with Professor Budd and it was a pretty chill class, you don't have to do much!

reviews.comment: Dr. Budd was awesome. She really respects students and treats you like human beings. I found the assignments to be interesting, and she is a very easy grader, so overall the class was very stress-free. It was nearly all group work though, which was fine for me but difficult if your group sucks.
Just the greatest, sweetest guy. Never thought a class about banking would warm my heart. He genuinely cares about his students!

Roger clearly has a passion for teaching and helping students learn. The he class is lecture heavy and can get boring near the end, it is relevant and impactful for students. He brings in over 12 guest speakers from banks ranging from CFO, CEO, Director to give students the opportunity to ask questions. Also many internship and work opportunities.

Busse is the best professor of all time. Caring guy who helps all students get jobs in banking if they wish. The class structure is very fair and based on the textbook he wrote, but he provides it to the class, free of charge. Nicest, most enthusiastic professor I know, 10/10 would take his class again.
G.O.A.T. that's it.

I heard Roger was the runner up to play the teacher in Dead Poets Society, kidding of course. But honestly, he's by far one of the best teachers I've ever had loved that every class we had a guest speaker from local bank from the CFOs to the CEOs. Thank you, Roger!
Just the best

Roger is an absolute gem, but I will say this course is a bit harder than I thought it would have been. He made it so much better though, and is someone who you can truly work with on a lot of different things that you might not fully understand.
Love this guy. Take him if you can!

Roger was the absolute best. You will not find a better teacher or course at Oregon. I 100% recommend his class, as he is a class act and very insightful. The course is useful, applicable, and enjoyable while not overly time-consuming or challenging.

Roger Busse is one of the best professors I've had in my four years of college. He makes his course relevant to people who are interested in banking, even having guest speakers in every class and opportunities to network with them. There's some reading to do but if you show up to every class and pay attention you'll succeed. He's also hilarious.

This was an incredible class. It gives you so much real-world applicable knowledge, and Roger is such an engaging teacher! As long as you come to class, listen, and do the work you'll do great. Roger is also so kind and cares so much for his students. I feel grateful I got to take a class with him.

Roger is an amazing Professor that teaches in an engaging way. There is a guest speaker from the banking industry almost every lecture. Students have time to ask questions to these guest speakers to gain additional knowledge. If you show up to class and complete the work it is an easy A. There is also lots of opportunities for extra credit.

One of the best professors at this school. Useful lecture content and constant guest speakers to provide real-life advice and scenarios within the banking realm. Super understanding and easy to talk to in case you ever need help!
This gotta be the best professor at U of O. The class content was great. You might feel a little boring for the first few class but later on, it's great. The most useful class I ever had.

Nice outgoing professor, but a bit scattered in lecture. Consists of one midterm, one final, and five problem sets, and some extra credit work. Not very hard, and the slides are very comprehensive, so you don't need to attend every class.

Professor Burlando is a great professor. He explains things well especially if you ask specific questions. The class isn't easy but its not impossible either. Don't take his class.

Thank god I passed. 311 is just uggh. However, he is a good professor. I really recommend taking his classes

Alfredo is a really cool, caring teacher. You definitely have to stay on top of your work to keep up with concepts, but he does a good job of explaining points of confusion during office hours. I thought I'd hate the class but I actually enjoy it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the guys who make you wanna take his class again, not for the topic he teaches but for his personality and lectures that full of laughing.

He is a very good professor, because in his class, I have learned many things useful. Finally, I got an A from this class. He is very kind.

Interesting guy, lefthanded so hard to see what he writes then he goes quick. Feel like he doesent really care if you know what yer doing or not. HORRIBLE!!!

Burland is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He is very nice. You just need follow his notes and homeworks, you will clearly make sense and get good grads on exams(2 exams, mid & final). U don't need afriad for his accent, he will post his voice-notes on blackboard. The only thing I want to compaind is that I got 96.6%, he just gives me an A, not A+.But his course is really helpful.

He is one of the best professors I had. His teaching is very intuitive and really makes sense. He explains everything thoroughly and step by step. I think he is just using fundamental knowledge of calculus for this term's class.

BAD. Writes in circles instead of top to bottom, left to right. Explains equations poorly. Bad handwriting. Doesn't answer emails. Takes what should be an economics class and turns it into a calculus class. Uses complicated calculus equations to show how to do simple economic graphs when we didn't need to learn the math in the first place. Very smart guy but the class is not supposed to be taught with calculus

Just writes on the blackboard all class with long, confusing equations. Has horrible hand writing and the class is basically laughing at him because its such a joke. Save yourself and just don't.

Different opinion from other reviews but I liked the class, she gave good insight and has a very calming voice (i fell asleep once or twice). AVOID THIS CLASS

Shes like weird? If you've ever been to Marin, California and met a rich hippie who cosplays being poor and zen... shes like that. Horrific. Save yourself

Michele knows her stuff but is so unbelievably rude. For someone teaching meditation, it's unfortunate that she creates such a negative environment with her attitude toward students. Michele is a great yoga teacher. She is very involved in making sure you are performing the moves correctly and follows up to monitor your progress.

He was the most knowledgable proffesor in his respective course material that ive ever had.
Lucas Burke is a great history GE. He was good at teaching and was helpful with things like essays.

Make sure you read the textbook chapters and try to teach yourself the material before lecture time. He has a tendency to share additional information that isn't going to be tested on, which can be confusing if you're just being introduced to a concept. If you teach yourself and view his lectures as supplemental, you should be fine.

Took this class online over the summer. This online course was straightforward, coming from a B-B+ student. The exams are pretty easy and you can master all the content in just a couple days. Can't speak for those who take his class in-person, but the online version is well ran and simple.

One of the most confusing classes and arguably the worst. You will sit in this lecture and take notes on a bunch of material that is truly irrelevant to the material you are being tested on. If the entire exam is econ problems, then why is that not what a bulk of the lecture is? Good luck if you take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Without a doubt one of the worst professors I've had the displeasure of taking. Lectures are long, and he provides information that has no point being in the class. He's a very smart guy, with a mastery in Finance, so much so that he has a difficult time simplifying information. You will be teaching yourself the material throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will need to teach yourself the content as his lectures are very hard to pay attention to and he doesn't get to the material that's actually on the exams until the last 10 minutes of class. Nice guy though.

Gabe is a clear teacher, his lectures are boring yes, but the material in quizzes and homeworks is identical to what is on the exams. I stopped showing up after week 3 and studied for an avg of two hours for the midterms and received above 85's. If you put in a slight amount of work this class is extremely straightforward and fair.

Extremely hard class but manageable if you focus. Explains things very fast and not well. But tests are not surprising material, all the exact same as the practice quizzes with new numbers. If you study well, you will do good. If you email or ask for help, he explains it well and will give the answer. Other comments are harsh, Gabe is a good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Buchbinder has been one of the best professors I have had at the UO so far. He is not easy. If you pay attention to his lectures, you will do just fine. He provides extra credit if you go to office hours or tutoring each week. And if you actually pay attention during his lectures, he is quite entertaining and has a dry sense of humor.

You're cooked if you get him for finance 311. Midterms and final are worth over 60% of your grade, his lectures are the most boring thing on the planet, and to top it off, his accent make it very hard to understand the points he tries to get across. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class as a whole is so confusing and the topic seems very useless, he does his best but at times I think he is smarter than he realizes and has a tough time simplifying things. The practice are multiple choice and make you feel confident about the test and then the actual test is much more difficult and fill in the blank. VERY DIFFICULT CLASS

Definitely not the most entertaining professor, actually pretty far from it. His lectures are usually an 1:20 to the full class period. His slides explain everything you need to know to succeed in the class which is nice. He also provides practice quizzes for every chapter which are almost identical to the exam formats which is really nice.
Lectures are pretty boring but you can easily get a good grade if you do the practice quizzes. Midterms are in the same format as the lecture quizzes so if you thoroughly practice, you will do fine.

I have never taken a class that was so poorly put together, taught, and graded. The exams are so different in format from the homework and study materials which completely messes up your ability to comprehend the material. He reads in a heavy accent in a monotonous tone and it is an absolute chore to listen. Avoid class with Gabriel at all costs.

This is for FIN 615. He should not be a professor plain and simple. He does not know how to explain material and it makes every person in the classroom confused. Nobody knows what they are doing and it is obvious he is doing nothing to assist. No examples, no assistance overall terrible.

He's a perfect of example of just because you know the material doesn't mean you should teach it. No idea how to explain anything and tries to include examples in class, but instead of having people solve it he just puts it up there with the answer so we have no idea how to do the work. Also talks too fast and seems in over his head.

I am shocked at how much i pay for courses here and get a teacher this incompetent. at a high level BA class he teaches worse than teachers i had in High-school. Each lecture consists of an on average 90min lecture of the teacher reading off his slides one by one. No college level course should be taught in such a laissez-faire way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in class and do the practice quizzes, you will do fine. Lectures can be boring but he teaches everything you need to know.  Guaranteed C if you do all the practice quizzes, but if you can do them then you will do good on exams. Not much hw just pay attention and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking this class with him he is terrible. Halfway through the term, everybody stopped showing up to class because all he did was read off of the slides with a heavy accent that made the content even more confusing. Worst teacher I've had since attending here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Buchbinder is a grad student with a very thick accent. He will lecture for 1.5 hours at a speed that is far to fast to really absorb. Would 100% recommend studying on your own extensivly or find help with a tutor because most students are in the C-D range before the term-end curve. I think he means well, but is lacking real experience.

Attending lectures are completely pointless since he's simply reading off the slides. He made multiple mistakes with wording and NUMBERS in the first exam, which cause him to interrupt us MULTIPLE times during the exam and confused everyone in the process. He takes points off little things, even though he consistently makes mistakes.

The lecture slides are the class. He uses the lecture slides solely as a means of teaching, simply echoing them, and finds great difficulty answering questions during class. The lecture slides are extremely dense and hard to understand. His grading is harsh and based primarily on three exams, with no room for error. Do not take him, ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I've ever had at UO

Do not take this class with this professor. Class is lecture heavy, with slides that are difficult to understand and even harder to follow at home for studying. The class is 2 midterms and a final that will make up pretty much your whole grade since there are only three homework assignments and no way to earn any extra credit.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Bad explanations of topics, boring lecture slides with black and white bullet points, usually 5+ extremely complicated topics rushed through in one day, and slides and quizzes/test contained errors that he would have to stop and correct. DONT TAKE BUCHBINDER OR ANY GRADUATE STUDENT for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first college course I've had to withdraw from. I will take FIN 311 again when a real professor teaches the class.

One hour office hours, no GE, one tutor available to all, and a teacher who isn't willing to take feedback. He goes unreasonably fast, and never covers the same topic twice, so if you don't understand it, good luck. 3 assignments in total account for 95% of your grade, and you get about 6 classes to learn it all in between. The worst class I've had
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attend lectures and try your best to pay attention. Class is very test and hw heavy. To be honest like most in the class I was quite lost after lectures but found it helpful to study the hell out of the homework solutions which he publishes with his own work. My best advice is to study homework solutions and to practice problems from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gabriel is a new professor; this is his first time teaching a college course and the lack of experience is very noticeable. He reads directly from the lecture slides and struggles to answer questions. Everyone fails the first midterm because it's only 6 questions worth 100 points. Only 3 homeworks + 2 midterms + final = Few chances to boost grade.

He is the type of professor that would literally not help you on any of the homeworks. When one of my friends asked a question about the homework, he refused to help since we have to know how to do it. This class is literally hard and hardly anyone in the class understands what's going on and passed the two midterms.

Homework and assignments are very reasonable, but very hard to follow his lectures. He often will go on a tangent and leave the class behind in the process. He gave a 10min break which I enjoyed, but an inability to follow the lectures made it hard to get much from the class and I was forced to study extensively on my own to even grasp the concepts

He demonstrates that he genuinely cares about his students because he takes feedback very seriously. Although there are debates, they are low-stress and he doesn't really require everyone to speak. As long as you demonstrate some level of participation you should succeed in his class.

I had Byron for his second term at UO and he was a great professor! Very discussion based class, so be prepared to speak. The students who do the best in his class are those who answer his broad statements. He is very debate heavy but the topics are interesting. Great guy, really cares about students. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! I felt like I actually learned in this class and left with a new perspective. There are five quizzes every other week and three 'debates,' but there is genuinely nothing to fear. They help engage you with course concepts as it is a more discussion-based class. I would go out of my way to take another class with him!

I had him for my Sociology 458 class (Sociology of Expertise). He's a phenomenal teacher. He cares about his students and makes the class engaging. Every week (for the most part) there is a quiz, however, they are cumulative and based on questions from previous quizzes. I would highly recommend taking one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Byron was an amazing professor and you can tell he cares a lot about the topic and he wants his students to do well. The most difficult part of this class was the 3 debates as he grades them partially on the topics from the readings. Quizzes were easy because they were cumulative.
Mark is great. You can tell her really cares about the content and his students. Fairly easy class as long as you do the readings and show up to class. Great guy fs
An amazing professor, very engaging lectures with content applicable to real life.

Professor Carey is a very thoughtful, caring, and well-experienced person. Indigenous Peoples is a powerful class that will (likely) greatly expand your worldview. It is sometimes disorganized in terms of grading. Also the class is very seminar style, so the quality depends a lot on your fellow students. Great Prof. feedback. Definitely recommend.

(Indigenous Peoples HC 231) I recommend this class regardless of my critiques. Very few assignments, I did not know my grade until finals week (I had a general idea of it during the term) and his grading scale is WACK. (A 91 is either an A- or B+, etc) We discussed important issues, I learned a lot, and the material is diverse and important.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Carey will push you through weekly writing assignments and in discussion. He is smart, but lacks the pretension and "I'm right you're wrong" attitude that you find in some other HC history professors. Genuinely nice guy with funny stories if you can get them out of him. DO THE READING and participate and you will love his class.

Mark Carey is a wonderful professor- caring, kind, helpful, and definitely challenges his students. Gives lots of feedback on essays, is great at facilitating discussion, and is very friendly and helpful in office hours. I strongly recommend his class.

Chad is the GOAT. I took American Deaf Culture with him and really enjoyed it. The class is taught in ASL as he is Deaf, which I found to be very enriching and enjoyable. The content was interesting and assignments were easy. Chad like's to joke around and tell stories to keep lectures interesting. Definitely recommend taking classes with Chad.

Literally so nice. He really seems like he wants us to learn ASL, but also doesn't want us to feel burnt out. Tests are chill, and he's patient and provides feedback. Classes Mon-Thurs, but only takes attendance on Mon and Wed. Would 100% take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite prof at UO! So nice and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students learning ASL. Tests were easy as long as you try you'll do fine. Mondays and Wednesdays were the only days he took attendance. I 100% would take his class again.

Professor Chad is a great professor! This has been one of my favorite classes, and Chad makes sure that you understand the material. He is funny and kind, and allows for late work with no penalty. There is a lot of homework as it is a language class but it is easy to manage!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Take his classes and I encourage you to actually go to class every day that you can. I have taken 3 classes with Chad. If you show up and try, you'll get a good grade. He is a little bit on the shy-ish side compared to Keith, but he's still great and there's an interpreter there.

If you take his online course, be prepared for: 10-20 assignments every week, no late assignments accepted, having absolutely zero help or communication from him throughout the entire term, and confusing/unclear lessons and expectations. This was a nightmare.

Take Professor Catron! You need a second language from highschool or community college to even get into university. American Sign Language, taught by Professor Catron, is a GREAT option. Weekly discussion posts, assignments, and quizzes. You get the hang of the workload after a week or two. He is understanding and helpful. I took both 101 and 102.

I've had both Chad and Keith Catron as ASL professors. If you have a choice between the two, I would recommend Keith as I found his teaching style to be much more engaging. Chad is a fairly good professor too though, and if you have some prior knowledge of ASL, his class is very easy. Attendance not graded but pretty much necessary for the course.

Although Chad is kind and teaches well, his unresponsiveness to emails and messages makes him not the best professor. He is essentially unreachable outside of class, and such a slow grader that you will forget what the assignment was about by the time you get the grade back. Also, a lot of busy work!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super kind and helpful, not strict on deadlines, very nice classroom environment

He's a super kind and understanding professor. He's always willing to help with extensions when you need them. There's also an interpreter twice a week to help students communicate with him and help the students' understanding. The textbook isn't physical, it's an online course thing that he uses for homework too.

Great class, it was over Zoom. Clear teaching, understandable, had lecture videos accessible outside of class for extra help. Good grader and gave good feedback on assignments. Well organized. It's hard to fail this class since he gives you all the resources to learn.

So fantastic. Span 339. Cares so much ab students and gives them the benefit of the doubt. V class-discussion heavy, which I loved. She cares ab your opinion and analysis and is open to many perspectives. Puts in so much effort to make the class as good as possible. I often feel a lot of anxiety in Span classes, and I did not w her! Mostly essays.

Great professor, passionate, kind & understanding. It was considered a Grad Class therefore she expected a lot from her students, was reading heavy, with at least 4 readings assigned each week & DP 2x a week. There were no quizzes, just a midterm essay and a final essay. She offered a few extra credit opportunities. Lowkey tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not extremely easy, though not demanding either.  IF you are familiar with the text (occasional skimming) it should be no trouble to produce quality work.  If you took english in middle school, the level of analysis will be similar. Her diction during lecture is rather annoying and frequently takes too long to say simple thoughts.

Cecilia is a really passionate, knowledgable professor. I love her enthusiasm for her subject, but also her students. In a such a small class you really get to know her. She expects a lot from students and that can be intimidating, but she's always willing to help. There's A LOT of reading and it's necessary to do well, but it's interesting

This was a very easy class, didn't put much effort into it. Essentially you only have to attend your discussion sections. The assignments are clear and easy and overall he is a great guy and taught the class well.

I love professor Ceballos! I've taken multiple classes with him, and both were very engaging, and very approachable. The only prof in the poli sci department who actually teaches 100-200s, the way they should be taught. Very clear explainer and grader. Essays generously graded, no homework, study guides are clear. Ceballos sets you up for success.
such an easy class and Rutger was chill, just really simple stuff which makes it kinda super boring
Very engaging professor, class was very informational and he was able to teach a lot of good concepts
He is super chill and caring, only lectures with dis once a week but no attendance, great guy and interesting lectures.

I would recommend this class if you're looking for a class that isn't work heavy. There's an essay, topic proposal, annotated sources, no mid term, outline and a essay final. There are readings to do every week but I never did them and I have an A. Put in work to the assignments and you'll pass. The lectures are boring. Discussions are mandatory.

PS 106: I had about as neutral an experience as possible. Not particularly fun, but an interesting and painless lecture-heavy class. Assignments are low pressure and doable for freshmen. Ceballos' knowledge base and specializations are interesting and I recommend learning from and talking to him. Do the reading and pay attention, you'll be fine.

BOOORINGGGG
his slides are ass and I think he gets off on his own voice

Professor Ceballos is amazing! He cares a lot about his students' success and is approachable outside of class. He is a great lecturer and makes it interesting. His PS308 class consisted of two essays and an in-person final at the end of the term. Will definitely take classes with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Ceballos, he was so chill, a great lecturer, and incredibly understanding when it comes to students' personal lives and very willing to give extensions. He's very eager to help his students succeed and really easy to talk to. Vibed with this guy so much that I asked him to be my thesis advisor. Overall a straight chiller
Amazing professor and really easy class if you just pay attention.

Professor Ceballos was an absolutely wonderful professor for an introductory course. Its obvious that he cares about the content, even if his lectures can be a little slow sometimes. If you're interested in political science this is a great place to start. Would take his class again!

Textbook and inquisitive for course, expensive. Two tests both provided with study guide of all potential answers and two essays. I never went to the lectures, just some of the discussions and got an A. If you're planning to do what I did and just use the study guide, you might not want to buy the textbook. Professor was really nice and handsome.

He is super sweet and very accommodating. You have 2 four four-page essays throughout the term, a midterm, and a non-cummulative final. Attending lectures is not mandatory, but attending discussion sections is. However, you can miss up to four discussion sections. The lectures are kind of boring, but the class is organized and easy to follow.

Professor Ceballos is so chill. You can tell that he is very passionate about early US political thought. There were only two papers, and readings before class are optional because he reviews them in class in detail. The material is basic but he makes it interesting and engaging. Pretty easy class would recommend as an intro to political science.

A genuinely fantastic person as well as teacher. I've literally never met a teacher who cares about their students as much as Jori does. Accessible, accommodating and so so kind. They give caring and thoughtful feedback, you can really tell they want you to grow and succeed as a writer.

Jorie is my favorite professor at UO. They are kind, casual, genuine, and funny. It feels more like a club than a class. There's a lot of participation and writing expected because it's creative writing and all workshops all the time, but you're allowed to bring snacks and the whole feeling is very light. They don't grade rough drafts, only finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Celona is so wonderful and you will not regret taking their class! They gave me great feedback on assignments and are overall so kind and helpful. A decent amount of reading (short stories) but well selected and enjoyable ones.

Professor Celona gives excellent creative writing feedback and was tremendously insightful about what makes a story work. They are especially good at giving feedback that is both specific to the story that is being critiqued and broad enough to be helpful to everyone listening. They also cultivated a very welcoming and encouraging environment.
Wonderful class and wonderful lectures. Excited to see it expanded into a full sequence.
Interesting lectures and fair grading. Projects were fun and simple. Decent amount of outside work, but definitely manageable.

Professor Cendes is incredible. She cares about her students and the subject she teaches. Her lectures are engaging and interesting. The class is easy, perfect for entry level astronomy. The projects were easy, clear to understand, and truly fun in my opinion. This is a teacher who will care about your wellbeing and will make your learning fun.
For a Journalism instructor, he is one of the worst communicators I have ever known. The assignments and midterm/final were designed poorly.

You have to buy into Carl. He's a little nuts but he understands this and he is one of the most brilliant people I've had the pleasure to learn from. A genuine character invested in his students. I strongly recommend his classes. He offers something rare and valuable. Easy to talk to, approachable. Be prepared to move your desks into a circle.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Do not take Carl's class. He expects his students to complete hours and hours of readings and group projects and essay writing. He is unfair and does not know how to properly create an assignment. His midterm and final is practically impossible to complete. Each assignment he asks 45 questions and expects them to be answered in under 200 words.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Long winded but caring. Open your mind to new theories and you'll appreciate him.
He cares about the students and honestly wants you to learn as much as you can while you are there. Grade is secondary. Carl is earnest and kind, and will help people achieve their best.

He was the WORST professor I had EVER had.  I honestly did not learn anything despite trying to pay attention. It truly didn't seem like he knew what he was talking about at all. His rants last forever and have no informational value whatsoever. AWFUL.

Took Cons Cult Enviro. Carl dances to the beat of his own drum--or bell. He often brought in a meditation bell and sounded it at the beginning of class. He is a brilliant guy. You have to have an open mind in any class with him and be willing to learn. I'm moderate, I hate left (and right) extremism and never felt like he was out of line.

I took Media Literacy from Bybee during zero week and it was great. It was pretty free-form in that we never followed the agenda, often ending up on long philosophical rants. Yes, he leans to the left, but he'll hear out anyone's opinion. He gets you thinking and he allows students to get him thinking--everything is totally discussion-oriented.

I do not know why students like this guy. Hands down the WORST teacher EVER!!! I purposely would read during class, not paying attention at all, and I still pulled an A. So I guess if you want an easy A, this would be the right teacher. Otherwise, most boring professor in the nation!!!

Carl is a brilliant man with quite a personality.  I guess if you're a Republican than you can  keep being close minded, otherwise, listen to a man that goes beyond a normal class. He exicites to think.  Every person in the room had a voice.  The class was moreabout learning and less about making the grade.
CProfessor Bybee is great. He changed the way I see the world. I can say this only about a handful of people (let alone professors) I have encountered in my undergraduate and graduate studies.

I took Dr. Bybee for Mass Comm theory back in 05. Great teacher, great person overall. t he is very interested in helping students learn and to see the world, specifically the media, for what it really is. His class taught me to think critically about what I see in media, and I've remained interested, finishing my masters soon and heading to PhD.

Bybee's greatest mistake is that he cares too much about his students and their souls. He wants to give them the tools to interpret the world for themselves. What he has to say is very difficult to hear and some people refuse to even listen but those who are open minded, enough to consider that the world isn't what it seems, will never be the same.

I took several classes from Bybee and found him to be one of the BEST. Brilliant man, GREAT teacher.   He does have a tendency to piss off the idiot children of the neocons who overpopulate the University. Some of these fools, I wondered how they managed to be admitted. Maybe Daddy was a big donor?  BTW, the "hot or not" question should be remo

I can't believe he hasn't been fired yet.  I would rather take InfoHell again than have to sit through another of his classes.  This was the WORST experience I've had in my education.  The texts he uses are all AT LEAST 10 years old.  Come on Bybee, this is not some goddamned poor public school-WE CAN BUY NEWER BOOKS IF YOU ARE WILLING TO FIND THEM

Do yourself a favor and DO NOT take a class from Bybee.  If you want to leave class everyday angered that you are paying money to hear a man's political agenda, by all means sign up.  If you want to read articles upon articles (some over 40 pages long) that have no worthwhile means but to confuse and annoy, sign up.

Easily the worst class I have taken thus far in college. Easy as hell, but you sit there every day and learn absolutely nothing even remotely worthwhile. Not once did I read the book, but I still managed to earn an A just sort of playing on his flamingly leftists sympathies in each of my papers. The guy wears a fanny pack for crhist sake!

This was the worst teacher I had EVER. A raging, extreme left-wing, boring, obnoxious man. If you want to hear someone criticize everyone he disagrees with every day, and tell students to f-off (yes, he did this), and teach you absolutely nothing (except maybe how to be intolerant towards even the most moderately conservative viewpoints) take bybee

If you want an easy A, take this class/professor.  If you want to be educated...stay far away.  This is hours upon hours of babbling and incoherent leftist, PC indoctrination.  The highlight was learning that dogs cannot read books.
No Comments

HOLY SCHNIKES, I had Bybee once and I told myself I would never take him again. He is the most monotoned individual I've ever had for a class. Thank god I graduated already, I'd hate to think I've have to have him for class again. GO DUCKS!
No Comments
Carl is the man... really smart, lot to offer

Bybee is my favorite teacher at the UofO.He taught me a lot about the comercialization of children and the effects of the Media on society. His classes are what you make of them and if you are smart enough to realize that he is open to anything than you can learn a lot. He is one of the smartest people I have ever met, just missunderstood.

Be easy on professor Bybee.  He is most likely the most open-minded professor on campus.  And his classes are what YOU make of them -- don't hold him responsible for what you don't learn or don't agree with.  I feel a huge amount of freedom in his class, which is what he promotes.

Worst prof I've ever had. Supposed to be teaching some form of cultural studies, but I don't think he even understands the subject fully. Focuses more on his own moral outrage than dissecting cultural phenomena. Class is totally disorganized, which is a shame because the topic is interesting

Carl Bybee's partisanship would make Michael Moore hang his head in shame.  Aside from getting his lackeys to do his dirty work, he also manages to make allegedly hot-button topics (ie: women & race in the media) seem terribly outdated & stale.

Far too much of the class time is spent on his political beliefs.  I'm not paying tuition to hear him tell me why the war in Iraq is wrong and how James Earl Jones voicing Darth Vader is **** against black people.

I had Prof. Bybee just after the Sept. 11 attacks, and can say that too much of the class was spent on the wisdom of going into Afghanistan and his opposition thereof. His GTFs were arrogant and ran the classes, and both shot students down who dared to gainsay them.

This last person was really on crack. Bybee was by far heads and tails smarter than the rest of the j-school combined. Unlike most of them, he had a conscience. His lectures were passionate and he was respectful to students that disagreed.

Just keep away.  The guy is nuts, and is offensively arrogant.  He uses his classes as a personal soapbox to go off about his personal opinions.  He cuts you off and belittes you if you disagree with him.  His assignments are haphazard, his organization is negligent and he spends class time ranting.
good luck if she's your professor or ge!

Cons: You will be held to the highest scholarly expectations and will not be coddled or given anything you haven't earned. Pre-reading is mandatory and quizzes are demanding. Pros: Her grading criteria and classroom expectations are reliable and her lectures highly accessible.  Passing her class indicates your full understanding of course material.
Extremely inconsistent grading. She admits to grading according to her mood. Very condescending instructor. If it weren't for her courses I would have a great transcript for graduate school.

I enjoyed this class, Anna always had an upbeat attitude and she did a good job teaching the material. She at times seemed unorganized but she clearly cared and her exams were fair based on what was covered in class. I would recommend taking this course with her, but know going into it that the course content is different than other math classes.
Just so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She lectured for maybe 30 minutes the whole term, doesn't believe lecturing is how you learn proofs. So she gives worksheets every class which add up to a significant portion of grade. She doesn't drop anything, though she said she would, and only inputs missing assignments when final grades are due. Had an A all term then boom half a grade drop.

Not sure why every new professor thinks theyre the one who knows what's right and everyone else is teaching wrong but she doesn't actually teach, she just gives worksheets and expects people to ask questions individually. She took her shoes off at the beginning of class, this aint evergreen state college, have some professionalism. Highschool-esque
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Math 307*. She thinks learning can only happen by 'doing', so she has you read the material before the class and complete an assignment that isn't graded, then every class is just a worksheet and YouTube videos. Not really sure why I'm paying $4k for this, she doesn't actually teach. On top of those there's homework, quizzes, and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Felt like the students were learning the course with the professor. She didn't put grades on Canvas until the end of Thanksgiving break, and wouldn't tell you your overall grade until after each midterm-where she gave you a slip of paper?? Shes a nice person, but it felt like we as a class were thrown under the bus as a "guinea pig" class for her.

Teaches very differently.  There are no lectures just talking with classmates and working on worksheets based on the reading done the night before class. The number of time readings and the worksheets given with the readings can take hours. She doesn't care about you having other tough classes. Good luck getting more than an 85 on the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was clearly new to teaching but always meant well and was open to feedback to accommodate students. She often confused herself when solving problems as she was relearning it herself. Homework problems sometimes seemed impossible but the tests were much easier.

Goes over subjects really well, stops and makes sure everyones together and understanding. Shes always really fun and energetic and she loves teaching so its easy so like the class. Showing understanding of material is more important than getting the right answer.

Clearly new to teaching, but was very open to student feedback. Made adjustments throughout the term about the pace and workload of the class to benefit students. Gave ungraded quizzes once a week so we could honestly gauge our understanding. Webwork problems and in-class examples were much harder than exams, which were 80% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: While Cepek cares about her students well being, her teaching definitely needs improvement. A lot of the time it feels as though she doesn't even know what she's teaching, and isn't great at explaining about why we have to do what we do to solve a problem. The only grades in the grade book are tests with a small weight for homework.

Nadia is a little disorganized, but I thoroughly enjoy learning from her. She creates a low-stakes environment where I feel comfortable making mistakes as I try to learn the language. It's definitely hard, but that comes with the territory of learning a second language. I'm taking my second course with her and I'm looking forward to it!

As far as personality goes, Nadia is amazing. But as far as her teaching method goes, that is a whole different story. Nadia is EXTREMELY disorganized. Everything is at rapid speed and she almost never answers your questions. There are so many homework assignments each night that it makes it hard to actaully learn and spend time on each one.

Nadia is one of the most passive teachers I've had. She is not understanding at all, she wants you to succeed but doesn't explain things very well. She complains a lot if your class isn't very enthusiastic because she has the energy of 5 year old girl. She doesn't spend a lot of time on things and is very unorganized.

Nadia is very knowledgeable in her field and clearly has passion for teaching Italian and Italian culture. I enjoyed her class but unfortunately it was quite unorganized, possibly because some family events occurred during the middle of the term. Overall I enjoyed having Nadia, she is a fun personality and knows what she's doing!

Nadia is a very enthusiastic professor and one of the greatest ones at desiring her students to not only pass her class, but also to learn the subject matter.  She is very willing to help you after hours and eager for her students to understand.  I would recommend her to any person with an interest in Italian, and even to those who are not.

Had her for Ital 150, 301, 303 and for a study abroad program. Amazingly energetic, always happy and wants to help. She expects your best effort, so don't slack off, but she totally understands if you have a bad week (or month, because I did).
Kind of an intensive class for a 200 level, but Nadia is nice. A lot of people disliked her teaching methods, but she cares a lot about her students' success.
No Comments

Nadia cares more about her students success than any other language teacher I've ever had. She is very helpful, and the woman has more energy than most 5 year olds I know!! Her class is very fun, and lively. However, she does expect for you to do the work...definitely see her in her office if your'e having trouble.
save yourself the frustration
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rarely makes a classroom appearance and when she does, she is disrespectful and dampers the entire mood of Straub 156, her class that she chose to teach, with slides from 2014. When she chooses not to make an appearance, she forces one of her GEs to teach, and said GE does not seem comfortable doing so. Good luck enjoying this course.

I'm not sure how the university continues to let Dayna Chatman teach this class. She is very rude and strict about attendance, yet she missed 6+ classes. She relies on her GE's to do everything and told us not to email her. For a class that seems interesting, Dayna does a great job of losing the attention of everyone.

Missed over 6 classes, but had a strict attendance policy for students. Taught by GE half of the time. Weird rules about not being accessible by email? GE's were wonderful, but weren't set up for success by Dr. D. The course content is interesting, but she reads directly off the slides. Dr. D is rude when students have questions and expects silence
She is so strict about everything and checks AI for every single thing

She will call you out if you're 5 minutes late in front of the entire class of 150-300 students, and say, "whoever just walked in, please see me after class." She reads directly off the slides, and the GEs taught the first 3 weeks of class because she wasn't there, and expects her students to show up when she skipped the first 3 weeks of classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely pretentious. Will stop the entire lecture to say, "I'll just wait until it's quiet." Even though we are adults, we get called out for whispering and leaving to go to the bathroom as if it were first grade. Cannot arrive 0.0001 second late. She has now hidden our grade from being visible in Canvas. If you can avoid her class, STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely pretentious. Will stop the entire lecture and say, "I'll just wait until it's quiet," like a first-grade teacher, even though we are adults and the class is in Straub 156, so you can't really hear anyone else talking. Will yell at you for being late. Attendance is mandatory even though she just reads from the slides. Will mark you tardy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hostile environment is no joke. She doesn't respect us nor has faith. Busy work for no reason. Disorganized. Uses ChatGPT to set up Canvas; very poor example set to JCOM majors.

Incredibly pretentious (only "Dr. D") and hostile (kindergarten-level classroom management). Just reads off the slides in lectures. Has no faith in, and constantly complains about, students in class. Frequently misses class without warning and leaves GEs underprepared. Clearly does not care about the class or her students.

I am not even halfway through this class, and this is honestly a warning. Half of our lectures have been taught by GE's and the environment in a 300 person lecture is hostile and honestly uncomfortable. If there is anyway to take this class at another time, or possibly with another professor, DO IT. I can not stress this enough. HEAVY on busy work.
I felt very disrespected in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Never in my nearly 4 years at UO have I ever been insulted when raising my hand and speaking in class, which this professor wants you to do. She constantly complains when people don't speak in class when she asks questions, and this is exactly why. While the content is interesting, she created an extremely hostile class environment.

her lectures are unbelievably boring because all she does is read bullet points from her slides. so much busy work and random stuff that does nothing to help you learn, and her tests are very hard for no reason. this is the first proffesor ive had that makes it seem like she WANTS to fail you. stay away if you can... dont say i didnt warn you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can't recommend taking a class with Dr. Chatman enough. This class was engaging and intentional. I would say it is incredibly clear that she genuinely cares about her students' success, and she is more than willing to help students who make the effort to reach out. It is rare to find a professor who is this passionate about her work.

I hope you understand every 5/5 rating was written by chatman or her GE. She is a horrible teacher. Grading is always late, and I mean always. Wan't us to call her Dr or Professor and demands respect yet doesnt respect her students. I once got called out for getting up to go to the bathroom, I was completely appalled. Very rude teacher, poor grader

I could put money on this class that every assignment was graded late. You aren't allowed to speak about your grades over email because of a law called FERPA. Why does every other teacher I've ever had allow you to speak over email. If you aren't doing it Chatman's way, you are wrong. Office hours are during the worst times so good luck.
This class is absolutely horrible, and if you don't need to take it, I would stay away. Chatman and her GEs constantly fail to grade on time.

Professor Chatman does not play around or tolerate much. She stops class at the slightest interruption, even students who quietly leave to go to the bathroom aren't safe. Assignments we submitted in week 2 weren't graded until week 5. She does have her good moments, and when she's in a good mood class discussions can be fun.

Dr. D will stop her lecture to call our students who get up to leave early, are talking, or go to the bathroom. The content is interesting, if you bother to have the slides up on your own device, because she speaks fast and does not often wait for students to finish notes on slides. Currently week 6, and we have gotten one assignment graded.

She is a good professor. She demands respect, which she deserves! 
However, she calls people out in large lecture halls for using the restroom, which can feel like wasting class time
Often has tech issues
Often doesn't get things graded by the time she says she will
strict no late work policy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The content was somewhat interesting, but she is a nitpicking, tough grader and needlessly complains about students not participating (in a large lecture environment). Her syllabus outlines the reasons and exact time frame you're allowed to email her, and when she asks for feedback from students she gets very defensive over her teaching style.

She would be a great high school teacher, cares about attendance which is normal but she cares about being late... and will mark you down by 20% for the day if you are late, which I haven't had my entire time in college. Her lectures are boring and she doesn't engage well with the class or encourage discussion, then gets mad when nobody talks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Chatman is extremely rude and condescending towards her students and creates an environment that discourages asking questions and seeking help. She treats us like 5 year olds and will stop her lecture to single students out for phone usage in a class of over 300 people. Her lectures are very mundane and unnecessarily long. Avoid at all costs.

She is the worst professor I have had at the University of Oregon. She always complains about class participation and how the student's work is never good enough. I highly recommend that you take the same course without her teaching. I would never take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While I'm grateful that white SoCal boys are required to take this class, I still believe 85% of the content was completely redundant. She acts like students are privileged to be in her presence but takes every chance to degrade the room because nobody wants to raise their hand to chat. The content is not difficult, but lectures are excruciating.

JCOM301.

- She opens class saying "good afternoon" and expects you to repeat it back like you're in elementary school. She demands to be called "Doctor." Hmm.
- Low-energy lectures. 
- Quizzes aren't about understanding concepts but instead rote memorization. More like trivia.

She's probably a great academic, but she's not a good teacher.

Avoid.

If you can take this course with a different professor, I recommend you do so. Dr Chatman is arrogant and clearly believes her opinion is the best. I firmly believe that your professors should be there to help you, but she did the opposite. I felt stupid whenever I asked for clarification, and you should NEVER feel that way as a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. For this being a 4 credit class, there was an insurmountable amount of work, and the clarification for these assignments was severely lacking, Dr Chatman is extremely arrogant and condescending in her teaching, especially when I needed clarification on assignments. I hated this course.

I took JCOM 301(Gender Media & Diversity. Extremely bias in her opinions and includes her bias all over the class teachings. Nothing is open to discussion unless you align with her views and beliefs. She said in a class lecture “I am an open feminist” and if that wasn't enough she shoves feminist ideology all over her conversations. Stay away.

She's ok I guess like the class is boring but I don't know a gen ED in the sojc that isn't. BUT she is having class with required attendance before Thanksgiving, and I feel like that is just wrong! It's a 4pm class. Like offer a video lecture with quiz to show participation. If she can miss for a doctor's appt allow students to go home!!!
Too much for for one class. Unreasonable amount of homewor every day. Would not take again because of how she interacts with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is so strict about formatting and requirements, yet provides the most unclear directions for each assignment. You WILL miss assignments because she doesn't put them on Canvas and hides them in the daily modules. You will also have to complete a 25 page research proposal for your final. Prepare to drown in homework and miss assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I believe that the entire course, as currently structured, could be covered in four classes. This class is a serious waste of time and resources. The teacher is constantly disrespectful in class. She uses each lesson she teaches to say that the underlying cause of all discrimination is ultimately the fault of straight and white people.

Grading feedback is so painfully, crystal clear. Final paper is a summary of relevant & interesting content. Readings are easy. Lectures are toned based off the sensitivity of the material & never boring if you have any social awareness. Dr. Chatman is witty and engaging. She only requests respect and basic reading comprehension.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class itself wasn't bad, she just has very strict on formatting and how she likes citations done. She is definitely a tough grader, but also had a good sense of humor throughout lectures. I think I would take a class with her again now that I know how she grades, but definitely tougher than expected.

she's got an insane superiority complex and yells at the class for being bored during her lecture. then don't be so monotone!! she makes no effort to engage the class or make the content interesting. your main paper will be 7-9 pages and the requirements are SUPER unclear. awful lecturer, you will fall asleep then she'll call you out.

People complain Chatman is strict and stubborn. All she asks for is respect. Readings are super short and easy. She's picky about Zoom attendance and email formatting because she's received threats and offensive messages from students. She formats the class for discussion so ofc she'll get upset if nobody participates. Respect her and you'll pass.

Dayna Chatman is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. She has such a superiority complex and is extremely judgmental. There are so many rules about everything from formatting emails to how we format homework. Her lectures are super long and boring, avoid her if you can.
