This course had a lot of potential. Dr. Chatman is one of the most stubborn and unforgiving professors I have ever had. She is very specific about most things in her class such as how you use zoom, how you email, how you format discussion posts, etc. It is a bit overkill. Chatman is very harsh and does not like a lack of lecture participation.

I took Dr. Chatman during fall term and at first I was nervous about her class, as she said that it would be difficult and that she could academically challenge us. But to be honest it was very easy, as long as you participate in class and show you want to be there she will be there to help you with what ever you need.

She assigns lots of readings and discussions. Expects a lot of participation in answering questions in class and gets easily annoyed when no one raises their hand. Picky about turned in work. Mandatory attendance with an iClicker AND a code at the end of class, and complains a lot about people leaving early or being late.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: My first time attending Office Hours with Professor Chatman, she nearly had me in tears.After she cut me off mid-sentence, raised her voice, and told me I was confused (without providing an explanation), I was extremely upset. The grading is fair. She assumes everyone who doesn't grasp a concept is unengaged and unmotivated.
It is unfortunate because there was so much potential with this course but there was too much busy work for me to justify it as an elective choice. Wouldn't recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was very insightful. Dayna seems very standoffish but she is very helpful with questions, comment and concerns. The grading was a bit tough but it was her GE's that did the most of it. Some of the stuff she lectured on was rather interesting. Overall she was okay, don't let her resting face scare you away she's nice.

I took this 320 class for my winter term in my sophomore year. I truly have no clue why Chatman is rated so low, the lectures are always engaging, amazing, funny, and very thoughtful. I never truly thought I would enjoy a lecture more than this class. Unfortunately, attendance is required. But overall a very fun class.

(J314 Intro to Media studies)
This course was a lot more difficult that I expected, Dr.Chatman requires a ton of participation every class based on the readings. There were so many readings each class (3-4) that were pretty long and challenging and if you didn't read you wouldn't be able to follow lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Course was J314
If I had to guess, I would say Chatman crafted a curriculum, realized it was too easy, then made it a scavenger hunt to be able get anything done to compensate for a lack of difficulty.
But I don't have to guess.
It's obvious she just doesn't know what she's doing. No responses to emails. Feedback is abysmal. Save yourself and don't
I'm a very understanding and forgiving person but she is the worst professor I've had at the University of Oregon.

Prof. Chatman is not a very thoughtful professor. I wanted to like her, but every time I didn't treat her class as the #1 priority in my entire life, I paid for it in my grade and the way I was treated. It's ridiculous to expect so much from students in a class that is basically an elective. That being said the class was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Chatman lacks serious empathy for her students. She is one of the only professors I would recommend never taking a course with. Expect to not a receive any A's as she grades extremely tough. Many bad things I could say about her skills as a professor, not many good ones.
Easy class and the professor was very clear and inviting in touching the different perspectives of the course. Midterm and finals were all based on the lecture slides & questions from the quizzes.

Professor Chatman seemed to have good intentions with her lectures but didnt treat the students the way she treated the books. She always got angry at students for small things and took it out on everyone by grading extremely difficult. She requires a lot out of everyone. Also she wont email you back if you dont have proper email etiquette.

Dayna teaches this class as though she is the arbiter of truth regarding race, gender and media. The concepts she teaches are overly complicated, and if you do not follow her strict guidelines regarding the required essays, you will fail. This class is going to result in 40 hours of my life I will never get back, I am appalled this is required
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dayna Chatman clearly has a vast knowledge on gender media and diversity, but her knowledge in this field is made up for by her lack of knowledge on students and teaching. Lectures were long a aimless, the material was presented sloppily, and overall she displayed a lack of professionalism. I gained much less from this class than I was hoping.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Cheney is really well versed in the subject of Ethnic Studies, and is clearly a scholar in the field, but I think this perspective limits her understanding of her students. Her assignments and tests are spectacularly hard to understand becase of the intensely academic language she uses. It is really hard to know what answer she wants.

Professor Cheney is SO OBVIOUSLY passionate in her teaching of Black studies, and GE Taylor is AWESOME! I never want to miss her class in the morning. Her authenticity is really admirable. If you're interested in Black studies, she is the BEST teacher to learn from. Don't be afraid to approach the GE in class to ask questions!!
fine but very hard tests
Not a fan of Professor Cheney. Lectures were disorganized with no real structure. She's not very responsive to emails and provides unhelpful feedback.

Dr. Cheney is a beautiful person and an amazing professor. She was really there for me when I was drowning in school work, and gave me the benefit of the doubt. She is funny and an excellent lecturer. Highly highly recommend.

Hit or miss class, depending on your GE. Prof Cheney is funny, really cares about the subject and her lectures are interesting but they are not mandatory. Discussion groups are led by GEs, and it is really hit or miss regarding how easy the class will be. There are about 3 assignments that weigh your entire grade, and so it all depends on your GE.

Dr.Cheney was great!! I found her lectures engaging, informative, and fun. The only thing that sucked is that the only time you really interact with her is during lecture, and the rest is all up to the GEs. BUT if you get a chill GE (shoutout to Alexander he's the best), her class is super fun and easy.

The professor herself is wonderful. Very charismatic, she visibly knows what she's talking about and is passionate about ethnic studies. She is engaging, talks to students during her lecture, and asks questions. The GEs grade all assignments, so it's hit or miss whether you get a tough grader or not, but overall I loved the class and learned a lot.

Her lectures that were uploaded online weren't even for the right class and for weeks 3 and 4 of an online course she didn't put up any lecture and had questions specifically about a lecture we had no access to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very average professor, lectures were often all over the map. I know this is an ethnic studies class, but she would sometimes get WAY too deep into the material. She leaves all grading to her GE's so interaction with her is next to non existent unless you go to office hours.

Professor is fine, she is very pationate about what she teaches but she isn't even the one who does the grading. The GE's that you are assigned to do all the grading so if you get a bad one you are out of luck because you are graded on 3 big papers throughout the term.

Dr. Cheney is very passionate about the subject and I love her personality. The class is rather boring, grades are only based on a quiz and three essays, and GEs don't know what they're doing. I stopped showing up to class after midterm 1 and still did good on the final essay so attendance is not required.

Content was interesting and she is cool. Only graded on the 2 exams and a big paper so that sucks. Received my first grade in week 10, had absolutely no idea where I stood until then. The class was in absolutely no way organized, by topic or by assignment clarity. Received assignments very close to when they were due w no guidance from GEs.

Lectures were great and super interesting, but Cheney is so disorganized and inconsistent. As much as I love the content of this course, I can't say I'd recommend her. There's only a midterm, paper, and final that are graded, but instructions are always so vague, and questions completely contradict lectures. Not worth the confusion. GEs rarely help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Cheney is nice in lecture, and the information is useful. Although she is really unreachable outside of class- only GEs answer questions which they dont 100% know the answer to. On the class side- you are graded by essays, which the prompts get released randomly and the due date is announced late. You really have to work to finish.
GE's are an absolute joke, Cheney is cool ig, all she does is read the slides. The discussion sections suck though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class in the Fall. Attendance is not mandatory but lectures will help with the tests and quizzes. GE's are extremely tough graders and do not care if you fail. Few assignments throughout the course but be prepared to write a lot. I think it was 2 essays and a bigger essay for the final. Final was a 6 page paper and was really difficult.

I thought this class was very easy. I took ES 101 and I sowed up to maybe 2 lectures the entire term. The only thing you need to go to is your once a week discussion period. The class is graded on either 3 or 4 essays and a couple discussion posts. Overall it was a light class and the discussions I went to were pretty interesting.

I took Cheneys class during Winter term, and immediatley loved her personality. I believe she is very passionate about what she teaches, with that said though, its a very difficult course for a 101 class and the readings are way too complex but necessary. Grading is strict, depending on GE, and there are only a couple of assignment your graded on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't usually enjoy lectures but I looked forward to her class. She is so engaging and finds ways to relate the information to current events. Tests are short essays but aren't too hard. Definitely recommend her class.

She makes lectures really interesting and funny. She posts all the lectures on Canvas so it is not necessary to come to class. The essays were easy to write and it also includes an interview which I enjoyed writing. Depends on your GE but I definitely recommend taking this class for easy credit.

Lectures were not mandatory but there were great discussions in class, we often would just watch movies and then talk about them. Only graded on 3 things and they are all essays (5 pages each) so if you are a bad writer maybe don't take, but overall I think that class was pretty easy and important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her ES101 class especially since she's really good at lecturing so it was easy to pay attention even with ADHD. I also had Tali Bitton as my GE who was amazing. He's funny and very supportive and willing to work with you. I talked to him about my midterm and got some really good criticism from him as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Content was complex and varied in how well she taught it. Some classes were just movies. Essays were the only grades and very little advice or help was given. I only passed bc I had a good GE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some lectures she was very engaged others she just put on a movie, class was only graded on three essays that ended up being graded late in the term so it was hard to know what your grade was going to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded on 3-4 things and there were three essays that made up a combined 85% of your grade. Lecture was painful to attend and oftentimes was just her putting on a movie. You could not attend one class and still do ok if you understand the readings. Dr. Cheney cares very little for her class and puts very little effort into class.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love the prof but the class itself was extremely difficult. Every week we have to turn in about 2 discussion posts and the readings for those posts were so hard to comprehend.

I love Professor Cheney, her lectures were very engaging, and she taught the class well. However, she graded on very few things, and there were a lot of tough readings all throughout the course. Midterm was very hard, and GE was little to no help throughout the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cheney is an amazing professor, with very informative and engaging lectures. I learned so much in this class, and I think it's super important and eye opening topic. Very few assignments for this class, and super interesting lectures.
Love her, one of the best teachers I've had. Super engaging, super caring and she has a clear passion for what she's educating us on.

Prof. Cheney genuinely changed my life with her class, giving me new and deeper understandings not only of the subject but new lenses to understand myself through. If you take any ES classes at UO, I highly recommend taking her class, and her recommendations for reading and listening outside of class are phenomenal.

She is extremely passionate and knowledgable about what she's teaching and does a great job of making everything interesting and worth reading/watching, projects/assignments were engaging and allowed for lots of creativity.

From the start, Dr. Cheney tells you she has taught this course for a long time. She really is passionate about what she teaches and is super funny! Attendance is technically mandatory, no one took attendance. Grading depends on the GE you're assigned to for discussion sections! Just do the reading and follow the grading criteria and you'll be okay
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this class. The topics were super interesting, and the discussions that came from them were great. There were three papers total and that made up most of our grade. The questions were easy to write about and there was a discussion post every week.

Dr. Cheney is one of the coolest professors I've met while at UO. Her lectures are funny and engaging. She is caring and compassionate. Her class is incredibly well organized and the assignments are fairly easy. I would definitely take a class with her again.
She is very passionate about the topics. She says "um" a lot and half the lecture is videos. Great lady though.

I enjoyed going to the lectures of ES 101 because they were always very entertaining, informative, and engaging. Dr. Cheney is very passionate about what she teaches. At the beginning of the class, she said she did not care to get to know the students. Additionally, we were only graded on three assignments which was frustrating.

Her lectures were always tied into modern day examples and she keeps lectures engaging, so it is easy to sit through. There was no personal interactions with her- all questions and grades are based on your GE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I'm convinced that sunshine is a person and she teaches Ethnic Studies at UO.

Wow, by far my favorite professor of all of my 4 years. Dr. Cheney is so funny and down-to-earth but also extremely smart and respected. ES 310 was an amazing class, the knowledge you gain about ethnic studies is vast but also the lectures are very on-par with current events and trends (we watched City Girls music videos) take this class!

Dr. Cheney is an intelligent and insightful professor. Provides an eye opening intersectional perspective. She does use videos frequently, which in my opinion helped me understand some concepts more thoroughly than I would with a lecture. I respect her very much and you'd be missing out if you didn't take a class with her!
She gives engaging and funny lectures, but they can also be pretty biased to her personal opinions. The exams all have the option to be take home.

She seems like a cool person & probably is a good professor, but I think (as someone else mentioned) she's tired of teaching ES 101 because she showed a lot of videos, the content was mediocre, and she didn't seem interested in what she was saying.. Very disorganized and not responsive to emails. She's funny though. Grading 100% depends on your GE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a good person, but as a professor she is inconsistent. One day she is invested in the class and teaches it well, the next day she is disconnected and just shows a film. Seems like she's taught the class so many times that she is over it. Theres a lot of potential for her to make her classes great, the course content is very interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is a great Professor, your grades depend heavily on your GE. She uses documentaries and videos EXTREMELY often, take notes! You'll need them for the papers! You need to do a lot of reading, but I suggest waiting to do them until the exams (which are a few days in length) so you only have to read what you need. Take the written exams!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Cheney is a great choice for this class. She makes her lectures interesting and engages students. She usually makes sure the class understands what she's talking about. There are a lot of readings but you don't really have to read them all. If you do the take home midterm and final and only read those articles you'll be good.

The class was extremely eye opening. Dr. Cheney made all of the lectures very captivating and intriguing. Everything we learned was very relevant to today's society. I apply what Ive learned from this class to my life on a daily basis.
VERY FUNNY AND PASSIONATE, MAKES LECTURES INTERESTING

Cheney is a really solid choice for Ethnic Studies classes. She really relates to students and presents information in a way that makes it easier to learn and absorb the information being taught. Not to mention she is just a really cool person in general.
Really passionate
Very fun and inspiring woman. Sometimes does not give much information about what is expected, but GTF's can help

Slides hadn't been updated in years. Some of the dates on the slides and syllabus were from a couple of years back. We were supposed to have a few guest speakers and she couldn't manage to get a single one there. She kept "forgetting." Very unorganized. Passionate and engaging, but lacked essentials to make it a great class.

Professor Cheney is very passionate when she teaches, something that I could not get enough of. She brings up very uncomfortable topics and tackles them with you. Controversy in her class is normal and healthy, it helps you learn and be opinionated. Cheney is not bound by society's "touchy" race discussions. Be prepared for her to challenge you :)

At first I was unsure about Prof Cheney but actually ended up loving her! She is hilarious and her lectures are riveting. Definitely recommend taking this class with her. Be prepared to read and study for exams if you want a decent grade.

Professor Cheney very knowledgeable and funny (pop culture references, anecdotes). She assigns great readings. I wish she wouldn't pause for students to copy the lecture slides- they're posted online!  It really slows down the class. Otherwise, I enjoyed lectures a great deal. If you do the readings, the exams and the essay are aaa piece of cake.

Lecture is formatted in a way that pits the concepts of whiteness vs blackness.  Instead of delving into all ethnic backgrounds, Dr. Cheney focuses primarily on her own.  She also transitions into every new idea with "SooOoooOo..." which can be irritating a couple dozen times per lecture.  Excessively reads from powerpoint. Moderate amount of work.

Dr. Cheney is very knowledgeable in her subject and is very intelligent. However, she does just teach from powerpoints which can create a lull, but is extremely helpful if you miss class. She is very opinionated but encourages you to challenge her if you disagree. She's so cool!
Professor Cheney was amazing, she kept the class engaged and really knew her stuff. I am hoping I will be able to take another class from her!

Critical Race Theory from a person like Dr. Cheney teaches  the implications of race in all facets of society. Being white isn't an identity, rather a means towards political power and upward mobility. Cheney characterizes the political, economic, and social ramifications of whiteness in U.S. society.

Not sure who she thinks she is, but after two classes with her I can already say I am not a fan. Her attitude is very poor, how she communicates with her students screams "I am the professor, I am better than you and am always correct". And please, we are not in high school, actually teach us something instead of reading from a stupid powerpoint.

A professor the first day shouldn't open up by telling the students she doesn't care about the subject she's teaching. Cheney teaches from her Powerpoints, and waits while students take notes without lecturing. It creates lulls in the class. She has issues with clarity as multiple students (self included) weren't sure what she expected from us.

Took it for an Arts and Letters class and it required more work than all of my other classes combined this term. Class is bassically entirely memorization of the art work identifactions. You have to memorize 100 works by there date artist style and time period for the final. Genuinely the most memorization heavy class ever, do not take for a&l cred
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Cheng's oasis of art history knowledge runs almost as deep as her pretentiousness.A tough grader who led me to a deeper love for Surrealism I will carry through my life. However, she sits on a throne of unhelpful office hours that will cut students at the knees for misunderstanding a subject new to them.A gifted scholar, not so much a teacher.

For an art class, she makes this class so rough due to grading and tests. The grading is done as if you are trying to publish a book; the smallest things dock you off points for absolute no reason. In addition the memorization level is a joke for what goes on. Do not recommend at all. Find another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Joyce is probably my favorite professor ever. I've taken three classes with her and they are the most in-depth, well organized, interesting courses I've ever taken. They are very mentally stimulating and challenging, but if you are willing to invest the time the course deserves your understanding of the intricacies of the art world will explode.

This course is memorization-heavy but you won't be quizzed on everything. For example, the final required us to know 80 works but we were tested on 10. There is a weekly assignment which can be either writing or a quiz. There are two essays which are graded fairly harshly, as are the writing assignments, so be prepared to put in the work.

Really knowledgeable and a great resource. Assigned readings were difficult but were all relevant and helped in understanding the course. 
There are a lot of readings, but this class really helped me understand the concept and how it related to the field of art as a whole. Discussions were productive and feedback was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very harsh grader even if you understand the content if you can't memorize things or are a bad quiz taker, you won't get a good grade. The course policy claims "grades aren't everything" and calls students who care about grades "grade grubbers", but the class also grades extremely harshly and leaves no room for error or improvement.

joyce is very passionate and knowledgable about what she teaches which makes lectures interesting. not only was attendance required, but so was participation (both part ur grade). shes a tough grader because she wants you to show that you have actually learned something and are not just regurgitating information. this class made me a better student

I received an A in both Western history classes leading up to this so I thought I was ready. This teacher is hard. Review your work and when you think you have it, go back and review your work. She is knowledgeable and her TA's are great I had Emily who made the class better. So don't slack and get ready to learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have to commend Professor Cheng and her knowledge on this particular area of art history, but I cannot emphasize enough how difficult this class was. This is the only class I've taken that has pushed me to the point of rethinking my major. I felt out of place at times and trying to understand some of the material made me want to cry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course material in Cheng's courses can be extremely challenging at times, but it is rewarding if you take advantage of participating in class and meeting with her outside of class. The curation of readings is extremely interesting and Cheng always presents students with various opinions on the course matter, promoting critical thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've had to take at UO and its an intro level art course. She displays a pretenious attitude and had us memorize over 100 pieces of art only to test us on 4 of them. It was an outlandish and inefficient style of grading. Would not reccomend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazingly challenging class. This is an instructor that teaches you to think instead of memorise and regurgitate information.

It is clear that Professor Cheng knows what she's talking about and is very educated in regards to art history. I didn't necessarily I have an issue with the way she taught, although the test format seemed absolutely ridiculous to me. To memorize over 100 works of art for the final to only test our knowledge of four of them seemed bizarre to me.

Professor Cheng is incredibly entertaining during her lectures and strives to make recordings of her lectures available to students who have missed class. Many people dislike this class because they misunderstand the subject ART HISTORY IS ALL MEMORIZATION, NOT ACTUAL ART.

When I first had Joyce Chang as a professor I loved her and her classes. That quickly changed when I decided to take her as a professor again but for an upper division class. I approached her during office hours and she assumed that Spanish was my first language because I was having troubles understanding the complex readings.
Has an elitist attitdue and is a textbook narcissist
Bad, insane workload.

Professor Cheng is the worst teacher I have ever had. I would not recommend this class to ANYONE even if they have a deep love for the arts. I was excited at first to take this class but as I got involved I realized that it was just ALL memorization. I have spent a ridiculous amount of hours just sitting down and memorizing pointless amounts of art

Although she may seem like a tough professor, her lectures are engaging and interesting. You can tell that she is interested in her field and knows what she is talking about. If you are truly interested in this class she will commend that. A "tough love" for your own good, kind of professor.

Professor Cheng is tough but fair. Her courses on 20th century art forced me to push myself to understand philosophy and theory that I had not considered before. She has high expectations for her students, but she provides meaning feedback during seminars and office hours as well as extra credit for those that improve throughout the course.

No organization in her lectures. She just talks about the paintings up on the slideshow. She bounces back and forth between the slides for that day and maybe a painting she wasn't planning on showing till next week. If you go to her with a private concern, she will say something about it to the whole class. Don't be late to class, she hates it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I genuinely respect and admire Professor Cheng. She is intelligent and passionate about what she does. She gets enthusiastic and excited during lectures. That being said, her demeanor can be very off-putting to students. She is intimidating and harsh. If you choose to take her class, do not let pride run your emotions or you will get burnt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very hard to please. Gave harsh criticism about my writing and would never say what I did well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I missed one day she took attendance (takes unfair random attendance) and now my attendance grade is at an 80%. Was dramatic as well and not in a good way. Just don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is interesting, but not the easiest. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend attending because it will be difficult to pass quizzes and tests without lecture information. A lot of memorization is required for weekly quizzes and the two midterms plus final. Also, a lot of readings! 2 essays are required and are graded fairly hard by GEs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is heavily focused around spending countless hours trying to memorize long titles with respect to complicated names and specific dates. On top of this, she might be the most boring lecturer I've ever had. Classes aren't too long but really hard to get through unless you're excessively interested in very strange art. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Be prepared to work extremely hard. Lots of material to memorize but if you actually try you'll pass. Her personality is outrageously rude and has a elitist attitude. Calls out students for mediocre at best things just to prove superiority. Uncaring and not willing to work with you. Had a doctors note on a test and still failed me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cheng is very well-educated/passionate and it really comes through in her lectures. She is a tough grader and expects you to memorize A LOT of material, however the memorization is not as difficult as it may seem. I attended her lectures twice and received a B in the class. I personally liked the class, but be prepared to memorize a lot...
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking this course. She wastes class time by calling people out when they are only a minute or two late. I found her to be pretentious and not very approachable if you need an extension or if you have a question.
Avoid at all cost.

She was entirely rude and unwilling to help when I was taking care of my girlfriend in ICU and wouldn't budge. She then called out my exact situation in class on a day I was absent. Upon hearing this i approached her very sternly and she apologized and allowed me more time. I hated her. That said she knows what shes teachin & you will learn a lot.
Good Professor, smart and excited about the material. I would take another class with her.

Very intelligent and knowledgeable.  Excellent teacher who challenges students and treats them as capable of understanding complex but very deep and important conceptual information.  Is very willing to help if necessary.  Expectations are generally reasonable but they are very strict.

Never boring, always informative, great feedback, AND she allows room for creative thinking in essays. The seminar on Surrealism was one of the most useful courses that I took at UO. I learned more than I thought possible.
Awful Professor. Horribly pretentious and arrogant. Watch out for unclear assignments.  She's unforgiving and grades on a whim.  Avoid at all costs.

Professor Cheng is crazy smart and her lectures are always engaging and interesting. She doesn't have too much reading and her tests were not impossible. Sometimes she isn't very clear in outlining tests or assignments--so ask, twice.

Professor Cheng's courses are certainly not for the faint of heart. She is reasonably strict to form and expects her students to actually learn the material that she is teaching. With that said, she is also passionate, eloquent, hyper-intelligent and extremely lovely. So, if you are seeking  a genuine education and are willing to put in the work...
lots of useless information, over the top tests (unfair questions). She has no understanding of how to teach and it is VERY apparent. Avoid at all costs. i wish i had.

Don't take this class expecting it to be easy because of the subject matter, especially with Prof. Karns. You are graded by three heavy tests, combined with iClicker participation and weekly quizzes. Wouldn't recommend this unless you're a psych major, since she kind of just assumes everyone knows all the parts of the brain already.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Both exams had a C average with no curve because "that's right where we should be." Overall, I enjoyed this course. Great professor.

I loved Karns lectures. Her GE's are tough graders but the content of her class and the work we do outside of it is SO worth the effort. I learned so much in this class, and Karns is very easy to get in contact with and answering any questions you have. Some of her other classes can be difficult but the attendence is worth the content of her class

Karns is a good prof but idk I didn't enjoy this class as much as I thought I would. She makes class interesting but the paper we had to write felt pointless. We had to use AI which was odd. She made us write 1 page peer reviews but we weren't able to go back in and revise our own papers using the peer reviews. That felt weird as well.

One of my favorite professors. As long as you stay on top of assignments and lectures you will get an A. One midterm and a final and both are multiple choice and not super difficult. Lectures are entertaining and assignments are relevant to the course.

Dr. Karns (prison mike) is intellectual; she puts care into her teaching. 
She has the moral spine of a jellyfish. Went out of her way to ensure that we use AI on papers when its unnecessary and unrelated to the topic. She presents herself as understanding, but if you're struggling or have a different opinion from her, do not expect a fair grade.

Dr. Karns is extremely compassionate and caring. You can tell she has a passion for teaching and helping her students grow not only academically, but personally. Her classes are not easy As but effort does not go unnoticed. She implements her background in neuroscience and applies teaching methods that really work. awesome lady

What makes her class bad is that her communication isn't clear which results in unclear expectations, and she's usually stressed out and disorganized which makes her hard to be around. She is a nice person and I'd take her again, but she's definitely not my first pick. I took her for 410, but there wasn't a 410 option.

I love Dr Karns as a person but her class is extremely hard. I am currently SCRAPING by with an A and am extremely nervous for our final exam. The term project guidelines are super vague and is weighted very heavily on your grade. Midterm was really hard and she said she was being considerate by making it "easy." Pray for me for our final exam.

this class should not be considered a psych class. all we talk about is music theory and physics. so so much work outside of class we have to watch pre recorded lectures in addition to in person lectures. term project and an in person cumulative midterm and final. average on the midterm was a 65 when she said it would be "super easy".

Dr. Karns is a nice person, but I didn't like this class modality. Even though it is an in-person class, the majority of actual lecture content was in videos that we watch outside of class, which she recorded during COVID. Actual lectures are more discussion-style, which doesn't work well with a big class. I often had more questions than answers.

Dr. Karns is a sweet person but I wouldn't recommend taking the HC 241 Neuroscience and Drug Policy class with her. Despite doing all assignments on time and adhering to rubric she gave me low scores without specific feedback.

I took the HC 241, and although the content was interesting and the discussions were engaging, the grading felt arbitrary at times and wasn't clearly aligned with expectations. Dr. Karns isn't a bad person but the lack of follow-through on basic academic support was really disappointing. Other honors students may find this class quite frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Slow to grade and didn't give clear feedback... was also rather condescending when people would ask questions in class. Would recommend looking for a different psych teacher.

Sweet professor, but feedback was unclear and often did not correlate with grade given. Also had very confusing rubrics and required a ton of reading, much of which never served any purpose for the class. Not a terrible professor but I would not take again.

Dr. Karns's lectures were engaging and entertaining! She is very understanding and will make sure that you get the best grade possible. The only problem I have is that there was one paper for this class that the GEs graded but gave no feedback on. Other than that, this class was a pleasure to take.
Great class and professor. Dr. Karns is thoughtful and makes the lectures interesting.

Karns was very enthusiastic and funny. Went into class thinking class was going to be super super hard but the content of the class is super interesting. She kind of jumps around during lectures so just take good notes about each specific drug. 3 tests(this was much easier than 2) and 1 essay (2 pages, 2 peer reviews, 3 pages really easy actually).

Dr. Karns is super nice. My gripe with this class is that attendance AND tons of reading from the textbook are mandatory. I understand the emphasis on the book if you didn't have to come to lecture, but both are required which makes the hours per week for this class a lot. The actual assignments are fine but textbook is $ and needed for tests.

Spare yourself and stay away from Dr Karns, she seems nice at first, but goes through the slides ridiculously fast and explains them loosely. She never uploads the slides on time, makes you purchase a $200 dollar textbook, but uses Acadly instead of iclickers to claim to be a teacher who cares about your financial wellbeing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't matter how much your read the rubric it's all confusing. Your best bet is to read the article and agree to the things she wants you to agree with. It's the most I have ever spent on any subject and it's still all confusing. It's not like I needed this class for my degree, I took it as an elective. She's sweet and nice. Grading is weird.

GE's grade EVERYTHING and give ZERO feedback. Super frustrating. I checked the outline and rubric multiple times before submitting a paper and got a B after spending literally hours on it. If you really try, you can do well. Otherwise, she's super sweet and tries to be engaging, but it's just really bland and boring content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Karns was very nice and caring! She did her best to make lectures fun and entertaining. Classes did have participation questions that could be made up online if needed. Weekly HomeWorks as well. PSY 301 however was quite boring to me but that was not her fault instead just the content in general. Overall great Prof!

She's a good college professor. Not easy, not unbearable. Engaging lectures - she wants us to understand concepts. HW are quizzes, 2 essays, 3 exams, graded on attendance. The GEs grade papers and give NO feedback. Exams really test you (not just multiple choice). Do the reading. You can definitely work for an A in this class if you try. Worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved psych 301 with Dr. Karns! She is so passionate and knowledgeable about psychology. Tries her best to make lectures easy and engaging. Tests, essays and homework are based on lecture material and easy if you attend class and take notes. Gave me an extension when I really needed it. Responds to emails fast, so friendly and helpful.

Karns was really sweet and you can tell that she likes what she teaches, but she was SO CONFUSING! This was taken during Fall 2020 so it was a remote class due to COVID which may have been the problem, but the Canvas class was really confusing and her syllabus was confusing on when stuff was due. She also didn't really go into detail in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved this class with Dr. Karns, but I will say her style was a bit confusing. I took it during COVID, and the first couple weeks were really difficult finding out what was supposed to be due. However, it was a fun and informative class, with weekly quizzes, discussion, and class. Two big exams and one final project. Difficult material yet fun

Prof Karns is so real! She really cares about her students, as well as the subjects she teaches. I took her class on Music and the Brain (PSY348) & she has been one of my favorite instructors so far (i'm a third year). The course was definitely challenging, but she provides a lot of inclusive, fun and engaging learning activities & environments.

Fantastic! She was the best lecturer I have had in college. Grading criteria is very clear and she does a fantastic job at answering all questions. Exams are straightforward and the textbooks are cheap and actually interesting to read. She's funny and I would totally recommend her class.

She really likes interacting with students during class. She really values participation and gives extra points if you get the iClicker questions correct (+1 for answering, +1 for correct, 0 for no answer)! The first midterm was only 10% of our grade to let us get a feel for her tests without panicking. Super fun and friendly.

Psy301 is a hard class and the material can be heavy at times but she did her best to make it engaging. There were 2 papers which were fairly difficult but were graded pretty easy. Attendance through iclicker. Dr. Karns is a fun lady and always was happy to answer questions or reexplain concepts. Clearly very smart and good at what she does.

With 10 weeks of class, there is A LOT of material to cover, and that makes the cumulative final heavy, but Prof. Karns is a great lecturer and she's good at making the materials easy to follow. Would recommend her! It's not an easy A, with quizzes, mandatory attendance, a term paper, midterm, cumulative final and homeworks, but you'll learn a lot!

Prof Karns is great. She teaches with a lot of enthusiasm and care. The final is cumulative. the study guides for midterm and final wasn't helpful, so i studies without one and still managed to get an A. The class content is actually interesting. she takes time to answer questions as well. Effort is needed to get an A (as with any other class)

I loved Karns! The class was super interesting and you could tell she was super passionate about the topic. I was constantly engaged during her lectures, but you'll still want to skim through the textbook in order to cover the topics she doesn't go over. She once scared me by throwing an iClicker at my feet as a vocab example for the class haha!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Okay this class had a lot of material and was difficult but Christina is a great teacher. She is there for her students and helped me a lot since I had never taken a psychology class before. She taught the material well and the readings were mandatory. There's a big term paper and the final was 35% and cumulative so it wasn't easy but interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a lot of science in this class. But it makes me want to know more. This professor is pretty interesting. I actually want to go to class.

I have a hard time imagining that she would refuse to clarify a test question. She is always super responsive. I'm learning so much in this class. Since when is it bad to admit when a test question isn't great? I'm learning a lot and her teaching style makes a lot of interesting connections to other parts of life.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While the class material was very interesting and fun I found Karns to be a mediocre teacher. Primarily, she is not good at writing succinct questions and her expectations are not very clear. She even said to me once, "Yeah, this is a terribly written question" and then refused to clarify what she meant by the question - and it was on the final!

Dr Karns is an extremely good teacher, show up to class because there are clicker questions that really help with studying for the online quizzes. There is one paper and you can work in a group or by yourself, so it's nice that there was an option. Overall, read the textbook and you'll be good for the class, which is a really awesome class too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seriously one of the best classes I've taken. It links information from different areas like history, biology, culture, and the law and makes me see things differently. She cares about social equality. I thought lectures were great and the readings weren't too tough. Midterm and final together are 65% of grade, but the other points are easy.

She is great and super interesting! She also is very open minded. Her tests are tough and she doesn't provide study guides. But if you make flash cards on your own, you will be fine! Attendance is pretty mandatory considering she gives graded iClicker questions

Overall an interesting class. Does assign a 7-10 page paper, and the majority of your grade is based off of the midterm and final. Exams are pretty hard and you need to study quite a bit. Lectures are pretty engaging, as far as lectures go. She is funny and answers emails back very quickly.

Nice, funny, and interesting. Makes tough stuff more fun to learn with clear examples, videos, discussions. She sets a high standard for herself and the class. You will learn a lot, especially if you keep up outside of class.
One of the best profs I've had. Very enthusiastic. Uses a lot of examples. Funny! Knows her stuff. I always found myself looking forward to class.

Easily the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are boring, and her blackboard site is impossible to navigate. The final was 40% of our grade and was nothing like the midterm and asked very in depth which made it very difficult. All i had heard was this was an easy and FUN class to take, but she made it a very unpleasant class to take.

This class was required for my major and it's honestly the worst I've taken at UO. The content is interesting and the professor is clearly passionate, but the course is completely disorganized. The slides make no sense, he jumps around constantly, and half the class is always lost. He's a good person, but the curriculum seriously needs to change.

he seems to care a lot about art history, but not so much about the successful retention of information from his students. i did not resonate with his teaching style at all, and i only did good because of extensive outside research.

great guy outside of academics but he grades so harshly for no reason. I hate art history but I had to take this class but I tried so hard in it and still ended with a shit grade. he doesn't give good feedback either and honestly would never wanna take a class with him again

Boring and very strict to the syllabus. I understand it is no longer covid times with relaxed late and absence policies but come on you're not a robot Simone! What differs us humans as teachers from AI teaching courses, compassion an understanding. It doesn't hurt you to understand, you get paid either way.

Ciglia is a caring and empathetic human being who loves interacting with students. Unfortunately, his lectures are all over the place. He has poorly formatted power point presentations that he barely references as he lectures. His teaching style did not work for me. As a result, the class did not feel worth my time and I dreaded it every week.

The most boring class I've ever taken. The professor's monotone voice is enough to put you to sleep, and his slides consist of black font on a white background, with minimal pictures. Many of my peers have admitted that they couldn't keep their attention on the lecture. My 2-hour coding class is more engaging than this class. I do NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much potential for an interesting course but no one wants to engage when they are sleeping in the mandatory lecture!

Overall he was a good professor and made the content interesting. The midterm and final projects follow the same format and they aren't too bad so long as you carefully read the instructions. The GEs always gave good feedback on discussion posts and the course was very organized. I rarely had to do the readings because I took notes in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, sad man who wants students to fail if they aren't tuned in 100% to his boring class. It wouldn't be too difficult if he made it interesting, it is a super interesting topic..... Wouldn't recommend if you enjoy engaging classes with human professors. I'm sure he's a nice guy in real life but idk I'll be steering clear of this guy.

Boring lectures, taking a physics class that I like better because the lectures are less boring. This class makes me sleepy and it's difficult taking notes when he jumps around so fast. I think it's an interesting course and he seems like an intelligent guy, but wow this is my second class of his and his lecture style is definitely not for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: honestly a boring class but SOOO easy, he offers so much extra credit and is really nice

I loved learning about the history of design with Simone. The grading by the GEs was pretty hard, and to succeed in the class, you must dedicate a lot of time to reading and note-taking. There is also a huge memorization factor to the class. But other than that, it was a super interesting class, and I loved the lectures.

I took History of Photography (ARH 359) as a freshman this year. I was impressed by the dedication Professor Ciglia put to art history and would recommend everyone should take this course while at UO. His lectures are very content heavy but there isn't much class work assigned. Overall, I would take this class again!!!

Professor Ciglia is great. ARH 440 was a museology class, and our time involved several visits to the campus museums+opportunity to talk to people in various positions/get a behind the scenes look while it was closed to the public. His lectures are readings regurgitations, but the quizzes are easy & assignments are interesting if you like subject.

Ciglia has such an odd teaching style and all of his lectures are straight from the textbook. Lectures are entirely discussion based with no real point in even going as you'll just end up having to read the textbook to retake notes as he moves so fast. Tests are somewhat difficult as they don't have a consistent style. Midterm and final was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
ACTUALLY TOOK 359!
Unfortunately, this class was not enjoyable. Just lots of reading and lectures were basically repeats of the reading. The only interesting thing was the one time someone visited and showed us old photos. Quizzes and essays were easy as long as you read some of the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Teaching style is unusual, based heavily on the book readings for each week but are made whole with the lectures. The midterm/final is formatted in 4 questions, 1.5 pages for each response. Compared to other Art History Professors, he's very understanding. Talk to him + go to office hours. Set aside 4 hours a week outside of class for studying/hmw.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The midterm and final exams were not that hard, just time-consuming since there were 3/4 prompts that were 300-400 words each. Also, there's a lot of reading, but my advice would be to skim, see which photographers Ciglia put on his slides, and then write about those photographers who seem the most interesting and refer back to the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: About one fourth way into the class I stopped going to class because of how poorly he structured them. He read only the quotes which were already in the readings and never elaborated or described why they were important. The bi-weekly discussions are really repetitive and hard to get a good score on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures were slide shows full of quotes and pictures with no real content to take notes on. There was EXCESSIVE reading for this class too. I ended up having to drop the class halfway through because the midterm was essay based and I didn't have good enough notes for it. How are you supposed to take proper notes with just quotes?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved CJ. She is the best professor ever and I loved her class so much. I am sad that her class is over, it made me so happy.

Pascoe is awesome, extremely helpful and just wants to see you succeed. I enjoyed taking this course online because I could watch the lectures when I had time. Discussions were great if you were still confused on the lecture content. There's many opportunities to get the grade you want and this course can give you so many new perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great and straightforward class, great TA, an Professor Pascoe was extremely caring and great at what she does.

Most of your grade is based on essays where you have to complete four out of an available ten. They are graded by the GE so it just depends how harsh of a grader you get. I will say that personally, none of the prompts really allowed much deep thinking or inspired anything in me, so I found writing each essay a crunch.

Super easy class, I def recommend. Watch video lectures and do a few short questions each week. Write a total of 4 papers. I met her and she was super sweet. The discussion was really stupid tho and attendance was mandatory.

This class was easy but still interesting to learn. Prof Pascoe makes lectures engaging and is accommodating with absences and late work. Online classwork and discussions are light and actually enjoyable. Would totally take a class taught by her again

Although I only experienced this class online, her lectures were always entertaining. Material was light and it was usually only two things a week that you had to do by Wednesday. Discussion class was also very light.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took her course winter term of 2023 and I loved how the course layout is. Her lectures were super entertaining, and I actually really liked watching her videos and taking notes. Plus you only have to write 4 out of the 10 possible essays and a final project at the end. Tons of extra credit opportunities too! Would take another class with her!

Can't say much because it was an async course, but I liked the way she presented the material. Took me about 2 hours per week to watch the lectures, plus a couple more to write the essays. 10 prompts and you have to write 4. Attendance for discussion was mandatory. Overall an easy course if you need a social science and/or U.S. difference credit.

I only had in person for discussion sections. Gives plenty of extra credit opportunities. Assignments are for the most part. You just need to write 4 to 5 750 word essay's throughout the term, but those aren't the worst. No midterm and the final is about a 1,000 word essay which isn't to bad and you have a week to work on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were insanely long, a lot of rambling. Course content and analyses presented in lecture was giving "duh obviously". No hard deadlines. A lot of busy work, felt like a giant waste of time. If you have the time to dedicate, this course isn't hard. Discussion was mandatory. No exams/midterm, just a final "project" which was basically a paper.

Professor Pascoe is amazing! I took this class online and it was very simple to do and you're only graded for 4 small papers and one final project. She makes her lectures very engaging and easy to follow, so I truly enjoyed her class. She's also very accessible outside of class and such a friendly person!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CJ is one of the best professors I have had at UO. I wasn't initially too excited to take this Self and Society class but I'm so glad I did. CJ is so funny and makes content that might not be the most interesting super fun to learn about. The assignments are very doable and you can do them in podcast format so you are not always writing papers.

Professor Pascoe was engaging and relevant. She used videos and pop culture examples to teach class concepts. There were 4 homework assignments that were easy to complete and had clear guidelines. Attendance was mandatory, but she allowed four missed classes. I highly recommend a class with Professor Pascoe and would take a class from her again.

Professor Pascoe is amazing! She is so understanding and makes lectures actually interesting and funny. The readings for the class were short and interesting, so they didn't take up much time. She is super flexible with due dates and the grading was done by a GE but was pretty easy as well. I actually enjoyed showing up to this class!

Pascoe, on top of being really nice and relatable, is an excellent professor. Her lectures were always really straightforward with real world examples and engaging. SOC 328 has plenty of opportunity for extra credit and is not super heavy on the workload in the first place - entire term was 10 required "in class activities" and 4 papers (no final).

Professor Pascoe is one of the sweetest teachers I've ever had. She is so caring and makes time for all of her students. She also makes lectures so fun and we have a very comfortable class environment! 100% recommend!

CJ really cares about her students. Class is designed to be as accessible as possible - encourages her students to take care of themselves before taking care of class. Only has 4 assignments, but you can resubmit 2 if you are unhappy with the grade. Really passionate about sociology and tries her best to make everyone else excited about it too.

I LOVED this class and professor. Her lectures were incredibly engaging, and her grading policy was fair and understanding. There was quite a bit of reading, but it was interesting and the textbook was very inexpensive and written well.
The lectures were very engaging and helpful but I recommend reading the assigned reading to get a full understanding of the material.
in the soc department, cj pascoe is about as good as it can get. turn things in as you finish them with no late grades and if you have a decent G.E., this course is a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CJ had an excellent lecture style that connected perfectly to the reading without reiterating the textbook directly. Her office hours are available and she always listens to student feedback.

The class is very simple, do assignments, and you pretty much get full credit as long as you follow the directions. She is one of the professors that actually cares about you and your health and will record lectures for people who might be sick.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to have CJ as a professor you absolutely should. Sociology is so interesting and fun i am glad that she was the first class i took of sociology. There arent any tests mostly just writing and she makes the information very easy to understand.
She is very engaging and overall a great professor. Connects to real world and is relatable to students. Makes learning less boring.

Professor Pascoe is easily my favorite professor I've had so far. She is so understanding and designs her class so you can do the work when it works best for you. There's only 3 papers all year and then a weekly reflection on class that week. The lectures were always fascinating with the best real world examples. Made me take another soc class!

I love prof Pascoe. She is super clear about what she is teaching and makes class really fun and interesting. The class is graded on the same things each week and there's honestly not that much work, just a good amount of reading. She seems super understanding and the labs were good too.

Prof. Pascoe was an incredible professor to have for my first term at UO. She is very understanding of the stress that comes with the pandemic and other tragedies in our community. Her lectures are interesting and she includes videos and recent events as examples (not everything about COVID, thank god). Take good notes and attend lectures!

Professor Pascoe is a real gem. She truly cares for her students and her GE's. Her class is set up for you to choose when it is convenient for you to do assignments and has made her class easy and accessible if you miss class, with recorded lectures and slide shows posted on canvas. I truly cannot say enough good things about professor pascoe.

Professor Pascoe was an amazing professor who was very passionate about teaching this class. She is very good at going over everything. You usually have a small discussion with a neighbor at least once every lecture. You had to complete three small essays throughout the 10 weeks and a very small assignment that took 3 minutes weekly. Very fun class

Professor Pascoe was an amazing speaker who had great lectures. There was not many assignments at all, besides 7/10 weekly responses, 3/10 weekly essay prompts, and a final project. You do not have to attend class always, as she posts recordings of her lecture. There is a textbook, but I chose not to spend the $1.50/chapter, it wasn't necessary.

Professor Pascoe is a really engaging lecturer, I definitely got more out of her than the readings - although they were helpful. Disregarding the readings, there wasn't much work. Just a weekly short journal and three essays throughout the term plus a final project. My GE was extremely knowledgeable and helpful as well.

CJ's lectures are fantastic and super interesting. In the class itself, I didn't have to try very hard at all. That's fine though because I learned so many things that I can still retain. I didn't read the textbook, I put the lectures at 2x speed, but I took heavy notes and got an A-plus. Take the class, just do it. Amazing material.

Anyone who's taken Soc classes at UO knows CJ is the best professor of Soc by far. She's amazing, funny, and really helpful! I talked to her about having to balance work and zoom classes and she (unlike other profs before) really understood my life situation and helped to prioritize my job when needed. SOC 457 Sex & Society was awesome with her!
Very kind and knowledgeable professor. Class isn't hard in terms of assignments or conceptual material you need to understand. Definitely recommend.

CJ Pascoe was truly an excellent professor. Her knowledge and qualification within the subject is astounding. Her class was very fair and not too stressful. As long as you kept up with weekly readings and did the essays she assigned, you'll get an A. Pascoe's class inspired me to change my major to sociology. Overall an unbelievable professor!

I liked CJ. She tried to make lectures fun but did not appreciate the grading as there were only 3 essays that weighed your grade down if you didnt get As on all. Hated how she poured her liberal views at us but I guess thats what I get for going to oregon. But thankfully I transferred bc of this

I LOVE Professor Pascoe. I had to take SOC 204 for a HPHY requirement and I'm so glad that I did. There are 3-4 weekly essays that are super interesting to write and the midterm/final exam are open note and book. She makes you into a well-rounded, socially aware person in her class.

Really enjoyed having her as a prof; not hard at all to pass; very understanding/accommodating; honestly, she blew my mind during some of the lectures; I had the textbook but if you show up to all her lectures and take good notes it really isn't necessary; guidelines are clear; didn't like having to go to discussion but it's mandatory for the class
Good lectures in class but assignments are graded get GEs that all have different structures so good luck figuring those out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is such an amazing professor! She knows her stuff and is really good at taking difficult concepts and breaking them down. Don't skip unless you have someone to give you notes, her lecture slides don't say much, but you can get the info from the book. DO THE NON-BOOK READINGS! They're crucial to the midterms and final! She's really great!

Professor Pascoe is an amazing teacher. She's funny and very engaging. She makes the material very easy to understand. She is my favorite professor at the U of O by far. You won't regret taking this course with her!

Great professor, super engaging lectures and very straightforward. Really cares about we students! Theres 10 essays but you only have to do 3, midterm and final are open book and open note. A lot of reading but the readings are interesting, and with the textbook reading she talks about most of it in class so you could get away with not doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Pascoe has been the best professor I have had at UO. She is so passionate and she really understands the material. She not only boosted my passion for sociology, but also for WGS. Easily the most inspirational professor. There are 10 opportunities to write papers, only 3 are graded, but if you write 4 the lowest grade is dropped.
She is such a great and kind teacher. She has interesting and fun lectures that make you understand things more and feel more involved!

Professor Pascoe gives you a lot of freedom; for the class I took, there was nothing stopping you from never going to lecture and doing the three essay minimum. I would not recommend this because she does a great job of breaking complex societal issues down, explaining the data behind various sociological studies, and bringing in current events.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love professor Pascoe! Love learning from actual respected professors unlike most of them at Oregon. I loved attending her lectures. They were entertaining and she really cares about how her students do and about their happiness.
I absolutely loved Prof. Pascoe's class. She is engaging and makes you genuinely interested in the course content. If you get the chance, I would 100% recommend er class to anyone.

CJ is a respected professor and a respected sociologist. The lectures are great, and while they aren't mandatory, the final is OPEN NOTES, so you should really show up if you want a good grade in this class. Otherwise, graded on 4 essay, pretty easy material and keep up with the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures. You have 10 opportunities to write 4 papers for a grade. Plus a final, lecture participation (you can miss multiple classes and still get an A) and discussion participation. Easy grader and very passionate about Sociology.

Super funny, lectures are really engaging. Gives great examples of concepts. Definitely an easy class, grade consists of four 1-3 page essays and a final paper. Attendance is mandatory in discussion, but in lecture 50% attendance gives you full participation points. Content is straight from the textbook so it's easy to find if you miss a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Pascoe is great! Apply for the honors research program if you are interested in Research. You will not be disappointed. The feedback is wonderful! You also get to be in a small class which only meets once a week. It's a very supportive environment in which one can blossom.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: CJ always had extremely entertaining lectures and had class involvement activities that made learning the material more interesting! Definitely an easy class if you show up to class and make it to your discussion sections! :)

Attendance is required in lecture and discussion. Grade is based on 4-5 essays, partipation, and a final(essay). Take good notes and read the book in case you need to refer/cite it for the final. Good class overall and no midterms!

One of the coolest. CJ is unusually gifted at Sociology and helping deconstruct concepts to make them more palatable. Excellent feedback, like rediculous excellent; actually takes the time and puts true effort into it.   On a side note.... You need to know this. Sometimes she may come across as rude but that is not her intent. She DOES care

Never posts slides on blackboard and never has any word on the slides so you dont have a fair shot at writing notes which i never have. Never really sure what was expected of me all year since there are only 2 tests that determine your grade. Examples are goood but lectures boring. Multiple choice tests are tough if you dont know definitions.

I don't understand why people complain that she doesn't post lecture slides on blackboard. If you do the reading and attend class it's an easy A or B. Any ways I really enjoyed Sociology 204 with her,  she made it fun and interesting with a lot of visuals that help you remember the information.

Prof. Pascoe is one of my favorite professors of all-time. I highly recommend her. Her lectures are clear, and she's fair and entertaining. Attendance is uber important. My only complaint is that sometimes she trails off at the end of sentences... but the lectures are amazing, using up-to-date studies that are relevant to our society.

Sociology can be a snooze, but she REALLY makes it interesting and extremely relevant to students. She uses memorable yet awkward examples, as well as using herself as examples in certain scenarios. Her lectures are hilarious and interesting, she's a great Professor.

Definitely a nice guy but at times annoyed me a bit because there were no slides and spoke to us like we already knew things about philosophy. Grade is determined on three four page 100 point papers and 10 points of participation. Lots of reading to do and kind of hard to follow but hes obviously passionate about the content which made it easier

Overall I really like Cisternino but he teaches in an old fashioned way. He is super nice and caring, but lectures can be boring because he talks for most of it and doesn't have slides or videos that relate to the content. I would take him again because overall he's a really good teacher.

I took PHIL 104 with him and it was honestly a really good class. He's very knowledgeable and knows how to answer complicated questions in a way that beginners can understand! Overall we had some really fun discussions in this class. Participation is the whole point, so if you don't want to think in new ways and discuss things don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For this class there were only 3 essays and 10 points of participation that was the whole grade book. I would miss at least once a week and spoke up a handful of times and got an 8/10 for participation. He graded very fairly. I turned all the papers in on the last week and was not docked points for it being late. He does value communication.

He teaches this intro to philosophy class like everyone was a philosophy major. I'm sure he would be great for anyone that is interested in philosophy but if you are taking this class just to fill a requirement, do not have him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Massimo was very cool. Great guy. He is from Italy. Gave my bad papers good scores even though I did not read the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was unfortunately so disappointing. The only essay assigned was an in-class essay, which made it hard to engage fully with the readings. It also seemed that contributions from students were only briefly acknowledged by her, which made the classroom kind of awkward and standoffish. She was also always late.

Nice person, BUT: ALWAYS, without exception, late to class (by 5-30 minutes), quite disorganized, un-rigorous (everything graded on completion except the midterm & final), NO essays (in 300-level PHIL class??!), & heavy focus on 1 or 2 strands of feminist phil to the exclusion of many others. Easy A but not smth I'd recommend.
She was good professor, but was hard to understand at times. The worst part about her is that she showed up at least 5 minutes sometimes up to 20 minutes late every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very passionate and caring. Classes were very interesting.

I've taken three classes with Dr. Velasco and each of them have been incredibly accessible, constructive and thought provoking. Yes, lectures can be difficult to understand sometimes due to language barrier, but it likely won't impede your success in class. Heavy in hand-written work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a little difficult to understand sometimes but the class content and structure is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MKTG 445. Dr. Cieslak is unlike any professor I have ever had. If you struggle with getting to class and don't want to work hard, this class is not for you. If you show him you care and WANT to learn, he will do everything he can to help you be successful. If you don't put in the work or come to class, then you will not do well.

He mainly just reads off of slideshows and show us youtube videos. He is a slight narcissist and loves to talk about himself every class. The content wasn't engaging, there were 2 chapters of reading and a weekly quiz to go with it. The final project worth most of our grade had no clear rubric for grading and he gave 0 feedback on our grade.

was supposed to be in person but was forced to take it online after a family problem on his end. The lectures involve a lot of unnecessary yapping and watching youtube videos of his own Ted talks. The only actual educational part is the final project where you pitch your product idea. 2 chapters of textbook reading every week that go with a quiz

If you like to learn by DOING, this is the guy for you. Yes, there are times when stuff can be a bit vague but if you SHOW your effort and COMMUNICATE anything you are unclear on then he will give you the feedback to get a good grade. Again he's a really nice dude, just participate and demonstrate your effort and you're in for a very good quarter.

This professor wants you to figure out what he wants from you. He sets very minimal expectations but constantly expresses annoyance in our failure to meet his assumptions. Loves to listen to himself talk but mood quickly shifts when he realizes no one else does. He is clearly somewhat knowledgable but seems to be teaching because he loves authority

Super easy class. You do not have to go to lectures at all unless you want extra details about the big project. There is only one big assignment with a partner of your choice. The homework was a quiz each week but they were easy if you read to textbook homework.

Took for the easy A but what a waste of a class. They say those who can't, teach. Well, that's who he is, he talks about all the companies he has failed and then just ego trips on how your company will not be successful. If you want to see a teacher play favorites this is your guy.
