Thomas teaches in a fun and energetic way and gives real world examples from his experience that help you understand the content. However, he stops the class to ask everyone obscure questions to try to get the class to participate, and if they don't answer he just stops talking. It's a huge waste of time and honestly ruins class some days.

Haven't finished the term yet, but this class has been great. It's basically just one giant group project, from the first day to the last day. He lectures and tells stories for about half the class, then lets us work together. Super respected and funny guy, he has plenty of experience in the business sphere. Very helpful and honest guy.

I took MGMT 225 w Cieslak. He is very understanding and knowledgable who is easy to talk to and cares about his students. attendance was not mandatory, although encouraged since he goes over material and information about tests and projects. The tests were all remote and online, we had a presentation at the end of term. I definitely recommend him.

There's a big easy extra credit task that's kept my grade up the whole term. The only homework is a simple quiz once a week, that you can find all the answers for in the textbook. Mr. Cieslak's a super nice guy and gives cool lectures but attendance isn't required. Definitely take this class for a good grade and if you're interested in business.
He is nice and easy, however, in my opinion I did not learn anything from the class. I felt this was a class that students joined just because it is easy not bc they enjoy the class materials.

Great teacher. Highly recommend Cieslak. He is personable, passionate, and teaches an easy-to-follow class with clear instructions and expectations. Attendance is not required but he's engaging, which makes you want to attend. Group projects cumulates throughout the term. I always enjoyed going to class. Easy quizzes regarding the lectures.
Professor Cieslak is a top G, super easy class that he made fun by allowing for lots of freedom in the one group project you do throughout the term. I would defiantly recommend any course he teaches

literally just one quiz a week (on your own) which perfectly followed the lectures and one big group project that you do throughout the term. Super cool guy and grades VERY fairly. Has a lot of real-world experience which he shares during the lectures - so it's easy to stay engaged
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor quizzes you before class, 3X during class (on a timer, a majority of students struggle to complete quiz before the time is up), and again after class on the content. We as a class still do not understand the context of how this class is helpful to us. Examples the professor uses are not relevant/do not add context to what we are doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best OBA professor at the UO based on the gossip I've heard about other professors as well as the other professor I took the next term. He has an accent, but it's tolerable. The reason I probably didn't get an A in the course is cause I underestimated the midterm but as long as you try your best youll do great. Wish he taught OBA 312

Prof Cil himself is an alright enough person and lecturer, but the class itself is often unbearably boring. Lecture could adequately be covered in an hr 20 type lecture, but Cil tends to drag on for the full two hours. Obtaining an A requires a 94 and grades are not curved like in other OBA 311 sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really liked Eren Cil. OBA 311 was very easy to follow. While I don't like that there are mini quizzes every day for homework, they aren't difficult and make me learn the material. If you forget about one he has a system that sends you a text reminding you about it. He's just a really nice guy with a decently easy class if you put in the effort.

LOVE professor Cil. The course is very clearly organized and he conveys the information in the lectures very clearly. Your grade is mainly the by-weekly homework, the midterm and final, but there you can get points by doing the pre and post quizzes that are super easy. He cares a lot about students learning, overall amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cil does a great job as an overall teacher. His accent is easy to understand and he takes the right amount of time to go back and explain if you're confused. Just make sure to ask questions or ask him to pause if he starts going too fast because at times he will move very quickly during the lectures.

Lectures can get long and boring and never seem to end early. He is very quiz heavy, they are easy but there are a lot of them so get ready for that. Exams are long and challenging with no curve. If you dont study for the exams you will not finish them. Overall nice guy and if you do your work you will do fine.

A little fast paced in class, but as long as you attend and pay a reasonable amount of attention in class, you'll be fine. Homeworks are done in duos and may take you upwards of 3 hours. Overall, he's clearly a smart guy and teaches reasonably well, just be ready to actually engage in the class because you will fall behind otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you go to class and do the practice tests the class will be easy. The homework and projects are completed in groups which is nice
Go to class, follow the lectures, and do the practice tests and you will do fine in the class. He is very willing to help if you get confused
He is nice but his class is hard
Smart guy who can explain complicated things pretty well. He can move pretty fast though, so don't get behind.

The format of his honors class relied entirely on student presentations - each class was a hour and a half of students recapping the required reading for the day. I really liked the books we read and the subject material, but I was hoping to get more from him. He clearly has a lot of info to share but instead I only learned from other students.

He is a great person, very kind, and knows his stuff. The class was organized strangely, with too many group presentations that were useless. There was a lot of reading as well, I loved the books he required but they were all over the place, and lacked a clear theme.

To say the least, Prof. Cina is a very kind professor, and likes to se an engaging classroom. He genuinely wants the best for his students and loves making conversation about the subject material. That being said, his class was disorganized and gets confusing fast. Also, his assigned essay prompts have little-to-no substance, and little feedback.

Professor Cina is a fantastic human being. The way he taught our class was very unique in the sense that he had students lead the class which got very frustrating towards the end. He also doesn't give great feedback on essays or on how you can improve and his grading methods are very strange - he doesn't give much reasoning for why you earned it.

Cina is truly invested in both his students' academic success and development. His section of honors general chemistry was our entire class's favorite by far. He is easy to contact outside of class and goes out of his way to assist in matching students with on campus research. Grade is dependent on weekly tests. A great teacher with a good sou;.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst prof I've ever taken. His lectures are useless rambles. He doesn't use slides, but handwrites lecture notes that are nearly incomprehensible and often written sideways, up-side-down, and in the margins of the page. The quizes and exams have almost no bearing on the material. He refused to give more practice problem when asked by 3 students

Great guy and EXTREMELY smart. However he over complicated the class, and went off on a lot of tangents. He should probably have taught 400 and up level classes. You will have to do a lot of reading on your own. Also, curves help definitely help out!

Such a nice guy and is very, very intelligent. However, he doesn't really know how to teach the material effectively so that students can successfully understand. His quizzes sometimes cover things he has never talked about or has mentioned just once. Some quizzes (like the redox one) were fine, but some were insanely difficult (incl. his final)

Professor Cina is an extremely nice guy, but incredibly frustrating professor. His lectures are almost completely nonsensical and his quizzes are so hard that I have had other chem professors tell me he is asking ridiculous questions. However, he does have a generous curve that puts the average at B-.

There are very few people in this world that are kinder than Professor Cina. That said, I have never learned less from a professor in my entire educational career. I literally counted down the days until the course was over. He needs to stick to his graduate students and stop assuming that the whole world automatically understands quantum mechanics

Cina is an incredibly nice man who is very supportive of his students and knows the material very well, however, for those new to chemistry his honors chem. course can be very challenging in that he assumes students know things that at least I didn't already know. His lectures are pretty boring and I've had to spend a lot of time with the textbook.

He is extremely smart and knows the material he is teaching but isn't very good at explaining it. His notes aren't complete and he often uses equations with variables he never defines. His tests are difficult but the class is curved so the average will never be below a B-. You have to teach yourself a lot from the textbook.

He is a nice guy but not a very good teacher. He knows his material but is bad at explaining and very rarely defines his variables in his equations. His tests are pretty hard but he grades on a curve and the average is never below a B-. You pretty much have to teach yourself from the book.
He's random but pretty fun. His notes are not complete but you're expected to read what he doesn't cover. He's a very nice guy
Very difficult to understand - he tend to ramble a lot about random subjects. He certainly understand what he's talking about, but it's difficult to comprehend through all the "ums."

My favorite class I have taken by far, I would recommend to anyone no matter your major! She is such a great professor and so knowledgeable. The homework load isn't bad and there are no tests, your final is a paper with a presentation. You also have the option to attend every class over zoom if you would like.

I couldn't recommend this woman more; she is a fantastic teacher, mentor and friend. I felt comfortable and cared for in this class and she is just an amazing person in general. Take this class if you get the chance!!!!!!

I could not recommend Professor Fowler and this class enough! She creates a very safe space to learn and truly wants her students to succeed. By far my favorite professor at UO thus far. You have a few assignments a week (papers, exercises, etc.) but she balances out the work perfectly, you will not feel stressed as the content is very interesting.

Professor Fowler was such an amazing professor! Yes, you had to buy 2 books for the class and read a chapter or two do the weekly assignments, but it was so easy and she always dedicated time in class to go over it and even start part of it. She was kind, and always valued what you had to say! Definitely recommend it, especially for an elective!
Claire makes it very clear on how to succeed in her class and will support you if you engage. Make sure you and your group have a clear outline of what you want to do and how you want to do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: uses ai to grade and gets defensive when pressed
Claire makes it very clear on what you have to do to succeed. Do the readings and show up!

Honestly if you email her for feedback, are on time for class, and do your work you will be fine. This was not a hard class except for maybe the group project but overall claire is empathetic and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She does not explain assignments very clearly, she also isn't super organized. I liked her enough as a teacher so I wouldn't completely say you should stay away.

Claire is a very personable professor who cares about her students and teachings. The course I took had a mix of personal and team assignments that tested things like leadership styles, emotional intelligence, etc. Although the course requires quite a bit of effort, Claire gives her students plenty of resources to thrive if taken advantage of.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is always 2 hours long she does not really shy away from that so expect to be there the whole time. There are random pop quizzes on things like a 23 page reading which can be a negative effect on ur grade if u dont remeber details. Claire is honestly caring and gives chance for feedback and regrading , its not a difficult class.

Claire simply doesn't know what she's doing, from the beginning of the term she is on a completely different wavelength and her own world, somehow she would find a way to complement everyone saying we are doing amazing while giving everyone terrible grades on assignments, she inconsistent and thinks her class is super important and hard material,no

Poor grading criteria and mixed instructions. Professors lectures are long and onerous. Rate my professor score is not reflective of her performance because she gets negative reviews taken down. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class covers a lot of different things, and is a lot of work. But Claire is a great professor who cares about her students.

GRADES WITH AI, pop quizzes on things like the author's name, starts the class by announcing that she doesn't give As out so don't even try. Bummer because other people say they loved BA 308 but this was my least favorite class I've taken. Not a 1 is because she took our feedback and worked on things. Clearly new professor. Gets defensive too.

If ur the type of student to agree over an A or B, DO NOT take Claire's class. Her grading is random, and will come back as 100% AI if ran thru an AI checker. Sure I learned some in this class but she came off as self absorbed and really out of touch. Also her husband runs the program, which makes sense lol

Professor Hennessy seems very tough at first, but she teaches entertainingly and directly. You will learn how to do everything pertinent to the course topic. She also offers thorough feedback on all written assignments. The Everest simulation was the most fun project I've participated in for any class at Lundquist.
Took Environmental econ with her. It was a great class. She always had lots of real life examples to go along with the material. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gulcan's lectures aren't the most engaging, but the information put out during them is concise, with frequent examples to further illustrate the point. While she does put the lecture slides online, not all of the information that is needed will be on them, so class attendance while not mandatory is nevertheless necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a very good teacher, what she said in class is very clear and helpful.
Not sure what's wrong with the earlier reviewers... Gulcan is great. It's a hard class. But she explains things pretty well and gives a lot of examples to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: very good teacher

This class is hard. No getting around it. Gulcan tries to make this class better and more understandable but the subject itself is extremely hard.  If you use the Midterm study guides you will be fine on the tests. She gives you so many relevant examples on canvas that you will literally recognize exact problems on the tests. She is a good teacher

Honestly, this is probably the worst class I have ever taken at the U of O. It's a hard subject and Mrs. Cil tries hard to teach it well, but she comes up devastatingly short. Lectures are long /boring. She literally writes her notes from canvas on a blank sheet of paper the entire class. I've never been so mad, trying to learn a pointless subject.

Not great... Not awful but if you can avoid Gulcan. Her accent is hard to understand but I guess you get used to it, she talks really quietly which sucks in a lecture class. There are quizzes every week which is actually helpful if you study and do well. The midterms were both easy but the final was incredibly hard. Try to take with different prof.
I personally did not have a good experience with this class - instructor combo at all, but maybe thats just me.

Has an accent but you will get used to it. Has absolutely no control over the class and seems intimidated by the students. Her lectures are pretty boring and much harder then they need to be. She goes over a simple concept but makes it more difficult. The multiple choice tests are difficult. I would NOT recommend.

Gulcan was a great professor. Gives great examples for everything you go over. Curves all assignments. Overall is totally being undervalued as a teacher, merely because she has a moderate accent. It takes time to get use to, but to use  it as an excuse to say she is a bad teacher is nonsense. If you pay attention and go over slides you'll be fine.
Impossible to understand. Class is much harder than it needs to be. Has little to no control over the students.

This lady is such a bad teacher. She is very unclear in what so is explaining and doesn't have control over the class at all. Her lectures are incredibly confusing and although she may be trying to explain a concept it goes right over the students heads. It's not because I don't understand the material because I do, she's just a bad teacher.

She is not a bad instructor at all! A little hard to understand at first, but after the first couple classes, her accent becomes more and more clear. She prints out easy to read handouts that are great study guides for the tests, and she shows a real passion for this subject! Great class!

Gulcan is really sweet but shes also kind of awkward in the sense that she seems almost intimidated by her students? I dont know but whenever I or one of my friends would ask her questions she wouldn't respond very clearly and it kind of felt like she was uncomfortable. The Multiple choice questions on the exam were tricky and in my opinion unfair.
no comment...

She really isnt that bad. Her accent is a little irritating, but it doesnt get in the way. Yes, she is powerfully boring, but a very thorough and organized lecturer, who's lectures are easy to learn from if you can manage to pay attention. Thats the hardest part, but seriously, if you just suck it up, go to class, and work hard, you will get an A
worst class/professor combo so far..
horrible professor. the final being 45% of the grade in my opinion is way too much not to mention its on a scantron! I plan to retake this class either online or with a better professor!

Seriously the worst teacher I have ever had. And I'm not talking about in college. The worst teacher I have had in my entire life. Ridiculously boring. Reading the book will teach you better in half the time. Avoid her.
Honestly the worst college professor I have had to date. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS.

Ms.Cil isn't THAT bad! Econ 201 is generally pretty boring it's not her fault. As for the accent it really doesn't bother me. She's a very helpful professor and her tests and HW assignments aren't that hard.

The absolute worst teacher I've ever had. It is hard to understand her because she is so quiet, unenthusiastic, and boring. It was difficult finding motivation to go to class because she repeats what she puts on BlackBoard word for word. Moral = DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. Unless you want to teach yourself or are very lucky on tests, avoid Gulcan Cil.
terrible
She is honetly one of the worst teachers ever. I couldn't understand a word she said due to her accent and quietness.

She has a thick accent and it's really hard to understand. Also very quiet, and for lecture situations is not the best. You honestly don't even have to show up to pass the class. The only help I get is my book, because I can't understand a word she says.
Span 193 is about vernacular Spanish, which would not be helpful to find work in public or private high schools.

SPAN 193 is one of the courses taught by Claudia at UCR, where I majored in Spanish. The prof. is committed to teaching Spanish for Heritage  speakers, so I thought her courses will take me in the direction of normative Spanish so that I get look for a job in the public schools, bc there are more positions today. To no avail.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
She is creative and has offered many courses here at UCR. However, I do not know which one is good for Spanish majors who 
look for a job in the public schools or junior community colleges. Teaching in Spanglish is not at all helpful, since we do need to
present our credentials in normative Spanish, which she does not know or will ever master.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claudia is doing good work in California.  Am not sure if the spanish language curriculum will help me get a job in the public schools or junior community colleges.

I follow the blogs attentively because at the U. of Oregon, Claudia was engaged in multiple projects, very creative indeed. However, I do not remember having heard that she speaks standard Spanish or standard English. She struggles with both languages; it is obvious from the multiple videos that she posts. She is not the model I need to get a job.

It was not too hard, and I did get a good grade. After all these years I wish she would have emphasized the importance of learning standard Spanish, cz' employers are checking this item over and over.
She promotes Spanglish in California, yet you cannot list your Spanglish in an application for work. I had to take more courses with other profs.

She is a great teacher and does a great job of teaching the class. But be ready to read because there is a lot of reading and they are very long. Her grading style is pretty good and not many assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Honestly the best teacher I've had at this university. She is motivated, cares about her students, and is obviously passionate about what she is teaching. 10/10 would recommend to anyone who has had bad experiences with spanish classes in the past because her classroom environment is just so positive. Some assignments can be challenging but doable.

Claudia is a phenomenal instructor and the most personable professor I've encountered at the UO. Her exams are relatively easy but rely heavily upon the material discussed in class and in the text. Quizzes are done in groups and if you present, students always received a 10/10 for both required presentations (20% of final grade).
I highly recommend taking a class with Claudia. The material was always interesting and she makes herself available to help you succeed and to answer questions.

Claudia is a fantastic instructor, she's passionate about sociolinguistics and she has designed an amazing course! Her Spanish is very clear and she is always very clear in her expectations. The course readings were very interesting and always extremely relevant. Her class actually changed my way of thinking about language, which is amazing.

Nice prof, but the lectures were confusing sometimes, and key concepts were often glazed over and not explained thoroughly. We also didn't do many examples in class, which made the hw more difficult, and sometimes the hw was unrelated to the lecture and was not tested on. Not a super difficult class, but the lectures definitely were mediocre.
He was the professor for CH218 and CH228. He made it easy for people to get A's and was very straightforward about his expectations.

Dr Clayton was a great chem professor. He cares about your individual learning, and will work very hard to help you understand the course content and work through any challenges. His lectures are rather conceptual so make sure to pay attention, but his class is NOT hard.

keeps having to fix his lectures days later. he gives little context on slides, and often has a blank slide with one picture. his handwriting is hard to read. easy grader but if you like learning you'll dislike his class. really jumbled explanations. i hope the TA answers my questions instead of him. he also doesnt know whats on the homework.

Nice guy but bad teacher. Really disorganized and hard to understand. He doesn't highlight important information, just writes it in the margins of a random slide in chicken scratch. Barely does examples in class, and doesn't give enough hw to practice. The PLTLs are all theoretical, no application. Could be worse, but still really frustrating

I took this class online and it was super straightforward and easy to succeed in. There is no final only weekly quizzes. I worked a job over summer while taking this class and Prof. Clayton adjusted the quizzes due date for me.
Totally chill guy, even with tricky material he cares more about learning and will make sure your grade reflects that.

I would without a doubt take a class with him again. He is very funny and teaches using examples that are relatable and easy to understand. He is available and open to answering questions and usually curves exams.

Theres a reason Clayton is one of the highest rated CH profs. Super easy to get a C+ or better in the course as long as you attend most of the lectures. Clayton has a great teaching style for such a hard course, and cracks funny jokes hella. Only 2 midterms, weekly homework, and 1 final. Only neg is ALEKS tbh but thats out of his control.
Very cool professor!

Great professor! Attendance isn't mandatory but the lectures do help a lot. He goes over the material at a good pace and really tries to make sure everyone understands it. Homework is very ALEKS heavy but it's not too difficult if you pay attention in class. He really cares about the students, and is super easy to communicate with. I'd take again!

Very fun and caring guy. I hadn't taken chemistry since sophomore year of high school and ended this class with a B+ which is really surprising. He cares about his students mental health and always made sure to be very fair with his grading and curved all his tests. You get a cheat sheet on all exams and his office hours are helpful and accessible.

He is an amazing, passionate teacher who cares about what he's teaching. Tests are slightly hard but if you put effort into the class, you will pass with no problem. Would take again and signed up so he will be my 223 prof.

I really like Don. He posts everything on canvas and is very easy to communicate with through email or office hours. Lectures are pretty straightforward and he makes them as engaging as he can. There are 3 midterms, 2 quizzes, and a fair amount of hw each week. He does curve his tests but be prepared to study, this class is not easy.

Dr. Clayton is very approachable, and he's extremely open and responsive to feedback from students.

He's very clear about what is necessary to do well in the course (working through practice problems). He also understands that different students have different goals and is willing to work with them to achieve their definition of success.
fantastic professor really prepares students for tests, and gives a ton of opportunities to up your grade. He also curves which is absolutely great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy but honestly his teaching methods aren't my favorite. We had 3 midterms on top of a final (not even a week after the last midterm) and the homework is doable but there is a lot. I learned a lot from his class but it definitely felt like an uphill battle sometimes.

I loved Dr. Clayton and wished I was able to take him for 221 and 222. Teaches in a very clear way that made chemistry easy to learn. 2 midterms and a final - none of the questions were there to trick you though, just a measure of your basic knowledge. Weekly homework and quizzes online.

I was intimidated to take college chemistry but Clayton made it super accessible. Clear grading, clear lecture, great study materials for tests. Not as engaging as some other science professors I've had but very straightforward and understanding. Tests were not too hard at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry 221 is definitely a difficult course but Clayton makes it much easier to handle. He curves the midterms and the final exam which are both worth a lot of your grade and also curves the final grade you receive in the class. 10/10 would recommend having Clayton as your prof if you are taking chem. You can tell he cares about his students.

I had Clayton as a chemistry 111 professor and I highly appreciated him. He was quick to respond to my emails outside of class even with his huge class numbers and gave many solutions and opportunities to better your grade.

never had a prof who gave MORE opportunities to improve your grade. its SO apparent that he cares about the subject and his students. he is strict ish- he wont pass you if you do not demonstrate effort to this class. he might spare you points or a letter grade if you show significan improvements from your midterms to your finals. HIGHLY recommend.

He genuinely shows he knows a lot about the subject, and is very open and welcoming to answering questions. He has also been a very good grader in that he is decently on time, its not graded hard, and as long as you just do the work in the class youre bound to pass with a decent grade.

I had him for ch111 he has good info in his lectures and is rly nice. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you do get graded on clicker questions in class. but he does provide other ways to earn that credit if u aren't at lecture. He does post his lecture slides on canvas, but they don't have the notes that he writes in class, so I'd recommend going.
You can tell he really understands what hes teaching-super informative and helpful. Very homework heavy and the exams can be daunting, but his grading rubric is great!
hes so awesome

His lectures were very straight forward, the course was very organized, and he was very clear about when content would be covered by the test. The textbook is online. Definitely keep up with the ALEKS and go to office hours. He is super nice, understanding, and willing to talk to you about just about anything.
Finished the chemistry sequence with professor Clayton over the summer, it went smoothly. Lectures were short and clear, make sure to study for tests.

Dr. Clayton is exceptionally nice and a great professor. He is very understanding and helpful with problems I encountered during his CH 223 summer course I am taking, instead of being rude like some other professors would. You can tell he really wants to help his students do well. If you are taking 221 or 223 try to take him if you are able to.

Dr. Clayton is very nice and will make accommodations for you outside of class if needed. He is willing to work with you and for such a difficult class he will take the time to break it down for you. He really does care about the students and wants to make sure you pass.

He's very helpful and is always willing to work with you if you are struggling. He's very clear in his teaching and his lectures usually fly by. He moves quickly but the material is presented in a way that actually makes sense.
Slay, He was nice.

For a subject that's generally difficult, he does a great job in helping students understand concepts. Lectures move fast, but homework helps reenforce subject material. Super understand and helpful professor.

He's an incredible professor who doesn't like to waste time in class but will teach as efficiently as he can. He might go too fast once in a while but he posts the slides after class and is always happy to explain it slower during office hours. He's also very generous with homework extensions so don't be afraid to ask if you need one.
Super great at explaining material and always willing to help outside of class too !
Clifford was a great professor and gave everyone a chance to speak in class. She is caring and understanding, gives good feedback on assignments as well. Would definitely take again!

LOVE PUJA!! Had her 225 but didn't let me put that as an option. She really cares about her students' success and encourages lots of discussion throughout class. She has a super calming voice and it's always so fun to listen to. Make sure you show up to class so you can stay up to date on the different medias we watch!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Clifford is amazing. She is an amazing teacher who is super inspiring. She is always available and wants to help! I would recommend her class to everyone! There is a lot of chats and sharing with classmates. I was undeclared but she has helped me think about a future in education.
Great teacher, take her class

Puja is a very smart and gifted woman. Extremely lecture heavy but also extremely organized and concise. Understanding of life happening but still upholds expectations. Would definitely take again maybe in a smaller class size though. Loved the GEs as well and her respect towards them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Clifford is awesome. The class is interesting and informative. The workload is consistent but not too much, and you will receive much support from her and the GEs.

Puja was truly an amazing professor. She cares deeply about the subject and about the success of her students. I took EDST 111 in 2023, and it was easy to pass. The course was organized and easy to follow, and all assignments were reasonable. The GE's were also wonderful and also seemed passionate about the subject.

I had Puja for 111 and 211, every term I search for her to see if she has other classes I can take. She is clearly passionate about teaching, and puts significant effort into using her knowledge about education to make long classes feel engaging, fast, and like a good use of time. Even when I had her at 8:30AM I rarely skipped, she's amazing
Puja is the best thing at UO for me, caring sweet and compassionate!

I didn't think I would like taking this course but Puja and all of the guest speakers made it a fun class. The homework can be a bit draining as the weeks go on but it isn't necessarily difficult! Overall, a good class taught by a good professor... I feel like I learned a lot.
puja is honestly a blessing upon this earth. definitely would take again.

I liked Johns class! The content is a little boring but he is upfront about that and tries to keep you engaged anyways. Always is clear and organized with assignments. Attendance not required, but useful. The tests are take-home but still difficult. Much better than most other professors teaching coding classes.
Great professor. It's pretty much just a coding class, but he makes the material easy to understand and the lectures enjoyable. Super approachable and keeps the class engaging. Would recommend.

John is a great dude and makes a boring topic of coding interesting. This class is entirely a coding class which I didn't expect. I like the way that he explains things and has good examples in class. He's a tough grader but overall he explains things clearly and I would take a different class with him again.

class is a LOT, clithero dumbs things down for us very well, but dont ask questions because he does not know the answer. many textbooks we use are free, no tests, there is a presentation and group project. if youre a marketing major i recommend john.

Dr. Evans is by far my favorite professor I have had at UO. She is passionate about her craft(s), and it reflects in her lectures, where she handles sensitive topics with tact and care. I went into SOC 385 knowing next to nothing about medical soc, and left with a newfound passion for a field I initially didn't know existed. Take her if you can!

Evans clearly loves what she teaches. Lectures were not just interesting but relevant to current events. I also enjoyed talking one-on-one in her office hours. If you like to write, then you should take her class.

Professor Evans was by far one of the greatest teachers I've had here at the University of Oregon. Her strive and passion to help students thrive both within the classroom and out in our daily lives is truly an inspiration. Professors like her make learning fun and still provide all the knowledge we need to move along college in a positive way.

Professor Evans was by far one of the greatest teachers I have ever had here at the University of Oregon. Her strive and passion for students to achieve their highest potentials both in the classroom and outside in daily life is truly an inspiration. Professors like her make learning fun whilst still providing constructive feedback.

Wish I could have her in person because she's truly the best! Very sweet, intelligent, and handles heavy/sensitive topics in her lectures with care. I enjoyed this class so much and assignments weren't exceptionally difficult but still challenged my way of thinking and connected to many relevant topics. Grading by her GE was chill too

Dr Evans is arguably one of the most caring and informed professors at UO. Her class incorporates hard topics but she approaches them with such delicacy. As for class work, there are a few 2 page essays and a longer final but they are just difficult enough where it challenges you to think and reflect without completely burning out

Awesome prof. Clare is understanding and takes care to make her classes interesting and accessible. Online 311 was a struggle I can't lie... I def recommend taking this class in person if possible. The zoom classes drove me crazy- the content can just feel a little dry. But Clare made this class so much better and doable under zoom circumstances.

I love Professor Evans! It's a nice breath of fresh air from my other lecture-heavy courses I felt like I learned so much from her. There is also a lot of small group discussion and I love that that aspect makes it more fun and interactive. There are a total of 6 papers though. 5 two-page papers and one 6 page final.

Dr. Evans is a very good professor. Her classes consists of 75% group discussions on readings done for the class, and 25% lecture/class discussion. There are five essays but all only two pages and very easy along with a five page final. you are allowed to miss four classes without punishment. Overall very easy class even without reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is literally the best. She cares about every student and makes sure her classes are accessible. Her lectures are amazing and very clear to understand. There is not any quizzes and the final project is easy. There are a few participation requirements but they are easy to make up. I have never had such a great professor. 10/10

Loved this class! Dr. Evans is very caring and passionate with her class and lectures. She is very understanding and lectures are open for class discussion. There are writing assignments that prepare you for the final paper. I am not a very good writer but I have gotten A's and B's on all the written assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: This is one of the best classes I've ever taken. Dr. Evans is incredibly knowledgeable, lectures are engaging and fun. Dr. Evans also handled serious topics with deep empathy and care. This class convinced me to add a Global Health minor, and I am sad to graduate and miss future opportunities to learn from Dr. Evans. Straightforward assignments!

One of the best profs at UO hands down! Learned so much from Clare and actually used the info in a lot of other classes. Weekly reading/concept reflection and small in class group activities. Readings weren't too bad, could be done on the spot and the night of. Concepts were also gone over in class lectures. If you see Clare's classes, take them!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This teacher was great! SOC 311 is actually a really difficult class, so I've heard from others, but I breezed through this because Dr. Evans is so great. She teaches really well and is very interactive. If you go to class and skim the readings, you will do great. Weekly homework assignments with a midterm and final. I really enjoyed this class.

Dr. Evans is wonderful. Research methods was not a class I was looking forward to, but she kept me engaged the whole term. She is knowledgable and is working on social research currently. There are a lot of readings but I didn't do them. She is funny and cares deeply about her students. If you participate and talk to her you can be very successful.

There are three tests and although we were given what would be on the test, the tests were still challenging. I thought the homework was challenging and the GTF doesn't grade them easy so its important that you try. Overall really great class and would take it again!

Dr. Evans is one of the best professors I have enountered at the University of Oregon. She is so passionate about Sociology and loves to help students understand. She always comes to class happy, with a great attitude. I always felt very welcomed in her class. The way she teaches made sense to me, and made me want to do well in the course.

You can tell that she is very knowledgeable and passionate about her subject which can cause some professors to let material go right over students heads, but Evans does a really good job at making the material easy to understand if you engage. She really wants you to do well and does what she can to see that that happens. Definitely recommend!

A talented and engaging lecturer. The readings are dense, but she goes over them in detail. The only irritating thing is she assigns group work daily for participation points, but doesn't give enough time to finish what she asks for. I would take her class again.

Robin is a great professor. Her class is hard but fair. She provides great examples in class and the exams are the exact same type of problems as the homework and in class problems. She is helpful in office hours too. The homework is a lot and we'll take a few hours. The challenging but if you come to class and do the problems you will succeed.

I genuinly do not know what is going on in this class. She gets so off topic and jumps around different examples in class. Most of her lectures she goes on a tangent that is irrelevant to her class. This class is very good, and prof. builds on the concepts thoroughly. DO NOT GET BEHIND though, you need to do work before and after class, and practice the assigned textbook problems to succeed. reviews.comment: This class is not easy. I have to go over every exercise before the class to catch up what she teaches.

Her homework is extremely hard. You have to spend a lot of time to do it.(working with your group is a good way to learn) but the exam problem is easier and similar to sample question. She is also a good grader. I suggest the students take her Actg 450
She was a great professor. It is crucial to do the book problems to excel in her class however. She is very nice and energetic even at 8 AM. I would definitely take her class again.

Excellent Teacher!!!  In fact I haven't had a better teacher at the U of O. I think a lot of the people who have given Dr. Clement a poor rating don't study enough.  And clarity is not a problem, so for whoever said clarity was an issue, I think you just need an easier class.  Accounting is by no means a mickey mouse class.
Her teaching style makes it so hard for me to learn anything.  I felt like going to class only confused me more.  And I love how the book used was co-authored by her.

I loved Robin.  I don't understand where everyone else is coming from (other than some people just don't get accounting).  She was always more that willing to explain things two or three times if you didn't understand.  I learned a lot in her class and wish she was teaching 350.
wow! HORRIBLE......where to begin, way too fast and expects us to master the material with little problem when the course is actually quite difficult  dont take her class!!!!
The subject was pretty hard, but those dances made it worth going to class
Fast unorganized lectures,  seemed to know very little, I took nothing out of this class and don't remember many of the key ideas we learned.

She's a horrible teacher! ****!

This teacher is horrible. She expects students to know everything when this is an introductory to accounting class. She goes so fast during lectures so it was hard to keep up with her! I think she is the worst teacher and I will never take another class with her again!

The best intro to PR professor. So kind, understanding, and knowledgeable. Lectures were accompanied by worksheets to apply the concepts. Easyish midterm, optional final.
I love her
I took jcom 203 writing as practice. Great teacher and kind human. I would highly recommend. I was excited to go to her class at 8am.

This is for JCOM 371: Probably one of the three best professors in the SOJC. Cares about every single one of her students and her teaching is super engaging. If you're between selecting professors, choose her 100%
Courtney was a great teacher. The class is based a lot upon revisions and she gives great feedback. It seems like she genuinely cares about improving our writing.

Highly recommend taking this class with Professor Munther. She's by far the best SOJC professor I've had so far. Her lectures are very engaging, she's always very clear about assignments, deadlines, etc. There's only 3 major assignments all term, which are nothing too hard and the midterm/final are online and open note. Take this class!

reviews.comment: Courtney is the best professor I have had at UO. If you can take a class with her, DO IT! Her lectures are very engaging. She uses real world examples and tries to use topics her class is interested in. In-class worksheets most days, so attendance is "mandatory." She is such a sweet, open-minded professor that I hope I have again!!

Courtney Munther is by far the best professor I've taken at UO. She's very nice and approachable and you can tell she really cares about her students. There's like 2 'big' projects throughout the term, which are only 2 pages max, the midterm was online and not in class, and the in-class assignments are done with a group. Take a class with her!!!!
Courtney is a wonderful teacher and I highly recommend taking a class with her. She keeps you engaged and has interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: By far my favorite class this term! Her lectures are clear, concise, and helpful, especially if you are interested in PR like me. 10/10 recommend.

Took this class during COVID. I really enjoyed Courtney! She's personable, kind, and has a lot of great information. This was one of my first journalism classes and she's made the class engaging and informative. There are a few major writing assignments, one midterm (worth a lot of points), some worksheets, but overall it isn't super hard.
She talked about herself the entire time and I didn't learn anything about Public Relations.
Really nice and the lectures were engaging. She discussed her professional experience as a PR practitioner throughout the term which was helpful to supplement the lectures.

Courtney has been my favorite professor in all of my time at UO. I have never had a professor who cares so much about her students. On every big assignment she gives extensive feedback and there are revisions for everything. I met with her multiple times and she is so lovely and always willing to help.

Courtney was an excellent professor for the final class of the Gateway sequence. She presented information about Ad and PR in an accessible way. She also brought in other professor's from the journalism school which gave new perspectives on the material. She always replies to emails. I would highly recommend taking a class with her

Courtney is an amazing professor and is very approachable and kind. She gives great feedback and all of her comments are respectful, insightful and constructive. I really enjoyed taking her class, and I absolutely recommend any of her courses to students; you'll learn a lot and your  writing will greatly improve.

This fundraising for PR topics class was great. The homework was tangible work for local nonprofits that can be used in a portfolio. I learned a lot, the homework was sometimes challenging, but it was helpful.

Courtney is awesome. She's easy going and really approachable which makes class fun. She's always willing to help you if you're confused and shows that she cares about her students. You'll learn a lot about PR from her and she always has real-life stories to explain things. Would definitely take a class again from her!
Courtney is the BEST! She is approachable, gives excellent feedback, and makes herself available outside of class. I highly recommend her!
Textbook definition of a well organized async class! Loved this class. Absolutely no complaints.

reviews.comment: absolutely loved her! she was super nice and her class was super interesting. dont remember having any issues with her at all

Great professor, you can tell she really cares about what she's teaching. GEs can be a bit slow to get back to you but are generous graders. Assignments were easy, final is very time consuming but not hard.
Dr. Cox is an amazing professor. Her lectures are interesting and I had a good time in her class.

Her lectures are so engaging and interesting! Simple annotating assignment due before each lecture, there is a lot of reading but if you don't get to all of it you will be just fine. Midterm and final project very straightforward and the GE's are very helpful with it as well.

Dr. Cox's lectures are fascinating and incredibly engaging. Readings are long, but you are not required to read everything, and are provided for future assignments. She truly uplifts any answers from any student that raises their hand in her class. Highly recommended!
Dr. Cox is amazing I really enjoyed taking this class! It's an easy credit :)

I would say one of the easier Professors I have had yet. Very well respected by class and understand that we are stressed college students. Midterm and Final are both take home and were easy. Pair project that was fairly easy. Easy way to get some credits out the way. She does a survey for attendance.

Dr. Cox is an incredible professor, with amazing and insightful lectures. I felt like she and her GE's were always there to help when I need and very reachable- just an email away!  My one complaint was that the assignment descriptions although very impactful to your grade were very brief with no rubric. 10/10 prof and class!
Extremely incredible intelligent and inspiring
One of my favorite teachers at UO.

Dr Cox is a really amazing professor, really respected by her her students, while also a really fun, relatable, and approachable person. I had her for Intro to African American studies and was a bit nervous to take the class at first. I am glad I stayed, Dr C incorporates a lot of music & art into class & assignments, not just your typical stuff

Doctor C is so intelligent, very accessible, so kind, and makes me want to be a better person. Her lectures are really interesting and she makes you feel comfortable participating. There is a lot of reading in this class but it' doable! She tends to give you the most work the first two weeks so stick around because it gets easier throughout the ter

I'm coming back on here because some of these reviews don't explain how bad she is. This prof assigned us hw but never graded them. She also created teams to compete against the other students but whoever won only got "eternal glory" not extra credit or nothing, along with a massive final project that wasn't even graded. DO NOT take this class

All of the coursework in OE1-3 is about doing the assignments and using them to learn and improve your knowledge in old English. here for a easy language class? it'll be tough, interested in the language and its history? you'll love it!

The class is a lot of work but Dr. Clark is clear about her expectations from the beginning. You have to put in the effort to pass for sure but if you are having trouble Dr. Clark is helpful and in my experience answered emails pretty fast. Like the other person said though the self evaluation part of the class is a pain.

If you do the work and show up consistently, the class is extremely fulfilling. Dr. Clark is very knowledgeable and passionate, she has clear reasons for assigning homework and projects, and she's super accessible in office hours and always happy to help students. Self grading is kind of a nightmare though.

the positive reviews are right that her expectations are clear and she's friendly, but unless you're ready to rearrange your entire life in order to pass her classes, I don't recommend taking them. there's too much work. at the end, you have to write an essay arguing for what grade she should give you, with receipts. it's just not worth the stress

This class has been tough and required a lot of work, but I genuinely don't know where other people are getting the idea that Dr. Clark is mean or doesn't care about her students. reviews.comment: Would not recommend under any circumstances. Would suggest and UO students avoid Old English at all costs. Just a horrible experience of busy work and unpleasant interactions with professor. No sympathy or understanding for students whatsoever.

reviews.comment: I'm surprised by some of these reviews. I've never once seen Dr. Clark be unkind. She is patient and will work with you to help you succeed if you put in the effort. ENG428 could be hard work at times but it was also my first upper division course and I found it manageable. She is extremely knowledgeable and well organized. You'll learn so much.

I usually hate language classes, but I LOVE Old English w/ professor Clark. Even online, she makes the class incredibly fun and rewarding. I don't ever remember having a class where I was just so motivated to learn the material. Professor Clark definitely deserves a higher rating than he has. I would seriously recommend this class to anyone.

literally do not take this class. there's an absurd amount of work and even if you do it all, she doesn't care and won't give you a good grade. If you even dare and try to ask her a question she treats you like you're stupid.

Dr Clark does NOT deserve the rating she has on here. She is very clear about grading and always willing to help you out if youre struggling. Dont take her classes unless youre actually interested in the subject, because you will do a lot of work.

The book you read TWICE and write TWO essays on is horrible, dense and extremely hard to follow let alone enjoy and interact with.

She was the worst teacher I have ever had in college. Actually in my life. She was so rude to me personally and treated me as if I was dumb and a child. I put so much effort into the class and she genuinely did not care.
awful. horrible. she is so mean. do not take ever.
she does not care about you or your success. she will tear you down and is 100 percent rude. she treats the students like the do not matter
worst class and worst teacher i have ever had in my academic career. This class and teacher will just effect your overall grade in a bad way. warning you now.

no no no. Recevied an absolutely horrible grade even when I did all of the ridiculous amount of homework given and put much effort into it. This class isn't even worth it. You don't learn, only get hurt from it.

I AM WARNING YOU DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Not only was the class itself ridiculous, professor clark is completely rude and makes you feel actually horrible as a person. I have never felt picked out and ridiculed by a teacher before. She actually goes out of her way to bring you and your grade down. She looks for reasons to fail you. do not take.

Dr. Clark is clearly an intelligent woman, but she is not very personable & the amount of course work she assigns is ridiculous. I spent between 14-20 hrs on her 4cr class each week & still only ended with a B. During class, she tends to cut her students off mid-thought when she disagrees with them & refuses to entertain points that oppose her own.

I think Dr. Clark is amazing.  She does expect a lot of her students, but I feel like I actually learned things.  That is, I learned about the content, but I also learned a lot of fundamental skills.  I really, really liked the consistency of this course.  I'm much better at finding a thesis statement!  She is honest and hard working.  Three cheers
One of the worst classes I have taken as an English Major, which is unfortunate because I loved the content. More busy work than I have ever done in my life. TERRIBLE.

I found this class quite challenging, but I really did enjoy the class. She is a good teacher and the class discussions were intriguing. I would recommend this class not because it is necessarily easy, but because you get a lot out of the class.
She's a tough teacher but she helps everyone who needs the help. The readings are super interesting and really are fun to read. She's nice but sometimes can be harsh.

friendly professor who seems to enjoy teaching, but is a hard grader!!! She expects you to already know the subject. She allows room for rewrites but only changes the grade unless you rewrite your WHOLE paper. Definitely not a 200 level class!!! Expect ALOT of reading. You've  been warned!!!!

She micromanages everything down to using the bathroom. I took two upper level courses in my major and received A's and then got a C+ in hers. Keep in mind this is an introductory class, so I should be learning about Medieval literature but she runs it like a higher level course. Her lecture were dry and unhelpful. Overall awful class and teacher

Great professor, she really knows her stuff!  There were daily quizzes, but it forced the class to keep up on reading, which let us talk about the text in depth (very helpful when writing papers).  It was a very fun class, but you have to be interested in the subject or else some of the texts might be boring.

I would not recommend taking this class, a ridiculous amount of homework, short essay do every week plus daily quizzes. She is a little too passionate and thinks everyone else should be about medieval readings

For a 100 level class, her expectations were outrageous. A quiz was given everyday in class, lots and lots of readings and journals, etc. Theres a reason there is 20 openings in a 40 person class on the second week of the term.

Her class was well organized and informative with a lot of class discussion and opportunities to get a better understanding of text. Not a professor for people who don?t actually want to work as there was daily readings and quizzes as well as weekly essays.

If you want to be treated like a child, take this class. There was no mutual respect in this class. And although the readings were interesting, her discussion of them was not as informative as they could be. She micromanaged all students to the level of telling them how to email professors and how to read on your own. I was very disappointed.

Quizzes make up 55% of the class grade. No partial credit awarded, quiz averages are often around 4/11. Quizzes are out of 11, includes question 0 which is a math problem not related to the course or rest of the quiz. He is a good lecturer, but due to low performance the entire class is graded based on performance relative to the mean.
better make sure you know everything you've ever known

PHYS 352 is an extremely difficult class. Weekly quizzes make up 40% of the grade, and the final makes up 30%. You will do well if you go to lectures, read the book, and GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Corwin taught well, he is an enjoyable lecturer, but sometimes has unreasonable expectations, but is generally kind and understanding.

I really enjoyed Eric's class. The content was hard, and the homeworks were very difficult. The class is very quiz heavy, but if you actually do the readings, and do the homework, you can do well. Go to lectures, but also do all the readings. There is not enough time in class for him to teach everything so you gotta read the text. Awesome shirts.

reviews.comment: Though Prof. Corwin is entertaining at times and personable to some degree, he holds stubborn values in his grading system. He does not curve anything and will not accommodate for purposes of equity - even when students cannot access the content he provides exams and quizzes on. AVOID.

Prof. Corwin is a great professor, and my favorite to teach physics so far at the University of Oregon. Though the content is tough, he is willing to answer lots of questions and gives lots of resources to build up your skills. Not only is he understanding and caring, but he also brings a light and entertaining demeanor to lectures :)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I like Eric himself a lot, but this class was rough. The quizzes were very tough, and the homework would take me hours to get just some of the problems. He spends basically every lecture answering questions, which means you have to teach yourself the entire course outside of class. Overall, not great, not terrible.

Dr. Corwin teaches in a way where it is clear that he wants the class to understand the material. This can be frustrating as he can spend a lot of time answering questions in lecture. He is always quick to respond and help at any time of day. It must be said that for a class like this one simply has to do a fair amount of learning outside of class.

Never in my life have I encountered a professor that can diminish my interest in a subject so quickly. Utterly baffled at how someone so intelligent can be oblivious to the fact that their class is structured abhorrently. It is not overly difficult if you put in the work, but the deck is stacked against you in many ways. Good luck with this one.

Not exactly sure why some people, especially in this RMP, disliked Corwin; if I were to guess I would place my bets on the fact that some of his students were not cut out for physics in general, and failed to do well in his class as a result. Corwin really IS a good professor. He's likable, reasonable, and willing to compromise.

Corwin himself isn't too bad, though maybe a bit negligent/apathetic but aren't we all. No, what's really bad is just his class. If you're a straight A student you can forget it because he grades on a curve and with his tests it might as well be a gamble where in class you place. He claims his class isn't about memorization but the quizzes disagree
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Corwin has unconventional mannerisms and teaching style that gives him a bad rap. You really can't fail his class unless you don't put effort in, even if it is retroactive effort. His quizzes and tests are difficult to study for, but his lectures are question focused. Do what you can, but cut yourself some slack.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Never met someone that liked Corwin for good reason. His class is awful, the content is hard of course but that's not what makes it bad. Corwin and his style is.

His class is bad. Full stop. As a person he's cool and understanding but I can't imagine anyone getting an A in his class without memorizing every homework question and answer. I could write an essay about what's wrong with his class but there's a character limit. It's awful.

His class is hard, His lectures are a little disorganized and not particularly helpful towards the homework and quizzes. However, he cares a lot, considers feed back and will go out of his way to help you. He does want you to feel dumb in class, but only so you can learn from being wrong, which still doesn't feel good. Not as bad as his score here.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Eric is a wonderful person who cares more about learning how things work than memorizing facts. The material he teaches in this class is very hard but if you ask questions he will go over it multiple times until everybody gets it. Homework is due on Mondays and you will get 20/30 points just for correcting your homework.

He's okay, Most of the time he teaches material that is only partially part of the lab. He also thinks that the class already understands a lot more than they really do. Showing up for lecture rarely helped me in the lab. But, his lectures are interesting, fun, and challenging. He likes to make you think about problems instead of giving the answer.
we were encouraged to ask stupid questions and be wrong, usually he helped us figure out answers on our own instead of just telling us.

This professor is horrible. Please stay away before you regret it. Eric shows no enthusiasm and does the bare minimum  in class. He is careless and the class does not make sense one bit. Nothing had correlated from class "lecture" to homework to tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Stay away at all costs. Doesn't explain concepts well at all. Doesn't use powerpoints only uses blackboard during lecture. Doesn't answer questions well at all. Homework doesn't correlate with class at all. Only good thing is the GTF. Very difficult to study for tests because there's minimal material that's available to study.

Dan was an amazing professor, He's the only professor I've had who kept me engaged for the entire two hour lecture. I would 100% take this class again. He's funny, you can tell he's super into what he does and his stories are amazing. Weekly quizzes but the answers are in the slides, and the final is easy as long as you mostly pay attention.

I LOVE AN ENGAGING LECTURER! You don't have to show up but it makes the class so much more enjoyable and way easier to pass the final (especially, the map portion). Dan is also quite funny and brings in both student experiences and his own. Incredibly knowledgeable about the backcountry. Even if you have no interest in the outdoors, take the class!

Professor Crow is the best. Taking Wilderness Survival will teach you so many amazing skills and is an easy A if you show up to lectures and pay attention. I would highly recommend taking wilderness survival if you are at all interested in outdoorsy life.
Really great teacher and class. I learned a lot and laughed a lot as well. I loved Dan and his insights on many years in the backcountry.

Professor Crowe rocks so much and has enough information and love for his subject for the passionate people and enough understanding and basic respect for the not-passionate students. He makes this class interesting even when the subject matter isn't and he doesn't seem to take anything personally. Great guy and a fair and respectable teacher.

Dan is super nice and even though the class is about two hours, it never feels that long as his lectures are very engaging. He has a lot of experience in this field and shares a lot of funny/ interesting stories. I learned a lot from this class, and the material we covered was super interesting!!
Great lecturer for the Outdoor Program at UO. Definitely recommend. Very fun class.

100 and 200 level lectures feel very old-fashioned, the slides are very convoluted, and the class material was never conveyed well. She is kind one-on-one, though, but if you have the opportunity to take class with someone else, you should!

If you're not willing to spend hours a day studying, don't take this class.The material we discuss is vague and quick because she feels the need to get in as much material as possible instead of focusing on subjects the class struggles with. I talked to my fellow classmates and all of them had a C average. Ruthless grader, would not recommend.

This is truly just the worst course, content doesn't make sense, she doesn't take time to review what people are struggling in. She's rude to students and does not accommodate at all. I have dreaded attending her class every day this term and cannot stress enough she should be removed from the University of Oregon staff.

very personal class, you will know everyone's name by the end because there's at least 3-4 times per class where you will have to speak to someone in french. if i could describe her in one sentence, i'd go with: tough, but fair.

Personally, wonderful woman, but one of the toughest graders I've had. That being said, I learned a lot more than I did with the TA's, but as a non-French major, this class easily took up the majority of my homework and study time. Toughest B I've ever gotten at the 200 level. She will not bend any rules written in the syllabus, so read it.

reviews.comment: She is a really sweet lady, however, her class is so difficult. Beware of hours of homework and harsh grading.

reviews.comment: teachs french in a very old school way, took french for 6 years, definitely my least favorite french teacher

I saw this page before taking 111 and it nearly scared me off. However, I've found Mme Dickey to be a really sweet person, and the most effective language teacher I've ever had. HOURS of homework, yes, but if you stay on top of it you'll be completely fine. Especially if you've ever taken an hnrs/AP/IB class, this level of work will feel familiar.

Expect 2-3 hours of homework per night, no late work is accepted ever. I learned so much from this class but it took up all of my time and made me extremely burnt out and stressed. For a 101 level class this course is much more intense than I expected.
This was the worst class I have ever taken. She destroyed my love for french. It was miserable. I literally switched to a bachelors of science because of this class.

Her cold-calling in class is brutal, and she has no forgiveness for late work. Uses a document entirely in French to tell you what homework you have daily, and won't always remind you when you actually need to pay attention to it. Be ready to devote at least 10-15 hours per week on her class, and avoid her 8am at all costs.

reviews.comment: She does not support her students getting outside tutoring and will accuse you of cheating if you do. She gives an INSANE amount of homework that cannot be turned in late. She is very rude and aggressive and will shame students for falling behind  She failed me with no warning and her syllabus was all in French so I couldn't understand it. RUN AWAY

Mme Dickey makes learning French WAY harder than it should be due to pointless rules and almost no flexibility no matter the circumstances. She is extremely condescending of her students. I have more homework for her class than I do for all my other classes combined. I would write way more if there was no character limit.

Mme Dickey is a fine teacher. Her course load is heavy but it *is* a five-credit class and your grammar/syntax will drastically improve. I learned a lot but it isn't easy to get a high grade in the class, she is a very tough grader. Advocate for yourself and don't be afraid to reach out, above all she is more than willing to give feedback.

I was nervous for every class. She cold-calls students very often, and is very open about when she's disappointed. She knows her stuff, but the courseload for this class was unreasonable. She expects students to teach themselves and the lectures are only meant to be a rapid review. I'm actively trying to get out of her 112 class.

This instructor give an extreme amount of homework needlessly. Is completely unwilling to listen to what her students need. Doesn't teach at all and if you say that you are struggling, she will just tell you to read your book more.
Madame Dickey is INTENSE. She gives an absurd amount of homework and forces you to participate in class, which made me anxious the whole time. She's very knowledgeable, but MAN was this class hard.

She's terrible, I had to drop the class because the first day she gives 14 assignments due BEFORE the next class.  She doesn't allow students to leave the class for any reason, even going to the bathroom.  She assigns huge amounts of homework, and requires so much printing.  If you are a freshman, or new to French, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just wanted to say that completing the 100-level sequence with Dickey as the course supervisor was one of the most difficult, unfair, and time-consuming things EVER. You're expected to learn major structural concepts that take years to master, crammed into an hour & twenty. Unfair to students and GE's forced to learn/teach an impossible structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor was really nice in person, but with hundreds; and I mean hundreds of online assignments, it was really hard to even get the credits for the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This lady was literally so rude and unhelpful that I had to drop this class.

Madame Dickey is an excellent teacher. You can tell she has been doing this for a while. Although the class and material is hard she is accessible for help and answers emails very fast. There is a lot of homework on the online portion of the class but plenty of in class examples and review. I recommend connie for anyone starting to learn French.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dickey is a good French teacher. She gives a lot of feedback and is always available to help outside of class. Her class is difficult with lots of homework, but her tests and essays are easy to succeed on if you study. I don't understand the reviews saying she was condescending; that wasn't my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Connie is an incredibly tough grader and only speaks in French with a beginning-level class. If you cannot ask a question in French, she will not answer it, she puts students on the spot daily, gives feedback in illegible writing ONLY in French, and is incredibly passive-aggressive with students. If you are a beginning French student STAY AWAY.

Do not take any class with Dickey. She gives no feedback, doesn't help solve your problems or explain, but rather scold you for not knowing. I had upwards of 4hrs of homework every day (not just on days of the class). I have learned nothing. I switched my degree to a BS this afternoon, which sucks because I LOVE romance languages and she ruined it.

She obviously knows French but is a human who severely struggles to understand other humans. She is by no means a people person. She is passive-aggressive and condescending. Her teaching methods are prehistoric. If you are somebody who feels you deserve to be treated like an adult, Connie is not your gal. As a female, I need to use the bathroom.

Connie is very passionate about French. She constantly belittles students for essentially not TEACHING THEMSELVES before class. She claims that lectures are just review, and humiliates students daily. She's a self-anointed autocrat who punishes struggling students and teaches like a 1960s Nun, and I'm sure if allowed she'd use corporal punishment.

She is not a good teacher. Shes difficult to reason with, assigns a lot of homework/ busy work on Mindtap, wont let you use the restroom, and doesnt explain things clearly. The only thing shes sometimes good about is extensions she will usually give you one but not always. Shes nice but a hard grader. Overall I wouldnt take her again.

Connie was not very clear with her expectations and assigns a lot of assignments on MindTap. You must purchase the textbook package, but it is used for the next course as well. You are paired with a student in France that you have to talk to 4 times and there are 4 essays throughout the term. Connie can be hard to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Connie D. is a natural language teacher. She puts endless work into her class and it very much shows through the always-informative lectures, abundance of information of Canvas, and accessibility outside of class. She knows French inside and out. If you put effort into her class and participate, you will have a very easy time learning French.

Madame was a really kind and helpful professor, but her class is definitely no joke. It is a lot of homework and participation, and she expects a lot of outside work for the class, including "10 minute conversations with your peers" outside of class every day. She was really kind but also really tough, so be warned!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Connie is a great professor that really cares about her students. She is a tough grader, so I think she needs to chill with that, but other than that, I enjoyed her class. She is very nice and wants the best for her students. She replies to emails on time and is respectful. However, because of how she grades, I wouldn't take her again...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a really nice person and just strict on grading! She cares about students and gives really clear explanations on grammar! I Also, she gives clear feedback on every tests and homework. think she is really helpful for your French knowledges but if you want a easy class to take, this class is not your choice!

This professor was so great for FR 111! She was so helpful whenever I needed it, and very flexible with meeting times. She gave a lot of feedback on our longer essays, but never marked down too many points for small mistakes. She really helped me improve my French ability; I really enjoyed her as a professor.

Lectures not too boring, attendance is 10% of grade, she goes through example problems & uploads notes.
