Four assignments, 20% total, lowest score dropped, takes about 2 to 3hrs, exams have similar questions. One midterm worth 30% and one final worth 40%. Practice exams provide a very accurate representation of the content on exams. No notes.

Honestly Anca's lectures in this class have helped me understand a lot of concepts I was previously struggling with in econ. She's great at explaining the intuition behind ideas. Lectures are a mix of slides and handwritten examples, and exams feel easy if you show up to class regularly and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't sign up for her! Anwful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No in every way possible.

As an online instructor she's a complete disaster. Dogmatic in approach and temperament Tests were a race against the clock because she's convinced the whole world is going to cheat and the less time she gives everyone the less time 2 or 3 people will have to game the system. Avoid at all costs...
Tests are rough, but if you go to class she covers most of the material and has a bunch of resources to help comprehend the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think Anca is a fine teacher. I learned a lot about outsourcing. Tests aren't hard if you take the class seriously. However many students don't take it seriously. I can't count how many were playing with their cellphones during lecture instead of taking notes.

So basically she's a super nice person and willing to talk more during office hour but the midterm and final exams this term are extremely hard for some reason. Final exam is worth 40% of our final grade and is  very different from the practice exams. Not sure if there will be a huge curve.
Lectures are very well organized and she was great at explaining concepts. Very approachable and nice to talk to. Exams are not easy but if you do the homework and sample tests you should be fine.
Will not email you back. Or if she does it will be to come to her office hours. Does not communicate well in person either.

She is really helpfull teacher and she could help you outside classroom too. I took 2 classes with her which are 481 internation Ec 481and globalaization410 both of them proabaly same subject. I really recommend take these classes with her
Nice, helpful, overall good lecturer.

Great Professor.  Organized lectures and goes over everything, that was discussed in the book, in class.  Willing to help outside of class.  If you go to class, take notes, and read the book you'll do fine.

Great lectures and makes it engaging instead of just talking at you, many students participated because of this. Wasn't a fan of lab group work that had to be done outside of class, but other than that it was chill. She drops the lowest exam so i skipped the final and ended with an A+. Pay attention and you'll pass!

Cristin is by far the best STEM prof I've had at UO. She drops your lowest test, lab, attendance score and more. She gives good simple explanations that makes content easy to digest. She doesn't give clicker problems because she wants class collaboration. Tests are very similar to the practice tests/ ungraded problem sets. She wants you to succeed.

Try to do good on the 2 midterms so you don't have to take the final. It is so much than the other tests and study material did not help at all, the average was a 38. Other than that if you study and do good on all the canvas assignment you can succeed. Cristin is very nice and helpful.

Very nice professor, tests were graded by GEs and sometimes a little too harshly graded. Read the lab material ahead of time, it can really bring your grade down as they are graded harshly as well (by GE)

Cristin herself is a great lecturer and made the material easier to digest. However, the tests are very difficult despite being able to use notes. Attendance is weighted pretty heavily, and she expects you to spend much of your time on her class. Make sure that everyone in your group proofreads your lab assignments because it can tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: beware of fill in the blank on tests

She taught alongside Tobias in 213 last spring term and she was genuinely the nicest professor I have ever met. She took tough concepts and made them so easy to understand. She also was super invested in the class and took time to meet a lot of people and get to know them. She is awesome
She is a very good professor! She explains things well and makes a normally difficult class do-able.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cristin gives tough tests, and several of them, but she does teach you all the material you need to know in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cristin was a fantastic professor who did a great job of explaining concepts. She truly wanted her students to understand the material. Going to office hours, doing the practice problem sets, and studying hard are necessary for success. There's no major surprises on quizzes or exams as long as you study and ask for help when needed.

she's unclear with instruction and poor at explaining concepts. she seems confused while she's teaching. this class is easy however if you can take it with anyone else do it. honestly just really not a fan of her

honestly, the class itself wasn't difficult however she is terrible at explaining the concepts and placing the concepts into any kind of context. when asked questions in class she is unable to answer them. she is unclear and confusing with her instruction. you'll have to learn from the book and teach yourself cause she's definitely not

Surprisingly easy course, but also surprisingly boring.  It wouldn't be hard to get an A and never go to class, but she uses iClickers to ensure attendance.  Plus, she screeches at students who pack up early (and then keeps all 200+ late regularly).
Pretty good professor. I understood her lectures and didn't find the concepts too difficult. I wouldn't complain if I she taught another one of my classes.
Nice person, but didn't enjoy her lectures or the project. It felt exactly like a high school class. The exams are pretty easy though, it's not difficult to get an A.

I've had two classes from Cristin, she puts effort into her lectures and is very responsive to questions. If she doesn't know the answer to something in class and you are actually interested enough in your own question to follow up after class she will gladly answer your questions via email etc. She has reasonable expectations. Quality instructor.

Teaching style is very slow, wastes a lot of time, pauses after every slide to double check if there are any questions, doesn't answer said questions clearly anyway. Kind of all over the place, loses track of her place in slides a lot. Takes way too much time for clicker questions. She's nice and grades fairly easy, but not an effective teacher.

didn't really like her teaching style, and the labs were the hugest waste of my time, but the class was easy. if you show up to class and pay attention you should get a solid B i f not A.  don't expect her to answer any questions in class clearly,
boring. if you've taken bio in high school you'll be fine in class. I hate the clickers.
Great teacher and nice person. Her tests aren't too bad and she's real easy going.
did not like her teaching style, really monotone and was scatterbrained.

Relies heavily on GTF grading and dont check them for fairness (only checks 1 from each gtf). Marks down points for missing 1 word(concept of question stated in answer). On the plus no muti choice tests.

Class was fine. There are 3 homework assignments, 2 midterms and a final. The test are short answer. Class is not bad at all, if you try you could get an A. If you show up and do the work you can get a solid C
Kristin was a great teacher.  The class was new for her, but she had a great understanding of the material.  A pleasure to work with.

Dr. Tozer is so awesome! The lectures are long and kinda boring (I am not a geology major), but attendance isn't mandatory. The assignments were pretty interesting and self explanatory. The final exam is online which is super nice. I highly recomend going to his office hours! He is really funny and will walk you through the assignments.

This is a great class for learning about the geology of glaciers and mountains. Lectures were super long and could get a little boring if you are not a geology major. The second day of class each week is mandatory and you will want to do if you want a good grade. Craig is very passionate about what he teaches and brings in samples.

I LOVE HIM!! His online canvas lectures are funny and engaging (as engaging as an online lecture can be...) and he is clearly passionate about what he teaches. Very kind and will basically give you the lab answers if you show up for office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is overly critical on assignments, and does not allow you to give your own answers based off previous knowledge. He has no grace for struggling to decipher very blurry images and does not give any partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You do a lab once a week, watch a video and answer questions, and have 3 tests. I am bad at science, but he is super helpful if you have questions. I got bad grades on all three tests, and he let me retake them to get a better grade. The tests are taken at home with no lockdown browser. You could only show up on Wednesdays and still pass.

You talk A LOT about rocks as well as glaciers, volcanoes, and tsunamis. Class lectures are monotone and long. Material was fine enough to understand with easy tests, since they were take home. A few of the labs would be harder if you didn't go to class. Craig is a super nice guy and loved getting asked questions. Great Professor overall.
Super nice guy. Easy class and interesting if you're into rock formations, mountains, glaciers.

Cool guy, knowledgeable. Lectures were very monotone. The information was interesting at times for sure, but I found myself struggling to pay attention due to the presentation of the material. I think if he had better delivery of the course material, this would be a 10/10 class. Assignments are pretty easy and not too many of them.

Super awesome professor. He is incredibly supportive will help/ walk you through any challenges you may have in the class. The class is lab heavy and the lectures can feel very long but overall really interesting class, especially if you love nature. Craig is the best! Thanks for being a great professor!

Prof. Tozer really does love geology and earth studies and that shows in his lectures. He is cool, funny and caring. The topic itself however, is ultimately incredibly boring to someone who isn't majoring in it. ERTH202 is interesting at times, the tests are quite hard though so beware. I'd recommend a different class just to get a science credit.
easy enough. Long lectures.
This dude is really cool I very much enjoyed this class, the material is not super hard but it's just a fun class to take definitely recommend

Craig is a great professor and cares about his work and his students. His lectures are a little dense and you don't need to come to class to pass or get the material. He posts everything on canvas and his page is well organized. Expect 2 online midterms and an online final, with 3-4 busy work assignments a week.
Craig is a great guy, but not a good teacher. His lectures were a cure for insomnia. Maybe if you are more into earth science you would like it, but it was very boring.

Prof Tozer is kind and funny, but the 2 hour lecture period makes it almost impossible to focus plus his lectures are hundreds of slides long making it difficult to review by yourself. The class is composed of weekly labs (which are VERY hard), weekly discussion posts, 3 online exams, and some video-viewing assignments.

Craig is a really nice person, but his lectures were hard to sit through. The weekly assignments are time consuming (1-2 hour long films primarily) and you hardly ever get full points on assignments. The tests were very hard. He is knowledgable and passionate about the topic and will gladly answer questions if you have any.
A dreadful drag of a class, sitting through all 2 hours with his fairly boring style was a struggle every single time

Although Crag seems like a nice guy, the amount of work in this class is ridiculous. His homework is based on movies he makes us watch every week and it's at least an hour long. If you're lucky it's on YouTube so you can see the transcript. Even if you get the answer right he doesn't give full credit on the assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There was no midterm or final, you just did the weekly assignments, which were philosophy of science questions, watching a movie and responding to questions, and a few quizzes with unlimited attempts to complete, and get the grade you want. The subjects were interesting, and if you have an ERTH background you'll be good! Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Craig is the kindest, most caring professor I've had in the ERTH / GEOG department. His lectures are interesting, fun, and he is always willing to answer your questions. I loved his ERTH 308 class and would highly recommend taking one of his courses !! 11/10 recommend!
This class is super interesting and Craig is very passionate and engaging. This class is lecture heavy and has weekly group projects but overall not too difficult to receive an A.

He's a funny guy, but he grades ridiculously tough for someone who gets his labs and video homework off the internet. I'm talking 50% for missing 2 questions on a fully completed 10+ question assignment.

Craig is obviously extremely passionate about the natural earth that he teaches about. He gives interesting lectures, and the majority of the homework is watching cool videos and answering questions on them. He is funny, kind, and entertaining.

There are 2 assignments a week - a lab & video q's. Both are easy & take minimal time. Lectures can be lengthy, but you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. He even brought his rock collection to class once. No midterm/final. There are 3 exams during the term. They're online & have no time limit. You have 4 days to do them.

Craig is the nicest guy ever. Takes classes on field trips when he can, even managed to take us to a "living fossil" tree on campus during covid when he couldn't pack us all into a bus. He breaks up lectures by showing pictures of himself at the places he talks about. The homework is also super easy. I highly recommend his class.

Craig is the nicest guy. He loves his subject so much, he even takes the class on field trips! Pre-covid, at least. But with us, he tried, and he took us to a tree at the school that was special and a living fossil! He shows pictures of himself visiting the places we talk about to break up the lecture. Such a nice person, and homework was easy.

Tozer is a fun professor and always wears shirts that match what his lecture is going to be about. However, as a non science student, this class is very challenging. The course preview said it was for non science majors but Tozer expects his students to know a lot more about geologic formations of the PNW and plate rates. Lots of homework.

Makes class accessible for all of his students and is passionate about what he does. Incredibly understanding and kind and always willing to help with labs or answer questions. Craig manages to be a great professor without making his class unbearably stressful and is overall such a chill, down to earth guy. Highly recommend if you like geology.

Only take this class if you are sure you can make it to every field trip because if you can't, you won't pass. Homework is very useful and actually prepares you for real field work. Craig is one of the sweetest professors and wants you to learn and succeed. You build amazing skills you wouldn't learn otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A. Craig tries to make it as stress free as possible. Not sure what an earlier reviewer meant about labs being group projects, I always did the labs entirely on my own. I think he just gives you the option of working on it as a group if you want to!

Tozer's vibe is perfect. He doesn't want the class to stress you out and it shows. Labs are a bit annoying because they are group work and group projects suck. But Show up to class and pay attention and its an easy A.

He loves what he teaches and writes lessons as if he was speaking to you, so lots of funny side notes and emojis like this :-) (dude, the moustache). He learns along with you and admits when he does not understand something. Lots of reading and movies, but he tells you what is just for fun, so no biggie. Lectures are hilarious!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Easy, straightforward class. There are "labs" in class and weekly assignments consist of watching short films and answering questions. Professor Tozer is one of the nicest and he genuinely cares about students.

Criag Tozer is really caring and just wants to help you be sucessful in the class. I am not really good at science but thic class was still enjoyable. The tests are kinda hard but he is really accessible if you need help.
be ready for reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Craig is a good professor-funny, and very agreeable. His classes are well organized, and he is flexible where other instructors may just say "tough luck." Good for both majors and non-majors.

If you are into this class (Mountains and Glaciers,) then I'm sure that Tozer is a good instructor. For me I was not into the material so it was tougher. Sometimes directions and help were not clear enough.

He doesn't grade things on time. I was doing incredibly well at the beginning of the course. Then he waited until finals week to input about 8 weeks worth of assignments. My grade dropped a full letter. I couldn't correct my mistake for future assignments because he never really gave me a chance.

Geology isn't usually an interesting topic but Craig does a great job of teaching it. Lectures are a bit dry but interesting and he's a very nice guy. The book reading isn't that helpful and lecture slides online are pretty much copies of what he says in class. Watch the videos but just read if you feel like it. You're in good hands.

If you're looking at taking a geology class take it with Craig.  His tests are not to difficult at all.  He's really passionate about what he teaches and he keeps his lectures entertaining.  He really wants everyone to do well in his class.

Craig is an awesome, passionate professor. He gives you lots of resources to learn with and his lectures are very effective. His tests/assignments were not too difficult. His online commentary is pretty hilarious. He's a nice guy and I definitely recommend him and the class.

This class was extremely challenging. SO much reading for an intro class and you will need to reference it in the essay-based midterm and final. Cramer is super passionate about the topics taught in the class and I enjoyed listening to her talk, but overall, this class just gave me too much stress when I'm not even a poli-sci major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jane Cramer is one of the smartest people I have ever witnessed in my life. Her Intro to IR class was certainly not easy but her genius-ness inspired me to work hard and I got an A. Her lectures are fascinating and I have genuinely never learned so much from a class in my entire life. Highly recommend if you are even slightly interested in IR.

Cramer might be scary at first but is genuinely the best professor at UO. She is so passionate and you just need to show a little bit of effort and she'll reciprocate. Everyone I have talked to about Cramer loves her. DONT BE SCARED OF HER OLD REVIEWS!! She'll challenge you but you learn sooooo much. Take her you wont regret it

Take her classes. She can be eccentric and her exams are tough, but it's so worth it. The content she teaches is incredibly relevant, and we've literally predicted wars in her class two weeks before they happened.

Cramers class is extremely reading heavy, hard tests, and there isn't much preparation for them. Lectures are long and feel very overwhelming, covering a plethora of topics, without diving deep. The grading system is not clear, so you don't know what grade you have until the END of term. For your GPA, do not take this. Not a 200, more like 400.

She is very smart, and REALLY knows what she is talking about. At times it can be a bit overwhelming just because she expects us to know a lot of background information, but if you can just quick google stuff during class you should be good. The organization of the class was a bit confusing, but you are prepared well for the midterm and the final.

Took a bunch of IR classes with her and did honors thesis with her. Very thorough lectures and materials. Emphasizes seriousness of each subject. As long as you learn and understand the concepts, you will ace the exams.

I think she does a good job at teaching a lot but it is not organized at all. I was in her Intro to IR and it was crazy. As a first term freshman it was very overwhelming. She has a BUNCH of weekly readings with write up summaries and full chapters you have to read to understand the class. She is also a super harsh tester for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cramer has made me a better student, not only have I loved every class I've taken with her, but they have completely influenced my perspective on the world. The classes can be tough, but the development and career readiness I have gained have been worth it. Cramer is a remarkable woman, and I'll always remember her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The first class I took w/ Cramer I thought she was cold and intimidating but the more I've seen from her, she is an amazing teacher with insane amounts of knowledge. Her classes will push you and you can't BS them but you'll learn a lot if you immerse yourself. She isn't a hard greater imo and she wants you to succeed just a really stressful class.

Professor Cramer is my favorite instructor I have ever had. She is so knowledgable on every subject she teaches. I took her fall term of this year and had to take her again, and I will be taking any other courses she teaches in the future. Put in the work and you will succeed, I have learned for much from her.

I was really excited to take Cramer because she is a PS icon but I am less than impressed. She goes on tangents, hard to keep up with her. Graded by only 2 midterms, 1 essay, and 1 final. During presentations, she shakes her head, makes faces, and then at the end she explains in front of everyone what you said that was wrong. Humiliation ritual.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lovely professor! Cramer was my first political science professor, and her quality has set a high bar for my future instructors. While I don't have a great frame of reference, from my experience and what I've gathered this is a very challenging class. Straightforward. Do the readings. Really get to know them. Hard class to get an A in, but you can!

Professor Cramer was an amazing educator who cares deeply about International Relations and understands the field deeply. The readings are interesting and relevant. Professor Cramer's lectures often went off on insightful tangents regarding her expertise in nuclear weapons. Overall a rewarding class if you are engaged and do the readings.

Jane is great. Sure she goes on tangents about nukes and stuff, but she cares a lot about what she does. She is super passionate and I would be more than glad to take her class again. There is just a good amount of reading to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Truly one of, if not the best, political science professors I've had the pleasure of taking a class with, Jane is an extremely passionate lecturer who loves her students and the material she teaches. Quite literally, she is one of the smartest people I've ever met, and her lectures reflect this.

I took International Relations (PS 205) from her in Fall 2023. While there is an immense amount of reading, she summarizes what you need to know from the readings in the lectures, so you don't actually have to read if you attend lecture consistently. I would also highly recommend my GE - Robin Bracket. Long, essay-style midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am in love with Jane Cramer. She is the coolest person ever and I want to be her friend so I can learn her whole life story. This was my favorite class I have ever taken. She is so passionate about nuclear politics and I loved having her yell at me every day about bombs.  This class was pretty hard, daily pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There was genuinely 6 hours of reading every week but I feel much more knowledgable about nuclear politics. She is very funny and lectures are mostly engaging, but you will have no idea what is going on if you don't read. For the tests she gives 20 possible questions you could have then only asks 6, but I highly encourage you to take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of reading, but the subject topic was incredibly interesting to me and Professor Cramer made it very engaging. Difficult to get an A but relatively easy to get in the B range as long as you keep up with the reading. She's very good at conveying the gravity of the subject matter and I would certainly take another of her classes.

PS440 PS384 PS479
This is my favorite professor at the University of Oregon. She is unbelievably knowledgeable about foreign policy and her passion comes through in every single lecture. Her exams are tough and her classes are a lot of work towards the end of the term, but she is very open and excited to help during office hours or after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jane Cramer is absurdly knowledgeable about nuclear proliferation and will talk to you for hours about if you want. That being said, her class is incredibly difficult with daily quizzes and lots of reading. You get out exactly what you put in, so work hard and it will be a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cramer is excellent. She is so knowledgeable and will talk to you about nuclear proliferation for hours if you'd like. Her classes are infamously hard, so if that isn't your speed I'd take different classes. However, I learned at a rapid pace and with high retention due to how the class was structured. Go to office hours!

Immensely knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches. Her class was super interesting and informative. Not an easy class whatsoever, definitely need to put in a lot of effort to get a desirable result.

Dr. Cramer is a LEGEND! She knows so much abt what she teaches, and clearly cares about the subject and her students so much. The only ppl who dont like her class are ppl who just want an easy A and dont care to work at all. I looked forward to her class every day, and i learned so much from her and the amazing readings she assigned.

This has been the best Political Science class Ive taken at the UO. Extremely informative and interesting. Hasn't been a boring class yet and uses real world examples. Professor Cramer is funny and knowledgeable about subject she teaches. There's lots of readings but she doesn't grade you hard. She cares that your trying and interested in the topic
Does not round grades (.1%) but excellent lecturer and the workload was fairly straight forward. Go to review sections/office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Is knowledgeable in her field but lectures and slides are unorganized, which makes studying for exams hard, even with study guides. "You should know this by now" attitude towards questions makes it scary to even raise your hand, but get over being embarrassed, and she can help. Not a class for the faint of heart so be ready if you registered for it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have had Jane for 2 classes now, and plan on taking more next term. Her quizzes and final are tough, but she is accessible after class or during office hours. She is incredibly passionate about what she does! Her lectures are always interesting and she is funny. Don't take her class if you want to skirt by with an easy A.

This class is very intimidating and not a good introduction to political science. The professor goes on rants about nuclear power and stresses out and just rambles about things that have nothing to do with the course. She is passionate but makes no sense and is hard to follow in lectures. She expects a deep understanding of content to even pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: i have taken 440 and 284 with Cramer and can confidently say she is my favorite professor I've ever had. She is incredibly knowledgeable and engaging and has provoking classes. Grading is tough buy you will learn A LOT if you want to. Don't expect an easy A in any of her classes: take her classes if you are actually interested in the subject

If you are looking for 400 level poly sci classes take anyone else. For even a B on a quiz you are expected to write 1500 words in 20 minutes per quiz, for an A you need to remember every page of the all the 400 pages of reading a week. The TA grades as if we are at Harvard law. For the final you will have to dedicate your whole week to this class.

PS 440 is the worst class I have ever taken. Jane Cramers lectures are chaotic and confusing. The quizzes are based ONLY on readings and there’s at least 150 pages of reading a week. The quizzes are closed note and closed book, but we are expected to quote the readings for a good grade. Haifa (GE) gave no feedback and hard to communicate with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from her class, but very little from her that's actually on quizzes. There's 4-5 20+ page scholarly readings a week and quizzes are entirely based on them. Grading is harsh as I've gotten 85/100 marks with no criticisms. She's harder than she needs to be and she thinks her class is the most important thing in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: PS205 was admittedly a very difficult class, but Cramer herself was a super engaging professor. I took the class as a gen ed, and with doing most of the weekly readings, paying attention in class and studying for tests, the class was easily passable. Cramer's passionate about the subject and it shows. Make friends to work/study with!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jane's lectures were one of the most interesting things I had heard. She focuses on real-world events and makes sure to repeat the information so that you can understand and learn it. The midterm and final are set up to be hard but do the paper and work with your GEs and you'll be set

To be honest the class was a little difficult for me the first few weeks because of all the assigned readings the professor would assign (as well as the online quizzes). Though it's not that bad of a class once you get the hang of it. What I would recommend is reading the first of the three readings each week and finding the summaries online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good intro professor for me and my friends. We loved taking the class. I understand why she has bad reviews but if you are a poli sci major that doesn't mind a quirky teaching style it is good. You have to be interested in what she teaches to get the enjoyment of going to class. She is friendly and funny and I loved taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Cramer is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Her lectures are very fun but not mandatory. The reading in this class is heavy. The weekly readings are more important than the textbook, which is important. Grades are led by the midterm and final, essay q's based heavily on the readings. Fun content, not an "easy" class

This professor has student success as first priority. In the midst of this pandemic, class was delivered in-person, and available via Zoom. This made a WORLD of positive difference for my success. Her knowledgeability and passion made class so engaging. The content of the course is SO valuable and I want everyone I know to hear what she has to say.

I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone unless they have time to read 150+ pages every week. The most challenging parts of this class are the midterm and final exams. We're graded on our ability to cite readings in our answers to multiple essay questions, but the test is closed notes which makes it difficult to quote the weekly readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just now realizing late in the semester that there are tons of work I have never heard of due because she doesn't put them on canvas like everything else that is due. It was sort of mentioned in the syllabus but it was very unclear and confusing. Would have graded higher prior to tonight if she had posted out work on canvas where EVERYTHING ELSE IS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Cramer is an extremely tough professor. She is very opinionated and wants you to articulate her opinions on quizzes and papers. Expect multiple lengthy readings every week. The class is fascinating, however Cramer makes the course far too challenging to really succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jane is super knowledgeable about her topic, dont recommend this class if you have no interest in nuclear war. Quizzes and final are super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely do not take this course if it's remote/online. There's DENSE readings that take up more than 15 hours a week PLUS lectures. It's not worth it for the grades, she grades WAY too hard. She also has quizzes that she "gives" the prompts to, but gives 20 prompts and only assigns 3, so studying will take up ALL YOUR TIME. Never taking her again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer gave really insightful lectures, and even though she went on tangents sometimes, she would never test on stuff she didn't talk about in class. Her classes were writing heavy, but it was nice to go into a final only worth 20% because of all the essays. There were no close-book quizzes , and she's one of my favorite professors in PS.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took the class as an online course so she had little to do. Only grade the 4 essays, which are the only "big tests", her prompts were always confusing too many questions for one prompt, imo. But also a very slow grader which makes it hard to know your progress since its all you have graded by her

Much supplementing course material is available online, which helps because this professor did not teach at all in the online course, only assigned readings. The textbook can be rather dense, but participation is easy and only graded by completion. Many long papers that feel like busy work, and the final is a very long research paper.
Love her! I wanna take another class from her soon! she is so passionate about her field and brings that into the classroom. She keeps your attention and is crazy funny and so smart!

Though Cramer is obviously well versed in her field, I found her lectures to be completely boring and overall not very helpful. I wouldn't take this class unless you want to waste time listening to her go off on random tangents. She is totally passionate and educated in all that she lectures about, but I wouldn't recommend taking this class .

Easily my least favorite professor I've had. We had weekly reading out of the textbook and at least three usually lengthy articles, but never went over the concepts in lecture. During lecture, she would usually rant about nuclear weapons or other topics she found important which never related to the readings. Boring lectures. Do not take this class

The class is challenging because it's a lot of dense information to be a substantial intro course, but I don't think that's her fault. I took it in four weeks online and pulled an A-. She made it clear what would be on the final, so take good notes and study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst professor I ever came across. Apart from dense readings the slides are too long and have too much information. I asked for help on the quizzes and did a bit better on them, but didn't get the grade I wanted. I feel like I wasted my time and I really put effort into this class but I ended up going straight to the trash!

50% if your grade is based on chapter quizzes (closed book) with questions that are often unclear. 50% of your grade is based on a final or a research paper. You are completely limited to the topic, she will chose for you. Doesn't always get back to you. Obviously gets upset when one asked for clarification. 4 yrs at UO, worst experience by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was the most difficult of any class I have taken. Cramer assigns a LOT of very DENSE readings, and you won't pass the tests if you do not read them! That being said, you get a lot out of it if you try! Cramer's a very knowledgeable and respected Professor in her field and she's passionate about her work, which comes out in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She knows a lot about what she teaches and is super passionate about it- theres not very much work and you can do well without reading the textbook. What sucks is that she rambles too much about her own agenda and goes on tangents.. towards the end of class she tries to yell super loud so we won't pack up our bags till the very end lol

She knows a lot, but is very biased. The class is ridiculously boring, and she focuses way too much on what she's really interested in. I thought this class would actually be interesting, but I am so bored and she doesn't try to draw you in at all. I hated this class so much. I'm so miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable which makes class very interesting. She is very demanding but  it makes excelling her classes more worth it. You will learn so much from Cramer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected by students--Inspirational

reviews.comment: She was new to teaching an online class this year and did not do well. She failed to respond to my emails and the mean on her final was 49% which she refused to curve, even though that is a reflection of her teaching. I would not recommend taking a class of hers.
Terrible online class. Teacher did absolutely nothing. The GTF does all the grading. Don't take this class unless you want to write a lot and take hard tests that are impossible to prepare for.

Took this class my senior year cuz I thought it would be easy, it was until the final. She gave us flash cards to study and practice quizzes and I knew everything she gave us well. I get to the final and the questions are so different and worded differently than any quiz and there were questions on things I had never seen. My graded dropped 7%

Cramer is very intelligent, inspirational, and animated. I enjoyed her lectures and teaching style. She started of each class with a current event and tied it to the material. 205 overall is VERY broad, hard to follow. Try to pay attention. You can do well if you try. There's a ton of readings, but I pulled an A without ever opening the textbook.

She's an understanding professor. If your having issues outside of school she'll work with you; if you missed an assignment. She is a busy person, so if you visit her office hours do your best not to make her feel like your wasting her time with you.

Brilliant professor that covers (what I think at least) incredibly interesting topics.  Tests are hard, and this is not a case of lecture just reviewing the readings.  You need to look at them and understand the key points to know what's going on Put in the work, and you might learn more from Cramer than any other Polisci Prof at the UO.

Professor Cramer is one of the smartest individuals I've ever talked to, buer lectures after the midterm become horribly scattered and insufficient. Her powerpoints often are just questions so you need to be in class to get the information. I did a lot of learning on my own as she covers a massive amount very quickly.

Very passionate, tons of knowledge, seems to be the most qualified PS instructor at UO in regards to security studies. Has some great, nearly breathless rants.  On the other hand she has a bit of a habit of covering an incredibly broad spectrum of topics  in a short amount of time. Also, final exams are very difficult, SAT-esque time crunches.

Also took 205 with her. Cramer has her quirks but she's also knowledgeable and available for help. Do the readings and cite them often for the midterms. Her intro classes are designed to weed out freshmen who aren't serious about PS. She also has a policy against giving higher than 95, so expect to put in effort for an A. Rewarding class.
Cramer is very intelligent, but she dumbs down her lectures. As a result lecture was boring, and in retrospect, they were completely unnecessary.
Very informative and smart teacher. Learned a lot. Kinda hard though

As previously stated, this class is intense. She expects grad level work out of you BUT it is the best class I have ever taken and her preparation has helped me immensely in planning for grad school. She has many resources and if you ask her for help, she will do whatever she can. Her classes are demanding but you didn't expect a free degree?

One of my favorite society of college scholars classes taught by her. Do the readings/work, you'll be fine. She is a passionate and well educated teacher from MIT. If you want a great teacher, and are willing to put up with the workload, don't hesitate!

this class is INTENSE. it's a lot of work, but you learn so much. if you put in work you're pretty much guaranteed at least a B.  i got an A- and i had no idea what was going on the first few weeks.  take classes with her, she's an awesome professor!

This class was harder than any of the 300 level poli sci classes I have taken. She assigns a lot of reading, but if you keep on it then you'll be ok. Tests are straightforward but extremely hard because you have to explain so much in so little time. My hand was in pain at the end! She is really biased, but we do go to U of O so what do you expect?

She DOES know her stuff... but she only knows it from the left.  I am actually a Dem but I respect all sides and this class was not really conducive to even allowing students to voice various opinions without feeling disrespected.
There's a lot of reading, and it's kind of interesting. Her lectures on the other hand and not interesting at all!!She goes off on random tangents that are worthless when it comes to the tests.
This teacher is legit. hella smart and informed. alot of reading but it is worth it if your into politics
Knows her stuff, will pass on questions to the GTF though.  Only complain is she teaches mostly from the left side, but as time went on, I saw that she brought other arguments in too.

Cramer knows her stuff, but like many profs in the world, she is a prof because she suffers from acute social retardation.  Sitting in her office talking to her makes for a highly awkward and uncomfortable experience.
She is extremely passionate and very intelligent. Yes a little on the crazy side but this class was amazing!! I learned more in this class than any other at the UO!

Are you people kidding me? She is a bright lady but not a great communicator. Very passionate on subject matter. Outside of class I found her to be very difficult to get ahold of and when I did she wasn't much help. She changes around her syllabus. The lady is too busy. Plus she told my friend she'd write him a letter of rec. and forgot to send it!

Cramer is an amazing professor..i have had her for 2 classes, and although she is on the crazy side, its a good type of crazy, she goes and goes and goes taking huge breaths every 5 mins and then keeps going... although i was scared by her (a little) she is very passionate about what she does and extremely helpful
Prof is on it
The class was very difficult, but she is incredibly passionate, clear, inspiring, and she basically knows everything. One of the hardest classes I've taken, but SO worth it!

The best poli sci teacher UO has.  Very informed, really passionate.  She has a very high bar for students, but is so clear and encouraging it is obtainable.  Go to lecture and you will learn more than you ever have.
She is tough, but a genius. GO TO CLASS, because the lecture notes will help a lot. Most passionate political science teacher I've ever had. I highly recommend this class.
the subject matter is great as well as the articles she chooses
A little on the crazy side.
No Comments
Cramer is very smart and very passionate about her work. The work is probably a little harder than most PS classes, but its worth it. You learn a lot. Great person to talk with in office hours.
very very passionate, loadwork tho. she knows her stuff, and that is an important quality
interesting class, ok teacher

Ms. Cramer was good, for the first two days, then it was all hell. Asking for help from her was like trying to ask a man-eating tiger directions to the theatre. She was also all over the board, which pretty much kills any possibility of actually learning something. Bad professor, no biscuit.

I took WMD and terrorism from her but her passion for the subject would apply in any course. She will provide you with a very liberal view and is willing to teach the contentious issues. Those who don't take the time to learn her material call her a conpiracy theorist. Take her if you can.

Jane works REALLY hard.  She is a fantastic prof.  Take her classes.  An Ivy League prof at our little state U.  You'll never regard WMD and National Missile Defense the same again after her courses...  Highly recommended.

The class was great, so great that I couldn't wait to go to it everyday, and it was so intense that it made me unable to sleep at night (sometimes).  Jane knows her subject very well, but obviously cares more about research than anything else.
very passionate -- sometime to a fault.  she, however, makes sure you know your stuff while still putting energy and passion into her teaching. take her!
She is a lot of work, but at the end of the term I learned a lot.
Very difficult quizzes and tests with little time allocated and material not taught in class, which ultimately resulted in a very low class average.

Cruz was very unclear about what they would put on tests. The final was way more difficult than they expressed in class. They had little to no remorse for any of their students not understanding the material. I've never gotten below an A in any of my math classes before this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are fine and usually provides lessons beforehand. Doesn't curve on tests, even if the exam average is a 51%. 2-3 webworks a week, a reading quiz, & weekly in person quizzes. Late work will go down 1% every hour its late. His last final is much harder than he lets on and doesn't provide any study guides for midterms. Would not recommend👎🏼
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cruz is a great teacher who cares about his students succeeding. He gives extra credit opportunities so make sure to do it, it can raise your grade a lot. Sometimes he goes through lessons quickly but go to his office hours and he'll review with you.

Do NOT take any class with him. He made precalc extremely challenging when others professors didn't. The class averages on exams were in the 50s yet he refused to curve. His class notes were paragraphs of unnecessary explanation so you have to teach yourself these concepts. Strict grader, lectures aren't engaging, and overall passive aggressive.
Very hard and the tests were too long for a 50 minute class

Cruz is a great teacher and makes sure all of his students are prepared to succeed in his class. At times he goes very fast and can make things seem harder, but if you do the homework and come to class you should be fine, the tests are very easy and he is a easy grader

His website is very helpful and the course content was not too difficult, especially if you already took 341 and 252. He is a nice guy and pretty reasonable with homework. He doesn't grade too harshly either, if you get most of the questions right then he won't take much off. I would heavily recommend taking his class.

Cruz is a decent lecturer. Tests are worth the majority of the grade but participation/homework factors in (and the lowest 2 of everything gets dropped). The assessments are quite difficult, and he does not give adequate time to complete the problems (in my opinion). Also, the homework can be veryyy tedious.

He is a nice guy, but I ran out of time on every test and quiz I took in his class because he asked insanely hard questions for a 50 min exam or 20 min quiz. Then after every exam he said he was gonna change the format but never did. The material is hard and the problems are time consuming to solve, I wish he could understand that.
Tough class for sure, luckily he's pretty helpful. He has a website which effectively is the textbook so if you're curious what the class is like just look up the website.

I had Cruz for Math 252 and overall he is a great guy and a great teacher. Extremely helpful during office hours, his lectures are informative and he covers topics thoroughly with good examples. All his lecture content is available on his website as well as custom graphs for visualizing topics like the shell integration method.

Cruz is hardworking and utilizes student feedback in order to improve concept understanding. He has a website with all his notes for the class uploaded and updates them as the class progresses. Utilizing his office hours is the best way to ensure success in his classes, the exams were not too tough. Study the notes online and you'll do great!

Cruz is an amazing teacher, he works hard and it shows in his lectures. Honestly I highly recommend him, but go to his office hours if you can. His website is just his name .com so definitely check him out. He has notes for all of the calc sequence and his notes continue to grow.

I actually had 253 with Cruz but couldn't select it here. Great professor. I recommend just being really attentive in class and understanding the concepts as opposed to taking notes because he has an AMAZING website where he keeps great notes for everything. Very clear expectations, great class.

This class was very hard. Cruz provided good notes on his website, but they were formatted very differently to his in class lectures. He was not very understanding of any issues with submitting homework, and did not curve any part of this class despite very low averages. Many people had to drop this class and he showed no remorse for them.

He is great at explaining concepts and is very nice. His class is difficult but he does his best to help students outside of class and made an excellent website. Quizzes and tests are difficult but I cannot complain about much else.

Cruz was a decent teacher, he explained things pretty well but assigned a lot of homework for a low-level math class. He also organized his lectures well but the main problem I had with this class was how hard the tests were, I studied for hours and still got a D+ on the Final which brought my overall grade of a B down to a C- with no curve at all

I don't know why I hated this class so much, but I also wasn't a fan of the teacher either. I just didn't learn well with him whatsoever and he made me feel completely stupid half the time for not understanding certain concepts. Would never take his class again.

Took this class freshman year and had to retake it bc I failed the first midterm and wasnt able to get my grade up. His lectures were pretty much right out of the textbook but were so so confusing and he even said the textbook was terrible. Do not recommend. Taking it over with a different prof and theyre so much better.
Cruz was a really good professor. He was extremely caring and made class enjoyable. His lectures were very detailed and easy to understand. I would definitely take his class again if I could!

His European Politics class is super interesting and informative, he really cares about the topic. There are only a few assignments, and sometimes there is a disconnect between him and the GE on what they tell us for grading expectations. Otherwise it's a good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thankfully he didn't include much of his bias in this class. Parsons taught European politics, and actually made it kinda interesting. he doesn't have much hw, just discussion boards, 2 papers and midterm/final. He posts his slides too incase you miss a class, and he doesn't count attendance. Better than last year for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Parsons' lectures were engaging and connected with the readings enough to be cohesive but still different enough to add value beyond the textbook. Speaking of, his textbook could've been a little more concise, but the readings helped my learning. The 3 essay assignments were short and easy (though GEs graded harshly).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting class, however the grading on the essays are unbelievably hard for the length/content. My GE would PICK APART anything I wrote even if the information wasn't incorrect.

Mandatory attendance to biased and uninformative lectures. Mandatory online textbook that he authored very much feels like a money grab especially because the textbook is riddled with biases, unnecessary tangents, and even typos. Limited if any feedback on areas of improvement or reasoning behind grades. He is theoretically educated but not smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the lectures in this class, but that's about all I enjoyed. Craig is a funny guy and makes the lectures really engaging, but the rest of the class work was overcomplicated and the grading criteria was really tough, especially for the 3 essays.

Lectures were usually pretty boring and hard to stay engaged in. But, Parsons definitely knows the material very well and is knowledgeable. Topics are interesting, essays are graded toughly, and the study guides are super helpful and make it easy to succeed. Overall Parsons is chill and a good intro level professor.

I had a family issue that significantly impacted my ability to attend class for 2 weeks and when I explained to Parsons he was so understanding and kind; even had a sit-down conversation with me JUST to talk about my mental health after the situation and not even the class. If you have Gao for your GE he is an amazing teacher and overall great.

Professor Parsons is a great professor. The lectures are pretty engaging and super helpful for studying. Attendance is pretty flex, but you have to email him or your GE before the class starts. Lots of textbook readings but only 3 essays. Definitely tough graders, but you can get a B pretty easily. Super good intro class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Unbelievably unprofessional. During the election season, he wasted valuable class time hating on trump instead of actually teaching us. Was unprepped tech wise and would go on long tangents that often wouldn't pertain to the readings or class itself. Class was very one sided liberally and he made sure it stayed that way. Avoid at all costs.

Honestly, this professor wasn't an outstanding one. His class was not very financially accessible, and his lectures only ever consisted of things in his textbook that cost 85 dollars, so they felt pretty useless. It was an easy class, but I don't think it's worth taking unless it requires you to take the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Craig Parsons is a great guy! Wonderful at public speaking, and is very good at allowing all people, regardless of political beliefs, to feel encouraged to learn. Was very understanding when I was struggling post-election (my fathers an immigrant). my TA was excellent!!

For my first polisci class, I think Prof Parsons was a perfect choice. Engaging lectures, reasonable amounts of reading, and was very warm during our office hours interaction (I regret not going more). Super knowledgeable guy, though perhaps a bit too insistent on playing to the center when discussing current events. Loved my GE Yuxuan too :)

The exams were written on paper and kind of hard but he split the grade up into a lot of participation points so it leveled things out. I had Isaiah as a GE, he was awesome. Prof Parsons has a lot of knowledge and is great at explaining things but can sometimes ramble on. Interesting class but you have to put in the work.

Craig is a great guy, I was just really frustrated with the grading criteria. I worked really hard on the essays and am a talented writer, but it was never enough. The essays are 500-600 words and don't leave space for nuance. The grading is harder than it should be. However, the course material for the class is well done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Parsons was the first political science professor I had ever had, he is amazing!

Great professor, he is very knowledgable and for the most part keeps lectures engaging. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss a few classes without it harming your grade. Exams were hard but very helpful study guides are provided and they are very easy to study for. Highly reccomend taking.

Dr. Parsons is a decent and entertaining professor; he's very knowledgeable and passionate. The papers (~500wds) are harshly graded but straightforward. The $60 online textbook he wrote is required but isn't bad or that long (~2-3 hrs/week), just do them. Parsons teaches from an incredibly Westernized/European bias, and GEs also have their own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Textbook is "required" but can pass without it. There are 3 essays. Midterm and final are both in-person written short answers. He's a super chill guy but boring lecturer. The GE's do most of the grading. I had Saima and she was the worst GE I've ever had; she had no clue what she was doing and was no help. DO NOT take Saima's discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty engaging and he's very charismatic. Homework isn't too bad but there is quite a bit of reading along with weekly quizzes. He also makes you buy the book he wrote lol. cool guy tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Parsons comes off a little strong in his class syllabus but is really an intelligent and fun instructor. His lectures were engaging and the homework wasn't too bad. He is a little self-absorbed but overall an understanding and funny guy who knows what he's talking about.
Professor Parsons had terrible lectures and made us buy the expensive textbook that HE wrote.
Loved

Parsons is funny and smart. Wouldn't recommend for his intro class unless you know a lot on ps already. His textbook and lectures are word-for-word but both are required. Plain and simple directions for tests. Just way too much reading to have to relisten to it all again for credit because reading quiz is due first. Also always on time!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've taken and succeeded and plenty of higher level political science courses, I don't think Craig should be teaching entry level courses. His portrayals of foreign policy relating to Russia and China are through a heavy "western-liberal order" give many people attempting to get into politics deep internal (white/EU) biases. Class itself isn't hard

He is very inspirational and makes poly sci fun. I enjoyed because he is easy to listen to and it's clear he knows a lot about what he his saying. The essays were clear and short (500-600 words) and there was very good study guide given for the midterm and final which made it easy to study. Textbook relates very well to assignments and lectures

Professor Parsons is a great teacher who makes the sometimes convoluted content of the class feel understandable. He also created the textbook for the class which is around $60 for purchase that involves most of the homework for the class.

His lectures were interesting, but there wasn't time for student discussion, and sometimes he went on tangents. Homework is easy, 3 papers but they are only 500-600 words and many easy extras can bring up your overall grade.  The final and midterm weren't too bad

I absolutely loved Professor Parsons. His lectures were extremely well organized and interesting. He wrote the textbook that went along with the class so his lectures were directly related and expanded upon the content. He was super reasonable with extensions and issues that came up. He is funny and down to earth and extremely knowledgeable.

Craig has good content and is excellent at explaining things. The work was manageable and easy to understand. He is very accessible through email and office hours. He is flexible and understanding. He is also very funny and a good lecturer.

Parsons is a knowledgeable and passionate teacher who does a good job of providing the framework for political science without getting too caught up in unnecessary political jargon. The course moves at a comfortable but steady pace. There are 3 very short essays, a midterm, and a final but Parsons mixes in other graded opportunities.
I love this man. Really good at explaining material, and makes lectures interesting.

Parsons always came to class with a great attitude and inspired everyone to learn. The attendance is graded, but he gives a lot of leeway for excused absences, and even allows some unexcused absences without penalty. The only thing I would say negative is that some of his lectures are straight from the textbook, but overall he was a great teacher
Very clear with assignments and instructions. Super fitting workload for 100 level class

Professor Parsons is a great guy! He's super caring, great at responding to emails, and is an awesome speaker. His political science 111 class was super interesting and relatively easy! Super accommodating with learning disabilities and cares a lot about his students!

I like his lecture format and how he makes it engaging, and he has an overall optimistic vibe. He also seems passionate about what he's teaching, which is nice because, as a student, it makes class fun :)

For hw, there were like three essays that weren't too bad (500-600 words). I would recommend this professor, :)
Hes so goofy I thought his class was fun and pretty easy

His lectures were entertaining and he is a great speaker. The class consists of three essays, a couple quizzes, the final, and weekly readings. This class was not too hard, but it could be easy to fall behind if you don't go to lectures/discussions often. His attendance policy is pretty leneint, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Parsons is caring about his students and is accessible outside of class. There is not a heavy workload- easy reading/video quizzes+3 short essays, but midterms are graded toughly by the GE and weighted 25% of your grade. Lecture and discussion are mandatory but easily excused. Parsons lectures well and if you attend and do readings you'll do well.
Short Essays, every other week. Weekly discussion and posts. Online coursebook with built-in quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a really great professor and clearly cares about his students. You have to do the reading (which there is a lot of) and the final and midterms are tough but an A is possible if you work hard.

Super enthusiastic professor who makes lectures interesting. Explains things clearly and engages the class well. Besides the mid-term and final, there weren't any other major tests but there were reading quizzes. The reading was really heavy and that was pretty horrible but the subject material is relevant and important.

Professor Parsons is a wonderful instructor and full of energy. He is clearly very interested in what he does, and is very capable and educated in the subject matter. The right balance of quirky, entertaining, insightful and interesting to keep your attention while learning all at the same time. very nice guy, very helpful and I really recommend it

Very good teacher. Lectures can sometimes be dull, but they are super straightforward. Go see him in office hours and he'll tell you anything you need to know. Easy tests, papers graded fairly easily. Would recommend his classes to any of my friends.

European Union: Prof. Parsons is one of the best professors I've had at U of O.  You have to do the readings and go to class, but it is worth it.  His lectures are engaging and he seems passionate about the material.  He is also very understanding of extenuating circumstances.

Dr. Parsons is one of the most dynamic professors I have ever had. He has a unique talent for synthesizing and unifying complexity and finding clarity in a sea of confusion. I would recommend him highly for anyone even remotely interested in this field!
Best professor I ever had!
I really enjoyed his class and his teaching style. Easy to understand and very approachable. I learned a lot but didn't feel overwhelmed with material.
Interesting class and very enthusiastic professor. Makes every topic fun. The paper topics are also some of the most beneficial I've had.

His lectures are amazingly organized and helpful. There is an extensive amount of reading that is slightly unnecessary because he covers it in the lecture. If you are interested in the subject it is very very intriguing and extremely well organized. The GTFs grade everything though and they are very easy on you and not helpful.

Parsons is an intelligent and highly engaging prof.  His power points are detailed and his lectures are fast paced and full of relevant information.  He is also a funny guy and will crack jokes that only die hard poly sci students will get.  Taking his whole sequence of comparative politics and european politics is really fun.
really funny guy and makes great refrences! but you need to print out the lecture notes before and then have them at class or you will get lost and end up writing more than you need to.
The class has quizzes at the end of each week and a few projects that are all easy. The final exam however is difficult if you don't prepare much.
Best Professor I've had, super sweet and understanding, lots of knowledge of and genuinely wants the best for his students
good lecture style and engaging without forcing u to do anything in class. homework is pretty light also.

took this class for SBUS 456 and loved every second of it. I didn't go to many classes but every time I did they were always amazing. The weekly quizzes are usually based on the textbook as well as lectures but are always easy if you pay attention. I loved the guests lecture speakers and have created connections with them as well. Craig is the best

SBUS 456 not 199
Craig is a great person and gives very engaging lectures but has a harsh late policy and he grades very slowly. There were a number of small projects that he did not grade before the next one was due so you had no idea if you did it correctly or not.

Craig and Lauren did such a good job. For it being a new class, they had it down. There were a few assignments that were challenging but they were there to support you. They would actually sit while teaching and it felt a lot more like a conversation than a lecture. I adored this class and it was so applicable to my job.

Honestly, he is a nice prof. But what the f is this class structure? No class schedule in the syllabus that could tell you when quizzes are...Genuinely confused how such a simple subject could get so muddled by his directionless lectures. Frustrating prof for us students who need clear and concise instructions/deadlines.

These reviews were so validated! All term I complained about this professors not actually teaching Social Psych. He constantly was changing the structure of the class. Had surprise group projects. He gives little to no guidance about assignments then grades harshly or in a confusing way. Final had nothing to do with class.

This course is taught like Research Methods with aspects of Social Psych here and there. In my opinion it is a very easy course, but if you want to learn a lot about Social Psych, maybe find another professor.

I was disappointed by this class because I went in excited to get into social psychology, but we ended up going over the structure of empirical journal articles the entire term! The material is taught on videos on canvas not in person, and the final quiz didn't have anything we talked about in class at all. I wish I had taken another 300 course.

I was looking foreword to taking Social Psychology but the way this class is set up got rid of my excitement. I feel like we focused way more on research methods and discussing validies than the actual social Psychology itself. I honestly feel like i learned more about social psychology in the video modules he had us do.

Took this class expecting to learn about social psychology and spent the entire timing discussing validities. The course was so unorganized and focused more on skimming research articles than actually doing work. Then when grades for assignments would come out, grading was confusing and points were docked off for nearly no reason. Would not take.

This class did not teach social psychology at all. Instead, it focused on reading papers and picking out the criteria, which is a research methods class. We did repeat assignments the entire term and he requires that assignments are printed, even when used for five minutes. Does not provide feedback nor listen to it. Find any other professor!

He's nice. However, for social psy, it's literally just a repeat of research methods. The entire class is more about the 7 criteria to analyze articles than social psy itself. It feels like a waste of time and nothing is interesting at all. First rating on here talked about the time he made us do a group and presentation the next class, it was bs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Clearly, he's never taught a class greater than 20. Expects a classroom of 300 to do group projects, a presentation in just one class period, and groups of 10 during in-class participation. He does NOT care about his students, and his classes are SO boring. He has 4 days of free attendance, yet docked points for people who missed even one day.

Phills himself is a great prof. Cares about his work, has his student's best interests at heart, and overall makes a great teacher that I enjoyed having. However the course itself and the way he chooses to teach it is unfortunately rather drab. Assignments are very similar to one another, all focusing around reading articles and not much more.
Do not take. Just do not. Find different prof.
The class was very discussion heavy but was very well organized. Professor Cummings plans very well and is super helpful!

I liked this class a lot! I think it was organized well. Professor Cummings really knows what they are talking about, and this is clear during the lectures. There are a LOT of discussions (like 50% of the class) but the grading is easy.
extremely dull class with very poorly organized structure. would not recommend in the slightest
it's a free A but if you want to actually learn something don't take it
They are awesome and so chill. They made science really easy and disgustable to understand. The class is so chill and so easy to get 100%, just talk in class. Lowkey did like none of the readings.
honestly just such a boring class but very easy grader

This professor is very knowledgeable and kind. They offer great feedback to students and encourage them to make the most out of their ideas through discussions or writing. Grading is pretty easy as long as you participate and complete assignments.
Really chill prof, and very organized too, not commonly seen in the CHC

7 essays, daily quizzes, unbearably boring lectures, and a final project due at 11:59 AM on a Sunday (type of professor she is…) If you're trying to find a global perspectives credit, don't take this class. Unnecessarily hard for a class about FILM and FOOD…
She is the sweetest most organized professor. Her quizzes were easy and if you attend the lectures, then you will do fine on the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Hannah is very organized, makes lectures fun and likes to cater to the students needs, is very understanding and caring. She isn't a tough grader and it is super easy to pass the class as long as you go to the lectures and discussion groups, not too many assignments. She's super friendly and is like a mom-figure, with a very bright personality!
(GSL 335) I love Professor Hannah Cutting-Jones, but be prepared to write an essay once a week. She is an awesome professor though!

Professor was very supportive and kind but has horrific control of the classroom. Lot's of what was discussed was either hypothetical or false. Doesn't demand respect or interest in the lectures and can drag during lectures. 1  paper every week so not terribly hard but good lord the class was a colossal waste of time.

Super kind and educated professor, the lectures are just long and boring because she pretty much talks the entire time. This class was pretty easy as long as you pay attention during the lectures and read the textbook.

Dr. Cutting-Jones was the first professor I had at UO, she gives very interesting and engaging lectures, and is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the topics she teaches. On Halloween she came dressed as a spider and passes out candy to everyone in the lecture. If you have the option to take one of her classes I highly recommend!

kind of disorganized, because she rambles we hardly ever made it through the entirety of her planned lecture slides, said we would have weekly quizzes but only began that during week 4. gives readings but its not vital to the course. super kind, entertaining course

Dr. Cutting-Jones was a good professor and is so sweet but I just didn't really like her style of lectures. She doesn't put many words on her slides which made it difficult to follow along. However, this class is extremely easy, I did both of the extra credit assignments she offered and it bumped me up 2 letter grades from that alone.

Prof Cutting-Jones was really enjoyable, lectures were interesting & assignments were fairly straightforward. Discussions/Group projects were kinda annoying but that's not on her. It was a very well versed intro class and a lot of room was provided to get the grade you desired. Short weekly quizzes online, 2 papers and a final.

The lectures were super engaging and interesting. We had quizzes each week, however they were open note and if you paid attention to the lectures at all they were fairly easy. Dr Cutting Jones was always available for office hours, and was super helpful whenever I had questions. Overall, really recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
- great professor; lectures are interesting as well as engaging. 
- LOTs of reading that is important for class
-short quizzes and tests every week; however, it's open book and, in my opinion, free credit. Your grade is mainly based on the quizzes, as well as the essay-based midterm and final.
-Fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cutting-Jones is very nice and a good professor, but she assigns a lot of reading compared to other HC classes. Her feedback is really useful and she will help you do well on your essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hannah is a wonderful person and an amazing professor. Everyone felt comfortable engaging in class. She walked us through assignments. She always let us know of events outside the classroom that could benefit our learning. The one qualm I have is she was kind of disorganized, but she was incredibly approachable and willing to clarify at any time.

She is clear, organized, and understanding. Weekly 2 question quizzes on specific lecture and reading content, 1 essay, 1 research assignment, 3 documentary responses, and the final was short answer vocab and one longer writing piece with prompt given before.
