Lectures felt like a high school environment, guest speakers were eh, very easy to do well

In class she was awesome and the discussions were always interesting. Outside of class, she was really hard to get in touch with and she didn't express clear expectations for assignments, causing more stress than needed. She provided great feedback though and was flexible in letting us rewrite papers which was really helpful.

I took HCJ first term freshman year and she inspired me to stay in the Honors College. Incredible class, interesting readings, and she genuinely respects student opinion. My gpa died during the term and she offered extensions on everything, missed attendance, and checked in with me personally on academics and life. An absolute angel of a professor!
They v nice n chill. Good class

I don't have an issue with professors being harsh graders. What I do have an issue with is professors grading harshly while failing to communicate what they want clearly. Unfortunately, I had that occur to me multiple times. I received feedback on multiple occasions that marked me down for not having something that wasn't mentioned on the rubric.
Really loved the class content and social engagement, but I definitely had to work hard on my 3 reflection papers and the grading wasnt a breeze. Shes an amazing human and I learned so much from her!

This class is a lot of work but prof Cutting-Jones is an amazing and she teaches so much info through her lectures. There is a lot of reading and work for this class but it is always really interesting. There is a discussion section (I had Nanosh Lucas) and he was a wonderful leader who had a unique calmness that I really enjoyed. I learned so much
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Cutting Jones truly cares about her students in and outside of the zoom room. She checks in and follows up with resources and assistance for anything that you may need. The readings are great and class discussions are lively, even over zoom. This class literally turned me vegetarian I learned so much about animal ethics. Take this class!!

Dr. Cutting-Jones was an awesome teacher. I took her HC101 course (Philosophy of Food) and I loved every class. All of the readings and lectures were incredibly informative. Get ready to discuss and get to know your classmates and their opinions. Absolutely would take another class with Hannah again!

I had Professor Cutting-Jones for an HC101 course, Philosophy of Food. Through the materials she provided for us, my ways of thinking about the world and food consumption were completely transformed. She is extremely passionate and knowledgable about the subject and extremely easy to get along with and reach out to. Would highly recommend her.

Truly knowledgeable and passionate professor. She knew how to explain and engage her students every class. Very responsive to emails and was always willing to help students with any difficulties. Definitely perked my interest in food studies which I had never though of before. Would take one of her classes again in a heartbeat!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Pat is a caring person. However, this class was the most disorganized and confusing course I've taken in the J school. She gets mad at you for referencing samples that SHE posted on Canvas and constantly contradicts herself in grading, telling you one thing this week and then marking off for doing what she said. Take this course with another prof.

I haven't done a review for a teacher up until now but felt the need for this wonderful professor. If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Curtin I highly recommend. She has extensive knowledge and experience with PR, and brings a humorous approach to lecture.

She is very old fashioned in that she purposely tries to trick her students. By the end of the term you come to notice that she will purposely quiz you on something she explained in one sentence rather than the example she spent at least five slides explaining. She also does not compromise on grades, even if you have a solid argument for youranswer
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: it's important to attend lectures if you want to do well in the class however pat is great and the lectures are engaging if you're interested in what she's talking about. grade is made up of weekly quizzes and 3 400 word case studies. Really enjoyed this class and her office hours were very helpful. she wants you to succeed.

Pat is super helpful, but her class can be challenging if you miss the lectures because that is where most of the quiz comes from. The lecture slides are also not very helpful because they are usually just pictures with little to no words. However, Pat gives amazing feedback on the assignments and is always there to answer questions!

Pat's class this term was extremely pointless. She makes you feel like a burden rather than a student. When I went up to receive help after class from her, she just blew me off as if I was a rock. Her quizzes are very difficult and if you do not attend class, the lecture slides are little to no help.!!! AVOID PAT CURTIN!!!

Such a great professor. She is super invested in her students and cares that they understand the material. Very understanding professor who understands that her students are human. Had her for J453, loved the class and got a B+/A.  I would definitely recommend Pat!

She's very helpful, professional, and compassionate. You don't have to try to be a smart-ass in her class. Just be honest of what you know/don't know, don't understand, or your difficulties, you'll be fine.
No Comments
There were some days I would often come in and wonder if she was on coke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class. No attendance and readings aren't important if you understand material and show up to class. Professor Cupo really values student participation and opinions. Would definitely take a class from them again. Midterm and final were multiple choice and pretty easy. Only one essay and it was pass/no pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are VERY boring. It does seem as though she is passionate about what she teaches though. She assigns too much reading for this level of a class, and papers due every other week. Topics are generally easy to understand, but discussions do not get you very far.
I would not recommend her as a professor; she was pretty uninformed on a lot of the topics we covered, and used outdated readings for lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My first impressions of Dr.Cupo was that she was monotone but she grew on me with her dry wit, willing to go more in depth on topics and understanding of the topics she teaches. I would heavily recommend this class, very beginner friendly for people who don't know much of social inequality.

Good class, but very lecture-heavy and usually boring. I luckily enjoyed the content, but the readings got tiring after a while. She is usually clear about assignments, but the discussion sections are where you should ask questions. As long as you sort of understand the concepts and do all the response memos/discussions you should be fine!

SOC207 is an easy-pass class with Dimitria Cupo. I paid attention to 1/4 of her lectures because they were so boring and unengaging. I like the topics she discusses but she makes them so dreadful. I don't do any readings and I get 100's on everything... Would not recommend it unless you need a nap. Final is tough for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: awful professor. she wouldn't allow us to see our grade until the term was over, so I had no idea I was failing the class until it was already summer
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cupo is an easy grader, but only if you agree with her ideas.  I took one of her upper-division courses in a previous term and she did not agree with my ideas so graded me lower.  She is boring and class is miserable to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cupo talks extremely slow and seems unprepared in class for the content. She sometimes will talk about slightly sensitive topics without a warning for her students. When she comes into class, she seems unprepared at times in the sense of the research behind her words or slides. She has long readings and doesn't grade quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dimitra is understanding with issues with tests. Very nice 1 on 1 but rude during lecture. Just very, very SLOW moving. It also seems very ignorant for a Social Inequality class, on multiple occasions felt like she was just perpetuating negative stereotypes within her teaching. Her canvas is confusing and changes often but she'll always address it.

The material was always surface level and most of the content we learned about was common knowledge. You did not get a review sheet for the mid-term, but as long as you had a basic understanding of gender you would pass. The final project also had no clear instructions and blindsided most of the class. I really don't recommend this class.

Not a terrible professor, but frustrating. She seemed unprepared during lectures, constantly fact checking her slides. Tests weren't reviewed, so several answers had to be given out or they were repeated without her realizing. GEs graded fairly, but left little to no feedback other than "expand" on some sentences.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is pretty laid back, lectures were chill but slightly boring. Overall if you went to class you could do pretty well on midterm.  Make sure to turn your assignments in on time. Would not take again, was blind sighted by my final grade because it was based off a weird point system.

This class was challenging but as long as you pay attention and show up to the detailed lectures than it is possible to receive a good grade. A lot of reading throughout the course but considering we only have 4 assignments it makes sense. Cupo is passionate about her class and provides a lot of information in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: only 6 assignments throughout the term, 4 2 page essays, two exams. It is almost impossible to get any higher than 85 on any of the essays because it is scored out of 10. They rarely give anything but whole numbers. Exams are on lectures. Which are boring and can be stressful due to cold calling. I think it is impossible to get much higher than a B

Very tough grader, an essay every 2 weeks that you will most likely get a C or B on... and you're only graded on those and exams. You won't pass the exams if you don't show up to class because exams are on lectures. Very mono-toned and boring lectures but you do learn a lot. One sided class..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading expectations not clear. Hit all the marks on rubric to get marked down for nor enough detail- it's 2 pages. No chance to study for midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the first day of class, she told us all to get the wrong textbook and was super confusing when trying to clarify the correct text to buy... Grading criteria for papers are super vague, but they are only two pages each which is nice. Her lectures are super super dry. But funny people in the class that add make it bearable.

I really loved Prof. Cupo. She was insightful and knowledgeable about the topic of the class, and her and her GE were lenient about grading in most cases. There isn't much feedback given on assignments but you have the opportunity to bounce your ideas off of Prof. Cupo in class and after lectures.

Its an interesting class, but if you have taken any soc/wgs class before youll already know all of this. Its just the basics of oppression. Shes an incredible boring lecturer too, and is weirdly condescending. She spends a lot of time trying to prove that shes knows more than the students (duh?), makes it hard to want to speak out in class.

If you have ever experienced any oppression if your life, this class is so simple. Class is very one-sided and very boring. She cold calls but doesn't know anyones names yet - we are in Week 6, so she just stares around the room for a while. You have journals due after every class and random quizzes on the reading.

I like Dimitra and her class is overall very chill and simple. There is a GE who does discussions one day of the week and he grades everything. I prefer the professor over him so as long as you do not get a GE that grades really hard on papers then this class should be really easy. Journals every other week and final project are low-key a lot...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really interesting class. Discussions were always fun thanks to the professors sense of humor and delightfully quirky personality. Although youre graded by very few things, she and the GEs are generous with extra credit, if you go the extra mile. Class is lecture heavy; take good notes because itll help you on the final.

Very one sided class. The grading criteria and overall structure of the class was very unclear, so its very difficult to know how to earn good grades on papers. I would not recommend for anyone to take a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: such an incredible class! she assigns 4 short projects, has 4 quizzes, sometimes has in class participation group assignments, and readings. but seriously this class was so interesting. just by showing up and putting in minimal effort can get you an A. she assigned us one extra credit assignment. Passing with a 98%. Just show up and be respectful

Jeanine is so sweet, and really goes in-depth during lectures on the readings. Go to class and you'll be 100% prepared for exams, no reading needed. However, all hard classwork was focused in the last 1/3 of class (a reading response, 10-page paper, and another paper, all within 3 weeks of each other).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Boring Soc class. It's required research methods. She did her best, there's worse professors for this class. The class setup was great. 4 HW preps, 4 quizzes, 4 HWs all with lowest dropped. Paper was split into 6 assignments and the final just brings it together. Extra credit if you do all 4 quizzes, HW preps and HW's. I'd try her for another class

Easy in theory. Could glean a lot of the lecture content in the book, but there is this odd push to try and make it tough. Grading is super harsh, miss four classes and fail, and so many times I hear, "This is tough". It's almost like Jeanine is trying to convince the class of how hard it is. And is alway positioning herself to be taken seriously.

Class total of 200 points. Final exam worth 40 points, 3 Short assignments worth 30 points, Group presentation 25 points (a joke), Best 2 out of 3 quizzes 30 points, & participation 15 points. Did everything last minute and got a B. So if you actually study for final exam which you get a page of notes front and back hand written, easy A.
Liz is one of the sweetest professors. Soothing voice, easy to talk to, and pretty easy going. If you read and write decent essays, you'll do well. Would recommend.

She is helpful and has great writing skills, but she irritated me. She tends to do a fake smile when you are wrong about a question and it was a small thing that annoyed me. If she doesn't like your idea of what your paper will be about she kind of makes it obvious by announcing it to the class on what you shouldn't write about. Revise your essay.
Good teacher. Just be sure to revise your essays more than she marks them and participate in class and you should be fine.
Great teacher who really cares about her students. No textbook, no webwork, easy quizzes and tests.

She is an ecellent teacher and I highly recommended her. I had her in the fall and it was her first time teaching the course. Ms. Currey cared about how her teaching was and wanted to know what she could do to improve her style constantly. She gave great notes that would be helpful for calculus. My advice is to stay organized and keep your binder.

I'm a math major and having her teach the class I thought was easy enough to understand. She loves everything Disney and most of her word problems consist of Disney related material. I never went to her office hours, but I heard if you went she was very helpful. She was a very nice person and her midterms and finals were very easy to pass.

she is very difficult to understand in class and does not do a very good job at explaining material. Once you go into tutoring or office hours though, the material is easy and her tests are easy to pass. Very, very easy midterms if you study.

Dr. Cycyk covers a lot in her lectures, but she frequently checks-in with students about their understanding and learning styles. She's definitely passionate about the topic and roots for her students to succeed. There are a lot of writing assignments, but she gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr.Cycyk does a great job at teaching the content. There is a lot to learn, but she does a great job. As long as you go to class and pay attention, you'll be good. She is a great professor. She has an anonomous suggestion qualtrics link which is great to give feedback anytime during the course.

Does a poor job at preparing students successfully for the assessments. Unorganized content is given to the students to rely on. Never made a study guide when requested by many students. The assignments are always unclear and graded the hardest for no reason. Puts way too much content in the slides and expects students to remember all of it. :/
Dr. Cycyk is not my favorite. Like it was really hard. Would love to have coffee with her, but I will avoid taking a course of here's at all costs.

I'll start off by saying Dr. C is a great person, but as a prof not so much. She acts as though she appreciates feedback from the class, but on important things that would help us with exams she refuses to implement solutions. There are no clear study guides for tests and homework is graded really tough and questions are vague. Study hard!

Prof.Cycyk is a good person, but not a good teacher. She tells you to focus on her lectures when studying for exams, where most of the questions are from the textbook. When studying for exams, I highly recommend sticking with the textbook. Also, make sure to spend time on the written assignments because she is a picky grader.

Dr. C is extremely hard and has at times berated her students in front of everyone. She created a hostile learning environment and I did not feel comfortable in her class. Be prepared for picky grading, tough feedback, long lectures, and constant stress. She expects a lot of her students and is not clear on her expectations. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is an unnecessarily picky grader/doesn't have the most organized slides & study guidelines. It's stressful to study for tests because slides are confusing and much is based on the textbook and not discussed in class. I did well in the class, but it was tough. And overall... unenjoyable. If you truly work hard you'll be fine, just stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Yes, Dr. Cycyk deals a lot of homework, but that just means your grade isn't so heavily weighted on just one or two things. Be sure to read the textbook chapters THOROUGHLY to prep for the exams. Her grading rubrics are 100% clear, I promise. If she doesn't give full credit in a section of the rubric, she gives feedback on why. A great listener!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are often very loosely based on lectures; Youll basically have to read the textbook and take a ton of notes to stay afloat. Doesn't grade assignments with the rubric provided and doesn't give much constructive feedback, if you are lucky enough to get any at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture is mandatory, but the tests relate to the textbook. Want full credit? You basically have to write a detailed novel and maybe you'll get the points. Assignments don't get posted until the week before, so even if you want to get ahead, you can't. She treats you like a child but expects so much more out of you. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It started out fine, but as we got farther in the term, assignments took a lot longer to be graded. She uses complete/10 instead of actually grading your work, so all the effort you put forth doesn't even feel counted

Cycyk is not a good teacher. Her class is organized so you'll have nothing for weeks, then a bunch of busy work due all at once. The tests don't relate to the lectures, and the assignments aren't actually graded on the rubric. If she says you don't need detail, she's lying. Unavoidable in CDS, but not a prof I would ever recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at the UO so far. She goes off on Chomsky tangents regularly, as well as tangents about Bulgarian a lot. Lectures are rarely clear, leaving students in class confused. Expect to spend 4-6 on every homework assignment (6) and more on the two midterms, and even more on the cumulative take-home final.

Nice woman and extremely smart/dedicated to what she does.I liked being in her class but it was extremely hard. I didn't think we were very well organized and I always felt at a loss when trying to do the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This woman is a genius! Her class is always fascinating and I feel like I'm learning what's on the cutting edge in her field. Her personality is so quirky and cute too, she is like a little russian mouse like the one in the rescuers.

Extremely knowledgeable and experienced professor, not for beginners though.  Avoid taking her 100-level courses as her topics are advanced and hard to follow if you're not into your senior year.  Super helpful at office hours, bright and bubbly demeanor.  Take advantage of this woman's brain if you're majoring in linguistics or neuroscience!

this teacher is a mess!  please do not take her class unless you have to.  her lectures are very scattered and lecture notes are almost zero help.  i have found that i have learned more from wikipedia than from her teaching.  she doesn't define technical terms and gets caught up talking about bulgarian/slavic languages for half the class.  look out

Terrible teacher. Do not take this class unless needed. For a Linguist you'd think she wouldn't say "um" every 10 seconds, go completely off tangent with her stories, or use language examples of anything other than russian/slavic (also in finals/midterm). Don't bother reading her lecture notes, you'll spend half your time trying to decrypt them.

Awful.  She teaches through examples (only slavic languages too) and doesn't ever bother defining technical terms we need to understand.  She also talks in a rather scatter-brained manner; there's very little lecture organization.  Also, on less important level, she dresses like she's from another planet.  Seriously.

Being a linguist you'd think she would realize that she says "um" every 10 seconds (not even kidding).  She is extremely disorganized and jumps from topic to topic.  She talks way too much about Lithuanian and Russian to make the class inclusive to those who have never taken a course pertaining to either language.  She's terrible at overhead notes.

Very hard to follow in lecture.  Disorganized.  Her lectures are a run-on stream of consciousness and she has a strange mumbling tone.  Her grading system is so unclear, classes are over and I have no idea what my grade is.  She is unapproachable and scarcely updates blackboard.  Bad choice for Gen-ed.

Knows her stuff, but has strange stutter/breathing problem where she says "um" about 2-5 times a minute.  Grading system is VERY wishy-washy.  Spent 30 minutes lecturing on vowels in Russian, and this is a "gender" linguistics class.  Experiments are time consuming and you'll have to ask strangers odd questions.  Not recommended for gen-ed seekers.
a very cool professor.  her class was hard but she was always available when i needed some help.  i was happy to see her when i graduated.
No Comments

An odd duck. Vakareliyska is extremely knowledgeable and can be fascinating in lecture; she's also really jumpy and nervous in a super cute geeky way. She dresses like a space alien. I sort of want to marry her.

VERY disorganized. She seems to make up her lectures as she goes along, and she doesn't write anything down on the board or have notes. Sometimes she tells funny stories, but she's pretty hard to follow. Midterm sucks. Boring, boring, boring.

Sped 410  Overvie of Autism. I really enjoyed this course and Cindy has wonderful examples and activities. If you struggle with writing, get help. Only a few papers, manageable. I wish she wasn't retiring!  Some group work, but fun assignment. Fair grader and does reviews for midterms and final.
EASY CLASS!! Get the Ebook you can control+f all of the quiz answers.

One of the easiest and most beneficial classes I have taken so far! Only offered as an online course. 8 online quizzes, 5 discussions, a book review, online midterm, and online final. There is also a 5 point extra credit opportunity at the end of the term. Getting an A  is more than achievable, just don't slack off. Would highly recommend.

Did no teaching and solely relied on you reading the textbook. In class, you would sit there and do a worksheet in complete silence. Bad study guides that didn't match the material on the tests either.

He relies entirely on the textbook to explain the broad ideas, but expects you to understand its nuances. His tests were nothing like the practice tests, homework, or reading assignments. If you are already super amazing at linear algebra, then sure take the class, but if this is your first time seeing it, I would try to get into another section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved him, make my math class super easy.

It is apparent that Dr. Steinberg makes an effort to give clear feedback and help accordingly. His lectures are pretty straightforward, and he is very kind. Sometimes his explanations when helping students individually weren't as clear, however it is the same for many math instructors.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, it's prevalent that he cares about his students and always tries to make class less boring. He's a good professor who is always open to questions and providing thorough details on how he found the answers. There are quizzes every Friday, but the quiz questions are on the easier side of the material.

Steinberg genuinely cares about his students, but his homework/projects are extremely difficult to understand. This isn't because they're hard, but rather, because most of the instructions or questions are phrased really weirdly to the point where it's difficult to understand what he's asking for. Great and funny guy, but very vague assignments.
He is chill, good for review but idk how good he would be at teaching new concepts. The class structure is simple and chill. He is also funny and likes to crack jokes.

I think, as an individual who aspires to be a math professor, I can tell when someone knows their stuff or is a good teacher. And I can say for certain that is not Professor Steinburg. He never lectures and is totally dependent on the textbook (which I'm not sure HE's even read). He seems like a chill dude, just not someone I want as a professor.

His tests are not like the "study guides" at all. He tells us that we need to be prepared because we are going to be tested on things we've never seen before... Why??? He is a harsh grader and gives zero credit and makes lots of errors when grading tests so make sure you check them. He doesn't lecture, we are told to read the book and that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have never switched profs so fast. I didn't take him for linear algebra 1 and the first class he made us spend a large portion coming up with justifications of why his "unique" teaching system is actually good and not bad. such a weird lazy way to try to get students who've learned the "normal" way all of uni to be okay with his style of teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Was a nice guy but just handed us packets each week and we worked on them independently. If we asked for help he would give us vague answers and he never lectured or taught us the way to solve things. This course was a waste of time and I took it to prepare me/refresh me for Math 111 and it turned out to be useless and super unhelpful.

The class setup requires a lot of reading outside of class. Lectures can be helpful if you ask questions and do the required reading, but if you are timid or don't keep up with all the readings, it can be difficult to follow. The final was 40% of the grade but only 6 questions, which I found frustrating because of how much content was covered.

He did not teach a single thing the entire quarter, handed us packets all year and told us to figure it out. Would only give help in abstract ways and office hours were not useful either. Clearly does not care about his students and is mentally checked out.

We read the text for the hw and readings then he goes over the problems in class. He is a nice person and accessible during office hours, he cares about improving the course, but he gives very little help to be successful in the class. The final was 40% of the grade and didn't cover questions similar to anything on the reading assignments/hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor relies on poorly recorded videos and uses class as glorified office hours. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but only attendees learned about using a note sheet on the final, leaving others disadvantaged. Solution sheets were often incomplete or unclear, failing to support effective learning. DO NOT TAKE if you learn best from a lecture

I would say I didn't really learn much from Dr. Steinberg himself, but rather from the worksheets and ALEKS. He occasionally went over the problems on the review sheets we get at the beginning of the week, but there weren't many lectures. The only way you'd really learn a lot from him was if you asked him for help.
DO not care about the students learning, neither teaching. Really bad attitude, dont like to answer question.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Lectures are boring, nothing gets dropped (unlike other 100-level classes at UO), GE's do not know the material, and neither does he. Dr. Steinberg refused to answers students' questions and does not care about their class outcome. I attended tutoring and office hours and still struggled in this class. Just don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: David has no concern for students with accommodations. He will ignore or deny them. He also doesn't communicate with his Learning assistants and two sections were unable to use calculators on an exam, when this was brought to his attention he did nothing to fix it and did not allow students to retake exam. Do not take a class with him

There is a good amount of homework, but the way the class is set up makes everything very clear and easy. The lectures are all on videos that you watch at home. You will have no problem doing well in this class if you're motivated and will spend time really understanding his videos and David is a nice guy. I don't know why the ratings are bad!

This was one of those "backwards" classes where you watch lecture videos at home, and go to class to do the homework. As a result, David did not really "teach" the whole term. On top of that, class time was mainly spent going over the video notes, so there ended up being SO much homework.

David's a funny guy, but a meh professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hardest math professor I have ever had. His style of teaching was very hard to follow. Had a hard time grasping and building off the things I was learning. If you struggle in math I would avoid this professor. I also did not like how we only had three tests that made up 75% of our grade. My class had a failing average score for our first test.

Steinberg began math 106 from the back of the book, beginning with logarithms in chapter 10. Then he moved backwards to chapter 5 which was meant to built students up to chapter 10. Chapter 10 repeated mentioned, as you learned in chapter 5. One third of the class dropped out in the first three weeks. Math tutors didn't know how to do the problems.

He's not very helpful if you are struggling and is not great with honoring accommodations. He will respond to your questions with more questions and just confuse you more. I did well in this class because I had an amazing GE. Would recommend avoiding taking math with him if possible. Attendance in discussion is also mandatory and quiz every week.

Really fun guy all around. He explained things very clearly and concisely, and was always really helpful when you needed something explained again. Lots of cool dad at the neighborhood barbecue vibes.

David teaches calc as if everyone already knows it. He doesn't explain new calc terms, and doesn't teach the material well. It was more helpful to spend more time watching youtube videos, teaching myself from the book, and other online resources rather than attending his lectures.
He only really went through practice problems and did not do a good job explaining the concepts. Also did not know how to use the projector and made it nearly impossible to see what he was doing.

David is in my opinion, a bad teacher. His lectures start off well and are easy to follow, until he writes something where you dont know how he got there, and he doesnt explain it fully. The class average for the mid term was around a 50% and he still didnt curve it and essentially told us that it was our fault we didnt do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good prof. Funny. I think he could be a little clearer on his expectations at the beginning of the term. Lectures get a little dry, but he really works hard to keep the spirits up. The feedback on grading is really good. Exam questions are challenging, and not very routine, BUT also extremely fair. Grading criteria clear. Curve was minimal.

Class consisted of 3 chapter tests, none of which were cumulative. He's a super nice dude and somewhat funny. The difficulty comes with the GTFs because David doesn't expect you to use a calculator and wants you to leave answers in a calculator ready form and there was miscommunication with the GTFs and they would solve problems out.

I hate math.. I really hate it. David explains things so well and makes everything very easy to understand. He tries to be funny and I appreciate that because math lectures are not very exciting. If I end up taking another math class I would love to take him again. Definitely recommend.
Awesome professor, very approachable and understanding.  Always tries to find a way to access the material without having to purchase a text book.  Homework is time consuming, but well worth it.
Really approachable and talented and explaning things. Quizzes and tests are reasonable. Just be prepared to do a lot of practice problems. His class made integral calculus accessible.

Very friendly. Very helpful at clarifying. QuizzesMidterms and grading was fair. Definitely practice a lot. Provides review for midterms-very useful. His lectures were easy to understand and follow. He likes participation, but not required. He has a bright smile in class and makes class comfortable. Would take again
so patient!!!!
He is the best math teacher that I've ever met! He is really patient and kind. His homework is really helpful.

There are two David Steinberg math teachers at University of oregon!!!!!!!!!!!!!  I had David J Steinberg and thought he was a great teacher! very nice, pacient, and helpful. Not easy course but not too difficult.
David is awesome! Definitely recommend him as a teacher. He is willing to help with homework problems and outside of class. Really nice guy!

David is great, definitely the best math teacher I have ever had. He goes really slowly and is really forgiving about homework (especially if you come into office hours, which I did pretty much every week) & grades pretty easily on tests also. He's very nice and he knows his stuff! Take him if you can.
Nice teacher! Really helpful!

Honestly David was an awesome teacher. I would definitely take a class with him again. He was to the point, and informative, and taught us in a way that allowed us to understand the material rather than just purely memorize it. He was often available for office hours, and he was really helpful in office hours as well.  Take this class.

David is a nice and awesome teacher.  He is engaged, and really tries to get people to understand math, and not just memorize math.  He is really helpful in office hours, and he'n overall good teacher.  I recommend him.
Nice guy. Really wants you to understand the principles BEHIND the math rather that just memorizing identities and formulas. If you do the homework, you should do fine on the quizzes.

I took math 243 from him over the summer and he was great. His notes covered everything and provided many very clear examples which really helped us with the homework/tests. Hes very nice and you can tell he loves to help out. His tests are very fair. If you read your notes and do your homework, there is no reason you would fail this class.
Good teacher. Explains things well. Test are pretty easy!

Took him for JCOM345 photoJournalism, He comes off as blunt and a bit intimating. You have a an assignment due each week, must turn in all assignments or you fail the class, you miss 3 classes you fail the class, you go through critiques in class with him. Photos quality and captions is essential to your grade. He wants you to be successful.
super awesome guy, very clearly cares about what he is doing.

Dan is the best professor at Oregon. He is the type of teacher if he can tell you care about what he's teaching he will give you a good grade. Go to his office hours get to know him I promise he's the nicest guy ever.
Dan Morrison clearly does not care about anything and is just in class to hangout and crack inappropriate jokes. His lectures are pointless and a huge waste of time.

GE is really the only thing that matters for this class. I unfortunately got a hard one and barely missed out on an A. Assignments really aren't too hard just start them early. Only really annoying thing is attendance is required and it's everyday. Class can be an easy A as long as your GE is chill.
Luckily I had a great GE, but many students in this class struggle to get good grades. DMORR himself is quite the funny and smart guy. He comes off intimidating at first but he's actually very nice!

Dan is hilarious and clearly very smart. He is passionate about what he does and will tell you if your work is not up to par. Do not take his bluntness personal! He's very accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed.

Dan is great, but the class is not (for non-journalism students). He even mentions this. This class frustrated me because I chose not to be in journalism for a reason. I don't like doing journalism. This whole class is just doing journalism. It's driving me crazy. I liked learning about photo composition, audio and video though.

Dan really knows his stuff, he is easily one of the most interesting people/professor I've ever met. He is really tough about his work and your work. He doesn't mess around when it comes to grading criteria and what he expects out of projects.

Dan is AWESOME! If you have him for any class, Gateway especially, take the time to get to know him. Gateway is a rigorous class with a lot of work, but Dan is always there to look over your work and give you feedback during office hours. He is also super funny and loves interacting with students, so start a conversation after class!

Dan has a lot of experience in the professional world and understands how hard it can be to get a job in these fields, so he can come off as a hardass. Don't let that stop you from coming to him for help though, he's very helpful outside of class. He's also the funniest professor I've had. Made me actually want to go to every class.

Dan is a very tough grader but extremely interesting. I was nervous at his speech during the first class, and he is a bit abrasive at times. He just knows what works and what doesn't, and he isn't afraid to tell you when your work isn't the best. The feedback is critical but helps you improve. Tough-love, funny guy. Don't be scared.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan is a tough grader but I learned a lot from him and his stories are great. I definitely recommend office hours because he's just a very interesting person.

If you're passionate about becoming a better photographer or just a better person then learn from Dan. Like everyone said he definitely comes off as harsh at first but trust me he will teach you so much. Take whatever classes you can with him and never ever be afraid to ask questions. He might scare the sh*t out of you but it's worth it.

Dan is very blunt, but I appreciated his advice and lectures. He has a ton of interesting stories and is easy to approach during office hours. I want to emphasize the importance of going to office hours when you take his class. It has been super helpful for me to get to know him and get direct feedback.

Dan is a beast, I bet he could wrestle a grizzly bear. However, he doesn't give very good directions in his lectures or Canvas organization, leading to a basic misunderstanding of most big assignments in Gateway. The class is rough because of his grading style, and he's not very informative. I respect him but I wouldn't take him again if I could.

Dan can come across as intimidating but he really is a big softy for his students. Stop by his office hours if you ever have a problem with an assignment. He'll help you learn what to improve, likely let you re-do the assignment entirely then change your grade if you did better on the re-do. Amazing instructor but you need to work hard in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Funny, but a dinosaur who doesn't give clear feedback or definitions. All the poorly made tutorial videos did not teach me/explain clearly enough to receive an A.

Genuinely one of the rudest professors I've had at UO. Unfortunately, this is a core class for SOJC but do anything to avoid taking it with dan. I sent him multiple emails over the term asking for feedback/questions and more often than not, he would reply with a snarky, unhelpful, unprofessional response.
Very tough grader, but he really just wants to help his students. Be sure to reach out and make yourself known, otherwise it will be a lot harder to get the help you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At first Dan comes across as callous and unapproachable but this is far from true. He is passionate about his work and truly wants students to succeed. Definitely go to office hours and get feedback before an assignment is due because he will give it to you real. One on one with him and you will see a different side than when in class. He is great!

Dan's class taught me not only how to use my camera, but how to use it with respect and curiosity. I've worked with Dan as a student in class and as a journalist in the field, and I can't recommend him enough. His early honesty toughens you up in the right way. His generosity toward and genuine care for students and the field are unmatched.

This class rarely met. When it did, Dan quizzed on details of assigned articles (what was the name of the subject's dog, etc.) -- not on feature writing (lede, etc.). Each day, we took an online grammar quiz (often incorrect coz the site was spam/didn't follow AP), then Dan went over it again saying "I don't know why this is the answer."

Dan puts on a very tough exterior. He seems like a hard, no BS, rough-around-the-edges type of person, and although that may be part of his personality, a lot of it is an act to get students to work hard. When you visit his office hours, he is actually a softie on the inside. He is a tough grader though so don't slack or you won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Loved taking Dan for Gateway. He is so funny and always adds fun to all the lectures. He tells it how it is though and you should expect very honest feedback.
If you want to be a great photojournalist, take as many classes from Dan as you can. He wants you to succeed and he will help you as often as you ask. Seriously, best professor in the SOJC.

Dan is one of the nicest people in the SOJC. He may seem scary when you first meet him in Gateway but he is incredibly kind and will always be there for his students. Take his class seriously and you will succeed. Work hard and you will have that hard work rewarded.

He comes off as rude and crass at first, but visit him in office hours and he's like a caring grandpa who plays with his grandkids  and enjoys himself thoroughly. (that was a weird analogy, but you get the point.) His no BS attitude really lets you see the industry as it is, and you come away having learnt a lot more than you thought you did.

Dan is a great teacher! He has a reputation for being very tough - and can be quite blunt in class - but if you go for help, he really provides a lot of assistance. It's definitely his way or the highway in this class - so don't take liberties in projects with what he explicitly states that he wants - and you'll get a good grade!

Dan is one of those professors you'll never forget. He can be harsh, but he gives great critiques and knows what he's talking about. Gateway was difficult, but you walk away having learned more than you even realize. I absolutely suggest taking Gateway 12 with Dan; might as well learn from the best. Just prepare to work hard and to be challenged.

I took Photojournalism in 2006, and it is one of those rare classes that has really stuck with me through the years. The assignments were tough and I spent a lot of time on the class, but after 8 years I am now getting back into SLR photography and I still remember so much of what he taught me. He was so generous with his time and guidance. A gem!

Dan is intimidating but obviously very knowledgable. I didn't like that specific things about assignments were withheld until sometimes the day before projects were due. He has little sympathy if you do something wrong and turn it in without fixing it. Also they took attendance every day.
Dan seems really tough but he's actually very nice and wants his students to succeed. Photo J is a tough class and a lot of work - but he makes himself more than available to help.

Just like everyone else, I didn't care for Dan at first.  But Don't let the big bad Dan Morrison mask fool you, bc i soon found out that he's not scary at all. In fact, he's actually very kind. And hilarious. Get to know him. And use his expertise to your advantage. His guidance has helped me excel in the SOJC and i cant thank him enough for that.

He was the advisor for our freshman class, On Location: Middle East. Once you get used to his no-B.S. attitude and his this-is-how-it-really-is rants, his class is the best. He wants students to understand that effort is what turns into success, so he sometimes makes things difficult. So worth it. I'm taking his travel writing class next term.

I have had Dan for Gateway and Photojournalism. At first I was really intimidated and he is very no B.S. about stuff but is an amazing teacher. He will help you with anything and really wants you to succeed. He also is just a really interesting person with lots of good advice and knowledge of the craft.

I was terrified of Dan as my professor in the Gateway series. He is intense, and expects his students to work hard. I was shaking the first time that I talked to him. Get to know Dan. He is seriously one of the nicest professors at Oregon, and he goes out of his way to help students. He is a gem at Oregon. He's also hilarious. Dan rocks!

Dan is a great educator.  He comes off as a little mean and uncaring but the truth is he wants you to succeed and is willing to help you any way he can.  He holds workshops on his own time to make sure you know programs and information that was not gone over in class.  I highly recommend this teacher!

I disliked him so much at first. Attending class was such a drag. He was very intimidating and came off as rude. but then i realized that's just how he is, he's extremely helpful and funny too. He pushes us to do our best. I thought i'd fail the class i was SO SHOCKED to see i passed with a B. I learned so much from him, HIGHLY recommend this prof

I love Dan!! I think he tells you like it is, and I appreciate that. Taking Gateway from him was amazing, he doesn't sugar coat things and he teaches you what makes for good journalism and what doesn't. I think if you are going to take gateway you should take it from him! He does use scare tactics though, but they worked on me! You'll b better 4 it

Dan has the grumpy old man thing down pat... and it works for him. He's seen it all, done it all, and has no patience for ****. Refreshing, and honestly pretty inspiring. Sure, he might be a better in-the-field journalist than an instructor, but he's frankly interesting. More than can be said for a lot of others out there...

Honestly not great. Graded on: reading, quizzes, tests, and essay. But he gives you a vague final essay worth a majority of your grade and never talks about it. Lectures and discussions aren't helpful. Mandatory volunteer work too? Don't bother with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I dropped...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Professor Hindery is committed to sustainable practices and his enthusiasm for sustainability shows through in his lectures. 
You are graded by weekly article writes ups and short essay based exams/a presentation. 
If you show up to class, participate and do all the readings you will get a good grade and enjoy this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Hindery is very committed to sustainability and his enthusiasm for sustainable practices shows through in his class lectures. You will learn a lot and get a good grade if you participate in class and do all the readings. 
Grades are based on weekly write ups and essay based exams/presentations.

I learned absolutely nothing in this class which is such a bummer, because the course is specific to my research concentration (Latin American development). He didn't actually teach us anything new and he used almost every lecture to plug his own field work that he does in Bolivia. Not a teacher... more like a conversationalist.

Professor Hindery gives vague directions and assigns readings without much consideration of their value.  Some of the assigned readings were just wikipedia pages.  He feels strongly about his beliefs and reminds his class regularly.  For some reason, people lost interest in the class and there was very low engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Easy course. You will learn about many issues, including climate change and minerals. There are weekly discussions and one question from his lecture. Also, every week there is a write-up. So essentially, you read and summarize two articles from that week. You will learn a lot and get a good grade, a win-win.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HIM!!! if you need any help at all you will not get it. He takes weeks if not months to respond to emails and makes it nearly impossible to get any type of feedback or support. He will assign very vague assignments and when you try and get more information about what he wants or help reviewing your work he ignores you

I took this class remotely, I would have enjoyed the lectures more if they were recorded zoom videos instead of a powerpoint you have to click through. GLBL 280's content was very engaging and you can tell Hindery cares about what he does. You are graded on a short paper every week, discussion, quizzes, one research paper and a final exam.

I swear to God, this man's lecture's are 80+ slides long and dry as toast. Get a coffee man, you sound passed out. Are you doing okay? The class isn't difficult, but it is by far the most dull two hours and thirty minutes of my life every Tuesday and Thursday (yes, that's how long it takes me to get through the PowerPoint). Ouch.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Hindery is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and is extremely inspirational. He truly cares about making our earth a better place and holding those responsible for destroying it, accountable.

Professor Hindery expects a lot out of students for a 200-level course. I have taken several online 4-week classes throughout my 4 years at UO and found that his course was extremely demanding and it's almost impossible to keep up. If you have anything else going on during your week, do not take this class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hindery is hands down the most boring professor I've ever had. I swear he pops a couple xannys then starts lecture. He has experience in the field and sure he's a "caring" guy but he's a professor not your pops. There's a sign in sheet in lectures for attendance, so you should go. The material is Interesting! But him talking about it is pure pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor takes himself way too seriously. In a lecture class he insists on having a "small class culture" banning the use of laptops and phones,  taking ATTENDANCE in a LECTURE, and getting upset if you try to pack up or leave early. Makes you attend outside-of-class events and cuts you no slack for what should be such a basic class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hindery is a nice guy, and the content he provides is important and has the potential to be interesting but he makes it boring. I thought he was a new professor for the first five weeks of class, super unorganized lectures and discussion sections, left for two weeks in the middle on the term  right before the midterm.

Honestly one of my favorite professors at UO. He clearly knows a lot about the subjects he teaches, and he really cares about his students. If you pay attention to the lectures you will learn a lot, and he also creates a lot of in-class activities that make the class interesting. Has the best and clearest grading criteria that I have seen at UO.

The material was interesting, but Hindery was not. Lecture seemed to drag on with him begging for interaction. Attendance matters a lot to him, but all he does is have you sign a piece of paper in the middle and end of class. All in all, class is easy to get an A weekly write ups and essay midterm & final. Just get ready for Bolivia.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: there are weekly write ups but they are only one page single spaced

Derrick's lectures can get long and a little boring, but it is all good material that is worth talking about. My biggest critique is that his upper division classes are essentially the same. It's not worth taking INTL 445 and INTL 420 because the classes are identical in structure and incredibly similar in content.

Doesn't teach, doesn't even lecture, he just talks and expects us to turn that into organized information that we can be tested on, then creates tests with rubrics that are a lie (midterm was based on how much you wrote more than anything else). Seems like a nice enough guy but he's just not a good teacher.

He is very passionate, but his teaching style is very dry and boring. It is a relatively easy class and informative, but unfortunately the readings are most interesting and class time seemed a bit wasted. Also, he presents a very biased argument, and tends not to mention others. This class could be done online easily.

I have really enjoyed Derricks class. He uses a lot of good examples- pics, videos, experiences... The class is really interesting if you apply yourself. I think people can learn a lot from him and i found him to be a great & helpful professor. I would take another one of his classes.

You cant get below a 50% on exams that is one of his rules so in short you start at 50 and if you get one question right your at 55%... He is a great teacher and if you show up to class you will get an A.

I don't know why people keep on saying he's fun and fair. He is fun to talk to and class material is interesting but it's too much information. At the end of every class it's like overloaded with information. I don't think his grading is fair at all. It's biased on what he thinks is good or not, even though the answers are right but he'll still mar

Derrick rocks. He's an awesome professor and really loves what he teaches. The assignments are pretty dang tough. Weekly write-ups, midterm, debate, research paper, research presentation, and a final. Wow has it been a tough class. At the same time I've learned a whole lot. Recommended to anyone interested in taking it.
genuinely nice guy, funny, interesting lectures. grading was fair, tests weren't too difficult as long as you went to class and went over the readings.

Derrick is a great professor who has lots of real experience in the field he teaches. He is approachable and happy to talk with students about anything regarding the class. His assignments are challenging, but definitely offer a lot of insight into the subject. I recommend taking his classes, they're what got me into INTL studies

Class was extremely easy, and just as boring. BUT, Deb did her best to keep it engaging and interesting when she could. She brought in a lot of cool and interesting guest speakers which was nice. Assignments were pretty boring, but easy. Deb's solid, class was just not fun (keep in mind I did take at 8:00 AM)
Very entertaining and fun personality, JCOM 101 was a super helpful class for getting started in the SOJC. She's very knowledgeable and is the perfect professor for a class like JCOM 101.

Deb was my first teacher at UO as an LCC transfer student. She's an awesome teacher to start your day with! She definitely made a tiring 8am class energetic and is easy to work with. She was also one of the first people to talk to me and make me feel comfortable at UO when I was new this fall term. The assignments in this class are super easy too.

Deb's a G. Especially is you're an Ad major. She's well respected among the J school. She's also funny. Its the kind of class you want to take notes in because she says a long of memorable things. There's a lot of guest speakers. There's some in-class assignments. 2 exams on Canvas and 3 creative projects. "Do the work you want to be known for"

JCOM 101 in general is a pointless and boring class, but Deb didn't necessarily make it anymore interesting. She was kinda annoying and made the class super hard to present/interested in. Not the worst, but definetly not great.

Super easy class as long as you show up. There are in class assignments that can't be made up so don't miss those. Very easy grader as long as you follow the rubric. Overall I love Deb as she is very friendly and passionate. The class got boring towards the end because it felt repetitive but that's the class not the professor.

Deb is the best professor to start college out with. I took this class for a platform credit in the SOJC and she really got me excited for my future here. She takes the time provide real information to use both educationally and professionally. Be ready for random in class assignments though, they will bring down your grade if you miss 2+ of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: a very informative, intro-journalism class for those interested in the sojc. deb is equally hilarious as she is inspirational, but the class is extremely lecture heavy.
Prof Morrison is a fun start to being a JCOM student but if you're not majoring in a j-school major, I wouldn't recommend this class. Project and lecture heavy class.

Love Deb and her class only rough thing is participation. I'm a good student + tried to attend all her classes, but as a freshman living in the dorms I got sick quite frequently and sometimes just couldn't make it to class. There was no way of making it up and any excuses made would not be heard. Attendance is graded through random in class points.

Genuinely the worst teacher I've had in 16 years of schooling. Your grade is 90% based solely on in-class assignments. Get ready to wake up at 7 am to go to class. Do not take this class if you think it will be a class you can skip a couple times. You can't even skip one class if you're sick without losing 5-10 points off your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Deb is so inspiring! Motivational for new students. Her class is really what you make of it. You only really have 3 fairly simple assignments, she just expects you to give it your best effort. Grading can be unclear and strict at times, but overall fair. You get a lot from this if you put a lot in. ATTEND LECTURES AND CONNECT WITH GUEST SPEAKERS!!

Deb is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's kind, caring, and not afraid to tell you what she thinks. She wants the best for all of her students and is an excellent resource. Make sure to go to her office hours!

Deb is amazing, her lectures are so inspiring, and I feel like I leave her class a better person every day. All assignments in this course allow you to be so creative. I would ABSOLUTELY take another class with her, and you should too. It's an honor to have been in her class. She is so experienced, and you can tell she loves what she does.
Very outgoing and good professor, always has guest speaker either on video or in person. The project are very inspirational and motivate your mind.

Deb is inspirational and esteemed, while still being accessible and approachable. The class is very easy, and offers a great taste-test of SOJC offerings/faculty. Deb does a great job of getting students excited about future opportunities. She's super personable, kind, and knowledgable — I hope I get the chance to take a class from her again!

Deb is so amazing! Her lectures feel like mini pep talks and she did a great job getting me excited about my future within the SOJC. The class is mostly guest lectures which I found super interesting, and the assignments are pretty straight forward but they take a little while to complete.

Extremely easy class only 4 assignments all term that can be done within an hour aside from the final assignment which takes some time and planning but is very manageable and useful especially if you actually know what you want to do. I would recommend not missing any lectures since that's the majority of your grade.
super evil

Dr. Morrison is great! The class is mostly guest lectures, and her passion along with the speakers really helped to make an inspiring class. Final test is optional and the last big project is a 4-year plan to guide your career success. Attendance is mandatory, and I'd caution against taking this at 8am as it can be hard to stay engaged so early.

This class was very easy. Not many assignments, the few given are pretty simple if you are interested in a career in media or related to the SOJC. Deb was a very inspirational professor and got me very excited about the possibilities of my career. This class is mainly just guest lectures which can be repetitive but overall was very interesting.

This class was not very assignment or test heavy, only one big final project that did take some time.  optional online final for extra credit. Deb is definitely a nitpicky grader and would mark off points for the smallest details. To add, attendance was graded and weighted very heavily which was stressful as this was an 8 AM.

She is a nationally recognized and extremely qualified professor. Deb values any/all questions and speaks of students with pride. Her lectures feel like Ted Talks- inspiring but they eventually repetitive. She is a great resource and always willing to share her networking. Super kickass lady!

I took Debs JCOM 202 class, not 199, there was no option. The first grade went into the gradebook the last week of November. Her instructions are unclear, and her feedback is not helpful partially due to the fact that there is no outline for the class since it's new. Says she's a generous grader, though usually takes 20+ points off assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Deb is fantastic. This class is her baby and she adores the students in it. She spends so much time talking about creativity and encouraging you to pursue a job in your niche. She exerts herself for her students. If you need a connection, she's got it. Homework is reasonable. Participation is important. Attendance is not required but very helpful.

Class taken Fall 23, Deb is awesome! She knows what she's talking about and is totally legit in the industry. Big group project stuff is most of the grade, class lectures are inspirational and will get you excited to work and not just bore for 2 hours. 100% take

Deb is phenomenal. She has created a home for her students in Eugene. 
I was skeptical coming into the year because of her reviews on here, though I can safely say Deb supports each and every one of her students. She bends over backwards to get you where you need to go and it amazes me.

Be careful with Deb. If you're not one of her groomed students, you won't get any attention. There's so many talented professors in the J school who have actually had experience and can be really useful. Find the other teachers in the school or reach out to J school alums. Must better advice than Deb, I don't know why she is the program director.

Deb is the reason the ad program sucks. Not only does she selectively favorite and groom certain students, but she is not even an experienced professional, she tells stories of her son's experience in the industry and uses his talent to look important in the industry. If you're new to the ad program, don't get brainwashed by the show she puts on.

She does not teach anything of use to this class meant for advertising. She teaches us about climate change and how to be a leftist, climate change activist and social justice warrior. If you are expecting to learn about useful insights and skills needed for adverting don't. She says as ad majors its our job to change the world lol.

Imagine reading LinkedIn job descriptions for 2 hours... Congrats. You now have the same hollow feeling that ensues after every class. I read one of the posts on here that says Deb is an "advertising goddess". She's never actually worked one day in the field. This class is her telling students what advertising is like through stories she's heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately you have to take this class if you want to be an Ad major and Deb really sets the tone for what kind of unprofessionalism you're going to be dealing with. She got in huge trouble for telling our entire lecture that "Black people don't know their family's immigration story," which was visibly offensive to AA students.

I would say Deb doesn't teach, she inspires. She talks about climate change and other important topics to get people, especially college students, involved in. Creative Strat definitely offers a different view point. idea book is stressful, group project isn't really outlined, nothing is graded until the very end too so you don't know your grade.

Deb is seriously such a horrible Professor. Im very confused why people like her because she only favors very particular and creative people and become obsessed with them. The whole two hour class is her ranting about random stuff that isnt helpful toward your future. The ideabook and extravaganza are the stupidest assignments ever as well.
This class is so inspiring! Deb is interesting, funny and very wise.

Deb is fantastic. She drives you hard but in the most motherly way possible. She  makes you believe in yourself and learn so much more than you would ever imagine. Her assignments are know for being extraordinarily vague which works great for those that love the room for their own creativity, but tough for those that like rules and structure.
If you're not inspired, she'll inspire you.
Deb is an adveritsing goddess. Best teacher I've ever had. Full of cool ass insights and connections. A good person to get to know.

Hands down the best teacher I have ever had, and easily the most enjoyable class I have ever taken. The Creative Strategist inspired me in countless ways, and Deb is incredible. She is helpful, funny, straight-forwrad, passionate, and wants her students to succeed. This class is a lot of work. Hard work. It will make you better. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
Great professor. She'll ride you hard if she thinks you can handle it and will blow you off if you are a slacker. Her classes are always 'you get what you give'

302 is a very lecture heavy class and you cannot miss more than one class or your grade will drop. She uses iclickers but honestly the questions are really engaging and make you think about the content. She has a really dry sense of humor which I liked, but I just didn't love the class

She is a very good professor. She has very organized lecture slides, and her overall structure of the class is easy to follow. Her lectures are engaging and enjoyable, and she provides a pretty thorough explanation of the material. She has hosted extra study sessions to help students prepare for the exams, which not many professors would do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good professor, pleasant class

Really appreciated her lectures, they were very clear and informative. Tests are very fair but they are a little challenging. She also granted me an extension on my midterm when I was sick which I feel like is rare from teachers. My only issue is she sometimes speeds through slides and does not give nearly enough time to write it down.

Professor Demircan is really nice and very passionate about the class. It can be hard to understand her, though, which makes it difficult to take notes. Her class is very lecture-heavy and you are only tested on the lectures. She also doesn't make study guides and state what we should know for the test.

Overall an excellent professor. She explains the concepts very clearly and genuinely wants her students to succeed. The weekly quizzes and homework were also really helpful and helped me understand the concepts come exam time.

I think that Dasa is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She is funny during lectures and is available to help outside of class. Her lectures are fast paced, so taking good notes is essential. She made all of the programs and textbooks used free for her students, which is much appreciated!

Dasa cares about her students and wants you to do well but she goes extremely quick during her lectures. She is sometimes hard to understand, but if you are good at stats then she is the professor for you. There are two midterms and a final exam that are in person, and you need to spend time studying for this class.

Dasa is cool. I think she wants everyone to succeed. I don't love her teaching style for stats though. I learn way more in the labs than I do from the lectures. If you're not great at math, I wouldn't recommend her. She covers content extremely quickly and doesn't spend a lot of time on questions.

Dasa is an amazing professor! She explains the difficult statistical concepts very well. There is a worksheet, quiz & lab due every week, no midterm & a final. The worksheets are collaborative & she goes over the q's during class if theres time. 2 attempts at the quizzes & the labs are pretty easy. She really cares about the success of her students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly writing this review to make one thing very clear. Dr. Zeithamova speaks perfect English and her accent does not in any way interfere with learning. She is a genius and cares so much. Everything is completely clear and I'm truly so disappointed that so many people are saying her accent added to the difficulty. It did not, and that's rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm so surprised she has such a low rating! I feel like she's a super good teacher and she's always down to spend more time explaining concepts if you don't understand them. I haven't personally found her accent to be too difficult to understand and I did much better than I thought I would in this class.

Dasa is a good professor and cares about how you do in her class. She tries to explain things as clearly as possible but she does have an accent that can interfere with her clarity of the lectures. Her tests are concept-heavy and there is not a lot of hand calculations to do. I definitely think you should go to class for this one.
she is the most confusing person when it comes to wording which will make you miss easy points. Also has homework assignment that can take up to 3 hours

Dasa is a solid choice for a professor. Her grading guidelines are really straightforward and she is always willing to answer your question in depth with you. She is clearly super knowledgeable about what she teaching which I really respect. You can get a B in this class doing the bare minimum (I would know) so I imagine an A would be pretty easy.

At first I really didn't like her, but as the class went on, I started to really enjoy her as a teacher. Her class can be super boring if you don't take notes. Her exams are not that hard as long as you know vocab.

Dasa is very smart and knows this material well. The lectures are long but she does her best to keep everyone engaged. iClicker questions are for attendance/participation and helpful to get an idea of exam questions. The multiple choice exams are pretty difficult. Study the lecture slides, read the textbook, make flashcards, and you'll be fine.
She is not that strict, but she really likes to test the conceptual stuff and the wording of question makes the test even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although the class is very lecture heavy, Dasa does her best to make it engaging. She is very funny and entertaining to listen to.
My favorite professor at the UofO! Take her... You won't regret it!
She is awesome. Very open, test are pretty straight forward. Homework is cake.

You have to purchase a device to take in class quizzes. Participation is the only requirement. Easy fun online homework assignments. Tests can be challenging but you should get a C at least. Must sign up for 4 hours of research time or something as well. Easy A or B with a little effort.
She's an awesome professor. Read the book, study the slides, you'll get an A.

She is a very nice professor, but she is super hard to understand due to her accent. And she says "Uhh, the uhhh, umm, the uhhh" through the whole lecture which makes it even harder to understand on top of her accent. Even while really trying to understand, her "Uhhh's" threw me off the topic even more so.

No a very good professor.  It was really hard to understand what she was saying most of the time because she does not speak very good English. There were four exams through out the class and one of them was literally a week before the final. She assigns online "quizzes" every week that are very specific to the book and take at least an hour to do.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. Her English and attempt to explain simple concepts fall short of below average. She's honestly better off as a researcher than a professor. The lectures are extremely long and she teaches only off the powerpoint slides. Along with being technologically inept, her class is quite boring

Very hard to understand and not very good at making class interesting. 95% of the learning needed to be done on your own through the textbook because her english is awful. One of the worst teachers I've ever had, do not taker her class.

Her power points are disorganized, explanations are gibberish, English is terrible, and she doesn't seem aware that nobody knows what she's talking about. You'll do better to read the textbook than learning the subject from her. If her class were a structure it would be a bunch of  nails and boards scattered across the ground.

Game Theory is an intriguing course; however, it can become a nightmare with the professor. Unfortunately, the professor is tenured, which means that the ratings at the end of the term hold little weight and cannot affect any change. I advise against taking this course with this professor.

Avoid if you value your GPA. The professor prioritizes rigid formatting over actual understanding. You can get every answer right and still fail an exam based on minor stylistic preferences. Unrealistic exam timers and a focus on 'pointless' busywork made this my worst experience at UO.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things
