reviews.comment: This was the worst course I've taken at UO. The professor cared far more about rigid formatting than actual understanding. Even correct answers lost major points if they didn't match her exact format. Exams were unfairly timed, and grading felt harsh, inconsistent, and focused on pointless requirements.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had at this school. 10 weeks of straight misery, and her grading rubric somehow makes the experience 100 times worse. Which sucks because Game Theory is a fascinating topic

She is an extremely tough grader, and her words do not align with her actions. She says there is no single correct answer, yet when grading, you are expected to write exactly what she prefers, word for word. Even if your reasoning is correct but phrased differently from what she has in mind, you receive zero. It feels unreasonable

I struggled during the class. It was brutal. However, on the other side of the final, I feel that she was a better teacher than I gave her credit for. She is very blunt and borderline berating, but at the end of the day I learned a lot more in that class than I have in any other micro theory class. Plan a light schedule if you take her class!

Anne has a rep for being a hard teacher, which she is, but she is also fair. Be ready to come to class ready to think. Respect her class by actually trying your hardest and you will be rewarded. She wants to see you succeed inside and outside the classroom but that's only gonna happen if you deserve it by giving it your all. She's also very funny

I would not recommend taking this professor if you do not have too, find another professor for this course. Has an arbitrary rubric that she uses to give whatever grade she feels you deserve. In this course you can get the solution to the problems but if it is not done in the manner which she " feels is right" it will be marked wrong.

Anne is incredibly blunt, and some of the things she says in class come off as downright mean. She is very unclear about her policy for grading assignments, and doesn't provide much clarity on what she is looking for. All of this being said, if you engage in class, laugh at her jokes, attend office hours, and talk with her, you will be fine.

Given the other reviews I was scared to take her class. That being said, she wasn't as bad as it's made out to be. Yes, participation is important and yes she can be very stern and intense when asking you questions during class, but overall she was a friendly person. The homework and tests were hard, but not impossible. Overall an alright time.

Game theory is extremely difficult. This is her field of expertise and she is knowledgeable on the topic. However, as others have mentioned, there are parts of her grading policies that are vague, and if you value approachability in a professor, she's not the one for you. The way she answers questions in class can come across as rude/condescending.

I understand where all these bad reviews are coming from, but I think she's great. She cares about actually getting students to learn the material, rather than simply memorizing patterns to get correct answers. Her class is a lot of fun, although everyone is obviously scared of her. I found her to be very available outside of class.

Completely opaque on grading policies. 
Will flatly refuse to answer questions in class.
Cannot seem to clarify anything, ever. 

Let me reiterate, would not tell us how we are graded and would change grading policies with no warning or notification.

An abysmally bad professor.

Explains things horribly, grading is based more heavily on useless semantics than whether you actually get the question correct or not. makes awkward jokes during class and lectures are very boring because she goes over the same thing over and over again. Doesn't have a set office hours time which just seems lazy. just not a good teacher all around
Does an awful job explaining topics in-class, and is relatively inaccessible outside the classroom. Homework is nothing like what you see on the tests.

From my experience in this class, even if you do all the homework's, attend lecture, and read the textbook, the exams are exceedingly tough. She tests you on material you hardly cover and uses a tough grading system. Anne is very bright, and she does a good job of teaching you how to organize high level economics problems, but this is a tough class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is somewhat condescending. Makes lots of jokes in class. The group work each class is good but the homework is WAYYY harder than anything we ever do in class. Office hours with her and her GEs are completely unhelpful, they give vague answers. You as a student get rated on how you behave with other students and then receive a "report card".
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Such an easy class but Anne makes it impossible. Very confusing, made fun of students for asking questions, and frequently reversed things she said. For example we were told we would be allowed to use calculators on the exam, then showed up amd she denied the use of calculators.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Have never had an economics professor I didn't like before taking her class. Not a kind woman, which would be ignorable if she was a good teacher, but she's far from it. Don't take her class, she makes material that is very doable and understandable much more complicated than it should be. Thank me later
I read the feedback before taking the course but ignored them. I regret taking the class with her!

I'm a doctoral student who take Anne's Game Theory class as an elective, which is turning into a nightmare for me. The material is actually easy but she makes the exams unnecessarily hard by being ridiculously picky on notations and formats, which drags people's attention away from actually understanding the material. And she's rude. Avoid!

Anne is rude, does not allow students to talk, and constantly puts down the answers we give in class. This is the worst class I have taken at UO. I leave everyday pissed because this class should be simple and interesting, but instead it's complicated for the wrong reasons. I regret taking this class and I would NEVER recommend Anne to anyone.

Worst professor I've ever had. Don't take her class. She is so mean. She makes you really bas if you want help in her office. if you don't come during her office hours she won't talk to you. She does't respect anyone but she wants to respect her. Try to avoid her classes as much as you can. I have went her all classes but dos't make any different.
Worst professor I've ever had. Don't take her class. She so mean. she dosen't offer help make feel really bad if you talk to her. DONT TAKE HER CLASS EC 311
Worst professor I've ever had. Don't take her class. She is mean, it is hard to communicate with her, and she wont offer help in office hour.

Her class is hard but fair. I would recommend taking at least one 300 or other 400 level econ class first to learn a few basic ideas, like a Nash equil. The average test scores are low but there's a big curve (~70%=B). She's closed off and some felt that made her seem condescending and aloof, but she's not a bad person and enjoys helping people.

This was the only class I ever had to drop. The tests were ridiculously hard. She provided very few practice problems but the tests were ridiculously long. Grad students and undergrad students had almost identical tests. This resulted in both grad and undergrads having mean and medians around 55%. Condescending and unhelpful.
She's the worst teacher ever. Doesn't care about her students, makes fun of them when they ask question. Refuses to make time to meet outside of class.

Probably the worst class I've had. She answers student questions in a condensing way that leads to a silent class. Her Lectures and homework do not prepare you for her midterms and final, which composes 75% of your grade. Medians for tests are hovering around 65%. Avoid.

Single Worst teacher i ever had. She was extremely rude to all students. Made me afraid to raise my hand in class. Tests were almost impossible to study for and the averages were a D or lower. should not be teaching at the University of Oregon. Shouldnt be teaching period. DO NOT TAKE A COURSE FROM THIS TEACHER. EVER.

She made this course much more difficult than it should have been.  She doesn't prepare you for the midterms and the final.  The examples taught in class are much easier than the problems in the exams.  Her classes are manageable as long as there is a good GTF.
worst teacher i have ever had. she refuses to answer questions or help in anyway other than just teach in class. she will turn questions around and ridicule students.

Her disregard for student feelings left class silent,we were ridiculed for wrong answers.Being shamed for wrong answers happened a lot and made me want to miss class.Her disregard for our feelings and wardenesque style of teaching made me feel unsafe.By far,this is the worst instructor I have had. I will never take a class with this woman again.

By far the worst teacher I have ever had in my 14 years of public education.  She takes a sick pleasure in calling kids out in class to shame them, and laughs when someone offers an incorrect answer instead of helping them.  I am an econ major, but will never take another class with this woman.
I got an A+

Teacher writes very confusing test questions, doesn't prepare you for the Home work questions completely. But goes slow enough through the book that you do have time to figure it out yourself. GO to class, even though technically it is not mandatory.
The material is not that hard if you find economics interesting and not too difficult. The average on quizzes is a D-. She doesn't care about students and doesn't like to help them

Doesn't appear to care about the students. Doesn't know how to engage them. Doesn't know how to explain things in a different way. Seems to take pleasure out of making students feel insecure and miserable.

This teacher is far less interested in teaching the material to the students than she is in making sure she seems brilliant. She uses simple examples in class that are in no way indicative of the difficulty of homework or test questions and she is not interested in helping students who need help. Pray for a good GTF.
This professor needs to get kicked out of the department! She is not helpful at all. She doesn't want to waste class time answering questions that students may have! I hate that teacher!

This class is not hard if you just learn to think on the level of a game theorist.  In fact, I never had a hard time with the coursework at all and only made things more difficult by working with my study group to come up with laws that could always be applied for certain models.  You need to take International Trade first so you have a foundation for Nash Equilibria.
worst professor I have ever had. When I went to see her in her office she tried to get me out as fast as she could. She doesn't care about the students at all.

She was a horrible teacher. She expects the class to understand the materials. A student came to her office hours and needed help, and she got mad and threw his book on the ground because he didn't understand the material. The student ended up dropping the course. Shes not very helpful and clear. She lectures way too fast + it is hard to understand

I liked but rec. only for the very smart. She is, although well hidden, a very nice person. I did well but the class is analytically demanding yet fair. She is obsessed with fairness(50%=B). She did not answer questions... due to equity, or so smart she does not get it-could be some superciliousness

The assignment rubric was not clear, and she was very picky about assignments. She said it's okay to add English in our writing, but it would bring the grade down. Online class, but made us meet with her in office hours in person, which was graded, and work with other people. Very nice, but cannot teach in online course.

Grecia is one of the best teachers I have ever had, She makes it difficult to NOT understand the work/content. 
If you have a choice to take any spanish prof at UO, CHOOSE PROF GRECIA.

I couldn't ask for a better professor. Grecia is very passionate about what she teaches, and cares about the success of every student in her class. She's really great at teaching the information in a way that you  can easily retain. As long as you show effort and participation in this class, you will do great.

Grecia is an amazing professor. She is very caring and wants to create a sense of community on campus. Readings were never too long and lectures are largely discussion based and engaging. There were frequent quizzes writing short reflection paragraphs, everything is open note. I would absolutely take a course with her again.
Great teacher, genuinely cares and is very helpful no matter what.
Grecia is truly such a caring person and incredible engaging teacher. She calls on everyone to challenge the class but always helps and never calls anyone out. Favorite spanish teacher by far.

I have had a different teacher for all 3 of my first year Spanish classes and Grecia has been, by far, my favorite. She calls on basically everyone every class so you do get solid in class practice and she gives good feedback. She has taught me the most and sometimes she even brings her dog.
Grecia really cares about her students and their success. Attendance is mandatory, but she grades pretty easy and tests aren't too difficult.
Very interactive with you and the class, makes sure you get through everything and believes in you

I took Spanish 101 with her and it was amazing! She is very helpful and will always work with students. She makes learning Spanish very fun and easy. Absolutely recommend for new Spanish speakers for beginning classes.

I absolutely loved having Grecia as my Spanish professor! Her presence in class is uplifting and encouraging, she made me want to participate more. It made speaking Spanish less intimidating, I was never afraid to ask for help if needed. I highly recommend taking her class for the whole sequence!

I really enjoyed Grecia's class!! she was very kind and easy to talk to and had no problem seeking you out if you needed help since the class size was smaller. the attendance policy is STRICT, you get 1 excused absence and after that she starts taking points off of quizzes/hw. hw/quizzes are weekly but can be long so don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was an absolutely amazing professor. Her lectures in class are interactive and fun, and she genuinely cares about her students. I have enjoyed her classes for Spanish 101, 102 and I am taking her 103 class as well this spring!
Very unstructured class, never responded to any of my emails when I reached out for help or questions. Very difficult to get an A due all the misleading a poorly worded exam questions.

I took this class as an advertising major and for the final the questions were extremely misleading and I reached out to clarify some of the questions on a weekday and he took forever to respond and then when he finally did respond he said he wanted his definition on a term when on the final it asked for our definition and he gave me a 0/4.

Dr. Buck was one of the best professors I've had at UO. Although he often goes on tangents I found his lectures to be interesting and interactive. He also cares a lot about his students and mental health, very approachable I would definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: best professor ever. highly recommend

The best! He's super nice and definitely works with you whenever you need it. This class was mainly PR writing and included assignments such as writing a news release, making a media pitch, etc. He always answered any question I had and looked over my work. Class was never a bore with Mundy. I would recommend definitely!
Amazing professor! Super engaging lectures that don't require attendance, and assignments are easy if you put the effort in. Would totally take again!

Professor Mundy is an amazing professor. The class is super interesting and the workload is pretty decent. relevant and interesting content. He is a funny and caring professor who makes lectures fun! Highly recommend this course.

I really enjoyed this class. There are only a few assignments in the class so they mean a lot for your grade, but for the work that aren't tests Dean and his GEs are willing to look over your work and give you feedback before you turn it in. His lectures are engaging and you learn a lot.

JCOM371. This guy owns. Lectures are engaging and interesting because Dean actually cares about the course material and is excited to share it with us. He's the epitome of a great college professor. The assignments are clearly explained and the exams cover the material presented in lecture. This class is easy because Dean teaches it so well. 10/10

Dean was one of my favorite professors. He has a lot of experience in the field which he brought to class every day. Truly enjoyed his class and I will recommend anyone to take his class if they can. Lectures were very informative but fun!

Dean is such a good teacher. He is so funny and always cracking jokes. I look forward to his class every time. He is the only reason I made this rate my professor account. You should take his classes if you are so inclined.
One of the best professors at UO. He is delightful, lighthearted, and really cares to make learning PR fun. I would take this class five more times.

Dean is a good guy that cares for his students and their learning. I really liked this class with him. There's not many assignments so make sure you do good on the ones that are assigned. The final is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have had Professor Mundy for two classes now but J350 has stuck with me. I originally went into the SOJC as a journalism major but after this class I changed to PR. Fun and amazing lectures, and while the class was big he made sure to connect with his students. Open note tests and even tho attendance wasn't mandatory you will want to go!

Dean was such a wonderful teach and is the reason why I am now majoring in Public Relations. His class was amazing and constantly kept me engaged. If you're a journalism major or a public relations major at University of Oregon I highly suggest taking his class. His instruction made class very easy to retain.

Dean truly cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. He responded to emails within minutes. The lectures were interesting and interactive which helped the lectures feel more engaging. Overall i would take any course Dean teaches and recommend you do the same.

Dean himself is great. He always replied to my emails (up until the last 2 weeks of the term... I don't know why I couldn't get a hold of him). His GE's were EXTREMELY difficult graders, and that is why I marked the class down. That being said- I didn't understand my grade from my GE, so I met with Dean, he reviewed my paper, and gave more points!

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Mundy is a great guy and his lectures were engaging. Two open note exams (midterm and final) and 3 written assignments where you analyze a press release (2 pages max). He also included a self-care project worth 10% to encourage us to spend 1 (screen-free) hour a week on ourselves. Great class highly recommend

Professor Mundy is a great professor and you will love this class! He is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are really interesting. The only hard thing about this class is the grades are just based on 3 writing assignments, the midterm and final. The tests are easy but the GE's grade pretty hard on the writing assignments. Overall recommended

Hands down best professor/educator I have ever had. I’ve never felt so cared by an educator especially during the uncertainty we all felt during this term. He prioritizes self care during his class and you can tell genuinely cares about the well beings of his students. amazing lectures, easy to follow, makes them interesting w/ personal stories

Hands down the BEST Professor I have ever had. Dean is the type of Professor every other SOJC faculty member should aspire to be. You can tell how much he cares about teaching his students. He has tons of real-life experience, making it clear he knows what he is talking about. Best lectures I have ever had and he doesn't waste your time.

Dean is amazing. Really a funny and genuine professor. I don't like PR, but he made this class enjoyable. We only have a few assignments, so it's really make or break. You've got to do good on the few assignments to get a good grade. I wish he recorded and posted lectures, but he does post the slides. Pay attention during the lectures!
I love Dean! He is a great prof, interesting classes, but there are very few assignments in the gradebook and tough to get an A on them. Still would take more classes from him, very sweet and funny
He was very understanding and a great teacher. He is very knowledgeable about the topics he discusses really hope to take another class from him.
Amazing class and an AMAZING professor. Everyone should take at least one of his classes.
Amazing teacher, truly a professor I will never forget. I also had him as my Thesis advisor, and he was great.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had in college! He really does care about his students, which is rare in classes that have 100+ people. He gives great advice and is super accessible outside of class or office hours, which is really refreshing since it seems like professors are even harder to reach right now. I highly recommend taking this.

Loved this class but I wish I could have taken it in person because of how fun the content is. He's a funny guy and is willing to meet with students outside of class and responds to emails pretty quick. Midterm and PR Newswire assignments were pretty easy and graded very fair. Pretty good class for being online.
Dean Mundy is one of my all time favorite professors. He makes his lectures interesting and the test are easy to understand. I definitely recommend him.
Took principles of PR during COVID fall 2020, he was very accomodating and the class discussion was optional. if you watched the lectures you would basically get an A

This class was amazing, and I cannot recommend professor Mundy enough. Even after our class ended he was sure to follow up with students and make sure they are doing well during the pandemic. Gives great school, career, and life advice too! Class isn't difficult if you pay attention and participate, but be sure to study for the midterm and final.

absolutely love professor mundy! he is one of the best professors i have ever had. he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. he has had a ton of experience in the industry so it's super interesting to hear what he has to say. would recommend any class he teaches!

TAKE THIS CLASS!! I feel like Dean has completely perfected his performance and style of teaching for this class. He keeps his content relevant and to the point. He gives real life examples and talks to us as if we are human. He understands the stress that a class like his has, and makes the class entertaining and interactive the entire time.

Easily has become one of my favorite professors at the University of Oregon. Wish I took his class earlier in my academic career. I would have changed majors had I met Dean sooner. Highly recommend other students to take his class and ask many questions. Dean has a relevant case studies for every situation.

I really enjoyed Mundy's class. I really appreciated the subjects discussed in class as well as the organization of the course. I'm excited to see more of him for my PR upper divisions. I would definitely take this course again because Mundy is an excellent instructor and really gives you a great overview of PR and what it entails.

I loved Dean. The midterm and the final were very straight-forward. The content is super interesting and he is such a funny and personable guy that he makes lectures really fun. I would take 8ams if it were with him anytime!

Professor Mundy was a fantastic professor who gave great lectures and was hilarious. He really knows how to teach Public Relations and made each lecture fun and engaging. He's a really funny guy who made 8am lectures less dreadful. Would definitely recommend taking one of his classes.

Dean is the best!! Even though this class was at 8am he really knew how to engage the class and make you care about the material. There is a lot covered, but the class is organized so that it feels applicable to the real world. He is also really funny, take this class with him!!!

Dean is a super nice and really caring professor. He really wants everyone to succeed and learn the ins and outs of the Public Relations field. You dont need the textbook. His tests are not scantron based and more like short answers, but he gives you enough time and info to be fully prepared.
Dean Mundy is a great professor and lectures are great. I did not use the textbook at all.
Great professor! Participation and attendance are both graded separately.
AWESOME!!! I absolutely loved his class. Very helpful, lots of extra credit, very straight fwd. TAKE HIM!
Loved taking this class. Mundy is the reason I joined the J school. Taking another class with him this fall and really looking forward to it. Overall, EXCELLENT professor.

Cool professor. Very nice and respectful of all students. I hope to take another of his classes. Class is mandatory, but it also makes studying for the tests easier. Instructions on assignments are clear and easy to follow.

Mundys class was really fun. He used a lot of real world examples that help explain things. You have to put in the work to pass, but the work is all fun. He is very helpful when asked. He's a really nice and considerate guy too. I would definitely recommendtake another one of his classes.

Huang LaoShi is a very nice person and her personality definitely makes class more fun. The only issue is she seems to pick favorites and will definitely call on some students more than others. Easily accessible for office hours though, and her GEs are nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doesn't force you to take the exams if you're not ready, zoom records the lectures so you can watch outside of class if you're sick, grades attendance but easy to make up for, not to hard of a grader and allows lots of opportunity to raise your grade. GE's I had were very nice and not hard graders either. Not hard to get an A if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Huang 老师 is very sweet and incredibly funny. The GEs (Jiang and Xi 老师) have high expectations but fair with grading. My only gripe with this class is that the textbook and character sheets sometimes have errors, and then we're marked down for writing something wrong, even though it was wrong when we learned it. Overall though, love the class.

Good professor for the most part. Places lots of emphasis on sitting in the front and being loud, so quieter students with better pronunciation will often get worse grades than louder students with worse pronunciation. Class is incredibly time consuming, expect 2-3 hours a day of focused studying to get in the A range, and GEs can be hit or miss.

In-class participation grading criteria is not clear. Attended every class and discussion just to be graded a 3.6-3.7/4.0. Dictations, character writing sheets, homework, and quizzes every week or so. Expects students to study for 2+ hours a night. Exciting teacher and makes class interesting. GE's are amazing as well. Needs to improve grading.

I had no trouble following along with the lectures. However, the GE's were most likely the toughest graders out there. There was some unfairness in grading and student favoritism. I dreaded my discussion classes with the GE's. Prof. Gigliotti was very enthusiastic and had a good sense of humor! Very time-consuming and a huge commitment
Tough grader, big time commitment, and so many tests every week. You have to spend so much time to even keep up with the class. I dropped for a reason

Huang Laoshi doesn't have the best language teaching methods and there are too many things to memorize before two quizzes every week. I guess if you really really have time to sit down for at least 5 hours a day to memorize letters and meanings, then this class is for you. The character handwriting sheets are ridiculous and an outdated method.

Focuses more on assigning and less on pronunciation. Grading criteria is on syllabus however, is not reflected by performance. Attend and participate in every class, may not receive full points even once. Inconsistent in grading. Gives students the "asian" grading chart and applies it: 
A: acceptable
B: below average
C: can't eat dinner
etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chinese 101 with Denise was the worst class I've taken in my entire college career. She is rude and treats students either "A students" or "bad students." If you come in with prior knowledge of chinese, no A. She has a unique way of being enthusiastic and it made me very uncomfortable. Both she and her short, tight dresses are wildly inappropriate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Huang's class unless you have a background in Chinese already. The few kids in the class that don't have prior Chinese knowledge fell behind fast. Difficult class with hours of homework regularly
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's kind of funny, but says some out of pocket things that make you think hmmm. Be ready to write characters a million times because its the only way you'll remember them. You'll have a few quizzes a week, but this class is doable.

This class is a lot of work. Show up to class looking alert & ready to be called on. You get graded based on answering pop quizzes in class. The grading standards are both clear and arbitrary. One person might do horribly in class, mispronounce words, but still somehow do really well, while another who is mediocre but uses tones well may not.

Huang Lao Shi is an excellent Chinese teacher. She's very engaging and extremely clear about what you need to be doing in the class. While her class is tough, you'll get an A as long as you work hard every day in and out of class. Overall an excellent and very fair professor.

She's great! If you try your best in her class you can do well (I put no effort and got a B). She does a great job of making expectations fair (different for students who speak Chinese at home vs. true beginners). I wish she used a standard grading system though. Still, great professor, very knowledgeable, and very fun and easy to learn from.

She cares about your performance and takes notes of your efforts and participation in class. You can talk to her regarding your issues about this class and she will be more than happy to figure it out for you. She is very clear about her expectations in this class and if you follow it and try hard enough, getting an A is super doable.

Amazing language to learn, but she makes you dedicated. Not a language if you're looking to easily fulfill a requirement. Be prepared for hours of homework at least 3 nights a week. Denise is a good teacher though. Understanding and funny.

Huang Laoshi is a silly teacher (in a good way). I felt like I was taught by a friend, rather than a teacher. She will brighten your day with her enthusiastic personality. It is an enjoyable class. You will have a small quiz every week and various assignments throughout the course. But guess what? No final exam!

Sweet heart prof. She will put you on the spot though, especially if if you wear something interesting. Does not give A+ unless you show obsession level interest in the class. Sit and lectures three days of the week with no activities or handouts. She reads of the powerpoint. I wish there's different teachers for 102 and 103 but nope.

Best foreign language teacher I've ever had! She makes learning Chinese, a language that is often seen as difficult and intimidating to English speakers, a fun and worthwhile experience. Bonus: sometimes she shows up dressed in costumes/wigs.
Great teacher! Gives a method for learning and studying Chinese
Really funny and really helpful. Couldn't recommend her more!

Great prof. She very clear about was is to be expected on exams and homework. If you keep up with the schedule and study/practice more than 6 hours a week on top of hw and quizes and you'll do fine. Though she is a great teacher this language is extremely difficult and not for those who are lazy or tone deaf.

Really nice and keeps things interesting! I don't think i've ever met a teacher who used One Piece anime for examples but it was awesome! She's a very cool person and her class is easy if you stay one step ahead of the schedule in your character writing and practiec
Funny sense of humor, easy to understand and answers questions.  Lots of memorizing and repetition drawing characters.  Stay ahead, memorize, and it shouldn't be too bad.

She is very funny, very energetic, and a great teacher. She takes a difficult subject and makes it something you want to show up for every day, which you have to if you want to pass with a B or higher.
Best Professor ever, really said she wont be teaching 3rd year chinese. Fun and random, covers what u need to know in class. If you study and pay attention its not hard to get an A
Great teacher, funny personality.  Loves Harry Potter and Frodo Baggins.  Lots of memorizing involved in the class.  Stay ahead and it's an easy A.  Pretty sexy too!
Great teacher, I wish she would take more control of the class sometimes.
Great teacher! She makes learning Chinese fun and interesting. She has a great sense of humor!

Awesome and clear. Always fun to be in her class. Speaks clearly and is always willing to answer questions. But she has virtually no control over the class. It's like a high school study hall in there sometimes, which she does really nothing about.
fun!
Great class, fun teacher I enjoyed the class a lot and am excited to continue the language
Great class, fun teacher I enjoyed the class a lot and am excited to continue the language
Pretty hip and laidback teacher who would talk about Darth Vader, Naruto and Jay Chou in her class. Fun!!
Great professor!
Truly inspiring and incredible professor, speaker, and individual.

Djiffack is truly the ideal french language professor. He promotes all students in speaking and writing, firm yet kind with his corrections, with a very lighthearted sentiment. Course content is heavy but he is exceptionally generous, with a lot of take-home work. He grades on effort in my belief, all around incredible professor, taking him again!

Professor Djiffack is OG. I took 3 classes from him (312 and 490x2). 490 was very book heavy and in 312 I had a textbook. He gives amazing feedback and he is inspirational, cultured, yet very humble. He is really into in-class learning, so make sure you pay attention to his lectures because they will rock your world. One of the best profs at UO.

Very knowledgable and a very good speaker. Lecture set-up meant there was no reason to read the article before class, just the ones you had a presentation on and for the midterm and final (Those were all the assignments, all year) Funny, but his accent takes time to get used to.

Really passionate and friendly guy. It's clear he really cares about the subject material and his students. That said, I was not that invested in the subject material so it wasn't that great of a class. Also there are very few assignments w/ no real grading rubric and he doesn't use Canvas so you don't really know what grade you're gonna get.
Amazing teacher! truly cares about his students! He is passionate, kind and so cultured!

Would take FOREVER to grade assignments. You wouldn't receive feedback until a day before your next large assignment, giving little time to correct mistakes. Lab reports would take days to complete, made o-chem reports look easy. Desperately needs to update her pre labs, so confusing, long lab days. Hated every week in this class, so glad it's over
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The post-labs and pre-labs are very confusing and the instructions are unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hawley is very kind, and if you have questions she is very accessible through email or office hours. That being said, lecture is very confusing and unclear at times. She will mix up her words quite a bit and it will be hard to understand what she meant sometimes. Also difficult exams that make up most of your grade (with a generous curve)

One of the worst teachers I've had ever. Terrible lecturer, gives quizzes that do not correspond to the material. Drones on and on in class, and assigns a mountain of out of class work. Very kind, but it doesn't matter at all because she's utterly incompetent at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes a nice person but it was her first time teaching in the Honors College and it was clear she had no idea what she was doing. She had very high standards that I think she thought matched the HC but they were almost unrealistic. The final grade depended on 5 essays but we only got feedback during Week 10 after everything had already been done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, and always willing to help. The course is fast paced and difficult material. There is a fair sized curve, but getting a good grade will require significant effort.

I really enjoyed Diane's lectures, and her office hours were some of the best I've been to in college. She's super helpful and wants everyone to succeed. The material is definitely difficult, but she does her best to explain things during lecture and she's extremely respectful of student questions during lectures and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Diane is very sweet lady but she was teaching chemistry 111 when she normally teaches upper division chemistry classes so she expected us to know more than what the class did know. Whenever someone asked her a question she could not explain how or why the answer is why it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the most basic of chemistry courses at the university, and she explained at the beginning of the term that if you took high school chemistry that it would be a breeze. Well boy was she wrong. This class is not easy, and she does not explain the material very well. The lectures are boring and she puts trick questions on quizzes/tests.

Hawley is more interested in writing tricky questions than actually testing comprehension of material. Tests use new vocabulary and symbology, questions are unclear, and generally I miss points because I she uses has so many conditional modifiers in her questions. I'd say her fairness is poor at best, and her interest in teaching is negligible.

I think Diane is a good professor. She isn't the best lecturer, but I think she does a satisfactory job of getting key points across. Biochem is a hard class. Ken covers the easer material, so naturally people like him more.

Fairly good teacher. Can be a bit unclear at times, but she is very willing to make her best attempt to clarify any issue. She would often stay even longer after a 2 hour office hours session to clarify something I still did not understand. Kinda cute too (although you don't want to admit, but its true, and stems mostly from her nerdy personality)!

She is extremely boring.  Terrible Lectures.  Explains things in the most round about way possible!  Her willingness to help students is sub par.  Fortunatley the class was split between her and Ken Prehoda, who I enjoyed much more.
Not the easy A it appears to be. Be ready to spend all your time studying for the quizzes and exams.

Professor Dicus always made the lectures enjoyable and interesting, but the lectures were nearly word-for-word the readings. If you pay attention in the lectures, you don't really need to do the readings because he even gives you quotes. The tests only went over lectures/readings.
Very passionate and interesting lecturer. One of the easiest classes I've taken. Enjoyed my time and the content was fun.

I wan't excited to take this class but it turned out to be really interesting. It was about power and tyranny in Greek and Roman times but it was like he was teaching about the modern day. Homework was a lot of reading. He didn't take attendance but there are pop attendance quizzes worth 5 points. Really good lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The content was interesting to learn about. Prof Dicus tries to make his lectures attention-grabbing, but they just aren't. I managed to get through the course by reading 30% of the texts because of the great study guides and extra credit. There is no homework in this course, which is great, but you have to do a lot of studying on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture-heavy class, but drops the lowest quiz grade. If you pay attention in class, it is not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be easy but no, this professor puts topics that were barely gone over in slides or in readings. He does not give any assignments and your grade will be based only on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't give assignments. Grades are based only on quizzes and tests, which are only on paper. Puts stuff not covered in slides on the tests. Attendance quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dicus's lectures were very engaging and interesting—easily one of my favorite professors! I did the readings and studied the terms lists and felt prepared for all the quizzes and tests.

Dicus is an amazing professor. Take 110 if you want an easy global perspectives course. The material is fun to learn, and he is very engaging, especially at 9 am. Attendance is not mandatory, but the material is way more comprehensible when coming to class. Quizzes are easy and useful to prepare for the midterm and final.

Dicus is really funny and his tests aren't too hard. Study the terms lists he gives you and attend the lectures!! He gives attendance quizes that can boost your grade - these are super easy though. Final project was a lot of work. Watch Monty Python and the Holy Grail, sometimes his extra credit is based off the movie and you'll get his references.

While Professor Dicus is very passionate about his work, especially Pompeii, I have never been so frustrated with a class's assignments. Virtually no thinking is required for this class; instead, grading for midterms and quizzes is wholly dependent on your rote memorization of a large-ish number of dates/places. Take this class only if you must.

Dicus is easily one of the best proffesors I have ever had. He is super interesting as a person and his life has been truly incredibly. He is very engaged and loves to chat about his work. Meeting him for office hours was honestly so fun and helpful! I would highly recommend taking Dicus at least once just to learn some cool facts about Pompeii!
One of the best professors I've had!

Genuinely one of my favorite professors at UO. Very easy course as long as you spend a bit of time studying. Class material is pretty interesting, and his lectures are mostly interesting too. He has a very outward personality and funny most of the time. I didn't feel stressed by tests, quizzes, or assignments. Quite a bit of extra-credit too.

One of my favorite electives and teachers. Super easy but know that an A+ is 99-100%. Quizzes/midterm/finals are all relatively easy. There's a textbook but I rarely used it. Fantastic teacher/lecturer. I took notes but I know a few who never did and still passed with an A. He does attendance quizzes every once in awhile but makes the class fun.
Loved this class with Prof Dicus. His lectures are entertaining and I learned a lot. He is very accommodating to schedule difficulties and is fairly easy grading wise but I learned a lot.

Took this class for fun and an arts and letters credit, but it was very interesting and engaging. Not very difficult, lots of free points given out. Professor Dicus has engaging lectures with physical artifacts and personal stories relating to the material. Could not recommend more strongly!

Dicus is a lovely professor. Even though classics isn't even remotely relevant to my major I thoroughly enjoyed the class and genuinely looked forward to lectures. Both him and his teaching team were super supportive and creative with the ways they taught and reviewed material.

Pretty much just memorizing stories. It's pretty easy if you pay attention. I never bought the textbook but I'm passing. He's a good guy. Knows his stuff. I found It hard to catch up if I missed class

Professor Dicus was amazing. I only took the course because I needed an art credit but I'm glad I was able to take this class with him. His lectures are honestly very well thought out and Professor Dicus clearly knows what he is talking about. As long as you pay attention and or read the book you will not regret taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I liked Percy Jackson growing up so I took this class on Greek mythology. He does talk really fast but is accommodating and posts the lectures. It is doable to miss class but lectures are the majority of the content. 2 assignments a week, a little reading. 4 easy quizzes, a midterm and a final. Just pay attention in class and you'll be fine.
Professor Dicus is great! I would highly recommend taking a class of his if you are even remotely interested in Classics, this was a fairly easy course grading-wise but I genuinely learned a lot.
Prof. has a lovely voice and way of telling stories, but his online course proves to be disorganized. Switches topics randomly, hard to keep up sometimes.
He brings lots of artifacts and cool findings from his dig sites for classes!

Professor Dicus is an amazing instructor. Even with the class being online due to the pandemic, he made his lectures lively and fun to watch. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches and it definitely helps to make the class interesting. The quizzes and exams are not difficult as long as you study, watch the lectures, and do the readings.

Prof Dicus is amazing in every way. He gives a lot of chances for extra credit and he's extremely flexible and caring towards students. His lectures contain a lot of pictures, but you kinda have to show up to class because he mentions things that aren't on the slides. I promise you won't regret this class. He really cares about student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This teacher is THE BEST. Everyone loved him and he made me fall in love with the subject of archaeology. He is respectful and understanding when you need to miss class and gives a lot of leeway for things. Super funny and great lectures, he's super experienced too so that helps! Just go to class and you'll get an A. U DONT NEED TO DO THE READINGS!
Professor Dicus is the only professor that I have had here at UO that is so willing to be flexible with schedules and understanding. Very engaging and thoroughly looked forward to his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class. One of my favorite classes I've taken at UO. The lectures were really interesting and the discussion section as really fun. He gave extra credit which helped a lot. His work in Italy is really inspiring too, so it nice to learn from somebody who obviously loves what he does.

Charlie's class was a bit slideshow-heavy, I often found myself filling in missing notes after class hours. He's very nice and he's easy to talk to though. For some projects/group projects in this class, the instructions are unclear and 2 sets of instructions were posted saying different things. He could work on clarity on assignment instructions.

On the first day, he made the class sound extremely challenging, but by the second class, it was clear it was actually pretty easy. There are very few out-of-class assignments compared to other professors, four-ish major assignments, heavily graded, just read the rubric, and you'll pass. He gives in-class exit tickets which you can share w/ friends

His class is kinda interesting. He loves listening to students' opinions about his topics mentioned in class. He can change the due if he feels like the major of class is not ready to submit. Don't miss any classes if you don't want to drop grades or fail.

This class made me realize I don't want to be a Journalism major. Deitz is a decent teacher, essays are interesting and fairly graded. It's less about journalism and more about learning what media is (kind of boring to me). I just found the class and slides boring (it was hard to stay awake at 8 am). If you miss 7 classes, you automatically fail!

An overall easy course, the readings are interesting and easy to understand. The slideshows aren't much help so the reading is necessary to keep up. Assignments aren't very hard and very clear guidelines. He's also an engaging lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are a lecture-oriented person, Deitz will work well for you. He gives back what students give him- if you're on time and participating, he might cancel a class or extend a due date. If you don't put any effort in, don't expect any flexibility in return.

Prof Deitz puts in effort to make his lectures engaging, and it isn't the worst 8am to take. He cares a lot to engage with students in class. Textbook is required but you'll probably get by fine from just paying attention to the lecture if you don't want to buy it. GE kinda sucked though, overly harsh grader, but that's not really on him
Relays expectations at beginning of term, so as long as you listen and do what is asked, he's a great professor. Very helpful lectures as well.

Professor Deitz is funny and made lectures engaging and more interesting. The biggest part of the workload was the readings assigned for each lecture. Attendance definitely matters but he makes his class policies clear and explains assignments well.

Charlie would be a decent professor if he weren't on such a power trip. His class was very poorly organized and the exams were not easy to prepare for. He also purposely released study guides the night before the exams to "encourage people to study on their own." This class was a joke. I truly could not tell you one thing I learned from it.

i've had charlie twice now and i cannot stand his teaching style. aside from him being rude, he doesn't teach at all. j213 in theory is an easy class but he didn't release the study guide for our final (at 8 am) until 9 pm the night before. i wish other professors taught this class. not his fault but his ge's are tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Charlie is awesome. His lectures are fun and interesting, and he has some crazy PowerPoint skills. He is really easy to reach and offers really good feedback during office hours and after class. The course content was engaging, and there was limited work and assignments.

Don't be thrown by your first impression of Deitz. He can come off harsh at first but wants to see his students succeed. The projects are intimidating but are graded easier than expected. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities you will want to take advantage of.

Gateway is the most unorganized class I've taken. The idea of gateway is cool, but the professors ruin it (not the GE's). Both Charlie and Dan inspire no confidence in their students. Every time I go into class, I leave feeling awful about myself and my work. Both professors contradict each other everyday. Wish someone else taught.

Don't be derailed by your first impression of Prof. Deitz. He comes off very strict at first, but he ends up being a great guy to learn from. The tests and projects are very easy as long as you follow the clear instructions he gives. Only gripe is that nothing gets graded in a timely manner. Don't be scared off by the reviews, he is a great guy.

Charlie is great. Super engaging, funny, and clearly knows what he's talking about. I think the negative reviews come from his straight forwardness and the fact that he doesn't take BS. He is going to push you and all you need to do to succeed is to take his advice and take initiative in your projects. I'm excited to show up every day.

It's week 6 and only 1 of our 6 assignments have been graded. We have no guidance on whether or not we are doing the assignments right. He promised a two-week turn around and yet only one has been graded. He's aggressive with his lectures. We have a midterm this week and our first midterm project hasn't been graded either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sends out the pettiest announcements on Canvas. Will literally crucify you if you email him something that he "already went over in class". Sometimes I like him other times I don't. Frequents the EMU Starbucks. Weird how my lowest grades in college have only been in his classes.

Charlie initially comes off as harsh, but he deeply cares about his students and their education. He'll teach you skills worth remembering for the rest of your time as a J major. Charlie always pushes you to do better than your best... it can be overwhelming at first but is definitely worthwhile. Loved him and Dan together too :)

Charlie was amazing during Gateway. He was always available after class to give feedback on our work or just have a conversation! He's a super funny and nice dude. He also spends a lot of time on his 'slide decks' and you can tell he really cares about what he is trying to do.

I didn't like him as much for j201, but in gateway he's awesome. His lectures/slides are engaging, and he's very helpful if you talk to him outside of class. You can tell he cares about actually training you to get a job in Journalism or whatever you want to go into. The class is not nearly as hard as they make it seem, so don't be intimidated.

The content of the class was interesting. I think he taught it pretty well, but he is not accommodating. If you miss a test, even due to Covid, you'll fail. Also, the first paper was pretty boring. If the course content was applied better I'd rate it a 5.

One of my fave J classes so far. Deitz comes across as "aggressive" to many but my class had a lot of fun with him. Interesting/informative lectures that help A LOT on the tests so make sure to attend class. I got by without reading the articles assigned to us just by showing up to lectures. Only graded on two or three essays and a couple of tests.

There are technically readings but for the most part, everything you need to know is in the slides. 2 short essays and 2 easy tests (if you go to class). He always talks about how hard his class is and how you have to fight for an A, but it is really not a difficult class. Very straight to the point/no-nonsense, but the class is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall fine professor. Lectures are interesting but not helpful on tests. Condescending and aggressive for no reason. Grade will suffer if you're sick.

The class itself was fine, lecture material was kind of boring and weird but essay assignments were intresting and engaging. Proffessor Deitz has a major superiority complex and probably wont respond to any email you send asking for an extention. If you come to class and take time on the assignments you will do fine.

He is an overall fine teacher and knows what he's talking about but is rude & incredibly annoying. Makes little to no accommodations for students with technological, personal, etc. issues. He tries to be relatable but it doesn't work and comes across as frustrating and really really irritating. Impossible to reach him or the GE's through emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had both Charlie and Dan for Gateway. It was a very "good cop vs bad cop" combo. Charlie made a lot of jokes during his lectures. He was always available outside of class for help and appeared eager to do so. Not a bad professor and wouldn't mind having to take another class of his, especially to engage with him as a singular prof and not a team

Charlie shows he has no empathy for students and doesn't care for anyone but himself. His lectures for this class were boring and not engaging, they had no relevance to the final exam and the majority of the class is just busy work. if you don't have to take it, don't. It is by far the worst class I've taken here.

I enjoyed taking Professor Deitz's class. He loves discussion and expects students to keep up with readings. He is also very easy to approach during office hours and offers good guidance. I'm now in his Gateway class, and I still enjoy him as a professor.

Charlie Deitz is hands down one of the best professors at the university of Oregon. There was never a time where he was not willing to help answer questions or provide extensions when needed. His humor, professionalism, and overall character provide an engaging academic experience. if you have the option, TAKE THIS CLASS  you won't regret it!!!

A solid class, Deitz made class fun even if it was at 9 am. A pretty strat forward class with clear directions and instructions. There's mainly two papers and tests that determine your grade. The test you'll do well if you go to class. The papers were really cool prompts but hard to really grasp what you're trying to say.

Charlie is a great professor, and you'll definitely learn a lot from him. Grading is tough for essays, but participation is worth 15% of your grade and can give you a 5% bonus (up to 105% instead of 100%), so go to class even if it's not mandatory. Very nice professor, impossible to reach by email, but great in office hours.

He regularly got really basic facts and concepts wrong and never corrected himself. He is a fine professor if a little overconfident (very 'hello fellow kids') and the class is easy but he just constantly made frustratingly basic errors which honestly seems irresponsible since so many freshman take his class.
If you can take another teacher, do it.

PRO TIP DO NOT SEND HIM A BUNCH OF EMAILS!!! wait to ask him questions during office hours. He is so FUN, super engaging on zoom, the class was fun to attend. There was reading, but he elaborated it very well to make since. He makes you work for your grade, for me, the class was hard and stressful, because I suck at writing! BUT so worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Most engaging online lectures I've had so far. He's funny in a dorky way. Available outside of class hours. Goes above and beyond for his students. Truly cares about current issues in politics and human rights. I wish he taught more courses in this department because I think he'd be better used in courses of greater depth in the field.

Great guy, cares a lot about his students and is very kind. The class was straightforward nothing crazy difficult. He was very supportive to the students. Also he is super funny, keeps the class entertaining.

Do not take if you want to go into journalism. Most of the content is completely unrelated, it felt more like a history class. Also, on one of my essays, the feedback said I didn't have enough citations (fair) and one of my paragraphs was too short (it was according to the rubric). I got a 75/100 on something that deserved at the very least a 85.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down has the best comedic timing out of any teacher I've had in my academic career, and has a passion for the subject that made me consider minoring in it. Always willing to communicate with students and always seems appreciative that people are taking his class. I'm not even done with his class and I know he's one of the best profs. at UO.

Wonderful teacher, cares about whether or not the students understand the concepts, ties everything conceptually together. Brings in interesting and relevant guest lecturers, a LOT taken from the book so be prepared to read a fair amount.

Overall not a bad class. Leans heavily on the textbook which is pretty hard to get through in my opinion. Lecture slides are posted and give the most essential information which is helpful for the midterms. Two essays and 2 Midterms. Not that hard of a class but also not the most exciting I've taken. Still would recommend.

Charlie is overall a good professor. I don't like that he pretty much requires you to have a laptop to bring to class for tests in class. He says you "can use a phone", but he doesn't recommend it. There's lots of reading and class is kind of boring. He also like never responds to emails. His lectures are decent and he is a nice teacher though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Charlie is a fantastic teacher and, makes it very clear what you need to know for during lectures. He was always helpful at office hours and was very accessible as well. The essays were easy to plan for because he did such a good job at planning for it. His knowledge and passion for media are immense and it can be seen throughout his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Charlie is passionate, caring and fair. You are graded on three different things: 1) Participation - Submit a two-sentence answer related to the lecture on Canvas after every lecture (VERY EASY). 2) Two exams - Non-cumulative and mainly based on the slides, some parts from the book. 3) Two papers - Clear grading criteria and rather basic.
Great guy, very knowledgeable on the topic, gives great lectures. like someone else said, if you think buddy grades on opinion thats your opinion, and its wrong. get better at reading maybe?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Joe is great! He prepares all of his material beforehand, knows it like the back of his hand, and is always ready to help students learn. If you don't like reading thoughtfully, paying attention, or asking questions, he's not for you; otherwise, you'll do great.

Also, whoever said "he grades based on opinion" didn't pay any attention. Stay mad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For anyone who wants to learn philosophy and put in effort doing so, Joe is second to none in his knowledge. His lectures are extremely informative and engaging. If you are looking for an easy class where you can disengage and get a free grade, he is not for you. If you are passionate about learning philosophy, he is absolutely ideal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE. Thought I was taking an easy 100-level arts and letters class. He doesn't give out A grades. Grades us based on his opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I just finished taking Kathleen for BA 325H, she is probably the best teacher I have ever had. She genuinely cares about every one of her students and wants you to succeed. She is incredibly inspiring and makes you want to be a better person. There is no better professor at the UO.
Shes a very nice and caring person willing to help as long as you are putting in the effort.

Took her for honors BA 325H, highly recommend! Easiest and most engaging honors class I have taken. Responds immediately to emails, though not super accessible outside of class, but only because she is involved in so much at UO. If there is one honors class to prioritize, it's this one with Kathleen!
Kathleen was awesome, she is so caring and takes the time to get to know every student. She gives really good feedback and overall is just a great lady!

Kathleen was an absolutely phenomenal teacher who is just so involved with her students. She really does get to know everyone so well and even remembered my name at the end of the term despite only talking to her once. Highly recommend taking her for BA308 because the stuff that she values and teaches is influential beneficially.
Kathleen was easily my favorite professor in college so far. She cares deeply about her students and always wants the best for everyone.
Best teacher I have had at University of Oregon.

Kathleen is an excellent professor who truly cares about her students and helps each student grow practical skills throughout this course. Very insightful and helpful feedback is given on all assignments that genuinely helps you improve your work. The team project is nicely spread out, so you do not feel rushed towards the end of the term.

Kathleen is a great professor and I would recommend her to anyone! She truly cares about all of her students and is very accommodating. She made BA308 really fun and manageable, despite the work load. I would recommend taking with Kathleen if you have the option!

Kathleen is a wonderful person, and my favorite professor at the University! She was dedicated to our learning and truly cared about getting to know each of us individually and aiding our growth. Her lectures are very informative without dragging on, and she provides clear guidelines and gives beneficial feedback on every assignment.

Kathleen was a great professor for BA308 and you can tell she really cares. She took individual time to get to know us all, and took extra steps to ensure our success. In a class that is notorious for having harsh grading, Kathleen was very transparent, helpful, and fair with her feedback. I would for sure take her again!

BA 308 in general is such a difficult course but Kathleen made it amazing. She is the most caring and inspirational teacher I've ever had. If you have a chance to take a class with her 100% do it. The course is tough and there is a lot of work, but the work all has a purpose. She's the best!!!!

So good!!! Nicest professor ever. 308 is definitely the hardest class in the biz college, but Kathleen makes it more than bearable. Lots of assignments but most of them are actually beneficial to you as a person. She is such a great resource outside of class too. Get ready for a lot of group stuff, but I absolutely recommend Kathleen.

One of the best professors I have had. She is a hard grader but she gives good feedback so you can improve. She cares a lot about her students and she if definitely worth getting to know so I recommend going to her office hours. Great professor and class.

I had Kathleen for two terms and she is just amazing. Brings relevant things into lectures that keep the entire class engaged throughout the entire term. She is worth taking BA 325 in person and easily has been one of the best professors in all of UO.

Wonderful professor! Teaches many relevant business law topics and is able to explain them in a way that is very entertaining and relevant. Class structure is awesome, would highly recommend taking this or any class with Kathleen!

I had her for BA 308 and she is absolutely amazing. She cares about each person in her class and she is personable and always able to help. She is a tough grader but her grades have a purpose and I think she does a great job of teaching.
Take her class! She is an extremely reasonable/down-to-earth person
She is very thoughtful, nice and caring. Her classes are very nice to unwind in.
Have taken her 3 times!

Though attendance for this class is mandatory, Joan was such a kind person and lovely story teller that I looked forward to going to yoga class. There is some discussion boards due outside of class time but that are quick. I highly recommend this course to anyone who is looking to balance out their schedule and learn about the practice of yoga.
Super chill and fun instructor! Loved coming to her class to unwind after a long day
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love her, very calm, peaceful, yoga, vibes

I loved Joan for gentle yoga! She was so calm and really cared about students, and is super passionate about yoga. This class was online for me, so she let us do the yoga whenever we wanted if we couldn't go to the live sessions. This class was also super interesting. If you're thinking about taking yoga, take it with Joan!!
Taking a class with Joan was one of the best things I ever did for myself! Extremely knowledgeable and amazing person & instructor.

I LOVE Joan! I took her yoga class because I have really short and strong muscles, but I wanted to become more flexible and less prone to sport injuries. She is so warm, hilarious, and her presence is so calming after a hard day of classes. She loves to tell stories of her yoga travels in India, which are super interesting and inspirational.
Joan Dobbie is an inspirational yoga teacher who is very caring. Her classes are easy credit as long as you show up. Take her class if you have the chance!

Good instructor. It was a fun and interesting class and she made me enjoy yoga. Definitely recommended, very easy and helped me relax. There's 1 quiz + daily journal entries are due 3x in the quarter. Very good instructor!
Hilarious, warm, funny. I learned a ton and I really like yoga now.

I took her Advanced Poetry class, CRWR 435.I always liked poetry and so I was excited. But after taking her class, I have completely lost the love and passion for poetry. She grades your poems based on her own personal writing style. If you don't write something that is in her own style, you're not getting anything higher than a B
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Spent the whole 3 hours just reading poems and talking about them, nothing truly interactive, no in class writing or fun activities to stimulate the brain. She graded based on her preferences and opinions instead of respecting creativity. You could follow the prompt and it still wouldn't be enough for her. Poetry is supposed to be subjective !!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Geri is a skilled writer, no doubt.   She was helpful during office hour, but in lecture seemed condescending.  Geri "disagrees" often, then proceeds to paraphrase the point exactly but with more elegance.  I found this unproductive and dogmatizing.  Where she was unable to out-do with language, she was dismissive of the unfamiliar.

Geri is really an inspiring professor. Whether you are a creative writer or not, she will keep you absolutely engaged. She is very talented, and although she is not the type to push her own works on a class, I would recommend reading her collection Resin. She is definitely a challenging teacher and a difficult grader, but fair. TAKE HER CLASSES!

Geri is amazing.  Take all of her classes!  Read her poetry. She is a wonderful poet on top of being a wonderful teacher. She is great at explaining things that people don't understand, and she was able to get me interested in allegory, which I would have thought previously impossible.

Professor Morgan is a pretty good professor, but your GE will make it or break it; he doesn't really look at your assignments, your GE grades them. I would say, as for lecture material, he does care about what he is talking about, but in my opinion, it's a little boring (plus it was at 8am in the morning). He also said AI art was good?

GE will determine your experience in the class, as Professor Morgan will not actually be grading your work. Course content interesting and he's an incredibly engaging lecturer. GET READY TO COLLAGE! Almost all projects have/could have collage elements. Lectures are very art history heavy, so if that's not your jam, probably don't take.

The best part about this class is that I never have to take it again. Honestly you will never interact with Morgan so it really doesn't matter how you feel about him. He will never look at your work. 

Lectures were sometimes interesting and he can be funny at times, but overall this class is a bit of a joke. Your GE will make or break it!

Anything representative is considered boring to Professor Morgan. Also - the AMOUNT of projects we had to do in this class was mind-blowing - if you fall behind in this class, you're cooked. Thankfully, not all of the projects in this class are surrounding abstract expressionism (formalism leaning), but wow - It sure did come off as pretentious.

Not very good with canvas. Only allowed to miss three classes with both lecture and lab. If you miss four then it is a letter grade deduction and if you miss 5 it's an automatic fail. One assignment due a week and they want you to produce several pages of work plus two brainstorming pages. Struggled to produce good work within the time frame.

Assignments are very demanding. The professor never looks at student work and doesn't communicate clearly with lab instructors. Lab instructors are grading with different standards than what he teaches in lectures. Graded on effort and creativity, not skill. GET COLLAGE MATERIALS!! Magazines are the best. Start collecting stuff early.

Generally a pretty good professor, but definitely is not very...Canvas skilled. He teaches the lectures, and the labs are taught by GEs. There is one quiz every week (on the previous week's material) and that's how he takes attendance. Don't expect to be able to miss many classes, you only get three absences, and that's for both lecture and lab.

Aside from the large workload of this class, Mr. Morgan is very smart and clearly cares about art history. I definitely learned a lot of things in his lectures, even if it wasn't always the most engaging.

Professor Morgan is pretty cool, no tests, lectures are super easy but long, The lab can be fun but the homework assigned is so silly.. when will I ever use these skills again? Never. Be ready to have weekly assignments up to 5-20 per week. I felt embarrassed to be doing elementary school art as a college art major.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: My main problem with Professor Morgan is that he assigns an exorbitant amount of work for each of his projects. You are expected to produce anywhere from 5-20+ individual pieces of work per project every 1-2 weeks, which was not only stressful but felt counterproductive as it affected the quality of my work.
Donald Morgan is such a kind professor!

This class was fun and he had interesting lectures. At the beginning of the course (in the syllabus I think) he says that most students will get a B which is kind of a downer but if you work hard and incorporate all the needed elements into your weekly art assignments you should get an A. You get graded by a GE though so it depends on the person
Great instructor, who made learning the basics of drawing entertaining. Get ready for lots of still life drawings though.
good teacher

Honestly, given other courses, this course kinda flew in the back of my mind. The professor is understanding of students and very accessible outside of class and explains things well. The lectures are extremely conjunct therefore class activities are hard to do. Quick pass, so be good at math and understand science to get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think they're a good lecturer and can explain abstract concepts very well. There are also the occasional crash-outs about poor attendance to the students IN attendance. Exams were fair, and the grading system was appropriate for an accelerated course.

Joel is out of touch with students and makes an intro physics course far harder than it needs to be. His lectures are dense, overly detailed, and ignore what's actually relevant for exams. He barely engages with the class, often ignoring raised hands, and seems more interested in lecturing for himself than helping students learn.

As someone who doesn't like science, I came into this course thinking that I wouldn't like it at all! However, Professor Doss helped me to learn more about astronomy in a way that actually made sense to me, and I did much better in the course than I originally anticipated. My only critique is that they tended to go over time in lectures!

Though kinda corny, Joel's lectures were helpful and simple. Take good notes, though, because the readings do not correlate. Strange grading system, it's frustrating that I can't really know how my stuff'll be graded besides "meets criteria" for 1 point until the end. Uses iClicker and Perusall.

Avoid if you can. Ridiculous grading system (ex. if you have an A in four categories and a D in one category your final cumulative grade is a D). Passive aggressive professor and teaching assistants. I took this in winter term, just finished my spring term- they are still grading assignments today.

The grading system for this class is very confusing, and you have to keep track of your grades independently as he won't put your total into Canvas. The class itself is easy, but he tends to go off on rants and make jokes that never land. If you're looking for a class that's easy to pass this is it, but know your patience will be tested.

Dr. Doss does require Iclicker for attendance. Exams, assignments, and  projects all online, except for an in-person final exam on finals week. Organized and mostly stays on topic. They are an easy grader. Just turn in the work and you will pass.

Joel Doss wasn't the best at teaching and tended to push his agenda onto students in the class when I took him during winter term. Assignments are just graded off participation as long as you get a 75-80% on most of them, making it very easy to pass besides the GEs that would give terrible feedback on required projects.
