Prof. Doss spent too much time with ice breakers and tangents at the beginning of class, and we often ran out of time to cover everything we needed to in lectures. Projects are relatively easy
She was tough, but she brought out the best in me and really stretched my mind.  I loved our talks about byzantine era mosaics.  I still think of her with a smile all these years later.
She was late to most classes.  Sometimes she was even 30 - 40 minutes late!! I just dont think she enjoys what she does anymore.

A completely incompetent professor! Tests are ridiculous, and she is an extremely harsh grader if you don't write EXACTLY what she wants, but never really tells you what that is. I got my midterm back only on the day of the final exam. And now my final grade is an X; she didn't submit any grade to the registrar! She also NEVER replies to e-mails.

Shows up late to every class, does not answer question; she just answers the parts that she wants to.  Talks to students in a very degrading manner and expects you to automatically know everything about the subject that she is supposed to be teaching.  No study guide and no indication of what she is looking for on exams.
I don't even think you can describe how awful this woman is. She is beyond any comprehension of horrible.  And when everybody does horrible on her test, she blames us!
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Van Dreel assigned a few longer pieces of media to watch outside of class, but only once a week for the most part. The assignments are well-explained and relevant to the class. They provide broad overviews that are sometimes hard to remember for the weekly quizzes, but if you review your notes before class, then the quizzes will be easy.

If you have another choice for another class take it. This was the most boring and worst HC I've ever taken. There are barely any assignments and when the final essay had incredibly vague instructions and Lydia decided they did not think my argument about opera was a new enough idea they tanked my grade.

Van Dreel is a great prof who is so passionate about what they teach. They are easy to reach and quick to respond to emails. Sometimes their quizzes can be a little tricky, or they are picky about grading them, but it's very manageable. They don't allow any electronics, but I will say, it did help me focus better and perform better on the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Van Dreel was kind and communicative and made an effort to get to know each student. There were a lot of readings outside of class, and we had to do 3 group projects, which wasn't ideal. The class overall was good though

Prof. Van Dreel is such a kind and understanding person. They are incredibly knowledgeable in music and has great insights in how music is a tool to understand identity. Their class environment makes everyone feel comfortable to speak their mind and share their experiences. I highly recommend!

I had Drew during his first term of teaching, and he did a great job. He is a truly caring professor who listens and makes classes interactive. Has great practice problems but be prepared for a very hard/long final.
Undisputed GOAT. Super personable, very accessible and communicates material in clear way.
final was lowkey hard! he is is soooo sweet & kind though. do the homework!!

Loved him! I personally found that the course content was very hard, but he really wants you to succeed in this class. Great at answering questions, and homework was optional (although if you don't do it, you will probably fail). Weekly quizzes and an easy case assignment for the midterm. Final was pretty tough but if you study you will be fine.

GOAT Teacher. Extremely helpful and is always willing to do the extra mile to help students. Really wants to see students do well. Test/Quizzes are challenging but they are very fair, study the practice problems and you will do well.
Drew is a very chill professor and cares for his students. You can tell that he wants his students to understand and succeed in the class. Office hours are helpful.

Drew is awesome. The content of the class is tricky, but if you put in the work you will get it. Drew will answer any questions, and is very helpful in office hours. Very knowledgeable about all things accounting and CPA.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He is very experienced and can answer every question you ask. He's also great at advising, would definitely recommend taking his class. I hope to have him for ACTG450. Very generous grader, one mistake won't ruin your grade. Make sure to do the homework!!!
Drew is the best

Drew is so nice! He offers a lot of office hours and they are very helpful. Grading guidelines are clear, and all material on tests and quizzes are discussed in class. Attendance is not mandatory. Definitely take classes with Drew if you can!

Drew is amazing! Weekly quizzes, a case study and one big final. Non mandatory homework that is great practice for the quizzes. Really good lectures and genuinely cares about his students. Show up to office hours, do the homework and he will help you succeed!

Professor Stevenson was amazing! He's super helpful in office hours so definitely utilize those as much as possible. He's super engaging and is a fair grader. The class itself is difficult but Stevenson gives plenty of opportunities to work the material. I highly recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drew is probably my favorite accounting prof so far, which says a lot given that he was new this year. Focuses on what's important in lecture, emphasizes examples and making sure we understand. Final was hard, but felt fair if you put the work in during the year. Does great CPA advising too, would highly recommend. Pay attention and you'll succeed.

This was Drew's first year, so I sense he is still getting the groove of teaching, but nevertheless he was good at teaching. His lectures to focus on material, but he did tend to get sidetracked with certain topics for periods of time. DEFINITELY study the material outside of class until you understand it well.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is for JCOM 472 but she is really not that bad. Her critiques are normal. You really just need to talk to her because she is helpful. I feel like Pompper is a nice caring person. She cares and puts in effort however you are graded on very little, one activity sheet a week, and it is not portfolio worthy. I appreciate her in class discussions, they are relevant to the course as we cover current fashion trends.

genuinely bad experience don't put yourself through this

reviews.comment: All of her emails are convoluted and overly complicated. Numerous policies that clearly demonstrate the only significant thing in this professor's life is academia, no consideration for people who have other things going on in life. Unreasonable expectations, doesn't want you to succeed.

Work was graded extremely critically with little to no guidance for improvement. Lectures never covered anything you wouldn't know by existing in the world and when I asked for clarification on an assignment she was condescending and rude. There was no "teaching" on her part, and with such an interesting class topic it was extremely disappointing.

She tanked my grade for turning in the very first assignment late. I understood that there was a no late work policy, but didn't understand why my grade in the class dropped from an 100% to mid 60s. I told her I thought it was wrong and she got mad and refused to change my grade for the rest of the term or correspond with me any further.

She had a lecture quiz question about how to refer to a person with a disability and two of the options were g*mp and vegetable... what are we, middle schoolers? I was hoping to dive deep into gender and media in this class but I learn more by scrolling through tiktok for 5 minutes than I did this entire term. Don't buy the books, I didn't.

She isn't the worst, but not the best. She is a really hard grader when it comes to the essay. I am one to always receive good grades on essays (85% and up) and she told me she didn't know how to grade my paper because it didn't fit her normal standards.. like what does that even mean. Avoid if you can but if its your last resort then don't stress.

Just SOME of my grievances: 1) Makes you buy 2 books ($70 each) that SHE wrote. 2) Material is from the 90s. Incredibly obsolete/inapplicable today. 3) If you ask a question, she gaslights you into thinking it's your fault that you didn't understand her unclear/illogical questions. 4) Overall, she doesn't care about her students & is very outdated.

She makes you buy the textbook SHE WROTE. The other professor who teaches this class does not. She's purely trying to make money. She's a horrible teacher who is extremely full of herself, and is an extremely tough grader. Trust me, save your time, money, and sanity. Leave this professor in the dust.

The appeal of the course is that it is easy and sort of interesting. I really wish students had more flexibility to get more into the topic because the homework is surface level.

One of the most rude and disrespectful professors I have encountered with. Never have I felt so disrespected and belittled by someone, let alone a professor. Dr. Pompper claims to be open and accepting but is condescending and rude privately. Not to mention, the content of this class is boring and unengaging. overall terrible. She has no understanding with students. lectures were super short and not detailed, also were prerecorded and used all year even though the assignments were different. Dr. Pompper doesn't connect with students, but makes many claims to be super understanding. comes off as really fake and rude.

Worst professor at UO. She will send you endless emails urging with you to meet her and when no one does, she guilts you and says "crickets." It's not cute, we don't care. Professor makes students feel like they cant ask questions, lest they be ridiculed and condescended to. Seriously, most condescending person ever. Although Dr. Pompper presents herself as a positive individual, she is rude, condescending, and unclear in her instruction and grading criteria. She was rude and condescending when asking for help or clarification numerous times. She was not a useful resource or very willing to help. No tests or quizzes so otherwise an easy class.

I dont normally post complaints, but I feel I have to this time. Really disappointed by her rude responses to questions.

The class itself is relatively chill and easy A. Points are very simple to earn. This professor is very passionate about what she teaches, but she seems to use that overly optimistic attitude to hide the fact that she doesn't know how to relate to the students, no matter how much she claims to understand. Says she's very accommodating, but isn't.

5 discussions aka 400 word "essays" for the entire term. No finals. Quizzes were given but they counted as extra credit - if you got it right, extra points, & if you get it wrong, no points & does not affect your overall grade. This class was more like a discussion class, she uploads the books pdfs so you don't have to buy the texts & no attendance

Sitting in this class is an entire waste of time and I feel like my life is wasting away in the two hours that I am in that classroom. She is rude and condescending and her presence genuinely pisses me off. When you ask questions she doesn't even answer the question.
Lots of homework and quizzes.

This professor on multiple occasions fails to show grace or care to students. If you don't adhere to his method of teaching, good luck doing it all in a 10 minute quiz at the start of class! Regardless of how determined you are to succeed, if you aren't a good test taker, you will not. Retaking things is not possible.

Prof Nobile was great to teach Theory 1. Not a crazy course and by all means manageable if you're entering the course with prior performance or theory experience. Prof Rothgery is very nice, and he grades pretty easy. The issue is that he often seems unprepared for class, and he takes a very very very long time to get anything graded.

Andrew was a very kind teacher. He really values teaching, and approaches all of his students graciously. Despite a few of the lectures feeling unorganized at times, it was a pretty easy class. Note, he does grade slow, but it wasn't that big of a deal. Would definitely take again!

This was the worst class I have ever taken at the UO.  He was unprepared on almost every occasion, would not post the rubrics, and then grade aggressively with them.  We had 2 absences before it affected our grade.  Avoid at all costs.

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

I personally loved this class! Rothgery switches between English and Spanish to help students understand, answers any and all questions. He properly prepares students for quizzes and tests. The one con is that he sometimes takes a while to grade things, so I didn't know my grade until the end of the term. Other than that really enjoyed this class

professor rothgery is a sweet guy and a very understanding and kind professor, but he tends to be pretty disorganized in terms of class content and grading. oftentimes he would mostly just read from the slides and sometimes it seemed like he didn't really know what was on them lol. he's so nice and understanding, though, so i can't really complain.
He is an easy grader but doesn't explain assignments well in person or on canvas. Regardless very understanding and accommodating.
Highly recommend super sweet and caring

I love this man with all my heart. He is hands down the most caring prof I have ever had. Extremely unlikely that you could fail his class. I absolutely hated Spanish and was lost all the time until I took his class. He is a relaxed grader. There is no more reading in his class than any other Spanish class, they all follow the same curriculum.

Professor Rothgery is an extremely nice guy who genuinely cares about the success of his students. This said, his classes were hard to sit through because he was usually frazzled and unorganized. We rarely made it through the presentations for the class, which made it hard to prepare for assessments... but he's a pretty forgiving grader.

Andrew is the best! Coming from a mean professor during the fall term, this class has been a breath of fresh air! The course is challenging overall, but that's just how it is. He is highly accessible outside of class and wants to help you! It's easier to grade but allows you to make mistakes without heavily penalizing you. Take his class!

This professor was super disorganized. Everything was a mess. He had no structure. Big mess. Learned nothing. This was a Spanish class and his words would mess me up. When he would talk he would throw me off. Im really good at Spanish and his way of speaking would completely throw me off. He never had a class plan. An extremely boring class.

Cares about his students a lot, but the class fell way behind schedule. He is a but disorganized and the class structure is a bit weird. Sometimes he won't teach you the content until right before the quiz. Very nice guy and class is useful, but not very organized.

Although quite disorganized at times and takes a while to grade papers, he is very caring about his students and believes that everyone in his class has the chance to succeed. There is a quiz every week, but most of the class time is dedicated to going over the materials of the quiz so he can better prepare everyone.
He's a super sweet and personable professor! He appears a bit frazzled at times but he's always willing to answer questions and is very caring toward students and helping them learn more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved Rothgery! He is a bit disorganized, but has his charm and cares deeply about students and wants their input, feedback, and creativity to flow and be welcomed in the classroom. Take advantage of the resources and advice he offers, he is super flexible and respectful and I wish he taught more courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While we got 2 days behind on the syllabus and he isn't the BEST span prof I've had, he certainly cares about his students. The quizzes/midterm/final are the hardest part and even those aren't bad if you take the time to study. He provides detailed rubrics and gives feedback on written assignments and will go over anything if you go to office hrs.

Let me just begin by saying that more than half of romance language Spanish department at UO are not qualified to educate, including P. Rothgery. The level of education I have received from this professor and others has been poor quality. I am so glad I switch majors because i did not want to deal anymore with the mediocracy of this department.

Great person, terrible professor. He is very unorganized, provides no useful feedback, his lectures are boring and he does not teach anything relevant to the course. He is a tough grader with high expectations which it is unfair considering how he does not provide any instructions or guidance about essays/assignments. Do no recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For 320, he has either a quiz or an essay due each class. However, as long as you pay attention in class, you'll have minimal work to due to prepare for the tests and the essays are only a page long. He is a great teacher and really cares about his students; his office hours are super useful.

I had to beg him so many times to PLEASE grade our stuff, as we had no idea what our grades were even on the last day of the term. He dropped the ball so many times that he'd cancel or change entire assignments, which was frustrating if we had already started them. He's a nice guy but if you care about your grades, avoid him- he won't respect that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking class from this instructor. The Spanish 200-level courses are difficult as it is, but when he doesn't use PowerPoints or writing/speaking practices, you have to essentially teach yourself. He also decided to completely change the presentation grading rubric that is supposed to be standard for all SPAN 202 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a super nice guy and I found him to be a pretty easy grader. There were six papers that we wrote and then three times where we had to memorize stuff for a speaking presentation. There's also online homework pretty much every night of class. He's a really slow grader though and students get annoyed by this.

never been more frustrated with a professor before. week 8 still don't know our grades, a girl asked him to TEACH lessons & he said SAID NO, class is just writing responses to Q's he puts on board w no help/discussion. He is the worst teacher and will not help you the least bit. Then he is a hard grader even tho ur being forced to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's very open to helping students outside of class and often has extra office hours to meet with him. He's understanding and takes the time to explain topics in class before we're quizzed on them! A little awkward but still an amazing professor. Not an easy A, but still easy to do well if you work for it.

Love Andrew! very personable and understanding of the process. Willing to help a lot. As a native spanish speaker, I think his Spanish is very strong and he has a lot of experience in what he does. I found myself laughing a lot in class, fun diversity of projects and assignments too! nothing crazy hard.

Quite disorganized but he truly cares about his students. If you do not understand something go to his office hours, he is incredibly helpful. Gives pop quizzes but if you actually do the homework you will be fine. He loves it when people contribute to class which is what makes the class that more interesting. Best teacher I have had in a while.

He's a very nice guy and an easy grader. He is very understanding if you screw things up and is always willing to help. The tests are pretty easy except for the culture stuff, but he prepares you well. I definitely recommend taking him.
He's been my favorite teacher this term. I love Andy.

He is a great teacher and is very passionate about his students and the subject. Best Spanish teacher I have had in a while. He is somewhat disorganized especially when  it comes to handing back work. Go to his office hours, he is extremely helpful. If you do all of the work and participate occasionally you will get an A. Ask him questions too.

Andrew's really nice but  very disorganized. He's passionate about Spanish & cares about his students but the grading criteria is very unclear & he grades things VERY slowly. You honestly don't know what grade you're at until about Week 7Week 8. Gives difficult pop quizzes and his tests aren't always easy. But somehow it's easy to get an A.

Very unclear with grading criteria. Fairly easy grader for the most part but springs pop quizzes on you that are way harder than the actual exams are. Poor availability for office hours. Takes SO LONG to grade anything. Don't expect to know any of your grades until like week 8. Pretty boring class overall. Didn't get much out of it.

Real nice guy, but so unorganized. Literally read out of the syllabus. I didn't feel like I learned anything. Would grade tests much harder than any classwork and tests wouldn't come back till the day before the next test so you had no time to learn from your mistakes.

Professor Rothgery is just about the nicest spanish professor! He is very understanding and makes everyone feel very comfortable to speak in class. It is very easy to do well if you do the work, he is a very fair grader. Probably my favorite spanish professor!

Andy is a decent teacher, a little unclear/disorganized sometimes, but mainly he is a really great person, and if you need help or extra time or whatever he's very good about it. Always gives us the benefit of the doubt on tests etc. I loved his class and I'm taking another with him next term.

As a freshman I did not know which teachers to take so he was a shot in the dark but I really enjoyed his class, he is pretty easy and nice. Funny at times but awkward. I personally enjoyed him and he is easy so if you want to get a good grade in 200 take him!

Class is fairly easy.  Basically you have a presentation, 2 3ish page papers, a mix of quizzes and 1 paragraph reflection papers, and daily participation points.  You will have some reading but its not too hard and Andy is super helpful and approachable if you have questions/problems.  He is a great Spanish teacher!
Andy is the best professor I've had at the U of O!!!!! Take him!!!'
I worked very hard, but got an A. Andrew has been my favorite spanish professor thus far at U of O. I hope to have him again!

He is such a great teacher that uses such creative ways of teaching as well as ways to help explain things that you do not understand. He uses ways to show you how to use the knowledge that you already have to find out answers that you have to problems and lead you in the right direction. He is by far the best teacher I have had in Spanish classes.

Andy was one of the better teachers I've had at UO.  Easy to talk to and very accessible. Generally enjoyed going to this class. Tough grader, but it was just one of the many things that showed that he really cared about his students. Assignments took forever to come back, but he had 3 203 classes this term.  Great experience with a tough class.

Andy is by far the best spanish teacher at the U of O. I have taken many spanish classes with many teachers, and Andy is the only one who i have signed up for more than once. Most teachers just try to pound the info into your head, while Andy makes sure that you understand it and will go out of his way to help. Highly Recommend him. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Andy is a great professor. He is not a native speaker and can be a little unorganized. However, as long as you participate and try in his class you will do well. Also, if you ever need any help from him he will make sure you get what you need. AWESOME PROF!
I took Cambios Sociales from Andy. He is a great teacher and his class is interesting! Would definitely take classes from him again!

He is an incredibly nice and helpful person. Do the readings, talk in class, take the quizzes and you'll be golden. I have definitely had better Spanish teachers though. The materials for this class are quite boring; also if you prefer a native spanish speaker, he speaks very slow spanish...
He is an alright teacher. Honestly not my favorite. He is not very clear and doesn't use class time to his full potential. I wouldn't reccomend him if you are someone who needs a lot explanation.

The first time I tried to learn Spanish in high school I failed miserably. The second time I took Spanish was as U of O and Andrew was awesome, I did great and learned a ton. For one, he actually cares about his students success, which is a rarity in the teaching world.
Very helpful. Spend extra time on things students don't understand. Only criticism: skips around too much and doesn't always flow when presenting related topics.
Personally I didn't like his style of teaching, i don't believe he is very clear, he doesn't use blackboard, he is an easy grader though!
Solid spanish instructor. Recommended.
Andy is very sincere. He really wants the student to "get it" more than play a game to get a grade. He's kinda hot too.

Andy is a great teacher.  He is so nice, sincere, and truly wants his students to succeed.  He is very patient with his students, and always tries to make his classes interactive so that they are more interesting.  He is a fair grader, enjoyable to learn from, and I would recommend him to anyone that can have him as a Spanish teacher.  Andy rocks!

I felt that Rothgary was interesting at time but extremely inconsistant. At one point, he would give the class a long time to complete an easy assignment, and then at others give you a weekend to write at 3-4 page paper. He sticks so closely to the topic of the class that it becomes redundant and you feel like your studying the same topic again.
Very helpful and patient.  Somehow always understand bad spanish when no one else could.  And he is so nice.
Awesome guy who's always there to help. Can be a hard class, but he'll help you get through it. A fair guy, too.
What a nice guy!

Very kind, knowledgeable professor who genuinely knows what he's talking about. Class is long (2hrs) and is on very interesting, but challenging topics (lots of confusing neural pathways). Tests are completely short answer, but drops one so I didn't have to take the final. Overall would highly recommend this class for upper div HPHY requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrew Lovering has a genuine enthusiasm for teaching and was eager to hear from his students during class. He makes learning fun and incorporates active learning in his teaching style. Although he's not a hard grader, he expects you to have a solid understanding of physiology and encourages you to ask questions. His exams are written exams.

Professor Lovering is over a good professor. However, all of his tests were written short or long answer, with no multiple choice questions. You must attend lecture to understand what is going on in the class. He is accessible outside of class for office hours.

He's a great professor. He makes time outside his office hours if you can't make it, and his tests aren't super hard but it was sometimes hard to know what he wanted in his answers. The labs are  every 2 weeks so it was nice having a break every 2 weeks as well. There are a lot of graphs and it is hard to interpret some of it but is a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very smart and nice guy. Passionate about teaching, and the way he teaches sticks easily, even though the material is tough. Definitely attend every class and study hard and an A is not that hard to get. I'm looking into taking more classes taught by him.
Very nice and helpful. He will go out of his way to help you learn the material.

Im not a science person, but I really liked this class. His passion for animals is really clear in his lectures. They arent mandatory, but good notes make it easy to do well on the exams. There are 4 online exams, and your lowest score is dropped. No HW besides readings that arent graded or tested on. Would 100% recommend this class.

He is very nice, but his lectures are pretty boring and so much text is on each slide. I took this class for a science credit and it was harder than I thought. Exams are online and you answer in one word, sentences, and then 3 easy questions. The questions were hard and difficult to find in lecture notes and readings. Labs were boring sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! he cares so much about the class, and it made me care. He is funny and such a good teacher. There are 4 exams and 1 final. Each are 2000-word essay, but because this class is amazing, it was honestly fun to do. If you can take his class. Make sure you pay attention in class; everything he says is important.

This was by far the most difficult and inaccessible class I've taken in my college career so far. Attendance is not mandatory but is absolutely needed to survive this class. Very little text on slides. Exams took me about 10 hours to complete each and require that you use weekend time. (I work 10 hour days on weekends so this did not work for me.)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking Dr. Dueppen, he is a great professor. He often cracks jokes and engages with students about thier interests. I especally recommend taking him if you are an Anth major because he is super knowledgable on field work and things currently going on in the archeological world at large. His lecture are clear and concise as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a great professor! I don't have a huge passion for science, but his lectures were wonderful and I ended up learning a lot. He was super nice and funny and interacted with students a lot during class. Btw, I would recommend taking the class with a friend if you can; the lectures aren't mandatory but they help a lottt with exams.

I loved this professor's lectures; they are a little fast past, but that is good because I could actually pay attention in class. The lectures cover interesting topics so does the discussion, which is just another lecture instead of an actual discussion, thank God. There are essay exams on the weekends, which absolutely sucks, but is open note.

Incredibly average. Doesn't support all learning styles; severe lack of information on slides. He says everything important out loud, so keep up with his pace or be lost. There aren't weekly assignments, but a lot of work because of the 4 exams & 2 article analyses which are all LONG essay questions. Would only his classes if I absolutely had to.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Dueppen's passion for animals sparked mine. Pay attention in class, take notes, complete the weekly readings and you'll do great on the exams. The exams were very easy and he tells you what is important to remember during lectures for the exams. His passionate nerdiness and quirky sense of humor made the lectures tolerable.
Professor was great and funny! Final grade was based only on labs and 4 exams. Exams were rather hard so you have to study hard before each one. Lectures were interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the class I learned the most information in, he is very passionate about this subject/ well informed. No textbook needed, barely any homework. The weekly readings consist of 3-4 articles that are pretty long and time consuming. Labs are pretty much mandatory and part of your grade, but you get 2 absences. Just lots of reading!!

Dueppen is a cute lil bean - is very punny and laughs at his own jokes. He also outlined the weekly "things-to-do" and everything was due Sundays at 11:59 - very clear. The only tick was that the readings were unnecessarily long, but you can pick out the details to write the bi-weekly (easy) papers. Zooms had little interaction; question + answer.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class and you can tell that Professor Dueppen is very passionate about the material. Work diligently and you should do well in this course. Also, his cat Lester hilariously crashed our zoom call on one occasion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dueppen was pretty chill, his zoom lectures were kind of pointless but he puts the main lectures on canvas. So it was nice and organized. In this class we only had to attend the discussions with our GE and then do 4 out of 6 reading analysis and then 3 exams. Overall it wasn't bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dueppen is a funny guy who is incredibly knowledgable. He will answer all of your questions and makes everything so easy to understand. I would retake his domestic animals class 10 times if I didn't already understand the content.

He is an amazing professor, hilarious, and just loves to talk about something he is passionate about. I would most certainly recommend him to anyone, and as long as you study well you should do well in the class.

Dueppen is the best professor ever. His lectures are inclusive, entertaining, and educational. He teaches to all learning types with slides of text, maps, and photos. He makes sure every student is on board before moving on; if you fall behind it is your fault. Snap up that opening in his class; you ought to regret it if you don't have him. <3 <3

Not the best lecturer. Speaks rather softly so if you're in the back, try to get him to speak up. Hold questions till the end of class because he won't answer during it. There's quite a bit of room to get a good grade. Study, be diligent, and you should do well.

super good professor. he makes class very entertaining and teaches in a way that makes it easy for you to memorize the topics. He is easy to talk to and gives good work examples too so that students may get an idea of what life after college will be like.

Fritz is a great professor. His lectures can be are enjoyable and he also does trivia for extra points. All of the material from the tests are straight from the slides and he gives you practice tests in canvas that have some of the same questions as the exams. There is also a group project that is pretty straightforward. Super caring professor.

Fritz is a great teacher who really cares about his students' success. The textbook is not required because his lectures are so detailed. The class can be a little boring with the long lectures, and the tests are very difficult. Participation counts as extra credit, and the group project is vital for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is so kind. He is helpful, both in class answering questions, and during office hours. I was really nervous to take accounting but he has made the subject approachable. I look forward to his class because he is a genuinely nice person who cares about his students.

Overall I really liked this professor. I think he wasn't great at explaining things at first, but if someone asked a question about something, he would go more in depth. I learned mostly from the homework and then my knowledge would be reinforced in class. As long as you do your homework, you should be fine as it is a decent part of your grade.

Take this professor for BA215. He was kind, patient, and a great professor. He understands the position that students are in and will accommodate for you. You can meet him during office hours and he is very understanding of situations! He made accounting easy to understand.

He is a master communicator. A term with him honestly felt like two terms worth of work in one, but I learned so fast and stayed on top of it all because he is motivational. Equally he is receptive, like he pushed project deadlines back for us. He asked if people needed more time and noticed when most were feeling swamped. Wrote whole T.B for us.

Ram is one of the most engaging CS lecturers at UO. He provides resources and supplementary materials for you and challenges you to ask questions. Also a great communicator. While I loved his class personally, I can't say CS 322 was easy. Projects were a bit out of date and sometimes a bit too vague IMO. Tests were difficult but fair. Solid 4.5/5.
He wrote an entire textbook because of us asked for supplementary material. Amazing lectures. Be prepared to spend a good amount of time on projects.

Prof. Durairajan is the kind of teacher that makes you want to keep pushing yourself and learning to the best of your abilities. He is what all excellent CS professors should be and what so few are. He should be running the department.
If you are looking to learn career-ready skills, take Ram's 322. Lectures were amazing. Answers were on point. However, I wish the course had been divided into two terms with fewer projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class seems to have two separate tracks, the projects, and the concepts. Make sure to learn both because you will be tested on concepts, but the projects do not help you remember precisely the words he wishes you to use on exams. Also, he seemed excited to not teach for another year at the end of the final lecture which was concerning to me.

Ram is clearly a brilliant researcher here; the information he provides about a future in CS and becoming a Software Engineer is invaluable. That said, he was noticeably checked out from the course regarding grading and the content of the assigned projects. Ram's lectures are great to sit in, but you will rely heavily on the GE for support.

Ram is a good guy who tries to actually teach real world computer science, which is a breath of fresh air. With that being said his class is for sure the hardest CS class Ive had at UO. He gives you just enough information to get by on the projects and encourages out of class questions. Lots of trick questions on projects too. Tests werent too hard

Ram is, I would say, the best teacher I've ever had. He's a very nice person and a good lecturer and all that; but the thing that really makes him next-level is how incredibly good he is at answering questions. It's like, no matter what CIS question you ask, he knows EXACTLY what you're talking about, and the perfect answer to give. Great teacher.

Professor Ram's lectures were super informative, and I learned a lot from them. Asking him questions will result in a direct answer, which is huge compared to some other instructors I've had. As for homework, be prepared to spend some time on each assignment. He is accessible outside of class, and I found him to be very helpful. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The weekly projects will consume a lot of your life. However, I learned more career-applicable skills in this class than any other CS class so far. I'd strongly recommend taking 322 if you're a junior and planning on taking a summer internship

She doesn't give clear examples/criteria for what she wants in her assignments yet if your work does not meet this criteria, our grades are affected. The class is called "Early Literacy for Diverse Learners" yet when asked for advice on supporting a diverse learner, her feedback was "Maybe reading isn't for him." Lots of reading, most is outdated.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Durán is very knowledgeable which I appreciated but at times I felt like she talked down to me. Overall nice person I just wish she wouldn't talk to me like I had no idea what was going on

reviews.comment: I took SPED 450 and I loved it. As one of the only undergraduate students in a class of masters students, I was super nervous, but Professor Duran was so sweet and she knows what she's talking about. She gave interesting lectures and made the long class pass by super fast. A lot of reading... but we go over it all in class.

If this course was taught by anyone else, I would have taken it in a heartbeat. Dr. Durbans grading is all over the place, and her expectations for assignments are extremely unclear. She just changed the date of our final the day before it was supposed to happen and added more content when we did the review weeks ago. Do not recommend.

She does not respond to emails and She has missed multiple classes this term. Grading rubrics are a mess and confusing. if you are taking this class virtually you are at a disadvantage to those taking in person.

Andrew Goble is a nice guy but he talks very quietly and his lectures are super boring. He will consistently go over time and also start talking before class even starts. I think Professor Goble is a genuinely nice person but his class structure is virtually non existent and he often goes over class time by rambling on without clearly explaining the content presented. A good GE is essential if you want to do good on the two exams and midterm paper because his rubric and expectations are very unclear.

Probably the only time I've ever been infuriated by a course in my 4 years here because of how lazy it felt. Only topped by an online class where the professor made us by his expensive and not that useful book and never was in his office.

reviews.comment: Make sure to read the Cooper book for the midterm! The final is take-home & 70% of the grade, but as long as you take the time with the couple of essays and the two exams, you should be fine. Attendance is very important, and for a class once a week that is no problem. Lots of extensions if you need one!

The professor is so fun! He tends to ramble a bit, but he cracks so many jokes, sometimes they are morbid tho. His assignments were a bit unclear, but he's a nice grader. The films were cool, but sometimes too violent for me. I didn't like that he let the GE grade everything, I didn't like her, but she was nice at least
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I couldn't understand a word he said in every lecture; he has a very soft voice and a thick accent. If you can understand him maybe he's great. Easy midterm and final is online. short essays that aren't graded too harshly if you follow the instructions. attendance is mandatory but you get extra credit for coming to class every time.

Amazing professor! I highly recommend! He's funny and engaging and understanding of mistakes or complications. I loved his lectures and I learned a lot about a super interesting topic. He doesn't deduct late points and though papers are long he's a super lax grader and lets you write about whatever you want as long as it's on topic.

He seems like a very nice guy, but his canvas page was very disorganized which made it hard to find instructions for papers. Speaking of papers, be prepared to do a lot of writing. He always runs out of time on his lectures, but he posts the powerpoints on canvas which is really nice for studying. Overall, not the worst, but hard for a 100 level.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Goble is a very kind and nice person. I didn't love his teaching or grading style. There was little to no communication with his students on most assignments, and even with that little communication, he allowed zero late submissions at all. His lectures were okay, but definitely not the most engaging.
Provided access to lecture PowerPoint, which provided a great source of summary/review for lectures. Most readings were online and well organized on a week-to-week schedule.

I took History 104 with Goble, and I did not enjoy it. In the end I got an A, but his lectures always ran long and he tended to ramble on during them. Most, if not all, of the test content came from the textbook and not the notes I took from his lectures. Attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures he gives are really unclear and poorly managed time wise, we never made it through the slides he would read off of in lectures because he just drones on. However, he is very lenient grade wise - all of my exams were virtual and open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't like the way he taught. It was all over the place. He is all over the place with his lectures and it's really hard to grasp what information he says is actually important. He barely touches on some of the topics he tests us on. he didn't make it clear to us that we had to read the textbook outside of class to actually learn something

Dr. Goble is an average professor, my only real complaint is he's terrible at time management. Will go up to 6 minutes over, and won't go back to the content he missed in the next lecture. Easy to pass though, just pay attention to the attendance policy!

This professor did NOT do a good job of communicating the expectations of assignments with the course GEs. This course was taken in person and it lacked so much organization. There are often times 2 hours of lectures before watching the movies. The grading for the essay assignments are unclear and have no direction/ rubrics. GEs are main graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't grade at all, the GE's do all the work and even with that there is so much lack of communication and clarity with the grading. His lectures also are almost useless for tests and essays (they don't follow rubrics) and as far as grades he only has five total grades which if you do semi-bad in one you don't get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: (class taken during covid so circumstances were different) such a good prof! Really a great grader, if you show up, do the work, study, you can't get a bad grade! Also a really nice man and let our class extend our quiz by a week because he thought we weren't ready! super nice. 10/10

The class is fine, its easy to pass if you do your work, but the attendance policy is BS, its worth 10% & lab is 30% of your grade. I ended up with an 88% and thats with a 94% on the midterm, a 92% final, and 95% term paper just bc I missed 1 lab and 12/27 classes, if I had gotten perfect lecture & lab attendance I wouldve gotten a 96%...

I'm on week 10 an I still don't know what the class is about. We go from testing criteria for government officials of the Shang Empire to Persian language families all in the same week. His lectures have mandatory attendance because otherwise people wouldn't show up. Huge waste of time. Nothing is relevant, just study and pass the tests and papers
Class is basically graded on three big papers, there's a midterm and a final as well, but if you study the vocab list that he gives you it is very easy
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Andrew Goble is the most monotonous teacher that makes going to lectures seem like an unworthy use of time. The grading criteria was EXTREMELY UNCLEAR and the GEs were horrible when it came to grading. Attendance is mandatory but it was a waste of time to go. Im failing the class because of their failure to teach it.

His class is dry. You just listen to his lecture. There are two parts of the midterm and the final that are writing test and takehome paper. the Writing test is about ID questions and multiple choices. The take-home essay is at least 3pgs. You will have a term paper which is 8-10pgs about history what this class covered. He's welcome to help you

Goble is the sweetest guy and always makes jokes. However, his lectures go off on tangents, and his slides are huge paragraphs that don't make much sense. He honestly makes no sense... There was 1-2 chapters a week assigned as reading, 50-100 pg which is absurd for a 100-level. Missing one lab was 3% of your entire grade. I don't suggest this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Goble's lectures are somewhat dry, but he is funny and keeps it entertaining. The only assignments were two short essays, and two quizzes. Attendance is also graded. If you show up and pay attention it is impossible to do bad in this class.

Goble is such a nice teacher, but his class is bone dry boring. You will fall asleep in class almost every day. If you are looking for an easy class, this could be for you cause nobody really does the reading and you can still do well. Quizzes not too hard, final is much harder.

Dr. Goble is very quirky but passionate about the subject and his lectures are usually pretty short during the class, most of the class is spent watching movies.  The Final is pretty hard, the midterm a bit easier. That being said, the work load outside of class is allot. The reading usually took up 6 to 8 hours of my life a week.  Dr. Goble

Goble is hands down one of the worst teachers I've ever had. His lectures are monotonous and he is constantly undermining the opinions of his students. He mumbles and ignores class input and disrespected our time.

He's a good teacher but much of the time he spent going over trivial things such as lineages that we were never tested on. He had a terrible habit of going over, an average of 3-6 minutes. It's a good class and you'll learn something but still.

Dr. Goble was outstanding! He made this class very interesting to anyone who took it, even those who weren't interested in it prior to taking the class, and he was very helpful and clear. He also was very kind and willing to help those. My grandma died during the term and he extended my due dates for homework. I would suggest Dr Goble to anyone!

Goble was the sweetest old man who had a good passion for history. He had this unexplainable energy when lecturing. The quizzes are not hard but the final quizz was definitely harder than expected. The lectures were tedious and long though, so try to drink coffe beforehand.
Professor Goble's lectures were interesting, engaging, and often funny. There were several days during which we watched interesting films, and his quizzes were not very difficult at all.

He is fun and very approachable. There are only two quizzes and you fail the whole class if you fail the second quiz. The quiz is not difficult if you do the readings and pay attention the films, but you don't really need to do all readings as the powerpoint is comprehensive and helpful for your quiz.

I personally think that Professor Goble is an exceptionally accommodating teacher and if you just focus on the identifications on the study guides then you will do just fine.  (You also don't even really need to read the books, but you might want to anyways...)
He is an excellent and knowledgable professor, very nice and fair, I love his class! And he always can make his class very interesting!

Goble was a pretty good professor. Samurai in Film is easy if you have your stuff together. The essays are graded liberally and the tests have study guides. If you go to class and read you will succeed, no problem.

Really nice teacher who goes above and beyond for his students. 3 tests with study guides given in advance. ID and mult choice. Not too bad given the powerpoints. The hard parts are the reading and test paper. At least 10 pages on any subject you wanted but info heavy! The readings are all on hard copy. 1 copy for 40 people. Get it early!

Great Professor. Really makes the material come alive and is very knowledgeable on the subject. Understands that most students don't have huge background in Japanese language or history. Great teacher, I love this lectures (his accent is great too!)  Highly Recommended!

Professor Goble's class is lecture based.  There are no powerpoints and he had the class watching a movie every week.  The main problem I had was that he is just plain boring.  If you can stay focused easily and enjoy listening, this class will be fine.

Overall a decent class, not as cool as i would have liked it to be. Interesting, but the 10 page term paper is terible. I wouldn't recommend this class to someone unless they really like Asian History.

I took his Samurai in Film class, which I had been told was easy but I bombed the final despite my best efforts because he asked the most arbitrary questions I've ever seen on a history test. His grading policy was that if you fail the final you fail the course, regardless of the rest of the work, which meant that I failed despite 2 A papers.

An extremely entertaining teacher if you take the right topic from him.  Karma and Choice was an excellent class by him, samurai in film was not.  It was actually quite boring despite its entertaining class title, where karma and choice focused on WWII and was actually a very exciting class... His tests are simple but moderately difficult too
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Goble is a kindly soul, and he is able to make even the most inane of things seem hilarious. The Samurai in Film course that he teaches is easy, but the professor's discussion of morbid things makes it somewhat more interesting, and worth going to class for.

Hilarious guy-clearly knows his stuff. I'd definitely recommend his Samurai film class. (It's very easy). Take home essays make up the majority of the grade on midterms/final, usually requires 1 research paper. Readings are usually from 1 or 2 books--not bad.He has an entertaining British accent especially when he's shouting Japanese.  Itadaki!!!

Pretty standard online course. Lots of readings and lecture videos (were mid-quality and often reused from previous years) so stay on top of weekly work. The GEs were what made this course engaging and interesting (shout out Kelsi!!)

This class isn't too hard if you keep up with all the little weekly assignments, but they can pile up. It gives you a fair amount of knowledge on the course topic. The professor isn't very understanding of late work and doesn't offer flexible deadlines.
Long readings that arent 100% clear, final is heavily weighted and you must do good, and the guidelines for it are pretty non existent.

Prof. DuBois is the type of professor to say "I am DR! DuBois and only refer to me as Dr." He acts like he's all that, with office hours being appointment only. He assigns work that is unclear about expectations, and then when we get graded, its by a GE who will pick out every bad thing you ever wrote.

There isn't a lot wiggle room with the discussions or work assignments. It's mostly graded by GA/TA and I feel like they might be a little bias. Questions are not really clear on how they need to be answered. They are presented as to how you think about the question while using the reading or lectures in your answer, but that is not the case.

This is for ANTH 365. The reading quizzes are hard but not too difficult if you have them open while taking the quiz. As long as you do the work and read the instructions you'll do well. There is a final essay that is not too difficult but the rubric is pretty much nonexistent.

wont let me select anthro 365. Awesome class! would highly recommend! definately the best online class I have taken. Fun, engaging, relevant, and interesting content, clear and cohesive guidelines, it is very hard to not succeed in this class, just turn everything in, not a lot of busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: An absolute gem for an anthropology class and the teacher. The rubric/grading is really clear and actually responds to his emails. The assignments and readings actually make sense of what you're learning and were very interesting. The exams are super easy if you pay attention to the lecture and take notes! Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives detailed lectures and one worksheet/discussion post each week. Lots of reading, and some of the reading is difficult, but it is all relevant and done by actual academics. Tests ask a lot of specifics from the readings as well, which can be hard to find even when you do the readings. No big papers, no group projects.
Prof Mason is the GOAT of pppm. So caring and passionate about her work. For those who aren't in PPPM, it may be boring but she is an easy grader and understanding
She is a great professor and so knowledgeable. She is understanding and cares about her work. I would 100% recommend this class.

classes are so simple and she definitely knows what she's talking about, but I wish she was able to engage more with the class. idk just feel like sleeping through them all. but she is super nice and an easy grader.

This class feels like AI. It's like AI planned the entire coursework and all of the assignments. I feel like a robot, a cog in the machine. Dyana is a kind lady though. The lectures are technically somewhat interesting and I am learning about the Nonprofit sector, but the way it's being done is incredibly boring and lacks soul.

No complaints, expect for the fact she SPEEDS through the socrative questions. If you are a slow typer be warned. Literally had perfect attendance but got half a point docked on my participation grade because I couldn't answer maybe a couple of the questions in time since she speeds through them.

Overall, a good professor and class. Many of the topics in the class were engaging to me, and she had quite a few guest speakers, most of which were interesting. My only critique is the final project throughout the class felt very confusing and underexplained, but my group got through it fine. Not too much homework, but a decent amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: PPPM280 is a somewhat interesting class, however wouldn't recommend unless you are pursuing a PPPM Degree. The lectures can be very boring but overall a pretty easy class.

Dyana is very sweet and caring, but she doesn't do anything to make the class interesting. Probably the most boring class you can take at this school, but it is extremely easy. The tests are very important to get a good grade. It is also video and guest lecture heavy with a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dyana is a great professor and is very passionate about her work. She wants the best for her students and is willing to help. Her assignment instructions are not very clear sometimes but when you ask her she helps a lot and gives you advice.

This class is a well organized class. It has clear and achievable assignments that you will be given plenty of support to complete. Her lectures are well spoken and she actively works to engage with her students. You do have to study, and her tests (midterm and final) are comprehensive. You will deserve the grade you receive, which is comforting

Honestly, this was probably one of the most straightforward classes that I have taken at UO. If you show up and pay attention, you'll pass. There were readings and some work outside of class, but if you review the materials before the exams, you will be fine. Prof. Mason cares a lot about students and wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Class can be very boring. The subject material is very easy but she does a poor job of explaining specifically what she's looking for on exams and the questions are extremely broad which can be frustrating. The class isn't hard, just very boring and annoying. It's a requirement for PPPM but if you aren't a major or minor in PPPM I'd steer clear.

Prof. Mason is a nice person but the class is very dry. The textbook readings are hard to get through, except for the case studies. There are a lot of guest speakers, which sounds fun but gets very boring very quickly. There are two written assignments, a midterm and a final, so the class load outside of the reading is fine. Required 3PM class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her intro to nonprofit class made me switch from journalism to 3pm. I think she's very knowledgeable, down to earth and a good communicator.

great professor that not only understands the world of non-profit but also holds an MBA and understand how to navigate both sides of the economy. She is very approachable and available for help. She genuinely cares about the success of her students and extremely knowledgable

I liked Dyana Mason's PPPM280 class a lot. It was only graded on the midterm, final, and two other assignments, which makes it tricky but she is very helpful and seems to want her students to do the best they can. There is a heavy focus on the discussion section.

Lectures were boring and her information didn't always pair up with what was in the text book. Even though I read and understood materials, I still never performed as well on tests as I expected to, and was very unclear of what was expected of me.

She is pretty boring. Doesn't seem extremely passionate about her subject. She's average, a run-of-the-mill public policy teacher who doesn't spice up lectures with anything remotely controversial, humorous, personable. This was her first time teaching the class and it's obvious.
I lOvE dR. dYlAn, GiVe HiM tO mE a SeCoNd TiMe, PLEASE!!!!

He definitely tries to get comfortable explaining topics to students on a person-to-person level, which definitely helped me and a lot of others understand the concepts more fully; he also has a wholesome sense of humor and seems to really love working with the math he teaches.

He was extremely challenging and expected a TON of work, but was also incredibly nice, obviously loved math, made class interesting and was a very fair grader. I alternately loved and hated this class. It was very demanding, but in the end I'm so happy I had Dylan as a teacher - he's great, especially if you like math.

He's hard, but he's fair.  He pushes students, is more than willing to help them multiple days in a row on the same problem, if they are really lost like I was.  At times the amount of work is frustrating, but overall he was a really helpful instructor.

I like Dylan a lot. He's an extremely nice guy. Even though his homework assignments are pretty hard and challenging, he's willing to work with the students. His tests are pretty difficult. Sometimes the questions on the tests are not on the homework. He's a thorough teacher though. If you're taking math because you love it, I'd recommend his class

Would definitely recommend taking this class if you're interested in upper-division math classes. Though his class is more difficult than many of the other sections, you will learn it much more thoroughly. If you're just taking calc for the credit, I would recommend taking it from someone else. He is always open to questions and friendly.

Just took the final and there was not a single problem on it we have ever gone over. AVOID HIM. Makes you feel dumb for asking questions. Must know everything about trig by heart, don't expect to be able to use calculators on the midterms or finals, and no.... he will not give you easy numbers to solve. Also he gives limited attempts on webwork.

Cool guy but the class is too hard. I get that he wants you to learn everything completely. But if I can get a 93% on another teachers final and yet get a D on his, then its kinda like I'd rather get a good grade and be less challenged then be challenged and actually learn more. I liked his lecture style, but again test/quizzes way too hard. AVOID

The homework is tough, but not impossible.  If you actually try it is definitely not hard to pass, and you can get an A. Quizzes were the most difficult part about the class, but as long as all of the homework is done and you do well on the tests its easy to get a good grade.  Seems like a nice guy, but I don't like his use of riemann sums.

AVOID! His testing strategy is impossible and hes not willing to work with students to change it. I got 100% on the homeworks and knew exactly how to do problems on the quizzes in the 1st couple weeks I was there, but he failed me on the quizzes i took because I couldnt describe each step adequately in 20mins. He makes the class impossible to pass.

Homework is obscenely difficult, and will take more time than it's worth. His lectures consist of two exceedingly long examples, completed while he mumbles and paces and writes small on the board. Avoid at all costs.

Avoid at all cost.  Class notes are useless-- they do not help with homework.  He "teaches" from the book, but doesn't actually. Quizzes and tests are exceptionally hard-- most people fail.  Does not care whether his students are learning.  Avoid.

Dylan seems like a nice guy and a competent mathematician. Consult him privately on problems & he's very helpful. Not good in the classroom, though. Lecturing, he speaks softly and hardly acknowledges us. He does nothing to foster participation. But I prefer his lectures to his days of nothing but grade school-style individual seatwork. Avoid him!

I hated the class!! I couldn't make it to his office hours and he refused to meet with me outside of that time, as he said "I'm pretty busy." His homework assignments are super hard and he doesn't ever go over anything in class. You can tell that he loves math but not teaching. He likes laugh at his students, as well, if they don't understand.

This teacher made me hate math.  I would never sign up for a class where I knew he would be the professor.  He taught differently then what he tested.  I went to office hours every day just to pass the homework.  The average on the final for our class was a 40%, with the highest grade a 60%..kinda show how terrible of a teacher his is. Dont take hi
amazing!!!!!!

Great teacher, very enthusiastic about what he's teaching. Gives extremely hard homework assignments, so go into office hours. The difficulty of the assignments ended up being a good thing, as I ended up knowing everything back to front, and his exams seemed really easy.
Teaches mostly by doing examples on the board, which is a bit difficult at times. If you go to his office hours, though, he'll help you with whatever you need.

I found his teaching style very comprehensible. He was very good at answering questions everyone had about homework, and especially giving the class time to turn the homework in once all their questions were answered. Whenever I went to his office hours he was very helpful. Plus he's not bad for looking at!

was always accessible outside of class and did his best to keep a small class engaged. i believe most of his studies were education based but he was our history GE. good luck with all your future endeavors, dylan!

he is so nice and caring about students. he wants everyone to do well and always makes sure students concerns are addressed. wish i could have him as a GE again cause he's super passionate about education, something rare to find in a GE

Dylan is super approachable and a very down to Earth kind of guy. He's very genuine when giving feedback and really wants students to pass. We had a small class but he still tried his best to keep students engaged with the material and with each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Super nice guy. He always keeps the class engaged and is enthusiastic about teaching/learning. He gives great feedback when grading papers and sets clear grading criteria. He is super chill and seems like he is a really cool guy outside of his job. He cares a lot about students, compared to other GE's I've had in the past.

His class was fine; it was the first calculus class I took, so it was difficult. He was exasperated with our lack of algebra skills, and his teaching style was quite ordinary. I wouldn't choose to have him as a professor again, but if I had to I would. If you study and keep up with the homework you'll do fine.
Was not understanding of any workload students might have outside of his class and was generally really belittling to students that tried to ask for help.

Professor Dugger taught stats very simply, allowing most to understand what was going on. I had no prior stats knowledge, yet I never really struggled because we constantly practiced the new methods we learned and Dugger went at a good pace. I highly recommend taking this class with him.

Dugger sometimes gets sidetracked in his lectures, and the study materials he provides aren't always that helpful. That being said, he's accommodating and is a pretty solid teacher for a hard class (Stats). Not the greatest ever but certainly not a bad teacher.

Good at explaining the why, not the how. Made concepts a lot more difficult than needed. attended almost all classes and went to tutoring, but concepts were still hard to grasp. If you have him for stats then he is amazing! calc, not so much
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best math professor I ever had. Extremely good lecturer with easy to understand explanations. Very accessible for homework help in class and via email/office hrs. Never makes students feel bad for asking questions, lots of time for questions in class. 2 webworks per week manageable problem amounts. Final replaces a midterm grade if it helps you.

Dr. Dugger cares deeply about his students and wants them to succeed. He makes himself accessible outside of class and was even willing to zoom with me for homework help while I was sick. His lectures are fairly clear and his explanations rarely confused me. Open note exams and test problems were similar to homework problems.

Textbook is open source online. His lectures cover what you need to know for the test, but not necessarily the homework, but the homework is online and you get infinite attempts to get the problems right. He goes over homework in class before it's due.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan is a great lecturer. All concepts are explained clearly and he gives plenty of examples. Every class was given both in-person and on zoom, and the zoom lectures were posted so students could access them at any time. The webworks can be a little difficult at times but are manageable. Attend class/watch every lecture and you'll be just fine.
THE GOAT of the math department, no question. Simple, clear lectures mostly just formulas. Webwork sucks. Big balls as well.

All lectures were recorded which was really nice because I got to go back and look at them. There are lots of resources for study groups and extra support if needed, and if you put in the work he does care and you will get a passing grade. Best math teacher I have ever had.

as long as you do the webwork and score okay on the tests you'll be okay. The tests might throw you off; they want you to know formulas and cal/excel commands in context rather than finding the actual answer. I found it best to take a few days to rewatch the recorded lectures before a test. my second time taking this class, and I passed bc of him!

Not the most animated personality but gets the job done. His teaching is clear and digestible. Definitely somewhat of a challenge, but doable. Webworks are a pain and really brought down my grade. The final was very very hard. Lets you have notecard on exams and gives good practice exams.
He was very clear on his homework, its consistent, he also recorded all of his classes so you can view later and also shares his notes from class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Duggar made this class very accessible. Attendance is not mandatory and he records all of the lectures in case you miss class. He will also replace your lowest midterm score (there are two midterms) with your final exam score if it will help your grade. There is no reason you should not pass this class as he sets you up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Dugger is the sole reason I passed this class. I am not good at math at all, but he structured lectures so there was time after class to ask for help with WebWork. Though I did great on WebWork, I bombed most of the tests cause I just forget everything. Despite that, I still passed the class. WebWork is the best and worst thing ever...
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dugger has been the most accessible math teacher I have ever taken. While he is not "warm and fuzzy", his expectations are clear, his grading is fair, his TAs are wonderful, and he builds in many universal design features that I respect deeply as a student worker for the Accessible Education Center. He is by far the best stats teacher.

Be ready to work outside of class. The professor does not teach the concepts behind the statistics, he simply relies on students to memorize formulas. If you do not understand something, you will have to study materials not covered in lectures.

I had him last term so I'm a bit late on the review, but Dan was great. Video lectures were concise with worthwhile examples and key definitions, and he's great about answering questions. Workload was on the higher end, but easy quizzes and slightly more challenging WebWorks keep you on track and get you well-prepared for the midterms and final

I only had him for pre-recorded lectures. They were usually short & easy to understand, but the WeBWorks we had were MUCH more difficult than anything we went over during discussions or was covered during lectures. The homework took HOURS to complete & had incredibly non-intuitive software. I like math, and I strongly disliked this class.

Only had him for lectures, but he was actually ok. Lots of Webwork homework and lecture videos, but the videos can help. You will have to go to office hours for this class and going to his really improved once I went to his. He is understand, but harsh on grades
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Only had prerecorded lectures but they were very descriptive and I felt prepared for any homework after them.

Assigns WeBWork problems twice a week and has 3-9 video quizzes every week. The homework and the midterm match up pretty well, but the pace and layout of the class are sometimes confusing. Also doesn't explain why things work the way they do (just memorizing and regurgitating concepts) and the WeBWork is often straight up wrong. It was fine overall

One of the better math teachers I've had. Explains things very well. Lots of assignments, but they aren't super difficult. Can be curt when it comes to answering questions and emails, but overall cares a lot about students and will help you get a better grade.

Daniel Dugger is a great professor. He gets straight to the point and tries his best to simply explain the concepts. He gives quite a few assignments, but I think it's only to enforce the notion that practice makes perfect (especially in math). He only gets frustrated after having to repeat something he just said, so pay attention.

He isnt the nicest professor and he does get frustrated sometimes. He is also hard to listen to for long periods of time because he is very monotone. I took this online and it was very lecture heavy, with class 2 days a week, lectures the other 2 days and a quiz on fridays. The webwork is not fun either. Just another class.

THE MOST IGNORANT CLASS I EVER TAKE AT UO. I took this class bc of all positive review he got on here but he is not like that at all in my class. He seems to not response to students in a positive way when they ask questions; like they are dumb or something. The TA and professor themself are careless about the students. I can not express enough.

The tests are kinda tough and count for a lot but he gives you good study guides. Really listened to us and adjusted assignments/gave extra credit if they were too hard. Webworks is a lot of busy work though and really repetitive on top of quizzes and hw. If you stay on top of EC, daily quizzes, and go to discussion meetings you'll be fine.

Takes criticism seriously, always trying to make things less stressful for the students. Have multiple opportunities to improve. Going to office hours really helps because he is amazing at explaining things. Extremely well organized and is the Math department head and he is really good at his job.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dan Dugger is a solid choice for math 243. He is very smart and makes concepts understandable even for someone like myself who isn't the best at math. iClicker questions are worth 2/1. There is a lot of extra credit. I did not buy the textbook, and I am doing well.

Dan's quite a good professor and the current department head, so it's good to know him. His lectures are well thought out, and he's really hard on himself, so he's always looking to do even better. Very good at answering questions.

Prof Dugger is SO good at using colored chalk. Besides that, he's really good at making concepts understandable and accessible to students. He's also really helpful during office hours. Favorite thing about Dugger is that he took the time to learn everyone's name.

Professor Dugger was overall a great professor. His assignments are extensive and can be difficult, but if you go to office hours and ask questions you can get it done. His tests are challenging, but admittedly fair. I got a C on the midterm and still managed to get an A overall so if you put the time in you can do well!

I was a bit disappointed, especially with all these "positive" reviews. The exams were fine- I just hate that the first one was multiple choice. The final was also tougher than I expected- he said there wont be a curve but I really hope that isnt the case. I think for the coming terms Mike price teaches this class. If you can take it with him, do!
