Great teacher. He lectures for the first 50 minutes of class, then uses the remaining 30 as an office hour which is optional. The homework is a large portion of your grade which makes it very easy to make up for lost points on midterms/final. Definitely recommend this professor.

Daniel Dugger is a fantastic Math professor. He is great at explaining things and can communicate to the classes level of understanding. I loved taking his class and was glad to meet him. One of my top favorite professors. Still talk to him outside of class about the class and how to make it even better for students.
He is a good teacher! He explains well, and he is also very helpful. His tests are pretty hard though, you have to know the material very well.

Profesor Dugger is one of the better math teachers at oregon. I have taken this class before at oregon and got none of it. After taking Professor Duggers course i get most if not all of it. Like went from F to B+/A-, that is why professor dugger is dank. If it is between profesor dugger and someone else, choose Dugger.

Calculus is hard, there's no getting around it. The only thing you can hope for is a good teacher and Dugger is. He's very helpful on homework, and good at getting new ideas across with helpful examples. Tests are difficult, he's really looking to see that you thoroughly understand the concepts.
Very clear and intellectual professor! Calculus for biological sciences and medicine, favorite class this quarter! Definately recommend!

I took both multivariable calc classes from Dugger.  Very good lecturer.  He is clear, straightforward and explains things in an intuitive way.  As others have mentioned, he can be awkward but he is always nice and very willing to help students.  Definitely recommend taking his class if possible.

This guys is a good prof.  He does a good job explaining the material.  He's a little socially inept, but we love him despite that.  He is a MASTER of using the colored chalk, and if you put in the effort you'll pass his class

Ive had Dugger for three classes.  He is easy to understand, and he teaches with his own materials rather than just copying what is in the book.  I think his explanations are clear, but  you still have the textbook as a resource if you need it.  Homework load is reasonable.  Probably the best math professor I've had at Oregon.

Prof. Dugger is an excellent professor. He does his own things rather than following the textbook, and he presents the materials in the way students learn the best. I truely enjoyed attending to this class. I highly recommend taking a class from him.

Dan had a hard time keeping the class engaged. He would ramble on his lectures for 50 minutes straight through, barely stopping to look at the class. Grades were not explained. The biggest problem was the inability to find anything remotely similar to the lectures/HW on the tests. Very frustrating class, would not reccomend.
Had Dugger for Linear Algebra. He was pretty good at explaining things. Didn't always stick with the book and he introduced us to a little topology. Happy about that.
Great teacher, has an awesome dog he keeps in the office. Office hours were fun. He is definately wierd. Saw a student threaten him, it was funny.
No Comments
Very few assignments were given and they were all graded very easy. He seemed a little stressed during some lectures, but he was good at explaining stuff. Could tell he actually enjoys the subject

Bruh this dude is so lazy. Like fr. During lectures, he has an uncountable amount of errors. Doesn't write out full answers because he forgot to do it in his notes. Lectures are terrible with extremely poor handwriting. And he makes everyone fall asleep cause he also doesn't turn on the mf lights. Really easy grader tho.
Dylan was awesome. He was super laid back and graded very fairly. He had some funny extra credit too. Extremely knowledgeable and willing to help.

I really liked this class and was able to learn quite a bit from professor Dyke. I thought the lectures were helpful and fairly easy to understand. I'm not sure if this was because he was a great teacher or if I just found the material really interesting. Overall I had a good experience with Professor Dyke.

Needs to retire or something. He is impossible to hear because of his stupid mic, and repeats stuff over and over that doesn't make sense to begin with. He's a nice guy, and you can tell he tries, but he's just not helpful in any way.
He didn't keep my attention at all, very boring lectures which were hard to follow and weird grading scale.
unclear, useless teacher, don't take this class with him. Fall term is really easy, then it gets harder and he doesn't make any sense.
No Comments
His lectures are not the best.  I haven't gotten and homework yet, so I can't complain about that.  I would never have this guy again.
I feel bad but he just doesn't have an organized lesson plan. He sort of just gives an improptu power point with confusing statements. I don't get anything he says.
Worst teacher ever - when are they going to fire this guy!?

His lectures are a little confusing, but he is a VERY fair grader, making this class extremely manageable.  He is also very open to helping students if they do not understand something.  I really enjoyed having him as a teacher and I would take another class from him!

Dylan Bennett is by far the worst instructor at the University of Oregon.  It is an insult that the University has given him a teaching position - I cringe at the thought of actually paying this man to mumble incoherently with absolutely no clarity when he is supposed to be "lecturing".  Save yourself the headache and never take a course from him.

Ebony is smart, knowledgeable, and eloquent. But the way she runs her class is insane. I'm a CRWR minor and this intro to literary nonfic class made me dread creative writing. Her policy is 2/3 grade reduction for every absence above 2 or lateness (late=1/2 absence). She is glib to the point of mean and is extremely unhelpful in office hours.

idk why people complain about her. im learning alot in this class & ive turned something in late and had her refuse it so i even have a basis for complaint, but can you really blame her? she said no late work. it sucks but its the policy. hard to get an A. also she doesnt check her email, but none of my other teachers do either so ?

There are many great creative writing professors at the UO - unfortunately, Ebony is not one of them. Her comments are vague, her notes at workshop are less than helpful, and her general attitude is disrespectful. Beyond that, she expects you to print 40+ scanned pages of reading (no joke) for each class.
Ebony is very nice, which makes it hard to complain about her.  However, she is very unclear with her grading criteria and her writing advice is confusing at best.
Great sense of humor. Fabulous man, difficult grader but very helpful in office hours. Definitely recommend.
Sincere, clear, hilarious, and engaging.
Although it's been years, I still recall Prof. Earl as one of my favorite professors at U of O.
LOVE LOVE LOVE professor Earl. Inspiring, passionate, 100% wonderful.

I would not suggest a class with this man. He is arrogant & lied about our final in class. Nothing like finding out you have a translation final in the 7th week out of 10. There are other options than his classes and I would take them.
Egotistic freak, who misleads students in lectures and assignment and tries to change your views and opinions towards life. You have him as a teacher, drop the class>>>

One of the most charismatic, intelligent, inspiring professors on this campus. Truly manages to draw in and entertain his students while teaching them. You couldn't find a better professor, especially for large freshman classes, at this university.
No Comments

Interesting lectures, intersting subjects, great guest speakers. Easy to listen to. Didn't like his grading procedures for essays for a 100 lvl class.  Heard that the average final test grade for this class was C-. Said he instructed GTF's to grade more heavily on grammer than on concepts. Very dissapointed. I will not take another class from him.
Very openminded professor, and always available to help.  Sometimes expects a bit much from the average student, however, his courses are structured with a good flow to them.

By far, one of the best Hum teachers (and professors at this university) that I have ever taken a class from. He is easy to approach, has lively lectures, and actually stimulates interest in the text we have to read. Take a class from him and you wont be sorry!
Prof. Earl is so sexy!!!!
I love Prof Earl. I'm a groupie definitly, even though his class is hard.
Prof. Earl is a very dedicated, gentle professor whose sincerity will win you over. He's also very knowledgable, clever, and approachable. Definitely hit his office hours.
Great teacher and a great guy. Very kind. Loves the literature. Is clearly concerned about his students' well-being and grasp of the material. His work on Beowulf is fascinating.
Rachel is amazing and anybody would be lucky to take a class with her. She is so cool, interesting, and caring!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rachel is a wonderful professor who takes her time to explain each assignment in depth--- if you don't understand something, office hours and emails are always open, and she is very kind about any confusion you may have! Her humor keeps the class lively and fun!

Rachel's speech class is straightforward and engaging! Her lectures are always amusing, and she converses well with the class. The speeches were always reasonable, and we had enough time to prepare our material and think of ideas. Would definitely take her class again, she's very easy to vibe with!

She made me reflect if I had internalized misogyny against strong, confident women or if she's just a bad teacher. I am a woman by the way. She's the type of person to be very confident in what she's saying, and you either go along with it or you get left behind. Attendance mandatory, it feels like she takes this required class a lil to seriously
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She picks favorites and does not give feedback, instead, she relies on other students in the class to give feedback to each other even when it is beyond their capabilities. She rejected 4 of my project proposals and barely gave me any feedback or advice. Would highly recommend finding a different professor for this course. She doesn't put in effort
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Rachel this past term! She is a tough grader but lays the rubric out very clear and tells you exactly what you need to do to get a good grade. She writes good feedback and is super funny! This class will improve your writing tremendously if you pay attention in class and try! She is super helpful in the way she teaches and provides support.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rachel seems like she is on a perpetual power trip. She grades things based on very few assignments, most things are graded pass/no pass, which would be fine if she gave clear instruction on how to receive a passing grade.  She has clear favorites. You must participate in every class to get full attendance credit, showing up isnt enough. no freebie
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rachel is very unprofessional when it comes to feedback constantly responding to questions with look at the rubric or completely ignoring your comments in total. Grading is awful and you will not know what you did wrong. Has clear favorites in her class and constantly talks about off topic conversation. Least helpful teacher I've had so far at UO.

A lot of this class could be taught asynchronous. Be prepared for a lot of reading before any writing happens. The grading is super clear, if you refer to it as you complete assignment, the course is straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rachel is so funny and engaging. The only thing is that she is a tough grader and has strict deadlines. Other than that, the class was pretty easy.
I had her Shakespeare class and thought she was super funny and down to earth. Does not allow phones out at all, but all the assignments were in class.

Rachel is a really great professor! She's quick and witty, whilst being really down to earth and kind. She assigns relevant and valuable material which ends up being really helpful in other classes too. I'd take another class with her, for sure!

So much unnecessary busy work, like annotating 18-page research papers, peer reviewing like five times with five different steps. Grades are harder almost to even out the grades for the class. Homework almost everyday and will make it a point to dock you points if she sees you even look out the window or look at the time on your phone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Rachel is a caring professor, but completely lacks regard for her students. She bombards you with information during lectures and is very unclear on deadlines. Take any other professor for writing, you will be better off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely tough grader, little to no feedback, Canvas is an unclear mess, overall just no positive aspects especially if you're not her favorite.

Rachel is not very forgiving and every class is extremely dreadful. Her canvas instructions are confusing and difficult to understand when in reality the content is not that hard but the way she presents it is horrible. Would advise people to take this class online, in-person w/ Rachel is an absolute and utter waste of time.

I took Rachel's class last term and really enjoyed it! The vibes were great in her class, and the readings were actually really interesting. She keeps engagement high, so just do the work and you're all set! She also has great style!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rachel is really chill about helping you work out ideas and make polished ideas out of them. She's super funny and relatable, which makes class really enjoyable. Would definitely take her class again!

Rachel is a tough grader for sure on large assignments, however small assignments are graded by mostly completion. Overall enjoyed her class, she gave lots of time to work in class, and deadlines were reasonable and flexible. Do not procrastinate on assignments though! It will be so hard to catch up!

Rachel is a sweet and approachable professor but she is such a harsh grader. I put an extreme amount of work in this class but continuously received poor grades. Assignments such as the outline and the rough draft should be graded on completion. I got a C- on both assignments. I recommend finding a different professor for this course if possible.

Having taken both her 207 Shakespeare class and her 407 Horror Seminar class, I can say this Professor knows what she's doing. She is obviously very passionate about what she does, and that translates into her classes. She's really funny and down to earth too, which make her classes that much more enjoyable. Plus, all the work is super valuable!

I took WR123 with her. She doesn't allow phones or laptops in class in the beginning of the term so she made us print out the readings, which would sometimes be up to 50 pages. She's very flexible with deadlines though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unclear on all grading and will seriously try to find any excuse to not grade your assignment at all. If you mess up the outline before the essay, it's a 0, and if you don't revise that on time then your essay is a 0. Lazy grader, you'll be relying on your classmates for all feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking writing with this professor as she is unclear with grading instructions and gives an insane amount of peer review work. It is excessive the amount of writing you have to do in this class compared to other classes and professors who teach the same class.

I had Rachel for English 405 and 207. I'm really surprised at all the negative reviews on here because she's amazing! I've learned a lot from her and I love attending her classes. She makes her classes super fun and engaging--and she's super helpful, approachable and encourages questions. She's also super understanding about any personal issues!

I had Rachel for an upper division English class. She was a great medium between fun and serious, I always looked forward to the class and the energy Rachel brings to it. Rachel is funny yet super caring and accepts everyone how they are. Love love love her, wish she was my mother.

ENG 407 Professor Eccleston is an amazing, caring, funny, professor! I loved taking this class on horror and she was clearly passionate about teaching it. She effectively guided class discussions, provided in depth individual feedback on assignments, and was always open for questions or concerns. I would 100% take a class taught by her again.

I had Rachel for ENG 207 NOT WR122 but it won't give me the option. She's super funny, really not hard. Just show up and do what she asks and you'll be fine. For assignments/ papers, she wants to hear what she already thinks, not what you think. So make her your target audience.

I feel like the workload for WR122 was a bit much, as there was 2 presentations involved in a writing class. She's super accommodating if you need more time or help on assignments. Super chill and relatable. She's very engaging, enjoyed her teaching style.

She makes a lot of papers and gave work over thanksgiving break despite her not being available for questions over the break. The work was the same word count as a paper which seems unfair. She takes awhile to respond to emails if you like to get ahead on work

Very nice and caring teacher, lots of writing but no more than expected for a writing course. LOTS of extra credit opportunities, and most graded assignments are based on completion, so I ended with over 100% in the class. Do the work and especially the extra credit and this class will be a breeze. VERY helpful in office hours as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Rachel is very sweet and funny and the readings she picked for us were honestly quite interesting. I can't say that her organizations skills are the best, but she is very understanding so just make sure to ask clarification questions about assignments! Otherwise, as long as you do the work, this class is an easy A!

If you follow directions, you will get an A. She doesn't grade based off how amazing you are rather she grades on how you try to implement what she is teaching. Allows for good group discussion and class discussions. She can be odd, but she is relatable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She grades really tough. The feedback she gives isn't clear unless you go to office hours and it's an online class so it's hard for me to go espcially since her office hours were during my other class times. At the beginning of the term, there were 175 people in the class. By the end, there were 20 because they dropped the class.

Rachel is a great choice for a WR professor. She gives good feedback but you have to go to office hours to receive most of it, some of which is specific and things you wouldn't have known otherwise (so go to office hours). She makes class fun and can relate to teens which is nice. There is a lot of writing (duh) but this class is totally doable.

Dr. Eckerman is not only an apsolutely lovely proffesor, he is also a phenomenal person. I would urge anyone that is willing to put in the work and dedication to the craft of greek to do it with Eckerman. It was lovely to study with you this year Dr. Eckerman (since I know you read these) and thank you for everything!

Prof. Eckerman was very nice and engaging with students. However, the course was incredibly taxing and difficult to follow. You must handwrite notes, lectures are strictly auditory, and there's no way to access the lecture material. He will call you out for using tech, talking during class, arriving late, and leaving early. Lots of reading.

Professor is a pretty chill guy. Class has numerous readings. But if you go to lecture, it recaps the reading for you, with Eckerman pointing out various points in the text for you to take note. No electronics; you get used to it. There's reading responses due every week during discussion. TLDR; go to lecture if you plan on skipping readings.
SUPER BORING lectures and horrible canvas, very dense and boring assignments and lack of information available makes test prep hard.

Terrible lectures- mind numbingly boring. Horribly organized Canvas. Everything is posted in announcement section. Are you kidding me? 

Expects you to read a novel's worth of reading each week, but can't take the time to figure out modern academic infrastructure. What a joke of a way to spend your tuition.

I really did love this class. Attendance is mandatory but its for good reason, if you come to class and take the most basic of notes you will do well on the tests which are all non-cumulative. He is understanding about sick absences and late work, and is overall a nice guy who will get to know you and work with you through problems if you have any.

Lots of work but the lectures are pretty good. No tech in class but you get used to it. Attendance is important. Teaches class in different sections with non-cumulative exams at the end of each. One paper is due each week on the readings. A very kind professor who tries to engage with students. Chill guy overall but tough class, material is cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is incredibly out of touch, his lectures are just straight-up boring for starters, additionally, he doesn't allow any technology in the classroom. Also beware, I have taken 300-level courses that have assigned less reading than I had to do for this class, and he assigns annoyingly in-depth reading responses every week.
Cool content, extremely frustrating class organization and professor.

Class consists of lectures on slides, tech not allowed but not a big issue imo. Content is mostly interesting. Has good time-management, topics not covered are scrapped from exam. Has a paper/script but they're just notes, it's completely natural sounding and he's very caring. Tests bit hard but everything is covered in class. ~$50 of materials.

Wow, this Prof. is not great. Lectures of a sheet of paper and often seems uncomfortable/nervous during lecture. Slides and canvas are horribly organized. Doesn't allow phones or computer in class while using online texts. Overall not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor i have ever had, tells you exactly how the test will be and what to study. Amazing lecturer and makes his points clear and easy to follow. Super engaging, the tests are hard but if you go to class they are very easy to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is far out of touch with students: doesn't allow technology in the classroom but simultaneously requires an expensive online textbook, didn't submit any grades until after the last meeting of class. Course material is split in half but not equally given time to be understood, first half gets way more. Lectures: monotone, dry, mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are based on memorization, but if you go to lectures it won't be hard. He does a great job of explaining the material and making it interesting. If you don't go to lectures you will not pass. Assignments never felt unnecessary and always helped build understanding. 100% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Eckerman is one of the best professors at the UO! He simplifies complex content and makes difficult material enjoyable. There were weekly one-page reading responses, a midterm, final and essay, all of which were very reasonable. He is really helpful outside of class and dedicated to getting to know all of his students.
Chris Eckerman has been my favorite professor since I started college. He was available outside of class and even helped me write a history paper. I learned a ton in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I really loved my classic class. It was a big class and I felt like I needed a little more support so I went into his office hours and got help and feedback on essays. We got to be close and he was a reference for me and I stop by his office every so often. Super important to go to class because the test is on all the lectures.

His class was so much fun, he is a devoted and smart man. His lectures were long, but rather amazing. He is understanding and willing to work with you. His ability to teach and reaffirm that teaching with his tests is amazing. If you need or want to attend a Classics class, choose him. You wont regret it if you want to learn.

Professor Eckerman usually reads off his notes for lectures-allows for students to get all necessary info but sometimes can get boring. Very structured class-begins with writing down IDs we will be covering in the class and then move on to discuss them. Lectures the whole class and does not like people asking questions during lecture

Lectures are interesting but the readings are incredibly long, oftentimes somewhat boring or hard to understand. He doesn't have any visual notes so you just have to listen and remember! Tests were straightforward but often had random, small, specific details that were hardly gone over in class. Great guy. Funny, intelligent, and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: i wanted to love this class but just couldn't. lectures are painfully boring (professor reads from a pre-written script) and even though the course is well structured with lists of terms at the beginning of each class, you better have a good attention span because he only provides information for each term verbally. readings are longggg

My favorite teacher at UO. He's passionate about his subject and is very clear in lectures. The lectures can get long but are usually interesting. He tells you exactly what you need to know for exams. Reading is a must but the material isn't bad. I always recommend this class to my friends.

He is my absolute favorite teacher. His class is the most structured class I have ever had. He is very clear and forward about what is going to be on the test. Short assignments due weekly, usually reading responses. Doing the reading is a must. Have suggested these classes to everyone I talk to
Easily the best professor I've had at the University. Very interested in the subject he teaches and very helpful and approachable.
Out of 300 students, he would remember everyones name who would participate or talk to him after class which was ALOT!!
Great lecturer, gives straightforward information on what material will be on tests. One of my favorite professors at the University
Very enthusiastic and approachable. Made this class a lot of fun. :) I am highly looking forward to taking more classes with him.
Great Prof, was very enthusiastic and draws you in with his excitement.
Had lots of interesting things to say about the texts, enthusiastic, and did a good job of keeping the class interesting. Thumbs up.

Mixed review for professor Eckerman. His class was reading intensive and I did not like his grading system. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. I think my problem is that Humanities is NOT my cup of tea.

Professor Eckerman is a wonderful teacher who has tons of expertise in the classics. He's very personable and charismatic, which makes class all the more enjoyable. If you have a chance to take a class of his, go for it because it will be time well spent!

This term he has been my hardest professor yet at the UO and I'm a junior. For the final he provided over 200 terms we are supposed to have memorized and be able to write a paragraph on, based off of 4 texts that have endless greek and roman names and characters that cross between the texts. Also we need to be able to identify 50+ pics.

By far one of the best professors I have had at the UO. He gets so enthusiastic about the topic at hand that you cannot help but grin at the excitement written all over his face and feel the same way about the subject.

I took him for Greek and Roman Tragedy. It was a really interesting class and he was very knowledgeable in the subject. I went to his office hours a couple times and emailed him and he was really helpful. I would definitely take his class again, he's really funny and enthusiastic. Plus, he's young and it's obvious he loves to teach.
Professor Eckerman has a great expertise in the classics.  He loves what he teaches and motivates others.  Fantastic!
ok professor who thinks he's smarter than others. easy tests with memorization sometimes seems uncomfortable in classroom.

I've taken him for three classes; the lectures are excellent, but he's very much like a TED talk. Grades are mostly on papers graded by GEs. He is very understanding, easy to talk to, and an amazing professor. I will always recommend him.

Dr. Eggener is great, he has a funny sense of humor and cares about architecture history. Attendance isn't mandatory but you need to show up and take notes if you want to pass. He can be a bit hard to follow during lectures, but the GEs are very helpful for filling in the gaps. The 3 (?) papers are straightforward, and the final was online.

ARH 399* I took this class not knowing much about architecture, and while that could have been a fresh starting point, it mostly made things harder. He assumes you already know how to analyze buildings and use architectural terms which is not a prereq. If you disagree with him, he'll shut you down real fast even though he "encourages" perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer and keeps everything very interesting. The class is graded on very few things, but as long as you put any sort of effort into the papers you will receive a high grade. Tests are fairly easy as long as you go to the lectures. I honestly didn't need any notes I just relied on what I heard in lecture.

He's a great speaker and has a good sense of humor. He explains everything very well. There's a great emphasis on European architecture in this class. Since there's no attendance, you're incentivized to take good notes since the slides are very broad, but he does post them on canvas. The GE's do all of the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not familiar with online resources/Canvas, slides lack information so be ready to take notes. Somewhat boring lectures, has a textbook for supplementary learning and does use that for some parts of learning. Weird obsession with Germany during modern-era discussion. Goes on tangents and can't link together ideas very well.

Great lecturer, one of the best I've ever had. Though he doesn't know how to use Canvas, after grades had been finalized, he had not put any grades in. Also, my GE(Lauren Dawson) failed me for reasons like exceeding word limits, minor spelling mistakes and 2 missed discussions. He is a great lecturer but relies on GEs for all grading and structure.

If you want to go to a ted talk about buildings twice a week, this professor for you. Dr. Eggener is an amazing speaker and is clearly a master of his concentration. Teaches a ton of valuable information and class is super interesting. Assignments are fun and engaging, would definitely take a class of his again.

Professor Eggener is, by far, the best lecturer I've ever had. He has such a wide range of knowledge and speaks directly from his mind. Your grade is based off of two, short written papers, a midterm, and a final (which will be easy to do if you attend lecture consistently).  This class was super engaging and informative. Keith is great!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class that consists of a midterm and final in addition to a few graded papers. The midterm was in person but the final is online. Overall this class was easy and a fun introduction to architecture history.
Very engaging professor. This class taught me a lot, and the course load was not too difficult. I would strongly recommend taking any class with Keith.

A very engaging professor who makes lectures interesting. The course content is very appealing and relates to other classes. There is not much homework, except for two assignments along with the midterm and final. Very reasonable class when taken with a heavy workload.
I cannot believe I passed this class. Unclear rubrics, impossible final/midterm, inaccessible outside of class.

I took Prof Davis for ERTH 418. Graded by weekly lab, in-class assignments, and weekly problem set. The midterm and final projects were very difficult and took several weeks to complete. Davis is very knowledgeable, but his GEs are not. Difficult topics are difficult to teach, but the group-oriented class structure worked well for my learning
His class is so much fun and he was truly brightened my days! I love his dad jokes and the pre class music! I would 100% recommend if you are needing an extra couple science credits.

Favorite professor I've had so far, not at all interested in the topic but I learned a lot of really cool things that are like fun fact trivia knowledge. He knows how to make a class giggle. Beware it's a flipped classroom and watch the lectures before class so you can ask questions.

Dr. Davis was an amazing professor to have for a 9am class! Even though I would be tired before class, by the time it ended, I had the energy to get up, move, and get going with my other class that day! He really made you want to come to class. The exams are pretty much just the study guides and it was an otherwise really fun class!

Davis was funny and smart and a great prof. He made the material digestible and taught interesting material. He let students guide discussion in lecture. Lecture is crucial to go to because the material will be on exams. Also the class before exams he goes through the whole thing and gives the answers.

He is extremely passionate about what he's teaching and makes attending this class fun. My only thing is that he has you watch the lectures that can be 15 to 30 minutes before the actual class, so you can discuss the material during the class. This format works for me, but if it doesn't fit you, it might be hard to stay on top of the material.
He is very passionate and wants to help students get engaged with the course material. Great classes, clear expectations, and the tests were collaborative with other students in the class.
Cute, funny and keeps the class interesting! Knows his stuff and explains everything very clearly. Tests are a bit tough but nothing unexpected.

He's a really good teacher. He really has passion for the subject and seems to be a better teacher than he was at the beginning of the year. He had some organizational problems earlier this year but is much better now. The course may be hard but he is a great teacher for the subject.

Lectures can be dry at times, but he was a great teacher overall and always willing to help students outside of class.  The tests were fairly easy and contained only material expected to be on the test (no curve balls, yay!).  If people had a hard time, I'm sure it's because of the class material, not the teacher.
No Comments

VERY DRY and boring speaker. I had a lot of trouble concentrating/didn't ever listen. Loves to talk about himself and his connections. He's a classic old guy, I can tell he is retired. Funny sometimes.
This man likes himself... a lot. Due dates are hard to figure out and he does not communicate well will the GTFs. Ask him questions personally so you don't get confused.
Funny guy. Class is still kind of boring though. Hard to stay awake. I put out minimal effort and still got a B so I would say its fairly easy. He was pretty understanding when I had problems.
He is a funny guy, but it is hard to understand what is going on in his class because there is no structure to it at all.

This class was a waste of time. All Weeks does is tell boring stories well you try as hard as you can not to fall asleep. He makes you feel like an idiot when you get a question wrong or ask for help. If you like planning at all, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS as weeks will make you hate the subject.

This class was a waste of my life. It was boring and hard to stay awake in the class. It assignments were difficult to understand and graded harshly. I would NEVER recommend this class to anyone unless its what they REALLY want to do.
Ed is an incredibly prof. I would take any class he offers. A great guy, incredibly helpful outside of class!
This Professor is a wolf in sheeps clothing...He is fine if you don't actually need help with anything.  At that point he treats you like you are wasting his time.
Ed Weeks is an interesting professor. He is very nice and funny. He cracks jokes and makes class enjoyable. I would definatly reccomend this professor to anyone
Excellent teacher. As far as PPPM teachers go, he is one of the most interesting.
Great Professor, Great Course. Nothing more needs to be said
Ed is hilarious, fabulous, and knows his stuff! The man is a KEY to networking in the Planning world and is a great mentor.

Not used to teaching undergrads. The course has no structure. Hope for a good team and excellent GTFs. (The GTFs are the real instructors.) He always keeps office hours and is incredibly nice and helpful.
No Comments

Intro to PPPM made me NEVER want to be involved in public policy. This class was a waste of money, and time. We really didn't learn anything at all. We sat around and talking about pointless stuff, and none of it applied to what the class was about. Boring, and meaningless.

Took a class with Mr. Muller that was a dual enrollment class, and he forgot to submit my attendance and got me dropped despite me never being absent. He also forgot that my group partners were students in his class. He mostly had us solve nonsensical math riddles in his lectures and expected us to read a non-published math textbook for homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Superb teacher, taught at a fantastic pace. Really exciting in lecture and kept the students very involved with in class activities. He has been by far my favorite teacher in all of college. (NOT)

I had Nick as a GTF for my 420 and 421 labs.  He is an extremely nice guy, but seems to have trouble communicating with people.  He's an inconsistent grader.  Most students disliked him immensely as he didn't explain things well (probably an understatement).  Nice guy, terrible teacher.  Should only be doing research.
Don't expect to learn much. Honestly he would probably fail his own class's, Not get a C, fail. He's a really nice guy though. If you ask for help he tries, that counts right?
Nervous, very slow, improvosises every class, horrible handwriting on the overhead, abbreviates everything to make you say "huh?".

Lectures are fine, answers questions. Assignments are worth 25%, takes all day. Lab assignments worth 10%, take almost as long. Neither is that helpful for the exams. One midterm worth 30%, final worth 35%. No notes. Provides plenty of practice exams, don't review slides. Questions are very niche so study everything. Decent curve though.

3-4 Problem sets with one midterm and one final. If you miss the midterm the weight moves to your final, and if you skip the final he estimates it using a regression model. Overall difficult subject but he is very good at communicating and helping with anything. I would definitely recommend for Econometrics 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ed is a really great professor. I felt engaged during lectures and learned so much. There are not many HW assignments, but they prepare you well for the exams. Ed provides a ton of resources and information for the course online, including lecture slides and previous exams.

Ed is AMAZING! Not only is he engaging, but he is also incredibly knowledgeable. I enjoyed coming to his class each day, and I feel like I learned very valuable skills in R. Not to mention that he is the best coder I have ever had! He works magic.

He cares about the students, very nice guy, funny too,So, that helps. He literally remembered everyone's name even the international one's. It is not a common thing in US. I got more and more curious about R and the methods in his class. Comparing the series professors of Econometrics at UO. He is probably the best one.

One of the best teachers I've had so far for R and econometrics. He uses actual relevant content in lectures like showing example answers from ChatGPT or using real-world data. He clearly knows his stuff but he tends to ramble and the math in the lectures can be confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rubin is really nice. He has a sarcastic sense of humor which makes the lecture fun. He is always willing to help in office hours and does his best to help with code when he sees a student trying to learn R. If you do the homework, you will do great in the exam. The homework is usually harder than exams on purpose which is nice.

Professor Rubin is a really good teacher and his lectures are very clear and organized. If you go to class, read lecture notes, go to office hours when you need help, and do your homework, you will easily do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: bad teacher, is completely rude to his students, talks super slow in the lectures, and grades assignments incorrectly multiple times, this was an extremely difficult course and id reckoned taking it with literally any other professor than this guy steer clear

I have taken several other legal studies courses and this was one of the most ridiculous course structures I have encountered. He gave harsh grades with no rubric and vague feedback. Many people scored below an A on our first assignment, which was a personal reflection. Tests were on canvas and people would use AI because he was unable to monitor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: this class start off good but after week 4 or so it seemed like he stopped caring or trying. grades super harshly with no feedback at all. i kindly asked him to round my grade .1 to get from a B+ to an A- and he responded with what i thought was a quite rude email telling me no. tests are on canvas, and he often puts the wrong correct answers in.

I liked him and this class was really interesting but one of the worst grades I've ever received in collage. Had to try to most in this class. He loves a follow up question but if you don't know how to answer its fine just kinda awkward. Hes funny and you can tell hes a lawyer just by the way he is so probably a great resource for prelaw students

Not very clear on assignment expectations. Participation and attendance are tracked inconsistently but matter to your grade. Professor WILL ask many follow ups when you answer a question. 2 writing assignments, 3 MC tests, in class group activities. Not a tough class but the professor definitely doesn't make it easier.

Material is used for all of his classes. Same assignments and same lectures no matter what he's teaching. Unclear assignments and grading. Get ready to read and participate heavily if you want a good grade.

Very good teacher who teaches from his experience as a lawyer. Assigns a lot of reading but you can pass without reading. A few writing assignments which he grades somewhat harshly but totally worth his presence

Very tough grader and lots of work. textbook is mandatory and so is attendance. Huge chunk of your grade is based off of actual participation and how much you speak up in the class. 3x tests, 2x 1,700 word papers with not much help. Expectation is to read a chapter from the book before every class. Very smart teacher and personable but tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Participation is a huge aspect of grade, he claims that he keeps track of when students speak, but rarely does. You can get participation by volunteering to do case studies, and they fill up quickly towards the end of the term so get on them asap if you can. Lots of reading and horrible grades for tests/essays with lack of feedback/guidance.

I think he lacked the social awareness that all students are most likely taking three other upper division courses that are time consuming as well. You can pass the class by speaking every single class, reading 30 pages of textbook per night, take three exams and write two papers that he will grade harshly and not give helpful feedback on.

Lectures were 2 hours of students asking pointless questions in order to get "participation," which he incorrectly tracked. For exams and papers, the class averages were horrible, so he explained to us how business students interpret his assignments wrong.. in a business law class..

Nice guy but other professors provide a better student experience
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Gerdes is a great person and is very personable. The class is interesting because he is very knowledgeable on everything and has a good personality. I will say the class contained mandatory textbook reading every class with 3 exams and 2 1700 word essays. Participation was also mandatory but class was fun if you stay engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had, I never was bored during class. Though he has "participation points" where you have to speak in class every day and did not keep track well, no makeups or absences allowed. Also very tough grader for essays even though he did not prepare us well. Exams extremely difficult even though open book, class average was 60%.

I really enjoyed this class overall, and lectures were very engaging. Participation is really important, as he tallies participation points. The class had good content and all tests are open book and open note, which was helpful. Content is still dense and hard to grasp at times. Definitely recommend taking.

I love this class and Madame Ekani is really caring about students, I could earn an A but I didn't put too much effort into this class plus it was my first time taking French so I didn't know what was going on bc half of my class at least know the basics, Attendance is a big deal so don't expect to pass the class without going to class.
Lise is nice, interesting and gets the job done.  She is understanding and works with the class to make assignments reasonable.  Participation is key.

She's a great french teacher. Plus, since she's a graduate student (currently), she tends to sympathize with the class when people are tired or busy. If you show up, participate actively, turn everything in, and study for the module exams, you should do quite well. Just try not to be late--she's not a fan of that.
He is super strict on getting work done, but make the class exciting and fun to be in... He is a fantastic teacher.
He was the most inspiring and thoughtful prof I have ever had.  He carried his love of language on his shoulder like a badge, and teaches as though he were ordained to do so.

He is the best teacher I've ever had. Very challenging and demanding. I'm surprised someone said the class had no structure but it was the best structured class I've ever taken. He's crazy about his stuff! To me, he's a class act. Always cleanly dressed (ties, pants, sometimes suits). Awesome!
He's an **** and the class had no structure.

(CRWR) A sweet person, but I learned nothing in this class. Lots of out loud popcorn reading (in class!!) which was excruciating to sit through. Take if you want an easy class for the minor requirement, but expect to be doing a lot of random stuff that isn't writing at all.

Very easy class! Be prepared to take a lot of handwritten notes that you'll have to turn in. There are only a couple of essays and a super easy group project that required no out-of-class time. I'm not sure that I learned very much, but she was very sweet.
Sophie is a great professor and I'm unsure why she gets such bad reviews. You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches and wants everyone to succeed. She also kept class pretty entertaining.

As someone who struggles with writing and didn't take AP Lang in HS, I found this class to be very helpful. Sophie's course material is simple yet engaging, and you can tell she really wants to meet students where they're at. Notes are handwritten and required to be submitted weekly as a participation grade. This class is a pretty easy A.
Does she care a lot? Yes. But I could have passed this class in 8th grade. If you're looking for easy 122 credit just be ready to be bored.

This class was a waste of college education, and I feel disappointed that I had to pay money for it. Material doesn't make sense to the course and there are only a few grades. The professor was unavoidable, it said "TBD" on my professor before the course started. I would avoid this class at all costs if you value your money and education.

(CRWR 340) She's great if you want an easy class you can pass without trying too hard, but I wouldn't recommend her if you genuinely hope to strengthen your writing. She gives good feedback and grades largely on effort. Very sweet and loves community building, and very understanding of late work, but she does ramble a lot. She's not for everyone

Sophie is awesome. I found this class incredibly easy in content (if you took AP Lang you will breeze through). Our theme was love, which I had a really good time with, and I honestly enjoyed her tangents. I agree w other reviews that class can definitely be a bit boring, and there's some forced social interaction at times, but Sophie is a queen.

Sophie's a wonderful person, but her classes are very boring. Every minute in that room felt like an hour and I didn't learn anything. If you took AP Lang, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. It's the exact same thing but less essays. If you're just trying to get the credits, go for it. If you genuinely enjoy writing, take literally any other writing class.

Seems to expect a lot out of our work even though we don't learn much in class. The classes are very easy, but her grading is extremely unreasonable—I only scored 2 points higher on an essay I spent hours on (even visiting the on-campus writing center at her request) than on one I wrote in a single night.

Professor Ell gives quite excruciating and meaningless lectures (thank God it was only a 50-minute-long class). She tends to drone on about nothing until the very last minute of class (she will even start speaking slower, lol). She's very sweet though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring and useless class. I learned absolutely nothing about writing. Everyone in the class seems to agree that it feels like being back in middle school English. Do NOT take this professor if you actually want to work on your writing skills. She talks super slow and teaches things everyone learned in 7th grade.

Super boring professor and class. But she grades EXTREMELY easy. Take her if you want an easy A. There is a 10-12 page essay and a final group project. As long as you show up for most classes you'll be fine, she doesnt really care about attendance but you need to know what to work on. She doesnt use technology so there's lots of print outs
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While a nice person, class is horribly boring. She didn't teach us a single thing about research. In fact, after taking  science classes I taught her about PubMed, she had no idea it existed. She talks PAINFULLY slow, while a very very nice person, but I would avoid her if you can. Shes super nice but makes it difficult learn and focus when talking

Prof. Ell was super sweet however, as I have noticed with required writing classes, really boring. She goes on tangents a lot so you don't really need to pay attention which is nice sometimes. You work on one paper the entire term so make sure to choose a good research topic that you care a lot about and then the class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her for WR 199, and although I went to only a couple of the classes, she made sure you pass the class, and she even gave me extended time on the assignments that were due at the end of finals week.

Personally, I loved Eleanor. College writing classes are hard in general, and yeah, you are going to be doing a lot of work in them. Even with a big workload (no midterm or final tho!) she made sure you are getting the right education while trying to help you enjoy and understand what you are writing. Take her class, she doesn't get enough credit

Dr. Wakefield is a sweet and funny person, but her class is very disorganized. She provides good feedback but you won't receive it in time to actually make any of those changes before the next segment of the assignment is due and her instructions are VERY long but still somehow vague and difficult to meet the requirements of within the word count.

Very easy material. No midterms or finals, but a lot of in-class work with peers. You are mainly graded on 4 small essays, 300-700 words, throughout the term, along with weekly annotations on Perusall. Overall easy A if you just pay attention and show up, and post on the discussion board.

Eleanor is a lovely person and has a relatively chill attendance and extension policy. She is just disorganized. Unclear discussion posts and things posted to Canvas super close to the due date. Didn't even know half the things we were doing in class were supposed to be turned in. Expectations were unclear throughout the course.

She really cares for the class and likes to connect with groups. The class is very group work orientated, so make sure that you find a good group to make class fun. Perusall is a pain but its not really her fault its just the settings. She will answer questions if you ask them so don't be afraid to ask about the perusall. Only 3 essays in the term.

Worst semester of my life due to so many factors, Professor Wakefield was a compassionate listener and was very flexible about due dates which helped me succeed. Ended up doing just fine and maintained by academics in other classes due to her kindness. I highly recommend her as a professor!

Expectations were incredibly high for an online class. Weekly discussion board posts/responses were painful. Lessons were overpacked and could take hours assuming you actually read through them. 2 essays based on readings used in disc posts graded ACCURATELY with highly knowledgable feedback. If writing isn't for you, try harder and be on time

Lessons made no sense half the time, and since it's an online course she felt like she could assign whatever whenever. She wanted us to watch hour-long lectures with even longer assignment tasks, would force you to meet with your "homegroup" for coffee and other events when it was an online course. +  I have never had my papers so harshly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Wakefield is amazing! Makes everything really clear and helps you along the way as you make the perfect essay. Very approachable.

I learned a lot in Dr. Wakefields class, although it was difficult. She graded harshly and if you were absent the day an assignment was due, even though theyre submitted online, you lose points. I do feel like a better, more confident writer now because of the coursework she taught me, although I found her to be intimidating.

Professor Wakefield is friendly, down to earth, and is clear in the way she wants things done in the class. She is personable, very qualified, and has a good sense of humor. 4 essays total, lots of in class group discussion, very laid back. Have fun!
Eleanor was super. I really enjoyed her class and would take it again. It is an easy class for the most part but the essays can be a little difficult. She taught me a lot in a simple way.

I dislike this professor very strongly.  I cannot fully express my feelings because of the "Do's and Don'ts" of this website but I'm sure you can imagine what I have to say. I feel as though this professor is not ready to be teaching college students. The material is hard to follow, uninteresting and tedious.

Nice lady, but she seemed very unorganized, most of the class was spent either doing peer reviews or watching peer presentations. She is also very slow at getting back grades on assignments. of the 15 or so projects we had during the term, only 3 had grades by the last week of class. She also grades a lot tougher than a WR 122 teacher should...

Eleanor has a great personality and is very easy to talk to. She is always ready to help you with any questions about readings/essays/etc. She seems to be an easy grader and gives helpful feedback. I got A's on all my essays except for one. She's one of my favorite teachers!

An awesome writing 121 teacher. Begins the class with funny commentary, lets you miss 3 classes per term without penalty, teaches fundamentals of writing well, and keeps the class interesting while teaching well, too. Great teacher.
Fun, easy writing class. Very helpful when you're looking to improve research skills. She goes out of her way to help you find sources.
Typical WR 122 class. She's really cool in class and is funny, however she assigns busy work and is a REALLY hard grader.

Great person, love her and her stories, the class is very reading-heavy, so get ready for that. Discussion posts also matter, even if she says it's for your own notes, IT IS NOT!! Also, get reading to make system maps and whatnot, that part is interesting, but she is picky and a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I really liked the discussions that we had in this class. Professor Fitzpatrick is great at leading discussions, but she is not great at technology. Professor Fitzpatrick also grades very particularly so that was frustrating.
Good teacher, I learned a lot! But the workload was very heavy, including weekly essays, and she was a tough grader

I really enjoyed taking this class. There was a lot of reading, but I found the topics interesting and the class discussion was engaging. Do not take this class if you're more introverted, as you will be required to speak basically every day. I also really like Professor Fitzpatrick. She leaves good feedback and is open to everyone's perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: None of her assignments make sense and she is a tough grader. The descriptions of what the assignment requires has way too much information and is very easy to get confused by. What we are learning in class isn't easily connected to the assignments due at the end of every week and much extra research is required. Participation in class matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Fitzpatrick. Her classes are discussion- and research-based rather than traditional. Assignments can be unclear, but if you engage, participate, and collaborate, you'll do well. She prioritizes real-world research skills and gladly connects students to jobs, study abroad programs, and research projects or discusses her career.

The class was designed as a writing workshop where you spend the whole term writing a research paper as a class, with teams of 2-3 writing individual chapters. Towards the beginning of the term I was frustrated with the lack of clarity of the feedback I was receiving, but I ended up enjoying the class and really growing my research writing skills.

All of our large essay assignments had no clear grading rubric and were extremely tough. While we had the opportunity to resubmit it, it was difficult to meet her requirements. She FORGOT TO ASSIGN US THE FINAL, then made us do it with way less time than another period. Her feedback was very harsh and unhelpful.

Professor Fitzpatrick taught my HC101 class on "Global Problems", where she repeatedly made false, misleading, and harmful comments about third world countries. Her instructions were unclear, and her grading was incredibly harsh and her feedback was unhelpful. She had no idea had to use Canvas, and accidentally deleted the entire class's midterms.

Do NOT take this professor. She offered some students that they can redo their assignments but not others? How is that fair? Her rubrics are extremely unclear and even if you provide everything she says that wants in the assignments, she will find another way to mark you down.
The professor was unclear about grading and offers inadequate feedback. She is a tough grader even if you provide all elements she wanted in the assignment.

I can understand why she has bad reviews for 301, but she's not too bad for 477. However, she doesn't give any feedback, she just encourages you to share things with your thesis advisor. Was hard to understand expectations from her because of this, but as long as you get your prospectus approved by your thesis advisor, you'll pass.

This is one of the worst honors college classes at the University of Oregon. Instructions and grading are unclear on the assignments, leading to massive grade deductions from following the rubrics. She met with every student and gave the "okay" for projects but ended up taking off points anyway. Class is extremely boring to top it off.

This was the most frustrating class and professor ever. Graded by 5 assignments total, extreme lack of clear instructions, feedback, and useless lectures. Prof. Fitzpatrick could not remember or understand any of our projects and graded us harshly despite requiring us to meet with her and ok our projects (she changed mine three times).

I loathe going to her class every day. Even though it is a small CHC class, it is week 7 of the class and she has not bothered to try to remember any of her students' names. She is self-centered, constantly asserts her superiority over her students, and shows attitude. She grades harshly for no good reason. Avoid.

I genuinely cannot believe she has a job. Seriously, whoever at UO hired her should be fired immediately. She has no idea how the CHC is. Every single class she behaves as if she has no plan.  The class is based around these hypothetical research projects and no matter what she just cannot comprehend so many simple things about our projects.
She was rude to some students; her tech policy seems unnecessary. Basically do not take it if its not required.
Inspiring teacher. Gives pop quizzes but gives the questions in advance. I learned a lot.
I don't remember the course code, I sat in on a lecture for a few minutes, She is a really good professor in college, you might miss out on college without one of Professor Otis' course code.

Very nice and passionate about her work. Easy grader but you have to do the readings to get a good grade or understand what is going on. Half of the reading is very easy half is more dense/theory related. My course code is not accurate but I had her for Sociology of Gender
Very overbearing, and she never does any preparation for her class.
Disrespectful.
She is disorganized, disrespectful, and technologically inept. Honestly unbearable experience.

Professor Otis was extremely disorganized. There were no due dates on anything and the canvas page was a complete mess. I checked canvas multiple times daily and had an A throughout the whole term. When I viewed my final grade, I had a C+. I just dont understand how this could happen.

Professor Otis is an awful teacher. Clearly so disorganized that she was unable to transfer to online classes effectively. I was only graded on 5 quizzes and a midterm. One quiz had only one question. She barley taught anything, rather gave us two 20-40 page outdated articles to read weekly. Was inconsistent and did not communicate well. Horrible!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best profs ever- if you read the book and show up you'll pass (scored over 100% in the class and barely studied). she's interesting, passionate, and so so nice. she's willing to chat about anything & can admit mistakes. just take paper notes, not that hard. if you're respectful she will love you. pop quizzes are super easy. gr8 lectures.

She is paranoid, micromanaging, and rude. She is constantly looking for reasons to call someone out and is spiteful if she sees people leave class early she will pop quiz you. If you are on your lap top or phone she will call you out in front of the class. All grades are pop quizzes she drops the lowest & exams. Worst college prof ive had in 5 yrs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She reads straight off of her slides that she posts online. She spends minutes at the beginning of class making sure nobody has any laptops open, and if someone gets out a laptop in the middle of class, she will stop midsentence to tell them to put it away. It is distracting and her interruptions make me not want to show up to class.

Professor Otis is a remarkable Sociology professor who is energetic and enthusiastic about the material she teaches. She has extremely clear grading criteria and her class is transparent in terms of assignments. She provides access to all the readings reducing the need for a textbook. She does use pop quizzes to ensure students are reading. Great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Otis's lectures are pretty boring and she tries to hold discussions so there is a lot of wasted time and (long) unnecessary comments from students. For a class on the sociology of gender, her materials are very outdated. We read articles from the 90s that could definitely be updated.

Simple class, 4 quizzes lowest dropped. Midterm exam was all writing. Final essay 7-11 pgs and was pretty open topic. I'm surprised how much I liked this class and prof. She was straightforward and had good readings and videos to watch/talk about in class. If you do readings, ask questions and study for the midterm you'll be just fine. I recommend
Excellent prof. If you are interested in theory and willing to get into the text in a deep way this prof will really help you learn

Otis is an amazing professor! The only reason people don't like her is because she 'calls you out' for being on your phone or talking but notice thats only for 200 level courses. if you are a mature respectful student who pays attention you will be amazed at how helpful and enriching her course is. Definitely recommend her!
Very nice and helpful professor. Class was pretty straight forward; few quizzes, midterm and final. Although the midterm and final seemed easy her was a harsh grader. It's a do-able class if you try.
Great prof. Interesting lectures and good class discussion. She uses examples from China but also knows about the U.S. I'm going to try to take another class with her.

i feel like her lecture is pretty great, since she just doesnt just read the slide, but i cannot like her as a person. she spends too much time calling ppl out when they talk, on their phone, and i feel like she tries to make the test hard to get back on the ppl that leave early or dont go to the lecture.
I would not recommend taking any of her courses. She doesn't teach all that well and will call individuals out if they're on their phone/computer. She doesn't teach with any enthusiasm.
she teaches like a MS/HS teacher would. just does not work in college..

The class was fairly easy if you did the readings and went to discussion sections. The lectures were painful to attend. She spends WAY to much time calling individuals out for using phones or computers in class, and consider there are about 500 students in this class that can take up a lot of unnecessary time. Really annoying lectures.

Eileen Otis is an amazing professor.  I have never worked so hard in a class and I loved every minute of it.  Though she does impose rules against laptops and cellphones; this actually helped me take better notes and be engaged with the class.  I would definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in gender/sexuality, communism and China.

Weirdly controlling of a lecture hall for a university prof. Forgets what the heck she is talking about from derailing mid-sentence to stop cellphone/laptop use and/or make the GTFs scatter all about the room.  The GTFs were all very helpful and pleasant. Overall not a completely miserable class to take if you need a gen ed.

She teaches a borderline intro class as if it were a 400 level class. If you're looking for something easy DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!! She doesn't test you on the core concepts you learn in the class/readings (ie: marriage issues in US), she tests you on how well you memorize the readings (ie: who said some quote). She doesn't know how to teach.

She is a really great professor. Although she can be a little spacey she is very interested in the material and makes the topics interesting for the class. I will try and take any class she teaches from now on.
very helpful, but topic can be confusing at times, but test was easier than expected, no tricks.

AMAZING professor! I learned a lot more than I thought I would be able to. Very knowledgeable professor. I wish I could take another course with her. Would suggest her to anyone. Topic was very amusing as well.
exceelent prof. I want to take another class with her.
Great class discussions. Some readings are hard but she explains them clearly in class. She loves what she teaches and she speaks Chinese!
I took this class because it fit into my schedule but ended up really fascinated by China. Prof. is clear, interesting, dry at times, but funny at others. She's really nice in office hours.
Full of herself and acts like a dumb blond. She also can't control the class - one student never stops interrupting.

Global Ethnography is a Great class, you got to put everything you have learned in SOC classes to use. Attendance is not mandatory, but she does randomly collect reading questions. Prof Otis is a fair grader as long as you do your work. I would take another class from her.

If you need to take Spanish for any credit I couldn't recommend taking it with Professor Ellister enough. Not only is she so good at teaching and making a classroom feel like a safe place for all, but I have yet to meet a Professor in college who cares about her students mental health and success whole-heartedly the way she does. 10/10 no notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was initially going for a B.S. because I wanted to avoid the language courses. Paula is the entire reason I switched to a B.A.! She not only is a great instructor that really takes her time to help you understand, but she is generally just a warm and caring person. If you're nervous to start learning Spanish, I could not recommend her enough.

Paula is absolutely the best Spanish prof at the UO. She does a fantastic job teaching for people who have little to no spanish experience. Super understanding and helpful, always good with office hours. Reasonable grader and does a good job preparing students for tests.

She really cares about her students and provides great feedback when you attend office hours. Attendance is mandatory, and she is not very lenient even if you're sick. I was told to come and sick in the corner if I felt too sick to participate. She is a nice professor if you need to take spanish

I've taken her SPAN 101 + 102 class so far and am making my Spring Term schedule around being in her SPAN 103 class. I'm choosing to take a 9:00am class with her because she is such a good teacher. You can tell that she is passionate and she truly cares about her student's success. The class isn't too hard if you show up and participate.
Paula is one of the best professors at UO. She really cares about her students. She goes over the exams before they are taken. And she gives good feedback for other assignments.
She was amazing, basically, my campus mom helped out a lot and really helped me just to be a first year, she gives lots of feedback and is really just an amazing person.
I love Paula! She is amazing and I actually learned so much in her classes! Definitely recommend!!!!

Best Spanish teacher I've ever had! She really cares about her students, I've taken plenty of Spanish classes in the past and picked up little to nothing. But within just a few weeks in her class I learned so much!

Paula is the best Spanish teacher Ive ever had and maybe even the best teacher overall. You can tell she teaches because shes passionate and she really cares about the students. She is amazing. You have to take her for span 101-103
She is amazing I 100% recommend her she is the best. Class is not too hard, there are breakout groups every class and a partner activity every week, other than that the course is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Paula was a great teacher, I wouldn't want to take SPAN101 with anyone else. She's very helpful, and she provides a comfortable environment to learn a new language.

She is amazing. She is really supportive of your situation if there is an issue and you bring it to her attention immediately. She works hard to help her students understand Spanish. I wish she taught the 200 classes.
She's great, super helpful and gives tons of feedback. Had her for two consecutive terms and plan to take her class again for 3rd year.
I absolutely loved Paula. She is an amazing professor who actually cares about her students. I would take her class again in a heartbeat. If you are taking Spanish 101, take it with her.
Wonderful professor and hilarious at times. Class has good demos as well which go hand in hand with topics. Sometimes he would be a bit difficult to understand but other than that a good professor.
He was very funny and interactive. Class is hard but I mean it's Physics. I would definitely take his course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great prof. His sense of humor was awesome! The homework was extremely hard but so is the content. Tests were fair. He does a quiz before the tests that don't count for much of your grade which can be a really good wake up call. Old school lectures, chalkboard and chalk, and reading. Also all grades are paper given, no grade book on canvas.

Van Enk as a person is amazing, but as a professor he was lackluster. He expected a bit too much of the class regarding mathematical ability and sometimes didn't explain concepts clearly enough.   The tests and quizzes were fair; however, the homework on quantum was too difficult, almost requiring to work in groups or go to office hours to do.

He's a really nice guy, however he's really soft spoken so if you sit in the back its difficult to hear him...if at all.  His tests and homework are curved, however they are extremely difficult.  A lot has to do with the wording of the questions and the extreme ambiguity of how it is asked.  Be prepared to visit his office a lot.

Nicest guy on the planet. His class was hard, but hey, quantum is no basket weaving. He has an open door office policy, which stands out amongst his peers (also, his intellectual ability stands out amongst his peers). Take his class. Work hard. Learn a ton.

He seems intimidating, but he is very kind.  He has a genuine desire to help, even those may be dragging behind.  He is neither condescending nor indifferent.  The U of O needs more professors of this caliber.
Very Clear, Great, but subtle sense of humor.  Good course layout.  Uses textbook only for homework and talks about concepts in class.
Great Professor. He really wants you to learn and he explains until you understand. Hilarious dry humor. Awesome accent.

Doesn't explain lecture material very well. Will repeat the same things during lecture for 30 minutes and then skip over other things. Foundation online project will wreck your grade. Stay away and take BA 101 with any other prof.
Good professor, not accessible outside of class. You'll be heavily graded on participation and online homework.

Terrible! He assigns a Foundation Capism business simulator as an individual project when it is clearly supposed to be a group assignment per the website and other students I've talked to. He never showed how to use one time in class. His jokes in class are often mean spirited and insensitive. No extra credit.  STAY AWAY!!!!!!!!!!
very boring would not reccomend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rude, he doesn't respect the diversity

He is condescending and doesn't show respect to the students. He likes to poke fun at your answers and if you ask a question he doesn't like he will call you out in front go the whole class. On the second midterm he said there would be nothing from the first half of the year but when I took it half of the test was from the first part of the year.

Engel makes it almost impossible to pass this class. The final is set up so about 3/4 of the class fails it and his tests are very hard. There is almost no time to answer iClicker questions and he doesn't explain anything. If you ask a question, he will call you stupid in front of the whole class. Avoid this class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He jumps at any possibility to embarrass his students and he's very rude. He won't help you, so don't even ask. His final is designed to fail you and his tests are very hard. He doesn't make study guides or anything so you're on your own guessing what will be on the test. The only simulation is very hard and poorly explained
