The online program was the biggest part of this class and was poorly incorporated in the curriculum a lot of outside resources are needed for this class. Do not count on him to help you.

I honestly hated this professor. He made inappropriate jokes and didn't seem to care about his students. He also refused to grade my final project because he accused me of not turning in my final assignment on time. He only reconsidered once I proved to him that I finished it on time.

I really hate this professor, you won't get helps from him and the tests are hard. want a curve? No, he won't do that. time for answering iclicker questions is short and questions are hard. it is hard to get an A in his class.
JUST DON'T!

TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Prof. Engel makes the class easy to understand and has a great sense on humor. He is the only teacher i have had at this school that really cares about his students. Tests are hard but don't carry much weight in the class.

I looked at ratemyprofessor first before signing up for the course and I was worried to take his class seeing the general negative responses, but I had to take it. Unfortunately they were right. The professor is very harsh, unclear, and doesn't give enough time to students to answer clicker questions. I wouldn't recommend him.

Not 100% sure if he is a bad teacher or he is stuck teaching a bad curriculum. BA 101 is all about the foundation simulation and not too much business. Everything is online except the two midterms which helps out a lot.

This guy is a terrible teacher. Jokes are rude and insensitive. The online business simulator is made for a team yet he gives it as an individual assignment. No help what so ever when your confused. No extra credit. Iclicker questions are way too fast to answer. STAY AWAY from this professor!

Professor Engel is very sarcastic and a little hard to handle at first. He won't help you but will give you resources where you can get help. Don't forget your iClicker--it's so important! He gives participation points but you can't get them all without an iClicker. He knows his stuff and teaches it fairly well. He tells some hilarious jokes.

Very funny, very sarcastic professor. H does not offer you help himself but will give you the resources to get help yourself. If you show up and pay attention, you'll pass. iClicker mandatory. Minimal Homework. All the notes, powerpoint presentations,  and the books are posted for us on blackboard.

I don't know what these other people are talking about, I thought professor Engel was awesome! Super old school dude, very blunt and humorous, and EXTREMELY clear with lecture and instructions. Definitely one of the more unique guys teaching at school, highly recommend.
talking aggressively and grade not fair after course evaluation . get rid of this professor!!!!

Hardheaded professor who likes to answer questions with questions and aggressively talks over students.  Fortunately there's not much homework and (for better or for worse) he teaches mostly out of the textbook.  Tests are slightly difficult but have a minor curve based on the class average.

HW/website is $100 you buy, the professor, can be rude, unreliable responding to emails/ goes too fast in lecture and has a thick Russian accent, and felt annoyned when I tried to explain to her about certain things. she accused me of cheating during a exam when I left for the bathroom for only 5 min, you need to ask and leave your phone in class.
Super sweet but very quiz and test heavy.

It costs $100 to access the homework. Prof. Kleshcheva often needed to be corrected on problems by students, and she explains things in a manner that is very hard to follow. The GEs are helpful if you have any questions. The material is mostly highschool-level, but I wouldn't take this class if you really struggle with math.

This is my third term with her as a professor because she teaches almost all of the lower level courses. She doesn't seem to know how to use the microphone correctly which makes her extremely hard to hear or understand. She also frequently makes mistakes while doing the lectures. There is also no tutors on campus that will understand the content.
It is a stereotypical math class. She is funny and personable with good lectures but its math and test heavy, so you have to put in effort to do well on tests.

This is the 2nd class I've taken with her, and the format is the same as math 105 -- 1 weekly worksheet (the GE does most of in discussion), 1-2 online hw assignments per week (lets you submit answers until it's right, if you're late, its easy to get an extension), 3 easy exams, and attendance gets you extra credit. She's also super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kleshcheva is a god. I can't express how much you should take her class. I've never met a math professor who arranged their class's assignments so that just showing up to class and literally doing the homework would get you over 100%. She even helped me when I couldn't get accommodations before the first exam. I love her, she's my fav
The lectures were nice, she walks through a lot of problems and explains them well so that when we get to our discussions it was easy to understand. Pretty good!

Elina was nice but explained things too fast to the point where the whole class was wondering where the numbers on the board came from. Seemingly simple concepts were incredibly hard to follow because of how they were explained (I am not a math person so this probably also had an effect) and most of the class failed the first exam.

She has a thick accent but it doesn't really get in the way of her explanations. I know a lot of people complain about it but her lectures are really helpful and she's not difficult to understand. There is a good amount of webassign but the worksheets are pretty easy. She drops the lowest exam grade and worksheet grade. It's an easy math course.
she doesn't answer questions in lecture very well and the tests are pretty hard

Her lectures are straightforward and the units are easy to learn. I have taken harder classes in on-level high school math. She has an accent but I have never felt as if I couldn't understand her. Her tests are not hard and the reviews are helpful. If you put in the effort, I don't see why you would have a difficult time in this class.
Does she know what she is talking about? No. She quite literally is reading off a script. Is she speaking English? I don't even know. But is she a G? Absolutely.

Found this course easy as 1-2 of the lowest scores in each category (homework/quizzes) were dropped. If you did better on your 3rd midterm the grade would replace the lowest of the other two. Elina was an okay prof but often made mistakes or was unclear in lectures. Overall, she was fairy good and the weekly quizzes and 3 midterms weren't too bad.
I will never be able to learn math under her teaching.

Quizzes done every week on Friday's on content that is not being taught in class the same week. It could be a quiz on chapter 7 Friday and the worksheet for chapter 8 due the same day. Lectures are not terribly boring but can be slightly redundant. She is a very nice lady but just structures the class poorly.

The course features two weekly online assignments (straightforward), lecture notes she goes through during class, and 3 tests throughout the term. The materials are clear, but the three tests greatly affect your grade. The instructor's heavy accent can make her difficult to understand at times. Overall, I recommend this course.

The class is good, found that the lectures helped a little bit with understanding but that may just be my point of view. Her lectures consist of just going through a worksheet and solving problems and you follow along, which I found beneficial but others might think differently.

Actually horrible. This is reflected by everyone in the class being confused and almost every single person scored below a 50 on the midterm. SWITCH IMMEDIATELY. She is impossible to follow along with and works so fast with absolutely no explanation. I don't know who is rating this class a 5 unless they are a math profesional because it is so hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was actually one of the best math classes I've taken. It was fairly easy and her lectures were easy to follow along with. Notes were posted after class. There was quite a bit of homework but I really enjoyed how everything was organized and structured. I never once went to a lab section and was still successful in the course.

Class is basically just based off the tests because worksheets and homework are a free 100. She is confusing to listen to because of her accent but if you take the time to study before the tests, they aren't that bad. She drops your lowest score of the two midterms and final so technically the final is optional if you do well on the two midterms.
Find a new math teacher ASAP! Her lectures are confusing and sometimes students would have to correct her that her work was wrong. I highly recommend NOT taking a course with Professor Kleshcheva.

avoid if possible. you will be teaching yourself and there are basically no resources to use for this math class. she gets confused and talks too fast and she can't answer your questions very well if at all. seems like a nice lady but she shouldn't teach this course. i earned my grade by myself because she offered little to no help.

Elina is great. She is very straightforward, writes out all of the notes with students during class, and offers 1 extra credit point for every lecture you attend. Those EC points are added to each exam. Always mentions to come to office hours and is good with emails. GE was not great at teaching, but overall easy A if you show up to class

most of lecture time is spent with her standing at the front confusing herself. she will do a problem, look at her notes, and realize she was wrong; this happens multiple times in class. talks fast and can be hard to understand but that's not the problem, it's the fact that she doesn't seem to know what she's doing and confuses everyone

Shes not even that bad of a professor, im just pissed because she wrote the study guide with the wrong answers on the back and it literally drove me insane. Spent 2 hours on the most basic question ever because the answer given was completely off and her explanation on the completed review guide was garbage and overly complex.

Her class makes no sense and I never understand what she is saying. She slows down and then speeds up really fast and just goes on making no sense. There's also no tutoring literally anywhere on campus for this class so you're just screwed. Don't recommend at all

The professor is great! There are two exams and one final, all carrying equal weight. Homework and quizzes are straightforward. Attendance isn't compulsory, but it offers a 5% extra credit, so attending is recommended. The final is online and open notes. Honestly, if you study for the exams, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kleshcheva is a wonderful professor, she really does care if you understand the material and encourages you to stay after class to ask questions. If you pay attention in the lectures, then the webworks and worksheets are going to be a cake walk. In my opinion, there wasn't much homework.

Professor Kelshcheva was amazing! She is very accessible outside of class. Attendance is not required but essential to doing well in the class, the textbook is confusing and off base from what we learn in class. She also gives out extra credit points from her attendance quizzes - I was able to add 5 points to my midterm score for going to class.

She sweet, but terrible and getting you prepared for exams. Homework and worksheets look nothing like exams. I only passed the class because I did all my homework on time and turned in my worksheets 100% accurate. I knew the material but the exams were brutal.

The only thing you need to know is that if you pay attention and study the notes, you will get A. Slacking off (like I did sometimes :) ) resulted in lower grades. Tests are like the lecture notes. There are also 3 exams not midterm or final. No cumulative tests yay! Sometimes she makes mistakes or mixes herself up but other than that she is fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Kleshcheva was really good for math 101. It was mostly a review from algebra in high school. She's very relaxed with due dates and quick to give grace on late assignments which is awesome. Easy to get a good grade if you put in any amount of work.

i literally loved this prof so much. she made herself super flexible and accessible to students, so if ur feeling confused at any point go to office hours. she really cares about her students and also really wants to make sure you understand. be sure to communicate with her if you need anything. she was great with explaining and answering questions

I had to drop her class because I was taking too many credits but she is by far one of the best math teachers I've ever had. She's very caring and understanding when it comes to missing class or assignments. I would 100% take her class again
Do your work and just ask for help and this class will be really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Elina is an absolute queen. I went to a solid 6 lectures and always attended the lecture right before a midterm. Easy A just do the worksheets and the midterm/final review like 3 times and the test is EXACTLY the same. She averaged our midterm grades and did not make us take the final. The best, love her.

Really sweet, kind, and understanding lady. Will assign a worksheet and projects which she will try her best to help you with if needed! There are quizzes every week as well. She has a bit of an accent but as long as you are following along it shouldnt be an issue. She also tells you when assinments are due which shos how mch she wnts u to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Elina is a very helpful professor. Her notes are easy to follow, especially if they are printed out. There are worksheets and webwork every week that are relatively easy to complete. The quizzes and tests are exactly like the homework. She is also extremely considerate and tries to make the course work for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Klescheva was a great professor for Math 111. She has a slight accent but I had absolutely no trouble understanding what she was saying. The level of challenge in this course is not terribly hard as long as you do your homework on time. Webwork is the worst but that isn't Klescheva's choice. Do your homework, use the math tutors, and it's not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Tech is not her strong suit, very nice and caring, very accessible, will answer any questions right away, will have a weekly group worksheet as well as a weekly quiz, great beginning level teacher.

I dont know if online teaching isn't her thing, but this class wasn' great. I expressed my concerns to her about due dates when I was sick, and she said I could turn assignments in for half credit. No one in the class finished the midterms and the average score was around 60%, which she refused to curve. Didn' seem like she cared about her students

She was absolutely awful for the online class this year she didnt know how to teach and would get confused by what she was doing herself. She is also hard to understand with her heavy accent. No one bothered going to her lectures anymore because she didnt teach us anything so we taught ourselves. If math isnt your best subject dont take her!!

I took this class to get acclimated with school after gap year. This class relies heavily on a computer program called ALEKS and if utilized to its fullest capacity (take notes from it!!), this class is easy. The course itself is pretty straight forward and the professor is very accessible outside of class. Usually very accommodating with appts.

She was great at giving examples and explaining concepts in detail. She also has office hours almost every day which is really helpful. If you pay attention in class and do the homework, it won't be hard to pass.

Elina is the best instructor I have ver had! She honesty cares so much about her students passing the class and it is the sweetest thing! She does have an accent that is a little hard to understand, but after like the third class it is very easy to understand what she is saying. She is very quick to respond to any questions and is so helpful!
Pretty good teacher. Her accent is a little difficult to understand but I would say as long as you do your work and go to class, you'll learn the material and do just fine.

WOW BAD CLASS! Last class for my math requirement. Calc was easier. She says attendance is for extra credit but if you dont show up she takes the points off your exam. Wouldn't recommend her as a teacher I learned so much more from my GTF who actually had office hours.

She was terrible. Worst professor I have had. Her accent is hard to understand and she always looks confused. If you can find another professor teaching the same course as her, I highly recommend that you get anybody but her.

AWFULLL! the worst class you will l ever take. you cant understand a word she says, she faces the board the whole time and makes about 10 mistakes every class.  in a lecture class of about 80-90 only about 20 people would ever show up.  its ridiculous. DO NOT TAKE IT, do a BA if you can
Good Teacher. Although kind of difficult to understand with her accent. Uses good examples during teaches, quizzes and tests are easy if you go to classes and get help if needed.
AMAZING!!
Awesome teacher, i hate math and shes the best I've ever had. She really needs to teach upper level so I can pass others.

I'm not sure what the previous rating was talking about. I never felt that Lima belittled me when I asked questions in class. On the contrary, he takes pains to thoroughly explain and go over class papers days before they are due, is more than willing to field questions after class, and genuinely helps students write better.Not easy, but worthwhile

He is a fantastic teacher. He expects what a professor should expect from an upper-division English course. Your writing will improve. He takes your ideas seriously instead of just smiling and nodding, and that makes me respect him a lot.

I enjoyed this class, though at first I thought I wouldn't. He grades hard on the first paper but if you are willing to work for your grade, he will help you. Very useful if you go to office hours. He wants his students to do well, which is a nice change from some of the professors I've had. He makes a somewhat dull subject pretty interesting.

Very awkward and uncomfortable in class and in person, but a ridiculously hard grader. Picks his favorites in the term early. He said that most of the class (mostly senior ENG majors) that we all needed to get tutors and learn how to write. Really, Enrique? After four years of English classes we still don't know how to write? AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

Great professor, though not recommended for non majors. This is challenging, college level stuff, and he grades accordingly, but it's well worth going through the rigors if you're interested in novels (and I am). Also, he has awesome taste in music (Tom Waits' Singapore to describe Melville's nautical themes...perfect) and a great sense of style.
No Comments
Definitely a tough grader. There's a lot of reading and it gets difficult to stay up with, but you got to in order to pass his pop quizes. Nice guy, but he expects a lot from papers.

Engelking's lectures are difficult to get through, especially if a monotonous voice makes you sleepy. The only bright point in lecture is the occasional dirty joke he slips through the boring stuff- they're totally unexpected and kinda hilarious.
The epitome of awful.

Physical chemistry is very difficult material, but Prof. Engelking does a good job teaching it. You can tell in lecture that he is very knowledgeable. Going to lecture and office hours are key to getting a good grade. The class average on his tests are low, but it is to get you to study harder. He also curves the heck out of the class.

Do not take a class with him. He does not explain the material well at all and his power points are pointless. He is the worst Chemistry teacher I have ever had and I would not recommend him to anyone.

Do not take a class with him if you don't have to. I learned everything from the text book and only earned about 15/75 points on the first midterm because it was that ridiculous. He gave us no class average and is more interested in the history of the material than the material itself.

I absolutely despised all of his tests and quizzes. He really didn't explain the material well. This is a self-learning class. I went to every class session but didn't end up learning much. I learned more from reading the book, then I did from him. If possible, don't take his class.

Awful teacher. Doesn't explain anything well. He's more concerned about the history of chemistry rather than the actual concepts. You can't understand him, his power points are useless, and you can learn more from the book. I didn't go to class half the time and the only reason I passed was because I took AP Chemistry in high school. Avoid him.
If you are good at learning in your own you will be fine. Don't waste your time going to class though, he is a horrible teacher.
avoid this guy at all costs. He's difficult to understand and he doesn't know how to teach. The book will teach you more than he ever will

More often than not, it felt as though I was expected to 'beat' his tests than display what knowledge I'd attained through taking the course. Attending lecture is useless as he simply goes over the textbook chapters via powerpoint. Do yourself a favor and read the chapters thoroughly before tests instead of going to lecture.
He cares more about the history of chemistry and comics than his actual lectures. If at all possible, I would NOT sign up for his class.

I would recommened NOT taking this teacher. You have to sit in the front to even hear him. Plus he rambles about nothing that has to do with our quiz or hmwk. The hmwk are much harder than anything he goes over in class. And the quizzes and tests are unfamiliar territory that are short, so if you miss one your screwed. Not helpful at all.
This guy needs to get a reality check. We are freshmen, not chemists at NASA. Give us a break big guy. Plus he needs to get a new mic. Because the one he has makes him mumble, not talk louder.
Awful, just awful

This guy needs to be filmed for one of his lectures and then go back and watch how he teaches. He doesn't know what the h**l he is saying have of the time and talks to the screen (not the 500 people in the class). He might be better for a class of 20, actually 15 people with a small room. Really wanted to take this class and he made me regret it.

Very nice person, but not very engaging as a teacher. It is my own fault I failed this class; it requires a lot of studying if you do not have a strong background in chem. There is an on-line homework portion which did not seem to synch with the lectures, the tests get progressively hader. I dont want to bash him, he is a nice guy.
TERRIBLE TERRIBLE TEACHING STYLE. FAILING HIS CLASS. SO BORING!! DONT TAKE HIS CLASS.

I feel like part of the reason I am failing this class is because of Paul. I put the time in and can do the HW no problem, but when it comes to exams and quizzes expect to be bombarded with stuff that was never introduced in class or the book. YouTube tutorials were my best friend in this class and w/o I wouldn't get these concepts

One word to describe his class... ridiculous. Doesn't care about his students. Thinks that the topics that he teaches are "basic concepts". He is an intellegant guy, but he cannot teach. He has such a deep voice and mumbles so badly that you can't understand him which makes lectures useless.DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY!

Let me put it this way: He gives you a quiz and demands you to do outstanding work on it because he spent 35+ years working in a laboratory. Oh, and he didn't teach you everything in the chapter. So you're supposed to take a quiz that is incredibly hard and he hasn't taught you anything about it. He expects too much from a 221 class.

Dear UO student looking to see ratings, Engelking is HORRIBLE! seriously.. i got an online tutor because he sucked so bad at teaching. everything about him and the class is useless for students' benefit. 2 words: AVOID HIM!!!!

Alright...just had him in chemistry... I learned more from my book than he ever taught...(which isn't hard to do since he doesn't teach a thing in class). I emailed him and he ALWAYS replied with a smart a** remark making me feel like an idiot. I dont understand how such a good university allows such a thing. He needs to be fired asap.
He is... soo... boring. He's not meant to teach. He's meant to be a scientist in his little desk. but not in front of 300 kids. he needs to do us all a favor and quit.
HORRIBLE!I studied for hours and hours for all the exams. NOTHING from lectures was included. Avoid like the Plague!
would not recommend. enough said.

Was a very discouraging teacher. He wasn't concerned about the needs of his students and didn't try to help them learn. He made a poor choice of making rude and inappropriate comments to me. He expects you to mostly learn from the text and not as much from his teaching. I would highly recommend a different teacher or having a tutor if you have him.

This professor is nice although like other comments for raging on those"{first year" students with "poor" work ethics  i would like to say some people aren't that good at chem and probably haven't taken a chem class since their earlier years of high school and join his class to brush up on things they might have forgotten just avoid this teacher.
boring...so boring... i learned about...NOTHING from him.
Such a boring Prof

Unlike many of the first-year students posting here just to complain, I actually put effort into this class. Although I will probably get an A, I don't think Engelking is a good professor. He's nice, but he does a poor job of explaining the material. Spends too much time talking about history of chem. Homework isn't mandatory, so I wasn't motivated

Nice teacher---difficult subject. I am not good at Chemistry, so I may be biased, but his teaching style hasn't worked for me. But I'm sure if I might with him and asked him for help he would give it to me. He is a very nice professor.

Great professor, the problem with most of the people posting here is that they are fresman and don't even know how to study, or use the book, and are just really good at complaing. He is very good for Quantum Chemistry and went to CAl TECH so he knows his stuff really well and is very helpful when you ask.

He doesn't know how to relate to his students well unless you ask questions.  He teaches everything that is needed, but students stopped coming to class because he's so boring.  One day he spent 30 minutes talking about pirates.  I'm not kidding.

Prof. Engelking is one of the most enthusiastic, good-natured, and genuinely caring instructors I've ever had. Negative ratings are from first-year students that were too arrogant to take the class seriously. They should blame their poor work ethic--not Paul's style of teaching--for their lack of success.
Avoid this guy at all costs! He made my high school chem. teacher look like a God. He is incompitent when it comes to explaining concepts to struggling students. Trust me, just stay away.
Worst teacher

Class average on 2nd midterm: 52%. My guess is that this is probably due to the fact that we were taught material that related to 9 of the 20 questions the day before the midterm. As someone said above, this guy sucks and he's probably going nowhere since he's on tenure.

Wow, I never knew I would learn about pirates in chemistry class. Unfortunately, for the half hour that we had to listen about this in class, there were no questions on the midterm on pirates. Wierd. Nice guy with really bad jokes. Needs to retire SOON!

I'm a sixth year student on a full acedemic scholarship and I've maintained a 4.0+ gpa through many good and bad instructors, so I know what I am talking about here!  This guy is the most inferior professor I have ever had.  Class time is grossly misappropriated, and lectures are absolutely useless.  Boycott Engleking by all means neccessary!!!!!!!

This guy blows. Not only his jokes suck, but he takes all the class time to try and get his punch lines out that don't make sense anyways. Save time by just reading the book since all he does is photocopy its pages for lecture. I've heard good things about Exton though!

Emily is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She's extremely sweet and cares about her students deeply. Her class was a great mix of practice simulation negotiations and short lectures, which made the time go by quickly. Rubrics were straightforward. Highly recommend!

Emily is very nice, and the material is interesting. Grading and feedback are a disaster, though. Feedback is maybe 1-2 sentences, and nothing actionable. Her rubrics are also odd--you can only get 0, 5, 8, or 10/10. If there was more feedback available (even if you go to talk to her), it would be a much better class.

Emily is an awesome professor. We run in-class simulations of various negotiations throughout the term, and they are extremely practical and useful lessons. She cares a ton about her students, wants everyone to do well, and offers lots of support. BA365 is also just one of the more useful classes I've ever taken at UO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Such a kind person and an amazing lecturer. The material was awesome and I left the class knowing I  gained a lot out of it. The hardest project in the course will be the Memo so make sure to build a strong connection with your group. As for the midterms they are pretty easy and intuitive if you do the readings, which aren't too hard.
The women is wicked smart first off and a great caring teacher. Not only did I actually learn, but the class itself was super fun. She's a wonderful teacher learned a lot would recommend taking!

I love Emily! This class is amazing to begin with, but her lectures are amazing. It's a very interactive class, but she won't call on you unannounced. Most of the concepts are easily digestible + the homework and exams are super easy. I definitely recommend!

Emily is a great professor, there is basically no way to easily get an A, that is just not how the course is structured. She responds extremely quick, she knows what she is doing and knows how to teach and make students better. She does NOT grade off of effort, only if it is what she asks for.

One of the most frustrating professors I have ever had! She provided no guidance with her feedback, and there was inconsistency in what she expected for assignments leading to inconsistencies with grading. Most of the assignments were not explained clearly, which does not set anyone up for success. I'm appalled by the 5.0 rating, don't believe it.

BA308 is one of my favorite classes I have taken so far in college. Not only did I enjoy the content of this course, but I truly enjoyed the way that Emily taught us. She taught us how to work with others effectively and how to become a stronger leader. I will use what I learned in this class for the rest of my life! Emily is the best!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had! She cares that you learn, so she grades tough, but fair. Everything she does has a purpose and she pushes you to become a better student and person overall. I learned MANY incredibly valuable skills. She is always willing to provide help as much as she can. Truly talented teacher- I couldn't recommend her enough!!
weekly writing, multiple quizzes and assignments but you get to do assignments in class. emily is also always willing to help. super dope and easy class to learn about sustainable business
Shes great
Emily is an amazing professor who cares about the success of her students. She purposefully makes the class pretty easy so that we aren't worried about grades but rather learning. I love her!!

She is very accessible after class and really helps with the group projects. The beginning of the classes is mainly reading and quizzes. The last portion is all on the final project. If you need help with understanding the projects assignments just ask her and she will give you hints to help guide you to what she's looking for.
Best class ive taken in college. She cares, she wants to see you get better, I think the class is overall hard grading but it is so valuable. I learned so many skills.

This is for BA 250 (Sustainable business) NOT BA 308; anyways she was an amazing teacher who was very easy to get along with. The quiz, midterm, and final answers were all on quizlet I stopped reading the text book after week 3 and was one of the easiest A's I have ever had.

Emily is one of the best professors I've ever had. She is genuinely supportive and cares that you learn something above all else. This does mean that getting an A is tough, you have to really show what you've learned. However, it's one of those classes that I took away so much from the course than a B+ was okay with me.
Emily is a great professor, but some of the assignments that she assigned are not clear. GO TO OFFICE HOURS you will do so much better if you attend office hours. Overall, great class!
Emily is unbelievably supportive and willing to help. She gives great feedback, and genuinely cares about her students. You will never regret taking a class with her.

One of the best teachers I have ever had at the university. She is super sweet, engaging, and fun and class never drags on. The class is pretty reading heavy, but the book content is digestable and really interesting, never dated or irrelevant. As long as you do the readings and participate in class you will for sure get an A. Love Emalydia.
Amazing teacher, couldn't be nicer and definitely knows what she's talking about

Overall she was an excellent instructor for this course. Her engagement during the course was good and she provided great feedback on assignments, I definitely think that this course helped make me a better writer. She was also very flexible about what you could write about for the most part and flexible/understanding with due dates and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shows that she cares about her students. Actively asking if we're doing okay and gives good feedback
I love Emalydia Flenory. She is so sweet and cares about the mental health of her students puts us on her level. Wish I could be best friends with her.

Emalydia was a FANTASTIC writing professor! Her WR 122 class was focused on Blackness and anti-Blackness in popular media. Her lectures are short and sweet, and work consists of two main papers (midterm and final) as well as some discussion prompts throughout the weeks. Emalydia truly cares about her students, would 100% take her class again.

You can tell she cares about the ARC but expects us to already know about the science parts of our field when we are just freshman. I recommend the ARC because you can make good connections but expect to be confused during the final group project because there is little guidance and the expectation feels like we write like scientists already.
I love Dr. Sylwestrak, she is very intelligent and approachable.

Its a pass fail arc, tho its the first year of it and its expected to not have all the kinks worked out; its not that great. It may be the women in science and MATH arc, she only talks about science things. The final project was really confusing and we had to work in a GROUP project over thanksgiving break.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Neurobio of Motivation & Addiction was really great! Dr. Sylwestrak breaks down the class so that you have a bit of a project to work on every week, and there's no busy work. We had 2 group presentations and a 1-page proposal, which seemed daunting at first but everything was very doable. The class was also very interesting and content was cool.

She is very sweet and I appreciate how she took the time to learn all of our names. I didn't like the class structure - it is very lecture-heavy even though it is a small class and was hard to pay attention. The homework sets are designed to be harder than the quizzes/exams so often I couldn't complete them and they didn't help prepare for tests.

Really nice teacher and going to office hours really helped me a lot but during lectures she often has mistakes explaining things and has mistaken quiz questions and often teaches like you already were taught calculus so people that haven't took it in high school feel behind as they step into class on the first day.

Very nice, but she expects everyone to come in with prior knowledge. 2 homework a week 3-4 days to do it, quiz every Wednesday 1-2 problems, 2 midterm and final. SHE POSTS NOTES ON CANVAS, very helpful, her office hours were during other classes of mine but I heard they were pretty good. Recommend her but study a bit before taking class and during.

She is a very sweet prof & understanding, but teaches in a way as if you already know the material. You can get a C+ or better as long as you put in the effort outside of class, that is expect to need tutoring and study for hoursss for the exams if you do not already have extensive knowledge in calc. Also the homework questions are horrific btw.

Dr. McGovern is very sweet. She moves at a quicker pace, which may make her less ideal for some students. She is thorough and provides lots of examples. This class will not be the easiest class you take, but if you put in the effort, you will learn. She is available after class and truly does care about mathematics and her students.

She was very nice, but it was a bit confusing. She moves fast and makes pretty frequent typos/ errors on quizzes, but writes on a whiteboard the intended problem and will usually grade lighter when she makes an error on a weekly quiz. Homework is really easy and her practice exams are easier than the exams a little bit. Good choice, but moves fast.

McGovern is very clearly passionate about math, but lectures can be a bit confusing at times. She is always available for clarifications and super helpful as a resource, though. She makes a couple mistakes on HW and quizzes, but no more than the other math profs I've had at UO. Very nice and reasonable.

As someone who has already taken this class in high school, she makes me feel like I don't understand the math because of the way she describes things. Her writing on tests is really confusing and she has made a mistake on each one :C I highly don't recommend
She doesn't teach she just give examples and expects you to connect the dots on your own. she doesn't know the material.

I do honestly dread this class every day. The drawn out "lectures" by Professor Scott are really more of long rants than anything else. I don't think she is at all passionate about teaching, and that's obvious. Only way to survive and get a good grade is to be SELF sufficient and REALLY take advantage of the cheat sheets for the midterm and final!!

For a prof who complains over lack of time each class, she sure indulges in anecdotal name-dropping to the point of exhausting irrelevancy without fail

talks about how lectures are so important but then just talks about the readings the whole time with random photos on the slides instead of words. you can skip all the lectures and still get a good grade in the class as long as you do the readings

I did not find the lectures beneficial to my learning, as Scott repeated the content I learned about in the assigned texts.

On the other hand, I loved the assigned articles and videos. As someone who cares about the environment and wants a career surrounding this, this class made me more aware of topics that I was unaware of.

reviews.comment: Prof Scott is a cool & intellectual person, but in my opinion, an awful professor. I worked very hard to meet requirements and the midterm & final were still extremely difficult. reviews.comment: Gets mad when people walk out of lectures early but her lectures regularly run several minutes late. I show up on time it's disrespectful to keep talking past time then get mad when I leave because I have other obligations

She says she is making all future tests pencil and paper because she caught people using AI this term... Also lecture slides have no words and the lectures are purely based off of readings. Very reading heavy class.

reviews.comment: Overall an ok class. Lectures hard to take notes on because they didn't have any words on the slides. The exams cover the readings, so stay on top of them. Open note/remote exams. She is passionate about the subject but it can be hard to stay engaged in classes sometimes. Also there are lots of extra credit opportunities to boost your grade.

The lecture slides had no words. Very hard to take notes in class. The course content was based on weekly readings. The Midterm was based on the readings. The Final was based on the readings. All open note and timed. So be familiar with the readings. It was a decent class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Evident she's not trained as a teacher. Hard to catch up if you miss a class because the content is all lectures and none of it is recorded/written down. Lots of reading before every class. On the bright side, exams are remote and open note. There are some essays but no rubric for the grading so you're going in blind. Repetitive content

Throughout the term there was pretty substantial reading but some documentaries/ videos were sprinkled in as well which was nice. If you dont do the readings you will definitely not pass the course. Extra credit was offered and you could earn up to 5 points! I passed the class with a %100.37. Honestly an easy A if you do the readings and show up!

I learned A LOT in this class and the TA's graded everything so I got an A. However! Make sure you read the materials otherwise you will struggle. And there is a crap ton of reading, definitely more than a 200 lvl course load. about 6 rin depth readings/ week (about 10 pgs long on avg). She provided all material. Attendance is mandatory
