reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor at Oregon. A lot of redundant class policies like having to check in (for an online class!) or having to go to a testing center. There are over 100 formulas or models to memorize and she doesn't do a very good job with helping us understand the,.

Emily was an amazing instructor if you are good at picking up hard topics quickly. She covers a lot of content pretty fast, and Econ is already pretty hard for some people, so her class is not for everyone. Lots of extra credit, and exams only had content she covered in lectures so no problem, but TAKE NOTES she has you memorize 50,000 equations.
She does not do a good job explaining the basic concepts. Be prepared to read the textbook and study on your own!

She tries to be very nice but the class is online so she fails badly. She may be a better teacher if you take her in person but definitely not online. Basically had to self teach everything cuz she is not good at explaining things.
Emily is really nice. She is willing to meet outside of class and help you whenever you need help. Assignments looked hard, but actually really easy if you attended lecture. 100% would recommend

Emily is awesome! She responded to my emails over the weekend, and was willing to meet with me outside of her office hours. The material is challenging, but she provides a lot of opportunities for low stakes homework. Her twice weekly announcements help keep me on track and clearly outlined what was expected of me.

DO NOT TAKE ECON 202 ASYNC
- 4 hour long lectures and in person tests
- not understanding, doesn't accept late work or respond to emails
- huge project with not a lot of instructions

She is very clear with her expectations and grades fairly. I would often attend her office hours that she regularly offers. She is very helpful and caring. Weekly quizzes but they are take-home! No problem getting an A in this class if you show up and submit your work. 10/10 would take again

Em was a great lecturer. Although attendance isn't mandatory, I would recommend attending class as they don't included all content on the lecture slides that are uploaded to Canvas. It was nice to be able to work at my own pace throughout this course, but required more work on my end. Highly recommend Em!

Professor Beecher is very knowledgeable, relatable, and cares a lot about their students. Lectures are interesting, representative, and engaging, utilizing a wide range of material from various sources. Grades are point based with no set due dates so prioritizing time is important to be successful. I would definitely take this class again.

I had her during Fall 2022. Em is very nice and cares deeply about their topic. In order to receive an A in the class you just had to reach 200 credits by doing whatever work you want at any time. There were many optional assignments to do to reach 200 plus a weekly required assignment. However they took way too long to grade without a clear rubric

Funny professor, attendance not mandatory but sometimes she gives quizzes in class which you need to be there for. Readings can be moderately long and lectures can be a little boring but easy content in general.
Great sense of humor and interesting lectures. The reading amount can get a little heavy, but it is manageable.

Prof Epstein was fine at the beginning of the term until the midterm paper she commented saying that I prob don't show up to class, which I confronted her about because I did show up to class. Overall, her lectures are long and boring, and tough grader for a 100s level course. Don't expect to get an A for this class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tough grader--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is one of the meanest, least caring professors you will experience at the U of O. She does not allow any makeup credit what-so-ever. I had a family member die and had to fly home for the funeral and she refused to work with me about extending the deadline. She responded with a one sentence email that just said "sorry, it's too late"
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: SHE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT THE UNIVERSITY OF OREGON!

Prof. Epstein is my favorite professor at UO. She is a teacher who cares for her students and the importance of learning. She is easily accessible to discuss grades and improvements.  If you do the readings and come to class ready to discuss with questions you will do well in this course. Also must be ready to do critical reading and responses.

Great professor, interesting class. Leave me inspired every time. The workload is a bit more than other class, but finish reading and homework will help you more engaged in the class discussion so that you can get something out of it. I would recommend this class to my friend who need to take a literature class.

A lot of these reviews are from his grad students, but Professor Epps is an incredible, funny, and engaging teacher to have in undergrad! He truly cares about all of his students, and that's why he pushes you! There is def a lot of reading so do it to contribute to class discussions (half of the class time is typically allotted towards discussion).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Epps is the best professor I have taken at the UO. He is smart, caring for his students, and passionate about law. I recommend this class to anyone who needs a legal studies class or just an interesting class with a great teacher. You are graded on 3 tests, but he curves the grade (i got a 66% on quiz 1 which is a B in his class)!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is overall a nice guy but I couldn't stand his teaching style. His lectures were just him going on tangent after tangent and the things he would talk about wouldn't really be on the tests that you had and they were incredibly boring. There were only three things you are graded on, two 10-point tests and a 5-8 page essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Epps has a kind soul and lots of education about constitutional law. You are only graded off of 2 multiple choice quizzes that are 10 questions long and a 5-8 page essay. The multiple choice were difficult but he curves them well. His lectures are interesting and he is very passionate about what he teaches. One of my favorite classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is extremely intelligent and a little arrogant because of it.  However, he is passionate about Constitutional Law and it rubbed off on me.  Some of the hardest tests I ever had in Law School, but never unfair or hiding the ball.  5 years removed from law school I use many of the things I learned under his guidance.

BEWARE of his multi choice qs. Ridiculously unclear and he bases 50% of your grade on two 7-10 question quizzes. He is not helpful in office hours, teaches via supplements. He is a very smart man but has NO IDEA how to teach his students what he knows. Buy a supplement (or three) and you may get a decent grade.
love love love
didn't buy the "my dog ate my homework" bit.
If you're as interested in Garrett Epps as he is in himself, this is the class for you.

He knows lots, talks in circles. Exams were totally 100% fair, no hiding the ball, which is more than I can say for some other profs.  Did a good job of guiding the class through some challenging topics.
No Comments
Oh the stories he can and will tell.  He is fascinating to watch, but when it comes to the test General Lee and Boss Hogg aren't on the exam!

I went from liking Spanish to dreading it after this teacher.  Took 2nd year a year delayed because of her aggressive, intimidating behavior.  She punishes the entire class when one student errs.  1st year all A's.  Withdrew after her, all B's 2nd year due to residual stress from her class.  I don't know if I want to speak Spanish now due to her.

people who know a good amount of Spanish will survive while all the other people die&burn. you need to know a fair amount of Spanish because she will never help you or explain anything to you in English.. well, she can't. But if you know Spanish pretty well, go for it, it's boring but not too hard. I remember I got a lot of 100%s in that class. why

If you value your grade this is not the professor for you.  She is unable to speak comprehensible english and often refuses to speak to you in anything other than spanish. Makes it VERY difficult to clarify and understand grades. Recommended: Michael Gray, or Jaime Pena
Sooo cute and sweet! Love her!

She was such incomprehendable person who barely speaks english that I had to drop the class one week end.  I never understood a word she said in english or spanish.  Her english was absolutley terrible and she should not be teaching this class until she can learn to clarify important things in English and become helpful and actually do her job.
I used to love spanish, but now I put off the homework and don't look foward going to this class. It is hard to understand during lecture and there isn't much help either.

She is a very inteligent woman, but she doesn't know how to pass it on to others. I like the fact that Spanish is used in class, to make us try to speak it better, but she barely understands English. It's a little difficult to get directions sometimes. It's dificult to explain to her that she  misplaced your assignment, even you have witnesses.
She doesn't understand english very well so it was very hard for her to explain to us if we didnt understand in Spanish. She also talks too fast sometimes while speaking.

She is completely unintelligible. Thick accent, little to no knowledge of English. Makes communication on important or unclear issues very difficult. Had her at 8am which made it even worse. If you don't mind teaching yourself spanish out of the book go for it. Don't expect to learn anything from her... her test grading is relatively easy however.

I couldn't really understand her accent a lot of the time. I kind of hate the way language classes are taught at the U of O. You basically just sit there for an hour just listening to the teacher go on and on in another language 4 times a week.

She is the worst language teacher I've ever had. I enjoyed studying spanish before, but now I'm beginning to wonder if I want to continue taking spanish classes. Some of the bad points: confusing explanation, no feedback on writing assignments, threatening, no preparation, lack of spanish grammar knowledge, etc.
Not good but easy grader
He mispronounced my name during graduation and laughed about it on stage.
He's not really good at teaching. He lacks the depth of material and a lot of the material is self study because he isn't able to teach competently.
He's one of the best for CS. cool guy and class is super easy

Very funny professor! Mandatory attendance but the way he teaches is fun. There's occasional moments where he asks you to talk to a neighbor but that's all the interaction you have to do. IMPORTANT: he provides a practice exam on Canvas, so you can take it as much as you want to practice (just because he does this, it helps for the actual exam)

Eric is a really cool guy, great professor too. My biggest thing is that he is super harsh with grading for no reason whatsoever, he refused to round a lot of people's grades who were within 1% of a higher grade for absolutely no reason. Overall, a great professor and you'll learn a lot from him if you listen

Solid professor and has a cool/funny personality. The course, lectures, and his slides were organized really well, and expectations were clear. Tests were moderately but not unfairly difficult. Programming assignments and labs were relevant and helpful. Better than most professors in the CS department, take him if you can!
Easy class but has a fake personality

Good guy, makes class entertaining but can ramble on sometimes. Some of the coding assignments took a while, but were never too difficult. Tests were decently hard but he made studying for them super easy. Good class

Very nice guy and easy grader; gave good prep for the midterm and final and dropped the lowest of 8 assignments. GE for my class (Andrew Teske) made a lot more sense to me than Eric did, however, so highly recommended that you attend lab in person. Records all lectures and posts slides in advance.
i love this guy. had him for 314 and 410 this year and it was awesome, such an incredibly chill and awesome dude

One of the best professors within the CS department. He's a big reason why the program is on track to be better aligned with industry standards. With 314's current format proof of this. Great lectures that teach difficult but extremely useful concepts in an approachable way. Projects align with the course materials and exams are thorough but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Eric is a great professor, particularly compared to others in the major. So far the best CIS professor I've taken at the UO by far. Loves what he does and it shows, even outside of video game courses. Cares about his students and the class was difficult but not too challenging. Weekly projects and two exams.
Easygoing and understanding. Best professor I have ever had. There are attendance quizzes during the lecture but the class is designed to help you succeed and Eric is always happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the first CS class where things start getting real, but, Eric does an amazing job at teaching. The textbook, which you REALLY should read this time around, does such a horrible job compared to Eric. Also, his office hours are at great times, he's super friendly and helpful, and an amazing teacher. I wish more profs were like him!

One of the best professors I've had in CIS so far. Genuinely cares about his students and a very relaxed class environment. He's good at connecting the theoretical to the practical and wants his students to be successful. Weekly projects are challenging but straightforward and doable if you have been paying attention. They help with comprehension.

No one cares as much as Eric. He wants you to understand his class, get a good job, and be happy. His lectures are a little fast, and the slides are busy, but if you come prepared, it's a fun and easy class. Assignments completely prepare you for the tests. A nice bonus is that he currently works in industry as well as teaching.
Watch out for Game of Thrones spoilers in lecture
Eric is the best CIS professor out there!

This class is easy enough as long as you show up to lecture and ask questions during labs.  The lectures are usually ahead of the homework, so as long as you're showing up you're getting the info you need for the homework.

Upbeat and friendly. Likes to write example code in class. Assignments involve writing working code at home. No group projects. No pop-quizzes. Expensive textbook. The course is easy but only because it doesn't cover the subject to any real depth.

If you get to know one professor in the department, make it Eric. He is the best teacher I've had at UO, and I've taken three of his classes. He is funny, thought-provoking and clear. It amazes me how easily he can convey such difficult concepts. This term we are learning x86 assembly, no small feat, and he goes out of his way to help us succeed.

Eric's lectures clearly relate to the assigned readings, and he also offers lots of supplementary details. His enthusiasm keeps the class focused on the lecture. His tests tend to be fairly easy and predictable based off the assigned material and lecture content—this is a great thing.

Unlike some other teachers in the department, Prof. Wills really tries to teach so everyone in the class can understand. He is always willing to work something out with you if you're having a hard time understanding or turning in assignments and is just a nice guy overall. Easy, but good for building your knowledge of/confidence in programming.

Cool guy, new to teaching but knows the subject well, goes over a wide variety of stuff and is really a great professor. He really gets you excited to be a part of the department. He has interesting projects but grades easily and his tests are a joke.
His class was very easy, but I learned a lot. He's good about balancing lecture and examples, and funny when he makes a mistake.
He is a fun teacher who is more than happy to help after the lecture class and during office hours.
Instructor was a lot of fun, very knowledgeable about related topics. Test were not very difficult. Very helpful, would recommend to students needing assistance.
I had the best experience is EDST448 with Eric. A super fun class and great professor. The class is easy as long as you do the work, abd Eric is a pretty easy grader. I ended with over 100%.
Nice person, some of the projects were a bit confusing but they offered good feedback when you reached out.
I enjoyed this class. Eric is a really caring instructor. The grading criteria could be clearer but the projects are fun and interesting.

Eric Braman is nice in person. However, the assignments lack good clarity, and the grading also makes no sense. I wish the school had a professor with more classroom experience, because that would make this course more applicable to our actual goals rather than just rambling on about things beyond our reach. Guest lecturers are great tho!

The course was overall an easy A, only 2 large reflections and weekly small ones. However the GE's did most of the work. Assigned extreme amounts of reading per week, doesn't consider students have lives other than the class. Expected to read multiple books. Don't take if you have a weak stomach because it gets into detail about slaughterhouses..

Easy class but poorly organized. Assigned a lot of reading, but spent the entire lecture going over the readings, so very redundant and boring. Weekly reflections that are easy and two in-class written essays that are decently easy if you can do what is asked of you + be creative. Easy A if you focus on the right things
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assigned seats in the 300 person lecture hall. Easy to pass because the only requirements are basically showing up, not being on your phone and pretending you care on the reflections. The content is very graphic. If you have a good GE this is an easy A. The 2 reflections are most of your grade and they're written in class. No other homework.
If you're not religous, pick one and start praying.

I'm lowkey scared of her. Assigned seats with daily attendance in a 300-person lecture. She yelled at students on phones. Pretty easy to get a good grade, but there is a lot of assigned readings, and lectures are long and boring. The content was interesting, and I learned a lot, but the course organization and teaching style was just odd.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. McKenna treats her students like children. Although the course content was incredibly easy to understand, she ruined the class for me. She would fully stop lecture to scold students for being on their phones, attendance was taken daily in a 300 person class, and she told us we were not allowed to use the bathroom during class (80 minutes).

McKenna is a passionate teacher who explains everything well, you'll learn a lot if you're actually interested in the subject. Grading is mostly attendance-based. But her GE's are unpredictable, and mine didn't grade anything until 2 months into the class, which set me up for failure. Would not take again.

She is very insightful and passionate about her work. However, the grading criteria and participation criteria are not communicated clearly. There is a lot of readings and she does fishbowl discussions and 50 min presentations in pairs before most classes. She is a super tough grader.

Course content was interesting, but heavy at times. Weekly readings and journal entries weren't awful, but the 3 essays had unclear instructions and were tedious. Class is graded heavily on participation and attendance is mandatory. Be prepared to read a TON and actively engage with the class, otherwise the professor gets frustrated.

The class was actually 170 but it was very easy, consisting of reading quizzes and 4 unit "essays" that were only 300 words max and graded very easily. Lectures were interesting but sometimes got a bit boring. The most frustrating thing was only allowing hand written notes and she actually didn't give enough time to even get the slide title down

Worst philosophy professor I've ever had. She doesn't accommodate at all and is stingy on giving extensions. Assigns way too much reading and expects too much from her students. Seems to only care about academia, given that she has no understanding or respect for student's lives outside of school. Don't take her class if you don't have to.

Phil315. Mckenna is probably one of my fav PHIL professors at UO. Lectures covered readings, she would always leave time for any questions or comments on them. It's philosophy, so readings are like 40 pages twice a week. Attendance + participation are huge parts of your grade but you are given tons of chances to make them up. 11/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was in Phil 315 and attendance policy was 2 absences the entire term. The TA, Augie was an extremely harsh grader and unfriendly. Erin is interesting to say the least, she very passionate about what she does but her lectures are hard to pay attention to with lots of rambling. Participation was a large part of grade but Erin gave very few chances.

Dr. McKenna is clearly very passionate about what she teaches, and I came into this class very excited to learn about food/the ethics surrounding that, and I feel that she delivered. My biggest issue with this class, though, was the heavy discussion based classes, and I felt that the readings were just too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. It's super confusing and there's a lot of unnecessary work and a lot of papers to write and random quizzes. Also I tried asking her a question once and she made me feel ridiculed. She expects too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor, just no way around it. Does not accommodate for disabled students in her classes at all from what I can tell, and refuses to give clear directions to how to complete assignments, but grades super specifically and severely anyway. Super uppity and elitist personality type, avoid at all costs if possible.
Very lecture heavy with lengthy slides, doesn't really explain the text rather than just reread quotes from it back to you, uses SEATING CHART, easy to fall asleep, hard to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Calls on students randomly in a 300 person lecture which is unusual (and terrifying), but overall a very engaging and thoughtful instructor. Papers were graded well with useful feedback. Final is only a reflection. Pop quizzes so attendance is important, but they are short and the material on them is covered in lecture thoroughly.

Erin was a good professor, and I loved how passionate she was about her teaching. She just had too many things to do. Quite a bit of reading, 8 hours of an experimental learning site that you had to do outside of class, journals due every week, 2 tests a term, etc. The reading was very relevant and interesting, although she used her own book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She really knows her stuff. Taking notes is a bit difficult because she talks and goes through her very wordy slides super quickly (though she uploads them to canvas). While you need to do the readings for pop quizzes, she thoroughly explains the material before them (They're at the end of class) so you usually can get away without them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: McKenna is a decent professor but your grade in the class all depends on your GE. Lectures are all based on the assigned reading. There are 4 pop quizzes all of which are pretty easy as long as you read. All exams are take home essays so you can do them with friends. 10% of your grade is attendance so go to lecture and discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Really great professor, she's super knowledgeable about current events and issues going on. She has interesting lectures and keeps people engaged. Class was really easy and GTF's are super nice and easy graders
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr.Hanna used a labor based grading system for this class which made it very clear exactly what you have to do to get the grade that you want. She is such a caring teacher and genuinely wants to see you succeed, I would love to have another class with her.

Niche class, but very interesting and concepts can be applied to various other disciplines. Professor has great lectures once a week, with discussions taking up the other class time. 4 essays and a final case study presentation. Readings aren't too heavy, and they are very engaging and interesting. Relevant topics help with understanding concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly one of the kindest, most considerate and most caring professors I have ever had. Dr. Hanna is a wonderful professor who cares very deeply about her classes and I sincerely enjoyed every lecture. If you take this class, take it seriously and contribute to discussions, she really stresses that there are no wrong answers.

Dr Hanna has been my favorite professor at UO. She is so nice accommodating and passionate about her studies. Attendance was not mandatory but I enjoyed going. The class topic was super interesting and relevant if you are a fan of anything at all. I learned so much in her course and her style of teaching is very accommodating.

This is the second Dr Hanna class I have taken and I will continue to take her classes. The way she organises her classes is so beneficial to student learning and makes you take accountability for yourself. Everything in the class seemed relevant and helped with the final projects and assignments. She's flexible on submissions of reports as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She cares about her students. She is passionate about what she is teaching. Despite being a history class, it is really interesting and easy. Would recommend taking for an art credit

If you're a cinema major, take a class with Dr. Hanna during your time at UO!! Her lectures are so entertaining, she is very compassionate and considerable about her students' needs, and she's very passionate about film which shows through her teaching style. Easily the best film prof I've had so far at UO.

Dr. Hanna is such a great professor. I really appreciate her entire way of going about teaching, as she is very understanding about absences and project extensions. She is really kind and easy to reach by email, which is SO nice. I also just enjoyed the class, I really liked the material and subject matter. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Hanna is such a kind & understanding prof. I most appreciated that about her because with COVID, it is so annoying that profs make attendance mandatory even if you're sick. Dr. Hanna did the complete opposite of this. Ensured that it was OKAY to miss class if sick and understanding with extensions. Class itself was easy but interesting material

My favorite teacher of the term.. She interacted with students and actually was interested in hearing about people's lives. While you do have a decent amount of work, she makes the class so worth it. She's a great teacher and super understanding. I highly suggest taking a class she teaches.

Dr. Hanna was so nice and understanding! The class was really easy , for sure an easy A especially online. I think the class would be way more interesting in person but the course work was still engaging even online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, and Erin is a super cool teacher. She really cares about her students succeeding, and organizes her assignments in a way that promotes growth and diving deeper into topics. Exams are mostly based on lecture material, but reading will help. I also got to watch some fascinating old TV shows!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Really fantastic professor and course. I took CINE111 as a random Gen Ed needed for graduation and it ended up being one of my favorites ever taken at UO. Attendance is mandatory but going to class is fun and you can have a friend sign you in if needed. Final is straightforward and all assignments are easy to succeed in if you do your best work!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Hanna is an incredible lecturer, a brilliant scholar, and a fascinating person. I would recommend her and her class to everyone I know.

I took Professor Hanna's "How to Watch TV" class. She did a great job of making the content appealing to everyone in the class, whether you were an actual media studies or cinema major, or if you were just an Ad or PR student trying to fill your credits. The assignments never felt like busy work, and were actually beneficial

Dr. Hanna is fantastic, the lectures are really great, get involved in them it really will help you understand the topics better. No book all the readings she posts online for you, show up participate and have Ashley Cordes as your GE and you're golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Hannah's lecture is very engaging, but unfortunately the class will be graded by the GTF. Make sure you don't take it with Laura, otherwise you may receive C or lower

Erin is really funny and well-versed in the subject but her lectures are painfully long. She assigns daily reading responses which she randomly collects for attendance so attendance is mandatory. This class is less about films and more about filmmaking and the logistics of producing, so it can sometimes be dry. You get cheat sheets for both exams.
Dr. Hana is Awesome! take her classes for sure, you'll be happy

The material is pretty interesting but lectures can get long after a while. The tests are very specific and in-depth compared to the material she teaches so beware. She's good about letting students give input during lectures. She does a good job of explaining but get ready to remember it word for word for the test.
She grades her whole class on two tests and decided to change the material of the final a week before hand after putting it on the study guide. Horrible professor.
Awful. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: assignments are reliant on in class live code though there are often important/helpful parts of code that she deletes b4 uploading to canvas thus it a mess of spaghetti code. also often has import statements b in the middle of code instead of being in headers.(Though she was 6 months pregnant at the start of this term so might be exception to norm)
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Erickson is the best professor I ever had throughout my undergrad and grad school. She cares about students and is very helpful during office hours. The lecture is very interactive despite being online.

Lowkey disrespectful, laughs when students guess wrong answers. The homework is graded off effort but I'm pretty sure she doesn't even open the files and just gives you a grade. The course is easy if you have any basic experience in CIS. The final is worth like 40% of your grade so beware.

A great lecturer (especially for an online class), she codes live and encourages participation. You can tell she always wants to do her best and cares if the students are understanding/learning the material. Very helpful during office hours and responsive to emails. She runs a well organized course with reasonable homework and final project.
One of the few computer science professors that I wasn't afraid to ask a question and have them call me stupid. Great professor and super relate able, would love for her to teach more classes
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Erdem is a great professor, and taking PD 330 from him has really increased my understanding of 3D modeling, a skill I thought I wouldn't be good at before taking this class. He's funny, gives really good feedback and guidance, and is very knowledgeable and easy to follow along with.

Erdem is a great teacher and he gives really helpful and constructive feedback. My drawing improved a lot over the course of the term and even though the main project is a lot of work, his expectations in canvas are always very clear and it was very well paced. I'm excited to take more classes from him.

Gives the best feedback of all the PD professors. He will give you feedback in a constructive and specific way that does not feel like he is critiquing your whole project. His instructions during class are very clear, and he is considerate if you're going through something personal. Only critique is that his canvas is a bit messy

Erdem is a great teacher. He covered all the important stuff, and homework was not mandatory for most of the term. But the class was graded with 4 assignments, one of them being 70% of the total grade and also the most work I've ever done for any class. It's in the syllabus but you still need to watch out for it, because it will eat you alive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course has been one of my favorites so far. Erdem gives tutorials every class, and you just follow along. The class can feel a bit long, but it's useful once you start doing your own projects. This class is graded by 2 assignments which is crazy, but the grading structure is fairly lenient. Erdem allows late hand-ins and has online tuts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Erdem is a great but tough Professor. He has a dry sense of humor which can come off as inconsiderate but is generally very easy to work with. As long as you communicate with him, he is a fantastic teacher. If you are a hard working students, he will work hard to teach you. His class is quite accessible as he posts lecture videos online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Selek was an amazing professor. If you work hard and are passionate about product design it wont be hard to pass and do well in this class. The structure is very rigid and easy to follow which means you know all your deadlines by the end of the first class. Asking him for advice severely helped my grade and he's a super nice guy!

One of the best, and most talented teachers I've had. This class was for design drawing and rendering. It was great to see he actually knew what he was doing, and did a lot of tutorials in class which helped immensely. He also is extremely chill and down to earth. Always there to help you, and definitely reasons with you if you have problems
Love his class, I have never draw so many Hair dryer in my live but My drawing have improve so much that its crazy.

This professor simply shouldn't be teaching. It's not like he's a bad guy or doesn't know his stuff. Personally, the quality of this class just felt like I was being scammed. I can't recall a single thing from lecture or one thing he said that stuck with me. Don't get me started on the exam prep (Nothing). A self taught class that I wish I missed.

His lectures are a drag and it can be very hard to hear him and understand what he is saying and writing. He takes attendance every day but they are free points in a very test-heavy course. With that being said, if you study the tests are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives the most boring lectures ever. Granted that finance is not the most exciting topic, but he talks so quietly, so slow, mumbles, and has an accent. All of these combined make it very hard to understand him and follow along, let alone be interested. Avoid taking him if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brutal class, highly recommend avoiding and finding a different class.

While Emami was kind and attempted to explain things when you had a question, it was often difficult to understand him and there was lots of material he never taught on the tests that were worth 90% of your grade. He also made us take the first test twice and changed the way it was graded last minute. No one was able to finish the final in 2 hours.

This is essentially a self taught course as you won't be able to understand lectures through a mumbled accent, and absolutely zero organization when "reading" through lecture slides. Possibly the worst class I've taken at the UO. Study for hours just to fail tests worth your whole grade. 3 tests 30% each.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors ever. Doesn't have an idea of your grade until the end of the class. Classes also felt different every time, where he would sometimes explain things well, while explaining things poorly at other times.

I feel like this class was a tale of two halves. Every up to Quiz 1, which was in week 6 of the class, was explained very well and thoroughly. After that, everything got much harder, he didn't go into much detail with things. Not open for support outside of class or helping you to succeed. Your grade isn't known until the end of the term.

Professor Ali Emami can be hard headed, challenging, and spiteful. I found out very quickly that he does not like it when students stand up to him regardless of the reason or if he is in the wrong. Sometimes he's approachable, sometimes he's not. He knows the material but his lectures are hard to follow.

90% of this course is graded by exams (30% for two midterms and 30% final) Each question on these quizzes is worth 1% of your final grade leaving no room for error especially when the questions are worded poorly. Ali is a funny and nice guy in a dry humor kind of way but this course was not enjoyable and I would avoid him if I needed BA318.

In all honesty the class wasn't that bad, contrary to the ratings. Most of the grade is the midterm and final, but as long as you take good notes and read the textbook you'll be fine. He asks if there are any questions after showing examples, and explains things thoroughly. The lectures do tend to drag sometimes, but overall Ali is a pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking to take FIN 283, save yourself the money and headache by just downloading the textbook "Fundamentals of Investing" by Smart, Gitman, and Joehnk for free on a book/pdf website. Anything I learned in this class I taught myself by reading the book. Ali is hard to understand and very aggressive when challenged.

Ali emami will make you buy a packet, just for his slides to be the packet. He will also just read directly from the slides without deviation. He refused to answer a question in a clear manner, his most frequent response being "Well it depends" without elaborating further. I am about to pass OChem while failing this class because of ali.

Professor Emami is really harsh and isn't a very good communicator. Get's easily frustrated when students don't understand what's going on, and doesn't do a great job of reading the room when students are confused. Not to mention he makes his classes 50% midterm 50% final which is really brutal and doesn't leave any room for mess ups.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor I've taken a course with at the UO. The midterm and final both 50% of your final grade. Doesn't speak clearly, mumbles for most of the lecture and expects you to memorize everything he says. Doesn't curve and I quote, "I don't care if I don't give out A's, its not my problem its yours"
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. Explains things in the most complicated ways then roasts students if they do not immediately understand when he asks for help. Because of this no one volunteers so he proceeds to say our entire class will fail in the real world. Class is 50% final 50% midterm and there is no curve, because "If no one gets an A its your fault"
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. Cant explain at all. You can study for the tests a week in advance and still fail.

Worst prof I've ever encountered. He was unable to transition to the online format and seems like he would've incompetent in person as well. Frequently joined Zoom meetings with a poor connection and lashed out at students who couldn't understand his choppy audio. Only lectures with his poor handwritte notes which may as well be Sanskrit characters

Worst Prof I have ever had by a mile. He would take large sections of class to take almost an hour to take roll out loud in a hundred person lecture class over zoom and was woefully unprepared to teach the course and interact with anything technological. Doesn't even know his own syllabus or due dates which makes it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: WORST TEACHER IVE EVER HAD! picks on kids and makes up pop quizzes and makes us prove our math through zoom. Terrible. Should not be employed let alone by a university. Bum!

Really bad Professor. Doesn't know his own syllabus, is VERY unclear and doesn't teach the course work well. Worst Professor I've had so far. Boring lectures. Fights students, STAY AWAY if you aren't scrappy.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Possibly the worst professor I have ever had. He clearly knows a lot about the subject but is not good at teaching it to others. He expects you to know the material on day one and makes you feel dumb for asking any type of questions. The final was worth 60% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. 50% of your grade is the midterm, the other 50 is the final. You have homework, but it isn't graded. He can't even speak clearly enough to teach, and he makes no effort. He disrespects his students regularly. His lectures make you more confused. You will have to teach yourself without any proper materials. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So here's the deal. Emami is a nice guy that cares about his students but his accent, age, and trouble adapting to an online format make learning in his courses very difficult. He is the type of prof to get upset if you don't have the answer he is looking for. He gets irritated that nobody talks but it makes sense given how cold and aggro he can be

Very rude and overall disorganized professor. Was genuinely afraid to be cold-called during class as he is very condescending and has no issue in making you feel stupid in front of everyone. Went on a rant about a story in the Bible for a good 20 minutes during one lecture which had ZERO relevance to the material, what is that about!

One of the worst Professors I've ever had. His lectures are basically worthless, he's rude and short with students, and his syllabus is outdated and confusing, along with the instructions to assignments/quizzes. An extremely misleading Professor.

The one positive is he's approachable. He IGNORES the syllabus with days notice, the driest lecturer I ever had, ignores own office hours, unclear in instructions, didn't grade anything for 6 weeks, non-responsive to emails, condescending by saying you should know something already. Material alone is hard. One of if not the worst professor I had.
Nice professor!
Unequivocally the worst professor I've ever had. Has zero regard for what's on the syllabus. Comes unprepared for lectures. Two weeks left in term, and has yet to grade any assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was horrible, 85% of grade is mid term and final. Also on the test even multiple choice questions you have to show work. The class averages were Fs and Ds on tests. Only passed cause of the curve, would not recommend. Nice guy, bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ali was disrespectful, a bad communicator, unclear in what he wanted us to do, and almost impossible to get ahold of over canvas or email. He taught us essentially nothing, and the average test score was well below 50%. If you have to take this, for the homework USE QUIZLETS!! They have all the answers, search the problem, do command+F to find them
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was easily the hardest class I've taken in college. Ali is a terrible teacher, as in he is extremely confusing in lecture & often moves forward without flushing out topics. The course material is also challenging for both Derivatives & International Finance. Avoid taking his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor! Breaks down key concepts and ideas to a very simple level. You need to be proactive and read all the material. When the effort and work is put in, you'll see good results.

If u want someone to hold ur hand and walk u through a class, he is not ur guy. This is an upper division Finance class that is applicable to the real world. The material is tough but interesting. He knows what is talking about and pushes you to work hard. I learned so much from him. If ur finance concentration, take . If not, I wouldn't (its hard

Professor was unorganized, did not know what chapter we were on each morning, was late almost every day, did not teach chapters that were on exams, would stare at us and ask the same question over and over in a condescending tone. The average score for the midterm was a 58% and the professor spent half of the following lecture chewing us out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very dry, boring class sessions with blackboard notes that are often times hard to follow. Graded heavily on two tests, good news is he lets you bring a cheat sheet. Still not an easy class and he makes an uninteresting topic as uninteresting as possible. Try to avoid taking this class with Ali.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst professor I've had his lecture is lack of organized and hard to follow don't take with him unless you like to teach yourself

Very boring lecturer. The stock simulation you do is pretty interesting but he does not make the outlines clear even when directly asked. If you ask a question about an assignment he will refer you to the syllabus. Expensive textbook and he made you buy his lecturer packet.
Love Emami!!
AVOID THIS PROFESSOR LIKE THE PLAGUE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I took finance with Ali and was initially intimidated by his attitude (and the idea I would be doing a lot of math for this course) but quickly realized that his teaching style is straight-forward and his expectations are even more so.  Do the online homework, show up for lectures, and bring a good note sheet to each exam and you'll pass!

Takes roll and requires attendance, yet teaches very little during class time. Expects students to do tons of reading, yet he's very unclear about which concepts are important and what will be on the test. The required course packet is a cluttered, unorganized mess.

Professor is so hard to follow. He grades exams harshly, and test us on some materials that were not covered. He wants you to read everything in the book so if something in the exam was not covered in the class, you supposed to know it. There are four exams which is a lot to do is his class. Do not recommend take with him at all.

The guidelines for class were extremely unclear. Lectures were confusing and out of the order in regards to the syllabus, which left students confused in the readings.  Tests were graded harshly and weren't on the material he said they would be on. The midterm median before the curve was a 48% ...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: one of the average of the midterm was pretty low so he decided to cut half of te points u lost! In other words, i was curved about 12& but the average after curve was still barely 73 % which i have no idea why. If you take notes and study what he mentioned important. there is no way you would get unsatisfied grade.

I greatly enjoyed Ali as an instructor, and have subsequently spoken with him and used him as a resource for recommendations and references. He has a great sense of humor and will keep you entertained during lecture (if you pay enough attention). I wouldn't say his course was particularly difficult, it's a matter of being diligent.

His English may not be the best or most fluent but he knows how to get across to you. He has some of the most hilarious jokes I've ever encountered from any teacher. Great sense of humor. He knows his stuff! Once you attend all his classes and do all the practice homework he gives you, you are ensured of getting a high grade. Best professor ever!

Ali is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. He cares so much about his students and his community. He brings in real world relatable and current examples to keep students engaged and learning. I would hands down take another class from him. However, the group project sucked.

Professor Emami was the reason I switched to business. I got an A+ in his class because I did what he fairly required. He curves his tests and is a fair grader. If you go to class and do the work, you will do well. He makes himself available to you if you need to see him both in office hours and at his business downtown. One of my favorite teachers
Bad teaching skills. Messed up lecture with no clear outline. The lecture notes suck.
Pretty strict, not very approachable.
So much to do in the class. We had 4 exams, 2 projects, weekly report due + small project related to the report every week, and 5 homeworks (online quizzes)! It was a lot!

This guy is great! If you want a class where attendance is mandatory but otherwise useless he's the man for it. Also, be prepared to read the entire book and study your ass off only to be completely blindsided on the exams with unrelated material!

Ali is a genius.  Sometimes he doesn't relate the material well to the class but by the end of the term I was convinced that was because he was just too intelligent for his own good sometimes.  Extremely helpful in office hours and wants students to do well even though he may come off as rude sometimes.

Unique person. Sometimes hard to understand. His examples are kinda weird at times. Heavy textbook use. About a chapter or two a week. Many project with 3-4 tests in the year. Class can be slow at times.

I really liked Professor Emami. The class was tough but no harder than any other upper division class. Do the homework and you'll pass the test. Lecture was fast paced but you can tell Emami is enthusiastic about the topic.

Emami comes across as rude and scowling but once you get to know him you'll realize he is one of the few who really cares and expects a lot from his students. Class is TOUGH but you'll learn so much from him. DO NOT get behind on the work. Very demanding class but worth it.
Do yourself a huge favor and do not take a class from this professor. His teaching is nothing short of a nightmare!
Has an accent. Expects a lot from you. Quizzes and tests are multiple choice. Funny guy.

Good class as long as you show up, he does take attendance. Tests are off what he posts on blackboard. No surprises in any of his midterms, everything is out of his book. Go to his office hours and you will pass with a descent grade.

Ali's a great guy. He's clearly passionate about the material and has real world experience. He will meet with you whenever to give you any additional help and is easy to get a hold of. It's not an easy A class but it's definitely manageable. He's a good professor and has tons of interesting stories. Worth taking a class from.

He will reward you if you come to class, go to office hours, show interest, and generally make an effort. If you don't, you will struggle and likely fail. He's a good teacher that recognizes students that try.

DO NOT TAKE BA 318 with Ali! I just came out of the final and seriously this guy feeds off you throwing you stupid "GOTCHA" questions. What he lectures on and his study guides/materials did nothing to prepare us for the obscure and poorly written questions on the final. Seriously, this guy shouldn't be teaching in our prestigious business school.

At first I thought Emami was very condescending and rude, now I love him! He's a really funny guy and I've learned tons in this class. There is ALOT of work, but he does these things to make you read the book and understand the material. As for people who complain about the work and or tests being hard and the material being dry, IT'S ECONOMICS!!

Ali is a nice guy and pretty funny! However, he is a terrible teacher. He spends way too much time deriving theories/formulas and not teaching what is actually being tested. Tests are very hard! His teaching methods are very hard to follow - scattered. The class was much harder than it needed to be.
Don't know.

Ali is a funny guy. Always cracking funny jokes to TRY and keep the class interested. The material is SO dry and SO boring. Beware, the maroon colored book for this class is essential to the class, because the other books offered doesnt have chapters what were tested over. The class has WAY too much homework, and HARD quizzesweekly. Office hrs!!!!

Professor Emami teaches difficult material. At first I thought he was cold and harsh. But after attending office hours I discovered he was willing to put as much effort into helping me as I was into finding help. I recommend him if you are a hardworking student because he will reward a good work ethic.

I had one of the worst experiences ever from this professor. I had an A going into the final and expected the final to be much like the other tests and half the material was on news items that had happened the last few days. The test average was a 58% and since the final was worth half our grade all of our grades suffered.

Demanding class, but good guy.  May seem a bit gruff at first because of his accent...but he's a very friendly guy.  On that note, his accent isn't that bad...you're an idiot if you can't understand him.
Can be demanding but is very helpful when you go to his office hours

I was skeptical at first BUT i grew to really enjoy this professor.  He is very helpful if you approach him during office hours.  Class time is enjoyable because he has a sense of humor.  I recommend that if you are struggling in his class, that you go to office hours.  He alays strives to make sure you understand.  A+
I really enjoyed his class. He is a good teacher and funny. The coursework is difficult but he is very personable and easy to approach.

I LOVED Ali Emami. Yes, he is very hard and sometimes is unclear about the processes that he is explaining. However, he is SO nice and if you are a good student and show that you are dedicated to work hard and try your best, you WILL get a good grade in this class. He just wants to test peoples strength sometimes. He is great and has a sense of hum

He's very hard to follow during lectures. He'll zip back and forth through slides randomly,rant at students for being stupid if they don't get it. And he puts stuff on the tests that was barely covered expecting us to just know. He's nice and tells good jokes but I would avoid him unless you have talent for finance.

SO hard to learn anything from this guy. his teaching is not very clear, and frankly I learned more from the book than i did in class. He doesnt understand when you ask him questions and his book that he requires for the class is confusing and overly wordy.

Emami is a good professor if you are a good student. I don't like office hours, but he will answer every question you have, ensuring that you know how to do what needs to be done. If you go before homework is due, you will be golden. He enjoys telling stories, so all info doesn't always get covered in class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS AND YOU WILL BE FINE!

Avoid this professor at all costs, he is terrible. he is hard to understand, it is unclear what he expects out of his students, and there seems to be no organization to his lectures. I WILL NEVER take another class with him

I had a hard time in this class because there is a lot of reading. If you take this class with Emami, be sure to go to office hours at least once a week. Do this before you turn in online homeworks, and he will help you a lot. Do the readings. Make time to study. What he teaches is really important. Take it in summer or with easy classes.
I thought he was great, fair, every interested in me and the topic at hand.  Only complaint would be it's difficult to get his attention for a question during class
It is very hard to understand him and he doesn't really teach to the book. He doesnt spend much time on each topic and doesn't explain what he is doing in class.

Ali Emami is by far the worst teacher I have ever had.  There is absolutely no organization of content, clear requirements, expectations or concepts.  Most of the class time is spent watching Ali patronize students while he tirelessly derives complex economic theories which do nothing to help our understanding.  Avoid him at all costs.

Professor was extremely helpful to students with questions and interested in the topics he was teaching.  Required you to keep up with his lessons outside of class, and if you did, it was easy to get an A.  The only people who struggled were those who weren't doing any work or paying attention in class.  Highly recommend.
Good Teacher, If you are able to do work without someone holding your hand.  Business students are such whiners.

prof. was extremely unclear interms of content and in terms of speaking the english language. while the class was an basic econ course he taught at a much high level which  made it extremely difficult to pass any tests. powerpoints were up to 95 slides, in addition to reading the textbook, and additional notes.  i do not recommend this prof
This teacher is very rude to his students. He runs a very strict classroom and is difficult to understand. I would not recommend taking a class taught by this professor if there are other options.

Esther's lectures were definitely more interesting than Jim's, but she also lectured with the lights off. Cool architect we learned about: Lina Bo Bardi! Check her out. The tough grading in the class still holds true and there was miscommunication between her and Jim about what would be on the test which was annoying and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most frustrating and mind-numbing classes I've had to take in an overall amazing time in the B.Arch program at the UO. Weekly readings can be up to 100 pages of dense philosophy and grading for projects is unclear. One of the most egregious readings was written by Heidegger, a Nazi. Expect to rush all of your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very passionate about design and has so much knowledge, especially dealing with interior design and color. She can be slightly unapproachable at first, but once you get to know her she is so caring and willing to help. Most memorable professor I've had yet, very sweet and witty and has so many stories to share.

Esther is a real character and may seem a bit unapproachable or difficult at first but she is really an extremely intelligent, caring, and passionate teacher. I had her for my first studio and she was perfect. She cares about true artistry and passion and while she may speak in metaphors, her critiques and advice are unique and insightful.
Erik is the best! I had so much fun in this class, and Erik helped me so much outside of class. I would definitely recommend taking any class with him. Amazing teacher.
He makes the class and syllabus very organized. Lectures were usually pretty interesting, easy to understand. I would recommend this class for an easy econ elective.
He is really understanding and a great prof!

I had Eric for econ 330. He is very nice and caring towards his students. Canvas course is organized nicely, and syllabus is organized. Offers extra credit opportunities. Gives good feedback on homework and is accessible via email/office hours. Attendance is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Eric as a teacher. He is very flexible with due dates and is happy to meet with you to go over questions one-on-one. Really liked his lectures

Eric was a great teacher! His examples in lectures were fun and kept me engaged even though I don't really like economics. It's clear that he really cares about students succeeding. The homework required you to extend the concepts from lecture a bit, but if you email him or go to office hours he will show you how things connect

Eric was a very enthusiastic instructor and had lots of relevant and current events in his course, however his virtual lectures were pretty scattered, and the problem sets and quizzes often had tons of material not covered in the (optional) book or lectures. Fairly easy class but only worth it if you already have some knowledge.

He was so nice, but not a good teacher. He would regularly say things wrong/get confused without correcting himself. Homework wasn't written by him, so the wording in assignments and lectures didn't match. Very confusing. Exams had large curves because of content that he admitted wasn't taught. Could get better w/ experience, still don't recommend.

Prof. Porras is now blessing here with here present at CSU Monterey Bay... All off the previous comments are very true! She is hard to understand and if I listen to her say blah blah blah one more time might head might explode! Oh yeah and as for tech problems her computer crashed and she lost all of our grades to date. Easy YES! BORING YES!

I disagree with the below comments that this class is awful. Easy and somewhat off-topic, yes. Awful? No. Estella is nice and not a hard grader. The material is interesting, and Estella does a good job of having it make sense. This class is more of a theoretical class and at times really felt like it. But it wasn't hard and somewhat interesting.

This class is really not bad. It's more interesting than most lectures I've been in, and at least Estella tries to let people participate. Her slides are clear and helpful in studying for the tests. There are sometimes problems w/ technology,but I think that's just the classroom. Why would you be upset about watching YouTube videos? They're funny

This topic sounds incredibly interesting, but she is an incredibly horrible teacher. Try to take this class with the other teacher if possible. . .if you can't get this class with him, just wait till next term, because it is not worth it with her. If this class was not mandatory, it might be okay, but to have to live through her lectures is hell.

This woman is an embarrassment to the University. Her classes are so incredibly pointless and she is the worst teacher I've ever had. I honestly cannot believe that anyone would hire this woman. Everyday after class my friends and I just talk about how horrible she is. There is something wrong with technology daily. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

I took this class because it looked easy--and it is. But it is a COMPLETE WASTE OF TIME. Prof. Porras has killed my interest in journalism. However, attendance is "mandatory" because an attendance sheet is passed around...in a class of nearly 200...ugh. Stay far away.

um....I'm in this class at the moment actually and everything previously said is sadly, very true. I just burst out laughing in the middle of class reading the comments because we are suppose to be watching a video on Guttengurg but after a minute it just shut off and she can't seem to figure out how to get it working again...

This class really should be called Mass Media and Society in Colombia. Class time is spent watching random youtube videos and extremely biased documentaries that seem like she looked up 5 min before class. She's a nice person, but should be teaching kindergarden not a college-level class.
She's entertaining at first but it gets old fast.  If you want to know where she lives via Google Earth, watch pointless YouTube videos everyday, and waste your time, sign up for her j201 class.

I am a Sophomore at U of O and this is the most pointless class I have taken thus far.  Every day in class there is some new catastrophe that she cannot fix on her own.  Today I can guarantee that the battery will be dead in her microphone and we will waste the first 15 minutes of class waiting for the GTF to go get a new one.

Professor Escallón is deeply engaging, informative, and fun.  I found her lectures very informative and heavily related to the work that we had to do outside of class.   However, the course is graded through a variety of means, therefore you will be doing lots of readings, projects, and exams which can feel like a heavier workload.

Amazing professor! Both she and her GEs are absolutely incredible. Super understanding and kind. She consistently started class a few minutes late to allow people extra time coming from other courses. Great lecturer, straightforward assignments, and super fun content! I definitely recommend her :)
She's very passionate about the work and you can tell she cares about the success of the students in this field. The assignments were very easy but super lecture heavy.
I loved her lectures, loved how she presented the material, and she genuinely cares about her students and the study. I would recommend anyone to take any of her classes. No negatives
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I recommend taking this class, even though the attendance wasn't mandatory; the professor was just super passionate, which made me want to go to class. She's super sweet.

She insists that you can't pass the class without the expensive textbook, but I got an A+ without it. The discussion post material comes from the weekly readings and videos, and the quizzes are based on common knowledge. Overall, it's an easy and enjoyable course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: profesor escallon was very kind, considerate, and had an engaging class.

I can really tell she was passionate about what she taught. However, for me, the lengthy lectures and all the readings resulted in me getting really bored and I didn't really pay attention most of the time. Quizzes are very easy since they are open notes and fieldwork assignments are straightforward.

Ms. Escallon is a queen! She is so sweet and kind and cares so much about this world and our environment as people. You only have one discussion post per week and a super easy and light project that takes up the whole term. Overall, she is so amazing and makes this class super easy as an async class - highly recommend this class and her!
Very engaging and wonderful lectures . Encourages participation and tries to be available as much as possible outside of class

I would 100% take another class with Professor Escallon. I learned so much in this class and was never bored. After taking this class, I changed my major to anthropology. She is very understanding during the pandemic and makes the class so enjoyable. She was extremely knowledgeable but not intimidating. She definitely made the class feel welcomed.

She is so nice and charismatic. I really enjoyed her lectures, although tests and quizzes were heavily based on textbook readings. She is very engaging and wants the best for her students. Just make sure to read the articles and textbook chapters she assigns and you will be good!

Professor Escallón is super passionate about teaching and learning anthropology. The grading scale is out of 100 points so nothing is weighted, you either love that or hate that. The course is very organized and she gives thoughtful lectures and invites relevant guest speakers. Overall, her classes are definitely worth taking for any requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Escallon is my favorite professor. She is passionate in her lectures and uses her own experiences coming to the US from Colombia to illustrate things being taught. She's funny, enthusiastic, and caring about how class should be structured to best benefit students. She does assign readings, which to some might seem a lot. Highly recommend!

One of my favorite professors... she really cares about every one of her students and will help them succeed. Some classmates did not seem as respectful of her time and how much she tries to shape the class around student interests, which is a shame because I learned more in one term of her class than I have in multiple terms. I would recommend.

Escallon made Introduction to Cultural Anthropology really fun to learn about. Her passion over anthropology really gets one hooked and wanting to learn more. The class was fairly easy, although, she does assign A LOT of reading! The lectures she presents are interesting, especially the films she shows the class as well.

SHEs an adorable professor and I like her a lot I just hated the class and how it was taught. There was too many movies and guest speakers that had nothing to do with the course material and we barely took any notes. If you didnt read the book you were screwed for the weekly quizzes. Class attendance barely mattered .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: She is an inspiring lecturer and fun to listen to. She strengthens the course with films and guest speakers which are also very engaging. She is one of my favorite professors at UO. The course is relatively easy except the exams are difficult and there's one final project. She does offer extra credit opportunities. You have to buy the textbook.

Escallon is a great professor. The only reason I rated the difficulty of the class 3/5 was because since the midterms and final are on canvas and not in class, you can't ask clarifying questions. I only say this is a bad thing because many of the multiple choice answer options were similar and it kinda messed me up.

Professor Escallon has great lectures and is easy to listen to. There are 6 films throughout the course and are amazing to watch. There are test questions on them so don't just skip out when the movie starts. She uses personal stories when she teaches and is very engaging. All tests and quizzes are multiple choice and timed on canvas.

He's a pretty good professor for EC 311. Apparently much better than the other EC 311 professor. Also the midterm was not hard at all, it followed the practice exam. As long as you studied the practice exam and the problem sets, you will have gotten an A.
Not too bad. Lectures are much easier to follow now.
He has redeemed himself.
Does not explain properly anything dosent ever answer questions. Exam is really difficult.

Eun Young has been my favorite professor since I've been at UO, which is quite the accomplishment considering that Korean has been my worse class (though this is on me rather than my teacher). She is caring, funny, and wants to help you succeed. Daily classwork can be tricky to juggle, but she is an exceptional teacher and I highly recommend her.

Eunyoung is one of the teachers at UofO that is amazing! She actually cares about her students and whether or not they do well. Although some of the material may be hard (it is a new language) she still makes it fun and does her best to make sure everyone understands everything. Also, she is super funny and has a sarcastic sense of humor.
She is incredibly kind, and cares so much for her students. She understands how hard learning a language is and really wants you to do well. Shes easy to get in touch with questions, study help etc.

Amazing Korean teacher, shes an adorable and hilarious lady. Heavy workload and lots of quizzes, but she's very forgiving about grading and you can tell she really cares for her students and wants them to succeed. Only downside is she's very serious about not rounding up grades. I ended the class with a 89.99% and there was nothing I could do.
Eun Young is a great Korean teacher, although the subject is very difficult, you should study a lot and prepare for a heavy workload
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a fun teacher! The class is difficult not because of her, but learning a new language like Korean is challenging! She is caring and if you show that you are putting in the work, you'll be fine. Go to her office hours! She will always help you if she has the time! Lectures are fun and some of the assignments are fun too!

Intense and fast paced. Get ready for quizzes every other week if not every week. However she gives you the materials you need to study and the quizzes are often like the handouts. There is a group presentation that's easy as long as you don't procrastinate. Some memorization but she's a forgiving grader. Wonderful, caring, funny, cute woman. 10/10

Tests are mult. choice and not bad, there is a study guide that is very comprehensive. People who say Jeff is a tough teacher probably just did not put in the workstudy time.I didnt even read the book for final paper and still got an A on the paper. not a bad or tough class at all.
Lectures were thought provoking.  Readings are good (though there's a lot).  Really nice guy, easy to get help from.  I learned a lot.  Would take again!

Really nice guy, mediocre teacher. His lecture slides are not very helpful, reading the book is the best way to learn the material in this course. He doesn't really teach you anything. Tests are all multiple choice but there are many questions where it could be multiple answers and you can't really fight him on it. Chill guy, but slacking teacher.

By far the worst sociology teacher I've had. Lectures are pointless, his power points are only quotes from the readings. Incredibly boring. Doesn't teach you anything that is on the test. Nice guy, AWFUL teacher. Will not be taking any class by him ever again.
cool guy

Best class I have ever taken. Not easy in the least but very rewarding. Highly recommended if you are willing to challenge yourself. Any hard working, intelligent individual can get an A in his class.

This person is amazing. Very quickly in this class I was doing things I never thought I'd be capable of. I feel no praise is sufficient for this professor. To call him a god would be to use the name of Luks in vain. The people who gave this professor bad ratings are probably just upset over the shock of encountering greatness far beyond themselves.

I don't know why anyone would give him a good rating.  He's arrogant and very unfriendly when you ask him for help.  He quite frequently gets confused during his lectures. I don't doubt that he is a brilliant researcher but his ability to teach is questionable. When he grades exams he doesn't tell you what you did wrong, just gives a bad score.
No Comments
Difficult material. Forgiving in determining final grades.
No Comments
No Comments

No communication skills. Lecture videos were slow and not engaging and he was yawning half the time. Provides no extra help. Most failed the final. Extremely unclear expectations for assignments at the end of the term.

Professor Hart seems like a genuine guy, he teaches in a very monotone voice and is not very clear on instructions. He is very knowledgeable but can't seem to break it down to an undergrad classroom. Homework & exams are very difficult but he tries his best to work through with students through it.

i took an async for econ202. evan is a grad student so i went to office hours and even he was hard to really help me understand. reading through lecture slides and applying it on homework -- homework was easy asf-- can be helpful in succeeding in final and midterm. couple of writing assignments/discussion post but overall easy work in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First off, he is an incredibly nice man. He is very willing to help if you ask for it! That being said, I don't think that he is very good at conveying information to students in lecture. His slides are overly dense, and when asked to explain anything beyond what is explicitly written, he short circuits. It may be time to hang up the hat.

Incredibly smart man. Incredibly bad teacher. The hardest class to stay awake for that I've ever had and I'm a grad student. More than half of my class has stopped coming entirely and the average on the midterm was still almost an A. Chalk. Dust. Torture. Wish I could've taken his class 10-20 years ago when he was still young.

His lectures are dense but he's eager to respond to questions and clarify until you understand. Super nice and the final was very similar to the practice final. Overall, I really liked the course because of the content but I can see why some of the reviews on here are negative. His lectures aren't the most upbeat I've ever had.

most unengaging lecture on planet earth and possibly the solar system

avoid if possible

Probably one of the nicest professors at UO. A really kind professor who definitely cares about the wellbeing of his students.
