I would take another of his classes.

Professor Evans is a kind and caring guy. He is approachable and always helpful outside of class. The material can be quite hard so the best way to do well in this class is to do the practice exam and make a good note sheet for the test. The tests are hard, but prof. Evans and how helpful he is offsets the challenging material.

Overall he was pretty good. I think that he was accessible, understanding, and patient. He seems to know what he is doing and his format is clear. Dull, slow lectures on material that he both uses more math in than necessary and intentionally makes harder than necessary. Grading criteria not always clear. Not terrible but will try to avoid in the future.

Professor David is by far the best EC professor at UO. He is very funny and is always willing to help after hours which is very appreciated when you are stuck on homework problems. I would take a future class with him again.

Professor Shenkin transferred to Linfield now, but he is a phenomenal professor. He is understanding and sweet. His class is easy just do the blog posts and essay assignments and you'll be good. Professor Shenkin has probably had to be the kindest professor I've had so far. Evan is one of the most interesting professors at UO. He is bold enough to let students debate the most heated of topics during class, without interrupting. This teacher is well rounded and dignified with his knowledge on the course which he teaches. Reading and writing is required, but his commitment to helping his students is a sign on making the class a meaningful experience.
Evan is a great professor who truly cares about his students. There's a lot of reading and writing for this course, but it's very engaging material.

reviews.comment: Took his summer 207 course. Super nice guy and genuinely cares about you as an individual. Highly recommend and interesting material, especially coming from someone who's not a fan soc or history.

Best GTF ever in sociology department! He is a very nice guy. He would love to help you out. He is also very considerate. He respects students. I enjoyed those interesting video clips and useful practice sheets. He will definitely help you on your homework and exams. BTW, his grade on homework is pretty generous.

She is extremely unhelpful and rude.  Does not keep track of attendance, but thinks she has the right to lessen your grade at the end because she thinks you missed too many days…even when you only missed the allotted one or two missed classes. friendly teacher, very patient. learned a lot from 110 writing course. highly recommended!!!
Help you how to speak English!
perfect

Kyle Evitts was the worst professor I had at the UO.  He is very vague when explaining topics, and when I asked for help, he made things even worse. REALLY young (like 23 or 24) and on an equal level with the students. Very chill and easygoing, calm and relaxed. Super easy to understand the content because his lectures are simple and he teaches at a nice pace. 1010 would take any class taught by Kyle
She was the best professor I had at UO. It was sad that she is no longer at UO.
Dr. Ki is a great teacher. She has a great sense of humor.
Professor Ki was always available to help students and willing to listen to. Great professor!

Prof. Ki was very easy to work with and was always very helpful. She has great interpersonal skills enthusiasm for teaching and subject matter.

Fabienne cares about her students and makes our workload highly enriching yet super fun and engaging. She gives a lot of feedback on assignments, and is very personable and understanding. I've taken two classes with her but would love to sign up for more!

She is genuinely one of the best professors I've had in college. I've taken multiple classes with her, and she is incredibly kind, accommodating, and truly cares about her students. She's a super kind and caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. She grades fairly and is always supportive. Attendance is mandatory, but she's very lenient and if you miss class, you can make it up with extra work. One of the sweetest professors I've had!

Dr. Fausey was a great professor! She did what she could to engage students and encourage cooperation, and was very helpful and supportive even outside of class. The coursework was pretty easy and the grading was not too strict. A lot of chapters of reading were assigned, but she covered everything from the textbook pretty well in lectures.

I took this class during COVID, and it was the easiest class I've ever taken. Dr. Fausey made sure we had plenty of time for questions, and kept the homework load extremely light. There was a short assignment and a class activity each week, four easy quizzes, and a short research paper for our final. Easy class with a kind teacher!

Professor Fausey is very understanding and is very caring of her students' mental health. She was always sure to check on us as we were going through COVID, and she would try to help alleviate any anxieties that we had. She is an all around amazing teacher and person.

Would not recommend.

Since when is nerdy a bad thing?! Dr. Fausey is awesome and hilarious! Very fair on grading. Teaches all you need to know during the lectures and doesn't require you to buy a textbook. Doesn't seem that interested in students; more likely more interested in research. Shows favoritism for sure. Her lectures are good she just isn't a people person. She is nerdy and thinks she is funny. It is not funny when you fail students on quizzes for responses that do not meet the unreachable answers.

A reading summary is due for every class, which gets uninteresting fairly quickly. Group work is required about once a week and the exams are fairly easy. She is great to go to if you want to talk about grad school. I liked this course because it goes into detail on therapy treatments.

Michelle is an amazing professor. She is extremely knowledgeable about psychopathologies. Her lectures are engaging and informative. Attendance is not required unless doing a group assignment, but showing up to every lecture is extremely beneficial.

One of my fave classes and professors! Really shocked by other persons rating b/c I came here to say she was super awesome. Really nice, structure of the class is really manageable, not too many assignments and allows for missing some classes. Midterm/Final were very doable. Would def take again.

Really sweet professor! Participation is required but the workload isn't intense. Easy to communicate with as well after class. However the syllabus was a bit vague and confusing.
There's a lot of unnecessary reading and the lectures are mandatory but nothing overly important usually happens in them. She's a super nice person, and I would take a class with her again though.

. Within the fall of 2023 this class was definitely the easiest one I was taking. Feba is super nice, caring and extremely easy to reach outside of class. Attendance is mandatory , the class is extremely laid-back
 things about

She's a good professor for a freshman or sophomore to take. She has a relaxed and quiet class atmosphere and she's generally nice and very knowledgeable. Not much weekly work at all, just read the material and you're fine. Only notes, she is a slow grader, attendance matters for your grade, and there is a 7-10 page paper at the end of the term.

He was so kind,  you could tell he truly cared about his students and their well-being. There is a weekly writing response, but as long as you read your textbook they're fairly easy, He was great and recommended
100% worth it to take this course.

great guy and professor. He was a cop for over 20 years and really knows what hes talking about. So passionate, and brings in the greatest stories to aid the lectures. Tons of guest speakers for various topics. There was a weekly reading assignment, 2 mini papers, and a final paper (that's it). I felt like i was learning w/o being overwhelmed.

Mao Laoshi is the sweetest. She is very encouraging and helps you to gain confidence in your Chinese speaking voice. I used to be more shy about speaking in class, but now it is easier to talk because she is so welcoming to your participation.
Took Mao Laoshi last year and she was great. Super caring and respectful teacher and genuinely wants to help you learn Chinese. Would take again 10/10

Mao Laoshi is the best teacher I think I have ever had. She is so clear and helpful, and she really makes the most complex parts of Chinese seem easy when learning from her. the class is a little hard because it is Chinese, of course it's hard. the mao laoshi wants you to succeed and will make sure you do. she is so kind and the feedback is amazing

Mao Laoshi is a phenomenal teacher. She goes the extra mile to make sure students really understand grammar points and she cares about her students learning outcomes. She is one of the most genuinely nice professors I've ever met. 10/10 would recommend taking her class you will learn a lot.

Fengjun Mao is simply great at teaching. You'll get clear examples, explanations, and all students are involved. The class is really well organized, Mao is always on top of things. Even though attendance is not graded, come to every class and do the homework w/o cutting corners. Prepare to participate because you will be called on. Fun projects too

Some explanations in lectures were convoluted and hard to understand. Not the best communicator in lectures, but he's easy to talk to and get help from in class or office hours. Weekly homework, sometimes challenging. You're allowed a note sheet on midterms and the final, and the study guides were always pretty accurate to what was on the exams.

Michael Feigen was cool. He taught the concepts straightforward and gave examples. Webwork homework wasn't easy, but was very useful to learn. 2 midterms and one final (comprehensive). He allowed one full sheet of notes (front and back) on each test, no restrictions so you could include entire examples if you wanted. No extra credit though.
Michael was very helpful. He gave us extra credit points and if you go to class, you will get a good grade. Even if you're confused or feel lost, he makes sure to help out so you will be successful.

Fern was amazing! So passionate and it felt like talking to another student. I had them for Trig. and I would absolutely take it again. I wasn't the best at math but they made my day worth while. Fern is more laid back and just wants to help you succeed.

Easily the best teacher I have ever had. Taught in a very clear and easy to understand way and wished they taught upper level math classes too. Grades are based on weekly homework, quizzes, a midterm, a final. Can do correction to get back credit on quizzes and midterm. Feel as if it would be very difficult to do bad in these class

Fern was a really enjoyable prof for someone with bad experiences in math. I really enjoyed the flexibility of this class, Fern cares a lot about how students do. Office hours were offered all the time and lots (I) utilized them. Weekly quizzes & homework, a midterm and a final. Very straightforward and easy to follow/remember expectations.

this professor atually cares about the learning of their students, their lectures are in depth and explains steps and the why's of the material. They are easy to follow, provide help and accommodations, and create a sound learning environment. they have weekly webwork but they create their own questions so the webwork makes sense to the classwork.
Great class. Fern is very understanding and very much wants their students to learn!

Fern was a fantastic instructor compared to others I've had. They really care and want you to succeed. I feel more prepared for future math courses and have more confidence in my math ability. You would have to really mess up to not pass their class. Go to their office hours they will make sure that you understand!

Martina's lectures are amazing and so informative that you only really need to skim the readings. She's a great person but very rigorous.

Martina had an excellent and clear-cut structure for her online Medical Ethics class. She posts lecture slides to complement the readings and help significantly for understanding the material for the quizzes. Quizzes are also fairly easy so long as you read and study ahead of time. Well organized and simple.

Martina is the most articulate, professional, and intelligent professor you could ask for in an ethics class. She's extremely generous to arguments and is clear and attentive to detail. While she is challenging, taking a class feels so rewarding with her. She's also an excellent writer if you ever have time to read her work.

Though sometimes difficult, Martina spent an exceptional amount of time with the content and cared so much that her students understood the material. She spent extensive amounts of time on Kant when we were struggling to grasp his theories and she even made handouts to make things easier.

She's one of the best philosophy instructor I've had to date. Not only is Martina inspiring in that she delves super deep into the texts, but she encourages class participation and engagement. Her main goal was always to make sure students understand some of the most complicated philosophical theories. Spent 4 weeks on Kant.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Unfortunately you will often not get through the texts with Ferrari, but that's philosophy. She's admirable for not merely summarizing the textsReadings are dense and lengthy, but she clears them up with her lectures and discussions. She's great at connecting with students on a personal level and is a joy to talk to. Very knowledgeable about ethics

Quizzes are supposed to test if you've read but her quizzes require that you memorize every line of the text. She asks extremely detailed questions that were never addressed in class. Might be able to improve her course with powerpoints and less dense readings. She's has great insight but she's more suited for upper div courses. Not an intro class.

Martina is passionate about philosophy and really explains the concepts well. She is really accessible by email and office hours and is willing to help you. That is, she assigns lots of readings and the quizzes are based on the readings. She is a tough grader, so be ready for that. Other than that, she's great and I would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great lectures and discussion-oriented class. You get a lot out of it just by communicating with peers. That said she needs to cool it with the grading. The class average for quizzes should not be a D in a class of 34 students. She's got personality though and explains reading very well. Easy to understand if you've read beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Martina's a great professor. She can be repetitive, but you get something out of her class every day. The level of depth she goes into the readings is astounding yet so applicable to your everyday life. You will find yourself thinking about the topics addressed in class all the time. Truly made an impact on how I think about life and decisions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ferrari isn't the easiest grader. She makes you work hard for it but she has good intentions. She's extraordinarily passionate about philosophy and her biases never show. She stays objective and is super engaging with both her lectures and discussion. She's encouraging and makes the mornings go by so fast. Lots of reading. Get ready to think!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Engaging and knowledgeable. John Fenn possesses a vast and diverse range of knowledge. Expect as much attention and energy as you put in.
John's a good guy who is obviously knowledgeable about music but this class is soooooo boring. That isn't really his fault.

baah so boring. he's a good guy, but still... it was so hard to pay attention to stuff.  i don't think i learned much of anything in that class.  this was supposed to be my fun/easy elective course, but look what happened.  i got A's and B's except for this class... I got a SIIIIIIiiiiiiiii.

John Fenn is a very straight forward professor that gives you the main point of the case studies and asks students to give their perspective on the information provided by the novels. The midterms are take home essays and the final is a comprehensive reflection on the material covered during the class. Very easy upper division course.
No Comments

Good class to take for Arts + Letters. Tests are easy if you study, assignments can be long but aren't too hard. It's very clear what you have to do to get an A and worth the mostly boring lectures (there are guest speakers that are cool though).
Such an incredible professor!! I HIGHLY recommend this class. His lectures are very engaging and the assignments are very easy yet interesting. This class made me very excited about astronomy again.
This was a very easy and interesting class, little work and an amazing guy

I really liked Fisher and would take his class again! Super easy credit and you can tell he really cares about his students. Easy weekly quizzes that have the answers in the slides he goes over. Videos can sometimes feel long but he makes them engaging even online. There is a textbook but we only read a couple chapters and it's free.
Genuinely the kindest professor I have ever had. So caring and genuine. Take his class!!!

Dr. Fisher was the best professor I've had at UO. He has the best approach to learning Astronomy! His lectures are easy to learn from and clear to understand. If you need a science credit, take this course! He is a really easy grader; as long as you apply yourself, you'll do great!

Dr. Fisher is the BEST!! He's an amazing professor that actually cares about his students. I don't like or really care much for astronomy but Dr. Fisher changed that. You can really tell he enjoys what he does and he just wants to share that with you. If you have a chance to take a class with him do it, you won't regret it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fisher is the best! As someone who struggles with understanding science, he is a good teacher to help you understand what is going on in class. He is very enthusiastic about astronomy which makes the class enjoyable. He assigns small quizzes and a major part of your grade is determined by exams.  Overall, I recommend taking a class with him!!
Professor Fisher is an extremely entertaining lecturer. Coming to class never felt like a chore. He obviously cares a lot about astronomy and I learned some interesting things in this class.

the BEST professor at UO hands down. his lectures were so entertaining that I actually wanted to attend them and he is such a nice guy. sit down in class and you will do well in the class. studied for a couple hours for the midterm and I got a B. overall 10/10.

Fisher's name is known around campus for a reason. He's intellectual and hilarious, but caring. At first the class will seem like kind of a joke because expectations are pretty low - quizzes, 2 tests, and a final. You'll learn to appreciate his teaching style and how he stresses science literacy. You should not graduate from UO w/o taking ASTR 122.

Dr. Fisher is an amazing professor! His lectures are organized and engaging. He is very passionate about teaching students about science. Attending lectures isn't mandatory because he posts all of the slides online, but he makes lectures so entertaining that you'll want to go! Super funny, down-to-earth, and always willing to help students.

This class was amazing! I took it to complete my science requirement and did not regret it. This class is easy but you also learn so much from the professor. He is funny, engaging, and is willing to help you to the best of his ability. You can tell he is well educated in his field and he is very passionate about teaching and his student's success!!

Dr. Fisher is amazing. This class is by far the coolest class I have ever taken, and Dr. Fisher genuinely loves educating students. Its clear that he is passionate about what he teaches, and I highly recommend this class.

Dr. Fisher is hands-down the best professor you can have here at the UO, he is genuinely passionate about what he teaches and who he teaches to. He wants to see his students succeed so he is always available and responds quickly to emails. He is funny and wants people to enjoy his class. He wants everyone to be involved in science and loves to talk

Professor Fisher is one of the best professors I've taken a class from. He cares about his student's success and is genuinely such a hilarious teacher. The class wasn't mandatory and he posted everything online but I literally wanted to go to his class every day. Really interesting topics and learned a lot about space and the solar system!!

Fisher is hands down the best professor I've ever had. A caring, extremely smart human being. His lectures are engaging, super funny and well organized. I can't say enough good things about this man. Take his course! He truly care about simplifying and teaching science literacy. The quizzes are simple and exams are well put together.

Dr. Fisher is a super fun professor who is honestly amazing! You take three 40 to 50 question exams throughout the term and a summary quiz for each video lecture, which you can directly look at the slides for so super easy!

Easy class while still effectively teaching about the subject even with the online limitations. No assignments are unnecessarily difficult in the slightest, and grading is pretty clear so I didn't need to send emails. While only having the quizzes open on Fridays was annoying sometimes, it's not that big of a deal since it's 10 minutes long :)

This class was just ridiculously hard. The professor absolutely intends for everyone to fail. He will assign 1-2 hours of lecture, documentaries, 65+ pages of reading and more just for a 10 question quiz that will only have incredibly niche questions said one time in the middle of the enormous reading. Worst class I've ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class graded only on async tests that were not related to reading. Very tedious, time consuming work. Teacher is not accomidating.

I tried getting in contact with him for a week, he never returned a single email of mine, nor responded to a single canvas message of mine. He was not present in his office hours during any of the times I joined, despite my joining during the periods of time he outlined on his canvas. He should not be a teacher.

I think that on the inside Scott is a good man, but, his way of teaching isn't great in my opinion. Every time I went to office hours, he would be very passive aggressive and made me feel stupid. He also would never really directly answer questions. Warning, there is A LOT of reading for this course, one week we had 76 pages and 3 quizzes to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns 4-5 assignments due on a Friday night for a 100 class, locks quizzes till the day of, to then get an email from him complaining to his students how he isn't getting paid enough so he may join strike. Most community college professors are for more talented at teaching then this guy. Seems like he took the job to sell his book and that's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have had Scott for 2 classes now, he is very passive aggressive, he doesn't seem to actually care about teaching or his students. He expects you to memorize very specific facts/details that he barely covers in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too much information taught for a 10 question quiz a week and it's nearly impossible to get 100% unless you can remember every niche detail from the lectures. The professor is actually very sweet though and he usually curves the class grade because he realizes people often struggle. I would highly recommend talking to him outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Second week into class we have 5 assignments due all on Friday, one of which is quiz he locked until THE day it was due which is completely brain dead if you ask me. Its almost as if he wants us to cram things until the last minute when he locks assignments until the day of. Terrible teacher for an asynchronous class. Not sure how he works here lol

Absolute worst class I've taken in 4 years. They say to email with any questions but when you do he won't answer the question and/or will make you feel stupid for even asking. 7 lectures, 3 quizzes, 4 inquizitives and 2 labs per week and occasionally a big test included with that. That is way too much work for one student.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Scott doesn't provide useful feedback to his students, and throws questions at you that are not covered within the course. Furthermore, he is very obiously proud of his work, as the only textbooks used for any of his courses are written by himself. Not a very motivating professor.

He tests on the most obscure information from lectures/readings rather than the basic and important information. He WILL require you to remember names and dates, and he will assign 100+ pages of reading PER WEEK. For any other class, you would be fine as long as you can grasp the overarching ideas from the readings, but not this one.

Gives quizzes that don't connect to the material and doesn't give feedback on quizzes when the average is 60% weekly, assignments usually have vague wording, expects us to read over 100 pages per week AND hours of lectures AND extra videos (as if we don't have other classes). Worst class I've ever taken in my 3 years at UO, horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst ANTH prof by far. Each quiz was super complicated and was hard to connect to readings/lectures and the prof gets surprised when the quiz averages are 65% and below. Also gives absolutely no feedback on assignments. This class is not worth it.

Overall this class was cool content-wise, it is entirely the professor that made this class horrible.  Weeks 1-10 we had weekly quizzes and I do not recall a week when these 10 point quizzes averages were above 65%.  He would tell us the average but give ZERO feedback as to how to improve. Also dropped the "cumulative" bomb the day before the final
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material was interesting, but Scott would give lectures with material that didn't show up on assignments/exams. There also were several hiccups during the class - which is expected with everything being online, but it always felt like we had to figure it out when the mistakes happened on his end. Not the worst class, but certainly not the best
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy and goes on tangents about things that are not related to the course, so it is difficult to know what will be on the tests. The course is not hard, but the tests have so much information that is not taught which has an impact on your grade. Unless you have previous knowledge on archaeology, then I don't recommend taking this course.

Fitzpatrick is lecture heavy and does not always explain things well. He then blamed the class when they didn't do well on the midterm. He is passionate about Anth but gets caught up in his stories and sometimes misses the important stuff which affects how well you do on the midterm.

Assigns lots of smaller assignments that, once added together, count for a good portion of the total grade. Just be cautious of his tests and study well for them. He provides a study guide for the tests, but they don't correlate very well to the tests. Also, go to lectures. Lots of info & he does NOT post lecture slides online, so don't miss them.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very interesting class if you ever had an Indiana Jones phase (or fantasy) and Scott really knows his stuff and will work with you to make sure you succeed in the class. Attendance not mandatory but it's hard to pass if you miss a lecture. Grade is primarily what is done in lab and tests so you do have to be ready to give this class hands effort
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is passionate about his class, he does not post lectures online so coming to class is important but if you do go its easy to pass the class. The labs are easy, the online homework is easy, the tests are a little hard to study for because he doesnt put anything online.

Very interesting class. Dr. Fitzpatrick has a lot of first hand experience which makes his lectures enjoyable. The tests are a little challenging, but the homework and labs are pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really loved Professor Fitzpatrick! He has lots of personal knowledge about archaeology and loves to share it with the class. His lectures sometimes got a little boring, but make sure to go because he doesn't put the slides online! Also, section is a lot of hands-on exercises, both inside and out. Overall interesting and not too hard.

Great Professor! I had him at L&C for Bioethics. He gives students the freedom to decide how they want to spend their time in class, but lectures passionately and with authority. A good amount of reading, but skimming will do.

NOT A uO CLASS RATING- I took him for core at LC in Portland, and he is the best, I loved having him so much. a lot of reading but you can get away with not doing it, he's super caring and seriously such a good teacher.

Devin is a great guy. He accommodated well to students, replied to emails pretty fast, and didn't grade unfairly at all. He was both funny and kept people awake when he talked as you could tell he actually cared about what he was teaching about. Would recommend.

An amazing teacher. I took the class for my arts and letters requirement but he made me want to take another philosophy class. Super clear grading criteria and available outside of class to help. Make sure to attend class and participate and you'll do great. He shows both sides of the issue and is a great instructor.

Devin is one of the best professors I've ever had. I wasn't excited to take philosophy since I was just trying to get the credit- but he made it so interesting. He somehow made me engaged and excited to learn at 9 in the morning 4 times a week. He also cares a lot about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed and grasp the material.

Phenomenal teacher who's passion for philosophy is inspiring to students, he makes the most in depth philosophical reading comprehndable and creates a space where everyone feels comfortable speaking their mind. His class is why I came to college.

Great instructor. His ability to professionally engage and connect with students, and explain concepts in academic but understandable terms, made for an involved and exciting classroom. The two-hour classes were never tedious. Devin is encouraging on an individual level as well. You will come away more interested in feminism and philosophy.
If you are a bad test taker do not even try her class.

TESTS. Do not take if you are a bad test taker like myself. You would think if the class average on every test was failing that there would be a curve or something like that but she doesn't do that. She was nice to communicate with and understanding.

Absolute Battle-axe, no nonsense. Course is very well put together and well taught though. Difficult, heavy workload, does its job of weeding out the weak. The stuff she makes you do which seems annoying (ALEX, large homework load) actually helps a lot with retaining the material. Takes a lot of work ethic but you can do well in it. Good luck!

For an asynchronous class I feel like her lectures were great, and I learned a lot. Fair warning though, this class is fairly difficult and test averages were around 65% for each, you have to study a lot.
Dr. Exton's fantastic at explaining tricky concepts and set up her class to allow any student to succeed if they just put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Keep up with ALEKS and do practice exams and you will be good. There were a ton of office hour options too which was nice. She was always happy to answer questions.
Many tests throughout the term and they're super hard without enough time. Teacher is understanding sometimes but also grades heavily based on participation so you have to be there everyday

The gen chem curriculum is rigorous- much of what people complain about have to do with the class itself, not the instructor. The material has to be taught very quickly, so she can't spend too much time on one topic. However, if you go to office hours, she will walk you through problems and reexplain concepts. You just have to go and ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She was the coolest and pretty understanding. Topics weren't super difficult and she did a great job explaining everything. Wish she taught CH222.
Not flexible

Dr. Exton is a solid professor but is not one that I would recommend to many. She's clearly passionate about chemistry but is not entirely effective at lecturing and giving information. She gives so many exams and they are all worth a solid chunk of your grade. Overall, I would take her if you have to, but look into alternate professors if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I only had her for the lab lecture. Very little amount of helpful instruction. I wouldn't have attended lectures if they didn't use iClickers for participation points. You definitely need to go to every lab session, though. Pre-labs and lab reports will take you hours to finish, especially because the guidelines are so vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: ehhh. Shes not a terrible teacher, she explains content pretty thoroughly in lectures. However, there is SO much homework. Be prepared to do enough work for 2 courses. And tests are pretty hard. Its very hard to keep up with everything in this course.

Chem is always hard, but Exton was actually a pretty good teacher. She listens to the feedback you give her and she does lots of example problems. The best way to survive in this class is to go to Superchem if you need help with the homework and go as much as you can. You do not want to fall behind, so go to office hours too. Lots of work to do ok
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Shes an alright professor, I wouldnt really recommend her, the class itself isnt horrible but you just have to stay on top of your work, I personally didnt use true text book or go to office hours but I recommend it.

Exton is a solid professor. It is explicitly clear that she knows chem, but she is not the most effective lecturer. She often fails to explain concepts clearly. However, she is a very nice woman and easy to listen to. It is easy to stay engaged and it is made explicitly clear what is expected... however, tests can be very difficult.

My biggest issue with the way she taught this class was that the homework assignments had to be completed before the lecture in which we actually learned the topics. Four times a week I would slog through assignments just to actually get an explanation the next day. Very frustrating. We also had 3 midterms and a final which wasn't ideal.

Debby brings a smile to your face. Her sidekick Mark and her have a lil something going on. They love to do demonstrations in class. The classis in fact difficult and you work for your grade but it is not debby's fault that we are not as talented as her. In full honesty this class is hard but do-able. Doing the Aleks sucks but helps review topics.
I love Dr. Exton! She is very smart and is a very good teacher. Easy to learn from. Don't be scared for Gen. Chem!!!

Prof. Exton has a ton of quizzes and tests every three weeks. She is a tough grader and her lectures are hard to follow, and sometimes what her TAs say doesnt match what she says. Pretty much self-taught myself through this class. Its manageable if youre self-sufficient, but maybe consider another Professor if youre not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expect at least 2 assignments a day PLUS three tests every 2 weeks that count for most of your grade. Says she uses a (fake) proctoring system during tests, and office hours are just extra hw. Made us spend a crazy amount of money on ALEKS and a book SHE WROTE, you teach yourself the whole time and do busy work, cant remember a thing i learned.

I learned absolutely nothing but I passed. The online format with the daily videos and aleks is a poor system. I learn mostly from outside sources that are actually banned. Im a chem major and I know the next classes I take are going to be humbling. Three giant tests that are most of your grade (more than half) and they are two hours each.

Exton is by far the best professor I've had during online. The lectures and quizzes are short and straightforward if you pay attention. The class is hard but she provides a lot of outside resources and extra help. Use the textbook and go to review sessions. I never had her in person, but online Exton was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach anything, I learned most of this course from outside materials and skipping through her lectures for answers. She only cares about homework and exam scores so if you don't want to spend 6 hours a day teaching yourself doing 6 different assignments, don't take her class

This class is TOUGH and I don't struggle with science. Changed majors bc I had to take 3 of these. There are 2-4 assignments per day and three two hour finals throughout the term. The homework is repetitive and is busy work, I rarely learned anything from it. Office hours usually have a set lesson plan so you can't go in to just ask a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exton is your typical old school professor that only cares about whether or not you do her assignments. Her online class was basically self taught bc she didn't even have zoom lecture. Doesn't give extra credit opp, doesn't curve ANYTHING, doesn't have student's best interest. The test for this course are literally 65% of your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the class online it's so much work. She told us at the beginning to plan to spend 20 hours a week on the course and there are multiple things due everyday. We had to buy two online programs, one textbook, and two more textbooks if you take the lab. The tests were confusing and so much of your grade. It's clearly a weed-out course.

I only had to take her again because it's required and she's the only one that teaches it. There's so much assignments that we don't even go over in the lectures and the exams were hard and confusing. The exams are worded weirdly and long which is super confusing. The exams weigh so much and impacts our grade by a ton if you miss a few problem.

There isnt anything special, but Exton is certainly a decent professor. The lectures were relevant, and the course wasnt that difficult. As long as you did the reading, there shouldnt be any problem passing. Sometimes the course and grading guidelines were disorganized, but nothing that couldnt be figured out before assignments were due.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Only problem with Professor Exton are her exams. To get a good grade you cant afford to miss more than three or four questions, but some of the questions cover abstract material never covered in class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was the reason why I transferred out of UO. Dr. Exton is very intelligent but makes it very obvious that she doesn't care about how students do in her class. For our comprehensive final exam, she cautioned us to "pick a letter of the day" for the questions we didn't answer because there was no way we could finish the final.

Dr. Exton was a good professor for CH221! I had her online so the lectures were confusing at times, but she is always available for office hours and willing to help you with whatever you need in order to succeed. Make sure you stay on top of the lectures and homework - there is a good amount of work to do but it is easy to manage.

Sigh. There were instances where answers were incorrectly marked on canvas for lecture quizzes, the lecture videos themselves just repeat the textbook, you have to pay an exorbitant amount of money on TWO DIFFERENT learning programs (Aleks isn't bad after the Prerequisite assignment though. Also holds proctoring over you to guilt trip you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know if it is because of the transition to online that has made her worse but I don't know a single person that enjoys her class. Her online lectures are not helpful and the TA's don't ever make anything clear. What really made me upset was that she assigned our longest homework the day after thanksgiving.

Exton requires you to buy the textbook that SHE WROTE for a crazy amount of money. Not organized and when the lab class was put online, she was not prepared to do that. She changes deadlines and mixes up the way that canvas works.
An absolute gem once you've taken other chemistry professors. I wish I would've stayed with Exton all year if she taught it.

Tbh, I prefer Exton over some of the other professors that I have had. She makes her expectations clear and tells students what they need to do to succeed. As others said, she isnt the best at teaching, but she manages to get through slides and will ask for any clarifications. She even will devote a few days to explain how to study and learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Exton is fine as a professor. She isn't always super available for students and usually has her TA's deal with everything. In terms of teaching, she does her best to teach a difficult subject. She isn't amazing but she also isn't the worst. Chem is a subject that you really need to study for so attend class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Exton is amazing! I've taken the same class from another professor at UO, and the difference is crazy. Dr. Exton is very knowledgeable and passionate about science, and due to her experience teaching (close to 30 years) she knows how to present the topics in a clear and interesting way, while cutting out all the unnecessary information.
She gives many examples and explains the chem thoroughly. The class was HARD but she did a good job teaching it. Prepare to Study!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You learn a lot if you really put in the effort. There is ton of help available all of the time and she cares about your grade. Grades go in pretty quick. Listen to the tips about how to study. Do what you're supposed to do from the start and you'll earn the grade you want!

There is a huge curve in this class, homework heavily boosts your grade and Exton is an AMAZING teacher. She also teaches you HOW to be a better learner which is great for first term college students.

Deborah is an amazing teacher, who really understands the craft of Chemistry. She really wants to help her students learn, however the content is insanely hard. Read chapters BEFORE going to lecture, their review them again. Her study cycle in her syllabus isn't a joke, I highly recommend following it. Overall great class, just be prepared.

Exton is really an amazing professor and wants you to succeed. She gets that chem can be hard to jump into and gives multiple opportunities for you to do well. Sapling, Aleks, and clicker q's make a great grade cushion and will honestly bump your grade up a good 7 percent as long as you complete it all. If you want to succeed in this class you will
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was not good at teaching and not helpful when asking questions. Was expected to just know how to do things without her even bringing it up in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Exton's way of teaching. The class is hard but going to class and taking good notes will get you a good grade. The exams reflect the clicker questions in class along with a few about the concepts learned in class and are not terribly difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Exton is a very sweet and caring person. She is extremely approachable and loves it when students ask her questions. She won't be annoyed if you ask something stupid. The lectures seem pretty long, but she keeps them interesting; she puts a lot of memes in her slideshows. Success in the course takes effort, but is very possible.

Deborah is great. 20/10, would recommend. Super fun, wears costume on halloween. Tests are hard, just study. Read the book! Preview and review. Go to office hours if needed, she's fun. Don't skip any ALEKS or Sapling, trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very hard course. Be sure to show up to each class to get credit and do all of the homework. Read the textbook outside of class and probably get a tutor too because it's fast paced and easy to get behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She expects her students to be very knowledgeable about chemistry from the start. She wrote the textbook but she never referenced it. By far the hardest class I have ever taken and I would not recommend unless you NEED it for your major. Tests are extremely hard and you will constantly be doing online homework every week. Falling behind is SO easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Exton is a phenomenal professor, extremely knowledgeable and really does care about chemistry. There is a lot of homework, but the homework is almost like a study guide and it helps a lot so do it! if chm221 is required for your major, definitely recommend Dr. Exton!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Exton is a solid teacher. Not the most interesting lectures, and the material is somewhat difficult, so you must put in effort outside of class, very possible to get a good grade though.
Very nice person, decent teacher. Has good lecture slides and usually explains clearly. She tells you what she expects from you which is very helpful.

Final grade relies heavily on the midterms and final, but if you can follow along in class you will do fine. You do have to study, but there's not many topics that are hard to understand. There's lots of office hours you can go to and SUPERchem helps a lot.

Dr. Exton is super passionate about teaching and wants her students to succeed. Do the online homework on time so you don't fall behind in the class and always do the practice exams before taking her tests. It's a challenging class, but if you pay attention and put the effort into it, it'll be worth your while.

Be prepared to work extra hard for a good grade in this class. You will have to truly understand the material, go to office hours or tutoring, read the book, and practice chemistry problems on your own in order to succeed. This course is demanding, but the professor cares about all the students understanding.

Make sure to attend lectures! Chemistry is no easy A, but read the textbook & go through lecture slides for clarification. Just do practice problems  and go to office hours if you need help. Great professor and class overall!
Deborah would not take time to discuss grade and was very unhelpful.
Gives plenty of recourses to study for exams, but you have to put in the time to utilize them.  Homework is all online which is either lame or cool depending on your own perspective.
Really hard class to get a high grade in. The average on the exams are around a 65% so study your ass off in order to get the grade you want.

Examples are not very clear, wastes alot of time with technical issues (daily basis), weekly homework, almost daily learnsmart online,  lots of reading needed to understand the class, delays on posting grades, tough tests, tends to get irritable with noise from people in the lecture hall. retaking class to understand material before going on.
She's very clear, her voice isn't irritating like some professors, and she always brings her dog to office hours
Hard course. You will have to work your butt off to get an A in the final class in the general chemistry series. The professor is highly recommended.
Great professor! Highly recommended.

Absolutely great professor. Highly recommended. Personally, I just transferred out of The University of Oregon and will greatly miss her. She makes extremely hard concepts easy to understand. If you need help, she is willing to schedule an appointment and also has fantastic office hours. Read the book before you go to class if you want an A.

Chemistry is a difficult enough subject on its own. It certainly doesn't need the added benefit of exams designed to be deliberately misleading to help it along. Exams list incorrect solutions or "correct" ones with rounding errors as possible choices to mislead you into thinking you did the problem correctly. Decent lecturer, but beware of exams.
Tough class. Good instruction. Midterm 1 and 2 pretty hard. Final exam slightly easier. Spend plenty of time on this class. Don't take this class with other difficult classes unless you have no job.

Chemistry is a pretty content heavy class...and has some pretty tough material to learn but Dr. Exton does a really good job of breaking it up and explaining it. Compared to what I've heard about other professors, I would recommend picking Exton. You still have to work hard, but she will help you through it!

I love Exton! She is extremely nice and funny in class. She keeps class interesting which can be hard with Chemistry. She is very clear and doesn't mind trying different styles of teaching if one way doesn't seem to work. She's a great Chem teacher and you'll miss her when you move on to Chimploys class.

Wonderful professor!  Her midterms and final is challenging, but if you've studied hard and kept up with the material you'll do well.  She explains things clearly, so even though she's a tough teacher, she teaches you so well that if you study, you'll be fine.

LOVE this professor. She is an angel and the sweetest, compassionate lady who is also brilliant and makes chemistry as painless as possible, even though the material is difficult. Best chemistry professor at UO!

Tests are standardized,avg. of 20 questions. Students who put tremendous effort getting extra help average C's while those who don't are peaking at F's. A lot of information, not sure what is important vs. what isn't. More explanation on concepts are needed, not only examples. It's a conceptual thing and if students don't get the concept they fail.

She is very intelligent and clearly conveyed the topics she was discussing, however there is SO much absolutely essential info that she does not cover in the lectures and it's extremely hard to keep up. There are no quizzes but two midterms and a final and the midterms (20 multiple choice Q's) are extremely hard.

She is a great teacher, and truly cares about her students. Most UO teachers are there for the research, but for her it's just a bonus. She isn't confusing, but the homework can be--and doesn't always correspond with what she's taught so you have to guess and check the answer to get it right.

I remember going into her class nervous because people told me her tests were much harder than the other professors'. But she is such a god teacher and she does examples in class that are exactly like all the ones on her tests. I really didn't find myself studying for that long before each test, but you do need to study. Don't expect an A without.

I really liked her! She does expect you to do some studying on your own but I took chem in high school and found this class pretty easy. She follows the chapters in the book closely and posts notes online, so if you miss something it's easy to catch up. She did a really good job at using examples and doing demos to explain the material. Recommend.

Overall, I think she's a great teacher, but her tests are hard. We have iClicker questions almost everyday, which means attendance is pretty mandatory or you will lose those points for that day. Luckily for 221, we didn't have any quizzes but the midterms and final are such a huge percentage of your grade, so take it if you're a good test taker

Extremely smart, and teaches well but hw is hard and the tests are just like the homework. the midterms are 20 questions multiple choice (harder than it sounds) so its hard to get a good grade if you screw up on only a few problems, no partial credit.
Exton definitely knows her Chemistry, but her articulation and teaching is a bit unclear. I had her for the labs, but she still seems to zip through the slides and assume the majority understands.

Professor Exton was wonderful. She is a very, very intelligent woman and knows her chemistry. Science was never my strong subject, but I was able to pass her lab because she explained in wonderful detail. I would say anyone could pass her class as long as they attend lecture and ask questions if they get confused!
I'm a non trad student, and this was my first science class is almost 8 years. She did an amazing job, kept lectures interesting, and the tests reflected her lectures fabulously!

Dr. Exton seems like a very intelligent, strong woman but she did not impress me as a lecturer. She moved very quickly through slides and seemed to expect students to already be familiar with advanced chemistry concepts. I had her for lab (so I only heard her lecture 4-5 times) and chose to avoid her for lecture class (chem 221).
Notes are misleading regarding homework and tests

Professor Exton is a very concise teacher who is obviously very intelligent and knows chemistry well.  She can water down hard chemistry well enough for intro chem. students and make it easy and comprehensible enough for anyone to pass. Going to class  is really, really helpful.

Deborah Exton waters down each lab until they are basic tutorials for fools. The grading rubrics are flawed and you will not learn how to write a college level lab report coming out of general chemistry. I feel scared and extremely unprepared for higher level lab classes because of her poor teaching and even poorer TA selection
She is so great! Just take time to study for this class and you will do fine!

Does not evaluate situations with a logical thought process.  Is not there to help the student succeed 100%,and is more about generality keeping all students  regulated to guidelines no matter if the circumstances are very obvious to go another way.
Dr. Exton is a great Chem professor. She is challenging but really willing to help you. You will learn way more than with the other chem professors.

Chem is a difficult subject- so keep that in mind when you take it! She makes clear what to memorize and uploads notes and test answer keys so you can check your progress. Also good at keeping students informed on chemistry help sessions if you still feel lost... not bad!?
she should not be teaching. Average grade was D- on the midterm.
This class is horrible

i went to every class and still did porrrly. her tests are non do-able. Difficult to understand. Lots of trick questions. Gen chem is not her cup of tea. Lots better at Chem lab lecture. She expects u to already know the things that shes teaching..like its review. =(

Dr. Exton is one of the best teachers that I've taken at the university. Chemistry is a tough subject, but if you put effort into the class and ask questions she makes everything as clear as possible. Her tests are tricky, but very understandable if you actually take the time to study the information. If you fail, it's your fault, not hers.

This is such a hard class to take.  After I failed her midterm I stopped going to her classes and started going to professor Herrick's classes (which, by the way are fantastic) and thanks to his classes aced the final and ended up with an A in her class.  Despite her being really nice, she just doesn't cut it as a teacher.

These comments are unfair to Dr. Exton; I found that she was very available to students, even though many did not go to her office hours or set up appointments to see her. I got a D on the first midterm, and then asked her for help. I studied everyday then after and ended up getting an A in the class. Make an effort and you will do well.

Exton is very intelligent but very bad at teaching! She made no attempt to make any of the material interesting! The class average grade on both midterm exams were in the 60's! Randy Sullivan the Lecture demonstrator was a better teacher than Exton!
She is a very nice person, but a horrible teacher. Her class is way hard and her tests are extremely tricky. Her class just makes you feel like you are stupid.
SHE-DEVIL! impossible tests. the quiz and test averages are always around 55% take a hint lady

She is obviously very intelligent, however she seems to feel a need to put waaay too many trick questions, not enough information on tests, does not give you information on your grade until the end of the term, and does not tell you what she expects out of you. you are stuck guessing what she wants all the time. Herrick for Gen. Chem though def.

She was extremely organized, clear and understandable.  Lectures were a must!  They were so clear that I learned best from them.  If you want to learn general chemistry in a way where you ACTUALLY understand it, and want to apply it to more advanced courses like organic chemistry, which is what I did, take her class!  Ochem was easier for me becaus
very easy to understand and open to questions for more clarity
Really clear in class, and good with office hours. Best if you read the material before and after class. All notes listed on website-very helpful.
Best if you do the reading and sample questions before coming to classs
Exton is great, explains things well. Go to her office hours, she is patient and is always willing to help.
Text was better than attending lecture. She talks so much it makes things hard to understand and confusing. Super hard texts. Amazing review sessions before hand though.
No Comments
No Comments
Her tests are hard, but she does a good job of explaining things in class and does an excellent job of helping you out in office hours.
Great prof. Got to be her student as well as peer learning assistant. Not the easiest class but liked the teaching approach.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

I didnt realize how unfair and hard she was until i took my last term with another teacher, She seemed like she was out to 'trick' students. Her test were not representative of the material covered in class. I am glad i swithced.

She gives good examples and suplements the text well. Chem is a hard class and reading the text is required. Exton helps to solidify and explain the confusing topics. She is one of the better chem professors at the univeristy. However, the drawback is that her tests are hell.
she's really nice and you can space out while she's talking and still learn something
She tries to be helpful, but she can be really confusing and boring. It's better to read the text than attend her lecture because she just keeps talking.
She is really nice but I never understood anything she talked about.  She was very confusing.
I sometimes find it tricky to understand him in both German and English. His voice is pretty soft and not the clearest. On the bright side, he grades pretty easily, which is nice!

One of the most unengaging speakers I've ever seen, which is a problem when learning a language. Class consists of Filip slowly and monotonously explaining German grammar, seemingly struggling with both English and German, and hardly giving any opportunities to practice German with your classmates. Nothing sticks in your brain. Avoid at all costs.
No. Not an english or german native speaker.

I took AI for Good as part of the honors college curriculum and I had a good time. I was a beginner to computer science and worried about this class, however, the class was very beginner-friendly. Professor Fickas was always available if you had questions or needed help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Took his AI honors class knowing less than nothing about computer science and it was great! very beginner friendly and you only get homework if you don't finish in class (probably like half the time). super accessible outside class! he even zoomed with me on the weekend when I was sick. super nice guy and recommend the honors class!

Stephen Fickas  is a nice guy and smart about teaching Python, however he forgets to tell you things or doesn't explain things clearly. Also, he didn't follow the actual description for the class. He decided to teach Python database, and the class was supposed to be about algorithms, hardware and networking. Confusing class overall.

Very helpful, and interesting format of lectures. He types code during class, such that the class builds a program all together. He answers questions throughly, and is friendly during class. He also is open to meeting out of class should you have more detailed questions. The projects do take quite a bit of time.
Extremely helpful and caring, one of the best professors in the department.

Fickas is an asset to the department in that he brings in tons of research money, and uses it to give undergrads work experience.  Android development is a nice specialty, though forcing it onto intro students is not a good idea. As far as teaching, he's not good. Has a hard time communicating ideas, poor class structure, and no help with the app.

Although he was a nice guy, I felt this class was disorganized. Lectures were pointless for most of the time, and the lab (Android development) had NOTHING to do with the main topics of the course. I was excited to learn about the theory of CS more, but the pointless Android project basically ruined it. Overall, this class was disappointing.
I really enjoyed the freedom he allowed us in this class. He was more of a peer than a prof. Great guy, great attitude. He let us direct the course material. Complete pleasure to learn from.
Too much work for a 200-level course, but it wasn't that difficult.  Otherwise I'm indifferent.
Programing assignments are very undirected for the level of class. Constantly tried to explain things in analogies that fail to get the point across.
Most of the work not too hard but the programming assignments take way to much time for a 4 credit class.
Great guy, nice sense of humor, and isn't too serious
No Comments

Love Florabelle!! She is so sweet and engaging in class. She gives amazing feedback while dancing and cares deeply about her students. She gives opportunities to participate and engage in the ballet world in Eugene. Her exercises are creative and artistic and challenging enough to not be discouraging but give good opportunities to try new things!
She is so sweet and passionate about teaching salsa. She didn't even have a problem with the people who weren't good dancers as long as they tried.
Her salsa classes are a lot of fun,not too hard to learn, and just a great way to meet people.

Very easy instructor. All the assignments were very easy and coursework wasn't much & she is not a harsh grader. She cancelled class a lot which was very nice so no idea why these ratings are complaining about it, you should be glad. Attendance is required for participation credit but you get to have 4 absences.

Canceled class so much, in theory sounds nice but is honestly very very confusing. On canvas said I had an A but I guess she did not put in the other grades and on my final transcript it says B- which is very frustrating and confusing. Other than that very easy class.
Felt like she cancelled half of our total classes which altered due dates of a lot of assignments. Pretty easy grader and nice teacher but could sometimes get confused with her own info

I had him for Math 251, and he's, overall, a pretty chill guy. He's a very lenient grader; there's a ton of opportunity for partial credit. Some of his exams were kind of hard, but it was unit circle and inverse trig related stuff, so just study up on your own, and you should be good. Also the homework is wayyy harder than quizzes and exams.

Memorization heavy. Only shows so many examples in lecture before moving on to new concepts due to everything we had to learn, it was pretty fast paced. Group work wasn't usually productive. He's a nice guy tho. Office hours are helpful. Also gives partial credit on quizzes/exams if you didn't get the exact right answer which is often clutch.

As someone who is not amazing at math, Joe made the topic actually pretty enjoyable and easy to understand. I would definitely recommend him to anyone who isn't very strong in math. Exams are curved like crazy and he practically tells us what is on the weekly quizzes. He is not very compassionate but is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Foster's class was orginally very challenging for me, as he is fast-paced and doesn't always explain concepts that he believes are universally understood - which is to be expected in a collegate math course. He gave great feedback, gave ample practice materials, little homework, and explained well. The tests were heavily curved.

Not the most exciting topic but Joe still makes it engaging and easy to digest. I'm horrible at math and still managed to get an A- thanks to his extra credit and teaching methods. Not a ton of homework which is nice, but tests are weighted heavily.

It was tough at the beginning because he was still getting used to what we knew, but after the professor review mid-year, all his material became really good. His lectures provided several examples for help, and he provided the subjects that would be on every Friday quiz. Overall, he was fair and understanding and gave generous extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to follow, as he treats the class like a 200+ student lecture, despite there being only 20-30 students. While the subject is complicated, the lack of personality, minimal interaction, and large-class approach make the class unengaging. He also has no drip. Like it's almost distracting.

Uses a ton of examples to explain material. Lecture is average, seems fairly clear in class. Opens up his schedule to accommodate office hours, but doesn't seem super empathetic or lively when you're struggling to understand the material.
If you have a strong memory of all previous math, you'll excel.
No calculators or notes allowed on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mark Fonstand is a great professor all around. He is a little boring, but 360 is a very easy class, and he has some good lecture stories: a few quizzes, some group projects, and a final paper.
He is a very passionate professor! It is clear that he loves the subject and teaching it to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor with very informative and interesting lectures. It is clear that he has a lot of passion for the subject and loves to share it with his students! The assignments are straight forward and his grading is very generous. Highly recommend any course that he is teaching.

Fonstad is an amazing professor. His class is very informative, with approachable assignments and applicable lectures. Professor Fonstad is clearly passionate not only about the subject matter, but engaging his students! I highly reccommend taking class with him if you get the chance.

I took Geomorphology back in 2024, it was a super interesting class. The way Professor Fonstand talks is quite theatrical. He knows a lot about the topic, and the labs were interesting, but could be tricky. There were two midterms and a final; they were challenging, but all multiple choice. One of my favorite classes I ever took at uo.

Any professor who teaches 141 gets a bad wrap. Fonstand has very interesting lectures, very kind and knowledgeable. The class is easy, no tests, only a few quizzes, and group projects. One final paper (2 pages). I really like him; you can tell he really enjoys teaching. I definitely recommend taking his classes.

This for Geography 360, not 485. I have had Mark for 3 different classes so far, super chill guy and really passionate about geography and natural processes of earth. GEOG 360 has been pretty easy, no exams just projects and mini canvas assignments. Very fair grader and accessible outside of class. Lectures can be a bit heavy, but you learn a lot.

The class wasn't bad at all, only reason I'm leaving a negative review is bc I finished with a 90.96% yet I was given a B+. Traditionally anything higher than a 90 is an A, yet professor Fonstad made it so a 90 is a B+. Normally wouldn't complain about something like this, but ngl it kinda screwed up my GPA. The TA Wesley was great, shoutout to him

Lectures were unattended by most and a little boring at some parts, although it had its moments of solidness and he is well versed in it. Material is extremely easy and it is easy to get a good grade if you do the work and that's all you care about. General course that covers lots of parts and climate systems around the world. Simple enough.

Excruciatingly boring lectures. This should not be labeled a 100-level course. The lectures do not follow a textbook and his slides only have pictures. If you do not learn from a man talking at you in the most boring manner ever I do not recommend this class. as of fall 2024 50% of grade is quizzes and 50% is labs. I taught myself the material.

The lectures were extremely boring and the tests were worth like half the grade. Fell asleep in class like 3 times. The content wasn't too bad, just a lot of memorization. If you're good at remembering a bunch of abstract geological stuff and can perform on tests, you'll be fine.

If you do not need this class, simply do not take it and save yourself some tears. It was incredibly hard for a 100 level course. I went to office hours for help on one of the labs and the GE straight up told me they could not help me because they did not know how to approach the question themselves. Lectures are long and not helpful.

This should not be considered an introduction. The topics were so hard to follow, the material was so heavy, this was such a hard class for me. I struggled so badly. The GEs never get back to you. Unless you have previous knowledge about geography do not take this class.

I took GEOG322 with Mark and the content is very interesting and this class has so much potential. However, its hard to take notes because lectures only include photos with him telling anecdotes. Labs were extremely confusing and GE's were often confused/upset as well. Midterm and final were extremely hard. Nice guy, but unorganized and naive.

Calling this class a 100 level class is an absolute joke. One of the hardest classes I have taken in college so far. If you are looking for an easy science credit stay as far away as possible from this class. Maybe it would be better in person but online it's horrible. The labs are excruciatingly long and confusing.

This is a graduate level course disguised as a 100 level class. Genuinely the hardest course I have take at the university. The lectures are excessively long and unhelpful. I would not recommend taking unless absolutely necessary.

The lectures are what the midterm and final were based on. Lab attendance is mandatory, and there is a quiz based on the lab every week. Not gonna lie it was astonishingly hard for a 100 level class. The professor was still very good and knowledgable which made it worth it.

Lecture was interesting given his own professional experience in the subject. Lab was written in a way that it was easy to complete independently, but still left some challenge. There are a couple quizzes and a final independent project which helps guide you in. Probably the most interesting GIS class I've taken so far.
Long lectures, and some difficult work but if you can get into the subject they're really interesting. He always ends the class with a nice existential monologue that leaves you feeling wistful.
Lectures are long and not very interesting, GE's and labs are pretty good though. Ended up skipping most lectures and literally falling asleep in the ones i went to.

Saw a lot of comments saying he was boring, but if you like the subject or are interested in learning, you'll be fine. He's super into his lessons, and sometimes spices it up with an existential monologue, it's great. If you're worried about falling asleep, take a nap beforehand, always did the trick for me. Great GEs too.

Professor Fonstad sucks. His lectures are incredibly boring and difficult to pay attention to. If you miss lecture, its extremely difficult to figure out whats going on because the slides are essentially just images. The labs are easy enough, and got me through the class with maybe going to two lectures after the midterm.
Very boing lectures make you wanna fall asleep. If you do not need to take this class avoid at all costs.

for GEOG 322, Professor Fonstad is a master of his craft and even though the lectures are boring he is still a nice guy and it can be very interesting. the GE's are caring and will help you through all of the labs and what he wants from you is pretty straight forward. An enjoyable experience and you will enjoy his class

Horrible, boring, lectures that drag on with way too much information that is mostly unhelpful. One of the most useless classes I've ever taken. Discussion sessions are where you actually learn and those are still bad. It is. not organized good and one of the worst classes I took. Avoid this class at all costs.

Lectures are a little dull, but also interesting half the time. The teacher cares more about learning the overall concepts rather than remembering technical details. Exams were half the grade but he graded really easily. Most questions were open ended and as long as you explained your answer you got credit.

Mark seems to be a nice guy and is very passionate about what he is teaching, but his class is boring and often times hard to comprehend. There's no attempt to engage students and people who seemed to excel in my class were science majors. The class is lecture-based with minimal slides. If you're looking for an easy science credit, don't do this.
i have taken 400 level classes easier than this class. do not recommend

Professor was knowledgeable about his subject, but lectures were long and often contained too much info / info that was not well organized to be useful. My lab section was where I learned most of what we discussed. Do not use phones or arrive late to this course; he often stopped the lecture to call out students for doing these things. An OK class.

He should not be allowed to be a professor. Rude to students and this class is a waste of your tuition. I learned absolutely nothing. What you learn in lecture and what you do in lab is completely different and he is the most unhelpful person I've ever met.

lectures are painfully boring-- only time i ever really learned anything was in lab section. grades are based off one lab and quiz per week, and two midterms. do not take if you're looking for an easy A science credit. extremely boring, lots of information to remember, and not easy

The 1hr 20min lectures are painfully inadequate for learning anything. He seems like he could be a nice guy but his hand-drawn slides for class and power points won't teach you much. Expect to learn things on your own or with a GTF.

He unbelievably unorganized (did not write the midterm until 3 days before and gave us a study guide which consisted of about 300 terms which weren't even on the midterm). The online labs and quizzes for this class should be easy but he skips over chapters and expects us to learn material by ourselves. He rambles all class and calls people out.
Pretty funny, but needs to take it easier regarding the attendance. It pops up for maybe one minute on canvas (and sometimes not at all) and if you don't submit it you take a hit.
Funny, cool dude. Needs to have more lax a

Amazing prof. Engaging lectures, accessible, and kind. There is light homework, and 3 midterms with no final. I found the midterms to be difficult but did fairly well on them all. If you pay attention in class and put in the time studying you won't have any trouble. Will be taking another one of his courses next term.

Simply a great guy who is very engaging in class, class says its a 110 minute class but he always ends class at about the 75 minute mark. Lectures are very clear cut and he wants the students to succeed. If you pay attention to the slides you will do well in this class. Homework was light in my opinion

I honestly don't understand why Erick Ford is so well liked.  His class is WAY harder than it should be, it is lots of work, and some of the information he teaches is incorrect.  I met with him in person and he was honestly very rude and condescending.  There is something very artificial about his positivity as well.

Erik is actually one of the best professors on campus! BA 101 isn't easy, but not hard. Easy weekly homework, exams are 60% of your grade but are made up of 3 midterms (no final) and aren't cumulative. The exams are hard(ish) but just attending and taking info in by listening and then taking notes, plus doing a quizlet you'll pass no problem!
