Easily the best professor I've ever had. He explains Excel in such an understandable way and is super enthusiastic about it. BA240 is Pass fail and it's really easy to pass if you do the work. I still use the skills I learned in BA240 and I switched to OBA because of Ford.

Absolutely love this guy, he is very caring and genuinely wants the best for you aslong as you show that you care aswell. One of the best professors at UO forsure, he provides clear feedback and will help you reach your goals.

He's great at teaching and his lectures are structured well. It can be hard to keep up with notes during the lecture because sometimes he goes pretty fast. However the lectures are available on Canvas and it can be very helpful to take notes prior to lecture so you can pay closer attention.

Super nice guy, lectures are easy to pay attention and interactive, he is very clear about what he wants, 3 multiple choice midterms no finals. I found those all very easy, it is very easy to get a good grade in his class if you just show up and do the assignments.

Professor Ford is the best professor in the business school and probably the university as a whole. Very energetic and excited about the material he teaches. I took his BA101 and BA240 classes, with BA240 being online and his presence as an educator was the same in both. He is a great dude, responsive to emails, and a fair grader too. Love this guy
BA 240 with Erik Ford was amazing! Interesting lectures, so sweet, and definitely learned a lot!
Erik Ford is the best. Take his class. He cares, is passionate, and is quite a hoot.

Professor Ford is great! He's really enthusiastic during his lectures and makes it easy to follow along. As long as you pay attention during the demos, it's really easy to do well on the homework and exams.

Lectures are very easy to follow and he takes the time to help anyone who needs help with excel for windows and mac. He manages to make a boring topic like excel more interesting with his enthusiastic personality. His homework is just like his lectures, but easier. It is the same case with his exams, as they are the easier versions of the homework.

Professor Ford is a really good instructor and his BA 240 class is really easy, you just have to do the work and you will pass the weekly quiz. He gives the solutions to every homework, quiz and test. He is very approachable and easy to contact outside of class. Highly recommend professor Ford

Erik Ford is an amazing professor! I had him for ba 240 and his lectures were so fun, so easy to follow along with, and he knows how to break things down so well! Because of him, I enjoy doing work on excel! Recommend him, he makes lectures bearable and he responds super fast.

Best teacher I've had by far and a class I look forward to going to. He's super nice and it's almost impossible to do poorly in his class. Gives about an hour of homework a week with super clear instructions. If you're taking BA101 make sure he's teaching. BA240 is also a great, useful class, and a super simple class.

I definitely recommend taking spreadsheet analysis with Professor Ford! He makes the course very easy to follow and almost impossible to fail. You'll be alright as long as you show up to the lectures and do your work on time.

This professor is scared of teaching. He is late everyday and teaches you nothing, if you want to do good on tests all you need to do is chat the study guide and you will be fine, the assignments are annoying, long and teach you nothing. super easy but so boring. don't buy the textbook.

I was told to take this class by my friends who took it. They said it was simple with simple assignments. I must have signed up for the evil JCOM 201 because wow. Once you think your SECOND final project is the last to do, he whips out another analysis out of nowhere like a magician taking a bird out of his coat pocket.

Def made Comm. Law a bit more understandable and digestible. Assignments may seem daunting or a lot, but are pretty doable, especially if you reach out and ask questions. He's always available to talk before or after class too! Decent amount of extra credit, which was very helpful to my overall end grade.
Earth-shatteringly boring lectures.

I've taken both 201 and 302 from him. If you participate in class activities, iclicker, and quizzes, you will be good. He's genuinely a really nice person which makes it easy to respect him as a professor. He talks a little slow in lectures, but he let class out early every day.
His hour-50 lectures felt like watching a video in .5x. He talks so so so slow and pauses so much!

Lots of reading for each class but comes in handy for lectures. Justin is a nice guy but often sounds like he is trying to use the most complicated words he can think of. Open-note Canvas quizzes, and papers with very clear instructions.

Is pretty lecture heavy and I had to purchase the Iclicker student online because that's how he took attendance, I never bought the textbook and did just fine. the final was multiple choice, and we were allowed a notebook size paper fora cheat sheet but honestly the class is super easy to follow and the lecture slides are really good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a fine professor, nothing out of this world or horrible. The class itself is a very easy going subject, just do the readings and pay attention to the slides and you'll get by.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have had Franchese for JCOM 201 and 302. His classes are lecture heavy. He is very passionate about what he lectures on and he is easy to reach outside of class. His class can feel very long sometimes, but overall it is not difficult to get a good grade. No tests, canvas quizzes and papers.

The lectures were long and sort of boring, but Francese is super duper nice and helpful. He gave me an extension on an assignment that I a) didn't ask for and b) didn't think I'd be able to turn it in, so I gave up. I can see how the info in this class could be helpful for someone wanting to go into law, but I definitely got bored bc im not
The 2 hour lectures for this class aren't super interesting & can be difficult to pay attention to sometimes. However, the professor is a super nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were not the most interesting and were difficult to pay attention to at times. That being said, Justin is extremely nice and will help you when needed. If it doesn't make sense during lecture, ask him after class or during office hours. The assignments seem daunting but aren't too bad (at least in my experience/with my GE)

Professor Francese is a dull lecturer; it feels like he uses unnecessarily complex vocabulary to demonstrate his expertise. That being said, he is extremely knowledgable and his class is thorough. The assignments (mostly case brief papers) allowed for creativity and variation too. In-class discussions and quizzes were a large part of the grade

You are allowed to miss four attendances by policy but he counters this by only dropping one in class reading quiz which are worth significantly more than attendance. Roughly 60% of your grade is class attendance, in class discussions, and in class quizzes, 4 essays are the other 40%. Slow lecturer, but he is kind and passionate, I would recommend.

Dr. Francese is a good professor; I will only say that the content can get repetitive and drag on, especially since it is for two hours. There are ways to participate, so there's always something to do in class. The GEs grade harshly, so carefully review rubrics and the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were long and could get boring but you do not really need to play too close of attention. All of the quizzes are online and you have access to other browsers. As long as you do the homework well you will get a good grade. Also had multiple extra credit opportunities that boosted by grade a lot.

This class was very easy as all tests are open-notes and not too in depth in the reading. There are two papers in the quarter that are relatively easy and short. His lectures however are very boring and he talks slow so it was hard to pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: overall professor francese was great in jcom201! it was a relatively easy class but it does help to do your daily readings, which can be difficult if you fall behind or get sick. pretty chill grader but his lectures aren't the most engaging. as long as you go to class & turn ur homework in on time you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While he is nice and the class is easy, his lectures are filled with long pauses and awkward stand-still moments that make me question if I am in a college course. His rubrics for papers are also quite flawed and should be remade, as the point values do not make sense. As a person, he is great. As a teacher, he is incredibly flawed.

Justin's lectures are not helpful or informative, so the mandatory attendance is kind of frustrating. The assignments and quizzes are fairly easy but the instructions aren't always clear. Make sure to clarify if you're confused about something.

This dude. I sometimes think he's not actually a professor he is just someone's dad who snuck into the lecture hall and started saying words like "media analysis" and "context literacy". I learned next to nothing this whole class 201 is terrible

Professor Francese seems very passionate and JCOM302 is a great introduction to law for those interested in the media field. Assignments can be pretty big but there aren't too many of them during the term. Prof. Francese is great at answering questions and giving feedback. I definitely recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mind numbingly dull lectures that drag on for hours I found myself nearly falling asleep every class. Nearly killed my love of writing.

Justin is such a nice professor, though his lectures are long and dreary. But, that's kinda what comes with the class. He does engaging group assignments each class for participation. Attendance is not mandatory but you will miss those points. There's a quick reading quiz each week and it's a walk in the park. Best prof for this class.

Justin is not the best at keeping the students engaged during the lectures. But he does a very good job keeping the course organized and he's very accessible outside of class. As a person, he is so sweet, understanding, and accommodating.

LITERALLY TAKE CLASS WITH HIM!

Literally such an angel, he offered so many opportunities for me to complete late work when I missed deadlines, and was always super open to talking about assignments and clarifying questions.
-extra credit boosted my grade by 10%... insane
-weekly readings (super interesting)
-weekly quizzes (fairly easy)

I really enjoyed my time in this class. It was extremely helpful to have such a passionate professor who really pushed me to pursue a minor in media studies. Really enjoyed the class, but more importantly, this is a great professor to have at UO overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class is pretty boring and he just reads off slides from the reading but was overall pretty easy. He has activities that you can only do in class so you have to go for attendance but quizzes are all open book and not hard. We had 2 papers and the final was take home which was nice. The content was interesting but the way he taught it wasnt the best

lectures are boring and monotone but class setup is easy to understand and the teacher is well organized and clear on expectations. assignments sometimes don't feel relevant but reading isn't too heavy

Francese has been an amazing professor, he really does care that his students do well. Unlike most professors, he is responsive outside of class and willing to answer questions. The classwork itself isn't hard but its not easy- if something is unclear then ask, instructions can be funky sometimes.
Clearly cares about his students and the success of his students and is a good teacher. Athough the lectures are long and can be boring the class itself is easy and fun.
He wants his class to succeed. He is understanding and gives out interesting and interactive material. I truly loved his class. I would take it again!

Justin is probably the most boring professor I've had. This class was for credit and it's a lot of work. So many different assignments and three major writing pieces. The labs were way too long for what they are. He was nice and helpful but so boring. Good luck if you take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself is grueling. He really tried to make lectures engaging even though the material is beyond boring. He did a great job handling lectures. Tons of busy work but in the end it pays off because you can remember what you're taught. Midterm and final were so easy. Good prof, taxing class.

The lectures were soooo boring. That being said, it might be impossible to make grammar/writing lectures interesting, so I won't be too hard on him. I recommend doing the many grammar drills/other hw in class. This helps with the two biggest problems of the course IMO: lots of busywork and mind-numbing lectures.

Professor Francese is a very down to Earth guy. His lectures are simple and not hard, just make sure to read the assigned readings from the textbook because a lot of that information will be on the quizzes. All your quizzes are given online since they are open note. His GE's grade your work and they can be really tough graders, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Justin Francese is a great professor. It's obvious that he cares about the success of students. One in class assignment per class for attendence each day, a couple of online quizzes, and 2 papers. Lectures are interesting and he is passionate about the topics. I learned a lot! Fair grading, ALWAYS clear instructions on things, GE's are great too.

Francese is a very middle ground professor. The class and content itself is relatively easy to understand, though he does not do a great job at explaining assignments. Attendance is not mandatory but if you do not go you wont be able to complete in class assignments, though with big point papers and projects he has a 72hr grace period. solid 6.7/10
Slow lectures but helpful material, the discussions on fridays were mandatory but felt pointless and way too long (2hours). Nice professor who cares about students though
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty fun class! The subject material was always really interesting, and Justin is good at getting discussions going. The two essays we wrote for the term were both based on really cool prompts. The quizzes weren't too hard, and there were extra-credit opportunities. If you find the study of media interesting, you'll probably like the class.

If you're actually looking to learn something don't take this class. His lectures were always about an hour less than the class was supposed to go and covered very surface-level and the discussions were also surface-level and boring. The final group project was a massive pain and doesn't hold members accountable. Most people are just there to pass.
His lessons were interesting and he made the class discussion easy to participate in. The overall course was very easy.

Attendance is considered mandatory but is taken with an online assignment that is always easy at the end he removes the two lowest so you can miss class twice. The tests and quizzes are online and open for a day, if you read or even just ctrlF the book its easy the book is free online he allows late work for no penalty. 100% recommend
He is a very good professor. My only complaint is the amount of notes in class and out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Francese is a great professor. He is caring, respectful and considerate of students. The only homework is to read before each class. In order to pass the quizzes, you need to take notes on the reading because that's where a majority of the questions come from. Textbook is $20+, but you can find it online too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor was very considerate of those in the lectures. He gave quizzes based half on readings and half on lecture topics, but they are very simple. If you pay attention to the course I would say it's extremely simple, however, if you don't pay attention it could easily be a difficult course. He also replies to emails within minutes.

Justin was a great professor. Class discussions were super interesting and lively, so it was easy to stay engaged. The class content combines sociology with media studies, which makes it really applicable to todays generation. On top of that theres only 2 short papers, biweekly quizzes, and a final. If you pay attention youll do great

His lectures are very drawl, and they seem to last for five times as long as they actually are. I just did other homework during his class, and that was probably the most productive I had been all quarter. The class is not very difficult. It just takes a little willpower. Take him if you want to improve your grades in other classes.

Don't graduate UO without taking ASTR 122 with Fisher! He's so inspirational and passionate about astronomy and science. Tests and quizzes are all multiple choice (all online and open-book), though you won't need to look at your notes. Everything he tests on is stuff he covered repeatedly. One of the easiest classes at Oregon and is a must!

Professor Fisher is one of the best professors Ive had at UO! You can tell hes really into what he teaches and it makes the class much more interesting to learn about. Easy homework assignments and easy midterm/final. 10/10 would take again

What's not to like about Dr. Fisher? He is such an incredible guy; he really cares about his students and is so passionate about the things he teaches them. He strives to make you like astro as opposed to making you memorize facts. That means you can enjoy the amazing lectures and not worry about hard tests. Highly recommend to take. Amazing prof!

I absolutely love Dr. Fisher. This class was interesting and blew my mind everyday. Dr. Fisher is hilarious and makes his lectures so interesting. He is a passionate and awesome teacher. There was little homework and he is very understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but I never wanted to skip this class. A great science class or elective!
Scott Fisher is one of the most engaging professors at UO--he is SO into Astronomy and his lectures are so fun. If you need a science credit and want to have a good laugh, take this class with him!

If you need to take a science class for one of your pre-reqs, DO IT WITH SCOTT FISHER! It is a fun, interesting, and light-work class. You take an online quiz after every class that can all be found in the notes from class (that get posted later too). You won't regret this class!

Believe everything you hear about this guy, very funny and passionate. This is both an incredibly interesting class that's also sooooo easy. Take to get an easy science credit, or to fill up a light schedule.
You can tell that he actually cares about what hes teaching. Very entertaining and passionate.
Such a good professor, I really enjoyed his lectures and he was super caring and flexible! I highly recommend taking this class with Fisher!!
Amazing teacher! You can really tell he loves teaching astronomy. Very kind and easy going.

Dr. Fisher is an incredible professor, would 100% take his class again. I was already interested in Astronomy before taking his class, so his lectures were super fascinating. He loves to crack jokes and he cares about his students' success. Little to no readings, two exams (midterm and final), short quizzes, and about five homework assignments.
Straight up the GOAT, take him during your time at UO or you will regret it.

I can't begin to describe how amazing of a professor Scott Fisher is. I never write things on rate my professor but I'm doing it now to encourage everyone at UO to take ASTR 122 when you're here. Besides being an easy A this is a truly mind-blowing class and he genuinely just wants all his students to be excited about astronomy as he is. TAKE IT!!!

Dr. Fisher's a great lecturer, though I think he's a bit overrated. He definitely cares and is responsive to students + he updates the Canvas page frequently but 3 exams was a little bit excessive for how little the course content actually was. I felt some of the quizzes were intentionally confusing and misleading even though I watched the lectures

Fisher is a great professor, but he is by no means "the best at Oregon." The workload is decent, just 3 lecture videos per week with (sometimes unfair) quizzes, 5 easy homework assignments, 2 midterms, and a final. While he's very inspiring, he often goes off on tangents that aren't relevant to the material, which can make the videos hard to watch.

Take his class! The best professor at UO and is so kind and cares about his students. Super passionate about the material and if you take notes in class and study them, you will get an A in the class. My favorite class by far!!!

Best professor I've had. He's so awesome. ASTR122 is an absolutely beautiful class. The content is mind-blowing. It changed some of my perspectives of the world and enlightened me to so many things. The class was an experience. I highly recommend taking ASTR122 with Fisher. He's enthusiastic and cares so much about his teaching.

Dr. Fisher was an amazing professor. I am not a science major but he makes the class accepting of all students regardless of their major. Enthusiastic every lecture and genuinely cares about students and their success. If you get the chance, I would highly recommend taking a course with him.

Dr Fisher is awesome and this is a great class for non-science majors. His lectures are funny and entertaining, even in the pure online format. There were 5 total homework assignments, several easy lecture quizzes and 3 straightforward exams. Highly recommend!

Nothing but positive things to say about him. I am absolutely terrible in science classes but he changed that for me. If you have had a previous bad experience taking astronomy classes, don't let that stop you from taking astr122 with him! He has your back and his lectures are very enjoyable.

Dr. Fisher is a true legend. I have slim to no intentions of going anywhere near astronomy or the science world. However, despite my low interest, Dr. Fisher is probably the only professor that can make me feel like I want to learn more. His lectures (which are online rn) are one of a kind and makes you want to watch them. He is very caring.

This satisfied a requirement & I didn't expect to learn as much as I have. Dr. Fisher is truly a one of a kind professor. His willingness to educate is quite simply unmatched in the academic world. Most professors will give you help within their class subject. Dr. Fisher will help you learn anything he can. Need physics help in ASTR122..? Sure!

Online web class, with a short quiz after each lecture. Quizzes were super easy with all answers on the slide shows. Lectures were short and easy to follow and entertaining. Overall easy and interesting class.

Dr. Fisher is by far the best professor I have ever had. He is so passionate and caring and it SHOWS. He grades every assignment and leaves video messages as comments about the assignment because of COVID and us no being able to be in person, a 300 person class that is insane. I wan him to teach more classes because I love him so much!
An amazing professor - if he taught every astronomy class I would take them. I've never been able to understand science very well but he made every concept accessible and engaging.

I mean he is famous. The best professor ever. I hated space before. After taking his class. Space is one of my main thing in life. I read about the news of space etc. I graduated in Fall 19. And I said, he deserves that I create an account here and give him my feedback. Thank you professor Scott for everything, you are the best. *I know he reads^_^

Very kind man. Cares a lot about the class but doesn't treat it like an upper division class, understands that most of us were taking it for a science credit. Easy A but I learned a lot and really enjoyed it. He's really fun and nice and passionate. Didn't feel like a 400 person class. He made personal connections with me and all of my friends.
Always an entertaining lecture to go to. I had lots of fun in this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is amazing and clearly passionate in the fields of physics and astronomy, he really brings out the best in his students

I was a little concerned about taking an astronomy class since I'm not much of a science person but Dr. Fisher taught me a lot and made it super enjoyable. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I didn't miss a single lecture just because it was my favorite class. His classes are considered some of the easiest at UO but they're way too under appreciated!

Dr. Fisher is by far the best professor I've had. He's the kind of teacher that wants you to learn, not just memorize and he does this by making lectures fun and relevant. He knows the majority of the people in the class are using it as a gen ed, so the class isn't too tough. Definitely recommend!! You won't want to miss class because it's so fun.

I took this class as a sophomore to meet the University's science requirement. I am by no means interested in science in any way, but Prof. Fisher's class was one of the better ones I've taken. His lectures were engaging, he clearly loves and adores astronomy, and is so so passionate about teaching and engaging with students.

One of the better Professors that I've had at the University. Pretty easy going, very entertaining, and has plenty of office hours. Really cares about his subject but he understands that the class is mostly used as an elective

Fisher is an incredible professor. He understands his course is an elective. His lectures are super entertaining, exams and homework are extremely easy, and very accessible outside of class. He is super passionate about his material and really cares about his students. I would seriously recommend taking his class for an elective!

Professor Fisher is the best professor I have ever had. I say this because he is really passionate and takes pride in his teaching. He keeps lectures engaging, interesting and really easy to follow. The class consists of 4 homework assignments, and 3 midterms. The midterms are easy as you just have to study his class slides!

Hands down best professor Ive had. He is aware that 90% of the class didnt know anything about astronomy so he teaches the class in a way that it is very beginner and straightforward (no BS). Exams are EXTREMELY easy (I got 90-100% on all of them). Lectures are like fun/interesting TED talks. Memorize lecture slides & youll ace the exams!

Dr. Fisher is such a rad professor. He is so funny and so passionate about what he is teaching about. There is a textbook but it is avaliable online for free. The homeworks are essays but they're easy to do. Lots of extra credit opportunities that are actually fun. He puts all of his powerpoint slides online right after class. Will take again

Dr. Fisher is such a fun lecturer and really works to make his subject matter (which is super abstract) really clear for his students. He is really approachable and enthusiastic about astronomy. He is also really knowledgeable and has a lot to share in his lectures. Plus he's really goofy and pretty funny so lectures are interesting and engaging.

Basically, if you show up to class and put a mild effort into paying attention, you're gonna pass with flying colors. It's not too hard to pay attention, either. He's very energetic and enthusiastic about the subjects he talks about. I don't think I'll ever love anything as much as this man loves space.

Professor Fisher is by far the greatest professor I have ever had the pleasure of taking a class from. He is incredibly intelligent and so so passionate about Astronomy. His knowledge of the subject matter is extensive and he is ALWAYS willing to answer any question. Not only is he an expert in his field, but he is one hell of a teacher.
Truly insightful lectures. Youll definitely see the stars from a different perspective after listening to Dr. Fisher.

Fisher is definitely one of the best teachers I've had at the University of Oregon. He is super approachable, hilarious, and always has your best interest at heart. I thoroughly enjoyed going to his office hours to get feedback on my tests and to just talk about astronomy stuff. He is super passionate about teaching and an all around amazing guy.

Take his lower division ASTR classes. You will never look at the world again. You will look up at the night sky in awe, you will begin to understand life beyond the biological level, but the astronomical level. His lectures are some of the most inspiring I've attended, and my mind was blown and had goosebumps of astonishment on a weekly basis.

Fisher is INCREDIBLE. Im a junior this year and have taken so many different classes but if you were to take one class at UO, it would be ASTR 121/122 with Dr. Fisher. You learn about the grand scale of the world you live in. You ever watch a Neil deGrasse Tyson video, and you get goosebumps from the shear astonishment? Yeah, this class does that!
Very passionate professor. He honestly just wants to teach you cool stuff about astronomy and is very good teacher of the subject

Dr. Fisher is super great!! There were about 5 homework assignments the whole term and 3 tests. He's really good at meeting you on your level. If you want to pass his class, you will. He is always available to talk outside of class. Would recommend him to anyone and I'm planning on taking him again in 121!

Honestly I came into this class not knowing any astronomy and rightfully so, I read these comments and assumed he was great and taught for beginners. However, this is not the case!!! do not take this class unless ya wanna get your GPA ruined. Do NOT believe the hype.... Tests are also graded toughly for a 122 course.
I literally love him like I want him to be my dad  he's such a great professor and gets so excited about astronomy it's awesome and wants everyone to do well
Best professor, I really recommend him for everyone.

Probably the best professor I have ever had. Seriously. No one has made science as interesting and easy to understand for me than Dr. Fisher. He preaches science literacy, which is an issue for many students. If science is not your best subject like it was for me, Fisher can definitely change that. Awesome dude, highly recommend.

Oh man, where do I start? I don't think I've ever met a teacher as passionate and invigorating as Scott. Such a great guy; an even better astronomer. It's interesting to learn from someone who actually has real experience as an astronomer. Only thing that sucks is that he has never actually been to outer space.

Honestly I had to take ASTR to fulfill a group requirement for my BA but Scott Fisher has been one of my favorite professors I've had in my 3 years of college.  He was funny and straightforward about the class and all that- but he is so passionate about astronomy and just getting his students to be as well. He was amazing and changed science for me

If you want an easy class with a even easier teacher take this class. If the school offers multiple ASTR courses with Fisher take them. Boost GPA with minimal effort. Plus you will actually learn something interesting.

greatest professor i have ever had. the class is not super easy but it is by no means difficult. he is an inspiration and is the reason i am no longer afraid of science. interesting class and interesting guy
Really amazing and very interesting professor

Hands down best professor I have ever had. I have had two classes with him so far and definitely will be taking more. He is extremely passionate about what he does and understands most of us are only taking his class for gen eds.
Dr. Fisher is pretty much a campus legend.

This class was a lot of fun. Dr. Fisher is engaging and keeps you interested even with the 2 hour long lecture period. The book was used for homework on occasion but for the most part if you showed up to class and took good notes you should be fine. The copious amounts of extra credit opportunities were great and were simple to do. Great Class!

Dr. Fisher is seriously amazing. I strongly recommend his astronomy classes for everyone, even if you're not really into science. He's witty and hilarious, and it's overall a really enjoyable class. And hey, you actually learn useful things!
Best professor ever. He is soooo funny!!  You'll learn so much and at the same time you'll laugh throughout the whole lecture

BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD. The lectures are fun to attend, but if you miss a few classes it is no big deal. Science is normally a scary thing, but Dr. Fisher makes it fun, exciting, and not scary at all. This class doesn't take a lot of time and it is very interesting. You will learn valuable info and your perspective on life will grow.

Incredible class, and a fantastic professor. Fisher's classes are popular and fill up fast, so if you get the chance, definitely sign up for one of his lectures. He has a really unique perspective on the world and on life in general, so you'll leave the class feeling like you actually learned valuable lessons, not just random facts from a textbook.

Fisher is by far the BEST professor I've had at UO. I've never been good at science, but he makes astronomy incredibly interesting and accessible without including  math. He wants the best for all of his students (his "peeps") and helps them become thoughtful, critical thinkers, rather than just focusing on grades. Amazing person; take his class.
Best professor ever

Really funny, really passionate about astronomy, and really easy to follow. He's easy to talk to if you don't understand something, but he's really good at lecturing and explaining everything in class.

Dr. Fisher is one of the best professors at the University of Oregon! He doesn't seem to really care about grades, his main intention is for students to start liking science again. He gives enough extra credit that you it is very likely that you will have over 100% by the end of the term.
Very easy class, if you're enrolled you will pass. Funny and good lecturer but goes on long rants  that have no point. So much extra credit, you don't have to past the tests.
Dr. Fisher explains the wonders of the universe in a fun, simple way. Easy A, but I learned a lot. 55 would recommend to anyone interested in learning about cosmic perspective.

Fisher aka. Our King (as he calls himself) is a great asset to the UO's staff. He's a great professor, fun and engaging and always ready to make things in class interesting. He's also a part of the science literacy program which means he gears his class towards people who want to learn but aren't very good with math or deeper physics.

I couldn't select more than 3 tags but if I could "There for you, Amazing Lectures, and Would Take Again" would be selected.  Excellent professor and easily the best on campus.  Is very passionate about his job and just loves astronomy and people.  I'm sure everyone learns better when they enjoy being in class and Dr Fisher does just that every day

Dr. Fisher is surprisingly excellent. He is extremely energetic, he'll make you laugh countless times, and he'll make you WANT to come to class. It is absolutely clear that he cares about his students, and that he wants them to be interested in what he teaches. He makes all the material super easy to follow, and super interesting. Fantastic class.

He is the funniest professor I have ever had, and clearly knows exactly what he's talking about when it comes to astronomy. He made the class so interesting and something that I didn't mind going to three days a week. Also, a large amount of extra credit is given throughout the term and the tests are curved so the class is not too challenging.

Dr. Fisher is the best professor I have had. He is engaging, hilarious, and makes what he talks about super interesting. He is always available for questions after class and explains everything in an easy to understand way. His tests get a little harder each time but if you go to class and study for a bit you will be more than fine.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. I took this class not expecting anything because I needed a science credit but Fisher changed my outlook on Earth and space. Never have I met someone more passionate about a topic and on top of that he really wants you to do well and take something away from the class. He's an awesome guy too!

Scott Fisher is probably one of the best professors on campus. He's engaging and hilarious - kids actually laugh at his jokes. I actually enjoyed going to class, because his lectures are so fun and interesting. I'm definitely no astrophysicist, but I loved this class. Definitely definitely take this course with Fisher!!!
Great lectures, hilarious, helpful, looked forward to going to class. Book is like $1.50 on Amazon. Take a class with Fisher!!!

Fisher is awesome and chill. Astr 121 is a cool class in general but sometimes the subject matter can be boring. However, Fisher makes everything a good time.  Class is an easy A but most of the stuff on tests are from his lectures, so it's not  a good idea to skip too much.
He is the greatest professor ever, I die laughing every time I walk into that auditorium. If he could teach every single one of my classes I'd be so happy!

Best prof I've had so far! He's really nice and funny and makes lectures interesting. Tests are a little tough but really not bad if you study a little bit. Definitely want to take another ASTR class with him.
I loved Dr. Fisher! Really cool material, you learn stuff you actually can use! Would recommend to everyone. No math required.
Dr. Fisher is the coolest professor on this campus. Such a great guy and he'll change the way you see the world. You're lucky if you get him as your professor.

Fisher is an absolutely amazing professor and person. He understands this is a course for non-majors, so he lays off the numbers and takes a more conceptual route. He forms unique + interesting curriculum for students, and he's hilarious + witty-- often has the whole class laughing, so lectures are enjoyable. Take this course, you won't regret it.

This guy is exactly who you want as a professor. He is so passionate about astronomy and you can clearly see it when he lectures. Very funny guy. He just makes the class interesting and gets students really stoked about astronomy in his own special way. I would definitely take another astronomy course just because of Fisher's talent with teaching.

Dr. Fisher is the man! He isn't really focused on teaching you astronomy, as he is on getting you stoked about astronomy. Most of his lectures are him showing you really cool space related photos, and then explaining the science behind it. The tests are slightly harder than you'd expect but not bad at all. He just really wants to make the class fun

What people are saying is true! There is a scientist on campus igniting a flame of science literacy into the heart of UO students. He teaches about the same material regardless of the course number. So if you really wanted to learn about the planets you might be disappointed when we never got to them.  What material he does present is fantastic!

the most interesting class i've ever taken, keeps the class atmosphere very loose but you also learn a lot and he makes you want to learn even more. He's one of those teachers that restore your faith in the all teachers

Probably my favorite teacher here at UO.  He understands that it's an into to astronomy course and teaches it that way.  No math or physics, just an abundance of interesting and important information about our universe and our place in it.
DYNAMIC. Only take this class if you want to get super excited about Astronomy. Dr. Fisher is charismatic, engaging and passionate. Best professor ever.

Fisher is exuberant and fun, his class was really lively and I learned a ton about a subject I wasn't previously stoked about. Good science credit. Tests were easy up until the final, which was much more technical than I was expecting. Class attendance not mandatory because he posts slides online, but totally worth going because he is so passionate

Seriously an awesome professor. I hate science and this class really changed that... At least for this term. :) Attendance isn't mandatory, but I actually found myself wanting to go to class! Dr. Fisher is super passionate about his subject and it shows.
Favorite class taken at UO so far. Fisher is by far the best professor I've ever had. He makes the class interesting and makes you actually want to come to class. TAKE THIS CLASS

Best class I have ever taken. The professor is passionate about the material and teaches it in an engaging, funny, and efficient manner. It is easy to pay attention as there are so many just awesome pictures and cool facts.
Best Science Teacher I ever met!

Fisher is one of those rare professors that you wish taught all of your classes. Very accessible, animated, and  excited (and knowledgeable) about astronomy. Makes you excited about science even if you don't like it much. Class is easy if you show up and do the [very simple] homework. Graded fairly. Very highly recommend him!

Best teacher in three years of college; in my top three teachers of all time. Regardless of your interest level in astronomy, you should definitely take a class with Dr. Fisher. It's an experience. He's not easy, but he's fair, and genuinely cares about student learning. Occasionally comes across as a criminal mastermind, but in a good way.
Amazing Class
Take a class with this man, he's the best teacher at Oregon

Dr. FIsher is just awesome!!! His class is interesting and very informing, and I'd totally recommend him any day. BUT don't let his niceness fool you; do your work. He isn't afraid to fail or mark you down. Best astronomy professor at the UO.

I've neve been a fan of science. However I had an absolute blast in this class. Dr. Fisher knows everything there is to know about space and he is incredibly willing to let us in on spaces little secrets. Seriously. Take this class you won't be disappointed.

Dr Fisher is the best professer I have ever had in my college education. He LOVES astronomy and has such a passion for teaching. He really cares about his students and is absolutely hilarious. Such a character! Pretty good looking too. Take his class even if you don't need the credits.

Dr. Fisher is incredibly passionate about astronomy. He has never taught before but is incredibly invested in being the very best he can. He offers a lot of help out of class and extra credit. He is very clear in class and answers all questions and makes astronomy very enjoyable. Take his class is you get the opportunity!

The best professor I have had at UO, super down to Earth and entertaining, really makes the class interesting. More focused on not pushing you away from astronomy/science rather than cramming together a bunch of useless stuff in his lectures. Definitely turned astronomy into my favorite subject. If your taking astronomy at UO get him!!

A TERRIFIC professor. He's basically a human wikipedia with anything related to space.  He has so much passion for teaching and helping students understand astronomy. He is not an "easy" teacher, but if you go to class, do the hw, read the book, and participate there is no reason why anyone should not get an A. 100% recommend him for any class.

The best professor at the U O. His teaching methods are great! High energy and enthusiasm. Seriously take this class. He is phenomenal. Will help you get an A if you try, not that hard, but a little effort goes a long way.

He is extremely engaged in class and often has really entertaining rants about the things that are most passionate to him about astronomy. Overall he is a great Professor and just  really wants everyone to not be afraid of science.

I love this class! I took ASTR 121 last tem and hated it. I studied hours over 40 pages of materials but still did not get good grades. But this class, even though we are not covering as much, I'm soaking in everything Dr. Fisher has been teaching! Def. recommend it!

Dr. Fisher makes this class very enjoyable with the energy he brings to this class. Other professors that I have had did not seem as interested in the material as Dr. Fisher which makes the learning experience very enjoyable. He takes his time with the material instead of trying to cram as much info as possible in the ten weeks.

I had Prof. Frey for PHYS-389 and PHYS-413. His lectures & reading assignments are dense, but he always responds to questions thoughtfully & gives us time to work through homework problems in class. More than anything, he really seems to recognize how difficult the PHYS path is, and will respect the effort you put into his class. Highly recommend!

I am not a STEM person what-so-ever but Prof. Frey has a way of explaining pretty complicated topics (for example, time dilation, dark matter, basically the entire history of our universe) that makes it very accessible. He is a great teacher -- I learned so much and see our existence and universe differently. Extremely fascinating class.

He is a really nice professor and he teacher everything very well. As long as you put in a little effort outside of class you can do fine in this class. The material is really interesting if you choose to pay attention. The concepts can be confusing at times but he is really helpful if you just ask him for any help.

Prof Frey was really nice, I enjoyed his class even though it was boring sometimes, its a really good class for a non-science major. You do have to attend class because he does participation quizzes everyday, but if you go to class you will definitely pass. Overall he is a very nice guy with a cool ponytail.
Professor Frey is a cool and laidback Professor with a very organized class structure.

Lots of hard content but he's a nice guy and teaches the class well, tests are meant to be doable provided you know what you need to, and he makes it pretty obvious what things you should know off the top of your head. Lectures can be slow but there's a lot of arduous math in the electromagnetism classes, so can't really avoid it.

He has always been so accommodating when I could not make class. He responds to emails so quick and wants you to succeed in his class. Quizzes are a little difficult, but are taken off of his lectures. The material is boring but he tries so hard to make it fun for everyone and I really respect that.

I absolutely loved ASTR 123. I'm a history major, so I am not the most STEM-inclined, but this class was awesome, and very very easy. Attendance is mandatory (there are iClicker participation quizzes at the end of every class) but the class is fun anyway so that's okay. There are no midterms or a final exam, just iClicker tests on the modules.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Frey is a sweet teacher and cares a lot about what he is teaching. Gives book pdf/only materials needed is an iclicker ($40+). Class consists of in class iclicker quizzes every class, module discussion questions (about 7 total) and module tests (mainly consists of the questions in the in class quizzes). No final exam or midterms

I enjoyed seeing all of his backdrops over this 4-week course. There were participation quizzes, a module test, summary exams, and one essay. Honestly, I just watched the lectures, never read any of the textbook, and did just fine. I found his lectures very helpful and he was always available to talk. As a non-STEM major, he was very entertaining.

Very easy, great for non-science majors. There's no midterm/final, just a couple of tests during the term. There's one paper, but the prompt is simple. Lectures are clear and concise, with lots of useful info. After every class is a participation based quiz, so you will get 100% every time as long as you answer. If you show up everyday you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Frey was a great teacher for this introductory class. You will need to attend class to understand his lectures. His slides have about half of the information and he presents the other half in the lecture. There is no homework and his tests are not too difficult if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Raymond is probably my favorite person ever, let alone favorite professor. Attendance is partially mandatory, depending on what grades you want  there's participation quizzes at the end of every class but they barely affect your grade. All the lectures and quizzes are posted online, so if you miss one it's fine. The tests are also super easy.

Despite COVID-19, these previous positive ratings still stand. Professor Frey is very qualified and has adapted well to remote classes. The group discussions over Canvas were not the most enjoyable, but the weekly quizzes were good grade boosters and I would highly recommend taking this course.

Weekly tests, but I feel like he prepares us well for them (unless you fall behind). He knows so much about astronomy, it's honestly wild. He's so well respected in the field and makes the information understandable. His lectures are rather monotone, but his slideshows & the textbook make up for not listening. He sent us a free pdf of the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Frey is an interesting person to take astronomy with because he is so involved with the field, yet he made the material accessible. I think it could be a little better organized, but at the same time if you study the quiz questions, skim the textbook and listen to the lectures, it's an easy class.

I really enjoyed Professor Frey's class. I found his own expertise in the field very helpful and inspirational. He spoke often of his unique time spent at CERN and LIGO. His lectures were informative and intriguing. The material was difficult, but that's to be expected from an astronomy course. I'm glad I had the opportunity to take this course.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had. There were participation quizzes every day and performance quizzes at least every week. Lectures were not helpful, and I found myself having to teach myself the material before the exams. On all three of the exams there were random questions that were never covered in class. Wanted us to do poorly.

Alisa shows strong passion for cultural studies in Japanese popular culture. Her preparation for each class and the effort she puts into her lecture slides make the material engaging. It's refreshing to have a professor who teaches with enthusiasm rather than simply reading from a screen.

Professor Freedman was so amazing, I am taking another course with her again. Not only is she very knowledgeable about what she is studying, but her courses also focus on issues in history overlooked. Her course does not shy away from hard topics to discuss, so be ready for uncensored information. Overall, a wonderful professor and course!

Alisa is a very kind professor you can genuinely tell she cares about her students. How good you do in the class is just about how much you pay attention and if you do the readings. Her grading is honest and fair. I would take any of her classes again because she is so kind.
Graded on weekly discussion boards, two tests, and a paper. If you come to class, and read/skim the readings you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As long as you read or even skim the readings and can form a thought about them, you will do well. Similarly, I think coming to class is helpful. It's graded by weekly discussion boards, two tests, and a prooject. Women in Modern Japan.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a very fast lecturer and her slides have too many words on them to fully understand before she continues. She will grill you if you don't even pay attention for a second. She acts like she knows a lot and is a very one-sided professor. The class is interesting, you only have this professor for 2 weeks but she's just not the best professor.

Professor Freedman is one of the best teachers that I've taken a class from by far. She is very engaging during lectures and is always ready to explain concepts more or help outside of class. Just make sure you do the readings, they're important on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Freedman. I don't have a personal interest in literature and I'm not a big reader, but this class was really interesting because of the lectures. Also, the readings were not very difficult and she provided them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very good class and teacher as long as you are interested in the lecture. Grading is mostly made up of 3 tests throughout the term. Overall she is an interesting lecturer and will keep most entertained. Best thing about her is her desire to learn and connect with the students. She is super outgoing and friendly. Does not do any attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course has five professors, professor Alisa is very nice and easy to talk to. The lectures were good not too dense and long. The book she assigned was very easy to read as it was a manga and the discussions were interesting and easy to follow. The paper we had to write was pretty easy as long as you read the manga.

Professor Freedman knows a lot about Japanese culture and pop culture, however she kind of assumes that you know a lot about it too. Lectures were extremely long. We had to skip topics because Professor repeated the previous lecture for every new class period. This class is kind of fun, but it began to get really exhausting towards the end. 3/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is truly angelic. I can't say much, but if you take one of her courses, you will leave with lots of knowledge as I did. Please take a course with her; you won't regret it.

Professor Freedman is an amazing teacher. You can tell that she really cares for her students. Her lectures are insightful and give you tons of information about Japanese culture and history. Her tests are not hard if you do all of the assigned readings and participate in discussions. I'm about to take my 3rd course with her, highly recommend her!!

Awesome teacher!! I would take any class she offers! She's super helpful and keeps class interesting. As long as you go to class everyday and take notes you will do just fine. Highly recommend her!!!!!

This course was taught at Waseda University while I was studying abroad. I imagine that is was slightly easier than her courses at U of O, but you still learn a lot about J-pop culture and globalization. She is a very helpful teacher, and is worth getting to know. U of O is lucky to have her as a professor, I selfishly wish UCSD had her.

She knows a lot about Japanese literature and culture. However, her syllabus was not very clear at all, she didn't even explain about the grading rubric on the syllabus. Even though you have A+ performance but you will end up getting an A only, and she won't reply your mail regarding to the grade, so does the GTF.

She knows a lot about Japan and does a great job conveying it. Her worst attribute is that sometimes she over explains very simple concepts. Lightly humurous and provides a TON of optional stuff to read outside of class, content that is very interesting and relevant. Some of her test questions are vague, but generally not difficult.

Great teacher, she is very clear giving many examples in class with well detailed slides. She does however expect you to learn from the online  readings on your own and will not provide the slides outside of the class she showed them in.  I would only recommend her if you like a challenging course that with force you to learn
A wonderful teacher all around.

Real easy teacher to get to know and get on her good side. She lives to help students through whatever they may want relating to the class. She is knowledgeable about Japanese literature through and through.
Amazing Professor, midterms were honest reflection of class and the homework solutions were very helpful.

She was very lenient in her grading of this course by offering extra credit, dropped quizes and homework, and graded exams nicely. She was a very good lecturer, and there were only a few times that she covered the material too fast and in a confusing way. The exams were alright except that she put a lot of tough graphing questions on them.

Laura's very nice, but her lectures are sometimes confusing and she goes fast. The tests were rather difficult and long but she's generous with partial credit (and curves if necessary). Weekly quizzes aren't too bad—they're homework problems with different numbers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Laura is super sweet and wants her class to succeed. Her tests are pretty tricky, but she does give you the chance to get some points back. Homework is heavy, but she only grades whether or not you submit something so you have some flexibility if needed. Not easy, but enjoyable.

There's a lot of homework, but the written assignments are just graded for completion. Laura makes all the material really clear and easy to understand, and cares about keeping the class manageable. This is by far the best math class I've taken at UO.
Prepare to be taken course the glorious path towards true mathematical knowledge.
Definitely wants students to do well. We had a day for homework problems every week and she let us make up points on our tests after she explained the problems. Very sweet and intelligent.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you need to take calculus with any professor at the U of O I would recommend taking it with Laura. Her exams are pretty difficult but she gives you opportunities to make up for lost points. Her lectures go through plenty of examples and she even walks you through some homework problems in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's wonderful in upper-level math! Great teacher, cares immensely about the students.

Prof. Fredrickson is new to the UO and sometimes can be hard to follow during the lecture but she cares a lot about her students. She will change grades to help people succeed and go over tests if there are a lot of uncertainty. She also always replies and is really helpful during office hours.

entertaining lectures. lots of interesting material we covered. minimal workload even for an Async class. tests were straightforward. grading was clear. canvas was organized. i felt that she cared about her students and was passionate about the class. thanks!
literally never had to go to class and was easy and understandable. the class wasn't rly interesting but easy and kind of common sense. The teacher is super nice tho and seems caring and super sweet.

the only thing I struggled with when it came to this class was when it went online all the rest of the term so that was more my issue than the professors. They were really interesting, lecture heavy, the tests were pretty easy if you do the readings and go to the lectures.
Pretty standard, not particularly tech savvy
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOTS of information via lecture and readings but is very clear, well explanations and content is easily applicable. Great professor!

Professor Fujiwara is an amazing teacher, her class was super informative, and I enjoyed how she incorporated movies and a graphic novel into the course structure. You can tell that she cares for her students, and focuses on topics that hold a lot of importance in the world today. This is a great class, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is so amazing. I learned so much from this classes and I want everyone to do the same thing.
Quizzes every Monday at 10 am that are exceedingly hard with low class averages. This class (human osteology) is like a full-time job of just memorization.

Would not reccomend taking this class if you are attempting an easy science credit. Half the class dropped within the first few weeks. The ammount of material is unbearable. That being said, I'd say Dr. Frost is great at delivering the lectures; just be prepared to make this class a new part-time job if you expect to pass.

As someone taking this 100 level class to fulfill my science requirement, this class was terrible.The class was held in Lillis182 and the professor did not use a microphone, so hearing him in a lecture hall full of 200+ people was extremely difficult. The professor also treats the 100 level course as if everyone there is there for a major in Anthro
Lectures were slide based

(366) Dr. Frost is amazing. By far my favorite course I have taken. Participation is very important, and you should take advantage of the lab after hours. This course is time consuming, and you should dedicate as much time as possible for studying. Do not take this course if you have other heavy classes. Get a pdf of the textbook and use Quizlet.

(366) Amazing guy and professor, he's accessible and helped me with my research whenever I needed. Lectures are online and class is used for lab so participation will make or break your grade. Dr. Frost always has the most interesting details for bones and bone formation, so talking to him during lab helped retain info. Don't take w/out anatomy!

(I took ANTH 366, no button for it) Professor Frost is very knowledgeable and kind, his grading system and assignments are just not the best. For this course, it's a lot of rote memorization which makes the quizzes which are a large part of the grade hard. Overall, I think if you're passionate enough about the subject, you'll like the course.

Worst professor I have taken, he was very knowledgable in the field he teaches but for those with no prior knowledge with Anthropology this course is a living hell. His lectures are so boring and lackluster not to mention his weekly quizzes are nearly impossible and the class average for nearly every quiz was a 4 or 5/8. Do not take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Frost isn't very engaging in lectures but the labs tend to be extremely interesting. Quizzes are online and entirely based off of the lectures and are easy to get a decent grade. However a large portion of your grade is determined by very difficult lab practicals and finals in which the averages were very low. Difficult class especially for Core ED
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was not that bad but the lectures are not connected to the main assignments at all. There was a lot of independent learning. If you take 170, don't buy the textbook, it's not worth it. If you need an easy class to get science credit, take a different ANTH class because this one takes a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes you need to do the reading for to pass nd they are not clear. The group project is very hard especially in an online class. There is an insane amount of reading each week around 80-100 pages at the least as well as many articles. If your looking for a class just to meet a requirement then I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool enough but run of the mill. Weekly quizzes, which were easy enough if you did the readings, but nearly impossible to pass if you didn't. Very responsive; we had a group project and one member wasn't responding. Provides very dedicated lectures for each week of classes plus weekly update videos as the quarter went on.

Probably one of the worst classes I've ever taken, the subject and content was so interesting but the weekly quizzes were next to impossible to get a decent score on no matter how much you study. Every person I've talked to in the class felt about the same, definitely a good subject but don't take it with this professor!
Was not helpful and did not give extra credit and made it clear would not take again.

Prof. Frost is an amazing guy but his class is something I wouldn't even recommend to my worst enemy. The 2 lab practicals were insanely difficult and the final exam seems impossible. Class points are given through iclicker points but the lectures are mono toned, and him reading off the slides which seems like no valid reason to be there.

This class is by far the most difficult class. There are 3 big exams, where no study guides are given and little information is provided as to what will be on them. The average for the first one was a 60%, and the average for the second was a 73%. You would think the professor would see something wrong with this but he doesn't. I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Frost has 3 assignments that will make up a majority of your grade. The two lab examinations and the final exam. These come with no direction whatsoever. There are no study guides, or even directions on canvas. The average score for the lab exams was around a 60%, so take that however you want.

I was really mad in the beginning but once you get a feel for the class, it's straightforward. A lot of readings weekly and quizzes, so you really have to make sure you are completely caught up. Lectures are very boring, but relevant to the quizzes. I really enjoyed the topic overall and it's interesting, but it is very hard to retain all the info.

Frost's lectures were fairly dry, but manageable. The WORST part was the weekly quizzes. Assigned 8-10 readings per week, and two chapters of a book (100 pages per chapter). No matter how much you read, the tests are VERY loosely based on the readings. The final is a group project as well, which is annoyingManageable class, but not very enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: His class is hard and has alot of readings but he is extremely charsmatic and lecture is fun! If you like anthro I would highly reccomend.

I took Dr. Frosts ANTH176 class last Fall and now Im taking his ANTH468 class. Yes he can be tough because of what he expects of you but it is only to have students gain knowledge on really cool subjects. The key is to communicate and participate. If youre willing to work hard then take class! He is one of my favorite professors Ive had at UO!

So much work! 3-8 long articles and an annotated bibliography for each article each week. The quizzes were hard. The lab zoom portion was very hard to be able to see details on the specimens as he tried to hold it up to the doc cam, but you were expected to be able to identify those details during quizzes. A group and individual final papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I think my class was a bit different because of the online format but Professor Frost made the transition to an online structure look effortless. He was very helpful and patient. He answered everyones questions to the best of his ability. The GEs are phenomenal. The class really isnt that hard and youll actually learn a lot of cool stuff

Literally the worst class I have taken. The quizzes are nearly impossible despite having read every assigned document. We are assigned almost 15 LONG documents each week in addition to an hour lecture. Do not take this class. Period.

I will agree that Professor Frost's Forensic Anthropology class was extremely hard, so if you're just wanting a science credit look for something else. If this is something you're interested in and you want to learn it you will love this class. So many people failed but if you work for it you will get a good grade. STUDY. Don't wing the labs.

I agree that Dr. Frost makes this class tough for a 100-level. Memorizing each part of each bone was tough, as that was what the lab practicals focused on, but I think being passionate about forensics/anthro really helps to succeed in this class. I suggest printing out pictures of the bones and labeling them to study. I think that's how I did well.

This class is EXTREMELY challenging for a 100-level - apparently it's common for students to fail the first half (as I did). But Frost knows his stuff and is good at explaining things in an accessible and lively way despite the dry and technical material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The number of times that I cried while trying to study this class, only to end up failing along with a majority of the class. Frost is the modern equivalent to Professor Snape- minus any of Snapes charming qualities in the last book. Don't even dream of taking this class, unless you're ready to suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think that this class (Forensic Anthropology) was FAR too difficult for a 100-level class. The only things graded are tests and quizzes. The information is interesting and Professor Frost gives very detailed and interesting lectures, keeping the information relevant. The issue for me was the amount of information we were expected to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult. The 100 level is inaccurate because there is so much complex material covered. Dr Frost is a nice dude but his lectures are so boring and he does not warn anyone about graphic images. The class average is a D, and he does offer any extra credit, or even a study guide. He does not care about student success.

If you're reading this before choosing to take Forensic Anth, I am begging you: pick a different science credit. He covers everything from each bone's features to every single detail of how a body decomposes within the first 6 weeks and then gives practical exams as well as extremely difficult exams. Please avoid this class and Frost at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken in my college career. With time spent on weekly lecture, required course book readings, required article readings, and required documentary watching, this course is very time-consuming. The lectures were awful, impossible to take notes. Average quiz grades for the whole class were around 13/21. Final group essay was horrid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Most of our lectures were from another professor, so it didn't feel like I was taught by Dr. Frost at all. Our final was a group paper, which was a very frustrating experience. When I explained my situation, Dr. Frost was not helpful and basically told me "good luck." The class itself is very interesting, but take it with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Frost is a good at his job don't get me wrong, he knows his stuff but the lectures are very dry and boring as its all biology based. iClicker questions every day in class, and he posts his slides on his page after class. Hardest part of the class are the lab practicals. The GEs don't give much direction during labs, which makes exams hard

Attendance is not mandatory, so about half of the class shows up. There are weekly online quizzes which are incredibly hard, 2 lab practicals which are not the easiest, and 1 final where the average was 51%. His lectures are dry and cover so much material it is difficult to determine what is important and what is not. I would NOT recommend him!

His lectures were the most boring things I have ever been to in my life. It was almost impossible to stay awake, and the course material was extremely dense. This should NOT have been a 100 level class. Even though I got over 100% on the lab practicals, I ended up with a C in the class due to the difficult final. Do not take this class, it sucks.

Very knowledgeable, very approachable. Lectures are easy to follow and usually very interesting. Attendance not required for lectures but I strongly recommend attending, as the written final is based on lectures and sometimes he adds useful information that is not in the lecture notes.

I have never had such a terrible professor in my entire life. Not only are his lectures incredibly dull but he spends entirely too much time on things that he wont even test you on. He wont guide your studies whatsoever, nor will he allow his GTF's to do so. His tests are so challenging for an intro level. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN AVOID IT

This class was so interesting. The tests were clear and came directly from the notes. Frost was great. He obviously cared about what he was teaching and seemed to have a great time doing it. Attendance was not mandatory and lots of students skip because all the lectures were online but it wasn't hard to go and listen. 2 lab practicals -hardest part
Attendance not mandatory but its the only way to pass! Professor is funny and engaging despite a relatively boring subject. Hardest part of the course is the Fossil memorization. Collaborate.

Prof. Frost is very well organized. He posts lectures on blackboard ahead of time and thoroughly explains the concepts in class. Also good at answering questions and keeping the subject interesting- enthusiastic about anthropology. Monya and Ryan are great GTFs. Lots of outside help, lab practice, study sessions. Good class; lots of info to learn.
Great teacher, explains material well and is super helpful if you go for office hours. Overall a good class but practical's are tough. Good online tests - hard but do-able

Interesting class at times, but it's not easy. It's not insanely difficult either, but you do have to work for your grade. All the tests are online which is nice, but they are pretty hard. His lectures can be frustrating sometimes because he spends 20 minutes on a slide with a graph on it and then at the end he rushes through the slides with notes.
Nice, but slow at times

170 can be a boring class at times, especially if you're only taking it for core req, but he is pretty funny at times, very concise, kind of looks like "eric" from tru blood and could use some hair styling advice. overall is you really like biology and anth, you should enjoy all the neat facts you learn

Soooooo boring.. He posts lectures online, so you have no motivation to go to class. I probably went four times the whole term. It was boring, but his slides are clear and precise. He knows what he's talking about. His humor is dry, and that's an overstatement.. I'm trying to be nice, because he is nice. But bring a pillow, you'll need it.

He knows his stuff but that's a given since he's teaching a college course. He's just very boring and nearly impossible to listen to, resulting in the majority of the class skipping class because everything is online. He needs to cultivate more interest within the students. We might not have liked anthro to begin with, now i strongly dislike it.
Scott, have some more classroom interaction in your lectures! SO SO MONOTONOUS, DRY AND BORING....bring a pillow for his 2 hour lectures, believe me you'll need it!

Dr. Frost's lectures are extremely efficient, organized chronologically. Lectures present a lot of technical data, but Frost is very good at conveying difficult concepts in plain language. Accompanying lab with the collection of ancient primate and hominid skull replicas was great, gave me lots of ammo in my debates against Creationist relatives ;)

Dr. Frost is awesome, perhaps a bit dry and I don't like the format of his tests, but his lectures are interesting and he lectures with clarity.  I find the subject matter much more interesting after taking this class.  I like that he's very to the point about things.

Subject is great but this class completely turned my off to Bio Anth. Boring lectures prof always seemed uncomfortable. Tests were all on the computer but difficult because of vague questions. Had to confront him about incorrect answers. One lab group got additional study time in lab for final while the other requested it and was denied. Unfair.

I love Furikado Sensei. If I wasn't already close to graduating, I would keep taking JPN classes just to have her as a professor. She's super sweet and very helpful, she always provides clear answers to any questions we have and is very supportive. She really wants everyone to succeed.

Furikado-Sensei is very nice and helpful! She was always willing to answer questions and gave clear feedback on the oral performances and writing assignments. There are sometimes kanji you haven't learned on the slideshows, so don't be alarmed if you don't recognize something. The vocab lists are out of order so be prepared to highlight as you go.
Such an amazing instructor, I hope to take her for as many of my Japanese courses as possible in the future. She's super chill and approachable, and she's very clear and fair in her grading.

Furikado Sensei is very nice and quite funny. There's homework every class and attendance is mandatory but it's all very manageable. My writing improved a lot from taking her course. You always do what's on the schedule on canvas. She appreciates it a lot if you volunteer. Sensei even brought us snacks once at the end of the year.

I love Furikado Sensei. She posts all lecture slides on Canvas and the slides are very detailed. This language is very difficult of course, but she makes it seem very simple. She is a pretty easy grader on oral exams and as long as you study, practice often, and attend class, your grade will almost certainly be an A. Highly recommend!
