Furikado sensei is so nice and is such a great professor. I wish she was my mom.

Furikado is a legend amongst the Japanese community. I strongly believe she is the reincarnation of Jesus. She is the nicest kindest chillest dopest professor at UO. The world would be a better place if all professors became like furikado sensei

Furikado is a great teacher. She's quite strict about grading but she gives her students a lot of opportunities and chances. The class is very homework heavy so be prepared to do it every night. At the end of the term, there is extra credit so make sure you do it. Japanese is a difficult language but she makes it an enjoyable learning experience.

Furikado sensei is so sweet and shows that she really cares about her students! Super organized, funny, willing to help, and just awesome! Use of textbooks is heavy but it's necessary if you really want to learn the language.

Furikado-sensei is very interested in her students and very helpful. There is a lot of homework but that is to be expected in 100 level classes. I have greatly enjoyed this class and will be taking the rest of the series with her if possible.
Helpful, funny, kind teacher who doesn't give out a whole lot of work. As long as you prepare for the oral and writing exams, you'll do well in the class.

Really fun and sweet teacher who knows her stuff but gives relatively little work. She's really thorough and explains examples very well. Yes, it's mandatory attendance, but it's a class I find myself always looking forward to.
Professor was genuine and enjoyed teaching but the content, more specifically discussion posts and tests were so complex and the prompts more often than not made zero sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: asked us about big brother

I was surprised by this class! I thought it would be a lot more political than it was, though it was pretty chill, and nobody wanted to start an opinion war. The content surprised me too with some occasionally really engaging stuff! Not everything registered/resinated with me, though the stuff that did was very informative and engaging. Cool class!

I think everyone should be required to take Ethnic Studies. Its quite mind-blowing. So many readings. (That I survived w/o doing) Other than that weekly quizzes that google had every answer to. The midterm and final is short answer (kinda hard) Take notes and you'll be good
Passionate about teachings and helpful with students.

Very kind lady, but she mostly just read off slides. Regardless, it was interesting, socially relevant material to learn. Super easy concepts to follow, just a lot to do each week in terms of hw and reading. If you're into social justice issues, take the class! if not, then you'll find the course incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fujiwara is amazing. I had taken ES101 before this, and that should tell you that she's worth learning from. I had her when in-person classes were still in session and after classes went fully remote. Both courses had no exam but a meaningful project where you learn a lot from. Textbooks aren't required but there are books assigned.
The amount of content in her course is heavy. She goes above and beyond to take student feedback into account. Her lectures were well informed, detailed, and eye-opening.

Fujiwara is just the best. Her class is extremely well organized and she is genuinely caring. She provides reading materials so that students do not have to purchase them. Just a wonderful little lady, you'll learn a lot from her. Assignments are straightforward and fairly easy. Just show up to class!

Lynn gave really long lectures that seemed never ending and assigned a lot of readings which were difficult to keep up with. However, her lectures were always meaningful and I learned a lot from the class, it was a huge eye opener and often left me in tears.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Fujiwara is a very passionate and kind professor. Her lectures are often long and a bit boring, but the content of the class majority of the time is super important and thought-provoking. ES101 is a very important class to take and will open your eyes to so much.

She's a nice lady but lectures are incredibly dull. She just reads from the slides or puts on a documentary. Everything is graded by GE, a few online quizzes and a paper. Midterm and final were short answer take-home. I only skimmed the readings to quote in assignments and was fine. Would not recommend

Super sweet person. She's funny and cares a lot for her students. While I already understood the topics going into the class, I would say people new to the subject would have little to no trouble understanding after her lectures. She basically restated the main ideas from the readings in her lectures. As long as you have that, tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Ms. Fujiwara is very passionate about the subject, and it shows in her lectures, but the workload and depth of subject makes this 101 level course feel like a 300 level course. Between the massive amounts of readings and the confusion about what is going to be on tests and quizzes and what isn't, I never felt good going into new assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I very much enjoyed this class. Fujiwara's lectures were sometimes a bit monotonous, but she was clearly informed and engaged in the class. The content felt relevant and mostly easy to understand. Grading was clear and easy to do well in- if you skim the readings and take notes in lecture you'll probably walk away with an A.

No textbook, all readings online. All the assignments were graded by the GTFs, and she has open office hours that I never really needed. Good lectures, with a few movies thrown in. Take good notes and a B is almost certain.

She was a really nice women and had quite a few interesting topics. I felt it was a little feminizing and pro-women more than she had wanted the class to be. I really liked learning about genders and how people feel about not fitting into certain categories.
Lynn is a great professor, she requires a lot from her students as far as reading, but well worth it!

I came into the class pretty interested in the subject matter but came out more confused and not sure anymore. I'm not sure if reading 200-400 pages a week was actually helpful. Going to class won't help clarify what the readings were about either. If you want to learn more about Ethnic Studies avoid her class or you'll regret it.

I really like her. She's passionate about what she teaches, she's really easy to talk to and you can really tell she wants you to do well in her class and understand the materials. Her quizzes and exams never go into memorizing details as she only requires you to understand the main points of things. She's also got a giggly light-humored side to he

There is a lot of reading for this class and some of it didn't seem like it really connected to her lectures.  There were dicussion groups where GTF's seemed to do a lot of the work to clarify the lecture.
Lynn is a very good professor. She is extremely knowledgeable about what she teaches and you can tell she's passionate about it. She also kept class fun and used a lot of visuals in lectures.
Fujiwara is a good teacher with a lot of passion for the subject, gained a lot of info from this class. Didn't give a lot of different views, was pretty much one-sided. GTF's were good.

Class is easy if you go to class and discussion. No exams just easy papers. Lynn does not know what she is talking about though. She gives one side of the information and does not know about the facts that she is talking about. VERY disorganized and comes across in lectures. GTF's gave the best lectures of the class.

Doesn't know the topic she teaches.  She has a lot of statistics and facts, but she can give no further information pertaining to them.  If you ask her a question it's generally deflected in some way.  It's as if SHE took WGS101 from another professor and just copied the notes with no background information.
good teacher. gtf's did the grading (not a good thing sometimes). good at explaining exactly what she expects from assignments and tests.

I loved Lynn's class! She has great personal experiences to talk about and is able to actually discuss the books that we were suppose to read. She also made the 3 hours class go by very quickly and never found myself bored.
I found this class to be very interesting and Lynn did a great job putting together interesting lectures. The tests are also quite easy :)

This is the worst class I have ever taken.  She does not have a firm grasp on race theory, despite it being an area of specialty for her. Her only awareness of racial theory is racial formation, needless to say there's much more in the academic literature. She cannot "control" classroom dynamics, basically she totally sucks.

Fulden's Feminist Philosophy class was one of the best classes I ever took at this University. If you're a real philosophy student you probably like to think (I do!), and I can guarantee that Fulden's philosophy classes in general will make you think. I was impressed with her knowledge of the subject, and the freedom I had to do good work.

Probably the worst class I have ever taken in this university. Her essay prompts are extremely unclear and she refuses to clarify. She only focuses on the writing of your papers and not the actual content. She mentions in the beginning that this is a reading intensive course, but it's also a writing intensive course. 4 essays in ten weeks.
Terrible. If you don't have the exact same views as she does prepare to fail the class. Extremely biased and completely unable to look at things from a different perspective.

He is an excellent speaker, but rarely speaks about stuff that is relevant to the lectures or tests. You're better off reading the textbook. He gives little examples and the quizzes vary on format. You still have to go to class for iClicker questions but I recommend just showing up and leaving after you get the credit.

Material would have been easier to understand with a different teacher. I went to almost every lecture but learned everything from the textbook. His expectations weren't clear and his tests were hard to prepare for.

Lectures were long and confusing. It seems like sometimes he just stands there and rambles on and on. Discussion leader sections were more helpful and understanding than lectures. Tests were tough. Would recommend this course, just with another professor.

Lectures were hard to follow and were confusing. He seems to just sit up there and ramble sometimes. Discussion leader was more clear and understanding than lecture. Material isn't hard but he makes you work for it. Take whoever else is available.

Dr. Furtado knows what he is talking about. His lectures are super interesting and if you miss them you won't be ready for tests. The slides don't really have info he just talks. His lecture speed is perf for note taking though. Other than attendance his classes are super straightforward and test subjects are never a surprise. Great class.
Loved this class!

Participation matters in discussion. His lectures were interesting and he posted the power-points. BUT, the power-points do not have a lot words - only pictures that he explains in class. So, attendance is not mandatory but highly recommended. mandatory attendance for discussion.

Furtado moves fast so you will need to make sure to be taking clear notes. He gives great lectures that make you want to come to class. As for homework you only have one, one page paper a week. Discussion is mandatory but very helpful. Make sure to participate in discussion in order to get a good participation grade. Overall great class!!

Furtado has great lectures that he actually makes very interesting and easy to understand. He definitely makes it worth it to show up to class. There are readings every week that pertain to the short 1-2 page paper due in section. The readings are not too long or difficult and are very relevant to course content. Section is mandatory but worth it.

The workload in this specific course 'HIST 298 - Medieval Knighthood' wasn't too bad it just required some reading, a few essays, and actually learning/studying the material especially before exams. Dr. Furtado is one of the best lecturers I've ever had, was very passionate about what he taught, and it was a class I actually looked forward to!

Professor Furtados is very knowledgeable and informational. His lectures are worth attending. Would highly recommend. You have to write a few short 1-2 page papers in section, but otherwise just a little reading. He knows that it's a 100 level class and teaches his students in a way that is easy to comprehend.

He is a great speaker and his powerpoints always let you know what he is going to be talking about so you can easily take his bullet points and add to them with what he has to say. Sections are mandatory but they're super helpful if you get the right GTF. Definitely taking another one of his classes.

Professor Furtado is a well educated scholar and a great teacher. His lectures are always fun, funny, and engaging. He assigns a lot of reading, which he expects all of his students to do. Sometimes specific readings are assigned to smaller groups, who will present what they read to the rest of the class. Paper assignments are open and manageable.

This class was super easy for me.  The lectures are okay, sometimes it's exciting, sometimes its not.  Tests are easy.  He pretty much lets you know what's going to be on the test.  Basically you just prepare three essays for the test and recite it on the test same as for quotes.  Love this class! Tutorial is helpful if you skipped lecture
He's a good speaker and lectures aren't as boring but it's like one of those professors teachings where you either learn well with the way he teaches or you don't.
He is an awesome teacher. I learned so much in his class. i HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING HIS CLASSES.

Really fantastic professor. You will have to put some effort in but other than that, his notes/lectures are very engaging and interesting. Lectures are not mandatory (discussions are) but I highly recommend attending lectures. He is very passionate about his subject which is extremely refreshing. Definitely take this class!

Very engaging, energetic, and precise. Prof Furtado is very approachable and constructive if you have any questions. No need to tape your eye-lids open because he makes his lectures very engaging, you'll wonder where the time went. Very clear and manageable midterm/final study guides provided. One of the best lecturers I've had
He was an awesome professor one of my favorite that I have had at the University of Oregon

The first half was confusing, and seemed pointless, but the second half was so much better and interesting. I loved going to class. There is no surprises. He tells you what you need to know. Great class.
Great professor but hard work load.
Awesome Professor. Definitely my favorite one I have had at UofO. He knows his stuff, and is very enthusiastic.

Prof. Furtado's lectures fascinated me. Coming to class is important, because everything he says could potentially be on the midterms, but I believe the grading is pretty fair. Definitely a very challenging class but extremely worth it. He can also be pretty intimidating, but I believe he's a nice guy in general.

I agree with all of the people ahead of me. His class is hard, but worth it. I have really loved it. His enthusiasm for history makes the class much more exciting and interesting. He is very approachable and I feel like I have learned so much from him.   I would love to take a class of his again.

Definitely my favorite lecture class so far. He knows SO MUCH about history it's very inspiring to sit there and listen to him talk about the material. I agree with the other comments, you must put in a lot of effort to get an A but it's totally worth it.
I'm a science major but i found his class very interesting and he definitely knew his stuff. He was very friendly and approachable. He is fair but the effort must be put forward to get the grade.
Great course. One of the best lecturers I've ever heard, super enthuiastic abut the subject.  Really made it come to life.  Don't expect an A if you don't do A work, though -- tough but fair.

Professor Hongo is the GOAT. For CRWR 230, there were only 5 assignments and as long as you are honest and show up to lectures, you will get an A. He is very understanding about missing class or turning in late assignments due to personal unexpected circumstances. Literally the funniest professor I've ever had and the most insane lore - 10/10 class

Mr. Garrett Hongo is a fraud. He thinks he's a woke wizard and grinds an axe against anyone who isn't a POC, and especially if they appear to have money. He does this while living large off the largesse of U of O.

Professor Hongo is a bully of a man hiding behind his 3 decades of tenure to belittle his students, often attempting to "trigger" them and then blaming their emotional responses on "white fragility." He is a bitter old man who does not deserve to be teaching students. No matter how good of a poet he might be.

Professor Hongo is a great poet but a terrible teacher. He went way beyond critique and insulted students and their work. For someone respected at UO, I was disappointed that he made us afraid to turn in our personal work (yet we were scolded if it wasn't "vulnerable"). I learned good techniques on imagery and also how to not teach a class.

The absolute WORST professor I've ever had. Never answered my questions directly, was extremely unorganized and confusing. TA's never seemed to know what was going on as if there was no communication between them and the professor. I could go on but theres not enough characters to describe how evil this course and the professor are.

The WORST professor I've ever had. He never answered a question directly, was completely unorganized and unhelpful at every moment. The TA's never seemed to know what was going on and there was a major lack of communication between them and the professor. There's not enough characters for me to express how evil this course and professor are.

He's clearly interested in the material he's teaching and cares about his students; lectures are a bit dry sometimes, but he was extremely understanding when issues or emergencies came up during the quarter.

It is sad to see the reviews about Dr. Nazin here. Yes, he was quiet and soft spoken but when you ask him questions, he explains concepts with depth. During his spring quarter sequence, I was dealing with a lot of health issues and Dr. Nazin went out of his way to grant me an INCREDIBLY generous extension. He definitely cares about his students.

Professor clearly does not want to be teaching this course. All lectures are extremely long and math-heavy but do not make connections to the actual labs. Makes a big deal about not accepting late work, yet over half of our assignments still haven't been graded by week 10. TA's also rarely know what's going on and do not provide help in labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures focus on math and derivations, not on the concepts needed to complete the labs. Most lab reports didn't get graded until the last week of the class. Lack of communication between the professor and the TAs, most of whom seemed to not enjoy working with him.
Terrible at grading criteria, bad feedback, and teaches irrelevant information . Slides are WAY too long, drones on and on about math, doesn't cover concepts.
Expert knowledge in her field with the ability to illustrate through engaging lectures that feels like a real conversation with the students.

This was an amazing class I took during Fall Term of my freshman year. The work itself is definitely fun and doable if you're confident that you have that level of French. There's a lot of reading, but the class is based on culture and literature, so it's expected. We had vocab quizzes which were not spontaneous. Get ready to watch some fun films!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing class, amazing teacher, best French class I've taken. There's no midterms or finals, just three tests spread throughout the term alongside homework. Expect to read a lot for homework, but none of it is particularly long. Tests are very important; if you tank one, your grade is going to suffer and it might be hard to recover if you don't try

If you aren't a good test taker, this class is not for you. All of the homework is easy, but it's 5 points per assignment. That being said, if you slip up on one test, your grade will tank BADLY. I did not pass the first test and my grade never recovered. She also gives no feedback on tests.

Easily one of the best professors you'll ever have. There's LOTS of reading, but she is understanding about late homework, and an incredible lecturer and storyteller. Highly recommend taking her class.

She's very nice, funny, and informative. She's very passionate about her culture and teaching it. This class puts a heavy emphasis on grammar, but written portions of tests are graded for content, not grammar. Her tests are easy and she gives you all the time you need. Also an awesome storyteller. No final either, just three midterms.
Just be ready to read. Overll she is awesome. You will easily get an A

SHE'S JUST AWESOME. YOU GOT HOMEWORKS AND DUE DATES FOR DATES BUT IF EVER YOU GET BUZY SHE LETS YOU TAKE YOUR TIME TO SUBMIT THE ASSIGMENT LATER. THE TEST ARE NOT THAT HARD BUT YOU'LL DEFINITELY HAVE TO READ A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Elle est une très bonne professeure. Elle enseigne dans une manière détendue et intéressante. On peut lapprocher si on a des problèmes privées, elle est très compréhensive. Je laime beaucoup!!! Prenez ce cours :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Gerdaline was an amazing professor. She really respects student who bring their thoughts into the discussion. She's not very critical of grammar which creates a great discussion course. Test are the expected difficulty and she grades written responses on content not grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very understanding and makes class very engaging, interesting, and efficient.
Very knowledgeable. Easy grader. Cares about the language. Not stuffy or unapproachable at all. Great storyteller and very funny.
Was very helpful and understand

Very nice and welcoming, you can tell she cares about how her students do. Very knowledgeable about French culture and language and history. Her world experiences benefit her teaching and her reading selections are varied and interesting. Little summaries of each article mean you have to read them, but the summaries are not graded hard at all.

Geraldine Poizat-Newcomb is by far the best professor I have ever had at the University.  She is an extremely compassionate and intelligent individual, but her ability to teach students so much beyond what’s in the syllabus is what I admire most.

She teaches in a way which brings each person up instead of glorifying the few.  Although she teaches significantly more than just the subject matter, she teaches people how to understand others and themselves.  In her classes, she teaches a way of thinking and understanding that can be applied to any discipline.  She is one of my top professors.

Mme Poizat-Newcomb was an excellent French teacher with an excellent understanding of her subject matter. While her class can be challenging, she has a great sense of humor and incorporates real world experiences in class. This was a class I never missed--would definitely take a class from her again!
Very great professor and super intelligent.

This profeesor is one of the most helpfull I have ever had.  She was always very willing to help me and make sure that every student understood the material.  Discussions were always very interesting.  She always gives a lot of constructive criticism on papers which is useful, and is also very understanding when extensions are needed.  This professor also facilitates a non threatening classroom environment for  all skill level.

Wasn't too impressed by teaching abilities. Really likes to translate so if not too good in French it's a pretty easy class, but my own skills were not ameliorated. Tests and papers easy. Just a boring class.

His lectures can seem a bit fast at times, but he's a great teacher, very willing to help students outside of  class with anything they need, in a very empathetic manner. Class is heavy on exams but they dont drift much further than what the practice exam is.

Yan Ge is usually quiet and calm, but really nice. When it comes to math, he gets super passionate and explains things well. He really values your approach to exams, and good ideas can earn a lot of credit even if the answer isn't perfect. I'd take his class again for sure.

Math 253 is tough, but Yan's class is actually really fun. The course covers knowledge for dealing with sequences and series, and those can get pretty complex. What I really liked, though, was how everything was tied together using different toolboxes, and it made things much clearer. The part I struggled with was entering answers on WebWork.

Yan Ge is thoughtful and helpful. He responds to feedback, explains well and supports students when they need it. The class is hard, but if you go to class and do the homework its doable. He gives formulas and partial credit on tests. The final grade also has a decent curve which helps. Would 100% take a class with him again!

The lecture and notes are great, though some of the calculations are tricky. Right now, I'm sitting at an A-, and I'm busy reviewing for the final. Here's me crossing my fingers and hoping I can bump that up to a solid A!

His canvas page is poorly structured. All term theres been nothing in the grade book (updates every few wks at midterms) Now its wk 9 and he just told us that hes just updated the grades to reflect the real weighting. I thought I was good at a 90 and now I'm barely at 80. It seems cruel that we cant know our grades until it's too late to change it.

Ge is a pretty good professor. His lectures are clear and the homework isn't too bad. Just make sure you study hard on your own. If you took AP calc AB in high school, I would recommend asking an advisor to take 252 before taking 253. Some of the calc 2 content isn't covered, leaving knowledge gaps that are hard to fill on your own.

Yan doesn't just stand in front of the class and deliver knowledge as if he has all the answers. Instead, he approaches teaching as a shared journey of discovery. He starts by guiding students to think through the problem from the ground up, encouraging curiosity and active engagement,  making learning both engaging and rewarding.

Yan is super nice and really easy to talk to! He explains things clearly, so even the tough formulas make sense. His way of answering questions in class is really clever—he makes you think but in a good way. You can tell he actually cares about his students, which makes Math 253 a great class to be in!

He is a really nice guy, he is just a little hard to understand with his accent. I wouldn't not take his class because of the accent, it just takes a minute to get used to. The tests are pretty hard but the class is graded pretty forgivingly. He's great at answering questions in a fun and exciting way. Only take Math 253 if you need to, though.

Had Yan for 252+253, truly a gem in the math department. Go to the lectures and pay attention! I never felt unprepared for an exam and did not feel the need to cram the night before. Very caring and understanding. I never even touched the textbook or knew that we even had one with Yan's teaching. He is the GOAT

Very chill professor and very caring. He walks the students through each topic slowly and effectively which is really helpful. Students can also ask questions about previous topics (such as 251/252) and he will explain it to you.

Had him in the Spring of 2024. His tests are fair and reasonable, without tricks or unfair questions. Any potentially difficult problems are covered in sample reviews. He encourages students to come to the front and work out problems during the office hours. While the lectures cover many examples, some appear in the quizzes and exams.

Yan has a pretty heavy accent that can sometimes be hard to understand. Despite this, he is probably one of the best math teachers I've ever had. Would 100% take a course taught by him again

Prof. teaches very slowly which is to our benefit. He explains concepts thoroughly and while knowledge of Math 251+252 is expected, he'll always be happy to re-explain older concepts to help you. His class is organized, HWs aren't too difficult & all on webwork w/ unlimited attempts, weekly quizzes are short and easy, and exams cover relevant info.

A pretty nice guy. He is very respected and organized in notes and lectures. The notes are all posted on Canvas, and he goes through the material slowly without missing anything. He is very helpful and accessible during office hours. In this course, the difficulty level is Midterm2 > Quizzes > Final > Midterm 1.
Test and quiz heavy. Tests were very difficult.
Good teacher

Rhone is without a doubt one of the best teachers I have ever had. I completed the entire 200-level cycle with him and learned so much. He truly cares about supporting and engaging with students which always made class fun. Rhone is truly an expert at French and knows exactly how to teach to students at all levels.

Rhone is great! I would definitely recommend his French class. He is super funny and cares a lot about his students. He's very passionate about teaching and loves French, and clearly wants his students to succeed. He is accessible outside of class and more than willing to work with you, one of the best teachers I've had.

Rhone is an incredibly sweet, super approachable and funny guy. He develops really strong bonds with the class and is a very easy grader. He gives clear and constructive feedback and is easily accessible outside of class, and doesn't take things too seriously. Would highly recommend, one of my favorite instructors ever.
I adore Rhone and heavily encourage everyone to take his classes! He makes the classes enjoyable, fun, and community-focused.
Prof. Geha was a great teacher for fr 201. Overall, he is super approachable and easy to talk to. He is an easy grader as long as you do the material and prepare appropriately.

She is very passionate about the material, makes it come to life, is very thorough with her teaching and makes sure to make space for students to ask questions and is understanding the subject and its complexities! I really love her teaching style and presence!
This class is definitely tough for some people. The key is to have a really good final project since thats 40% of your grade and make sure you don't miss any of the museum visits!!

I had her for arts of the silk road. She can be tough but it's bc she has high expectations and she expects you to put in work and critically think. Rly not that bad if you pay attention during lectures and study. She can be tough with technology stuff tho which kinda sucks, but other than that I don't get the hate.
She doesn't care about any outside situations. What goes on in canvas is the only thing that matters. Does not care about technology issues.

This professor did not care about technology issues. This professor grades strictly and designs tests poorly. It is impossible to get a decent score in this class. The lectures cannot be studied even if they are online because they are mostly just pictures. She will do everything in her power to fail you.

Dr. G lectures by showing pictures and talking at you, instead of putting the information on the screen. This can make it hard to digest info in the lectures. The grading system is extremely harsh and confusing as there doesn't seem to be a grading rubric and sometimes grades are negotiable if you email them with reason.

Lectures were heavily information-packed and Slides were not posted for students to see afterward, making it a task to find information and study for tests. Grading is done by GE, there is little to no feedback on assignments on what can be improved.

I have never had a worse experience. Her lectures are long  and nothing makes sense. She hates answering questions. The GE's are terrible. I took the multiple choice midterm with someone and we had 20-point differences even tho we put the exact same answers. She is completely rude, a terrible teacher, and has no respect for her students.

she is horrible at giving lectures and there are only a total of 5 assignments each worth 10% of your grade and only 48 hours to do each one. Doesn't care about how unfair the grades are and does nothing to clarify expectations. Very passive aggressive to students and sometimes her info is just wrong. this class was very difficult
love this class! Not

Gasparini would hardly put words on her slides leaving you to only gain information from her speaking but she has a very thick accent that I personally struggled to understand. reviews.comment: I lost brain cells in this class because of how bad this professor is at teaching

This professor is really stingy when it comes to grading and will mark you down for the smallest thing ever. Dont take this class

One of the most unfairly graded and difficult classes I have ever taken. Weekly readings dense and difficult, lectures and slides hard to understand for studying, teacher unhelpful and condescending to student struggle. Got 100% on almost all assignments, somehow got D on both tests. Even got graded down on EXTRA CREDIT despite simple instructions.

Class is easy to follow until it's not, even with a solid background in the subject. This is the worst class I have ever taken at UO & would not recommend it to anyone! A 200 level course but the amount of detail the prof expects is insane. Don't take this class
Meh

Disorganized course layout- readings hard to find, due dates often at unclear/strange times and 0 credit if late. Lots of dense academic readings that were only addressed at surface level. Such an interesting class and such a great teacher. She talks about a wide range of things and doesn't get stuck on subjects. You learn A LOT in a short amount of time, but she definitely makes it interesting and worthwhile. Easy to get an A in the class as long as you show up. The final projects are pretty big and daunting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Assigned readings are jumbled, not chronological nor seemed to be that related thematically, and were uninteresting. Lectures are unspecific and unclear which information is important for test.

Really enjoy the way she lectures - definitely plan to take another class taught by her next term. She listened to previous feedback and implemented a new testing system (midterm was only 20 questions, open note, held online over canvas, and you had 2 hours to take it). Only downside: a lot of reading, but it's all posted so cost effective.

I enjoyed the content of this class and take thorough notes so I enjoyed it but the midterm was unnecessarily long - 3 hours and I barely finished. I understand there's a lot of content to get done but I think maybe this class could be an intro and there could be a second class covering it. I took Japanese Art history & it wasn't nearly as intense.

reviews.comment: Her lectures are unorganized. She is just constantly throwing information at us but in a way where I do not know which aspects are important. The tests ask us about extremely specific pieces of art and will sometimes call back to things she only spoke for a couple of seconds about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not put yourself through this. The workload is unnecessary and ridiculous. Criteria for grading couldn't be more unclear, and she won't hesitate to give you a bad grade. reviews.comment: Despite being a measly 200-level class, as well as the circumstances of a literal PANDEMIC, Professor Gasparini shows no lenience for her students. The assignments for this course are INTENSIVE, and grading is harsh. Don't waste your time with an instructor who lacks compassion for your humanity and well-being as a student, you deserve better.

Miriam is nice and offers great insight and feedback on writing, but be aware that you cannot earn an A in her class unless you do the extra credit assignments. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The instructions are clear for every assignment, and even if you do well on something, she will always offer helpful feedback. It is important to note that she will often say you did great on an assignment, but give you a B. The extra credit offered really helps with bumping your grade up.

This was the easiest class I've ever taken. It was honestly more akin to 7th grade english rather than college level writing. The teacher has a really stupid grading system where if you do everything right, you get a B. She also says she "doesn't grade on the quality of writing" so assignments are practically only for completion.
Helpful, inspiring, kind, and generous with her time. You can't find a better writing instructor! She's the best.

It's true that she doesn't like to grade papers with an A. Her comments will say something like "Excellent, good point," etc., but she will never give higher than a B+. Also I was early for class every day, talked in class, and had no absences, but she gave me a B on attendance/participation.
Very Enthusiastic about what she teaches.  Enjoyed very much taking her class and wish to take a class with her again in the future.

Miriam is a great example of what professors should expect of their students at a college level. Students that have complained about Miriam's grading are going to have a difficult time with upper level courses. If you disagree with her expectations, chances are you'll disagree with the expectations of most professors at the university level.

Very nice teacher I liked a lot. She'll give u a C for showing up and handing work in, but expect effort for anA. She gave me a good grade, but I had to rewrite a LOT. Use her office hours and she'll tell you EXACTLY how to fix your paper.

Miriam is fun!! Her workload might be a lot but if you are on top of schedule u'll do fine. Class time are usually discussions. She explains what she expects and if u meet the criterias it's an automatic A. If u attend all class and turn in work on time she garantees u at least a C or Pass. Definitely recommended.

It is not impossible to earn an A in Miriam's class. She's doesn't let lazy freshman that still belong in high school get away with bad papers, being late, or texting during class. Effort is needed to earn a higher grade and if you have questions, she is  personable and helpful. Students get out of the class what they put into it.

Miriam is actually a nice teacher but dont believe what she said. I turned in my first draft of my essay and she put comment on my paper. She said that my paper was good and just needed a little bit of touching. However, I got C on my paper. SHE ALWAYS SAY "GOOD, EXCELLENT" Dont believe this, it means you will get C!! Do not take her class!!

impossible to get an A. her grading system is ridiculus. a lateness (or absence) is very likely to cost you 5 grades on your overall average grade. her whole lecture ''style'' is simply asking students what they think about the subject at hand.

Miriam was nice. Very helpful during office hours. She made sure everybody participated in class. But...her way of grading was dumb. Nice person but not good in grading. I couldn't believe I got a C for missing 5 lines to complete my whole paper, even though I had a good argument. >:-(
She is funny at all. Its not easy to get an A in her class. I don't really like her!

Miriam was great.  She was the best teacher I've had at stimulating discussions, which is hard to do when some of the kids don't want to participate.  She's smart and knows her stuff.  Great experience
Miriam was an great teacher, the class was fun but she graded kind of hard.
No Comments
an informative class, and she knew the material well...but i really didnt like her at all
No Comments
I got a good grade in the class, but simply put this teacher is garbage.

Miriam Gershow is an excellent teacher and very friendly. She doesn't, however, put up with any baloney -- especially from lazy freshmen who'd rather socialize than write -- so always do the readings and always show up on time.
Worst...Teacher....Evar

Lectures were a little boring sometimes, but also pretty interesting at other times. I didn't like the wording on the tests and the topics in the lectures were a bit dry and confusing at times. With that said, the papers were short, and the tests weren't too tough.

Man this guy is a goood teacher man. I mean he just really listened to me and was able to keep me in focus. I actually love this class. He had very easy grading and rounded my grade from a c+ to a A+ what a good guy. AM I RIGHT?

I enjoyed his class. Nothing amazing, but a solid experience. He is a hard to contact at times, but his tests are straight forward and the paper is easy. Follow the study guide and do all the homework and you will do well in his class.

This class is very boring and the professor is very bland. His lectures are unorganized and hard to follow, but overall the class is very easy. He takes attendance sometimes and there are some in class activities, but it was a pretty easy A. His tests had clear study guides

I honestly cannot stand this professor. Ive taken him twice now and both times I got the worst grade out of all my classes from him. His criteria on the essay makes no sense and the final is worth 35%. He literally ruined an interesting topic. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

I enjoyed the class overall. Attended every class. Had near perfect on all assignments and 91% on the midterm. I had a bad finals week dealing with family issues. I received a "C" on the final bringing my overall percentage in the class to 89.6%. This is literally 2 points on his grading scale. I was given a B+ and grade was not rounded up.
Lectures are engaging, and easy to understand. Majority of grade comes from midterm and final, but the exams are pretty easy and study guides are very helpful.
Very Knowledgeable. Very nice guy. Expert on his topics. His slide shows are great, if a little bit plane. He has very little stage presence and is a VERY boring lecturer.

The subject matter itself is interesting, but I caught myself dozing off during lecture from time to time.  He will occasionally do things in a manner that does not make much sense, but he is clear enough in his lectures and study guides to make the class easily passable.

I would highly recommend taking a regular statistics course before taking this course with this professor, or you will be so confused. His classes were incredibly boring, and he was not very good at explaining any of the information. I just relied on my previous knowledge of statistics and the book.

Extremely boring. Reads directly from slides, so there is absolutely no point in coming to class. GTF is very helpful and does everything (grading, holding review sessions, etc). Prof seems uninterested in his own topic.

One of the most boring and unhelpful professors I have ever had! Read directly from slides. Monotone voice that really puts you to sleep. Also, doesn't really teach you anything, you need to learn from the book.
Dull professor. However, class was pretty simple. GTF's graded everything. Relies heavily on the book. Trys to be funny, but lectures ended up being really boring.

I went to him to help me out with a problem with students in class two times and he did not help me out, actually contributed to the problem.  Also, I heard him call a student a "sh-- head."  The class material is very generalized across personality psychology.
Dry, boring, thinks he's funny.  Doesnt know how to respond well to students' questions.

Good Instructor. Overall, he is organized, informative, and a pretty lecturer. The class isn't particularly difficult and is interesting to sit through. The materials assigned are fabulous, he chooses the most "readable" texts I've had yet.
funny teacher, but I didn't find him very helpful in one on one questions nor during lectures although he made them bareable.

One of the best classes I've ever had at UO. Pooya has a calm lecture style. The exams are mostly based on what is reviewed in class. I liked the live engagement assignments.
