This course is hard but great. He is genuinely invested in the subject materials and puts a lot of care and effort into presenting them. The exams are open book, but you have to do the readings before the exam if you want a good grade.
Gives good feedback and is a fair grader
Very clear in expectations and very willing to help in class and during office hours. Very approachable, and truly wants students to learn. This class has a lot of writing though
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy but he isn't the best professor out there. He's only taught a few classes but you can tell he really wants to improve and asks for feedback. There is a lot of writing but that is with any PSY 303 course, he is very approachable though. I would take him again.

The textbook wasn't required, which is nice. Labs doable but sometimes hard, GE was helpful, and so was Thomas. He is friendly, approachable, and helpful. Quizzes are done with iClicker mainly for participation credit. The final project was fairly easy and simple. No exams. Just show up and take notes. Time for labs in class. Easy and fun class!

He himself is a good professor. He's really passionate about volcanos and earthquakes. It's the GE's that stink. The labs are graded super harshly and wording makes no sense. Please don't take this class unless you wanna be confused by every lab

The class is very easy. Lectures are good and in class quizzes are simple things from the slides. I see a lot of people saying labs are graded harshly and they can be confusing but if you talk to him or a TA about the labs they are actually fairly simple and easy to complete. He drops your 4 lowest quizzes and lowest lab grade.

Thomas is very passionate about his profession and very knowledgeable. However this class felt like I needed a pre-req. The labs are graded harshly and worded confusingly, switching to pass/fail bc this class will tank my GPA. Thomas said that the course would be tailored to the difference of majors and experience in college. Don't take this class.

The labs in this class were graded really harshly, I don't know if that is because of the professor or the GE. I don't like group projects but this one was easy enough. The lectures are not too dense and he is knowledgable and passionate. Great class if you need extra credits.
Favorite professor I had this past term. He cares for his students and the class is not hard if you just show up and pay attention.

Thomas is very clearly passionate about what he teaches and it makes for an interesting lecture. English is not his native language so there was some difficulty for me personally to fully comprehend everything immediately but it was not at all a problem for overall comprehension. Attendance isn't taken but iClicker quizzes are given every lecture.

I enjoyed the course material in this class, and he is a great professor. The labs are hard but if you stay and get help from the GE you should be fine. Thomas is very educated and passionate about volcanology, I would not recommend this class if you're not actually interested in the material or you will be very bored in lecture.

I really like the content of the class however some of the labs were EXTREMELY hard to the point where I reached out to other students and they also had no idea what to do. A majority of labs I didn't even turn in because I couldn't figure them out.

zero communication and essentially nothing on the canvas modules. everything is on the syllabus which wouldn't be a problem if any of it made sense. has required films to watch but expects you to hunt them down yourself even saying some are available on "paid streaming services"? do yourself a favor and pick any other class.

The class itself seems very interesting, so it is a shame that she has structured her class to be this way. I should've dropped this class when I had the chance. 50% of your grade is the midterm, and 50% is the final. If that tells you anything.

Took an online class with her, and she's very nice and helpful when you ask questions and such. But I think she's an unnecessarily hard grader (e.g., would give positive feedback but then take away a petty number of points on assignments without saying why?). It felt like she was just grading lower to grade lower. The material is interesting, IG.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Span 344, wouldn't let me add. Professor is super unorganized and the class felt like a hot mess. She rarely responded to emails, if she did, they were short responses that felt passive aggressive. Class content was interesting, but the teacher's organization made it almost unbearable. Only had her online, so cant speak to how she is in person.

Best Spanish professor I had at the UO. She comes from a Castillian speaking Spanish background and she is extremely well versed in her subject matter. I found her tough, funny, and very interesting to listen to in lectures. If you try hard and enjoy your studies she will respect you and be a great asset to learning!

Her class wasn't very difficult in the actual material we studied, but she was so disorganized (sometimes straight-up not coming to class and then yelling at us next time for being behind) and rarely answered my emails asking for help or clarification, that I can see why others struggled. Most of class time was wasted, but it wasn't a tough class.

I was repeatedly frustrated with her lack of interest in helping me. I received short, condescending responses to  the few emails I sent her and felt that my concerns were unimportant to her. She knows what she's talking about and the class itself wasn't bad, but her unnecessary rudeness made me completely disinterested in attending her lectures.

She definitely knows what she's talking about. Not 100% organized, but she's always available during her office hours to clear any doubt. Not arrogant at all, in fact, she's one of the best professors/person I've even known. Very engaging, A+.
Not my fave teacher here at all.  She treats you like your in elementary school and assigns busy work.  I feel like I'm wasting my time.  And when I asked her for some help she seemed annoyed.

Wow...she is just about the worst teacher I have ever had!  She is so unorganized and for some unknown reason she has decided to single me out and pick on me by putting me on the spot or calling me names.  She is very unprofessional, rude and arrogant.

The coursepacket that she assigned was not ready on time, and she wasn't much help as she still assigned us readings from the packet. She also assigns A LOT of unimportant tasks for us to do that are just busywork.  Her lectures can be interesting, but that're mostly about history and not literature. She seems arrogant as well.

She's a great lecturer, but she assigns a lot of little tasks that have to be done a specific way. Some of the requirements remind me of high school busywork. Very strict, attendance is taken every day in lecture AND discussion, but she's ready to help you in any way she can if you're struggling.
Best Prof I've ever had, always there with a smile and tie die t-shirt and brings the good vibes to class everyday. He goes on a lot of side tangents so be ready for that.
He is an amazing professor with a lot of energy and passion every day. I would definitely recommend taking his class if you like teachers who joke around and kind of go on side tangents a lot.
Engaging lectures, amazing personality. Always open to feedback. Learned quite a bit in the class, information was conveyed clearly.

Spike is by far one of my favorite professors. The passion he has for Linguistics is so admirable. The work for this class can be a bit tedious but that's to be expected in 100 level classes. He is lenient on late work and is a fair grader. If I were more interested in the Linguistics field, I would definitely take another one of his classes!

Very engaging lectures and tries his best not to get carried away. Class is fast paced so if you miss something and don't go back to learn it you WILL fall behind. Discussion sections are very helpful. Not much to be graded on so you have to put a lot of time on the assignments. Tests aren't too hard or too easy, but you HAVE to know the material.

Spike is an amazing lecturer whose passion for his work is infectious. Sometimes the workload in the class was bothersome, but he makes the classes well worth it. Spike is also lenient and cares about his students. He is a friendly guy and it is easy to ask him for help or clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy assignments, easy to pass, attendance isn't required. Moves and talks very fast, is unorganized. Does not accommodate to Section 504 students. First class he will go on a rant about how cussing shouldn't be taboo and cusses a lot, then says get ready to hear me cuss all term, then never really does which is strange. Okay professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moves fast, very passionate. Graded readings. Really funny guy but sometimes rambles off on somethng irrelevant to the class. Sometimes the readigns are really long ans give you informationt that isn't really tested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I took him for my FIG class and he was amazing. Very fun to listen to and even though attendance was mandatory, he wouldn't care as long as you don't fail the class. Also knows things get in the way so he accepts late work until the end of the term.

I wish I had the same experience as the other reviewers. Class has 6 homework assignments and 2 exams, which didn't feel like enough time to get familiar with the skills we need to do well. Often gets distracted during lecture and can make getting the important information hard. Discussion section is used for practice, but could be used better.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Spike is absolutely hilarious and his lectures are always engaging. Very knowledgeable and open to questions. Reading material is interesting but tedious. Tests have study guide questions but are quite hard and long so make sure you do your readings. Luckily, Spike is pretty flexible to student feedback. Overall would highly recommend!

The online class was fairly easy, just make note cards to study prefixes, roots, and suffixes. The exams weigh heavily, with the first few being easy, but the final exam and last exam being more difficult, so study thoroughly. But as long as you study & understand the assignments (that are not for grading and repeatable) on Canvas, should be fine.

Spike's definitely unique. He's so down-to-earth, funny, foul-mouthed, and intelligent. PowerPoints aren't used in this class, and I found it hard to immediately grasp key points. However, Spike builds upon things we learn from day one and I eventually understood everything. I learned more in this class than any other.
Interesting class, and Spike makes it funny. Do the readings, go to class and take good notes and you'll be fine. Test aren't if you are prepared.

He's passionate and loves what he teaches. Doesn't take attendance but doesn't use powerpoints/post notes either. GO TO CLASS! Talks fast so sometimes it's hard to keep up. Very colorful guy and isn't afraid to cuss in class to make a point! Overall a class worth taking. Covers a multicultural and Soc. Science gen ed credit!

I found Spike's class to be really interesting. Everyday he comes to class with an interesting shirt on. He is a funny guy and is really helpful when you email him questions. There is a lot of reading involved but all of it is not necessary. Go to all of the lectures.
Best prof I've had at the UO. Super enthusiastic, helpful, and beyond knowledgable. He is a ridiculously cool guy and everyone should take at least one class of his.

Don't know what y'all are talking about, Spike is tasty! He literally cannot shut up and is always positive about everything, ever. My kind'a people. He's exactly who SHOULD be teaching Linguistics, a mouthy word nerd with a heart of gold and a passion for people. Cheers, Spike!
Spike was awesome! Gives great preparation for the tests, if I had covered it further my grade would easily have been an A.

As a freshman, I was initially really worried about how my professors would be. When I walked into my first Ling 101 class and saw Spike in the front with his Darth Vader t-shirt, I immediately felt better. He talks fast, but as soon as someone brings it to his attention he slows down. He is very passionate about what he teaches, TAKE THAT CLASS
The class I took with Spike was one of the best I have taken at the UO.  His class is never dull, always interesting and I never wanted to miss it.

Best prof. I've had at UO.  He teaches way over his student's heads, but he knows that, and doesn't expect everyone to catch on.  He obviously loves his work and is extremely enthusiastic.  Spike was really laid back, easy to talk to, and was always available for extra help.  If you're taking LING 101, try to take it with Spike!
No Comments
No Comments

Fabulous prof, though he teaches over the heads of everyone the class.  He knows this, though, and doesn't expect people to get everything that he says.  If you remember that you don't need to understand everything (half is probably enough), it is a wonderful class.  The problems people had were when they felt responsible for all the material.
I think this prof is now at UNC (busi 286) very nice guy - entertaining lecture and overall 10/10. He just wants you to learn, put in the effort and you will get an A.

I took Finance 281 with Dr. Gilbert Roger and it was such an incredible experience. He is very passionate about his teachings and did an amazing job at connecting to his students. The entire quarter was a pleasure and equipped me with so much knowledge on financial stability, budgeting, investments, credit, and more. I would definitely recommend!

The class was overall pretty boring because of the material but Rogers is super nice, funny, and a great professor. But most of the material was out of the textbook with weekly quizzes on the reading.

Chad has so much more passion for math than any professor I've had before. By far my favorite math class I've taken. If you do the reading and make sure you understand all the homework/ In-class activities you'll do fine. You can tell that he really cares about every student getting the material so If you meet him half way hes an amazing prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectured at students rather than engaging them. Gave ridiculously long homework assignments (even over spring break). Super hard tests. Unforgiving grading. Not enthusiastic about material (openly admits to disliking it, even). Goes way too fast (even when class doesn't understand). Overestimates student capabilities. Not enough examples in class.

This man does not know how to teach. He readS directly from the book, gives 42 problems over spring break and makes the tests nothing like the homework. He is the worst teacher I have ever had, and I've had some pretty bad ones. If you don't want to teach yourself, DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS.

Chad is an awesome teacher. He explained calculus in a way that made it easy for me. The homework was challenging, but he was very willing to help with any problems. I ended up really enjoying this class.

Chad is a nice guy and a wonderful teacher.  Lightens up the material by not taking himself very seriously during class, but is very serious about math.  I recommend him very much.  Very helpful during office hours, also.

Very, very nice and Extremely helpful and accommodating. Likes class to be vocal during lectures. Would definitely recommend. Class also goes pretty slow compared to the other calculus sections. Chad was on a speaking tour this term, so we had two other subs: Mark Richards and a guy named Johnny. Both were good, but I liked Chad's lectures the best

Chad is a really understanding professor who really wants his students to understand the subject. He does have the tendency to get sidetracked during lecture, but he never expects you to know any of the weird proofs he goes off about or anything. Would definitely recommend.
No Comments

Great professor, very clear.  His in-class notes makes the homework/tests a lot easier.  For a math class, I actually enjoyed it.  Very reasonable and accommodating and funny too.  Nice guy, excellent teacher.
Very hard. Very very Hard. Very very very hard. Don't take his class it is really hard (!!)

I took Dr. Nikolaishvili's class at WFU. He clearly loves economics and did a great job introducing me to the subject. A lot of the final grades revolve around the tests, but you are allowed a cheat sheet on a A4 piece of paper. If your cheat sheet is good, the tests aren't too hard. Overall he was a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am taking Professor Nikolaishvili's class at WFU; the experience has been good so far. He is knowledgeable on the material and the class syllabus gives a solid introduction to the main foundational economic concepts. Class is test/final heavy but they are not too difficult and important material is outlined the class before the exam.

I think this is Gio's first year as an economics doctoral student. This class was online but very quiz and test heavy. The final is cumulative and requires an extensive amount of knowledge of a variety of equation functions and theories. However, he seems like a chill guy. Clearly passionate and knowledgeable
Always great lectures
A prankster
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very passionate about architecture and if you love it it's a very fun class. He can be repetitive and sometimes a bit boring but that's more so the course work itself — as a professor, great guy.

The GE's in this class were horrific they graded things like they had a gun to their head and weren't allowed to give A's, horrific communication as well never responds to emails, dont even need to show up to get an A

Givens is incredibly passionate about architecture, and he tries to imbue you with as much knowledge about it as he can. He gets repetitive after a while, but you will see a lot of cool pictures of buildings. If you have time, I would highly recommend doing all the readings to better understand architecture and the ways to understand it.

Givens really loves what he does and it shows in class. No quizzes or tests. Only hw is weekly discussion post graded on completion and a term paper. Very funny guy, interesting class. Lectures have a QR code for attendance.
Cool lectures

The most passionate professor I've had yet. Has an insane amount of knowledge of design, and he is an inspiration to all. Gives great feedback on design and the design process and is very flexible with due dates and whatnot. He is always willing to help at all times of the day (literally) and responds very quickly to any messages or questions.
Good teacher, knows what hes doing
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Givens is very passionate about his work. The lectures can get a little boring and are mostly focused on examples with no real application you can do yourself. For an intro level class it was good and I would suggest to anyone interested no matter if you're in the ARCH major or not.

He is very poetic and passionate in his lectures and very generous when it comes to extenuating circumstances (e.g. extended midterm deadline when many students didn't get it in on time, gave me an extension when I missed the deadline)

Professor Givens is one of the most passionate professors I've had. You can tell that he loves what he teaches and is open minded to new perceptions and ideas. His lectures were a highlight of the week, they were refreshing and inspirational. This class taught me to look at the world differently. I highly suggest taking this course!
This is the only professor I'm willing to hear a lecture from at 8AM. Protect this man at all costs.

VERY INSIGHTFUL AND PASSIONATE ABOUT ARCHITECTURE. LECTURES ERR TOWARDS A MORE ABSTRACT WAY OF THINKING BUT YOU CAN TELL THAT HE TRULY WANTS TO PROVIDE A GOOD FOUNDATION FOR HIS STUDENTS. I HAD TROUBLE COMMUNICATING BY EMAIL BUT WHEN APPROACHED AFTER CLASS WAS MORE THAN GLAD TO HELP WITH ANY ISSUES

He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He can be hard to reach through email, so talking to him before or after class is best. The class was pretty easy, it had a hybrid format so we only had to go to one lecture a week, and the rest were online. Graded with a midterm and term paper, as well as discussion posts.
The best professor here. Really cares about what he teaches. A real gem.

james is a good architect. he clearly knows what he is talking about and takes things straight to the point. im really glad he does his lectures hybrid mode but he can get carried away with the length that he makes them. the quizzes after the lectures are relatively easy but the term paper is a little hard
I love this man. He is so passionate

The prof. immerses you into the reasons why to love architecture; boiled down, how BEAUTY encourages sustainability. Givens is one of the most understanding people and gives leeway, extensions, and extra help when needed. Lots of bookwork and the lectures are plenty (online), but interesting! Visit the building for your final essay if possible.
This professor was awesome; I enjoyed his class a lot that was not difficult. The only struggle was the term paper. His lectures were hilarious.

I love this man. He is a great professor that listens and genuinely wants to help you further your design ideas. He's pretty funny, in an awkward dad kind of way, and he always dresses really nice which makes me respect him even more. He also gives the students the opportunity to work more independently than other professors i've had.
Givens is such a great prof. All of his lectures are so deep and he's such an intelligent guy. I cannot wait to have him as my prof for whatever I can get him for in the next four years.

Professor Givens knows the material and is passionate when it comes to his practice and his teaching. He is an experienced and engaging lecturer as well as a helpful reviewer. He is eager to share his experience in hopes that his students will be better suited for not only their life in school but their careers after graduation as well.

I loved this professor. First studio professor that I actually like. He is funny, he knows what he is talking about, he knows how to design, and he works with you in developing your design rather than trying to take it over like a lot of other studio professors. He is funny and he cares about his students.

Very inspirational professor. Uses a lot of visual descriptions when talking about buildings. really inspires you to be an architect if you have any interest in the way buildings look. Be prepared to read

The professor was not accessible at all and barely responded to his emails, lectures are not clear. He loves to talk about his work and the examples he gives in class are not useful at all because they do not correlate with his lectures. Unfortunately this class is the introduction to architecture; therefore, there is no way around it . GOODLUCK!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Had him first for ARCH 201 and it was awful, lectures are definitely not his strong suit. He seemed very arrogant and wasn't very clear with what he was trying to teach. However, I later had him for studio and he is the best studio professor I've ever had, he is very straight to the point and gives great feedback, also super funny!

Lecture Heavy. Only 4 graded projects and 2 midterms and no final exam. Final portfolio due on the last day of class that includes the 4 projects you have already done and the midterms you have already taken.

Tries very hard to speak poetically and metaphorically, which makes the lectures needlessly unclear. Most of your communication and grading will be directed to the GTF's in the ARCH201 class, can't speak to his studio classes. I don't really know why he teaches, it doesn't seem like he gets much out of it. Average, uninterested, droning prof.

This professor does not teach about architecture itself but rather the ideas behind it. He loves to talk about his own work and will glorify other works and expect you to do the same. It was a struggle each day not to fall asleep because the lectures were so incredibly hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the most unique designers left at the University of Oregon. If you have the chance get to know him. Under the deeply professional top layer you'll realize he is hilarious. He cares a lot about the students and while he seems intimidating he is always open to critique and debate. Great person and great professor.
not bad
Seemingly one of the only conceptual designers left at that school that is teaching studio. Great guy and has a lot of insight into the DEEPER questions.

Not bad for an intro to architecture class. His tests are more memorization than knowing how to use architecture to create a aesthetically pleasing environment. Not my favorite professor, but definitely not a bad one

Prof. Given's philosophical approach to architecture got me very interested in the subject, but is somewhat different than the types of challenges you'll encounter in studio. I especially liked that he would discuss famous buildings in detail and help us see exactly why they were so successful. Overall he is a good professor.
Mr. Givens is an extremely interesting man who dedicates his life to his work, and not to his women. The class is a little too philosophical for me but somewhat interesting.

James Givens is one hell of a man, I even told him so myself. At first I was infuriated by his philosophical talks of architecture, but soon I realized I was only mad at him because I wanted to be him. Mr. Givens knows everything there is to know about architecture. His lectures are astounding. If I was a woman I'd do my best to bear his children.
givens is very philosophical, when he speaks which i find awesome. he also is one of the most pationate people i have meet in any field. this is a great asset to have.

He is very excited about what he teaches. I checked his work out online and was impressed. This man knows what he's talking about when it comes to architecture. I absolutely loved the class this is one I would get excited to attend. Projects were fun and challenging.
he's very arrogant and pompous. not very helpful and does not respond to your needs. likes to show off his work thinking it's great, when unfortunately...it's not.

He is very passionate about human depths and meaningful experiences. One of the best professors I've had. He is very inspirational for those who are seeking something deeper. look past your iphones and myspace and you'll discover that there is something very true about him.
Givens is a great speaker, although a little arrogant. Classes are almost always fascinating, surprisingly not a naptime class!  Overall a good class.

Givens is engaging to listen to my lecture was at 9 am and always seemed easy to wake up for. I will agree that the GTFs grade differently depending on who you get. That can be frustrating, but they are always willing to meet if you want to debate your grade.

A fairly easy class, just 5 projects and a little quiz the last class. Givens knows his material but is quite arrogant (he laughs at his own jokes consisyently). The lectures are engaging. The GTF's are the ones that grade your work, some grade significantly more easily than others.
Liked the lectures. He was very passionate. Slightly arrogant though. Really high expectations for assignments.

Though this guy's lectures are fun and he's charasmatic it seems like there's not much to him past the "show" that he puts on when he's on the lecture podium. He didn't hand back ourfinal papers at the end of the term. It was only after complaining to the department head several times that we did receive the papers with vague commentary.
No Comments

One of my most inspiring professors ever. Actually got me off my ass and working hard. He's passionate about architecture. He's a bit of a black sheep in the department of architecture, he's not into the latest sexy thing on the cover of a magazine, instead looking for deeper, LASTING architecture, not cotton candy fluff of Ghery et al...
this guy really turned me off from any sort of architecture in the future. he is super arrogant and tries to sound super smart. the class was boring but easy.
arrogant but engaging
He's very detailed on his lecture! I like the way he presented his knowledge through his lecture. He's funny. His slides are fantastic!
No midterm OR final! Can it get any easier than that?
Prof Givens gives a fantastic lecture, but he certainly does carry a bias towards classical arch... but can we blame him?
"Quintessential!" Those of you who are going to succeed in ArchiTORTURE know what I am talking about.
Hes pompus, an amazing speaker and riviting to watch in action. Sadly,  his architecutre is not, but hey its eugene.
No Comments
Good intro class.  Gives solid basics of architecture although Givens is a bit (a lot) errogant.  Shows quite a lot of his own work.
Great teacher, but strange grading system (GTF's). You wont mind going to class at all!
No final exam, very interesting lectures, difficult but satisfying projects due every other friday; not neccessary to be an artist.

Attendance is required and you get marked down every minute you are not in the zoom call. Tests are based on specific details from the slides and random guest lectures. The course is interesting but difficult to pay attention to due to the teaching style. Every person in the class was upset over the final, so be ready for unexpected grade changes.

This class is inaccessible, lecture slides are not posted on Canvas, and Mark has refused to give them to students who requested them. There is also a lack of communication in this class which makes things very confusing. This is, unfortunately, a required class, so make sure to take lots of notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class wouldn't have been so bad if he made any effort to make it accessible outside of the lectures. If you miss a lecture, there is no way for you to view the slides. This class is mostly a series of guest lectures followed by slides which are breezed through which Mark usually won't slow down or go back to.

Mark is a great professor, very passionate and experienced in architecture and urban design.  His studios are real-world projects that relate to his work at the architecture firm he owns.  However he is busy and relies on guest lecturers or employees from his firm to teach, but in my experience the lecturers had relevant expertise.

Sometimes we had lectures without actual lecturers being there, for instance he didn't show up to class but then made us come and had us wait for twenty minutes while the GTFs figured out how to phone-call him in, and we had a guest speaker over skype which also had technical difficulties, lectures were interesting, talks about his house a lot

Mark expects a lot out of his students. We had a paper due every class period. He has memorized lectures that he gives each term, so if you take him for more than one class then you will see a lot of repeats. He also has a second job and gets a lot of subs because he is out of town all the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Proably the best studio Ive had. Mark is very passionate and knowagable about Urban Design. His studios work with real projects/clients and students work collaboratively on designs, so its more like a real world experience. He also puts a strong focus on research/theory/precedents. In Mark's sudio you'll work A LOT, but learn even more.

A wild ride.  Mark is like a machine.  He never stops moving, thinking or working.  I have to question his sanity.  Mark gets VERY wrapped up in his work and needs to slow down.  His instructions and advice can change from day to day and the scope of our project flew out the window.  But wow, I learned SO much! His lectures are VERY well organized.

Professor Gilkey is an eccentric man. His puffin is quite interesting and sometimes a bit endearing. Aside from that, he is a very intelligent math professor and cares about his students passing the class. One of the best math profs I've taken at the UO. His homework are not much to sweat about, but his exams can be quite difficult

Hilarious professor! You'll have to deal with his Ekaterina Puffini, his stuffed animal puffin, but if you're into that, you're going to have a hilarious year. Most of the class time is based on him teaching you how to do the homework. Quizzes once a week. Understand the homework and quizzes, and you'll be set for the test.

8am lectures consist almost entirely of textbook examples worked on the blackboard. Not capable of explaining things in multiple different ways, repeats himself a lot, grades harshly and blames it on his goddamned stuffed puffin. Gets impatient with non-native english speakers. Is creepy to female students. Generally vindictive. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: weird but SMART dude. I personally am not a fan, but he is a good teacher, but a ridiculously tough grader, with minimal partial credit. The bird is weird and "funny". Also not very accommodating to special requests like athlete travel, doctors notes, etc.

He provides a lot of examples in class of what will be on the quizzes and in the homework. However, often times he'll leave problems unfinished or just not explain in detail how to work the problems out. Be prepared to seek a lot of outside help through tutoring, youtube videos, study groups, and reading the textbook thoroughly.

An eccentric whose passion and ability to teach went the way of his youth. Lectures mostly take the form of him reading equations out loud as he writes them on the blackboard, sans context or explanation. Easy class if you just copy down all his formulae, difficult if you want to actually learn anything.

Professor Gilkey is a really nice guy and never really frowns. The material can be fairly difficult to grasp at times but he tries to make it as clear as possible. If you can get past his bad jokes and can deal with him using stuffed animals during class, then I recommend taking a class from him.
Prof Gilkey is a perfectionist. The harder you worked the more he would give back. Always encouraging. Take his class and use him to learn all the math you can.

Gilkey's lectures were almost like story-telling; unlike some other profs who only regurgitate the textbook, he emphasizes theorems and examples that he thinks are highly important, and you will always learn something at the end of each lecture. Whether it's a course in vector calc or real analysis, his lectures were clear, organized, and exciting.

Its really difficult to get motivated to go to class at 8am to listen to him speak through a stuffed puffin named Ekaterina.  If you like math or you are good at math then take this class, if not then avoid him.  He tells the same jokes multiple times per class period and its always the same set of jokes.
My first math class at U of O, Ekaterina puffini, institution of technology  helps teach this class you will be impressed!

We all know there aren't a lot of excellent math instructors at the UO..so take him when you have the chance..even if his class is at 8:00am. I'm not saying you'll get an easy A, but the chances of you understanding math will be better when you take his class. Wonderful lecturer. His notes are excellent and great to study off of.
He is So good at teaching and it is fun to have his class. You will enjoy it very much!

Analysis is a hard class, and while it's not easy with Gilkey, it's at least easier. He allows a notecard to every exam, but if you have to rely on it you'll probably be in trouble. Also, I had 281 from him, which was a breeze. I think he'd be great for the 25x series, although I didn't have him for those classes.

I really liked his style of teaching, but granted I took AP calc in high school. He was very entertaining in class though, and I quickly relearned all of the calculus that I had forgotten. And the puffin is awesome!
Best math teacher I have ever had. Interesting, funny, genuine, and great at explaining calculus.

Awesome prof! His lectures were very clear and organized, did a lot of examples in class, and made sure his students are learning the material. Test questions were very fair (no surprises). For those of you who don't like the stuffed puffin-- get over it! It's entertaining, and there IS a reason why he brings the puffin to the class!

He is out of his damned mind.  He is probably a closet furry, as he has a full complement of stuffed animals...which he brings to class.  He will spout Lewis Carol poetry spontaneously.  It is suspected by some that he is part of the eugenics movement.

This guy rocks, yeah he does teach vicariously through a stuffed puffin, but he is fun at 8 am.  Really makes sure you understand the material, very clear.  does lots of examples.  Not boring in the least.  Takes classes from him.
No Comments

Sometimes when I forget where I am and think I'll think I'm in kindergarten and then I realize nope it's just Multivariable Calculus with Peter Gilkey and that's why there's stuff penguins everywhere and sweets for me to eat.
bizzare guy,

Gilkey is a bit eccentric.  He is known to bring puppets to class.  But he will be sure that you know the subject.  He worked us, but I felt like I learned more in that class than I had in many math classes before it.  He taught me a lot.

Gloria is a very sweet person, but it is obvious she just does not care about teaching this class anymore. Every single day she arrived late and unprepared while reading off slideshows it was clear she had never seen before. She cancelled class last-minute, rescheduled exams multiple times. Very frustrating. She needs to retire.

Gloria was very disrespectful and told me my exam made no sense and that I had no idea what I was talking about and that I wasn't ready. She lowered my grade from a D+ to a D- and got mad at me because I challenged her and I left in tears because of how rude she was. I know I'm not this bad at spanish because I got a B last term from a diff profe.

I had this class then promptly wanted to switch my BA to a BS because of how stupid I felt despite my hours of studying. I went to office hours for help multiple times for her to basically tell me tough luck you don't get it. HIGHLY recommend Yosa, who is all of the things Zabala is not: encouraging, kind, and a fair grader.

She was a great professor and very willing to help students out, but her health problems had a huge impact on class and there were multiple instances of Gloria telling students she was heavily medicated during class.

She had health issues and left before the end of the term. She was good with explaining concepts, went out of her way to try to maintain a learning environment during a power outage, and understood that most students in her class weren't actually trying to be proficient in Spanish and thus used more English than she was supposed to.

It feels like she doesn't really care about her students and puts minimal effort into teaching. She never wears her mask even if she is sick and even when she's not lecturing. It doesn't feel like she puts any effort into teaching or preparing lessons, she will often just search for pre made presentations while in class.

Native Spanish speaker, cares about students learning the language well. Easy coursework, understanding of external circumstances. Sometimes feels as though she doesn't are a lot about teaching/ giving lectures, but otherwise was very enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class was very engaging and provided many opportunities to learn. I liked that we were able to look at many different types of art and the stories and poems we read were interesting. There is a lot of analysis in the class that isn't put online so I would definitely recommend going to every class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class moves pretty fast. Lots of online homework, it feels like you're supposed to learn the material on the homework then review it in class. I didn't feel like we got taught the material in class it was like we were supposed to have figured it out on our own at home. Lots of projects, which can be annoying but she's a nice grader.

Gloria is a funny woman who really knows the language and wants you to succeed. She may seem harsh, but she just wants you to do your best in her class. Shell be very caring and understanding if you try hard- but be prepared to do a lot of supersite homework and various blogs. Pay attention in class and follow directions and youll be fine.

If you think that you can transition from 200 level Spanish to 300 level Spanish seamlessly, you'd be wrong. She makes it incredibly tough to get help, to find sympathy or understanding when the material gets tough. No recommendations for tutors or any extra course work to practice. Also has no empathy for personal circumstance or situations.
Lots of pop quizzes so don't miss class. Pretty easy test grader. Really knows the language but isn't always very approachable.

Gloria is a good teacher and a REALLy interesting person, but for some reason I got the sense that she didn't put much effort into the class that I took; everything we did was straight out of the book.I'm not sure if that's normal for SPAN 301, but 303 was more creative.I was often frustrated by the tests also. I would give her another shot I think

Really nice woman and I love her teaching style. You have to go to class though because she doesn't use blackboard to post assignment descriptions and there is a quiz every day. Speaks clearly and makes learning easy!

Gloria is a fantastic teacher. She speaks very little English in the class, but she is very helpful with you don't understand something. There are a lot of pop quizzes and the tests are all essay questions, but you go over everything on them in detail in class.

Great teacher all around. Expects a lot from her students. Assigns a lot of readings but makes sure to hand out vocab lists. Gives a lot of pop quizzes so be prepared and do the readings! If you put in the effort, you should have no problem with this class.

She is a very animated professor. She speaks using her hands and very clear facial expressions that make following her lectures pretty easy. Grade consists of exams (including a final: written AND oral separately), irregular homework and projects, and attendance. She is very pleasant and open.
No Comments

I have taken multiple courses of his. They are very well informed lectures of the topics he teachers, lots of information. Participation and attendance is graded, but he loves a good dicussion in class. He will go on fun tangents but also focus on the work.

If you're going to take one of Walley's classes, make sure you're genuinely interested in the topic. He is focused on a very specific part of Japanese literature and doesn't really offer any help to those less familiar with the class subjects. Very little empathy towards students who are struggling, and never responded to any emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Walley was amazing. This was one of those rare classes that I actually really looked forward to going to each week because of the great vibes the class had. We had a lot of fun discussions and I wish this class lasted an entire year instead of just 10 weeks. 11/10

I wouldn't always get 100% on the DP because she would feel that I would not fully answer the question (even though I thought I did). 1 DP per week. Quizzes and readings were fairly easy. Does not offer Extra Credit. No midterm and the final was a group project. Would take if you want an easy A.

Found that although we did read from textbook, there was no prove you read. Really hard grader, often times was not clear on her guidelines, and focused more on grammar that the quality of your work. Class discussion was not engaging, and the readings were contradictory to what she wanted in the essays. Sometimes could not answer questions clearly

Wow...I thought I was doing well in this class til I saw my term grade.  Idk what went wrong, I studied, read the material, and I felt like I was doing A work.  I'm still not sure what more she was looking for on the test...

This was my first survey lit class so of course it was hard, but she is pretty hard herself.  Even my study my partner who is fluent got a 70% on the midterm.  Lots of reading, and it's all written in the 1800s so hard vocab- stuff you can't just lookup in a dictionary.

While the course content is fascinating, this class is very writing, reading, and lecture-heavy, and sadly the lectures aren't particularly enrapturing. Very basic powerpoint style, sometimes he rambles a bit too much and it can be hard to stay awake and pay attention. Tests he allows "cheat" sheets which is good, because the tests are hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class or this professor. I am a senior and this is the worst class I've ever taken. He is the most boring professor and harshest grader that doesn't provide adequate instructions, feedback, or lectures for that matter. He also threw together a ridiculous group project for our final that he cut multiple groups off from presentations

DON'T TAKE IT. By far the WORST prof I have had, I'm a straight A student and question if I will pass even though I have attended every class, gone to office hours and done all readings. Will assign you 80p of reading. Lectures are incoherent. If you ask for help he says he doesn't know what to tell you. Grading is arbitrary, harsh, no feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: probably one of the most boring profs Ive had as an undergrad. For his one class he teaches one term a year, there was very minimal structure/effort to keep students engaged online, and would throw us in breakout rooms for 15 minutes at a time. Incredibly hard grader on small assignments and tested on things we learned a week later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mittermans lectures go on for what feels like forever and tend to be very boring. Overall the class is interesting, and there are daily iclicker pop quizzes based on the assigned reading. There are also three papers assigned. Overall a fairly straight forward class, just not the best teacher.

Personally, I loved his class. He's the reason I chose my major. He's very knowledgeable and willing to work with you. He's new to teaching and has a few things to figure out but considering he wasn't supposed to teach this class this term I thought he did well. Also if you go to class you dont need to do the reading.

I found the content to be very interesting. But I feel like Glenn's lectures could be a bit more engaging as I tended to lose interest. He has iclicker quizzes every day and they're based on the readings, so make sure to read because he assigns quite a few readings. Other than that, I found this class to be very informative and I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Learned a great deal of new information without ever being bored to death. Great professor. Take the class.

Awesome professor. Always there for you with a smile. Loved to put us in discussion groups and always liked to make sure everyone got a say. Likes to put people on the spot but not in a bad way. Tests were essay style. You can learn a lot from him as he worked for the UN for a long time.

He can be a little boring sometimes, but he has so much experience in his field that it would be foolish to ignore or skip his lectures. You can really learn something from him, I know I did. Plus he really welcomes questions and is always willing to help.

The instructor is very enthusiastic about Japanese everything which makes for great lectures. Very good at leading discussions. The more the class participates in the discussion, the more he will reveal, otherwise he moves on to the next slide. I knew nothing about the subject beforehand and finished the class with a wealth of knowledge.

If you are interested in the content then it will be fine. The tests were kinda difficult. You had to write one seven page paper. He clearly knows what he is talking about and wants you too succeed, however you have to work for it. There is a lot of material but overall if you are not interested in the material it will be tough.
I had a great time in this class, although I was already interested in the material. Perhaps not the professor for you if you're not ready to be engaged in the content.

Very enthusiastic about the topic. Good power points and lecture/discussions on the topic. He was a little vague about what he wanted on the first paper. Would not mind taking some of his other classes.
Lectures were long and dry. Didn't find the class or professor interesting.

He is great and extremely helpful! I have taken multiple classes with him, he is very knowledgeable. One class required books, we read and were tested on them all. His PPTs are great and very helpful. Overall a great Prof.
Seemed smart and into the topic, but didn't keep the class interesting. Overall boring and hard class that I regret taking.

I took his Medieval Japan class and had to drop it because of how difficult it was. Even when I did the readings, I was extremely lost in the discussions. I also felt his midterm was too difficult as well.

I went to the first class of Hist 388. I am sorry to say, all Professor May did was ramble. He spoke a lot while somehow saying nothing about the class. He also spoke very quietly and was hard to hear. While he may have been a good professor in the past, I think he is too old to teach now. I dropped after the first class.

Mr. May knows the material very well. He is able to convey it very well, as far as I'm concerned. My issue was not with him but the GTFs. The GTFs gave you little even if you gave a lot and you'd get hammered even for the smallest mistake or leaving something out such as essays.

Relatively nice, but sometimes off-putting old man who teaches Vietnam War history and other Asian history. He's funny at times and loves to show his military background. The paper topics were fine, the only problem were GTFs and his grading. Unforgivable difficulty even when you try. He doesn't like people to go to his office hours. Avoid
No Comments

Class was decent.  He knows his stuff, but does not lecture in a very organized fashion and its sometimes difficult to follow.  Gets sidetracked occassionally.  For the paper, be sure you do EXACTLY as the intructions say, or you will lose points for being creative, like I did.
took him for Vietnam & the US, class was great. one of the best ive had at the UO. definitely recommended.

Best Professor I've ever had, bar none. He knows a ton about and has personal experience with his subject matter, and is relatively easy grade-wise to boot. This makes for lots of learning, not much BS, and a good class overall.
I recommend Dr. May to all of my friends still at the UO... he's the best history prof I've ever had... great lecturer, great sense of humor, and will meet students at their level.
This is by far one of the best classes I have ever taken at UO.  If you are interested in Vietnam, take this class!

One of the best teachers at the U of O.  knows what he is talking about, take his classes people.  Teaches interesting topics so unless your an idiot you should be really interested by the course material.
Very passionate about the material.  Amazing lecturer, very funny.
Best sense of humor, very passionate about the material.
Nasrin is a wonderful professor. She is very much inspiring and has a lot of experience. Always cares about students and help them.
Nasrin knows what she is talking about. Very caring and knowledgeable.
She is amazing! Very much caring and helpful!

Outside of an academic setting, Nasrin  is actually pretty great. However in an academic setting, especially one where designers are starting out, she is unorganized, unhelpful, and sometimes needlessly cruel with her feedback. She often mistakes current skill level with future potential of the designer which is nuts for a beginner studio
Nasrin is the one of the most knowledgable professor in the department. I learned a lot in ARCH283. The class was well organized and super informative.

I had a very enjoyable experience taking Nasrin's class. She is very much supportive and caring about students in class. Very organized and transparent when it coms to different assignments. I wish I could have a chance to take a different class with her.

I would not describe her as sensitive and caring. In fact, it's known in the program that she's harsh and a bit cruel. I don't throw this around lightly. Be prepared to pull multiple all-nighters on last-minute assignments that have been emailed to you over the weekend. 1st year studio should be creative, imaginative, and insightful, but it wasn't.
Nasrin is extremely caring and sensitive to students' learning. She is one of the best professor I have had in my classes in architecture this year.
Professor Golshany provides excellent feedback. I understand that she is young and does not have many years of experience. I feel she can be an excellent teacher in near future.
Amazing.  She is VERY clear and insanely understanding. Its hard to believe that people get grades other than As in her classes.

Professor Golshany is such an amazing professor, She is so nice and caring she will let you make up work and contact you to help you get a better grade on an assignment. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and her assignments are so easy!
Hands down, the best! This professor really goes above and beyond for her students. She is such a gem. Definitely recommend her.
Of all the classes I've taken at UO, Professor Golshany is easily one of the best professors I've had.

You can't pick your professor for ARCH 283, so if you get her, good luck. She is very confusing, so pay attention and ask questions, but once you learn how to decipher what she says, her feedback is good. She will give you more work than other classes and is rude. Learning how to manage your time is a huge part of this class. Pass/no pass only.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Feedback is harsh and confusing, rambles and doesnt give clear feedback or instructions. Harsh grader and expects a lot out of a new class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I will start by saying that she is a new teacher and therefore has only taught one studio class prior to this one, so she is rather inexperienced and some flaws could be attributed to that. Overall, her feedback is often incoherent and rambling, and rude, and she is very unclear with requirements for assignments. A rough experience
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: WHATEVER YOU DO, DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. The difficulty comes from the mental strain of existing within her class, her inability to lecture clearly without long inconsistent rambles, and how the GE has to help with the tech every class. Plus she reworked the class to be able to teach about NEW WAVE CINEMA instead of the HISTORY OF CINEMA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WHATEVER YOU DO, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, SAVE YOURSELF. The mental strain that existing in the class causes is where the difficulty comes from. Her lectures are made up of senseless rambles, she doesn't understand the technology for the class, and she reworked the class to make it about New Wave cinema rather than the HISTORY OF CINEMA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely on the worse side of my professor experiences at UO. The Canvas was poorly set up, quizzes were mostly just "gotcha" questions about random details. The lecture felt completely redundant to the readings, and it had a grade school vibe cause nobody really cared. Attendance was mandatory, and was a trainwreck cause it was taken on paper.

The lectures are a little hard to get through, leading me to skip a couple times. She's not a bad teacher necessarily, I just found myself disinterested and felt as though the focus was never on the interesting things in the history of cinema. Take this class if you need the cinema credit, if not, I'd recommend choosing another class.

Very kind and definitely excited about cinema, but lectures are sub-par and test material is on pointless facts and trick questions. Discussion sections were boring, and little engagement involved. Easy class given you do your work, but not enjoyable for those not interested in cinema. Course fee as well, not worth the 25$/credit for the quality...

Dispassionate pre-recorded lectures that were hard to pay attention to, even on 1.25 speed, quizzes that were based on memory of inconsequential details rather than ideas, trick questions, handing all the work off to teaching assistants. If I hadnt already had a love of cinema this class might have completely discouraged me.

I would not take any class with Professor Gopal. I have had her for two terms -- and this class was horrible. The lecture slides make NO sense. She expects you to review the PowerPoint outside of class and uses lecture to ramble about random things. She is unclear and I learned nothing from her lectures. Again, WOULD NOT RECOMMEND YOU TAKE HER.

Sangita is a great person, but would not be my first choice for a teacher. There is no clear grading criteria and she is very unorganized. The 2 hour class was full of lecture and sometimes could be very confusing to follow as the professor would easily go on tangents.

Dr. Gopal is very clear on her expectations. She does not do Powerpoint presentations (except on the first day), so take notes! Don't be afraid to speak your mind with her, she actively encourages it. The readings could be a little long (I didn't have much time) but she explains everything really well. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: I've never taken a cinema class before this one, so at first it was a bit difficult. But she made sure that all of the concepts we'd be expected to know for finals and midterms and whatnot were well-explained.

Probably the worst professor I've had throughout my last two years at this school. Completely unaware and disorganized, not to mention very disrespectful. I tried to ask her where her GTFs office was because it was not posted. She scoffed at me, said she didn't know, and waved me out of her office. Unprofessional. 0/10 would not recommend.

I am honestly astonished to see so many good reviews for Professor Gopal, and I suspect they are due to the simplicity of her class. Never have I met a more unprofessional, unaware, and overall bad professor. She lacks a basic understanding of the technology she uses in class and will often blatantly give misinformation on topics and terms. Awful.

There's no doubt that Gopal knows what she talks about or that she's very passionate about.  However, I often found her lectures hard to follow. She personally emphasized her own lectures as studying for tests, when her midterm exam for the course was almost entirely on information from the textbooks. Read the book.

Awful. Tests are ridiculous. Teacher has mood swings. Would yell at the class for not knowing a term she never taught us. Very rude to students. Unprofessional. Only "doctor" I know who doesn't know basic grammar or spelling. GTF never there. Would never recommend it. Did culture of Muslim world.
i loved gopal's history of motion pictures. she showed movies that were different -- also i liked the emphasis on historical background. she also connected the different weeks effectively.

I have fond memories of Professor Gopal's lectures.  Though they were often long and drawn-out, it was difficult *not* to enjoy them.  She was very helpful in terms of answering questions during her lectures, but her tests were extraordinarily difficult.
Her kind demeanor throughout the course made the class extremely enjoyable.  We only had 4 papers to write throughout the entire term, read very interesting books and watched wonderful films.

i love gopal. she knows her stuff, speaks beautifully and she dresses so elegantly. she is funny and brilliant. she listens carefully to students and then says what you are saying sound very smart when she repeats it back. yeah. i love gopal but she is not for everybody. she is strict and quite demanding. she will make you work for that A!!!

Gopal was a fun and engaging teacher. She tried to make all students excited and the books we read for class. She wanted our honest opinions about topics in class and about the books we read. Some English professors do a horrible job at trying to lead discussions but I Gopal's class was always interesting. Good reading list for global fiction too!

i took the film survey with her and i totally and absolutely loved it. loved it. she makes you think really hard and i learnt a lot. i agree she has high expectations but i figure when i take a class and i am working hard to do well, i am learning and getting my money's worth.

I thought her film class was pretty annoying and boring. When I say there's textbook use of 5, it means her tests are incredibly hard. She asks questions about what the third film of some obscure director was, and she puts chronology sections with non-film information on her tests. You have to work pretty hard or have a good GTF to pass.

I have a bit of a love/hate relationship with Dr. Gopal...she is a smart lady and really knows her stuff, but her assignments are a little confusing. Some of the books she picked to read were terrible as well..."The Hungry Tide" made me want to give up literature forever.

He's so chill and nice but the readings are long/get repetitive, the quizzes/in-class writings are easy though, and even if you skim some of the readings you can get the point. The class feels like his historical special interests but in a good way
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Sayre is very sweet and well-educated on lots of things. He assigns a lot of readings, and I wish his lectures had more slides to help with note-taking.

While this is a required course, I would not recommend Sayre. Pro: Passionate about what he teaches, gives extra credit, and responds to emails. Cons: Grades harshly on in-person quizzes and does not provide feedback, can't answer questions. He often jumps around the textbook and quickly goes through the material. Passable, but is time-consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty average class not too hard

Really good professor but is often vague when answering your questions. Therefore, classwork is mostly self-oriented. Lectures and class content in general were amazing. I had a hard time in the class due to essays and readings but the class and professor were not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's well-intentioned but not tech-savvy. You can expect mistakes on canvas. I took ENG 209 Craft of the Sentence which was much more technical than expected. Course topics are relevant and he's eager to help. My class was petty about grades and took out on him. He's never intentionally done any harm and he's understanding if you're proactive.
No

I've loved conversing with Professor Sayre and the insights he's had on the texts 
He seems to have good intentions with horrific follow through. Assignment directions are unclear at best and weren't discussed in class until about a week before the due date. Canvas is a nightmare. Syllabus was given in person, never uploaded on canvas.

Prof. Sayre is a good person deep down. But as a professor, he does not do well. The quizzes were very difficult and there was no prep for them. He tested on things he didn't explain. This class is required for the English major and hard to pass. Lectures were chaos and his attempt at Canvas was appalling. Take someone else if you can.

Be prepared for little elaboration on the purpose of the class material and content. Course content hardly seems to go together, and the final exam was shocking and irrelevant to so much of the course. The average grade on the final was a D, but it was not curved. The class as a whole is just confusing, and I'm left not sure what I even learned.

Sayre teaches about early America from a settler-colonial perspective. Indigenous Americans, who he exclusively calls Indians, are given no voice in course materials or themes. The final exam asks about irrelevant information and the study guide is useless. The average for my class was a 24/40 (D) on the final. He does not answer questions/emails

The class is supposed to be American literature, and this far we have watched three movies all dealing with Native American captivity. The class description does not match what we are doing in class and instructions are very unclear for nearly every assignment and quiz. Do not take this class!!!!!!!!!!

Gordo's eccentricities are fun at first, but after a few days the novelty wears off. You're left with a professor who jumps all over the textbook, explains things with the finesse of a bulldozer in a shopping mall, and teaches things only after testing on them. He doesn't give enough time for quizzes and can never adequately answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gordo is completely lost in what he is teaching. He jumps form chapter to chapter indistinctly, he drones on and on and is never helpful in class, and his quizzes are way too short. Nobody in my class of about 20 can clearly and concisely reiterate any of the material we have learned. Save your money. Take a different English class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sayre is a good professor who explains the material in a way that is easily understood. He does require you to read the assigned textbook, and if you want to do well on weekly quizzes, then it is crucial that you do the homework, even though it is not graded. He also gives a few extra credit opportunities and curves the overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Sayre is very good-looking. He is engaging and willing to go the extra mile to help me. He's very in to what he teaches and obviously very knowledgeable. Highly recommend his class (English 300)

I understand when a prof gets a flak for teaching a hard class but Sayre is a TERRIBLE teacher. Unprofessional, boring, his class consists of you talking amongst your group about the 50 pages of reading he had you do that he does not care to explain. His essays are graded out of 15 (WHO DOES THAT?) and will not provide feedback. Worst prof in 3 yrs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Car Culture is one of the best classes I have taken. Since it is new, the teacher is still trying to figure everything out and is very relax on the students. The tests and essays are super easy and he gives you plenty of time for completion. Lectures are pretty interesting since he uses lots of photos and videos. One of my favorite teachers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Sayre teaching style is unprofessional, confusing and boring. His class isn't the hardest but bluntly is a waste of a class tuition. There are easier classesmore interesting classes to be taken. Assigned reading is monotonouslong ultimately learning  the most uninteresting things about cars. Be Warned he will read emails but wont reply
Very intelligent and interesting.
Class is structured closer to a 400 level vs a 100. high amounts of reading. Between 60-120 pages per class.

This class boring, however it is super easy. I managed to get a B grade without reading a single book. I spent 98% of the class doodling and 2% writing down words that Gordo mispronounces. Is it too much to ask to have an English prof who can correctly pronounce "narrator"?

He started out ok, but his structure for class was pretty poor. His seemingly clear expectations turned out to be very vague in terms of his expectations. The class itself isn't too hard, although the material gets to be pretty repetitive. He knows the material, but he doesn't teach English. He rambles off topic and is an extremely difficult grader

This teacher is really slow and boring. The books are relatively easy, but it's a lot of reading for a 100 level class. If you get on his good side you'll do really well. Go to class read the books, and you'll do fine. If you really like to read about alter egos or dual personalities you will really enjoy the class

Very dry, with a quiet voice. Books are all about doubling, so the theme gets extremely boring, and out of all the 7 books, only 2 of them have any appeal. Take the course only if you need the credit, otherwise it's not of much use. Very writing and reading intensive!
Gordo is an okay teacher. He's easy, but the books you read are all on the same topic of doubling, so you already know what will happen to a certain extent. Pretty easy class, but hella boring

Not a very interesting teacher. We break up into groups to discuss or he talks about themes in novels...which all novels have basically the same themes because they all are books surrounding the idea of doubling...I wouldn't suggest taking this class. I like most of the books, but it isn't worth it because the class does not excite or motivate me.

Makes himself availible during office hours, however he isnt much of a help when you go in. His class was kind of boring and most of the novels we read didnt really make sense. Showing up to class seemed pointless and he assigns a lot of reading. He means well, but he is somewhat awkward
A very student oriented professor. Speaking with him after class and during office hours will help a lot.

HORRIBLE! He doesn't teach any of the material on the exams. He wanted us to buy a textbook for >100$ and didn't even use it in the lecture. The labs didn't share anything in common with the lecture; honestly, I wanted to fall asleep in every one of them. The canvas page was messy, and he was unorganized throughout this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took GEOG201 with him. Nice guy, but we almost never heard from him the entire term. Aside from weekly quizzes and exercises, labs were time consuming. Each was 15-16 pages long with repetitive deliverables and I honestly never felt like I really learned anything from them. I'm a junior, and this was the worst class I've taken in college.

Professor never appeared. Entire class was taught by TA (overburdened PhD candidate).  Entire class was basic pdf set up in PowerPoint, very difficult to read.  A labs are essentially readily available ARCgis online tutorials with no support or introduction.  Honestly, it is probably easier to learn this from ARCgis for Dummys and YouTube.

Goslin is exceptionally long winded, in my discussion based class we often do not make it to the discussion because he takes too long getting through the slides. In addition it is currently week 4 of the term and he still hasn't posted the syllabus, and generally seems to struggle with canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For the level of this class there is far too much expected of students. Goslin knows a lot about the subject but doesn't translate that back very well. Lengthy class slides and he doesn't say much of anything other than what's on them but attendance is required. Most questions asked in class were answered with "I dont knows" or straight guesses.

Professor Goslin is a great guy. His class is not super easy by any means, but he is always there to help. There was a shortage of textbooks at the UO bookstore so rather than not caring, he copied a good chunk of the book and uploaded it online for us. It is really easy to see that he is passionate about the course and his students learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Laurie is really fun and cares about her students. She is always willing to help you outside of class. SPAN102 is the same structure as 101, 2 Diarios A+B, 2 exams, and 2 orals. Do your homework and take notes.
Laurie is a great professor overall! She's hella funny and goofy. My only complaint is that her accent sucks, which you think would be better for a Spanish professor.
One of my favorite teachers ever, so funny and amazing in class. Makes sure no students are left behind. 10/10
Laurie made me love Spanish again. She's so nice and amazing and as long as you don't absolutely slack off, she's amazing.

BEST TEACHER EVER. literally could not be more helpful and caring about her students. she's person that wants you to learn and help you understand. Will meet you out of class, u can text her, motivating, empathetic. I asked her to be my advisor for my major later, bc she made me feel like I had a mom-figure at school. Work hard and it will pay off
I adore Laurie. Best Spanish teacher ever!

She is kind and hilarious but a crazy hard grader. I know about five people, in my class of 18, who switched to Pass/No Pass including me. I have yet to pass a single test in her class even though I have always done well (high B or low A) in Spanish.
Expect a lot of homework, but the professor is hilarious, kind and makes the class entertaining and interesting. I would definitely take a class with her again.

People act like this class is so bad, but because you are graded on so few things, the curve saves you. Just pay a bit of attention and study, and you will be totally fine. Glen is a super kind guy; make an effort to get to know him, and you will find that out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These lectures are very boring and didn't learn much from them, the discussion sections are optional. Waddell is a great and funny guy just his teaching methods aren't great if you are really trying to learn from lectures. The curve will save you though and do the practice questions

I know Waddell has a pretty low rating and everybody seems to hate the guy, and thats what I thought at first too. But he genuinely wants the best for his students in his own way. No homework at all, only two midterms and a final. He also replaces your lowest midterm grade with your final grade so try to do well in that.
2 midterms and a test only grades, rambles nonsensically, rude to GEs, spelling/grammar mistakes on tests, lost my first midterm. 0/10 not a fan.
Rambles a lot. Average on the two midterms were a C-C+. Only graded on the two midterms and a final. Discussion section not mandatory.

Grade is just based on midterms + final. Optional lectures and discussions and no other work. Lectures are unengaging. Only plus is that the curve for tests is very forgiving and makes it so no one fails. Easy class because of no work and big curve, but he doesn't explain things well and I didn't feel like I was learning anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty average professor teaches in a large class-setting, so hard for him to give individual feedback, but if the discussion sections with GEs are worth it to you there is that. Good lecturer, just hard to concentrate. If you struggle paying attention, I recommend just reading the slides. Didn't appreciate having three tests determine my grade /:

Professor Waddell is clearly knowledgeable about course material, and was always happy to answer questions.  Lectures could be dull, but so is the content of ECON 201 (in my opinion).  He is a great professor, and extra credit + exam curves are generous.  I definitely recommend attending office hours before exams.
Starting the class I could barely keep my eyes open. but as it progressed my eyelids became lighter and lighter. Dudes kinda funny and the class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, he's funny and has dry humor. Lectures can be a bit long. Class is easy as long as you attend lectures, take notes, and take the time to study. Tests are very similar to the review, which is also super nice. Just put in the work, and you will succeed! He is also super nice if you ever need help, just ask!

Waddells teaching style is not suited for a lecture in Straub, unfortunately insanely monotone, he is a little funny here and there but he overcomplicates simple things which makes me feel like an absolute amoeba. Initially I was intimidated, but when I talked with him I realized that he just wanted me to think for myself and was giving me room to make mistakes before just telling me what I wanted to hear.  His has changed the way I think.

He was a smart guy and he was pretty fair in that what was on the test was lectured on in class, pay attention and you should be okay. Can be kind of boring, but everything he says is mostly relevant to the class and the tests. No homework or textbook, all tests with extra credit assignments.

He definitely knows what hes talking about, very smart guy. He doesn't require a textbook, everything you need to know is learned during lecture. One great thing about him is he doesnt put foreign material on exams, what you learn in class is what will exactly be on the tests. I highly recommend taking him for Econ 201, I wish he taught 202!

He's a great prof and very knowledgeable. Does a great job explaining how everything works and relates. His tests are hard but fair.
