They require you to think beyond solving equations and regurgitating HW to show you really know the material. He doesn't require a book but lists texts for those who learn better by reading. My favorite prof so far.

I know many people who enjoyed him he could have done somethings to make his class better.A book is important to have because not everyone can learn the way he wants all to learn,by going to lecture.I attended everyone of his lectures took pages of notes,payed attention to his facebook page and went to every lab but didnt learn enough to pass

Lectures are fine but it's really hard to study the material. The optional book wasn't helpful. The tests are hard and I feel like they're not reflective of knowledge of the material. The midterm was better than the final. The final felt unnecessarily hard. I studied a lot yet felt I did poorly. Luckily he has a good curve. Least enjoyed econ class

It's a shame that someone gets the reputation of a hard ass when he only demands what other professors should. I wish I could have taken more of his classes, as I feel like I've actually learned something for once.

These comments are so pathetic and aren't at all what I experienced.  I actually did go to class, and probably learned something every single time I was there.  40 percent get As or Bs, which is the department's expectation.

Glen Waddell is the worst professor I've ever had at the University of Oregon. His smug arrogance about his profession ruined ECON for me. His lectures consisted of rants about obscure examples that were irrelevant to the material. He has misleading study guides, and tries to use sophisticated language to make Econ seem more difficult than it is.

Didn't like him at all. Very boring. Had a lot of trouble staying on topic, and used a lot of irrelevant examples. Would have liked it if he had actually used a textbook. Always seemed arrogant. The only way I learned in this class was to write down the terms he mentioned and research them for myself. I love econ, and he almost ruined it for me.
I did not enjoy his lectures at all. They were boring and hard to understand what he was talking about. I do not recommend taking a class from him.

I hated this teacher. There was something about him that I could not stand and I never went to class. The only way I got a B- was because of the huge curve and because everyone failed the final as well. He is not helpful and does not explain the material well. I liked my GTF way better.

He is an arrogant teacher who doe snot transfer the material well to his students. He is more about telling stories and giving examples than actually teaching the basics of ECON, which are needed. Also, he gives you no textbook to reference when you don't understand his lecture. Avoid him if possible.
best prof ever!!! take him!
Does not explain stuff well.  States the obvious over and over again.

I despise economics, but Waddell made the class somewhat interesting. I have no interest in econ so I never did well on the tests but he curved the class so much, I somehow managed to pull through with a B. Lectures are not posted so you should go to class. No textbook, no homework, and discussion is not even required. It's your own effort.

he was a really good professor. he is really clear with his power points that basically sums up the entire lecture. he posts the powerpoints online for you to study from. attendance is not mandatory for anything except for the mid terms and final. could be better about giving a study guide. but if you understand the lecutres, you will do fine

The class was pretty easy, if you remembered just a little bit of calc. The prof thought pretty highly of himself, which I thought was weird since he was obviously nowhere near the top in the econ dept especially in research I heard

goes off on tangents that do not pertain to the class. unclear about what he is teaching. at the beginning of class basically tells his students that he knows 2/3 of them will fail because they are stupid, great guy :)

Waddel is an interesting kind of teacher. He teaches mainly on logic and ideas of micro rather than textbook tterms and memorization. I didn't open a book once but the only reason I got a decent grade is because a friend is 4.0 student that ai could study with.

Without a doubt the best professor I have had at this university. This class is difficult content and requires a lot of time. Effort is required to succeed. He is very efficient with class time..the most I have ever learned in a single economics class. Thought he was great and helpful.
Very inconsistent with lectures, very hard to study for his tests, assignments, etc. Nice but I'd recommend a different instructor if possible.

Glen is fantastic.  He is fair and pushes anyone who is willing to learn as far as he can in 10 weeks.  Those who aren't willing to invest shouldn't take his classes as he has a strange ability to target attention to those who are putting time in themselves.

WORST prof ever.  Does not post notes online, yet blazes through enormous amounts of information in one lecture. He doesn't recommend a text and therefor you have NO REFERENCE to help you out for the tests. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM, CHOOSE ANOTHER PROF!!

Liked him for IO, however found that his system of standardizing the grades and dropping an assignment in labor econ was irritating. Lots of inconsistancies in the grading, which may or may not be his fault. Don't think i'll be taking any more classes from him as the grading system in labor econ was incredibly frusturating.

Waddell is great.  I so wish I had him in principles.  I'm sitting with someone who did and she had such a strong start in econ and she thinks it has helped her in all of her classes. He's funny, too, in a smart way.
knows his stuff.

I took this class last term. He was a bit dull but his lectures were interesting and comprehensible. The exams were a bit tough but my advice is to see him or your GTFs during office hours if you have any questions about the class; both will gladly help you. We hardly used the textbook but they are helpful.

monotone voice and dryness of subject made lecture VERY boring. I found the concepts of the class very confusing and poorly explained in lecture. He should have provided more resources for teaching the material, especially considering that people learn in different ways. a long powerpoint lecture doesn't cut it for everyone. nice guy though.

Glen's awesome.  the class was really hard, but if you actaully try and put in the effort, he'll pick up on that and help you till the cows come home and you'll learn.  really funny if you like dry humor.  and no, he doesn't teach 202, he calls macro "a bunch of hand waiving."
I really enjoyed my class last term.  Since then, I've spent the summer wondering if I should change my major to econ.  If the rest of the econ department is at all like Waddell, I'd really be sold.
knows what he's teaching, but tests are pretty hard

This teacher is extremely boring. Didn't learn anything from his class. Learned more from reading the book, but the book was useless too. There were too little practice questions. Overall, it is a very bad experience. Made me hate econ more than ever.

He is a great teacher. He keeps describing the material until people stop asking questions. I think that this is great. He seems to be very boring, but you learn the material. He is really nice after class when asking him questions. The GTF never attended the lectures, and wasn't clear or even sure about what we were covering. I recommend Glen.

I don't know what the Econ202 guy is commenting on... Waddell doesn't even teach 202.  I know becasue I wanted to take it with him and he told me that he was not scheduled to teach macro.  If he did teach it, I'd be there.  He's the best prof I've had in three years.

I like him, enforces class ettiquete (did i spell that right?) Doesnt put up with ringing cell phones or people laughing away in their laptops. Very good at taking a very boring subject seem a lot less boring. Very helpful. If you HAVE to take EC 201, make sure he's teaching it.

Dr Waddell cares about his students and how they do in the class.  He really emphasizes intuition and I feel that I learned alot even though I only got a B.  He also cares about students outside of class, which is nice.  He really made me appreciate econ and he was the reason I switched my major.
boring lectures, stays on one topic and never moves on, easier to do the work yourself than listen to this guy, it also helps if the GTF is helpful to lessen the blow of not really having a professor
No Comments
My favorite professor at the University of Oregon.  Very acerbic.

Glen is not easy.  He is a very difficult professor but if you are willing to put in the work he is willing to help guide you to the correct answer.  He will help organize the class into groups and these will essentially become your study groups throughout the term.  Don't take his upper-division courses and try and do them solo, it's just easier with some support.  He is a little dry in his lectures and doesn't put anything online, so coffee and attendance are mandatory.
He has high standards but helps you meet them, which I really like.  I felt like I got my moneys worth.
lectures were clear and a little boring but he wasnt the most personable professor
Most boring teacher ever at U of O, still even after 4 years
Glens seems to like the "power" of his position.
don't put up any metirals and hard to follow~~~!!
Probably one of the best teachers I've ever had.  He explains everything perfectly.
No Comments
Glen is probably the most demanding prof I've had, but also the most helpful.  I have learned more in his class than in any other class I've taken.  He's a great guy to talk with too.

Dr.Gupta really cares about the success of her students, her lectures were fun and kept you engaged. If I had any suggestions, I would say to review the study guide well, as most of her exam is based/ directly comes from it.

So nice and educational. The class is a bit of a waste of time, though; it has weird pacing and is just weirdly paired with the two other chem classes required. She's awesome though. Attendance matters or else you lose an entire week's work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Gupta isn't there to be your friend. And she says that on the first day too.
shes actually hilarious and an amazing mentor figure. attend her office hours and you will succeed. 10/10 reccomend. but if you dont attend lectures... you wont pass
The professor is great - this class is not. It is a corequisite with the lab (new for this term) and we learned absolutely nothing. I hope they change it in future terms but it needs a lot of work
She has a somewhat thick access and is very strict about attendance and due dates. I never had any problems with her but did not some people that had some problems with her.

Would not recommend. Though very knowledgeable, she is an insanely harsh grader. THREE midterms EACH 20% of total grade, final is only 15%. No curves, no replacements, nothing. The other 221 class only has two midterms each 25% of the grade. Absurdly harsh grading for a general chemistry class. Wish I could've had Clayton.

dont take her class. its so test heavy even if you do good on homework it wont save your grade if your a bad test taker. no extra credit is offered. not the best teacher kinda hard to follow and understand. seems like a nice lady but Id take a different teacher.

It's not really the professor, it's the class. "Chemistry Tools" but there's not much learning of tools, all we did was make a SciFinder account, and write a lab report for like 3.5 weeks. Attendance is mandatory or you fail pretty much, and Dr. Gupta would crash out weekly when people would leave early, and it's such a waste, but it's required!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So funny and makes the lectures actually bearable. The class is hard, but she's a good teacher and gives a lot of resources to practice and study for exams.
She is very nice and explains things in a clear way

Dr. G is a good professor, somtimes it can be a bit hard to follow her(stronge accent) but overall very good professor, caring /nice, and has alot of office hours. 3 Mid terms for this part of chem, and one final and 30 question muitple choice fyi

Makes lectures painfully boring and not helpful. Received a snappy response when I emailed her a question. This was after I went up to her after class and she left without saying anything, leaving myself and other classmates confused.

Dr. Gupta is truly one of the most caring professors I've ever met. Of course, chemistry is challenging but she puts so much time into making sure students can ask for help when they need it, and does a great job explaining concepts and has very engaging lectures. I have so much love and respect for her. I highly recommend taking chem with her

She is a very nice and caring professor who tries to be funny, but unfortunately that isn't all that matters. She doesn't explain things very well, doesn't cover basic topics, the class doesn't feel very organized, and when she gives out practice quizzes with answers they tend to be wrong a lot of the time. Very unfortunate.
Material can be difficult but Dr. G gives great practice tests and reviews to set you up for success.
Awful teacher, super rude.

I LOVE LOVED LOVE Dr. Gupta and Im incredible sad I wont be able to take her again 
Super easy person to talk to, friendly, and had lectures that made sense. She was straightforward, but also incredibly helpful whenever I asked for help outside of lecture.

Lectures are important if you intend on doing well in the class, but she makes them so much fun. She tells many funny jokes and genuinely cares about how her students are doing in class. The only complaint is that we had modules due on Friday, homework on Saturday (which you can get ahead on if you want), and Sunday.

Dr. Gupta is easily the best professor I've had at UO so far, she's very humble and makes mistakes but it never interrupts the course. She's so funny and the lectures are super lighthearted even though it's a lot of content. Class averages on exams were always above passing, and she does a great job preparing you for them. She's such an icon too!

One of THE BEST chemistry teachers at UO. So funny and lighthearted during lectures, making the hard subjects easier to get through. Used a lot of comparisons to real-world experiences or instances to make the conceptual parts much easier to grasp. She has the homework set for 2-4 times a week but not every day as some other professors do too!!

she was honestly great. I withdrew from chem first semester and im so glad i got her next time around because she goes through the basics of chemestry in such a way that prepares you for the rest of the chemistry sequence. her tests arent that hard either and im a bad test taker

super rude and has cold, short responses when you try to talk to her in person or over email. instructions are unclear & she isn't good at explaining them. she tries to be funny but isn't. attendance is via multiple iclicker questions so if you want attendance points you have to stay the entire class. chem is hard but she makes it sm harder.
Would not recommend her at all. Ever.
Awful professor, do not take her class
Very lecture heavy, but if you do all the hw and study class shouldn't be too hard

Good professor! She is really funny and her lectures are great, I had a really good time in that class. The homework was pretty difficult though and so were the tests, but if you pay attention, you should do good.

Mean for no reason. Horrible communication. Asked simple, clarifying questions, received cold, confusing response. I don't understand why teachers like this do not want to help students succeed, or even just understand assignments better. Im a senior, never left a review before, but nothing good to say about her. Avoid her class. Learned nothing.

Good teacher and kind heart, slightly hard to follow lectures because of lectures, a loooooot of homework, you gotta be able to put in work if you want to do well. Office hours and/or self teaching is necessary. pretty tough class, but do-able.
Would never take her class again. I've taken a few and every time she's a difficult grader and has a superiority complex

I find her class to be fine, lectures are fine, she has bad communication about assignments and is a very difficult person to email as she has short and rude responses. I would not take her class again nor would I like to communicate with her again.

Dr. Gupta clearly cares about her students success, she has many office hours available and encourages students to use their resources. Grading criteria, class schedule, and assignment instructions were clear. Be prepared to commit significant time learning content outside of class as some  topics are tricky and lectures often were not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I have ever had! Dr. G. is very caring and it's very clear she wants you to succeed. Her lectures are entertaining and she is great at explaining things.

No surprises on exams as what is taught during lecture is exactly what is found on tests. Clicker questions are helpful to stay engaged during lecture acting as "knowledge checks." Very approachable and office hours are helpful. Dr. G. clearly loves teaching and is very knowledgeable of the subject and that is clearly felt as the student.
Easy to follow

Took this as my first chem class. Prof Gupta is a GREAT professor, she's funny, her lectures are clear and mostly easy to understand, but because it's a 50-minute lecture you have to be ready to absorb as much of the info as possible and take good notes. The hw and quizzes are manageable but you have to put in time to study for the exams

This course is a great prep course for Gen Chem. Gupta is a wonderful and organized professor, and she cares about all of her students. Mandatory attendance for a reason, the lectures and discussions are super important! Make sure to turn in your work on time and go to OHs. Study well for midterms and cumulative final!

I didn't love the class but it wasn't horrible. As long as you attended lectures, it should be fairly easy. Achieve hw and quiz every week, midterms are fairly difficult. You do have to really try to do well, but if you put in effort you should get it. iClickers are used for attendance and have an impact on your grade, so attend all lectures.

ACTUALLY TOOK: CH227
Write stuff down, go to lecture (she speaks decently clearly, but has an accent- actively listen and you'll be good), and pray that you get a good TA for lab.

ABSOLUTELY LOVED HER COURSE!! Explains coursework clearly and doesn't hesitate to slow down to make sure students understand the topic before moving on. Attendance is mandatory and weighs heavily on grade but other than that it's not so bad. Topics are easy to understand and made me fall in love with chemistry again :)

Gupta is an amazing instructor. Her class is really hard because of the content but the lecture relates to the homework which relates to the quizzes which relates to the test. You really do need to study a lot but she provides resources and holds office hours. She is hard to understand in lecture but doable if you are focused.

Gupta is caring and answers questions until you understand. Weekly homeworks, quiz, readings, and worksheet. 2 midterms and a final exam. That said, work all feels relevant to the exams and you are given the info to succeed if you attend. Only issue is how lecture would get behind on content, and make discussion worksheets difficult.

Dr.Gupta is very caring and wants her students to succeed. She was kind to give us practice exams before our midterms which was very helpful. Everything she teaches is straightforward and helps with our exams.

did this for summer for online and teacher was helpful. homework/achieve homework daily(ish). had to do like 6 homeworks over the span of 1 week but they were relatively easy. lecture videos were from the book but didnt read the book. good class if its the only one ur taking for summer

would recommend class

You can tell Dr. Gupta really cares about her students and wants them to do well. She teaches exactly to what is on the test and is very straightforward. If you work hard and pay attention you will do well.

Dr. Gupta is a very smart woman and knows what she is talking about. But her way of teaching just did not work for me. The best way to prepare for lecture is by skimming the section of the textbook to at least know what to expect. She does several clicker questions every day of lecture. But as hard as it was to learn, she is very funny and caring.

Dr. G is a very knowledgeable and respected professor. She is caring for her students and her lectures are bearable as she makes a lot of jokes. However, she teaches very fast and does not explain concepts that well. In addition, exam reviews were much different from the actual exams. Her policies are fine but expect to work!

amazing professor! had her for 221+223 and she made every lecture interesting. provides a lot of support and clear assignments. 2 aleks modules a week (3-10 topics per module) and 1 hw on aleks. 2 midterms and a final. provides great study material.

Tanya keeps lectures fun and engaging as well as useful and applicable to the course material, she also does example problems that help with the coursework too. You can put minimal effort in and still get above a C because she gives you all the information you need to complete the course.

I had Dr. G for CH 221 and now 222. They are certainly difficult courses, but Dr. G is a fantastic professor that really cares about her students and gives a lot of support, especially with review leading up to exams. I wish she was teaching CH 223 next term so I could finish out chemistry with her.

She keeps you on your toes and can go a little fast during lecture but is thorough. People like to complain about her accent but when you think of all the people who don't speak English and have to listen to Americans talk, I think the scale evens out; all you have to do is listen closely and simply ask if you don't understand :)

She is a great professor with a passion for chemistry. She is very willing to answer questions and help you understand the material. She gave us "cheat" sheets with information we could use on the exams. There is homework due each week, along with a quiz that is easier than the HW. It was a great class and was really helpful and not too hard.

Overall, Tanya was a great teacher and made class interesting. Her grading system is very reasonable and all her exams are multiple choice. However, she goes really fast and can be hard to understand. Her handwriting can be hard to interpret as well. I definitely recommend going to her office hours!

I was worried after reading the reviews, but Dr. Gupta was incredible! Some reviews said she's "hard to understand", but I didn't get that (she has an accent, but that's about all). Her attendance policy is a million times better than other professors I had. She does go pretty quickly but is happy to go back and explain things again if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love her!!! Gupta is a professor who always makes sure that people can follow and gives plenty of time for questions to be asked. She is really easy to get in contact with. She's funny and lighthearted, but seriously knows her stuff. I recommend sitting in the front, so you can interact with her and let her know you more as a student too.

Very knowledgeable about chemistry and does a great job of effectively communicating the steps to complete problems and gives lots of examples. The two hour lectures without breaks were sometimes really exhausting, and the content was boring at times, but the tests were very representative of what was taught in class. Responds quickly to emails.

Dr.Gupta does not receive the credit she really deserves. She truly cares about her students, very understanding, and really wants them to succeed. The lectures are long and easy to get distracted, but other than that they are very informative. She is very helpful and willing to help until material makes sense. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Gupta is completely reworking the Gen Chem sequence at UO. As such, she takes feedback very seriously, wants her students to succeed and loves teaching us. She is not an easy professor bc it is not an easy subject. She is accessible out of class, accommodates as able. She is very busy, but takes time to send out basic need resources to students

A good teacher who cares about her students. Appreciates that students have an outside life and doesn't want students to be swamped with homework so she typically makes in-class worksheets due the Monday after the weekend. Lectures can feel long and boring, but really any 2-hour chemistry lecture will feel like that. Would take again.

Literally couldn't really understand her lessons at all. Made everything so confusing and although she his nice and you can tell she is passionate about chem, really not a great prof. Her tests are all questions that are found on chug so thats nice

She means really well and is nice and funny but her accent sometimes makes the topics a little more difficult to understand. She is not the most accommodating and the class is hard but doable. 3 midterms all online and a final in person. You do have to buy 2 programs to be able to do the homework.

She is a very knowledgeable teacher, but this knowledge leads to the over-complication of many general concepts; this, combined with the strong accent, can make the class difficult. To better understand her teaching read the book before class. Test questions are not as related as one would like to the homework and clicker questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice person and cares for students but not flexible. The class is only lectures which are long and get repetitive, definitely participation based so you have to be in class everyday to get a decent grade.

She posted the lecture slides before class, taking notes before class allows you to pay a lot more attention to what she says in class. Has a tendency to ramble about unnecessary information, just taking the notes teaches you a lot more than she can.

Professor Gupta is a nice person, but her teaching style leaves something to be desired. Her lectures move very quickly, and her explanations are often rambling and confusing. The guidelines of the class, and what is expected of students is very clear, making it easy to stay on top of things. Expect 3 midterms and 1 final exam.

Dr. Gupta is obviously very intelligent, but can be hard to understand and jumps around a lot during lectures. The tests are difficult but reading the text book will help get you through the course. I would not recommend taking this unless your major requires it.

Bro was honestly doing his best, but his best wasn't great. If I didn't have a chill GE I probably wouldn't have gotten an A because his lectures are just him yapping and he had to cut half of the content because he got caught up on certain topics.

I took ARH 314 in 2024 with an excellent professor and learned a lot. In 315 (2026) with Prof. Guxholli, lectures were monotone, unstructured, and hard to follow. Labs with Michelle clarified concepts. Only 3 graded assignments (midterm, writing project, final) made engagement crucial. Overall, lectures needed more clarity and structure.

His lectures were interesting, but were not super organized or easy to follow. He did not communicate well what was going to be on the tests. For our final, we had to write 2 in-class essays, and we were supposed to respond to quotes from the readings, which was not made clear, and we also never talked about those readings in class.

He is clearly passionate about architecture, but his lectures are VERY hard to follow. He makes very little effort to communicate with his students or GEs. He gave us zero guidance on how to prepare for either exam, and very little info on the term project which he announced a huge change to 2 days before the due date. Disappointing class.
Exams were oral and fun, but lectures were boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assigned seating in a huge lecture hall and the content was boring.There were 2 oral exams and you get randomly assigned a prompt. Don't recommend taking this course if you can avoid it.

Probably one of the most OD teachers. Who makes a seating arrangement for a 500 person lecture hall? Graded by weekly assignments, participation, and 2 exams (mid and final). Exams are oral, meaning the GE you get decide your fate. I got unlucky and got a harsh grader for the orals. If you're not a philosophy major this class is a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are mandatory, which is especially difficult given that they are not engaging whatsoever. There is a seating chart in a lecture hall which holds 400-500 people which says a lot in it of itself. Difficult to understand at times and generally not easy to listen to. There are weekly readings and assignments that are quite time consuming.

There was lots of difficult readings, this class had about 1 assignment per week where you analyze something and relate it to the readings. Then there were 2 oral exams where you're GE pics a prompt out of 3 questions and you have to talk for 10 minutes answering the questions and quoting the readings. Not a bad class, but the orals were stressful.
Probably one of the most boring and tedious classes I had to take for a credit. Mandatory lecture hall seat assignments, oral exams, lots of reading. Avoid if you can, take another arts and letters.
He's an incredible teacher and lecturer who cares deeply about his students and the topics discussed. So knowledgeable, take a class with him if you can!

There was some reading each week, but he made sure to go over it all during lecture. The 2 oral exams made up like 50% of your grade, but everything else was easy to get 100%. Attendance was mandatory, he made a seating chart for a 500 person lecture hall, and your grade dropped if you were absent. GE's were so helpful, definitely go to discussion!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very vague instructions, requires a lot of outside hours to be successful. Just not a great teacher with difficult course material. Would recommend taking with another prof if at all possible.

One of the worst professors here at the UO. Does not actually teach the material but just expects you to know what to do. Quiz questions throw you off completely. Terrible quiz prep and little to no guidance at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best way to sum up this class is that for our first project we had to build an intricate excel model to graph asset portfolios but because canvas was down the day he posted it, he never uploaded the instructions on how to make it. Here's to you, Ro and the many nights lost because of your lackluster teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You're essentially all by yourself in this class when it comes to learning. Ro doesn't teach you the material he is presenting but it doesnt matter anyways because the big quizzes are nothing like the slides he uploads to Canvas. His instructions for Excel homework is very vague and no excel skills are taught throughout the course. Avoid this class

Ro was probably one of the worst profs I've ever had. So vague, essentially throws random material at you and hopes it sticks. All the homework assignments required outside research to complete. Instruction was super dry, lacked explanation, and clear demonstration, probably should have chosen a different profession honestly. Wouldn't recommend.

He cares deeply about participation. He always tells students to talk among themselves about a problem before he will talk about it. He's prone to a few pop quizzes. The homeworks were normal difficulty but did require knowledge of some programming. Exams were normal difficulty, study guides and past exams are extremely helpful. Fine professor.

Ro is straight up a bad teacher. He has a severe Napoleon complex. He has no real world experience but thinks he does. He grades subjectively, he has no respect for his students and is incapable of answering a question directly. His understanding of finance is purely academic. If you ask a question he won't answer it. AVOID THIS CLASS.

If you have the chance to take a different teacher, do so. Ro is one of those teachers that comes to class and asks his students to "discuss the question with the people next to you". Ultimately he wastes his class time asking students to talk with one another, yet everyone is waiting for him to give us the answer. Hard HW, hard tests. Stay away!
Absolutely horrible professor. Purposefully tries to trick students on tests and should not be a teacher because he clearly does not enjoy it.
Fantastic professor. He really knows his subject and has an obvious love for finance. The class I took was not easy, but I learned a lot.
Ro knew the topic really well and was very organized in presenting the material. He was very knowledgeable on the topic, and on a personal level, he was fun to talk to in and out of class.
This class is tough for sure, but Ro is a great teacher and will answer any questions you may have.

Great teacher. He's tough, but fair. Will answer any questions you have and will keep working with you until you understand the material. He can be vague at times, but keep asking him questions and he'll clear things up.
tough, tough, tough
Great class. Lectures are example heavy which help a lot.

She was a good lecturer. Attendance is essential since all of her tests are based on in class examples. There was a pretty big disconnect between in class and the outside of class required readings/homework.

The Good:
In-class examples are great, super helpful for the exams
Test retakes help you learn from mistakes
Funny teacher

The Rough:
The math is taught, but the chemistry is not. I understand the math behind the test questions, but I cannot physically relate them to the real world
No practice exams make it really hard to study for the tests

Says funny things without realizing. Her lecture slides are kind of messy, but they work. Offers retakes for exams for anyone, regardless of the grade received. Exams can feel like a race against the clock, and she grades them on a scale of 10 points. Recaps the previous lecture's content to drive the concepts home.

Dr. Guenza has a great sense of humor which I appreciated. She also had input from students in lectures, like pausing to ask questions to make sure we were understanding, and having people come up to the board to do problems. In my experience, she's approachable and willing to talk things out. Have fun with the class and don't miss her jokes.

I've taken a few courses from Dr. Guenza and have always found her to be a joy. She is a passionate Italian woman with a lot of experience. If all you want to do is pass the class, just show up and take notes. Exam content is always practiced. As with any prof. approach them with a growth mindset and you will have a fantastic time!

Enrolling, I was worried because my math background is not strong. However, I found her demonstrative lecturing style to be clear and easy to follow. The problems on HW and exams were fair and the class content was interesting. Professor Guenza is very sweet in office hours and always encourages her students to participate for extra credit!

for class 447/547 

lecture slides are poorly organized (cluttered, not relevant, repeated), often gives important info not based on slides and doesnt always write these on the board so you can easily miss important HW/exam content. files in canvas also poorly organized. if she had better organized slides class would be okish. class relatively easy

I attempted to communicate and was shot down. She didn't support me in any shape or form. I limited communication as she had no issue talking down to me. I didn't she care for her students. Her lack of support harmed my mental health, and I was suicidal. I didn't tell Dr. Guenza, because I expected her to shame me. She sucks and will fail you.

Exams are very difficult to prepare for, and the homework takes a lot of time and energy with very little direction beforehand. Ro goes over the homework AFTER it's due, which makes it really difficult to understand his expectations for the assignments. Attendance is “optional” but definitely not optional if you want a decent grade.

Not sure why the other ratings are 1*. They are not wrong about the difficulty of the class, but are nowhere near correct on the professor's ability to teach. First class I've taken that was somewhat based in theory but felt applicable to the real world. Would 100% take another class from this professor.

Ro puts on a masterclass on how to make finance as confusing as possible. His slide decks are impossible to follow. He isn't clear about what types of questions will be on his 4(!) midterms. I found it harder to study for his midterms than any other professor I've ever had. I wouldn't recommend Ro to anyone.

Ro does not care about teaching any of his classes. He is rude and refuses to give any assistance likely because he has no clue what he is doing. The issue is not the material he teaches as there are other amazing professors who teach the same classes (FIN 606, FIN 380, and FIN 683) who do a much better job. Terrible at explaining material also.

Avoid this professor at all costs. His assignments are all homemade and unrelated to what he teaches in class. Tests are ridiculously hard. Terrible at explaining concepts. Our grade calculation was locked for the entire term, and almost no assignments were graded until Week 10. Completely failed at the basic responsibilities of being a professor.
Ro is a great teacher who seems genuinely interested in the content he is teaching. He wants students to learn and do well, however, the content is difficult.

This professor and unfair and unreasonable in his expectations during class and for assignments. He doesn't allow you to see your grade and doesn't grade assignments during the term, so you don't know if you're passing the class. I don't recommend taking a class with this professor unless you already understand finance and/or can teach yourself.

One of the best professors I've had in the business school at Oregon. He's a smart guy, so his class is tough, but if you put the work in the class is super enjoyable. Ro is straight up but clearly cares about the students taking his class, especially if you make the effort to get to know him and participate.

He teaches like everybody knows the topic up and down. His teaching style is all over the place, and he goes so fast. Rarely provides examples and goes through any that he does offer way too fast and jumps around. Answers questions very poorly and leaves you to figure everything out on your own.

He is a nice guy but assumes the class understands way more than they do. Often times is confused why no one participates, its cause no one knows whats going on. Assignments can take 3-4 hours if you understand them his words (it's true but longer). Don't get your hopes up, these are assigned almost every weekend. Attended every class, still lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super confusing teaching style. You have to figure out the chapter on your own, then he grades the homework, then he goes over the answers and how to do it . Doesn't explain the material at all and the chapter readings are extremely hard to understand too. If you're good at learning everything on your own with no guidance then you'll be fine.

The class was poorly organized. The syllabus did not list the material covered for each class. The class is confusing. Ability of answering questions was undesirable. Would not recommend this class. Waste of my tuition.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures often were not focused on the readings for the day. Most people had background knowledge on mythology, causing professor to expect people to already know everything. Readings were confusing. Final project consisted of picking a myth to research. Class did not teach me a lot about research, just a lot about mythology. Triggering content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gantt is a great person. 10/10 guy. But who has time to read 7 chapter books. I'm talking about hundreds of pages a week on top of essays every other week. Do not take his class if you can't read fast and do not take his class if you can't pretend to be passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with this professor if writing is not your strength. The workload for this class was so overwhelming and it was all crammed at the end of the term. He also contradicts himself regarding the feedback he gives you in person and the feedback he gives you when grading your paper which is extremely frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is super nice and really willing to help you, and you will become a better writer. However, the course is super super reading and writing heavy. I think we read 6 novels over the entire term, which meant you are reading almost every day for this class. Do not take a class with him if you do not enjoy analyzing literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a very supportive professor, but provides little clarity on the assignments. You will read 7 different books and have little time to discuss them in class. He expects you to come to class having read the books, but will talk about an entirely different topic the whole time. There is no set schedule for work, and does not follow the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class feels like you are on drugs in the best way possible. There is definitely a lot of reading, but the class conversations will be the most interesting you have had in a classroom setting. Gantt can be confusing but if you take the time to meet with him he will help as much as he can and is a great guy overall.

The biggest ego of any professor I've ever had. His sole mission seems to be to make students feel stupid. I have considered myself (and been called by educators) a good writer my whole life and Gurley completely destroyed my confidence. His way or the highway, and your grade depends on how well you can conform to his preferences. AVOID AVOID AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor is probably one of my favorite. he is very funny in class and respects his students. however he is incredibly disorganized so you are better off asking him question rather than reading his syllabus, but again he is easy to talk to so it is not to big a burden. despite that I would recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Weird guy but fun. Gantt assigns a lot of readings that you don't always go over, but no matter what there's great discussion. It was difficult to figure out what he wanted from my writing(grade-wise). My advice is to skim the readings and go to office hours.

HC 421. There was lots of reading, but too often we didn't talk about it in class. Discussions often veered way off topic, feeling like a waste of time. One class about Dracula was spent discussing college administrators and US politics. When we did literary analysis, it was always very interesting. 70% of the grade was 1 paper, 30% participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gantt is so funny and awesome, he goes on random tangents about the craziest things in lectures. His essay guidelines are disorganized/very specific to his tastes but hearing what this man has to say is well worth it. Discussions are great and interesting too. Make sure to do citations in ur essays for him and never use semicolons. :)

THE hardest HC101 from what I've heard. A LOT of reading and writing and thinking but about some really cool stuff! I highly recommend treating his office hours as second lectures; sometimes he goes on tangents in class and we got behind. Class was so fun tho! One time I cried in his office hours and he got me a cookie and asked if I was ok.

This class was frustrating a lot of the time but very rewarding. Gurley is an engaging teacher who seems like he is ranting about useless stuff but I promise it all matters in the end. he is incredibly disorganized, often surprising us with readings and changing dates from what the syllabus said. But he will work with you if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man is so specific in what he wants from your writing. I like him as a person, not a teacher. You will either love him or hate him. Class discussions, will read your writing in office hours and offer advice. Will mark writing down and complain over ridiculous points.

Really disliked the class itself (felt like a useless waste of money) but that's on me for not doing more research on what the class was about. Gantt himself was such a great guy and an absolute joy to be around. I really struggled during my first term of college and he showed me so much kindness and warmth when I needed it most.

Weirdest, funniest professor I've ever had. Makes class so engaging. Oh my gosh so much reading though. Definitely will make you a better writer and reader if you put in the work. You should go to office hours in his class, it's really important to get his feedback before he grades imo
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Gantt's HC 301...was not what I expected as this is described as a "research writing" class. We did one annotated bibliography that determined our whole grade. Gantt is a very intelligent guy and you can tell he cares about having thoughtful discussions with the class, but sometimes his chosen discussion topics were a little offputting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class lectures always strayed SO far off-topic, and not in a fun silly way. In a "I'm wasting my time here" way. They turned into a discussion with the loudest people in the class and made no effort to make space for other people to talk. Our class average on essays was always shockingly low for an HC 101 class, super harsh with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gantt is awesome! Grade is determined by a Midterm and Final Paper and Final test. There is a lot of reading but its interesting. Make sure you go to his office hours and he will explain everything and help you on your papers before theyre turned in. Really off the cuff guy but is very approachable and funny!

Gantt is engaging, thoughtful, and has a big personality in class. I enjoyed every lecture, even when I was not knowledgeable about the material. One thing that bothered me was the lack of organization - he often deviated from the syllabus and that doesn't work for a lot of people. I often had to come to class without knowing what we had to read.

Gantt is a well-read, articulate, and engaging instructor. He assigns a great deal of reading to preface his lectures, but it's well worth it. You will learn more than you ever would on your own, because he is so dedicated to bringing the material to his students in a captivating and thought-provoking way.

Gantt was a good guy, but this class is not for the faint of heart- make sure you actually do the readings. You have to read five family sagas in their entirety, plus other readings. There is only one paper, but the midterm and final are challenging.

Do not take this class unless you have already read the viking sagas prior to enrollment, unless you're down to read an entire saga every week . Most students in the class are already experts on the sagas so it's hard to stay caught up and participate in discussions. Apart from that Gantt is a very funny teacher who keeps lecture entertaining.

Gantt is a personable, funny guy with seemingly infinite knowledge on just about any topic. This can lead to wildly interesting tangents, but tangents nonetheless. Class material can get pushed to the side sometimes. It's inspiring to see his passion for what he's teaching and how he invites all student ideas and arguments. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would not recommend if you have no background knowledge in Judaism. He doesn't use slides, and won't provide a prompt for our giant research paper. He is the type of teacher who says "Study everything" when you ask for a study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is passionate, and tries to get to know his students, but he is very disorganized, didn't give us instructions for our paper or a prompt, didn't see grades at all this term, and strays off topic very easily. For example one day we were suppose to be talking about pirates and then trailed off to why tuition is so high.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most disorganized teacher I've ever seen in my life (never learned our names), and I've never seen a professor less clear about project guidelines. Project turned in in week 5 wasn't handed back til week 9. Two final projects? No guidelines as to what he's looking for. Still, he knows the texts and his subject like the back of his hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Gantt is easily the best professor I've had at UO. He shows a clear passion for the subjects he teaches and very clearly wants to pass that passion on. His lectures are long and very dense if you do not do the reading. Take notes and engage with him, it will make your class experiences ten times better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gantt is the worst teacher I've ever had. His lectures are long-winded, very boring, and he finds a way to make stories about vikings boring. There is barley any work to do; this class was a  waste of time. He is also very unorganized. He thinks he is very funny and constantly makes terrible jokes that made me despise him and his class. AVOID!!!

By far my most enthusiastic professor. Gantt's class is actually fun, we all spend most of the class laughing. He is a little bit scattered but that is what makes it fun. I would highly recommend taking a class from him.

An absolutely amazing professor of Scandinavian. If you are having a hard time finding what you're interested in, please take any Gantt class. You will have fun and he is the most entertaining and there-for-you professor on campus. He makes it pretty hard to not fall in love with medieval Iceland.  Take his Old Norse so it can be offered more.

I thought this professor was extremely nice and entertaining. He was very passionate about the stories. He would speak fast and sometimes go on tangents. Be aware in his class and you will be fine. It was an amazing class. He peaked my interest and now I am attending SCA events. Super comical character, but make sure to pay attention.

You absolutely must keep up with the assigned reading or else you will feel lost in lecture.  I figured this out about halfway through the course.  He also doesn't post his Powerpoint slides on Blackboard.  The reading load is pretty heavy, but if you do it, the midterm and final will be very easy.

Gantt is super chill and I'm pretty sure he's a stoner, but I found it really difficult to focus during his lectures. He doesn't really use slide notes and I couldn't take notes on his spontaneous analysis of the text. This is definitely a challenging class, you have to be super into viking sagas because the focus is on trends and techniques.

Great professor! He was funny and informative at the same time! "Lectures" were always very interesting... and took on more of a discussion format. LOTS of reading and the paper WAS difficult because you make up your prompt. But definitely worth the work, and there were no other assignments. Overall, a really laid back, fun class!

Gantt taught a great class. He's very laid back and really nice. He doesn't really structure his classes very well- it was really based more on discussion, so reading was very important. Overall, he was one of my favorite professors. He's hilarious and keeps lectures interesting while relating to his students really and wanting them to succeed.
Great prof for small classes. Go to his office hours!!! Usually a very relaxed class. Lots of reading. Really hit or miss with him. Friendly and a great person to know.

All the feedback we received on every assignment was copy+paste from AI. Comments including tons of em-dashes and "[insert student name]." He also grades very harshly for no reason. Loves talking about "the real world." Asked him in office hours about a specific assignment but just told me I'll be fine because my grade is good rn. Very bad prof imo

He can come off as intimidating in the first few days while clarifying class policies. However, as the class continues, his anecdotes and humor really show through. You can tell he cares about his students and our success. The lectures can drone on, but the group discussions/activities are the best part. Participation graded heavily (incl. no tech)

An amazing professor. He cares about his students success and wants them to succeed in life. He seem scary in the beginning but it helps set clear expectations. Idk what the other review is talking about, he encourages students to use AI ethically if they do use it, except for one assignment so students can fully learn the skill, also no $25 fee.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Uses ai to grade assignments and but limits student from using. Students are required to buy a $25 case from his friends company that only gets mentioned once in class.

Dr Hennessy places heavy emphasis on preparing his students for life after college - focusing on professionalism and reputation. He may seem mean, but it comes from a good place. No other upper division course has left as big of an impression on me than Dr Hennessy's. The actual work is fairly reasonable for a 400 level. Overall would recommend.

Greg tries to scare people away but he is a gem at heart. He really cares about your success post-graduation and stresses the fact that grades will not matter when you're in the professional world. The class content was relevant, and although participation can be stressful, he cares about your responses and gives great feedback. Highly recommend.

The best professor I've had at UO so far is very understanding and can be strict at the beginning of the year but is extremely understanding. Gives great feedback and wants you to succeed if you're willing to put in the work.

If you fall for the scare tactics, I don't know how you function as a person. He's not scary, he wants you to succeed and think critically. He doesn't care about memorization, there are zero tests. Just show up and be a team player. You honestly learn through play and engagement. It's a fantastic foundational class.

He will try to scare you on the first day but as long as you do the readings you'll be fine. He assigns a lot of readings but there are no midterms or finals it's just group work. You can tell he really cares about his students, and tries to prepare us for the business world through a lot of in class discussions.

Greg does really want his students to succeed, even if he does act tough in the first couple classes. Put in the work, participate, and be a good, professional team member, and you will have a good time in this class. Also willing to communicate, and will give out more credit if you're clearly doing more than the rest of your group.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Didn't like him at first, but ended up learning a lot. He grades things very harshly, but if you read instructions carefully you'll do well. Not too hard to get a good final grade even if you bomb a few assignments. He has a bit of an attitude but nothing too bad or hard to manage. He seems abrasive but is understanding if you communicate.

Take this class with a different professor if possible. The guidelines for assignments and tests are confusing and unclear, leading to low grades despite effort. The professor also requires students to buy $25 worth of unnecessary papers from his friend's company. Overall, the course is disorganized and frustrating especially if you want a good GPA

Overall, good teacher. Make sure to come to class prepared as we always talked about out of class readings. The entire class is group based (BA 308) so make sure to be ready to participate with others. There was a lot of work and meeting outside of class with group but very do-able.

Originally, I was scared to take this class because of ratings on this website, but now I am so glad I did. I honestly love Greg. He is understanding that students have lives and other classes outside of his class. As long as you come to class prepared and ready to participate you are all good. Really enjoyed his class
Professor Hennessy is a must take professor. He's an extremely kind, understanding, and easygoing professor. His class is challenging but not too hard. Homework is fine

Mr. Hennesys class is great he is super kind and caring. The course is project based individual/team with one written midterm that wasn't hard. If you go to class and take notes you should have no problem passing the class. You have to do some class presentations but is very understanding for those who have are tough time talking to a full class.

I liked how Professor Hennessy taught this course. Similar to Harvard Business School, there were short-medium length case studies to read before each class, and a lecture/discussion during class. Group projects were informative and great practice. Hennessy is caring and knowledgeable - if you put in honest effort and participate you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Greg has amazing industry knowledge. You are able to learn a ton from him if you show up and engage yourself.

Professor Hennessy has valuable experience that he uses to teach material. He expects participation and engagement from his students to create an interactive classroom environment. I appreciated his honesty about the business world and what is expected of you. 

I think the negative reviews are from people who expect to skate by in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Tied for worst professor I've ever had. Loves listening to himself talk and makes a business strategy class so conceptual it's painful and you leave lectures feeling like you learned absolutely nothing.

Very interesting class! We were given the choice to choose between 3 essay prompts to complete and we only had to do one. Quizzes almost everyday in class based on the readings and lectures. So as long as you paid attention during class and took notes, you're good. Wish she gave us more discussion time as promised for the project though.

Prof Gretchens lectures were super fun and I found them interesting. The class was super easy you just have to show up and do the quizzes and you're all good. I did find some of the stuff she said in class a lil bit controversial, but honestly I enjoyed the class so much because of my GE (shoutout Suenia the goat)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Participation is tracked through an easy quiz at the end of class. No final exam, only a group project you work on throughout the term. She is very funny and her lectures are interesting. Light work, you only need to complete one of three essay options. She is super sweet.

Within the first ten minutes of the first class of the term, she said race is a social construct. She is also a high school drop out and makes it known. Do not really know if I want to be taught be a high school dropout. Also she sometimes makes weird comments such as mentioning she has a spit kink? She also said some gay slurs and she is not gay.

Gretchen is one of the kindest professors I've ever had. She really cares about her students, and she's a very inspiring person. The readings & lectures are interesting, and the class is not a lot of work. Main assignments are short Canvas quizzes at the end of class based on the lecture. There's one essay and a final group project. Take her class!

J320 was a class that stayed with me after I took it. The lectures were always interesting and relevant, and all the examples Gretchen & the GEs used helped me understand the occasionally difficult readings. The grading was fair and the writing assignments were actually fun, and my grade was never a mystery because of good feedback on the essays

I'm so glad I had this class! It was at 8 am and a lot of students didn't really want to come, but the lectures were so informative and interconnected with current events. I sometimes called my mom and brother and discussed things we talked about in class. LOVED it!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved this class and found the content and lectures eye opening. Lots of essays, but the topics are interesting & the tests are open note. Dr. Soderlund really seems to care about her students and the subject matter. I would take her again.

I mean, the class was okay. I thought a lot of the concepts we learned to study media were well-taught. However... this class almost only centered on the white experience. The discussion of how non-white people were represented in media felt disrespectful at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Soderlund is amazing, and held engaging lectures that always felt topical/worth attending. My frustration is with the GEs from this class. I did 3 essays (starting in week 5) and none were graded until week 10. My grade has dropped 9% right before finals. The comments they left are not clear/there is no rubric. Great class, beware of bad GEs!

easiest class ever. The content in lectures were pretty interesting and attendance is not mandatory. The grading consist of a midterm, optional take-home final and 3 essays (she puts prompts up every week and you choose which 3 you want to do) which were easy and interesting prompts. Gretchen is just a sweetie, i would take her again for sure.

Gretchen seems like the kind of professor students might walk all over, but she is actually knowledgeable in the area of gender in the media. Class was super easy and still interesting. 3 900 word essays based off of 6 offered prompts, two tests but the second one was canceled. Reading online every week but I never did it and I was fine.

easiest class ever, and very interesting too. The grading consist of 3 essays (she provides a prompt every week and you get to choose what prompt and when you want to do it), a midterm, and a final which she just cancelled and changed to an optional take-home final. Amazing and so easy.

Soderlund is funny and inspires interest in the topic. The class moves fast, but the lectures and readings are all interesting. There were 2 essays, 2 exams, and some quizzes that were extra credit. Soderlund is such a cool professor. Take her class!
J201 was a bright spot this quarter and a good introduction to the J major. I learned about media from a lot of new angles. Gretchen was also an engaging professor to talk to during office hours.

She doesn't use class time well. She's disorganized and doesn't relate different weeks lectures to any kind of larger lesson or themes that should be learned. I didn't get a lot out of this class (still got an A) and wouldn't recommend taking a survey course with her. She was very nice and approachable, though.
Professor was really engaging and quite funny at times as well. The subject of Media History at 8:30am would usually be boring, but learning from her actually made it fun! I'd highly recommend her!

J412 was one of my favorite classes at the UO so far. Gretchen was passionate about the material and assigned great readings. Thanks to this class, I'm now obsessed with all things investigative journalism. Gretchen is an amazing professor. I want to take all her classes.

Professor did a good job making a personal connection in spite of the size of the class. The lecture and readings were interesting. You have to do the work and take it seriously. If you do grading is reasonable.

I dreaded this 8:30 am class, but Professor Soderlund was upbeat and kept my attention the whole time. She gave extra credit quizzes to encourage people to attend class. I wasn't really into the subject when I signed up for the class, but I found it a lot more engaging than I expected.
I enjoyed and learned a lot from this class. Gretchen was a clear lecturer and very sweet. Her passion for the topic rubbed off on me. I'd recommend any J major to take this course.
Her class has opened my eyes to things I didn't know before. You have to read and be prepared, but you don't have to buy any textbooks. I would definitely recommend.
Love her!

I learned a lot from this class. Professor was very nice. You definitely had to work for your grade because there was a lot of information to remember. The writing assignments were interesting and not graded too hard.
interesting class if you like history

Material is not very interesting but there is A LOT of it! Tests are long as well as a lot of work with papers! Shes really picky even to the point of emails! Comes across self-righteous and i wouldn't recommend her

Prof. Soderlund is one of the best professors I've had at the university. I had her for Gender&Media, Media History, and Investigative Journalism, and I'm so glad I took these courses. Prof. Soderlund is extremely knowledgeable and inspiring. She will make you fall in love with the subject. She is also very helpful and has a great sense of humor!

Gretchen is one of the best professors in the J School. I've had her for 2 classes and now for media history. J387 is a little harder than Gender & Media. It's still very interesting and like the professor a lot. She seems genuinely concerned that students do well.
Professor is knowledgeable on the subject material. It's an interesting course. Tests are hard. Go to all lectures and pay attention and you'll do fine.
talks about own books too much boring
she was irritating and was never clear on assignments
Best, most thorough math instructor I have ever had. Super understanding for those aren't math savvy, gives crystal clear instructions, and is just overall a pretty nice guy.

I had him for  psy302 and 308. Both were test heavy with I clicker participation. A decent amount of extra credit and very kind/entertaining. Tests weren't hard but require a lilbit of study. 308 had a bigish paper. I did poorly but got A bc extra credit. He's great. If given opportunity I would always take his class. He records his lectures too.

Professor Guthrie is amazing. He makes his class so accessible and fun, and doesn't forget that we are all human beings who have commitments to more than just this class.
Most lectures recorded and posted online. Attendance not mandatory. If you study and complete the work with some effort, will receive an A. Very supportive, kind, and funny Prof.

Dr. Guthrie is one of my favorite professors at UO! He is extremely kind, caring, and a great lecturer. His lectures are simple yet interesting, and he is super approachable. Unfortunately, this is the last course he is offering at UO before he moves to the Netherlands, but I am so grateful I got to know him and have great conversations with him!

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Taylor Guthrie, do it. Truly, of the 120 credits I have taken, I have never had another professor come close to the level of Guthrie. He is great both as a professor and as a human, which is hard to find.

Amazing psych professor. He cares about his student's well being and learning environment, making resources extremely available. Work with GE's on assignments if the class material is difficult because they are allowed to regrade.

Amazing Prof! Super clear lectures and great at explaining concepts. Super friendly and obviously cares a lot about his student's success. Attendance isn't mandatory but earns extra credit points for midterms/final, which are all multiple choice and pretty easy. Take Guthrie for 302!

Taylor was such a kind and compassionate professor. His lectures are very well organized, all the materials are very accessible and organized in Canvas too if you missed class. He clearly knows the content very well and explains them in a great way. I think he genuinely wants his students to succeed.

Compassionate and accommodating professor. You can really tell there is a passion for this course and helping others. Great lectures that break difficult concepts into digestible slides. Unfortunate to hear he is leaving the country, I would love to take more of his courses.

100% take a class with Taylor Guthrie. Genuinely the best professor in psychology. Made learning psychology stats so easy and gave extra credit on tests just for showing up to class. Wish he was staying at UO for longer. Take his class!!!

I was putting off PSY 302 for a few terms because I'm not interested in math or stats. Even though the information was boring, Professor Guthrie made it entertaining. He gives clear exam advice, walks through examples, and wants students to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but go to class. You'll get extra credit and won't have to study much.

professor Guthrie is ok. He is very nice guy and a good lecturer and will gives lots of chances for free points. But he also seems like he doesnt always know what he is talking about in depth and is just keeping up with what he is teaching us right before the lecture. Anyone can pass his class even if you dont really learn anything.
Great professor, he made everything very clear in his lectures.

Good class. Hw every monday but theyre easy. Tests are kinda hard but not very mathy and you can get extra credit for them by showing up in class and doing i-clickers. Otherwise he records all lectures so you could technically never show up. Smart? Probably not but you could...

Dr. Guthrie is hands-down the best professor I've had at UO. He created the entire class on his own and is highly skilled in keeping his students engaged. The lectures are incredibly interesting, and the exams come straight from the slides. He offers extra credit and makes you feel like he truly cares about your education. Would highly recommend!

Dr. G is probably the best professor I have had so far in Psych. He is so nice and super easy to talk to. His lectures are super engaging and he clearly cares about what he talks about. There is no attendance unless u want to go for extra credit, and all the lectures are recorded and posted on canvas. Can not reccommend him enough!

Took 302 this past term and as someone who has a hard time with stats, I think that he is an excellent teacher. The class is multimodal and the homework is not too math heavy, and relates to psychological subjects we study in other courses. Going to class is worthwhile and significantly helped my grade and understanding of the class.

Dr. Guthrie's class PSY 383 was the first class to truly inspire me as to what to pursue after school.His teaching style is well-rounded and makes it worthwhile to attend class. While this class was lecture based,it's incredibly interesting which makes it easy to retain information.Dr. Guthrie fully prepares students for tests and is accommodating.

One of the best professors Ive had at UO! He gives extra credit just for attending class, makes content super easy to understand, and truly cares about his students. I was a little nervous going in because of stats, but he teaches in a way that is super beneficial. Exams are pretty easy if you study, and are weighted less than the homework.

Dr. Guthrie is by far one of the best professors at UO. He cares about his student's success. The lectures are fill in the blanks and the blanks are what the exams are on. The class is heavy in memorizing but bc the lectures are easy to follow, they were not too difficult, just study and you'll do fine. I would recommend this class to everyone!

I had Dr. Guthrie for PSY 383 and PSY 302 in one term. I couldn't have picked a better professor to have for a whole term. By far my favorite professor I've had. 
Very communicative and actually cares about his students being engaged and interested. Makes a huge effort to give us the confidence to succeed.

Best professor I've ever had! Dr. Guthrie genuinely cares about the success of his students. His lectures are very engaging and super interesting. While grades are only based off four assignments (two midterms, final, essay) there are optional extra credit discussions weekly. This is the first course I've genuinely enjoyed at UO. Highly recommend!!

Definitely my favorite class of the term and one of my favorites from all of undergrad! You can tell Dr Gutherie is really passionate about what he does and really wants you to learn and succeed. While you are only graded on four assignments, there's weekly extra credit discussions, the exams aren't difficult as long as you pay attention and study.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly cares about teaching and his students. Attendance isn't mandatory but there is iclicker extra credit if you attend, he also records all his lectures. The weekly lab and quizzes actually help to clarify assignments. While this is a class that people take because it's required for the psych degree, he actually makes it enjoyable and engaging.
Take Dr. Guthrie if you can! He is one of the best professors I've had at UO. Very organized and genuinely cares about students education.

I can't recommend Dr. Guthrie enough!! He explains everything in lectures and they are posted after so if you miss something it is easy to go back. He is also super caring, wants everyone to do well, and very accommodating. Also gives extra credit just for coming to class!!

This was my favorite class of the term. Dr. Guthrie is a great lecturer and every lecture was super engaging and interesting. I would absolutely recommend taking one of his classes if you get the chance.

Professor Guthrie is hands down the best professor I've had in college. He designed the entire class on his own, and was able to keep a class of over 100 students constantly engaged throughout each lecture. Not only is he very kind, helpful, and funny, but he offers extra credit opportunities. He genuinely cares for his students, highly recommend!

This review is for 383 but there wasn't an option to select that course. This class was interesting and engaging. Lectures are important so go to the lectures. The only homework is one paper, and the rest of the grade comes from the three exams. I like this format a lot because there was't much homework. Highly recommend

He is one of the best professors I've had. He really cares to teach his students and wants people to learn. He is always available to ask questions and clarify anything you may be stuck on. His test are really easy because he makes lecture interesting and tells you exactly how to study.

Dr. Guthrie is one of the best professors I have had at UO. He clarifies SO much. I took AP stats so this class was review for me. However, anything new was explained in an understandable way with amazing worked out examples. Labs were just added details + easy. Funny and actually takes time to care about students. Plus attendance is extra credit!

I am not good at statistics at all, and this is the one teacher that can get me to pass the class. Attendance is not mandatory, and if you do go to class, it's extra credit. He cares so much about the subject and makes it super easy to understand. He's super approachable and is an amazing overall teacher.

Professor Guthrie is an amazing lecturer and shows that he genuinely wants each student to succeed. He offered us many extra credit opportunities, made the content very interesting by lecturing with passion, and made it incredibly easy to study for exams.

Taylor was my GE for the psych 302 lab section & he was amazing! He gave super clear instructions for HW and even went out of his way to make videos we could watch to understand it better. He does such a good job of describing concepts in a way that makes sense and he truly wants everyone to succeed! I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Taylor Guthrie is a fantastic professor. The three case studies were all interesting reads and easy questions to answer. The 2 exams and the final exam were all the fairest exams I have ever taken.Take this class as it is a chill class, with interesting content, and an awesome, caring, and incredibly flexible professor.

Taylor is an amazing instructor and this was one of my favorite psych classes here at UO thanks to him! He understands the importance of building a supportive learning community and provides students opportunities to interact in meaningful ways. His lectures are straightforward and the quizzes are over the emphasized points.

Taylor is easily one of the best psychology professors at the University. His lectures are casual, relevant, and intriguing. He is very knowledgeable and provides unique perspectives on all of the topics discussed in the class. I wish I had the opportunity to take more courses from him during my time at the University.

Professor Guthrie is truly an amazing prof. You can tell he cares about his students & wants them to succeed - he made the class extremely accessible, his grading criteria was clear & he put a lot of effort into lecture materials and group activities. This class has been incredible, would highly recommend! 4 tests, 3 papers, & 1 final
