Taylor's care for his students is made extremely clear in the way he teaches. Lectures are easy to understand and the wealth of knowledge he shares is incredible during each class! We took three tests (including the final) and had one essay. Very straightforward teaching and expectations. Would definitely recommend this educator to future students!

One of the best Professors I've ever had, everything was clear in terms of grading criteria and what we should focus on studying wise. COVID-19 ruined the term but I'd gladly take another class with Professor Guthrie!

Taylor is one of the best teachers I've had in my college career. He cares cares greatly about every one of his student's success. I strongly believe his teaching style is one that should be adapted by more teachers and has greatly encouraged my success in his class. The fact he recorded his lectures proved to be one of my most resourceful tools

Taylor was an amazing instructor for this course! His lectures were easy to follow and study guides for the exams, making studying for exams less daunting. He always recorded his lectures, which helped when referencing it for study materials. in other words, I recommend taking any class that is taught by Taylor, including this one!

Professor Guthrie was one of my favorite teachers in the University of Oregon Psych department. He has a clear passion for the subject which makes his lectures engaging and enjoyable. He recorded every lecture and released them online, something I had never had a professor do before. The lecture recordings were an extremely useful study tool.

I took his class for Cognitive Neuroscience and it was hands down the best class Ive taken at my university! He posted all of his lectures online allowing for great study preparation. It was his class that reminded me what I wanted to get out of my education. Also highly recommend if youre interested in medicine-he has worked in the field

Taylor is hands down one of the best teachers I have worked with on Campus. He goes out of his way to make sure his students are learning the material in the clearest way possible. He is willing to schedule appointments if you are unable to make office hours and he puts together extra study sessions before exams. Would absolutely take another class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taylor was my teacher for chem lab even though he was a psychology grad student. Always came prepared and honestly was better than any of the chem grad students I previously had. He knew the class was designed for us to fail and routinely helped us out with lab reports and assignments. 10/10 would recommend

Taylor has the unique ability to make seemingly complicated material accessible. He really cares about his students' success. He goes above and beyond providing supplementary materials and/or holding review sessions before exams. I will definitely take another course by this instructor!
Taylor is an amazing educator. He truly cares about instructing and his students learning.
My time with Professor Grossman has trained me to be a better musician and player. He fixed so much technical issues I had.
Professor Grossman is amazing.  I have never had such an organized and supportive teacher.  I wish I had started with him in my undergrad

Professor Grossman often uses students as examples for each other in studio class and lessons which fosters a competitive and toxic environment because each student is working hard to be noticed for doing something right. Being founder of the No Pain All Gain Grossman Method, he is not really as helpful as he claims. Everyone comes out traumatized.
I have made so much progress in my technique with Grossman. He is the most organized and thorough teacher I have ever had. I look forward to continuing my lessons with him.

Grossman thinks highly of himself but lessons with him were traumatic and triggering. I was hopeful studying with him due to his reputation but unfortunately, I found that he created a toxic environment in his studio between students, and would publicly humiliate them. His personal vendettas for individuals overshadowed his priorities as a teacher.

Very good at what he does, knows his stuff, does not know how to treat people well. Yells at some students, blames them, makes them cry. If becoming a better violinist is worth verbal abuse or you are strong enough to make him listen and treat you better, he is a wonderful teacher. he is not for the faint of heart, or those who are not confident.

Hal Grossman is one of the worst teachers I've ever worked with. He frequently shames and demeans his students in lieu of actually teaching them, and creates a toxic atmosphere where his studio is made to feel superior to others. Additionally, he is profoundly rude and condescending to collaborative pianists. Highly, highly do not recommend.

Ian is a great lecturer who keeps the material engaging. Some of the content was definitely challenging at times, but that's expected in an upper-level course. The only thing I wish he gave us were practice tests, but if you could explain the concept to someone else, you'll do well in the lecture.

Ian has streamlined lectures and exam content is clearly outlined. He makes succeeding in his class easy if you just take notes on his lectures. A bit lazy at times, a handful of information on Canvas was incorrect throughout the term, and he didn't really use announcements at all.

Ian is a decent prof, course content is interesting. Learning objectives outlined exam content. Big group project for the class, project only accounted for 10% of course grade, was absolutely a giant waste of time. GEs must be bored, graded reports harshly for no reason. Exams were tricky, class average was about 72% across all 3 exams.

His exams are pretty hard, very specific detailed when he briefly goes over lecture material. I did the learning objectives and studied the scientific evidence, barely got by. His tests are tricky but everything else is manageable.
This class was amazing and he is super awesome. The assignments have very clear instructions and are pretty fun, he is a super understanding guy and really wants you to succeed.

Doctor Graham was awesome to have as a professor. Yes it is very lecture heavy but they are very interesting and I genuinely enjoyed them. It's not easy and does take work but he gives everyone opportunity to succeed if you do the work. The work is doable and consistent but not easy. Pay attention in class and try and you will do great!

This class was hell. I hated the lectures and dreaded the class. In 11 weeks, we did 3 papers, 3 group projects, and a final paper. He is a harsh grader but does offer good/clear feedback. Be prepared for him to randomly yell at you in week 5 or 6 for no reason and out of the blue. Lectures are also very long and incredibly boring.
10/10 recommended

Material was clear. Matt made lectures fun and engaging. Can make up assignments for full credit and turn in assignments past due date for full credit. Also, got to leave early a bunch. 10/10 recomend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's awesome I loved this class

Amazing teacher. All quiz answers are on Quizlet so that made getting an A easy but the content is SO interesting and he teaches it very well. Uses his own kids as an example of what he is teaching which really puts it in perspective. 


I was in EDST 225 but it won't let me put that.

Wonderful professor and I would definitely take his class again. He is very clear during the lectures and makes it very easy to understand the material. An A is very easy in this class, every point can be made up because he really cares that you learn the material. There is a lot of reading but the textbook is very easy to read and understand

One of my favorite professors I have had. Very personable and values your life outside of school. Every single point in the class can be made up. The lectures are great and make the material very easy to understand.

She is a bit sporadic in her teaching, but she has great ideas and allows for students to express opinions. A nice and easy approachable teacher who will give you advice and critiques on your work for the better.

Outside of being heavily against Ai, Groppe does a great job. Her in class discussions are great but nobody really shows up. Have a quick homework assignment for every class but this class is an easy A if you just do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: I'm taking this to satisfy a gen ed and would highly recommend it. She understands that students have other classes & does not assign much outside of the films. You can tell Professor Groppe loves what she teaches and if you participate in lectures and watch the films you will do well in her class.
The class was overall boring and lots of materials to read before every session.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Let me get something straight, I love Chinese movies, or foreign films in general.  If you like film, take this class.  Instead of having a lecture focus, it was almost all discussion.  Only 4 essays total for the class (that includes the final).  All mercifully graded.  The films were REALLY well chosen.  A balance of eras, genres and directors.
She's really nice but pretty scatterbrained. Participate during lecture and she'll love you. Seems to have a genuine interest in the subject

This class was an easy A. It can be time consuming because you have to go watch a film outside of class and discussion time but it's not so bad. I was only taking this class for my global context requirement for business and I thought Alison was nice and helpful.As long as you go to class, discussion and film, you'll get an A for sure.
Horrible lectures. Too random of in class writing assignments. Terrible movies. Much too hard for a 100 level course. Alison should really try running a better course.

not super helpful, but relatively easy. She is one of those teachers who values everyone's opinion too much to actually give critique, which ends up not making sense in the larger picture of a discussion class...

Professor Graboyes was an incredibly caring and thoughtful professor. I took her class GSL 345, which is a Global Health Ethics course, and she was awesome. She is so passionate about her work and the courses she teaches, and her tests are extremely straight forward. If you go to class and do the readings, you will get a very good grade. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Here is what I noticed: She gives unhelpful feedback as to why she graded our papers the way she did. She gives no concrete grading criteria. When I reached out for help, she did not provide help to make me think about the material in a new interesting way. In class, there was little room for creative thought, as the questions were fact based.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Graboyes is so passionate about teaching and she is even more passionate about the research that she has done. At the beginning of the term, she told us that she was going to treat us like her high level students which slightly made me nervous but she is all for making sure we know that material and understand it clearly. A lot of reading

This was the first time Graboyes had taught this normally 400 level course as a Freshman seminar, and it was so interesting! A lot of reading every week, but very easy to get a good grade if you like the subject and take the help that she so freely gives. She required respect and maturity, but very nice and really knows her stuff. Favorite class!!

Melissa is an amazing professor! You are really fortunate to have her as an instructor. She is extremely passionate about her subjects and is really easy to talk to in office hours. She really wants everyone to succeed and do well. This has been my favorite class all year and I am SO happy I took it with her!

I find the class topics very interesting, however I do not agree with having a guest lecture for every single class. I feel that the registered professor should teach the class and I don't feel I get that at all with this class. Shes very nice and helpful, but does very little teaching.
Super interesting guest lecture based class. Not an easy class but not too hard either. Attend class or you will be completely lost!

Love her! Incredibly knowledgeable about Africa and disease, super helpful and friendly, breaks down class into lectures and discussion, fair assignments and tests, only complaint: wayy too many articles to print out

The prof really knows her stuff. The Essay was hard and she is a very tough grader, but it is worth it for what you get out of this class. Worst thing is how much we have to print. I have already blown through two printer cartridges for this class alone! Plus the 2-3 other books we also had to buy adds up quick! Beware extra costs of this course!
More focused on encouraging students to be orchestra musicians than anything else. Not educated on
Great!

This class is boring as hell. The assignments are tough, but he is a very easy grader which is why he is rated so high on here. If you know music well you will be fine. However, if your like me and don't know anything about music this class will not be easy.
Great teacher, odd sense of humor, but lots of fun to be around and to listen to.
Song in the mind and wind at the lips
Super fun dude who knows a lot about music. Watch out for Thursdays!
Song and Wind!

Hilarious! The class was really fun, and even though it was 8am I still went just to listen to his great lectures. Some kids even got extra credit for trying to tell a worse joke than him. Awesome class and awesome guy.
He certainly knew his stuff and could lecture on and on. He was very easy to listen to and he has a great sense of humor too. Great environment and no homework! Quizzes are easy if you attend class.
best teacher ever i would for sure take another class from him he made me laugh even though the class was at 8 am i still went everyday because it was interesting

Professor Grose is a pretty cool guy.  His jokes are a little corny, but sometimes they're really funny...you just have to have the right sense of humor.  I'd take another class from him...if i was in the music field...but i'm not...dangit...........

extremely dry, very boring, strange guy, kind of a tool. not really recommended. and the class is ridiculously easy, which seems like it would be a good thing, but it makes it just that much more boring.
No Comments
Easy yet interesting and engaging class. only problem was 8:30 AM
Easy class.  Lot's of audio/visual excitement.
No Comments
No Comments
Prof. Grose makes understanding music enjoyable. He's off-beat with his humor, knows the material well, and the work he assigns is pretty good.

I loved this class.  The subject was interesting  and only made more so wit her interesting and relevant stories.  Also she seems to be fairly formal I wouldn't call hee by her first name without being invited.  Tests were v straight forward

One of the worst teacher I have came across, does not care about students, is so so so rude when asking about extra opportunities, might be a good researcher but not good when it comes to teaching college students.

Prof. Gwartney is confusing, writes illegibly and then does not post her slides, hw and tests are written poorly and are impossible to get an A on. She also stopped emailing me back in the middle of a conversation where I asked her very nicely to post the slides online frequently. Also doesn't check disc board. Bad teacher and won't acknowledge it.
She was actually quite nice and relaxed. Was pretty strict about her grading, but was also fairly understanding. I liked her class, but might have been because it was summer term.

I believe that Professor Gwartney has good intentions, but as she said the first day of class, she was not educated on how to be a teacher. She may be a great social researcher but her expectations are unrealistic as a teacher. She is unorganized and confusing with her connection to the book. If you take this course, the book will be your teacher.

I will never take a class from her again.  I have never given a teacher a bad review and this teacher deserves the worst.  Her lectures are confusing, she doesn't use power points but writes in illegible handwriting, and is extremely short when you ask a question.  I admit, she is knowledgeable in her research, but some people should not teach.
I would avoid taking any classes with this professor if at all possible. Unclear guidelines, constantly changing syllabus and awful tests.

I took this class as an elective and Prof. Gwartney really isn't that bad. She lets you use a front and back 8x11 cheat sheet, typed or hand written, for all exams.  However, she doesn't use power points in class, she just talks and you take notes and read the book. It's a very quiet class and not much going on but it's not terrible.

Uses out-dated data, constantly unprepared for class, doesn't seem to really know the material, reiterates what the textbook says, flip-flops on answers which gets VERY confusing. Has a problem reading the graphs that SHE incorporates in her presentations. I feel ripped-off. Wait until someone else teaches the class you're trying to take from her.

2nd attempt at my post:Patricia Gwartney is selfish, stuck up, and haughty woman?her elitist attitude is brought into the classroom everyday, which makes for a gut-wrenching environment.  She?s unreasonable, picks favorites and makes class time academically fearful. Her seniority in the Soc. Program scares me as a major...Gwart....any negations????

Patricia Gwartney is selfish, stuck up, and haughty woman—her elitist attitude is brought into the classroom everyday, which makes for a gut-wrenching environment. She’s unapproachable, picks favorites and simply makes class time academically fearful. This woman is a self-righteous and generally pompous person—I had my father and two of his colleagues (all work for Nike corporate) sit in on her course wearing sweats one day, they concluded she was a b*tch both are graduates of the PAC 10.

She is absolutely nuts, and a horrible teacher. Her rules for class etiquette are truly bizarre, my friend and I even made up a joke about not being allowed to breathe or she'd scream at us. Grading scale was non-comprehensible to the sane, I don't think anyone knew what she was looking for, and extremely self-absorbed. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

She is insane! Probably the worst teacher i have ever had. The class itself shouldn't be that hard but she wastes time on a daily basis and treats the class like we are in kindergarden. For someone who has been teaching for 10+ years she doesn't act like it. Do not take her class!
she is CRAZY! get out of any class she teaches...seriously the list of rules is probably going to be two pages...NOT A GOOD TEACHER AT ALLLLLLL!.

She is in love with her own research. No matter what topic we would discuss in class, she should somehow tie her own research in. Even if it wasn't related to anything we were talking about. If she had taught my first soc class ever it would have made me completely lose interest. With that said, she is a nice person and well meaning.
She has impossible standards; assigns a ton of group work. She assigns a ton of homework. And she is unapproachable.

She is by far the best instructor in the sociology department for research methods.  She expects a lot from her students, but if anyone else taught this class, it would be pointless.  She teaches her students more about methods in one minute than a book could do in a lifetime.
She was horrible and made me drop the class without willingness to help me work through an injury. Told me if I didn't drop it, I'd fail.

i hated her. she sucked. she was rude. i asked her to make the files on blackboard saved in a different way because they were so large and my computer at the time couldn't open them. she then went on to ridicule me via email to the entire class and then tell me to go to the library. her class was all about RESEARCH and not social aspects. SHE SUCKE

you would think that someone who is so "organized" wouldn't run such a circus of a class. maybe if she spent time teaching instead of telling us about how she teaches. follows a very unclear syllabus. won't answer emails, even if your question is very specific. sad as a soc major that this is my last soc class, don't wanna leave college hating soc.

absolutely ridiculous class. feels like a freshman  high school course. She spent 10 minutes teaching us how to read a bar graph WTF?! The class is pointless lengthy videos, small group activities like crossword puzzles and word jumbles, and mostly INANE power point presentations filled with generalizations, stereotypes and big buzzwords. ARG.
I think she's great! Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, and genuinely seems to want to help people however she can!
Extremely boring and unhelpful teacher. The groups are a total waste of time.

On the first day of class she spent the entire hour and twenty minutes putting everyone into groups, gave every group a "team name," and then proceeded to give everyone a piece of paper with their team name on it and said "This is your passport to learning." Enough said.
No Comments

I have never been in a class that was such a waste of time. It was a joke to go to class... she just wanted to show us her power point slides. She was always late, rude to the students, and she even lost assignments from students. HORRIBLE teacher.

The course is incredibly comprehensive and educational.
The tests are pretty difficult for a gen ed course. There is little direction given as to what will be on them, and the course covers a lot of material, so studying for them can be frustrating, but not entirely unfair.
Recommended if you are a major or have a special interest in the material.

Dr. Green is a knowledgable professor. There are times where she rambles on about other things, but they can be interesting.  I would recommend that you buy the Bible she recommends because it has annotations given by the author. !There is a group project and a short paper! Prior understanding of the Bible might be good to have.

Truly one of the most incredible professors I've ever had, taking so many of her courses are why I ended up adding a religious studies major to my degree. She is direct and honest, and provides excellent feedback. The discussions are so interesting and I learn so much from her, both academically and through her lived experience.

She is one of the most caring and knowledgeable professors I have ever had. While it's a lot of reading, it absolutely is what makes the class the amazing experience that it is. The discussions in her class are very intellectually stimulating, while not being overwhelming or feeling high-stakes. She does so much to make the class more accessible!!

Professor Green is a thoughtful and understanding professor. If you come to class prepared, having done the reading, it is easy to succeed in her classes. There is a group project worth 30% of your grade, but Prof Green understands if you get stuck with bad groupmates. Coming to class will give you all the information you need for the final.

Dr. Green is an amazing professor who clearly knows what she is teaching and is able to convey this to students through her material. The class was very engaging in topics and she was always open to answering questions both in the class and afterwards. The projects and class overall was very fun and easy if you showed up and did your part!

I mean She's really smart in her field, but she should not be teaching an -intro- level bible class. This class is perfect for Catholics and religious nuts. Unless you want to read the bible 4 different times I would not recommend. The worst part of this class is the lectures where she rambles about some niche topic. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want a horrible class with a horrible professor I would strongly recommend her, if you want to save your GPA and time, I would not. This class, while not even finished yet, is the worst class i've ever taken at UO. Green babbles on in lecture with no slides, so good luck taking notes. If you love to read the bible then go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The only way you will enjoy this class is if you have read the Bible multiple times or are a practicing Catholic. I thought this class would be about studying the Bible, but it's more about Mrs. Green—who, granted, is very knowledgeable—incoherently babbling about something super niche. If you value your time and grades, find another class.

Homework and lectures were very tedious for this course, Prof Green is very knowledgable but definitely tries to pack too much information into one class. Homework involves reading the Torah and very long and dense articles regarding Judaism, very fascinating but it can be incredibly time consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: REL222 is the best class I've taken at college and Prof Green is fabulous! This class is dense and difficult, but it is so rewarding if you put in the work. I believe its useful to anyone in any major! The class has 1 midterm, 1 essay, 1 final, and weekly quizzes. The exams are writing heavy and closed note and book, but they're okay if you study!
loved her class!

REL 222 is a VERY dense class. In it, you will receive an overview of the entire Old Testament (which is very long). Beware of the quizzes - even if you have done the readings, the questions are tricky. The midterm and the final are writing intensive and you can expect to use the full time. Grading on the paper is easy. Professor is a great though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take Deborahs class if you're not ready to read a million pages of the bible. Her lectures are very boring and you're graded on a few HUGE papers. The final is all essay questions closed notes on basically the entire bible. It's a very hard class is all I can say. Horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super Nice! Attend CLASS and DISS, attendance really counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Green is no push-over. You will need to participate and do your readings or you will fail the pop quizzes in section. The midterm and final are a bit ridiculous for a 200-lvl course, I wouldn't take it as an elective unless you're super interested in biblical history. However, she's a fun and engaging lecturer and you will feel rewarded.

Professor Green made the content very engaging even if you're familiar with the Bible. Her lectures were incredible, though you really need to take good notes as her slides lack content. She's very inspiring and knowledgeable, but her quizzes were a bit unfair. The midterm and final are very long and writing-heavy. Study hard for them.

Not necessary to have grown up with a religious background in order to pass this class. But, it would make things a bit easier at least during the beginning of the Bible. Really interesting lectures via Zoom and Discussions would be interesting as well. Lots of reading, but all interesting stories. Great professor and it's obvious she loves her job

Slides only give vague bullet points. Talks too fast to understand and take notes. Definitely have prior knowledge about the Bible before taking this class. Doesn't give much info about what's needed to know for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's really nice, but so confusing when she talks. Clearly she knows a lot, but is not clear--GTF saved my grade. Tests are fair.

Wonderful professor. 1st day I noticed her voice was kind of pitchy but now I can't tell, haha. You have to go to lecture! Not only for credit, but she is an amazing lecturer and her insight is pretty much vital in your understanding of the text. She's funny and EXTREMELY passionate about her work. You will never fall asleep (and you better not)!
Awesome class, great professor!

Although she at times has some strange points of view on the Bible I definitely learned a lot in her class. Not an easy gen. ed. class by any means, but she is very passionate about her work.  Also, even though she can come across as rude, she provides you with all the info you need to succeed on the exams.

I looooooved this teacher! She was so passionate about what she taught, and she made learning fun. The course was more challenging than I thought it would be, but she made me want to work hard. She is very funny, and very smart (not often you get both). TAKE her class! You would be crazy not to!

Disrespectful to students. Although very passionate, I don't think she really enjoys giving students in-depth knowledge on the material, its just thrown at you without making sure everyone understands. Too much information, it was difficult to keep up with with a hard class schedule. Prepare yourself for a boring class.
She is the best professor at the UO. Her passion for the material is very strong.

Professor Green is the best teacher I have ever had. She is really interested in helping her students and really enthusiastic about what she teaches. If she can tell that you want to do well and work hard, she will treat you well and help you.
Fun teacher with lots of energy, very passionate about the subject and very knowledgeable. Hard class however, no study guides will be given, your expected to know a lot

Prof. Green is extremely helpful & actually cares about her students. The class is quite tough and requires lots of time. However, I highly recommend her if you are interested in Biblical Hebrew, she's an awesome professor!

Professor Green is one of the best professors I have had at UO. She has completely changed my perspective of the bible. She has an indescribable understand and love for what she is teaching. Her lectures are incredibly engaging and her passion spreads like wild fire. She is one of the most  caring teachers I have come into contact with.

3/4 way thru her term- She really knows what she's talking about. She's devoted years studying what she teaches and teaches it like a history book not religious truth. Those who use it otherwise (religiously) close-mindedly may voice a problem with her but really it should be a problem with the text. I enjoy her class, am also christian. Be open!
She is a great teacher and very knowledgeable. The lady deserves some peppers!!!
Dr. Green is awesome. She is really knowledgeable and is fun and engaging. Unlike a lot of professors, she has a good idea of what is going on in her students lives.
She is mean. Don't take a class from her unless you have a thick skin.
I like her. You have to study a good amount, but she tells you exactly what you need to know for tests. She's helpful.
She knows her stuff, a lot of what she goes over in class is fuzzy but if you go to her office hours she makes it a lot clearer. Dont be intimidated, she means well even if seems sort of cranky.

Professor Green knew a lot about the bible, but did not know how to teach.  I took a class on teaching the same term, and she did everything you are not supposed to do as a teacher.  She's a very smart woman, but very cranky.  The GTF's were more helpful than she was...a lot of people in the class were afraid of her.  Good subject, bad professor.

Not clear at all. Did not work well with GTFs. They gave criteria, but she gave others. Made mistakes with Bible details. Taught her own interpretation like it was fact. Included weird generalizations about historical Jews and existing Jewish culture. Refused to offer any guidance for studying. Poor communication.
Best teacher I had at U of Oregon.

I took martyrdom with her and thought she did quite well.  Very eager to discuss things outside of class and offer any help, any time.  In my class there was a very high percentage of christians (like hardcore ones, one even admitted he would slaughter his children if he thought god was telling him to) and that impeded the diversity of discussion to a certain degree and i don't know if she really knew how to handle it.  She certainly did better than i would though.
No Comments

Prof. Green is probably one of the worst professors in dealing with Religion. She is factually incorrect most times, is unyielding when it comes to exams, and in my opinion, seems to have this fascination with denegrating the Jewish people into some sort of Pagan-stealing group of people.

i had writing 123 with her instead of 122, but these reviews are still super accurate! she lead lectures that were actually helpful with assignments, gave good feedback on assignments, and is overall a very nice professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatay is the most amazing, sweet, and caring teacher I have ever had. She gives great and helpful feedback and makes her instructions/grading extremely clear. I genuinely looked forward to her class; she made it so easy to want to show up and participate! I highly recommend her.

Molly was great and very accommodating. She made classes interesting and really showed that she cared about our success. She was always there to help and made her grading criteria really clear. She was also very funny and connected well with her students. I would definitely recommend her.

I love Professor Hatay. She is so enthusiastic about what she teaches and gives good presentations. She also answers every question you might have in and outside of class. She really wants you to succeed!
10/10 would take again

She's very sweet and very passionate about her subject matter. Pretty easy grader too imo, and she wants to help her students so she encourages questions if we have any. Also very real. She knows you have a life outside of school, so if you have any issues or concerns, let her know and she'll try to help you out. 10/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hatay is my favorite professor I've had so far in college. My favorite thing about her is that she keeps it real. I felt inspired to write when I was in her class. The weekly assignments and papers are not too bad. She is really caring and understanding, especially if you communicate with her. Just an extremely funny, chill professor.
I absolutely love Molly. She is kind and understanding as long as you communicate with her, her grading is clear and fair, you can get extensions and redo a few assignments if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have literally nothing bad to say about Prof Molly, she is so kind and sweet and the work is super easy. I enjoyed going to her lectures, she is also super supportive. She does labor-based grading and emphasizes it's not about the quality but more the fact you tried on your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Molly was a great professor to have. Very easy to reach and is always willing to help her students whenever she can. She met with me during finals week to help me with the final which was amazing of her. Her grading is labor based and it was a pretty simple class. Attendance is required but her class was great to go to.

She is engaging and very supportive of her students. I enjoy coming to class. Her grading is participation-based but she still gives feedback on the big assignments. I would 100% take her class again.
Molly is an amazing professor. She gives great lectures, is so caring and always willing to help. Has a clear grading criteria and always gives feedback.

Molly is extremely caring and one of my favorite professors I've had. She is always willing to help you out. You can miss 2 classes without it taking away from participation points, but its still a minor percentage of your grade. I definitely recommend taking her class.
Very nice professor, always upbeat in class and kind to students

Sweetest Professor I've had in a minute. You start to realize that your Professor's attitude and general personality affect the effort you put into their class and Molly encouraged me to actually want to engage and write. You can tell she just gets it. Down to earth and could not possibly be more authentic. You're in luck if you get her.

Molly is by far one of the most amazing teachers I've ever had, not just at UO but in all of my education experience. She is funny, kind, easy to talk to, and gives amazing feedback. She creates a safe and welcoming classroom environment, and I genuinely look forward to attending each week. Very clear on grading policies, and fair with extensions.

Prof. Hatay is easily one of the best teachers or professors I've had. She is friendly and very funny and loves to build relationships with her students. She is very accessible outside of class and offers clear feedback on assignments. It's easy to earn good grades in her class if you follow her grading criteria. 100/10 would take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: An awesome professor, provided really interesting readings and held great group discussions/analysis

Molly is an amazing instructor! She is clearly passionate about literature and was very energetic during lectures. The assigned readings never felt like too much work and she is mindful of keeping workloads reasonable. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, you should!

Extremely personable. Will push you to your absolute limit with studio work and desk crits, but everything he says or has you do is perfectly curated to truly make you a better architectural designer when it's all said and done.
High expectations for his students, but very friendly.

by "get ready to read" I mean his EMAILS. every night you will receive an essay of what to do for the following period. He says a lot, but not much of use, one of the worst ramblers ever. He may be a good architect (no idea), but I did not like his teaching Has very specific ideas, and though you dont have to use them he will be annoyed if you dont
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best intro studio professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Best studio professor Ive had so far. Do your work and follow a clear and well-presented idea and youll pass no problem, if you dont do this you will earn his disdain but will probably still pass. Hes super kind and knows a lot about sustainability if you talk to him he can teach you a lot.

Has a very boring style. Once told the class to stay away from innovative ideas because inventing something new is too expensive. He expects you to listen to his suggestions and not have ideas of your own. He is very nice as a person, but as an architect his style is too dull.

He will talk for hours without saying anything of substance or actually tell you what he expects for the next class. Expect long emails that night. Lacks common sense and has terrible ideas to "fix" your project. Your work will be worse than the other studios but at least you'll have extra time to drink to forget how bad this studio really was.

Really nice guy but really bad at teaching. Had him for architecture studio and every class he had new ideas to give me and they always contradicted what he told me before. This happened to a lot of people. Does not give good feedback. He was not clear with what he wanted from students, super unorganized.

I absolutely loved this class! Haruka is so kind, cares deeply about student feedback, and has very valuable insight into global issues since she previously worked for the United Nations. She makes a huge effort to know students by name, and is always available to help. Not too difficult a class, but very engaging! GE Michael Cook was great too.

Incredible professor!!! highly recommend taking a class taught by Haruka. This was a reading heavy class. She grades very generously, and just wants to see your effort. One of the best teachers I have had at UO.
This is the second class I have taken with her, she is so wonderful and caring. She put so much emphasis on communication and students wellbeing. One of my favorite professors at UO.
I found the lectures to be super long and tedious. The lectures are not taken into account; only the discussion classes are. The class is easy, but it is very repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and kind, and the class is super easy. There's weekly readings that are kind of long but overall if you attend the lectures since she doesn't post the slides, you should ace the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Really easy class. Lecture heavy but the slides aren't posted outside of class so attendance is key. Really easy assignments and exams.

She's a great professor if you show up and do the work you'll be just fine. Attendance is only mandatory for the discussions but what is talked about in the lectures will not be found anywhere else and you'll need them for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is super easy and would heavily recommend. If you attend the lectures you don't have tpo read at all and assignments are insanely easy
dont sleep on the goat. Hashimoto sensee is accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: dont sleep on the goat. accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So much work for this class, and mandatory attendance. Tests are easy and professor is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I know 200-level Japanese is difficult, but I still felt extremely discouraged. Her feedback was unhelpful or nonexistent, and she went through material at a pace that was hard for me to keep up with. I highly recommend taking someone else, or if you have to take her, only take 2 other classes so you have more time to devote to this course.
Hashimoto Sensei is a good professor

People need to understand that the UO Japanese language curriculum is brutal, but rewarding. Hashimoto Sensei does what she can to make it reasonable; she's dedicated to being a teacher, and I respect that. She obviously puts in the work to give us all the feedback she can, while also pushing us through the storm that is 200-level Japanese classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She went over material very fast at a rate that's too difficult to understand. Although her slide shows were great. Everyday class with 2/5 days of the week devoted to quizzes and dictations. Not very personable nor lenient on any situational problems that you have in your life and work.

She can come off as a bit too serious initially, but if you try to get to know her a bit, you'll realize she's a very kind. She's a harder grader than the other JPN professors, but she understands that the class is fast-paced and wants to push everyone to keep up with the curriculum. She lectures faster, but reviews more than other professors.

She comes off very intense initially, but it truly is because she cares. Go to class, do your best, and go to her office hours, and you will see a kinder side of her. She brought us candy on Valentine's Day, and she's always willing to answer questions if you are willing to ask them. Her grading feels harsh sometimes but it's because she cares.

Hashimoto has been pretty unhelpful on all fronts as a Japanese professor. She knows what she's talking about, but is quite condescending in the classroom. Constantly snickering at the mistakes of students doesn't exactly yield a good learning environment. If you work hard you will do well, but may find yourself frustrated by class structure.

The Japanese department at UO is set up so that no teacher will be actively bad for your learning. Slides are helpful and it is doable to teach yourself outside of class. Reiko can come off as cold at first, however, it is easy to warm up to each other. I would highly recommend always going up to her before/after class for any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't mind this professor but I feel as though she expects a lot from students when it comes to how quickly we're able to memorize things. She's not the most empathetic person but her lectures are informative.

Do not take this professor. There are so many other options to choose from and this isn't it. She wont give feedback on what you mess up on even if you ask. When grading assignments she doesn't have any leeway or will give comments that either don't make sense or don't matter.

I recommend taking any other professor. If you like to overachieve during assignments, she is not for you. She expects everyone to be at the same level. If you do better, she is skeptical that you are receiving outside help. If you do too well, she finds something to take points off. Many errors when giving feedback. Handwriting is tough to read.

I am passionate about learning Japanese, so i always try to make the best of any situation. But, I would NOT recommend this professor to anyone who is a beginner learner. The homework load is the same as any other class. Her grading is very unrealistic and SUPER strict for freshman/sophomore learners. She can be a bit passive-aggressive too...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hashimoto looks very intimidating at first but shes actually a very sweet and understanding professor once you get to know her. Ive taken 3 classes with her and they definitely require a lot of effort in order to pass but its honestly not that bad if youre actually committed to learning.
Hashimoto Sensei is tough but she cares for her students. She is a bit intimidating at first BUT when you get the chance to talk to her, she actually is really nice. I liked her

This is my 4th Japanese teacher at UO, and she is by far the worst. I'm on target for an A-/A, but it's not without extremely poor to non-existent feedback from her (her notes on writing assignments are unhelpful at best, despite using the same exact grading code/criteria as all the other teachers.) She is also quite condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Over demanding on workload, and is very condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You get 3 excused absences and after that your grade gets bumped down. There is homework due every lecture day and quizzes every discussion (That is not just her, it is department wide). She posts class slides. She is extremely understanding and accommodating. Sometimes when you ask for clarification, she just shows you the class slide again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Clear, organized, fast paced class. If you're serious about learning about Japanese, take her class. Cool to see how much my Japanese improved in less than a year!

Clear & Organized. She only talks in Japanese which is overwhelming at first, but perfect if you really want to immerse yourself in the Japanese language. Hashimoto sensei is really funny, cares about her students, and is willing to help if you put in the effort!I would say the only downside is the discussion section which is kind of pointless.

Hashimoto sensei talks only in Japanese during lectures but it's actually extremely helpful when you are seriously trying to learn the language. She is one of the most organized professors that I've ever had. There is a lot of work, but it's a language class so that's a given. The pace is fast, so make sure you keep up! Very helpful class for sure.

There are 2 quizzes every week and homework everyday so it's a lot of work. If you do the homework everyday you should be fine, as there are no surprises on the quizzes and tests. Hashimoto is very nice but does go fast so be prepared.

Professor Hashimoto is a very nice lady, but as a department head one would expect her to have more realistic expectations for a freshman-level language course. She teaches extremely fast, and the only truly successful students have prior experience. Expect very little English, and very direct answers to questions.

She teaches strictly from the slides and textbook. She is very monotone and tends to not fully explain things. It's very daunting to speak to her, and I felt very self-conscious about asking questions in class, but she's not the worst teacher I've ever had.

Hashimoto sensei is overall a good sensei. She is understanding if you have to miss class, but is strict on grading policy when it comes to attendance. She can be daunting and speak very quickly at first, but you get used to it quickly. She explains often and doesn't go above your Japanese knowledge if at all possible. Good teacher!
This class was extremely difficult. Not worth it. I'd say more if my comments didn't repeatedly get flagged for not meeting guidelines, but just trust me, this class is not worth the effort.

She's incapable of communication, and has unrealistic expectations for homework(one week has a 200 pages of academic literature to read). I am not through week one, and am already regretting taking this class. Lectures are usually unintelligible. Has circular arguments to support her claims.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were group projects; however, if one person did not do it, it did not reflect poorly on you. timed quizzes every two weeks, done by week10. Multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and two short answer questions (max 300) Everything is from the LECTURE in these quizzes. Some of the short answers will be from the readings.Class kinda hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests were unbearably hard and ruined my grade. Only a few assignments so if you don't do well on the project you won't get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IMO: It's not that Dr. Lee doesn't care, this just comes down to a language barrier, a lack of clear expectations, harsh grading and a TON of complex material to cover. The lecture reflections are very difficult, the lectures do contain the information, but it's very difficult to uncover. The other hw is okay. This class should be taught in person
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She doesn't care about her students whatsoever, grades on the most specific things, and the tests seem just to be trying to root out cheating. DO NOT TAKE!!! I am a Junior ANTH major and I think of myself as a good student, I have done all the work in the class on time and I still am barely passing. Worst prof ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As others have said, this has been an awful experience. The lectures, assignment instructions, and grading criteria are all unclear and you are graded harshly. The class average for exam 1 was a 67% so there is clearly something wrong. I will never take a class with her again. Please save your GPA and yourself a headache and pick another teacher.

Pretty much what everyone else is saying. I am a senior and I would say I am a really good student and I have never struggled with a class this much before. Her standards are incredibly unrealistic. No matter what I do it never seems to be enough for her. Do not take this class! Not worth your time and money.
If you're expecting perfect grades in this course don't take it. If you're a type A person maybe this is the class for you.

For some reason nothing I do in this class is good enough for Lee. I am notably a great writer and researcher, and I literally have never gotten below an A in a writing-based class and no matter what angle I approach my papers; Lee wants something different. The online class is a joke, the lectures don't matter and they're hard to understand.

This class was just an atrocious experience. You are graded vigorously and unfairly on 8 assignments across a 10 week span, not necessarily sure how you can judge a persons level of understanding on 8 assignments, but go figure. The professor and GEs are unresponsive when it comes to emails, and the quizzes are abysmal. Save yourself the time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never rated a professor, but it is necessary. This course has unclear assignments/grading criteria with minimal to no feedback. The GEs and professor grade harshly without cause. You can do 99% of the work correctly but lose 20% of your grade on a minor detail. Quizzes are specific and several answers are incorrect based on course lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All assignments except two lecture tests are based on your research paper, but receiving grades and feedback takes 2-3 weeks. You're doing research without having feedback until the last minute for each assignment. She is not great at responding to emails, and her lectures are too long and specific for the assignments. I do not recommend it at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. Very hard to understand especially when she wants you to memorize specific things said in her lecture videos for the quiz. No examples for any assignments which would be fine if they didn't pull out the most harsh grading criteria. Save your money, time, and mental health! Ruined my GPA and dean's list.
I never made a rate my professor before, but she made me. It's week 8 of school and there are 2 things in the grade book, Emailed her several times with no response back. Please do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As pretty much everyone else has said, don't take this prof if you can avoid it. She picks very specific random tidbits from the lectures for her weekly quizzes, and her lectures and hard to understand, so her quizzes are a joke. She made this class way harder than it needed to be and very little learning actually happens.

5 online tests where half the questions are fill in the blank sentences directly from her lectures. It does not matter if you watch the lectures, it does not matter if you do the readings odds are unless you have a time accommodation and a fantastic memory you are going to struggle hard for no reason. Disappointed and frustrated. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard to understand, subtitles don't match videos, I am disappointed that I payed to take this class, I have learned nothing and I would not take this professor ever again. I am a senior and the 2 online classes I'm taking with her rn are the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. There are many great anth teachers better than this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As others said, pretty hard to understand the teacher. The amount of reading assigned is ridiculous.Took a gamble on the second week and decided to not read, got a better grade on the quiz (A vs a C-) by just taking thorough notes on the lectures. Teacher wants you to just regurgitate the info given in lectures, so the reading is pointless.

Horrible! She does not want to teach you, she does not want you to learn. All of the lecture quizzes consist of highly specific questions where she wants you to regurgitate a singular sentence from the lecture back to here. The rubric for the final project is extremely vague, and she will grade it extremely harshly which is incredibly unfair.

As an ANTH major, this class was a total waste of money. I learned nothing because her lectures are difficult to understand and the quizzes expect you to remember random facts rather than understand the material. The syllabus and rubrics do not make sense, and the grading is extremely harsh. I recommend taking ANY other anthropology class.

Professor has had zero engagement or communication with the class the entire term.   The final project is graded unreasonably harsh with nothing but an unclear rubric to describe what she really wants. Lectures are completely unengaging, and as a non major I have taken nothing valuable from ten weeks in this course

Lectures are hard to understand, not about learning just remembering random information. The quiz to lecture information is sometimes different, she will miss the quote herself. The final project makes no sense, and the requirements are unclear! This is a frustrating class and I will never take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: for one, the powerpoints are an overload of information and trying to take notes is extremely difficult. Multiple people have asked her to post the slides before lecture so that we can follow along better and we were turned down. it is incredibly difficult to follow along which is unfortunate bc the tests are all written responces :(
Strict teacher who doesnt care about students well being, lectures go on and on and on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As a non-anthro major, I found this course to be challenging only in that I did not know some vocab. Dr. Lee made a great effort to help those of us who were non-majors out, for example, posting a list of terms to know for the class. Tests are easy if you show up to class, she gives you what will be on the test about a week before hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anth: 341 You are unable to understand her and she is unclear on what she wants, yet she still grades extremely hard on her 20 point tests.
This class is horrible, you are expected to know the difference between burnt seeds that look the same. waste of class time, multiple 20+ pg articles a week. dont do it

Hard to understand sometimes.  Basically left the students to teach themselves by having group presentations starting week three and going until the end of term. So NOT worth my money when she doesn't even teach the class.

Dr. Leonard is so passionate about this topic and is a great professor! She lets her GEs teach if they want to so if she isn't teaching much then that's why. Overall, if you show up and try your best then you'll be fine. She's also super accommodating if you communicate with her. I would 100% take a class from her again!!

Best class of fall. Clearly cares about the topic, but also about everyone who's there to talk about it. Gives GEs the chance to do some lectures, but usually picks up their small group discussions for the week, it's clear she wants to interact with the students any way she can. Her office hours are clearly posted and she usually brings food too!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, but her teaching is kind of bland. She also doesn't teach for half of the class and makes the GE do it, so you're kind of at the hands of the GE and if they're good at teaching.

Dr. Leonard obviously has a passion for what she teaches. I believe that this course is necessary for anyone pursuing an FHS career. However, I felt I learned more about diversity in FHS from my GE rather than the lecture. Some examples of racism and bias seemed a bit vague and I would've preferred if we went into more detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is my 3rd time taking a class with Prof. Leonard, and it is NOT by choice. First of all, she willingly chose to have a class at 8 am. She is not clear when giving projects at all. This whole class is a big, unnecessary review of FHS 213/215. She also lets her GEs lecture, and it's terrible, she just sits on her computer doing nothing.

I took her FHS215 class. It helped me figure out that I do NOT want to pursue FHS as my major. I probably would've enjoyed the class more if I was a FHS major. Only 3 big assignments that are essentially projects. Lots of guest speakers. Attendance was taken at the end of class and was required. Made it a point that she's there for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I have taken two classes now with Dr. Leonard. She is great! Her classes have easy grading, and she is excellent at facilitating discussion. I have learned a lot from her classes and definitely recommend her!

I have taken FHS 215 & FHS 328 with her! Also, her GEs were amazing!!

I chose this class somewhat arbitrarily to fill a requirement, & I couldn't have gotten luckier. Prof. Hessler is incredibly knowledgeable & kind; lectures are dense but engaging, & homework assignments were quite manageable. Readings are lengthy but often covered in class; if you pay attention, ask questions, and take good notes, you'll do well!

This is a really awesome informational course, but there is a lot of reading.  Don't get me wrong, you have to be down to read a lot if you're going to study History, but it teetered on unmanageable, especially when taking a full schedule. That being said, the professor is very enthusiastic and fun to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like this class, but the grading here just feels entirely arbitrary. Her rubric is supposed to have to only two aspects for consistency (argument and evidence), but in effect it feels more like it causes insanely random results with minimal feedback on exams. Meeting with her doesn't tend to be terribly helpful either.

Her soviet history class is excellent, but you only get out of it what you put in. She is more knowledgeable than anyone I've ever known on the topic, and has never been unable to answer a question of mine. She's also just a nice person and funny professor. Outside of class work can be a bit of a pain but not too difficult. Highly recommend!

Professor Hessler is a tough grader with no room for reason. She is very difficult to communicate with and can be very offputtting. Her lectures are ok. I wouldn't take this class if you aren't super into history. She is honestly one of the most difficult professors I've ever dealt with and she is not very kind or approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hessler made a very reading heavy class enjoyable. She is very humorous in her lectures and takes the time to answer questions insightfully. You write a lengthy research paper, have two in class exams, two reading reflections, and weekly mini quizzes, so if putting in the work is not for you do not take this class

She is so passionate and insightful about what she is teaching. There are a lot of assigned readings, but she goes over the entirety of the readings in class/discussions so you don't necessarily have to read all of them. You will get an A easily if you take notes and do the assignments. I loved the food history course, it was so interesting.

I really enjoyed Professor Hessler's HIST215 class. I found her lectures to be very interesting and I was excited to show up for class. The course is writing and reading heavy, with the only tests being timed-writes for the midterm and final. If you don't like writing, I'd consider a different class, as most of your grade will come from essays.

The class isn't that hard, there's just a lot of assignments that you need to do. The in-class essay midterm and final are annoying, but really not that bad. Weekly discussions are worth a lot of your grade and you really just need to show up. The lectures are boring, and you can get most of you information form the weekly canvas overviews
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved the enthusiasm of professor Julie Hessler. This professor definitely assigns heavy loads of weekly readings which was a lot to juggle (especially as a freshman). Her teaching style was very engaging from her obvious passion for culinary history and I admired her way of romanticizing topics and bringing her lectures to life with cheerfulness
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The general idea of this class is super interesting, and Professor Hessler seems okay. my problem was her grading system is really weird, like a 1200-word paper worth 8% of your grade?? And the questions for writing assignments are incredibly wordy and broad. There is also a LOT of reading for this class. don't take if your a freshman.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't take this course as a freshman!! The midterm and final are both in class hand-written essays, which is okay, but they are supposed to be extremely detailed and the midterm doesn't allow a notecard, and the final only allows 100 words on a note card for THREE essay prompts that must include information from the readings and the lectures.

Oh god there are so much readings. The lectures are great and echo off of the readings. The quizzes are reading heavy but also expects incorporation of lectures. Beyond the heavy reading load this was a very enjoyable class about Soviet society.

Professor Hessler is very kind and knowledgeable. Her lectures are long but extremely interesting if you listen! I didn't do all the readings, but did put a lot of effort into the essays. If you work hard and ask for help you can get an A, but get ready to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: while the content was mildly interesting, her delivery was very all over the place and honestly sometimes confusing. it was difficult to understand what was expected on written assessments since it was graded by different people every time and there was no clear rubric

Hessler is sweet and makes a clear effort to engage with students despite teaching a larger lecture. Readings are not necessary, but interesting in content! Grading is harsh as she doesn't "believe in perfection." Lectures never finished during the period. Writing-heavy course with back-to-back assignments and ~50 pages of reading per class

Professor Hessler is very sweet. She cares a lot about her students and tried to get to know everyone personally in our big lecture class. The material was slightly boring at times, but overall an interesting class. There's lots of reading/writing and most of it isn't that difficult. Attendance is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: While a nice enough Professor, it didn't seem like she was familiar with the course material and we got stuck using out of print textbooks with out of date information, and Professor Hessler even requested students google a spice in class because she forgot what it was. Also called the Torah the "Jewish Bible", which isn't great.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you really like history, this is the class for you. Hessler is extremely knowledgable and will answer any question you have about Russian history. However, if it's not your thing, don't expect to get any revelations about a new passion from this course. Lots of reading, meandering lectures, "quizzes" that are actually two essays.

I took my 407 seminar with Professor Hessler this term. The class was 3 hours long on a Friday afternoon and she still managed to make it an enjoyable class experience. Cares about her students. The reading was very heavy, around 200 pages a week. I was usually able to finish half& still did ok in the class. Knows a lot& gives rly helpful feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a nice lady and clearly very knowledgeable, but 'Food History' is not her strong suit. I'm a comp sci major so I'm not familiar with history classes, but I could tell that this class was abnormally chaotic. Assignments and grading criteria were extremely unclear, and lectures/readings rarely connected to the assigned essays/discussion posts.

Super nice lady and definitely passionate about her subjects but she tends to ramble A LOT and there is a lot of assigned reading. Also most of the readings and lectures in class had nothing to do with the assignments so a lot of the stuff we learned was irrelevant. Most of the assignments involve independent research outside of class.

So much reading. Multiple weeks will have over 100 pages of reading. Every assignment is worth 100 pts but is weighted differently. Final 3 essays? 100 points, worth 25 percent of your grade. Each of your 6 discussion group posts? Worth 100 points. All added up? 15 percent of your grade. Not recommended if you value having any free time/have a job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: super sweet and supportive, her course was definitely heavy in terms of knowledge but not work. lots of reading involved as well as viewing the lectures. lectures were easy to understand and take notes from. two essays due every two weeks on topics (counted as tests), just do the work and youll definitely pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took this class b/c I thought it seem interesting, and conceptually it is. The problem with the class and prof. Hessler, is that this is not her primary field and seemed to pick up the Food History class without much understanding regarding how a class like this works. Her expectations were EXTREMLY unclear and the majority of work seemed unneeded.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Though the course was occasionally interesting, most assignments were not thought out very well and were thus difficult to prepare. Even after turning in assignments, it was unclear whether or not expectations or criteria were met. Extremely frustrating to take this class as it was nearly impossible to understand what i needed to do for assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was really enjoyable. Prof. Hessler's lectures can be a little scattered and not all lecture material is useful for graded assignments, but she is lovely and if you have any interest in food, you'll like this class. The readings are important bc there are surprise short essays. Most people take this as a gen ed class so it's not v hard.
The midterm is horrible!! You have to prepare for 6 essay questions, even though you only end up having to write 2, and it's way too much information to cram into your head for one exam.
Exceptional professor. Passionate and knowledgable about her field of study. Lectures tended to be slow, but thorough. Approachable outside of class for help or clairifactions.

Some of the info in the lectures was useless on the tests and essays. She isn't that organized when it came to the lectures either. She wasn't clear with what she wanted exactly on the essays, and she is a terrible grader. Avoid
Very, Very Intelligent professor.  Worked to get the whole class involved in discussions.  Feedback was very helpful.
A great teacher, knows more about Russia than is probably healthy.  Lectures can be a little slow, but subject matter is great.  She's cute too
Thought she was one of the best since being here

Beth is by far the best professor that the Lundquist College of Business has to offer. You will end up learning more about business and how to succeed in her class than all other combined. Putting in the effort to read, participate in class, and completing the assignments to the best of your ability will be recognized and rewarded.

This class was EXTREMELY informational - exceeded my expectations. I learned so much more from field trips to various food businesses like coconut bliss than I ever would have learned in a textbook. She offered extra credit and helped us out through everything.. We had 2 intensive assignments and had great guest speakers come talk to us. Educating.

I was worried to take this course  as I heard she was difficult. She was. But this was by far the best class and my favorite professor at UO. She truly does care and wants her students to exceed. Don't take the easy way for your capstone and take Beth. You'll learn more in this class(if you put in your hours) then all your other BA classes combined

Beth is an amazing teacher. Sure, her class is hard, but it is sooooo worth it. I have learned so much from her. She knows so much about the business world and really wants you to succeed, but you have to work for it. I am so glad I had her as a teacher before I graduated.
Reinspired me as a business major. Incredibly caring women but also will make you work for your grade. Stop by office hours and get to know her.

The course is well-outlined and Beth is organized. Weekly readings, case studies, discussion boards, 3 quizzes, 2 exams. The book was SO boring with endless vocabulary but she doesn't test on most of it. Case studies are relevant and interesting. Be prepared to work hard and pace yourself. Hated the software for narrated lectures, good otherwise.

Absolutely insane about of work. Crystal clear teacher, tells you what is expected, but every class requires 2 or 3 hours of work just to walk into the class. If you want to work more than any of your friends and write a paper at least once a week, then this class is for you.

Lecture attendance is mandatory. Students are graded on a midterm, final exam, group project, group paper, and attendance/participation. She is very helpful but the class is not easy. She treats all her students with kindness and wants everyone to succeed. She is personable and knows all her students by name. Overall, a great teacher.
Beth is a great teacher. She is very hands on in lectures, dont try not talking, it won't work. If you put out effort and do the work its a very beneficial class, and she is very undertstanding.

Beth actually expects students to perform according to a certain level of standards. I know this concept frightens many students who are used to being coddled; however, I enjoy having a class which challenges me to learn.

Dr. Hinkle was very kind and easy to talk to. I highly recommend going to office hours, she's very open to helping you and gives good feedback. I would definitely take her classes again, especially in the honors college.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As an instructor, I liked her and thought she did a good job of explaining things. However, the grading system was unnecessarily harsh. 77% of our final grade was exams. Each midterm was 17% and the final was 26%. She will write on slides during class but refuses to post them so you're kind of screwed if you don't go to class.

I got a B+ in Gen Chem 1, I couldn't even pass this class, now I'm not a rocket scientist but I don't think that could entirely be my fault, the lack of support and guidance combined with the extremely heavy load  of lecture material was a recipe for disaster for a kid like me.
The test is not what you learn in class. MCQ questions on the exam are worth 4 % of your grade per piece. I don't know of anyone getting above a 73 after the first eam.

Exams are brutal. Actually criminal. 3 midterms and a final. The midterms are weighted heavily on short answer questions that are the hardest questions. The short answers also have multiple parts most of the time so if you don't understand the first part you're screwed for the whole problem. I've never gotten this bad of a grade on tests.

Very energetic and easy to follow during her lectures, and is one of the nicest professors I've had so far; answers her emails in detail and in a positive manner, is willing to meet outside of her given office hours, and wants you to succeed in her class.  3 midterms and the final, along with online end-of-week homework and quizzes.

HC101-Symmetry. Awesome, caring, funny professor. She has an amazing grading system that allows you to sit back and just enjoy the class and let the information wash over you--stress free! Absolutely an easy class, but you really will learn! If you're interested in chemistry and patterns, you'll enjoy the class! No tests. You'll like it. Trust me.

Prof. Hinkle is so amazing. She is clearly very smart and passionate about what she teaches which makes her class very enjoyable and engaging. She is funny, too. She is a tough grader, particularly with writing, but her feedback is specific and helpful so it is easy to improve over the term. Hers might be my favorite class I have ever taken at UO.
Prof. Hinkle is very organized and very smart. Her Pick Your Poison class was well structured and very interesting. Great class.

I absolutely loved Dr. Hinkle and the class (HC 241 PYP). She is brilliant, funny, and I've learned so much from her in and out of class. She is the toughest grader I think I've ever encountered, but she gives really good feedback. Once you understand her grading (after the first few assignments), it is easier to succeed in the class.

I took HC241: Pick Your Poison. She is a really nice person and I even find the class content interesting, but unfortunately she is the hardest grader I've ever encountered and it's usually the little things that she takes points off for. I found that my classmates had similar feelings as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Hinkle rocks. She is genius and hilarious which is rare. Beware of strict grading, but other than that, take from her! She's da GOAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Hinkle is very good at teaching. She's super organized and ensures that the content for each class is digestible.
