She explains things pretty well and I'm always able to retain information in her class no matter how much attention I'm paying. She's a little bit tough on the grading but her constructive feedback is helpful most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Each class she was handing out a rubric for an essay. They comprised our entire grade, apart from some participation points. Hinkle's grading is so harsh that no one in my class could get above a C. I would receive a bad grade every time no matter what preparation I did. There is no success in this class if the professor does not want to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hinkle provided a lot of helpful and relevant information about the CHC thesis and was very easy to communicate with. She was very willing to answer questions and help connect you to other faculty. This class made me feel a lot better about the actual thesis process and I am glad I took it from Dr. Hinkle, definitely recommend!

I took HC241 Pick Your Poison but that's not an option. Very nice person who cares about her students. The subject matter is difficult if you struggle in science subjects. Very tough grader on writing assignments, nobody gets 100%. Plenty of assignments so not a big deal if you tank one. Harder to get an A than other HC241 classes

I took HC241 from Hinkle, but RMP wouldn't let me select that. She grades SUPER harsh on written assignments, you HAVE to follow the rubric down to a T. However, she is ALWAYS willing to clarify and always responds to emails super quick. Pick Your Poison was so interesting, and Hinkle's classes are never boring. Love her and the class!
amazing person, very funny, made class entertaining, i looked forward to class every week. super well-organized class, incredibly helpful information.

I took HC441: Water from prof Hinkle and at first it seemed pretty easy but she is the harshest grader I have ever encountered even for the honors college. She docks tons of points for tiny pointless things and refuses to even discuss it after. I would never recommend taking a class from her.

Joel truly is a fantastic and intellegent professor. Each lecture was dense but fascinating, incorporating current policy & events into lecture. He encourages group participation & general student engagement - he's usually only talking half the time. BEWARE: the weekly quizes are very difficult, take good notes and pay attention and you'll be fine.

Joel is a funny, charismatic guy who is clearly incredibly passionate about what he does. That being said, he tends to drone on during his lectures. Most of the class is graded on group work (group essays and presentations) and there is no final, only a mock climate change convention game at the end. Interesting class on a very important topic!
Very funny professor, the only thing I didn't like about the class is that group work is a large portion of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joel is a intellegent professor & very passionate about what he discusses. His lectures can drag on a little bit but he breaks it up with group work and class presentations of readings (which aren't that bad). You HAVE TO DO THE READINGS though, as there's weekly quizzes worth 40%. No required attendence, but it's really in your best interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I hate statistics, so I struggled in this class. However, Dr. Hicks was an excellent professor and made the content enjoyable. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but you will not do well if you do not show up. This class has a lot of confusing content, and it all builds on each other, so showing up and doing the readings are crucial. Super chill prof.

I came into this class thinking the worst and it lived up to the expectations. The upside to this class was it was light on overall work compared to other profs, most of the lectures felt pointless and wastfull of our time and the assignment was rarely mentioned until right before it was due.
He does not stop talking. you will have no in class time to work. he is very demanding.

Being in Tim's class for architecture studio was a terrible experience as he assigned unnecessary work and expects insane deadlines that do not correlate with the rest of the architecture studios in the department. He makes an effort to discredit any positives in your designs and his teaching mindset is dated as he doesn't allow online work.

This was the first studio I'd ever taken and he was deeply uninspiring. barely made it through that term of studio. since then I've had amazing professors who affirmed my interests and I've done very well in studios, but Tim was so uninspiring that you could barely call my final a project.
Only wants work done in their style and doesn't really teach the class. Very nice individual but not a great class. Only take if necessary. Take with another professor.

They did not even grade the final project. They actually submitted final grades without grading or commenting on the final project. Assignments were based off whether you checked off all the boxes, not skill. No advice was given. My art never improved. This has been my least favorite class I have ever taken at the UO and was a waste of money.

this professor was not understanding or sympathetic of situations outside of class nor were they willing to help with software problems. lectures were rushed and spoke a lot about their own work. tons of time consuming assignments with unclear directions. didnt learn much in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kinda just yaps about who knows what, the only teacher i've had difficulty with in the art + tech program. More concerned about showing the class her work than actually teaching. If you are like me and have any sense of self respect and a passion for learning you should take this class with another teacher. I don't believe the 5.0 ratings are real.

Arrogant, self-centered, and incredibly boring to listen to. We were forced to look at their personal unrelated art projects and listen to them spew about how talented and hardworking they are. More interested in proving to us they are a good artist than actually teaching, restricts creativity and forces own interests/style into students/ work.

Prof Ali runs an engaging and fun class. Participation matters but if you show up and are present, you will be fine. They are a kind and genuine person do their best to cultivate an environment that encourages learning and discussion. If you put the time in, you will walk out with a more holistic understanding of the content and learn lots!

They read directly from their slides which were filled with text and had neon green as the background. There was barely any class participation or engagement. Just really boring and unnecessarily long lectures that taught me little. The prompts for the assignments were limiting and the turn around for work was very fast. Enjoyed the lab enough.

If you have the option to take this class with a different professor, do it. Prof Ali (as they like to be called), is extremely unorganized and tough grader. She expects deep concepts of art in photoshop, when it is supposed to be an introductory class. I've never gotten below a B in harder art classes and i'm struggling to keep a C+ in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was less about art and more about following instructions. You would lose points if you didn't follow instructions exactly. The work is mostly making collages - something I don't think refines skills in Photoshop. The work is monotonous and you never actually expand much beyond a certain point. A lot of busy work for little payoff.

Prof Ali is a kind person and creates a good classroom environment, but was by no means an inspiring or exciting professor for me. Considering that this is a 300-level digital art class it felt honestly demeaning at times to be looking at the art we looked at. If you are an art major, or looking to be at all challenged creatively, do not take this.
Class attendance is a most because it is important to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I loved this class!  Professor Ali is extremely knowledgeable, thoughtful and rigorous.  They taught me to think differently about concepts I thought I was familiar with through readings, lecture and creative assignments.  I felt challenged but also very supported.  Definitely take this class!

Participating in this course, about networks of surveillance & the tools to resist them, ranged from the conceptual (panopticon) to the practical (Unity and Blender). At the end, a group show & performance gave students a way to demonstrate their responses to the work in a multifaceted, communicative way. I will never forget this class! Legendary.

I had an amazing class with professor Hiba! Their class was on point with the right amount of technical AND critical theory complementing each other. The course material always invited me to think about the why and how. Always found myself being inspired every class. Will definitely take more classes in the future.

One of THE best art classes in the department. Learned everything I needed to know about digital imaging and the curriculum introduced me to the incredible work and processes of living artists. Professor has fantastic presence and a sense of humor!
Working with Professor Ali changed my life. Their attention to detail combined with nuanced instruction and boundary pushing examples of art has made me grow as an artist and as a person.

Hiba is a great person with great commentary, however they do not know how to teach a Digital Imaging class. The class is supposed to be a studio class but we rarely open Photoshop or any programs. Class is filled with busy work and does not follow course description whatsoever. Cannot recommend taking their class.

For an upper level art class they show honestly the most terrible artwork, a lot of bs stuff. Just because it's 3-D and online doesn't make it good. Super disconnected out of class. The only way I got an email back was after I had someone at the dean of students give them multiple messages. Awful to work with in a hard time.

She shows you youtube videos all day instead of teaching and has to google the answers to your questions. Will lie to your face. I pointed out an incorrect statistic and sent her the right ones assuming it was a typo and she said she was smarter than me because she had a PHD. Only good thing is that she grades easy.

Went by they/them pronouns which a lot of students did not respect. It's ok if you don't like the teacher, but that's no reason to not respect them as a person. I thought that the class was pretty ok as an introductory class for photoshop. As long as you follow the directions for projects and assignments you will pass easily.

Seems to have less of an understand about art than most of their students. Too politically correct to the point where she isn't understanding if that makes sense. Also expect a week for any email response. Good heart, bad teacher.

Class did not follow class description at all. Classes were long and wastes of time. Classes included meditation and 30 min breaks in the middle of class. The class focussed on videogames and conceptual art (IDK why) and she didn't seem to understand either.

Professor Hinde works with students to ensure the succeed. He is plugged in to many organizations in Eugene and can help students get connected with the right people. He always holds a super study session (google doc included) before all major exams. He is also vegan and super hilarious.

Professor Hinde spent time getting to know each student individually. He gave tests in alternate formats for those who needed additional help. He works to be inclusive and values different opinions. You will learn a lot from him but he will also make you work.

Prof Hinde was by far one of the best graduate teaching assistants I have had at the U of O. He is kind and cares about his students. He will go the extra mile for any student in need. He is extremely knowledgeable and kinda cute too.

Math used to be my favorite class in high school, then in college I met this guy. Messy, unorganised, terrible overall. He makes things harder than they should be, and its pretty obvious that he doesn't care about any of the material he is teaching. 70 thousand dollars to attend an Ivy League college, and I get stuck with this baboon.

Do NOT take classes from him if you aren't good at math! This class was supposed to be for people that aren't amazing at math and yet he STILL managed to make it impossible to learn. Please, other math-haters... Save yourselves.

The homework is harder than what's in the lecture, and the tests are harder than the homework. Hilburn is an okay guy, but he'll say things like "this is easy" when it isn't, and he'll repeatedly ask the non-responsive class "does this make sense". I found it very difficult to learn the material while he used these kinds of phrases.
He's a nice guy, but his tests are way harder than the study guides. He moves really fast in class, and his catchphrase is "Does this make sense"
he is a horrible teacher. I didn't learn anything in his class
A good professor to choose for math course. Clear explanation for the contents in the textbook. And the best part is you can get half points you lost in tests back by correcting them after tests.
Terrible at teaching math. You will have to learn using just your textbook. Very easy tests however as his study guides are the tests basically. Gives credit for correcting answers as well
Horrible at teaching math. He has been corrected by the class many times. Not helpful at all.

I love Math when I am able to grasp the concepts and work out on my own. With teacher Martine Hiserote, I was unable to understand the way he taught if you called it teaching at all. He lacks the fundamentals of teaching. I would describe his teaching by talking directly to a chalkboard just talking through problems you've never seen before.
He used to write clear notes on whiteboard and usually give lots of examples to help you understand. When you have some questions, he will slow down and explain them step by step.
Martin is an awful teacher. Very hard to follow. Shows very little care for how his student do in the class. If you need to take math 111, do not register to take it with hiserote.

His teaching depends is helpful if you learn the way he teaches. He teaches by word problem examples.He uses a lot of examples and those exact same examples are typically what the test are about. All the homework was on webwork and not what the test are about. He doesnt hold your hand, but if you understand things fast through examples you're fine.

Martin is pretty difficult to follow if you don't have any college algebra background. His lectures are usually difficult to follow not because of the material but because he  mumbles most of the time and writes so small. Be prepared to be in his office hours at least once a week.  His tests are also more times than not completely irrelivant to HW.

This class was very easy if you attend every single class session. If you miss one in-class activity, your grade will drop. It's heavy lecture in the beginning, but it isn't bad at all. After, it's just group projects. She also has a grace period on almost every single homework/project assignment. I recommend if you want to take an easier class.

Class was discussion based and the professor really encouraged everyone to participate in discussions. Attendance not mandatory but very important. Complete/Incomplete grading. There were a lot of weekly readings but most of them were fairly short and they were all very interesting. No tests, final project was a research poster.

Prioritizes hands on learning which keeps classes dynamic and interesting. Lots of opportunities to meet and work with peers but low stakes in terms of grades. She also engages in behaviors that are textbook white fragility and in several instances made me uncomfortable as I felt she was missing some important nuance regarding race and racism.

She understands accommodations and wants all students to enjoy the class. The first few weeks are lecture heavy and then group project heavy after. Final was open-book application of research methods. She has due dates but a grace period of a week for most assignments. I suggest looking at model reports before turning anything in.Textbook was free.

didn't like this class at all. Wrote the longest papers in my life, put so much effort and immense amount of time into this class just to receive a B- on the verge of a C, not what I deserved. GE was harsh grader and so was the professor who wasn't understanding of accommodations at all. Don't take it if its not needed and if it is, good luck.
Jocelyn Hollander is a gem, her lectures are informative and enjoyable. A solid portion of this class is group projects, but the class felt like an escape.

Professor Hollander puts a lot of effort into her class to make it enjoyable and engaging for students. Attendance is not mandatory, and there are 2 weekly papers. No big tests or big assignments. She responds to emails fast and cares about her work. I would love to take a class with her again!

Also: get ready to read, lots of homework, and skip class? you wont pass. Hollander is a thoughtful professor, which is evident in every detail of her class design. Lots of assigned reading, and Key Points for every class (homework).

She's 10000% willing to work with you and values individuals' opinions. The readings are free and assigned with stable frequency, nothing huge or impossible to get through. Gotta show up though to get full credit
I hated her feminist ways. If you like that then this class is for you but if not then do not take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hollander is a very warm, nice, and down-to-earth prof; I very much like her as a person. But this class was wayy too easy. You basically only need a third grade education to understand this class. That being said, if you want a (very) easy A, take her class. If you actually want to learn important/challenging, avoid her class.
Her class made me want to take other SOC classes. Very knowledgeable, interesting class, used slides, tests were straightforward.
She is a great professor. She is very approachable and enjoys chairing stories of her small child while applying it to the material. I have taked two of her classes and will take many more!!!

She uses good examples and makes the theories easy to understand.  We didn't have a text book, but she posted articles online.  The tests were easy to understand.  She tried some group activities to help us remember the information.  I've taken two classes with her and I would take another.
i loved her!

Extremely easy tests and essays. I misread one of the essay prompts and wrote about something else and still got an A. If you half read and go to half of the lectures you can pass easily. The section was pretty much worthless except to turn in the papers. Easy, easy class; it's a good gpa booster.

She wasn't the greatest. I was interested in the class until it started. Her tests are trick questions.If you dont goto class you will fail, even though theres no attendance. She is boring, and the class is overall a joke and I didnt learnanything. I wouldnt recommend it at all, however it was relatively easy. You DO have to read the book to pass

Horrible teacher. Honestly has no idea on how to make lectures appealing and meaningful. She was worthless in keeping class organized and knowing what she was talking about. If her GTF's weren't so good I would of been completely lost in this class. Avoid her at all costs because her exams are ridiculous and have no relation to anything she covers.

She managed to clearly convey the principles of Sociology in a class of over 300 students, which is no easy task!  Her lectures were very interesting, and she mixed things up with videos and guest lecturers.  Assignments were fair, even if they were a bit dry, and the tests were very well written and covered the pertenent material.

loved her class, probably my favorite spanish professor so far. Kelly is super composed, supportive, and approachable, making you feel very welcomed. her feedback is also very helpful. would definitely take a class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is super nice, and the class is super structured.  She always leaves feedback and gives your support.  I recommend her classes.

Take this class is you have an extra 10 hours to burn/w. The assignments are long and low-effort on the part of the teacher, but time consuming for the student (3 hours per). Despite easy grading, the tareas are mentally tasking. Most are just Word docs pasted into canvas. This class could be interesting with some attention and revamping from Prof.

This was the first 399 class taught, so I can give some leeway for that. However, the project at the end of the term was SUPER vague. Even when asking specific questions about the content it seemed she didn't really have a clear criteria for it. Not much speaking, just a lot of reading and if you've taken 308 there were a lot of repeated topics.

Profe Kelley is super kind, approachable, & accommodating. She has a great grasp of Spanish and is a patient and easily-understandable teacher. The course itself heavily utilizes the online textbook for daily homework. There are weekly tests but they never felt unmanageable. Highly recommend taking this class with Profe Kelley!

The class itself is by far one of the most interesting Spanish classes I've taken. Prof. is passionate about the topic and is well-versed in it. There is a lot of reading and writing involved in homework: it took up the most time out of any of my classes. She initially seemed like a very hard grader but seemed to ease up as the term went on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a really great teacher and her class is super interesting. Just be aware it is a lot of writing and reading in Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lots of homework for this class and tests are pretty hard so get ready to write. However, the content was really interesting and she was super engaged and passionate about everything. Does a great job applying it to real life.

I thought that Kelley was a great professor. She kept the students engaged and seemed interested in our lives as well. She tried different ways to improve our learning and genuinely wanted us to succeed. Very nice too!
Lots of homework.. almost as much as my other classes combined, but the course content was good and I learned a lot.

Kelley is a wise, however her support for students is lacking. She is condescending, spiteful, unapproachable, dull and intimidating. She is not excited to teach, therefore her students aren?t excited to learn. Makes students feel stupid, inferior, belittles them, is rude and grades hard. Spanish should be fun, with her it isn?t. She rarely smiles.

Good luck trying to keep up with her all her exams,quizes, oral presentations, in and out of class assignments, video sessions, etc...This class will consume all of your time and on top of all of that she is very strict with the grade book and don't even think of trying to turn something in late. If Spanish is your life and major you'll love it!
She is a great Prof. and you will learn a lot, but she is a very tough when it comes to grading and she's not afraid to pile on the homework week after week.
Very tough.
She's actually pretty good at teaching! I don't know if I like her as a person but she's aight. Homework load is moderate and quizzes are not so bad! No curve balls!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Often times I wondered what was going on... in her head. This class really made me question the validity of math departments, holistically. I couldn't understand what she said but the book was crystal clear. Halfway through the course I thought maybe some of the front row kids should be teaching the class. In spite all of this, I do recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Berri is a nice lady. She does have an accent but her English is pretty good. She holds office hours everyday and she will change work to make it easier if kids are struggling. She curved a quiz and allowed a note card on the mid term. I enjoyed taking her class.

I love Berri! The best math instructor that I have ever had at UO. It's a shame she teaches at Lane now instead. She explains things in a manner that makes it easier for the students to grasp the concept. I highly recommend her for any math class but be prepared to be studious! She will expect that but she is very supportive and helpful as well.

Very condescending and rude.  Would one day tell me I was one of her stronger students, and the next, when I was struggling, tell me I didn't read the text book (I read every chapter, thank you).  Would not count work in syllabus towards the final grade.  Even forgot to post completed assignment points but refused to fix it! Students beware!
She is a great teacher, she really likes students to be confused and ask questions about their confusion in class. One of the better professors I have had.
A good teacher that is easy to understand but is a little intimidating when it comes to visiting her in office hours.
Awesome teacher
A great teacher.  She is really approachable and helpful, but she does make you work, even if you don't want to.  Be prepared to work, but if you do, she will support you.
A waste of my tuition
Best math teacher ever!
she keeps a pattern at every class so its easy to not get confused even if you miss a class, plus she is flexible and easy to talk to.

Berri is a great teacher. She is very friendly, and very helpful. She loves to have students come to her office hours, and gives candy as an incentive!! Her teaching methods are clear and concise. I took more than one math class from her, and I did wonderful in both of them and enjoyed going to class...and I hate math!!

Incredibly poor professor. His lectures were nearly incomprehensible, he was rude to students, and he was not convincing that he actually knew what he was doing. It was a challenge to go to class and I began dreading it. Tests were much harder than homework. I would not recommend this professor to anyone.

This guy is just terrible.The information he covers in class has nothing to do with the homework, or the data covered in the lecture is an overly simplified version of the elaborate text. 100/200 of his students fail his quizzes and yet he refuses to review for the information covered by the quizzes.
Rude to students. Cracks a lot of jokes...some of them are funny...sometimes.
Really good teacher. Really easy if you go to class

This course has a strong structure in his lectures, he lacks organization skills for his assignments. His grading for the group projects are unclear and is difficult to understand what he wants you to change for a better grade. He seems to have a clear preference for what he wants his students to write and can feel like he isn't evaluating fairly.

Patrick is an incredible professor, I have taken 2 classes with him and he has consistently been engaging, professional, and caring. He genuinely wants to support his students and really makes an effort to get to know names and is super understanding. His intelligence and knowledge in his field really come through in his lessons.

Dr. Hunnicutt is fantastic! A significant portion of your grade comes from a group project, so if that's not your thing you won't enjoy the second half of this class. However, his lectures were great and he's a fair grader as well. Also, definitely take advantage of his office hours, he's super helpful. Learned a lot and had a great time!!

Professor Hunnicutt has been one of my favorite professors at U of O so far. The structure of this class was so organized and clear, all of the expectations of the course were clearly stated and very easy to find. Patrick is also just a very engaged, smart professor who puts a lot of effort into his teaching. Highly reccommend

Patrick is incredibly caring, thorough, and intentional with all his lectures. Attendance is mandatory, but all content is engaging, complete with small-group and whole-class discussions, and is highly applicable to real-world events. Weekly reflections and "practicums" as well as a group paper/project at the end of the term.

Prof. Hunnicutt is the best professor I have had at UO so far. His class feels applicable and grounded. Prof. is clearly passionate and experienced in his field and wants to inspire his students to feel that and get interested. He is willing to talk outside of class about career opportunities, research, etc. I would 100% recommend.

Patrick is very intellegent and truly engaging in lectures, if you talk he will learn your name. - his grading can be tough but it's constructive & fair. The midterm is much harder than anticipated, he'll say it'll take 2 hours, expect closer to 6. Very articulate lectures though, would 100% take his classes again.

Professor Hunnicutt is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is engaging, passionate, and makes clear connections between the class and the real world. The class is structured clearly, and he communicates extremely well. I would recommend taking any class taught by Professor Hunnicutt.

Hunnicutt is an amazing professor. Coming into this class not from the major, I did not know what to expect, but he made all the material easy to understand. One large midterm and a big group paper are the only two large projects, but both are framed well so that if you're on top of work, neither should be an issue.

Professor Hunnicutt is amazing! One of the best professors at this University. He is talented at explaining complex concepts, while never talking down to his students. His projects are interesting and left me wanting to learn more about the topics as opposed to being academically burnt out. All assignments were useful for future PPPM careers too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is excellent and knows the content. I wish I could take more of her classes.

The course sequence was not enjoyable at all. Although the instructor is knowledgeable, the classroom atmosphere often feels unwelcoming and tense. Questions seemed discouraged, policies felt overly strict, and interactions could feel dismissive, which made engagement difficult and reduced overall support for students.
She really cares and took time out of class to work with me when I needed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: We did so many things in class that had nothing to do with our grade or the class. I found her to be a very disorganized professor. She often looks down on us, does not respect our questions, and thinks it is her way or the highway I would not recommand taking her unless you have to to graudate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is brilliant in her field and one of the most kind and caring professors I've had. I had a really rough term and she was kind and empathetic and understanding. I also have gotten so much from her courses.
She is supportive and the class is easy, just beware it is the most boring class EVER.

Jenefer Husman is a lovely professor. Cares about the content and walks around the class, doesn't just read off slides. One negative is the organization of the lectures -- sometimes we come to class and lecture doesn't seem to connect to our readings and goes a bit all over the place. Overall, very caring and fun professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Is not a clear or concise professor. Fostered a negative learning environment, and looked down upon students when they asked questions. If you can avoid taking one of her classes, do it ALL costs.
She knew it was a hard year and was supportive.

I found this class to be easy but also pretty boring and this is coming from an education major themselves. The homework was a bit tedious and repetitive and I found having to go to class pointless because we learned everything for the week through the homework and readings but attendance was mandatory. I would take it again if I needed to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wow what a turnaround. Had her last term for EDST 332 and the whole class really struggled, this term you can really tell she's been listening to feedback and has really transformed her teaching and targeted it to help her students best (during this COVID-19 crisis). Awesome.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Math 251 (Calc 1) Actually a HORRIBLE Professor! Lectures were random and more difficult compared to other calc professors at UO. Disorganized and doesn't give helpful feedback. Stay Away.

Math 251 (calc 1): Very disorganized. Lectures, quizzes and homeworks feel unrelated. Bad lectures and doesn't post lecture notes. Low averages on tests/quizzes with no curves. Tests are worth like 70% of grade but are written poorly, and he tells us he writes them the night before. Definetly thinks hes the chill prof but everyone hates him.

Andy needs to get his act together if he wants to pursue teaching. Bad lectures, bad at teaching, the averages on tests were 60%, probably lower. Rambles a lot and says useless information or will not be articulate or say enough about a concept. I don't know how he is allowed to be a teacher.

I took Andy's Calculus 251 class. He is a nice guy and incredibly smart, understanding stuff, conceptionally. However, he should be nowhere near a class teaching. The lectures were highly disorganized and didn't align with the material inside and outside of class, but the tests were way too hard and did not align with the coursework. DON'T TAKE!
andy, maybe take a break from your bad art and focus on your job as a GE. you do not know how to lecture.

Stay far away. Had to drop this class or else I would have failed. I don't know how anyone passed this man is incapable of explaining concepts and unreachable if you ask for extra help. Very disorganized and doesn't seem to even understand what he's teaching.
He seems super checked out and is unable to actually explain concepts well. Test averages are consistently below 60%. Not sure how anyone is passing this class.
He’s a nice guy, just very obviously does not know how to teach. It was nearly impossible to actually be able to absorb anything in his lectures.

Complete lack of consistency in grading. Brings up completely irrelevant and sensitive topics in a way that truly detracts from the experience. It felt like just a class of her interests not disaster relief or our interests. It was often an awkward experience and I do not recommend this class at all. She was kind, though
This class was just a mess I would highly recommend you avoid. The assignment and grading criteria are extremely unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Word of warning to anyone who has Haisu as a GE, SHE IS HORRIBLE. She will blab on and on about unrelated topics and grade you unfairly. I will be sure to avoid her like the PLAUGE in my coming years. The makeup for discussion sections is absurdly difficult. She's a joke and I am glad I never have to have a class with her again.

The lectures for this class were so boring and hard to sit through. Oftentimes, they barely made sense, were hard to grasp, and if you tried to take notes with the slides outside of class, they didn't make sense. Assignments and quizzes were pretty easy, but the final exam almost took me out. Studying for that was like being at war with 0 resources

Where do I even start? The structure of this class was unfortunate. It's 10 relatively easy open canvas quizzes, light participation, and then BAM prepare to be sledge hammered by a cumulative final worth 25% of the grade. He probably doesn't try to confuse you deliberately, but he certainly succeeds. What's on the final? Who knows. He is an enigma
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks SO FAST. Would be better if lectures were recorded/he kept more info on slides. Reviewing for the final without being able to review exactly what he said was rough. Weekly quizzes weren't bad, 1hr/each with open note. Just wish more info was available for review.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He talks SO FAST, it was impossible for me to keep up. I think the content would stick better if he slowed down and gave students a chance to process what he said before moving on. His slides have no info, so you have to hear it or you miss details. Attendance is taken via iClicker app, but you can do it from anywhere.
Great guy. Made hard things make sense.

I really enjoyed Ben's online cognition class. We only had ten quizzes (one per week), and a cumulative final at the end. All lectures were recorded, and he held class to answer questions (attendance was not required). Quizzes were timed but open note, so notes during lectures are important. He was funny, nice, and always answered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm still currently taking this class, but so far the only thing we have been graded on are weekly quizzes. Anything but 10/10 on the quizzes can heavily dent your overall grade. I don't personally like it all being weighted on one thing. I do like this professor though because the classes are asynchronous, light workload, and his lectures are good
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cha is super cool and his lectures are easy to follow. One midterm that was open note but in person and a final that was in person with a cheat sheet. He's a great guy and he cares for his students and their learning. There's two big group projects and there's a lot of in class group assignments so make sure you sit with reliable people.

Seriously one of the best classes I've taken at UO. Hyeonjin Cha is so funny and charismatic but such a great professor too. His teaching style is very engaging and interesting which is hard to come by for the BA courses. I was sad when the quarter ended, if you need BA 316 take his class!!

Finding this class is like you just found a hidden treasure map - "X" marks the spot and it's a "for credit" course with an INCREDIBLE teacher. A few group projects (that are very easy to manage) should not steer anyone away from such a fun class. Professor Cha is the best you will find at the U of O and cares about his student's success.

Professor Cha makes this course so enjoyable. His X-factor is that he is funny (from a human sense not just as a teacher) and it makes the period fly by. He is probably the most caring teacher I've ever had. A perfect way to earn the necessary credits in the business school, I can't recommend him enough.

Professor Cha was actually easily the best professor I have ever had. Dude dressed up in an inflatable dinosaur on Halloween! Super understanding and engaging and made me never want to miss class. The most funny and engaging teacher you could prob find at UO. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Professor Cha has been the best teacher I'e had at the UO since high school - I haven't had any classes were I've been excited to go because of the teacher. Professor Cha is extremely caring and wants his students to be successful! His lectures are also very entertaining and helpful. I will definitely be missing him throughout my time at Oregon:(
His test are a little difficult, but easily the best professor I've had. Super understanding and also very entertaining.
Hyeonjin is a beast. I love this guy. Legend in the Oregon community.
A pure class act, always cracking great jokes. Highly recommend taking this class to anyone.

Overall really good teacher. He tries to make the class interesting with unique examples relating to what we're learning and doesn't require you to buy a textbook which is nice. My only complaint is that his tests are very difficult but he does give out a lot of extra credit to make up for it.
Hyeonjin is a great professor. I would absolutely take his class again. Thanks for a great term.

2nd class with Hynes and wish I could take more from her. Engaging, positive, funny and really knows her stuff. Has a way of taking the most mundane information and making it interesting. Flexible on assignments but also strict and clear with deadlines. Gives detailed, personal feedback - rare!  Awesome prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm taking the SAPP 408 Problem Gambling course through Julie right now, and it's a really awesome course! Definitely one of the best in the SAPP program and really interesting! I attended a Gambler's Anonymous for one of the assignments to write about it, and it was a really eye-opening experience! As a psychology major, I'm glad I took this class

I really enjoyed this course and wish I could  take of her more classes. Hynes was extremely proficient with the online format, very good at organizing content and communicating requirements, and great at giving feedback. You could also tell that she genuinely cared about the topic and the students in her class.

Julie is engaging, energetic and FUNNY. She is obviously experienced in the class topic (administration), which I didn't care about as a career path before, but because of her class I'm getting ready to graduate and actually interested in it. Julie obviously cared about us and treated us like professionals. Inspiring, GREAT teacher.
Julie was so kind and wanted the best for and from her students. She truly believed that we would change the world

I really liked Julie's style. Her slides were interesting and recent and made me think, which made sections go by very quickly. I liked the way she gave the "menu" of assignments so we could choose the ones that were practical for us, and she was quick to respond and grade. Great class!
Directions and requirements were very clear. Class was very easy to complete and the time given was acceptable.

GREAT class! I enjoyed the course very much because the material was presented in a fun way through power points and there was a lot of interactive material, like video clips, links. She was always available for questions and very personable. I think cutting down on the writing assignments slightly might make the class a little more easy going.

She was very personable and passionate about the topic and made it easier to understand.  I liked that it was connected with Oregon a lot so it was more personal. The instructions and expectations were very clear.

I don't usually rate things but have to rate this class because it was awesome. Online classes are usually boring and they are all over the map but the material was engaging and recent and very organized. Julie was very friendly and had super clear instructions. I wish I could take more online classes from her.

Best online class and best SAPP class I've ever taken.  She keeps the sections current and uses humor (hates the huskies) and has flexible assignments, all very organized and clear. I came in not caring about problem gambling but LOVED this class.

Really great professor! Made all of the course materials available online in an organized manner. She managed to make the class interesting and engaging without ever having met her. I would definitely take a class from her again!
fun class
Best SAPP class i've ever taken. Really nice and responsive.
Very helpful and personable. Shows passion about what she does and throws in current events. Pretty easy class by showing up, exams mostly on lecture slides.

Koo is the best teacher I have ever had in my college career. I am sad that I will no longer be having a class with her after this term, but I know that if I ever need a reference, or ever need any help with Korean, she would be glad to help me. SHe is a great teacher who takes a great deal of time and interest in teacher her students.

Koo Sung Seng Nim is awesome hands down one of the best, personable instructors at the Univ. of Oregon. The only con is that the amount of hw, b/c its a language class, is quite a bit. Lets just put it this way you will never be bored if you are "planning" on trying to get an A- or a B for that matter lol.

She has been by far my favorite professor so far. I struggled because I was one of the only kids in the class who didn't grow up with a korean background or any knowledge of Korean language, but she was willing to take her time to help me. Few professors or instructors will do this. Definitely recommend KRN 101 with her. I can't wait for 102!

Koo Sung Seng Nim is awesome highly recommend taking a course with her. If you show a willingness to learn she will help you to succeed, however being a language course there is a lot of tedious material.
Dr.E was the best prof I ever had. The capstone was rather easy due to his availability and feedback. I was inspired by his lectures and the video feedback was a plus. He has a great sense of humor.

Dr. Edwards gives clear and constructive feedback in a very accessible manner. He makes himself available for any and all questions, and he really cares about his students. I am so grateful that he was the Professor for my capstone. I would not have succeeded in this class without his feedback and guidance. Love the video feedback!

I had Dr. E as a professor of my Anthropology capstone course. He was easily accessible and constantly let us know he was available for extra help, and a resource for our research or just gaining guidance for the profession. He is a relatively quick grader and provides helpful and encouraging feedback. He is a solid choice for a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Ian is one funny dude. He was always helpful in his office hours. His little side stories was interesting and made the class flow smoother. Quizzes and tests are easy if you listen to his hints. He will say "Remember this" or "Burn this into your brain" those are code for "this will be on the quiz for sure".  I learnt a lot.

Mr.Edwards is an awesome professor! I really enjoyed this class. All these comments about him talking about his trip to Mali..so what? It has to do a lot with the lecture and I found it pretty interesting.

Anth 161 is a glorified discussion of Ian's travels in Mali. He loves Mali and always talks about it which pisses me off sometimes. Online midterms/exams. Really easy class. Discussion attendance is mandatory. I would recommend reading the Mango Rains book cuz there's no summary online and you eventually have to write a paper on it.

horrible lecturerer, uses lots of distracting body language and speaks way too fast. the class is world cultures but he uses the class to talk about his time in the peace corps and his trip to Mali to do his Phd. throws tantrums when people dont read for class. loves to boast of his achievements rather than teach. could be more efficient.

Professor Edwards, is an awful lecturer. He's one of those professors that loves to attempt to engage a class. Even if the class is giant. Honestly, recognize what class you're teaching. You're not going to get a discussion going in a 300 person class. He has had multiple rage fits and ended class early because he couldn't get a discussion going.

The class was very interesting, and he was an engaging teacher. He really helps you understand the material with clear examples from his travels and videos or case studies. He makes it possible for everyone to succeed and do well.

Very interesting and involved professor. Knows and loves his work. Uses stories of his own work and time in Mali to help reinforce concepts in the class. He makes himself very available for helping students understand the material. He tries hard to make sure everyone does well. Amazing to take a class with.
social instructor that has a profound interest in helping students understand course material.

Ian is a cool guy with lots of great stories about his time in Mali. I loved his class and it was one of the best classes I've taken. He's young and caring. He wants what's best for his students and he shows that through his teaching. He really wants everyone to learn.
Ian is the best professor I've had so far at Oregon. He is really smart, really nice and the class is really laid back and interesting at the same time. An AWESOME guy. Highly recommend him.
Nice, interesting, clear and open to class input

(Env. Anthro) Great teacher, and great class. Very interesting (even at 8:30 in the morning). We have quizzes and a take-home final, but this class is largely based on actually learning more so than test knowledge. Such a cool and straight forward guy, I would recommend any class with him

Best teacher I've ever taken. I cannot believe that he doesn't have more reviews than this. He is incredibly knowledgeable and is a teacher that you can relate with. Many professors are sometimes intimidating, but he's a very approachable guy with many stories about his work in Mali. This guy is young, but is by far the best I've ever had.

Henderson is a nice person but her teaching isn't great. The only reason I understood material was because the math in the class is relatively easy. The absolute WORST course I have taken in my entire life. Does not teach her lessons and lectures only consist of typed word problems with her solving for the answer. She doesn't teach. Just uses older material, aleks and desmos. Not like the class is anything crazy but it does not provide really any value.

Although I agree that the homework is ridiculous when compared to what we learn, I did not think this class was all that bad. I really appreciated the professor. This has to be the worst class I have taken throughout my ENTIRE LIFE. I didn't learn anything at all. The material didn't make sense and the GE's are complete jokes. You will have to use Webwork and it will make you want to drop out of college. I DO NOT RECOMMEND this teacher at all!

Her classes usually consist of her doing long example word problems and her teaching with a stream of consciousness style. This teacher refused to offer any help to several students that reached out about the overwhelming and unrealistic work load/homework. i DO NOT recommend this teacher
wouldn't recommend. she teaches by solving equations without giving written or verbal step by step explanations so you're both lost and cant keep up with her lectures.

reviews.comment: Personally, I would of given this professor a 1/5 because of how irrelevant the videos were to the homework and the time it took to do the ALEKS. Although being one of the worst classes I have taken at the University of Oregon I decided to give Henderson a 5/5 as I had a 67% in the class but she gave me a C- anyway. I love you Kristen Henderson.

As the other reviews have mentioned, she uses ALEKS for homework. It is VERY time-consuming. Luckily it is only 20% of the grade...but the class average for ALEKS material is 50% yet she continues to use it. As far as tests go, make sure you complete the practice ones. They are very similar to the real tests.

Uses ALEKS for hw- I spent 12+ hours on homework each week, as well as a weekly written hw assignment. Also hours of video lectures. We couldn't use our graphing calculators on tests but had to use them to complete the hw so I never truly learned how to solve without a calculator and therefore did bad on the tests. Would not recommend!!!!!!!

I took a hybrid version of this class and I wish I didn't. We needed to watch videos that were made by her that were three years old, we used ALEKS which did not line up with the videos we were watching every week, and our weekly assignments seemed to have even less to do with the things we had learned. She made little effort to teach our class.
She likes microaggressions
Horrible

I don't understand the bad reviews I haven't taken a math class in 4 years and with her teaching and explanations I'm able to understand concepts so easily. This class, math 101 was extremely easy even with concepts never learned before because she's a great teacher. The only thing is she always asks for everyone to group up.

She was actually a pretty good professor, I thought she explained the topics well in lectures. It is not hard at all to get an A in Math 111 as long as you keep up with the concepts, and if you don't get something she's helpful during office hours. I did also have a great GE so that helped.

reviews.comment: Prof. Henderson was THE best math profs I've ever had. She was super clear and gave great explanations & examples. If ur taking math 105, I highly recommend her. She was just about the worst professor/teacher I have ever had. honestly not bad. there was a lotttt of midterms but the content always matched the homework and study guides. homework was time consuming but helpful for tests. zoom is available for every lecture which is really nice and they are recorded in case you miss something. overall would take this class again.

Professor Henderson was not a good math teacher. The lectures, which consist solely of easy problems as examples, are nothing like the homework packets, the online homework, or the midterms. Just to give you a sense of Henderson's teaching style, it is currently week 10 and she has two WebWork assignments due tonight (the assignments that are unrelated to lectures), a homework packet due tomorrow, a THIRD MIDTERM on Friday, and next Friday is our final exam. All of this because she could not teach us what she needed to in time.

Ms Henderson consistently was struggling to coherently teach concepts and the class was also very un involved. She does not seem like a natural teacher or natural people person, and is probably just a natural math fanatic. This does not translate to being a good teacher, I recommend no one to take this class and if you have to find a different prof

Do Not take Math111 if she is your professor. Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Never was on the same page with TAs and often cancelled class. Midterms would look nothing like the homework/quizzes

I would rather die than take a class taught by this woman ever again. She is extremely disorganized, spends over an hour teaching us nothing and has to push back homework so that two assignments are due in one day because she cant teach. Teaches the most simple things in the most difficult way and the homework is 500x harder than examples in class.

Would teach very basic concepts in lectures but assigns homework that is absurdly more complicated. Have to reteach myself everything because she is so awful at teaching what you need to know in order to do the work.
Took this class as a requirement but seriously considered switching to pass fail because of how bad she is at teaching.
she is confusing, home work is hell

I would 100% give this teacher a 0. She assigns homework and only on the day before it is due does she teach what's on it. Just not helpful at all
Do not take this professor. She was not clear in lectures, didn't really care about how students were doing, and gave quizzes on topics we hadn't covered. Super unorganized class. DO NOT TAKE HER

She's not willing to help her students succeed in class. She also confuses herself with her own teaching.

Her voice is extremely annoying and the classes are not enjoyable. Professor Henderson is far better than her score here makes her seem. She clearly explained each topic, answered all questions, and was always engaging to listen to. reviews.comment: Professor Idemaru is the best professor at this University. She is genuinely so kind and caring and you can tell she wants everyone to learn and succeed. 100% take her classes. She is the best.

The materials were very accessible and for my class she gave out a couple of extra credit opportunities on the midterm but also the final and throughout the term. There were about 2 major group projects however these were fairly easy and your task was to write no more than 300 words which could be done in an hour. Very nice and brilliant teacher.

Professor Idemaru is very organized, her lecture slides are easy to follow, and the homework workload is small. The attendance policy and assigned homework is super reasonable - there were reading quizzes due before each lecture as homework, but most were 4-7 questions and not hard to understand. She is super sweet and cares about her students!

Professor Idemaru was a great professor to kick off the year with. Her class is easy, doesn't require a textbook, well organized. If you show up to class, do the readings, and study the lectures you will do fine.

Ihab is very knowledgeable about sustainable design and connecting heavy engineering concepts to architectural design. Although this course is about architectural technology, I feel I learned about design and design quality and architectural precedents more than I learned in other studios. His lectures and in class demonstrations are awesome!

I had Professor Elzeyadi for architecture studio. This was the best studio I took in graduate school. What he taught me in skills and design sensitivity was essential to my career and job opportunities after school. I'm indebted to him for all the knowledge he shared with me!

Ihab is awesome! Extremely knowledgeable in ECS and sustainable building sciences. Listen closely to this man, he will drop a beautiful gem of knowledge nonchalantly. Hope to take more of his classes in the future.

Ihab is a fantastic professor. The best classes I took so far are the ones he taught. He's dedicated, knowledgable, and compassionate. I feel I learned a lot after this term and I also feel that I'm empowered with very applicable knowledge that I can use in my design studios. Thank you, Ihab!

I had professor Elzeyadi for my first introductory graduate studio. He was an amazing instructor and I learned a lot from him. I'm comparing how much he taught us and his excellent feedback to what I'm getting now in another studio with another professor and I only wish we have him in our current studio again.
I enjoyed having Ihab for this class and would love to take more classes with him. I feel I'm talking to a real professor with solid academic experience and practical knowledge of the field too.

I would recommend avoiding Ihab's classes if at all possible. His lectures are incredibly boring. His class was highly dependent on group projects. One of our team members went awol for weeks. We were told that we would lose points if she wasn't in the group photo. We had to resort to photoshopping her into the picture.

We have spent the term learning a terrible program that he insists we use while designing our project. He spends hours a day talking and the objective is still unclear once he has finished talking. We were supposed to have studio from 1 - 6:30 Monday and Wednesday and have Friday off, but instead we have been coming in every Friday.

I had Ihab for a number of studios. He is exceptional at connecting sustainability and technical knowledge with design. This is what studio should be about and the UO needs more of studio instructors like him. He encouraged me and mentored me to submit my studio design into the AIA COTE and I won. Thanks, Ihab!
He's ver knowledgable and experienced both in cutting edge research and in ways to connect the subject to practice. I really enjoyed his course and also in studio.

This class is super hard- because Japanese is a difficult language. Ikei sensei is clear and very good at teaching this class. She cares about your success, you just have to work hard. She can be stern, but she's also kind and funny. She is very accessible outside of class to help. Way too much homework though.

Ikei Sensei is great, is engaging and gives good lectures, accessible outside of class and promptly responds to emails. However, the course structure feels a little unbalanced. The content of the learning  started very easy, and ended much more difficult, all while keeping a fast-pace with lots of quizzes. However, I really recommend the course!

Rika is a very good teacher and is extremely accessible and helpful. The class is challenging, but it's literally Japanese lmao. Grading is consistent and clear, gives feedback and tons of extra credit opportunities. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed in her class.

*Make sure that you purchase the Nakama textbook through the Duck Store with the audio component.*

The course itself is quite intensive and you need to do the homework, show up, and study. However, she's very kind and totally understands how hard the class is. The two lowest quiz scores are dropped at the end and she's a really forgiving grader.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ikei is an amazing teacher. She has good energy, makes her expectations clear, and expands upon the course materials for better student understanding. She cares a lot about her students. I took JPN 101, 102, and 103 with her and enjoyed having her as a professor. Be sure to read the textbook and do the homework and you'll do well.

Professor Ikei is an amazing teacher. She has good energy, is very clear in her expectations, and helps expand upon the course materials for better student understanding. She cares a lot about her students. I took Japanese 101, 102, and 103 with her and enjoyed having her as my professor.

Ikei Sensei was such a great Japanese teacher! Although we had our classes online, she made sure we greatly understood the content that we were learning. She is very kind and makes funny comments here and there. Highly recommend her for JPN 101!

Very good at controlling the classroom. She speaks very quickly, so do not slack off on your listening skills.  She is always available for office hours, which many students utilized. She has a very good sense of humor, and is very friendly. She got very ill during the term, and still gave 100% in the classroom. Outstanding teacher. Good class.
She is really responsible for all students. She is kind and knows details about how your study goes.

There was some grumbling in the classroom about her. She puts forth a good effort but her lessons look exactly like the textbook which shouldn't be so in a 400 level class. I'd like to be guided through a few usage examples. But continuing through the sequence. Not bad. Helpful at office hours when preparing final drafts for essays.
Great professor, she takes a strong interest in her students, and as long as you show effort and come to class, you'll do great in the class.
Top-notch Takes great interest in all her students

Ikei-sensei is a good teacher. She is kind, but is firm when people act up. She also is very informed about things, and works really well for beginners. She does go fast, though, if you're taking summer course.
funny and likes to give examples. sometimes strange, for instance, when asked stupid questions gives funny answers. goes hee-hee alot.
Excellent but a little frosty around the edges.   Show the proper respect and you'll be fine.
She wasn't that bad of a teacher... it was a little more difficult to understand her giving directions in japanese, but within a week i was able to pick up on it
i dont like her

Professor Colaiacovo is the best professor! She can be a tough grader and class participation is a large portion of your grade, but if you put in effort, you will do really well in her course. She is amazing and always willing to help every student outside of class. This has been one of my favorite courses, I would 100% recommend it to anyone!

This class was awesome, professor Colaiacovo (don't worry, you'll learn how to pronounce it) is an incredible teacher. She is a tough grader, but is fair about it and will regrade and work with you to help you do your best. I took so much away from this class and am so grateful!

This was one of the best classes I've ever taken. Professor Colaiacovo is such a fun teacher. The lectures are really engaging and exciting. She uses a lot of real world examples which is also always great for MGMT classes. She's a tough, but fair grader and gives a lot of feedback. If you put in effort you'll get a good grade.
