There is weekly essays that short/easy, but your grade mostly depends on the two midterms/final. He is a good professor but you have to keep on top of the readings and pay attention in class to understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but lectures are awful. You can't hear anything even the GE said she can't understand him. He uses no slides or resources for the lectures and the key terms posted after are not helpful. Homework is easy but majority of your grade is the exams. Don't recommend

Tim is a nice guy, but this class was one of the worst I have taken at UO. He lectures with no slides or visual aids whatsoever, even when people asked him to use them. I found myself sitting in each class wondering what was going on. He provides some "study terms" for the two midterms and finals, but these were not very helpful for me.

She was very passionate about what she was teaching which made everything so much more interesting. Loved the class and loved how engaging the weekly discussions were. Assignments were pretty easy and I loved the textbook readings. Definitely recommend.

Very kind, and does her best to make the class interesting through her short lecture videos. I would only take a class with her again in person. Online, the class structure is uninteresting and just bland, her assignments and quizzes are easy too. I did enjoy our weekly discussions, as they gave an opportunity to talk about our own opinions.

Funny panopto vids with her cat, lol. Super laid back and is more interested in the discussion than the hard assignments. About 6 quizzes and 6 assignments throughout term, discussion with GE every week. Very funny and forgiving. Would recommend.
Very awesome professor but her class was relatively complicated, I feel like my fellow students got the short end of the stick cause they weren't all 101% there and I still only nabbed an A-.
She's hard. Very nice but hard.
One of my favorite teachers of all time. She makes learning Spanish far beyond the language and into cultural conversations that supplement very well. She's someone I'd love to be friends with.

Iris is a lovely teacher. Although the language department at UO has strict guidelines and policies for the criteria and attendance, Iris connected really well with the students and myself in her class. She has a great teaching style, and gives clear grading criteria. She wants you to succeed and her office hours were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: It's not so much Iris as it is the class. She's a grad student so I assume she didn't get a lot of say in what she taught. SPAN 101 should be for students who have never taken a Spanish class before, not for those who've taken 2+ years. My roommate compared my homework to her Spanish 3 Honors class she took in high school. Way too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Shiekh in really down to earth and caring about her class and students. Her class on Muslim Women in Early Islam was really easy going and enjoyable. There were a significant amount of readings, but if you got the gust of it you'd be fine. Learned a lot in her class and enjoyed it a lot!

The best professor I have ever had. She is so encouraging and down to earth professor who not only possesses vast knowledge but also deeply cares about her students as well. I really enjoyed her class. She is funny, and she loves her job! Highly recommend taking a class with her.
She is AMAZING. Super engaged, an easy class thats actually interesting and where she genuinely wants you to learn. Just turn your stuff in on time and give genuine effort and youll get an A.

Professor Shiekh selects relevant readings or films to be discussed in class. She encourages discussion of thoughts and new perspectives. Class is calm and always enjoyable. I loved both classes I have taken with her and look forward to more in the future.

There is a lot of readings and two "exams" which are pretty easy as long as you have read the articles that she provides. Enjoyed the class and Professor Reyes-Santos was very open to hearing discussions if you didn't agree with her. Goes over the readings to help you understand them better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I respect her demand for respect from her students as a woman of color (DOES NOT TARGET WHITES BTW). She is an easy grader, enthusiastic, funny, caring, expert in her field, assigns great material, but is terrible at teaching. I learned more from the internet. Constant tangents, never addresses reading, doesn't regulate lecture discussions.

I've had her for several classes and I've never been disappointed. She seems hard at first, but actually doing the assignments is fine. Don't worry about the trolls on her ratings. They are the ones who need her and Ethnic Studies the most, as they can't seem to respect a strong Afro-Indigenous woman.

I LOVED this class and Prof. Reyes-Santos! She was so passionate about the topic, and was very knowledgeable. She was so clear in all the information she gave the class, and repeated the main ideas. She held study sessions before all the tests, which were so helpful! Despite the large amount of reading, it was a great class with a fun professor!

About as liberal and feminist as it gets, to the point of ignorance. Tries to seem like a hard professor. In lecture she talks as though white people are the spawn of satan, aren't we supposed to be fighting for equality?

I gave Prof Reyes-Santos a perfect score because she deserves it. This woman knows what she's talking about. When she wants you to remember something, she says it multiple times. Before every exam, she takes class time to go over what is on the exam. Exam essay questions are in the syllabus. Easy class with challenging material. Take her.

I have taken two classes with Prof. Reyes-Santos (301 and 442). Very helpful. The class itself was pretty hard, but if you come prepared you shouldn't have a problem. Lots and lots of reading. So if you don't like reading these classes are not for you. Midterm and final are also fair as well.

Prof Reyes-Santos is extremely bright and committed to helping students succeed. Introduced me to a # of my favorite books&essays of all time. ES can be confusing/frustrating to students who aren't used to being truly critical of racism and sexism in the United States. This probably accounts for negative reviews that Prof Reyes-Santos has received.
A very bad teacher she can't even keep her own thoughts straight.
Totally committed to her students.

Professor Reyes-Santos is one of the best professor I have had at the University of Oregon. She has demonstrated great teaching skills that many do not understand because of the intersectional approach of the field of Ethnic Studies. A passionate professor that center social justice at the core because fo the tradition of Ethnic Studies.

Absolutely HORRIFIC class...I have never been more bored in my entire life. Professor is useless (and you must call her professor)...I would have learned more teaching myself. All she does is quote from the articles and then go off on some tangent about how it's somehow the fault of white people...how did this woman become a teacher??
She doesnt seem to know what she is doing at all.  Shes horrible at explaining things, and very boring class. She makes sure that you know to respect her authority too.  Not a good teacher at all

Terrible, awful teacher.  Frequently contradicts herself, misrepresents students, and shows (ironically so) how ignorant she is.  If you're looking for an easy "A," just turn off your brain and you'll do fine.

zzzzzzzzzzzzz... the ethnic studies intro class (part 1) was tedious and its approach to racisim was hostile and very focused on finger pointing.  ES 101's primary objective was only pointing out the problems in our society without looking at the possible solutions.  It was the presentation of a problem without searching for solutions.
No Comments
No Comments

Iris was my teacher for public speaking at Indiana University.   Iris is nice, but if there is an alternative teacher, DO IT. Iris makes this class extremely difficult. She is the hardest grader I have ever experienced. She will give you feedback on how to do better but you never will. Your best speech will be a B. Nobody in my class got an A.

Iris Bull was the worst GTF I have ever had. She took 9 weeks to give us our grades back, 9 weeks!!! And even then she still hadn't given us back our grades for the first assignment for which she had TWO MONTHS to grade. I'm not making this up people, she's the worst and you will regret taking her lab. seriously, don't do it. DON'T DO IT!

Iris probably has more experience than all the GTF's combined and is really cool in lab. Professional, great taste in music, really helpful--will stay after class to help you. However, her grading is tough. Forgetting your name = half a letter grade. That sucked a lot.

I took her Child Language course and it was terrible. The homework & exams were impossible because it wasn't even over material we covered. LING101 was much easier; I think she eased up a bit once she saw everyone in her 294 class do terribly. Very nice woman that is approachable but did NOT know how to make exams...the wording was SO confusing.

Quirky accent. Very approachable. Sets high expectations. Make sure to start the homeworks early cause they're hard, talk to gtfs / prof about the hard questions cause they are graded unforgivingly. Don't depend on her lecture notes, use the book instead. Longer answers usually gives a better grade.

She taught an interesting elective during zero week. She was really creative with the topics. I think that I would have enjoyed if the class was a semester long instead. Kind of quirky and has a sometimes-hilarious Russian accent. Worth taking a class from.

The course was graded based on the midterm, final, attendance, and one class project. I didn't receive a midterm grade for 3 weeks after taking the exam. The midterm and final were writing heavy and took 5x the amount of time she stated. She gives horrible feedback, no constructive criticism, and is very unhelpful when discussing grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor focuses on children's literature at the expense of the actual subject. Hard grading

Great professor who is very supportive and wants to see students succeed. I was a little nervous going into this class with the reviews but the scariest thing was participation in class. Each class always focuses on the content that you finish at home. As long as you keep up in class you will do amazing with them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Millan is a VERY tough grader, especially for a lower-level class. This class (a few years ago) was definitely focused on ethnic studies in addition to WGS, but I think that's a good thing. Lots of interesting reading and fun topics. Tests are HARD, you need to study. If you do the reading, study, and engage thoughtfully, you will learn!

One of the absolute worse professors Ive had the displeasure of being taught from. She would LITERALLY grade papers with feedback as not good. Her only note for my midterm paper was do better. I know a student who attempted to take their life during the pandemic whilst taking her class and she asked for proof for an extension. AVOID!!!!!

Only graded on 4 things, attendance, midterm, final and one project. The class was WGS but we didn't even discuss women's issues; it was all about transborder children. It felt like she wanted to be teaching an ethnics study class. We read picture books every class out loud and discussed them. Tests were graded very hard. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice guy, just doesn't teach as clearly as a tenured professor might. You gotta do the reading before class, or else join the class majority getting 50% on quizzes. Class format easy though. Pay attention and it's not much harder than any other econ class.

Now teaches at montana state in bozeman, but is very helpful. If you don't understand he explains further in different ways. One of the best Econ teachers I've had and I've always had trouble with economics

The class was fairly interesting.  He is easy to understand and tests are all multiple choice.  For a GTF he was better than most professors I've had.  Had no homework and did not require a textbook (used a free online one), which was a plus for me.

James is a very nice guy, he's helpful and actually pretty funny. But he is an awful teacher. I have only gotten A's in university math classes including an A+ in Math 315, but this is so much harder than any other. Not a single person finished the first midterm on time or was able to answer every question. You have been warned.

Lectures were very difficult to understand. He doesn't follow the textbook very well. However, he was very helpful and knowledgable outside of lecture, and his tests were easy and fair. Great teacher overall just needs to work on his clarity.
His lecture is pretty fast, could be a good or bad thing depending on the student.  Completely willing to explain things further if asked to.  Gives good examples.

Very helpful if you have physics before taking this class.  his lectures were very unclear and the format was very unorganized.  he is really smart though, maybe too much so to teach. really nice guy though
He makes some smart ass comments some times, but that's what makes his class fun.
There is only one name here, Italo. He is the best of all professors of every class I have taken. Excellent in every aspect.

The class was amazing, a great professor, he is a must concerning SPANISH. Although a lot of work, he is always working with you. And also a charming person if you can talk with him personally. Always trying to help.
Great class, great guy. I have never seen nothing like that. The ideal spanish teacher. Nothing like him.

Italo is a very fine professor, gentle and human. I learned a lot more than spanish. Knows a lot and has a very methodic approach. Everyone was having fun in his class. TAKE SPANISH 201 with Italo, you will not waste time. Also, he is very intelligent and kind.

He doesn't do very well explaining topics in class, he could also use class time a lot more effectively. He seems very condescending if given the wrong answer. He really needs to work on getting students to actually learn the material that'll be on the test.

Doesn't explain what we need to know. Seems very condescending if you give the wrong answer. Not very effective use of class time. Really needs to work on getting students to actually learn the material that is on the test.
While Italo is super easy, his class is very frusterating. He isn't very clear on his expectations and directions, and if you say or answer a question wrong he treats you like an idiot.
No Comments
barely any grades and barely any instruction

This class feels unorganized and irrelevant. There is no correlation between the classes and tests compared to the homework. The notes and lectures are haphazard and over complicated. The tests cover a ton of content but there is no study guide or notes sheets available. His lectures are very boring and don't cover the actual content of the class.
Lovely guy. Class is absolutely not as hard as everyone's saying it is. Imamura's lectures are always engaging and interesting, and his tests cover material discussed in class.
The overall class felt highly unorganized, and the lectures were hard to follow, mostly because the PowerPoint slides were close to unreadable.

Meant for non-STEM majors, but the content on the exams are ridiculously hard for someone without a good understanding of physics and chemistry. Poorly organized class. Exams do not accurately reflect the homework or the lectures and he gets off topic fast. The exams pretty much determine your grade. However, he does curve the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took ASTR121 in fall of 2021, hes a nice guy who can tend to get off topic during lectures but if you pay attention and read it can fill the gaps. Anyone could definitely get an A if they really try to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the subject itself and the professor's lectures were pretty good. The professor himself was funny and was helpful at times. However, this class was far from easy, especially for a 100 level course. This is due to the tests and its weight of content. To succeed in this class, be prepared to do a lot of studying.

This class is so hard for no reason.If he was better at teaching he wouldnt have to curve grades like a maniac because students would understand the topics better the only way he can help is by curving test grades insanely.Unless youre super into this stuff and know most of it already,ur going to struggle if ur just taking it for a science credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take the class. He never goes off what he calls his slides and makes learning so hard. He will go on random tangents in class. What I thought was going to be a simple GE was so hard. He expects his students to know what he talks about when it is supposed to be an intro of Astronomy. Nothing that comes out of his mouth makes sense. Save ur GPA

Prof Imamura is obviously a really smart guy but teaches things that are incomprehensible for a 100 level class. The midterms and final are absolutely impossible, I think that the highest grade for the final was like a 40/60 and he doesn't enter the curve into canvas. Super difficult and taught super quick and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID & SAVE YOUR GPA. Everyone has a D or F, he doesnt enter the curves into canvas so you have to guess what your overall grade is. This class is an incoherent unorganized nightmare. The lecture slide notes are webpage format & take you on a wild goose chase as well as the HW & has barely any instructions. Do NOT take for GenEd science credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The format of this class is painful. His "slides" is a long-winded website-style word jumble that is impossible to decipher. He is a really nice person, but the class is a nightmare. I thought it would be an easy science credit, but sometimes it feels like rocket science, especially on the tests. Lectures are long and hard to understand

In lectures he rants about random things constantly and gets side tracked the entire time. Less and less people show up everyday. Only 6 homework assignments and 2 tests. Tests are worded weird and questions are about a "bigger question" or "bigger meaning" that he never covers. Everyone I know in it is also failing with a D or F.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely the most incoherent lectures I've ever heard. Homework assignments are confusing and unclear and seemingly given without purpose. Assignments and test review sheets are given in awful, webpage format and must be tediously transferred to different apps. Tests are awful. Avoid at all cost.
Sometimes he sounds a little rambly but he's a nice guy.
Insanely hard for a 100 level gen ed. Would not recommend unless you actually are interested in astronomy or else it will feel like rocket science. Tests are extremely hard and specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was enjoyable because you can tell he is extremely passionate about the subject, unfortunately the lecture does not easily transfer and the tests are so hard to pass.

Class can be a bit more challenging than the average GenEd, but it's given a good curve so even if you don't do so hot on the exams it will probably work itself out (example, I had a C- and ended the course with a B, edging on a B+). Textbook isn't necessary in my opinion. Professor is quirky & funny & class was overall a pleasant experience.

Class is not as hard as everyone says that it is. Jim is a cool guy, and the tests have a nice curve. If you put some effort in to reading the website and paying attention in class then it will not be challenging.

I thought this would be a good way to knock out my science gen ed but the class was much harder . The homework only sometimes came into play on the tests & typically took an hour to complete. His lectures only touched on the topics covered on the exam so regardless of attending class or not, you still need to read through all the lectures.

I learned so much from taking Jim's class. The content he presents is really interesting, and it helps that he has so much knowledge about it. Sometimes it is hard to stay awake, but definitely worth taking

He is very quirky and eccentric at times, but he is a very intelligent man. If you show up and pay attention to his lectures, you should do fine. Textbooks are completely unnecessary and often make concepts more confusing and long-winded than they need to be. He also posts practice exams--study them! A lot of the questions will show up on your test

I understand some of the comments about his difficulty but the curve on these tests is so high it's outrageous.  I can honestly say that I received a solid D on every single test but ended up receiving a solid B in the end. If your an undergrad looking for an easy grade I wholly encourage you to take this class.

Was very unhelpful and more than one occasion he told me he didn't have time to answer my type of question and then answered other's similar. He made half the class laugh, but it wasn't a fun class. His analogies are unrealistic. For ex. "the speed of light and the speed of sound are the same" and then proceeds. And he has a science background?

The tests were extremely difficult, to the point where a C was welcomed. For this class there wasn't much room for screw up and his tests didn't help. The HW had little to do with the material. Funny guy but I'd avoid him for a teacher.

Cool guy, hard class. You'll need some coffee before class to help you pay attention, but if you do there's never a reason to open your textbook. He hops on one leg during lectures and really enjoys throwing chalk. He curves tests and the class which makes up for the difficulty.

What are these people talking about?! He is literally the worst professor I've ever had. He is extremely smart, yeah, but he doesn't have ANY idea how to convey that to a bunch of underclassmen taking this course as a GenEd requirement. If you're looking for a reasonable GenEd, do NOT take this. I don't understand this man at all.

Imamura was hilarious. He'd go on tangents about really cool space-related things when you asked the right question. The tests were awful but the curve mostly made up for it. I probably would't take the class again though, it was pretty difficult.

Class is hard to follow, but if you just read his lecture notes you can get an A on his test. He gives a Huge curve and he can be interesting at times, and really funny.  He knows what he is talking about just hard to stay awake.  I would take another class with him if I were to take another astronomy class

He is a strange guy. The homework is a little hard but it makes sense after going through his notes a few times. The tests are not that easy but he gives a NICE curve. (I got a 78, that meant an A) :) He rambles a little

I really enjoyed this professor. He gives beautiful curves on tests (72-100=A). With that said, though, his tests are pretty tough. I think he is rather entertaining in lecture, for he stretches and twirls and bangs his head on things whilst rattling away subject matter. Sit up close, though, because he doesn't have a loud voice.

Those people complaining about Professor Imamura most likely aren't going to graduate college with a GPA above 2.5. Test averages are extremely low (~65) but his curves are so generous (>74 is an A...) that he makes it easy to succeed. Also, everything he puts on his tests are on his review guides. Very easy to talk to as well.

Imamura is an interesting guy.  He is very knowledgable about what he teaches but sometimes in the lecture setting he has trouble being clear.  If you take this class go to his office hours he is very helpful there.  Also the class is curved
Extremely boring, easy to fall asleep, tests are rediculously hard. Very random person in a weird way

Professor Imamura was definitely not my favorite teacher. Thought he could be hilarious at times, he also could be super boring, tedious, had homework that had nothing to do with what we were learning in class and tests that had nothing to do with the study guides.

I was extremely excited to get into this class since astronomy has been my 'thing' since i was 5. However Imamura has yet to keep me awake during class. I'm never tired when I go to his class but he has the ability to lull me to sleep within 5 minutes. His voice is a constant drone and, even in my class of 9 he refuses to engage us in any way.

Jim Imamura is one of the most badass professors I have ever had. He jumps up and down, slams his head against the desk, and starts breathing heavily in the middle of lecture. He also once slipped on the chalk dust that accumulated on the floor, and the look on his face as gravity enacted its force on him was one of poetic beauty. So badass.

Kinda weird guy. He randomly will start jumping up and down or breathing heavily in the middle of lecture.  ADHD maybe? His tests were super hard, the material is difficult, and lectures were boring, but he gives a huge curve on grades.  I wouldn't recommend him.

Homework was very difficult and time consuming.  Tests were quite difficult; I never walked out with an accurate read of how I'd done. Grading, however, was very friendly, and if he goes too fast in class (he will), he's very approachable, and more detailed, in his office. I would take another class from him.

He's great for Astronomy, but in Thermal Physics he comes up pretty short.  Lectures meandered so much we wound up turning in homework on topics we hadn't even covered in class, so expect to teach yourself with the textbook a lot.  He's actually pretty good explaining one-on-one though, so don't be afraid to go to office hours.

Nice guy.  Keeps students awake by randomly launching chalky projectiles.  Lectures seem to meander, but at least he assigns homework from the book (a book that has selected answers and plenty of examples, which allows for self study.)
what, come on guys. did you not get an A for 0 effort, did he not entertain you by throwing**** and jumping around like a crazy person?  GREAT CLASS. HOW ABOUT A GOOD JOB.
Boring class. All the students leave the class after 30 Mu. Hard Exams. Nice Curve. Don't take his class

This guy is hilarious! He jumps up and down during class, hits his head on the blackboard, and takes breaks in middle of class!   He is a fairy good teacher.  His lectures are very boring, and so they are pointless. The good thing is that if you study the review tests, and understand them, you will do great in this class! He curves everything :)

This is an easy science class if  you want to stay away from classes with Labs or Discussions. The curve is ridiculous, so while you may only get 25/50 questions on a test, you will still get a B. The material is hard but exact knowledge isn't necessary - take this class if you want to get your science credits out of the way
It was okaay... i did better than i thought

Imamura was a really interesting person, but a pretty boring and off topic lecturer. I enjoyed the topics discussed in the class, and would love to have the opportunity to talk to him about such things on a person to person level, but as a lecturer, he really falls short.
easy science class, kind of interestsing, lectures kind of random.
its easy to get an A in his class if you study for the tests, he usually has a huge curve
jimmy is the man and keeps your attention by throwing things across the room. Easy class and if you can't get a B there is no hope for you in this university
gets off topic, very smart but not a good teacher. tests are hard but there is usually a curve
he doesn't really stay focused in class, and his explinations of the material aren't clear or easy to understand at all
No Comments

Class isn't that hard if you read the book/study. He gets distracted and goes on tangents easily, but they are usually interesting tangents. Not the easiest 122 class you could take, but nothing too difficult.
he seems somewhat crazy and is easily taken off topic by students questions
I owe this guy my career! I hope you appreciate what he does for his students as much as I do 15 years later.
Colin has rockstar energy with great finesse and confidence. He is quite hilarious and a great artists. At the core of it he cares and is one of the kindest professors in the program.

Colin does what all art teachers should do, give the student full creative freedom. While being one of the most kind and caring professors around, Colin is sure to inspire you to put yourself in your artwork and unlock sides of your creativity you didnt know existed

I had Colin for an experimental "art of drones" class. It was the first one he'd taught, and it went really well. One of the nicest and most interesting professors I've had so far. He really pushed me to work to my full potential.
Great Professor, and great taste in lecture material.

Colin is a great Instructor.Really knows his stuff, great advice, keep your ears open, do ALL the readings. Shows a love of learning, excited to learn as much from students and projects as we are to learn for him. Colin taking you seriously makes you take the class, your work, and yourself more seriously than before. Is the man.
Colin rocks!
He's super awesome! Glad I was able to take ENG104Z with him last term since he's no longer teaching. Super rad guy.
He's awesome.
Chris is one of the nicest professors I've had at UO. He is very laid back and this class was enjoyable to take.

I had little interest in the fiction topic of monsters starting this class but because of Prof Ivy it has truly been one of my favorites. If you put in the work you can get a good grade it is participation that matters. Often brings snacks to class and just a enjoyable lecture. If you ever have the oppurtuity to take his class I highly recommend.

This was probably the best classroom environment I've been in through college yet. He is really funny and genuinely cares about his students. I would 1000% recommend Chris if the opportunity is available.

Super funny, super friendly. Will give you extensions on any assignment, no questions asked. If you turn in an assignment early and email him, he'll give you feedback before the due date so you can make corrections and resubmit, which basically gurantees a 100% on the assignment. Brought snacks to class just because he said he liked us so much.
Had Chris for 2 classes. Probably the best GE I've had at UO, and I think a lot of people would agree. Really personable & engaging in discussion, generous w/ grading as long as you put the work in.

I had Mr. Ivy as my discussion section teacher for CINE 267, and I fought duckweb registration in order to have him again for CINE 266. He gives hilarious lectures and brings snacks for the class sometimes. Very understanding and flexible when it comes to deadlines for the class, just email him! Literally my favorite teacher at UO.

Chris is one of my favorite professors of all time. He's super personable and provides great feedback. He teaches writing tactics and skills we'll actually use and need, and provides us with really great resources. Some of the resources at UO I didn't even know about until I took WR122 with him. I looked forward going to class, which is rare.

Difficult subject to understand and you're only graded by three exams and participation so any hiccup made on the exams can hurt your grade. He does grade on a curve though depending on how the whole class did.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is difficult because it doesn't have homework or any forms of grading besides 2 exams and participation (easy 10%) But demonstrates a good understanding of the economic concepts he teaches. Makes it easier to interpret by asking us questions and relating it to real examples instead of just theoretical models. Just pay attention you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I finished with an 83 in his class BEFORE THE CURVE. 80A-, 60 B-, 40C-, 20D-. First of all, do yourself a favor and ignore the bad ratings, this class is not difficult at all. We met twice a week for 2 hours with 10-15 slides per class. All you have to do is attend lecture, take notes, and study the lecture slides for the 2 tests (40% , 60%)

By far the worst class and professor I have ever had, and I do not say this lightly. There is no homework, either mandatory or optional, and the whole grade is solely based on the midterm and final. The lectures are long, dry, and boring, not to mention useless, to the point where half of the class would not show up. I retained absolutely nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. Doesn't understand how to teach students at all. Awful at relating information in a way that can be grasped. It is surprising that this man is a teacher at any level especially a professor. If at all possible don't take a class with this man. Whatever it takes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was 40% midterm and 60% final. Lectures are long and its impossible to follow along . English is not his first language. feel bad for him because he seems like a good guy, but if possible do not take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever had. Gives us nothing to study and curves our tests twenty percent to make himself look better. Then proceeds to tell us failure is a part of life. If you see this professor on your schedule change you schedule no matter what it takes. Thank me later.

Easily the worst professor Ive ever had. His lectures were dry and unengaging. It's even harder to pay attention when he talks completely monotone and also mispronounces everything. The grade was solely based on your midterm and final exams. The tests were weirdly written and difficult to study for since we had no homework or prior preparation.

Joey does not give any quizzes, and tests are a very big part of your grade. Make sure if you do not understand something to go to his office hours. He grades homework very hard, marking the majority of points down for work that you show. Same goes for tests. In his syllabus he says you should spend 16 hours on the class in a week, but its more 20.

Gives a lot of feedback on assignments. Speaks clearly, but is still learning how to write. Has a tragic case of pedantry. Seems to know maths by rote rather than having real comprehension - this is okay so long as you stay between the lines of convention. Friendly and easy to talk with. Willing to help however he can.

I took calc for bio majors from him and I found that he often made things more complicated than they needed to be. He was not a terrible teacher was exceedingly inflexible. He also makes it clear that he reserves the right to change your grade to not passing if he does not think you understand the material.

He was unnecessarily difficult, giving questions that he would get wrong during class and have to fix them. He would spend almost entire class period figuring out a problem that you would have to do something similar for the test, but you would have to do 5 of them. I personally aced 4 out of 5 questions but the 5th bomb it and get a C on a test.
Great guy.His handouts,notes,and solutions of homework are clear.Patient and helpful in office hour.Rational grading.You can make a makeup chance if you didn't do well in midterm.Rational grading.
Really good teacher. Provides great guided notes which contain examples very specific to the current concept. Readily available outside of class to help you, really enjoyed taking classes from him.
I'm excited to be taught by an intelligent instructor.  I have no problem expanding my horizons with "tough" problems or difficult exams.
He's a very hard grader when it comes to the final, and it's unfair how he doesn't curve the class.

Joey is the worst gtfs i've had. He is a busy graduate student andhis class that he teaches is not his priority. he doesn't have time to make study guides, comes/leaves right when class starts/ends and makes you feel bad when you can't make it to his office hours and need to make an appointment. he doesn't teach whats on the test and goes very fast

Knowledgable but lacks the communication skills for teaching. Every example he does in class comes from the book, but he goes through it way too fast to follow and you basically right an essay for notes. He goes through it like we know it when half the class has no idea what hes even talking about.

Joey is not a good teacher. He is really smart and all but can't teach. He just assumes you should know everything and gets frustrated when the whole class gets confused and doesn't know what he is saying. His tests are also extremely difficult.
Joey is a wonderful GTF.  Very knowledgable and extremely helpful.  He's easily relatable and patient with all styles of students' learning.
:D

Great professor. Allowed us to either do Perusalls or one final test, in which we chose perusalls. One presentation in groups, followed by personal essays based off your presentation. Talking during class gets you more points, so make sure to engage in class convos. Jett was very responsive and reachable outside of class as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Would not recommend for fellow disabled students. She refused to provide a very basic and reasonable accommodation for me. The tone she took with me and the way she treated me makes it clear to me that making sure her classroom is accessible and welcoming to all students is not a priority for her.

Such an unorganized prof who doesn't know what she's doing. That being said, she's very nice and would raise my grade every time I came to office hours. But her class is one of those that you have no idea what's going on, even though it's not difficult. Frustrating and a waste of time.

Professor Jett was fantastic, and the course topics were interesting and relevant. Attendance wasn't required, but there was a chance you would miss an in-class activity that was graded for extra credit. Exams were easy, and there were so many extra credit opportunities. Would recommend for PS majors or anyone looking for a nice GPA boost.

So so accomodating, when I was sick she gave an extension within reason and provided other resources, and when I had a conflict with the midterm she allowed me to take it at 8am so I wouldn't miss it. Very welcoming in office hours and grading support. Material isn't difficult to understand, just hard to memorize all the models for exams.

Overall, I enjoyed her class because the readings are fairly easy, and she analyzes them in class as well. She races through the slides and does not post them before class, so be prepared to take pictures of the slides on your phone. I can never keep up with how fast and monotone she speaks. She is witty, kind, and a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was one of the best I've had while at UO she lectured on relevant issues in the world and catered the class if students were more interested in certain subjects. To do well I rec. participating in class discussions. The class is lecture heavy but is broken up with videos and graphs which helped me a visual learner. GREAT TEACHER!

Professor Jett is can explain readings and terms in simple language, which makes concepts easier to understand and recall for tests. The sources she uses is very relevant to today which makes class more interesting! However, she does speed through her slides quickly making it hard to write down notes. But she posts her slides after each class!

I won't lie, start of this class at the beginning of the term, I really wasn't a fan of this guy.

Seemed grandstandy, disorganized, and as if he was relying heavily on his GE to carry the class. I was pleasantly surprised halfway through the course to find that things generally just shifted, his lectures were passionate and discussions thoughtful.

Overall a difficult 100 level class but not much more than that. Very interesting topics and classes. The grading is a bit strict and there is a lot of busy work, but it is really not that bad. Reading is mostly optional, you just have to understand the authors core claim/idea. Maybe skip if you are a first year but really not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a good guy he's chill, and lectures you can actually understand the content well. Him and GE's are rough graders though and don't give good feedback on how to fix problems.

You can tell that Professor Neal is passionate about what he teaches, but I hated attending that class. You don't get feedback on almost any of your work, there is (occasional) cold calling, essays, group work within lectures, a midterm, quizzes every Friday and before every class. I wouldn't take this class unless its' required.

Theres 5-7 weekly assignments (mostly busy work) but its very very light. Readings help but are not required, attendance and weekly quizzes means you cant miss any classes. Interesting topics covered, it is "hard" for a 100 level class but if you're taking this as a required A&L elective at the end of your undergrad years this will be very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Expect 40–60 pages of weekly reading. Lectures are mandatory twice a week 1.5 hrs and cover readings. Quizzes every Friday are challenging and will require you study. GEs grade harshly, their policy is to not give 100%, expect to score in the 80s-90s on most work. If you're just trying to fulfill an Arts & Letters requirement, not the class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Politically preaches the entire class, argues with students that ask questions or outright ignores them. Wants students to participate but when they do their opinion is wrong if it isnt exactly like his opinion.

The amount of AI usage in the content and feedback in this course is damaging to any potential value this class may have. I ended up finishing it feeling like my spanish was worse than it was when I began. He clearly has passion and potential, but he hardly taught. It's unacceptable to pay such high tuition just to be taught by Chat GPT.

He can be harsh but overall a kind guy and you can tell he wants his students to succeed, prepare to be doing a lot of work, the class has a very heavy workload and this was the main class I would always be doing work for so it is easy to fall behind, textbook used but you don't need to be spending all your time on it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The professor introduced a tool he made in ChatGPT for the class to guide us through the final project writing process from proposal to final oral presentation. I thought it was helpful, but then a few days later we were told that the tool had to be taken down because some other students complained about it being in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very kind professor and helped improve my writing skills a lot!

Easy A if you try at all. Coursework and content is extremely AI heavy, most of the lectures and assignments appear to be AI generated. Gives lots of feedback but that also seems written by AI. For such a small class, very surprising to have such minimal interaction and discussion with peers. A very nice guy but not a good professor.

Jon was a great professor, the best one in the Spanish department that I've had. He is incredibly understanding, caring and supportive of all students and wants everyone to succeed. The class itself was fairly easy, with papers and projects being the majority of the homework (not much busy work). Overall, 10/10 and would recommend him to anyone!

The class itself is not too challenging, he is very understanding of people's lives and will work with you as long as you show you are doing your part. He also is implementing the use of AI into the class so that was fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Jaramillo is hands down the best Spanish professor at the University of Oregon. I would recommend his course to anybody in a second. He is the best!
Extremely chill professor who just wants you to succeed, 10/10 recommend

THE best Spanish teacher I have at UO. I took his summer online session and he made it great. He is very good at explaining things thoroughly and speaks clearly. He obviously cares about his students very much and wants everyone to succeed. I appreciated that he explained instructions in English before the oral exams. I cannot recommend Jon enough!

Jon is so caring. He is a PhD student and I had the honor to be a part of his last term teaching at UO. He really understands the struggles students face and wants to help everyone get an A in the class.

He's such a great guy! He really tried to engage the class and add material that deviated from the normal SPAN curriculum. He gave several opportunities for extra credit and always answered the class's questions. I really liked that he let us ask things in English if we weren't understanding something completely. I'd really recommend his class!
Jon is SO NICE! Easily the best Spanish professor I have had. He actually cares about students and really wants the class to do well. He is SUCH a nice guy. You will be super happy with him!!!

Jon is a genuinely nice guy with a laid back personality. The curriculum is set by the department, but he does a great job of individualizing the material for his students. He is willing to make appointments if you can't make it to his office hours. Encourages people to speak Spanish in class without fear of making mistakes.

Jana is a sweet professor but lacks the ability to teach her students subject matter anywhere near in depth. Get ready to not have a life while you get quizzed on the most irrelevant content in her lectures. Hard to succeed in the course when the content is unorganized and sloppy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Jana is the sweetest professor I have had at UO. She genuinely cares about her students. However, the subject matter is extremely confusing and her lectures aren't super clear.

Just take Dr Connolly; she uses all of her video lectures, and uses the in-person lecture time to go through the pre-class quiz except she can't really give reasonings on a lot of problems. Just take Dr Connolly, you'll get better answers when you inevitably have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was much harder then it needed to be. These topics are ones you've most likely seen before but the class content, reviews, and practice problems do not cover the kinds of questions shown on the exams. The professor also seemed to confuse herself in lectures and thus confused everyone else making the content harder to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jana is really nice, but I had a difficult time learning in this class. I wish lectures were clearer. I feel like the exam questions were not straightforward. If biology doesn't come easily to you (it doesn't for me), then you should get prepared for this class. The practice problems are important.

Jana taught a hard class in Fall of 2022, and while the content was difficult, she was generally very smart and knew what she was talking about, the lectures were organized and it was clear she kept up on current research. I understand why some people didn't like her, but I felt her rambling and talking about herself kept us engaged

While the class, specifically lectures, is fast-paced, provided resources make keeping up much more manageable. I would suggest watching video lectures and taking notes before class so that you can listen and do clickers during the lecture. My biggest complaint is that practice tests/ practice resources do not resemble exam/ quiz content or style.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mandatory lectures are often a bit rambly and tangential, but other class resources (recorded videos and labs) were very useful for learning the content. Grading by GE's was often confusing so don't be afraid to ask for clarification. Jana was nice and approachable, even though some of her decisions about the class, in general, were questionable.

Jana is nice and will answer questions. Generally responds fast to emails. Is inclusive and takes time to address racial and sexist issues, respectful of pronouns

Not accommodating, condescending emails, difficult quiz every week that are useless for studying for the exam, attendance mandatory, but almost no material is ever covered during class
ONLY PROF IVE HAD IN THREE YEARS THAT I FELT TRULY UNDERSTOOD MY QUESTIONS AND FRUSTRATIONS AND MADE AN EFFORT TO ADRESS THEM. LECTURES CAN BE SCATTERED SOMETIMES SO OUTSIDE RESOURCES ARE HELPFUL.

She is very kind but not concise whatsoever. She rambled you will learn nothing at all in her lectures because theyre just so short. HOWEVER, her video lectures are incredibly helpful, so I highly recommend taking notes on these! She spent a lot of time recording them so theyre so useful. Easy class if you take notes this way, I promise!

This class was incredibly hard. If you want to pass make sure to make extra time to talk to GE's, use office hours, and practically teach yourself. The lectures were confusing and I felt like I didn't learn anything. The tests were incredibly hard and stuff would come up that we didn't go over in lectures. Even Einstein would be confused.
Terrible teacher in lecture, would rather read her textbook than listen to her teaching

Lectures are not very clear and what is written on the slide does not always match what she says verbally. Sometimes the information on the slides is inaccurate. Problems that she makes you solve, she does not do any examples in class, so you are left on your own to learn the material. Problem sets do not match the content that she does teach.

Jana is extremely knowledgeable and also very caring and sweet; however, she is very sloppy. Her curriculum/videos are FULL of spelling errors and she makes so many vocal and spelling mistakes that it actually makes it impossible to accurately absorb information. She's not a good teacher. Just use other sources and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Jana is a great professor, who clearly wants her students to succeed. The problem sets are really helpful for learning the material. There is a ton of information to learn, so make sure to keep up on the material. This isn't a class you can cram study for.

By far one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. Printing out the lecture slides to take notes on really does help. The problem sets and tests are insanely difficult, but if you spend forever studying, you will be okay.
Jana was always prepared for lecture and her power point was very helpful for homework and studying for tests.  Be prepared to work hard for your grade! Go to the study sessions, it is very helpful!

Really nice, very helpful one-on-one, but in class it was very hard to follow her. She  didn't really stress points that were key to understanding the material -- things like knowing that the inside of a cell was negative, which made understanding basically all of the material impossible. Be prepared to work HARD if taking over summer

Honestly one of the most enjoyable teachers I've ever had a UofO. She actually wants you to do well in your class, and has reasonable expectations. If you work a decent amount, you'll get the grade you want.

THE BEST professor I have ever had. I have never been so engaged in a lecture than I was in hers. She really wants her students to succeed and I would highly recommend her class. I took BA 215 and it was honestly my favorite class that term.
Great professor, always makes accounting actually interesting somehow, even if it is at 8 AM, 100% would reccomend taking her again.

Mumford is the actual goat. I came into BA211 very nervous given its rep, but ended up deciding to be an accounting major halfway through the class. She is so helpful and very knowledgeable about accounting & explains the content well and in ways that click for college aged kids. Cannot recommend her enough, I love accounting because of her. #goat

Prof. Mumford has a way with words because the way she explains accounting is amazing. She truly knows how to teach, its my first time taking a proper accounting class and she made it easy to understand. (i took BA 215 its not letting me select it)
Super approachable

I really don't know how students would get below a B+/A- in this class as long as you go to class every day. A young teacher who cares about students and understands what it is like to be in college. Tells you exactly what is going to be on the test, great professor.
Genuinely so goated. Easily top 3 professor I have had at UO. Super young too so she understands how kids function and whatnot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Cool Beans. she's pretty cool and will open office hours for anyone. would definitely take again if possible for higher classes.

She is one of the best teachers ive had at UO! Cares so much about her students doing well, super helpful outside of class with office hours, and her lectures are funny and have good references which makes it easy to stay engaged. I was intimidated at first with the pace and content, but the class is very doable with some time and effort.

She's lowkey the goat. Thought this class was gonna be hard as the first accounting class but she's a great teacher and made things very easy to understand. Make sure you pay attention in class though because these topics add onto each other and if you miss one you'll fall behind.
Best professor i've had at U of O. She also posts a lot of practice problems before exams which is super helpful
Content can be challenging but, she breaks it down in a way that makes sense. Super caring about students and clearly wants all students to pass. Best professor I've had so far!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The big JM is the Michael Jordan of accounting professors. Her lectures are entertaining and productive, she is super helpful and while the material difficult, getting a good grade if you study at least 10% is pretty easy. Overall I love this professor and want to take more classes with her.

She was really nice, but she talked through lectures SO fast. The clicker questions she gave dropped my grade substantially because she only gave like 30 secs-1 min to answer the math problems, and if you got them wrong, it counted against you, unlike in my math class. I BARELY got a B- in the class, and this is coming from a HS valedictorian lol.
she the truth, if you go to class and talk to her the class opens up and you realize it is easier than people say.
Fantastic teacher for a pretty difficult subject. Helpful review videos before every test. Definitely watch those and do the practice test and you will be good on the midterms and final.
She was a wonderful professor with a lot of professional experience. She truly cares about the success of her students and goes above and beyond to be accessible. Best professor I've ever had.
Best professor I've had at UO. Lectures are very engaging and she gives a ton of study materials to make sure you are ready for exams. Class is hard by nature but definitely is a must-take for 211.
First time professor, she explained course material very well and gave lots of opportunity to go over things you don't understand. Clearly cares about student success.
It was her first time ever teaching, but she did a great job. She clearly cares about student success and puts effort into finding what students need to best prepare them for exams

One of the best professors I've had so far at UO. With a challenging class like Financial Accounting, it's crucial to have a knowledgeable and understanding professor, and that's exactly what she provides. She truly cares about her students and is very accommodating, especially with her office hours. I highly recommend taking her!

Easily the best professor at UO. She really cares about her students and is very accessible through office hours or email to provide assistance. The course content is what it is, but she does her best to make lectures entertaining and informative. I would highly recommend taking classes with her if you can.

Jaqueline is such an amazing professor. Material can be challenging, but just by the nature of the course. Jacqueline gives you so many opportunities to learn and is so accessible and personable in class and in office hours. She truly cares about her student's success and has so many amazing resources to help you do well on exams.

She is a really good professor! All of the lectures are engaging and relevant. She prepares you really well for the midterms with practice questions and review videos. I highly recommend taking financial accounting with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She made the class way more engaging than I thought it would be! Very good at teaching.

Best professor I've had at the UO! I'm not going into accounting but professor mumford make the subject so fun. I will say lecture goes pretty fast but she gives plenty of helpful resources to work with outside of class.

Probably one of the best professors at the University, very accessible and is also very helpful if you have questions on anything you have related to accounting homework or exams.  Would recommend attending office hours if you do have any questions that seem to be major in anyway, get the help weeks earlier before the midterm than week of it.

Professor Mumford is a great professor as offers a lot of chances to understand the lessons taught and provides enough office hours to go in and ask for clarification. She is really flexible with scheduling as long as you email her. Her lectures are fast paced and in order to pass, you need to study and pay attention in class.
Jesse really cares about his students and wants to succeed. Jesse gives great advice as well.

Jesse seems to really care about what he does, which was nice. The lectures can get a little boring. The best part of the class was the guest speakers who were brought in at the end. The worst part was the attempted full-class policy simulation.
Professor Maldonado was a very inspirational person to talk to after class and his feedback and advice were very helpful for me. Great guy overall!

Jesse is one of the most down-to-earth profs I've ever had. Teaching is his side-gig, his main job is literally working in Eugene's public policy mechanisms so you'll spend just as much time discussing local politics & guest lectures as you will with the textbook. Highly recommend.
meh. relies too much on his own experience as a young career politician.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jesse is a very down-to-earth instructor. His day job is working in the field, and has very current experience in the system. We always discuss the current news before jumping in class. His lectures are very textbook-based. However, the second half is largely guest lectures and unique presentations. Would highly recomend.

Jesse is a really nice guy and this is not a hard class, not always the most interesting though. He starts class off with what's going on in the news in relation to policy which was cool but the lectures themselves are just from the textbook. The guest speakers however were always super knowledge and fantastic.

I didn't expect to like this class, but I did. I took it in Winter 2024, and it was one of his first classes as a professor. He's caring, knowledgeable, and kind. He's always willing to help and responds quickly to emails. The class was easy but interesting. Even without reading the textbook, I got an A. If you put in effort, you'll do great.

It was his first term teaching and I think he did a great job. He clearly cares a lot about the subject he is teaching, but it was also pretty apparent he was figuring it out. My only real complaint is the amount of time spent each lecture talking about news and answering questions. Not necessarily bad, it just gets tiring when it's to this extent.

Jesse is one of the best professors I've had at UO so far. I needed this class for my major and wasn't expecting much out of it because it's an intro-level class but it was so interesting. He's really engaging in all of his lectures and is so understanding when it comes to assignments. I hope to take one of his classes again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Jesse in as a professor in PPPM201 and without a doubt, it was one of my favorite lectures by far at UO. Jesse did so much to make class engaging and interesting. We talked often about current events, news, and issues, both in the community and on a bigger, national scale. Jesse is a super cool, younger professor, who's always down to talk.

Talks like a robot, very boring, slight accent. Amazing teacher, goes over plenty of practice problems, and very well made and helpful slides. Very organized course overall. Finishes early almost every class. Go to class and you will learn everything you need to know for HW and exams (but yes classes are very boring).

Really rough class. OBA312 is hard enough as it is without the long lectures. He seems like a nice enough guy, but his lectures were hard to follow at times with his voice being pretty monotone and having a bit of a strong accent. Difficult class to take online, but he seemed very willing to help students succeed.

Ming's class is lecture heavy and involves a lot of examples and working through problems. The content itself is pretty straightforward if you attend class regularly. He is very reasonable with grading and hw assignments are always helpful when preparing for exams. Some of the class is Excel-based but it also involves other statistics problems.

The lecture videos for the class are very boring. They take a long time to watch. The midterm and final are both very tricky are just harder versions of the practice test. I found it best to teach myself the content from the slides and not waste time watching the lecture videos. The class can be very low time commitment if you do it right.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Jin is way over-hated in the school of business - his thick accent does not make him impossible to understand. His lectures can be boring, but the way the course is set up makes it easy to get a good grade. As long as you attend class and work through the in-class problems, that is more than enough for preparing for the exams.

Honestly, I think he's a great professor. His classes are all lectures but he goes through all the materials in detail making it quite easy to follow. The bare minimum is to attend class and you'll pass the class. I would take the course again with him if I could. Plus he lets you have a whole page of notes for the exams which is really nice.

Professor Jin tough person to grade. His lectures were clearly written, but he just reads directly off his slides for 2 hours in a thick accent. Homework/study guide is in depth, but the final was very different (unlike the midterm, which reflected the content of the course well). Everyone failed the final, so the class was curved massively

this man is so inconsiderate! He does not protect the safety of his students when a woman on drugs was in his classroom and making students uncomfortable he acted like class was going on as normal. He made the midterm the day after the election and a take home test due during thanksgiving break. He doesn't even use excel for an excel based class.

This professor has a heavy accent so can be hard to understand sometimes. He is very caring and wants his students to succeed. The assignments prepare you well for the tests, but the midterm was pretty difficult. He doesn't fail students which makes the class less stressful. Would recommend.

Barely any work, only a Canvas homework every week or two and a quiz every now and then. Make sure you are nailing these easy points! The midterm was pretty difficult but you are allowed a large cheat sheet so as long as you are prepared with that, you'll be fine. Great flexible online class for those busy schedules, I totally recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jin teaches by example, so be prepared to follow along with example problems and copy down formulas in your notes. In my book this isn't a bad thing, and in fact makes it easier internalizing the necessary info for exams. I don't have too many thoughts on Jin, because his overall performance as a professor isn't outstanding but gets the job done.
Nice professor. Hard exams but a really easy class overall. Doesn't fail students which is cool.

Professor Jin is an all around great professor. He understand that Business Analytics isn't everyone's calling. Due to this, he passes everyone as long as you complete every assignment and just try to learn the material. His accent is hard to understand but all around very nice guy and very knowledgable person.

Impossible to understand, reads lecture slides for 2 hrs straight, doesn't go into detail (if you ask for clarification he most likely won't even understand what you're asking), doesn't let us use excel on the midterm for an excel based class, very few assignments in the class so grade is weighted heavily based on midterm/final. Avoid if you can.

He is one of the only OBA professors who could teach the material in a way that was easy to understand and follow. He is extremely knowledgeable and cares about his students. I would recommend taking any OBA class with him.
Protect this man at all costs. Super nice and cares about what he teaches. The accent can be hard, but he clearly shows how to do example problems and will always answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems very knowledgeable but he has a VERY heavy accent that makes it hard to understand him. Adding to that, he talks fast, making it harder to understand him. Also, his English is not very good, so when people ask him a question, he will repeat the same thing he just said as if he rehearsed what he as going to say and that is all he knows.

Perfectly decent professor. His lectures clearly explained how to solve every type of problem on the homework (HW) as well as the exams (with a few exceptions). The modules/lectures are long and the HW can be long as well, so give yourself plenty of time. He allows a formula sheet on exams and you pass if you complete all HW and exams.

If you don't already have a good background in statistics, then don't take his class. However, if you are good at statistics and enjoy it, then you will find his class very easy. We have 5 homework assignments for the term, a midterm, and a final. So the tests are weighted pretty heavily, but overall not too bad.

If you can take ANY OTHER professors for OBA 312 or 335, DO IT. This is my first week, and already I CAN NOT tolerate his fast-talking speed COMBINED with his heavy accent any longer, like many others said, he would literally just read his pdf for 2 hrs straight, and barely any student-instructor exists.

Extremely long, difficult to follow lecture videos. Only 7 graded assignments for the entire term, so you better be good at what youre doing. Seems like a nice guy, just not one I would like to take an online class with again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a well designed online course in statistics. The lectures were thorough and clear and incorporated practice problems throughout. If you take notes while listening to the lecture videos and do the practice problems in order, you'll go great on the tests. Overall, it was a really great course.
Hard to understand, goes through things quickly, I don't understand whats going on the majority of the time but am banking on the fact that its online to help me with the midterm and tests
All you need to do is show up to class and do the example with him, tests are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Go to class and get an easy A

reviews.comment: Professor Ming Jin is a great teacher that would go through every problem, exercise, and example step by step during the lecture that could give us a chance to practice the problems. The lecture slides are very clear.

This guy shows up, opens up his powerpoint, and reads from it for the entire 2 hours. Everything he says is almost like it is read from a script. He doesn't even say hello. It is also very difficult to understand what he says. His classes are very easy, because the answers on his test go in a pattern: #1 is A, #2 is B, #3 is C, #4 is D, repeat.

Minimal diversity in architects/places during lectures: Corbusier, FLW, and Colin Rowe. Lectures will put you to sleep! (Lights off, lulling voice). 100+ pages of reading of dense philosophical/architectural jargon each week that show up on the test. Taught jointly with Esther. You can miss up to 6 classes, though.
