I have had 2 other Span Profs at UofO and both of them surpassed Juanita as teachers by a long shot. Nice person but highly critical. She hardly let us speak Spanish in class, we could never choose our own partners or subjects for projects. Always telling us to be creative but her classes were very boring. Not a native speaker and plays favorites.

Juanita is a great professor.  I loved her class.  The only constructive critism is I think we could of spoke Spanish more but she is a great teacher.  I think she is very entertaining and pushes for creativeness, which is nice.  You could never think too far outside of the box for her, which was nice.  I would highly recommend her to anyone.

Juanita is a fun professor who makes class go by fast while being productive.  Her stories are fun much fun and by the time tests come around you feel very prepared.  Also, Juanita makes an effort to get to know students on a more personal level rather than just handing out grades....a great class overall.

Superb instructor and person. Juanita is really in to her students, and tries to get to know them on a personal level as well. Great class, she made it fun...I took it in the summer and had a blast! Take this class from Juanita for sure, tests are very fair (essays and defining vocabulary in Spanish). There is also a group presentation (not so bad)
No Comments
Juanita is by far the coolest!
Love her leftist politics and stories about Chiapas. Really good teacher.
She is a wonderful, fun teacher who really tries to make it all understandable

This professor focuses the course on her interests rather than allowing students to bring in their own creative ideas. She also continuously calls out students and student work during lectures on assignments she gives little to no detail on. Along with this, she also selects a few she likes to call out and create conflict with over and over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I have been in Kuttis' class for 2 terms now, and I can safely say she is the best prof I have ever had. She goes above and beyond for her students, like helping me connect with possible future careers as I am near post-grad.

She's okay, the concept of the class is like 3rd grader stuff. The midterm is the hardest part, its on Canvas in-class and it's closed notes. Everything else is pretty easy, good to have friends in the class if you miss a class. She lovesss AI and it's really weird.
Easy class and nice teacher. Her class is very easy. But, the majority of your grade relies on attendance (JCOM202 was taught at 8am).

I graduated from oregon over four years ago and have gone into a professional career into media relations and i can safely say professor kuttis was BY FAR the worst professor i have ever had at oregon. She never provided enough context, was moody, would lash out at students and also just has no idea how modern media relations work.

Kuttis is not as communicative as she says, does not answer her emails. Attendance is mandatory but she talks the entire time and randomly assigns things for attendance that sometimes arent relevant at all. Condescending and rude to students that ask questions and is overall just rude and not helpful

Great passion for storytelling, but can be very condescending when responding to questions. Often, you will feel inferior when asking questions, even though they are encouraged. Prepare yourself to listen to her speak while you are doing assignments. She will often hand out papers and talk the entire time you are completing it (hard to focus).

I would take this class again if I needed to, it wasn't that bad. It was incredibly easy and there was little to no homework and zero readings. She appreciates when you are one time, and will call you out if you are more than 15 minutes late, and she'll call you out if you are not paying attention and are messing around on your computer.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly mixed reviews with Kathryn, but I thought she was a great teacher. Always willing to provide insight & my writing has definitely improved because of this class. She has experience in corporate comm so thats kind of what she focuses on. What some may see as “harsh,” I see as her being honest and wanting to help students improve their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are a lot of mixed reviews about Kathryn, but she is an amazing teacher who cares about her students and gives great feedback. At first, her feedback can seem blunt (even harsh), but I really appreciate the honesty. Take the time to get to know her, be polite in class, and be respectful of her and your classmates, you will have no problem!

I love Kathryn. Her lectures are funny, engaging and actually applicable to the real world. She also went over several professional paths that you can go down with a PR degree, which was extremely helpful. 
I had a smaller class, so it was nice to get more personal and get one-on-one advice. Kathryn ily don't listen to the haters

Literally worst professor ever. She is so incredibly confusing, passive aggressive, and plain annoying. She also is weirdly touching without asking and it made me so uncomfortable. It was so incredibly easy which was the only good thing and sometimes ended early but it was almost too easy that I didn't learn anything. I hated her by the end.

Kathryn is one of the most supportive and engaging instructors I've had at the UO. Her clear and thoughtful feedback helps you grow as a writer. The class is structured well, balancing lectures, hands-on writing, and real-world applications. She genuinely cares about her students' success and always encourages creativity and improvement.

I will never take a class from this professor EVER again. Genuinely the worst experience I have ever had. Not only did she make condescending comments to me and other students, she was extremely passive aggressive and got too close and comfortable with students. I felt personally attacked many times, and even left crying one class.

it's for JCOM 371; she's actually such an amazing teacher and is really involved, no complaints and the work is applicable to future career options and relatively easy to keep up with material in class; no readings, essays, big tests

You have to get on her good side. This won't be hard if you just stroke her ego and ask about all those Fortune 500 companies she's worked with. She has great insights, but she's quick to get angry and call people out. Some of her assignments were helpful, but many lacked a clear purpose and relevancy to the course materials.
She is inspiring and a great teacher. Learned the most from her I have ever learned in college.

Does not provide clear grading criteria. Kuttis will sometimes give feedback in person or in class and then forget about her suggestions and grade you down on suggestions she requested. More clear and consistent grading material would be helpful.

Professor Kuttis cares about her students. She is willing to meet outside of class times and will respond to emails at odd hours or on weekends. There is a lot of group work in the class, and she gives good feedback, although her delivery is sometimes unnecessarily harsh. She sometimes gives pop quizzes or pop assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I am a Kathryn lover to my core. She is a tough grader, but wants all of her students to succeed. As long as you are willing to put in the work, you should be okay. Best to get on her good side
genuinely the worst professor I have ever had

Extremely condescending to students and definitely not a good teacher for people who have anxiety, because she will call you out (especially people of color) for literally the smallest things, like if you're not sitting right. I honestly believe she does it out of entertainment and enjoyment for herself. A straight up bully.

Kathryn is very condescending and lacks empathy. She often calls students out/and makes them feel bad for not having a correct answer. Her canvas was confusing with due dates changing frequently with no announcements and unclear instructions. Her grading was harsh with the comments not matching the actual grade.

Kuttis is awesome. on average I'm a B-level student so I know and honest review when I see one. she makes the class not extremely difficult and reiterates how her class should not cause you too much stress. she doesn't force a ton of readings which makes the class enjoyable to be in. Group assignments that take no more than 20-30 mins.

Campaigns with Kathryn is tough. She doesn't provide much structure for what she wants to see in your projects and is extremely critical and somewhat rude about your work. I have excelled in all my PR courses but Kathryn has made me feel bad about work that I was proud of. She has deffinetly prepared me for the real world....

Kathryn will be one of your harshest critics but that is only because she sees your potential and wants you to see it too. Kathryn's campaigns class was difficult, but the experience and things I learned from her were priceless. I know that I will be able to walk into the job world because of Kathryn and for that, I will be forever grateful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: IK Kathryns reputation in the J school is not the best however, she really is a great resource for PR majors. From personal experience, I was not a fan of her or her class until senior year. After I began going to office hours, asking for help, and really trying with course work I realized how great Kathryn really is. She will be there for you!!

I had Kathryn for J100 & J454. Her teaching style is inconsistent, unclear and does not foster a positive learning environment. Instead of feeling like she was a resource I could go to for help, she consistently left both me and my group feeling defeated without offering us help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kuttis is the worst professor I've had yet. She is a bully to not only her students but guest speakers as well. It is almost impossible to get an A in her class, she told me so herself. Would not recommend anyone to take a class from her. She is down right disrespectful and inconsiderate and condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Plainly stated, Kathryn Kuttis is a bully. She consistently berated students in class and encouraged her other students to do so too. She is inflexible and condescending. The class itself was fine because she didn't do much teaching, but I would never take a class from her again. Would not recommend under any circumstances.

I personally loved Kathryn. She picked amazing speakers for us and I was enthralled by the majority of them. There are reflections based on each speaker at the end of every class, so attendance is mandatory. No final. Participation is based on the amount and relevance of your Tweets throughout the course, and how respectful you are in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was a decent teacher and provided many interesting guest speakers. She was never rude to me and I find that the students she was rude to were expecting her to change her rules for them, so that they could pass the class without having to show up. I don't think she deserves the bad wrap and would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Would not recommend unless you want a C in a two credit class. There is no final or midterm but that does not matter since Kathryn makes up her own rules when it comes to final grades. This class is based around guest speakers but somehow you are suppose to give 120% participation to get a good grade, even when she does not tell you what 120% is..

Kuttis has an outstanding career track and has proven to be a very successful woman. However as a professor she is undermining and rude to both students and guest speakers. She gave many inaccurate final grades after grading participation and professionalism at the very end of the term. Would not recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: To get an A in this class, Im not sure what you have to do. Its definitely not outlined in the syllabus, because even if you follow those standards and exceed them, you will still receive a poor grade. Even through she never learns any of her 400 students names in the class, she still grades you on participation. So horribly unfair and bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Is an easy course but Kathryn is extremely disrespectful even though she preaches that students give respect to the lecturer. Calls people out in class while speaker is talking, and is an overall distraction. I had 100% all term and it managed to drop 9% because of my participation even though I surpassed the average standards do not recommend sry
Super easy course and had the chance to learn a lot from the speakers. Kathryn is easily accessible outside of class and if you show up and take the reflection quizzes youll get an A easy.

Even if you attend class, participate to the extent she asks, properly complete all assignments, and behave professionally she will still find a way to mark you down. Unfortunately this is a mandatory class for all pre-J students but was heavily skewed towards Advertising students. She is not kind and unaccomodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best class I have ever taken in my entire life.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kathryn is very intimidating, and spends most of class trying to find and call out students who might be on their phones for a split second, or are even just slouching. She also tends to interrupt the speakers quite a lot, and is in general a teacher who is not well-liked by students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She cares about her class and has high expectations, but can often be rude to students and speakers. She tends to interrupt and will call out students to the entire class over trivial things. It's easy and fun but I think it's because she's not the one talking the whole time.

Kathryn Kuttis has been one of my favorite professors at U of O. She is smart, funny, and knows her stuff. But just know she's only a great teacher if you're a good student. If you're going to skip class, be on your phone, or talk, she is not afraid to call you out on it. This is an important lesson though; you need to learn how to be professional.

Kathryn comes off very intense she has little tolerance for students that aren't in class to get an education. If you pay attention and show up you're golden, if you text in class and have chatty friends find another professor cause she will not just pass you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kathryn is a good professor, and I definitely recommend her. She's funny and gives engaging lectures. Yes, she's known to call out and be little harsh sometimes, but it all comes from a place of love. She really cares about making us into professionals. She's a little intimidating to approach, but it's worth it.

While this class is super easy to pass, Kathryn is HORRIBLE. She walks around the huge lecture hall the entire class period looking for students to call out in front of the entire class, even calling students out for even just sitting a certain way. She is so rude and makes everyone very uncomfortable. This class is the worst part of my week.
We use Twitter in class # revolutionary

Professor Kuttis clearly outlines her J100 expectations at the start of the class: Show up on time and be attentive. No homework,  no tests  this is the academic equivalent of needing only a heartbeat to pass. The flipside to this approach is similarly outlined in the consequences for anyone who falls asleep in class: Immediate ejection and a totalitarian approach to attendance. But no one in the SOJC hides that classes in this school are meant to teach soft skills as well. Attentiveness and networking can't be learned by sleeping through lecture no more than jobs can be done in the real world by ignoring work.
reviews.rating_tags: LECTURE HEAVY--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Avoid Kuttis for the intro level PR class if you can. She's pretty moody and inconsistent in her teaching. Every class was based on her personal interests and ignored a lot of aspects of PR.
So disrespectful, unhelpful, unorganized,  mean, unprofessional to students AND guest speakers? Worst teacher--do not take.
WORST teacher I have had in the SOJC. Avoid at all costs--completely unfair and unorganized. Only gives lectures on personal interests. Full of herself.

I have never worked harder for a professor before, but I have also never learned as much. She is an incredible teacher with real-world experience. She is direct, honest and real. She holds her students to high standards. I think students who don't take her classes are missing out on key life skills.

As a required class for the J school, I expected more from this course. Kathryn is very disrespectful to students and guest speakers and will only help/care about you if you are interested in PR. She makes the classroom feel like a very hostile and awkward environment in what should otherwise be a fun class. Very disappointed in this course.
Loved her attitude, passion, and willingness to teach.

I usually like teachers who challenge students and don't take any bs, but I've never had a prof who is so intimidating. Kathryn is incredibly smart and talented, but she is really difficult to talk with. She can be very harsh even when you're trying your best. The overall class environment is stressful and feels like you're walking on eggshells.

Kathryn is an incredible teacher who has a hilarious sense of humor. Although she may seem hard hitting, she really cares about her students and just wants them to do well. She is not one for bs so don't try. If you listen and pay attention you will do great. Paying attention is key, get on her good side and you are golden.

Kathryn is intelligent and witty but be warned. She's disrespectful to any student that doesn't get things the first time around. She isn't approachable for questions and she was personally insulting to me a number of times. A comment she sent to me via email reduced me to tears. Intelligent? Yes. Compassionate and respectful? No.

At first she can seem really intimidating, but she really only wants the best future for her students and she's not gonna help you get there by beating around the bush. She has an amazing background in public relations and is always willing to share to inspire. It wouldn't hurt to go to office hours just to introduce yourself.

She has lots of experience and can make lectures interesting, but she doesn't take into consideration that there different types of students in her class. She thinks everyone thinks quick and on their feet like her. Also, she will call students out in the middle of lecture and is not that approachable when asking questions individually.

Amazing professor-very motivating and provides students with a dynamic and a fresh perspective on careers in PR. Lectures are informative and interesting; Kathyrn's  powerpoints are effective & artistic (she has a uniquecool style). Definitely take a class with her, you'll benefit from having an inside perspective on the PR industry.
TAKE THIS PROF. Great presence in class and willing to help one on one whenever necessary. It's very apparent that she wants you to be in the best position for your professional future. Do it.
This class was amazing. She is super funny and has had a very fascinating life.  #j100
Her lectures were different and fun, she makes jokes and explains and helps really well.
She's super cool and I aspire to be like her.
This is a very fun class. Kathryn has high energy, and creates an environment conducive to personal and academic growth and success.

Kathryn is the best teacher at UofO! Take any of her classes. She is hilarious, excited about what she does, and genuinely cares about all of her students. Awesome lady & prof! Learned so much & got inspired in this class. Never skipped because I enjoyed the class and all of the interesting guest speakers.
I really liked the class. Kathryn makes it fun and enjoyable
Kathryn has been one of my favorite professors at UO yet. As a public relations major, she made me excited about the field everyday in her class. Kathryn is a great J prof!

She is a very good teacher and I found the lectures to be interesting most of the time, however the way the course is designed does not give any reason to go to the lectures because everything can be do online. Overall it's a super easy class and she's a very kind professor.

Her class was very easy to pass because all the work and instruction were online, so going to class was totally optional. However, she did mention that she will run classes differently in the future because she's seen a decline in attendance. Lectures were hard to sit through and the most feedback I had gotten from an assignment was "good"

DONT TAKE HER. I literally fell asleep every class. Thankfully her in-class assignments are available online so you don't have to go! The assignments are a little confusing because she explains them differently in-class than they're written on Canvas. There's 1 exam online and a couple confusing projects. Easy class, didn't like her tho.

Very easy class. She doesn't take attendance and all of the quizes are online open book. No reason to go to class what so ever. Very easy A plus. She's pretty nice when talking to her and very understanding about life if you email her. She let me retake some things I missed.

I enjoyed Professor Kazmi's class. At least one of the projects weren't very straight forward and confusing to understand, but other than that this class was great. She tries to make the classes a little more entertaining as she's teaching which is also nice.

Attendance is not mandatory. She made the class fun to be in; there were only 2 assignments per week, one mini quiz and one in-class assignment. Both can be done in class. Funny person, likes being relatable and hearing from the audience. Be ready for point-heavy projects, but easy to complete. Don't buy the textbook; you don't need it.

The only work was 1 easy in-class assignment and quiz once a week with no homework. There was three very heavily graded projects which if you do badly on will completely tank your grade. She offers a good amount of extra credit and there is no midterms. The final is also online. Overall pretty interesting class and attendance is not mandatory.

The reading killed me before I realized she goes over it in the lectures. She seems like a nice lady but the content of this class can be boring. If you show up, skim reading, do the in-class assignments it's easy to pass. Topics can be interesting if you go more in depth and apply the terms outside of class. Our GE's were tough graders at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I feel like this instructor is out of the book for all her slides and lectures. Her classes are not engaging, and she has made an effort to tell the class that she will not learn your name. You can pass this class easily, so if you're looking for a low effort class, this is it, but it did not contribute to me learning much of anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her assignments were very unclear

JCOM 456 - Surprised by the other ratings. Saima was a great professor & obviously very passionate about the course topics. Consists of 3 tests (lowest dropped), 5 group case studies, 2 group presentations, a report and a journal diary. Some content could be boring but class was relatively easy & always gave class time to work/ended early

Saima was a really good journalism professor, but the lectures were a bit boring. All assignments were graded by GEs. Some GEs sucked at grading and would poorly grade you on the same assignment you turned in as a group project compared to another GE that would give full remarks for the assignment.

Personally went to this class twice and I have an A. The cheat code is having someone send you the quiz code from class and that's about it. Assignments are graded by amazing tas who grade easily. The two times I did go to the lecture Kazmi just didn't give me the best vibe, and I'm all about energy girl. Mainly why i couldn't get myself to go tbh

This class was easy and straightforward. Lectures sometimes feel like she's rambling, but if you show up and complete the in-class assignments and quizzes it's an easy A. You can get by with skimming the reading before class, most of it is gone over in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring class and content, but also incredibly easy to pass. As long as you do in class activities and quizzes, you can easily get a good grade without much effort.

Incredibly rude and harsh rules. Despite attendance not being required during the lecture, the assignments and tests are only available on Canvas during class time. She is often incredibly late uploading slides to Canvas. Highly do not recommend. 0/10 experience.

You can't use your laptop to take notes, but you can use your phone. She's strict and is a tough grader, even though she claims to be lenient. Beware of her accent, it makes it hard to understand at times, and she often gets hung up on words and it becomes painful to listen to.
Given the boring material, she did a good job of keeping lecture engaging to the best of her ability. It's a pretty easy class, as long as you show up and do most of the readings

Kazmi brings the best she can to the class's boring required curriculum. Very easy and consistent class format (T/R lectures: T lecture + activity, R lecture + open-note open-book quiz). Textbook "needed" but I read it like once, plus it's free online! A few assignments that are a piece of cake if you follow the rubric. Adds pop culture examples!

Kazmi creates an interactive environment for lectures and succeeds in keeping the material relevant despite the content (media/technology) frequently expanding and changing. Attending classes is crucial because most assignments can only be accessed/done in class, which was frustrating at times. Other than that, I was always engaged. Do recommend!

There's usually required reading before class, but it's all useful to the course content. They're not a harsh grader and are also super flexible with deadlines. I felt like I was very supported as a student by this teacher, but make sure you participate during class...it gets awkward real fast if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best professors I've had at Oregon State and it was an online class. She is clearly very interested in what she teaches, and it shows vibrantly in her lectures. One of few professors who will keep their door open constantly because she actually cares about her students immensely.  I'm taking more classes in Physics due to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kathy is an incredible instructor. She has so much knowledge to impart, and her enthusiasm for the subject just pours through her lectures. She enjoys discussion settings, and so constantly encourages students to ask questions. She wants to make the material accessible to everyone, so she is always willing to help. Bottom line, she's great.

This class only has 4 assignments, which amount to 90% of your grade so be prepared to lock in. Attendance is mandatory and taken every class. Ken is very kind and knowledgeable, he makes a sometimes boring and dense topic engaging and easier to follow with his stories or examples
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are interesting but can drag on and I've almost fell asleep multiple times during class. The grading is 10% attendance, 45% on the midterm, and 45% on the final. He curves HEAVILY to the point where the class average was curved from a 63% to an 85%. The low score on the midterm even got curved from a 28% to a 69%. Good class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every lecture was a journey through the subject accommodated by his extensive sports knowledge and array of stories. If I could tell people to take 1 professor at UO it would be Ken, this was my 3rd class with him and I wish I had more.

Great professor. Lectures are long and can get boring at times (it's law though, what do you expect), but he tries to keep things engaging with stories, examples, videos, and even a short debate our class did. NO MORE POP QUIZZES. Exams are hard but curved. Doing the reading helps. Attendance is graded. Overall, he's fun and cares about the class.

Ken is one of the greatest professors at UO. His class is engaging if you listen and all you have to do is show up and pay attention and you're basically guaranteed to pass. He's funny and he cares about the stuff he lectures on. I would take all of his classes again.

Ken is awesome! He gives really good feedback and teaches content that is very relevant. He is very passionate about what he does and he will always be open to help you if you ask for it. The lectures can get boring at times but I would still highly recommend. TESTS ARE CURVED AN INSANE AMOUNT MAKING IT ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO FAIL!!!

i took sbus 250 : ken is maybe the sweetest professor i have ever spoken to. he really really cares about sports and the class. there are quite a bit of readings, which you have to do because there are 8 reading quizzes, but its not horrible. if you listen in class and then take notes on the presentations which he posts later, you should get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ken is a super genuine human. He wants you to succeed and it shows with his student-friendly late policy. If you read all the material and pay attention the class you can easily pass. The paper grades are usually all within the B range. Tests are a bit difficult but there is a large curve. I would reccomend Ken for BA 325.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class wasn't very hard and Ken is a good guy. The surprise quizzes really tanked my grade. They are hard to prepare for because the readings are over 40 pages and he asks very specific questions. Lectures could get boring, but Ken always tried to keep students engaged. Overall good guy, just get ready to read and ready for hard pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Getting an A in this course is challenging, but don't worry about failing. Most paper grades were between a B- and B+ for the class. The only negative is there are surprise quizzes that are hard to prepare for. Taking notes and reading in-depth is the best way to prepare.Overall Ken is a super nice guy and very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ken is nice and funny with a lot of knowledge about sports, but his lectures are long and you need to do the pre-work and/or readings to keep up. His midterm was quite difficult because many answers could have easily seemed correct unless you paid full attention and studied extremely hard. Attendance is mandatory with a physical sheet or pop quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ken's class has required attendance via a sign in sheet and/or pop quizzes. The class is graded only on the papers, attendance/pop quizzes and the midterm test. The midterm test is very difficult as he has his own way of thinking about it. I asked Ken for help on a paper, he was very condescending, vague, and unhelpful.

Ken's sports knowledge is unmatched, he can talk about any sporting event endlessly. This might be the only reason the class is interesting. He reads off slides the entire class period and doesn't post the PowerPoint. Graded by some writing assignments and a group project at the end. Doesn't grade unreasonably but isn't necessarily easy either.

Ken was extremely knowledgable on sports conflict resolution. His classes were incredibly interesting and thought provoking. One of my favorite lectures dove into how The U (Miami football) transformed American football and our implicit biases of the African American athlete. Thank you for all your hard work Ken!

He knows EVERYTHING you would ever need to know about sports and then some. He is highly knowledgable about the history behind how sports began and the time periods. He assigns a decent amount of reading, but his exams are difficult. However, if you do bad he curves it (in some instances). Overall, he is a very nice, funny and pleasant professor.
This guy is passionate about his sports and loves what he does!

Great teacher very enthused about sports. There are many classes under the CRES 410 tag, this one was soccer and sports conflict. Super interesting class if you are interested in Soccer. Grade is 40% midterm 45% final, 15% quizzes you will have at undisclosed times. Very professional individual.
Love this class!Ken is a cool guy i would recommend this class if you need the credit.

Ken's classes are extremely interesting because they blend current sports news with historical references that help you to grasp the larger issues at hand. Ken is an amazing story teller and a fountain of knowledge when it comes to sports statistics (all sports, soccer, football, baseball, etc). I would definitely take any of his classes again.

Keith is such a sweet and caring professor! He not only encourages others while we learn ASL, but he also makes the class fun and engaging! Attendance technically isn't mandatory, but I HIGHLY recommend going, as you will have the best time!
Keith is literally the best. He is so supportive of new learners and is so helpful. He is also so funny and tells stories all the time. Take his classes I would highly recommend

TAKE HIS CLASSES!!! Keith is my favorite professor in the whole university. He is so kind and patient with students who are new to ASL. I just finished my last class with Keith (ASL 203) and I am so sad that I can't do another year. 
also,
Go to class everyday you can and try. I promise its worth it

I've taken ASL with both Keith and Chad and while Chad is a good teacher, I love being in Keith's class. He tells very funny stories and is willing to work with students to help them out, and doesn't count it against you if you mess up. Attendance isn't graded, but attending frequently really helps with picking up the language.

He was genuinely the kindest professor I had throughout my first year, he is straightforward to work with and the classes were fun!! don't be afraid to ask for help, and even though attendance isn't mandatory I still really suggest going for the active signing experience.

Lectures are mostly going over vocab, but as fewer people show up (attendance isn't graded) he tells more personal, funny stories. Very patient with novice signers. He gives the homework/quiz answers in class if you go!

Where do you even begin? Chuck has no real business or management background, yet he constantly tears into student work and invents extreme scenarios to discredit projects. It's nearly impossible to have a productive discussion because he always pushes back. Ironically, he cites the Dunning-Kruger effect while clearly missing the point himself.

Chuck is an excellent professor. Make yourself known to Chuck. Work hard. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. I didn't use it once. Be prepared for harsh feedback. Massive group project! Come to class prepared and participate. Don't slack off, Chuck fact-checks everything in your project. Chuck teaches so many valuable concepts.

He's a very, very hard grader. But it's because he wants to challenge you to do good, which I respect. His lectures are fun and the class was honestly a great time, despite being challenging. He cares about his students. Overall he's a fine choice just be ready to put 100% effort into the class for a decent grade.

Great class in theory, but any useful assignment is overshadowed by the mammoth group project. Nightmare class if you get stuck with a group of people who don't pull their own weight. He sometimes gives useful feedback on writing assignments, but overall the course doesn't quite fulfill teaching its promised skills.

Chuck is a good teacher and I think anyone who takes his class will comes away with something they didnt have before. That being said he is not an easy grader by any means and expects things to be in a very particular way. Still a nice guy and always there to help, just wants you to work hard.

This class is very specifically focused on one group project and a multitude of other small homework assignments. The project takes up a ton of time, but I learned a lot from this class and this project specifically.

This class is solely based on one big group project, a presentation, and a few written assignments. The group project takes up a lot of time. He rarely gives out A's, but if you work hard you can get a good grade. Really good teacher and class, but time consuming. Your grade can also be effected by how your group rates you and your professionalism.

He is a tough grader, and it's hard to get an A in his class. This class has lots of group projects that can be very challenging. Worse, if you have social anxiety. But he cares for his students' improvements. He pushes you to get out of your comfort zone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I've never felt so motivated to excel in a class before. He made me feel valued, and at the same time, pushed me to succeed.

Chuck cares about the improvement of his students. He is a tough grader, but prepares you for the real business world by giving you clear assignments that push your limits. If you are engaged in class and put effort into the main group project, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Chuck cares a lot about the success of his students. There are a lot of readings and homework. The group project is a lot of work so try and get ahead of it. I'm not sure if anyone got an A in the class so be mentally prepared.

I have mixed feelings about this class, I think Chuck is a great teacher and I learn a lot but I'm one of those persons that prefers to do my own work and I absolutely hate public speaking.  I'm sure you have to do presentations/group work in other BA 352 classes.  I dreaded this class everyday but it has pushed me further out of my comfort zone.

Chuck is honestly the best professor I've ever had. Hardest grader -- I don't think anyone in my class got an A. But I learned SO MUCH from him. BA352 pretty much changed my groups lives because we became such great friends and had a great time learning in class.

Awful. Class is a regurgitated "motivational" handbook. Chuck does not teach, just shows old "inspirational" videos you could get from UpWorthy. Workload was moderate, all of your grade hinges on two assignments. My advice? You'll get the same assignmentworkload in every 352 class, but skip the migraine that is Chuck. 010 do not recommend

He was always interested in helping his students grow and always spoke to you by name which is a lot to say about a professor at the university of Oregon. He made sure that his students turned in superior work and left the class with real world knowledge. I honestly believe that this is one of the most important courses I have taken in college.
So far, best teacher I've had at Oregon. Tough teacher but everything you learn in the class is real-world knowledge.

Chuck is an awesome guy and teacher. One thing that impressed me about him was the amazing readings he assigned. They were short and very useful. Grading was fairly hard but if you try then a B is easy.
Best teacher I have ever had.  He has a great sense of humor and really cares about this students.  He does grade hard but he lets you know up front.  I recommend taking this class from him.

Chuck is one of the best teachers i have had at the UO. He grades hard but gives great feedback so you can improve throughout the term. BA352 is a VERY busy class, I reccomend taking 12 credits when taking BA352 or taking it during the Summer. There is a lot of group work, papers, and other work to do for this class. Overall, it is a great class !!

One of the best teachers I've had at Oregon.  He really challenges you and grades hard on the assignments, but it only makes you a better student.  By making you work hard on the memos you will do much better on the proposal.  Prepare to spend lots of time with your team, because that's what this class is intended to do.  Great teacher!

Chuck is a very good teacher. Grades hard to make sure you continue to work hard throughout the course. Group work will take up a lot of time. Put in work and go to office hours and you should be fine. He is very easy to talk to.

Chuck definitely challenges you.  However his grading does not offer any feedback on your performance so it is hard to learn from your mistakes.  He makes an effort to be helpful, but is not very successful in his efforts.  It seems like he picks a couple students who get the short end of the stick on all assignments, so don't get on his bad side.
Great prof. Has high expectations and will hold you accountable!

Kalnbach is a good guy and a good professor. The class he teaches is pretty hard but it will push you to become a better student and employee. Group work was fun but also very time intensive. To get a good grade you should expect a pretty intense dedication to the course. In my opinion, he's definitely one of the better BA352 instructors.

Great professor, but tough class. No curve offered. Tons of group work, but shows funny movie clips. Very down to earth. You can do well if you study for the quizzes and do well on your proposal/presentation.

I took her women and gender studies Bodies and Power class (WGS221) and she was one of the best professors I have had! She is really flexible, keeps on task and there are lots of opportunities to do well. An easy A, I would suggest it.
Amazing professor. Learned so much in her class. Definitely take Dr. Balogun's course if you have the chance!

Dr Balogun is very kind and definitely starts a lot of good discussions. I enjoyed this class a lot and the papers she had us write were thought provoking and meaningful. Participation does matter but attendance is flexible. The readings can be a lot, (but I am a STEM major taking this out of interest so it might be normal) but were always good!

Super kind professor, but lectures were a little boring and not the most engaging. She does not require attendance which leads to low numbers in class- which is annoying because every class you have to do a group discussion about the readings with your peers and share out. Graded only on the essays and you have to put in effort to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Balogun is very sweet and I can tell she cares deeply about the material, but the lectures were not very engaging. 2 3-5 page essays and a 2-3 page one, but the instructions are incredibly broad and unclear. Be prepared for a LOT of reading, and weekly assignments tied to the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I found the course content interesting, but the lectures were not very interesting. This class was hybrid but there was no more work on canvas than a fully in-person class. Usually only one small assignment per week (based on the readings), and three 3-5 page papers throughout the term. No final, just a paper.

She's super nice and a great professor. The class was interesting but some of the assignments are a bit tough. Be prepared for multiple papers (including a research paper), and a pop culture analysis. Overall pretty good class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AFR 215* Attendance isn't mandatory at all, two super easy quizzes per week, midterm isn't hard is you just look over the slides and reading. No final, just a paper. She's nice, accessible, easy class. Honestly, if you want an easy A, take this class.

This class was a 50/50. Professor Balogun was very kind and knowledgable, and the course content was interesting to learn about but the grading was very strict. Coming from someone who gets straight A's, I barely passed the essays. The rubrics are very informative but even if you study it, you'll get the same grade as if you didn't.

I loved Professor Balogun. She has such a nice voice so I never felt bored by anything that she spoke about. Very easygoing when it comes to essays and other work. She also allows a lot of time to talk with others about stuff, so you're not just listening to a lecture for an hour and a half. Very great professor!!

I took this class in the summer, and it is a pretty easy way to get four credits. There are a lot of readings, but you can just skim them for the quizzes and discussion posts. There are also two essays, which are the biggest part of your grade, but they are not too difficult if you put some effort into them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken P. Balogun twice. Both classes have been easy as long as you do the readings and can write well. Tough grader-there werent rubrics or feedback comments so I never knew why points were taken off essays. Doesn't like giving out 100s or A+, but you can def manage to get an A if you put effort in. No exams, just quizzes, discussions, essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed Soc355 taught by prof. Balogun. Easy to talk to, intelligent, and seemed like a sweetheart. Bring an open mind and you'll do just fine.
This professor is pretty cool. The class was easy enough and you can get by with only skimming the reading without have to study hours on end.

Not best but not the worst. She gives horrible feedback that doesn't help you improve your grade. She doesn't grade in a timely manner so you never know what your real grade is. She was 4 weeks late entering in final grades. Reading isn't hard, gone over in class. Quizzes are easy & right from readings, papers are the usual. Her grading is whack.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Balogun was a real gem! She really digs deep into her studies and gives the insight of a sociologist mind. Just have three essays for the class and one of them counts as a final. There is heavy reading, but she's very good about going over it.

Kemi is very friendly and the lectures are easy. Easy to get distracted in w/ a laptop. Readings are dense, 30+ pages (online photocopies); reading quizzes after certain ones. 5 reading quizzes, she takes your best 3. Lots of EC. Grades  based on reading quizzes, midterm paper, final paper, & group project. Readings  needed to write your papers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kellen is awesome! Math has always been a struggle for me but he made it 100 times easier. He answered questions clearly and explained/showed how to do problems people were stuck on. He is super accessible outside of class and is always willing to work with your schedule. Would totally take from him again.

I had him for math-111 and he was truly one of the best teachers I have had so far. Like any math course, put in the work and you will see positive results. Would take again and a 10/10 experince and so kind and flexible with his and your schedule!

This professor works very hard and wants you to succeed as much as possible. I didn't miss any classes, which helped my learning because the lectures are really important. he is a super nice teacher and works through all you questions on the material. If I could have him for every math course possible, I would choose that.
He seemed pretty new to teaching, but his a nice guy that gets nervous. His a little quick with the notes though and sometimes complicates things.

Though this class might look like an easy A, it's not!! Especially if you're a non-stem major. Dr. King is really caring and easily accessible, but she is a tough grader. Points can be made up if you revise though, and she gives better feedback in her office hours. The birding can get boring but if you're in it for the grade it's manageable.

Avian Ecology with Dr. King was a fun class. She is a tough grader in terms of citations. Lectures were boring but the bird watching outings were fun. Good HC science credit for non-stem majors. Dr. King is very caring.

Dr. King is a great professor. She is so sweet and usually responds to literally any email within an hour. I took her for HC241 and really enjoyed getting to know her during our bird watching field trips. This is a super chill class that is an easy A as long as you keep up with her lectures.

I've had this prof. for two terms in a row, and she is the sweetest ever. Very good at responding to emails (literally responds within 5 mins) and eager to provide references for scholarships/jobs. She is particular about work, but that's just because she's a scientist: she expects conciseness and quality. She is very passionate about birds!

Dr. King is an amazing and caring professor and human being. This was the first time this class was being taught, and there were some issues with grading, but she was willing to change things that didn't work. Majority of assignments are take home, group lab report final, professor is willing to look over assignments before they are turned in.

She is really sweet and nice in person, but grades very harshly, especially when it comes to citations. We did a lot of field trips to go birding which were fun, she's just a very tough grader. The essay assignments take a very long time, so make sure you plan for that. It is also her first time teaching this class, so I can cut her a bit of slack.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take her. I took her bird class and it was awful. Unless you already know every species of bird ever, it will be a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So useful for anyone interested in going into research.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Everything is super organized so you know what you need to do!

This hybrid class was interesting and fun. Sterner's lectures were comprehensible and well rounded. The labs were helpful and definitely a key to success. She was lenient and understanding, when appropriate but held her ground. Lectures could feel never ending sometimes but were interesting and important for tests in the long run.

I really enjoyed this course and Dr. Sterner. The exams were very reasonable if you went to lecture/discussion sections (especially before exam days--like flat out would tell us some of the questions). When I had a family emergency at the beginning of the term she was very empathetic and offered to let me reschedule our midterm no questions asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Boring class. She drones on all lecture and is kind of self important. If you are a bio major its easy. Abuse the notecard she lets you have on exams and put everything on it. I basically never went to class and am doing fine. The discussion is boring. Less about learning more about their opinions on genetics and how they intertwine with life

I really enjoyed this class. Her exams are very lecture based, and the readings she requires every lecture WILL show up on the exams (but will be straight forward). The lectures are very interesting and I found her to be a very engaging lecturer. There are weekly pre-discussions assignments and 5 or 6 annotation assignments that are pretty short.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, made me fall in love with Anthropology and primates. Clear grading, very passionate about what she teaches.

While Dr. Sterner is extremely knowledgeable in her area of study, she's extremely unapproachable, unaccommodating, and a super harsh grader. The content of this course was difficult, but Dr. Sterner's rigidity made it all the more difficult. I would not recommend taking a course from her unless you are ready to fight for your grade.

Easy overall but there is just no winning with those written answers on the exams. The worst type of subjective grading - you could write a whole mini-essay showing how deep you understand the question and still get marked down a point with zero explanation. So infuriating
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class hybrid when I took it so the lectures were held in person for about 1/3 of the course material and the other 2/3 were recorded lectures assigned with homework and quizzes. I found it easier to watch the lectures on 1.5-2x speed. If you watch the lectures and show up to class its pretty easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sterner is pretty hands-off in ANTH 270. It's a hybrid course so she records lectures for Tuesdays and has in-person discussion lectures Thursdays. The GEs do most of the work for grading, and the GEs this term were a little intense. Just overexplain everything and hope that's the right answer during the Unit quizzes, but the activities are easy.

Professor Sterner is incredibly inspirational, kind and intelligent. Ive taken multiple classes with her and have enjoyed and learned tremendously in all of them. Her lectures are THICK but she is willing to help and nerd out with you whenever. Requires you to study and work hard but overall it is worth it if you like the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Kirsten. Her class was a great mix of anthro and practical application with a lot of fun medical/bio stuff included as well. There was a textbook assigned but you dont need to read that so much as the novel she assigns for 376. It was a fantastic read and was more interesting than any text book. I would love to take another class from her.

Did not have experience with genomics other than some base level stuff from hs. Didn't find this class that difficult, 3 exams and 2 essays is rly all you have to do and the essays are straight forward. Spend more time studying for exam 2 and you'll be good. Final might be hard but idk cause it got switched to online due to the virus. Good luck!

ANTH 376 is basically a molecular anthropology class. As a Biology major, I did not find this class that difficult. Tests are all pretty straight forward and she tells you what to study. Only downside is that the lectures can be boring and you have clickers.

Most of Professor Sterner's lecture material is fascinating, but it also covers a broad range of topics at a relatively shallow depth. Most of the 80 minute class is lecture, and it drones on. The class functions as a Biological Anthropology survey course. As a hard Biology major, the class is relatively easy. Bring coffee and do the readings.

I really enjoyed the subject matter, but the class itself was terribly difficult for an introductory class. A ton of material to remember in a short amount of time, tests were terribly difficult and, when asked to clarify something she addressed you as though you were stupid. I strongly suggest taking a different teacher!

Dr.Sterner is a very interested and interesting professor.She cares about the course material and the videos are relevant and entertaining. I recommend this class and this professor. It is not an easy A, and you need to go to class but it is worth your time.
Good teacher and knows her stuff. Unfortunately, a very hard grader. Kind of wished she would curve because a lot of people struggle and the average grade is like a D+/C-. Too hard
I absolutely love this class and this professor. The content is a lot to remember, however Sterner makes it easy to understand. I would definitely take another class with her as the professor.

Anya is fiercely passionate and kind, and wants the very best for her students. She genuinely changed my perspective on art. Her ideas and technical mastery inspire her students to expand both their artistic abilities and expectations of themselves. Anya truly cares about each of her students and has a wealth of knowledge and experience to share.
not very friendly or kind. Was not supportive of my work or many other of the students in the class. would never recommend taking a class with her

Anya changed my life. She is frankly brilliant and will challenge you to think critically, research rigorously, and work sensitively. Metalsmithing is time intensive. Be prepared to work hard. Anya has high expectations, and is also patient and genuinely wants her students to succeed (go to office hours! ask for help, she will work with you!).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anya is very intelligent and a good professor, but she shows a lot of favoritism toward certain students.  She always has pets, and that can be difficult to deal with.

Doesn't know how to use canvas and won't respond to emails. Really cares about their students and is honestly a good "teacher", but their assignments make no sense because they don't know how to write instructions or effectively use canvas. So you don't know what to do and then will receive a harsh grade

Class was always great with Harinder; she balances speaking Italian and English very well. She cut down on the homework from previous Italian classes, which was appreciated as Italian is usually a homework heavy class. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to thrive through encouraging participation. A great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a great Italian professor. I feel like she doesn't stop smiling. Makes class fun and entertaining, while incorporating nicely made lessons. Definitely recommend!

I love Harinder. She always make class fun, with entertaining assignment and lots of time to talk with other students. Her feedback is always clear and beneficial, with the vast majority of her assignment actually benefiting my learning. She's also just a very sweet lady, would love to take another class from her.

Seriously one of the kindest persons I've met in my life. She is passionate, interested in her students, and makes you feel valid. Her lectures are vivid and entertaining, and she actively encourages interest and engagement with the subjects outside the class. However: Lots of homework. But the classes are fairly easy, so that's not a big issue.

Khalsa is very kind and understanding. This class is really interesting if you like the subject. There is a lot of time consuming homework including assignments and readings, but she is a very generous grader and you can turn anything in late up until the final. You don't need to do the readings. No exams. You'd really have to try to not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Absolutely the sweetest woman I have ever met. I would look forward to going to this class. She made the class fun and a safe place to mess up and learn. Felt like a mother more than anything. Gives great feedback in a respectful way. I just want to give her a hug and bake cookies with her.

I took LING 199 (how to learn a language) and it was interesting but the amount of reading she gave us was a little absurd at times. Each week theres a quiz with assigned readings to it. Harinder is great about giving extensions and shes a very kind grader but the homework can be intense. Shes also a great person and cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: A very engaging teacher who really wants you to succeed. Prepare to be challenged, but still to enjoy your learning experience.

Harinder is my favorite instructor of all time. I began in her 104 course and took 105, 202, and just finished 320 with her. I wish I could take her forever. If you are considering picking up Italian DO IT. I'm a Spanish major and now I love Italian. Harinder is caring, compassionate, talented, and loves her students. Takes out to pizza every term.

A great language teacher. On the first day of a 100-level language course she came in solely speaking Italian and continued to do so until the last day of the term. This is crucial in assimilating non-speakers into a new language. After week 8 I was speaking fluent Italian (small talk) to a native speaker and family friend over the phone!
Wants to see you succeed, and success to her isn't about passing the class, it's about how you learn and how much you learn.

Harinder is awesome! She's super nice and funny, especially when she doesn't quite understand American concepts. Has a real passion for the language, and it comes through. Participation is key, and she doesn't like it when people chat in english during class. Really interesting person to talk to!

Haridner is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. She requires quite a bit of homework, but none of it is ever hard, just a bit time consuming. Her tests are very fair, almost easy if you've done all the work prior to the test. I would recommend her to anyone.
Sweet woman who truly cares about her students. She is funny and is always willing to go over confusing aspects of the class.

I adore her. She is lively and funny. She goes above and beyond the textbooks and curriculum to teach Italian. Italian is not her first language either (she's Turkish), so she understands that it's not easy to pick up a second language. She cares about the well-being of her students. She's  a fantastic teacher. Put in the work and you'll like her.

I had her for Italian 104 and 105 and I love her! I'm very sad not to have her again this year. She really cares about the students and is a fantastic instructor. She's always willing to practice with you if you ask.
BEST ITALIAN TEACHER. Very helpful and very funny. Highly recommend her.

Took her 104 class and will take her 201.She is great at getting beginners comfortable, and she doesn't make you feel like a fool if you screw up answering a question. I got a bit lost during 105, but she really helped me out in office hours and by email. I don't have a RL background, so I really appreciated her attitude and helpfulness.

It takes a while to learn her style, each teacher talks very differently. But once I was used to it, she made me feel comfortable-for the most part- volunteering my answers even if I thought there was a good chance that they could be wrong. Still tough though.

Intensive First Year Italian: taught in Italian from the get go. I walked into this course with NO previous skill in Italian. Came out with quite a bit (still a long way to go, but...). She is an exceptional instructor: kind, patient and knows her stuff. Her enthusiasm about the language is catching. Brava!

Khaled is by far the best accounting teacher. Accounting, in general, is hard, but Khaled cares about students learning it, and he repeats himself several times to get it to stick to students' heads. He is overall funny, and he tried to make zoom as entertaining as he can. I hope he continues to teach at UO because he actually cares about students.

Khaled is hands down the best teacher I've ever had. His class is hard (because what accounting class isn't hard) but if you're going to take BA215 you need to take it with Khaled. He gives you like 5 answers to every quiz and offers a ton of extra credit. He also drops a lot of your bad scores to help you out. He hands out chocolate every test!

Khaled is an awesome guy. He really wants his students to be successful, and it shows in lecture. Accounting can be a tough subject at times, but the energy he brings to the topic makes it much easier to grasp. Students are graded on exams and online homework. As long as you pay attention in class, you will probably do very well in this class!

he really listens to students and truly cares if they do well or not. accounting is hard and he does his best to offer as much help as possible lectures can be boring, and the homework is online and does not correlate with whats on the test and whats being taught in class tests aren't too bad but he gives a thorough study guide

A difficult class (accounting, duh) but he is so passionate and willing to offer up any time to work with you. He genuinely cares about your understanding of class criteria. Doesn't hurt that he's young, hot, and super sweet.
A good intro to meditation

I don't recommend this class. I personally did not gain anything from it. I went into the class hoping that it would help my raised anxiety levels, and it actually made it worse. The instructor isn't approachable, understanding, or fair, so I might reconsider this course and take another PE class, like yoga.
Viriam is a wonderful meditation instructed and I would recommend his class to anyone and everyone!
Really knows how to talk with students and inspire them to do their best work.

One of the best profs I've had at UO. Really cares about his students, and just a great guy overall. You can tell because there's always a line down the hall of people waiting to speak to him during office hours.

Torsten is by far my favorite professor I've had in the J school. He made the gateway sequence bearable for me. Going to his office hours helped me a lot throughout the term. I continue to talk to him and I look forward to taking other classes from him.

Torsten is an amazing professor. He makes Gateway an enjoyable class and goes above and beyond to make sure that everyone feels prepared with what's going on. Also, he is an amazing photographer! I would definitely recommend taking a class from him.

Torsten is the MAN and I definitely consider him one of the greatest teachers I've had. He always makes sure that you're getting what you want from his class. He has an incredible way of viewing photography and his portfolio goes to show that. Also on a side note, he will most definitely make you laugh on a daily basis. Take his class.

Torsten is an amazing Professor. He specializes in Photography and Photojournalism. I loved him so much that I immediately  switched to him as my adviser. We've only known each other for a short time and he's been incredibly helpful and supportive.

Torsten is definitely an amazing teacher. In fact, he's one of the most amazing teachers that I've ever taken so far. He's so helpful and nice to everyone. His sense of humor is also a plus as well. Even though the class was a little bit tough, but all the professors were so fun and helpful.

He's a nice guy, the only thing that I disliked about his class (and wish I knew beforehand) is that all of his assignments are available from Thursday to Sunday, which was a big problem for someone like me who works on the weekends. He won't open up the assignments any earlier or have them stay open late, you can only work on them thurs - sunday.

He is at Weber State University in Ogden, Utah. Let me say, he is incredible. Most of what you learn is what you continue to practice, but he is a really understanding guy! If you want to learn German, he will put in as much effort (if not more) as you do.
Commanding voice, extremely well-structured classes, encourages participation, relevant topics, good sense of humor. He's very helpful, responds to email quickly, and overall just a nice guy.
I love Joscha!!!! He is super nice, and I am honestly obsessed with him. I learnt so much from this class and would totally take it again!

GER223 with Joscha was one of my favorite classes so far at UO. He was clearly very passionate about the material, and really genuinely cared about hearing students insights about the readings and lectures. The subject of the class itself was very interesting as well. He and this class inspired me to start taking German next year.

Joscha is great and is the best teacher for the 200 and 300 level German courses. He utilizes every minute of class, which means the day is pretty packed but he does a good job of keeping it interesting by including games and jokes. You'll learn a lot in his course and miss him when you get to the other professors.

Joscha is awesome! He's my favorite GE yet! My favorite thing is that he is actually from Germany, since not all the GEs are. It makes class more interesting since he can give better info on the culture and what the cities are like. Hes also very kind and approachable if you have questions. The class is easy if you go to class and do all the work

Joscha is super kind and hilarious. He is the only GE I will suffer through an early morning class for. The German curriculum is not the best but he teaches it the best he can. TAKE HIS CLASS! He's been my favorite GE/professor I've had! I've had him for both GER 201 and 202.

This professor is very smart and I enjoyed the literature in this course. Lectures can sometimes feel slow but are usually fine. He reviews tough texts and necessary concepts in depth in class. Lectures are not posted, but if you take thorough notes during lectures you can get an A+ without ever doing homework readings. Also, participation is huge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Spends lots of time talking and gives huge chunks of reading without anything else to go off of. There are no tests or pop quizzes but you tend to feel very under prepared when the time comes around to take a test or an assessment. Overall very nice dude and class was interesting, but it is hard to remember most of the information given in class.

This professor spoke in a way that would make anybody fall asleep in just minutes. There were barely any assignments and opportunities to test your knowledge outside of asking questions in class, and he occasionally asked the class what they thought. would not recommend it to anybody.

Martin is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. Lectures are much more interesting if you ask questions, he really appreciates when you have a curious mind. I would recommend taking his class and would take this one again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think this was a great class by a great professor who knows very well what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Can not explain anything in a way that the class can understand and he continually made us analyze old pieces of literature that had no relation to money which is what this class is supposed to be about. Also the lectures are extremely boring and he grades everything to the point where any mistake hurts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors at this school. His lectures are him droning on about a topic that has no relation to money which is the whole point of this class. He also one uses 4 grades for the whole year and grades them very harshly for small things like punctuation and little mistakes so if you make a mistake you're done in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a waste of my time, We didn't talk about money for 8 weeks. We were tasked with reading a lot of translations from German to English which were mostly boring and meaningless to a non German fanatic. Martin Klebes, is a German fanatic. I honestly believe he is a smart guy and likely a good professor in spite of this class. DONT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Martin is fantastic teacher and I strongly urge people to take at least one class with him. He is insightful, kind, and fair. I attended his office hours (he's writing a book on terrorism, chat him up about that) and always came to class so following along was quite easy. His class on Kleist is one of the best around and his lectures are fantastic.

Klebes is well organized and clear in his expectations. Mid-term/final are fairly difficult but not out of line. Chronologically linear course. Open to new interpretations of material if you can support your argument,something of a rarity in the social sciences and speaks well to Klebes confidence in his subject knowledge. Ideologically neutral.
BEST professor of literature EVER
No Comments

Klebes is very intimidating at first, but once you get used to his style it's a bit better.  The class I took with him was very very difficult and had some of the most difficult readings I've ever read, even when I found the english translations they were incomprehensible, but he did a very good job of explaining them.
Good teacher but the tests are borderline impossible. Not super realistic to hope for acceptable grades in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really great professor who gives very fun and interesting lectures. The workload for this course is very manageable, however your grades rely heavily on how well you do on the midterm and final. The tests in this class are pretty hard, but he always curves them so you should be fine.
Only issue with this class is how hard the exams are. They are curved pretty heavily, which was fine but still. The class average was like a 49 for the midterm and not that much higher for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His humor definitely made the lectures easier to get through, as the content could get quite dense. The exams are hard, but there was a very generous curve and plenty of extra credit opportunities. Discussion section attendance wasn't mandatory, but showing up definitely improved my grade.

This guy really cares about teaching. Professor Miller is funny and candid while also being a strong advocate for student success. He made the content accessible and relatable to the "real world" while bravely asserting his values to a large audience. It took countless hours of studying to succeed in this course, but the hard work paid off.
He's a good professor that teaches a tough class but he generously curves grades and provides opportunities to earn extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall he was a great professor with really good lectures. His lectures were engaging and were taught very well. There is a lot of homework, but I found the homework to be useful and comparative to the midterms. The only downside is that his tests are very difficult. He curves them heavily which is nice, but if you want an A you need to study hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun guy, but lectures are kind of boring, but econ itself is a boring subject. Tests and exams are really hard, so he has to apply a very generous curve. He does give quite a few extra credit opportunities. Isn't the worst, but still is difficult.
Makes lectures interesting and entertaining when they otherwise would be a snooze fest. Exams are hard, but heavily curved
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome guy

This class was probably the most difficult class I took for the term. 40% of your grade is homework and 30-35% of your grade is your midterm/final. His lectures could be hard to follow but as long as you go over slides, study, and use the resources he gives you, you should do fine in the class. He also curves heavily so that helps a ton.

If you utilize the resources provided to you (textbook, homework, practice exams), it is easy to excel in this class. The exams are a huge part of your final grade, and attendance is not mandatory. The professor is silly, and he has good lectures.

Tests are kind of obnoxiously hard for a 201 class. I don't know why you would have tests where you have to curve 20+ points just to pass students. Got rid of 4 years of open note policy this term. However, he is a pretty decent and accomplished professor. Do all of the extra credit. (I can say that was my biggest academic mistake this term)

I can agree with other people that it is one of the hardest classes I've taken at UO. His lectures are ok. He often rambles about random things. He's made interesting remarks about his salary and contract with the school. He also claimed that he's notorious for making hard exams. That claim stands true. Do all extra credit that he offers.

This class is one of the hardest business classes I have ever taken. It is almost impossible to even get a B. None of the exams are open note, it is on canvas it is multiple choice but you will have to study for hours if you want to succeed. Hw is worth a lot so I say make sure you focus on that just as much as the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Keaton is a great professor. Class was easy and straightforward. Take notes and study slides.
He was an alright professor. The lectures were boring, and the homework would take many hours to complete. Tests were very hard and the average class scores on them were below a passing grade...

I really enjoyed this professor, his lectures are engaging and thoughtful. He's genuinely tries to make students succeed and curves pretty heavily on exams. If you study well enough you should get at least a B+. Would definitely take another course with him.
