Keaton is such a knowledgeable guy who does care about his students. Lectures do get long but he keeps engagement of students easily. He's a super personal guy and it felt like I was listening to a real human not just reading off slides. Tests are difficult, but they are open note, and you just have to be well prepared.
DO NOT TAKE. Brags about awful scores on tests, and does not care about his students at all. Little time spent per person in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take any other professor if you can, save yourself. Keaton Miller is one of THE worst professors I've ever had. His use of vocabulary is far to complex and causes more confusion then resolution. It's almost as if he gets an egotistical boost from using vocabulary that is far too sophisticated. He also often brags about his test's difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and you can tell he cares about what he's teaching. The midterm is completely open note due to it being very hard. If you actually pay attention and do the homework understanding the material shouldn't be too hard. His lectures can get a bit boring sometimes, but it's worth going so you don't get behind.

Honestly he gets a bad rep but he's great at what he does. The homework can take a while so definitely set aside enough time to get it all done. Only 2 exams, but they're graded pretty harsh. The curves usually round out at about 75 or so. Honestly if you pay attention and do the homework you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Holy homework. The weekly assignments take HOURSSS, so be prepared. His lectures are mostly dull but sometimes quirky. The content overload makes things confusing. Does iclicker attendance but drops a few of them i think and they're like one point or something. Only two exams (midterm & final), so messing up one hurts. Not the best, not the worst.
Keaton Miller gets off on his students doing bad and gets a power trip off of the midterms and finals averaging 68 percent. He flexes this constantly

I don't recommend professor Miller. Homework's are LONG, and not necessary for the class. You're going to have to do a lot of math in the homework. Lectures are long and boring. Only one midterm and one final. So not a lot of wiggle room if you do bad on a test. I recommend Waddell. Waddell gives NO homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very hard! The lectures were long and hard to follow, the homework did not connect to what we were learning and felt like a waste of time. The professor was hard to listen to and did not give many examples.

Keaton Miller is a fantastic teacher; the lectures are, memorable, interesting and funny. No readings, but there is online homework. His class teaches principals and the equations but not really the applications. Make sure to go to the discussion class as that's where you'll learn how to apply those equations. The tests are all open notes.
Really animated lecture giver, has all these dry asides that some find super funny (I do). Good at explaining content and keeps a good pace. Online textbook subscription required for homework
Great professor but the tests are hard. He is understanding and is helpful in office hours.

It's obvious the professor cares about his students; however, the tests are extremely difficult and not similar to the lecture slides. The practice midterm and final are identical to the one you'll be taking so I recommend you study that the most. Homework is also challenging; would take me about 3 hours to complete. Class grade average was 78%/C+.

I loved this class and even though the tests are fairly difficult, Professor Miller was always really helpful and super friendly. Any question you ask him he has an answer, and helps you easily understand it by using examples. He's definitely my favorite Professor yet, and if you're looking to take Econ 201 you 100% have to take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The concepts we went over in class were identical to my HS econ class but the midterm and final were much harder. Also, the homework seemed random and  we didnt learn enough in class to do it so i ended up bsing it based on patterns given in the solutions after getting a problem wrong. final is weighted 40%, which is what screwed me, harsh grader

Terrible professor. Exams are closed note and to and doesn't offer any support when you ask questions about the material. He is a very strict grader with no room to try to make your grade better. Reassures you of his policies in the syllabus then completely changes everything and leaves you with a terrible grade and tells you its your fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures and relevant homework to go along with them. Practice exams provided which are identical to the midterm and final, just different questions. As long as you stay on top of the homework and understand the content from the lectures, you will succeed in the class. He is available by email or outside of class if you need help too.
Exams are really hard even tho they are open book

This professor did not teach me any of the content that was then tested on the weekly homeworks and then midterm/final. His lecutres never have specific problems or samples where we can actually learn how to solve. I felt so unprepared for the tests.

Easy to follow lectures, cares about students, want them to succeed. Weekly homework, but the homework helps explain the content in more detail with several examples. Very personable and happy to answer questions in class and out. Several easy extra credit opportunities. Both midterm and final are completely open note on your computer.

I actually took two classes with Professor Keaton. One was EC 410 and EC 460. They were both difficult classes, but Keaton makes sure to give you all the support and resources you need. He gives you multiple ways to earn credit, meaning you're not only graded on exams. If you get the chance, take all of his courses!

He's fantastic.

Don't take any other EC 201 professor. Keaton was a joy during lecture and gave plenty of sample problems and specific examples. The midterm and final are both online (on your laptop) that you take in-class. You can have notes or refer to the slides, which makes them VERY easy. The only annoying part is the online homework which can be frustrating.
He's great. Very knowledgeable but also explains things really well. He's also very generous with grading at the end of the term. Makes me really enjoy econ!
The class is tough to follow, but he is a great professor, tests were really hard even though they were open note.

He made lectures quite interesting and engaging. I think the midterm and final were a bit tricky since the highest score in each one was like an 85. I also wish we had more work to determine our grade other than two tests and homework. The homework was pretty time consuming, but it was helpful in understanding concepts.
He makes Econ somewhat interesting, pretty easy class if you pay attention and do practice tests. Tests are completely open note. He is a super nice guy with a really well structured class.
funny young guy

Professor Miller is not only a great professor, but he is such a cool human. He is a great lecturer because he bounces between jokes/personal stories to economic theories, so you rarely fall asleep in his class! EC 201 is just a hard class for most people so do study hard but if you have the choice of taking it with Miller, I recommend!

Throughout my entire college experience, there hasn't been a professor who radiates professionalism quite like Miller. Lectures are informative, interesting, and he really does care about the students' success. That being said, the work in the class is pretty rough, and the average grade in my class is C. Even so, I highly recommend him.

Class is relatively easy with just weekly hw but tests are hard! They were even open note and online and people still struggled. But, he does curve them and genuinely wants to see students succeed. Lectures are pretty good and he's kinda funny. Would def take again and recommend!

Prof. Miller was a good professor and I would recommend him over any other 201 professor, however, this comes with a few caveats. The Midterm and Final are extremely important in your grade and they are also difficult (class averaging around 70% on one in particular that was 30% of our grade). These exams are curved but study up, they're hard!!!

Super funny, relatable, and understanding too! Makes class accessible to everyone and definitely allows space for grade improvement at the end of the term. Only downside is that you have to purchase an expensive textbook to do any of the homework!

He is super great guy and makes jokes during his lectures, because at times they can be really boring. There is homework every week that can take up a large chunk of time, plus the textbook was a little expensive. The midterm and final were kinda hard, but he's curves them so that was helpful.

Keaton is a pretty good lecturer, sometimes dry, but that's econ for you. Tests are a big part of your grade, but also curved. Stay on top of homework, the discussion sections help, and reach out if you need it. PS - he loves to bring up Burning Man.

Loved Keaton. Super entertaining. Midterm and final are extremely difficult. But he offers lots of extra credit. The homework sucks but helps your grade compared to other econ professors. He is the best. Take his course.

The midterm and final were hard but heavily curved. He is a very engaging lecturer and teaches a little more in depth than the other Econ 201 profs, which is helpful for upper division classes later on.

I have had a wonderful experience in this class. Professor Miller is very respectable. He has very interesting lectures as well! The homework sometimes takes a bit of time but is very worth it when assisting my understanding in the material. I highly recommend Professor Miller!
The class was so fast and hard to keep up with. The tests were extremely hard no matter how hard you study. If you miss a class its impossible to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Literally the worst class i have taken at UO. Dry lectures, not helpful, and unforgiving if you dont go to office hours. Studied so hard for the midterm and final, ended up getting a 46%. His lectures do not give example problems making it ridiculously hard to complete the homework, which does not effect your grade, even if you get 100%. DONT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great intro course. Professor Miller really knows his stuff, is fantastic at explaining concepts & answering questions. Also does interesting research, has fun life stories. Lectures are long so do your best to pay attention. Watching asynchronously during online school helped me a lot, could pause it or speed up. Take notes and do extra credit

In his lectures, he gives example problems, but the homework and exam Q's are much harder. Lectures were so boring, I stopped attending after week 7 of 10. Homework was the only way to learn, but I had to waste homework attempts to teach myself. He admits that his exams are much more difficult than typical Econ exams (class avg on final was 64%).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is an amazing teacher of economics. Good lectures, makes things easy to understand, homework is not too bad. Midterm and final is pretty tough but if you study, there shouldn't be an issue. I highly recommend Professor Miller.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Miller is a sub par teacher. His lectures mainly consist of reading of the slides in a confusing manner. Definitely not my learning style. Tests were ridiculously hard and the curve does not end up helping. Great guy but would not recommend taking this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a so nice professor and taking care of his students. If you do not understand his lecture or have a question, you should talk to him in his office hour or after the class. The exam is hard, but if you study hard, you will be fine. He will curve both midterm and final.

SOOOOOO much homework and the tests were ridiculously hard. All the other Econ201 classes had literally no homework and easy tests and there is so much homework for this class every week. All tests were so confusing and impossible to get an A on

Professor Miller is a real great professor at the University of Oregon. He is a entertaining fun guy in and out of class. Highlights of the class is his specialty lectures given at the end of the term, extra credit, and if you go meet in person for help. All in all, it is a great experience. Also guys, do not be a idiot and miss extra credit! DON'T
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you don't go to his office hours, good luck trying to get above a C in the class. He makes lecture interesting but they are nothing close to what you do on the homework online (which takes hours to complete).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is a phenomenal teacher, and clarified concepts fantastically. He wasnt entirely reliant on the text for the content, and answered all questions in the lecture, and answered swiftly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a great teacher for Econ 201, this guy is the man. Miller provides in total of 6 extra credits, make sure u get them all which can add 6 extra percent on your final grade. The tests are pretty tough, but his practice tests and study guides are super helpful to make sure you do well on the actual tests. Overall, take his Econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes a dry topic like economics entertaining. Miller helped me gain interest in the subject because of how passionate he is about his work. Great class.
Keaton Miller's a good speaker. Class was pretty tough not gonna lie but it was very enjoyable and challenging. It helps to have an intelligent professor.

One of the easiest classes I've taken at the UO so far. Practice tests make the course painless. Miller is a funny guy and knows his economics. He stays professional and explains material in simple language.

Keaton makes his time available for students who want to learn the material more in depth. Take the practice midterm and practice finals. The questions are exactly the same with the values changed. He tries to joke with the class and there's awkward silence because of how corny they are, but he is a knowledgable professor and an easy A.

Class was alright. He attempted to make economics appeal to the newcomers as best he could which worked usually. The class overall wasn't too difficult, but definitely wasn't a breeze. Practice tests were a life-saver. Respectable guy and good to meet with individually. Textbook and Aplia wasn't too reminiscent of the tests.

Class is fun and captivating. Explains the information clearly and the slides are easy to understand. Lectures provide lots of clarity the textbook doesn't and Miller's comments are well suited to the homework. The course is challenging but a gratifying experience.

Keaton is super knowledgable about this stuff and accessible during office hours. He really lightens up a dry subject (taking this for pre-business) and at least tries to make it interesting. Class is heavy on the workload but if you keep up, you should get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don't kid yourself. This class is no joke. The homework is extremely difficult and tests are a struggle. That said, Miller's lectures work well with the text and he is entertaining. If you pay attention and work hard, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a funny guy. Explains concepts very well and tests are straightforward and simple. That said, understanding the material can be a struggle but once you get used to it it's fine. Section is helpful depending on your G.E. For the most part the homework is good practice.

Professor Miller is a great choice for Micro. Explains material simply and precisely, does not make anything too hard. He's very straightforward. Homework is a lot but the midterm and final aren't too bad

Miller goes through lectures pretty quickly but manages to explain the concepts well. Micro isn't the easiest subject matter but he explains it in simple language. He's a funny professor and classes are enjoyable for the most part. If you pay attention and do the homework, it's not too hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty funny dude, do the practice midterm and go to discussions and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lecture-heavy, but gives good examples of the points he presents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super friendly + funny professor, made class enjoyable even though I was terrible at the subject. Weekly online homework assignments are sometimes challenging so start early in the week in case you need to attend office hours to ask questions. Tests were sorta difficult for me but they're generally curved. Also he likes Homestuck which was amusing.

Econ 201 is a tough course, and while he is an extremely smart prof the lectures and homework doesn't help on the tests too much. I would take upper level classes with him but he unnecessarily complicates the low level stuff.

The lectures in this class are very thorough, but a bit boring as well. The homework is all online, and fairly easy. Attendance will help you with the test to some degree, but with the amount of information this class provides, it's easier to just study the necessary material. Professor is very knowledgeable and professional.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Keeps class fun for a hard topic
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He's chill

The tests are tough and they do not correlate much with the online homework. However, he does give you a practice exam with a correction key beforehand so that helps. He has good lecture slides and is funny but goes fast, so be prepared to take notes when you come to class.

He talks pretty fast but you can tell he knows the material really well. He expects you to attend lecture since some of the questions on the midterm and final include stuff not in the textbook. Really willing to help during office hours.

Tons of HW, but the lectures were worth it. makes a lot of jokes which keeps it interesting. moved a little quick so you need to pay attention the whole time, but was clear and allowed you to get all information needed before moving on. Discussion was a joke however.
Dr. Boose was deeply compassionate and extremely educated. I was impressed every single day. She is so intelligent but she also makes time to relate with students.

I took an online class with Professor Boose and she emphasizes a lot that you can reach out to her for anything. When I did have questions regarding the content of the class, she gave very thorough answers. My one thing to look out for is that some of the material on the final was not covered in class, and be sure to take lecture notes.
Professor Boose is one of the only professors I've had a positive experience with. She is extremely intelligent and educated and cares about her students. She's also hilarious.

She's super nice, passionate about her work, and wants her students to succeed. Taking this class in four weeks was great. It would probably be too slow if you take it during the school year. Just take good notes for the lectures and watch all the videos.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a very nice teacher and answers your emails quickly. BUT her online open note exams are hard. She states that in the syllabus. You have to work for your grade in this class. Do not take this class if you are looking for an easy A. Take this class during the school year NOT the summer
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Honestly one of my favorite teachers at the UO! Klaree is super nice and is there for her students anytime we don't understand material. Her classes aren't mandatory but it's best to go to lecture to be taught the information instead of having to self teach outside of class (she has very full lecture slides). Classes aren't too hard and she curves!

Klaree is one of my favorite professors. I've taken two classes with her, and she is really great. Sometimes rushes through slides because they are so packed with information. Primatology is her forte, and it really shows in lecture. Clear grading, however, 270 is only graded on exams and a lab practical, so make sure to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are jam-packed with material. She reads the slides that are heavy with info and sometimes rushed to catch up. Thankfully they are all posted on Canvas. She is nice and funny. Group paper/presentation at the end of term. Exams are challenging if you don't go to class. She does a final review and allows a full page of notes front and back!!!

She brings a good energy into the classroom but sometimes has lengthy lectures so she goes by them quick; she posts them on canvas though, which is nice. The tests are challenging if you don't study but if you study your lecture notes you should be fine. Labs are super easy and you never have to open your textbook.

Few quizzes throughout the term. A midterm and a final. One 11x8 in paper (both sides) may be used for the final - you can type it up and shrink it down if you'd like. Final group project at the end including a paper and five minute presentation.

Awesome professor. Obviously puts her best effort into the class and brings in an interesting guest speaker. Super accommodating and very helpful to students needs. Overall i enjoyed the class and would definitely recommend her.

I really enjoyed Dr. Boose and her approach to this class. Her lectures are very well structured and you can tell she spends a lot of time making the power-points. She takes student's comments and questions and expands on them to tie them into her lecture. I think she is a great, very smart instructor and has a lot to offer.

The class was average in how interesting it was, but Boose is not my favorite anthropology professor at the University of Oregon. It is so clear that she reads off the lecture slides. If we fall behind in slides, she rushes to catch up. She gets really nervous at times but you can tell she tries. The tests don't reflect the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, the class was interesting, but Boose is not my favorite. It is rather obvious she reads from a script during her lecture, and if anyone ever asks a question 80% of the time she will not know the answer. The tests are also ridiculously hard for being a 270 class. DO NOT BUY THE $200 TEXTBOOK because we never opened it or addressed it once.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Klaree is a young professor. New to lecturing. She is so smart, and also funny, you can tell she is nervous at times. I take 10-15 pages of hand written notes per lecture, expect to write VERY quickly. If you miss class, you can't piece together the lecture based on the slides so don't skip if possible. Overall, intelligent, funny, flustered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've taken several online anthropology course, however this one was very different. Klaree was very helpful and always responded to emails when help was needed. While this is an online class, do expect some work and effort to receive a good grade. Weekly assignments, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm and 1 final, which all involve writing.

He has a very disorganized way of teaching. This is the most confusing math class I have ever taken. I would say not to take this class because of the way it is taught, but he curves so heavily, so people will pass if they don't quite understand the material. My recommendation is to do self-studying to get higher than a B.

I don't normally write reviews, but after taking this class I needed to give my two cents. I normally am great at math, but his teaching style was far too disorganized and rigorous. He was not supportive with explaining/helping outside of class and is an extremely tough grader. His exams are terrible. He's a nice guy but save yourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was confusing and you can HARDLY read his handwriting. Do yourself a favor and wait till someone else teaches it.

For the latest review in March 2025, the highest 78% was me. For your "extra" information, it was just a mistake, and I already got my grade fixed, which was 90%. So, what I wanna say is please go to the tutor if you don't get the material, please study and prepare well. I'm not saying he is the greatest professor but he is caring and really good!

This class is curve-heavy! Our second midterm, the average was a 34%, highest grade was a 78%. He curved so that 52% was an A. Weekly quizzes that try to trick you, a philosophical approach to calculus, webwork that doesn't match tests/quizzes. He is engaging in class and is helpful if you ask the right questions.

He has 2 midterms and one final that is optional if you have completed the homework and worksheets. He posts a solid review for the exams. We were also allowed to bring a full sheet of printer paper for notes to exams. On top of this if the class does poorly, like mine did the exams will be heavily curved. I would 10/10 recommend

Honestly I'm not sure if I will take a math class at UO from a better teacher. Good math professors are hard to come by but Professor Kleshchev is great! Quizzes each friday aren't worth much but they keep you on track, 2 midterms and optional final (all with generous curves). His lectures are also packed with example problems which is so nice.

Quizzes are given every Friday, there are two midterms, and the final was optional.
Professor grades on a curve for each assessment. 
Professor has office hours to help students on any homework or test related questions.
Study guide looked exactly like the midterms.
I looked over the lecture notes and did some self studying to do well in the class.

Great Prof. Really knows what he's talking about and can answer any questions students have. Very passionate. I thought I was failing this term until he explained the curve on the class. A 40% =D, 55%=C, 65%=B, for this class specifically. Could vary. Gives helpful study guides and very responsive to emails. Unconventional exams, but difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof has amazing lectures that are both clear and concise. He always clears up any questions you have and can explain concepts in several different ways. Grades are curved heavily.

My favorite math professor I've come across at UO. Class is hard, and the tests are pretty difficult. Rest assured through that he does curve, he clearly states it on the first day of class. Quizzes every week. Lectures were awesome, you actually walk away with an understanding of the homework. Most exam / quiz problems come from lecture notes.

One of the most helpful math teachers on campus. He likes to make dry math jokes to lighten up the boring class, I mean it is linear algebra. He has a slight accent but that does not take away from he clear he is with the material. I really recommend this guy. Fair warning: Tests are very challenging. They will see if you KNOW the material

He's a great professor--he has a way of explaining difficult concepts in a very straightforward manner. His lectures complimented the textbook. Tests were challenging, but almost fun (he curves generously). Overall, he runs a great class--would recommend him to anyone.

Good professor, but he was a bit of a curveball. He gives a difficult (or nonstandard) exams, but he also gives you a generous curve (35% = C). His lectures were excellent and demonstrated his knowledge. He puts a lot of thoughts on proofs, which is unusual for this class.

Great professor!His lectures can get confusing at times, but if you do the homework and go to class you will learn alot from him. Also his tests are not standard, which sometimes makes them difficult to study for( you need to know the concepts really well). However his curves are amazing and pretty much everyone ends up happy!
Take the class for the curve!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Good Class.  questions are often generalized which makes them harder, but he has complete understanding of material.  Most thorough teacher yet really digs into  proofs and theory.  The class is tought at a slow pace so there is plenty of time for Q&A.
He really knows how to teach. He knows applications and he knows how to describe things in a way that students can understand easily.

I must say this teacher is great! His lectures were clear and his midterms were challenging, but the class curve was AWESOME! Everyone didn't do too well in the class exams, and I 50% was a C! cool aint it?
Very good teacher.  Was deemed (sp?) the nickname of  Dex .  Definitely takes classes from again. I hate math.
Good teacher, knows how to explain what you need to know without adding extraneous information.  Very clear and organized.

Dr. Knowles is a passionate Special Educator with a lot of knowledge. Sometimes her instructions can be unclear. She encourages students to 'figure it out' because that's what it will be like in the field. I often felt like I was floundering, but eventually by the end of the term it started to all come together. Projects were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Knowles is one of the most incredible professors that I have ever had. She genuinely cares about her students, makes lectures engaging and accessible, and is one of the kindest humans. Her content is so well-chosen and applicable to realistic teaching, and she honestly makes me want to continue after my masters program to get my PhD.

This course was all web. There were weekly discussions and quizzes, but the quizzes we open notes, open books, and didn't have a time limit. Gives extra credit opportunities. Very quick at replying to emails. Seem like she cares about having students succeed. No lectures just videos, textbook readings, and additional resource pages.
Most amazing prof I have ever had!! So sincere and genuinely cares about your well-being. Her lectures are interesting and meaningful. 10/10 would recommend and take any class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chris did a great job teaching this class online. Her expectations were clear, she gave opportunities for extra credit, and she even made power points and extra videos on each chapter of the textbook. She also made herself easily available to zoom if you needed to, even though we had so synchronous classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is interesting and the professor shows proficiency in what he teaches. However, he is very strict when it comes to grading assignments and he's very quick to call students out for mistakes. Instructions are sometimes unclear and confusing. The subject was interesting but the professor did poorly in carrying it through.
Funny, insightful lectures and excellent reading choices. Very useful and rewarding class, which seemed to go by quickly even though it was 3 hours long.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Chris was an absolutely exceptional instructor! For a three hour class once a week, she made it fly by. She made sure everyone understood the topics and would go over in detail if needed. However, since the class is only once a week be prepared for lots of reading!

Greg is a good instructor who cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. Good communicator, clear grading criteria, and very nice. His lectures tend to go off-topic and we progressed pretty slowly through the material until the last few weeks when we had to play catch-up. Highly recommend going to office hours for homework help too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Greg is not the best teacher. His methods for helping students study for his tests are shoddy and he tends to put the hardest problems possible on all his tests. He is not very accommodating either. He penalizes your grade for drinking/eating in class. I understand he is learning but this guy needs a lot of work before becoming an actual professor.

Greg was the best math teacher I have ever had, and he made so many accommodations for me that came in clutch for the class. He is really flexible and is willing to help you catch up anytime. Furthermore, he is super approachable, professional, and great at explaining things to you in different ways until you understand it.

Even though I got a bad grade in this class I'd like to say that I appreciate this teacher. Coming in to this class I had been unmotivated and depressed. His no nonsense approach motivated me to be a better student. So far during my summer break I've been practicing math every day so that next year I can come back and be successful. Thanks again.

The class was very entertaining. Greg was very good at making the lectures interesting. It was a bit too easy to get off topic though. He grades very generously, and writes helpful feedback on HW and Quizes. The textbook is fairly useless.

No empathy towards mental health, even given the climate of the past year. Makes you feel bad for using AEC accommodations & makes you explain yourself which feels like a breach of privacy. Absolutely do not recommend this guy's class if you're dealing with your own mental health concerns because he isn't well educated in supporting someone in that

There's 1 quiz, multiple webwork & txtbook hw due every week. Attendance is taken every day. There are 4 exams & the difficulty of it and the homework are a lot more difficult than what is covered in lectures. My friend took the same course with other profs & the materials & tests were way easier. This prof is great but he challenges the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Greg is an awesome educator and yes, even lets you call him Greg. I've only had him two weeks so far but he's great. The absolute only thing I could complain about is that we're actually getting through material a little slowly. This will probably end up being really nice later when things get harder but right now it just feels a little tedious.

Greg is the best! He really helped all of us out who were struggling with learning calculus online. He is always available to help outside of lectures and is very fun. The homework is difficult but the tests weren't too bad.

Greg is one of the most kind and caring teachers I've ever had. Greg genuinely wants you to succeed. If he struggles to explain something in office hours, he will go so far as to email you a better explanation later because he just wants you to thrive. He loves math and tells very interesting anecdotes. Tests are very reasonable. Homework is tough.

Greg is a super great guy, he's super accessible outside of class and helpful in office hours. The homework is the hardest part of the class, but the tests are super reasonable and not that bad. If you're struggling, let him know, he wants you to succeed and will help you in any way to get you on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really ended up enjoying Kristen Bell's criminal law class. I find her use of iclickers to be engaging and encourage class discussion (from someone who normally hates iclickers). Unlike a lot of 1l classes this class felt very class discussion based, which I appreciated. She also is able to clearly lecture about the material and explain it well.
She will make time for you if you make time for her. Incredible teacher. I didn't do as well as I could have because I didn't put enough work into the class. Nonetheless, great class!

This was the inside-out prison class "Mercy and the Rule of Law." Very small class so I don't want to give too much personal info but I loved this experience and Professor Bell was very helpful, sweet and generous.

Very fun teacher, clearly loves her job. The class is based on essays called 'Field Posts,' not on tests. There is a large group project in the end, however you get to pick the people you work with. Often the class feels like I am in kindergarten however it is extremely enjoyable. Content is well explained and feedback is of high quality.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Rahilly is kind and caring. She is clearly passionate not just about the material she teaches, but about her students and best teaching practices. The assignments are participatory and engaging. She really wants everyone to succeed and has inclusivity in her mind always.

I took Geology of Campus and that class was really cool. Professor Rahilly is great, she is really open and gives really good feedback on assignments. There are 4 field posts to do and those took the largest amount of time, but even those weren't bad and become easier as you do more. You should really take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Rahilly is super welcoming, caring, and makes an effort to give students the support they need for both in-class and online assignments. The assignments are super easy, but the material is still valuable. As long as you participate and try on the assignments it is easy to get a good grade.

Overall, a very easy and manageable class. Tests are open note which is quite helpful. Reading is recommended but I got away with rarely completing all of it. One complaint is that the lectures don't cover anything the reading doesn't and vice versa, so it was very tempting to skip class as attendance wasn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is easily the most boring class I have ever taken. I was excited for this class, but Professor Seaman makes the information very hard to digest, as her lecture style is very very slow and monotone. The only upside was that the exams were take home, and moderately easy if you come to class. Do not reccomend.
my review speaks for itself
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's super knowledgeable about the topic, has a lot of interesting stories, and really cares. The class was also really easy as attendance wasn't mandatory, you're graded on a couple of simple essays, a midterm, and a final, and everything is really well organized. Only drawback is that it's supremely boring and not engaging whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class consists of the professor pointing at a slide show the entire time, no discussions, no activities, nothing. I feel like I haven't learned anything in this class because it is incredibly boring and un engaging. The homework is just readings and there aren't many assignments, plus she doesn't take attendance, so it is an easy class.

Obviously difficult since a grad level class and I was an undergrad taking it, but Prof seaman is so clear with feedback and I have taken her more than once and always gotten an A since her expectations were easy to understand. She also cares a lot about her students and helps them to succeed. Intimidating personality but a giant heart.

Prof Seaman is the most wonderful professor I have ever had the privilege of knowing. She is rich with feedback and her students are the number one priority. I have had her 4 times and always got A/A+s, she is very accommodating. Don't listen to the negative reviews clearly all written by one disagreeing with her inclusive and progressiveness.
Prof Seaman is an incredible mentor, fair grader, and is not afraid to give you tons of feedback.

Professor Seamans seminar was informative and a great introduction to graduate level art historical study. The reading was on different critical theories in general, allowing us to apply the theory to our respective areas. The feedback in office hours was clear and informative. If I could have, I would have taken every course from this professor.

Professor Seaman is very knowledgeable about her subject and will name drop researchers left and right. She gives very thorough study-guides for tests that include everything you need to know except for essay questions. And even then, she will discuss with you potential questions. Be prepared to memorize art. But this was the first A+ I ever got!

VERY poor instructor. I had to drag myself to class because it was so unbearably boring and uninformative. She simply read the "raw" data of the slides, &did not introduce a theme. The topic is intriguing, but I can say that I did not learn anything of substance. The AH department is limited in faculty, and that is the only reason she is employed.

Linda was a great teacher who explained things very well. Her slides are very easy to understand, but I would recommend going to class because she doesn't post all of her notes. The tests are very hard, but there are two midterms and 1 final so it's split up well! Def recommend taking this class with her

The best choice for ACTG470, hands down. Graded on 2 midterms, 1 final, 2 graded homeworks. Gives optional weekly homework and solutions, as well. Easy to understand lectures. Tough class material, but Linda is a great teacher and makes it more manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best tax professor, highly recommend getting her for ACTG 470 if possible. While tax accounting is somewhat boring to most, Linda is the best teacher of tax within the college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a tough class, but with the amount of examples she provides helps with engagement and understanding of the material. Class is only graded on 5 items: 2 Homeworks, Group paper, Midterm, Final. Tests are pretty similar to practice tests she provides. There is a slight curve to the class that helps. I would love to take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough class, but that is the nature of tax accounting. She teaches the material in the best way possible. Usually a decent sized curve in the class. She cares about students and knows the material really well. Very respected teacher.

Over all Linda is great - very helpful, very nice, and highly knowledgeable. Her lectures move extremely quickly though (as would any tax class) so be ready to write and brush up on what you missed outside of class.

Overall good professor. Surprisingly - the only way the class would have been better was if there was more homework made by her!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was scared to take a taxation class but Linda made it so much easy and fun. Linda is very accessible outside of class. FYI I don't know about other tax classes but her class has three exams - 1st and 2nd midterm and final. So you have to study to keep up with the class to do well in her exam. It's not easy in 10 weeks of the quarter system.

She was a great professor! The class was challenging but she made it as interesting as possible and broke everything down in a way that was easier to understand. Go to class and take good notes and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hard exams, confused slides and explanation, textbook is must to understand if unclear class. Not recommend it!
Tough class, there is no way around it. Do the work and you will be fine. She is very helpful, willing to help anytime and explains things clearly.
Great Teacher! Does a good job explaining material and tries to make it interesting. Class is challenging but not hard if you study and make good note cards for her midterms.

Federal tax is a very hard class to teach, A LOT of material, and it's widely perceived as boring material. However, I thought she did really good. She made it as interesting as possible, and she used great examples. This is a very useful class, and she is very knowledgeable professor, I thought she did a great job.
Very boring class, exams are super hard. Gives a nice curve though.
No Comments

Tyler was a great teacher for some difficult material. He color codes his notes on the board and frequently stops to make sure there are no questions or confusion. He is a great teacher and I would definitely recommend taking his class.

The class is not easy, however Tyler does a great job of teaching the material well and making lectures very useful. He makes the content as easy as possible and prepares you well for the tests and finals.

Though he's now at the University of Arizona, I had a great time in his class. He's a really funny guy, and still manages to teach all the content. I already more or less knew the content for the class, but he made it as enjoyable as math can get.
Tyler is the best Math professor you will ever have. If you think otherwise you are simply wrong. Enough Said.
The best professor ever! I learned Calc 1 for a lifetime!

Very helpful and willing to be flexible with his schedule to fit needs of his students. He genuinely wants students to understand and his methods of teaching are beneficial because he will encourage you to work through a problem before he tells you what to do. I definitely recommend him for a tough class such as calculus.

Excellent lecturer with an excellent grading policies. His use of four exams rather than the standard two made for a good representation of your actual knowledge of the material. I would definitely have him as a teacher again.

I enjoyed having Tyler as a professor. Very personable guy. The class was hard, but that's expected in the third level of calculus. Very accessible in office hours and goes out of his way to make sure he's available for students in need of help. I just wish he taught higher level classes so that I could have him again.

Tyler could not explain the material very well, but he gave HARD exams!! Expect to see surprise questions on the exam. The review session did not help. His class do not have curve or cut off no matter how low the average is. So you need to work super hard to get a good grade.

Tyler is the best! He is an extremely good GTF. He really cares about his students and goes out of his way to make himself available. His lectures are very helpful and clear, and he provides lots of examples. I would recommend him to anyone.
Terrible instructor.Avoid take any classes with him if you can.
Terrible teacher. Hard exam without curve and cut-off.

Very organized and clear when explaining things in lecture. Notes become your best friend because the homework follows them closely and they are easy to take with his examples. He is always willing to explain things out of class and makes you work your way through the problems to help learn. It works. Highly recommend taking him for a math class.

Great teacher, very helpful, understands your strengths and weaknesses. The problems on the quizzes and tests are all reasonable, although they require some thought. Math becomes fun and not intimidating at this level

Tyler is absolutely the best math teacher I've ever had (that includes college and high school teachers who've been teaching for decades). I felt like I fully understood the material at the end of the quarter. He dedicates a lot of time out of his busy schedule to help students. Fantastic teacher.

Tyler may seem intimidating at first, but if you take the time to listen and pay attention, everything in the class will be very approachable. He made me love calculous when I thought I would hate it. If you have to take calculous, take it with Tyler.

Very good teacher. Took lots of time out of his busy day to help us who are not blessed with good math skills. I would highly recommend. Very hard test though, that do not go well with what is assigned for homework.
Great teacher, highly dedicated!
Great teacher, incredibly dedicated!   Clearly explains concepts and is dedicated to answering questions.  Promptly responds to emails at all hours. HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommended!
Fantastic gtf. Mixes lecture with group work and actual student participation. Twice weekly homework instead of every night. Really engaging lecturer. Total babe.
No Comments
Tyler is a great instructor.  The material was extremely difficult but he gave it his all and everything else rested on us.
Tyler is always willing to help outside of class. Seems like he  cared about his students.
This “professor” seems to have STOLEN his entire curriculum and all inspiration from our previous awesome instructor Amanda Powell. She knows her stuff inside and out, and he is a hack :(

Kramer is my absolute favorite professor I've had. He always makes class time super fun and I was always excited to show up. The works assigned in the course were extremely engaging and are now some of my favorite literature. I'll never forget this class and how much joy it brought me!!

I love this professor so much, their classes are engaging and enjoyable. Attendance is mandatory, but that wasn't an issue, I wanted to come to each class meeting. They put so much time and effort into the readings and presentations. I would take this course again if I could.

I love Prof Kramer! He made class so fun and engaging and definitely helped me break out of my shell! I recommend taking a class with him because he was incredible and I wish I could take more of his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Kramer is an amazing professor! They took over my class when my past professor was unable to do her job and the class was a mess. He was able to totally turn the course around and give us engaging work. So funny, so nice, and gave us a lot of really interesting insight and new ideas. Would take their class in a heartbeat :)

I don't like reading nor did I think I'd like this class. But he's truly an amazing professor and it was by far the best class so far this term. I had fun in lectures, the workload was easy, and the assignments and readings you'd get interested in so it didn't feel like work. Highly recommend overall amazing. great guy, great class/ structure.

Professor Kramer is the best teacher I have ever had. Ever. He's very real and authentic when teaching and makes you actually want to go to class. There is a good amount of reading but it's worth it. They are interesting, educational, and inspiration. This class taught me a lot about the world and made me a better person.

Fairly easy class if you do the readings and are good at writing. The class is small which is helpful for the topics that you discuss. Kramer is an amazing lecturer and makes an effort to know the students. If you're looking for an Arts requirement I definitely recommend this course.
Best professor ever!! Kramer is so funny and chill, but also an amazing teacher. I would 100% recommend taking this course! Lots of reading... but the readings are actually engaging.

Such an amazing teacher, he's so funny and you learn so much. I would recommend this class to anyone. open always down to understand I grew so much as a student I only missed 1 class I loved it so much!!!!!

He was a great teacher for my comp lit class. Canvas and lectures were organized with a reasonable amount of work. He was really entertaining and fun. I liked going to class and I feel like I learned some interesting things.

Great professor! He is super chill and down to earth, he is young and easy to connect with. We had 5 short reading response papers and 2 essays, for the essays he only grades on how well you edit it from the first draft (super easy grader). Very welcoming and overall great professor. Attendance is mandatory and participation is required in class.

Matthias is a fabulous teacher and I would highly recommend taking a class with them. They work hard to make students feel welcome and encourage them to try their best. Super nice and engaging prof! Class has 2 reflections, 2 papers and weekly reading quizzes that are easy if you do the reading.

Class is organized really well and I actually enjoyed taking a writing class. There is a lot of reading, but everything is online. Quizzes are straight forward and it's clear they want you to succeed. Would recommend for people who need to fulfill their wiring credits because the class was fun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class is overall super easy. There is a good amount of work to do with essays and assignments but they are easy to do. If you don't mind doing lots of busy work then the class is not bad and very structured. There is also an exam every 2 weeks which can be annoying but the tests are generally just easy versions of what you do in class

LING 150 is technically a 100 level course, but it has the most busy work of any class I've ever taken here. The assignments are not hard, there are just a million of them, so beware. I also feel like the prof is a super picky grader. Overall though, if you're looking for an easy online arts & letters to take, this one is fine. Annoying but easy.

Calls infants/children "kiddos," which says alot about him in a good way! Assigns lots of/some bland readings but explains them in lectures, slides are pretty dense so type fast. Tries to include real world examples whenever possible (very helpful). Well-traveled guy, funny and sweet. Class got more rigorous later in term: lab test lab lab final :0

I took this class asynchronously and there were no video lectures, instead there was textbook readings and professor written readings. This made it difficult to grasp some content. Additionally, there are lots of small assignments that add up quickly. Besides this the course is interesting and lots of extra credit is offered throughout the term.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Excellent professor

As a senior English major, this class is definitely mislabeled and should really be a 250-300 level course with the amount of work due and lack of quality teaching. Not that he doesn't provide ways to learn, but they aren't good. There are no recorded lessons and he relies on the book to teach everything. The topics are complicated and confusing.

reviews.comment: Very few videos or lectures to watch which makes it very easy to read the textbook and online lectures on your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Has a heavier courseload, as mentioned before by others. Exams are easy as long as you read and do the exercises, which are quick and simple for the most part. Written assignments are annoying and graded harshly, but are only 15% of the grade. Overall, if you're willing to put in the time and keep up, it's an easy class for an arts and letters req.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class has a huge workload for a 100 level course. There's 10-12 exercises per week, a discussion post, weekly readings, weekly written assignments, and 4 exams. The written assignments are graded hard and the feedback is terrible on them. Getting a good grade in this class is achievable, but get ready to spend a good amount of time on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class has a crazy amount of work due each week for a 100 level class! 9-10 exercises, a written assignment, a quiz, and a long reading. It's do able, but takes up a big chunk of your time. The professor also isn't great at responding to emails. I've sent him a couple so far and have gotten no response.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Online class, so hard to Judge Prof. Kyle's specific teaching style, but the class's workload is obscene for a 100 level class. 10-12 exercises (small quizzes, but unlimited attempts) and 1 discussion post a week, and 4 exams across the class. Not hard to get an A in the course, but so much work.

Kyle was a very relaxed and fun teacher to be with. But be warned that LING302 involves a lot of reading very long linguistic research papers that must be only interesting to people who are really really into linguistics.
Really, really interesting class and Yarris knows how to lead a discussion and get people engaged with the readings. Wish I could take this class again!

Poorly utilizes Canvas, making it very difficult for students to track due dates of assignments. Discussion sections feel disconnected from lectures. Students are discouraged from asking about exam grades or for further feedback as she threatens regrading them negatively.
horrible lectures, makes no sense, canvas is set up in a way where you cant see your assignments, grading does not make sense, GEs also make no sense. Dont take unless required.

Her lectures are very engaging and she often uses her personal experiences to relate to the content. My biggest complaint is the way she uses Canvas. I've missed multiple assignments because she doesn't make them assignments on the Canvas page. They are hidden within each week's individual module. It's also hard to reach her when you need help.

This prof does not care to use canvas in a way that is helpful to students. I missed several assignments that she refuses to post as "assignments" to encourage students to engage with the canvas page. (sort thru module after module?) The class is generally confusing and a regurgitation of 2 other more valuable courses.

Dr. Yarris is a GOD. She is a great professor who has developed an amazing class. In 270, she would make it an in-class assignment for us to write OUR OWN midterm and final exam questions and she would choose her favorites from there. She gave us the questions prior to the exams so we could outline our responses, and she gives ample time to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, very knowledgeable about public health. The exams are heavily based on the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: even if you do not have accommodations ask her for them. she is very good at helping if things go missing or you are late. very fast at email. talks very quickly in lecture so be prepared to outline your notes before hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dont take a class with her. She teaches by talking at you the entire time. No slides outlining what shes talking about, no asking questions or engaging you in any way, just talking at you. Kept her doors open even when it was 45 degrees out. The midterms (one in week 3) are worth a lot of your grade and are only out of 20 points.  Ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yarris is very knowledgable and makes sure to leave time for any questions people may have. If you attend the lectures and ask questions you will easily pass

Professor Yarris knows what she's talking about and chose interesting cases. I even added a GH minor after this class! The single midterm at 30% was stressful but I do think getting an A or B isn't that difficult if you attend class or at least catch up on your own time. Lectures could be dry but I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Yarris is really sweet and funny. She's really passionate about Global Health and it shows. Lectures can get kind of boring, though. Overall the class is easy as long as you show up. Because the tests are worth such little points but still a big part of your grade, it's easy to drop % so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yarris is a good teacher. Her lectures are interesting, but can get a little boring at times. The midterm and final are not too difficult, if you go to class and pay attention you'll get a high grade. Interesting material, I recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yarris helps present new perspectives on GH that I found very interesting. She is an engaging, approachable prof and really made me interested in GH as a career. I appreciate that she addresses critiques of GH because she wants to give students real insight into how the system works. If you read and attend class, you should do well. I recommend!

Yarris is a knowledgeable woman, but she is not interesting. I do not recommend this class unless you like to fall asleep... If you sit in the front you should be fine, but I thought this class would be super interesting and Yarris honestly is not cut out to be a teacher. She is boring.

Professor Yarris is one of my favorite INTL professors. She is incredibly organized, knowledgeable, and passionate about teaching. Her lectures are also very well prepared. She treats students like adults, so don't expect to be coddled. If you are interested in global health, I recommend Global Health and Development without reservation.

Dave is the best professor ever in my school history. He is always heartwarming, respectful, patient,professional to everyone and giving amazing lectures. He provides support to his students in and out of school about study, work, like, and even mental health. I feel grateful for him about what he's done for students. He loves his job and students!

Lectures were pointless to attend because he didn't really cover anything about advertising,lasted prob 15min. There's a lot of assignments and they're not time consuming as it's almost like discussion posts. He doesn't grade any of the assignments until after finals week and there's no clear grading criteria so it's a guessing game. He's chill tho
Best professor ever!! If you are interested for advertising and media planning, you should take his class and enjoy it!
Best professor ever!

AWESOME Teacher. I have had him for 3 ad classes and he is great. Very easy and laid back, fun and knowledgeable. He can be a little spacey sometimes but he is human. You learn a lot and he knows a lot of people in the advertising world so is a great contact to have. A lot of group work, but its helpful since your work in teams in advertising.
Dave is the man.  Not too tough, but you'll learn a ton.

i came to write this from an assignment of his because i am so bored. the entire class is just garageband and while he does make you use his textbook for the tutorials, the later ones are so hard to follow. i don't even care what my song sounds like and i don't want to sing for it but there is no other choice unless you have a friend who sings
Yeah, you can't sell your own textbooks, guy.

I honestly don't agree with the reviews on here. MUS 151 is structured so that if you follow the instructions written in his textbook exactly you will get an A. It was frustrating to not have complete creative freedom, but it's a good introduction to music production. Fair warning- he talks so slow. 2x speed on the lectures is a must.

Toby is not a good professor. Yes, his class is easy, but it's a scam. You have to buy a $90 textbook HE MADE, which is just instructions you could find anywhere. Another review called him a fraud, and I agree. It's a waste of money, and he doesn't respond to emails.

MUS151 isn't what you think it is, I went in assuming I'd learn how to make music and be creative, however Toby makes you follow his $90 gate-kept textbook (insturctions) for how to make a terrible song. Toby is a fraud, I know those are harsh words but this class wasn't exciting in the least bit, he couldn't make it more monotone and uncreative

Online lectures were super dull, he talks in a monotone voice which is super easy to tune out of. The two assignments song projects graded allow for zero creativity. You have to follow his instructions exactly to get a good grade. Work load was more of a 200 level class as well, I would not recommend

Toby requires you to purchase a $90 textbook Toby wrote that is literally just the instructions for his assignments. He has his GEs do all the grading, doesn't record more than 10 minutes lectures TOTAL, and doesn't interact with students. This class is focused on following instructions and does not encourage creativity or songwriting. Do not take.

You definitely need to enjoy the topic to be able to enjoy this class. Hes really interested in this field and I thought he was a good professor, but his organization definitely needs work. The rubrics are VERY minimal. Coming from someone who isn't great at philosophy, the class was honestly fine and kinda fun, people on here are overly critical
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Colin's class structure was assembled around the syllabus which included a schedule for the entire course. While this may sound like a good start, this was as far as his effort went. The canvas page was nonexistent, readings were excruiciatingly hard to find and it seemed to me as if he had a very low knowledge of philosophy. You will drop week 1!

One of the hardest to navigate classes I've ever taken. I spent more time looking for the course material, and making sure I wasn't missing assignments or readings than actually reading. Colin seems like a well intentioned dude, but its such a selfishly formatted class I would never take him as a professor again.

The professor himself was good, however the class lacked organization. Canvas sight was very confusing and hard to find readings, ect. The GE's are very harsh graders and I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you don't need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some bums who dropped the class first week review bombed him which is lame. Do not take this class as a random elective, this is a class you take only if you are into the content. It is difficult and a lot for a 100 level class but if you do the readings you will learn a lot. it changes how you think about the way the world works. I loved it.

This was one of the most unpleasant classes I took all year at UO. It was mostly because the assignments were all over the place. It was never straightforward, you had to go searching through the files and announcements to even know what was going on... super unorganized and one of the GEs was extremely rude and unwelcoming, but Colin's chill.

reviews.comment: If one truly wants to get a better understanding of philosophy and how technology is influencing society you will learn a ton but only if you are up for the challenge. Three essays and a group project. Essays were pretty easy. Every class has a reading response and the readings are about 20 pages every two days. Class is good lazybones will fail.

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Just don't. Every other 100 level is better. Passive-aggressive and condescending, assigns a ton of work.

reviews.comment: Cons: this class will challenge you. the papers are hard because it tests your intellect and critical thinking. You need to work for an A. There is a reading assignment for EVERY CLASS. Slides are a hot mess sometimes. Pro: easy to talk to if you have questions, you will improve your writing and adopt a deeper understanding of ethics.

reviews.comment: From the lecture Colin struck me as a professor who doesn't care about his students. His instructions are extremely difficult to understand, as are his power points. He assigned 6 books, one of which was written by a known white supremacist. If you care about ethics you will be very disappointed in taking this course. I will be changing my major.

102 is a hard class, it is not what I was expecting out of a PHIL class. However, it will help you improve your writing and your intellect. Koopman is sometimes hard to understand mainly because he is highly intellectual. If you want to challenge yourself take his course if you don't reconsider why you're in college. College is hard people.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He might be the most passive aggressive person Ive ever met and he keeps saying if you are struggling in the class or think you might be struggling you should just drop. On the first day he spent a solid 10 minutes telling us how to pronounce his name and that was the most interesting thing I learned in this class. Theres also 6 required books
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ridiculously petty teacher. Consistently tried to pressure students who weren't serious enough about the class to drop it . Makes lectures and sections mandatory with an assignment for each every day we had class. His lectures are excruciating, and I personally did whatever I could to avoid sitting through one.
Super enthusiastic professor that really knows the material and is super easy to talk to.
Amazing professor!  Love his lectures!

While his appearance does remind me quite a bit of Jack Skellington, he was an interesting, witty and sharp teacher. Lectures were always interesting and he has a way of engaging a class into thinking about what he is passionate about. I strongly recommend any of his courses.

Clear and straightforward. Sometimes funny, always helpful. For an experimental course, or even by the standards of any course, Koopman easy to listen to and learn from. Recommended. Note, he is a little bit intimidating.

Colin is an excellent teacher,very engaging, very helpful and interested in helping you during office hours. A lot of reading, definitely a demanding course, but his class piqued my interest in philosophy greatly, and I would take him again in a second

While this class was difficult for me, Colin was extremely helpful. Attendance was mandatory and for a class at 8:30 in the morning, this kind of sucked, however I was always ready to get out of bed and go to class.
Great professor

I took this class last spring and Professor Russel is an amazing lecturer breaking down topics and inspired me to minor in ENVS! However, if you take this class be ready for a group presentation worth 100 points and a heavy annotated bibliography. Only four actual homework assignments in the term but they're (slightly) harshly graded. :)

He had incredible lectures and always brought positivity into the course which is helpful for those in an environmental major. Him and his GE's were great with communication whenever I emailed. He always posted the slides which helped me go over everything if I needed to after class!

I really like what he teaches, but criteria for grading and assignments are often unclear, which can be frustrating. There are readings before every lecture which are often dense and cannot be expected to be completed when considering work from other courses. On the flip side he seems very passionate about the work that he does which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lots of readings but other than that, was an easy A. Prof Russel was super enthusiastic about the content in class and was engaged when talking to him during office hours, tried his best to help out. Tests were not worth too much of the grade and there was extra credit. Would recommend!
Russel is very passionate about what he teaches. Lectures often finished early, but were still interesting. Very nice and flexible, and a pretty easy class overall.

He is a very well-rounded and clear professor who gives good lectures. While the class itself is a bit simple if you have any knowledge in science or environmental studies, it is still not boring. As long as you do the assignments clearly stated on the syllabus you will do great.

only 4 homework which is nice and one big group project. homeworks are worded in a way that make it seem difficult. Lectures & professor himself is engaging but lots of visuals in the lecture slide so be there for lecture to understand what is going on. open notes for mid term and final. highly recommend this course, teacher and overall solid class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were interesting and short (50 minutes). I didn't take notes because there were no tests, but the lectures were engaging. He said at the beginning there would be surprise quizzes but we never had one. The grading depends on your GE, mine was really nice and generous with grading, especially because it was all projects.

Very lecture-heavy, but he's a good speaker and the slides are engaging. Biggest problem is that he talks about a LOT of things and it's hard to distinguish what you need to take notes on. 

Low number of graded assignments so far, which can be a small issue.

Midterm test was fair but difficult. Homework has been relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He said our midterm was multiple choice + short answer, but there was no multiple choice. After question 17/25, they got harder and worth more. We were not informed this would be the case. He also arranged it so you can't return to prior questions. I studied hard, yet possibly failed. Absolutely unacceptable behavior from a PhD professor here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Caused me to switch my major, little hw but is very easy. Puts memes in his lectures. GEs will help you more that the actual professor so it matters which GE you have, overall great class.
Pretty boring lectures but not too difficult of a class.

Lectures were only 50min twice a week and you dont need to take notes. You dont even have to show up really since he posts the lectures online. Project instructions could be unclear at times. Easy grader, procrastinated a lot in this class and put in little effort and still got an A. Has weekly readings but i never read them and he never quized

His lectures were very long and boring with no class interaction. Grading took forever, and he didnt give much help for tests, (He posted a study guide less than 24 hours before the final). However he was a nice person, not a harsh grader, and definitely has experience in the field he is teaching

Kory is an excellent professor, and if this was a normal school year and I had him in person, I'm sure I would have given him a 5. However, the class was not managed as well as I would have hoped. Grading took forever, lecture quizzes were speratic and not uploaded for weeks, and overall communication was limited. Fun and easy class though.

He gives a multiple choice quiz based on the readings each class, they are not that hard. He does assign 4 papers, but some are only 1-2 pages. There is a group project. Easy grader, but slow at grading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kory Russel is an outstanding professor. He is extremely qualified, and has tons of experience in Environmental Studies/Public Health etc. I would recommend him. Get ready to laugh and feel comfortable in an engaging and productive learning environment. Get engaged, do the readings, and you will have no problem.

Professor Russel doesn't seem to know a lot about what he's doing and often seems distracted, but he cares a lot about his students and has interesting career experience in the field. He's a nice guy, but kind of a messy teacher.

Felt like an unreasonably high workload for a 100-level class. Sometimes felt like the readings and weekly assignments didn't help you learn much. Lectures are somewhat dry, the info is good but he would sometimes repeat himself from day to day. Labs are pretty attainable.

Professor Kohler is a very interesting guy; his lectures are slightly boring, but it's an easy class to pass. There is a big lab project that is every week, and most of the other work is busywork. Overall you are doing most of the work in your lab.

My least favorite GIS prof at UO. Lecture activities/discussions consist of AI generated handouts and handouts essentially asking you what he should be teaching you(?). Labs are much more applicable to real-world work than other GIS courses, but have the most unclear/frustrating/conflicting/outdated directions. I learned a lot more from the GEs

I think this class would've been so much better if it was just in person. It is a LOT of material to go over. The assignments themselves can be long and wordy, making them hard to understand, and I struggled a bit as someone who has never used Storymap before. The assignments can also have some hard word counts to meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Kohler is extremely average. Nice enough, just fairly boring during lectures. The class is set up well, with labs every other week or so, and weekly quizzes and homework. Brought in some interesting guest lectures. Fairly easy A.

Lecture material was pretty standard and boring. The assignments were pretty easy; lab assignments were often frustrating due to outdated instructions.
