Nick strangely used a lot of generative AI to create handouts and supporting materials. Has a super generous late-work policy, -1% per day. I feel we covered too many topics, which has pros and cons

One of the toughest classes I have taken at UO but to be expected from a 482. Lectures had mandatory assignments attached to them but helped a lot with the projects so might as well go anyway. Majority of the class grade is based upon the 4 labs that take anywhere from 3-20 hours to complete depending on your GIS skill level.

Tests are easy, labs are slightly harder but mostly just time-consuming. I thought the labs were fun and really helpful for me to start figuring out the basics of GIS and mapping software. He's a really nice guy too, decently funny.
For a geography professor tho, he could be a bit better at naming the states on a map though, lol
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: did this for summer course. professor is nice and willing to help but does take awhile to grade things. easyish class but does require a lot of work for a 100 level course, felt like a 200/300 almost. gave feedback on lab work and tests. weekly pop quizzes along with a lab and then some writing assignments. no lecture video, just reading chp online

I enjoyed this class. The lectures were short and not super important, but they were somewhat enjoyable. I really enjoyed the labs. Not to many assignments in this class and the tests were take-home and rather simple. I learned a lot about GIS so I would recommend.

I just really enjoyed class with this professor. He was always trying to make class interesting and engaging and you could tell he was very knowledgable in GIS. He was a little hard contact him via email but that was my only complaint. Other than that we was very nice and a good teacher.

Nick Kohler is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He is very hard to understand in between all of the "ummss...." and groans. He never made the class interesting or exciting at all. Not only is he the worst lecturer, this class GEOG 181, uses Top Hat which is by far the worst online textbook you will ever have. instructions are vague.

Couple of intensive assignments through out the weeks, but nothing too difficult. The tests/quizzes are plenty, but you'd have to be pretty damn stupid not to pass. Lectures are boring as hell, but the professor seems like a genuine guy. Just skim the powerpoint notes, read the chapters, and you're good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This dude is a straight up legend. He pulled on on abraham lincoln hat in the middle of lecture. He has dorky, corny jokes but I am here for it. He is very kind and reasonable and respectful to his students, even though it can be hard to pay attention during lectures. Take this class for the gen eds, you will not regret it.

He's a nice guy, and he is definitely passionate about the subjects he teaches. The only problem is that his lectures get very boring. He cracks a few jokes every now and then but expect 90% of class to be looking at a powerpoint. If you don't manage to pay attention the whole class, take advantage of the discussion portion which is very helpful

Very nice guy, passionate about his subject. Unfortunately his lectures are disjointed and they do nothing to liven up an already dull subject (regional geography, with emphasis on economy and historic settlement). Adds up to a two hour lecture that's hard to stay awake through.  You'd have to LOVE geography to get anything from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy,  and enjoys what he teaches. But his lectures feel disorganized and hard to follow,  making it really difficult to take notes of good substance. His tests have to be the worsted part.  Part multiple choice,  part short answer based off 5 chapters of reading and will ask very specific questions, so memorize every fact you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am a person who has no interest in Geography, and I thought this course would be an easy way to fulfill my General Education requirement, but it was challenging to pass it. The professor is kind of a funny person, he is very understanding and helps you when you need it, he goes very quick through the slides and you gotta catch up quickly.

I think he's a good instructor. he tries to liven things up a bit during long lectures with jokes & current events. Tests are hard; mostly essay format. I studied the slides & my notes & only skimmed the book for tests. Most Qs were based on lectures. He's very good about answering Qs & helping if you are stuck on an assignment.

You really need to attend the classes to learn the material. Pretty much everything is in the lecture, so pay attention & take good notes. Tests were mostly short essay format. I felt like he was pretty good about giving credit for showing you've been paying attention & know the stuff. The material is really hard, but he made it fun & manageable.

Difficult to follow and his slides were just a series of pdfs with links to other sites. Definitely trails off a lot. He is very knowledgeable when it comes to field work and software but you really need to be proactive about communicating with him if you want help.

I had him for a freshman seminar and the class was interesting but almost too long and sometimes i felt bored. However he makes things interesting by adding references to lady gaga or gwen stefani and someone relating it to the topic. He's a funny dude

Found it difficult to follow and unorganized. I found it impossible to take notes, making studying impossible. He does not speak up and trails off important information. Lecture slides are a joke and are only headings and no in depth information. I suggest sitting in front with a voice recorder so you will have something to get the info you need.
No Comments
Well-made lab exercises, very knowledgeable and understanding.

Really supportive professor who gives helpful writing feedback. The class has regular weekly assignments, which can be a lot if you fall behind, but she's flexible with deadlines. Great experience overall.

I would 100% recommend Anna for WR 121z. She is extremely helpful, and gives good feedback. There is a lot of small papers, but you get time to do them in class. She is very funny and kind and genuinely cares about getting to know her students. If you can, take a class with her!

Anna seems like a nice person and this class was good overall. I learned a lot about making reports, tailoring to audiences, and providing/receiving feedback for peers. Her feedback was a bit generic for all but like 2-3 assignments and there was a lot more work near the end unexpectedly. It's not a hard class but don't expect an easy A.
I loved her class... She has great energy, very understanding. Open to questions. She lets you write as you are. Not a hard grader she grades on completion

I do not understand why Anna got so many negative reviews. Personally, I had a great experience with her and I feel the class improved my writing immensely. It was very easy to get assignments done on time because there was a built-in 48 hour extension on every assignment. The workload was not too heavy. I would recommend taking this with Anna.
I cannot believe that after going to office hours and the writing lab, Anna would not raise my 88 to a 90. She is insanely annoying and assigns way too much work for a writing class.

I'll keep this review simple becuase I have to get back to my second paper due for her class this week alone. She assigns an insane amount of work for a WR122 class... they are known for being the easiest-cake-walk classes of your life but not hers. for the amount of work I'm talking about anywhere from 2-4 assignments a week (LONG assignments).

very passive and aggressive. The feedback was okay, not very detailed on what she wanted on the homework. The only upside was that there was little work, but it was graded very harshly for a 122Z writing class. Overall, she was okay. I would try to find a better professor. someone who is more understanding.
she is a tough grader. she will find every little "mistake" and mark you down.

I do not think Anna is as bad as these reviews make her out to be, while her assignments are a bit repetitive and she highly recommends attending class she is a pretty understanding prof. Her feedback could be improved, but she is generally very easy to talk to and work through any confusion with.

I think other people's ratings are a little harsh. She is pretty understanding and isn't a super tough grader, at least in my experience. My only complaint is that there are a lot of discussion post assignments a good amount of 2-3 page essays. These assignments aren't super hard, just pretty tedious and boring.

She was very nice and understanding, but could grade a little harshly. Class is easy if you put in just a little effort. No tests, just a few papers, discussion boards, and a final project. Half the classes you don't have to go to because it's a "work day" for project. I would recommend her, pretty easy class, but you do need to put in some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although the professor clearly cares about the wellbeing of her students this course is a lot of busywork. She grades very harshly, taking away points on assignments while giving feedback such as "Excellent work!" Despite this assignment instructions and lectures are very clear

Very condescending and unhelpful during required 1-on-1 meetings. Lots of points would be removed seemingly at random without much explanation and without opportunity to recover them. It was nice taking this online but every interaction with her via email or zoom left a really bad impression.

If you are like me, don't take the online version if you aren't good at meeting deadlines. I know you may think it isn't a big deal, but trust your gut. Long course readings that were tough to include into the essay and takes off points but doesn't really explain why, even if you have felt you have done every part of the assignment.
Literally the worst teacher Ive ever had. Never take her if she aint the last option. Trust me lol this is a terrible experience

Surprised to see the ratings on here, but maybe my experience was different than others' because I took her course online this term. I thought she was a great professor and was super caring. She gives great feedback in office hours and genuinely cares about the wellbeing of her students. Lots of readings in beginning of the term though.

This professor clearly thinks she's teaching an advanced course at an ivy league. This is supposed to be a base level course and she is assigning readings meant for someone going for a masters in philosophy. There are lots of readings that are unclear and terribly structured for a course like this but don't expect any help from her in any regard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Kolvachuk, so it was extremely shocking to me to come on here and see such negative reviews on her. From my personal opinion out of all the English teachers Ive had, shes the one that's pushed me to love writing the most because her class wasnt just an easy A. I highly recommend her to those who are willing to work hard

shes defentily not compassionate or caring. I was going through stuff and she did not excuse it. I told her to put herself in my shoes and show some compassion and she just said I dont favor students its not fair for you to be excused... wow someone help this lady find compassion and caring for her students well being.
lecture heavy +boring
yeah, same I went to office hours and when I explain or try to talk she interrupts like what kind of instructor interrupts her students I am trying to communicate my issues
I was unable to work on a assignment because of my prescriptions given that day and she still deducted credit even though I was unable of performing such task given. Ridiculous!
dont expect special treatment if you get sick or have a surgery. she wont make any exceptions
Dont like the way she teaches
Wouldnt recommend taking writing 121 with her
Wouldn't recommend going to office hours she will only repeat what she said in class
she isnt good at giving back feedback. Maybe include examples?
I wrote an essay and her feedback did not provide any examples of how I could improve.
Anna gives good feedback and provides clear information. She is a little tough on grading. If you do all the requirements and follow her feedback it should be a moderate class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anna was a fantastic professor who clearly cares about your success. She's very reachable in office hours and you can get more specific feedback there. I personally feel like the topic we had for the term, pseudo-science vs. science was very boring and not something that is easy to follow. There's a lot of reading, but she's a great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's super sweet and understanding that her students have other classes, will give you an extension as long as you ask two days ahead and really wants to connect with you as a person
Anna was super nice and very open to new ideas and perspectives. She can be a tough grader and I found a lot of the topics we wrote about to be kind of boring and repetitive.
If you're looking for a good grade in this class, talk to Anna as much as possible, go to her office hours and you'll get the right instructions to write an A paper.

Overall, the class was interesting and engaging but she is a difficult grader. Definitely go into her office hours and she is very willing to help with essays, discuss materials, and grades. Reading assignments each night with two essays and an in-class midterm. She talks very quickly but try to write down what she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Anna is a great, knowledgeable professor. The course helped me understand film to the extent where I could use my knowledge from this class and translate it to other film classes. She is tough grader when it comes to papers; however, you get the feeling she wants your writing to improve as the course progresses.

Simply put: unhelpful and opinionated. This class was basically a review on WR121 with less material and less work. If you take this class make sure you have the same perspective on controversial issues and you'll pass with flying colors.

Anna tends to grade certain assignments on personal opinion. If she disagrees with the essays perspective on a topic she will grade harshly despite time and effort shown. As well as giving advice in terms of avoiding any research that isn't your own.  I reccomend a different teacher if you wish to write informative essays.

This teacher does not seem to put any real effort for the students writing in the future. She also does not fight for her students when they have issues and would rather hide away on the sake of expediency. If you want to get an easy A from a Teacher that doesn't seem to care, she would be the perfect teacher.

Anna is honestly the nicest professor you will meet at UO. She is a great teacher. She encourages you to do your own thing and gives really good feedback on essays. She is funny and makes class interesting. I love her grading style and eagerness to help. This review doesn't do her justice. Take her class if you get the chance

Very good for people who do well with boring lectures and reading the textbook every night. Lectures are poorly formatted, slides are unstructured and you will have to filter out what's important on your own. TA's do a better job explaining, and discussions are necessary to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Koscho has clear guidelines and is a great lecturer. However when working under his TA Hunt, I felt that I was harshly graded and could never understand what I was truly being graded under. Went from a really good grade to being surprised with almost a C and this is after two labs being graded after finals week! Point deductions are brutal here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor lectures on and on but doesn't do anything regarding participation, no iClicker or turning in lecture notes to make sure class is paying attention. Has office hours, but explains things in a way that makes you feel like you're stupid for not knowing things. Doesn't curve or drop tests. Gives poor feedback.

Koscho is the best teacher for Organic! There's certainly a lot to learn and expect to be doing studying outside of HW/Quiz prep if you want a good grade. Koscho has a unique, dry sense of humor, but he does care about the students he teaches, and is great in office hours. Tests were the hardest part but the overall average was never super low.

Dr. Koscho's lectures are clear and rather detailed, and he is direct as to what his expectations within the class are. If you are someone who usually gets a lot out of lectures themselves, then you will probably enjoy his classes. He doesn't tend to do much in-class practice, so be prepared for a lot of studying outside of class.
Overall, the class material is really difficult but I think he does his best to simplify it down. The tests were toughly graded though.

Koscho is a great ochem professor. His office hours are very helpful and his lectures are very informative. Doing practice problems outside of class is important for success and mastery of the basics of ochem.

Koscho was really effective at teaching organic chemistry. Every thing mentioned in this lectures was thoroughly and accurately explained. His class was especially good because of how easy the tests were. You basically only need to know the beginning of each chapter the test covers.

First of all Koscho is a nice guy. I think he teaches well to a specific kind of person. If you are okay with reading the textbook every night and then you will exceed. If you are like me and enjoy worked problems in class and participation (clickers as a minimum) this class will be mundane to say the least. He works for some, not for me.
Hey was very nice and gave a lot of resources

Best OCHEM professor during a remote summer class! The way he had the class set up was amazing and there's lots of chance for you to ask questions with other students or the teacher himself. His tests are essentially the same as what we've been learning. There wasn't any homework, more majorly a test each week on the chapter and practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was online (due to COVID) and Koscho prepared lecture videos for every chapter. The course itself was difficult because of the structure. Quizzes every Monday, hw due on Wednesdays by midnight. I was always studying or doing hw, it felt like. But I learned a lot. Koscho communicated the material clearly and effectively.
Dr. Koscho is the best professor I have had at UO, supper cool guy and easy to reach outside of class. Make sure to do the practice problems/readings and you will be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were concise and helpful, and I really liked the textbook we used. This class is a challenge, but if you put in the time to do the readings and the lectures and work through the problems, you'll be fine.
He was great during covid times
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Koscho is a tough grader on tests, but gives access to all of the information you will need to know in lectures and PLTL is very helpful. DO ALL PROBLEMS until thoroughly understood. If you dont know the answer to a test question, say sterics or resonance. He is a great teacher with a tasteful amount of sarcasm and self deprecation. He is a fav.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found Koscho to be difficult to communicate questions with. During office hours and tutorials, I often felt stupid for asking a question because his response would be that it was easy and that we should already understand that concept. I ended up learning more from the TA's and went to their office hours instead. The curve is nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very clear teaching style. Tells you exactly whats on exams and has practice tests. Theres a curve too

Funny guy, but man is that final brutal. It's tempting to skip class all term like I did as attendance isn't tracked, but you'll end up getting hammered by a final that goes even beyond the scope of the post-lab questions asked throughout the term. Don't read the textbook, just go to lecture.

Koscho is one of the best O chem professors. Took his class in the summer so its even more fast paced and ended with a B. O chem is not an easy class but he tries to make it really easy for you and is really helpful during office hours. The tests were super straight forward and there was like a 15 percent curve on ur final grade. Take him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of material was covered. The final exam was extraordinarily difficult, even though we had a whole page of hand written notes that we could bring. It is really important to understand the concepts: why you do in lab what you do. His teaching is good, nothing special. He has a weird scene of humor but that helps break up the monotony of lab.

Solid, down-to-earth individual. Wish he taught more of the upper division chem classes instead of the self-important "if you are doing research for me you'll get an A" crowd who masquerade as teachers. ZERO BS coming from this guy.

Koscho is hilarious. Took him for Ochem 1 and lab 1 in the summertime and learned a ton. He's very approachable and friendly, and good at teaching the stuff he teaches. Honestly, this guy made learning ochem enjoyable. Would absolutely recommend him to any fellow student. That said, ochem is not easy. If you put in the time, you will get the grade.

Homework every week. You either have to read and understand the text, or go to lecture. Picks helpful GTFs each term. Good lectures and posts lecture notes. Homework is pretty light, but supplemental problems are a must for passing midterms (there are 2) and finals. Discussion sessions are SUPER helpful!

Koscho is a hilarious guy who is always there to help with questions. He keeps the class involved and interested. The exams are tough but reasonable given the subject. Wish he was teaching 342 next term as I'd love to take more classes with him.

Easier lab reports than the first term of ochem lab, however, the final was harder. He rewards attendance at his lectures with notes that are EXACTLY replicated on the final. Final also includes questions from your post labs. Do well on the lab reports, because the final kicks everyone's grades down. Mikes a cool guy and his TAs are great as well.
Favorite!!!!!  Lectures are so entertaining and informative!!  Great guy. Great prof.  Win.
His notes are hard to follow. Tests are hard too but he is a really good teacher.
funny guy. lots of material was covered, but there are plenty of resources for help. recommend taking class from him because he is pretty clear about what you need to know.

Hilarious! Loved his class! He makes Ochem easy to understand. Very approachable. In general just a great person and wonderful teacher. I would take any chemistry class with him for the simple fact that I would understand it.

Funny, entertaining and fair.  He's the best teacher I had this year.  He was especially funny during third term, I think this was because he already weeded some students.  (He hated the kids who couldn't handle organic chemistry)

One day before a test I asked him for a calculator and he said that he doesn't provide them and it was our responsibility.  So I sat down down and five minutes later he made an announcement to the class that if anyone needed a calculator there were a couple up front. Hahaha!!! And he sounds like the scientist from the Simpsons
He's super nerdy, but very clear with what material we're responsible for.

he has probably the most annoying voice i have ever heard, and his lecture sometimes put me to sleep.  other than that he is a good prof, clear on what you need to know and there are plenty of resources for help

quiz or midterm every week on thursdays, DO NOT TAKE THE MORNING THURSDAY LAB. curves class, no homework, lots of study materials available online. there are 3 midterms and 7 quizzes with the two lowest dropped. great guy!
Rather sarcastic. I liked Johnson better.  :-/
This guy is hilarious and smart as hell too.  Excellent insructor and cool outside of class.  Margaritas!
No Comments
meh.

Sarcastic at times, but intelligent and more importantly clear & reasonable. Lacks the charisma of D.J. but makes up for it with a sort of nerdy charm that anyone spending 3 hours a day in the library studying o-chem can relate to. I like him more in lecture (335) than lab (337, 338).

Even now that his textbook conflict of interest is resolved the course is still poorly thought out and heavily weiged to Mac users. If you are a windows user you can choose to pay $50 extra or use a library Mac that cannot access the required material. If you can, get your arts and letters credit elsewhere.
Scam professor. DO NOT TAKE

he made 570,000 dollars off students by requiring a poorly written textbook he wrote, without a third party publisher. This is illegal. Read about it on the eugene emerald. I want my tuition money and to be refunded for the book. Dude needs to be fired and hit with a class action. shameful.

This class is obviously a money making scheme for Toby. All 500 of his students are required to pay 90 dollars for HIS textbook. That's $45,000 in revenue a term. The textbook is just a step by step to completing the project and should be a free canvas page. You don't even get to keep the book after the class. Useless info that could be a youtube.

Took class for an easy A, and while it can be easy, I wouldn't recommend. There's a substantial amount of work and he grades pretty harshly. It can be an easy A but you actually need to put in some work. Not the worst class to take, but if you want an easy A, I wouldn't recommend this class.

Biggest gripe: You MUST pay for his required $90 book. Past that, assignments were fun, quizzes were easy, readings were bit boring. It's a class to learn so most creativity comes AFTER the course by yourself. I don't know why reviews are so poor. You MUST follow the general structure of songs, but otherwise you CAN be (kind-of) creative.

This isn't a good class, the school doesn't care either. It's very clear how they treat the students in the SOMD. 
They need to figure this out. He charges for a book he wrote, you cannot be creative, you need to follow his boring jazz stuff. Yet you lean about People like kendrick lammar? this doesn't make any sense.

I thought the "Song Machine" assigned readings provided a really interesting behind-the-scenes perspective on the pop music industry and aspects of the business. The assignments are very specific and graded as such; there were one or two that allowed for more creativity. Quizzes are always very clear and easy if you watch the lecture. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I think Tobias has unjust reviews for his RMP. His class was easy, and the lectures were interesting. Was he the greatest, most inspirational professor, no - but he was good.

The class is based off a textbook Mr. Koenigsberg wrote so as long as you follow the textbook instructions you'll get a good grade. There's about 5 total homework assignments a week but they take roughly a hour to do, excluding lectures. If you want to be creative don't take the class because you will not pass unless you follow the textbook.

Im very confused about the previous rate my professor reviews. Tobys class is very interesting and the content is very interesting. Dont let the previous reviews sway you from taking this class as its very interesting and lets you be creative!

Incredibly harsh grader, especially for a 100 level arts and letters course. Makes you buy his book for $100, and revolves the entire class around it. The book is literally a garage band tutorial. Had a lot of technical difficulties in the beginning of the year trying to follow his instructions for the assignments, and got no assistance from him.

MUS151 is a class that I was very excited to take, however the class is structured very weirdly and does not leave any room for creativity. It looks easy, but the grading is EXTREMELY rigid and doesn't allow for any experimentation. The class is async and all instruction comes from a $90 textbook that he wrote. Very disappointing. Also quiz heavy.

WORST CLASS I have ever taken. It is unfortunate because the subject has a lot of potential since it is about music and songwriting. The professor is probably the worst I have ever had throughout my college experience.

This is by far the worse class I have EVER taken at UO. I initially took this class because I thought it'd be an easy arts and letters credit and a fun way to learn about music. The textbook is written by the prof and is 90$. It's a heavy workload, and the songs are graded so harshly without ANY feedback. MUS151 was painfully stressful

I took this course because I needed an extra course for 4 credits. With it being a 100 level course, I never thought I would be graded so harshly on how I make music. This class was awful. Not only did he charge us $90 to purchase a textbook that he wrote, but he was extremely slow and unhelpful with his responses when I reached out. Not worth it.

This class is the killer of good art. He grades the songs you produce with a strict format that leaves no room for creativity. The first 7 weeks are spent making one beat following his shitty Garageband tutorial that he makes you buy for $90. In the 8th week, he makes you make 2 more beats that follow the same terrible format. This guy sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Worst class ever. Wrote his own textbook so doesn't think he needs to teach. Don't take this class if you're looking for a fun and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I took at UO. It is criminal how much of a scam this class was, a complete waste of time and money. Learned nothing and never once saw or heard anything from this professor. It was entirely just following a textbook, how is this even allowed in a college course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class would be easy but was i wrong. They grade hard and the final was horrible. I even studied and the answers were not previous test questions making it very hard to know what to study. Making a song was fun but you had to follow how he wanted it made and there was not that much freedom. Very time consuming. They grade pretty hard

For MUS 151
Probably the easiest 4 Credits I've ever taken. However, he does charge for a 90$ textbook made by him, which doesn't teach you anything but is required as it holds the instructions for the weekly assignments. Also if not using mac you have to buy a program called Ableton with will be 50$ extra (if you buy the textbook).

I’m not surprised I’m the first review for this Professor as when you look up Toby Koenigsberg you can’t find him on here. He made his own textbook then requires you to buy it so he makes extra money (not sure how that’s even allowed). Class isn’t too hard but as a teacher he sucks. He also doesn’t teach just makes u follow his book.

I LOVE Pearl. They are one of the most insightful teachers I have had. They are understanding, educated, aware, and passionate. I have learned so much about cultures all over the world, and about artistic expression within the world of film. I would 100 percent take this class again.

Professor Pearl led one of the most thought-provoking classes I've taken at UO. The films we watched were really interesting and the discussions we had were equally interesting and relevant to our lives. Her labor-based grading took stress off passing the class, but allowed for those who strived for more to achieve a higher grade. TAKE HER CLASS!
Really great professor, very insightful, intelligent, and passionate, and the films were good.
The workload of the class is very easy. She's a good professor who cares a lot about what she teaches. My only complaint is that she just talks at you for hours without stop.

Professor Lee is really caring toward their students and wants everyone to succeed in the class. The class was really easy and interesting, you watch a film about every week and write 1-2 short discussions about them, and there's 1-3 essays throughout the term. It was a really easy class and they give good feedback! Easy A!

The professor uses the labor-based grading module, nice because you could just do the work and not think too hard, which allows you to put out the best work because you aren't worried about getting the best score. You can do "extra credit" to get your grade higher than the base grade. Work consists of papers and discussion board posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Lee is absolutely amazing. She grades with a labor-based model. If you put in the work and try your hardest, you can earn the grade you want. She was extremely passionate about what she was teaching, and it made me want to go to each lecture.

Nayoung was a great professor and her lectures were interesting. You will have to attend class for participation and there are readings that are required for the quizzes. The quizzes are semi-hard but not that difficult. Overall, this class was great and she is a very good listener and actually cares about her students.

The readings that were assigned weekly and for the quizzes were quite dense and somewhat difficult to understand. In class the professor explained concepts so it was understandable, the discussion section was very useful in this regard. The reading quizzes were difficult despite being open book. Overall this was interesting and not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kwon seems like a nice person in her teachings as well as e-mails! Always gets back to you, only problem I had was that even though the tests were open notes/slides I always got a low score (even though all the questions were practiced before with the GE) So she either put in trick questions or didnt put the right answers in Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kwon is caring. She has semi-difficult quizzes and assigns pretty intense linguistics readings. The topics she covers are interesting though! Pay attention to lecture and do the main readings and you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. She shouldn't teach a class for architects as she's definitely not a good one. This class was boring with lots of redundant busy work.

Alison Kwok is a very effective teacher. Her lectures are robust, yet well outlined and easy to understand. She is very approachable for questions or comments and is consistent with her office hours. Her homework assignments and labs are well designed to reinforce material that is covered in the lecture.

Alison is a wonderful professor. She cares about all of her students and is eager to help them in any way she can. Extra credit is offered often and if you are still struggling, she is very understanding. I wish she taught studio!!
She's an awesome professor. Very energetic and she has great lectures. She's very available to meet outside of class, and very helpful.

she is so amazing. her classes are inspirational and very informative and i wish there had more professors like her. she really engages the students in class and  her class is hard in terms of if you don't go to class and pay attention in the labs you cannot get a good grade. she makes you work for it and that's how i learned but working for it

Alison is one of those rare teachers that is incredibly dedicated to the subject and REALLY wants her students to be as well. She is an inspiration and an amazing person to get to know. She makes the difficult subject fun, interesting and more important in the eyes of her students. It was a joy to take her class, and I would take this class again.
The lectures are pretty long just because they are pretty dense but Alison gets so excited about everything that it makes you want to get excited whether or not you have any interest at all in ECS

Allison is one of the most amazing teachers i have ever had the pleasure of knowing and learning from. She genuinely cares about the subject and her students. Best teacher in the department at the uo BY FAR!

Allison is the greatest professor ever. She notices you even in a giant lecture class. Her passion is apparent in all her lectures.  It's a shame she has so many guest lecturers because I would love for her to teach majority of the class. A lot of work and a little difficult but worth it.
Very knowledgeable and intelligent teacher.
Very awkward lecturer, she is clearly an expert but does not come off well speaking to large groups. Stickler for the rules.

Alison Kwok is one of the nicest teachers I have had. She cares about students and the subject matter. She is dedicated to being a good teacher and becomming a better one. I reccommend her whole heartedly.
Alison can be very helpful and encouraging, however at times socially akward in her lectures.
this professor sucks
Some day the heavens will smile upon me and Allison Kwok will make out with me.
great professor!  the ecs class is too big, but is good.
No Comments
No Comments

Very knowledgable in this subject, some interesting topics, too, but the quizzes make it so attendance is practically mandatory, even though you aren't graded for being there. Switches slides too fast to take notes, and the lectures can be very long and boring often, and the content is pretty difficult to learn, ironic for a memory class

Professor Kuhl is a great professor. He is one of the most brilliant professors I've had at the U of O. He is fair with grading and his quizzes are really easy as long as you skim through the chapters. That being said, his tests are pretty dang hard. They cover a lot of material and questions are worded so wrong choices can seem right. Great prof.

Great professor! His attendance isn't mandatory but he does give out 8 pop quizzes (5 questions) throughout the term and makes this very clear in the beginning. He even drops your lowest 3. Very knowledgeable and open to questions. Makes lectures fun and interactive with examples, definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kuhl is extremely knowledgeable and is an efficient person. That being said, his exams and quizzes are difficult. Beware that his exams are cumulative so those 9 chapters that you read for the second half of the term and previous information will be on the final. His quiz's are super short and thus, the class average is pretty low.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor! His lectures are very organized and he gives great examples to make sure you understand the concepts.  Very prompt with emails and is very helpful in wanting you to understand the material. Loved his learning and memory class and highly recommend taking any of his classes!

All his directions are very straight forward. There is a term paper, but he gives the instructions for it in week three and is more than willing to go over it and help out. There are pop quizzes, but they are only five questions and they are super easy if you did the readings. They are meant to be gimme points.

he is a great professor. You can absolutely tell what is going to be on the exam because he revisits the most relevant information. he is a good professor who is very helpful. The class it not easy because his exams are kinda rough.

Mike was AMAZING, he is such a supportive teacher. I got a C-, which is the lowest grade I've gotten, but I'm just grateful I passed. If you aren't good at math/calc... good luck. But if you get Mike, you are in good hands. The curve was huge, my C- was a 56%. Def go to his office hours because he is so nice and genuinely wants people to do well

Michael was awesome, very kind and funny, explained difficult concepts in very simple terms. Posts everything online, so if you really wanted to you wouldn't have to go to class at all, you could learn it all yourself and show up for the midterm/final and be fine.

I really liked this class. Attendance is not graded but you should really try and go as material is a tad confusing. He offers extra credit and homework is 40 percent of your grade which is really nice. I would also suggest going to his office hours as he is very nice and good at explaining things. Definitely take this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor teaching one of the hardest business classes. You should REALLY consider doing extra credit each week instead of saving it all for the end of the term, it is absurdly long. Other than that, Kuhn really tries his best to make this class easy for everyone and truly an amazing educator, highly recommend his class if you have to take!

I think Professor Kuhn is a very kind guy who is very well-versed on economics. EC 311 is simply a very, very difficult class, and it's hard to find a teacher who will change that. Only thing I don't love is how the class is essentially 90-100 mins of straight lectures and no breaks. But Kuhn is a very kind guy, always open to questions, etc.

One of the best courses I have taken. Professor Kuhn makes great slides, his lectures are interactive, and he makes sure the class understands the intuition behind the concepts instead of just memorizing formulas (this is an econ course, there is still a good amount of that). Skipping is a bad idea, and a little participation goes a long way.

Took this class last spring, this course absolutely requires you to immerse yourself into the material. If you find economics to be uninteresting, you will certainly have a difficult time with this class. Professor Kuhn is one of the best at this university, and if you find yourself having to take this course, do it with this guy.

Absolutely horrendous class with a great teacher. The assignments are only somewhat helpful for the tests. Frustrating that the final review questions where pretty different concepts compared to what was actually on the test. Super nice and understanding and explains things well but the slides are super boring.

Just finished his Econ 311 course which was an absolute disaster. Average grade on midterm was 27/60 and final 28/72. Genuinely a alright teacher but nothing he taught in class was really that touched on in the midterm and finals. The amount of stuff you are expected to know for tests is unreal and overall super frustrating class and grading system

Amazing teacher teaching a god-awful subject. The homework is easy if you do it in groups and it is very important to do well on because the tests are impossible. Got 24.5/60 on the midterm and with my perfect HW grade I'd be sitting at a B. You just need over 50% to pass the class.

Such a solid professor. Yes the class is hard but he makes things clear and understandable. Does his absolute best to make sure you pass the class. Lectures are fun, interesting and always organized. Homework is very manageable. You can tell he really cares about his students. Probably the best professor I've had at UO. Definitely take his class.
Awesome guy, really explains everything well, would recommend if you struggle with the graphing parts of economics! Take this guys classes.
I really enjoyed this professor. It was a difficult course, but he does a good job of explaining the material in a way that is easy to understand.
Just the best
Keeps the class engaging, and lectures on both the theory, as well as the real world research methods, which is crucial but often overlooked by other professors.

Very funny and engaging professor. Very laid back. Difficult class, but there is a substantial curve. He is very patient and explains concepts clearly. He also does a lot of examples and provides ample practice exams and test review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mike is my favorite teacher in the Econ department here. Hard class but a very big curve. Average on midterm was 27/70. I went to class barely and still passed it. If you go to class there is no reason not to receive a good grade in the class. I recommend him for EC 311 as well.

Weekly homework with the lowest two grades dropped. One midterm and a final. If you don't go to class you probably won't be able to teach yourself the material with much success for the tests. Mike is a really good, laid-back teacher and I would recommend him for any course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor, very helpful. Definitely recommend.

Professor Kuhn is a wonderful teacher and truly cares about his students. The class is very focused on applications of Labor Econ and this is helpful for understanding. If you go to class and study for the tests, you will get a fine grade and Professor Kuhn is more than willing to work with and help students outside of class. I highly recommend!
Max is a great mathematics professor. I learned more in his class that I did in my whole high school career
Max is super nice and gets that people don't understand calculus. Go to office hours, he's so helpful and understanding and will go through the homework with you. He's cute too.
Great math GTF. Made calculus passable. And I had already failed it once before. You ought to utilize his office hours, he's very helpful and flexible with his hours.

Max is the best instructor I've ever had. His lectures are extremely clear and he's very approachable and helpful during office hours. He has a way of changing the way you look at math in a good way. I also enjoy his math puns!

Great instructor, but you also have to do your part and go to office hours/math library if you need help. Wants students that care to succeed and Kutler helps you out. Highly recommend him. Very good examples in lectures.

Love his class and the way he teaches this class. I have drop my Math 251 before with other professor (I thought I will never understand cal. forever in my life at that point). He safe my Math and I recommend people taking his class.

Max Kutler is the BEST GTF ever. He's beyond helpful in making sure you succeed in the course. Explains in detail and makes a difficult subject easy and fun. Doesn't hurt that he's great to look at also. Sign up for his courses any chance you get :)

I haden't taken math in 2 years and having to take calculus, I was extremely worried. Max really helped and made this class a lot easier. He would answer all of my questions and be patient. He would provide many examples to made sure myself and the rest of the class understood, inside and outside of class. Best math GTF ever!
Was my GTF and was extremely helpful, always answered any questions whether they were in his discussion or over email with total clarity. Couldn't have asked for a better GTF

I had not taken math in 3 years and was very worried about jumping back into it. Max is one of the best teachers I have ever had, he is extremely helpful, organized and clearly loves teaching. He goes through helpful examples and is fair in regards to homework and quizzes. I would recommend him highly.

Max is a great teacher for this course. He does a splendid job of not only showing the students how to do the math problems but also explains the mathematical concepts behind them. Great guy, very kind and is interested in helping students completely. Recommend him 100%. Max Kutler for president. Like the other guy said, "He's a boss". Nuff said.

Great teacher, wants to make sure you understand the material by answering any questions that anybody has and does great examples in class. His quizzes are one per week, but are very straight forward with material learned in the week. Tests are easy too, definitely recommend Max, and I'm not math lover either.
He's a boss
even after you're done with his class, you can see him for help with writing.  try it out.
Great guy, hard grader... good teacher though

a bit out there, but will improve your writing, especially if you let him know you want help. get to talk about interesting media. he used to work for a gov contractor and sometimes talks about your paper by saying "is it contract ready?" or "now we're selling contract!" weird but worked for me.
No Comments
Let's the class pretty much run itself, is very fair to students, doens't assign too much work, but is sometimes unclear about what he wants out of his students.
No Comments
will spend as much time with you as you want helping you one on one.

She is by far the most helpful and understanding language teacher I have ever had. There is never a feeling of pressure, which makes class participation easy and routine. I would recommend this teacher for any Japanese class you decide to take.
Much more helpful than the actual professor for the class. Amicable, better grasp on english than many japanese professors, all around great teacher.
Best GTF ever!!!!!!!! If you can enroll and have her as a GTF you won't regret it!
Awesome GTF!! Take her class for a good time and to learn!
Very nice and easily approachable.  One of the best GTF's I've had.  In class her points really make you think too.
She's hard to understand but it is what it is.

She shouldn't be teaching any calc classes, she overcomplicates a lot of material, including derivatives and integrals. Her course load is pretty heavy and gives meaningless quizzes every Friday. She is a kind person but outside of that I wouldn't recommend to anybody, sincerely from the bottom of my heart.
She is trying, give her a break

She is so sweet, so I feel bad for the review I'm about to write, but this class is so insanely stressful. The flipped classroom structure drives me insane. It is expected to teach yourself out of class how to do the material and then in class, we do the crazy amount of worksheets given. I wish she just taught the math and we did our homework solo.
JUST ABSOLUTELY NO NEVER AGAIN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult class. I never understood what we were learning and I attended every class. She just hands out lots of worksheets/packets throughout the week that you pretty much have to figure out how to do yourself. She never really taught us in class. If you ask her for help on the worksheets though, she will help and provide useful information.
JCOM 203. Learned nothing. Feedback was always late. Moncia was never prepared, always had excuses, very flustered, but she seems like a nice person.

the assignments made little to no sense, she doesn't explain well, and most of the time we asked each other in class what to do and we were all guessing. almost every class we played games to help us improve our grammar but it doesn't help. felt like a waste of my time but if you missed 3+ classes it was an automatic fail. shes nice tho :/

This was the worst class Ive ever taken. The grammar mistakes in the weekly quizzes are so slight its like playing spot the difference. The way this course if taught you will not learn grammar. Its just frustrating.

This was the worst class I have taken. The material was poorly taught and applied, so I had to teach myself the required material. The course is "gamified" but poorly made, confusing, and blatantly inaccessible to those with ADA needs. I never thought I'd say I wanted a refund for a college course, but this was terrible and wasteful of my capital.

I've had Professor Kwasnik for a couple of classes now, and I can confidently say she is much better in an online class than in person. I didn't love her teaching style at all for J201, but in J101 I didn't mind it as much. Make sure you turn in your things on time, and don't fall too far behind in the class.

Sadly this class is mandatory for several majors, its not hard but to say you learn from anything other than the textbook would be lying. The lessons given directly from the professor are often unhelpful and delivered poorly.
Easy class but Professor Kwasnik is not a very good public speaker and the material is fairly surface level. Not a bad course if you need it but I wouldn't take it as an elective.

Professor Kwasnik is a kind and sweet person outside of being a teacher, but as a professor, she is unbearable and boring. She does not know how to hold a class and she sounds like she's on the verge of crying every lecture. She seems afraid of us and has technology issues EVERY CLASS. DO NOT take her unless you need to. Super easy class though.

While she seems like a kind person, she genuinely doesn't know how to teach a class. She was constantly confused and every single class something would go wrong with the technology, the discussion, or she would get overwhelmed. I was confused almost all of the time. If you can get a different professor for this class, do it.

This class has some of the hardest quizzes I have ever taken. You would think it is a straight forward class, but she is very particular on the grammar being used. A lot of lectures during the week with skills checks you have to, but don't matter. Quizzes and discussions every week that are graded so harshly. Seems like a nice person though.

I only took this class because it was part of my fig. She has no clue how to work a computer and always sounds like she's about to burst into tears. the classes are so boring and you don't learn anything. there is an in-class assignment every day and that's how she takes attendance. it's a rly easy class tho, no homework 2 papers, 3 take home tests
She seems nice but sitting through her lectures were rough. She sounds like she is always on the verge of crying and seems very nervous talking in front of big lectures.

The hardest part of this class is getting through the two hour lectures. She is not engaging at all and seems to always have problems. Seems like a nice lady, but teaching a 200 person lecture might not be her strong suit.

Dreaded having to sit through every lecture. She seems terrified to speak in front of big lectures and is not prepared for classes. I hope to never have a class with her again. Do not take this class unless its a requirement!

In-class assignments every day. For a journalism professor, she sure is afraid of talking in front of people. Always sounds horrified of speaking. Assignments do not make sense. 2 papers, 2 finals that you actually dread every single time. Unfortunate that she is the professor for a prereq sojc class. DONT TAKE UNLESS YOU HAVE TO! (lol sojc majors)

I only had to take this class for a FIG, and would not recommend it. Monica is not very tech-savvy and seems to have problems in every class. She also does not have great speaking skills making the 2 hour class a drag. If the class gets too loud for her liking she will stop talking and say "I'll wait."
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zero connection with her students, and is never prepared for class. She always forgets things crucial to the lecture, and a few times is totally understandable but it is every. single. class. She is a very sweet human but speaks so quietly and always seems so petrified to talk in front of us. I didn't take much away from the class.

Monica teaches Newspaper Editing now which is a smaller class (it wasn't an option for this rating). She seems nervous when lecturing and it can get confusing, but the editing labs are pretty straightforward. She gives good feedback during the labs and can answer any formatting questions. Nothing like the J201 reviews!

I have no idea how this woman passed her dissertation. Do not take this class unless you wanna go back to a high school-like curriculum and teaching style. She gets so PRESSED when it's not dead silent in her class even if she's not prepared, half of her class is just awkwardly sitting there as she tries to phrase a simple question to discuss.

Boring lecture. Unenjoyable in-class assignments you're forced to do because they're graded. Freshmen somehow love her, even though she's so unengaging. Desperately needs to work on her public speaking confidence. Nice person, but can't hear a thing from her. Don't take class with her unless you want to be surrounded by stinky, sick freshmen.

Do not take this unless you need it for your journalism major! Monica is kind and funny, yet she has no public speaking presence and cannot engage with students, making 2 hour lectures a drag. Assignments took forever to get graded and little feedback was provided on papers. She does have a lot of good insights into current events though!

Such a boring class. Two hour long lectures that feel never ending. Not that many assignments/Homework but two unit test that are take home. There are two papers and they are not that long or hard but the GE's are really tough graders. Maybe if this class was online it would be better. Try to take it wit a different teacher if you can.
This chick sucks. Harsh grader, mandatory boring lectures, do not waste your time.

Lectures are long and uninteresting and she pauses every time someone speaks and says "i'll wait, everyone needs to be quiet before I can continue" feels like high school. She is un-savvy when it comes to technology. She cares about the subject but doesn't make you care about it. Teaches a 200+ lecture class like a 20 person discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Almost every class Kwasnik has an issue with technology. Class engagement is the worst I've ever seen as she has no public speaking skills, she is very much an "i'll wait" person so class rarely begins on time. Although I find the course material highly interesting, she goes too slow and makes sitting there for almost two hours intolerable.

Kwasnik had long/slow lectures which often came from problems with technology and lack of direction with the course. While seemingly nice, we pay thousands of dollars every quarter for a direct, prepared, and developed course, which falls short.  Sadly more time focusing on testing the syllabus caveats rather than showing direction for the course.
This class was very slow but the information was interesting and the class was easy. Very nice intro class to Journalism if you're interested in Journalism

Professor Kwasnik is very caring as a person, but her in-class assignments can be hard to stay engaged in considering how the prompts aren't posted in canvas. Grading feedback also takes forever (around a month) for a unit paper. Overall, her content is interesting but her teaching style could be better.
Long lecture. I found them interesting but they were long. Learning about social media like instagram, Tik Tok, Snapchat, Facebook. A couple big essays.

This class is not hard-lectures are just very long and it can be hard to stay engaged. She is very kind and it's clear she wants everyone to have a good experience. The main negative has been the grading for essays which has taken forever to get back (a month). Not a bad class, just make sure you know the basics of the material covered.

The lectures were very long and hard to pay attention to. The essays also took forever to be graded and we couldn't get feedback on our previous essay before the next one was due. She's a nice person but the class itself wasn't my favorite.

I literally owe this woman my life. She checked in on me consistently and was very lenient with late work when I struggled. The class was very long, 1 hour and 50 minutes two days a week, and she would have a classroom assignment almost every day that would close when class was over. But, you are able to complete most of them without attending.

I don't want to be mean, but this class was hard for me. The lectures are hard to pay attention to because she's so quiet and she had difficulty connecting with our class. There's quite a bit of textbook reading, but it was bearable for me. She does know the material well and I hope she continues to improve as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am shocked by the negative reviews. She's clearly new to such a big classroom but she is trying. Not every class was about 'Kanye' and it tied into the material. A lot of information for sure. However, it seems like this is just a bunch of people being mean for no reason. Next time drop the class and pick something else instead of being cruel.

Everything that was assigned did not connect with class, and did not connect with tests and assignments. Feedback was not given. Most classes were about "Kanye" and had no connection to what mattered about the class. 0/5 overall. This was a bad class because it made no sense. DO NOT TAKE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are painful, has little to no public speaking skills, slow at grading assignments, and shows up to class late. She clearly has interest in the topic but she is horrible at teaching it. The most interesting part of the class is the football players in the back. Makes everyone uninterested and discouraged from taking more journalism classes.

Shows up late to class, in class assignments are super confusing, and I swear we have not gone over material she puts on tests. The almost 2 hour class is long, slow, and boring. I would be asleep if I wasnt playing angry birds the whole time. I consider myself a good student, but personally its difficult to learn and do well in this class.

Her lectures are painfully long and unnecessary, I learn more from the guided reading than when I'm in class. I really want to like her because she seems like she's trying, but I'm not learning anything new or interesting from her. She doesn't really give any clarification, even when you directly ask for it.

Obviously this is her first real stint as a professor in college. Every time she opens her mouth she sounds like she's on edge and is going to break any moment. She also shows up late to class, sometimes as late as 10 minutes. A subject I am interested in and lost interest because of her. Lectures feel pointless and work is self explanatory/easy.

lectures are a little hard to focus on because her voice shakes when she talks, making her sound like she's scared or about to cry. She goes over material very slowly, almost painfully slow. The class would be super easy if there wasn't so much reading- the required textbook is quite dense. Overall very boring but not difficult.
Incredibly boring, learned absolutely nothing, absolutely do not recommend. I would rather die than listen to another lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kyle is a great professor, as he made his lectures enjoyable and understandable compared to a lot of other accounting professors. The course itself is very difficult if you don't put your effort into it, as it's heavily weighted towards test grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It's actually a marvel that I scored as high as I did (thank god for the curve). Do the homework. Don't be like me. Professor is super chill, and the course is super "hands on" which means I actually retained some of this stuff! The way he does homework is really nice too. Just turn in everything even if it's not done and you'll do really well.
Steve Kerr was a very good professor!

He is a good prof, not bad not amazing. If you read the textbook and study the given materials he provides you'll do fine. I wont lie some of the material is difficult but if you actually try at the homework and take notes on the chapter ahead of class and pay attention in class its not hard to understand. I promise! Overall a chill guy
Kyle is a great professor he also never fails to make me laugh.

This is not an easy class but from my experience, showing up to class and being fully attentive was all I needed to wrap my head around the material. Attendance isn't required but do yourself a favor and show up because KP is good at explaining concepts in a way that makes sense. Looks like Steve Kerr.

Would take a class with this guy again in a heartbeat, he made a very difficult class tolerable and is an amazing instructor. One of my favorite business school professors to date, just be ready for some difficult course material.

Very Very good professor, super easing to understand, and explains the content very well. He is willing to help you learn 1 on 1. If you do all the work and study you will succeed in this class. He is very funny and his lectures are super interesting.

KP is goated. The class is pretty hard and you have to spend a lot of time doing homework (first one took me 6 hours). But he makes the class very fun and the materials will make sense if you just follow the worksheets and readings.
High-stakes exams, but crazy high curves for overall class scores. My 64% was rounded to a flat C. Good lecturer, but it is just a challenging class to teach to beginners.

Steve Kerr Doppelganger. Super funny guy, and really knowledgeable/passionate about the topic. Homework takes a while, but can easily work ahead if you put some time into it. final grades are curved slightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ACTG 211 is a tough class, but Professor Peterson makes it as enjoyable as possible. Caring and funny, he ensures that the material is taught clearly. While the HW might seem like a lot, it really helps you learn the material-- I was able to only study for 1-2 hours for each exam because of those HWs. Best professor I've had!
A great professor. Made accounting fun and interesting. Inspired me to become an accountant. Take his class if you can.

Kyle was one of my favorite professors I've ever had. While accounting is a difficult subject in general, he made lectures engaging and didn't mind answering any questions or taking extra time to explain. Homework due at 5 pm on Saturday was not preferable, but the homework itself was very beneficial to understanding the content. Take his class!

Kyle is so nice and funny, & always tried to make class fun. Brought us candy for Halloween. The lectures were extremely helpful & informative. The only downside is the weekly homework assignment was due Saturdays at 5:00 pm. There were 2 midterms and a final. If you do good on the tests you finish toward the top of the curve.

Probably the best professor ive had so far. Very kind and helpful, keeps it interesting. Very easy to follow and hands on teaching style. still lots of homework to practice the material but 10/10 class and professor.

2 midterms, 1 final. understanding the homework and applying what you learn from the slides/lecture is helpful in passing on the final and midterm. if you bs or chegg your way through, youll fail final and midterms. he does curve grades but this is a good class to develop basic actg skills. teacher is super cool and engaging but didnt go to lecture

Great professor. Gave good lectures, except I felt that I learned mainly through completing the homework assignments. Could sometimes be a little passive aggressive, but overall a nice and caring professor. Funny!
Great professor. He's teaching a tough subject, so it's never going to be easy, but he cares and understands what students need.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: its a hard class but he teaches it very well
love this guy. should teach every class.

KP is the BEST, he made boring lectures more entertaining and he cared about his students. The tests were hard but go to class and lab every time and you are guaranteed to at least pass if not better. Accounting in general is hard and he was very good at going into detail and answering questions during lecture.
ps He looks like Neil Patrick Harris
Loved taking this class from KP. Heavily based on 2 midterms and final, but he made an objectively boring subject interesting.
Big fan of KP. Covered the material very effectively and efficiently but also did it in a way that was engaging and enjoyable. Definitely recommend taking him if at all possible!!
Kyle's class isn't an easy A, but he explains material well and gives students lots of practice before tests.

I was nervous about ACTG211 but KP is great! Super clear lectures and he's kinda funny. There's quite a bit of homework but all worth it if you want to do well. Tests aren't overly difficult but def study! Overall cool guy and I wish he taught 213.

Prof does his job well given the course material is particularly tricky. However multiple times I approached kyle outside of class with either general course questions or about approaching a career in accounting and was met with an unnecessary amount of attitude and sass. Respect is important to me I would rate him higher if not for this.

It's intro to accounting, so concepts are new, but no reason you can't get an A if you go to class, do the homework, and study the prep tests. Accounting 211 only has 1 answer. You either study and know the material or you don't. I like Peterson's dry wit. Most jokes were lost on me initially as he drops a lot of 80-90s references, but you catch on

Listen, YOU'VE GOT to do the work if you really want an A. He's a fun person, but the material was tough. 2 Midterms and 1 Final. Here's the good part ... as long as you read and study the TEXTBOOK, you're chilling. Lectures don't matter at all, maybe extra content in your brain. Do practice problems from textbook and study hw to prepare for tests!

I'm writing this comment right after my last class with the GOAT KP. Let me tell you this; it's impossible for you to find someone that cares about his students as much as this man here at the UO. He makes accounting so much better, and if you just pay attention in the class you will ace it. He's an exceptional and amazing professor.

The main thing people need to remember about this class is that its course structure is heavily regulated by the school. Yes, it is mainly graded on tests but that isn't Peterson's choice. He is funny but straightforward about what it takes to do well in this class. If you didn't pass, you didn't listen to his recommendations.

I enjoyed taking accounting with Kyle. While the homework and tests are hard, he did his best to make sure students knew about office hours and tutoring options if they needed help. The lab wasn't mandatory, but it can help you if you're struggling. Lecture material can be tedious, but he's generally cheerful and has a funny joke every now and then

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you can. If you can't avoid him like me, I would get ready to study very hard. The tests are multiple-choice, however, they are incredibly difficult. Peterson's awesome. Very clear. The intermediate series is rough, but he was the best of my intermediate teachers. He's a very nice guy, but definitely could be taken for condescending. If you don't know you have the right answer for sure, don't speak up.

Otherwise, his teachings in class are clear.

Prof. Peterson's class is difficult but all of the intermediate accounting classes are challenging and require ample time outside of class to do well. He's a good lecturer and covers material that isn't in the book but that's relevant to real world accounting. Highly recommended.
Kyle was a really good teacher, easy to understand, and he made the class fun.
Very good accounting teacher. Test are difficult but if you work hard and study a B or even an A can be achieved.

Said the f-slur several times in one class, even after someone told him that he shouldn't be saying that.

Worst professor I have ever had at this University and most likely the worst professor at the school. He does not care at all about his students and if they are passing, his grading is extremely difficult, and unclear as well as his assignments too.

Youm has one of the hardest-to-digest class structures I've ever had the pleasure of dealing with. His slides contain almost no information and usually just questions that he answers. Youm is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He gives much more reading than is manageable and has unclear but sky-high expectations for research papers. reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. So unclear and confusing. The amount of times I had to email to ask things that should have been told to us (like guidelines for our 10 PAGE ESSAY) was ridiculous. I am an A student and yet struggled to pass this class. Youm is a HORRIBLE prof and difficult to communicate and work with. Not understanding.
Hardest teacher at UO. He is unclear in his instructions, expectations and answers to questions. Very hard to understand. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

Lots of reading, but  much of it was relevant  news articles (recent & easy to read). Also a big research paper. Go to class, read and you'll do fine.

This is the hardest class I have taken at the UO. That being said, Prof. Youm is a world expert on comm law and is dedicated to this subject. This is a class where you will need to read everything and STUDY. Good grades are possible and office hours are great. This is a class where you will actually learn - this is what college education should be.

The most humble professor I have ever had, yet the hardest course I have EVER taken. No guidance, no true schedule of topics or discussion. Every 2 hours of class is a complete flurry of law cases and difficult topics to follow. There are no study guides and getting a good grade is extremely difficult even with %100 effort.

Although he is very knowledgeable in his field and a nice person, I have no idea what his objectives for the class are. There are no study guides and the GTF has no idea what is going on either. It's very unclear what he wants on the tests. There are no clear guidelines for exams, he doesn't specify what we need to focus on.

Although he is very engaging with his class lectures, it is quite a bit of information to take in and remember for the exam. You will learn a lot, but you will struggle to pass this class. I have talked to many people who have failed it. I am a good student, but this class was excessively challenging for me.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. Youm is very knowledgeable about the subjects he teaches but with his heavy accent and not being able to communicate exactly what he is trying to say it is very hard to follow his lectures.

He may  have a heavy accent but his grammar and vocabulary is impeccable. He also puts in a lot of efforts to keep students engaged, not only with visual aid and well-organized notes, but by having students participate in the materials and having them work as groups. He is also extremely helpful outside of class.

Professor Youm is an expert in the classes he teaches. He has world renowed contacts in every country and uses them to help educate his students. He expectgs alot from his students becuase, bc he wants to educate them.
Worst professor ever. Couldn't understand anything he said. His assistant took creepy photos of me and my friends during class.
Worst.Teacher.Ever.

Professor Youm is an amazing teacher.  He might have a thick accent but this was the most engaging class I've had at UO.  It really made me interested in communication law and even though it was a hard class you actually learn something.

youm is a good professor but the class is demanding and hard.  it is very possible to get an A, just don't expect to go in the class hungover and ace the exam, lol.  grading is a lil strict but youm gives a lot of help in the office hours.

Youm is extremely difficult and expects a lot from students. However, he really knows his stuff (International Comm was boring, I admit, but I loved his Comm Law course). He is one of the worst professors I have ever had. Adding to that, his english skills are poor which makes understanding him a challenge.
He is a nice guy... but he's hard to understand and his class is hella boring! It seems like no one in there takes him seriously. And his tests are kinda hard.

The worst professor I've had since I came to this school.  He has a really thick accent so it's hard to understand what he is saying.  He is very boring and manages to draw out a 2 hour class with about 20 minutes of actual information.  He is horrible.  Do not take this class unless you are extremely interested in Comm Law. Trust me.

Never did I think I would laugh so much in a law class.  Heck, he even told a moron kid in the class to shut up!  Great professor

He had us edit wikipedia pages as our major assignment which was really cool but he does expect you to do it right.

Kyle is the best prof. I've ever had. He totally changed the way I think about environmental studies. He really knows and cares about the subject and its clear in the way he teaches. Ask him what he thinks about ecomodernists.

Inconsiderate of other's time. Always starts meetings and lessons 30-40 minutes late. Calls at innapropriate times such as over the weekend or at night. Makes everything as unnecessarily difficult and time-consuming as possible. Makes the composition department a toxic environment.

Truly awful experience. Just seems to care about himself and will do whatever it takes, and manipulate and crush whomever just to make sure the smallest micro-task he wants done, gets done. Calls students late at night and over weekends when an email would have sufficed. Has bizarre mood swings, nice one day, screams at you the next.

Robert Kyr can be an excellent ally, but in general, he is a poor quality professor. Very cool and relatable. Understands students and very fair. The right direction for professors
