shes almost too nice, sort of a pushover but she means well. the class is very easy (i actually took WR122z) and dont have much else to say about it. extra credit is easy to get, i have 102% right now just from doing the (easy) work and emailing her a picture of a garden. if you need an simple class this is a good one, just gets boring sometimes.
I LOVE THIS WOMAN. She is one of the best professors ever and is so reasonable and understanding. LOVE HER

One of my favorite professors, she's very laid back and so funny. I wasn't good about keeping up with the readings (there are a lot), but found you don't really need to in her class. Would take this course every term if I could.

This class was actually really interesting, and the professor makes it really enjoyable and engaing. I did struggle coming to class towards the end of the term because attendance isnt mandatory, but the slide shows made catching up very easy. Dr. Selcer is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate, but unfortunately not an engaging lecturer. An easy course, especially if you actually engage with the readings/classwork.

Dr. Selcer is incredible. All materials are clearly organized and explained on canvas. Lectures are very engaging and funny. My only complaint is that the class is only 80 minutes. Lectures were often cut short and I feel that this class would benefit from being 110 minutes. I would take every single class with Dr. Selcer if I could!

Very nice person and a straightforward professor. Doesn't really accept late work, but lets you make up attendance grades. Assignments were pretty easy, and her directions/expectations are very clear. You get lots of feedback on drafts, which makes it easy to get As on final papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Selcer as a professor! They did a great job of making sure lectures were understood by allowing the class to engage in optional sharing and she made slides easy to understand with lots of flare. Overall, very helpful and clear on directions. Will definitely take a class with Dr. S again!

Prof Selcer's lectures is extremely informative and genuinely important in this day and age. Attending class is not mandatory, grading is pretty straightforward, and the weekly logs is honestly kinda fun. I would recommend her class for an easy A.

Easy review assignment on canvas weekly, 2 essays and a larger writing assignment for the final project. No tests. Would be good information if you're interested on the topic. They're very passionate in their lectures, keeping it engaging. Very educated on the topic. Class feels informal and more casual.
I took WRI 121Z. Really great writing class. I loved the content in this class and our mid and final papers. Super sweet professor and our conferences together were very helpful.

reviews.comment: Even just for a 122 class, I learned a lot and I think my writing skills did improve which I wasn't expecting from required writing credit. She is very smart and well informed and our class was overall really interesting to me.

I took her class last year and learned more about history than I would have expected. She teaches history and activism, not just identity terms. She talks fast and the lectures are text heavy, but I like having them for notes. I actually loved doing the creative project! Overall I learned a ton and it made me take more wgs classes this year.

If you want to listen to students trauma dump for 2 hours, this is the class for you. I personally was annoyed that  it felt like I was paying money to listen to other students talk than actually learn from the instructor. She was a great talker but does talk A LOT about topics that don't seem to align with the course very much. It was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was great. I did not know what to expect going into it but I was happily surprised by what I learned in this class. Two assignments per week: a short essay and a quiz. I found that she was a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Engaging during lectures and is passionate about what he's teaching. You dont have to love history to understand his teaching. Minimal assignments so doing well on big ones is important. This might be the first time I remember something about history after taking the class and not just trying to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about Japanese history, but if you don't have any background knowledge on Japan, it can be difficult to understand the readings. There are a lot of readings, and he doesn't have a grade tab on canvas which can be annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Leisure's class. His lectures were fun and engaging, his grading policies were clear, and I liked the readings he assigned. Go to office hours! Its worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he knows what he's teaching, but doesn't teach it well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Leisure is truly one of the best history professors I have ever had. He is very clearly both incredibly intelligent and passionate about his work which translates into interesting lectures and discussions. The course readings were always interesting and accessible and he made me care a lot about a topic I had never thought about before!

Brought energy to every lecture, you can really tell John takes his studies seriously and has a lot of care for sharing his findings with his students. Learned a lot in this class I would've never known about.

Intentionally, this was my second time taking a course under Professor Leisure, his lectures are very relevant to your learning and his jokes are funny. The writing in this course is heavy but if you are interested in the topic, its worth it. The course is pretty difficult to understand at points conceptually but if you do the readings its fine.

Professor Leisure makes what could have been a very mundane course about Transpacific Asia interesting. His knowledge of the subject matter and curation of primary and secondary sources we use and read for class make it engaging. The assignments are not too bad, but be ready to review a good amount of material and write semi-substancial work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was between this class and an African history class so I wasn't really anticipating this course too much but Professor Leisure made this class exciting. The lectures are set up really well and are really engaging. The reading for the course is curated very well and he is clearly passionate about his line of work which works in the class's favor.

Professor Leisure is an awesome teacher. He really knows his stuff, and makes class an enjoyable part of the day. All of the information he gave about Tokyo was incredibly interesting, and with the midterm and the final he helps you create the tools needed to do well. Super awesome teacher I definitely will be taking more of his classes.

Highly recommend 192 to 1st years who are just getting started. John is a really caring person & the lectures for this class are absolutely amazing. Grading system is clear & its a (relatively) light workload. If you do the work there's no reason to not get an A in this course. Plus he's hilarious. He kinda reminds me of John Mulaney lol
What's good John
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Leisure was so nice. He really cares and is passionate about his work. His class is very easy and does not take much time out of your regular life. No midterm or final, just essays, but he preps you all term for those papers, and they're extended versions of the weekly assignment you do! He really listens to student feedback as well!

Sugiyama is clearly very passionate about what he teaches, but the class is very difficult. There are so many hours of lectures and readings every week and he's a very harsh grader. I wasn't able to get a single A on an assignment. The class and content is interesting, but it's a lot of work and hard to do well in.

The lectures weren't that bad and you're able to get by from skimming over the lecture slides. There is a weekly quiz which is worth 50 points and if you fail one it's hard to get your grade back up. There is a major assignment every couple of weeks but as long as you over explain your answers you'll do fine. GEs either grade very harsh or easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Funny guy and interesting content, but that's it. So disorganized it was stressful. It's the day before term ends and just now have had ONE assignment get graded. A 12pg (minimum) paper is due in 3 days, and he only now provided feedback on progress and expects big changes. If he doesn't have the time to care, he shouldn't teach the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy A class: One quiz and one worksheet every week. Don't bother doing the readings, just take notes on the lectures. Lectures were actually recorded by the other Sugiyama. GE's grade the worksheets a bit harshly but just add detail. No midterm or final. Lectures are kinda boring, but the films you watch for the worksheet are pretty interesting.

This class had fascinating information but it was lecture-heavy with at least 2-3 hours of lecture videos to watch a week and at least 5-10 papers to read that vary in length. You HAVE to watch the lectures/read otherwise you won't be able to do the assignments with the correct information or take the quizzes and get higher than a 20/50.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An aspect that is important but is not mentioned here is that this class may be difficult if you have body image issues (male or female). He mentions this, but people should know here too. He talks about bodies that are scientifically attractive, and if you think you may be bothered by this to a large extent, you should find another science gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he was very understanding but a very hard grader

reviews.comment: This class is one of the most interesting classes I have taken, but it is VERY reading/lecture heavy. Weekly quizzes are timed, and there are big assignments once every couple weeks. Make sure to watch the lecture (skimming through it will work) because in my experience, that's where most of the quiz questions come from. Prof talks a lot in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 3 hr methods class that meets once a week. So far, he has consistently managed to fill 2.5hrs of the lecture with personal anecdotes and the rest is meaningful information. Assigns 60-80 pages of reading a week, plus 3hrs of field exercise, and 1-2 assignments per week. It's all just a lot. You can resubmit any assignment, so that's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loads of lectures and all the quizzes are based on them. No answers online either. Watch the lectures on 2x speed. Im talking 3 hr to 6 hrs of lectures total per week. Loads of reading but you almost never have to do them unless the hw is relevant which it only was once. Over elaborate answers on every question on assignments and u'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was really interesting and Sugiyama is very passionate about the subject, a lot of the papers we read he either co-authored or wrote. This class was very time-consuming. Some weeks you will have two hours of lectures, some weeks you will have six. There is also excessive reading assigned. He does ramble but I would take his classes again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sugiyama's lectures are detailed and thorough. Make sure you have time to sit down and take good notes and you'll do well on the quizzes. There are assignments every other week which you need to put a lot of detail and effort into if you want a good grade. Besides that this is a great async course to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes each week that are 10 questions but hard, projects every 2 weeks to help the rest of grade-- lectures are long but easy to follow along
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Though he is sometimes funny, his lectures are way too long. Also, the assignments are not clear and graded very tough. TAKE NOTES ON THE LECTURES. The weekly quizzes are a huge chunk of your grade and mostly cover the lectures.

Super easy because his style of teaching only requires you to watch lectures. He posts readings on canvas but he goes over all the important materials in his lectures. One quiz and sometimes with one Worksheet. No final or midterms. It is super low maintenance and has no surprises in structure.

I don't know how you can make an interesting topic so incredibly hard to learn. His lectures are very long and dense ranging at least from 50 minutes to 180 minutes with multiple lectures for one week, not including the readings. The grading for the quizzes- horrible miss one question and you barely pass. My classes average for quiz grades ar 30/50

All his videos are longer than life itself and impossible to get through, along with miles and miles of required reading material. Your grade is based off quizzes that you only get a short 15 minutes to do. Worst online class I've ever taken (And I've taken BI212 online- that's saying something).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute character. He has a style of teaching that you will either love or hate. Longer lectures (anywhere from 20-100 min with 70 being average) and a weekly quiz/occasional worksheet for homework. If you watch all lectures and take notes you will pass, if not you're f*cked. Also grades the worksheets like youre submitting them to the president.

I have taken several of Prof Sugiyama's classes, all of them I've enjoyed but he is a very tough grader and expects a lot on worksheets without really telling you that. If you take his class, write more than you think is necessary on the worksheets and you will do well. The quizzes are hard, but passable if you watch the lectures and take goodnotes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Weekly worksheets seemed easy but TA was not helpful with what we needed to do and instead just out "Not enough". The Prof sometimes wouldn't even open the worksheets until Tuesday or Wednesday of the week. Way better Anthropology classes out there. Im sure he's a good researcher, just can't teach to save his life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor wasnt really helpful, The tests were worth a lot points and at first it will feel like a passable class but if you screw up on these tests your not going to make it.

I took this class online so take my review with a grain of salt. But his lectures are super lengthy, have absolutely no rhyme or reason to them, and you are only graded on a few things in the class. I agree with some of the other reviews; he can be offensive and make offhand comments at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ANTH 330 was one of the hardest classes for me because our GE graded our Weekly Video Worksheets really hard. The average on the worksheets were a B and the GE always said there wasn't "enough" even though answers were like paragraph + long. Quizzes every week (10 min limit). TAKE NOTES ON LECTURES. Long lectures and sometimes more than 1/week.

His lectures were bizarre and sometimes tangent-y but damned if they didn't stick in your head as examples of the concepts he taught. I loved him he was so funny and interesting and I looked forward to every lecture. The GE was awesome too, she always helped fill in the gaps and answered our questions.

Absolutely horrendous teaching ability. Frequently relies on either his own research papers, those that cite his papers, or on ridiculously non-credible data such as out-dated okcupid blog sites. Frequently makes inappropriate comments with no educational value, and his teaching lacks any structure whatsoever. You'd be better off not taking it.

Sugiyama is a smart person, but very offensive in lecture. Also has a meandering lecture style. Interesting dude if you get to know him, and doesn't mean to be offensive, but would not recommend him until he learns to present bettermore nicely.

310: Human beauty. His lectures have a slow start through the term and he can get side tracked, but if you go and listen to him and his stories you can actually be pretty well entertained. The only work was a midterm and final which was totally 'ace'able if you take the time to answer every question on the study guide he provides.
The worst teacher I have ever had. Extremely inappropriate and disrespectful.
So much reading, study every single short essay question in the study guide.

Oh Sugi... What a unique man with good stories! However in a small class be prepared to be mocked. There was SO much work for this class which I had no idea going in. Although he lets you redo any assignment you did not do well on. Only downside he is very slow at returning emails and has an issue staying within class time.

As students, we taught the class using journal articles, not very easy considering we were in there to study and learn the articles.  We also had to depend on our other classmates, who knew nothing, just like ourselves, to get the info.  Tests were based on the info we were given by other students.... SCARY

Sugiyama comes off as a jerk in lecture- he has a crude, **** sense of humor.  The readings are dense but interesting if you can handle it. His tests seem really tough but if you do the reading you should be OK
No Comments

the way he teaches this class does not match the course description at all.  he goes over too many cultures without focusing on any at all.  answer all the questions on the study guide, since it's basically write it in essay form for the exams.
No Comments
No Comments

This might very well be the worst math professor I have had in my academic career so far. Weekly quizzes, no practice midterms, bad handwriting, boring lectures, and an overall attitude that he doesn't care whether you learn the content. I highly recommend staying as far away from this prof as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My worst experience at UO so far, and very disappointing considering this is a required course for Data Science students. Was extremely rude and condescending when asking for help. 30% of your grade is dictated by a daily quiz that "covers the material from last class," but rarely has relevance. I am extremely lucky to have passed this class.

i've never been more dissapointed in a professor than i am in david levin. he's rude, condescending, doesnt explain things correctly, and overall just a terrible professor. your grade relies on quizzes every single lecture that may or may not correctly cover the previous classes lecture notes and his handwriting sucks so bad. :// do better uoregon
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've never felt so bitter about a class that I've had to write on R.M.P. until now. 30% is based on 20-minute quizzes in each lecture, with material loosely associated with the last lecture. Homework is ridiculously abstract in comparison to exams for how little it's weighted. No enthusiasm, condescending, unstructured lectures, and constant typos.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have taken 8+ math courses at the University of Oregon, and Prof. Levin is by far the most condescending, out of touch, disorganized, and just generally angry. Daily quizzes worth 30% of your grade are supposed to be based on material from the previous lectures but oftentimes weren't related. Homework is useless for tests. Avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Does not teach you, expects you to know the material already instead of teaching it to you. Gives daily quizzes that test you on the previous lecture, but can have material from nothing involving the last lecture. Best part of my day was getting out of his class. Very mundane, if you can find a way to avoid his class, do it.

Homework was worth just 15% of our grade, with the midterm worth 40% and the final 45%. The professor is kind, but his lectures were all over the place. Never clear what the lecture topic was, nor how it related to the textbook. More efficient to just study from the textbook. Class average on the final was < 50%; many people failed the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you never want to make eye contact, take his class. Taking lecture from a brick might be more interesting. This is a weird class with not really a set curriculum but everything we went over was much beyond the scope of what I feel like should be covered in this class. He's pretty lenient on due dates and most of class was graded on completeness.

While Dr. Levin is a little dry, he is good at teaching and passionate about his work. He also made a great effort to connect to all of us, and cares about his students. If people were struggling to keep up or wanted extra time he's very open to changing due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Does not answer emails. Monotone and very uninterested in the topic he's teaching: voting and election systems. Not easy to understand and overall just a terrible teacher. Listen to other reviews saying you will learn more on your own by looking it up.

Levin is very much so okay. It's not a hard class for something like "math" just learning about different types of voting systems. He seems very uninterested in this topic, and students correct him constantly. I also had to email him every week to remind him to upload lecture slides. I had more fun counting how many times he says "ummm" in class.

I am just finishing math107 with David Levin. He is by far the worst professor I have had here at UO. He is extremely boring, and is not engaging with his students what so ever. He makes the content way more confusing than it should be, and I have learned more on Youtube than I have from going to his class. He is not helpful at all.

Professor Levin is the rudest and most unorganized teacher I have ever had. His lectures are boring and confusing and he literally does not know what he is teaching more than half of the time. He is rude and unclear when answering questions or responding to emails and I have had to teach myself the content of the class through alternative sources.

Rather rude, and also very blunt with emails (one worded responses). Will not answer everything you ask in an email. Weighted grading system. Really disliked the subject matter of the class: voting and elections. Semi-reliable with academic accommodations.

I am in the middle of the term with professor levin and he is the most unclear and unorganized teacher ive ever had. its like he doesnt know what hes teaching. this class is miserably boring and i go into tests not knowing what im doing. he is so monotone and takes about 10 minutes to complete a sentence.
He is really smart, but he is not great at teaching the material in a way that students comprehend. He often goes on tangents, making it hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had quizzes every week (or every other week), which werent too bad. The midterms were also not too bad. But the final was wayyyy harder than the rest of the course and had stuff we barely covered. Prof was patient and friendly, willing to answer any questions.

David assigned everyone in the class a number to refer to them as even though our class is rather small. During lectures he often makes mistakes, making it hard to learn by reviewing notes, as they likely contain errors. If none of the students catch a mistake (hard to do when you are there to LEARN the material) he won't find it. No doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: After taking 461, 462 and 463 with Levin, I've found that he is the worst math professor I've ever had. Period. He doesn't seem to be interested in actually teaching his students at all. His lectures are extremely disorganized and he goes on tangents that only confuse more. If you have a choice of professor, DO NOT PICK LEVIN.

This class was awful.  First, the assigned text "A first course in probability" is an abomination upon mankind.  Second, David Levin's unclear, very disorganized lecturing combined with  very unclear grading criteria and distracting, borderline childish temper tantrums  made this class intolerable.

Professor Levin is one of the worst Math professors I have had at University of Oregon. His lectures are dull and he makes things so unnecessarily complicated. The text does a much better job explaining the material then he does. Try to avoid this taking his class and if you can't, avoid going to class.

Possibly one of the worst teachers i've ever had, and I was in the smaller statistics class which was about 40 students. He is very vague and difficult to learn from in his lectures, not personable whatsoever during class, basically had to learn the whole class from the book. Definitely not recommended
Professor Levin is a really good teacher. his subject is obviously boring if you dont enjoy math ( which i dont) but i got a A+ on his midterm and im horrible at math. definitely recommend.

Professor was very knowledgeable of the topic and explained it clearly. He does not tolerate people talking or walking out of class. HW are long so it's best to start working through them as soon as possible. If you're willing to read the book and go to lecture while staying silent, this class is just fine.

Levin was nice in office hours. He had his flaws and the material is boring, espcially in a 500 ppl class. The problem was the class. This was the rudest class I've ever been in. I would have yelled too when people got up and left or said rude things in class.  I was embarrassed by my fellow students. No one should treat a prof that way.

Prof Levin, though knowledgeable, was both rude and unable to teach a large lecture.  I chose to take this class, it was not required, and I was disappointed with his teaching of the material.  Honestly, his stuck-up teaching style and downright frustrating temper tantrums made this course a total let down.

Levin is the worst professor ever (you can't say I'm bitter as I got an A-). He is incomprehensible, rambles on about math without actually showing you how to do it, is rude (the GTF's told us he hated our class), and his tests don't test your ability to solve problems, but are 50% true-or-false misleading, trick questions designed for you to fail.

This is statistics, not a Ducks game. You aren't going to be entertained with cheerleaders.  But if you do the work and THINK a little, you'll do fine in his class. He's always around in his office and doesn't mind students coming in, so go see him. He's hilarious one on one. And he knows alot about bikes.

I took this class because it was required by my major...and I wasn't that excited about it. But the Prof made the topic totally interesting and accessible. His clear and straightforward teaching style, not to mention his dry wit, makes learning statistical methods fun. If you're going to take this class, take it with Professor Levin.
Very boring, very unclear... I highly recommend any other statistics teacher

Lectures the entire class but sometimes has group collaborations about readings/concepts so come prepared. Very caring and you can tell she's passionate about her work. Exams are not too bad, they're MCQ and short answer with no notes that are graded by GE's. Takes attendance with pop quizzes but they're graded on participation.

The weakly assignments are fine but graded unnecessarily hard by GE's. No feedback so you won't be sure why you got what grade. Prof. wanted to take away technology bc no one would pay attention to her boring lectures. Final is insane for a 100 Level. Feels above students and makes everything racist like the word "finna" idk how that's racist.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loved this class and professor Weaver! Interesting lectures and really enjoyed the material. The coursework was very manageable and the readings weren't too heavy, but definitely take notes on the readings and lectures to do well on the midterm and final.

The tests are easy if you study the terms (use quizlet). Other than that she takes attendance and the lectures are boring/repetitive so it's hard to stay focused. There's also weekly assignments based off readings that's a big chuck of your grade and the grading is harsh.

I LOVE Dr Weaver. Incredible and interesting lectures, very respectable, respectful, and knowledgeable prof. Overall great experience in this class. In GLBL 102 the assignments are minimal and easy to understand with fair grading. Would take this Prof and this class again and 10/10 recommend!

AMAZING prof, so knowledgeable with real global experience. Readings were super interesting but there is a moderate amount. Decently short weekly assignments but you have to get out and do stuff for them. I learned a lot & stepped out of my comfort zone. She cares about students and understands it's an easy pass, you get out what you put in!
Great professor, wish I could take more classes with her. Easy class, fun material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Weaver is AMAZING! Loved GLBL 102. Learned more than I have in any uni course (most importantly about ethics, tolerance i.e. how to be a better human) while doing the least amount of work & w/ minimal stress. She's very understanding: freebie absences, etc. You have to be trying hard to NOT get an A in her course. 10/10 recommend.

I loved GLBL 340 so much that I added the global health minor! If the content of the course appeals to you, Dr. Weaver takes you through it in a way that is both engaging and easy to understand. The course covers a lot from all over the field of global health, so it can be a lot of info per lecture, but if you show up and lock in you'll be fine.

Joe Weaver is one of my favorite professors. She gives great insight and is very passionate about her work, I would recommend her Global Health class above all. Not a very hard class and grading is straight forward. My final was just multiple choice with a few essays during the year. It is lecture heavy so be prepared to maybe got somewhat bored
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Weaver is great. Readings before class & participation quizzes during every class to make sure you did the readings but those are relatively easy. There's only one assignment a week and those are also very interesting and engaging. She is super passionate and great at teaching the course content. I would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is very focused on attendance but there is really no reason to go. Two-hour lectures that barely scratch the surface on issues. Nothing talked about in class is used in assignments or even brought up again. Professor pushes heavily on giving respect but doesn't respect students enough to actually teach them something useful.

Boring rambling lectures. Insane amounts of reading. You would think a 102 course would be used to draw interest into this area of school but this class has turned me away. Way too much input into the class for zero takeaways. Suprise final essay out of the blue at the end of the term! Stay away if possible!

2-hour lectures of information that could be summed up into an hour. There were a lot of assigned readings and out-of-class readings. Assignments aren't hard but very time-consuming. The week before finals she changed the final from a reflection to a 1000 word essay out of the blue. A little to much work for a 102 level class

Really do not understand the recent awful ratings... The class is easy, insightful, and I really have enjoyed the discussions we engage in. Prof. Weaver comes off very sincere as well and provides interesting anecdotes about her time abroad. Definitely not a challenging class, but I am pleased with the course.
she is the best professor ever, so much experience, wants her students to learn and succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Weaver genuinely cares about the material we learn in class, and I recommend taking INTL 410 as it is extremely relevant to ongoing racial tension and matters that exist today.

I felt her class was extremely easy. I basically did one reading per week and felt barely challenged when discussing the in-class topics/readings assigned. INTL 199 was a breeze, not sure about other classes. Super nice and friendly professor though.

Prof Weaver is a great teacher I feel like I learned so much in this class! She knows alot about health and medicine too, so if you're doing the pre-med track you might like it. Probably I never thought about the things we discussed in the class in regards to race before. she gave a exam and some written essays but these were takehome. Awesome!

I really enjoyed this class, and I definitely recommend this professor! I liked the way she delivered her lectures and found the content very interesting. Pretty much all the quizzes and exams were open-note/open-book and take-home. Be prepared to do some writing. It was a fairly low-stress class that I would take it again.

Prof. Lewis is incredibly passionate about PPPM and makes this class engaging. She is very understanding and reasonable, and the projects are nice ways to apply the material. Reading is not too heavy. This class may be difficult if you haven't taken PPPM classes or if you don't have much prior knowledge about housing.

Prof Lewis is a great instructor who is very knowledgable in her field. Her lectures are engaging and they involve discussion questions to keep track of attendance. Classwork involves discussion posts, weekly reflections, reading quizzes, and 3 memos throughout the course of the term. Interesting class if you want an intro to PPPM.

She is very kind and cares about what she is talking about. Attendance is not required but is tracked with in-class surveys. Open note quizzes and open note tests, she is very understanding and is willing to work with you. Overall very easy class, a couple of assignments a week, and a couple of short essays throughout the term.

I really liked this class and the professor. The material itself was pretty boring, but all tests and quizzes are take-home and open-note. A lot of your grade is dependent on your GE so make sure you are doing good on your assignments in the discussion classes.

aside from the class being extremely boring, rebecca is a very nice professor. i wouldn't take this class again, however. very lecture and reading heavy, with little to no actual "planning" assignments.

Class was relatively simple. go to lectures sometimes if not make sure to do a little reading before attending the in-person discussions. Tests are online and very simple as well as open notes. Overall would for sure take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice person and was a very good lecturer. Her slides and lectures were very helpful and informative along with the in class participation aspect when she engaged the audience. Her assignments were easy and clear and exams were flexible.

Lewis is so awesome! She uses a lot of picture examples in her lectures, which are SUPER helpful. Assignments are through discussion sections. Textbook she uses has summaries at the end, so I basically never had to read the whole thing. You can feel her passion when she speaks and she is great during office hours

This class did have a LOT of reading. However, it is doable to skim. Every quiz, exam, etc., is an open book, which makes for a pretty easy class. Rebecca is a great professor, though. Her lectures were good, and she made sure to incorporate active learning. I also had her as my FIG leader and have gotten to know how kind of a person she is!
Interesting content though sometimes hard to stay engaged. Really kind and understanding professor. Few assignments, all just open note quizzes and tests and some papers.

Readings for this class were quite heavy, but lectures and class participation were engaging. The assignments are small and doable as long as you keep up with the readings. Professor Lewis is passionate about the subject and it is beneficial to hear from her.

Not sure why it doesn't let me select PPPM410 Planning Growth&Housing, but I simultaneously loved that class and it was the hardest one I have ever taken. I looked forward to every day because the content was so interesting, and really pushed myself to work hard. I felt like I gained a lot out of her instruction, highly recommend to anyone else!

Overall, a solid class. Lectures were full of resources and pretty easy to follow, she brought in guest speakers frequently. Discussion sections were kind of boring sometimes but it's an easy grade if you read the textbook and ask questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rebecca has great lectures that are clear and concise. I was bored maybe twice in the 20 lectures I had with her. Cares deeply about class and adjusted future content based off of what the class wanted to learn more about. Always stayed after class a little to answer questions. Overall easy class with quizes that were easy if you did the readings.

McLees makes assignments way more complicated than they need to be, online class and little to no communication from her. the few times i emailed she has been rude/dismissive (spelled my name wrong every time). canvas page is confusing and you have to use a dif website for most assignments. overall avoid

Very poor grading criteria, and whenever I'd call her out on things she noted in the rubric that were simply not part of my project, she'd have nothing to back her up. She makes excuses for not being prepared for any classes. I'm upset she's still teaching, honestly.

Incredibly convoluted instructions make assignments much harder than they need to be. Additionally, feedback that conveyed the reasons points were removed was often not listed and sometimes subjective. Additionally, the course load exceeds the typical expectations for a 4-credit class. Assignments are lengthy and are almost daily.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For a hybrid class, it is engaging -- the weekly meetings are interactive and fun, and usually involve group projects with posters. The homework load is heavy, but the readings are generally interesting enough to make you want to keep reading. The final project being a combined storymap of the smaller weekly projects was a cool concept.

Mclees is a great person, just not suitable to run a college class. She is constantly all over the place and complains about how much work she has to grade, even though she over assignments work like nothing. Very unorganized class work, as our canvas page was never truly clear as what was due. Lots of work that will have you up for hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Yeah, this class is taught by two professors which, in a perfect world, would be good but the class is all over the place. On top of that, most of the course material seems like it's meant for someone in high school. We spent the first few weeks talking about what a resume and cover letter is, I learned that 5 years ago!

She's nice but she's kind of all over the place. This class is taught by two professors so it's either her or the other one conducting discussion sessions. She's rarely there and when she is, the class periods are less than structured. The class itself has an unreasonably high amount of busy work and guidelines are sometimes hard to follow.

This 2cr course's workload is heavier than any 4cr I've ever taken. Wkly Perusalls, essay, reflection, & written quiz. Leslie is condescending and berates students for making her have to do more work (respond to emails) because students ‘don't care enough' about her class. 0 flexibility or consideration. Overly complex instructions full of typos
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: this class was lowkey irrelevant. i didn't have many problems with it; most of the work lies within the kritik assignments and peer review. basically your peers give you the final grade, which was kind of annoying so if you take this class please go easy on your classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her course is disorganized and grading criteria for assignments is difficult and confusing. Peer review is mandatory on almost every assignment and annotations are due every two weeks. She grades strictly but inconsistently, relies on external sources for everything, doesn't actually teach anything, & doesn't explain what's expected from students.

I've never had a professor as disrespectful as ‘Doctor' McLees. Her emails were full of typos and poorly written instructions, showing little effort in communication. She claimed the course was preparing us for ‘real life,' yet her lack of professionalism and clarity made it clear she wasn't practicing what she preached. The irony was hard to miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a lack of proper organization in the course which has a resulted in multiple cases of misinformation amongst the class. Sometimes figuring out what to do for an assignment and the criteria is harder than the assignment itself. Plus, there is no feedback besides peer feedback, so you have to guess on what you did wrong. Not really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took Geog 468 and it was horrible. Aside from horrible course housekeeping, DR. McLees's teaching style is just bad. She cares about her students and offers a lot of flexibility when asked, but overall, this class is bad and could be taught way better; the topic has so much potential and the instructor ruins that.
A lot, a lot of homework. Very strict in terms of grading.

I would avoid this teacher, she parades on the fact that she lived in an African country but still refers to Black people as the blacks; very unprofessional language. She also has consistent typos and mistakes in her lectures and quizzes, it is clear she did not review her work before publishing, I get it's an online class but we matter too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is disrespectful, snappy, disingenuous, and confusing. Almost every assignment/quiz had multiple typos in them making it hard to decipher pertinent directions. Responses from email are limited, vague, and rude. Makes excuses instead of just stating the facts or responding to a question. Complicated responses that are not coherent.

Dr. McLees truly cares about helping students, but is very unprofessional. Assignments and course content each week have spelling and syntax mistakes, and she talks in an unintentionally patronizing voice toward students. Frequent errors and mistakes on quizzes and assignment guidelines. Overall, interesting content, but is very unorganized.

There is reading you need to do to before class to be prepared for discussions and interactions with what you read. It is not lecture heavy, but interacting and asking questions in groups helped to clarify topics. Attendance is not mandatory but you miss a lot if you are not in class. Responds to questions on assignments when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Horrible. Horrible, horrible, horrible class. The ONLINE class which is already hard enough was made even more hard by her teaching method and grading style. The content never made sense, we had tests/quizzes every week, annotations every week (heavy load), a lot. of reading, big projects every two weeks, and she would take 5ever for to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Leslie was always very unprofessional in my class and would constantly talk negatively to fellow students.

an extensive amount of writing and revisions of yourself and peers writing work. made it more into a writing class compared to a geography class. vexing teacher as well. treated us as childern during the in person classes. uses kritik and persuall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor clearly doesn't care very much about this class, all her material was littered with grammatical and spelling errors. She also put blatantly false answers on tests, and used an incredibly patronizing tone while communicating via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She really doesn't care about the students and really tough grader

First of all, a huge section of the syllabus talks about a basic lack of compassion for students with disabilities (specifically ADHD). Course modules are confusing and use way too many websites and talks to students as if they are children and just simply didn't read the instructions. Get ready for a lot of busy work for a basic gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was extremely confusing to take. The fact that Dr. Mclees uses so many different platforms for assignments and took a full month to get the assignment schedule finalized made it difficult to keep track of everything. The class content is quite interesting though, and she grudgingly let students make up assignments.
All over the place, never prepared. Used three different sites for work, constantly makes mistakes. On top of everything she is a tough grader.

Leslie McLees was by far the least professional professor I have ever had. She treats her students like children, rather than adults, and only gives out busy work. She also went on a weird email rant about Russians allegedly prank-calling America??? that she accidentally sent to our entire class
Online classes have a lot of work but it is clearly written out. Staying on top of material and meeting deadlines is absolutely mandatory for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most difficult thing about this class was making sense of the instructions and grading criteria for assignments. Her GE's are extremely rude and tough on grading when it is the most disorganized, hard to follow course content. The best thing is that the textbook she uses is free.

GROUP WORK. Built around weekly group reports (~250 words) about a self chosen topic that are combined  into one final project. Groups/topics are chosen Week 1 and are locked in, make sure you get with people that work evenly. Weekly quiz is pulled from book, which she gives via pdf. My group was A+, made the class very easy and work was light.
The organization of this class makes it feel as though Mclees does not care about the success of students. Grading is unclear, and feedback is not helpful.

Easy class but prof is disorganized at best. Unclear on grading standards and just seems kinda bored and uninterested. Sometimes won't show up for things she makes mandatory for students, then gives lame excuses. Do the work, dance around the disorganized BS and you will be fine.
I dont feel like I learned what I couldve. Professor is passionate about what shes teaching but theres a lack of communication from her part and her GEs.
She teaches literally nothing. Her GE's grade so hard for no reason and are incredibly rude.

Not a horrible prof unless she decides she doesn't like you. Disagreed with me on my homework and took off points for it, then turned around and used the same point infront of class. Also took points off of my work but not my peers for the same thing. Over half the class is focused on one author's work. Little guidance on assignments.

There were no class meetups so any contact was through email in which I heard back from her once through the whole term. So many unanswered questions and grading issues. Lots of typos and wrong due dates throughout readings and assignments. She clearly wasn't interested in teaching this class. Odd feedback on assignments, almost snarky comments.

I usually try to be positive/kind, but I'm not impressed. She expects professionalism from students, but does not reciprocate. No need for textbook is nice, but supplied material is riddled with typos/grammatical errors. Gradebook/Moodle are chaos and assignments unclear. Seems nice and well intentioned, gives decent feedback, hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her 100-level course felt more like a 300+-level course. Grades pretty critically and locks grades throughout the semester. Makes you use this map-making services which are pretty annoying to use and have a steep learning curve to make them look good.

Took Leslies 100 level class in my last term of college. I can say with certainty that I only had one instructor worse than Leslie, and that individual was a grad student. Leslie is standoffish, not helpful, unorganized and unprepared. Coming from someone with 180 credits, please listen when I tell you its not worth the 4. Avoid Leslie.

I think this is one of the first time that Prof. McLees does an online class and if there are any mistakes about anything online, she is very open to correcting it. The class had an extremely clear criteria of about 4 assignments per week and the description is very detailed that it's hard to not know what you're doing unless you don't read it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lecture slides contained almost no useful information to reflect back on after lecture or for studying. Watched a lot of videos about topics and talked about them. material wasnt difficult, but following along and recognizing what was important material was difficult because everything felt like discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor McLees is an okay overall professor. However, she does not inspire students to learn and her class was EXTREMELY dull. Very boring. Attendance is mandatory, which really blows. I would definitely not recommend taking this class. It was very, very boring. Easy, but boring.

I'm assuming she changed the course looking at the past bad reviews. This class was extremely easy yet extremely interesting. You cover a lot, but you can easily get away with skimming the text book before exams. There's almost no homework except fun project based assignments. One group project but altogether not very intensive outside of class.

I was not a big fan of Leslie, but I think that has something to do with the subject matter. I took this class for an elective credit thinking it would be somewhat interesting, but as the term went on I never looked forward to going to the class. The lecture slides have no information and she bases the tests off of things said in class by students.

This class is so boring. I do not understand what she talking about. Lots of work!! Reading book, do project. The exams are so hard. Don't have answer for study guide. I ask her about answer, she said no. She think you should understand all question. So sad. Hoping she can give high score for projects.

Class is way more work than its worth. Should be worth 6 credits, not 4. Every week expect: reading 2-4 chpts & slides (+ extra articles), 3 discussion posts, study guides, quizzes (including midterm & final wk) & a weekly diary project (900+ word essay on a website you create). She expected too much. I only recommend it if it's your only class.

She is a very very strict teacher.I took her online class. She always asked you questions and do not tell you any possible answers. She thinks you should understand everything and find out the answers by yourselves. Too much homework. I spent much time on this class,but I don't  think I learn something useful. Will not recommend her  class!
Stat away! She is extremely monotone and an overall horrible teacher. Her class is extremely boring and she kills you on exams. I'm an honors student and I struggled in her class.

very nice teacher, understanding and willing to help other studnets! she is extremely experienced about Sub-Sahara Africa and she kept the class intersesting and fun. the research paper was helpful for students to know more about the region. excellent teacher take her class won't regret it!
Leslie is awesome! She's very patient with her students and is very clear with her intentions.

evil. her voice is low she's too strict it's pathetic. i didn't learn anything from her class cause i could barley hear her. the gtf was really nice though, he was always willing to help. she sucks though. i don't recommend her. too many short essay questions in the exams it's ridiculous.
she had trouble with our large lecture class. very knowledgeable but often seemed angry with students and approached interactions with hostility.
No Comments
good class. I learned alot. Leslie is very patient with students. I would def recommend her to others.

Leslie is still learning how to teach and structure the class but she is patient and fun. Doesn't know this field very well because her specialty is Human Geography. Easy going. Has a lot of patience too.

Professor Middlebrook's class was okay until she discovered a few select students used chat gpt on one of her assignments. She spent a whole lecture scolding the entire class and changed the syllabus on the spot. Her instructions are vague and confusing. For the sake of your mental health, DO NOT sign up for one of her classes.

Prof. Middlebrook is clearly passionate about the course material, although I wish I'd known before registering that we'd just be reading one book the entire term. She spent an entire class lecturing everyone about AI, which felt like an unfair waste of time to those that didn't use AI. Deadlines and course requirements were unclear/inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She changed the syllabus week 5 because she was paranoid that the class was using Ai chat.

I am very confused by these ratings. Professor Middlebrook came across condescending and was very critical of my writing without providing any feedback. She changed the syllabus in week 6 after suspecting students used chat and lectured the whole class as if we were all at fault. So unfair to the students who put so much time into her class.

Professor Middlebrook's class was okay until she discovered a few select students used chat gpt on one of her assignments. She spent a whole lecture scolding the entire class and changed the syllabus  on the spot making it more difficult for everyone (during week 5). Her instructions are vague. She farms stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I felt that the work that she assigned was similar to the work that I did in middle school. Her teaching and style are "effort-based," but she didn't assign any work until week 6 and changed the veryyy strict attendance policy in week 3. I felt it was a waste of money and time. Wayyy too much work for a 100-level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Middlebrook's labor-based system of grading did alleviate a lot of the stress revolving grades. Her lectures were mostly fine, but did have a lot of uneccesary information. She is very likable and willing to help. My main complaint is that Middlebrook is a brutal grader and grades each assignment as if everyone in the class is a COLT ph.D

Dr. Middlebrook is very passionate about what she teaches and her students success and wellbeing. She keeps her lectures very engaging and values student input. Her class provides different grading options so that students with differing schedules can manage the coursework accordingly. Also she is very accessible in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have no complaints about this teacher. The workload is manageable if you plan ahead and the lectures are informative. I will say to make sure you're good about attending class.

Dr. Middlebrook is super kind & passionate about literature! The class (lectures, quizzes, essays) centered around 1 book we read throughout the term. She uses a unique grading style where you choose the grade you get based on how much work you do. I chose the work plan for a B & found the workload very manageable! Highly recommend this class/prof!

This professor insists on using grad-level course material. Readings are so dense that even as a fluent Spanish major who can understand it very well in person and in text, you are forced to spend hours on end simply to understand the readings. Such readings are worthwhile (at graduate level) and other Spanish professors have confirmed this .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a kind professor. Provides several different grading options to accommodate students with differing schedules. Easily accessible outside of class and is willing to meet to discuss grades and turn in dates. Gives constructive feedback on assignments. She genuinely cares about the course content and the success of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the nicest instructors I have ever had. She cares for her students and wants to include everybody in class conversations. If you are passionate about Spanish and challenging yourself with some guidance I 100% recommend her. Lots of reading, which can be difficult, but she is more than happy to talk during office hours.
Super nice and easy going. Lots of writing but if you put in some effort and follow the guidelines she laid out for getting an A then you will get the grade you want.
Professor Middlebrook's grading rubric for COLT 102 allows students to experiment creatively. She allows for growth and asking questions, and is very inviting to her office hours.

Prof Middlebrook was a good teacher for my COLT102 class. She's super into the material that she teaches which actually made the class interesting. The material is just one book for the entire term, but you do have to put some effort into knowing the text. There were a few quizzes but most of it was on the material she discussed in class.

Leah is  the best teacher I have had at UO. She is very personable and always eager to answer questions and clarify in discussion. I learned a lot. The class I took was very laid back paper and test-wise but demanded good discussion which I liked a lot.
I enjoyed the class overall, I was able to get a good grade and not have done much of the reading (I did do most just not all). Can miss up to three classes and NO FINAL

Nice lady, but not very good at helping you actually learn the material. She's kind of in her own little world, and she's really strict about being late! Had her in fall 2013, and the class was really difficult for a 100 level. Wouldn't recommend it unless you're really into comp. lit.

I thought that Middlebrook was passionate about her teaching but could be really condescending with her lectures. I think this course was harder than a lot of people were going to think it was for Comparative Literature 101.
Very surprised with how much work was expected for being a 100 level class. Unless you're really into comp lit, I'd pass on it. There are definitely easier gen. ed. classes you can take.

She is super knowledgeable on the subject and presents it with much eloquence and enthusiasm that is very inspiring. Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. She wants you to do well and is excited when you also show enthusiasm. She's awesome.

She is one of the most genuine and passionate teachers I have ever had. She teaches the subjects in a unique way-one that will open different ways of seeing the world. Very interesting stuff and highly recommended
she's a very good teacher and she's beautiful

This is the only professor that believed in me my freshman year. I got a D- on my first paper. She emailed me immediately and had a meeting with me and I ended up passing the class. I love her. She is an amazing motivator and I followed her classes to continue having her as my professor. If you want to learn, take Middlebrook.

Leah Middlebrook treated all of us students in our class as if we were in high school. Called me out in front of everyone. Very hard grader and expects a lot out of everyone. Thinks it was a 400 level, not a 100. Everyone who posted good things about her must not have ever went to class.. sorry to be so harsh but it is the truth.

Great professor. She makes the material interesting. She is a difficult grader, but if you show up and take an interest in the class, she'll help you out. She lets you rewrite papers for a better grade, and is warm and easy to talk to. Had her for Comp Lit, liked it so much I took her 466 Spanish class.

I understand why a student would like Leah, she's very energetic and knowledgable. She repeats the phrases to remember over and over.  However, she has a very condescending attitude.  Her in-class essays are difficult to do poorly on and the essays are very formulaic.  I hardly attended class or read in the last month or so and I did fine.
She is pretty awesome, and easy as long as you show interest, respect and show up to class.

She's a really genuine, passionate, and a nice person, however for the level of the course she expects a bit too much.  For a 100 level class she expected us to page through and analyze 3 books a play and 4 poems in one quarter.  So if you're thinking of taking this class with her then be prepared to read a whole lot, like a book per week.

This Professor was extremely clear with her teachings. At first I was unenthused about the class. Which was because it was a challenge. Even though my grade was not exceptional, I feel like I took a lot away from this class.

This is a professor with clear passion for her wrok.  She comes everyday enthusiastic to share her ideas with a participating class.  Some of her ideas can be a bit uncomfortable for the conservative mind, but all is approached in an appropriate manner.  Loved the professor, but the class was rather unchallenging
She was really intense about everything.... all the time... and she just was so serious about the class.  I just didnt like her or the stuff we learned about at all!

(Poetry course in 400 level)                  Leah is an incredibly gifted professor. She is dedicated and receptive to her students' ideas. She's funny and a bit quirky (in a good way!). Demanding but also willing to let you revise papers or re-do midterms (though I think you can only get a partial boost in your grade).

Middlebrook is a good professor.  Overall I enjoyed this course a lot.  I will admit that I did not find all the texts life changing, but I still understood the points she used them to make.  Do the reading, even if you're not hooked in the first few lines.  Go to class and do the writing assignments, showing interest.
The class itself is pretty easy, as long as you do the work.  Leah is pretty cooky in her interpretations of the lit but just go with it...
No Comments

She is a freaking psycho...I think her ideas are for the most part way off base and her disposition is incredibly annoying...the only thing I enjoy in the cass is laughing at her stupid concepts that she thinks she has formulated so brilliantly...she is nice...but overwhelmingly wacky.

Leah is an amazing professor and an amazing person. She is bright and sunny, very funny and willing to pay attention to your individual needs. If you are a critical thinker who enjoys reading, her course is flat-out fantastic. Just keep up with the work, put thought into your assignments, and pay attention during lecture (which is far from difficult, as she is very engaging), and you'll do just fine.

Leah is an amazing person, it is a freshman intro class so most of the kids are uniterested! She tries to be as engaging as possible, but when students dont read it becomes very hard! She is very willing to help, but the student must make the first effort. She will let you revise papers which is nice!

I was excited for the class in the beginning...she completely killed it. I did not like her at all! Her movies sucked, her papers were on boring material, and I wanted to skip everyday so that I did not have to deal with her. Comp Lit has boring classes! Don't take them.
good teacher with fun movies to go along with her class. upbeat as well.
The class is very lecture and reading-heavy, but his lectures go over the readings in depth; you just have to pay attention. Very understanding professor, and his lectures give a lot of info.

The content itself is something I am quite interested in, and he is kind and cares about the subject matter. Unfortunately, his lectures are uninteresting. It feels like listening to an audio recording of a textbook. Very few visuals and no efforts to have it engage with or relate to students. But the class itself is quite easy.

Dr. Lievanos is engaging, insightful, and deeply passionate about sociology. His lectures are thought-provoking and inclusive, blending theory with real-world relevance. He truly cares about students' growth, is always approachable and supportive. Highly recommended!

This class was very easy. Dr. Lievanos is passionate about what he teaches, however, the lectures were often boring and many of the student-athletes were disruptive and never were reprimanded. The discussions for this class were informative and reflected on the material perfectly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor. All readings are available on Canvas. Lectures are extremely boring and I found myself falling asleep most classes. Midterm and final are pulled directly from the study guide, just use basic reasoning and you'll most likely be right. Forgiving with late assignments and easily accessible online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Would not recommend. Extremely lecture heavy/boring classes. Only things you're graded on is two tests (midterm and final) and the 10+ page final paper (that is VERY difficult). I did go to every class and participated but found that my work went unnoticed. Prof didn't crack a smile once during class and wasn't focused on engaging his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable, respects that students have lives outside of class, gives good feedback, and is always open to help. Midterm is exactly like the study guide, same with the final. Large task is the 10-page term paper, start working as you learn the content. I didn't start ahead but kept up with readings, never missed class, and did well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took the accelerated online course over the summer. Very lecture heavy with lots of readings, but as long as you put in the effort he'll give you a good grade. I was really impressed with the amount of feedback I received from him; you can tell he really cares about your understanding of the content.

This class is a very easy A and does not consist of a lot of work. It does not make sense to go to lectures but the professor is very organized and makes sure that everything is clear. For the 8 page essay he gave us VERY clear instructions which made it very easy to write and succeed. Although I do not go to class, I respect him a lot

It is almost the end of the term, and I feel like I have not learned anything from this class. The professor is extremely dull and boring, even though the subject matter is interesting. Nobody listens to his lectures and people don't really come since there isn't much of a point. Definitely wouldn't recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring, usually have little to do with what we are graded on, vague course guidelines with little clarity. I wouldn't recommend taking his classes. Talked to other people who have said similar things as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is terrible. He makes no sense when he gives his lectures and they have nothing to do with the final 8 PAGE paper or midterms. The midterm and the final paper is the only thing you're graded on and the midterm is very hard and I haven't learned anything from his lectures that have to do with them.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is AWFUL. The GEs are somewhat helpful. The whole course is based off a final 8 page paper. His lectures have nothing to do with the paper. He talks about the most random things that are useless when writing your paper. Don't take this class. He's terrible. Waste of time and money. Midterms are also wack.

Rubrics for papers are vague and is a very hard grader. Lectures are very boring and incoherent. Lectures also don't help with writing his 7-page papers. Don't take the class unless you absolutely have to.

Nice professor. He has an insane amount of information, however he is full of himself & you can tell my how much he refers to himself throughout lectures. Other than that everything is clear; every week a quiz, every other week an assignment & the final paper is the biggest portion of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Liévanos is very kind, smart, and funny. His classes are lecture-heavy, but not difficult to keep up with if you do most of the readings and pay attention in class. There were discussion boards, two essays, a midterm and final, and one group project. If you put thought into your work and talk to him when you have questions, you'll be fine.

He does not really respond to your emails if he even does at all. His lectures are really hard to follow and his assignment prompts are lengthy and confusing. The way they are worded are difficult and could easily be phrased in a better way. Though he's not unfair and I did feel like I learned new material, his teaching methods are not for me.

She is strict about presentation time limits, but she also asks students for feedback on how she can improve the course in the future.

Lisa is extremely passionate about PR and is very knowledgeable, and has lots of real-world industry experience. She is very honest about what she thinks of your work, but I saw it as helpful feedback. She loves AI and taught me more about how to use it. I would definitely recommend her; she was also a relatively easy grader.

She's a super communicative professor and asks her students what she could do better in the future regarding the assignments and criteria. Very strict on presentation guidelines–mainly the time limits. Taught useful skills on using AI and how to prompt them. She's also super friendly and more than willing to help you with whatever!

I have had Lisa twice and she is amazing! She is so knowledgeable in her field and you can tell how passionate she is. Learning from her has been great and if you are especially interested in Tech PR and AI, TAKE HER CLASS! you will learn so many valuable skills.

JCOM 372: Lisa is great and very knowledgeable. The comments about favoritism are true, but just follow the instructions she lays out, and you will be fine. This is a writing class, but even so, there was SO MUCH writing due each week. She is a fair grader.

I'm currently taking her JCOM475 class and I wish I never registered. Her canvas is SOOO MESSY. She is very passive aggressive and has favorites. If you like wasting 4 hours every week this is the class for you. Extremely boring lectures!!!

The coolest leader.

Campaigns class with Lisa was awful. She will pick on students for no reason in front of the class and it's so uncomfortable to watch. She doesn't actually teach you anything, you just do the work and she critiques it in front of the class. Find a different teacher for campaigns.

Taking his online digital marketing class and its pretty interesting if youre into marketing. Group project would suck if you get a bad team. He assigns them randomly. Taken him twice hes a great dude.

His lectures are very entertaining, and he is very caring! I look forward to going to his classes and would definitely recommend him!

Nick is a really chill professor who brings a lot of excitement for his lectures. What a great professor, he makes the class as easy as possible for people are really wants you to succeed. Nick is awesome! I really enjoyed this class because of his engaging lectures. Nick is also a respectable man who has good principles and is always professional. Take this class with Nick if you want to learn about marketing in a fun way.

LOVE!! Nick is great, super accessible outside of class, answers emails in like 30 seconds. Group project and weekly discussions but honestly learned so so much in this class because I wasn't weighed down by pressure of doing well on an exam etc. Take him if you can!

I loved Nick Light. His Marketing 311 class was incredibly easy to follow and very interesting. He has a free online textbook for the class and all the tests are open note. Favorite Teacher I have ever had. The class finishes with a group project and he is kind of strict on no phones but I loved taking his class everything was easy to follow along. Take him!!

Nick is a top 3 teacher I've had at this school. His lectures are engaging, everything that you need for exams comes from said lectures. Full open note exams. He is the GOAT. Do anything you can to take his class if possible, he is the reason I'm now a marketing major.
super sweet professor! although attendance was mandatory, i always loved showing up to her class. participation does matter though, so she will probably move you guys around to talk to new people :)

She's great and is very passionate about the topics discussed in class. Although she gives out a ton of assignments its pretty bearable and mostly only requires just an hour to complete. shes the goat fr

Liliana was my favorite professor at UO. She is a hard grader, but outlines her grading criteria well. Her lectures were always a lot of fun, and she always made the class laugh. I would definitely take her classes again.

Liliana is a very good Spanish teacher, the way that she incorporates real-world experience and present day events into her teaching makes the language feel much more applicable. Liliana is such an amazing Spanish professor! She is so sweet, understanding, and very attentive. One of the better teachers I have had at the UO. Even though she speaks Spanish the majority of the time, you understand almost everything she says. The first day

JCOM 311: I feel bad becuase he is really sweet and cares about his students, but the gradings speed is abyssmal. By week 7 only three assignments have been graded. Gives a fiive minute break halfway through class which is very appreicated.
