The course description said we were gonna learn to edit newspapers

This class has hardly anything to do with editing. We only discuss/read about race and gender all class. And our homework has nothing to do with editing, we write reflections about race-related content. These reflections have little to no instruction and are harshly graded. She is also the only prof. still requiring masks in the SOJC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's really passionate about journalism and does a good job adjusting the class so it fits the group's strengths and weaknesses. She always has great advice both in the class and about life and really makes you think deeply about journalism. The only thing I might change is more specific feedback.

Wow! Lori is my all-time favorite SOJC instructor. I had her for Gateway last year and Reporting I this year and I would always leave every class feeling inspired and like I could change the world. She cares deeply about her students and journalism and is one of the sweetest people ever. Would 1000% recommend.
Loved taking Lori for Gateway this term. You can tell she cares a lot about her students as well as her profession. Definitely a hard class, but Gateway will be that way no matter what.
The best professor I have had. I learned a ton and could really feel that she cared about my work and making it better.
Lori genuinely cares about her students and bends over backward to provide opportunities for students who want to learn.

Lori is loved by everyone I mention her to. She has so much passion for Journalism, each class I'd go to, I'd come out feeling so inspired to change the world. She is a really genuinely nice person. Take time to get to know her, she is a gem and meant to be a teacher.

Prof Loza is excelente and organizes his online course really well. The class is easy to follow and each module has a video lecture and a plan of study which tells you exactly what you need to study. Someone said below that there were few video lectures. I think that they didn't actually pay attention to the class because there were plenty.

Professor Loza is one of my favorite instructors I have taken from at UO. The course is so well-structured, the lectures are highly engaging, and he is always willing to help students in any way. I could not recommend taking from him enough.

Profe Loza is awesome. I took his SPAN 324 online (manageable & fairly easy) and SPAN 420 in person (engaging & great). He's passionate, caring, & always willing to help. Highly recommend both classes & Profe. Only downside: his email responses can be same day or never.
Profe Loza is such a great person and professor. Passionate, knowledgable, fair grader and gives great feedback. One of the nicest professors I've encountered.

This online class was easy, but Loza does not respond quickly to email and often only uploaded reading for us to learn from instead of lectures as well. He was often unclear or made mistakes with instructions which is difficult for an online class. He seems like a great guy and the few lectures were good, but this class was obviously not a priority

Prof Loza is one of my favorites in the RL department, he's really personable, accessible, and helpful. Gives constructive feedback, creates useful assignments, and is adapting to student learning practices throughout the course. Have taken 2 of his classes, and looking forward to a third!

His class is really great, he is very helpful and communicative. Professor Loza is also very funny and I throughly enjoyed his class. I also did learn a lot and he really knows his stuff when it comes to phonetics. I recommend taking his class.
Great prof all around. Learned a lot.

Loza seems to understand how to navigate his online class well, and he is quick to respond to emails. The worst part about this class is there is no late work accepted. I take online classes because I have a busy schedule and want to go at my own pace. I don't get why he has this rule in place, I've never had this in other online classes do this.

Professor Loza genuinely cared about his students and was passionate about the spanish language. His classes were interesting and based on group discussions. He made learning remotely very easy, as everything was easy accessible. His midterm and final was fair and based on the information taught in class. Overall a great instructor.

I have no idea why her ratings are so low. Maybe she's different in other classes, but in FLR 250 she made class extremely simple and easy. She's also very approachable and makes the environment of her lectures comfortable. The ratings here had me worried about taking her class, but she was great.

overall not a very hard class, the midterm and final were just 600 words. however, the grading is very unclear and lowthorp is basically reading her notes word for word in lectures. she also comes off as condescending in almost all of her communications

Posting this because her ratings are not very good and I took ANTH119 this term online and it was very easy. Yes it is a lot of material, but that is how most online/anthropology classes are.. Discussions and two 650-750 page papers are bulk of grade. Not super hard.

Although this class was lecture heavy, she made every topic engaging. I really enjoyed my GE for this quarter, as our discussion period was just a brief overview of what we had learned the previous week and our big folklore project (which happened to be pretty easy as long as you pay attention to what she's looking for). Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There may as well be no professor for this class. The lectures are asynch and everything she uploads is years old. The GE's constantly have to clarify changes and what's no longer true. The only interaction she had all semester was to make the rubric harder halfway through the semester. I could not recommend less any course with Leah Lowthorp
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: professor lowthorp is super nice and extremely knowledgable. lots of readings but if you like folklore they're very interesting. if you watch the lectures and do the readings/discussion posts you'll be fine. midterm and final are pretty easy. no papers, just a term fieldwork project. overall super fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is not a normal 100-level anth course. I've had my fair share of upper divisions and I have never been graded so hard in my life than in this class. Boring readings, hard grading, feels like grad school. A ridiculous class that somehow made science fiction boring. NOT an easy A or even an easy B. A huge waste of out of my state tuition.

Professor Lonergan himself is very smart, but the way he explains things is not very comprehensive for the beginner-intermediate chemistry student. The labs are instructed by the lab manual he made, but it is extremely dense and difficult to get through. Felt underprepared constantly no matter how much I studied beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take Mark for CH219 or CH229. His grading is unreasonable and unnecessary. Tell me why our grades in a 1 credit lab course are determined by two exams, rather than the actual labs themselves. It would be much more manageable if the TAs knew what they were doing and if the labs were consistent with what we learned in class. Disappointed..

Mark is a great professor. I've had him for both CH 222 and 223. His grading system seems confusing or unnecessary at first, but it genuinely is the best way I've had a class graded. He uses standard-based grading, meaning if you don't meet the standards on his scantron exams, they will show up on the next exams until you get them right.

Mark has been my favorite professor at the university by far. He wants everyone to succeed. He individualizes tests and gives you vast opportunities through this to still get an A in the class if you fail one test. He's worked through questions with me or emailed me back within an hour. Highly recommend if Chem is difficult for you!
Mark often teaches as though all of his students are chemistry majors with a lot of previous chemistry knowledge.
I think he is a great professor, the subject is tough but he will always go out of his way to explain things.

Great!! He has a different grading system but it actually works out in our favor. Decent amount of clicker questions that are both participation and for correctness. if you miss a lecture he has recorded ones on canvas so it's chill. But, if you pay attention and show up it's pretty easy to get an A

I took him for CH222, and he is a very good professor. His grading system is very confusing and not until after taking the first midterm (3 midterms and one final total) did I actually understand how it works. Going to his office hours constantly is extremely useful and he makes personalized exams depending on what people need to work on.
Doesn't do his job. Bottom of the barrel, take this guy if you want to struggle the entire way and eventually get a bad grade.

Do the pre-labs and watch the lecture videos, I cannot stress this enough. So many people say this was too much work for 2 credits but I really enjoyed it and had no issues. Go to the office hours for post-lab help and you're golden. Was my highest grade all term.

Was really nervous about this class as a freshman but Mark is very kind and thorough. The grading was a bit confusing as it is standard based but he was happy to reexplain to the whole class and even make adjustments. This type of grading overall benefited many students. It also pairs really well with the lab as for application. Not a lot of hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, as long as you put in the work, Mark is there to help you when you need it. The screencasts are very helpful and everything is "open note" which is a plus.

I love mark! He's an amazing professor and genuinely wants you to learn and succeed. His lecture was very test heavy but practice exams were basically the same as the exams. I only have beef with him over lab bc it was way too much work for a lab

Mark is very sweet and really wants all of his students to succeed. He came up with a new grading scale, which sets every student up for success and a passing grade. He does everything he can to make sure everyone knows the content, and is not afraid to go back and change policies. Some lectures were a snooze fest, but still worth going to.

This class was way too much work for what it is. There is genuinely no reason for this lab to take as much time as it does and doesn't even translate well into future chem labs. Additionally, he does not care about the success of his students-at least in the lab-as multiple people I know have had bad experiences with him.

Mark is one of the best professors I've had here. He seriously wants you to succeed and makes it easy for you to do so. He's super approachable and understanding and replies to emails in a timely manner. GOAT.
Great clear lectures!

Very test heavy lab course (2 practicals and a written final exam). I did not enjoy the structure of lab as much as I did the lecture course. I found the lab manual and assignments to be very long and sort of confusing. Succeeding in this course is definitely possible if you stay on top of work and take good notes.

Very ALEKS heavy course (~1-3 topics/day). Mark was a very clear, engaging, and thorough lecturer. Offers a lot of office hours and makes it clear he believes his students are capable of succeeding and is super willing to help with that. Also is very responsive to emails and easy to communicate with. Grading is this course is very fair

Lonergan's expectations for this course are far too high and make the course inaccessible for disabled students. The standards set for lab are never clear even after completing the term, his automatic grading leads to errors, and he is overall inflexible. His formatting is dense, while still expecting students to perform to an absurd standard

Dr. Lonergan is a great person and a great lecturer. I took both 223 and 229. Lecture was a bit slow, but he ensured we understood each topic thoroughly. The first 3 weeks of lab are hell, but it gets much easier once you understand his standards. The worst thing in lecture is daily ALEKS homework. It's inflexible and forgettable. should be weekly

Mark makes the course way more difficult than it needs to be. 2 lab practical exams and a final. The post labs are confusing and we never have enough information to do the assignments up to his standards. His web lectures are helpful, but does not go nearly enough in depth to complete assignments. For a 2 credit class, it's a lot of extra work.

Love Mark! A great professor and genuinely wants his students to succeed. The thing with this course was you had to go the extra mile, meaning attending office hours and really understanding the material and experiments prior to attending lab. I would say the issue with this course was that most GEs were not that helpful, which made it hard.

Mark had helpful web lectures for the homework assignments, and if you followed along you would get a satisfactory grade. However, the amount of homework we had for a 2-credit class was a bit ridiculous. Definitely need to go to OH. The final is weighted heavily, which can either make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: mark is one of my favorite professors! he was entertaining and down to earth, and the way he lectures was easy for me to understand. chemistry is hard but taking it with mark made things feel easier. the ALEKS work is a pain though

This is possibly the worst and hardest lab I have ever taken, Mark is very nice and although he takes time to work with you extra if needed it doesn't make up for how unnecessarily hard this lab was. Our TA would often give us information that led us to the wrong answers and we weren't given enough guidance to compete the post labs.

Mark is very nice and will take the time to work with you outside of class if you are struggling, however his lectures did not make much sense in comparison to what we were learning and tests are expected to be completed in an unreasonable time leading to lower test grades even in you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: mark completely changed the format of the chem lab and wrote his own book for no reason. the assignments were incredibly difficult to complete and I never felt like I had enough information to do them. he is also giving us a in person final exam which none of the other classes with different teachers had to take and he said most people fail it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This term he decided to change the format of the tests, leaving us with not enough time to adequately complete them. He is a lovely human being and a caring professor but he is doing too much. Many of his comparrisons make no sense and leave me more confused than when I showed up. Also, he gives a midterm 6 days before the final which is insane.

I've had Mark for three classes now and he's definitely my favorite chem professor. I don't really know what to say about him because the thing that's so good about him is how normal he is. Mark is gonna give you a class with absolutely zero surprises and is gonna be extremely clear about any info that you need to know.

Mark is an absolute professional, there is no better instructor to take for gen chem. The class is impossibly hard, but that's just chemistry. Mark makes it feel easier than any prof I've had so far. I waited an extra term just to take 223 with him.

I actually don't have a problem with Mark. But there were 3 midterms and a final which was super stressful for me. As well as 4 homeworks and 1 quiz a week. My main problem was that during the tests, there would be 2 or 3 questions that were there to trick or confuse you which made my test scores not very good.
mr. Lonergan is awesome! He's super friendly in and out of class, and super helpful during office hours.

Even though it's just a lab course, we all know the General Chemistry labs are a lot of work. Mark is extremely thorough when it comes to grading and rubrics for all the lab assignments, and his office hours are super helpful (and almost every day too). He puts in a lot of work for his students and it shows.

Dr. Lonergan is the BEST!! He really cares that students get the most out of his class, all you have to do when struggling is email, office hours, or raise your hand. Sit in the front and give it your best and engage; you'll learn so much from him. Daily-ish homework, but it's super well-designed and preps you enough to not need pre-test cramming.

Dr. Lonergan is THE BEST!!
He is super caring towards all his students, super easy to reach by email or in person, and has really well-planned lectures. He is kind and fun as a professor, and he knows how to explain things. The homework setup can look like a lot, but 1) it's SO doable and lowers the time you need to cram for exams by preparing you!
Best professor I have ever had! Made chemistry understandable. Take practice tests and pay attention in class and you will be fine.

Amazing, funny, and super kind. His lectures made a lot of sense and he stayed as long as people needed during office hours. Test heavy but majority of it was covered during lectures. Uses clicker for participation/attendance.

Mark was an amazing professor, and if you need any sort of help I suggest going to office hours. He is very caring and will get you the help you need! Do be prepared for 3 midterms (1 happening during week 10, and a hard one at that). I suggest getting ahead in the class as much as possible to have ample time to study for the tests.
great class

Mark is great! He helped make chemistry feel a lot less impossible. He always has applicable real-world analogies for chemical processes or concepts that make them a lot easier to understand. If I could take the entire genchem sequence from Mark, I would.
He's the goat...

Chem 221. Amazing person and professor. Sometimes overcomplicates simple concepts. Very accommodating. Four exams. Tons of homework. Drops lowest midterm. You will spend a lot of time in this class and it is hard to pass, but longergan is great and very helpful. Class moves very fast and you will feel behind if you miss a single class. iClickers.

Great professor for a tough subject. He was super accessible and provided lots of support in office hours, you can tell he cares about his students. Would 100% take him again for another chemistry course, in order to succeed I would recommend attending his office hours with any questions you may have.

He is funny and interesting and makes sure you are aware of all the resources that can help you be successful in class. The best chemistry professor I've taken a class under and is genuinely honest and straightforward when it comes to topics that may be more difficult. Not condescending, and is super nice and helpful during office hours.

Mark is great! He genuinely cares about his students success. He was always willing to provide additional help in several office hours or zoom meetings. This class was difficult but he was amazing at making analogies during the lectures!

Mark is the best professor I have had at the University of Oregon so far. He's very engaging, understanding, and approachable. He cares deeply for his students and their learning, and he answers emails quickly. I highly recommend having him, especially because CH 223 is not easy. He also provides so many study resources. I really respect him.

Mark was the best Gen Chem professor I had. He talked in a way that really helped you understand the material. CH 223 is a really hard class, but he does such a good job at teaching the material it makes the class very doable. I wouldn't take CH 223 with any other professor. He's a great person to ask questions to.
Great professor!
The professor was good.

Mark was really nice and understandable when lecturing. He was the first chem teacher out of my gender chem sequence that actually made attendance optional by adding online recordings which was so nice and so helpful if you didn't get something in class or couldn't make it. Super accessible and although tough, his tests felt fair to what he taught

Mark is the best gen chem prof I have had at UO! He is so caring and I always felt like genuinely wanted his students to succeed. His lectures are very engaging and well thought out, and he provides a lot of resources like pre- recorded videos for every topic. Highly recommend taking chem with him if you have the option!

Great professor, very organized and great instructor/communicator. Passed the class even with a difficult schedule that required me to skip in-person lectures frequently, all thanks to his system of homework and pre/post-lecture resources.
He was super engaging and explained topics in very digestible ways. The class is definitely difficult, but he was an amazing profesor!

Professor Lonergan was my favorite chemistry teacher I've had so far. He did a great job explaining difficult topics and has a great teaching style with tons of analogies that make things easier to understand. He really cares and is passionate about chemistry. 10/10 would recommend.
Although the course concepts are difficult, Mark puts so much effort into making sure everyone understands what is going on. He offers so many office hours and is always ready to help.

mark is an amazing prof super nice and willing to stay after for specific help on problems. also super flexible in how to help if you struggle on a topic/ testing issues. when i told him i got a concussion right before the midterm he offered multiple other test taking options in order to put my health first.

Great teacher. Very good at providing a clear information. Homework went well with the work from class. Tests were hard but the course set you up good for them. He also has all lectures recorded from online classes so if you miss class you can still watch the lecture and get iclicker points. 100% would take

Although this class was online (due to coronavirus), Mr. Lonergan was good at explaining things in his lectures and is accessible outside of class. He's very helpful if you ask for help, and he's pretty reasonable with grading and helping you improve. CH223 is by far the hardest class in the gen chem sequence but he did a good job.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Lonergan is the best. Physical chemistry lab is difficult, but he explains the concepts well and makes himself very accessible to students. Plus, he is super nice and quite funny.

Dr. Lonergan is funny. He is very accessible. One of my friends had some issues during the term and he was totally understanding about it, even worked out a plan for the person so that they could still get a shot at passing. P chem lab is a HARD class but he was open, clear, and very helpful. Thanks to him (and the TAs), I did not fail!
He is a great Professor.  It was my first University class, he made me so interested and looking forward to more classes. He is very helpful if you asked.  Test you in what he teachs only.

Mark is one of my favorite professors. He's super intelligent but explains things in a way that anyone can understand. He is very into the subject and makes it as interesting as possible. Highly recommend. Also his grading is really good, tons of extra credit available.

I really  enjoyed Mark's class. He is a great lecturer and really enjoys teaching chemistry. He makes a tough subject bearable. Most of his quizzes and exams reflect our previous quizzes and homework problems. For exams, he also gives the class last years exam as practice. I would recommend taking his class for sure!
Tests and quizez are very reasonable and reflect the HW problems and lectures.  He is amazing.

This class was pretty easy. As long as you do all the clicker questions he counts all those for extra credit. the review sessions are really helpful. If you do the homework guide he assigns and ask questions in office hours you can get an easy A. he's just a really respectful guy and he's hilarious and is not boring at all. My favorite professor.
Very accessible, explains things fully, more strict than most but is not unreasonable, do the work and you will get a good grade, reading really helps
Honestly the best Professor I've ever had!! Very helpful! He cares about his students and wants them to succeed! I highly reccommend him for Chemistry 111!
Very good teacher
Best professor at the University of Oregon. Actually made me like Chemistry. You have to study but you will want to study with him as a professor!
In the top 3 best professors I've had. If you're taking chem, he's definitely my recommendation.

Very intelligent and explains everything thoroughly. I knew absolutely no Chemistry before taking this class and walked out with 106%. (He gives some extra credit on tests and with iClickers). I would highly recommend him, but only if you don't mind actually trying. He's a lecture kind of teacher, not a handout/hands-on kind.
One of the best teachers I've had so far! He knows the material and explains things really well. Always willing to give extra help when needed.
He was really awesome. He was always willing to meet with students and was incredibly accessible for our class size. I hate Chemistry, it's only my gened, but he was a great teacher for this class!
He was very organized and clear in his lectures.  He was very funny and nice.  He was very good at answering emails, and he genuinely wanted the students to learn.  He made it an easy class!

LOVE this guy. Brings us candy when exam averages are high :) Great teacher, always there to help, very encouraging, wants everyone to succeed, knows what he's talking about and makes his lectures interesting.
This is an awesome class. Lonergan is a very good teacher, super smart guy and knows what he is talking about. Would definitely take another one of his classes again.

He really is there for you if you need help. He puts a lot of time away to help his students. Everyone talks about how hard he is, but that is because they are being lazy and not reading the text book and doing the homework. If you do that, show up to class each time. You will be fine. If you don't understand, go to office hours.

Longergan is a GREAT professor. He tries hard to help people who are having a hard time and is thorough with his lectures. He gives out helpful pretests and goes over them before exams. As long as you attend class, do the homework and get help when you need it, the class isn't that bad.
Confusing at times, often had to correct mistakes in his notes.

He thoroughly wants everyone to succeed and tries his best to accommodate everyone. The pace of his class is a bit slow, but he covers the material well. Straight forward tests, no surprises, with good pretest.

Mark is the hardest science teacher I've ever had. He too intelligent to teach a lower division chemistry course. We only had two weeks of lecture (three classes, one day of going over syllabus) before our first 100 point midterm. The test was 12 pages of hell. If you are not a chem or science major or it doesn't come easy to u don't take Lonergan.

Rewarding but hard course! If you like "mathematical" thinking (I do) then you should be fine and you will learn a lot, otherwise this course will hit you hard! He's fair, but very rigorous with deadlines and grading. He's definitely not hand-holding and expects you to do most of your learning. Make sure you go to the labs!

This course is hard, as the material covered gets quite complex fast. The prof is well-versed in his material, but sometimes the pace and workload can be challenging, so be prepared to work a lot for your grade. On the upside, I learned a ton of coding, which I very grateful for! Would I take this class again? Yes. Is it everyone's cup of tea? No.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: If you can take another MAPS course, I highly recommend. He did not prepare lecture slides-just scrolled through the textbook, wrote out half of a code on the board and would tell us to "read about the rest later." No study guides given...study from labs and homework assignments. My hw was never graded in time to study from it. I could keep going

Third class with Sean and he is hands down the best professor in the school. The lectures consist of him openly debating his own students in a very constructive way, as well as going over his notes from the readings assigned. Take class with him, you will not be disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, and a great person. The class has too much arguments and discussions in my opinion but it's a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor had a great sense of humor which always helped keep the class engaged. The class material itself was quite interesting and covered a vast arrange of ideologies. Thoroughly enjoyed the course and recommend it for anyone.

Second time taking Long, and he once again delivered an incredibly insightful term. GE grading was lowk BS, but Long himself does regrades that are typically favorable. There was this nazi-veteran guy that always shared his awful views, and Sean was really good about hearing him out, yet he always made sure to slyly diss his awful preconceptions.

Assigns lots of readings, but between you and me, I didn't do any of them. He goes over the readings thoroughly in class. Very funny and kind, plus lenient on deadlines (except the final) if you need an extension. If you have a bad GE, he has a standing policy where he'll re-grade it on his own.

Sean is awesome. His content is very interesting and the structure is very simple. He cares about his students and just wants us to engage with the content. The readings are long but interesting and he explains them well in lecture. He is easy to reach out to and very helpful. Only graded on the midterm, essay, and an optional final.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Long is probably the most transformational instructor I've had in a very long time. He cares about his students a lot and just wants us to engage with the material. His office hours are a great way to connect. I would heavily recommend any class he is the professor of. Not too much structure but not too little to where it's annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Longs' teaching. I thought it was good and engaging, my only complaint is that his voice doesn't carry well so it can be hard to hear/understand him. Other than that he provided great feedback on work and very clearly just wanted people to succeed. He posted all the readings and although they were dense, explained them well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sean Long is probably my favorite professor I've ever taken. Idk how someone could not be satisfied with both the class and the person who leads it. A lot of hard reading, but he does a lot of clarification in class on both the readings and essay requirements. Only two assignments and you can just tell this guy just wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I took professor Matter Life and Death course in the winter term of 2023 and he was amazing and engaging. He is pretty straight forward and knows what he is talking about when it comes to the lecture and readings. However, he does not have slide shows, everything we discussed is directly from the textbooks he provided us with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is very beginner friendly, however if definitely feels repetitive at times since we go through the same four or so poses over and over again for the first half of every class. Also it's a no-tech class so if you want to track class with a watch, you're out of luck.

Nate is very kind and makes sure to greet everybody before each class in a genuine way. The yoga class is organized really nicely and is very enjoyable. Nate also adds insightful and positive commentary throughout the class that establishes the overall takeaways from the class.

Nate is so kind and encouraging of everyone and gave tons of options to make sure everyone was getting what they needed. Exactly the relaxing thing I need during the term and I'm looking forward to continuing yoga because of him.
Really nice yoga class that helped me relax every week. Nate was a great instructor that gave easy-difficult poses for everyone to practice.

Nate was a great instructor, and made me feel very welcome in the class even though I am not great at yoga. The class was graded on attendance and a "final project" (a selfie of yourself in a yoga pose). I will be taking Nate again.

Took this course non-credit for fun and absolutely loved it. Helped me clear my head during some stressful times during fall quarter. Nate was a great instructor and never pushed us too hard and always gave options for difficulty level. Really loved this class!!
so so kind and respectful of all levels of exp
I live for Nat. Super caring, understanding, and helpful.

His extreme structure around yoga and attendance really comes through in the way that he teaches and talks with students. I just saw him lecture somebody outside of the classroom in front of other people. Not for the first time and it is always condescending. Not a relaxing class and not an empathetic professor. I do hope he changes.
Great yoga teacher very supportive and nice routine, passing this class is super easy if you just don't miss over 4 classes.

Very funny and caring guy! I took PEMB110 and 211 with him because he's so great. Makes the class environment so welcoming and gives multiple variations depending on skill level. He's very understanding and can come off as intimidating but just talk to him and he is great! amazing instructor 11/10. You can miss 4 classes.
Great yoga class from a great yoga professsor.

Nathaniel was an awesome yoga instructor! My roommate and friend had him some time age and absolutely loved him! He's super friendly and offers multiple different variations of a pose one could do depending on their experience or if they are having pain or trouble with a pose. Can only miss 4 classes and is a P/N grading scale.
Awesome class, such a kind human. Would heavily recommend

I honestly did not enjoy him or the class at first, but he grew on me really quickly once I realized my bias was not against him, but against sun salutations. I really enjoy each practice now & even the sun salutations are growing on me. I would take a yoga class with him again.

Nice teacher, hard class

great guy

Awesome Class!! He is passionate about the subject and makes it fun to learn! Definitely take a class with him if you have the chance
beyond funny, keeps class setting loose while also maintaining an atmosphere conducive to learning, and makes sure you have a great time while doing everything the right way

great teacher!
