He's nice and means well, funny lectures, but the grading is 90% based on 3 tests including the final. I took the class pass/no pass and attended literally every single lecture and still struggled lol. I felt Peng used so much of his lectures to explain a concept with 0 difficulty level then the homework went to 100 real quick. Good luck y'all!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All lectures are just him introducing the topic then giving examples of how to do it, not actually explaining why wor how. All test grade averages were D level and the review for the final was just him saying to review our last tests, not actually giving us new questions to try. If you struggle with math already I do not suggest taking his class.

This professor has an attitude problem and will not accommodate your AECC requirements without making you feel like you have terribly inconvenienced him. Does not take feedback. Lost his patience because of cheating but the fallout wasn't fair to those who actually needed help.

he over explains and makes things more complicated then they need to be. very long lectures where he just writes on the board. he also at the end of the term the day before our last class he finally weighted all the assignments correctly which took people from passing to failing with no chance of doing anything to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor was nice, but he didn't give very good feedback on tests. This class has 3 main exams (2 midterms and one final). The class average grades per test were pretty low. His accent is kind of strong but he is understandable. Not the best class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. You definitely have to take detailed notes on the lectures to understand everything, but the material is clear and he does his best to answer questions. Tests are difficult, but he is very clear what will be on the test. Before the exams we did review problems exactly like the ones on the test. Very funny guy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lu is a really good teacher and very helpful in office hours. The content for this class is very abstract and challenging, but he does his best to explain in a way that's easy to understand. 100% recommend

Be sure to show up to lectures unless you are good at self teaching! He has somewhat of a thick accent, but he is still easy to understand. Material was not too hard to comprehend, as long as you pay attention!

He is a great teacher! He always finds a way to help us visualize the material, even if it is in three or four dimensions! His teaching is easy to follow and makes sense. He gives a reasonable and doable amount of homework. Just enough to get the concepts. His accent is easy to understand. He is really funny, and makes class engaging.

His accent is pretty easy to understand and his lectures are super clear. Hes also incredibly eager to go over anything you dont understand- ask him questions he gets super excited. Hes a little manic though and it made me sad when hed hit himself in the head because he made a simple algebra mistake. Also his metaphors are lit.

The Math 420 was kind a abstract class to some extend but prof Lu made it easy in the test. Once you go to class every time and focus on each of your hw. You will pass the course with no doubts. At least in this course, I got failed score at my hw but I still got A at my totally weighed grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tried lots of times but this website doesn't pass my comment. Anyway I'm not able to say the truth here. Just one thing, Chinese students don't take his course. Because he is a "Gou Tui Zi" I've never been so regret to take a teacher's course.

This class was awesome! I had a terrible prof in 253 & I was super nervous coming into 281 but Prof Lu was awesome! His English is a little shaky & the material is hard but if you go to class everyday, his notes are so thorough that it's impossible to not understand homework. But if you don't understand hw go see him before the test! Super helpful!

I guess nobody rated this class in particular. He's very clear about lectures, homework, and exams. If you needed an equation during an exam, he'd write it on the board for everyone to see. The exams aren't even hard. He likes to be visual as well, especially with vectors. Needless to say, I'm definitely taking 282 with him next term.

Not only is he the worst math GTF in the department, he's arguably the worst professor at the university. I also saw him for undergraduate advising, where he misled me on several key factors concerning my degree that made it so I have to attend another full year of school. Avoid him at all costs! He will single-handedly ruin your academic career.

Do not take this professor for 253... He gave no study guide and the class bombed the first test. Then he gave out a study guide and the class did slightly better but he made the test 10x harder than the guide Q's. He uses analogies that are not helpful or relevant. He may be better at other courses but I did not find him good at this one.

Gotta go with everyone else on this one. The class is just awful. Terrible lectures. I can't say anything nice about this class. I am not a "Math" person and I had to work my tail off for a C, a grade I am NOT used to getting. Avoid if possible.

I did not go to a single day of this class. I found that my discussion sections were much more helpful considering there was 600 people in the lecture class. I found it to be a very easy class, but only because i am good at math. could not understand the teacher at all, so i just taught myself with the book and discussion leader

Given that it was a huge class I thought that he did his best to teach the material. The class is just a really hard class overall, tons of studying if you arent fluent in math, but his jokes made going to class worth it, he is super funny! People failing the class didn't think the jokes were as funny though.. haha
Tough class. The size, professors accent, and terrible GTF only made it worse... I pretty much had to teach myself since going to class really didn't help.

Huge class size for 241, so I rarely went.  When I did go however, it was hard to understand him. I'm sure he's a good teacher, but getting past his accent is hard.  For his MATH 241 class he leaves most of the grading up to the GTFs, so try to get a good one.

When I got on here and saw Peng's reviews, I thought I was in for a tough term. Don't listen to those reviews. Peng is the man and is possibly the best math teacher I've ever had. He's really well organized and lays out every single step on the board. Yes, his tests aren't the easiest, but if you've done the homework, they're totally doable.

His strong accent is difficult at first but the more you go to class the more you understand it. But going to class is very helpful and he does give extra credit several times throughout the term when only a few are in attendance. Tests are very difficult but curved. And do all the homework problems because graded very closely.

Peng Lu is bomb! It will take a while until you get used to his accent, but the overall class is not that bad.  If you attend class, he goes over things and makes you understand the material.  If there are just 30 or so people who are in class, he gives you extra credit! He did that about 5 times this term! His tests are hard, but curves!:)
His accent is a road block but he tries very hard and if you come to class and actually listen you can get passed it. Is VERY anal about homework and throws some curve balls in his tests.
Gets rather excited, which can make his language incomprehensible.

listening to him say "coefficients" has to be one of the funniest things i've ever heard.  fantastic lecturer but tests were 90% of your grade and i found them to be really hard.  it wasn't the dif eq that was hard, it was the algebra.  he'd throw in weird little tricks that if you didn't pick up on you were screwed.  i learded a lot, but failed.

IMPOSSIBLE to understand!! literally no point in going to class because you do not know what he is teaching. i don't mind math, but the course would have been much easier with another professor. although, quizzes and tests are fairly easy

Although he may be hard to understand sometimes but he definitely tries really hard to get his point across. His accent is hilarious, and he uses the words "basically" way to much. Tests are super easy, dont know if that is a good thing or not.

He seems like a nice enough guy, but it is impossible to understand him.  He faces the board a lot and does not interact with the class.  It was so hard for me learn in his class that I had to drop it and get a W and I love math.  Wouldn't recommend this guy.
****in hard class, hard to understand. Got a B-, but barely. Good luck!

While I agree to a certain degree that Peng may make it too easy in that you might be screwed in the long run, atleast it isnt impossible and you are lost in it all.  Peng makes everything crystal clear and entertaining at the same time.

Makes CALCULUS way too easy.  I will never be able to use calculus in the future if its anything more challenging than a simple antiderivative.  You may think you are in for an easy class, but you will be screwed in the long run.  He writes everything on board, easy to follow.

Peng...He is definitely not American & is hard to understand sometimes,but when you do understand, he explains things very well. He is willing to sacrifice his ego to teach by doing embarrasing things and making an ass out of himself so you can learn. EASY tests,ask him to say "derivative" for you!

Professor McKinley is probably my favorite professor I have had in law school. She is so caring and kind and open to outside ideas. I've loved her class and have loved getting to know her. Some would say her cold calling is intense but it get the best out of the students.

The midterm was open for 3 hours. It took 5 hours on average. Does not answer questions directly and is often condescending. Grades are given pretty arbitrarily and group projects have almost no explanation.

Mckinley herself said that this was a similar workload to legitimate law students. That being said, if you are able to read a decent amount and talk once a class, you should get an A. However, Mckinley does look for specifics in quiz answers, so I would suggest utilizing office hours. You should take this class only if you are serious about law.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor McKinley expects a very specific answer to her discussion questions in class and on quizzes, if you gave an answer she wasn't looking for she will slam her hands on the desk and get very agitated. On her quizzes, she gives zero feedback. She is very knowledgeable, but she could improve the structure of her class (and her attitude).

Professor Michelle McKinley expects specific answers to her broad questions. If you dont give her the answer she is looking for, she will shut you down or not acknowledge what you said. Her quizzes are okay but she is a tough grader because she looks for specific answers. Her class is not based on lectures but it is based mostly on readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I absolutely adore Nikki! I've had her twice now and she's the best. She's super open and caring to her students, making it a point that her door is always open to her students. Her feedback is very constructive and helps in the long run. We did have weekly reading quizzes, but the ?'s tied into the textbook (which was online) and were very doable.

Wonderful professor who clearly cares about her students and the topic of PR. I felt like I learned soo much and everything we discussed was very applicable and interesting. She made class a place I wanted to be with her positive attitude and ability to make lecture interesting.

Attendance is mandatory, and it is taken by doing class activities in groups. Everything you learn comes from lectures/ slides. All tests are open note, so if you go to class and take notes, it's the easiest class to take.

Professor McClaran is such a good professor! I had her for JCOM370 PR Fundamentals during the spring. She gives a lot of extra credit options and is very communicative with her students. We do have weekly group assignments that are required and count as your attendance. Exams were open book and lectures were very thoughtful and intriguing.

Take this class. 
I promise you'll enjoy it, Brian's the best
what a guy! he's so odd but also so funny. very easy class and pretty interesting stuff too.

One of the best professors in the CHC. Super witty guy who is not afraid to banter with students. Started crying in class a couple of times when talking about stuff that made him emotional, so maybe don't take him if that makes you uncomfortable (it doesn't for me). All-around a solid, deeply intelligent guy who is operating at a whole other level.

The lack of instructions for papers felt a little weird at first but it's actually pretty great. This class felt like a group therapy session, partly because Brian would get emotional so easily. He's probably one of the weirdest professors I've met, and it's truly so awesome.
Flat out the best class I have taken and he is an amazing human, if you get the chance to take a class with him drop everything and do it.

Prof. McWhorter is so funny and a wonderful professor. It is fun to joke around with him in class, but you still learn a lot. He is very supportive and kind. Class discussions were always interesting and enjoyable.
One of my Favorites

Brian is the best professor I have had at the UO so far. He genuinely cares for his students and their livelihoods in and out of class. His approach to higher education is unique (less focused on the accumulation of knowledge and more so on each student gaining something from the assignments) and felt like a breath of fresh air. Highly recommend!
Super easy class, and a really relaxed grader. Also fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There aren't enough words to describe how great of a professor Brian is. He is funny and genuinely cares about his students. The assignments are very fun and he always makes class enjoyable. I would highly recommend him!

If you get a chance to take velocity of gesture TAKE IT. I promise it'll be your fave class of the term. Not only bc it's easy (he grades btw 90-100), but bc its so fun. The only people I wouldn't recommend it to are people with extreme stage fright. But don't be intimidated! Brian is super accommodating, and the class environment is v accepting.
Really easy and interesting class. Grades easy and little work load. Midterm and final aren't that hard if you watch and take notes on lectures.

Best teacher ever. Really cares about his students which is super nice. Helps you with a lot of the stuff you need. Super clear on what he wants us to do for assignments. Love going to his class. Talking to him with my problems always helps me feel better and he always has the right thing to say to help you.
Brian is a good teacher. In the class, you have to make a song, but it's really not a big deal.

Brian is a very entertaining lecturer every day, he will always make you laugh. If you show up and complete the few assignments for the term, you will get an A. Very easy, and going to class is not necessary, but they are entertaining lectures.

Professor McWhorter is a great teacher! He's so funny and makes class entertaining. It's easy to get an A in his class as long as you show some sort of effort in your assignments. There's one midterm which you can take on your own time online, and the final is making a garageband song which isnt hard. I have no music background, & loved this class.
He's really a great teacher, and you can tell he's passionate about what he is talking about! He makes it relevant and interesting. Projects, papers, and tests were all super fun!

Brian is amazing. I have no knowledge about anything music related and Brian made everything so fun. He is one of the most humorous professors at UO and really cares about his students. If you follow the directions and put in your best effort, an A will come naturally. Favorite class I took the whole year.

Funniest professor I've ever had. Makes class really entertaining while still offering constructive criticism. At first, I thought he was crazy and I was frightful of what I was getting in to, but as the term went on I realized he's just a goof who's having fun.

Absolutely loved his teaching! I'm not personally interested in music but he made the lectures so enjoyable and easy for the class to understand. The material was clear and the one test and two projects were minimal. Would take any class of his.

Matt is awesome and his lectures were the highlight of the course, but beware if you are a biology, hyphy, or neuro student, this class is BORING. It's basically little baby bio for psych majors, and just kinda goes over some surface level biology ideas. Also, the entire course is graded based on three online exams, 5 “labs”, and 10 discussions.

The material is difficult but he makes it as manageable as he can. He records all of his lectures to make up if you miss one, and has a live zoom option if you can't or don't want to make it in person. All tests are on Canvas (synchronous), open note and open internet (no AI). He allows retakes and curves grades. Expect a multitude of dad jokes.

Dr. Smear is clearly passionate about what he teaches alongside being really funny, which makes his lectures much easier to pay attention to. Attendance isn't mandatory (except for the lab section), but I highly recommend going - the slides alone don't completely cover the course material, and his lectures fill in the gaps.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Busy professor so you have to schedule office hours if you want to meet up. Super funny and smart guy. He makes class interesting. Open note online exams (2 midterms and a final). Only weekly homework is lab work and writing discussion posts, very light course load. 
However, you won't know your grade until the end of the term.

Dr. Smear is a very enthusiastic professor! 80% of your grade with be made up of the midterms and final, but they are online and open note, which makes them manageable. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would recommend going. I would also recommend taking notes on what Dr. Smear is saying rather than copying down the slides.

Matt is a great guy and cares about what he is teaching you. However, his lectures can be confusing, and he can go fast. Don't let this review turn you away from taking this class. I found that going to the review session and hearing the content from another perspective was helpful and helped me better understand the contet.

I loved Matt! His lectures went fast but he recorded lectures so you could watch them later. In-person attendance wasn't required. Labs were cool. 3 tests and easy homework. Test were online even though this class wasn't an online class, and this helped tremendously. Tests would've been a lot to memorize if they weren't online, so just be aware.

amazing guy and information, terrible organization. very little communication to students about what is due, graded tests released 3 weeks after the test was taken, was not accessible outside of class, was a no-show for a meeting i set up with him. little info about test content. Loved the info, loved the labs and goal of class. very sweet guy

Solid teacher but unorganized. My issue with the class is that he lets students retake an identical copy of the midterm in lab, which opens the door very wide for cheating. I heard that there were answer keys circulating for the 2nd midterm and I had midterm grades of 81 and 82 vs an 89 on the final. Imo this class isnt viable until this is changed

Professor Smear is awesome! He is one of the best professors at UO and makes learning about biopsych fun and enjoyable. His lectures are great, but sometimes he can go super fast through them. He gives two midterms and on both, you can retake those midterms to get a better grade.

In order to do well don't miss class and read the textbook. Lectures are super dense and will be easier to understand if you've read the chapter before. Tests are pretty hard but you can retake the same one the next week and take the average of the scores. He's really funny and sometimes talks too fast but is good about going back if someone asks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Matt is a great professor! You can really tell that he is passionate in his field and it makes his class much more bearable and he delivers the material pretty well. he is also really good with responding to questions. theres only 2 midterms and a test. the tests are hard, but if you go to class and study before the tests, you'll get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Matt Smear made going to class and learning about biopsychology really fun. Labs were also very interesting. Class is not an easy A but if you pay attention in class and put some work its totally possible.
Class has no homework; two midterms, and a final. The only other points come from in-class quizzes, and iclicker questions. Just show up, pay attention, and you will get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great course and very interactive with groups. Dr. Meek is a very easy grader and loves his job and we had calls with outside lecturers. The class was always super interesting and midterm and final were really easy and interactive.

Dr. Meek is an amazing professor. Such an easy grader and lectures are super interesting with real world applications. Three projects and they are all really easy and applications based. Lectures are long but very interesting when you interact. Overall a really easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Meek was great! While the course is homework-heavy, the assignments are simple and quick.
Good class and very interesting material; however, he should probably retire.
All I'm going to say is don't take him for any of the classes he teaches. If you do... I told you so.

DO NOT TAKE PROF MEEK. He is the least understanding professor I've ever had and will not help you if requested. Just beware that he doesn't have your best interests in mind. UO... please don't hire professors that clearly hate their jobs.

If you are expecting a super easy online class, don't take this. That being said this class isn't hard there are just a decent amount of assignments/ readings. The midterms and final aren't dense assignments. There is a 24 hour grace period for assignments (including midterms). The Prof is a sweet person and this class is interesting.
He did give lots of readings, but they were short and easy to understand. This online course will be easy if you stay on top of the assignments, but the midterms and final were relatively easy.
One of the worst, most disorganized classes I've ever taken. Way too much homework. Absolutely no support from the professor. I learned absolutely nothing from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SO MUCH BUSY WORK. I needed electives so I took this online course expecting it to not add that much to my workload because it is a 200 level. Boy was I wrong. There's at least 5 long readings a week, at least  2 discussions, and extra written assignments. He didn't even lighten the extra assignments during the week we had a midterm due.
Hot take, I liked him he was genuine when I had issues that forced me to miss class.

Honestly, going to Dr. Meeks' lectures was the worst part of my week. Listening to a cishet white man ramble for over an hour about the struggles that minorities face in education was genuinely agonizing. Would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Meek is an incredible professor, and for a 400-level class, it was actually relatively easy. There are lots of readings, but material is interesting. He gives great feedback on projects and is very easy to talk to. It's obvious that he cares a lot about his students and is passionate about what he's teaching. I'd highly recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Meek was a very kind and genuine professor, you can tell he wants his students to succeed. He is also incredibly passionate about what he teaches about. He assigns a fair bit of reading yet grades fairly and provides clear guidelines. The tests were curved and class sessions were engaging. Would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doctor Meek is one of the best professors. In class be prepared to talk because he tends to put you in groups at the end of class. You get a point each time you attend class and there is one extra credit opportunity if you provide questions about the readings each class. There are lots of readings! Projects can be difficult but are well explained.
Assigned way too much work per week (sometimes midterm projects on top of 5-7 assignments), didn't put his UO email anywhere so we couldn't contact him, made so many lecture videos every week.

This class was online but David seemed nice and understanding from what I saw. The class did have a lot of busy work but lots of opportunities for extra credit. For everyone saying the class was hard it wasn't- the assignments are easy and short with some reading. Getting an A is very doable. The final was super chill.

Professor was nice enough, but the class was awful. Badly structured, not engaging, way too heavy on the workload and lots of busywork. My GE was very mean. Not a good Global Studies class--convinced me to quit the major. Very disappointing. This class has gotten bad reviews for ages yet the university does nothing about it. Do better U of O.

Way too much readings and discussions. Way too much busy work. Everything was confusing and didn't relate to the course description. Not worth it at all. Professor was nice tho and responds to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: For being a lower division class, the amount of work throughout the term is insane! Multiple readings and discussion posts every week, and so many lectures. I understand that it is an online class but he was not as helpful in course organization as I think he could have been.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is so boring. Workload wasn't too bad; weekly discussion posts, occasional lecture reflections, 2 midterms, 1 final. Weekly extra credit, but it barely does anything for your grade. Since this class was online, I didn't interact with the professor, but this is just an insight as to what the course was like for those thinking of taking it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The amount of work is not worth it for this class. Get ready for a lot of busy work, as well as three-page essays for midterms one and two. The topics themselves are interesting, but the readings given each week can be very long and difficult to parse. I found myself spending more time on this class than my core classes for my major.

Online course is extremely disorganized, unclear, and messy. Unfortunate because the course covers interesting topics, and I was unmotivated at the start due to confusion, lots of busy work. May change this rating if communication improves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Meek has been very supportive and is very passionate about the content. He understands that everyone is able to offer something to the discussion despite their major or interests. There is a fair amount of work, quite average considering it's an Honors College class; and was discussion and essay heavy.
Not engaging an unfortunate missed opportunity for connecting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is a very nice person but the class was an absolute mess. The most confusing go figure it out yourself class I ever took. Most assignments are either common sense or opinion-based but with evidence from readings. Lots of readings. Lectures were posted in a very confusing way.

Very heavy workload for a 100-lvl class, mostly busy work, and readings were long. Meek himself is knowledgeable in the field but I never interacted with him, just watched his lectures. There were miscommunications b/t him and the GEs, which was annoying. Tests are project-based and fairly easy. I did well but getting through the class was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Meek was ok but just a ridiculous amount of homework (between 4-10 assignments a week) and as a senior, I have never had that many assignments in any class.  The presented information was thorough and straightforward and directly applied to the assignments. Tests were just projects and fairly short/easy. Only email the GEs as he wont respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Meek is very thorough and knowledgeable, just not my style of learning. Despite being an asynchronous online class, he maintains a class schedule where assignments are due twice a week (at least) which is both nice and annoying. He assigns WAY too much HW for a lower series class (4-8), all of which is busy work. His tests are easy & project-based.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I struggled some early on, mainly because I was out sick for multiple lectures. Reccomended book, but not required (instructor had extra copies we could borrow if we couldn't afford our own). She made time outside regular office hours to help me catch up. Ultimately, the course material was very accessible and tied to everyday life.

Reads directly off slides. Confuses herself. Condescending and kind of rude. Often late and was even late to the final. Final wasn't on material ever covered and had to curve the class a ton because everyone failed. Would not recommend.

Her lectures are very uninteresting, lit reads the exact stuff off the slides accessible online. She goes very fast through the content, it's difficult to write down all the info. You also lose focus halfway through the class because she tries to shove so much information into one class (sometimes we would talk about two chapters in one class).
Reads off the slides and often mixes up class examples. Half the stuff on the quizzes she doesnt even go into detail in, so your left searching though the slides trying to teach yourself concepts.

Read off the lecture slides. Didn't provide much information. Only graded on a midterm, two quizzes, and participation. The quizzes are like the practice example she gives, but midterm and final are nothing like the review or practice problems. Lectures are boring and hard to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do I respect her as a professional and academic? Sometimes. Would I ever step foot into a class taught by Lisa Redford again? No. I genuinely hated taking this course. What is presented as a lecture class turned into a seminar where she hated the fact that we didn't understand the overly dense and long readings she assigns and does not explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
She is a bit intimidating but kind and very knowledgable. 
This class is very reading and discussion heavy. A large part of your grade is attendance.
She tailors material to be interesting for students and really encourages active engagement.
Helped me learn a lot but is a bit challenging, especially if a slow reader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Will you come out of her class knowing more than you would from any other professor? Absolutely. Will it be the hardest class you're taking that term? Also yes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Redford is extremely smart and a nice person but the amount of work and out of class time expected to be dedicated to this class was ridiculous. We were expected to watch lectures before the class when they were posted less than 12 hrs before and the homeworks were overly convoluted with pages of instructions that say a lot but dont mean much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Redford is very knowledgeable in her field of study. The labs are time consuming but helps you develop important skills in Phonetics research. Some concepts are hard to understand but if you ask for help, Dr. Redford will explain to you in many ways. It was challenging but it is an upper division course, if you do the work you will do well!
Wonderful professor that offers engaging and challenging courses.

So Dr. Redford has all of this knowledge on a ton of psychological and linguistic ideas from her work as a researcher. She knows experts in the field and has done her own experiments and can tell you about important ideas in normal conversation. This is really helpful when you need to know a lot of in depth info about a subject, for projects etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Lisa was the worst professor I've taken a class from at UO. The class was full when the term started and more than half the class either dropped the class or switched majors all together. She's helpful outside of class, but her lectures are hard to follow, she goes off on tangents that no one understands. I'm never taking a class from her again.

Melissa Redford is nice, but her teaching is hard to follow. It's an intro class but there are terms she throws around that I had no idea what she's talking about. Her class is 2 hours long and I barely gained anything. She is really frustrating and it's hard to be patient with her. She goes on and on about nothing and expects you to understand.
Do not take a class with this professor. The class is very difficult and she does nothing to help. She is extremely unclear and expects a lot of work.

The WORST professor ever. Stay away. Impossible to understand. Impossible to talk to during office hours cause she cuts you off and starts talking about herself. She makes your life miserable in class by talking about irrelevant complicated things that have nothing to do with the topic or class and just because she wants to destroy your confidence.

Very scattered teacher, probably much better for upper level classes. This class was very difficult, mainly because of the way she jumps around and uses terms that no one knows, then expects them all to be known by the test. Not a ton of outside work though.

Melissa is cool but she sometimes comes off as extremely pretentious and scattered throughout most of her lectures. Unnecessarily complex word choice and heinously boring material made her class painful. Nonetheless, if you even put forth minimal effort you'll be fine in the class.

She's a really cool person, the challenge is to stay awake in her class. Also, if you don't  understand jack with a D going into finals, don't give up. Somehow, everyone seems to end up with a B in her class. Just sayin'
Not a bad prof. The tests seem intimidating and I thought I was screwed, but ended up getting a B in the class. Definitely interested in teaching, knows a lot.

A great professor.  Really loves her field and is very attentive to her students.  Sometimes a bit scattered, but in a brainy professor sort of way.  Redford is HYPER intelligent and abstract, but her abstractness is grounded in real-life phenomena.  She's fun in class, but makes her students work.  Her class was very worthwhile.

Professor Redford was very helpful and always willing to answer my questions.  Very nice and happy, and not a bad class to have to start your day with.  Tries to tie in language to real life which helps you understand why you're paying $200 a class to be there.
I felt like she was still getting the hang of teaching.  She works hard, and is willing to help her students as much as possible, but isn't incredibly organized.  Still, I enjoyed her class.
Uses really unnecessary big words, but is really good with e-mails and helping before a test.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

I was interested and really wanted to enjoy this class however, it was not what I wanted it to be. Dr. Casement was very hard to connect with outside of class, and often would not respond to questions until after assignments were due. Her instructions were consistently unclear and class structure was strange compared to other college classes.

Attendance is graded which is crazy in college. She is lecture heavy, mostly photos and vague content. She will ramble about the actual information. Be ready to read. She is boring/not engaging and treats you like a high school student. Took this as an elective thinking it would be fun but wanted to drop in the end. Students were distracted 24/7.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Sat in 70 minute "lectures" of student discussion of their thoughts of the DSM 5.
The tests are worded in ways which make it hard to figure the logical answer.
If you put in the time to read, attend class, and write the 3 short papers, you can get an A. If you, like me, prefer more engagement besides with the textbook, it will be frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: 3 quizzes that were difficult if you didn't do reading. You had 2 chances to take the quiz, but weren't able to see your score the first time taking it and she didn't take the higher score. Lectures weren't detailed so if you didn't do reading or attend class, lectures didn't help much. Big group project and didn't have a great grading rubric.

I am absolutely appalled by my experience in this class. This was the firs time that this class was offered, yet there was no grade leniency even with a mean of 62% on one of the quizzes. If the mean is that low, you're doing something wrong. Had a GE write about how my paper was incredibly thoughtful then given an 8/10 w no explanation. AWFUL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's very engaging and organized. My only issue is the group project. I understand teamwork and collaboration is a life skill. However, when your grade is reliant on working with a team, it becomes inaccessible for those with anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I didn't attend more than half of the zooms and finished with an A-. Every single assignment added up to 100 points (with no weight) so every point counts. It just sucked because her GEs were in charge of grading essays and always gave me bad scores (I had never gotten below a 90% on essays, and I consistently got Cs) with no reasoning or feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a huge disappointment. If you're a psychology student, chances are you will have to take this class. Group project for the purpose of "teaching you how to work in a group" because it's valued by employers. I signed up to be taught psychopathology, but she taught me nothing. Just buy the textbook and read it. You'll learn more.

The class itself is very interesting, and the professor shows a lot of passion for this subject. She is very accommodating to the students and helps them succeed because she cares. There is a lot of readings assigned though, so beware of that. Otherwise, this class is fun and the professor does a great job at keeping students engaged!

I was really disappointed with this class. Her lectures are very surface level in terms of the material . Most of her lectures are discussion based, which is not conducive to a 100 person class. I cannot stress how sluggish and boring class is. If you do the work- its an easy A. If you want to learn psychology + disease, take a different class.

If you are genuinely concerned with learning about mental illness, don't take it. Much time is spent on a useless group project and unnecessary "workshops" instead of actual psychology. It's an easy class, no exams, only book-report style short essays and HW quizzes. Doesn't go in-depth, kinda wastes time, but very kind and approachable.

If you show up to class, turn in assignments on time, refer to the textbook for open note quizzes, and go to TAs office hours you'll do well. She spends WAY too much time on irrelevant subject matters that don't delve deeper into the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Awesome!

Group project was terrible. Lectures were boring and the slides weren't helpful. The "quizzes" were more like exams - no notes allowed, high point value in relation to your grade, etc. The reading assignments were just busy work. The essays were like college-level book reports - easy and more busy work. Prof is very nice & approachable though!

Class itself was very information heavy, much more emphasis on memorization. I feel like she would be better suited to teach a better class, because I found her interesting to listen to, but she would go too fast. Days with quizzes have lecture after, and readings due before class, every class. Even with a midterm. Group project is worthless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The course material for this class isn't that hard and she is pretty good at explaining everything and answering questions. The slides are not useful at all; I barely ever went to lecture and will probably get an A. Make sure you read the textbook if you aren't going to go to class though. There are no exams, just 4 short quizzes and 3 short essays
She's okay.

Took ARTD 410 Advanced Digital Drawing. This was by far the best class and best teacher I've had. He seems intimidating at first, but if you talk to him, he will give you amazing feedback. The class and teacher will encourage you to improve. I've never improved this much artistically in such a short span of time.

Good class overall, I think he was a great teacher in the way that I feel like I learned a lot and it felt like a boss and I was the employee. did not grade anything till after finals, which was hard, but if I needed to reach out to him, he helped me understand the guidelines and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecture. I like seeing prof grades people who have no idea how bad their work is.
Cool teacher, knows his sh*t.  Highly recommend him if you want to be pushed to make quality work

Great professor. Cool guy. Extremely helpful, all you have to do is take the time to ask and he'd give you great advice. Can be a bit blunt, but it's always constructive and never a waste of time. Highly recommend any class if his if you want to have freedom with projects and exposure to some sweet digital art work.

Great professor.  He doesn't make his class mandatory to go, but most of the class goes because its so interesting.  Hes very honest and blunt about things but in a good way.  He's really helpful if you go talk to him after class.
honestly he pissed me off for a couple of days but, he inspired me to push myself harder. This is why I think he is excellent. Salter, if your reading this: Thank You

he had a huge ego. most of his lectures were on his own work.  he barely ever explained the projects assigned and when questioned about the grade i received he became very defensive. he basically told me that i screwed up on the final project when he said in the last class "no matter what you do, you can't mess this project".

His lectures are like watching a performance piece. Perhaps a little egotistical, but in this field getting advice  and learning from great artists is essential. I have had only great experiences talking/working with Michael. And he's easy on the eyes... which helps.

I found the class not at all interesting. There were no guidelines for any of the assignments. At the last moment he assigned a project due during Dead Week. I don't to take more classes from this professor.

Great instructor. Open to sharing experiences, answering questions and encouraging students to explore what interests them. Classes have loose structure, depending more on labs to teach software versus actual lecture time. If you don't know InDesign or CS2, GO TO THE LABS. Overall, I'm looking forward to taking more classes taught by him.
No Comments

Grades 100% arbitrary, which would be OK if he accurately explained what he was looking for in the first place and stuck by it, instead of changing his mind every 3 seconds.  Also, it is the GTFs who actually works with students -- Salter just lectures -- and their opinion never matches.  The GTFs never know what he is looking for, either.
No Comments

You'll have a hard time if you are unwilling to realize that your work could be better.  Michael will gladly tell you if your concept sucks, but he's really just trying to get you to make the best, most creative art you can.
No Comments
Very easy class, not super interesting tho
Easy pass/no pass course. Content was fairly interesting but a lot of reading. Does not ask much of you so take it if you want an easy course.

I really liked the class. I found that the class was very interesting especially for a pass/no pass class. He was a generous grader even when I missed a couple of due dates. Overall just a great class and a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Mickey mouse easy class. Take if you want the easiest class of all time
Super easy pass fall class! Super easy grader and as long as you do the work you will pass this class!
Awesome and informative professor. Cares about material and students!
Online class, really didn't have to do much besides a small reading and one homework per week.

The class was interesting and he grades very generously. He will give you points even if you don't have a perfect answer and just refer you to check your answer so you know what you did wrong. The book is impossibly boring, use Google. Lots of assignmentsquizzes but easy stuff. PassNo Pass. Was great to take with hard econ classes for a breather.
Such an easy class. You would have to work harder to fail. Take and get the credit. Only offered passno pass. Good way to get credit done to graduate, and maybe learn something.
I took Prof. Wismer's online FIN240 class. Extremely easy class and was also interesting. Recommended
Interesting class and he is super engaging.

I had Mus'ab for COLT 211 and learned a lot. I appreciated the opportunities for discussion. He's very anti AI use because it is a literature interpretation class. He is adamant that you be specific in your papers, but I didn't find him to be a harsh grader if effort was put in. If you do not want to discuss literature, do not take this class.

**COLT 211-Love this guy. Super caring and passionate, combined with engaging material. Witty, charming, and funny as well. I'm a business major, but for years, I loved English/writing classes, and this was no different. Class was lot of discussion that was fun if you like to talk about the material. Mus'ab will be a wonderful professor one day.
Extremely Paranoid teacher. Believes everyone uses AI. Refuses to change grade even after you prove you did not. Horrible teacher and not understanding at all. Would not recommend.

Professor Salam was very difficult to say the least. I had him for COLT 211, not writing, but he has by far been the hardest professor I have had at UO. He is the toughest grader for writing; he expects you to have proficient knowledge about comparative literature, even if it's your first COLT class. Don't take COLT 211 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice and would definitely take again! And I actually took 211. Just do the readings and you'll do fine. Graded on only a few things, and the instructions for the final was a little unclear, but I asked and he was very nice if I had any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relatively easy grader but instructions for essays were vague, so when points were missed they had an extreme effect on your grade. Nice professor but A LOT of reading for this level of a class (50+ page readings before some classes). Hard to keep up with since this wasn't even a class for my major.
Flexible and accommodating of any outside situations. Very nice teacher, class was engaging as well.

ACTUALLY TOOK 211!!! I really enjoyed this class! The professor is super nice and very accommodating, he would respond to my emails very quickly and answers my questions. Not many assignments were due but there was a lot of reading that sometimes felt a little repetitive. His lecture style is engaging and informative. I would take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher and always had interesting lectures. He did take attendance every class and you could only miss 2 classes before it starts to affect your grade. Essays are graded for completion and there are optional "advanced labor" assignments to do at the end of the year that will boost your grade a lot. Loved his class and his jokes

Ive taken a few courses with Dr. Myers, his lecture are pretty boring and slow. At times his teaching can be a little bit vague and therefore confusing but still manageable. However, he was my lab leader for PSY 303 and he gave a lot of clear and genuine feedback throughout the term which was helpful. His grading is very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I really appreciated that the class had clear structure (the same sorts of assignments due every week). There were lots of articles to read for class but they were relavent to class material and pretty interesting. He is open to feedback, and fair grader, with a straight forward lecturing style.

I have taken multiple classes with Dr. Myers. While his lectures can get a little boring, his grading criteria is very clear and he is easy to contact if you have any questions or want to talk about grad school. He also runs the PSY202 Peer Labs, if you are interested in getting involved with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: psy 439 This professor uses material that hasn't been replicated in other studies, and for good reason.

He does not do any grading and reads right off the slides. I don't think I took notes once for his class. I emailed him about grades multiple times with no answer. You are also required to do notes and inquzitives before the topic is taught in class. If you would like to teach yourself everything for the class then this is where you do it.

I liked this class, as a college class hater that means a lot. He's a nice teacher but his classes can feel a little long and his voice is kinda monotone so don't take this class in the morning but his tests are vocab and applied vocab heavy. i enjoyed taking this class and he's a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: An absolute joke of a professor. He created a hybrid class for Psy 303 and had another professor teach it. Imagine paying hundreds of dollars in tuition per lecture which are only 5-15 minutes a piece. Myers is the epidemy of lazy teaching. Prepare to teach yourself and not to use any of the official material.

I really like Prof Myers so far, he is interesting to listen to and tells some funny stories to lighten up the lectures. There's lots of inquizitives, but you can drop 2. Somewhat lecture heavy but if you're pursuing psychology it's worth it. He seems to want the class to succeed and I think he's great!

Psy 303 is a mostly self directed class, but Dr. Myers was helpful when asked. You are not expected to stay for the whole 80 minutes of class. Expect to rely mostly on the GE if you have questions, as they are doing most of the grading. This class is an easy A if you turn in work on time and respect the critiques given on drafts. Overall good class

Dr. Myers is a really frustrating instructor. He is condescending and dismissive for people who have questions and doesn't teach anything - 90% of every class is "work time" where everyone leaves as soon as they sign attendance. Pretty easy instructor, but if you want ANY help, he will not be useful and will likely make you feel dumb for asking.

I've had this professor previously for 301, and during that class he was more accessible than I find him to be now. He just reads off of the slides and seems frustrated when questions are asked. He can be condescending to confused students.

Dr. Myers made his class a blast with his lively lectures and quirky habits—who else names their pen "Freud Jr."? Beyond the classroom, his knack for deep conversations and wild adventures made our time together unforgettable. If you want a class where you learn and laugh, Dr. Myers is your person. - Jones

Lectures are long & boring, he just reads off the slides. You have to stay until the end due to iClicker. Weekly inquizitives and discussion question you create based on the article that week. Midterm and final are 50 MC questions. Both are easy as long as you read the textbook. One paper that is simple and easy to get an A on.

Lectures are basically just reading off slides from the reading. Attendance is mandatory and he waits until the last minute to do the iclicker question so if you dont stay till the very end you get marked absent. Only had one paper that was easy but the midterm/final are pretty different from the study guide. Probably wouldn't take his class again.

Professor Myers is fine but definitely not my favorite. The class had the opportunity to be super fun and interesting; however, he was very dull and lecture-heavy. His slides often didn't have what was on the tests and he didn't communicate rubrics and expectations very well. He is also a little condescending and passive-aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He teaches things irrelevant to current class topics, then after people try to understand them says they aren't needed on the tests.
I had Myers in evolutionary psychology. It was my favorite class I have taken. You have to read a lot and exams are pretty long. It was a lot of fun though.

Myers is nice but lacks organization. He does not communicate with GEs in how they're supposed to grade your paper. Ie our first research paper was supposed to be in APA7 but the GE graded us in APA6. he often does not properly label due dates on canvas which is confusing. But, if you stay on top of your work you should get a good grade no problem.

Seems like a nice guy as long as you're as passionate about the course as he is and participates. The books are really confusing which makes it easy to lose motivation when reading them. He yells a lot if you don't participate but the material itself is hard to participate in. Lectures are extremely draining. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: VERY passionate about his job. If you don't share the same intense interest in the content it's gonna be difficult to pass. Had 2 books with a fast paced schedule which I found hard to keep up with and he values participation a LOT. Many times he would stop mid class to yell at us for not raising our hands though he made it intimidating to do so.

Good professor. It was an interesting class because of the material. He does make you read a couple of books and other small readings, so it's heavy on that. I ended up not being able to keep up with the amount of reading, so it made it hard to do the midterm and final essay, but it ended up working out. Good class but would not take again..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gets upset when class isn't participating in discussions, but as long as the class is engaged he's great. The reading can get pretty boring, if you stay on top of it and pay attention in class you'll be fine for the essays.

i took 251 because i needed to fulfill a graduation credit, but if i hadn't taken advanced english courses/had experience writing essays and analyzing writing, it would have been a struggle. the reading is boring but doable. there are no tests, just in class discussions. essays are easy if you've done the reading or paid attention in the lectures.

Michael is really good professor, as long as you do the work for the class and participate. The books are quite confusing and it is easy to lose motivation when reading them, but if you reach out to him for help then it can be a bit better. He can get frustrated quite easily, but I think it's only because he's so passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but if you're not going to do the reading, don't do the class. It's a very good class and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Be ready to talk about the reading, it's okay if you're not a big talker, but he does want to know that you did the work. There are no exams, but there is a midterm and a final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is okay but he gets kinda upset easily and kinda talks to the class like they have never read before, but at the same time the books are pretty confusing and hard to stay caught up on if you have lit anything else going on in life. Overall he is nice enough but his lectures are easy to get distracted from. Will question almost anything you say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stern is the best. He cares about his students and the coursework is actually conducive to your learning. He is a great professor and has a lot of knowledge, yet isn't opinionated and still very open to student's views.

I thought for being such a small size, it should be more discussion based. Ironically, it felt that the majority of the time I was listening to Michael lecture a class of majority women on Scandinavian Women Writers. We were blamed for not talking, but I would argue that this reveals that the discussions didn't feel like a safe space for people.

Youuu shall spend lotssss of time reaaadinggg. Take reading notes, seriously. The stories are super crazy fast paced, never boring. Micheal does take some things personally but he is very interested in the subject matter so the lectures are super fantastic and interesting. He welcomes other viewpoints but expects that you can back them up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was clearly set up and expectations were given early. Lectures were meant to promote critical thinking/analysis and any texts that were difficult were usually explained further in class. Professor Stern is a great guy and a good lecturer, and I'd take more of his classes if my schedule allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Michael is a good professor and I think he teaches the material well. He strives for clarity in his lessons and really encourages participation. My problem with Michael is that he can be condescending towards his students, acting personally offended and guilt tripping us (interrupting the lecture) if he THINKS (not knows) we didn't do the readings.

Michael is a kind man, who cares about his students and is accommodating to our struggles. However, his teaching style was not for me. He would often go off on tangents and long, confusing lectures that would leave me bored. That being said, his class is what you make out of it. If you want an A, pay attention, go to office hours. It will pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really appreciates if you attend lectures and stay after class to chat. Very understanding of personal issues and schedules. Gave us the option of an essay or test for the final and never forced anyone to speak up or turn their cameras on if they didn't want to. Took this class 1st term freshman year and it was a great intro to college!

Michael was by far the best prof I've had at UO, he was incredibly caring and considerate of us and our struggles through COVID adjustments. I would absolutely recommend him to anyone that likes intellectual conversations based around lectures. He cares about your participation but doesn't make the class difficult.

A very kind man, but tends to lash out at students for not participating in very verbose and intimidating discussions. Lectures are sometimes convoluted and confusing. Says attendance is not a concern of his but takes it very personally if you do not attend. Always available for office hours, and will schedule outside of them, so take advantage.

Professor Stern was one of the most intellectual and sympathetic professors I've ever had. Everything he said resonated with me and I felt totally engrossed in his lectures. His imbues both practical knowledge and intellectual experience into almost everything he says, and I loved it. Class is relatively easy. 2-page paper every week. Participate!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: There was a lot of reading in this class, but most of the time it would be discussed in-depth in class so really only skimming was necessary. Michael is a great professor who cares about his students and gives great feedback on papers that's actually useful. Attendance is mandatory, but it's doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a really great guy and truly cares about his students. Although there was a 2-page paper due every week, they were film analysis papers and he is a very gracious grader on them and is very lax about due dates . I would definitely recommend him if you're interested in film or are doing a Scandinavian global context like me.

While the class was a little hard to follow sometimes with really long and difficult readings, Michael is a really great professor. He's so nice and genuinely wants to help every student succeed. His lectures can be a little difficult to follow and sometimes boring but if you're struggling he'll put in the effort to help you understand and do well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This professor is by far one of the most memorable at the UO. His influence by Nietzsche's ideas is quite apparent and he uses many references to him during his arguments. I found the class very intriguing as it did not limit you to the textbook but rather set you free to construct your own argument and refute others. Absolutely recommended!!!

Took this film class as a freshman. Never will I take a film class that's in the 300 level again. He doesn't have any midterms.  His final, five essays take home, and four in class. You must know some film terminology. You're allowed a sheet of paper with notes. His discussions are long, boring unfortunately but he's a nice professor.

I took his Scandinavian Text and Interpretation class. From the first day he encouraged us to voice our opinions, but whenever I tried to do so, he would say "you are incorrect" in one way or another. DO NOT SKIP ANY OF HIS CLASSES. He takes it more personally than any other teacher and will grade your papers & blatantly treat you differently.

Michael is a challenging professor however he gets his students through. He cares about his students significantly and is willing to meet his students outside of his office hours if necessary. As for his style he loves using metaphors and leaving room for interpretation. He will give you his opinions but never refute his students views. Great Prof
Very nice and considerate professor. However, his teaching style is very wordy. If you know how to write a papaer and are a fast reader you will Ace this class.

He is a wonderful professor. His grading style truly made me understand the content for the tests and paper. He is extremely well spoken, and sometimes it's hard to follow his theories. However, after a few lectures I was already drawn into the material. Great class!
Awesome!! Great elective class and professor.

I took his class on the Icelandic Sagas, and absolutely loved it. We had to read six sagas over the course of ten weeks, which sounds like a lot but they are quite short and the reading level is not that difficult. Professor Stern really knows a lot about his subject, and lets his passion about it show through during his lectures. Great professor!
Great teacher!! He gets involved with each and every one of his students and is really approachable outside of class.
Awesome Teacher!

One of the most selfobsessed people I've come across since attending the university.  He's one of those professors who in a philosophy/english class no less, seems to think that only his opinions and interpretations ae correct. Likes those brown-nosing kids who come up and talk to him after class, but anyone who doesn't suck up to him gets shunned.

Eh, he's alright. Once you get him out of the classroom, he's very easy going, but in, i found him dull and very difficult to take notes from. He has somewhat unrealistic expectations for the reading, we had to read 5 sagas (two of them quite lengthy, and all five difficult to read in the way it is difficult to read the Bible or the Odyssey)

Wonderful professor!  The class is not easy, but he has a passion for his subject that is incredibly engaging.  He's also more than willing to help you out with anything.  I would HIGHLY recommend this course and this professor!

He's very passionate about his field of knowledge. Watch out signing up for his classes, as they are described as Medieval Studies or English based, but once you get there, it is easy to see that the focal point of study is Philosophy. I enjoyed his class even though I dislike Philosophy, and I am sure anyone interested in this field will love it!

the guy is really intersting, but can talk for hours about stuff that makes no sense. has a great ability to make you feel retarded during his lectures, but he really makes an effort to teach. really good guy, just gotta make sure you keep up with his speed... reaing everything will help a lot, and go to lecture. grading was harder than i expected.
Very helpful teacher, but some of the material goes right over my head. Office hours prove very useful.

Misha is an interesting person. He does not respond to emails well, and his chalkboard notes are often ineligible and resembled chicken scratch. His class will leave you frustrated, not because it's particularly hard; it's the lack of instruction and not sure what he's going on about in class. Prepare to hear about Russia, Ukraine, and Trump.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Half of our class time was spent talking about current events and applying game theory to them, which was cool. No lecture slides, hard to audibly understand, and his minimal notes on the chalk board were often unintelligible or needed extensive explanation that he did not provide. A lot of things on exams weren't covered in class.

Professor Myagkov has a very unique lecture style, and it's definitely not for everyone. Class is discussion based and has a tendency to wander into bigger picture questions and contemporary issues, and notably lacks any slides. But he is very funny, and every discussion felt like I was learning something important. Pop quizzes based on lecture.
That he is very accommodating if you come to class prepared.
Pop quizzes every other week. Not fun.
