reviews.comment: Terrribleeee. Honestly, a waste of time and money. First of all, he ends class like 40 minutes early. Does not have organized lectures or a structure. He simply does not teach. If you don't understand something he assumes that you don't do the readings or listen. One of the worst poli sci classes I've been in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but for sure is just grading off vibes. Participate and ask questions to get on his radar, otherwise you will not get a good grade in his class. Class does not really have a structure and the lectures are kind of all over the place. The class was fun but I feel like I could just as easily have gotten a D instead of an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm sure this class was great for some people, but if you're a visual learner like me, this class might not be for you. There's no visual aid for lecture, it's also probable that zoom made that a bit more difficult. If you put in the work you should be okay, but it was hard for me to stay engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Admittedly his class was online, but most of his in class structure was debate centered and really hard to follow. He isnt specific on required amounts of work for test answers, but he gives them to you in advance so its easier. Super challenging material though, I would have wanted more definitions/explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Misha is a great teacher, but you need to do your part, something I think is pretty important to regard after reading the other ratings below. If you do your homework, don't skip quiz days and study for exams (for which he literally gives you the questions beforehand) the class - even with the tough subject matter - you'll do absolutely fine.

Misha is a very good professor and will give you back as much as you put in. The subject he teaches is hard, and he won't reward you if you are unwilling to be invested and show him that you are trying to learn. He will reward effort if he sees it. People who take his class complain too much. He is smart and knows what he is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His class is unorganized, his quizzes/tests are poorly written, and he is extremely unclear about what he expects to see on assignments. He doesn't follow his own syllabus. Avoid!

I took two of of Misha's classes during the same quarter. He subtly introduces students to the social science behind modern socialist thought, while interpreting current political developments. I and other students found his grading method elusive. Grades felt like they were given almost arbitrarily, as though to satisfy a normal distribution.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great professor, inspired me to major in Political Science through a new perspective. He does give out pop quizzes which is how he manages attendance, so it is important to attend class. However as long as you attend class and complete all assignments you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you want to get an "A", go to class, you will certaintly gat an "A" with no doubts.

Professor Myagkov explains everything fairly well, but he doesn't have any slides or anything, you so must come to class and take notes to pass. He also doesn't tell when quizzes are, and attendance are part of your grade, so it's better in the long run to go to class. It's a fairly bland subject.
Best professor at UO. Extremely intelligent and very easygoing.. He makes going to class fun, you forget that you're learning when you listen to him talk. Highly recommended.
Excellent
VERY HELPFUL PROFESSOR I WANT TO TAKE ALL MY CLASSES WITH HIM. HE IS A SMART MAN
I'm pretty surprised at how many people dislike Misha. I've found him to be funny, clear, informative, interesting, and rocks an awesome Russian accent!
completely worthless class and teacher... waste of time.
Very funny stories.

taken multiple short classes. very easy, seem like good little windows for getting exposed to more of the 'science' and math part of PS. after taking several of his classes i can mimic his Russian accent pretty good.
awesome
Brilliant- but poor teacher

I actually learned quite a bit from Misha. And with respect to not learning anything from him, as the rater prior to this posting had mentioned, it all depends on much you put into it. If you are a passive learner then you probably won't learn much. But in my experience, I paid attention, and learned a lot.
He doesn't care about students or teaching and isn't teaching us anything.  Panders to students by grading really easy.  Should only be teaching lower division classes.
No Comments
No Comments

I don't know what all these other people are talking about. Misha was a great instructor and I acquired a lot of knowledge from him. Maybe the course topic was a little over the heads of some of these raters who rated him poorly.
He is easy going, and full of crazy stories. The classes are fairly easy if you pay attention. I never found him **** and in when I see him around town he comes up and talks
Misha is a **** pig and I'm not even a feminazi! He believes that women should be seen, not heard.

This was a very difficult class. The theories presented seem hard, especially when he is trying to explain it. Take notes and you will do great. I got an A+ in 2 of his most difficult classes and I am still clueless on subject matter covered!
need a boost in your gpa?  suffer thru this course!
politics of everyday life? i didn't see any life in this course - the theory was dull and does not speak to my personel experiences

Mafia in Russia...sounds interesting, right?  It is, except not when everything is looked at in political science terms.  Weekly quizzes that cover basically any news story that is covered anywhere in the world, ever, killed my grade.  Nice guy, thoug
this guy may be a gnome-like russian, but if you can write a coherent paper and aren't a stupid sorostitute you'll do fine.
He really sucks...don't think of taking a class with him!
He is very knowledgable of the given subject matter, however, he is a tough grader and does not explain why you receive a given grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is very good at teaching ethics. Class consisted of lecturediscussion. He has a  quiz on the readings every 2 weeks, lowest score gets dropped. There is quite a bit of reading for this class. There is a midterm paper and a final paper, he didn't seem to have graded too harsh as long as he could tell you read the material and had a good thesis.
Good guy, he's a GTF at this time, but I see no problems.  He makes sure we know what's coming; what more can you ask for?  Class runs mostly on pdfs. one short novel.
he is very knowledgeable and really gets you thinking about the ethics behind environmental issues. He is also very helpful on making sure you understand everything
Extremely knowledgeable. He loves this topic and is very helpful. This class required a lot of reading and he is a tough grader of the assigned essays.

Dr. Myers was really great! We read Twelfth Night, and she made each lecture interesting and informative. She cared about our success and worked to answer any questions we had about the text or assignments. Since the class was on Zoom, we also got to see her cat sometimes :-) would recommend taking a class with her
Average class

Confusing directions on almost every single assignment. Laughs at your questions in Office Hours. Says a lot without saying anything at all. I haven't learned anything from this class, and am disappointed that I took it. No lectures in this class which I thought would be nice, but instead I'm always confused.
Easy class. Graded on completion.
super sassy, when you ask question she makes you feel stupid...

We spent the first week just getting to know each other and that made doing group projects and individual presentations MUCH easier. I'm super shy and her class never made me nervous. She lets you pick course paths which guarantee your final grade as an A,B,C as long as you do the work. You can always re-do stuff too. The best writing class ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was pretty mediocre. She has "course paths" and depending on which one you choose you get a different grade. The result is that she doesn't grade your work she just checks to make sure it fulfills the requirements. A lot of the assignments seemed monotonous, and generally designed to waste your time. Don't bother getting assigned readings.
I would not recommend this class to anyone. Her lectures are hard to listen to because they are so boring. Her assignments rarely make sense. I didn't learn anything except that I hate writing.

I was afraid of taking the course with Dr. Myers because of the reviews on here, but I realized that she is a great caring professor upon taking. She gives good feedback (feedback relevant to your papers), and it is not like most professors who provide general feedback. One thing is sure; you will learn a lot.

Took WR123 expecting it to be straight forward, which it sorta was. You choose "paths" that correspond to the grade you will receive at the end. I chose the A path but it came with A LOT of (boring) work & she never really tells you if you're on track. Feedback isn't helpful... she doesn't post on Canvas so I found my grade out from my transcript.

Kate's WR123 class was so boring and hard to sit through. Her final research paper was hard and didn't really make sense. However, you do decide what your grade is so it is easy to get an A or B. Go to her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Was registered for an online class in the summer and she gave out so much work! She wanted you to log all of your readings and time with the material.

She is a horrible teacher and gives Cs for almost every assignment. Very tough grader. The smallest mistake will give you a C. The mean for very assignment is a C and very few people can get a grade above that. I would never have taken her if I knew. She doesn't provided good feedback if she provides any at all. Take anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a harsh grader, meeting all expectations gets you a C. However, you learn a lot about how to interpret and break down passages with ease. She has a story behind everything. Very tough class but very rewarding when you do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very demeaning teacher, and not flexible at all. I would never take a class from her again. Class is dry, and each essay has an overwhelming number of required criteria. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Kate is the best writing instructor for Gen ed required courses. You will will, but if you go and ask questions in office hrs you won't be sorry. I just finished this course in Aug after a10 yr break in school. She cares and is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Class tad dry at times, but not really the instructor, more the students and subj. matter.  Get help out of class, many missed opportunities if not.  She breaks the material down simple (1 on 1) and is clear on expectations.  Lots of revising the same essay to improve your writing/grade.  Fair policy if you make an effort.
Rude. Boring. Demeaning. Very exacting and expects things to be done in a convoluted fashion. Class isn't very informative, and quite frankly boring.

Often singles students out for no reason. Didn't know "economically" was a word. A student looked it up on their phone, and they were chastised for it. Her grading policy makes no sense, papers arent graded on content, rather on "how much revision was done" papers given a B for example, might be downgraded to a C, due to the ludicrous prior reason

Kate is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I went into this class thinking that it was going to be horrible, but Kate made it worth my time. She has helped me so much with my writing and I am now much more confident in my writing skills because of her. She is always willing to help you too. Definitely worth taking her class.

She is a wonderful woman who is very helfpul and dedicated to her work. If you take the time to go and see her, she gives great help and it is easier to do well. Keep an open mind going into this class. Do not think it's going to be easy because it is not simple, but Kate tries to keep it easy.
Somewhat helpful outside of class, if you can make the time for an appointment. Otherwise, she isn't helpful in the classroom environment. Bad at starting discussions... bad jokes too.

Chang was awkward speaking in front of the class and always passed out the attendance sheet half way through or in the  beginning of class so everyone left. Tests were difficult. Doesn't provide practice exams nor gives answers after quizzes. Take the course if you need to, just with someone else.

He is a very boring lecturer. He takes attendance, but after the attendance sheet is passed around, many students sprint to the door.  He doesn't give a clear study guide for the exams like the other teachers for BA 215 so either sign up for another section or find a buddy in another class with a helpful teacher and use their notes to study.

He reads straight from printed pages of notes. He does not seem to care about the student's nor how to keep students interested in class. The lectures are really long and boring, it's hard to keep focus and pay attention. He also does not give study guides, so be prepared to know everything comfortable. I would never recommend him as a teacher.

I did not enjoy this class. You never knew where your grade stood because everyone fails the quizzes and he always has to curve them. Quiz questions are worded very strangely. He is knowledgeable of the subject, so you kind of have to be too to get an A. If you just need this class as a science requirement, take something else.

Expect to work hard in the class, if you do, you will learn a lot. He explains concepts very well and expectations are clear. Tests mostly cover information from lecture. He can be intimidating, but really is nice. He let us retake every test and would record the best score. He also curves if the class doesn't do well.
Good teaching skills.  Engaging to listen too, with excellent PP slides.

Amazing prof. 2 online quizzes week 3 and 8, 1 midterm and a final. Attendance required for labs, or can't get credit, but labs are a lot of fun. Memorizing is key but you are hands on with primate skulls or bones each lab. Lab works midterm and final worth 30% each, but posts notes and final not cumulative. Fun and tries to make lectures fun.
Do not take this class if you don't want your entire grade dependent on the 2 tests you take

Thoroughly enjoyed the lectures as you need to go since posted slides leave out lots of detail. They were very engaging and entertaining and was the favorite part of the class for me. Midterm and final are heavily weighted with the final being much harder. Labs were enjoyable as well.

This class is very dependent on the mid-term and final grade. The second semester final is much harder than the mid-term. Almost all lecture material is on the tests and there is no reading in class or much outside of class work besides labs. I really enjoyed Ting's lectures and the material and learned a lot about anthropology.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The final grade is heavily dependent on how the midterm and final go. I feel that they grade pretty harsh since it's an online class. Tests were essay based. The content is honestly pretty interesting and his lectures are engaging. Overall a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my second time taking one of his course, I took 172 my freshman year and really enjoyed it now just wrapping up 472/572 I have never been more happy with how a class has turned out. it wont let me put my course but it was 20-30 people rather then the huge lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He makes lectures really fun and interesting. In his online class they were split up in 4-5 sections each week, which made the work load a lot more digestable. Class is made up of weekly quizzes based on lectures, a few simple discussion posts, two simple lab assignments, and a midterm and final, both of which were straight forward.
Considering this was an asynchronous class it was very engaging and interesting. He's very funny and you can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Took him for Monkeys and Apes my freshman year. The class is information heavy and definitely not super easy but damn is it fun and interesting to learn. You can tell Professor Ting is passionate about the subject and he makes it fun to learn.

Great professor, exams rely alot on his lectures but he's funny,passionate,and fair He posts slides and online lectures so everyone has the same access Grading criteria is very clear so there is no extra credit but will curve exams, exams are easy to pass if you study and rely on online lectures instead of just the slides bc he includes all info

I took Intro to Monkeys and Apes with Dr. Ting and it was one of my favorite classes ever. The tests definitely aren't easy, but if you put in the work you can see clear results. All of the readings come from free online sources and his lectures are really clear and detailed. I highly recommend ANTH 171 for freshman in need of a science credit.

Very heavy lectures, must go to class, the labs were very easy and were 40% of your grade if you go and pay attention you'll succeed in this class, he always covers topics throughly. I came into this class scared from the other reviews but it can seem like a lot, im currently at a 89.5 but could be rounded up

Fairly tough class with a lot of information tested on, but if you study hard you'll do fine. Take notes on the lecture because that's all he tests on, and complete the labs for a large portion of your grade. The labs are pretty much graded by completion. Super cool class, but it's not just watching videos about primates.

I really enjoyed Introduction to Monkeys and Apes with Dr. Ting! He provides great lectures, and this year he uploaded online lectures so if you had to miss class for any reason you weren't totally screwed. He provided fun videos and seemed really passionate about the topic. The labs were a bit boring though and almost pointless in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ting makes class very interesting, especially the videos about the monkeys and apes (highlight of my term tbh), but the class is very lecture heavy. I did find that my notes were very helpful for studying, but your grade is basically just the midterm and the final. Luckily, the labs were graded on completion.

I was in his Monkeys and Apes class and loved it! Very interesting course, hes very organized although the lectures are a little long. The tests are a little difficult but if you go to lectures or read the notes on canvas youll be fine.

Professor Ting makes class super fun. I took it online this term, and I had to take this class for a FIG. It's mostly lectures and then quizzes, and a couple of discussion board posts. He doesn't give a midterm or final. The class was fast paced and interesting.

Dr. Ting does an amazing job teaching ANTH 171. The lectures are interesting and the videos are fun to watch. ANTH 171 is heavy on memorization so flashcards help. It is not a class you can cram for when it comes to the midterm and final. But overall a very fun course!

I just took this class for my science GE but Nelson really I think made this class more interesting than I expected. So much easier to just go to the lectures and pay attention than not go and rely on slides - your test grades will thank you for it. He paces out the class well and is a kind person. Not as hard as a class than I thought.
My favorite professor and class so far. Professor Ting is funny and knows what he is talking about. A really good mix of lecture and video helped me learn the material.

Four words: Get ready to memorize. I actually really enjoyed this class. I took it for a science gen ed and wasnt really expecting to like it but it was actually really cool. It is a lot of memorization of different types and characteristics of primates but Prof Ting is really willing to help and so are the GTFs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures were informative, but definitely a hard class. Studying is required in order to pass the midterm and final.  Would not recommend if your are not interested in monkeys or apes.

Definitely one of the hardest I have ever taken in all my years of schooling. The amount of detail you have to know for this class is INSANE, literally impossible to study for the midterms and finals because there is SO much to study! Only reason I passed is because he curved final grades and I went up to a C-. Hardest class ever!!!!

I thought this class was easy until I took the final. He emailed us and said the mean for the final was a whopping 59%. The mean for the entire class was a 73%. If you don't want a c do not take this class. He ended up curving it a +- letter grade solely because everyone failed the final. This anthro class is by far the worst and hardest one /

He is an ok teacher. The class is interesting but it is very fast-paced with a lot to learn. If you are willing to put in the effort, you will do well. The videos he uses are interesting and help make the lectures less boring. If you are interested in primates and are willing to work, go for it. You will have to memorize a lot of info.

Ting uses videos in order for students to learn the material, however he goes way to fast in lecture and it is hard to keep up with him. It is a lot of material being thrown at you and he expects you to know it all. During lecture he uses the world "um" constantly while lecturing. He is a nice guy, but it would be nice if he slowed down.

Awesome professor. Enjoyed lectures when I went to them. Included supplemental videos that were hilarious and helped students learn material. Very clear on grading and instructions. I recommend taking a class of his.
Great professor, explains the material really well. Work hard and you will get a good grade.
The professor doesn't make the subject matter interesting, he uses dull information and overcomplicated concepts to describe easy and fun topics.

This professor has to be the worst professor I've had here at the UO. He's extremely boring, and loves to overcomplicate simple concepts. I was ecstatic to take this class when I signed up, I was severely disappointed in his class. I resorted to teaching myself the martial to avoid having to hear him "lecture". I do NOT recommend taking him.

Great teacher but I think one of the reasons why he was so good was because he had an awesome GTF. They worked very well together in making the students understand the material and truth be told, there is no reason to not do well in the class. There's a lot of room for redemption if you mess up and section is cake. 30% of your overall grade.

Very difficult class w/ a fast pace, lots of material covered. Don't take if u won't have time to put in requisite work outside of class! I learned A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Nemirovskaya is very kind and has a strong passion for math, but I felt like she suffers from "expert blind spot". She realizes that her pace is too fast and will slow down for 5 minutes, but then immediately speed-up. BEWARE OF EXTREMELY HARSH GRADING! Discrete 2 homework is v. challenging, but she does use good examples. Use Office hours!!!

Seems like a great person, but she is very difficult as a professor. This was a 2 credit lab class, yet it took more time than any of my other courses. Her grading on homework is very difficult, and there is a lot of it; expect a ton of homework. The class spiked in difficulty halfway through the semester and she went over material extremely fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 2 credit math lab that required more time per week than any 4 credit class. Homework were to be graded on "completeness and effort", yet when I'd spend 2-3 hours on five questions I would get 60-70%'s. Rude, took weeks to grade small assignments, puts down students in class, do not take. She is smart but one of the worst math teachers I've had.

Sweet person but I would avoid her as a lecturer. Her accent/handwriting made it difficult to understand the course content. Retook the class with a different prof. and did just fine. LOTS of homework. Might just be me but she was too intimidating for me to ask for help when I was struggling. She is pretty lax with midterm/final grades though.

A sweet person, but a terrible professor. No final review or practice exam, and same thing for the midterms. Provides very little examples for new material, and then assigns homework with 20-30 questions all much harder than what was in class. Accent isn't an issue, however the speed at which she lectures and assumes everyone understands is insane.

Felt daunted taking the advanced option for Calc I as a freshman; this professor helped me reach a high level of understanding in a subject I knew nothing about and struck me as an absolute saint. Very "old school" feel to the class but she was kind and helpful, gave us a chance to recover our grades by doing well on the final. Terrifyingly smart.

Felt daunted taking the "advanced" option for Calc I as a freshman; this professor helped me reach a high level of understanding in a subject I knew nothing about and struck me as an absolute saint. Very "old school" feel to the class but she was kind and helpful, gave us a chance to recover our grades by doing well on the final. Terrifyingly smart

Went through things very quickly and without much background info/"whys". Had no idea there were even integration rules until I looked into it myself. There was a lot of weekly hw that required many, many hours to do, but she was always willing to give the class an extra day to complete it if we needed.
Homework questions were a good mix of difficulty, and more challenging ones were fun and graded for completion. she lets you write on the chalkboard :D

This prof is super cool outside of class and runs a children's math festival. I had taken this class in high school with a C so I dropped it and took it in college. I think it was reasonably paced and I had an enjoyable time getting to know this prof.

Prof. Nemirovskaya is one of the more challenging Profs. Accent is not an issue at all. Material is sped through at times, and there is lots of HW's/Exams. Time is given in class to ask questions regarding both however. HW is not difficult, however it often does not reflect the type of questions asked during Quizzes/Exams. No note-cards allowed :(

Her quizzes are just like the homework, so as long as you can finish the homework on your own the quizzes will be a piece of cake.

reviews.comment: If you have not taken Calculus in high school prepare to be confused. She jumps right into things, skipping beginning steps. Homework is hard and there is a lot of it. Not that helpful, but very nice.

Awesome professor. She is very clear and helpful. Not sure why other people think so, but her accent is not that thick and she is easy to understand and more than willing to repeat herself. She has given me a solid understanding of calculus. Would definitely recommend.

She is not clear at all and doesn't post your grades anywhere. Goes at a very fast and unorganized pace. I would not recommend her. Her russian accent is also pretty annoying. Had to make it a pass or fail.
Hard to understand, assumes your from Russia and have already taken calculus.

I have generally always had a good sense for math. Until this class! I passed 111 my first try with a B. I took this 106 in order to try and get a high grade and boost my GPA. That isnt happening. She is so confusing and so "ADD like" during lecture that its hard to see what shes trying do. Ive never had this much trouble in a math class ever.
Very sweet, understanding. I feel very prepared for Math 111

Very passionate teacher. It is agreed that her accent is heavy, but she is always happy to repeat herself. She teaches hard classes and I think people blame her instead of the material. She's fair with her curve (50% usually passes you in the discrete series) only complaint is she is heavy on proofs- But take that as it is.
OMG!She is 100% comfusing me with math!!Russian accent is OK for me, because I am not a natural speaker either! But the relation between HW and Quiz or Exam is kind of make me feel sick!

Does have a Russian accent, makes it a little difficult at times.  Class wasn't as bad as other people have said on here, so I guess she's gotten better as a teacher.  When she gives examples, the reasons why she is doing things can be vague.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She's terrible. Can't understand a single thing she says because her accent is so thick. She doesn't answer questions, doesn't make herself clear, and spends too much time on easy examples during class. I would highly recommend not taking this class.
Has a very thick accent and is hard to keep up with in class. A little better in office hours, but not by much. If you're Russian, you might do very well, otherwise, you'd better be a math genius.

Simply horrendous, she is an awful teacher and you can't understand a word she says. She understands the material, but can't seem to relay the concepts to the class. I would avoid her at ALL COSTS. The only reason I am getting an A in the class is because I have a fantastic GTF. For the Love of God, stay away from her class. She is a BAD teacher.
Hard to understand. Overall bad experience.

I took J302* It's obvious prof. Newell cares about his students and lecture material, but he talks extremely slow and monotone, which is awful when learning something like law in a 2-hour lecture. Regardless, there are many opportunities for extra credit and you will succeed if you keep up with the work.

You can tell this professor really wants you to succeed. There are plenty of opportunities for EC, and the weekly assignments are easy. The late policy is extremely flexible as well and everything was super straight forward. This was probably one of the best professors at UO, but beware the GEs. The don't give much feedback/respond sadly.

This is the J385 professor you want. The class is not always the most interesting or fun, but it has some good information and Bryce does it the best. Advisors will also tell you this. Weekly quizzes are open note. Final exam seems to be a rehash of those. Reading annotation takes about an hour per week. 2 papers scattered throughout the term. 9/10

She is constantly making stupid errors in her lectures that make it difficult to learn the material. Her tests even had multiple errors that she had to correct-after I spent 20 min. confused at how to find the volume of a 2D figure.

She was a great teacher. I am terrified of math, but after taking her class I'm more confident and feel prepared for MATH 111. If you have to take MATH 095 or are worried about math in general, take MATH 095 from her. She's super clear, gives great example. Attend all classes and pay attention and you'll get an A.

I really liked Tammy for a math teacher. Yes, she does make the quizzes harder than you would expect but she only does that to prepare you for the exams. I failed the first three quizzes but ended up with a 95% in the class. As long as you go to class and go to office hours when you dont understand something, you will do great! I loved her teaching

She has been my favorite math teacher so far. Extremely helpful outside of class. Yes, tests and quizzes are harder than the in class examples but they use concepts she did present. She's just seeing if you can apply them. Passed the class and wished she taught calculus so I could have her again.

So far from what I read, people don't think she's a good teacher.I on the other hand dissagree. She has told us she hated math for a long time and that it is possible to enjoy it. I I felt it was honest and I didn't feel dumb for asking questions. Whenever I didn't understand something she was quick to break it down for me.

Absolutely horrible!  Worst teacher I've ever had. I did everything in the class-attended every single lecture/discussion, 100% on all quizzes and homework, but when I got the tests, I was so lost. She tested us on material harder than any examples we ever went over. There's also a huge project due at the end of term on top everything else!

Horrible! Believes a 50% is a good score!!! Voice is screechy, almost like nails on a chalkboard! Doesn't understand math, has to go off notes the entire class!!!! Complains a lot. Contradicts herself, and not very clear. You are basically going to fail if in this class.

She is a very annoying teacher. Her voice kind of makes me want to never go to class. She is decent and explaining concepts, but prides herself of failing everyone which to me shows there something wrong w/ her teaching. Her tests are prett hard, but more than that it is hard to know what she is asking for. Doable class, but why would you want to?

She is absolutely terrible. I think she is good at explaining the concepts, but doesn't know how to test, hold realistic expectations, provide adequate help outside of class, etc. One of the worst teachers I've ever had.
She is inexperienced and needs to figure out how to do the math before she comes to class.  Not to mention how to teach it!

Easy but having this class 4 days a week really takes its toll on you. The lectures, the jokes, and the "mini" quizzes get old after a while. The room is usually a comfortable 98 degrees and it feels like a dungeon.

If you want to hear "Let's kick it up a notch" or some variation thereof at least 10 times in one class period, Tammy is your gal. Also, fans of nasally mouth-breathers should definitely take this class. She is one of the best! At the end of the day, she isn't the WORST teacher in the world, but she's pretty darn annoying.
No Comments
Awful, just awful.  The funny (sad) thing is that she wants to become a teacher.

Ngo is very kind and gives great lectures. Coursework is easy and the exams are rewarding if you keep up with content. She encourages lots of discussion and conducts the class discussions well. The guest lectures are also refreshing!
Professor Ngo is super passionate about her curriculum and genuinely wants everyone to learn and succeed. Studying is definitely required for this class though.

Professor Ngo is a great teacher who keeps class interesting and applicable to the modern world. She always connects concepts back to real-world stories and news. Assignments and tests are medium in difficulty but are graded fairly.
Dr ngo is an awesome professor who helps her students excel in class. Easily approachable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors of all time. She is accessible outside of class and really does care about her students. Although the lectures can sometimes be boring, I still learned a lot from them.

Professor Ngo is awesome! I cried twice in the lectures; they are deeply engaging. She builds in discussions in to them so you are constantly discussing and interacting with the people around you. A very lenient late policy, I had a tough term and turned in two big assignments quite late and still got through with a B+

I have taken 3 of her classes, and she is one of my favorite professors. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The classes can be difficult because there are a lot of slides to go through. But as long as you pay attention and try your hardest, you'll be good. I highly recommend her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nicole is very clearly invested in making her classes engaging, inclusive, and participative. Some of the guests she brought in were also very knowledgeable and interesting to hear from.

Professor Ngo is knowledgeable, caring, and a clear and concise educator. I took Sustainable Economic Global Development with her, and she was easily reachable, communicative, and a fair grader. I learned a lot, both from the lectures and from the readings. Nothing was too unnecessarily complicated, and I recommend her as a professor.

Has weekly quizzes on the readings before class. If that's your jam, you'll love her. She's cheerful, enthusiastic about the subject matter, and provides lots of guest lectures from local groups with volunteer and internship opportunities.

Very kind and respectful person. She was very considerate of everyone and really cared about our class engaging with the content and not only learning but being able to apply it. There were 2 short quizzes a week that covered the readings and 2 exams that weren't very difficult and really reflected what was discussed in class. Plus a group project.

Professor Ngo was awesome! This class was genuinely interesting, and all of the assignments were also interesting (and there were not many of them, and I think she graded fairly easy). This class seemed like a well-oiled machine, there was at no point that I felt that Professor Ngo didn't have a clear plan. Will be taking future classes by her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: (PPPM 370) I really appreciated how she attempted to learn everyones name in her lecture class, something many professors don't do. This class was a nice switch away from other PPPM material, and I thoroughly enjoyed her and her class. Decent amount of reading, but that is every PPPM class. Would strongly recommend Nicole.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: WOW. Prof Ngo is great. Her class is interesting and more relevant than any other course amidst a pandemic. I would recommend this class to anyone interested in public health.

Someone said it already- brutal grader. She does care for students, super kind. However, lectures can be super boring if you're not interested in public health because of the way she teaches. We go through a million slides per class. She tries her best but sometimes that's not enough... :/

Super great teacher, nice and comfortable to talk to! the lectures are fast but EASY to follow. directly connected to the book. Good textbook too, an interesting read. Very economically focused, but super interesting and you learn a lot about sustainability around the world. funny teacher and would LOVE to take another class from her again!

Prof Ngo is very nice and says she wants you to succeed, but her teaching style in confusing, to say the least, and she is brutal in her grading. Be prepared to constantly follow up with her for clarification on everything. She will also test on things not covered in class.

I have no doubts as to the qualifications of this professor, however, she is a terrible lecturer and will constantly interrupt herself mid-sentence, making for confusing and unclear lectures, doesn't provide good examples, and will change her evaluation criteria on you.

I'm not really sure why Professor Ngo has any bad reviews. she is very caring and gives you lots of feedback on your papers. she always open to look over a rough draft, and give you good feedback so you get a good grade. she cares about how well you do in her class, which is refreshing. i recommend this class and her as a teacher.
Course is easy. This was her first time teaching so think her flow will improve over the years. Nicole is very responsive and gives feedback. Don't go over her page limits.

Prof Ngo is very helpful and answers all questions to the best of her ability.  Unfortunately her lectures are bad.  She reads word-for-word from power point slides.  Her slides often had typos which seemed to really trip her up.  The flow was choppy and hard to follow.
Each class had at least 70 slides and attendance is mandatory which made it hell but the work is easy if you give it a good effort. There is a lot of coursework but very easy.
Attendance was mandatory - you had to attend and listen to her read off of a power point every single class. The student presentations were much better than hers.

Often seemed unprepared. Often started lectures with tangents and wasted so much time with several passes to erase the blackboards, then ran out of time for the course material. Often illegible writing on boards and in presentation notes. Didn't learn much from lectures, so the awesome TAs are why I got an A in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for PHYS290. I had her for PHYS252 and it was a trainwreck, she feels like a different teacher in 290. Lectures are amazing and the labs are actually very fun. She is learning but it feels like she is in her element teaching labs. We made a mini railgun in lab.

This class was disorganized and she rarely covered material effectively. She is new but she is also completely unprepared, so you must rely on TAs, YouTube, and AI to learn anything. She doesn't actually know/understand the difficulty of the content, so exams are excruciating, though passing is easy if you do the work. You just won't learn much :/

She is new and is obviously learning how to teach. People tend to dislike because the class was hard, but much of it is not her fault. Her lectures aren't the best, she tends to read out of book, but if you pay attention you can learn the content you need for the class. I would have preferred a more seasoned professor, but she did fine.
Very nice person, very smart, but not great at teaching.

This class was co-taught with Prof Majewski, who is way better than Kayla. She has no idea how to explain concepts clearly and succinctly, doesn't know the material, and has so many technical issues. Get ready for lots of questions, her math mistakes, and "um..., ok, wait no...". She's nice but I wouldn't have passed without Prof. Majewski.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly people need to grow up.. This is a CS class it's not going to be a free A. But all projects are entirely graded by automatic tests so there's no reason to get less than 100% in that category, and there's a full 5% free extra credit. Make sure you remember your calculus and you will do fine, tests are quite easy and he allows notes.

Realized way too late that a lot of the things in the lectures aren't even tested. Class is pretty tough, don't get discouraged when you don't comprehend something because the tests aren't as tough as the HWs and lectures, just don't fall behind.

I understand some of the other lower ratings but taking him for ML was pretty good.The class is obviously difficult as there are whole degrees on just specific topics within this field but he did a good job of only holding us accountable for general stuff.Projects were fun and not graded to harshly. Always available, does rely on TA's a lot though.

The homework covers difficult concepts, but overall is manageable and the grading is not too harsh. The course had great extra credit opportunities and the professor took his time explaining concepts during office hours. He was also very quick to respond to emails.

I am surprised Thien has such low ratings! His lectures are sometimes hard to follow, for sure, but he is always willing to provide clarification and clear feedback on assignments. He's brilliant AF and knows his stuff, just gets lost in the weeds sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Nguyen is a very intelligent person who I do believe cares about his students, but a woefully inept professor. Going to lecture was a total waste of time, any learning in the class was done online or with fellow classmates or in the lab which wasn't awful but not fantastic. Stay away at all costs.

Lectures were incredibly disorganized. The labs weren't graded until literally after the final grade was due. The tests only had a few questions, so even just getting one question wrong can plummet your grade. Avoid this teacher.

Thien cared about learning, he wasn't the best at explaining through his lectures, handwriting was illegible and he would write on the slides with no structure which was hard to follow. He was genuinely doing his best though and wanted everyone to do well. If you're proactive and do the readings you'll be fine. Be prepared to learn on your own.

Thien was a great professor with good intentions for his students. He constantly made sure that we were asking questions before moving on to the next material. Jared was a fantastic GE and clarified many ideas covered in lecture and helped me debug my code multiple times. His lectures, though, were very scattered and seemed to have no structure
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: See the recent comments- I agree with them. It's also fair to mention this: It was not until the last hour until the class Canvas page disappeared that he actually put in the proper grade weights for the grades, so I didn't really know until it was all over. The GE is horrible, it wasn't until the last day that the grades for 3 lab assn's came in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Nguyen is a very difficult professor. The class I took with him was plagued with inconsistency and frustration. He is difficult to understand during class and quickly strays off topic. He is very hard to reach outside of lectures. His lectures are very dry and have little to do with course material. Very behind. The GE was also terrible.

He constantly shows up late to lectures, runs over the assigned class time, and forgets to record lectures. Lectures are scatterbrained and always left me more confused than learning the material on my own. Written assignments and programming projects are graded slowly (3-6 week delay) so it's impossible to know how well you are doing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my worst college course experiences. He is impossible to reach outside of lecture, his lectures are thorough but can often be confusing. I received feedback for 2 assignments at the start of this term and then it was 5 weeks of flying blind because I didn't know if I did previous assignments right or not. Student requests go unheard too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 1. He is a very good researcher and his lectures are quite good 2, he is never accessible outside class 3, He was never found in his office during the office hours 4. disoriented class 5. there was no textbook for this class, it's hard to study from his unclear/errored/ concise powerpoint slides for the tests 6. doesnt care for students

I've never met such a rude and condescending teacher. He doesn't offer extra credit, yet he's a really tough grader. He has tiny handwriting and you can't tell any of his numbers apart from each other. He seems to get a power trip out of his job honestly. Your job as a teacher is to teach and help your students.

Mr. Nguyen was such a good professor… I know he gets lots of bad reviews but honestly those people just didn't have the relationship that we had. I loved going to his office hours and all the help he gave me one on one. Just ask! Would take again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super helpful outside of class and quick to respond.

While Dennis is generally a nice dude, this was the worst class I have ever taken. Dennis did not lecture at all and instead handed out homework packets and told us to figure them out. He is very soft spoken which doesn't help when trying to get help with the work. He also introduced new topics on exams which was ridiculous.

Dennis is very clearly a graduate student. I had him as professor for math 101 which you would think would be actually a super easy class... it was not easy. Most students stopped going to his class, including me. I would not take his classes again as he never actually taught anything to my class and only gave us packets with no lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: In my experience, Dennis was a great teacher. He is still a graduate student, so if you're looking for someone who is experienced and can explain everything easy peasy then you might want to look elsewhere. Show up to class, take notes, and ask questions because the tests and exams can be difficult. Work with others! and don't procrastinate!!!

As someone who has always struggled with math, I did have to put a lot of effort into studying for the 106 course. However, Dennis is always willing to help in class, office hours or over email if you are confused. While the course was test heavy, the notes we completed in class were very helpful for studying and creating a good note sheet.

The only reason I passed this class was because of tutoring  I learned literally nothing in this class, and the professor is inaccessible and just generally a terrible teacher. All he does is read his notes and he never explains anything in detail. I would urge anyone who needs to take this class to take a different one.

One of the worst math teachers I've ever had. He just goes through the list of problems in the lecture notes and solves them with no explanation. You pretty much have to figure everything out on your own, and his office hours are very unhelpful. He also draws graphs and writes equations with his trackpad so they're basically illegible.

The worst professor Ive ever had. Even if you go to class and take all the notes there is no telling if you will pass or not. He make the class way harder than needed and I would not recommend anyone taking this course with this professor. I wish I knew before taking the class how honestly awful it would be. WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD

Even during lectures it was really confusing. He skips many steps in teaching and just does the work to the point where we reach to the answer of the questions and tells you to solve it on your own. Makes it harder as there were too much homework and worksheets that he didnt even teach us how to do. Yea save yourself.

Get ready to, cry and have a ton of homework. Along with being extremely confused. Rarely references the textbook though it was helpful and made more sense than he did. Have study groups and go to office hours for help. He tends to have to curve basically everything because he can't teach.

If you can avoid taking a class taught by him, please do. He's a horrible Professor and I promise you you won't learn anything from his lectures. This class relies heavily on your ability to find tutoring groups and teach yourself.

Lectures were very hard to follow with a lot of the material not being covered in the homework. More time was spend teaching myself the material and crying while doing the homework. He acknowledges that he makes the quizzes too hard and makes multiple errors on the quizzes.

Lectures were not helpful towards homework or quizzes. Quizzes were assigned every Monday before learning the material and heavily influence your grade. If you take this class I highly recommend connecting with tutoring resources at UO. You will not pass this class without help from online resources or study groups.

A majority of tests and homework assignments contained numerous errors (such as not having the right answer as a choice on a multiple-choice question). Lectures were confusing and often didn't cover the content needed to complete the homework. Ended up using a lot of outside internet resources to teach myself.

His lectures were so hard to follow and quizzes were pretty tough. The majority of our homework was webwork and the quizzes nor the written homework were similar to those questions. Was accessible outside of class though and is good about responding to emails.
Makes you want to cry every time you see the tests/quizzes. Has admitted to making quizzes too difficult. Has you record doing final, isn't nice with late work.
Hard to understand. Questions in homework aren't specific. Will help if you attend office hours, but still very unclear of what is needed. Quizzes are due before homework that covers quiz content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I'm an accounting major and this was my favorite class I've taken at UO! This course was very interesting and also incredibly relevant. He was very neutral allowing all students to feel comfortable sharing their opinions/perspectives.The overall course load is very light with two green book exams. Could not recommend this class and prof enough!

I took his class before the pandemic during Fall of 2019, he was an amazing professor who really appreciated his students! I walked into his class as a Human Physiology major and now I am minoring in Ethics. Really amazing class!

I came into the class from a purely STEM-based background. Nicolae Morar, however, had a deeply fascinating class that held my attention, changed my opinions, and gave me an edge when discussing medical issues. Extra credit is available, expect a ton of reading, really fun though sometimes morbid. Just do what's asked of you and you'll get an A.

Class turned out to be amazing for me and I'm now minoring in ethics! Great professor, he cares and does anything that he can to help. Lectures are LONG but he does post them on Canvas. A few "pop quizzes" but he hints about them a few classes before they come. The hard grading came  from the GTF. Midterm & final are papers. LOTS OF READING

Enjoyed his Human Nature course. A few pages of reading for each lecture, but for meeting 3 times a week it wasn't bad. His lectures are very organized and he is good at utilizing powerpoint to help. Super easy 5 question reading quizzes once a week or so, 3 exams over the quarter which are straightforward if you pay attention to the material.

This class was great. The readings are REALLY interesting. If you pay attention to his lectures, the quizzes are fairly easy. He gave us multiple options in terms of extra-credit from watching short movies at home to lectures. Tough attendance policy, you really have to be in class.

This is an ethics class where in the syllabus he states that quizzes are open book then when it comes time to take the quiz he doesn't let you actually use them. This does not seem very ethical to me? Oh and his extra credit is literally worth 1.25% for writing a single spaced paper on a 2 hr lecture outside of class. Hardest 100 lvl class I've had

She was the GE for my JCOM301 discussion section. I had her prior in a summer class and loved her. She's super understanding and very sweet to her students. She can be picky with certain criteria for the rubric, so make sure you go over it before submitting. Overall, Nishat's awesome and I would love to take another class with her again!

Love her down and she was lowkey one of the best teachers that I have ever had. She is extremely sweet and understanding, and made sure to make her classes interesting and engaging. Would definitely recommend taking her class!!

I had her over the summer. She was super nice and understanding! You could tell she really liked what she taught. The course was shortened so we had daily class assignments as attendance, 3 quizzes, and 2 papers that had 2 pre-assignments prior to the actual papers. Responded very quickly to emails. Overall, a really great and supportive teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ken is by far the most helpful professor i've ever had. He does whatever he can to get you prepared for his exams. If you want to do well, do his in class problems and suggested problems before quizzes and you will do well. don't forget to read and  go to class or you have no chance of passing.
Just read the PPT for each chapter, by the way, I can study ppt at home also. Never do the accounting sample question on class.lazy or not?  Please notice this is accounting class, not history class.
his class is so boring, just read the slices and copy the answer of book question on blackboard. I feel like if you take his class, you have to study this course at home.
Ken's a Legend. Had him at 8 am and I loved going to his class to wake me up. He's better than coffee. If you want to take an accounting class, you want to take it with Ken.
Ken's great. Has tons of knowledge. His lectures are very helpful (terrific sense of humor). I highly recommend.

cost accounting is tough by nature, so I highly recommend taking this professor. Unlike other instructors, this professor actually researches cost & is very knowledgeable in his field of study. He tries his best to make it as painless as possible. Sometimes the book is confusing, but he shows us easier ways to solve problems. Very cool guy!!
One of the best teacher i have taken at UHD, It makes you work for your grade even though it gives you a lot of extra credits..
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Never seemed prepared for class, simply copied notes onto the chalkboard, posted no material online, tested on material covered on homework a week after the test expecting you to be practiced after copying his lecture notes off the board.  Very tough grader, not to mention he cancelled the final review class period with no sub to cover.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Nganou is a bit intimidating at first but once you get used to it he is very fair. He teaches the material fully and wants you to understand it. Not friendly by any stretch but plenty willing to help. Very clear with expectations and tests mirror study guides nearly perfectly. I took 256 and 315 from Dr. Nganou and would take from him again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are easy enough to follow and he will help or elaborate on anything if you ask. But like others here have said, he expects you to basically be a mathematician by the time you take tests or do homework. Tests on material not covered in lecture or HW. I'm an A and B student,  especially in math: Struggled to get to a C in this class. AVOID
Awful professor who has tests that cover material not covered in class or HW. Homework takes hours and is only accomplished by teaching yourself how to do it. Do not take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I thought the class was a pretty good difficulty for the level of the class. Nice guy, and gave lots of examples. Expects you to do some proofs during the tests. Homework due every week and 3 tests. Lectures are important to understanding material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It was hard to approach Prof. Nganou during office hours because he expects you to have read and understood the material in the textbook before coming into office hours (but the textbook sucked!). During lecture, he goes over easy examples and then the homework is way harder, which is annoying. He expects you to know stuff not covered in class.

I love math, but I had a poor experience in his class. Discrete is hard to begin with, but with him it's abysmal. His teaching style is confusing, disjointed, and difficult to follow. He does not treat the class with respect and expects you to know the material before it is taught. Would not recommend.
Very straightforward with what he expects and he stands by his own standards. He may seem intimidating but he is helpful and understanding when you approach him.

Professor Jean knows everything. His lectures are very straightforward and informative. He goes at a quick pace but is ready to answer questions whenever. He is very helpful in office hours and responds quickly to emails. I'm surprised he got bad reviews here. Hes one of the best math professors I've had.

I thought he was a wonderful professor. His lectures are straight forward and the examples he uses in his lectures are used on the quizzes and exams. As long as you take good notes (which he makes easy) and study them before quizzes and exams, you will do fine. He does have a thick accent, but I got used to it within the 3rd lecture.

This teacher  has a thick accent and he doesn't speak in proper english. His lectures are straight out of the text book. Seems that his favorite phrases are "this is easy for a mathematician" and "you should be able to do this in just a few minutes". Very condescending and expects you to know how to do it before he teaches it. Poor teacher.
He was terrible and couldn't teach the material at all. Only take his class as a last resort.

He is the type of math professor who knows what he is doing but cannot convey it to you. This makes an introductory course like proof very difficult. Will often say you should just memorize this, then ask you to explain and prove why something happens without showing you the math behind it first. Very first class I have ever failed.

He is very confusing at times and is not very helpful when the class seems confused. He just says, "You should just memorize these or you're going to be in trouble". Class consists of writing down as many theorems as possible without much explanation. I would not take a class from him again.
He takes time to warm up to the class but once he does, the class is more fun.  He is a tough grader though!!

Dr. Nganou is a very good instructor. His lectures are very, very clear and his examples are very helpful for homework and exams. Everything on the homework and exams is covered in class. He is very welcoming in office hours and does his best to make sure everyone understands everything. Favorite math instructor of all time.
Bored. Much homework online and written down.
SOOOOOOOOOOOOOO much homework. terrible worst ever.

I've had 3 calculus teachers total, and compared to the other two Prof. Nganou is... identical.  His teaching seemed just like every other math teacher I've had.  His accent takes a little getting used to, but his handwriting is very legible.  The textbook for diff. equ. is a piece of junk, but the whole math dept. uses that book.
Please AVOID!

I have always done very well in math but I had a frustrating and unsuccessful experience with this professor. Teaches as if you already know material. His 'class' is just him writing his entire lecture word for word on the board straight from the textbooks (there are 3). Was condescending when questioned and very vague with poor examples. AVOID.

To be honest, worst math teacher I have ever had, and I have taken a lot of math. He teaches in non-inutative manner and students are quickly lost. Tests were hard and did not match lectures or HW. He was rude in class and did not treat students as mature adults. I would never take a classs with him.
This professor is not helpful at all. He doesn't respect students, and he expects you learn everything by yourself. Definitely not recommend him to anyone.

He is one of the worest instructor in UO. He is totally useless. The only way I can understand this calss is reading the text book by myself,and the next time I attend the class, he confuse me again.He wants to take off your point as many as possible , such as what color of paper used in homework. I strongly recommand NOT take his class.

Probably one of the best calc teachers at UO. His lectures are great and he prepares you well for the tests. He has a bit of an accent but it's not difficult to understand. As along as you try you can get a good grade in his class. Also, I don't think he comes off as rude at all, he just wants his students to understand.

His lectures were superbly structured.  He is very clear, organized, and has many examples.  He is always super happy to help during office hours, and is very easy to understand.  His accept is not a problem at all.  He is a very nice person, and overall great professor.  Awesome guy!

This professor is unclear about his expectations, and the lectures never match the homework problems. Tests are extremely difficult, and if you ask him a question he talks to you like you should already know the answer. This is one of the worst professors I have had. AVOID! ! !

Professor writes quickly, but presents many excellent examples and is easy to understand. Lectures are beautifully structured, with each topic naturally leading into the next. Exams are not easy, but if you do ALL the recommended problems there will be no surprises. Things that end up on the exams are always well covered in homework and class.

This class was taught in a small lecture and Dr. Nganou did a good job of teaching it. He has a little bit of an accent, but does a good job of writing everything he says on the chalkboard to compensate. This class was easy, I got an A+, but there is a good amount of homework.
Very hard to understand, tries to joke in class but ends up coming off as rude. Overall not a terrible teacher, but definitely not the best.

This professor was rude to students and incredibly unhelpful. He asks questions in class and makes you feel incompetent for not knowing the answers. His tests are extremely hard and he doesn't teach you well enough to pass them. I would not recommend him to anyone.

Fantastic lecturer, always straight to the point. His German accent and perfect rhythmic cadence make the information easily understandable, even satisfying. Even the most math-stunted students can't fail the quizzes as he gives practices quizzes and video walkthroughs of each problem. You will learn a lot!
This class is equivalent to a fastball right down the middle, a decent amount of assignments none being too difficult.

Jens is a God-send for those of us who need to knock out science credits from our degree guide. Although there is an in-person lecture, attendance isn't recorded and literally EVERYTHING is online. Easy A class, and a great character. Highly recommended.

such a chill science class. i went to class 2 times all term and got an A. everything is accessible online, very little homework just weekly quizzes that r super easy. definitely recommend if you need a science credit!!! prof is super nice as well and extremely smart
prof is great
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor.   He appeared more interested in you learning the material than the grades or process like other professors.    He provided support beyond the lecture to further explain material.      He is very passionate in physics and his love for this subject shows.   would absolutely take one of his classes again.

I had Professor Noeckel last term, and I think he was one of the best professors I have had! The textbook was free and one time I got two questions wrong on a quiz and emailed him about it, and because I got the question right in the email, he gave me the point! Very caring and you can tell he loves his job! His lectures/lecture videos were great!

Jens is an absolutely phenomenal professor, especially if you're a freshman. Each week, there's 1 short homework assignment and a few reading quizzes. The midterm was only 25 questions and very easy, the final was online and very similar to the practice final. Go to office hours if you need help with a homework, he's very friendly. Highly recommend

reviews.comment: Amazing. I have taken 3 classes taught by him. Definitely recommend 11/10. Easiest A of my life

Great professor. Minimal assignments and can retake quizzes once or twice depending on if it was reading or quantitative. Also drops the 3 lowest quiz scores in total. No midterm and the final was online.

The entire class is available online or with in person lectures with just a few assignments each week including lectures, reading, and quizzes. There was no midterm and a final that was only worth 20%. Doing the homework is very important in this class but it is not very hard.
Great teacher. All lectures were accessible online which was extremely helpful.

This professor is amazing! He brings an awesome aura to class, and puts so much effort into explaining concepts. He once swung a nut on a rope to lift up a bottle. I wish I could take his class again.

reviews.comment: Very easy and very understanding and nice

Jens was a wonderful professor for the term I had him-- he made the course easy and accessible online during COVID, so showing up to lecture was not mandatory, and was very gracious to us during the pandemic. He was also a treat, and his class was always fun. Even without the need to show up to lecture, I still did every day because he was so fun!
do the weekly quizzes and you will get an automatic A. You can learn the material easily without going to class and the textbook is provided online for free. really nice guy too.

Hilariously easy - if you want a free A, take PHYS 101, PHYS 155, ASTR 121, or ASTR 123 with this man. His classes are pretty boring - pick your Plickers partners and rotate who goes to class in your group of 4. reviews.comment: bruh.... I am recommending this professor for the most proper and organized schedule in the whole of U of O! this class was easy, didn't have to read to get A or even show up for lectures. His class is the easiest of any other class in the whole of U of O.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took 2 Physics courses and the ASTR 123 class with Professor Noeckel. He is by far one of the easiest professors on campus. His lectures are admittedly very dry and boring, and you don't really need to listen to him to get an A in his class. I recommend referring to the textbook for homework problems. Reading and lecture quizzes are a joke.

love prof noeckel. this class was really easy and understandable. there are no tests, just lectures and lecture quizzes as well as reading tests and problem tests. best part is the book is free! love the german accent toooo

Great Professor! His lectures are a bit lengthy but very easy to understand. I really enjoyed learning about astronomy but also being able to understand it a lot easier. I also love how the text book is free!

Jens is a good teacher. He gives very involved lectures, that can be lengthy, but they are extremely easy. No tests, just 3 problem reading quizzes and problem sets. If you care for a good grade, you can get one, and it's not hard. Extremely minimal effort

Class consisted of video lectures, lecture quizzes with unlimited attempts, reading quizzes, and 3-problem weekly homework quizzes. Everything was multiple choice and straight out of the textbook. There are no midterms or final. ASTR 123 with Prof. Noeckel was by far the easiest class I've taken in college.

Took an honors physics class in high school which was very difficult, but this class was no problem for me. I watched the lectures at twice the speed which made it feel like less work. He makes it very easy to get an A+ with minimal effort, if you pay attention or have taken a physics class before you should have no issues.

He is a super kind and helpful professor. Lectures are well thought out and easy to understand. Assignments are not difficult. Take this class if you aren't a STEM major who needs to fill a requirement. Highly recommend!

Professor Neockel is really sweet and since we aren't in person, his class is super manageable and easy to get done throughout the week. Each lecture has "quiz" questions throughout but you get as many tries until you get the right answer. Each week there is a math problem set but he puts out a video with each problem set and explains each one.

Professor Noeckel is a great professor. He is a smart guy which really shows in his lectures. But the downside of this, is that he speeds through information, sometimes becomes disorganized due to referencing outside materials, and makes the lectures hard to understand. Due to this, go to his office hours for help. Why, tutors dropped my grade.....

Hes nice & passionate about physics. The majority of your grade is HW which takes like 15 mins to do & you turn it in online. Never used my textbook & quit going to lecture 3 weeks in bc for some reason this class attracts kids who talk and play games on their computers all class when attendance is optional, idk why they dont just stay home.

I didn't often go to lectures but everything was uploaded quickly and accessible on Canvas. I got an A+ mostly just going to class for exams (and a few lectures). Great study guides and HW hints make everything easy to understand. Passionate, helpful and very nice professor. Would take 100 times over.

His lectures are pretty disorganized and hard to follow, but if you go to office hours/ask him questions individually he'd explain things better. He goes over the homework and study guides in class. His exams are exactly like the study guides with just the numbers changed around, and he lets you use a page of notes.

Homework is incredibly frustrating, and not enough guidance is given on it. The course expects you to know advanced biochem without building up to that point. Content is extremely esoteric, and lectures are not engaging.
Cancelled CH 466 less than two weeks before start of term.

The class was pretty hard, and Prof Nolen did not have set office hours every week. BUT, before every problem set/exam he had an office hour. It was definitely a doable class if you put in the work and asked questions. Although we did get a lot of personal attention since there were only 8 students.

Excellent lecturer!
Hard to communicate outside of class, don't have office hour, tests are difficult and he very like to test about very detail things that may not even on the slides.

Fairly young guy, definitely easy on the eyes, but he had no office hours and seemed to think it was the GTFs job to help us outside of class, not his. Give you multiple attempts for problem sets on Blackboard, which means you actually learn the material. Tests are still insanely hard though.

His tests are really hard. even with the study guide it is unclear what to study. you come out of the test feeling tricked and cheated. the material from the hw and quiz sets are not what is on the exam. he expects you to be able to remember all the facts, if you understand all the material it will not help you. after this class I changed my major
Decent lecturer. Explains things well and is always ready to help by email (he didnt have office hours....only the gtf did). Young and attractive guy.

You can tell that that he hasn't been teaching long. He is kind of nervous in class. He just reads you his slides basically in lecture, but is a total hottie. All of his material comes directly from the book.
Very straightforward, like him as a person, gave us the previous years final and a practice final to study. Got a 77/80 on that final.

Exams were all extremely straightforward and the homework wasn't bad (a little bit of written hw and webwork). He's also just a cool person and will gladly explain things if you have questions about anything.
I took math 112 and it was a difficult class for me but he was good at doing lectures and helpful during office hours

explains concepts very well and always checks for understanding. the homework can be tough, but you start it in class and he can be flexible on due dates if your aim is to improve understanding; it prepares you for the exams well. In general, he's just a cool and good-natured guy--passionate about the material, too. 
highly recommend!
very cool and nice guy

Course was CS322, not CS330. Chill class and more than happy to receive suggestions to make the class more entertaining (literally states at the beginning of class). She's very kind when you go to talk to her and replies same day for online messages. Definitely tries to get students to engage and gives lots of great examples to help with projects
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: By far one of the most Boring lecturers that I have seen, puts absolutely no energy into lectures and doesn't know how to keep students engaged.
