Ms. Norris research work is a testament to her prowess in the field of computer science, a fact that does not translate to the classroom. While she provides lots of resources and feedback, she does not adequately prepare her projects and assignments. There are always errors and she even replaced a project after it was assigned, yikes.

boring lecture and tends to over explain with examples and it honestly takes away from the point especially when the classes had her for were for python fundamentals (often takes 10-30 min trying to explain through example simple coding concepts that can be easily understood and taught simply by just defining it in easily 5-10 min)

Prof. Norris is a very accommodating professor. She is very kind and her lecture are good. There's lots of opportunities for extra credit in this class and you don't even need to show up. You can just watch the lectures on Zoom in the comfort of your home or go to class physically. Loads of TAs that are extremely helpful too. Overall great class.

Professor Norris is a caring professor. She is extremly understanding of circumstances and situations that may come up in your life and affect your performance. She is willing to hear you out and try to compensate. However, the best thing to do is not give up. Come to class even if it's not required. If you put the effort in, you will be do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very thorough professor. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities. I missed multiple coding projects and the extra credit of the final exam was enough to make up for all of that.

This class has been absolutely horrible. The only way to do well is if you have prior coding experience. She has yet to teach a single thing, but rather all we do is play Kahoot. The TA's that we have however are absolutely, and I am so grateful to them for basically teaching me.

Disappointed in this class.  It was more of a seminar class then a lecture.  The material was only in the texts and the lectures assumed you knew much of the material previously.  Testing was not for understanding but how well you could regurgitate syntax.  Her and her TA's were very helpful but it was not a good class.  Poor feed back on programs.

Awesome

reviews.comment: Nute has exceptional attendance, so youd better turn up as well. He is definitely looking for a particular style in his projects so if youre trying to express your own ideas this isnt the professor for you. Unseemingly so, this is helpful for creativity because it teaches you to create around a clients needs. In arch: professor  client!

He's extremely smart and articulate; I enjoyed his lectures. But I did not appreciate his interactions with students.  It's as if he feeds on crushed dreams. But when he reviews students projects he's insightful and has a civilized conversation. But ask him why you got a C on a project he'll make you feel inadequate.

Nute has a "do as I say" type of attitude toward education.  He is not the least bit interested in encouraging students to explore their own ideas and learn to develop them, and would sometimes become abusively insistent about his views.  Not at all in the spirit of a liberal design school.  The result: 16 nearly identical projects...whee.  Avoid!
Awesome teacher. Really into the class. Very helpful when it comes to what you need specifically to succeed. Highly recommend taking this course.

She's not a teacher. All the lower level french teachers aren't, but she has no interest in being a teacher and it showed. I felt like she didn't understand my questions or put any effort into teacher, rather just expected the class to learn on their own. Good sense of humor and wonderful person, but not a teacher.
Pretty good teacher, but intimidating and strict.  Not an easy class.
Great prof! Always willing to help. Really wants to see her students succeed.
She was always well prepared and very easy to reach.

The class itself could be a good and useful class for many students but this professor does not teach well and going to class feels pointless. She is very nice but just a lousy teacher. I would not take a class from this professor unless it was absolutely necessary.
Professor Odell was an awesome professor! His lectures were engaging, and I felt that I learned a lot.
Professor Odell was a great communicator and wanted each of his students to succeed in his class. The work load was pretty light, overall great experience.

Ross was a great professor. Super laid back and very understanding. He made it so easy to ask for extensions and kept this class very low stress. He was always very accommodating. I highly recommend him for any writing class, he was just the best.

My favorite teacher I have ever had. He uses different grading than other teachers but it was a nice change. Lots of extra credit opportunities and really cared about his students. Was always willing to work with students after hours and gives good feedback. If you have the chance please take his class!!

Ross is such a good professor. He has humor, unlike other professors I had. He does not give you unnecessary homework and the brief articles he provides are very interesting to read. Take his class and I guarantee you'll like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He wants all of his students to succeed and gives you the opportunity to receive a good grade in the class if you're willing to do extra credit. He is super supportive and gives great feedback on essays. Overall, a great human.
he is a great professor the labor projects are super nice he said that if you hold up your part doing assignments you get a b no matter what.

Ross Odell is a great professor and an overall amazing human. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is a great person and if you are looking for your writing 121 prerequisite, do go out of your way to get Professor Odell. If you do all the work and complete all of the extra-credit you will receive an A in the class.

Ross Odell is a very good professor. I just had him for Writing 121 in fall 2021. His class is labor-based meaning if you complete all of the assignments you get a B. And if you do 3 additional labor projects that bumps you up to an A. Amazing Professor to take if you need to take your writing prerequisites.

This class has extremely confusing and uses databases not compatible with iPads which felt inaccessible. The directions are frequently unclear and leave students guessing on assignments worth a lot of points. Uses MRI Simmons which is one of the most obnoxious database to use. If I didn't need this course to graduate, I would have dropped it.

bruh this guy is the most awful lecturer ever. the lectures are so long, so slow, so boring. He insists on calling on people to try and define every term before they have been taught and no one wants to answer, everyone is silent and the lectures could last 20 minutes but they dragggg if you want to take this class, take it with another professor.

J 460 Green Brand Strategy. Senyo is a nice professor but this class was all over the place. I took this class online spring term due to COVID-19 and everyone in my class was confused most of the time because instructions for assignments were confusing. Overall, wasn't a hard class but I wouldn't take another class from him.

Senyol is an outstanding professor who really cares for his students and makes sure they understand the concepts. Media planning is not easy, but he took his time to make sure we were all on the same page. I definitely recommend taking Senyol.
Honestly I found his class to be pretty easy. If you go to class and actually pay attention, youll be fine. Also, his accent is perfectly understandable.

reviews.comment: Senyo is okay for a professor. My lecture happened to be two hours and nobody could leave early without being called out for it. Daily attendance quiz and participation really matters. The tests and assignments weren't particularly hard (3 of each). He is a really nice person who cares a lot about the subject but his teaching style is average.

Senyo is an excellent and passionate teacher. Although at first his accent is slightly challenging to get past it's always fun listening to how he pronounces certain words. A man full of character and humor which mostly consist of dad jokes. The only challenging part was understanding a few assignments entirely. Tho to clarify was easy.

His lectures are pretty heavy but I think he's overall a really good teacher that invites discussion in the classroom and cares about how we all do in his class. The exams aren't too bad if you don't skip class and you do the reading, although there's a lot of reading. Overall nice guy and good teacher, would definitely take a class from him again.
Nice, but gives way too many quizzes.

reviews.comment: This guy is from Ghana so if you're bad with accents avoid him, but he knows what he's talking about & tries to make it as easy to understand as possible. reviews.comment: Ofori is honestly the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. He gets mad when people don't answer his obscure questions that have nothing to do with the class. I was excited to take this class but he has made me hate research and anything to do with consumer insights. Never take him. Horrible.

He's a smart guy which is seen in his past accomplishments but he's not the best teacher. Very unclear and does not stick to the syllabus whatsoever. Very confusing, and it's not just me who thinks it, our entire class is always lost in his thoughts. Turned a class I should have loved into a class I dreaded.

He is hard to understand, doesn't explain very clearly, and often asks the class for answers to vague questions, waiting over 30 seconds in awkward silence in which no one wants respond because he immediately disagrees with them. Made a subject I love into something I had to tolerate. Easy grader but very unhelpful; avoid if you can.
Passionate about teaching. Looks for a lot of participation from students in class. Unclear on most assignments however, grades easy.
Very dry lectures.  All exams are open book canvas tests

Lectures are not interesting, feel like I did not learn much from him. It is not super hard, but also not that easy either. He just does not make any of the material interesting or engaging. There are two midterms and a final, no other opportunities for increasing your grade. There are weekly quizzes but they are worth nothing.

I think Professor Ofori isn't for everyone. Many of the other ratings talk about how he isn't the most engaging lecturer. However, I connected with many of the course materials he presented and found the class interesting, relevant, and helpful for a future career in policy. He focuses heavily on economics but doesn't make the students do math.

Never learned much in class and had to teach myself out of class. Am taking PPPM415 not by choice with him next term. I learned more in labs than in class...honestly just look up Youtube explanations and it'll be a thousand times easier to prepare for tests.

Most boring professor I have ever had. I dread coming to class every day. No one listens to his lectures and he is requiring an I-clicker this term for this class. You are allowed 3 absences and I wish I could take more. It is a very easy class, but be prepared to be bored out of your mind for 3 hours a week.

In my experience, Ofori is nowhere near as other reviews make him out to be. His lectures are a bit boring, but the material isn't the most interesting to begin with, and he is clear enough with grading criteria. Attendance is graded, but our tests were all online for an in person class. For the group project and presentation, everyone got a 100%

I think winter term had it a lot better than fall term. The lectures were boring and sometimes when he would try to give examples he would mess up. The exams are closed note but curved well. The class is hard and boring but as long as you work hard you will do well. Go to his office hours and he will try to explain things well, better than lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is a class that is dense in policy and economics, so yes, it can be "boring". Prof Ofori does seem to care about his class, though, and I believe he really wants to see people do well. He is very kind and chose a great guest lecturer. This class could improve with a little more structure to group projects and slides with more visuals/examples.

Most boring PPPM class I've taken. He had poor structure for the class, I was never really sure what we were talking about, lectures felt random. He's knowledgable but so tedious to listen to, I taught myself. Terrible canvas page, no organization. Weekly online multiple choice reading quizzes. In person closed note midterm and final, curved.

reviews.comment: Honestly, despite what others say, Roland did a fine job under the circumstances he was dealt. Absolute trash professor, can't explain concepts and when you go to him for help it's even worse. Don't know how he was hired to teach this class because its important for the PPPM major. Don't take him or wait for someone else to teach the class.

He also made our class do hour long presentations essentially making us teach 10 of the lectures for him and didn't give us grades for presenting.

He canceled so many classes and didn't prepare us for the midterm. He reads off of slides and the GE was more helpful and understanding of the content. The midterm was so hard.

Don't take this professor if you have a choice not to. Doesn't grade anything until almost the end of the term, and reads directly off slides. The worst class I have taken.

reviews.comment: Gabe provides packets for each section with detailed notes and practice problems throughout the packet. Its really helpful in that you dont have to scramble to write everything down. He has lots of extra credit in his tests which help a lot. He wants students to succeed and gives them the materials to do so.

Gabe is one the first math professors I have had as a freshman and he what I expected. He goes through the chapters of the book in decent form to which I get a vague idea of the concept. Every class then ends with a short "quiz" of the discussed problem in order to see if we understood the material. He does well as a professor I would say.
Math 111 is a hard class to take in college, he really helps explain things, goes at a really good past, asks for questions and is always ready to help out
I hate math but I really liked taking his class, he's a great instructor who really wants you to succeed. I would def. recommend him for this or any other math class!

Gabe's class was really hard, as it is the most failed class on campus. I feel as if he explains things very in detail. If you want to know why your doing what your doing and where the formula is derived from then take his class. I felt as if it confused me more than it helped, but depends on the person I guess!
Gabes great this class is a little tough but he's pretty helpful and has good grading policies especially for students with text anxiety issues..
gabe was cool. had a beer with him after finals.

Never got our hand-in HW's back. Test reviews never had solutions. Webworks were much harder than quizzes and exams. Grades are not posted on BB. All these things made the class more challenging and frustrating to me at least.

I'm really not sure what to think of this class. I'll be taking the final soon and the rule is if you fail the final, no matter how well you did prior to the exam it wont matter because you cant pass the class unless you pass the final meaning %60+...no pressure :-) I really did not like this class nor the grading system, kind of regret taking it.
Gabe is great, he's really helpful and tells you exactly what he wants you to know for quizzes/exams. He also replies to emails quickly and is helpful during office hours.

I really enjoyed Gabe's class as much as a person can enjoy MATH 111. He was really clear about what he wanted in the class. We had weekly quizzes and homework and two midterms. Gabe is really easy to reach when you have questions. The only thing I didn't like about this course was that we did our homework on this site called "webwork" is was awful
Super caring professor; cares about your wellbeing. Challenges you to rethink what is given and to think outside of the box. Gives great precedent studies to improve your ideas and learn new things.
Yt was the best!
Amazing professor. Really cares about his students and their wellbeing. He will always put you and your health before assignments. He gives great feedback and has good assignments. Love him!

Dr. Ohman is such a great example for teachers, especially in black studies. As a white woman, she addressed her privilege immediately and from that moment forward, she had my respect. She is not only an expert in her field, but she also always has office hours to hear her students' ideas and empower them. She is a life-changing force for good.

One of my favorite professors that I've had at UO. She gives great feedback and responds quickly to emails. She is also very understanding of personal situations. She will also provide trigger warnings before sensitive material is talked about in class and will have a half-time break for about 5 minutes.

reviews.comment: she's sweet and funny all through the term. she's really engaging in her lectures, open to criticisms, and actually cares about her students and what they take away from the class. there's a lot of reading and in order to do well on the midterm and discussion project, its important to do them(however she does emphasize the power of skimming a text)

Carmel was one of the best teachers I have ever had at UO! I took her WGS101 class during COVID and online school and she was more than accommodating when needed and gave insightful feedback on assignments. The readings were interesting and the course load was very reasonable.
She comes across as someone that just picked a focus based on what is most popular at that given time. Do NOT expect genuine feedback.
A product of the institution. If you'd like original thoughts on your work, look elsewhere.
If you take any class with her involved, her input will be very skewed to the status quo. I felt like it was having input from a writing guide.
She is a very rank and file type of teacher. It seems she's just going along with the status quo for the most part. Avoid if possible.

Ohman is sooo sweet and genuinely gives good feedback and responses to discussion posts, as for the class itself with Bufalino it's very easy and enjoyable. As long as you do the work, you'll be fine.
I was not really engaged much at all in her class. It seemed very copy paste to me. You can tell she's trying very hard, but it doesn't really work out.
Definitely not my cup of tea for a teacher. Needs much more experience.

I took WGS 101 with Carmel for winter term, and I can genuinely say that she is one of the most caring and thoughtful educators I have ever had. Her class is structured much like an English class, with frequently (usually short) readings and some written assignments. I loved how often she allowed students to expand upon the conversation in class.

Carmel was extremely approachable when it came to asking questions and I felt supported academically. She's passionate about what she studies and what we learn in class which I appreciate. She was also really funny and engaging, so going to her class was never a bad experience.

I LOVE Carmel! She made WGS really interesting and fun, and she's super nice, caring and generally awesome. There were quite a few assignments but they're easy to complete if directions are followed, and she grades pretty fairly. Projects were fun and all the readings were available online. Loved this class--take it with her!
I loved her. WR is generally not very challenging, but she makes you work for your A. Very relatable and nice

This professor is actually amazing. He is so nice and understanding and a great teacher, he really knows the material he is talking about. But get ready for the work. The workload is insane and the tests are extremely difficult with M/C never available.
Great professor! Acceptable HW load

Class was very lecture heavy, it was easy to get lost if you weren't paying attention. However, Professor O'Hare was always open to suggestions in how to make our learning experience more enjoyable. Overall not the easiest class, but he is not a professor that wants to see you fail but definitely requires some work from you.

reviews.comment: Fairly difficult class and very lecture heavy. Hard to comprehend and remember information through the lectures. So much information is thrown at you in just one class.

Mr. OHares class was my first online class in college so far. His lectures were easily accessible through podcasts and were easy to follow along with! He always replies to questions with speed and gives very informative answers. Would recommend as an online professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors, creates a close community for her classes so that you generally become friends with everyone by the end of the term. Though there are many tests and quizzes, she gives out extra credit and gives you every opportunity to study as well as make up for work. It is not difficult to get an A with effort and studying.

She's hilarious and easy to talk to. The class is usually small and you see these people everyday so it becomes kind of like a family. She keeps the class fun but it is hard, fast paced, and takes a lot of memorization. There's homework everyday, just little things. If you study like 5 minutes a day you'll do fine. Its a hard class but its fun.

Bomi is an amazing teacher who loves to teach. Her class is hard, but learning a new language is hard, she gives you a lot of homework for a reason, and that is for the extra practice and help. Her class is easy to get a good grade in if you put in the effort.

It is really hard in her class. She gave too many hw to do everyday. Also have record. And also the test were really hard. And even she give the extra credits, it doesn't work at all!!! Dooooooon't take her class!!!!!!!

Her class was hard to keep up on. There was a lot of busy work everyday and the tests were kind of hard. You really have to know your stuff because she tries to include everything. It's really easy to get a bad grade in this class but she will work really hard to not let this happen. Hard but you will learn a lot.

I've taken Korean 101-103 with Professor Oh and honestly her classes are really laid back. It's fun to be in class, and it's the only class I looked forward to everyday. Expect hw everyday and interesting assignments! Not hard at all just put in effort!

ALOT of busy work. There is homework almost every night and expects a lot from the students. Some material that are on her exams are given to the students a week before the test. Unless you need a language course or like busy, I wouldn't recommend this class.
No Comments

Robin Okumu is one of my favorite teachers. She is such an amazing teacher. Her lectures are clear and the assignments as well. The grading system is weird, but she will explain it well and she gives Extra Labor activities so you can raise your grade to an A which is awesome. It is not hard to get an A as long as you complete your work.
An interesting grader, but very helpful and kind. Attendance and getting work in on time matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Robin really cares about making sure her students can not only reiterate the French language, but making sure they understand it as well. You have to work for your grade, but she helps a lot outside of class, and really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Robin is a very honest and clear grader. This course is definitely not easy but this is not due to the professor it is due to the course itself. Robin was always willing to help when needed and was kind when I was straight up terrible at French. I am terrible at French so this class was no easy feat but she made it much easier and now I love French
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Oman is an excellent professor. The class is more writing intensive than other writing classes, but you learn a ton. Oman makes writing 121 an interesting, fun challenge.

This is an overall good and fair class. Just keep up with the readings and the busy work and you'll be fine. Go to her office hours if you have writer's block. She tends to procrastinate when it comes to grading essays, which ends up pushing back the due dates for the revisions.
Expects way too much. Seems to have something to prove. Not that helpful. The topics she gives are very difficult to write about, but she doesn't offer much in the way of suggestion.

There are a few req books, but you can find them free online. Lots of readings for each class. Olivia is willing to help you understand concepts better.  Talking about societal stuff so it's sort of easy. Occasional reading and discussion quizzes, table discussion work, take-home Midterm and Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Olivia was great ! She always worked to engage with students, as well as worked to give great individual feedback. The class is not a class you can just put off until the last couple of weeks, and there are multiple books to buy and read, but as long as you come to class, take notes, do the readings, and generally engage you'll be golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Olívia is a super sweet teacher. She is super communicated and works with students to allow the classroom to be compatible for everyone. There is quite a bit of reading and you do need to purchase books for class but you can find it online. Her assignments are straight to the point and if you struggle, shes always willing to help. Highly reccomend
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't take him. tests are horrible.

He is the worst teacher i have ever had. DON"T take him!@!!!!!Seriously, he so ridiculous and does not provide any efficient sources to study for his tests. His tests consists of specific multiple choice questions which he fails to clarify when teaching. he ambiguous teaching style is frustrating and annoying!!!!His tests are horrible!

He seems to try to fit too much into each lecture and ends up a bit rushed or scattered at times connecting everything.  He is most effective in giving examples to help explain concepts more thoroughly.  He will be very helpful in explaining further if asked a specific question, but only if asked.

I am taking another course by him just because I had a great experience with him for 335. He is a very engaging lecturer and is passionate about what he teaches. He keeps the students engaged and makes the effort to remember names and encourage us all to be involved in discussions.

Very good teacher, very animated and keeps you awake if you have an early class. He has great stories and is really interesting. He is a little socialist but is very good at seperating fact from his thoughts. Tests are pretty easy if you go to class, but he doesnt make you. 4-1page journal entries, mid term, final, and final project.
No Comments

Amazing teacher, keeps things clear and understandable. Tests are super easy. explains everything to a T. He doesn't grade his homework on if you got the problem right just if you put an answer down. Greatly recommended for Soc Stats. Plus he is a grad student so he understands what it is like to be a student.
Professor so far has been awesome to listen to during lectures, very on point and knows his material.

Professor Hawkins was a very good professor. He explained things very well in class and was very understanding when I let him know I had to drop it. It was a super interesting class, and I might take it again:)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Orlando's class fall term and I really loved it. He is really nice and understanding. He provides a lot of readings but as long as you skim over them, he will explain them in lecture. The class felt really relaxing and I felt like I actually learned from him.

He isn't any help at all, I will say he does have a good sense of humor, but he will lecture forever and never shows up on time for class. Overall, I would highly recommend not taking any of his studios because he isn't fair at all grading wise. You can put in all the handwork you want but it won't get noticed.

Fantastic, experienced, knowledgeable professor.  You must have a thick skin, however, as he says what is on his mind.  Brilliant designer in his own right.  He actually does care about his students?but those that don't "get" Otto will likely hate him.  Those that do will love him.

One the most valuable teachers on the faculty with far more practical experience than the rest. Cares deeply about your progress. Full of stories and cynical as hell. Learned more from him than anybody else. Those with thin skins need to stay away.
Little interest in teaching.  More interest in sharing his own experiences.  Don't waste your time.

One of the best and most valuable. Otto should be respected for his willingness to share his experiences and provide invaluable advice to students. Many students who speak negatively of Otto don't understand the intention of his comments/lectures, and will pay dearly later on in their professions if they get beyond recording other people's designs.

Not impressed. He has lots of experience, but spends more time telling irrelevant stories than actually teaching. Is not clear about what he expects from students, and really doesn't seem to care whether they succeed.
cynical, but very interesting and can answer questions (understand just what the heck we're trying to ask) with the best of them
Agreed, he was horrible!  He was soo much by the book that he never wanted to interact with students.  Barely got by class, more help from friends and previous students than him.

This professor is horrible! he is never on time, sometimes doesnt even show at all. He blabs on and on about random crap that is ilrelevant to the course. He expects the world of you and fails you if you cant meet his pushy standards

Super easy class where if you just show up you will easily pass. I studied for probably 20 minutes before the tests where we knew the questions beforehand, and I didn't even have to show up for the last test or the last 2 weeks of class to get an A+. Lectures are interesting and you don't have to take notes to pass.
Great professor, he makes the lectures interesting and is a very funny guy. The class is just based off participation so very enjoyable.

literally so easy just have to go to the lectures and do good on the tests. u pick the essay questions u wanna answer its literally such an easy A and professor norton is so chill he's super easy to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and class! Lectures are easy to understand and follow along with. If you go to class and pay attention, this class is an easy A. Honestly don't really need to read textbook, only comes up on exams, but you choose your exam questions so it's easy to get around textbook stuff. Plus you can revise your exam for full credit back!

Easiest A class I have ever taken. Prof. Norton is a skilled + engaging lecturer and I really liked his grading system- as long as you show up and participate, you will do well. 204 is a great introduction to the fundamentals of sociology.

Man oh man what can I say about Matthew Norton. One of the coolest professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking a class with. Uses a different grading system that rewards initiative so if you go to class and put in effort in assignments it is an easy A+. One of the most random arrays of coursework from Earthquakes to Genetics but awesome guy.
the chillest professor I've ever had

I would absolutely recommend taking a course taught by Norton. He has been one of the most engaging professors I have ever had and never fails to keep me focused and interested in topics that my major does not even align with. Attendance is technically not mandatory, but it is strongly recommended and required if you want a good grade in the class.

Professor Norton is AMAZING. If you have an opportunity you should absolutely take a class with him. He makes it clear what you must do to achieve an A and helps you get it. There was no homework and everything was done in lectures and discussions. Tests were super easy and you are able to revise them if you don't get an 100% to get full points.

Professor Norton is such a sweet man and one of the only professors who can actually make me pay attention in lectures. His grading criteria is super lenient and simple to understand, though unconventional. Highly recommend taking any of his classes.

I am really happy I choose to take this class with him. He clearly cares about his students and their success, he uses a unique grading system and allows corrections on assignment to work towards the grade you want. Really great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: So understanding and caring of his students. Truly the nicest professor ever and very accommodating. I love that he allows his students to freely pick what they want to write about and I thoroughly enjoyed his class. Class has two essays, one in class midterm where questions are given as study guide before hand, and 5 easy quizzes.
Wonderful class and easy to follow along. Presented interesting discussions and the essay prompts left room for creativity. This class made me add sociology as a major and was thoroughly enjoyable!

Norton is funny, uses lots of anecdotes and some viral videos/movie clips to explain concepts, and lets you know exactly what to do to get the grade you want. Also, he remembers your name if your introduce yourself, which is pretty rad. Attendance DEF needed to pass. Some pop quizzes, but every quiz, test, paper can be revised for full credit. slay

I would recommend this class to anyone! Very straightforward and light workload. It was very easy to apply previous knowledge/personal experiences to the class concepts, and the material was genuinely interesting. It is very easy to succeed in this class, so I would recommend taking it alongside more strenuous classes to balance your workload.

Professor Norton is an amazing teacher, so I would highly recommend him. He's very kind, forgiving and understanding of students. Relatively easy class as long as you do the reading and show up to class. He is an easy grader, and you are even able to improve your grade if you don't do well. He's awesome!!
Pretty good prefessor, but the lectures are kinda unneccesary except for the lecture activities. There's only 3 exams and it's easy to get 100% on them with a bit of effort. Overall not bad.

reviews.comment: Such an easy class, attendance is mandatory but it's so chill and grading is so easy.

reviews.comment: Professor Norton is genuinely passionate about sociology and you can tell by the way he lectures. The material is very engaging, and the grading system is set up for student success. Take this class if you can, your grade is entirely up to you and you'll find yourself actually wanting to go to class.
Professor Norton is very passionate about sociology and the lectures are quite engaging and interesting. I recommend this course every time my friends are registering for classes.

Dr. Norton inspired me to declare a minor in sociology. He is incredibly passionate about his topic and makes his lectures very engaging. You will NOT regret going to class. No exams, just three very easy and clear written assessments. Even if you aren't familiar with Sociology, I highly recommend this class.

Professor Matt Norton is kind and genuinely cares about his students. However, the class lacks substantial content, making lectures feel unengaging and mostly filled with irrelevant video clips. No one around me seemed engaged, and the course felt like a waste of time and money. Unfortunately, I would not recommend this class.

Professor Norton is a great teacher and is very engaging in lecture. It is quite easy to get a good grade in the class if you attend lecture and do alright on the tests. Tests are shown in advance so that students can prepare, and revisions are given for up to full credit. This class is set up so that students succeed.
Vey engaging lectures and easy grading, with just points from participation and the discussions. Not much homework except reading. Definitely recommend!
Prof. Norton  makes the lectures entertaining and interesting, and he's an easy grader who wants his students to succeed. I highly recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor I have ever had here, as a senior, im bummed I couldn't have met him sooner.

Matt is super passionate about his work and fun activities in class. 3 assessments which he gives the questions before hand, graded either 0%, 50%, or 100%, and you can make up if you get 50%. The rest is participation in discussions and lectures done randomly in class so go to every class.

This is my second time taking a course with him and once again, Professor Norton taught with so much passion and I took away a lot from this class. He does do periodic reading quizzes, but you can always make these up at home. Every large assignment could be revised to 100. You do need to do an extra project to get an A+.
Amazing professor!! Very understanding, accessible, and very easy to communicate with! I'm very lucky to have had Professor Norton twice now. I recommend him if you're looking for a Sociology class.

I loved this class and felt I took so much away from it. Every grade you get can be revised, including tests and papers. He is an amazing lecturer and truly sets the class up for your success and understanding. The papers you read are so inclusive and really interesting. The exams are open note and the lecture recordings are posted online.
Best professor I have had at UO. Super nice and understanding, I would take another class from him if I could. Never could go wrong with him as your professor!

He really cares about what he teaches and makes sure the students succeed in his class. His class is relatively easy and it's very clear about how he wants assignments. Overall he's a great professor who enjoys doing what he does and the class has interesting material if you pay attention.

Super nice prof. Lectures could be boring at times, but you can tell he cares ab what he's teaching. 3 assessments and the questions are given ahead of time. You can either write a 1200-word paper or do a test with short answer questions. Would def take this prof again!

Matthew Norton truly cares about sociology and it shows through his teaching. Lectures were a tad boring, but attendance was not necessary and you could make up the in-class work. I do recommend going as the notes you take during class help with the three exams. I did the 3 short answers everytime and as long as you write a page you're good.

reviews.comment: Mr. Norton is great...SOC204 is boring but easy. You're exams are 75% of your grade, but you can choose to do a test or a 1,200 word essay (essays are graded less harsh!). No attendance isn't mandatory but he does lecture activities which you usually had to in class but you can make them up. You also only have to go to 4/6 sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are kinda boring but he is funny and makes it interesting. You get an option to write a paper or take a quiz and you get to see the questions a week in advance. Was pretty easy overall and somewhat interesting. I would take his class again! He also shows a bunch of videos in class which makes it less boring.

Super duper nice, very engaging, and funny lectures. Definitely a professor to remember! Would 1000% retake this class. My discussion leader was amazing as well! I highly recommend to take this class!
Very engaging and clear lectures. The assignments are pretty simple and you are given a lot of choices in what and how you answer during the few Assessments.
Easy A for soc credits. Flexible, understanding prof - great & entertaining lectures.

Really great professor overall. You can tell he really cares about what he is teaching and the class is very interesting and fun. Im always excited to see what we are learning about. The course overall is an easy A if you put in just a little effort. Mandatory Discussions but they were fun. Always cracking jokes and just a really fun class.

Best professor ive ever had at the UO! 2 papers, take home final, open note midterm (just no laptops), optional reading pop quizzes (you can opt out for a reading response instead). Just do the readings and group activities in class. He is so kind & understanding, emphasizes how he wants to make this easy for both us and him. HIGHLY recommend:)

The professor himself? Great. His lectures are very interesting and I would definitely take another class with him. The GEs? Nightmare. If you choose to take the test assessments they are HARSH graders. They make the concepts out to be way more complex than they actually are- make sure u basically memorize the lectures tbh

I love this professor. His lectures are super enganging and the assignments for this class were super easy and straightforward. He's an easy grader and the material is interesting and enganging. I'm definetly registaring for another one of his classes.

This guy was great. Mad respect for his ability to stand up for an hour 20 and lecture the whole time with so much passion. I am not a sociology person, but I enjoyed his class. He has 1x week lecture activities you must be present for and his exam style caters to multiple types of students. I would 100% take a class from him again, nice guy.

Professor Nortons class was a breath of fresh air. With that said, it wasn't easy but wasn't so hard or dense that you'd drown in work and questions. Go to lecture and review the slides and you'll do great, honestly.

Super easy class if you just go to class and pay attention. Lowest assessment of 5 is dropped. Range of options for assessment options- so super accommodating. Tests are entirely based on lecture, didn't even need to read the textbook.

Professor Norton was an amazing professor. He's very responsive via email. You had options of what to do for each exam (paper, open note exam, group project). Attendance wasn't mandatory but I HIGHLY recommend that you go. I believe it would've been hard to pass had I not gone to class. I will absolutely be taking a class that he teaches again.

Amazing Professor and keeps the class engaged with actual interesting content. Best sociology prof I've had and would definitely recommend taking a class of his! There were 6 pop quizzes and all were easy if you did the readings, the lowest two were dropped. He doesn't use slides but is a very good lecturer, just take notes! I

Norton was a good teacher, he was very passionate about sociology. He cares for the students and is supportive in any way. If you go to the lectures and pay attention, you'll pass. But if you dont go, good luck- very lecture heavy. Only real problem was the GEs, they were sorta confusing and tough graders.

Norton is a very a good professor. He covers the test material in his lectures around the main concepts of sociology, although these lectures are long, hes engaging with his audience and has "class activites". Hes very caring and always on top of things, I genuinely enjoyed taking this class.

Norton was very fun and engaging. Different lecture style than I was used to but it ensures that you pay attention. 5 assessments throughout the term, but you have a lot of flexibility on what you do for them, & he drops the lowest one. Very clear communication and made lectures interactive with 8 "lecture activities". Would definitely take again!

Matty Nort is the GOAT! Seriously one of the most caring and understanding profs. There were 6 quizzes (lowest 2 were dropped), two papers, a midterm (which was open note), and a final (which was take-home). He doesn't use slides when he lectures, so you have to attend and pay attention, but he's super engaging and knows what he's talking about.
Probably the best prof I've had so far, the lectures were super engaging and interesting. The class was super easy, attendance isn't required but definitely needed to do good on the assignments.

Matthew is a great professor who had engaging and thoughtful lessons. The course material was super interesting and had many different types of readings. Most of the grades in the class were 6 pop quizzes, 2 papers, 1 midterm, and the final. Overall, he was very lenient on deadlines and allowed extensions. I definitely would take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Norton is undoubtedly the best professor I've had at UO. The content he provides for reading and lectures is interesting and engaging. He is kind and really cares about his students doing well. I know his classes fill up fast so if you see an opportunity to take one with him, I highly recommend it.
Very caring individual, and genuinely funny. Each lecture is rich with useful content, and he summarizes concepts well. If Professor Norton is an option, you must take his course.
Professor Norton is a very engaging professor and is incredibly knowledgeable.

Taken many classes with him, he's the best of the best. I missed weeks of class last term and he didn't pry about my circumstances, he just empathized helped me make a plan to get back on track (I passed with an A-). Go to class and do the readings, but if for some reason you fall behind, you can count on him to help you find a way to succeed.

Professor Norton is awesome! I recommend this class specifically if you've never taken a sociology class before. His lectures are engaging, and interesting. He is a funny and light-hearted professor, definitely take one of his classes if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really enjoy the way he lectures, he has a way of explaining it well so it makes it more interesting. Really understanding and you can tell he wants you to do well, doesn't sweat the small stuff like strict deadlines. As long as you try, you're good!

I wish Norton could teach every Soc class I take. His lectures are so engaging and each class is the perfect mix of lecture, videos/media, and discussion time. He really encourages you to come up with your own ideas about the theories and creates space for you to discuss with your peers. Super chill about deadlines, overall just a great professor!
Super kind guy and wants his students to do well. He cares a lot about his work and you can tell, also very good at explaining and being understanding.

This was my first class with Norton, and I gotta say he is by far the best teacher I have had at UO. He makes the lectures interesting and makes sure to present them in a way that everyones understands the material. He respects his students and is super lenient and understanding with the Covid circumstances. Great teacher, I highly recommend!

I had an amazing time in this class even with the stress of being online. Attendance wasnt technically mandatory but there are surprise pop quizzes so youll want to be there. Plus, his lectures are engaging and helpful so you dont want to miss it anyways! There were papers as well as exams which was a bit heavy but I really enjoyed the prompts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: an amazing professor would definitely recommend. lecture heavy and there are little to any slides so you have to pay attention to what he says, but the information is very interesting and he really cares to make sure students understand and learn the material. very forgiving during COVID.

Norton was kind and respectful with engaging lectures. Only two mandatory discussions, with multiple options for how to take exams if one method did not work for a student. Great guy and great professor!
Super easy and he actually cares about his students and is very flexible so his students succeed! Loved the class too
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: By far one of the best professor's at UO and in the SOC department in general. He's very clear/educated on the material he's teaching and talks to you during lecture, not AT you, which is super helpful. If you do the readings, and ask for clarity during office hours, you are guaranteed to pass with an easy A. The only con is the group work.

Prof. Norton has been one of my favorite professors at UO. The class was super interesting. I was never bored and his lecturing style was great-he's super easy to listen to. He is extremely approachable, understanding, and respectful, and he genuinely cares about his students' concerns. He was willing to give extensions on papers/exams if needed.

Prof. Norton has, by far, been the best professor I've had. He makes this class so interesting AND open. Some of the subjects can be tricky topics to teach because your personal views can get in the way (controversial or sensitive topics) but Norton teaches in a neutral way. He is so easy to learn from and listen to during lectures.

Norton is a very good teacher. For the most part the class is very free, as students have a lot of say in what they want to write for the assessments. That being said, the assessments can be quite time consuming so it is good to start early. Also it is a plus if you get a good GE, since they grade all of your work.

Professor Norton is an amazing teacher. Sometimes his lectures can be boring but it's easy to get a good grade and he doesn't take attendance. The only things that go towards your grade are the papers/take home tests. Every once in a while he will hand out a worksheet to do in class but they're easy and he does it like every few classes.

This is a really interesting course and he teaches it very well. He gives every opportunity for the student to succeed. The Assignments are on the easier side and material is easy to understand. He gives sections to read but its just over what hes already talked about so if you do not understand just read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Fairly easy course, and straightforward lectures. I wish that he uses powerpoints more, his visual aids are fairly minimal, when he does use them. The midterm/final are short answer/longer answer, not multiple choice, but if you focus at all in class in regards to readings, you'll be okay. 6 quizzes, drop the two lowest scores.

One of the best teachers I have had here. He talks a lot but it is engaging and kept my attention. I learned a lot in this class but felt like it wasn't too difficult. Definitely recommend. Seems respected and caring.

Professor Norton by far is definitely one of my favorite professors at UO. He has a great personality, is extremely intelligent, and sounds like Aristotle when he teaches. This class was awesome and really made me look at the world so much differently. 10/10 would recommend taking.

There are six random quizzes but only 4 are graded. There is 2 papers but as long as you pay attention in class, there is no reason why you wouldn't do well on them. The midterm was pretty easy as long as you did the study guide and paid attention. I wish there were more powerpoints as they are easier to study from them memory from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Doesn't use slide shows or any visual media when he lectures. It is purely him lecturing at you, and you taking notes. There's a midterm and final, and 6 pop quizzes - but he drops the lowest 2 quiz scores. Two papers - very straightforward.

Very chill class - interesting lectures, easy grading, and no homework at all. Just two take home tests and two in class tests - all of which you pretty much get to decide what you write about. Take this for an easy A that's also interesting!

Matthew is such a great teacher: he's funny, kind-hearted, and very sweet. Soc 204 is one of the easier Soc classes, and he made it so much easier to understand! All of his exams are either open-note or take-home. Easy class, fun teacher, cool lecture material; if you want an easy A, take this class with Mr. Norton!

He care's a lot about his students and it's clearly shown through his teaching style he is always willing to go back to explain something. The essays are very simple despite being about 3-4 pages long. Midterm is also very simple thanks to the study guide he provides. I was able to study for entire midterm the night before without reading to get A+

Professor Norton is a very caring person. He often rambles and moves quickly in class but he always posts the class slides and the in class exams are open note. It's an easy A if you just show up to class and listen. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him for SOC 204, SOC 380, and SOC 465 and he is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had here at UO. He really cares about his students, and the readings he assigns are always very interesting. I also learned a lot in his class, and he always makes class concepts fun and engaging. Would take a class with him any day.
my favorite professor at this university. i took both 380 and 480 with Matt and i learned more than i could have ever imagined. 10/10 professor, 10/10 guy.
one of the best professors ever. he's a humble genius that deserves to be recognized for empowering his students to excel. He is amazing

I loved Professor Norton, he obviously cares about the material he teaches as well as his students. He is very approachable and flexible. In order to succeed in this class, you MUST read and pay attention during lecture. I liked that we were not required to purchase a textbook
Very interesting lectures and not a ton of reading.

Professor Norton was great! Loved the topics we discussed and his class helped me realize I want to minor in Soc. Dropped our lowest grade out of five assignments and discussions were really interesting.

Super easy class, especially for an intro course. Have over 100% in the course and he drops your lowest score from a  pool of 4 tests/1 paper (basically not taking my final). Class is easy and posts all lecture notes online.

This class is super easy and the professor is awesome. As long as you go to lectures (And by go to lecture I mean that I went to 70% of them), and take notes there, you're golden. The topics he introduces are super straightforward; however, if you are confused he gives great examples during lecture so there's no way you won't understand.

Prof. Norton may be the best Soc teacher at UO. Had him for Soc310 and now 380. Class consisted of 6 quizzes lowest 2 dropped, midterm, 2 essays (4-6pgs) and a final. All readings posted online, no textbook.  His lectures are always interesting and he breaks up the time very well. I'd take any class with him. This class is an easy B, and possible A

one of the best professors of my academic career and definitely in the sociology department. the way he teaches you things, the way he phrases the info just make total sense and studying for tests and quizzes wasn't necessary because the way he teaches you can't forget. hard to explain, but listen... take this professor

Norton is the best. 6 quizzes, drops 2 lowest. Two papers, midterm and a final. He makes boring topics interesting and is a very good speaker. Some said his class was hard. It wasn't. Show up, listen to the guy, and go through the readings and you'll do well! Best Soc prof here. I learned so much from him. Will take any and all classes with Norton
Great prof!
Professor is a fantastic teacher. He is very fair, explains what he's teach and he's easy to talk to.
Best teacher I have had at the U of O!

He really loves what he does! Took him for 310 and had no interest in Political Soc but wanted to take another class with him! He makes you work hard but hes really reasonable and willing to help as long as you show understanding and read! You should take his course he makes uninteresting things seem interesting
Great lectures, clearly very passionate, but also wants you to be interested in the material as well. Very approachable and helpful if you reach out to him. Would highly recommend this professor!!!

He's a fantastic teacher and encourages students to elaborate and engage in topics. He knows a lot about his class and is great at determining wether or not the class is understanding the lecture. Absolutely take this class! He does pop quizzes so attendance is recommended.
The very best instructor in the Soc dept. Take any class you can. Try not to develop a crush. ;)

Professor Norton is great. Take any class you can from him if you are a Soc major and you want to actually learn the material.  He is very approachable and has a relaxed teaching style.  He never goes off on rants, which I love.  He is super intelligent, yet humble--the best kind of professor.

Awesome teaching style - open note tests! The material is HARD, but he does a wonderful job of going through examples in class so you understand how to use the formulas. Attendance is not mandatory, but he doesn't post notes online and the notes are essential to do well on the test. Definitely one of the best Sociology professors I have had.

Amazing teacher!!! The class material is horribly boring, but he created activities so that we could get participation points and to help us understand. For a class I never wanted to take, in teaching abilities, he is one of the best teachers I have ever had.
Amazing teacher, makes things super clear and has interesting lectures. Highly recommended
He is definitely one of my favorite professors here. I love the way he teaches the class. He is very nice and helpful. His lectures are far from boring and makes the readings easy to understand.

Professor Norton is without a doubt my favourite professor I have had thus far. He is incredibly knowledgable and passionate about his field. This class was incredibly interesting and I learned a lot. Professor Norton flawlessly integrated the class with group discussion, readings, videos, and even NPR articles. Strongly, strongly recommended.
Awesome professor - genuinely passionate and interested in what he's teaching.

Professor Norton is the best teacher I have ever had. He makes a topic that isn't extremely interesting relatable, exciting, and clear! I STRONGLY suggest taking a class from him! He is reasonable with what he expects, easy going, and extremely helpful!

Probably the best professor I've had.  Very good at incorporating discussion and group activities into lecture, and excellent at facilitating discussion and engaging students.  Expectations on tests and for the class in general were clear, and he is a fair grader.  Highly recommended.

he has great perspectives other than the fact that he teaches his opinions as facts... meaning he gives lots of info about marx. To which.. he for sure is marxist. if you like socialism/communism, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Oscar appeared to be very unfamiliar with the expectations for some of the assignments. He was extremely hard to get a hold of and was very convoluted whenever replying. His feedback on assignments was also very hard to read and convoluted. The class itself was easy but he made it much more complicated than needed.

Oscar Ralda's class "Philosophy and Literature" is easily one of the best classes I've taken at U of O. The way he structured it, heavily focused on reading and writing, helped me understand the readings in a much deeper way. The readings assigned in class were fascinating too! His lectures and questions were always thought provoking as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Philosophy 101 with him, as I was interested in the subject and expected to learn a lot. Instead, this class is essentially a rant on modern politics. Rather than discussing actual philosophers, we largely talked about political issues where Oscar presented his opinions as facts. If you'd like a class that preaches socialism, take this.
Oscar is a great GE! He always explained readings and allowed room for discussion. There is a calm presence about him that makes him approachable.
Talks a lot about philosophers and gets really boring. He even messaged us on canvas absolutely no electronic devices are permitted in class, instead of just saying it in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was very passionate about the topics that we covered. It was my first philosophy class so at times I struggled with determining the meanings behind the texts. However, he was very thorough and very respectfully disagreed with difficult students, I appreciated that about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Young grad student so he's a real hip dude who's much better at relating to a young undergrad than the average crusty old professor. Does not tolerate skipping which I feel is appropriate in a studio class. Good at making you think in new ways and very patient with all students. I got C+ but that's because I blew off all the written assignments.

Drew was a very interesting and helpful teacher. He teaches the 100 level in art so he gets all types of students, but I felt that he was very patient and funny. Some of the projects were kind of hard, but he got us all through it and I felt like I really learned a lot in his class.

Drew's a weirdo, but really fun to have class with. He's good at expanding your mind and making you create art in ways you haven't thought of before. Sometimes he's not very clear, but you can always ask him to clarify.

Xiao was an amazing TA, he explained the material very well when the professor had trouble simplifying Ancient Greek philosophers. He is a hard grader though, but he is willing to work with you if you talk to him.

Had him as a GE for Latin American Philosophy w/ Vallega. Xiao must do the readings several time, because the breadth and depth of his philosophical knowledge and contextualization is unparalleled. He works hard + provides excellent feedback on papers. During section, he lectures more than usual, but it helps you understand the finer concepts. 5/5.

One of the best GEs I've had at UO. I had Xiao for my philosophy in media and pop culture class. He knew how to build off the material taught in class and really made the discussion section very enjoyable. He was also very approachable outside of class. He is a really cool dude overall.

Xiao is one of the best GEs you can get in the Oregon philosophy department. He reiterates the main points of the reading and provides supplementary lectures, while still maintaining an engaging class discussion. He is a very fair grader and will leave substantive feedback for your next week. Very flexible, easygoing, and intelligent.

She's incredible. She was flexible with final papers during the last few weeks because she is well aware of the crunch. She brings in stellar GTFs that care about film and students. She brings in scholars and professionals to go more in-depth during discussions. It really isn't a hard class, but the Mid-Term and Final require serious studying.

Professor Ovalle was great. She realizes what students are going through and does all she can to make class easier you. She regularly asks for student feedback through iclicker questions and always listens to it, as she often structured tests around that feedback. Can be a little unclear at times, but she knows what shes talking about
Her teaching style is not very direct or clear. She doesn't really go over the material very well.
Sometimes class can be a bit disorganized, but she really does know what she's talking about and at the end of the day does a good job of conveying that information to the class.
knew material. tough love with student athletes.  loved 265 with director of cinema Michael Aronson, all around better professor.

Professor Ovalle clearly knows what she's teaching, but nobody else in the entire class has any idea what she's talking about until the day of the exam.  Everyone basically tones her out or skips class altogether and reads the book and powerpoint before exams.  Read these very carefully if you want a B or higher and attend 30 mins of screenings.

Why are there hardly any positive reviews for this woman? She's professional, clear as crystal, always prepared, manages time well, and showed mostly excellent films. Yes, there's a lot of material to be covered in a film history course and you will need to work for an A, but that's college for you.

Her exams were ridiculous! Be prepared for slide identifications, short answers/essays & multiple choice questions based on insignificant material from the textbook that you just wouldn't expect to be quizzed on. You'll probably do well on the exam if you read the chapters 3 times each and take hours and hours worth of notes. Good luck.

The way she taught class was really engaging. You could tell she really loved this subject. Her slideshows were very clear. The midterm and final were easy if you payed attention and did the readings.
Just bad, doesnt even speak loud enough for the first row to hear her

I have enjoyed this class and thought the lectures were good and the films shown in class were interesting. I found it very frustrating that assignments were not returned for weeks at a time and the only feedback we got was a few sentences on Blackboard. This made it very difficult to learn from your mistakes and improve your work.
She is a hard grader and talks really fast. She is pretty helpful though and makes the movies watched in class pretty interesting.

She made the class bring nametags to class. Her class discussions were terrible, because she was always looking for a specific answer and did not let students speak their mind. A large chunk of the grade is a group presentation. This teacher seems very amateurish and fresh out of school; she comes off mean, as if trying to prove herself.

Victor was an excellent professor and was very knowledgeable regarding class material. Like all upper-division math classes, the course is lecture-heavy with long homework and challenging material. The exam questions were straightforward and in line with the class content. Go to class, learn the material, and everything is manageable. Fun Class.

I greatly enjoyed his class, it was probably one of my favorites of my college career. He has a large amount of knowledge and familiarity regarding class material. Very interesting and straightforward lectures. Asks for any questions on the current topic before moving on. Would love to take another class with professor Ostrik!

Victor is super dope, he is so great with partial credit and really understands what he's talking about. His accent is not as bad as everyone says trust me. As long as you complete the homeworks and study for midterms you will do fine!

Super hard to understand concepts in lectures because he went so fast and contradicts himself a lot. My whole class is failing, yet he won't curve anything. The homework is graded for credit based on the correctness of 10 random problems that he selects and doesn't tell you. My classmates cried and even gave up on the midterm.

Incredibly tough to understand, ended up skipping most of his lectures because I never learned anything. Two midterms, one final exam, webwork, and discussion worksheets every week. Would've done better if I didn't have to teach myself everything.

He is a little tough to understand, but luckily the content is all in the textbook and posted on Canvas. If you really focus in class, try to understand, and do work outside of class to understand the concepts you'll be just fine. The tests aren't that challenging and there is a lot of help available for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The tests had good curves to them but you can't really understand him. The lectures were relevant but didn't really matter that much because you just learned stuff from your discussion leaders. I think he could be better than a lot of math teachers but he was not amazing. Lots of webwork.

I never went to a single lecture because I never learned anything. I ended up going to tutors instead. Lots of webwork, 2 midterms and a final. Discussion worksheets are better done with a group. He's really hard to understand, which discouraged me from going to the lectures. Be ready to teach yourself a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I never showed up to class and I would cram study 2-3 days before the 2 midterms and the one final. I thought that midterms 1 and 2 were very easy to learn all the material the day before if you set your mind to it but the final was rather tough. Mr Ostrik is a really nice guy, sometimes a bit difficult to understand with his accent.

He was a good Professor, but he always seemed to be inconsistent in lectures. Jumped from topic to topic and moved on quickly. If you already have a grasp of statistics or are math savvy, I would recommend his class because it is easy. However, if it is completely new material and you struggle with math, I would recommend a different Professor.

Extremely thick accent that makes it impossible to understand him most of the time. This isn't his fault, but rather the schools. If you don't like math, don't take the course with him. If you have to, be ready to teach yourself everything. The discussion section assignments are pathetically easy and don't prepare you for the test at all as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Actually cannot understand 75% of what this guy says. The accent is one thing, but he rambles with "well" and "uh" between every other word. Complex concepts just get dropped into lecture and his train of thought jumps all over the place. My GE grades extremely hard and the only thing he does in discussion is pass out the worksheet. Don't recommend

seems knowledgeable, but rambles too much about complex theory that isn't even on exams. Boring lecture, hard accent, and has bad handwriting that is sometimes illegible when copying his notes. Sometimes he doesn't even cover what is on the worksheets in time for doing them. Discussion leaders are more help than himself most of the time
VERY TOUGH LANGUAGE BARRIER

Homework was sometimes a week ahead of lectures. Jumped around during lectures which could be confusing. Grader was very harsh. I dropped the class because I got sick and couldn't study before the midterm, which I probably would have failed regardless and needed a good grade on to balance out homework.

His accent is a little hard to understand. Attendance isn't mandatory because he posts all his lecture slides and solves out the example problems. I think this class could've been taught online. He has great notes however doesn't teach you how to use calculator functions for stats so you have to solve the whole equation out.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Language barrier was tough at first but don't be discouraged. Make sure that you show all of your work, even silly work because they are very strict graders. 243 was pretty straightforward and so I felt like he explained the concepts fairly well.

I stopped attending class after awhile because its hard to understand him but the material is pretty easy so you can learn from the lecture notes yourself. There is a lot of homework but its worth the effort because it better prepares you for the exams. The exams are short and fairly reasonable.

Honestly? I've showed up to 3 lectures at this point and I have no problem. My suggestion is to look at the lecture guides he posts on canvas. The guides mention everything you need to know and then you don't need to understand his thick accent.

This was an advanced class, but he went extremely fast. He liked to write few details on the board and say paragraphs out loud, so it was easy to miss stuff. So, read ahead if you can. He also isnt that great in office hours, but he is patient and willing to help, which makes up for a lot. His accent is fantastic. Youll understand it after a day.

Ostrik's a beast. Super chill, really intelligent, and does a good job explaining. Used to teach at MIT. The accent takes some getting used to, but is understandable. However, he worked in some algebra stuff that may have been advanced/difficult for a basic ODE class. Recommended for sure, regardless

Go to office hours, he will help! about 4 Quizzes 2Midterms & is consistent with his lectures. It's easy as long as you understand the concepts. Practice and you will do fine. His accent isn't that bad, got used it to within a few days. Easy class. Felt comfortable. He is very good at clarifying confusion. Not good at math, but he made it possible
Takes a class or two to understand him, but after that the class is great! Very helpful and fair with grading.
Nice
No Comments

His accent isn't even that bad as long as you pay some attention to him. He was a very nice guy who was willing to clarify if I had any confusion, and he explained stuff well for most of the time. He sort of made this class a little too broad (and not much depth), but he did make combinatorics interesting.

Although the guy is really smart (he used to teach at MIT!), it is impossible to comprehend is voice because of his strong russian accent! What is sad is that he tries really hard to communicate with us, but he doesn't know how to so he usually likes to end up saying, "I can't really explain this....", or should I say "I chan't wheely esplane DIS"

Elena is very enthusiastic and helpful. She is generous with hints for exams and announces when there will be quizzes. Some spontaneous assignments she assigns are difficult, but overall she is a great instructor.
the best professor, so helpful and relatable. it doesn't hurt that she's hot either

Elena is helpful, enthusiastic, and kind to her students. She has a fun sense of humor and makes the class more than bearable. Come to class a little early though, because she tends to give hints before the class officially starts and you will miss out on important info if you come in right on time or late.
Awesome writing professor. Really clear in direction and expectations, while also very helpful as a professor. Super funny and makes class entertaining. Take his writing classes!!
Best teacher I've had at Oregon so far. Best going away speech ever.
Always willing to help. Fun. He keeps the class entertaining. Always making jokes. Very flexible with student's schedules.
Really funny! He keeps class very interesting- the 2 hours go by really fast.

Pretty energetic about the subject matter, uses lots of videos, which can be cool.  Lots of easy points in case you have trouble with the mid-term or final.  This class is mandatory for all business majors, so it was nice to at least enjoy it!
No Comments
He is a great teacher who truly(!!) cares about his students. If you have a chance, take a class with him
The best professor ever! He actively supports and helps his students and always encourages them. I would love to take his class again next time.

Paul was a great professor to take Advertising Campaigns with. You will need to meet with your group both in class and outside, but most of the time, you will be collaborating with your group on your final project. Very nice guy and wants the best for all of the advertising seniors finishing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul knows everything sport so he does a great job with this class. It was only once a week though and we had speakers every week. I wish he would have given more of his insights but his feedback was always great and he is always reachable and willing to help.
Paul is perfect for a capstone class. He structures deliverables so well and is insanely supportive. I literally would not want to take campaigns with anyone else.

For a class that only meets a total of 2 times throughout the whole term, this guy left a great impression on me and other students as well! He's hilarious, understanding, and really there for you outside of class when working on your projects. This class is built around just group work, but Paul is always ready and able to help which was great!

Paul is a really caring, deeply-involved teacher; he's breathed fresh air into the Campaigns course and works hard to cultivate genuine relationships with his students (and make sure their work is good). Paul is very available to reach outside of class (via email); would definitely take a class with him again.
SAVE YOURSELF

Pradeep is not a good professor at all. He assigned a 92-question homework assignment solely for the purpose of bringing the mean score. Then, we couldn't use that assignment to study for the final. Not a helpful professor at all. Avoid if you can.

Generally, an extremely confusing teacher.  Lecture slides dont really help during tests because they dont have any context or explanations. I had a great grade for most of the term and then messed up a minor calculation on one of the homeworks, and it dropped my grade from a B+ to a C-. I dont recommend taking this class with this professor.

Honestly one of the worst professors i've had at Oregon. He takes a non mandatory attendance when class is supposed to be getting out. Like he will open attendance at 1:50 for a class that ends at 1:50. But if you stay til the end he'll be annoyed. Seems knowledgeable on the subjects, but doesn't know how to teach. Switched requirements for hw.
had to take him twice. Rude and lectures are boring, take with someone else.

Lectures and material were dense and not really presented in a useful fashion. Definitely a figure stuff out on your own class. Test questions were always super tangential to material we covered due to it being open notes and open resourves. Most of the other reviews are right, take another section.
Listen to all of the reviews. I should have. I thought I would be fine. I am not.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things
