reviews.comment: This guy is awful. I was talking people in other 335 classes and they had no clue what we were doing. It's a dense class with terrible lectures that don't explain it. Good luck studying for the test without any actual material. He was also very condescending during office hours saying, "you don't understand this, we did it in class".

The course is well-organized and easy to follow. Even if you are new to R, you can easily understand the course content and gain valuable knowledge, especially in R programming. The instructor is knowledgeable and understanding. He is kind, and it's clear that he cares about his teaching. keep his slides for future reference! they are very useful!

He has an awful accent and in general his lectures are not good. Additionally, he knocks off points for the smallest errors such as spelling which makes no sense considering this is a coding class. He also, is very upset when asks for help and never guides you in the right direction just gets angry and tries to just do it himself.

Pradeep has a thick accent, talks fast often mumbling/running words together. Packs SO much into each lecture he gets rushed/frustrated if the class has > 1-2 Qs.

The tests are very difficult. I am active in every class and have some experience coding, but don't feel prepared.

The homework assignments are unnecessarily long. Rough class...

The homework I often have to figure out mostly on my own as well as many of the concepts because in class it is hard to fully understand what is being explained. There are also concepts on the homework and tests that have not yet been in class and yet again you pretty much have to learn it on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are brutal, tests are hard, often gets frustrated and gives confusing answers to questions. Plus, homework/test questions are easily misleading. HOWEVER, open note tests help a lot, and he is willing to try to explain things to you, even if he doesn't do a good job in his explanation. But, this class was brutal, I'd avoid if possible.

Pradeep doesn't deserve the hate he has received. He cares deeply about his Job teaching his students and allowing them to do well on the homework and exams. He cares about the fairness of the course and can show signs of being upset if requesting an extension but that's simply because of course curving regulations. Exams are mildly hard.

He's ok, class is inherently hard if you don't have experience coding in R or coding in general. There are few assignments so everything is weighted super heavily. He is very knowledgeable about R but a boring lecturer. HW and exam ?'s can be confusing and sometimes will ask about topics not covered at all in the lectures.

Pradeep dislikes teaching and could not care less about this class. His lectures are incredibly fast and rushed through to watch videos that he absolutely loves that have no real implication in terms of course content. Has an incredibly thick accent and is generally rude when answering questions. Take any other section.

Professor Pandem doesn't deserve the negative comments that he has been given, he is a very generous, caring, and knowledgeable professor. He cares about his students, and is very willing to help students who are struggling in class during office hours. As long as you attend class, you will have all of the tools to succeed in this class.

The accent in lectures is too hard to hear, the question descriptions of exams and assignments are vague and easy to mislead students, the emails are often not returned, and the questions of courseware and exams are often wrong

I see some people saying he's easy to get irritated and upset if you cannot understand the concept immediately, and that's 100% true. However, he's a teacher who's super willing to help you outside the class. Flexible to make appointments of office hour even on weekends. But like I said, he has some accent that you cannot understand. Professional.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not very welcoming. Switches rapidly from being overly pedantic on some topics to blazing right through others. Not very good at answering questions, and he audibly sighs in frustration quite frequently. Gets frustrated. Not very helpful, will simply tell you to "figure it out". His code files are quite useful and organized, but otherwise, eh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Gets frustrated if people are not understanding concepts. It was a 400 level coding class in R, and constantly answers questions with "This is a graduate level class so you need to figure it out on your own". Moves incredibly fast through tough topics. Would not recommend taking this professor, save yourself the headache.

He gets very upset/irritated at students who do not understand the material and ask questions multiple times. He is bad at teaching and explaining complicated topics. Does not seem welcoming or like he wants to be there. There is a reason he got demoted from the Honors College.

Raghuveer Parthasarathy is a caring and informative professor who gives somewhat interesting lectures. His assignments and quizzes, though short, can prove to be frustratingly difficult if you are not on top of the work, or if you miss any lectures. Not recommended for those seeking Gen Ed credits, as the coursework can be uninteresting at times.
Never again! I never understood what was happening
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I thought he taught the subject really well, I learned a lot! I found the quizzes, homework and tests to all be very challenging. I recommend not taking this class just to get credit; only take it if you are genuinely interested in the subject.

Amazing professor who explains concepts really well. Yes, the class can be difficult and that is frustrating for students, but physics is meant to be challenging as we apply these problems to real-life scenarios. Highly recommend

He's a nice guy but not always the most interesting to listen to. Quizzes aren't hard if you can remember the simple important facts but homework is more in depth, math heavy, and long. And harder in general.

In my opinion, Parthasarathy could only be described as an OK professor. His class covered only the bland mathematics required to 'do' physics rather than having any interesting conceptual conversations. He also tended to be condescending when students answered in-class questions incorrectly, belaboring the point beyond reason for innocent mistakes
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The good thing is that there are a lot of assignments to help your grade because the exams can be difficult

I really liked this professor. I would recommend going to his office hours. As long as you do the homework and go to class you will be fine. Class attendance is not graded, but it is really worth going to class as you will probably be confused by just the slides he posts. As a non-stem major, I liked this class, the material was interesting.

Take only if your major requires it. NOT AS A GEN ED! Very work heavy. Doesn't accept late work. Which I do not like at all (even for a 100 level class). Laughs when people ask questions as if we should already know this info?!?! 0/10 do not recommend as an "easy science credit". If math is NOT your thing stay away from this physics class!

Professor Raghuveer above all else is a really nice guy. If you went out of your way to attend his office hours, he would recognize your hard work. However, when I would ask a question IN class, he would laugh in frustration. He became passive aggressive if you asked for help at times. I would not recommend this class if it's not for your major.
There are a lot of small assignments, but you will succeed if you do the homework. The topics that were covered were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were super insightful and I probably ended up learning the most in the class compared to others. If you miss a class you will fall behind as he does post slides from lectures online, but he hand writes most of the information during class and youll only beable to learn it if you attend class.

He seems like a fine dude, but he raised his voice at me when I asked for help once, and it made me upset...he also does not take a single assignment for a late grade, which frustrates me to no end; if you forget to do something, that's gonna stay a zero. He does not offer any extra credit options either. Overall, a big source of stress for me.

He covers the material well but when people ask questions he'll say that we're gonna cover it next week. He just gave us a text and gave us 10 minutes for 10 questions. I did them slowly but I pay attention in class so I was not able to finish them on time.

I honestly am so upset that a 100 level course caused me this much frustration. The content seems interesting, but prof explains everything so blandly, and his lecture slides are chicken scratch. this is a physics course and I find it nearly impossible to locate the fundamental equations we use as well. Makes me not want to pursue this field

This is the worst class I have ever taken. Not only is the homework, quizzes and tests impossible to get a good grade on, Professor Parthasarathy will laugh at your confusion. I have heard multiple questions asked and he either laughs at you or gets mad and skips the question. I highly recommend finding another class unless you want to be furious!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I have ever taken. I did the weekly homework with a science tutor and still received almost failing grades on almost every assignment. The professor gets mad when people are confused and tells them to review the material instead of explaining it. Most of my class was confused and was receiving failing grades.

Prof Parthasarathy is a great choice for beginning BS's, his grading criteria is very clear, but do note that graded assignments start right away, so don't fall behind. i have never really been interested in Physics, but his lectures and attitude while lecturing makes the hour fifty lecture fairly enjoyable. Definitely would take agan.

Easy class. Show up, do the work, youll be fine. The guy had it out for me though. Every time I ever emailed him or asked a question he was rude and condescending. Asking for help was not rewarding. Also embarrassed me in front of the class for asking a question about when he was to submit the lecture slides. Never taking a class from him again.

Professor Parthasarathy is by far the best professor I've had at the UO. There is weekly homework that isn't too difficult and the tests are straightforward. He breaks down the information well so it's easy to understand. You can easily see how excited he is to be teaching and how much he loves the subject. I couldn't recommend him enough.

Professor Parthasarthy makes physics very approachable to non-math/science types. He often checks in the with class to gauge how well students are comprehending the material, makes good use of breakout rooms and provides occasional short quizzes to keep everyone on board. He's enthusiastic about the material and personable. Best prof yet.
Ragu is charismatic, and the best lecturer in the physics department I have had yet!

This was a challenging class, but there is a huge curve starting out (88< is an A). Tests were multiple choice/short answer, and there were 2 midterms, no final. Homework was the hardest and most tedious thing of the class... I'd spend hours on HW and get a bad grade. Daily mandatory reading quizzes via iClicker, and missing class sets you behind.

Raghu is super caring and wants all of his students to do well and is happy when they do, but this class was just way too hard. I did okay, but I went into office hours at least once a week and unless you're willing to do this, I don't suggest taking his class

Raghu is a great professor who wants all of his students to succeed. It's pretty easy to do so if you do the assignments and show up most of the time. He's a quirky guy that likes to make jokes during class and makes it enjoyable. If you're taking any physics courses at the U of O, I highly recommend that you take one of his classes.

He is a great teacher who really gets excited about you learning the material. I will admit, if you don't like math and science you might have some issues because his homework is based a lot on the math involved but he cares more about you understanding the setup than the actual answer. Class is fun, and you have to go to pass. I highly recommend.

Lectures and slides easy to understand but in now way represent the Test and Homework which are very hard and he does a terrible job of preparing you for. lectures are a waist of time and he doesn't get that over half the class is failing because of he's inability to teach. seems like a nice guy but would NEVER recommend him as a teacher.

This class was absolutely miserable for me. I was so excited to take an "easier" physics class (aka for non science majors, less math involved) and I was CRUSHED. The first topic we learned was Quantum Mechanics and my emails asking for help went unanswered.

The negatives appear to have taken him for phys classes for majors. In the non-majors class I took with him he was AWESOME. Funny, super clear, he loved us all, always said what great q's we had and was always super excited to teach us. Lectures/readings were interesting and demos were so fun too. I loved coming into his class!

One of my fave professors. Somewhat challenging but he explains things extremely well and loves those who go to office hours. He'll really help you out if you show you're trying! Lectures are very interesting, he saves the "dry" info for the readings (that are all very short). Love the way he structures his class.

Don't take his class. His lectures were so slow and full of information that we didn't need to know for his exams. They were a huge waste of time. What's worse is that he doesn't tell you what you need to know and what you don't. He spams emails (it can go up to 4 a day!) and the day before Finals, HE DOESN'T REPLY.

Every negative comment that I have read has been dead on. Homework is not covered in class and is entirely based on math. His whole class consists of him asking us questions. He makes us do stupid group projects for no reason where we are docked points for not having enough group members or for a few typos. Even though all his work is full of them.

On many occasions he has called the class "undeserving".  I feel like he has the type of personality that believes that he is always right and who ever deviated from his perspectives are complete "losers" It makes me feel less guilty for sleeping through lectures.
Very strict, and the homework and tests are a step up from what's in lecture, both in difficulty and amount of busy-math.  However, the actual teaching is very good.

This professor after the class ended sent out an email to the entire class about what failures everyone is who couldn't understand physics. He yelled that it was a lack of interest and not his bad teaching abilites
Very interesting, clear, and all-around good professor.
No Comments

Prof Parthasarathy has good lectures and typically tries his best to be clear in them but the homework is above and beyond the lectures and most of time was unclear on the intent.  Exams tended to deviate farther from testing knolwedge to testing math skills.  simple errors could cost all points.  Average on an exam 20/50 was common.

Super considerate as long as you communicate with him. Extremely engaging class with group projects that he makes fun. Lectures are engaging and include whole class discussions that make you want to pay attention. Funny and considerate of his students.

His lectures are super boring and never note worthy. Most students have taken maximum half a page of notes all term. As for his assignments, he has unbelievably vague instructions. Not to mention, he'll doc points for things that he never asked for. For example, he'll ask for 15 sources then take points off because you didn't have 40 sources.

Stolpe was an excellent professor, super charismatic and made the material a lot more fun to learn. Discussions in class were always really insightful and got me really interesting in Sports Business as a future career.

Dr. Walker is so passionate and so encouraging of engagement; he also does great impressions when he breaks them out once in a while. I left the last lecture feeling like I was leaving that one awesome class in high school before summer vacation. I loved the class so much, I bought his book just so I can continue learning "from him" over summer.
great professor. mumbles like hell tho. i could understand maybe 80% of what he's saying. lecture heavy, but no midterm/final, only weekly quizzes on readings and 3 essays throughout the course.

Professor Walker's lectures have relevant content, but as a lecturer he's really dry. I found myself skipping classes because I didn't find them helpful to my learning, and ended up just scrolling my phone.
Cool, passionate professor. Seems very down to earth. The weekly quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention and do your homework, and I really enjoyed the case study we did for the final essays.

Lectures can be hard to pay attention to. I passed and didn't do much. Interesting class. Curved the final and no midterm. He can be funny sometimes and it makes my day. Lots of reading (that I didn't do) He's so passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Walker is an okay professor. The course material was very interesting to me, and I normally enjoyed the readings that were assigned. However, the lectures were pretty boring and he often goes on long tangents, making it hard to take notes. This class is easy though, as long as you go to lecture and pay attention you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only reason I didn't give professor Walker a 5 is because he's a bit monotonous, but once you get past that he is a gem! He's BEYOND passionate about what he teaches, brings in real world examples as they're occurring, and is a kind person. Lectures aren't mandatory but discussions are. If you do the weekly readings you will pass the quizzes!
Peter assigns lots of reading but they are interesting. The classroom setting is open and mainly discussion-based. He wants his students to succeed and is an engaging professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Peter is very intelligent, thoughtful, and clearly wants the best for his students. Being an environmental studies major I have taken many ENVS classes, non of which I have loved as much as I did Political Ecology. The lectures were insightful and very thought provoking. Walker fostered an amazing community within our class, and inspired us all.

Classes are lecture heavy, but Peter knows what he is talking about and is pretty good at explaining class material. He can get pretty boring though. A lot of reading but he gives an extensive study guide for the tests so that helps. Pretty easy class overall if you skim the readings and go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are super long and typically pretty boring. Hard to sit through. Your grade is reliant on a midterm, final, and discussion participation. Only good thing about this class is that attendance isnt mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's an easy class. Just skim the readings, and learn the main ideas of each reading and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I didnt understood what was going on 90% of the time. Peter talks the entire 1 1/2 hour leaning barely on a SHORT powerpoint that gives very little information. multiple HEAVY readings assigned each class (ranging from 2-40 pages). grading based soley on midterm / final (80%) and discussion (20%). im dropping this class b4 the midterm. BEWARE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Each lecture comes with readings that are tested on. Some of them are 30+ pages so it's really reading heavy. In class he just goes over the slides, but he is hard to follow and isn't engaging. The tests and the section participation are the only graded things, which puts a lot of pressure on the tests which is super frustrating.

Very knowledgeable in his information. Lectures really arent necessary to go to but still helpful! He puts all his slides up on canvas. Just be prepared to read A LOT. So much reading, but if you understand and study the readings youll do great. Also understand the main themes and how they can be applied to certain issues for the in class essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dude is so monotoned and puts you to sleep with how boring he can make one subject. That being said he was probably the easiest teacher I've had, maybe it was because it was a summer class and he seemed to be just as checked out as we were, but it's hard to not get an A. No exams, papers or homework our grade was attendance & a 2HOUR group project.

This whole entire class is only readings. Nothing from lectures is on the midterm or final so don't even bother going. The midterm and final are the only two grades that get put in. He says you don't need to know specifics about the readings but the final and midterm only cover specifics in the readings. Worst class I have ever taken. DONT take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I usually love environmental studies, but somehow Professor Walker made it the most boring class I've ever taken. The class consisted of lecture, a discussion section and 2 tests, each worth 40% of the grade (and the study guide for those were a JOKE). He definitely knows what hes talking about and is very passionate, just not a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely boring and a huge let down for what could have been a great class. Completely regret taking this class, avoid at all costs.

The class was interesting, but the quizzes were multiple choice and very specific regarding who said what in the readings when Professor Walker said we weren't supposed to know specifics, just general ideas. Good material, but could of had a way better professor.

Most boring professor ever. Needs to take some public speaking classes, lectures are long, he says "um" more than anyone I've ever met and repeats himself ALOT. However the class is super easy if you attend and do the readings you'll get an A. Despite his horrible teaching style, the guy is clearly super informed and passionate and I learned a lot.

I really liked Walker. He's a little long winded at times, but he clearly knows what he's talking about. He does teach his opinion quite a bit but he really tries to preface it with "this is my opinion but ..." Also he does his best to be a unproblematic as possible - doesn't use sexist language, addresses social justice issues, etc. I liked him.

Walker is one of the most boring professors I've ever had. I feel guilty for paying hundreds of dollars to hear this guy ramble about his own interpretations (mostly all elementary- undergrad in nature) of sustainability and the readings he assigns. He poses a question, that he then answers himself, giving no chance for class input. TERRIBLE PROF
Some people had a problem with Walker's teaching style. I loved the subject so I was engaged. If you do the readings, you'll ace the course. They are worth reading. Very interesting.

This class was REALLY easy to do well in and extremely difficult to stay awake in. Felt like I was taking Walker's opinion on envs studies. He's not so great on time management during his lectures will spend the most time on the topic he feels is more important. Would not take any of his classes in the future.

Peter has been my favorite teacher so far. If you are interested in Environmental Studies 201, don't listen to any other reviews and take the class. You will be happy you did. The people who thought it was boring were lazy and obviously didn't care about the material.
Not too terribly difficult if you can manage to stay awake during lecture and skim the readings provided.
very enthusiastic.  readings are important because many quiz/test questions are on them.  he selects interesting articles.  very liberal.  good instructor

i thought his class was boring. you definatly need to READ all the readings that he assiagns if you want to pass....his class is kinda hard! be prepared...the final was a bit challenging...he took it all from the assign readings and the lecture he gave. GOOD LUCK..YOU'LL NEED IT! dONT TAKE IT IF YOU DONT HAVE TO...ITS NOT WORTH THE TIME
He was very passionate about what he was teaching. smart and funny.
Very passionate and informative
Really passionate about his subject! You will learn and get your eyes opened to the world! I def. reccommend taking his classes!

The beginning environmental studies class was awesome. Professor Walker is very passionate about the material and likes to stimulate discussion  even in a big lecture class. I loved his enthusiasm. Some people thought the class was difficult, but it is definitely managable if you try.

Laurel is a very passionate lab professor and her pre-lab lectures are genuinely helpful. The labs are fun but lab reports are graded pretty tough however you can get them checked as long as you can make it to office hours. Laurel makes lab accessible, informative, and inviting. Lab balances out the tough exams well.

Laurel is so so so helpful for the lab portion of BI281H. She is by far the best lab instructor I have ever had and I love that she is actually IN lab unlike the chemistry profs. She is also so helpful in clearing up things from lecture that we didn't understand.

I can tell that Laurel is in it for the students - she is truly passionate about teaching. I can attribute much of my success to Laurel's robust explanations, which were often more effective than those of the main lecturers.

She also happens to be a wonderfully kind and patient person.

Laurel is an amazing instructor.  She cares a lot about her students and works to foster an inclusive and fun learning environment.  This class is difficult, but the lab is the best part!  I am actually really sad I'm not taking Bio 283 because I'll miss Laurel and her labs so much!
Passive aggressive most of the time, outright rude the rest of the time.

Laurel is the most entertaining lab instructor I've ever had! It's clear she cares both about her students and their success in lab. She has been nothing but accommodating and kind, I've learned more in lab than in lecture under her guidance!

Laurel is the best!! I'm so glad I have her for the next 2 terms for bio 282 and 283. Make sure you always print out your lab before hand, and keep in mind that the accelerated bio is a hard class. Laurel is super helpful and really nice though and she explains stuff in ways that make sense both in lab and during office hours. Love laurel!!!!!
Laurel is a good lecturer and is very knowledgable and helpful when you need it. She can become a bit condescending if you ask questions regarding thing that are answered somewhere on canvas.

Laurel is relatively laid-back and is always willing to help. She is an amazing resource and it would be silly not to use her to clear up any questions you may have. Her lab lectures are a strong point.
Shes very intelligent and great at explaining material and concepts. love her!

I took this class over summer and she is honestly the best professor I've had so far. She explains the material very well and is always down to meet with you 1 on 1 if you need help. The Friday quizzes weren't too bad just make sure you take notes and you should get an A. Go to the optional lectures they are very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Laurel is very skilled at explaining things, and was helpful and friendly in lab. I think she would be even better in-person too.
Shes the only reason why I got an A in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are a lot of comments from spring 2020 but I dont feel like that genuinely reflects Laurel's teaching ability. Even online, she listened to feed back from her students and was very accessible. While TAs did provide more office hours she was always available whenever I had a question, had funny easy lectures and will change grades if convinced
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: There were two professors and they did nothing the entire term. Total waste of time. Made quizzes hard and basically told students to figure it out themselves with TAs who are hardly experts on the topics.

Does not care about student success or learning. Simply cares about assigning busy work to make sure students are "working" for the term credits. Quizzes have NOTHING to do with the homework, lectures or practice quizzes. Be prepared to teach yourself way more than any other class. BI212 was a lot harder than this class but I got an A in that class
Very great lab instructor for the honors bio 28x sequence. Makes sure you understand all the material, whether in lab, class, or office hours.

Laurel is one of my favorite professors at UO! I had her as a lab instructor for all 3 terms of the honors bio sequence. She is great at explaining stuff in a way that's easy to understand, but not dumbed down. She is also super considerate of her students and works hard to make her lab the best learning environment it can be for each student.

Laurel was a really good lab instructor for BI 281H. She was very helpful both in class and out and was really easy to reach. The subject material was hard, but she made it accessible for all students and answered questions in a constructive manner. She is also very nice and very approachable, and I would recommend taking a class from her.

She's the worst professor I have had at UO.  She loads students up on high school level busywork - we literally had something due (midterm, research papers, homework) every day for a few weeks - but rarely is it relevant or helpful.  She always seems surprised and disorganized, plus pulls her lecture questions verbatim from other textbooks. AVOID!

The main thing that kills this class is the readings. The readings she assigns are extremely long and will be on weekly quizzes. There are only two a week in theory but some questions on the quiz will come from bonus readings so its more like 4-6 reading per week. The quizzes are very hard but too be fair she does let you have one retake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This professor was by far the worst one I have had in college. She only cares about her research and was incredibly vague with instructions. She'd claim stuff would be graded a month before they were and gave most of her seniors graduating bad grades on the paper the night of graduation. Very unprofessional/would take so long to respond to emails.

Weekly quizzes were incredibly difficult, even if you went to class every day and did the readings. The concepts were generally easy to understand and she did an ok job at explaining things. Expects you to have background info in developmental psych. Final project is very intense and requires to do a large community service-based volunteer project

Awful class. She seems nice but has no idea how to structure a successful course. Nearly impossible weekly quizzes, giant group project/presentation (you have to do community service), and the most insane essay requirements ive ever seen. Take this class if you want to lose your mind and get daily panic attacks. Do better, Prof Pfeifer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: A mess. Constantly confused by her own slides and how to use them. Large group project that you get class time every day to work on, but even then, she was lost in setting everything up. Amount of readings given is absurd. Group project, midterm, final, and 10 question of the days are what you're graded on. Puts mean questions on midterm. Beware.

Dr.Pfeifer is a great professor! She brings her enthusiastic to her class every time and shows her interests in this subject a lot. Her tests are relatively hard but fair, only if you do all the readings and attend the lectures you can do well on the tests. Hightly recommended!

Dr. Pfiefer is an extremely helpful, nice lady and a great professor. Her lectures are easy to follow, and you can tell she is really interested in what she's teaching, which helps a lot. Definitely recommend Child Development from her.

Jennifer is a great professor. Her lectures are very clear and easy to follow, and if you do get a little lost, she is genuinely happy to meet with you and help. The class itself is heavy on reading material, and you must do all of them if you hope to do well on the tests, but everything is pretty straight forward.

Jennifer is a great professor. Her lectures are very clear and easy to follow, and if you do get a little lost, she is genuinely happy to meet with you and help. The class itself is heavy on reading material, and you must do all of them if you hope to do well on the tests, but everything is pretty straight forward.

I'm sure Jennifer is a nice, good-hearted person, but that doesn't mean she is qualified to be a professor. Seemed just as uncomfortable, unconfident, and inexperienced teaching her PSY 478 class as she did in her PSY 376 class; this really deducted from the class for me. Also has a very difficult time adequately answering students' questions.

Very knowledgeable professor. Her lectures are clear and interesting. This term we did not use a textbook and had assigned 2-3 research articles per class, which to me is too much. However, her tests are fair and her assignments worthwhile. It is difficult to get an A with so few points in the class.

Dr. Pfeifer is a great teacher.  She doesn't make it easy for everyone to get an A, and people resent that, but her tests are fair, and her lectures are engaging.  She is extremely helpful outside of class, and genuinely cares about the material and making sure that students understand it.

Ok, So before I signed up for this class i read the reviews and i figured oh great this is going to be HELL, but it wasnt that bad. You HAVE to read the text and go to lecture and the quizzes are worth alot, and she was kind of rude the first day but she changed her attitude QUICK, I think she realizes that people have lives!

I'd heard bad things about her and her teaching style before, but it sounds like she's changed her method of teaching and testing style. She's really nice, really tries to make sure everyone understands the material. Helpful as well. I recommend taking a class from her!

Ignore what others are saying. She is a good teacher, she does allow accomidations and has made them throughout the term. She is helpful outside of class. However, she does hold you accountable for info from the lecture and text reading. So if you consider that unreasonable than maybe you shouldn't be in college!

This lady is mean! Quizzes worth 60% of ur grade r on Sunday nights 7-10pm thats it only time to take it. So if you work, your screwed. She makes no accommodations for anyone, if you can't see the PP well then to bad for you.
super hot, definitely worth the class just to look at her..

I did not think this teacher was good at all. She spent more time talking about how much better her students were at UCLA than we were. Her tests were long and I felt she was trying to make it impossible for us to get a good grade. Class average for the first test was a 62%... and no curve!

This class was very difficult. Her teaching method is hard to figure out at first - and then you eventually realize the reason it is so hard is because she holds you responsible for every detail  in the book. You MUST read the book to get a good grade on her exams. She is very helpful in office hours though, and is friendly and genuinely cares.

She seems like the sweetest person ever. She is not. She is very into herself and it has to be her way. Does not give enough time to write down the slides in lecture and when you ask to slow down she snaps at you. Boring lecture.she spent a class explaining why it was our fault 1/2 the class failed the test and not hers.

He has no compassion at all, pretty cold-blooded. He needs to work on his professionalism, actually, he should take the professional development class because he swore so many times at his office hour. This kind of behavior is not acceptable. He made so many mistakes in his codes. Definitely made my life harder than ever. Do not take this class.
You won't like this class if you want to learn python in class.
Nice person, bad teaching.
The class itself is pretty challenging for sure. He is really approachable and good with emails. His office hour is super helpful. Compared to my previous CS instructors, he's the best so far.

First, he's a PhD student allowed to teach, second, this is only a 2 credit class, and yet he literally said he's "flagrantly" ignoring that and giving us a lot more work than 2 credits warrant and it shows. EVERYONE spends all their time on this class, not the other 3-4 credit courses we have. We're not CompSci majors. He's funny otherwise.
BEST GERMAN TEACHER EVER!! AMAZING AND FUN!
She's great! very funny and enthusiastic, made class cool. take 313 w/her, since she loves the book 'Momo'
supi.

Doris is one of the best instructors at the University.  She is always extremely enthusiastic and really cares about her class and her students.  She is always available outside of class and very open to suggestions on how to make the class better.
Doris is super energetic and fun to learn from.  If there were any questions she was not able to answer, she would find out and get back to us often e-mailing the same day.
Best teacher ever!

Whitney made this class as useful as she could because she knew people only took it because they had to. Attendance isn't mandatory, and the work is very clear, and you will get helpful feedback. Overall, she is very caring and approachable!

One of my favorite classes and I'm not even a journalism student. Such a kind and caring teacher. Easy lectures where attendance wasn't required. Clear that she cares about her students and is passionate about the topic she is teaching. Would take her again.
Definitely one of the better professors out there. Caring, understanding, passionate, etc.

Loved this professor so much! She was very witty & had a couple good remarks every class that lightened the mood...definitely needed that some days! Attendance is only mandatory in Week 10, but the lectures were entertaining & fun to go to even though attendance wasn't required.

Dr. Phillips is awesome. I had her for media ethics last term and you could tell she was so passionate about the content. The class was easy and attendance wasn't mandatory, but I honestly enjoyed going to her class because of her lectures and her enthusiasm. Would choose her again as a professor in a heartbeat
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Might be one of my favorite professors at UO, she is incredibly passionate about her work and gives amazing and fun lectures. Her media ethics class ended up having a true crime focus, and was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Very little work and super interesting, makes slides intentionally wordy so you wont fall behind if you skip

TAKE MEDIA ETHICS JCOM 303 WITH WHITNEY! This was my favorite class I have taken here. Such a kind professor who really cares about her students. Loved her class and she is so knowledgeable about true crime. You are doing yourself a disservice if you take media ethics with any other professor!

I've had her for both 311 and 303 & both were extremely easy classes. No attendance policy, weekly reflections, no exams. Depending on if you have a tough GE, you may have to put extra work into your reflections for an A. Whitney is very nice & makes sure the students feel supported. Each class I've taken has been super easy and light workload.

Jcom311, Somewhat lazy teacher, GE did all her grading. If your GE is picky or annoying it could be a hard class. 8 weekly assignments made up 40% of the grade, while two final projects were 30% each. She was just average, idk, nothing stood out and it was a moderately easy class. The way she formats assignments is slightly poor.

This class focused on the presidential election. Whitney is so nice and makes sure every student can express their opinion without any judgment. The work is super light overall and I would definitely take this class.
Not much guidance, a lot of busy work, instructor not very helpful with student concerns.

Completed most of the assignments within the lectures themselves. Lectures were often the full 2 hours, but she was very informed and passionate about the subject. Had to write 1 "paper" at the end of the term to connect the content to outside-of-class media. The structure is easygoing and consistent workload. Whitney is super sweet and awesome.
hands down one of the best professors I've ever had! The way she handles the true crime focus of the class with such empathy was awesome.

She is hands down one of my favorite professors. Such an interesting and compassionate person. Lectures are long and heavy but very interesting. Insightful and thorough. The class made me rethink my consumption of media and increased my media literacy. Came out with so much gained knowledge. Fair grader and genuinely cares about her students.

Whitney is passionate and knowledgable in her research. She's just overall a great person. She does lecture for the full two hours which can be a lot and her slides are a bit sore on the eyes because of how much she writes on them. There's a lot of busy work, but if you just read the rubrics and do the work you're guaranteed an A

Prof. Phillips is a really awesome person who is passionate about what she's teaching. This class is engaging, but the 2 hr lectures are too much, and drag on even if you love what we're learning. This class is hard in spring, as attendance for 2 hr lectures twice a week are mandatory! But love prof. Phillips.

I am usually not one to complain about professors, but in my 20 years of living on this earth, I have never had a worse teacher or professor than this. He is a graduate student, and it is his first year teaching, so I place more blame on the university than on him for assigning someone with no teaching experience (as far as I know) to teach calc 3.

This class on its own is a challenge - especially if you are a freshman with only Calc 1 as experience. This teacher not only wastes most of the mandatory class time but has a thick accent and writes in cursive. Pretty much had to teach myself the material at home. Overall, he's a good guy but the lectures and course work could use some improving.

Seems like a genuinely sweet, earnest guy, but not the best at teaching. He clearly knows what he's talking about, just isn't great at conveying it in a way that's understandable if you're new to it. The concepts themselves weren't too bad once you figured them out, but I pretty much had to teach it to myself with the textbook.
Great speaker and lecturer. Class organization can sometimes be confusing.

not a great experience. while the lectures can at times be interesting, they're very jumbled. irrelevant things are focused on, and when it starts to get interesting, he'll pivot. announcements are also never given for any assignments, quizzes, or essays (thank god for the GEs). class consists of a long lecture, and a 5 min question time.
Wonderful speaker.
Very good at what he does. You're lucky if you get the chance to take a philosophy course taught by someone as brilliant as Professor Warnek.
Incredible, life changing lecturer. Very thoughtful and somewhat inspiring. However, I can see why he would be polarizing. Extremely slow grader which is irritating
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are long, dense, and sometimes hard to follow, but if you apply yourself, you will learn a ton. Professor Warnek is incredibly knowledgeable and thoughtful. This is a life-changing class if taken seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: more of a father to me than my father ever was!

I thought I would glaze this guy till I died, but 320 was a whole different rodeo. Peter is extremely knowledgeable no doubt about that, but this class was way more confusing than his others. Granted this is a difficult subject to teach but still. Please note that he is not a canvas guy. I would recommend him for a winter term class not a spring.
You will think about him constantly. Nobody is more influential on your education than this man. Lots of wisdom to share.

I've taken many philosophy classes at UO and this is by far the worst one. He lectures for 2 hours straight, doesn't ask us anything to stimulate conversation/discussion and expects us to still talk. He brings in irrelevant information which gets very confusing. Dense lectures & he gets off topic a lot. Doesn't know canvas well/no email reply ever
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing. and hot.

This is an entertaining class. Lots to read, but it's all interesting and relevant to understanding religion through philosophy. Unfortunately, he doesn't go through the texts and is prone to tangential digressions, so it will be hard if it's your first time reading them (namely Kant). He also doesn't answer your questions well or directly.
saw this man on tinder. i am 20 years old.

I'll probably glaze this guy until the day I die. His class is very lecture-heavy, but he is extremely well-versed in philosophy. You will walk out of class feeling overwhelmed because many of the concepts he discusses are difficult to grasp, but the small insights you do understand will be profoundly impactful.

Warnek is a captivating lecturer, but he does not follow the course syllabus and spends far too long on small amounts of pages in readings. Very interesting readings and lectures, but a bit repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Warnek is a good dude, with humor and charisma, but I did not like as a professor. He ventured into tangents that didn't support points made. He wouldn't even go over the readings, moreso just his own convoluted interpretation of it. Lectures are unorganized.Grading is painstakingly slow with zero rubric so you are left to guess your grade.
I've seen this guy countless times at the local college bar creeping on undergrads

Had Peter a few times now. His 200/300-lvl classes are similar: 3 papers, 1 midterm exam. Take a familiar GTF if you can. If you take his 400-lvl classes, he only requires 2 papers, no exam. I would like to think he actually reads our work, but I emailed him asking about my grade for Aristotle this term and he never responded. Overall entertaining.

Warnek was an experience! Very interesting content and he worked to make it more captivating. I was crazy overwhelmed at first as this was my first course in PHIL and the culture in his courses definitely feature more involved students than usual. Be confident in yourself but know that the course will likely feel like a lot.

This class was by no means an easy A. Warnek expected a lot from us for a 200 lvl class this winter, but his lectures were amazing. He tends to go off on philosophical musings rather than talk about the readings specifically for the three papers, but he is engaging and hilarious. I'm taking his 312 class this term because he's interesting.

There was only one paper for his Merleau-Ponty class because of the George Floyd protests. Kinda sad I never got to write a final paper. But Peter made Zoom classes really engaging and fun. Classmates sparked interesting discussions. Don't expect to ever get feedback from him though, you don't know your grade until the end of the term.
A smart, interesting professor. Stuff was graded by GEs, which sucked
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Very knowledgable in his field of philosophy, and is an incredible speaker. His philosophy lectures are a real joy to attend.

I loved Professor Warnek's Plato class. He has a dedication to ancient philosophy, especially Plato's Republic and Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics. It can be jarring sitting in his class for the first time, but you'll come to find his classes rewarding and philosophically rigorous. I would highly recommend taking an author's course with him.

I really like Peter as a person. He has been exceptionally accommodating and understanding during COVID and can be really down to earth at times. That said his class is unhinged and out of control. He takes well over 20 minutes to respond to students' questions at times and there doesn't seem to be any structure to what he says in lecture.

Had no idea what he was saying most of the time, but certainly a radical and inspiring speaker. If you take his upper level courses he won't ever update your grades and you won't know what you have in the class until the end of the term. Papers are not difficult, though no rubrics exist in his classes. Very unstructured and disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty disorganized and doesn't seem to care about anything but the sound of his own voice. He posts 20-50 page readings the day before they are due, posted the midterm study guide three days later than he said he was going to. Hasn't updated the syllabus all term and the GEs email/office hours aren't on it either.

Warnek is a true intellectual, a bashful personality, an engaging lecturer, and a comic, among other things. His classes are definitely worthwhile. That said, he has come to be known as class canceller-in-chief.

I dont understand how this professor isn't rated higher by most. I took his 211 course and he is an inspiration to me and my interests in Philosophy. His vocabulary is impressive and his lectures cover the reading so well that you don't have to read every page of the readings. Dont miss class and youll enjoy his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mostly incomprehensible rambler, the only thing he makes clear is how he disagrees with reasonable interpretations. He is off in his own world, Attendance is required for a class you teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awful class. The instructions for papers are vague and directionless. Lectures can barely cover more than a few pages into the readings because of Warnek's arrogance and insistence upon himself. There isn't enough room in the class to engage in a reasonable amount of philosophical dialogue. It feels like we're there to watch him show off.

Warnek doesn't go through the readings in any systematic manner, not does he give appropriate context to the readings. Instead of slides he reads a sentence from a random point of the reading and then goes off on a tangent about it. He operates mostly off of student's questions instead of sticking to the texts and explaining them for papers.

Peter is a truly intriguing gentleman. He utilizes a rather haphazard technique of lecturing his students. Often times he cannot get through a sentence before losing his train of thought. Unlike his other courses, for this course he does not use slides and instead uses his charisma and jokes to entertain students, leaving them to learn on their own
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pete Warnek is an amazing professor if you get to know him. Take his class seriously, it's not for the philosophically weak. His teaching style is a bit chaotic but his course is structured well and you will learn if you do the readings.

Tends to ramble a lot. Greek vocabulary is annoying. The GEs grade very harshly. Pete has trouble staying on topic and doesn't explain material clearly. Be prepared to do all of the reading for yourself.
Good person really, but not friendly for people just start their philosophy life. The concepts he said were too broad and complex. It was really hard to follow when he is talking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Find another professor. His ego is too large for there to be room for students. Lectures are pointless, off topic, without any structure, and entail stories as to why he is so great in his own eyes. I felt like a prisoner. I can't believe I paid for that experience. You write required papers without any rubric, and just cross your fingers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Get ready for the Warnek show. He's in his own world and the rest of the people in the room are just mirrors. He's obviously a smart and nice guy but he's too excited and gets carried away. Dude. Chill.

Warnek doesn't hold back. Personally I loved the challenge and thoroughly enjoyed the course, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who doesn't have any experience in philosophy. Treat it like an upper division course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a funny guy but the lectures consisted of him rambling for an hour and twenty minutes and then asking us to understand everything he just said. Assigns a lot of reading, our GE did all the grading so idk how he is on that
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is extremely hard for a 200 level course. This professor tends to ramble during lecture and its difficult to track his train of thought. It is very interesting though, so if you are a philosophy major or really interested in philosophy you should take it. But other than that I do not recommend for the sake of your gpa.

By far the best class I have ever taken. Everyone should take this class, it will change your life. Warnek is so intelligent that at times the lecture can go over your head but he for sure knows his stuff. Challenging in a good way. Made me a philosophy major. DO IT, trust me.

Very interesting subject.  He was very amusing.  The topic is hard to understand and he is not always very clear.  His powerpoint slides are confusing.  There are no papers, only tests.  It's a hard class, but very interesting.

I've never been so into existentialism after his class! He's a funny teacher and I actually looked forward to attending his class. Sometimes makes up stupid words that don't exist in his lecture. Doesn't grade, GTFs do that. Make study groups with other students. I didn't understand the material expertly but managed to get a B b/c of study groups
I love Professor Warnek. He's taught the first lecture class I could bear at the UO. Not only that, I loved it.
Class content was interesting, yet lectures were confusing. It is obvious Warnek is an intelligent man, but his lectures were confusing and hard to follow.

Maintains his title of scholar  and even has interesting conversation outside of class. Doesn't try to be vague, but it's more that he thinks his students don't get the finer concepts and theories. Thus, he seems to depend on his unctuous charm and carefully chosen attire to woo students.

Peter was very intelligent although his person to person skills are similar to that of a dead chicken. His overall intelligence adds to the dryness of his lectures, you do not even need to attend. Read the material and go to section and you will get an a high grade. As for his personality, Ive seen more in dying whale. Oh and he loves his man-heels
funny...and hot

Professor Warnek is one of my all time favorites. His approach to the ancients is fresh (i.e. he helps us hear Socrates when he sang to us in our moment of anxiety, ah the beautiful 2nd sailing) and his devotion to the Greek Pantheon is inspiring.

I have never had a professor as bad is this man.  He made fun of students for asking questions and he made a large effort to pick and choose material without teaching it as a whole.  Towards the end of the year every other word out of his mouth was****.  He looked terribly uncomfortable lecturing and always stumbled over his own slides.

310 was a total ramble fest. Warnek would just blabber about whatever happened to come to mind. His charisma made up for some of the cheap, crude jokes but the lack of focus was unacceptable. Nearly all lectures were filled with contradictions and vague explanations and 'you get a sense of...' reasoning.
Good

This professor is the worse professor I have ever had. He could engage the material, but often did not. Instead he liked to joke or talk about movies. When he did engage the material he simply ripped off Heidegger and Derrida and claimed thier ideas for his own. He does not really teach and is not avilable to students. Take anyone but him!

Warnek is an absolutely awesome lecturer - he really engages with the material, and all but drags the class along with him. He's not particularly approachable in office hours, however - I found it easier to talk to my GTF if I needed outside help.
He is an engaging lecturer most of the time, but he definitely likes to hear himself talk. Don't ask questions unless you want to be publicly humiliated.
Great character, interesting lectures, good jokes, though not overwhelming often.
Very engaging, clever, funny. Makes you think.
Good

The guy was a great lecturer and he definitely had people swayed in the class.  He definitely gives off a feeling that he thinks he knows everything, which for me is comical anyways.  Don't be to swayed though cause he just like most teachers at the college level who think they're Jesus.
No Comments
No Comments
Hes on point
No Comments

One of the most amazing profs. and classes I have ever had.  A must for anyone interested in philosophy in the slightest.  I wish I could take every class with this professor...intelligent, inspiring, witty, and one who truly cares for his practice and his students. A+
Not only in the class extremely interesting, but the professor is ****ing hott! Oh my...a sexy, intellectual professor? Yes, please!
Really likes the sound of his own voice.
No Comments
This guy knows his stuff! He's not very approachable though :(
No Comments
I'm not even in Prof Warnek's class this term but I think about him CONSTANTLY...just in case any one is trying to get on his good side, call him Dr. Warnek.

This man is brilliant.  He is interested in some of the most important philosophy the world has ever known.  He loves Socrates as everyone should and he knows his stuff.  If you want to push yourself to new levels of thought and challenge your mind in ways few ever do, then Warnek is the man to study with.
Ancient Philosophy was the best class I took in college! Extremely difficult but incredibly engaging.
The best prof in the game.
No Comments

Professor Warnek is an awesome instructor.  His lectures are amazing, he uses a lot of funny analogies, and he totally clarifies really tricky material.  He's just plain fun to listen to and totally good looking.

I really loved Philip as a professor. He wanted students to succeed and was super accommodating. His lectures were slowly paced but used active learning and revisited challenging concepts often so it was really helpful. My only issue with this class was how long it took assignments to be graded.

Philip is a very knowledgeable professor and great at explaining concepts. However, his lecture slides are very disorganized and include lots of graphs and pictures. His exams are difficult with ambiguous, doubled-barreled questions to test your true knowledge of a concept. I did like how he prioritized active learning, but he could be more clear.

I love this man. Lectures are so fun and engaging and he is truly skilled at instructing. Lots of the hphy teaching team says they prioritize "active learning" but I think Phil does the best. He is so smart and knowledgeable and his EBs are always so light. Tests actually test how much you know instead of regurgitating facts from the textbook

I found this class to be engaging since there are a lot of white-board activities and in-class discussions. Phil is great at explaining hard concepts and making them easy to comprehend. He always answers questions in a helpful manner. He is very passionate and overall super nice!

I was worried about taking another class with Phil since I didn't do great in physiology, but this was the best class I've had at UO. Phil is so nice and knowedgable. His classes are a good mix of lectures and active learning. Being in a smaller class with him is a big change from a huge lecture hall, but it's been a fantastic experience.

Labs were definitely boring, but grades were participation only. He does not speed through content in the way Mark did and lectures are recorded so if you miss or need review it is always there. Exams are decent as long as you memorize needed pathways. Pre class assignments will always prepare you for content gone over in class.

Nice guy, but lectures way too slowly and he treats the class like kindergarteners. "Settle down, come together" every 10 seconds. However, he's great at explaining things 1-on-1. Teaching team (not just him) takes forever to grade anything. Every topic in this class other than muscle phys is in BI212, so learn it there and this class will be easy.

Class was kind of boring but overall not difficult. The preclass assignments (EBs) are really what you learn from. The exams are not extremely difficult, but make sure you review the 'learning objectives' during the term. He records attendance through clickers but also records his lectures, rewatch the lectures before an exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't really like Phil at first but he's grown on me; he's kind & pretty accommodating. Go to lecture to understand anything. He says you don't need an iPad but you kinda do. Lab is boring but chill. 2 pre-class assignments every week, plus "mini exams" on Thursdays. Can't ask questions during exams. Some memorization but can also work things out.

Lectures are so hard to follow, he just shows pictures and talks so slow. He also showed so many topics & kept saying "you should know this already" and just never explained them. I'm sorry but a short refresher would be nice instead of me having to go back and look at my old notes. Also, be prepared for "quiet down" at least 10 times every class.

if you do not have an iPad, this class is not for you. He is simply not a good lecturer, and cannot create slides that a student can take notes from. He relies on the fact that students are able to take their notes directly on the slides, which is not an option for those of us without an iPad. He just puts up a picture and expects us to understand.

One of the best professors I have had at UO! He cares about teaching and you can tell he wants his students to succeed. Taking 321/322 is a full time job, so you must attend lectures and study a LOT in order to learn the content. Test questions are pretty straight forward; if you study the learning objectives, EBs, and quizzes you will survive.

Phil is a great lecturer and one of the most kind-hearted professors I've ever had. I had him during covid and had a terrible mental health year-- Philip was so understanding & accommodative, I never felt uncomfortable reaching out to him to ask for help. He is a gem in the HPHY department & should be protected/respected at all costs

Philip is amazing. He has so much on his plate, but will still respond to emails and save an entire lab group from grading mistakes like he doesn't have an entire department to run. He's very passionate and is very knowledgeable. The class is hard though, so you might have to learn to not be a perfectionist if you want to survive mentally.

Professor Matern is my absolute favorite professor at UO. I took this course in person, and his lectures were amazing. The content was well organized. He was highly accessible outside of normal class hours. He would even hold online office hours the weeks of the midterm exams for students to ask review questions. Please take a HPHY course with him!

Dr. Matern is such a great explainer and leads incredible lectures. His lecture slides are very easy to take notes off of and he goes at a great pace during class. If you engage with the material, you can get a great grade in the class. He is also so caring in class and during office hours, and is committed to your success!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Matern is one of my favourite professors and I'm so excited to have him for Physiology I! He teaches the content in a way that's easy to grasp and also very interesting. He is extremely caring and wants you to succeed. Dr. Matern's lectures are engaging and easy to follow along when taking notes. Highly recommend taking HPHY 212 with him!

Phil is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so caring and so obviously passionate and knowledgable about what he is lecturing on. Sometimes his lectures are a little quick, but he posts notes and lecture audio so you can go back. He makes an effort to get to know students and makes himself extremely available outside of class.
Took HPHY 212 over the summer, lots of homework but he makes the lectures super fun and interesting! Grades slowly but grades fairly.

I love Phil! Super nice guy who tries to make it a point to get to know his students. I love his lectures because at the end of each section he goes back and summarizes how everything ties together. He makes getting help very accessible with his NB notes online. Tests are reasonably difficult. Probably my favorite professor at UO

Phil is obviously very knowledgeable and passionate about teaching. His lectures do pack a lot of information and it can sometimes be rushed. However, Phil is constantly holding office hours or you can contact him basically at any hour if you have questions. To do well in the class, you HAVE to go to office hours and really prepare for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great teacher but grading takes forever. Start studying early! LOTS OF MEMORIZATION. You have to learn the synthesis/breakdown pathways for glucose, glycogen, fatty acids, protein, & how they all connect. There are two easy 2-page debate papers w/ two 1-page rebuttals, & a 10 min presentation on a diet of your choice, each w/ a different partner
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures were soooo boring. We had class twice a week for an hour and a half but the class seemed to take ages because the class was so boring. His tests are hard especially because he didn't have practice tests so it was hard to know what to expect. Weekly quizzes were really hard too. He does have lots of office hours though and seems nice
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He was organized in his 371 class, but this class he was behind on his grading all term. It was an easy and interesting class, but I didn't get my first grade till after week 8 and the class itself was somewhat disorganized. The topic was super interesting and it was easy so I definitely recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great knowledgeable teacher that made this class very insightful and enjoyable. Respected and entertaining professor. Well organized lectures and clear course expectations. Definitely recommend this teacher for whatever class he teaches. If I can, I plan to take his Physiology of Exercise.

Phil is awesome. I took him for Biostats this summer, and I was impressed. Going into the class I didn't think I'd enjoy the subject, but he presents it in such a way that makes it interesting. He also teaches HPHY 371 Physiology of Exercise. Definitely recommended if you want a clear, concise teacher who is organized. Very helpful too.

Philip is a really great, clear, and knowledgable professor. The way he presents the material is very clear cut and elegant. Let's be honest, biostatistics is not the most interesting subject, however, Philip does his best to make it engaging and interesting. Getting a good grade in this class is easy if you pay attention and turn things in on time

If you want to do well in this class you need to show up and do the work. Incorporate all of the feedback you get and don't get too attached to your creative vision if you can help it. Participate fully, ask for clarification if you need it and be a good team member!

She's tough, but she's going to tell you exactly how to succeed in the film industry. This class was awesome and introduced us to so many fields and so many industry professionals. Nearly daily homework, but it won't take very long and it's interesting/important.

Knows her stuff as someone who's been through the whole Hollywood thing. Gives some truly brutal feedback sometimes, but is there to help you improve and will grade generously if she sees that the effort is there. Super funny and entertaining as well, this was a good class despite being taught online. If you want to learn how to write, take this.

CINE 320 Screenwriting. Alissa is incredibly knowledgeable in the field, having worked in producing for 20 years. Her feedback is never sugarcoated (which means her compliments mean the world). There's a good amount of homework, but it's always fun. If you want honest feedback that will teach you crucial lessons in film, Alissa's your instructor.

Ex-producer, still absorbed in the sticky sheen of hollywood namedropping and inside-baseball brio. Brilliantly knowledgeable about any on-set situation imaginable, but often so caffeinated her lectures are hard to parse. Always trying to enunciate 3 equally crucial tips simultaneously. Grades are stupidly honest, some unfair. Snappy but seasoned.

I'll admit I took this class a while ago. Alissa had absolutely no idea how to teach this class. The structure was all over the place, she couldn't even figure out how to work Canvas. She didn't even know how to work the equipment she was grading us on. Missing even one class seemed to be equivalent to the end of the world.

The best film professor at UO! This was my second class that I've taken with Alissa, and I always tell people that they should take at least ONE class with her during their time here. She structures her classes so you feel like you're actually learning. She's legit--I love her insane/hilarious stories from working as a producer for decades!

My favorite class! VERY engaging lectures, and he fostered quality scientific writing. Graded on a presentation and three short papers, and easy post-lecture quizzes.
Only reason I rated 4 is bc the last three weeks were student presentations on jargon-heavy papers. Valuable to learn how to present a complex topic, but super boring to watch others.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took material from a pretty boring textbook and consistently made it engaging by adding in applications of the content in research. Tests were all online and not hard. Perfect class for Neuro majors as he talks about neuroscience research a lot. Would totally take another class from him in the future. Brownie points for being British.

This was a fun class! You can definitely tell he loves cell bio and his lectures are interesting. He takes you on field trips around campus to see some of the equipment used to do research at UO, too. Tests and quizzes are all online.

Wow, I couldn't disagree more with the previous comments. Dr. Washbourne is one of the most engaging lecturers I've had the pleasure of learning from. Each class felt like storytime, and I always felt enriched and inspired by the end. Insightful, individualized feedback was provided for each written assignment, which really fostered scicomm skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy A but very boring. Prof Washbourne was sleepwalking through lectures and it showed. Didn't learn much useful info.
One should avoid this course and this professor. The content is interesting but is presented in a boring, rote manner. Washbourne is sleepwalking through this course as if he doesn't care.
Boring lecturer. Easy to do well.

Teaches cool topics + goes into detail. Detail is often unclear as many examples are figures from his research he is using to advertise to teacher's pets to turn into his lab peons. Taught us over zoom from vacation destinations like swiss alps and is as full of himself as that sounds. If you love stroking old rich white guy egos, take this class!

I took this class over the summer as a four-week long class, so it was a lot of material each week (2-3 chapters per week). However, he let us go at our own pace (read the chapters, chapter quizzes, chapter tests) which was nice (no Zoom lectures). There were 2 midterms and a final. I actually really recommend this class over the summer!!

No tests. Just a MidtermFinal paper, but was a bit unclearconfusing: cares about the style more than content.  A short online quiz on a film. Lectures was interesting at first, but gets dull over time. A few group presentations (not graded) and 1 individual presentation (graded). If you are a great writer, you'll do fine. Harsh grader, has curve
This guy is just fantastic; he has high (and appropriate) expectations for you but his is the one class I would not miss if at all possible.
Easy class taught by an instructor who is more interested in research than teaching. Sometimes is interesting but more than not is dull. Doesn't know the material very well either. Skip this class.

Lecures are very interesting and full of detail so you want to attend class every lecture. he does tend to go off on tangents in side stories but they are interesting and relevant. his tests are by no means easy, he expects them to be clean cut and straight to the point. But if you attend every day there is no reason not to get a good grade.

Love the accent and he's really cute. The text book sucks, it's very convoluted and the worst part is that he bases his lectures off of the worst textbook ever written. This makes his tests hard because his questions tend to be vague so even if you answer the question, you'll lose points for not mentioning things that weren't even asked.
Distractingly hot! Knows his stuff. Fair tests. Fair grader.
No Comments

Speranza was a decent professor for the number of students he teaches. There are definitely a lot of biases against him and he could be very arrogant, however, I personally learned a lot from his class. It is also not too difficult of a class and very manageable if you stay on top of your work.

I have never met a man more conceded in my life. He stood on top of a students desk and on his model. He said he can't teach us water colors without a brush, because some students forgot their mice at home that day. I agree students should have their mice, but if you can't teach without it you shouldn't be allowed to teach a University level class.

Had this professor for ARCH 222 & 484 and had a terrible time during both classes. He is disorganized, irrational, moody, and frankly kinda rude. reviews.comment: Behrooz is a very nice and understanding professor, who lays out the course clearly from the start. His lectures are pretty boring, however if you can focus, he will prepare you well for the midterm and final. Having a good cheat sheet for exams makes a major difference. Retaining the material from BA240 and STATS243 are key to success as well.

Behrooz is not outstanding, but it not horrible either. He is monotone which makes his lectures hard, but he does explain what he is doing. He does mean well, and you can tell he wants people to succeed. I wouldn't reccommend him, but if the course is required he is tolerable.

Behrooz is an awesome guy who cares about his students. He might seem harsh at times but it's because he truly wants you to succeed. He's always accessible and down to help his students (& give points back!). Pay attention during his long boring lectures and you'll actually pass the class. Definitely recommend getting to know Behrooz :)

Pros: Cares about his students, passionate about OBA, material is straightforward, allows a "cheat sheet" on tests.
Cons: Boring lectures, takes a long time to explain simple concepts, sometimes moody (yelled at me to "not work ahead" on in-class activities), doesn't understand how to use Canvas so there are frequent grading errors.

He's a very caring professor and willing to help, but his lectures are extremely boring. The course is very clear and grading isn't too bad. He makes the homework pretty rigorous, I'd say having a decent background in basic stats is neccesary to get a good grade on the homework. Most of your grade is on Final and Midterm.

His lectures are super boring, but the class is not very difficult if you know how to work excel (passed BA 240) and know the basics of statistics (passed math 243). He is a nice person and allowed me to take my final earlier than scheduled. He gets the job done. Two quizzes, a midterm, a final and weekly HW assignments determine your grade.

Pros: daily attendance activities that help check understanding, short weekly homework, open note midterm and finals

Cons: Some material on the homework, as well as midterm and final was not directly covered in class and you had to read the book

Psaki is a great prof., albeit a bit quirky. She cares a lot for her students and the course content. Grades weren't kept on canvas but if you follow the syllabus you should be able to figure out your grade. All in all she's funny, cares a lot, and if you do the work- you will likely get an A.
