Professor Psaki loves what she is teaching and it definitely shows in class. She is very willing to meet with students and has a great sense of humor. Quite a bit of reading, but never unmanageable. Two essays and then a final, but students have the option of writing another essay instead of taking the in class final. Overall not too hard!

All reading was done in English, lectures were in Italian.  Gina is an amazing professor and passionate about what she does.  I did not care for the material in class, but she made the class worth taking and also participating  in.
Gina is very clear in what she expects from her students.  She is also enthusiastic and patients with her students.  Would recommend to any person thinking about or already taking Italian.

Gina is a dedicated and very helpful Italian professor.  Be prepared to read a lot, but if you ever need help, she is more than willing to set aside time to make things clear for her students.  She is full of energy and life, and makes learning more than something one feels is mandatory, but something one can enjoy.

She has an immense passion for what she teaches, which makes learning it all the funner. Her approachability and demeanor are some of the best I've experienced. Her way of teaching the subject matter got me very interested in Humanities. If you do the readings, the class is fairly easy. I highly recommend this class regardless of major.

Professor Psaki is a very kind and funny person, but the subject matter (the Divine Comedy) was incredibly hard.  She does grade fair and offer extra credit, but overall, keeping up with the reading is a must.  I got an A- in this course, but it was the hardest I ever had to work for one in all my years at the UofO.

Prior to taking this class I had no interest in the material. Through her enthusiasm Professor Psaki made this my favorite course.Would definitely recommend her! She is fun, helpful, and entertaining.
Great professor that loves her job. Her lectures are interesting and engaging.

Professor Psaki is amazing! She is a wonderful, engaging, encouraging professor. She is quirky and enjoyable. She is easy to talk to and help you out when you need it. You can tell she loves her job and really cares about her students. I do not recommend skipping her class though, she tends to give a lot of information/details which are on tests.

Amazing professor! She is passionate, easy and enjoyable to listen to during lecture, approachable, funny, and a little crazy (but in a good way). She is my favorite professor by far and I would recommend her to anyone.
Brian was the man. He shifted the curriculum to better suit a college student's passions.
Nicest Professor I've ever had. He is clear about what he wants and very helpful and understanding. His classes are really laid back and easy but you also learn a lot.

Fantastic teacher. Sometimes he goes off on random tangents about irrelevant things but overall he is really great. He is helpful, super nice, and very laid back. I recommend this teacher to everyone.

Really great teacher who is open minded and really gets the students. I personally wished he taught upper divs just so I would take his class. His work is pretty easy, but relevant and he is pretty lenient about late work and whatnot. Always in a good mood which really helps!
Great Guy, Great Teacher, just get involved and you will be fine. Also its awesome because he looks like Leonard from the Big Bang Theory!

He such a great teacher! He is really organized and down to earth, and he really cares about his students! GTFs are usually pretty awful, but he is definitely the exception. He's also really great with international students. I recommend him to everyone.
Bro doesn't know how to teach... his notes are sooo bad and don't help at all. He's always rude and passive aggressive for no reason and he's honestly no help when you ask him questions.

Let's just say, Dr. Potter is a true G. He didn't quite know how to teach a class and would show up 2 minutes late sweaty from his bike ride, but he sure did have a kind smile and was always available to hear a good joke. I would never like to experience taking his class again but his presence was exceptional and he is quite the cool dude. No cap.

Jake was horrible. On the first day this man said he wanted to make video games instead of be here, teaching and only does it for money. His classwork was easy, but his explaining in class was horrible. Everyone tried to get the FRESHMAN TA for their questions, and avoid Jake. He got mad when people called him Mr. Potter and not Dr. Potter.

I would have been better off paying my tuition and textbook money to a hs student to teach me. ge taught classes can be a mixed bag but this man does not have the talent, inclination, or work ethic for teaching. i cant believe he got payed for this...

The class is way to hard for a 4 credit course. Jake gave wayyy to much homework and was not a very good teacher. That would be one issue on itself but he also graded harder then any Professor to ever exist. DO NOT TAKE.

Jake is never prepared for lectures and never available to give help outside of class. Even at his office hours, which I went to every day, I was lucky if I could get a single question in during the entire hour. He simply does not care. Save your tuition money and take someone else.

He literally showed up to class the first day and said he was lazy and unprepared, that has been the constant of this entire course. Grades came back for the midterm average was 40% he said he was being generous by curving it by 3 points out of 50, and that he didnt think any of us should pass. Avoid his class at any and all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He will literally do examples on the board and then realize he did all the work wrong, and erase everything. Will take points off for small mistakes, and the class overall is weighted too hard on tests for the assignments to do anything. If you dont do the homework it will hurt you tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally drop this class if you have him unless you are ready to do so much work for it. I took this class when it was async and it was just Calc 1, but he expects you to already know everything about calculus. He will do problems on the board and teach you them in the most abstract way possible and it wont help you on homework.

Learning concepts between videos and textbooks were mismatched, and none of the lecture time was spent working through problems together. Quizzes day after learning new material, and mostly felt self-taught. I'm struggling to understand how UO is 'the best in the state' with some of the experiences I've had here--this class included.

First week of class his main lectures were videos created by him on material relevant to the textbook. Then from second week to final week he made us watch YouTube videos about the course material, none of which he made himself. Has quizzes the day after we watch the related videos and we don't really get a chance to work on any related problems.

I saw the terrible reviews on here and thought it wouldn't be that bad, but it is. Avoid at all costs. Lots of homework that is irrelevant to tests and quizzes. Constantly makes mistakes and confuses himself in lecture. Doesn't follow the textbook, so there is no way to learn it yourself. Save your sanity, don't take his class.

If you work hard, you'll receive what you deserve. However, all the Khan academy and office hours didn't help. Had to spend roughly 6-8 hours on each homework and live in his office hours. Confuses himself during lecture, and isn't well organize. Nothing against Jake, he's just not suited for teaching. Nice and smart, but teaching is not for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Thought he was going to be a chill guy, and he is for the most part, but he lives by the philosophy of a 14th century monk: no calculators. It's one of the most confusing aspects of this teacher; the fact that he won't let his students use calculators during quizzes and tests. Take If you're good at in your head multiplication and powers of numbers
No matter the professor Math 252 is going to be a difficult class. Jake held a lot of office hours and had study sessions before exams all of which helped a lot.

great at explaining the content, answering questions, and highly available outside of class (email or in person), except when we got to a topic he didn't like, which didn't go very well. Besides that, the rest of the class was great

He assigns Webwork (online homework) that has nothing to do with what we are learning in class. Its a good portion of our grade and I am lost every single time I look at it. Someone asked a question in class and he cant even answer it, and its assigned as homework lol

Jake Potter is one of the worst instructors I have ever had in all my years of school. Consistently confuses himself during lectures and forgets what he is doing. The way he words the tests and quizzes is completely different than the way he teaches us to understand in class. Study all you want, but you prob won't pass. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awful instructor, gets confused by his own lectures and is constantly making mistakes. Quizzes and tests are way harder than the lectures and homework. Most likely hates teaching and it's not worth it to take his class.
Isnt great at explaining things, very confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This man is the only math teacher at UO possibly tied with Hayden Harker for being the worst. He confuses himself as he talks and will give you the wrong answers. He likes to say "just for kicks" a lot but the only thing that is getting kicked is yourself in the face if you take this class. Do not take him.

Truly is a good person. Very approachable and intelligent. However, he needs more experience teaching. He's constantly making errors on lectures which confuses his students. His tests are the problem. He'll teach a formula through remedial examples, but on the test, he'll ramp up the question above and beyond challenging. Class avg was around 67
Awful instructor, nice guy but he doesn't thoroughly teach material. He'll skip steps, give you wrong formulas, and gives an excessive amount of homework. I highly recommend avoiding him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: good guy. he made it clear which stuff was important for us to know for tests
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Preston is amazing! She reads everything that you write and always has good feedback to make you feel seen and understood. She's very accessible outside of class so don't be afraid to reach out to her with questions or concerns. I loved all the things we got to do in 122Z!

I loved having Dr. Preston as a professor and would 100% recommend her! She genuinely cares about her students and wants to help them improve in writing. All of the class material is super straight to the point and easy to follow. It's not too much work, but it's still slightly challenging, which makes it a very engaging course.
Dr. Preston is the best professor I've ever had and I cannot recommend her enough.

Dr. Preston is one of the best writing profs at oregon! She's no bs or busywork, all assignments are relevant, easy and the workload is small. Generous grader, and she's always happy to work one on one with students to help. Very accessible, answers emails fast, personable, understanding and very very sweet. Definitely the best choice for 122z.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super passionate teachers. I had her for Native American Literature ENG 244. The class was super passionate, and actually got me to engage with the text and write some of the best pieces I've ever written. Truly recommend taking her class.

She's a nice teacher, and the work is easy, mostly just essays and analysis. The grading system is labor-based, so if you do the work and meet the word count criteria, you usually get 100%. The late work policy is 3 days late, which is nice. Attendance is pretty much mandatory, so make sure you go if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A lot of reading, but one of the best profesors that I have taken at UO. Like everybody else says, very caring, and she will read and engage with every peice of writing that is submited.

Best professor hands down. She is so caring and genuine. Class was very interesting and the few assignments were simple.Attendance is mandatory after 2 missed classes is takes away from your grade. Only class I looked forward to. Definitely take her if you can.

One of the best professors I've had at UO. She's super clear about assignment requirements and gives feedback on every assignment, including discussion posts. I also found her very approachable which was wonderful for me as someone with anxiety. Definitely take her for WR121Z/122Z if you can!

Dr. Preston was the best professor at UO I've had and this has been my favorite class. She is super sweet and cares deeply about our class content. I learned a lot in this class about food justice and writing skills. The library assignment was great! Easy grader as well on the labor-based scale. I would take this class again and again!!

Dr. Preston is one of the best professors I've had at UO. She genuinely cares about her students and it shows through her teaching style and course policies. She does labor based grading and has a one week late policy. She has 3 major assignments plus weekly discussion posts and responses, which can feel like busy work but overall, great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: grading is super clear and very accesable out of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An AMAZING professor! she is super sweet and understanding, gives amazing feedback on work and makes class enjoyable to be in

The sweetest human alive. You could tell she really cares for everyone individually and tries her best to acclimate every student. Very clear about grading and what even to do when projects and papers are at hand. One of the easiest classes I've taken here as a senior English major. Highly recommend.

Preston is one of the nicest teachers you'll find on this campus. She treats all her students with respectful and is very passionate about her teaching. 122z is very easy if u do the work. Very fun class and professor.

Intro to environmental literature class I was worried about taking and concerned I would do poorly, but this professor made it almost impossible for that to happen. She's kind hearted and gives great feedback with every assignment. The class was mad up of weekly discussion posts, an online midterm and some small assignments. Completely manageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Preston is phenomenal! She takes the time to know her students personally. Her grading is very fair and relatively fast, but weird. Papers are P/NP, so quality matters less. Additional work is needed for an A. Papers are open-ended, and the class cares more about the content & effort than conventions. Two essays ~1k words, two papers ~500

If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Preston, do. She was an amazing professor. She took the time to get to know each and every one of her students personally. 

She was very accessible outside of class. Super clear on grading, and very accommodating. Passionate about what she does, and wants her students to thrive. 

100/5 stars

Wonderful class! I found the topics to be incredibly relevant and accessible to people with a limited previous knowledge on them. She gives excellent feedback and encourages participation (and no the cold calls weren't horrifying like I worried they would be), and is all around very knowledegable and cares a lot about her work and her students.
I absolutely loved this class and Professor Price. Professor Price is an amazing professor, but you will have to read SO much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Price is an inspiration. They clearly know what they are doing and have made me very interested in law. I took their class Civ Right in Higher Ed and I would recommend it. There are small group presentations and you will need to attend consistently to get credit for being "On Deck," which sounds much worse then it is.

I can't recommend Price enough! Her accomplishments speak for themselves and her teaching style is fantastic.  The course consists of readings, lectures, presentations, participation, and quizzes. If you put in the work you will pass. She has inspired me to continue forward with law. I wish she taught other courses.

She was an amazing lecturer, and the guest speakers she brought in were very inspirational. Her professional experience definitely adds a lot to the class. I also liked the structure, you know what days you will be called on so you can prepare. You will have to read and brief a lot of cases, but if you're interested in law, it's really not that bad

Professor Price is one of the best instructors I've had to-date. Her experience in law as an attorney are what set this class apart from a prof who simply knows the material. As long as you do the assigned readings before every class, (honestly only truly matters when you're "on deck" and know you will be called on in class) and brief cases, EZ A.

Professor Price is very knowledgeable and obviously cares about her students. The class is reading heavy, but the lectures present reviews on it. She gives multiple extra credit options, and actually uses the terminology while teaching so none of the material is overly confusing on tests. Overall, one of my fav teachers :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was my first law class and I LOVED her class! It was online through Zoom, but she's very sweet and obviously cares for her students. You get out of the class what you put in. If you put in the work with the readings, you'll do well on quizzes and keep your grade up. One bad quiz can affect your grade- but she gave lots of extra credit chances.

Really interesting topic and lectures. You can tell that she is very passionate and knowledgable about what she's teaching. Lecture is very engaging. Tests are fairly easy because she's very straight forward about what's going to be on them. Favorite class I've taken at UO.

Really interesting class, she is a very smart woman and you can tell she loves the content she is teaching. You get a couple of excused absences, and there is a good bit of reading but it is all interesting stuff and super manageable. The tests were insanely easy because she is so clear on what they will be on, and their format. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, not great teacher, but class set up is so easy. All exam questions are EXACTLY from the hw, so just memorize them and it's an A. I taught myself everything and he's picky about the details but he's the best you can get from a math teacher.

Wonderful professor! His lectures are well thought out, with clear signposting and examples. Homework is manageable and collaborative. He makes sure to post solutions and give individualized feedback. The exams and quizzes come straight from the homework, so if you do that you should be good. Office hours are helpful and he is a great explainer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor was an extremely nice guy. It was hard for him to connect with the students. He talked in a way that was difficult to understand for such basic learners. He talked in complete math language and it was hard to follow him taking notes. This class is challenging as it is and I recommend using the math library when possible.

Nick is often criticized for his fast-paced lectures. While he is indeed fast, I thought his lectures were well organized and he captured important concepts. His exams were demanding, but the curves were generous. I can't speak for what he's like in business calc, but I think any serious math major would enjoy his class.

Nick has good intentions as he allows you to have a page of notes for every quiz and exam. However, he doesn't explain things very well and his lectures seem unorganized. Homework is doable with help from discussion leaders. Exams are tough. If he is the only instructor for Calculus for the term, I highly suggest putting it off, if you can.
Really helpful and easy. But not that clear.
Terrible, terrible teacher. Posts the longest and most difficult homework assignments. Moves way too fast in class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

The class, being big, is generally hard to teach and keep the material focused. However, I felt lost in the majority of Professor Proudfoot's lectures. Every lecture a student had to correct a mathematical error of some type. He is good natured and means well (a page of notes is allowed every quiz/test) however he is a bad fit for large classes.

Ignore the previous comment. Most students taking the class expected a calculation based course and those students dropped the course. Proudfoot gave clear explanations and covered most of the book. The only reason the first test had poor scores was because he could not gauge the difficulty of the subject, but later tests showed decent scores.

I think Mr. Proudfoot is smart, but he isn't fit to be a teacher. He doesn't explain anything in class and basically everyone failed his midterm. Unless your a GIANT math nerd, then don't take this class.

Because this is the first time he ever taught this class, there were few occasions where I felt the class was confusing. But overall, he's a good professor and a very nice guy. YOU NEED TO BE AN ACTIVE LEARNER in his class. His lectures are relatively fast, so make sure you focus a lot, and ask him questions during class and/or in his office.

Professor Southwell is undoubtedly knowledgeable about local politics and beyond. Effectively, her brain thinks faster than she can speak. Disjointed sentences and self-interruptions are a given. She refuses to use Canvas to publish grades. However, I believe she is a fair grader. Read summary passages, remember key terms, and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lecture slides were a very minimal outline of what she was talking about, and then she would ramble the entire class. it was super difficult for me to learn anything because she would go on tangents and interrupt herself, rarely finishing her thoughts. exams were on green books with no guide on what would be asked, and difficult to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Total waste of time. I did the entire class in a couple of afternoons. This wasn't worth money, it was just "free" credits.

I really did learn a lot in this class, it's only graded on 3 exams. The class it's not hard, but it can be if you don't do the readings. She is very knowledgeable in what she teachers and is kind. The only thing that I did not like about the class was that she cancelled 2 classes but that's it. Be ready to take good notes on what she talks about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice, but that's where it stops. Isn't very helpful nor clear. She goes off on long tangents during her lecture, wasting time. Respectfully, it's time for Ms. Southwell to retire.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know how Southwell is still a professor here. Her entire grading structure is based off of three exams that cover the same material over and over, and her lectures were so terrible that most of the class straight up never went. For our second midterm, worth 30% of our grade, she couldn't even show up with a paper exam. Abysmal. Resign.

I can't believe I paid for this, she is incredibly unhelpful. I would get answers wrong on my 2nd attempt on quizzes that I got right on the 1st attempt bc we couldn't see what we missed. she told me to write down the answers I got right on my 1st attempt to which I told her that I couldn't see the answers and she said that was correct.

her class was a waste of time and money. I emailed her a simple question and she couldn't even treat me like a human being. She put absolutely no effort into the online class there were no lectures or slides (just the syllabus and assignments) and her name was not even on the syllabus. (PS 349)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rambles incessantly throughout lectures and posts nothing in canvas. Very knowledgeable but not a great professor. That being said the class was still very interesting but don't expect a lick of support from her whatsoever.

Do not take this professor. She posts nothing to Canvas, not even your exam grades. The exams are the only grade in the class, and she's an insanely tough and unfair grader. She rambles in lecture, and the exams don't even relate to lecture--only the outside class readings do. I rarely receive B grades, and I got a B.
She relies heavily on lectures. She reads from the slideshow for the entire class everyday with nothing else. That being said she is incredibly knowledgable and overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Southwell is an alright person, but maybe the most boring and genuinely unstimulating lecturer I've ever had in the poli sci dept. Lectures tend to be unfocused tangents that are mostly completely unrelated to the slides at hand. Tests have an emphasis on the arguments of long and also boring readings but she is not that hard of a grader.
I feel genuinely ripped off that I had to pay to take this class. The "course content" was links to youtube compilations and several chapters of textbook readings. That's it. Avoid this at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was 4 quizzes (combined for 50% of grade) and 1 paper or final (50% of grade). Besides the textbook, a few documentaries and powerpoints were offered as learning materials. I felt like this prof put the least amount of effort as possible into being involved with the class (even for an online course). Didnt enjoy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Entire class is based off of 4 quizzes, and your choice of a final exam or paper. The quizzes are rather easy, decent time limit, multiple choice, you get a second attempt (although you don't find out what questions you got wrong after the first attempt). No rubric for final paper- very disappointing, if I'm writing 8-10 pages I want to do it right

I asked this professor for a grading rubric for a final paper worth half of my grade. Not only did she flat-out refuse to provide a grading rubric, but literally kept refusing even after the relevant Dean contacted her. I can't know if I'll graduate because graduating depends on a grade that there are no published guidelines for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was fairly easy, but was 80% based on the readings which were like 5-10 chapters per week. She does not mention really anything in the readings in class so you have to do both but I mostly just skimmed the readings before the tests and got 100-105% on the tests because of extra credit as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable, very energetic. She can go a little off track on a single topic, but her explanations are great.

One of the most difficult (and most interesting) classes I have ever taken. Southwell is very smart and makes class interesting but good lord. Grade is based off of 3 tests. If you do poorly on either of the first two there is no chance of doing well in the class.
PS 350 with Priscilla was based off of 4 quizzes and a final test. The final test was not clear on requirements, other than that the course was easy.

Your grade consists of three tests total (worth 40%, 40%, and 20% of your grade) do well on the first two and she likely wont make you take the final. Super chill and interesting lectures with a fair amount of reading, but the tests are super easy if you just minimally study or pay attention in class.

PS 201 is an easy online class with Southwell. 18 quizzes of 25 questions that are taken at your own pace, and one 8-10 page opinion paper that you can pretty much write whatever you want about. Easy to find something to talk about during election season. I would take this! I'm a PS major fulfilling my lower-division requirements and this was great

This was by far my favorite PS class I've taken at UO so far. It really helped that it was during an election because it brought the material to life. Southwell is EASY, the reading is heavy but not all is necessary. Prof is smart and very, very, very willing to help (you can literally go up to her during a test). Take this class! I loved it.

all this class is, is reading the text book and taking quizzes based on each chapter. If you have self discipline this class will be easy. The final is scary because its 50% of the grade but the material is easy and she curves the final grade.
Online quizzes were super easy and you can do them at your pace. Highly recommend this class, but the final is the only tricky part.
There were 18 online quizzes (25 questions and 30 minutes to take it, 2 attempts) and one final you had to go in and take. I believe most failed the final so there was a big curve

I took PS 204 from Professor Southwell online last term, and I couldn't believe the differences between the two. PS 204 was very manageable, with about 2 hours of reading and one to two short online tests per week. PS 205 had close to 6 hours of reading with an average of two extremely specific 55-question tests per week. Take this class in person.

She's definitely a lecturer. The class was fairly small, only 30-40 people but it was my first lecture style class ever and it scared the crap out of me because I thought all lecture professors would be like her. She flies through what she's teaching, so don't expect to be able to take clear notes. But she is a good professor and posts the lecture.

WORST ONLINE COURSE! I've been taking online course at UO for the last 3 years. They have been great easy and time efficient, considering I work for a living they have been a life saver. She gives you a quiz per week 60 questions, 60... They are specific to the text, not in order. You would have to memorize word for word to pass this class.

Pretty interesting class, although attending the lectures was almost unnecessary, since the bulk of what we learned was in the hundreds of pages of required reading. Prof Southwell knows her stuff and she is engaging to those who engage with her independently... however, her tangential lecturing sometimes has the tendency to become sleep-inducing.

Under no circumstance take this course. The powerpoint slides are useless, along with her jumbled and confusing lectures. Three test grades make up the entire percentage of your grade and she doesn't give study guides or reviews for them. The worst part is that she doesn't give you back your test grades until the term is over. Find another course.

This was a pretty clear-cut course. Read a chapter, take an online quiz. It's just fine to take this course as an online course since it's all rudimentary stuff. I had no interaction with her in the term, and that didn't matter. Taking online International Relations from her next term.
Attributes of a good chair: Vision, clarity, enthusiasm, fairness, value teaching excellence.
A rare visonary
She is extremely friendly and is more than willing to answer questions and discuss ideas in class.  I would not hesitate to take one of her classes in the future if possible.

Moves very fast in lecture, but she is easy to understand and tests were more than generous.  After one idiot complained of a take home exam she worked with us and gave us the choice of how to take the final.  No mandatory attendance, and slides posted online.

Very fast lectures, goes off on a lot of tangents, jumps around through slides, hard to follow esp when she talks so fast, given way too much information (all readings/lectures/movies fair game for tests), not focused enough on points that really matter, tests on general ideas, hard to take anything away from the material, tons of reading.

Talked way to fast in lectures, near impossible to take any notes. Learned more from the 1 lecture by a graduate student then the whole term from her. Very opinionated in both lectures and grading. Have to say what she wants to hear in order to get a good grade.

If you have a conservative bone in your body do not take this course, yes it was easy, but unbearable. I realize it is Eugene, Oregon and a Very liberal college, but some of this woman?s comments were simply ridiculous, I had a hard time not leaving every time she opened her mouth. She needs to find a medium to convey her ideas and keep her highly
Get the coffee beforehand- she lectures fast. Lots of reading, not too much bs theory. Finish class with good understanding.
Great teacher, knows her stuff really well. Moves very quickly in class so come prepared.
Went to class 4 days - once for every test and got a B. Boring material and boring readings.
Read, Got an A.  I Liked a professor who actually got out of the ivory tower and stired **** up!
I took 4 Southwell courses and learned a lot in each one. Got an A, A+, A, B+. Time consuming as there is a lot of reading, but the knowledge gained is priceless, seriously!!

I had Southwell lo these many years ago and thought she was great, and fairly easy for a 400 level class. Re: opinionated, we had clear differences of opinion and it a point of interest to both of us, not a problem. Wish I'd had her for more courses.
No Comments
Too opinionated!
Unbelievable amount of reading, no assignments, 100% of the grade is the final.

Professor Pratt was alright. He seems like a great guy and his lectures were pretty good. I wouldn't recommend taking this class if you don't have an interest in philosophy. The oral exams are way easier than they sound, and it's really easy to do well in the class if you do the assignments and study for the exams.
He is super passionate about philosophy! If you do the work you should be fine.

In my experience in a level 100 class, if you receive a poor grade, it's because you didn't try hard enough. Professor Pratt has incredible lectures and gives students all of the information they need to succeed. The written exams are difficult, but with time and studying you'll do fine. The oral exams set you up for success. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pratt is knowledgeable and I always gained a lot by going to lectures. The class itself is very difficult and one of the harder 100-level classes, but if you put the effort into understanding the work, the two oral exams and the two MCQs aren't that hard. Make sure you go to the discussions as you learn a lot in the smaller classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Pratt is passionate about philosophy but teaches at an extremely fast pace and expects you to know the topics. Gave out an oral and multiple choice exam for both the midterm and final(both are hard). Would not recommend taking this class.

Review of the book: Pratt wrote the textbook for logic and its basically incomprehensible. Its the worst textbook Ive ever read. It takes pages to say what could be said in sentences and is so muddled that the already-difficult subject matter is made almost incomprehensible. Hes an intelligent guy but doesnt know how to dumb things down at all
LAZY

I do not know how he has been getting such good reviews. In my opinion, he is a pretentious, privileged white old man with a narrow thinking mind. He is the wrong person to be teaching a diversity class. His intentions are good and he can be kind, but he can be very, very condescending as well. The weekly quizzes for his class are ridiculous.

Great professor. Had no previous experience with, philosophy before his class, but he kept it interesting. Teaches from a powerpoint, and he's a great lecturer. Funny and definitely knows his stuff. Tests are very fair if you do most of the reading and pay at least a little bit of attention in lecture.

Scott seems alright but the Logic class was bad.  It's the worst class I've ever taken. The GTFs were clueless, the exams took too long for many people, the 50-minute class was too short.  The book that Scott wrote needs some blatantly obvious revisions.  Way too much work on a topic nothing like any philosophy class you ever wanted to take.

This class is difficult if you don't do any of the readings but his class is really interesting and he great! He knows how to speak well in front of lots of students and he is always willing to take in your questions. Everyone did horrible the first test, but after that I think a lot of us did well. I worked with my GTF well. AWESOME CLASS.

Great professor, very great articulate speaker and extremely respectful. Some funny and random funny moments in class, lectures are awesome. Love this class & professor!! PHIL 216! Structure of the course is great, I learned a lot especially through writing those essays, AAA!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! If you're not a Phil major then DEFINITELY don't take it. It is sooo much work for something that is basically useless. There are 3 tests and 3 papers due at the time of the tests. The tests are HARD and the papers are WORSE. Tests usually have about 20 MC and then about 7 short answer.. essays suck. don't take this class!
No Comments
Solid
LOVED LOVED LOVED Pratt, he inspried me in so many amazing ways and touched my life forever
No Comments
Great guy. He was very helpful as an adviser.
No Comments
No Comments

Phenominal professor! I have also interviewed him for another class and he is an interesting and personable human being! One of the few professors that wont talk down to students and is very informative. Good class, better prof!

Prazniak is a very kind teacher, but her lectures are very slow and tough to get through without falling asleep. I enjoyed speaking with her during office hours and felt like I got more out of that time than the entire course. We had minimum 60 pages of reading a week not including additional articles or videos. Grading was confusing but not harsh.

History of the Silk Road was the blandest class I have ever taken. Professor Prazniak is a very nice woman and is very knowledgeable, however it was difficult to sit through her lectures because they were so boring. On the bright side, she graded me pretty easy as I never read a single book and got an A.

Prazniak if you are willing to talk up and know somewhat at least what you are talking about will like you.  Go into her office hours!  She is super kind and if you show initiative she will respect you even if you don't agree.  That is perhaps my favorite thing about her, you can contradict her, even straight up say she is wrong, just back it up
Her lectures were really boring and the instructions for assignments were often very unclear. That being said some of the topics were interesting and she really does know her information.
Really nice older woman, just kinda dull.

She is a very nice woman, but her class was very boring. I did  hardly any of my reading and still got an A. Lectures would be painfully dull and I feel like I learned very little in the class. The reading was somewhat interesting but there was a lack of direction from her as well as a lack of interesting opinions in the class.

She definitely has interest in her subject, but that also makes her a little too proud. Kind of monotone speaker. A little vague in presenting. Rarely just answers a question- just repeats in back to the class so all one gets to hear is monologues from the same few students. Tests are nice - in class essays that you can prepare for before class.
She appears a little absent minded. Classes are terribly boring. She's not particularly difficult or easy.

I took Prazniak's class based mainly off the reviews here. I left the class with a very strong grasp of the material, I learned a lot through her. MANY students though that I talked to were bored or found the class to be very ambiguous as quiz/test preparation can be confusing. Lastly, I felt that her essays were far from an 'easy A'. (not alone!)
Prepare to be bored out of your mind in a world without structure or direction.
Very helpful with essays. Would take a class from her again!
She really knows her stuff. I had no prior interest to this material, but am finding that I am taking another class on the topic. She doesn't take roll but I would recommend going to every class.
Nice lady, material not very interesting (personal view). Lectures unstructured and does not explain what she expects from certain assignments. Overall, easy class and very easy to get A's on essays.

Prazniak is a very nice lady. Her class is rather unstructured. Attendance is definitely not mandatory, and it is very easy to slack and still get an A on papers. The material is interesting, and she is very knowledgeable. However, that knowledge isn't always transmitted into a form comprehensible to her students.

lectures are vague and follow no particular direction, like maybe she doesn't prepare for them (though she knows her material). grades waaaay too soft for a 400-level class. I'm not really sure how she teaches honors classes if she's this slack. make sure you like the subject matter and are self-motivated regarding research papers.
A lot of reading, lectures will be boring if you're not interested in topic ... but she's a superb lady and grades fairly.

Prof. Presto was incredibly kind, full of personality and a great teacher overall. There is a lot of reading, but if you're into the topic you should have no problem keeping up. We had to write two essays, but she was super light on grading, and provided opportunity to revise and gave great feedback. Passionate and knowledgable, highly recommend.

Great Prof., super sweet and clearly very knowledgeable. Classes are almost entirely discussion based, lots of reading, nothing an undergrad couldn't handle. Only two papers and participation in grading. Easy grading and gives shockingly detailed feedback! Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was a bit disorganized but not in a way that bothered me- if you like a class that strictly adheres to a schedule this may not be right for you. She is a lovely person, passionate about the subject and well spoken. I only wish there were a few smaller assignments instead of only two big papers which your final grade is based on.

Vast knowledge of the subject, inspired me to read more and to explore other authors.  I found myself completely immersed into the subject.  If you have questions, she will spend time with you.  And if you pay attention in class and read what is assigned, you should not have a problem on exam.

Has extensive knowledge of Russian/Eastern European studies, literature, film, etc, can bring a number of different angles to analyzing any sort of material. Lectures do get sort of confused, but they are never boring. Textbook use wasn't too bad, attendance wasn't mandatory, tardiness went unnoticed. Very easygoing and helpful, great class.
Great teacher, one of my favorites at the U of O. If you have any interest in literature you should take this course. She's very helpful if you seek her input outside of class.
Jennifer is wonderful, and her courses are fascinating and challenging. Only for the serious student of literature.

Easy grader as far as essays are concerned, come to class with a slight idea of what happened in the reading for full participation points--this is an easy A, people. Her lectures get fairly tangential but I found them interesting. Reasonable amount of reading: you are in college, be prepared to read like a college student.

Presto is very kind even if she's a bit flakey (in a good way I think). Russian lit isn't easy, but her lectures made it interesting and even pleasant, and she'll spend all the time needed to help you out in office hours.
The class was very busy because of the amount of reading. The papers are total BS and she is crazy.

The course requires a lot of reading. Toward the end of the course, 100 pages a week is a good estimates. Class lectures are short and interesting, with discussions of the literature following. Two papers assigned, plus a final exam. Participation is important. Professor Presto is entertaining and kind, if occasionally flustered. A good class.

Incredibly disorganized professor and her lisp is especially distracting. This class is for student who doen't speak russian yet she asks questions regarding the origin of russian words and english equivalency of the word. Her final is over Russian gov't, not the books your required to read! If you can BS papers and a final, you'll get an A.
Is not a good teacher, should not be a teacher. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tom Ptak is a professor that takes his job seriously.  He expects you to too.  But guess what?  If you show up to every class with your reading assignment completed, you're going to get an A. Seriously, it is that easy.  Sit back and enjoy his vast knowledge of our planet and be prepared to view the world in a new way.  Negative reviews  FAKE NEWS

Tom taught classes at SSU knowing it would be for only one semester, so was under constant pressure to find a job. He also was living apart from his family, and was asked to take on too many students, in too many courses. Being in a stable position will better allow him to make use of his passion and talent. Who's great working with tons of stress?
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is one of the most unprofessional professors I have encountered, he doesn't explain anything clearly and then gets upset when you ask for clarification and goes back on his word. He is not approachable and not helpful at all. Don't take a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Spends more time telling students to not ask stupid questions than explaining things.

Not helpful at all, if you try to ask for help he just tells you "I don't think that's the right answer..." and  doesn't do anything to help you find the right answer. SO frustrating, especially when you are really trying to understand the class material.

WORST EXPEREINCE AT OREGON!! He was easy going for the zero week class, and then gave the entire 8 person class D's & F's on the final projects and papers (50% of the grade). We all expected A's and B's and all received low C's. When approached, his conduct is unprofessional, aggressive and argumentative. Avoid this professor at all costs!!!
Tom is by far the greatest professor I've ever had. He really makes the class interesting and is very helpful if you seek it.

Tom was one of the best professors I have ever had, probably because he has traveled EVERYWHERE and speaks from experience. If you attend class and do the online readings you will be fine. The midterm and final are essays so as long as you pay attention they are pretty easy. One of the best classes I have ever taken!

Tom was the best instructor I've ever had, hands down. He was extremely passionate about teaching and abut the materials he covered. I've never had a class that made me think so much about the people of the world and about myself. He doesn't like standardized grading which I think is wonderful, but it did throw some students off. Overall loved it!
Amazingly interesting lectures with real life examples. Attendance is not necessary except for labs but you won't want to miss anything anyways! There are a few pop quizzes which are easy.

Grading policies are clear, and homework is flexible. He was generous with curving the test grades and distributing grades. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are occasional quizzes that cannot be made up. Calc 253 is relatively difficult but the professor tries to make it fair.

I really like him, he takes his time to make sure everyone understands and is a funny guy. He is also more than willing to help students if they miss an exam or something. The tests make up 90% of your grade. I found it helpful to go over problems from the lecture closely.

Personally I loved his classes, he is always gives space for questions and will take the time to answer them thoroughly. He gives a lot of partial credit on tests and his homework policy is very fair. Overall interesting lectures and positive support.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class averages were in the 60s always. I would say half of the class was failing. However, there was a huge curve on the class in the end. His tests match very closely to the reviews, just with different numbers. He is very helpful, accessible, funny, and kind. He is eager to help and truly is rooting for his students to succeed.

He is a very funny and approachable guy, but he covers the material very quickly. it is critical that you study outside of the class using other material if you want to maintain a good grade. midterms/final are worth 80% of the grade, and some of the exam problems are on topics we only covered once, but he does give a practice exam for each.

Love him. He gives out packets of his lecture notes + puts it on canvas, and his tests are exactly like the problems he teaches. Attendance not mandatory but it definitely helps to go. Super fair grader and reasonable guy. He's really funny and open to suggestions from students because hes a new professor. No complaints. Wish I could take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pu-Ting is very receptive to suggestions and is still learning how to teach the class. English is not his first language so he teaches mostly in theorem, outside materials are really helpful to support class. He cares a lot and is a very generous grader, the material is just hard. Once you adapt to his teaching style, he is great. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So, all he does is yap and he doesn't yap about what he needs to yap about. Only a little about what he says is important to learn, so it's hard to do the homework sometimes. But he is a really easy grader. He's like really smart but can't communicate subject matter to students.

Very open to suggestions in grading and assignments. Gave multiple opportunities to lower the amount of homework throughout the course, and gave us access to all of the homework for the term from the beginning with retries. The grade of the class is very test and homework dependent, but overall the professor was fun and open to suggestions.

Super knowledgeable in the subject, I learned a lot from the class and as a professor she conveyed information very well. Class itself was harder than any upper level classes I have taken yet though, going to lecture and staying on top of readings is crucial. The grading is strict, but she gives good feedback especially on the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's an extremely tough grader and abnormally strict. I took this last year, and during that time I was going through a tough situation where a racial hate crime had been committed against my family's business, making me miss the midterm deadline. When I asked for an extension or a way for me to make it up, she refused, making me fail the class.
Shes a tough grader and expects a lot from students in engagement and writing, but she clearly cares about her topic and works hard to get that across.

The lectures are long and boring. If you miss class, you won't get the full experience because her slideshows only have about 25% of the info you need (gotta take notes on what she SAYS). She also assigned us seats because of COVID so be ready to not make friends in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a very good student and Pulido missed a lot of crucial marks for me that are needed to be a good professor. She is unreasonably hard, her lectures were not recorded(COVID), and her slides were never very helpful. I emailed her numerous times asking legit questions and her responses were always unhelpful and oddly unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Pulido is incredible, and my only warning is that there are 3 things your grade depends upon: midterm, final project, and final exam. If you skip class and/or don't do the reading this class will be hell. BUT I personally LOVED it. Such important insight into environmental racism from a professional in the field. Amazing guest lectures. 11/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm not taking 330 but she is currently my EC320 TA/GE. She is extremely picky on the problem sets and the last class average was a 5.4/10. FIRE HER. DO NOT LET HER COME NEAR ANOTHER CLASSROOM EVER AGAIN.

Lectures and homework did not prepare me at ALL for the exams. You also aren't allowed any notes or formula sheets on exams, which is pretty crazy with how formula-heavy this class is. Delivery of class content is also super sporadic and the material isn't really organized into logical units or topics.

Probably the worst professor I have had in my 4 years, and that says a lot. Her lectures and HW did not prepare us one bit for the exam. She raised the grading curve two weeks before the final. Your average person will receive a flunking score on the midterm. Stay away at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Puja is by far the worst professor I have had at this university. The average on her exam was a 51% with no curve. She is extremely hard to understand and does not give you the proper materials to do well in her class. I recommend taking any other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Puja no good

The Economics Department here at UO is a joke. Puja's class holds true to this statement. When an incorrect answer is marked wrong, the TA/Puja don't even bother showing what you got wrong. They say they don't have time to explain since there are too many kids in the class. So you're telling me you don't want to do your job? Awesome. Tough tests 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if you don't have a math brain or any type of learning disability, do NOT take her class. I am miserable

His lectures are great. I really loved all the films we watched in class. There are only three assignments so you'll want to jump on those early and make sure you put the effort in. Pay attention to how he wants you to do the assignment and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Na

Professor Purnama was a really caring nice professor, but he graded EXTREMELY HARD. He didn't submit grades until the last day of class when the grades were put in the final transcript. He graded way to hard, you probably wont get an A no matter how great your writing is...

Lectures lacked formality which made key information hard to distinguish from tangents. The assignments (which there were few) had very unclear guidelines and those doing projects first had more risk, it was a pay attention to what others get wrong to get it right situation. The final projects were also worth 80% of our grade, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ari is a great professor and ultimately makes the time in class enjoyable. You spend about 1 class period a week watching a movie, and the second you discuss the readings and how it relates to the film you watched. Pretty simple homework. Very hands on and interactive.
Always helpful with any questions asked, will always stay after class to help you edit your work, extremely funny and made Lab super enjoyable

Zach is awesome! I'm so glad he was my gtf, he made the gateway experience awesome! His feedback is super helpful and he somehow managed to make an 8am Friday lab fun.  Definitely take his class if you get the chance!

This teacher that actually cares about you and your future. Someone who can actually keep you up for a two hour lab, starting at 8 am on a Friday morning. He always keeps you on your feet and pushes you to become the best possible version of yourself. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Zach was a wonderful GTF. He's clearly very experienced and always gave incredibly helpful input. He made our 8 AM labs fun with his energetic attitude and awesome music selection. Whenever I would email him with questions, he would always get back to me in a very timely manner.  Anyone would be very lucky to have him as a GTF!!

Zach was the best GTF I've ever had in college. He was always available to answer questions even though he doesn't live in Eugene. The feedback he gave was very constructive and detailed so it made it easy to correct your mistakes for the final project. Overall, a great dude and would recommend for anyone who is looking to have a fun lab!

Zach Putnam is one of the better professors that I've ever had. As a GTF he was the sole reason that I was able to get by in this class. His instructions were always clear, he was available for help whenever, and he gave great feedback on our assignments so we could improve.
Zach is amazing!! Super helpful in and outside of the classroom. He is a fair grader and is truly passionate about the work he does. Anybody would be lucky to learn from such a down to earth fun guy!

He does a great job of making a challenging class a lot of fun. He was always available to provide helpful feedback on assignments and cares about students success beyond just this class. He even brought us doughnuts on the last day of class... I would literally take any class he teaches in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class has a reputation for being hard, and it was, but Zach made it fun. I would definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: ENG205 (Topic: Lyric) literally changed my life.

Professor Pyle is such a passionate professor, and he chooses some great articles to read. I will say that he lectures the entire class, and for someone who can't sit still very long, it can be hard to obtain what he's saying the whole time.

He clearly has a passion for what he teaches, and it made the class so enjoyable and interesting. I had him for the ENG205 Top Lyric, and it genuinely changed the way I approach literature. I would take the class again in a heartbeat. Homework includes lots of reading, but also music and videos. Very few assignments. An absolute joy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This is feedback I got, in part, in a class of his:

"In part perhaps due to the difficult matters you address, your writing sometimes displays stylistic infelicities (particularly an awkwardness of syntax) but these are minor matters far outweighed by the lucidity of your thinking"
.
This either appeals to you or it does not.

I've taken multiple classes with Pyle, and I can't recommend him enough, especially if he's teaching a course on something you're passionate about. He's very kind and enthusiastic. He makes interesting assignments, and always gives thoughtful feedback. Pretty lax attendance policy, but you'll want to go to class anyway because he's so great.

Overall solid professor, but his lyric 205 class is bizarre and I wouldn't recommend. An average amount of work but it's basically made up literary devices that are purely subjective. Sometimes his grading is a little inconsistent, but he's super nice and very passionate about English so I'd still recommend him, just stay away from lyric.

I didn't enjoy Pyle as much as other reviewers. If you're into romanticism, you'll be happy. But the course texts he assigned all blended together a bit (imo that is the nature of the genre, tho) and he can be hard to follow in lecture. I think I would like Pyle more if this course wasn't co-taught, it also makes it harder to get into the groove.

Amazing English professor! His lectures are really interesting, but he also encourages class discussion. The readings for his class are challenging but there is not an obnoxious amount of work. I'm not sure if you would like his classes if you're not an English major because they are pretty in depth. He's also just a super nice guy.

He's great for people who aren't English majors and just need the credit. He assigns an act as homework and spends the next lecture summarizing it, so if you understand Shakespeare without help, this class is a waste of time. Tests are super easy as long as you read and understand the plot, but he grades harshly on attendance (and lateabsent)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Pyle is by far my favorite teacher I've had so far. He is very clear and straightforward about the material and will make you love and appreciate Shakespeare. 10/10 Recommend.

Professor Pyle is an excellent teacher and very passionate about his material. If you are a person who likes Shakespeare, he will make you love it. His assignments are fairly straight forward, but don't expect to pass if you don't do the reading. Showing up to lectures is a must, but Pyle makes it an enjoyable experience.
Great professor!! Made ENG 205 fun and great!  Great inspiration for english major's. He is very passionate about teaching and great.

Loved him. He was hilarious and passionate and he made Shakespeare easy to follow and enjoyable! The essays he assigns are non traditional: (ex. he asks you to cast celebrities as the characters in the plays, choose your favorite act and summarize) which I found much easier to write. Definitely recommend.

Would recommend Pyles to any aspiring English major, or to anyone who just wants to attend a class where your professor is clearly passionate about his subject matter. Silky smooth voice, and loves his Romanticism. Assignments were straight forward and nothing any English major hasn't already seen. Highly recommended, did I say that already?
Best teacher ever, completely made me understand Shakespeare! Really straightforward and essays are creative and interesting!

Professor Pyle gives interesting lectures and has a voice that will keep you tuned in for the entire class. He picked really cool topics and great novels to read. He's probably my favorite prof that I've had in college. I'd recommend him to anyone and I hope that I have the opportunity to take more of his courses!
he's a hottie so that made listening easy. really great professor. take any of his classes, regardless of your major. you'll be glad you did :)

I agree he is reallll attractive in that professory way--made listening to his lectures much easier! But regardless of his looks, he is an excellent instructor. Not stuffy in the least and really engages in the material.
a brilliant, helpful and wonderful professor who makes my heart go pitter-patter.

The best professor I've ever had. When I think of his classes (I took 3), I sorely miss college. Brilliant oratory, and a great fusion of literary and pop culture material. Very supportive. And as someone else mentioned, incredibly sexy in the most unconventional way. He will make you fall in love with academia.
I'd definitely recommend taking a class with him.
With Professor Pyle as your teacher, you can't help but love the English language.
I don't if i can agree that he is that atractive, but I can say the professor promotes critical thinking, and loves culture.

Tres Pyle seduces you into loving English literature. He whispers, he smiles, he says brilliant and confusing things, and then effervesces about poetry and sublimity. He's not conventionally attractive, but he is one of the sexiest men I've ever known (and I am not alone in that), and I think that's because he's among the most passionate.
She was great she listened to us as a class and individuals as well as being very clear when helping us
She is a very engaging instructor, made class entertaining and actually worth going to.
Amazing teacher! She pretty much has this online school down she was my best teacher this quarter.

She's knowledgable on the subject and was accessible, . Her lectures are dry and she's probably one of the hardest graders I've seen. If you do the work, she won't fail you, but it is extremely hard to get all points even if you do the basic requirement. Getting an A means doing extremely well on her tests, which are difficult to begin with.
The entire class is boring lectures and common sense. This instructor is not good at lecturing and the textbook is never even used so don't buy it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Elayne is super cute. I absolutely loved her. It is very clear that she is trained and has studied the art of Yoga. If you have any issues with anything she is very understanding. She's very sweet and kind. My class was only allowed to miss two classes without it affecting your grade. The only hw is a project that is due on week 7.

I took Elayne's Ashtanga class as a challenge after taking only one other yoga class. It was tough (Ashtanga is a tough style of yoga), but she made it relaxing. Only one assignment (an art project or short paper), and her only request is not to leave early. Literally just show up and pass, even if you just lie on the floor. Great workout, though!

I have taken both Hatha 211 and Ashtanga 302 with Elayne, and she is wonderful. Ashtanga yoga can be very daunting and hard, but Elayne makes it easy and pressure-free. She lets you take breaks when you need to without judgment, and she really cares about everyone. For me, her voice is easy to get used to. Seriously, take her class, she's the best!
Took me a bit to get used to her voice. She seems very knowledgeable however
AWESOME CLASS/TEACHER. Dim lighting, relaxing music. 1st time taking yoga. Thanks to her I will practice for the rest of my life. Really a mind/eye opener

I had no experience with yoga beforehand and this was a good class to take. I am a former athlete so I was not very flexible before, this has greatly increased my flexibility, not to mention relaxing you for your entire day.

She was an amazingly good teacher.  I have had more than 10 yoga teachers, and only one other was as good as her.  She has a deep grasp of the basic philosophies of yoga, and explained everything basic/ foundational (such as breathing) in detail (which my other teachers skipped).  I was happy that I took her class. Still am.

Definitely not the best yoga teacher I ever had. Her voice is really annoying and she doesnt change it up much at all. I would recommend someone else.  If its your first time ever taking yoga do not take her, she will turn you off yoga.

His lectures are very clear, and he's definitely willing to answer questions; just be ready for the lectures not to really represent the difficulty that the homework has. He goes over questions in class for practice, but homework & tests will be significantly harder.

I know he almost has a 5-star rating, but I'm telling you that is the biggest lie. The material itself is already somewhat hard, but his ability, or lack thereof, to explain it makes it even worse. He never explains how to do the math and instead just writes it down and immediately moves on, leaving you lost, and his lectures aren't engaging.

Mike Price is probably one of the best professors out there, he's a great lecturer and seems to care a lot about his student's success. This class is very test-heavy but you get to bring a full sheet of notes for each one. A lot of people struggle with this class but if you attend every lecture and take notes you'll do well.

Mike Price is genuinely the best professor I could have asked for. His jokes are funny and makes it bearable to be in a huge lecture hall. He genuinely cares about his students. It is very easy to excel in this class especially with the lowest test grade being dropped. (I didn't have to take the final!!)

Hands down my favorite professor I have ever had, and that is coming from someone who hates math! You can tell he loves being a teacher and loves what he teaches! He is very friendly and humorous. He explains things very well, and he gives students lots of extra credit opportunities. He also drops your lowest test score (out of 5)!
One of the best teachers I have had at any level.

Mike Price was great. I like math, but I found the content very hard. There are 5 tests, but the lowest score is dropped, and there are opportunities for extra credit and an online test to boost your real test score. There is also a course project, and I felt that they graded it generously. If you have to take his class, take it with him.
For MATH241 he was great. Just pay attention, take good notes and go to office hours if you need help and you will do absolutely fine.

Professor Price genuinely cares and wants you to succeed. He is super helpful and clearly loves his job. The class is structured for student success and lots of bonus opportunities are offered. Put in the work and you will do well in his class. 10/10 best professor I have had. If you plan on taking 241 you HAVE to take it with professor Price.
Literally the best math teacher I've ever had. I loved his grading criteria, understood what he was teaching in lectures, and he's so sweet. 10/10 would take again

mike price is the goat. its obvious he loves what he does and lectures are very easy to follow. You take 5 tests throughout the term and your lowest gets dropped. I'm god awful at math and I was able to get a pretty good grade in his class. Theres also one big course project that is a good chunk on your grade.

This is genuinely the best professor at UO. It's the first professor that I have had here that is understanding of students needs, he provides multiple extra credit opportunities, He understands that students aren't only taking his class and that most of us have at least 3 other classes and jobs.
He's a really fun professor and he teaches the class really well.
Genuinely explains the math concepts in an engaging and easy to learn way. I cannot say enough good things about him. TAKE HIS CLASS. HE IS AMAZING. Not to mention funny and very kind. 10000/10
Although he is a great guy, he teaches very quickly in lectures, and it can be hard to keep up with him sometimes. Loved the dad jokes though.
He is the best! The class itself is pretty difficult but he makes it manageable.
I love him
Mike Price is by far BEST math teacher ever. Made this class feel so easy, not too much homework and lots of study guides/extra credit for exams would 100% take again!
Great professor. Business Calc is known for being one of the toughest classes. Can't imagine taking it without him.
Best prof ever and it's not even close. Used to hate math, but he genuinely made it interesting and fun for me. Finally understand calc thanks to this guy.

Excellent for Business Calc, probably the easiest way to take calculus. I got an A in this class and am proud of that. If you put enough time/effort into this class, you should have no problem at least passing. Take Mike Price if you can

Great! I am terrible at math and did struggle in class, I had to get tutoring but that's just because I need one-on-one help with math, he was a great teacher and down to earth! he is even lenient with late work, helped me with an assignment I forgot to turn in during finals, and gave me full credit. 2 midterms 1 final, drops lowest score!!!.

Mike is easily the best math professor I've ever had as a college student. He truly cares about the success of his students with his clear and concise grading, his attention to detail during lectures, and his personable attitude. However, make sure you attend every class because Mike does iClicker questions that reflect on your participation grade.
Super down-to-earth guy and is very thorough and straightforward with his lectures. Lots of personality and expresses he genuinely cares.

the sweetest professor i've ever had :) took this course Spring 2023, my freshman year, & i still rave about what a great professor he was! very encouraging & wanted his students to succeed. exams were easy, & he would often give out extra credit codes in lecture. the class is structured for u to get a good grade as long as you participate & do hw.
Best Prof I've ever had! Very thorough explanations and truly cares about topics and students. Nice and hilarious, just pay attention in class and you're solid.
Mike is a phenomenal professor. I was worried about taking calculus but he is very good at teaching and I really enjoyed his class. He also has a great personality. Take a class with him if you can!

Mike's a great teacher, he does his best for every student in class and his lectures are very good in my opinion. This class was very hard for me but Mike is not the reason for that at all. You will have to do a course project thing that is very confusing as my GE didn't explain it at all.

He might be the best professor i've ever had. He is so helpful and respectful. If i could i would have added every single positive tag to this review. His lectures actually teach!!! He is a rare enigma of a professor. I took his class because it fit in my schedule but now I felt like I won the lottery. S tier level professor. Take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took this class freshmen year winter term and flunked out of it, now as a junior I have a B+ without a curve, Mike is by far the best teacher I have ever had for math and explain and really cares about his students. Mike if you are reading this keep up the great work class was difficult, but you made it manageable, thanks!
Mike is literally one of the best professors I've ever had! All the lectures are so funny and he takes the time to actually engage with you even in a five hundred person lecture

This is hands down the best teacher I have had! If you want to succeed you have to go to pay attention in lectures but his iclickers gave you extra credit. The homework could be time-consuming but overall his grading was fair. He also had the option to drop the lower test between your midterm and final which helps your grade a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing at teaching and explaining topics. The GE's are a hit or miss. He always wanted to show up to class and was excited to teach.

Mike is amazing and I would 100% take another class with him if I could. He explains the lessons really well and his office hours were so helpful. He does move pretty fast during lecture, but always makes sure to check in with the class. Attendance wasn't required, but if you're not good at math then don't skip. 10/10 GOAT'd math instructor

Fairly easy course with lots of extra credit opportunities. If you struggle with exams the way I do Price is a must take. There are all sorts of opportunities to boost your grade through projects and EC.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mike was super friendly and kind. This course is fairly difficult but if you put in the work it is manageable. I recommend going to tutoring and encore classes. Mike does offer quite a bit of extra credit if you pay attention in lectures and through posts on canvas.

Very easy to get ahold of and wants students to succeed. Lectures are easy to understand with guided notes available. Weekly guides on canvas help to keep track of work. Seriously, best math teacher I have had since elementary school.

Even though I had a background for calculus I found this class to be far more confusing than it had to be. Some topics were explained well but others were not explained in a way that someone who does not think mathematically would understand. The information for homework assignments was explained after the assignment was due which was frustrating.

Although calc itself is pretty hard he makes it pretty easy to pass the class, 2 midterms, 1 final, but the lowest one gets dropped. Lowest quiz is also dropped, project over the course of the term which is awful but he helps you a lot if you have questions. He is an extremely nice, caring, helpful teacher that just wants his students to succeed.
He is very understanding and wants students to succeed. He tries to make the class as enjoyable as possible with it being a calculus class. He is very knowledgeable

Wow. Amazing. I'm sure many students taking biz calc as a freshman are like me: "ahead" in math in high school, but not necessarily great at it. I took this class last year in high school (calc AB), and did horribly. I'd always been a good student, but there's something to be said about an effective teacher. That's exactly what Price is.

Mike was the best possible stats professor I could've asked for. He made an 8:30am math class fun and I learned so much from him! Mike really wants to see everyone succeed and offers a lot of extra credit. The workload can be a lot but it really helps you understand the content. Definitely take Dr. Price if you get the chance!!

If you have to take a math class, take it with Professor Price! He's a really nice guy who genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He offers tons of extra credit, and his lectures are easy to follow.
