Professor Price is the best of the best. He is so funny, caring, and understanding of the students. He really wants you to succeed and makes 8:30am classes worth it. He gives LOTS of extra credit, so if you show up to class and put in a little bit of work. You'll do just fine. If you can take math with Professor Price, do it!

Mike Price made it worth waking up at 8 every morning to go to math. He was funny, understanding, and gave clear explanations for the content. It's pretty easy to get a good grade if you just take the class notes. He gives extra credit through getting iClicker questions right, and allows for a page of notes on tests. Fantastic professor.

Mike is an amazing professor who truly tries to get to know his students. He helped everyone throughout the term and genuinely wants students to succeed. His class is homework heavy; however, they are short and don't take much time. I found that they helped my understanding. If you can work with Professor Price, you definitely should.
Mike Price is very nice! Webwork is not as nice though...

Cool dude. Took it online but the structure was amazing and it never felt too heavy. He really cares about his students and you could tell through his videos, an amazing professor who taught super well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Online Math 111 has 3-4 lecture videos to watch each week around 20 minutes each. There are weekly quizzes, two midterms and a final. For the homework it is often WebWork 2-3 times a week and a written packet. This class has a lot of homework but is not very hard as long as you don't let yourself fall behind.

I took Professor Prices Math 111 class ASYNC, and I loved it. He explained concepts well, and he had lots of example questions to help you grasp concepts. Test prep for his class was very helpful, and he always let us have a sheet of notes for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Recorded lectures were great, if he didn't use WebWork religiously for tests, quizzes, and HW the course would be great. He made the final optional and was a great professor in all ways. Course structure was very organized and easy to follow online. Avoid Sebasian for GE at all costs.

Mike is the best. The workload is manageable. The tests are easy. He is super flexible and understanding. He is funny and has clear lectures and lots of office hours. If he is teaching the math class, TAKE IT! Mike truly is awesome!
Super nice and very understanding!

Mike's lectures are great and make sense a lot of sense. However, he refuses to give paper tests out and only uses webwork which makes partial credit impossible, even after over half his students complained in the survey. This class is so well taught but so poorly graded its a shame to see mikes ability to teach go to waste by his stubbornness

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He is so bad I would give him a zero but I can’t so I give him a one. So much work, you put way more time into it than you would for a in person class. Webwork is extremely hard, i got under a 50% on each midterm with a tutor. So hard, so much work.

I had Mr. Price for an online math course.  His lectures are extraordinarily clear, the grading standards are clear, and he actually makes math fun to listen to.  I'd highly recommend him.  He might be the best math teacher I've ever had.  He is willing to meet outside of office hours as well.  Expect lots of homework and hrs/week though.

He's very understanding & wants everyone to do well. 1-2 hrs of lecture almost everyday + hw. There's a final project AND exam, but he cancelled the final & made an @ home one for extra credit. Quizzes & tests can take awhile, was never able to finish them in the time limit. If he taught other classes I'd take them, but I wouldn't take calc again.

Mr. Price was ok, really caring and nice guy and was very accessible outside class BUT he is extremely hw heavy, will spend upwards of 10-15 hours a week on his class alone and half the time I was not understanding what was going on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: OK so Professor Price isn't a bad professor by any means. He clearly understands the material and explains it well, the only issue I had with this course was the amount of work. It was solely online, but I would spend an average of 2-3 hour per day (upwards 20 hours per week) solely on work for this class. In the end my grade curved from a D to a B

His online lectures were really easy to follow/take notes on and the videos were surprisingly calming. I didnt like the course project because of how hard it was graded, but the grading really depends on your GE. He was a great prof that I would definitely take again

Mike was an amazing teacher, he made a pretty hard class into a fun lecture. he lecture videos were helpful,a good length, quirky and fun. although this class was tough there are plenty of resources to help you succeed. mike is easy to get in contact with, flexible and a great communicator.

This class is extremely difficult and I spent hours every week in tutoring. Part of this reason might be b/c it was online, so I highly recommend taking this class in person if it's offered. Other than the numerous videos, lots of webwork assignments, and difficult tests, Mike was a nice professor that usually responded quickly when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I literally made this account to express my gratitude for Mike; you can tell he's a super nice person and cares about his students and math. I took the class online but he was always helpful and understanding through e-mail exchanges. I recommend his class, as long as you do the homework and put some effort forth, you will understand the content.

Make sure you pay attention to lectures and attend office hours, he will work with you in any way possible and is a great guy with hints of humor in his lectures as well. I enjoyed listening to him teach.

Fall 2020: Mike Price was very accessible outside of class and was very accommodating to his students. If you go to office hours and show effort in this class, you will be alright. As for his teaching, he was very informative and had very good pace for the class. Highly recommend taking one of his math classes.

Mike is by far the most kind and understanding professor I've had at UO so far. If you email him with questions he typically responds fast regardless of the time of day. I found the math itself to be hard and a little time consuming, but Mike made it bearable!
Mike Price restored by faith in the University's math department. Someone, please give this man a raise.

A gem!! One of the only professors that really cares about his students and goes above and beyond. He never makes you feel dumb when you are confused and genuinely wants to help you understand the material. He is also so funny and you can email him any time of the day and he is quick to respond.

Professor Price is your best option for any math class at the UO. His lectures are incredibly thorough and clear, and all the assignments and tests are very clearly related to the course content. He very clearly cares about his students. You need to put in the study time for tests and quizzes but the study material he gives will get you an A.

Mike Price is the best math teacher you can get for Math 241. He is clear and concise and his lectures are great. They can be lengthy at some times but he makes a great effort to ensure that his students really understand the material. He will always help you with any question you may have. I made it a point to get Mike Price for 241 after 111.

Mike was an amazing teacher, however, make sure you are putting in 100% effort and advocating for yourself. Webwork is really the only tricky thing. Make sure to ask questions when confused, you will get them answered 100% of the time.

Surprised as to how many good reviews he has since online learning was bad. He posts lectures but GEs are the ones doing all the work & teaching us in discussion sections. Final was extremely hard, but daily/weekly quizzes were pretty easy. Mandatory face reveal for Discussion to get Attendance points on weekly math packet, & Webwork is HARD.
Asynchronous lectures online and mandatory attendance for discussion sections

reviews.comment: This dude is an absolute legend through lectures online. He is always cracking jokes and make math as fun as possible. He actually cares unlike other teachers during this pandemic.

Thank god for math teachers like Mike Price. I really cannot sing his praises enough. If you think you're "bad at math" he will prove you wrong, inspire you and empower you. Learned a ton. I never thought I would ever say this but I love calculus!
Mike is a gem! He's super nice and funny, plus he gives extra credit opportunities a lot! The best math instructor at UO and that's on period.
THIS MAN IS A KING, he's def the best professor i've had in a mathematics class. Def cares about his students and if he sees your trying, will provide you the help necessary

Price was one of my favorite professors Ive taken. He cares so much about his students success, and as long as he can see that youre trying and not making excuses he is always willing to help. his lectures are straightforward and the homework is always way harder than the tests (the hw has unlimited attempts) so tests seem easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved taking Math 242 with Mike, he is THE best professor ever. I'm not a Math genius but when I took his class I really did feel like it, Math 242 is the easiest class I've taken in college. Mike is very good at explaining the concept so it is very easy to then do well in the midterms, plus he gives plenty of opportunities to get extra credit!
Really nice guy. Easy to understand. He used the ALEKS math program for homework. Test were easy as long as you went to class and practiced the work.

I've never rated anyone on here before, but Mike Price was so good I had to. The content and material was difficult, but he did a very good job explaining it. It is very clear he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Extremely nice guy. He is my favorite professor at U of O, and I am so glad I got to have him twice.

Mike Price is an excellent instructor, who you can tell has been teaching for quite some time. I took his Math 101 class in Fall of 2018. He is a talented teacher when explaining a math problem he is consistently patient, thorough, and effective. ALSO! He is Math department head, he has also wrote the MATH 111 textbook used at the UO. He is not dry
Professor Price is an awesome professor! Lecture is not boring, and he will keep you laughing! Plus you ll actually learn statistics

Mike is not only the best math professor Ive ever had, but is the best professor Ive ever had in general. I took this class the term before and received a D, took Mike's class and had a solid A all up until the end of the term (I got a B+ because of the final). He actually cares about each and every student's success and it shows! HIGHLY recommend

Professor Price is one of the best professors at this university. He made learning the material extremely easy. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you go to class all the clicker points are extra credit. Theres a lot of webwork but doing it really helps ur grade. The test were super straight forward. I only went to half the classes and got an A.
He would give us bonus codes for extra credit to use on tests.
Price is such a great teacher. He gives out a ton of extra credit, but all in participation. Show up to every class, do the assignments and you will get a good grade.

Awesome Teacher. Super helpful and accommodating and wants his students to succeed. If you pay attention in lecture and do all of your homework to the best of your ability, you're almost sure to get an A. He's also just a really nice and genuine guy.

Literally the BEST math teacher I have ever had!! I would 100% recommend his class. I had him for Calc and Stats. He explains everything really well, and he really cares about his students and if they understand the material! He offers lots of extra credit too!
I hate Math but Mike makes everything easy for the student. He IS THE BESTTTTTT!
I hate math, but loved this class. The lectures are easy to sit through and the material is explained well. Not a lot of homework.

Hes a great professor. Really funny and he really cares about the students. This is a hard class just because of the content but he really tries to make it easy and he will definitely go out of his way to help you if you just ask for help. Definitely reccommend.
Best math teacher ever! Mike is hilarious and really cares about his students. He makes it easy to pass even if you're not the best at math.
Mike is the best math professor at UO and makes it really easy for you to get a good grade in his class

reviews.comment: he makes me feel good about math. definitely recommend!!!!
Great professor. Helpful lecture. Caring students. Definitely highly recommend!
AMAZING!
Mike is an awesome math teacher for his class size and I highly recommend him.

he is super accommodating and easy to reach outside of class. No mandatory attendance but he uses clicker question every lecture for participation. Only homework is weekly Webwork and an occasional case study. Always posts notes on canvas and study guides before each exam.

Mike Price is the best math teacher I have ever had. His notes are easy to follow and he posts them on canvas too. He gives weekly quizzes during discussions, but you get 100% for just taking it and extra credit for every right answer. He gives out bonus codes for exams to give you a couple extra points.

reviews.comment: Even though the material was difficult, Mike explained it very thoroughly and made sure his students understood what he was teaching. He was always in a good mood and made class a little more exciting with his funny comments.

The best math teacher at the UO. Lectures are extremely helpful, and he gives out extra credit like it's candy. I had him for both Math 241 and Math 242 and honestly, I wish he taught MATH 243. Do yourself a favor and choose him as your teacher!

Best math teacher on campus. Lots of work on occasions (ex. case studies will kick your butt) but other than that just go to class and pay attention. Iclicker questions in class to give you points and the quizzes during discussions are only for participation (not graded for accuracy- correct answers give you extra points though!). Love Mike!!

Best teacher I've ever had. Makes lectures well worth your time, iClicker and discussion quizzes boost your grade a ton! Make use of the TLC tutoring in the library if you need help and can't get to office hours. Incredible teacher, the only time I've really enjoyed math class.

I didn't pass 241 the first time I took it, but I took it with Mike a second time and got an A.  Mike is an absolute god of a professor and he is funny as well.  He wants you to pass and even gives you bonus codes to help you out on the exams.  Calc is hard in general but Mike makes it as simple as possible.

Best teacher I've ever had. He offers about 4% extra credit so take full advantage of that. His lectures are clear with individual problems building up to complex word problems. He always color codes everything and you can tell he's genuinely so excited to teach this class. If I could take him for every course I would.

Although Business Calculus is not the best class ever, Mike takes a ton of of time going over the material and making sure his students understand the concepts. There is a lot of work for the class, but if you go to his lectures and stay on top of things, you'll pass.

Mike is a great professor despite this being a hard class. He is helpful during office hours and via email if need be. Extra credit during discussion is helpful but the curve was not nearly as large as the 241.  Tests and Homework are hard but if you go to class often and office hours sometimes you should be fine.

Mike was an outstanding professor. He had clear lectures and was very helpful outside of class. He is really easy to talk to and he will help you with any math problems you would have. The class itself is extremely difficult but Mike tries to make it clear and concise as possible.

Mike Price is honestly one of the best professors on campus. I took math 241 and 242 with him and I don't think anyone could have done better. Lectures are tough because theres 300+ people, but he is very good about posting sample exams with solutions before every midterm and final. The class is unavoidably difficult, so expect to work VERY hard.
Best math teacher I've ever had. Wouldn't want to take a math class with any other teacher.

The Kobe Bryant of all professors. Its obvious how much he cares about the well being of students and how much effort he has put in. An overall great professor and easily the best professor I ever had

Great professor! I recommend printing out the lecture notes posted and taking notes during class. Show up to the review session and understand the concepts and you should be fine. Extra credit was given for each test. (Including final) He did curve the class, so try to score above average! GTF's are always helpful for hw.

Great professor! I recommend printing out the lecture notes posted and taking notes during class. 2 midterms and 1 final. Show up to the review session and understand the concepts and you should be fine. Extra credit was given for each test. (Including final) He did curve the class, so try to score above average! GTF's are always helpful for hw.
Great professor!

Homework each week. 3  projects , they are hard but GTF always helpful. Exam will be similar to the study guide, do it and go to office hours. 2 midterms, 1 final, 3 projects (only 3% of your grade but they are hard)

Mike Price is one of the best professors I've had so far. He explains everything very well and will answer any question you have during lectures and takes the time to make sure you understand  it. Also his tests are easy if you pay attention and understand the material.
This class was very difficult and I am not pleased with my grade. But I guess all math 241 classes are this difficult so what can you do

One of the smartest math professors I've ever come across. Highly recommend. You will learn a lot, but don't take his class if you don't plan on working hard. Answers questions very thoroughly, is very helpful and precise with his language. Cares about his students. Would definitely take again.

Awesome professor. His lectures are interesting and his teaching style keeps you engaged. Be ready to study outside of class. Unless you are a genius in the subject, you have to work for your A. I found myself teaching myself certain portions of the material because I hadn't done algebra in 2 years, but if you need help, he's the best person to ask
Mike is a great teacher. He really wants you to do well and understand, and is extremely helpful. I reccomend taking math with him!
Does more then most professors due, such as the videos he makes so you can watch before class. Super helpful. Watch them.
The class is awesome, he is a great guy. He is super helpful during office hours. I strongly recommend him.
I like Mike a lot. Wasn't an easy class but he really cares about his students and he's a genuinely nice guy who will help you out whenever you need. He has it together.

The only math teacher I've had in high school or college that could demystify math for me. He could explain a theory 5 different ways until everyone in the room knew what he was talking about, he even made sure to go all the way through his examples.  He always made himself available to students even if that meant extending his office hours.
Mike is great! He has a super awesome attitude and a great sense of humor. He makes things make sense too and will spend the time with you to make sure you understand. He was super fantastic!!
Nice teacher and very helpful, but class is hard.
Best Math Teacher I have ever had!!!
A fantastic, helpful, enthusiastic teacher. One of the best math teachers I have ever had.

I found this class pretty difficult and didnt really like the exam format at all-spent too much time on True/False and not enough time for the long answer Q's (my mistake obviously but they are pretty tricky). The reviews are supposed to be "at least as hard as the exam" I found the reviews a lot easier than the exams but maybe its just me.
Very helpful and excited to teach. He made the class interesting.
Best teacher I have ever had. Do the work, study and you will ace this class
Great Professor, explains concepts well and uses good examples. Very passionate about teaching, set up a review session outside of class before every exam.

This is the best math class I have ever taken. He is extremely clear and well-organized and isn't patronizing at all. I was dreading completing my math requirement but he made this class both interesting and entertaining.

He has a good reputation as  a meh professor in math 242 and 111, however in math 247 he is hard grader. The quiz are always hard and the final is insane hard. Its not a regular calculus class, it cover more in depth differential equations. Its more word problems than solving problems.

Very clear lecturer, approachable, wants students to succeed/cares about students.very patient, tries to be available for help all the time.realistic with good sense of humor.Enjoyed this class only due to his teaching.

Great teacher. Math 242 was extremely difficult, but I went to every lecture because he was really helpful with his example problems. Print out the lecture example problems before class and be extremely organized with your notes. Very helpful when approached. Excellent handwriting. Tests took days to study for, but it was calculus.
Professor Price is by far the best teacher i have had in math. if given the option to sign up for his class DO IT! im still amazed at his perfect hand writing on the chalk board.
Simply the best teacher I've had at UO to date. He goes over the material really well and makes a normally dull class fun :] Also, take note at his many tie options..
Good guy, very good for student. But if you want get help from a 500 class(Math241), you'd better work hard at first.
He is a great professor,and always with patience.It's really helpful to study with him.I LOVE him!!!!!!!

Mike Price is the man. He makes class entertaining and is very clear during lecture. Take his class! his weekly quizzes were relatively simple. only gave one webwork assignment a week. His tests were pretty hard as expected when you take calculus though
Mike Price is an excellent professor. He makes math (a rather dry subject) actually interesting. His teaching is also easy to understand for both his MATH 111 and MATH 241 classes.

If you have to take a math class, take it with Mike. Like everyone else said, he is an amazing professor. He's hilarious and really helpful. He's definitely one of my favorite teachers at Oregon and I hate math.

This professor is AMAZING!! He is one of the best professors in the math department. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!! he writes out all the steps and gives full explanation with examples. HIS CLASS FILLS UP REALLY FAST so, if you have senior friends ask them to hodl the spot. You will pass the class. i got 40% on the final and passed. BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!!!

best teacher at the U of O!  so outgoing and positive, keeps students entertained and made me always want to come to class.  he explains everything in detail and clearly and knows what he is talking about.  love him!!!

Hes awesome! If you are trying to find a teacher for a math class and he is available, PICK HIS CLASS!! He likes to joke around, he clearly explains everything, he has review session, an amazing friendly guy and knows how to have fun in class so its not deathly boring!! HE IS THE MAN!! A++
Great teacher.  Knows how to get students interested and focused.
THis is guy the best teacher alive!! no joke, he is amazing at teaching and he does a great job on everything. Too bad he doesnt teach much anymore. but i would major in math if he teaches.

Great Teacher, he explained class material very clearly and very effectively.  I hate math and find it pointless but needed it for Business credits, and he made the class as enjoyable as possible.  good sense of humor.  And worked with your schedule nicely.  I took the summer session and it was fabulous!
BEST professor ever! i had him for 95 and 111. i wish all the math professors are like him.
Love him, a great teacher. makes the class not dull and is clear in his lecture notes and actually tells us what will be on the midterms. I recommend taking any math class with him!

Take the Math 211, 212, and 213 sequence from him if you think you might struggle with it. Mike is the best! Not to mention he keeps the 9am class entertained with his jokes. If you need to visit him during his office hours, get there early. He is extremely helpful.

Mike Price is a wonderful teacher. He is funny and makes jokes in class and laughs at himself. The way he explains things is very helpful. Very clear when giving examples, very neat penmanship. I would recommend this teacher to anyone!

Mike Price is a very helpful teacher. He cares about his student's understanding the material. He jokes all the time and the class not borig like regular math class. Very good teacher. I totally reccommend him.

Mike is a great teacher.  He's patient, helpful, understanding and clear.  He is also fun and humorous.  About the actual course: We used the textbook pretty much every class and, unless youre good with math, you should probably be there everyday.  If you have to take a math class, definitely try to get one with Mike...you won't regret it.
good teacher
makes math much easier!

I really love Mike Price. There were times when I would ask questions, some of them were probably stupid, and he would patiently go back and explain everything. He is really concerned with his students understanding the material and doing well in the class. He's awesome!!!
easiest class I've ever had - only went on test days - mike seems like a very nice guy.

Seriously the best math teacher iv ever had. So clear, funny, easy going, and young. What more to ask for. Test are very clear doesnt try to trick you. Tells you everything that will be on it. By far best teacher at UofO, no joke....take him!
Mikey Price is the best math teacher i've ever had.  Campared to the girl I have now for math 111 this guy is jesus.  Take any math class possible from this guy, you will love him.  Such a good guy!

I have never had a math teacher that used different colored chalk and spent time on the apperance of his examples.  He is an amazing instructor, young, easy to talk to, and humorus.  I would take any math class you can from this guy.
Phenomenal teaching ability. Tells it like it is and doesn't waste your time. Clear, helpful, pleasant. If available I would reccomend Mike for any math class at Oregon
I really liked Quinn. She's very thoughtful and open minded. Take her class! As long as you work hard and come to class, there's no reason you shouldn't get an A or a B.

Quinn is honestly so sweet. She made WR121 not as boring as I'm sure it usually is. She really likes participation but has a rule where every student can miss three classes before their participation grade goes down. Wish I could have her for WR122!
Best professor in University of Oregon. She is very generous and helpful. Her class directly helps improving the writing skill! Highly recommend!!!!
Quinn's wonderful!

Quinn is really great! Very sweet and cares a lot about her students and their writing. As creative writing teachers go she is more encouraging than critical, which I know is less helpful at times, but she also gave me plenty of very helpful feedback over the course of the term. She always helped me feel like I was progressing as a writer.
Funny guy, always pleasant lectures.
He is a very good professor, I would recommend taking a class

If you have a chance to take a class with Prof Radcliffe, DO IT! He is truly amazing, and you can tell from the way he talks/cares about his students to his lecture material. He wants you to take class material and adapt it IRL. I appreciated the way he would compile feedback from assignments/in-class materials and adjust his lectures accordingly.

The peofessor I enjoyed him a lot. He adjusts the class based on students feedback and gives extensions for class assignments with out questions. The two exams turned into fun projects. the lectures/speakers were enjoyable and helps with networking, goea deep into the media business, shares his experiencea, assignments are straight forward

He's a great professor and will keep you engaged throughout class. He's very clear on assignment expectations and allows for creative freedom. The guest speakers he consistently has are very informative and helpful if you pay attention. Great class for networking. Would take this class again and will look for his name for future registration.

One of the BEST professors at UO! Such a kind person and it's obvious he cares a lot about his students. All of our assignments were really fun and engaging and I learned a lot from this course! Definitely would take a class with Damian again!

Prof. Radcliffe's J100 class is something I'd recommend to every single person at UO. It shows students the resources we have available and a look at the wide variety jobs within the J school. Class is guest speakers, take small notes and respond at the end of the week. Guest speakers are very interesting and give you a lot of real world advice.

I loved taking J100 with Damian. He is a great professor, assignments are clear and relatively simple. He brought in amazing guest speakers throughout the term. If I could I would totally take another class with Damian. Attendance is mandatory but I always wanted to attend since the speakers are great!

This was the easy class Ive ever taken. Weekly reflections and a weekly quiz about the material in class. There are new guest speakers every class that speak about there life experiences and careers. You learn lots of tools for success that can help you in college and beyond. Attendance is "word of the day" that gets revealed at the end of class.

Act professional in this class, and you will be treated professionally in return. Take a lot of notes, because you'll need them for the pop quiz on what you listened to that day. There is minimal outside work. Overall, 5 star instructor. You'll get a lot out of taking J100.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absolutely goated professor. Radcliffe was very communicative and helpful, and one of the best professors I've had at UO. His classes were incredibly helpful and entertaining, attendance was mandatory but was never a burden or not enjoyable, highly recommend taking a class with him!

Damian is a fantastic person, and I learned a lot from him. Most of his assignments were very beneficial, and he wanted to get the most out of his students. I wish he had been a bit clearer and more direct with some feedback, but overall, he's an awesome professor, and I recommend taking it.

Radcliffe is a cool guy. He's funny, easy to understand, and selected really great guest speakers for our class. I like this class a lot in general, I feel like I was able to learn so much not related to my major, just simply in career advice and paths I can take, which I find to be most beneficial.
Very Nice!!! This class was just filled with guest speakers every week and creating reflections. He is very understanding and cares about his students! No exam or tests for this class.

Damian is British and one of the nicest professors. I'll warn you--he is not an easy grader. You will definitely have to work, especially if you want an A. However, he gives great feedback and cares greatly about your success in the course and beyond. I recommend him entirely.
Elizabeth is truly a wonderful professor. She was respectful and understood at 8 am we would be more tired or sometimes late. The readings weren't heavy at all. I would take her again.

Makes lectures very long by consistently lecturing. When there are breaks in lectures, they are mainly pointless "brain breaks" that are more annoying than helpful. She is very nice but doesn't offer any kind of feedback and brings very little to my learning as an EDST undergrad.

Elizabeth is an easy grader, but lectures directly off the slides. Feedback is limited, especially during class. Her classes are required in the Educational Foundations major, but do not recommend by choice.

Elizabeth is a wonderful and caring instructor who made starting off the morning early at 8 a.m. a breeze- I highly recommend taking her for any of your education related courses! As long as you show up- and are willing to socialize and interact in table groups you will be successful.
Would never take again.
Very easy class. You don't actually have to do the reading. Lots of discussion. Show up, do the 4 assignments over the term, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Avoid Rhonda Nese at all costs!! Taking her class was a horrible experience. I passed no problem, but their inability to teach even the most basic of subjects was embarrassing. They went on about their personal life w/ no regard for the students' education or well being. Each time I attempted to speak to her, I was dismissed or talked over.

Incredibly passionate and caring professor. One of my favorites and you can really tell she knows how to  get the class to care. If you don't know where to start in social work this is 100% the class for you. It's important to know is it's more important to write about the texts than your own experiences for the writings. Trust me, cite cite cite.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nese is incredible and I often left her lectures really motivated because her passion for her work is contagious. There are readings assigned every week but minimal assignments compared to my other classes and although you lose points when you're absent, there are extra credit opportunities to make it up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Nese was very easy to work with. The course was very well made so I barely even had to contact her for extra help.

Overall a very well-rounded class. Allowed lots of self-reflection and thoughtful discussions. The work was enjoyable and challenging in a really good way. Definitely would recommend taking this class if you have the opportunity to.
Such a nice professor, it was online but still very helpful. Canvas was organized and both textbooks were free, which was great.

I took this winter term 2021! She had a super calming voice and it was a web class. All you have to do is read from the two FREE textbooks and take reading quizzes throughout the term. Then write two papers( easy) mostly reflecting on yourself. And discussion posts every week. You can get by without watching every lecture and reading every chapter.
I love professor Zimlich, I had her for WRIT 100 and she was super helpful and gave minimal work. Definitely an easy A but still was able to learn. 10/10 recommend!

Rhonda is an amazing teacher who knows her stuff! She is incredibly kind and cares for each of her students. If you've taken writing courses before it isn't hard, but if you haven't she definitely tries to work with you and help you. Would take a class of hers again!

Rhonda was AMAZING! Take her class if you can! She was very kind and helpful. She was very accessible as well. She did a great job making the class (most students take only because it's required to graduate) interesting. She also gave plenty of time to work on ideas and writing during class.

Funny guy, but since your grade depends so much on participation, it makes lectures pretty stressful. This class is very hard if you hate talking in class, I recommend sitting up front. His grading system doesn't work because GE's miss people talking, and its just not possible for him to remember so many names. At least the assignments are easy.
Just show up and participate and you get an A, and his teaching style was very engaging and taught us how to critically think.

40% of your grade is participation (not attendance) in a 200-student course. Unless he happens to call on you more than twice a class every class, you're hard-capped at receiving ~60% of this. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

I would have preferred exams over his way of grading participation. I wasn't shy and participated almost every class, sometimes multiple times in on lecture. In a class of 130 people I felt I was doing alright, not the best but I didn't expect to receive an 45 percent in participation. I just wish there was more transparency.

actually hate this guy bro. participation is 40% of your grade in a class of 200 people. his lectures consist entirely of him stroking his own ego and him saying "can you rehash this in your own words" or "can you rephrase that" like please. one of his assignments actually was rate my spotify playlist. dont take his classes for ur own sake

In Dr. Alvarados class participation is 40% of your grade, which is ridiculous. I understand he wants his students to participate but the class feels like you're in high school and the whole class you're essentially just listening to your classmates speak. It's not particularly hard but I wouldn't take again.

This guy is awesome, he's super well-spoken and very insightful. In-class participation is worth 40% of your grade, so if you do not like talking in class, do not register for his class. Overall, funny guy and really seems to enjoy his job.

This class is really participation heavy with it being 40% of your grade. So if you are shy and know you wont find yourself participating, I wouldn't recommend this class. But if this isn't the case, I would recommend this class. A lot of the class discussion was pretty interesting and made me think more critically about data topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3 assignments outside of class, graded really lightly, and don't take that much time to do. Be prepared to participate in class because it basically determines your grade. Some lectures are harder to participate in than others and can be boring, but no finals or midterm so fair enough. Teachers chill, gave opportunities to participate.
participation not required but it is 40% of your grade. lectures can be boring sometimes but sometimes not.

I like the teacher, I like the subject, I hate the class structure. The weekly assignments are repetitive and time consuming. The attendance is the worst part, 40% of your grade is "attendance" that is based solely on quality and quantity of participation. Class is to big for this type of policy. It seems nearly impossible to get an A.

Expects you and everyone else to participate like 5x in each class when theres 130+ students. Graded 40% off participation, sounds impossible to get an A. he said his grade average last term/year was an 83%, not good in my opinion.;
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF IT'S NOT REQUIRED FOR YOU! 40% of your grade is participating but only like 1/2 the class will get to participate per day. Introverts avoid this class! If you have to take it.. good luck soldier. There's also a big written assignment that's 10 pages worth of analyzing websites. Dropped it on day 1.
Good lecturer and funny guy. Cares a lot about attendence and participation but if you show up to class everyday and raise your hand a couple of times during the term, you'll get an A.

One of the first things he teaches is the value of honest reasoning and constructive argumentation. Yet, he was consistently overconfident and even patronizing in regards to his stances. Some of which are well beyond agreed fact amongst philosophers. ("Morality is objective"..?). Communication is poor. Doesn't believe in handing out A's.

Honestly I really liked this class, the material is very relevant and the essay for this class was structured week by week so there was no stress for finals. The professor is also very engaging and passionate. That being said, I think he should lower the 40% weight of participation. It's not realistic with this class size and can be competitive.

I want to preface that in no way is the professor bad at his job, it is more the change in syllabus and the structure of assignments I would like to point attention to. If you enjoy 40% of your grade being participation with mandatory attendance, then this is the class for you. I would not recommend it unless absolutely necessary for your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes participation 40% of the grade in a class with 200 people in it. Can never get anything meaningful from the lectures because the time is filled with people repeating themselves five times to get credit. Absolute waste of a class. Very condescending and sure of himself when he has no right to be. Easy but worthless. Steer clear by all means.

He is very strict about formatting, but as a result, assignments are very clear and not particularly difficult. This is a class that you take for the lecture, not the work. Alvarado is a good lecturer that manages to fit many complex subjects into a short timeframe while making them easy to understand. Great class if interested in tech ethics

I absolutely enjoyed Prof Alvarado! Class topics were super interesting although he is heavier on participation/attendance. The final paper is built along the weeks so each weekly assignment is a piece of the paper that comes together at the end, so it forces you to not procrastinate the entire thing. Super enjoyable guy, you can tell he cares!

The class has 3 weekly assignments that can get very repetitive. Weekly reading can be very long and is the martial that he goes over in lectures. Weekly cumulative assignments aren't hard just tedious. Makes a huge deal about lecture attendance/participation. nothing is given a rubric so grading is confusing and slow. GEs make or brake your term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't have to. Participation and attendance is MANDATORY, everyone must speak in his class and is written down for speaking/if you do not speak (not just discussion section). He is passive aggressive when it comes to students not participating and will make comments throughout class if you do not speak.

Dr. Alvarado is my favorite professor so far. He is an absolutely AMAZING lecturer. The class is formatted fantastically, instructions are clear, and all work is relevant. He strives to offer the best education possible, even organizing a conference hosting multiple renowned figures. The class is truly interesting and his lectures are 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My experience with Alvarado was rough. He has easily made Phil 102 the most poorly structured class I have ever taken in college. Quizzes are not regularly updated. Feedback is slow. I can't even see my grades, so I don't know where to improve. I would stay far away from this Ethics class. He's a very smart guy, but the structure is the worst.
She's amazing and super caring. Always has a very positive attitude and keeps the discussion engaging.
It is a super awesome and pleasant class, outside of the readings this class is engaging and exciting. The professor is the entire class and learning is fun with this class.

Annie is the most amazing professor I have ever had. She is passionate about the subject, accessible during office hours and over email, and anything you need assistance with she is willing to help. She is incredibly understanding, kind, and accommodating along with posting readings online. She is incredible and I strongly suggest taking her course
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Annie is so fun. Her lectures were well structured and informative. She also had great discussion questions that helped students understand difficult topics easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very nice

Very knowledgable about the topic and you can tell she really enjoys talking about anthropology. She is very type A so if you need an extension or you find yourself missing a lot of classes, TALK TO HER! I swear meeting with her in office hours helped so much and I realized she may seem strict but she's honestly so understanding and approachable.

her attendance requirements can be daunting at first, and she can seem pretty tough but she does an amazing job explaining the material, very thorough, and if you're struggling in the course you HAVE to communicate because she will be very understanding. Not an easy A but very engaging. Also not a bad grader and gives good clear feedback

Info is interesting but does not feel like a real class. Lectures are just inaccessible slides. People are dying from COVID and we have to turn it into a final project. Even if you are faced with life emergencies, even COVID, ironically, do not expect to be allowed makeup work. Too strict for a 100- class that is a lot of work without much quality.

Vapid teacher, very vague instructions. I'm not huge on anthropology, but this course/prof didn't help. Can't think of a single exercise/assignment that wasn't pedantic busywork. Not too challenging, but even less inspiring. Perhaps she'd be better in person? I'd definitely shop around for another prof/take a different class if you can't find one.

SO MUCH READING. some weeks it can be over 100 pages (txtbks, book chapters, articles, etc). honestly, with the amount of work this class had for being a lvl 100 course, it literally felt like the professor was being disrespectful to our time outside of being students. DO NOT take this class unless you're an anthro fanatic.

Please do not take this class if is an online course. Has to be the worst class I've taken through covid. Very little homework, but mounds of readings, lectures, and videos a week. Expect to be reading and watching more than all your other classes combined. Really lazily slapped together. Good subject and info, horrible execution.

Really depends on how strict your GE is with the outcome of your grade. Richlin herself is super laidback but my GE wasn't so I had to work a little harder than necessary imo lmao. but otherwise, Richlin is great!! Lectures are super interesting, overall one of my easier classes. Very few assignments throughout the course so be careful with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Im a Bio Anth major and I found this class extraordinarily boring. Some videos were cool but the lectures drag on. Lots of 'talk to person beside you' exercises, very little homework and its really easy so thats a plus. If you're an Anth major then take it cus its required, if otherwise I would take something else.

One of the greatest professors I've ever had! Interesting lectures, engaging, and helpful. They offer extra credit and there's been one big project so far, but it's spaced out and there are lots of opportunities to get help if needed. Explains everything, answers questions clearly. Will def take more classes.

She's cool as a person and as a dancer, and nice and helpful if you come to her. Had to take p/f and class quiz averages were D-. In class activities were fun and made sense for embodiment, but no clear grading, rubrics or prompts. Quizzes were impossible to receive a good grade, no one ever got 100%. Slides are from 2020 as well and outdated.

Worst teacher I've ever had. If you enjoy dancing don't take this class, better yet don't go to the UO. The dancing done in this class is minimal and the professor is ignorant to technique and general teaching skills. She uses words without knowing their meaning. The woman knows nothing of anatomy and continuously uses incorrect statements.

Rita is a very different kind of professor. Nothing is ever clear, no one gets above a 65% on her tests and she does not care. if you miss class, your grade will drop significantly and there are no excuses. She failed me even though I had a very rough year and even confided in her. I do not recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Astounded at this teacher being at UO. I have enjoyed all of my classes until this one. Save yourself and don't take this class. Unprofessional, unprepared, lectures DID NOT cover information on tests, etc. Don't miss class, even due to physical or mental illness, you will not be given the ability to make it up. The worst teacher ive had at UO

A super interesting class and I actually really enjoyed the content however Rita's tests were super difficult and tended to be not what was taught or focused on. The embodiment aspect of the class was a really good learning tool and helped tremendously. Just be prepared to not do well on tests that you can't really study for.

Literally so bad. Never take this class. She has no empathy or understanding for anything and can't teach for the life of her (lectures are literally just pictures and she expects you to hear everything she says after she goes over it once) but grades unnecessarily hard.

Really cool - intimidating at first. Lectures are very messy and not super informational. It is really cool to embody each thing we learn about though. Quizzes rarely have to do with the lectures so read the textbook. Weekly one page essays. Shes really cool but grades hard and isnt super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rita has a lot ti work on. She seems nice, her quizzes and tests never match her actual lectures. She thinks if you do not participate in class you're an awful student. Overall I would not take this class nor recommend it. If you like dance, don't take this class.

Definitely intimidating at first, but I found this class to be eye-opening and not too hard. Weekly 1-page writing reflections graded mostly on effort, and open-note tests. I would recommend going through the PowerPoints on canvas to create a study guide to use on each test, this technique saved me. Great class for science credit!

Lectures are very vague. Even if you read and go to class, getting good grades on her tests are hard (class averages for both test weve taken have been less than 50%... even with open notes she told us about after we had studied) shes a great woman and easy to talk to... but not the best teacher ever.

She's disorganized, bad at explaining things, and honestly it seems like she doesn't even know what she had planned. If you ask a question, her answer will have nothing to do with what you actually asked and she just assumes you know what she's talking about. She flips through slides very fast which makes taking notes very difficult.

BEWARE. She describes this course as being for non science majors. However her entire class consists of anatomy, upper level anatomy topics and even human physiology topics. This is not introductory level science. She is awfully disorganized and acts like a strict high school teacher. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The book has nothing to do with class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Honka is a kinda scary the first day, but by day two, you really respect her as a person! She's extremely smart, and she's wild! I respect her intelligence and her ability to just be herself and let loose. She's also extremely open-minded, and it shows!

Dance 301 I would recommend to so many people. Throughout the entire term all that is required are 3 papers, and thats it. She assigns readings that are to be read before class, but many students do not read and still get get a good grade in this class. One day of the week is lecture heavy, the other is all dancing. Very fun, and very easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rita is scary at first but as long as you don't screw around or get on her bad side you will get an A. Participation is key. Actually doing the reading is recommended. You write 2, 3-page papers (that are honestly really easy to BS) and 1 10 page paper at the end (which, if you're on her good side, is also really easy to BS). The class is fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 10 page final, longest Ive done in college so far, but very doable considering how well prepared we were for it from lectures and experience. Doesnt put in grades on canvas, but as long as you communicate with her and do well on your papers, you should know where you stand. If you dont put in the effort, dont be surprised when upset at the end.

She is witty, talented, cares about her students and her passion for her research is contagious. I went into this class with no understanding or interest in African dance and I came out with a complete different mindset about so many things. Hard class because Rita takes her research seriously, but if you put in the work, you can get an A.

Overall, I thought this class was a waste of money. The professor was extremely unorganized, did not use canvas to upload any grades, and gave contradicting instructions in class that were not on the syllabus with no rubric to reference. She never responds to emails and is sarcastic and rude.

I would not recommend this class. The professor is unapproachable and does not give good feedback when help is asked for. Assignments do not have clear directions and the professor tends to contradict themselves.
Best teacher I've ever had

Professor Honka is very clear on what she wants out of a movement and once she learns of your potential, she helps you achieve it.  She is a good teacher who uses her wit and sarcasm to teach which is fun. She enjoys dance and as a female in her class, I try to move like her too.  She's got skillz!  She's interested in everyone"s success.

One of the most difficult professors I've had.  Difficult to talk to, difficult assignments.  Longest paper I've ever written for our final. She gives vague, rude answers to questions and emails. Feels impossible to succeed in her class.
Took African Dance from her. It's a hard class, very demanding, and she moves fast. But if you ask a question, she'll be sure to answer it or demonstrate the step for you.
Ridiculously hard grader, very aggressive personality.  Teaches an interesting and at times fun class, but not the most peronable person.

The course was Media Coverage of the Middle East. He defined "media" quite broadly. Classes are mostly discussions of readings, so staying on top of readings and participating in class is very important

This professor is very passionate about anything that he teaches, and is encouraging when it comes to in-class student engagement. He is super communicative and makes time in his schedule to meet with students even if they can't make it to office hours. One thing to consider when taking this class is that he has an unorthodox project in this class

Great professor, really fun and passionate about the topic, good mix of discussion and lecture and the resources we are assigned are interesting and topical, sometimes he can talk over people but it's just because he's so excited about what they're saying.

Very passionate professor who knows what he's talking about. The Reacting games might be frightening if you don't know how to roleplay or do public speaking, but the class helps you ease into it. There can be a hefty amount of writing during games, depending on your role, but it isn't graded on quality. Participation is paramount to succeeding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not worth taking the class, you need to do 8hrs of work per week, so 2 hours for each class period, if this is your major its worth it or if your into the topic, the info is very interesting, but for a 100 level class it was not worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course is a very fun interactive class. Participation and enthusiasm is necessary, and not for those with stage fright. Some heavy readings in short bursts but overall not a big workload. A casual class that you meet friends in. Prof. Colby is accessible outside of class and very understanding. Read syllabus often b/c due dates not always told

Amazing class with a fantastic professor. The lectures were accessible and informative while handling the difficult issue of covering how the Middle East is portrayed in the media. Instead of textbooks, you will use graphic novels and have an open discussion. I would take another class with this professor without a doubt.

Sometimes the workload would get intense when it came closer to the beginning of a new game, but for the most part, this class felt like an elective that also happened to satisfy a history requirement!

Prof. Colby does a good job of conveying material to an educated audience, so make sure you read the assigned materials before class or else you'll be lost. His grading style is very fair and he gives good feedback. Tests were very fair as well. Overall I'd recommend him as a professor for a REL class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was by far one of my favorite classes! He really cares about teaching his students about the roots of Islam. Even if you are Muslim, you will learn so much! You have to read the textbook and the books because those are on the exams. His review sessions are SO helpful! As long as you pay attention in class and take notes, you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you like lectures, which I do, Colby is great. He knows a lot about what he teaches and is obviously very passionate about it. Even for students that have trouble in his classes, if he knows you are trying to grasp the subject and at least giving him a well worked paper, you will get a good grade. He's fair, but does expect work. This is college

If you listen and take notes on what he says in class and actually work (like University was intended to be for) then you will do just fine. I found his lectures to be extremely compatible with the slide shows.  Yes, they are difficult to glean information from if you miss class.. so just go. He is extremely knowledgeable and very approachable.

You will get the grade you deserve.  He is a passionate instructor that cares about the topic and I think truly cares about how much his students learn.  He is very approachable and willing do discuss anything.  You can't be lazy in his class.  Do the readings and he will keep you informed, on track.
Painfully boring lectures, no clarity, grades are based on three ridiculously hard mid terms and final.  Would not recommend at all.  Nice teacher, hard class.

A ton of readings for an intro class, and he does not go over the readings in class or in discussion. The powerpoints were not helpful, because they only included keywords and it was hard to take notes on what he said, because he would talk very fast and include unimportant things. GTFs did not know what was going on in class. Would not recommend.

His lectures were very enigmatic. A decent amount of what is on the tests is from the textbook and he does not go over the readings AT ALL. His powerpoints hardly make up for his lectures. I'm never really quite sure exactly what to take notes on.

Nice guy, but his lectures are boring and extremely confusing, especially for an intro level class. His GTFs clearly have no idea what's going on either. His insistence on occasionally speaking in Arabic to a class full of non-Arabic speakers is bizarre.

He is a nice guy but repeats himself a lot on points that don't seem very important. Knowlegable but I think the way the class is set up doesn't allow him to teach the info very well. He speaks in arabic a lot, sometimes i seems like he is trying to show off how much he knows. It was a difficult class for a 100 level course. Tests were hard.

Colby was very smart but was not able to teach that knowledge. He failed to use the lecture to teach us what we should know to excel in his class. He made no connection with the class and thus he just had 100 blank faces staring at him during the lecture. He made what could be very interesting material very bland and dry and hard  to digest. AWFUL

He is a great guy and the class is very interesting, but for a 102 class it is very confusing. This is supposed to be a introductory class so we obviously don't know much and he rambles on in Arabic like we know it or something. Tests were ridiculously hard, all essays and a lot of reading.

He is very thorough.  There is a lot of information given in a short amount of time. It was the hardest class I've ever taken, but also the class I gained the most out of.  If you attend class and keep up with the readings (which is a lot) then you can pass the class with flying colors.

Nice guy, tough grader, speaks arabic a lot, 2 texts 1 novel & handout readings. 2 essays,1 outside activity. extra credit worth 40 pnts. GTFs are seriously lost.boring class.MUST attend discussions. I got an A- but it required so much work. not recommended if you're not interested in the subject. PS. it has nothing to do with ISLAM or the prophet.
tough grader. Uses Arabic words during the lecture which makes it hard for non Arabic speakers and does not translate the words. his GTFs dont know what they're talking about.

Rick's a nice guy, but doesn't know how to teach. If you're looking to learn how to use any of the game engines the class is asking you to use, that's not gonna happen. He can't give any technical help. The class will mostly be comprised of teaching yourself at home with Youtube. Mandatory attendance classes are just watching artist inspirations.

Silva is a really good guy but lacks in the direct teaching department. You could chat with the guy all day as he has a lot of experience in the ARTD field and he does a few demos, but nonetheless, you will learn more on your own while doing the projects than in class. I still recommend him though, he's nailed the relaxed learning environment vibe.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rick is a super nice guy and I've never had trouble setting up meetings outside of class, however, all we do during our class meetings is watch short videos of professional animators. Not a single tutorial is done in class, so you have to go out and spend your time watching Youtube tutorials to figure anything out...
Rick is a nice guy, but his lectures are mostly about watching artists who use animation. If you are looking to gain technical skills within 3D animation you wont get much from this class.

Rick is a good guy but isn't an effective teacher. He will not meet outside of lab hours, nor teaches practical uses of game engines. His classes consist of two hours of watching videos on the industry and only 1 hour of lab but does not actually teach the subject. Frustrating to spend long hours on projects but get very little help when necessary.

Great guy-horrible teacher. He does not offer guidance not does he supply his students with the proper tools to succeed. He time and time relies on knowledgeable students teaching others instead of getting hands-on himself. Very disappointing.
the best! super funny and nice overall great professor!

She is literally one of the best professors I have had so far. She gives amazing feedback, will go in depth about how your essay could use improvements and she grades decently easy and will give extra points usually. She cares about actually teaching students and making sure they can apply what they learn for the future. Overall 10/10 teacher!

Prof Schuman genuinely cares about the success of her students and gives really good feedback. She is always available for question and willing to help. She is trying to make her student's lives easier, not harder. She's also really funny and makes class interesting.

Dr Schuman has been the best English teacher I have had, she is funny, gives great feedback and wants to see you succeed. All you need to do in this class is actively participate in it and don't use AI 😭 if you're lucky enough to get Dr Schuman as a teacher I would highly advise you take the class for the credit!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a very good professor. She is understanding of students predicaments and doesn't assign that much. If you stay on top of your work, you will literally never stress about her class.
Switched to everything analog this year; very few things were digital. She is very funny, though, and the class was never not entertaining.

Dr. Schuman is by far one of my favorite professors I've had at UO. Our course was centered around cults and conspiracies, and there was a lot of room for creativity in our (uniquely structured, yet strangely helpful) assignments. This professor is quirky, passionate about her craft, and engaging in lectures. Take her class if you can!

Incredible teacher and person, had her for a core ed writing class and never enjoyed a core ed more! She makes the class fun and uses all sorts of media for teaching purposes. Extra credit is handed out like candy and she does everything in her power for you to succeed (a first draft is an automatic B-) overall 10/10
She is the funniest professor and so willing to help you with anything you need. I wish she taught all my classes.
Very very funny and engaging in class, super kind and understanding teacher overall who wants everyone to succeed. Would 1000% take again.

Dr. Schuman was a pretty good teacher. I liked her style of teaching, it helps you understand the information (relevant to the course). Its also a good credit course for those doing business as we engage in money discussions. Would recommend!

Rebecca is a fantastic professor. She makes learning about German history fun and engaging and encourages us to think deeply about the subject. The course is laid out very nicely, with not too much homework. The group project is fun, and the workload is spread nicely across a large team. You should take this class!

She's nice and passionate about what she's teaching. Very easy class I'm a freshman and think it should be 100 level. if you need to take an arts and letters take this one. little/no homework besides the study questions that we mostly go over in class and aren't required, just helpful for studying for the midterms that are also easy

Prof. Schuman is an amazing person that truly cares about the content she is teaching and her students. She is deeply passionate and only asks for participation in regards to the readings. She is beyond kind and her anecdotes are very impressionable. Read, do the study questions, show up to class, and you will most definitely succeed.

As a non-physics student, he brought the world of physics alive in the physics of light and color. His lectures were engaging his material was interesting and he is a light in this department. I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot that shaped the way I think about things today. take this class with him if you need it.

Taylor is a very accomplished scientist with many teaching awards. Unfortunately, in my experience he has been unresponsive to emails and uninterested in helping during office hours. His lecture format is awful. The slides are the same as the provided notes and it very difficult to actually write anything. Lots of wasted time in lecture and lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. he's very goofy,  quite a few fun demos which makes the class entertaining. he really knows what he's talking about, you learn a lot. only 3 exams, relatively easy if you study. no quizzes or projects. hw is fast and easy. if science isn't your thing, take this class. definitely an easy A :)

One of my favorite classes at uo! Richard is an incredibly interesting guy who teaches a very interesting class (imo). Although the homework questions may not be directly addressed during lectures, he gives many hints & explains the concepts well enough to where they are reasonable. If you do the hw & pay attention during lecture you will do well.

Great guy, not so great professor. The class is filled with concepts and demos, but he doesnt really show you how to do the problems on paper. The lecture, homework, tutorial and exam materials are all very disconnected, and it makes it really hard to study successfully and pass the exams.

Being a student that took physics before I have done my job learning Kinematics and conservation of Energy since they are pretty easy to remember. The tests and homework that he gives will be the easiest you get as a science major. He works really hard to know you know the material and gives exams that are not too hard. Textbook was unneeded.

His lectures are not helpful. He teaches you the concepts in a physical sense through demonstrations, but provides little to no information on the concepts and how to use them on paper (which is the only thing that matters on the tests, which are very tough). The lack of a clear curriculum makes it tough to know which topics are essential.
Richard Taylor makes physics enjoyable and relatively easy to understand. Very laid back and incredibly smart in a welcoming way. Definitely would recommend to anyone interested in physics.
Great professor! Every exam question is from a lecture or homework. So pay attention to those! Use the physics help center to understand and complete your homework- they do a great job helping you.

Professor Taylor offers engaging and interesting lectures, but you really have to go to tutorials, office hours and read the book to get a thorough understanding of the material. He and his TA's are very fair graders, but the exams are usually pretty tough.
He is a great story teller and knows how to present the material in an engaging way.

Such an awesome guy!! I was completely dreading this class because i had a horrible physics teacher in hs and really struggled. Taylor made each lecture interesting, related concepts to real life, and was very engaging. Homework and exams were straightforward. Go to office hours if you need help! Easy even for nonscience majors.

This class has been so enjoyable. Taylor is so enthusiastic. He always makes his classes so interesting and always has stories to tell. One time he was constructing a demo and apparently the class didn't seem too excited.. well he got the boys and girls pumped by making us sing 'Hey Jude.' Such and awesome and useful class for everyday life.

Professor Taylor is fun to listen to (He's British). His lectures are bearable, but not very helpful. I spent hours in the drop-in center trying to complete the homework. However, the homework is a lot more difficult than the tests. An "A" is guaranteed if you put in a decent amount of work.

Sorry about one important mistaek in the last comment. Although he shared fun videos, his lecture was boring because he DID NOT teach further than the textbook. I need to find many outside rescources to do his homework. The final totally sucks! If you have confidence in your physics learnig ability, you'll be fine. He is a nice person, though.

Although he shared fun videos, his lecture was boring for me because he did teach further than the textbook. I need to find many outside rescources to do his homework. The final totally sucks! If you have confidence in your physics learnig ability, you'll be fine. He is a nice person, though.

Overall he is a good professor on teaching, just! However, he is irresponsible on helping students during his office hour. He always said that he would be in his office in certain time but then leave without any notification.

Prof. Taylor is a great professor! His lectures, while they're 2hrs long, are very entertaining. He's from England and somehow finds a way to relate his lectures to his life. If you want to see pictures of his dog Buckley, take this class. :) He's really helpful if you come to his office hours and the hw and tests aren't bad at all too.

good teacher, fun lectures. test r easy but diffrent from HW and does not give a study guide so its hard to know what will be on the tests, i suggest to go to ta or his office hours both very helpful  and nice.

Prof Taylor is the best professor I've had at UO. He is extremely fair, encourages you to learn, and is always available to help. Lectures are entertaining yet still very informative. I had to take the class for my major but would love to repeat it just to have Taylor again. He threw an egg at a sleeping student!
He's awesome and he's not Richard Taylor, he's Jim Morrison.
This guy rocks..literally!
Great teacher, really funny guy and very invested in making physics as interesting as possible.
a very good man. i like that he speaks very deliberately, makes class easy to pay attention in. funny dude too.

He does crack some jokes and he seems like a really nice guy.  However class pace is very slow and I easily lose interest.  My biggest peeve is that he is really into art and photography so he seems to be searching for connections because its what he is interested in and not necessarily what we should be learning, in my opinion.
great guy. hilarious. example: he once threw an egg at a kid who was talking while he was teaching. awesome. good teacher who cares about his students.

Taylor is the man! He is the best teacher ever. His good humor and class demos keeps class interesting. He cares a lot about his students and will really help you. The class is tough, but what physics class isn't? I never missed a single class session!
Great! It's been several years now since I've had him, but he is no doubt one of the best teachers I've ever had. Anyone who can make an analogy with physics to Radiohead is badass!
Great examples, hard class.
No Comments

201 was one of the hardest classes Ive ever taken, but Richard is also one of the best teachers Ive ever had also. What you learn in his class can be used in real life. Very funny guy, wild hair, British accent (you picture it) Great class demos.
funny teacher, even at 9 in the morning. pretty easy, has good presentations

Prof. Rosenberg had really well designed and thoughtful lectures, super interesting! Weekly assignments were simple and consistent, the midterm and the final consisted of both essays and multiple choice, everything was graded by GEs.

Nice guy, but lots of homework.150 page study guide for the final that was a significant portion of our grade. We also had weekly readings which were long, and then an achieve module to go along with it that would generally take an hour if you actually tried, but you get 100 percent for completing them either way. Insane midterm and final.
Final was basically a grade tanker. Also 30 percent of our whole grade, plus study guide was 150 pages long.
Super lecture heavy and tons of textbook readings. There were study guides provided, but they were pretty vague, and both the midterms and the final cover so much content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable. We went to the UO archives to look at the stuff we were studying and he showed us a bunch of super useful digital tools. He explains assignments very clearly and if you stay on top of it the work it super manageable. Beware though he does not update/use the Canvas Grades page so it can be difficult to see what your grade is.
As a course studying the historian's method itself it was very insightful by exploring the different aspects in depth.

Prof. Rosenberg is a sweet person and is passionate about history. His class can be difficult to participate in if you're not open to philosophical thinking. My major focuses on objectivity so I was quiet during discussions. Nevertheless, he makes sure to acknowledge your ideas and include any praise in feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was "anti-Canva" which confused us about our real grade, we didn't know it until it appeared in official grades. There was so much reading for just one post we had to do before every class, and he is very particular about how he wants them organized. The final writing essay was hard because it was unclear what he wanted it to be about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. R. is very knowledgeable about history. That said I felt that throughout the term he was a "sage on stage" rather than a "guide by our side". I put A LOT of effort into the papers, however his comments and assessment of my work were not helpful. It did not seem that he truly tried to understand my work and direct my thinking.

I had him first term of my freshman year and he was excellent. The entirety of your grade is 2 essays and participation. Every class is discussion based. He fishes for answers a lot and if you are following him, you will learn a lot. As for the essays, he looks more at the content than structure or syntax. As long as your ideas are there, you're ok

Rosenberg is awesome. He's clearly the most intelligent person in every room he's in, but he doesn't make you feel like an idiot. His class was fascinating and those 80 minutes flew by every time. You have to do the reading though. He calls on everyone and expects a well-reasoned response. His high expectations make him a tough but fair grader.
he is amazing. get in his class. it was engaging, he is helpful in office hours and very clear. great GREAT professor.
Professor Rosenberg is amazing!  I am currently taking his class and I don't feel I am doing well, but he is always there to help.  He is a very fair grader and he likes to discuss the text in depth.

Prof. Rosenberg is amazing! His class focuses on the ideas and thoughts that were developed in history, and a lot of them were very interesting. This is a "hard" class because he expects you to think a lot about the readings. But it was a very rewarding and interesting class, and he made me glad that I stayed in HC.

Even the "smart" students of the Honors College think he is intimidating. Maybe this is because he expects a lot from us, but there's a better way to encourage learning  than scaring the freshmen.
