On the other hand, students will learn a lot from his seminar formats. Just don't take his course during your first term!

Don't expect to come to class without having finished the reading because few people get away with not being called on in any given class. His discussions are based on the text rather than lecture on historical facts. Overall a challenging class (he grades really hard on papers) but good if you like to talk about what you're reading

Tricia was a very fun professor to have for my first term at UO. She's very funny and caring and constantly is keeping the class entertaining. There was never an assignment that was truly difficult. If I had any questions, she would be right there to answer them. No exams and the group projects were very collaborative and engaging!
Super easy class, i recommend for an easy arts and letters class
Tricia is the best. Super accomodating and fun in class, 100% reccomend
Had Tricia as my FIG teacher. Very nice woman, is willing to help you if you ask. As long as you put in some effort, you will get a good grade.
No matter what level of acting you are at, Tricia makes this class very fun. Only thing is it was very long class so make sure it's not at the end of a long day of classes.

Tricia is simply put, a very easy-going professor. Her assignments are not hard but if you like theater at all are fun and engaging. Even so, she is very lenient and will work with you if you talk to her. Only thing is I would not take the class if you do not like group projects, as those are pretty much every week.

Tricia is probably one of the nicest professors I've ever met. I already liked theatre arts but her class made me like it even more. She is very accommodating and kind. She is very helpful and wants you to learn and succeed in her class. It should be noted though that attendance is mandatory.
so sweet and fun! I always looked forward to showing up to her class :)

Tricia is very kind and considerate. If you need anything, just email her within a decent time and she is usually willing to give extensions or meet for office hours. The only complaint was the number of times you get sent to a breakout room. It was kinda annoying. But she is a good professor.

I loved taking Tricia's class this term. I didn't have much experience with theater yet she made everyone feel welcomed no matter what level you were at. There is a lot of reading in the beginning but it's fun reading. She is a great teacher and you can tell she cares about her students. I had so much more fun then I thought I would!
Josh is easily in the GOAT conversation. The lectures are super engaging and he is really easy to work with. Would 11/10 recommend taking a class with him.
Almost everyone failed the midterm and final, had good lectures, but surprisingly bad exams with no preparation. He made an easy class hard for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Josh was a great guy. I am not a science person at all, so class was hard for me to understand. Josh, however, made it bearable. only thing to worry about for this class is that his tests are more conceptual, so even if you've studied your heart out, it's a 50/50 shot that whatever you studied will be on the test. If you need the science cred do it

He is a great lecturer but the midterm and finals had a 50/50 chance of actually having material that we learned thoroughly in class, so that was very disappointing. However, I respect him for being a little more flexible during the final. Despite it not being much help overall.
Josh is so funny and loved his Earth Science class. Would take again because he's so funny. Team Josh

Josh is a great professor. I learned quickly that to get a good grade in his class, you need to make sure you show up to the lectures and take good notes!! The midterm was extremely hard but he saw the average and changed how we are doing the final. Great guy!!
fantastic professor. the midterm was wack, but he realized that and revised his plan for the final. super chill dude.

Not a very difficult class, not really any homework. There was a midterm and final, he let us use notes on final after the class didn't do too well on the midterm. The lectures were pretty interesting, I would recommend this for a science credit!

I LOVE PROF ROERING!!! He's so so so kind and helpful both in class and in his office hours. The TA's Alex and Gordon were also very helpful both in lab and office hours. The content is confusing but he sets up the class to help you succeed. He makes me wish I was an earth science major just so I can take another class with him.

Josh was a super fun professor and wants his students to succeed. He makes this class super easy and understandable by using visuals and explains concepts in a understandable manner. Labs felt like busy work and also impact your grade the most, so if you do good on labs you'll pass the class. Attendance required for labs and lectures.
Really good lecturer, you can tell that he wants you to succeed and he will work with you to make that happen

This was a stats class with a lot of time spent in the computer lab - it was never gonna be super fun but Josh definitely made it accessible and relatively engaging. No tests but the midterm project was super intense. You have to be able to use the material, just not from memory. Weekly homework took an hour or two and that was it.
Best dude out there, def take GEOL418! Made me love rocks on other geo related ologies. Would 100% refer a friend.
This is a hard subject with very little outside help but Josh explains concepts very well and wants students to succeed. He is funny and very accessible outside class. Overall a great professor
Super friendly guy and gives lots of explanations and writes on the board a lot w good visuals. would definitely recommend and take another course

Hes very patient with the class when tough geological concepts come up. Also, if youre a visual learner like me, take his classes!! He uses both the blackboard to draw out concepts for easier understanding, and also uses slides, with helpful videos too.

He is a great professor! Super engaging. I hate science but he shows videos, makes jokes, and does experiments. You get points for going to class and doing your labs, and the tests were like a C+ average and he curves at the end. Super rad guy!
It's amazing how someone can take the interest out of an interesting  subject.

Professor Roering jump-started my interest in geology! He's funny, and makes the class very entertaining even though it's such a big class. He's really clear about his explanations and the tests are really easy if you take the time to understand the material. Not bad on the eyes either!

Fantastic professor. He made the subject of geology interesting and I wanted to attend lecture. His tests aren't easy but if you go to lecture and look over the notes then it is fine. I would take another geology class just to have him as my professor again. He is very kind and makes funny jokes.
Solid teacher. Tests are fairly difficult, but paying attention in class helps

He's great and funny! He's young and knows how to relate to the avg. college student its funny. He makes class interesting and the tests are really easy if you pay attention in class. Midterms are mostly from lectures but going over the ch. from the book helps. Labs are annoying but really easy. TAKE THIS CLASS, Pay attention = A

Interesting class. Professor Roering is a nice guy and his class is definitely do-able. Labs are easy points as well as daily in class clicker questions. Midterms are a bit difficult, but reviewing the notes and slides helps a lot.
Josh is so entertaining and succeeds in making such a huge class interactive. He is very passionate and even though his jokes are cheesy, he makes everyone laugh and pay attention. Great class.
One of the smartest and most enthusiastic professors I have ever had.  Genuinely cares about his teaching and always willing to help outside of class.  Great professor!
Josh is a great teacher and really funny. His lectures were enjoyable and if you paid attention even a little it was easy to get an A on all of his tests.
I took this class as a requirement for another major, but it inspired me to switch to geology. Roering is a born teacher, and a really nice guy.

Roering is the man. His test almost directly reflect his lectures and if you read the book and go to class you'll be golden for all the tests. The lab is really easy to get 100% in which helps to boost your grade along with daily iclicker scores, this class should slide right by like a piece of jello.
Hilarious. Awesome professor, easy class.

Interesting subject. Not a fan of the way he teaches to the "jock" in the "rocks for jocks." The tests had easy questions, but definitely some left field, whats the point questions. Get the lab and clicker points and you should be fine.
Had no previous interest in geology, but after his class geology seemed kind of awesome. Also, he's pretty adorable in his cheesy humor way.
He makes really boring stuff interesting with corny jokes and visuals.
makes boring things interesting

Nice guy, difficult material to make appealing to everyone but he does his best. Tests were alright, there were your easy questions and your downright, evil, out of left field, I have no effing clue questions. Get all of your lab points and you should be fine in terms of your final grade.

His style of teaching is so effective--engaging us and treating us like human beings. How novel in a university. You will not be wasting your money by taking one of his classes, even if you didn't think you weren't interested in geology before.
Very organized powerpoint lectures are a tribute to his love of the subject.  Tests can ask very specific, detailed questions so pay attention in class.  All geology field trips rock!!!
Best teacher i had in college!!!!
Josh is just plain boring.  You can tell he loves what he does but he's a poor lecturer and his tests are insane.  Don't expect to stay awake much in his class.
great teacher and enjoyable

I love Rocklin. I have taken every class he offers because he is so good. Everyone loves him, and his dad jokes are the best. He is a realistic grader, which scares people, but in reality, if you do the work and you study for tests, you will do well. It's a 400-level class, so you can expect the workload of that. Just study, you will be fine.

Professor Rocklin is truly one of the best professors I've had at UO. He's incredibly thoughtful, organized, and genuinely cares about his students' learning. I left his class feeling more confident, more capable, and genuinely inspired. If you get the chance to take a course with him, do it. He's a rare, exceptional professor. Lots of dad jokes!

Rocklin is my favorite professor at UO. He is the best and cares about every one of his students. He is well-educated, evident through conversation + job-track-record. Everyone wants a letter of recommendation from him because he is him! I wish whoever left him all these bad reviews would be honest. (They were all left on the same two days #sus)

I absolutely love Rocklin! He is one of my favorite profs at UO, and whoever wrote him all of those bad reviews (they were all published on the same day) is lying. He is one of the most caring individuals on this campus and his teaching reflects that. He is so knowledgeable and has crazy lore. His dad's jokes are legendary, and he is a fair grader.

Absolutely love Rocklin! He's incredibly knowledgeable and always makes lectures engaging with dad jokes and pet pictures. Tests are straightforward if you study the material and attend class. Accesible through email and willing to let you negotiate your grade a little. Love him and would definitely recommend!!

Honestly my favorite professor at the UO. Always has some funny dad jokes. I've taken two classes with him and I would take so many more if there was an opportunity to. I always learn so much in his classes. Would recommend!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Rocklin's class! He is very passionate about the topic and loves to teach. As long as you participate and do the readings you will succeed!
Great teacher I've taken his classes twice!

Grading criteria is unclear. For example, on one of the essays we were supposed to create a question and answer it. He took points off for my question being longer than other students', even though he NEVER said our question had to be a certain length.

His texts are INCREDIBLY unclear with long long hypotheticals that make no sense. His lectures, while thorough, are FAR from in depth in enough to prepare students for the final. The kind of professor who rarely gives out perfect (or even good!) scores.
I found this class incredibly confusing and Professor Rocklin made zero attempts to help me despite having reached out over email. I felt alone and would not recommend this class or professor.
Very dense slides that are copy pasted text from the textbook with little explanation about it.
Doesn't create a supportive environment for students. I don't feel like I learned anything. Don't take.
Just don't do it to yourself.
BAD. His grading criteria is really unclear.
Robert Rocklin should not be a professor. He plays favorites and completely neglects some students and will mark them down on things for no reason. Please avoid this man at all costs.
DO not take his class. You will regret it. Do yourself a favor and avoid him.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS
I don't think you should take this class. He is not willing to help students and can be very rude and abrasive.

This professor is boring and the lectures are genuinely so hard to listen to. Mainly he plays favorites and his grading makes no sense. He takes off points for things that were completely his opinion and he never put on the grading criteria. Don't take a class with him.
His grading is extremely arbitrary and makes no sense. Plays favorites. Avoid him.

My favorite professor I've ever had at UO. Very interesting class material, and he makes lectures so much fun. Grading is pretty straightforward, if you pay attention and study his study guides you should get an A. Highly recommend.
Clear and fun lectures. Graded by a few things, but Prof. Rocklin creates helpful study guides and is always willing to meet with students during office hours. He tells dad jokes during class.

Best prof I have had at UO! Lectures are entertaining, material is interesting, very understanding and accommodating. Really enjoyed this class! Gives good study guides for exams and is always helpful on office hours. Finds ways to make a 2 hour class go by fast. 100% would recommend and I plan to take more classes with him!

Professor Rocklin is my favorite professor. I took LAW 102 and he is amazing at teaching. He makes the class interesting & entertaining (his dad jokes LOL). He connects very well with the students! It's not common to find professors who are as eager as him in helping out students. He is willing to sit down with students for hours if they need help

I have taken LAW 102, 103, & 410 with him, and I would take any class he teaches. Rocklin is by far one of my favorite profs at UO. His tests are fair and he does a great job helping you learn the material. Despite the dense material we work with, he makes the material interesting and comprehensible. You will love his class! He is also pretty funny

Great teacher, super interesting. Lectures were filled with great content and I learned a lot. He also included many jokes in his slides which would lighten up the mood. Tests weren't hard if you payed attention. Super knowledgeable. Absolutely would and will take another class from him.

He is an amazing prof and makes class fun. However, there is a lot of homework and reading. He does not curve the class or any of the exams. He does not offer extra credit. So make sure you do well on the bi-weekly quizzes and two exams. Those are the only thing going towards your grade and are HEAVILY weighted, so take with caution, but loved him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a great class that I enjoyed very much. Professor Rocklin is really nice and is good at engaging students in his lectures. Tests arent too hard at all. Great class, I highly recommend!

Told lots of cheesy jokes which I honestly appreciated. Class is probably different when its in person and not on zoom, but a lot of the points (aside from the midterm and final) came from the two reading quizzes a week. He sets a time limit (about 1o min for us but he said he was decreasing it) but I was able to skim and locate the answers easily.

One of the best professors I have ever had! His class is graded on a structure so like a 70% counts as an A. He is super knowledgeable. Midterm and final were really easy. Clicker quizzes in every class and one writing assignment that is graded harshly but it doesn't really matter because of the grading scale. Definitely recommend this class!

Rocklin is by far the best professor I have ever had. I have already taken 102 and 103 and it pains me to know he doesn't teach anything else. He is incredibly supportive and truly cares. His tests aren't difficult at all if you do the readings and take notes. Please, please, PLEASE take a class with Rocklin; you will not be disappointed.
He's the best! Very engaging lectures and interesting material. There is a lot of required reading, but keep up with it and the class is easy. Would highly recommend

Professor Rocklin was the best Professor I have ever had. He is so incredibly helpful and is so understanding about every student in his class and truly wants people to succeed. He gave weekly "pop" quizzes every Monday but if you read the reading for that day, you'll get 100%. Sit in the front and participate, he really loves having a discussion.

Professor Rust was the best professor that I've had so far at UO. He is the most laid back, chill person and is flexible with various things through out the course. Just try your best, do the work, and show up to get a good grade in the class.
Very flexible and always responded to emails quickly. Would definitely recommend for anyone needing writing credits.

Professor Rust was a great WR122Z professor. The class was super accessible and the assignments absolutely helped make me a better writer. He gives great feedback and very obviously cares about teaching and his students, highly recommend!

It feels like his main goal is to "check off the correct boxes" not actually engage or teach people anything. Ironically, the boxes he's checking off are the "how to engage and teach" boxes. If you don't understand just take him and you will. Anyways, pretty lame class (WR322-- no option so I selected 122).

Understanding of late submissions for me. Homework is lots of writing so show interest in what you're saying and actually answer the question. No classes on Friday, just an assignment that needs to be completed. Meet with him in-person because him knowing you definitely helps. His feedback is detailed, be aware of what you write he reads it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awesome professor for asynchronous WR 122, very clear guidelines/grading scheme. Everything is based on completion, get things in on time with good effort and you'll be chillin. Gives great feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class, but it was difficult. There were weird deadlines that made things complicated, and the assignment structure was more intense than in the other class sequence. Lecture slides don't get posted, and participation in every discussion is mandatory. Dr. Rust seems passionate about the topic,but there are just a few difficult areas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class can be frustrating On the days that we have screenings, the discussion opens at 5 pm and closes at 11:59. If you work or have other commitments, you're out of luck and will get points docked for turning it in late. Lectures are okay. Weekly reading quizzes. Not much time given for the group project at the end of the term.

Terrible terrible terrible, was so overbearing with assignment criteria compared to other professors I had when taking the first two courses in this three course history of cinema run. All of the questions on quizzes were awful and the questions for discussions were limiting and extremely boring. I couldn't write about what actually interested me.

Dr. Rust was able to construct the class in a way to make it feel as though I could actually get better at writing even though I was behind a computer screen. He is also the only teacher that allowed me to have an extension on an essay when I had pancreatitis and was in the hospital for a week.110% take his class. I can not recommend him enough.

I feel like this class should be easier than Dr Rust made it. Somehow this introductory writing class is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Every piece of busy work counts exactly as much as a final essay, so it's really just a litany of assignments, and ignoring any of them will tank your grade. Professor wasn't helpful after reaching out
Dr. Rust took the time to get to know people in his class and was alway accomidating to peoples needs. He is a fair grader who gives good feedback on submitted work.

Dr. Rust is my favorite professor I've had so far at UO. Very smart guy, knows a lot about movies and books. He can make even a boring topic interesting and knows how to inspire students to do their work. The best part about his class was that he had very clear expectations about how to get a good grade, so I knew what I had to do to get an A+.

I am taking his online cinema class right now and its horrible! I love the subject but he needs to calm down with all of the work! We had to make TWO 6 minute video analysis and for the final, I just had to write a 6 page paper. WAY too hard for a 200 level online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Rust is a good teacher. The class was easy and interesting. I never interacted with him that much, but when he was lecturing he always seemed pleasant. I'd recommend taking him if you're a Cinema Studies major like I am. Also note I was in the Summer term for ENG 260 so we had barely any homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This teacher is condescending and rude. I tried emailing him asking about a grade I received and his response was so rude and unhelpful. He never even answered the question I asked, but instead seemed angry that I questioned his grading. He also does not teach anything in class! I am walking away feeling as though I learned nothing. Never take him!
As long as you aren't a terrible writer and pay attention to the films in class, you'll easily pass if not get an A. The final project is easy if you pair up with good people, if not then watch out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took a Sci Fi class summer term with Rust and it was rough. It was a 4 week class so time was limited but he basically just showed up and showed us movies. We hardly discussed any content described in the course description or any of the concepts we were later tested on. Plus we had two huge beasts of projects with very vague guid lines.

I am taking an online course at OSU from this same teacher. It is the second term he has taught it online, so some things are not quite figured out yet (how to post assignments on the calendar so they pop up when they are due, etc). Gives concise, detailed feedback on assignments,  getting full points is hard. Tests are not proctored. Fun course!
Lectures seemed uninformative and disorganized. Homework did not seem relative to subject, I feel like I took very little away from this class.
Clear and concise. Can't wait to take his WR221 in the fall.

Dr. Rust so far has been my absolute favorite professor. He is extremely nice, very helpful and is not too tough of a grader. He always allows a hardworking student to re-do assignments they did not do well on and gives his students a chance to also revise essays after he grades them. Stickler with citations, but helps you fix for a better grade.

I got so sick the entire term and was on the edge of not passing, on top of having a major dilemma with the Duck Store and the required textbook. Through it all, he was an angel. He was always helpful and ready to talk about how to succeed. Also pretty funny and very smart. Taking WR 122 from him if I can!

His lecture notes, expectations, and ideas were clear. He stuck to the textbook, and expects students to have a grasp on concepts addressed in class. He was very prompt and helpful answering questions. His lectures were engaging.  I don't understand the negative reviews at all. He is one of the best teachers I've had at UO.

He was my favorite professor by far. He is super helpful when it comes to papers, responds quickly and is totally cool with grading. I actually feel as if my writing has improved by taking this class and he is super sweet. He does give a decent amount of work and reading in the beginning but it was not as bad as they syllabus makes it. take him!
very nice and helpful, encourages group discussion and is open to creativity when it comes to projects. Id reccommend him. Not an Easy A , but useful skills learned putting. Totally do-able
Better than what I expected. I don't understand the previous negative reviews. He's not bad at all. I highly recommend him. He's chill and he likes group discussions.

This guy is the man! Best teacher I have had so far. Expects a lot out of his students but you can tell from day 1 he loves what he does. Never diss this man and whoever does is just being disrespectful.
Best teacher I've had thus far in college. He engages what you have to say and challenges you to make it better. Completely understanding of student's needs, and makes class entertaining.

Easily one of the best instructors I've had in college. He genuinely cares about what each and every student has to say, and is willing to go out of his way to accommodate the needs of students. Furthermore, he allows students to engage the campus community through trips to the art museum, library classes, and midterm conferences. Highly recommend!

Awful. Attacks students remarks and makes us feel like we are stupid. Does not explain himself at all about what is required and grades on length. Is super anal about it and format.  Worst class I have taken yet. He assigns 2-3 drafts per essay and you go from 3 pages to 5 pages to 2 pages on 1 paper. Do not take.

Mr. Rust has many quirks that become unbearable over time. His consistant battle with the overhead projector has lasted an entire term, yet he still wastes 10 to 20 minutes of every class on his movie clips. He grades almost everything by length, so dont kill yourself over content with him. Avoid asking questions as he takes them as personal attack

Probably one of the worst GTFs I've had. He is very condescending. He makes offhand comments as insults to the class at times as well. It seems as though he just likes to hear himself talk. Should a film history class really be this boring?

Rust is extremely defensive when it comes to his teaching style, and thinks all questions asked are the students fault, which makes him angry and he refuses to answer them.  First paper I got back was graded a B simply because it wasn't a full 5 pages, on a 4-5 page assignment.

Generally two main issues- 1) talked a lot about himself and though experience as an expat, generally so unhelpful and did not resonate 2) did not talk at ALL about current global events. The class content is cool but highly recommend taking it from another professor
Very heavy on participation. Hardest tests I've had for a management class.

Would avoid if possible. Getting a good grade is unnecessarily hard for no reason, class content isn't difficult. Got marked down insane amounts on participation and subjective papers despite doing well on exams. Big group project at the end which is fine.

Avoid taking him if you can. He will get upset at tardiness/missing class/lack of participation. Grades harshly. Some lectures are engaging, but require a lot of preparation and full engagement for the entire class.

Very lecture heavy, attendance and participation is mandatory and graded harshly, two papers early on followed by a group project. He will call on you in class and even if you speak every class you won't get a good participation score. He loves talking about himself/pretentious. Can be nice at times but is overall demeaning, unapproachable, etc.
Dense lectures, grades hard on participation, how sure how anyone could get an A in this class. Does get mad for tardiness and absences. Will be graded down harshly. Talks about himself a lot

Engaging material, however he can come off as a little pretentious sometimes. Will get upset at students for coming less than one minute late. Very participation and lecture heavy with a ton of readings. Dense lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mike is a great professor with amazing stories to tell from his journeys around the world. Lectures are engaging, but you must be paying attention and doing the pre-readings at home: he will call on people at random. There are two papers early on, then after the midterm it's all about the group project. It's a dense class, but I recommend it!

This class won't be available anymore but I encourage everyone to take his Coaching classes. Even if you don't coach or never will, the class gives you such good life skills you can use everywhere. Dave really cares about his students and truly tries to make his lectures fun. You can live without the textbook, but don't be late.

Dave is actually my favorite professor ever. You will always have great conversations with him. His classes may seem like they're random but I promise they're so engaging. 10/10 I would take his classes every time over again.
I love this professor and this class. The teacher is very caring and funny, and even if you don't think this class will benefit you, trust me it will.
great guy,

This guy is so brilliant, he really cares about the students, and he is an amazing teacher especially in very subtle ways. If you are on the fence about one of his classes, please take it. The only thing I would say is that showing up to class is the most important thing easily the biggest part of your grade.
Dave was the best professor I've ever had. The content in this class was amazing. He was very straightforward and very nice. As long as you pay attention in class, you'll do great!

Dave was such a great professor. He really cared about his students and what he was teaching. Plus, the class was extremely easy. There are seven short quizzes throughout the term in person (taken online in Canvas), but he always does a review on the class before the quiz. I would highly recommend his class if you need a couple credits!
Great professor. Highly encourage taking this course along with his coaching course. Show up to class and the class will be easy.

David Rubino is truly a gem. Take his Coaching I class, he's very passionate about what he does so it's super enjoyable. Attendance is mandatory, but honestly it was so fun I didn't want to miss a class. Everyday we start class talking about sports news, then we get into the lesson.

chill man. one can only miss four classes and then it negatively impacts your participation grade. he's funny likes to make jokes. very friendly. run all the time. Understanding if you run slow or have injuries. He does have  favorites though but he's pretty nice to everyone.
PE with Mr. Rubino is very enjoyable. He cares about the students because he gets to know every one's name and he is very respectful.

Being a marathon runner, I had Dave for a 5K Training class twice a week in the morning, and it was really fun and enjoyable! He's a very easy-going guy and is eager to help students succeed, and encourages people with improving their running form and ability. He's an awesome guy to have a conversation with and made the class really fun.

Coach Rubino is an awesome guy with a sheer desire to share his passion of coaching. He provides the opportunity to embellish oneself in the coaching world within Eugene through a written project. Overall, he simply wants students to excel as coaches and ALWAYS put their best foot forward.
makes sure you don't hurt yourself doing something stupid, but is one of the most polite, kind, and enthusiastic people I have ever met. Must take weight training with him
Pretty helpful. He gives you time to actually workout and doesn't waste very much of your time working out. If you know how to work out and don't want anyone bothering you take this class.
I took Jog/Run class with Dave Rubino and it was really fun. He is super easy going and a really fun teacher. Not to bad to look at either.
best/funnest PE 'jogging' class teachers ever. gives you a disposable camera when you graduate. good guy.
Excellent teacher, very knowledgable, and curteous. A genuine joy to be in class with.
Cool and chill guy, assignments & projects had clear instructions -- grading was very gracious. Would 100% recommend, never had any problem in this class. :)
Very nice and funny guy. Really resonates with students. He did an amazing job teaching WR 321 for his first time. Absolutely would take again.
Really enjoyed taking writing with him, great feedback and clear expectations. Extremely straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was his first time teaching the class, but he did very well. He left a lot of good feedback and really wanted you to do well. He assigned some readings but hey were easy to skim and not something you had to stress about. There was a lot of writing assignments but he gave students a lot of creative freedom which made them fun.
I took WR122 online but it was quite easy and definitely recommend taking it with Prof. Rust.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rust was a great teacher for Writing 122, his grading scheme is a little different (more based on completion) and he understands that students have different levels of writing skills. He gives constructive feedback on even his smaller assignments. There was a fair amount of writing, expected in the class. Props for reinstating group activities!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great guy, gives great feedback especially in office hours. Workload feels like the right amount for this class, super manageable throughout the week and only two real essays throughout the term.
He was a really nice and cool professor, and he wrote back to emails very quickly, even on the weekends. Pretty chill dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a great professor for writing. He is extremely understanding and helpful when it comes to turning in assignments. There is not a lot of work compared to other writing classes. If you want an easy A, but also a class where you actually improve your writing, this is the class to take. I would highly recommend taking his writing classes.

Professor Rust is a great teacher! He really makes class interesting and engaging for students. He's also very clear when it comes to his grading rubric and what he expects in order to get a good grade in the class. Participation is a must if you really want to get an A! Try to at least attend one office hour and get to know him!

Took Disability Studies with Rye. Class was really engaging and pretty easy. I found the lectures to be somewhat interesting and Rye would tell lots of stories that made it even more interesting. Very minimal assignments that were very simple and easy.
Had Disability studies with Davies and it was a pretty easy course. Straight forward and easy assignments.

Rye is hilarious. They are super supportive and give amazing feedback on literally every single assignment. Attendance is not mandatory and the class is super accepting and chill. Even held conferences with every student to gain a connection and know everyone. This class is awesome, low stress, and even fun. Do recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ryan is super chill. They would go super easy on workload. We hardly had in-person class. They give long and detailed feedback on every assignment. Such an easy class. Y'all NEED to take WR122 with Ryan!!!!

Jack clearly cares about all of his students and I've never heard him say anything negative about someone's work that wasn't constructive. He's engaging and very knowledgeable and expectations for assignments are always very clear in canvas.

He has horrible communication with students and has little to no concern with their grades. He refuses to elaborate on his vague answers and his overall demeanor towards understanding the concerns of his students is disappointing and infuriating. Don't bother taking his class, he is not fit to be a teacher. Pretentious. Unconcerned. Redundant.

I tried to get an extension when I was going to my grandma's funeral, but he didn't give me one stating that he made his expectations and due dates clear (I didn't know when the funeral was happening so I couldn't plan ahead. My other teachers were understanding and gave me extensions). His feedback is pretty vague and his lectures are disorganized

Jack Ryan was a decent professor. Semi-clear in what he expected, gave good feedback. There was at least four to six or more hours of drawing to do every week, which is to be expected in a drawing course, in addition to the weekly projects, that would take about an hour. I never received a perfect score on any of my drawings in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jack expects top quality work from his students and will push them to do work outside their comfort zone and ultimately be better artists as a result. He does expect you to be on time everyday, which is also pretty much standard studio policy. Jack introduced us to many interesting artists/ideas and is an all around great person & professor!
Large lecture class that was fun and engaging.  Helpful Prof. that i liked and he brought in weird and smart content.
great lecture covering many topics - perhaps more advanced then you would expect for a 100 level but all relevant information.  Labs were also a great place to realize the lecture topics

The lecture is absolutely useless. The lab time to create the work is what really matters in this course, and what you are graded on mostly. Going to the lecture was purely for the attendance points while listening to the most absurd comments and the weirdest videos one could ever find on the internet. Try to take it with someone else if you can.
he'll meet with you anytime out of class and go out of his way to work with you. learned a lot, interesting and helpful.

I thought he was a great art professor. He had a lot of abstract thoughts and was someone who provoked abstract thought. If you are open to learn new things he is very helpful. i thought the class expanded my artistic vision. good class!
I recommend it. Interesting survey of artful thinking and how the arts relate to ourselves and the world around us.  Lots of opportunities to try new contemporary projects.
Solid class.  I enjoyed the lectures.
Welcome to college- great class, surprisingly tough for a 100 level but i learned a lot. Ryan will meet with students any time, anywhere (which was amazing for a lecture class of this size).

Makes no sense. Makes no points. Shows abstract work but not in way that provokes interest - rather in way that causes confusion. Emphasizes "don't be cliche!" and what not to do but never anything inspiring or the least bit interesting. Left this class disturbed, upset, bored, annoyed...

Lot of frat guys and jocks taking this 100 level are disappointed that Ryan views art and rigorous and engages in that. Don't believe them. Lots of sophisticated ideas and not for students who think art is just expressing yourself and painting still lifes. Sign up for Geology 101 if you do.  This class is about expressing culture.
Since it was mandatory the place was packed at the start of class then by the end only half were left. completely ridicoulous
The only way I managed to stay away during lecture was to write down the absurdities coming out of this guy's mouth. My favorite quote: "The visual world is a conspiracy of form." I mean, WHAT?!!
I honestly have no idea where this man gets his thoughts from. A quote from last class: "words....words...oh as in language?" enough said. he's an idiot.

Great lectures, loved lab! A very hard class, no way around it. Exams ARE HARD. Jon seems to write test questions to trip you up and measure how good of a test taker you are not your knowledge. VERY HARD TESTS!

Lectures have a consistent and very familiar format. If you take notes on the slides provided, it's incredibly helpful! Sit in the front if you want to learn the best. It's very helpful to be able to ask Jon questions personally and he usually walks around when there's clicker questions, so if you're confused, ask!

It's not that the professor is hard; the class is hard. Anatomy is not easy, and Jon makes it so much more fun and easy to understand. Get ready to study at least a couple of hours every day because there is a lot of content to master, even moreso in Anatomy II. Genuinely the best teacher for the class, though. Attend office hours, don't miss class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jon is well-intentioned professor who truly cares about his students success. That being said the class is difficult, 80% of your grades is tests, and lectures aren't super helpful. Utilize office hours, LAs, and study at least a little outside of class everyday.
Worst professor ever! Don't know how he is still teaching.

At first Jon seemed like a funny guy who cared about his students. However, after having to leave the term early for personal reasons, he was the least understanding of any professor I had and impossible to work with one on one. Don't let the in class persona fool you. He doesn't not care about his students, only his reputation as a fun professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 2 because I liked the content. He is a terrible professor, rambles in lectures, makes uncomfortable jokes, bad slides, brags about his student's successes when it's literally all the students putting in their own work. He is unreliable and never answers emails. Says a bunch of inspirational stuff during lectures but doesn't actually mean any of it

Lots of content but you will be fine if you put in effort and study hard. Lectures don't provide much as Jon just rambles / frequently makes unsettling comments. Use your lab LA's / GE's, great resource and will teach you more efficiently than the prof. Ranking of 1 is due to how uncomfortable Jon is. Would not want to be alone in a room with him.

Jon cares and he recognizes effort vs toxic med school mentality. He advocates for his teaching team when people aren't kind during open lab. He gave us a foundation of knowledge to take with us into post-grad. If you say "he tries to be funny but isn't"...then you aren't there to learn, grow up. Make an agenda for lab & update your EB with Jon's

He's the best professor I have had at UO. Ignore the other 'reviews', he is completely professional, engaging in class, and never steps over the line. If you get a bad grade in this class it is entirely on you. Jon is thorough and clear in his lectures. If you are a stem major you should expect to study outside of class. Welcome to the real world.

The A&P sequence is the HPHY major, it is the foundation of what we want our professions to be. Of course its going to be hard. Going in we didn't know our own methods of learning and routine, but Jon is very clear about his expectations of EBs and the time necessary outside of class you need to dedicate. He cares, but you have to care too.

While I appreciated the knowledge I gained in Professor Runyeon's class, I cannot go on without warning my fellow UO women that he is extremely perverted and inappropriate with young women students. He repeatedly made me feel extremely uncomfortable, and I wouldn't feel right with myself if I didn't warn other women of his behavior.

Your grade reflects the work you put in, so working with your peers and teaching team will help drastically. Make friends with ur LAs. Makes jokes that are sometimes just feel inappropriate. Nice and fun guy but kinda weird. Will secretly curve tests when the average is too low. IMPOSSIBLE TO GET IN TOUCH WITH, DO NOT ASK/ EMAIL FOR ANYTHING.

I'm not sure what people expect out of an anatomy course except what Jon provides. The entire course is memorization, so of course you have to learn on your own time. He is not going to baby you through the course. Structures are clearly defined every week and practice is sufficiently given. STUDY and ask for help when confused.

Easily one of the worst professors at UO, he does not care about your learning. He tries to act funny but isn't. His presentation slides are all over the place and he does not care to annotate or present information in an easy manner for students to learn from. He mentions the grading paradigm a lot but doesn't care to teach well at all.

Jon is a nice guy but not a great lecturer. He makes weird jokes a lot. Exams make up 90% of the grade. Go to open labs. Certain GEs are on a huge power trip and Jon won't do anything to help you. Be very careful with pre-class assignments, multiple people got reported to the dean for plagiarism by said GEs for forgetting a single image citation.

This class is entirely effort-based. You get the grade for the level of effort you put in. Jon is a fantastic teacher, but in order to be successful in this class, you need to dedicate hours into your own studying. The exams are fair, and lectures are very engaging. He records his lectures, so rewatch ALL of them before an exam and you'll do fine.

Funny but sometimes makes bordering-on-inappropriate jokes. Good enough at teaching, there's just a lot to learn, but a lot of the time the material in lecture & lab doesn't line up. 2 pre-class assignments due every week; don't spend too long on these - mostly graded on completion. Lab is very memorization-heavy. 2nd lecture exam is super hard.
Might be worst than Mark Carrier and that says something

He just assigns readings and expects you to know everything. Broad guidelines, hard tests, horrid lecture slides. Rambles in lecture and tries to act funny instead of teaching. One minute you're learning about the basics of a structure, then you're expected to know 100 parts. Class rewards rote-memborization over problem solving skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jon is a really nice guy that is fun to talk to however sometimes he spends too much time trying to deploy W rizz on the students rather than tea

Tries to act funny. His class is revolved around “pre-study” and active learning but is done in a horrible way. Assignments due before every class get overwhelming. Lectures slides are horrible and lecture is just rambling with clickers. Not clear abt content on exams. Gives you resources and expects you to learn from it rather than the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bro is not it

Jon is such an amazing professor, he tries to make sure everyone does well in his class. He is very clear about how he grades and how his class is set up. His lectures go very quickly in the beginning when taking notes so it's helpful to have the lecture pulled up next to you as well as on the screen. you need to take advantage of the LAs.

Jon's classes are tough and his tests are hard, but If you dive into the class and take advantage of all the learning opportunities, you'll come out knowing a ton. He is a fun teacher, but most of the learning happens on your own time. There's just so much to cover, and not all of it gets covered in class, so yeah... lots of self-teaching moments.

Engaging and enjoyable lectures, but move very fast and note-taking is borderline pointless as youll inevitably pore over the slides later and other resources when you're cramming the boatload of information you're responsible for knowing on exams. Could make the open book/closed book divisions clearer in terms of what you need to know for each.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jon's lectures move quickly and are packed with information so utilizing the course learning objectives helps to see what we are expected know, since 90% of our grade is made up of our test scores. This is the hardest class I've taken at UO, but Jon was a great professor to have along the way since he was so knowledgable and positive in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wanted to come to lecture to learn, but instead, got photos with no explanation. The online videos he posts were... interesting in audio quality. It's near impossible to study if you did not record his audio yourself or was a fast note taker. It was fun to learn but MAN does he need to fix those lecture slides. Exams were HARD!

Classes are engaging and the material is presented in an interesting way.  Jon is extremely knowledgeable and cares a lot about the students and their well being.  I would definitely recommend any of his classes!

Seriously awesome instructor. You can tell he's passionate about teaching anatomy and getting students interested in the content. Total wizard when it comes to anatomy lab too and can answer just about any question you throw at him.

Professor Runyeon was the BEST, most inspiring instructor I had at UO. He's an engaging lecturer who cares deeply about the success of his students and their mental health. The best way to reach him is to stick around after lecture to ask questions or attend office hours. His courses set me up for great success in my DPT program.

One of the worst professors out there, he doesn't care about his students and is horrible at teaching. His slides barely have notes and he rambles a lot. The tests are hard, especially the open book portion, the EBs don't really help. He never responds to emails and is just plain rude. Makes the whole HPHY courses disappointing honestly.

Do not take this class if you do not have to. The time I sopent on this class was far more than the reccomended fro a five credit class, Jon never responds to his emails, is unclear about grading, makes the first two tests of the year impossible, and works you dry till the final. Studying in this class is also a nightmare as it has no direction.

Uggghhhh It's a good thing the teaching team is so helpful and that the class is fun because about half of this class is just figuring out what you're supposed to be bothering to learn and how to parse through the way he words questions. He takes himself less seriously than Phil though and is really approachable

I took this class in 2020. I have been upset about this professor since. He literally quit his job in the middle of the term because he received constructive (and valid) criticism from a parent that is an MCAT teacher. Awful teacher. Left us all lost. I feel bad for the TAs that had the unfortunate experience of working with him.

This professor cares more about being funny than teaching. Unless ur apart of the "Cult of John" (the kids who sit in the front and ask questions 24/7 and treat him like god, he wont care about u. I took the adjacent class of physiology with robin second term for A and P and got the same grade yet I had a such a better experience.

If I could take the A & P course with a different professor I would. He makes the tests extremely difficult just in the way that he words questions, and doesn't give us enough time to finish. He is the worst at answering emails so its almost impossible to contact him unless you wait in line at the end of class for 20 min.

If you care about your mental health, dont take Anatomy or Physiology. If you have an outside life other than focusing on school 24/7, dont take it. They do not take into consideration students who have work or other life obligations. This class has to be your only priority if you want to succeed- some people dont have that luxury.

Jon is a great lecturer, really knows the material & how to present it in an engaging way. He uses active learning in a way that makes class attendance crucial to your learning xp. He is, however, awful at communicating, & very hard to reach. Tests are hard. You need to take this class very seriously & can't treat it like gen chem or bio. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You cannot prioritize your mental health and get an A, but you can still pass! This was the hardest transition from online to back in person and he understood that which was nice, but their still could have been more preparation or structure given before the class officially starts. I thought I was going to fail the whole term, but didn't.

Jon is a phenomenal instructor with engaging lectures. Yes, the anatomy sequence is detailed with difficult exams. Why be in a 5 credit, 300 level class and not want to be challenged? It set me up very well for medical school. We will miss you Jon.

The lecture/slides were all over the place & not to the point. Lecture slides were mostly images & few text so you had to listen. He jumped around a lot so it was difficult to follow. You had to put so much time into organizing your notes because the class was so disorganized. The EB were helpful though. Tests were hard but fair if well prepared.

Jon is one of the most caring, animated, and successful professor's I've met. His lectures are fast but you learn a lot in your time with Jon. His tests are difficult, but if you create organized notes and take practice quizzes, you will succeed. The anatomy lab portion of the grade is big, but spending time in open lab is so worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Will not respond to emails. Tests are wildly unfair (30mins for 20 LONG questions)

Jon is a great teacher, but there is alot of course material to cover and this course will will take lots of work outside of class. Would not recommend taking any upper division science classes at the same time apart from HPHY 324.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've always loved anatomy, but Jon made me love it more. He is one of the most animated teachers and can lecture in such a way that you are addicted. His tests are tough but once you take a few of them you start to realize how to study for them. Very nice guy too, wants you to succeed and is always willing to help. By far one of the best I've had.

Very few teachers are as passionate about their subject as Jon is about anatomy. He's been teaching for a long time, and is amazing. Jon will inspire and teach in a way that will make you feel like you're meant to do what you're doing with your life. Yes, the class is hard. He knows that, and provides you with all the necessary keys to success.
Anatomy in general is a hard topic but I'm glad I took it with Jon. Some lecture exam questions were really long and lab exams were kinda hard. But not as hard as BIO 212, but not easy

Human Phys is not for the faint of heart... 323 is a completely different ball game from 321. Don't take unnecessary additional upper divs at the same time, you need to put a lot of time into this class. Jon is AMAZING, everyone loves him/wants to be him. Go to office hours, get to know him, and prepare to do 3x the work from 321.

Jon is great. He's fun and he's passionate about what he does. But this class is insanely difficult. It's the hardest B you will ever work for in your entire life. Likes to trip you up on questions. The lab exams are impossible, even with open lab and office hours. This class is by far the hardest class I've ever taken.

Jon is one of the best professors I have had at the U of O! He is enthusiastic about what he is teaching and just really wants you to understand the anatomy! Difficult tests but overall very do able! GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

Awesome professor, by far my favorite at the UO. Strongly recommend taking a class with him if possible, as he is moving into a more formal position as the main Undergraduate Advisor and is reducing the classes he will be teaching in the future.
He is awesome, with a great heart for helping students learn!
Jon is the man, probably the best teacher I had at UO.

He was very engaging, cared what he taught, and his sense of humor is THE best. I highly recommend taking a class taught by him. He assigns packets we have to create each week that have to be creative and accurate, but that's as hard as it gets! His lecture slides are very straight forward.
he was funny and gave great lectures, i felt like i was actually learning interesting information in his class, but the weekly quizzes were difficult even if you thought you prepared enough.
This class is very interesting however it is toughly graded and a lot of work for a level 200 class. If you want to do well you need to go to every class and take as many notes as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Jones creates a really welcoming and discussion-oriented environment, even in a larger lecture class. Lectures are interesting and funny, and homework isn't difficult if you keep up with class content. My only complaint: class became a platform for some to hijack the lecture and yap, and he is not good at getting class back on track
He was lit and super interesting stuff. it is a hard class, tho can't slack.

Very interesting, lots of reading, weekly quizzes, 2 essays and an easy final exam, all graded a bit tough. You can get lots of extra credit for participating. Didn't submit a testing agreement so can't use AEC accommodations. You must take thorough notes from day one because you can't find what you need to study for the exam from the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really good professor. A lot of reading for homework roughly 40-60 pages a week but nothing too crazy. Weekly two question quizzes that werent hard as long as you pay attention and do the readings. He overall is good at teaching but if you are a word-for-word note taker it is difficult as he goes through slides quickly and his slides arent detailed

Decent lectures, tells you quizzes are graded to see if you did the reading but I always did and he still gave 75-80% for nearly all of them. No curve in the class and papers are graded harshly as well. Hard to do well even if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a very tough grader, I don't know how do you get a A on his courses but, he grades by the book meaning even if the highest grade of the class is 70, you are still graded on a basis of 100 Be prepared and beware
Took this class Fall 2020. The lectures were fun and the readings were interesting, but I can't stress it enough  take lots of notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great prof
Really good professor, 10/10 recommend. Attendance is not required but there are easy reading quizzes on wednesdays
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ryan is an amazing teacher that truly cares about his students. He explains drills so clearly and makes it easy to understand. He really made me fall in love with martial arts and I am now continuing to train at a local gym. Take MMA 1 and 2 with him!
Ryan was a super great teacher; I could really tell how much he cares, and it made me feel very comfortable in the class.
His classes are so fun and he genuinely knows what he's doing. I will definitely be taking his class again.
Great PE teacher and knows martial arts very well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
good intro to martial arts.
i took jujitsu 1 & 2 not pema115 but thats not an option.

he is clearly super passionate about what he teaches and I loved listening to him talk about it! super nice guy and care a lot about his students! love him! take one of his classes it was super fun!! he also did a good job at making everyone comfortable and you could sit out at any point no questions asked.

He is amazing!! Ryan always makes sure people that want to take his classes actually get the chance to. He is so sweet and obviously cares about the safety of the students. He definitely knows what he's talking about and has a curriculum that is definitely more realistic in comparison to other martial arts. Take his classes!!!

Ryan was super caring and wonderful about teaching Women's Self Defense. He made the class a safe space and was super understanding about our levels of ability and backgrounds. He also made sure to fully demonstrate any activity before we ourselves did it, and was open to answering any questions we had.
I took self-defense with Ryan Kelly and would 100% take it again. Hes so caring and understanding. It was really interesting learning from him, hes a great guy!

Ryan is an incredible women's self defense instructor! He is so kind, inclusive, and teaches the skills in a fun environment. I have learned so much from Ryan; through it can be tough to think about having to get very physical, he encourages us to give it our all to protect ourselves. If you have time, take the class!!
i LOVED HIM!! he made class so interesting, and if you ask for help he really shows you how to do grips and holds himself. I will be taking another class with him as well, and I'm so excited!

Ryan is very knowledgeable and caring. This course was women's self defense and despite being a male teacher made it a very safe space and answered any and all questions. The class itself was a little mushy but very good. I'm planning on taking his classes till I graduate. You have your excused amount of absences but he usually starts w/ review
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment:
Pretty intersting class! I enjoyed his daily quizzes (which were used for attendance, not credit).

Note he posts his lecture slides AFTER class. Also doesn't really give time to ask questions during lectures, but most of the material was pretty straightforward. Readings are very outdated and optional. Labs are tech-heavy but relatively easy.

Professor Ryan was so awesome. I was expecting to dislike this class just based off of the content and ended up actually loving it. He makes lectures so easy to follow and really engaging. The weekly labs were the only homework and they always had super clear instructions. Tests were fair. I would recommend taking this class.

For this class, the lab is kinda tech-heavy and requires time to do them. Lab attendance is mandatory. He will link textbook chapters but you don't have to read them. Go to the lecture because he goes over a lot but there is a way to join online. you have a daily quiz=attendance. The exams are open books but the questions are mostly short answers.

You'd be doing yourself a disservice if you chose someone other than Ryan to teach you. He is phenomenally funny, smart, and patient. I've learned so much from him, he's one of the best professors I've had.
Ryan is a very nice guy but the tests took up the majority of the grade for this course. Hard subject and didn't offer many assignments to balance out the grade for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is super nice but the class was hard enough.  30% of final exam was on cash flow, on which he only spent one lecture.  Don't care about the percentage of your grade, because everything is based on your standing in the class.  Highly recommend but you have to study really really hard for this class
Best professor at the university of oregon by far. Really tough teacher but super fair and he is just a boss. That is all he is a boss.

Was pretty scared to take my first intermediate accounting class. But Ryan is a very good instructor and made it bearable. He's kind of awkward sometimes, but in a good way if that makes sense. Always there for students during office hours and is quite helpful. Tough class, but it was expected. Read the book, study hard, and make an effort.
Great Teacher, hard exams, miss him already
Huge boss. Let's you know what he is looking for and probably the best actg teacher I have had this far. If you can get into his class, do it!
He was extremely funny and easygoing. Very self aware and relate able.

Great professor. Rally knowledgeable of the topic. Try to make things fun but hey you only can do so much fun things when it comes to accounting. Exams are really hard but in general all the material is hard.

Wilson was great at connecting with students and helping them to understand the material. The only thing I wished was for him to show more problems on the board which he did after the midterm feedback. Overall a really nice guy who made a difficult subject approachable and enjoyable.

Ryan is a great teacher. He is excels in finding common ground with students. He is the ideal "accounting person" that sticks to routine. In Office Hours he'll do all he can to help and makes you feel comfortable. He made the class (almost) fun, honestly. Exams are difficult but most intermediate accounting exams are. Classes= Lecture/PracProblems

Not an easy course but he is very willing to help. He is incredibly personable in OH and spent a lot of time helping me work through my struggles with the material. He moves fast in lectures, doesn't mark off small arithmetic errors on tests, doesn't allow a note sheet, and homeworks are harder than tests. Good for those that actually want to learn

I would highly recommend NOT taking a class of his if math is not one of your strong suits, attendance isn't mandatory, however if you miss a class you will be very behind, & he does not post his lectures. His class consists of him and a chalkboard, with a lack of specificity of the topic he is going over during the class.
He'll answer questions you have but other than that his class is difficult because he doesn't give us a full week of reviewing instead just gives us like 15 minutes before a quiz which is every ot

Takahashi is a great guy. He explains the material well, is a generous grader, and is very willing to work with you if you're having trouble. But his exams are brutal, and the homework is a bit too difficult (and necessary to understand the material) for being such a small part of the grade. 232 with him was rewarding, but 347 was a bit miserable.

Ryan is incredibly brilliant and you will learn a lot in his classes. I've had discrete and number theory with him, and while they were challenging, he is a very supportive professor and I was able to overcome most of the hurdles I encountered. If you are persistent and willing to seek help when stuck, you'll do well in his course.

Professor Takahashi is one of my favorite professors I've taken at UO. His lectures give a great base of knowledge to apply to the homework, which take a little more creativity and time to figure out. However, if you understand the lectures and take good notes, I believe you will do well on the exams. The practice exams are great.

Homework is not trivial. You will definitely have to go to office hours to understand what's going on. His office hours are often held at the same time for all courses he teaches, so show up early. One of the most brilliant people I have ever met, and a phenomenal lecturer for someone so early in their career. If you actually like math, take him.

Ryan is really brilliant and he's a great lecturer. This class is intentionally very hard because he expects you to push yourself. My only gripe is that his office hours were double booked with other classes so sometimes it was really hard to get help with homework which was very very difficult. The tests are totally reasonable though. Great prof.

Expect to do lots of outside studying. Ryan's classes move extremely fast but he's always open to questions. Homework sets are extremely hard (every assignment had about a 50% avg.) but tests are very realistic and manageable. To pass his class, you will have to stay on top of things and make sure you understand the material very well.

I really enjoyed my Discrete course with Ryan. The class was very interactive and he would crack jokes pretty often. It was always really easy to pay attention. The only things that were graded were the homework, assigned almost weekly, and the exams -  2 midterms and a final. Office hours are a saving grace, and work with peers! Hw was TA graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ryan is a cool guy, but his class is pretty hard. You can tell he's extremely smart and passionate about mathematics, but when it comes to teaching he's a bit hard to follow. I would recommend watching YouTube tutorials outside of class on recurrence relations and graph theory to supplement your knowledge on topics presented in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Passionate about math and seems happy to be teaching. As a math person, I loved the depth of this class, but it's not for everyone. Take this class with Ryan to get a solid foundation of linear algebra and advanced math language/techniques, but avoid if you're just trying to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher but there is a level of knowledge higher than I had anticipated that he expects students to have going into the class. Tests are pretty fair, but the homework is incredibly difficult. The homework is graded quite harshly and answering the questions on the homework often takes MUCH more knowledge than what was taught in class.

Highly recommend discrete 2 with Ryan; Such a fun class, and you are set up for success if you use given resources, such as office hours and good note-taking. Also, ask a lot of questions and work with peers.

He seems like a nice guy and is definitely a genius. But he is smart to the point where he cannot explain material well enough for students who are unfamiliar with the concepts. Writes his own homework and the class average on the midterm was an F. I wouldn't recommend.

Ryans class is very fast paced, it was honestly pretty hard to keep up with it and I personally didnt understand Ryans teaching style. Tests are pretty tough and Ryan writes his own homework which goes outside of the concepts he teaches. Ryan is very accessible outside of class, but If you do not actively go to office hours, you will not pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to any positive reviews on this guy. Literally teaches things outside the scope of the class. I had math professors from other departments and tutors at school completely confused on why he was teaching certain things. Class was all proofs and his tests would not line up with the homework. Only take this guy if you have no other choice
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I feel like Ryan gets a lot of unfair criticism. I understand that some peers feel the level of rigor is excessive, but I appreciate his commitment to teaching the full range of the subject. For many, like myself, it was a really hard adjustment, but I feel like I learned a lot from him. I do wish the hw was more application based instead of proofs
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ryan enjoys math. He shows you how to solve a math problem and why that method is the best/easiest/fastest method. The homework and tests are hard. Going to office hours are the only reason why I understood anything in his class. Take Ryan if you want to put in the time to learn math.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework is very difficult, but if you go to office hours Ryan is incredibly helpful, and the lowest hw grade was dropped. I found the lectures to be clear if not terribly exciting. The tests are very doable and graded fairly, with extra credit problems.

Ryan is a great teacher because he is a genius. His class is challenging, but he is very helpful. You won't do well if you don't go to office hours. His homework is super hard, but he goes through it all in office hours. If you study, the tests aren't unusually hard. I suggest taking his class if you want to put in the effort to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I know 252 is hard, but he still the worst. He made the hw by himself and it literally not what we learn from class, and hard grading on the hw. Class is okay, just the hw and exams are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If there is zero, I would definitely chose it. Never take this instructor's class. He does not teach according to the textbook, and does not have a specific outline prior to the class. His homework and test sometimes beyond his lecture and even textbook. Hilariously, a beginner's calculus class have to learn linear algebra!
Rude and not understanding to students circumstances. Teaches and tests outside of class level and topics.
HORRIBLE INSTRUCTOR

Ryan is a great professor and a great guy. He makes a very difficult subject  very manageable. He is very against WebWork so he writes his own homework, but that  means that he is very helpful at helping you understand the material. He gives you a practice test to study prior to the test. If you study, and go to office hours, you'll love this guy!
very patience

Hands down one of the best math teachers I've ever had! I'm not the best at math, but he made it super easy to understand and is 100% willing to help if you go to his office hoursmake time to get help.  He also creates all of the testshomeworkquizzes himself so you know exactly what to expect for tests.

Discussion section matters most. I didn't listen to most lectures and still managed to get an A+. Super easy & honestly super interesting when I did listen. Tests are online which relieved a lot of test anxiety + everything is common knowledge. Few memos but rubric was good & fun activities in the discussion section. All grading is done by GE's.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Scholssberg is very educated and cares deeply about the topic of city planning. Sometimes the lectures were very repetitive so lectures seemed unnecessary. The discussions were what really helped me engage with the content. The exams and assignments are fine and he had decent content for lecture. The readings were a little heavy though.
Overall, this class was pretty easy only if you do all the readings; it is heavy reading. You have weekly quizzes upon the readings.

For someone trying to declare for PPPM It hurt a lot for this course to come down to four papers and two large tests. I was inspired and than had that almost smashed by the end of week 10. I scheduled two office hour meeting with him and he didnt show up to either. Doesnt offer many points. Very clutch tho, he let me make up three quizzes.
Loved marc. He was great to listen to and very insightful. He gave us so many outside resources to learn more about the city planning realm of things. An overall easy class. would recommend.

Marc is very knowledgeable with city planning, but I agree with what other reviewers have said regarding the lectures and HW. Throughout the term he kind of coasted with the lectures and just had guest speakers take up good chunk of the term. Very reading heavy, but quizzes and assignments are super easy. TA basically did all the gradings.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Interesting guy and definitely knows a lot about city planning. However, he talks on and on about nothing. Could have gotten all the same information and notes that I got each 1 hour and 20 min lecture in 30 minutes tops.  He repeats a lot, trails off, and talks a lot about nothing in particular. The guests he brings to class are interesting.

Professor Schlossberg is passionate about what he does. However, his lectures are, at times, quite boring. Even though he uploads his lecture slides to Canvas, I would recommend going to class since he will elaborate on the minimal slides. Your main source of homework will be readings, it's not too bad but it certainly takes some time to get done.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Marc is an amazing prof! Extremely understanding as long as you communicate with him. Lectures are a bit dry sometimes but he likes to crack jokes in hopes to make it fun. Loves it when students participate in lectures. Homework is easy but time-consuming as the majority of it is reading. Weekly quizzes usually worth 5-10 points based on reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Marc was extremely helpful when I was having struggles with my group project. A lot of opportunity for exploration of the course topics with other students and he was incredibly flexible with assignments when I needed more time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Such a kind and caring professor. He really cares about what he teaches, and that should through his fun and enjoyable lectures. Its a casual setting yet makes you care about what you're learning. The readings were easy to digest and the assignments were easy to complete. A really great introductory course to PPPM!

I took PPPM 205 because it's required for the 3 PM major. After taking this class it has actually steered me away from public policy as a career.
