This class was beyond boring and he talked about the same thing everyday. Lectures were dry and not helpful regarding test material. He also isn't helpful when preparing for exams. Wouldn't recommend.
Absolute worst lecturer I've ever had in my life. The lectures are so boring and uninengaging. He's a nice guy, but he can't teach. Be ready to read because that's the only way you can learn.

Really interesting, and inspiring lectures! I really enjoyed this class, but it was difficult in some aspects. He does not give study guides so preparing for the midterm and final were hard, but doable.
Great teacher and highly knowledgeable in his field.  Loves his job and the work that he does in and out of the classroom.
Marc needs to focus more on teaching rather than SCI and his research. He seems to just go with the flow. I appreciate his motivation techniques, but his teaching: ehhhhhhh

Clear he has some experience in the field. However, he also catered the class more heavily to PPPM majors, since there were so many in the class, which was annoying and alienating to those who do not want to work in city planning. It also would have been nice to discuss at least some of the text in class, which for some reason he was against.

I thought he was going to be a great teacher, but what resulted was an empty suit in front of the classroom. His research and SCI take a lot of his time, but this is no excuse for poor teaching. His ppts are old and simplified with no real meat. Push yourself and demand that he give you feedback - he wasn't that responsive to my efforts.

I took several classes taught by Prof. Schlossberg, including a quarter abroad. I found him to be very engaging and relatable. His passion for the subject is apparrent and it definitely motivates his students. Everything we discussed and every assignment we completed had a real life application. He was my favorite professor in college...hands down.
A wonderfully inspired and engaging professor.  Always open to novel ideas and a wonderful resource to students.  Couldn't recommend his classes enough.

Prof. Schlossberg has a tremendous amount of knowledge in community planning. He relates most of the course material to his personal experiences in the field. I found the class to be difficult in the grading but very interesting topics. I would recommend it for students majoring or interested in the major
No Comments
Took her for 325 and it has been a great time. Her class is never boring and I actually look forward to it.

Took this class for pre business requirements, not such a hard grader as everyone says. As long as you pay attention during class and work on practice problems/homework you should be fine. Lecture can be boring and repetitive sometimes, but she does call on random students sometimes if no one volunteers to answer questions to be aware.

Mary Savage is amazing. Many people on her clearly don't like her cold calling nor her very blunt personality. Her cold calling makes you understand the material though, and if you don't get the question right, she walks through it on the board and explains it until you get it. Accounting is difficult and her teaching made it easy to understand.

super bad professor, you can be confused and instead of helping you she puts the blame on you and can sometimes be disrespectful. Instead of doing her job as a professor, teaching students, she puts students down rather than motivate and teach them. distasteful.

When I was in Fallujah my squad was pinned down under heavy fire, but Professor Mary Savage managed to bring us home safely. Several years later, my wife and two children were trapped in a house fire while I was at work, but Mary rescued them and also put out the fire. Truly one of the greats. I would definitely recommend taking this class.

If accounting is something that clicks for you, you are going to love this class and this professor. If it does not, you'll probably not like it.
However, great professor, absolutely loved the class, always available to help you out, especially if you show genuine interest in accounting and put in the work. If you don't, though, you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Its financial accounting so it will be around 6 hours a week of homework whoever you have. Mary is a good professor, and she will prepare you well for exams and future accounting classes. She also wants to see her students to succeed and heavily promotes opportunities related to accounting, almost every class.

Difficult course with long homework assignments and tests were weighted heavily and difficult, curve at the end of course is strong. Her explanations seldom clarified material for me when I asked. Lectures are a must in terms of attendance and reading the book is highly recommended. She was at least funny at times and is genuine.

Don't listen to the other reviews on here. If you're a student that pays attention in class and actually does the work outside of class you will do fine in her course. I enjoyed class with Mary, she is very knowledgeable and wants to see her students succeed. I know a lot of students who really respect her.
Bad teacher

Awful at explaining core topics in the class. Assigned homework is difficult because of the bad explanations. Dry lectures and does not give help for in-class assignments. Professors like Mary make me wonder how people like her get collegiate-level jobs. Review sessions with other professors taught me more than she did the entire term.
homework was incredibly long for no reason at all. Not very accessible outside of class and its very hard to follow along in lecture because she makes every subject so mind numbingly boring
Is a nice person but terrible at teaching. Makes every subject extremely complicated and boring. It's comical seeing the grades in her classes compared to other professors

The lecture is incredibly boring, and participation assignments are required. Weekly homework is lengthy, with 30-50 multi-step questions. Quizzes are graded harshly, and new material is introduced just before them. After the midterm, only six students can see their answers during office hours, so if you miss out, you won't know what you got wrong.

Terrible teacher. Some of the worst lectures I have ever had the displeasure of sitting through. She has no idea how to teach accounting or explain things clearly. She has the unique ability to make even the most simple concepts mind numbingly dry and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is just overall a bad teacher. She will go on long tangents not related to class. Asking her a question will only confuse you more, and she won't know the answer half the time. Wasnt able to help with the online homework assignments. There is a lot of homework, but the test weigh heavy. This class will frustrate you, please avoid if possible.

Horrible teacher overall. Her lectures aren't helpful, and she doesn't provide clear explanations whatsoever. I don't recommend her at all, just as bad as Wadell. Doesn't notice if people raise their hands, and doesn't understand students questions most of the time. By far one of my top worst professors at UO. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!
He has awesome humor and funny listen to and he knows a lot of knowledge but it is just too much for an 100 and extreme hard test... our mid term and final had to be curved significantly.
Amazing how he hasn't been fired yet.

reviews.comment: Not a great experience. Prof does not seem equipped to teach the material.

Did not communicate, lacked ample material, study guides sucked, boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly horrible. Never will take a class with this prof again, I emailed him multiple times about grades and assignments and never heard back once. No assignments so midterm and final are worth everything, which wouldn't be bad except the tests aren't really based on the lectures. Lecture heavy fr.

Reading the prior ratings I was really nervous going into his class, but he's genuinely great. He's one of the most laid back professors I've had. He keeps you engaged all class with his humor and examples. Your grade does nearly solely depend on the exams, but he curves and allows you a cheat sheet on the final exam. Would recommend!!
Incredible lack of knowledge and understanding of the concepts. Like he's reading from an outline he pulled off the internet and when asked a question he freezes and says he'll "get back to you."

Sati is smart professor, but he should not be teaching an undergrad 100 class; he was expecting graduate-level work from students who had never previously taken a law class. Also, if you are taking any class, be prepared to take very difficult tests. I was able to get As in all other (mind you upper-level) law classes, but with Sati, I got: B+.

He is a really new prof. and it shows. He is fresh out of law school and it seems that he barely knows the content himself, which makes it extremely difficult to learn. I ended up self teaching myself a majority of the course. Unclear grading standards. It made for a long semester.
Grading standards unclear
In over his head.

I would agree that Sati is the worst teacher I've ever had. I am shocked by how bad it is. I think I could teach a better class on criminal law if I had to, and I don't understand it (mostly because I've taught myself all semester). His class is like listening to a student who hasn't outlined the class try to recite the textbook from memory.

I will agree with the ratings that speak to Sati's kindness. I have an eccentric uncle with a pet squirrel who is kind. I would not want him to teach me the law. His tests contradict the rules he teaches. He tests material he did not teach and doubles down when he is wrong. If you like receiving grades that feel like drawing straws, go to UO Law!
Ask me at the break or after class.

Professor Sati is a gem of a human being. His class will make you laugh, but it will also make you cry. He is clearly a newer professor, and as such cannot answer more in depth questions. You are going to have to spend a lot of time teaching yourself, because his presentation of the material can be at times more confusing than helpful.

Sati is the worst teacher I've ever had. He has given us wrong information multiple times, he can't answer questions, his slides are convoluted, he doesn't know the law well enough to teach it. Multiple students have gone to the administration to provide feedback and nothing has gotten better. Most students have resorted to teaching themselves.

Professor Sati is a great guy and a kind, caring professor. He is only in year two of teaching law, but it is cool to see him learning the best strategies. His class is hard but his door is always open and he is willing to go the extra mile to help if you're confused.

Professor Sati a kind and engaging professor. His class is hard, but he has regular office hours and makes sure to adapt as the students request. He's only a second year law school professor so it's cool seeing him improve each week.

Sati is the worst professor I have taken in law school. It is abysmal that the law school continues to allow him to teach. Giving him the keys to 1L doctrinales is alarming. He is unable to answer questions, relies on text heavy slides to get through lecture.
Nice guy but terrifying as a professor. Traumatized.

Great guy, less than ideal teacher. He's funny and engaging, but grades harshly and doesn't offer many tools for success (study guides, etc...). Additionally, attendance is mandatory and graded on accuracy.

I would not recommend taking a class with Professor Sati to anyone. He refuses to provide students with any form of study guide and then acts surprised when everyone does badly on the mid-term. He is super hard to get in contact with outside of class and tweets about his students online. Super passive-aggressive, and condescending DO NOT recommend.
I really liked Sati I don't know why he has such bad ratings on here, one of my favorite professors at UO. nuff said

does not assign homework, has students complete "daily quizzes" through iclicker, but he doesn't know how the iclickers work, no one can register theirs, and he posts the scores at random. The only things severely graded are tests and he offers no help, except for "look at the slides" "the slides have the information".

reviews.comment:
Though it is the universities fault, this was the worst course I've ever sat through. The professor has no rubric or knowledge of how to teach. He is smart, he just doesn't know how to teach students.
To top this all off, he's a frequent flyer on twitter. He posts about the students and asks professors for syllabuses or tests.
He is the most caring and understanding professor I've ever had. The only downside is that you do have to buy a 20 dollar textbook with all the materials in it. Definitely recommend.
Super easy class.  He was really nice and the class was easy to follow as well.  He posts all the readings and has Canvas super organized.

Jesus cares very deeply for his students. There is a lot of reading and movies in the class but if you do the work he is a very easy grader. If you go to class and do all of your work you will get an A in the class. He is a very friendly guy and I recommend getting to know him

This class is fairly easy, but if you are not interested in art/poetry you will get bored. He is very active with his lectures, it is almost completely in Spanish, but if he can tell that you are not understanding he will explain more. There is a lot of reading but some movies too which was a nice change.

Good professor. He knows a lot is passionate and active in the student  activism.  Lots of reading but you didn't really need to do more than a surface level skim for most of them. You can miss 5 classes before you get penalized.  There are tests but he basicly tells you the answer (hard to fail)  hardest part is the final essay and presentations.

He was my favorite Spanish professor and this was one of the more interesting classes I've taken. It seems like as long as you put a decent effort in to the assignments, he's very rewarding with grades. He's clearly very well-versed in the topics of his class and taught us some really random but cool things (such as the origin of the word snob).
Best Spanish professor I've had at UO

Jesus is the best professor I've had so far at U Oregon, and you can tell he actually cares about his students. The tests are extremely easy as long as you have done the readings and shown up for class. He is very organized, and a great author as well. I had to purchase a $50 course packet.

chill professor, but lectures are hard to follow and he does a lot of writing around on the chalkboard that is difficult to keep up with as someone who is minoring in spanish. he is a kind grader though and is giving supportive overall so thats fab! ** class i took is SPAN342 but i couldnt put it in the review
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Jesus is by far the best spanish teacher I have had at UO, or ever. He is extremely attentive to his students needs, creates interesting lectures, and you can tell her loves teaching. He is a renowned poet and we are lucky to have him at this university. If you can take a class or classes with him at some point, do it!!!!

I was in their SPAN 202 class but RMP didn't provide that option. Jesus is an amazing professor. They always have a smile on their face and is generally such an approachable person. Being in their class is chill but not boring either. Grading is super easy and I never had to stress about this class.

Really interesting lectures. Take good notes because the quizzes are all based of what you learn in class and the readings. Do the reading and take good notes and you will have success. Jesus knows his stuff and is really passionate about his teaching

Professor Sepulveda is one of the best professors I have ever had. His classes are interesting and it is very clear that he has a passion for and understands in-depth all the material taught in class. Definitely go to his office hours, he is worth getting to know. I highly recommend and class with him

He is an esoteric man. A great teacher for those who are interested in a foreign perspective as well as a truly Latin American way of teaching. I felt transported in his class and he taught me to be unafraid writing in another language and I never forgot his classes.

His guidelines were never super clear. The course I took (Spanish Writing) was graded completely based on grammar and sentence structure and not at all on the content or ideas that were presented. He was definitely passionate about teaching and the material we discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you get the opportunity to take a class with Jesús Sepúlveda, do it. He is the best and most inspirational Spanish professor that I have ever had. There is a lot of writing but he grades you based on whether you did it and on grammar and not based on your writing abilities. He is a rare professor that actually cares for the students.

Jesus was a great professor! He pushed us to dig deeper and learn to enjoy writing. As long as you work hard and put effort in, it is a fairly easy A. Some people had trouble understanding his accent, but I had no problem AND he tried to make sure everything was clear. I loved his class and passion!

Jesus is such a great professor! I enjoyed his class so much - the material is easy but really helped improve your writing ability. He is so adorable and is easy to understand. Definitely would recommend his class!

Jesus is a great teacher. I recommend taking his classes as Sophomore or Junior rather than his lower level classes.  If you are not accustomed to a thick accent, it may be difficult to understand him but he is a very nice guy and I learned a lot from his class.

He improved my Spanish more than any other professor at UO. When you speak in class, he politely corrects mistakes that other teachers let slide which helped so much! Also he isn't too hard. I took Advanced Writing with him and the longest paper we had to write was between 2-3 pages. If you want an easy class and want to improve, take his class!

Jesus is a fair and very in depth teacher. Very smart and very knowledgeable. ! I found him very attentive to peoples questions, and glad when they asked. And what's this about his accent?? If you want to learn Spanish, you need to understand native speakers. He speaks clearly and asks if he has been understood all the time.

Jesus was an amazing teacher! He does have a Chilean accent, but he makes sure that all of his students understand him. His class was so useful and he was always available to answer questions outside of class. He goes the extra mile for his students and he DOES expect the same in return.

Jesus is a nice guy and knows his stuff (our class was on drugs and their uses) but his accent is extreneky hard to understand. I strugled with it. He is very laid back and is a definite go with the flow guy but the amount of reading for the class was extreme overkill. If I had had the choice I would have chosen a different professor.

Not a good teacher comes across as being very arrogant.  Doesn't explain things clearly and gets visibly irritated with students asking questions.  I think it put me behind in spanish.  He has a heavy accent and is hard to understand.  I did not enjoy this class and do not recommend him...Pick someone else if possible...

I disagree with people. I think he doesn't prepare you very well at all, especially for oral tests. You basically just get put on the spot without a strong basis for knowing what you're going to do. He graded kind of hard too at the beginning, but then everyone failed so he got easier. He's not the nicest person either.
he just gets straight to the point. hes a fair grader too.

Loved him! He was an awesome teacher who made learning spanish fun (hard to believe huh?). His tests wern't extremely hard and he didn't count you down in oral exams if you asked in spanish how to say an english word. I really enjoyed his class!!
Best class i ever took! i didn't know it was possible to learn this much in one class. He is amazing!

This was, by far, the best class I have ever taken in my life. I didn't know that it was possible for me to learn so much in so short a time. It was a bit intimidating at first,with everything in spanish after resting 2 years, but, damn.. he knew how to teach. he is native chilian, so he often corrects the book.. makes it all more interesting. A+++
Great Professor, Great Human

Professor Nah would ask individual students how they were doing in the middle of large lecture classes. He extended my final project  because my computer broke and he totally understood and almost immediately extended it for me following my stressed email. He essentially allowed me to graduate on time so he's a GOAT in my book.Thanks Professor Nah!

It's not even worth my time to describe how awful this professor is. DO NOT take this class. Endless busy work it and the way the class is conducted made me lose braincells. Also assigns a huge research paper at the end with 0 help. He posted a rubric on Canvas and two example papers which are basically of no help whatsoever. Gave 0 explanation.

Professor Seungahn is absolutely amazing but get ready for a 20 page paper and a group project. He's a genius and super helpful though so if you really want to challenge yourself and learn real-world skills take J201 with him in the spring. If you're looking for an easy Journalism credit, take 201 async instead.
Hes a homie

Professor Nah is by far my favorite professor. He is very kind and patient. For the class level I think the work load is average. There is a group paper that doesnt have the clearest guidelines. Group papers are also not my favorite. The lectures are discussion based so be sure to do the readings.

Professor Nah is one of my favorite professors I've had at the UO. He genuinely cares about all of his students and is very understanding. I've taken 2 classes with him and would take more if I could. He is very passionate about what he teaches and provides amazing feedback. Take a J class with Professor Nah if you can! I love that man

Professor Nah is a really nice professor but this class is really poorly organized and does not fit the course description. Most of the graded assignments are busy work and the midterm and final group project are tedious and excessive for the amount of content we had to work with. I wouldn't recommend this class for the required B block.

J213 is a really boring class. Professor Nah does his best to make it interesting. He is a really kind man with a huge heart and lots of respect for his students. The lectures are extensive and the group project wasn't exactly ideal but he was a really great professor. The class is not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nah is hands down one of the most caring, passionate, and hard-working teachers I've ever had at UO. He comes to class each day with a smile and genuinely cares about each student. He is very flexible with any needs, he is happy to help with questions, and he is very well versed on his topics. He is a great person and a great teacher.

Professor Nah is a great guy and an amazing professor. Hes really passionate about Journalism and cares about his students deeply. As long as you do the readings and participate its a guaranteed A. Would love to take a class with him again.
I love the information he can offer but lectures can be boring. Great guy but lectures are limp

reviews.comment: Very kind teacher. Really passionate about learning about his students. Take time to listen to what he has to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Im sure that Nah is valued in the journalism school for his amazing expertise, but, he is just not the best professor in terms of courses. reviews.comment: Failed jazz musician turned into a teacher is such a bad combo. It seems like he doesn't even want to teach but since he failed as a musician this is his only option. Never take a class with him it's such a terrible experience.

He is really bad at grading and very unclear with assignments. He will just straight up give you a 0 even if you complete the assignment in it's entirety just because your opinion is different. Also he does not care about students at all which leads to the worst possible class. The course material isn't even reflective of what happened historically

(MUS 363 async) Sean was incredible helpful in providing feedback and commenting on all assignments, especially for an online class. Most assignments were discussion boards and forced you to engage with classmates, which was helpful. Very compelling class-- it's clear that Sean is very passionate about music and loves hearing from his students!

Do not take this guys class. He has absolutely 0 regard for student experience in his classes. He is a terrible grader and will not work with you at all. Very passive aggressive and rude as well. Genuinely my least favorite teacher at UO!
He is a terrible professor and you should avoid taking at all costs. He grading doesn't make sense and he is so bad.

Im not sure why Prof Peterson has such low rating, he's such a good professor!! His lectures were so engaging and so helpful for people who didn't know anything about music (me). I think that the GE grading for the essays can be a little harsh but you just gotta make sure that you hit all areas of the rubric in order to get a good grade. WTA!

I enjoyed history of jazz - Prof. Peterson seemed to be very passionate about the subject. Be ready to do timed writes for both midterm and final. Sometimes would grade hard for what seemed like no reason, like giving an 80% on an assignment and the only feedback would be "great work!" Course was straightforward and didn't require too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a super nice professor. The homework was pretty simple: you read and annotate articles every week and then have three "big assignments" but no finals or midterms. The lectures are kinda long, but he does engaging activities, and they do provide helpful insight into the materials. I took this as a freshman and was able to pass.

Class was Music in the americas, professor seemed to have barely any in depth knowledge of music in central/south america (which was the whole of the class). Multiple times GEs knew the answers to questions posed by students when the professor did not. Professor was so behind schedule at one point the GE taught some of the course content in disc.

Even though the content matter is relatively easy to understand, he manages to make his lectures unbearable. Also, after a reading has been assigned you lose access to it. He doesn't post slides either. Any study material for the class solely consists of whatever notes you take, despite him being super strict on having specific citations for papers

Lectures are super long, super boring, and do not help with the homework. He assigns readings every week that vary in length from 25 pages to 55 pages. All readings are bad quality images. I took this class because it sounded fun and ended up stressing about my grade THE ENTIRE TIME. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. The prof is a super tough grader, ave=65
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell Prof Peterson is extremely knowledgeable on what he teaches and he does it in an engaging, interesting manner. I came into the class with little to no knowledge about blues & learned so much. The weekly assignments are easy once you get the hang of the format and the bigger assignments are not too hard. I highly recommend the class.

Prof Peterson is clearly very knowledgeable on this matter. He is very into music and loves to listen to it in class. I had fun in this class and joined it without knowing anything about Jazz music at all, and learned a lot. Though the tests are a little bit harder, as long as you keep up with the weekly assignments which are easy, you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Long lectures, weekly hw assignment, weekly quiz, and 2 exams. Overall I thought he was really nice and made the class easily passable, he literally gave me the hw answers once just because I went to office hours, and my ge would give me quiz answers during discussion and they were both overall really helpful

Professor Sinclair is a really nice man who cares about his student's success. He is easily accessible by email, and has frequent and helpful office hours. His lectures are boring but if you pay attention it is really easy to do well in this class.

I feel like you have to learn how to do some things on your own because the lectures don't cover some of the content on the homework/quizzes. He's a chill professor but I feel like some of the content in his lectures is unnecessary to succeed in the course.

This class may not have been taught in a perfect way, but I got a lot of respect for this professor. Just an understanding chill guy. The exams are 50% of your grade but honestly the midterm was very easy but the final may cause you problems.

His lectures never fully covered material that was on homework or quizzes so you have to teach yourself. Grading criteria also varies based on your GE. I would go to different GE's office hours to work on homework and my assigned GE would mark me down on things another GE said was correct.

He is very passionate about stats, but doesn't actually teach what you will be tested on. Everything is on Excel, and he lectures on basic things that are common sense about data. Rarely will he ever teach you how to do anything in Excel, so I had to learn with my peers/AI. All tests/weekly quizzes are on Excel. Lectures are not mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are boring but he's super sweet and supportive. If you go to office hours he is super responsive and will help with everything, same goes in the discussions with the GEs , it's a super easy class all online with excel.
bad terrible not worth

Very nice guy, but horrible class. The homework and quizzes (both of which are weekly), are entirely done in excel, but he never uses excel in class. Lectures are usually not applicable to HW, quizzes, or exams. If you want a good grade I would join the class encore, go to discussions every week, and get TA's to help with homework. Good luck.
Lectures, quizzes, and hw don't line up together. Only class that uses excel, he only teaches us the formulas for anything but excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a really cool and nice guy, but the class itself was super unorganized. The lectures don't match the homework and barely cover the Excel skills you actually need, so you end up teaching yourself through YouTube & Google. The timed midterms are so stressful, especially since assigned seating makes you wait in line and lose time without warning.

I am on my fourth year of college and was required to take this class to graduate. Hands down, this is the worst professor I have ever had. He rarely gives in class examples to assure that students understand the material. In fact, he gave answers on our Midterm review, and a decent percentage of them were WRONG? How am I to know if I understand?
Lectures are hard to follow, but he always answers questions and occasionally half of the homework in class to teach the excel commands stats is a difficult subject in general.
Absolutely a joke, drop the class when you can. If you can't use Excel, I can't stress enough to drop it.

Bad lectures, nothing is related to the homework that is given out. The lectures are long and boring and have nothing to do with anything. None of the material on quizzes or homework is taught in class and there's no study materials for assignment. This is a stats class and all of the homework and quizzes is in excel but that's not taught in class!

This stats class was an Excel class in which the content felt worthless. Luckily, I took an Excel class last term, but I'm sure it was much harder for those who hadn't. I liked Sinclair, but the lectures felt absolutely meaningless in comparison to homework and exams. The assignments were fairly straightforward and simple.

The slides were jumbled nonsense, and there was really no point in attending lectures. He never actually explained how to use excel for the most part, just gave us formulas we never used bc everything was done on excel. And the homework and quizzes are very inconsistent. He seems like a nice guy, but the class just wasn't helpful.

God awful Professor. Everything (hw, quizzes, and exams) is on excel despite him not touching excel in his lectures. Get ready to learn everything about excel by yourself because he doesn't even answer his emails. However, when he feels like it he will post a short video on excel on SOME of the things you need to know about excel commands. 243.
Great lecturer, fair assessments and consulted with students about what we wanted out of the class. Personable, helpful, and caring. All exams were take home which was nice.
The class was difficult, however, it was Math 513 so it should have been. His explanations of class material were really helpful! I enjoyed this class. He has nice handwriting.

Very hard class as it is easy to fall behind. I had to get help every week on my homework, because the stuff he showed in class did not really have to do with the homework. The final was hard as the study guide he gave us had nothing on the actual final. He assumes we know what he is doing in lectures when most of us dont.

I took two calculus classes in high school and because of them, I passed this class. I can't imagine how difficult this class would be for anyone who has never taken calc. He was confusing during lectures because he didn't seem to know what he was doing at times and would go back and forth between what he was trying to say. I do not recommend.

Sinclair doesn't seem to know what he is doing wrong--he must be aware that he's a poor teacher in some way, else he's unfortunately oblivious. The majority of reviews for his class show that the issue is NOT with students being unable to do calculus. It's with his overdifficult, unpredictable tests, overpaced lectures, and lack of self-criticism.

He was an absolutely terrible professor. I have never taken anyone worse as a junior at UO. I am generally an A student (3.9 GPA) and I am struggling for a C+ maybe a B- if I'm lucky. His lectures are taken straight from the textbook, he is not helpful nor communicative outside of class, and he is condescending or rude when answering questions.

I would not recommend him not just because I had a negative experience in my class, but many, if not most, did not enjoy him as a professor. One of the more disappointing classes I have taken. If you are okay with self learning, you may be able to swing by, but if you are looking for an engaging professor, this is not who you should go to.
Awful.

Terrible teacher. I haven't finished the class yet, but I'm almost positive I'm going to get the lowest grade of my academic career, and I'm in the honors college! He basically just copies his notes out of the textbook which isn't a good textbook in the first place. He only explains the abstract ideas and not how to solve any equations.
His handwriting is awful!. He like to write on a paper,and then use the projector to show us. That is terrible, Can he just make PPTs since  nobody knows what he is saying

the worst teacher i have ever had. If you go to office hours and read the text, this class isn't bad.
Worst professor I have ever had to teach math. Does not care about students at all.
He doesn't teach well and does not care if students fail. Hard tests and homework. Notes are not that helpful. Not a good experience.

He is by far the worst teacher I have ever had, he could care less if you fail. During lecture he gives you the most basic examples and then the homework and exams are impossible. The class average was about a 50% for exams. He should never be able to teach again.

WORST TEACHER AT THE UO BY FAR. He makes things way harder than they need to be, mocks his students, and does nothing to help his students succeed. If you are not expecting to spend at least 20 hours outside of this class, dont take a class from Sinclair

He is just a fine teacher. Not great, and def not as awful as all these people said. He is just average, gives good examples in class and the tests are similar to those examples. The webwork was way too hard though.

I am getting an A in the class, got an A on both midterms only because I took calculus in high school. He makes things harder than they need to be. Completely useless as a teacher. Not just people who are failing think he's a twot

Your life will be a living hell if you take this class. Sinclair gives terrible lectures, laughs at his students failing, and is just in general a horrible teacher. Do not bother taking a math class if sinclair is the only professor available.

Who uses definitions in math? Thats all Sinclair does. I had already took calculus in high school and still failed

Worst teacher EVER. His teaching is unclear! He always skips steps and when you ask how he got an answer he says "I've just been doing math for a long time" I got a tutor for this class and still Failed his midterm with the rest of the class.

I am an excellent student. For this class I hired a private tutor, went to office hours, did my homework, went to class, took notes, and I failed the second midterm along with 55% of the class. He does not care about the whether his students are learning the content.
Ugh, he could not make the material more difficult and hard to understand then what he did.
The worst instructor I have ever had. He was rude, obnoxious and couldn't teach to save his life. Do not take this class if he if the professor.

Math 241 is a hard class, but this teacher is probably the worst i've had. He regularly laughs about how hes going to fail people on the tests and 50% of the class will be not passing. I would say i'm a pretty good math student. I second that opinion; this is the worst teacher i've ever had.
Worst teacher I've ever had. Like seriously. 60% of the class is on track to fail right now.

I personally found his class very helpful for math, although kind of confusing in his wording very straightforward and clear for a math 101 class. I would take his class again. He's well-intentioned, but does a bad job of explaining concepts in a way that helps students understand and apply them. Low averages (around 50%), if you have a math brain you'll be fine, but otherwise, avoid.

Very nice guy but for MATH 101 he was incredibly lecture heavy and would not go over problems in class which is not helpful because you are left to your own devices to figure it out, and on top of that his tests did not reflect what we go over in class nor the homework. overall if you can avoid this professor, do it!
Awful and so confusing.

Prof. Simon Venter is a nice but flawed Calculus I teacher. His exams are way harder than class content, causing low averages (around 40%). This guy sucks

reviews.comment: He clearly loves math and knows the subject well but he is not good at teaching and explaining it. He also apparently uses unusual notation at times which makes it hard to transfer what you learn to future classes.

All he does is show examples and vaguely explain it out loud. There's a lot of extra credit offered through web work assignments, anything over 80% is extra credit. All quiz and exam scores tended to be very low and questions didn't always correlate with the webworks, which is basically all the direction given.

Chill person that is easy to talk to casually. He is very helpful when you have any questions and is very accessible outside of class through office hours and email. He was alright, made our last midterm too long to complete in 50 min.

2 Webworks a week, anything over an 80% on them is extra credit. Ive loved his class and have done great. My peers have not. Last midterm the class median was a 54, he adjusted it with a curve but the average after that was still really bad, but I got a 95. I swear if you just do the required work and study in areas that you need it, youre all good
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Only 2 homework assignments each week, and all had the opportunity for extra credit. Replies super quick to emails.

Classes were pretty straightforward, but there are times where it felt he didn't have a plan for the day. There were quizzes every Tuesday and homework assignments twice a week. The homework didn't really correlate with what we learn in class, but the quizzes were pretty easy. He did a good job explaining concepts and you could ask questions too.

I feel like this class was an average introductory class, most big lecture classes are graded on only a few exams so i feel like that wasn't too unexpected. As long as you use the study guide and get the online stuff done you will do just fine. Margaret tries her best to be engaging but it's hard w/ basic intro stuff
I really enjoyed this course. Margaret is incredibly knowledgeable in this subject. Exam heavy, but questions are based 100% off the slides. Study the slides, and you will do well.

It's currently week 7 and we've had 2 homework assignments, 2 exams, and we have 2 exams left. I think classes that are that test heavy with little to no assignments are extremely frustrating. When your grade basically solely relies on exams it can be annoying.

Class itself is pretty easy. Weekly inquizzative and ZAPs assignments. Lectures are long but content is easy to understand. Professor is really sweet but can be boring because she just reads off the slides.

This class was much easier than I expected. The powerpoints are easy to follow and almost all the concepts connect and make general sense. The hardest part was the Inquizitive assignments. If you study the materials on the study guides it is easy to pass. Just make sure to pay attention in class as the exams are heavily based off of lectures.

Assessments are worth 65% percent of your grade, and the Inquizitive homework assignments are my number one enemy. Very nice woman and I enjoyed her lectures but it is hard to remember and understand certain concepts that are taught within the class. Overall fun though but would never do again.
She isn't a bad teacher, but simply just reads off of her lecture prompts. The class consists of very boring lectures and tedious homework but it isn't too difficult.

Lecture-heavy course with basic introduction material, so it can be boring and hard to focus, but if you do the online assignments and take some notes, it's pretty straightforward. The online homework is an easy way to help your grade. The lecture slides are also a good tool to study for exams.

Very disorganized course; she reads directly off the slides and gives no further explanations on the content. Course is exam-heavy she wouldn't review content and would assign homework right after an exam on content we hadn't learned yet. Margaret did not elaborate on lectures at all. Slides were minimal info and boring. The tests are multiple choice and difficult, she does not curve. To be fair this course is material heavy but she doesn't look at your assignments through the textbook. You have to obtain sona credit that is mostly in person, so try to get that asap.
Doesn't really teach. She reads straight off the slides. The study guides for exams are so extensive that they'll leave you studying for 6+ hours at least.
horrible worst teacher at oregon

I loved her! She knew her stuff and was very passionate. I was able to follow her lectures easily and learned a lot from the class. Her lectures can be a bit dry but the content was interesting.

reviews.comment: Pretty disgraceful that this professor isn't rated higher by most. I thought she was a great teacher and the slides were super helpful for understanding the chapter content. She's one of the better psych professors at UO. Nobody likes InQuizitive and ZAPS labs as assignments but she probably doesn't control that.

lectures are boring but other than that she's not bad. attendance is taken on iclicker and she does 4 exams instead of MTs and a final which I actually liked; all multiple choice and relatively easy. very assignment light class and an easy a. if you did ap psych in hs its the same thing; nice refresher course and mandatory for psych majors anyways

She was pretty chill, basically your grade was made up of the multiple choice tests, had to do an inquizitive and zaps lab every week or so, as well as research participation outside of class. The classes were all lectures and were pretty long and boring.

Not a difficult class by any means, though I came into this after taking AP Psych in highschool so I had some knowledge. Did a good job trying to keep us interested in memorization-heavy content. As long as you read the textbook for a bit each week and take notes you will be fine.
Extremely test heavy, easy to fall behind with one bad grade and not have the flexibility of redemption.

Sereno gets a bad rep because the lectures are boring and monotonous. most boring class I've ever taken, professor doesn't really do much just reads slides and clips through them, I would rather watch an episode of Talk Tuah podcast and do the missed class stuff, feels more worth my time.

The homework program she uses is very frustrating. Her TA wrote all the exams and when said TA gave a guest lecture, it made more sense than Margaret's usual lectures.

I truly do not understand all the negative reviews for Dr. Sereno. Yeah, she's dry, but exams are all MC and so straightforward that you do not even have to read the book. reviews.comment: 70% of your grade in this class will come from 4 midterms which are closed book. It was frustrating because if you do bad on one your grade was basically tanked. Read and take notes on the textbook for sure! Also she does not do extra credit so that sucks.

She's a good teacher overall, def passionate about psychology. However her grading was mostly test heavy, 4 exams ( no mid-term/final) which was worth a lot, and if you do "badly" on one/two and completed everything else you probably won't get an A. She doesn't do extra credit which sucks. Definitely watch the lectures and take notes!

A pretty typical lecture class. If you read the textbook and study a lot, it is easy to pass. She is eager to answer questions and explains stuff well with examples. However, it is a little test heavy, given there are 4 tests that are worth a lot of your grade.

Professor Sereno is very test-heavy. There are four mid-term exams, none of which are cumulative, but are easy so long as you study for them. Most questions are directly off the slides, so don't bother reading. Other than that, this is your very standard lecture class: inquizitives due every week, online labs that take 5 minutes. Overall easy class
Be prepared for sudden changes in the grading percentages with little explanation. Participation points are very difficult to figure out for 5.5% of your grade.

Professor Sereno is amazing! One of the few professors I've had that seems to really care about the students. The end of the winter term was very chaotic but she went out of her way to make sure everyone succeeded (she even dropped the lowest test grade!)

For the entire two hours, she reads directly off of the slides. It is useless to go to class because we could do the same thing. She doesn't teach, she reads. Her tests are pretty normal except the sensation and perception. She gives a HUGE list of things you need to know and tests you on one topic. I do not recommend her.

Absolute worst teacher. Her tests are not related to the study guide. I studied for 3 weeks and got a D on my midterm. Examples of what you talk about in class are the subtractive and additive colors. Study guide just says colors. Test questions are in a room of 201 students if the person next to you is shaking uncontrollably then what shoes are on
One of the most boring and bland teachers I've ever had. I was typically dying to get out by the end of class. Do all the readings or you won't pass.

reviews.comment: To pass her tests, you must study. It is all on the lecture slides, but it's heavy. She tried to find ways to make it up, but she put up a bit of a fight. Nice lady, just be wary of her grading.

she changed the entire weighting of the class during week 8 of 10. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Everything on the tests are on the slides; does a good job of outlining and organizing material. There are four exams but they are easy if you paid attention. Won't need much study time for this course.

LOVE HER!!! Her class consists of four exams (no final) and 5% participation. Its very test heavy but she curves the class hard. This term an 82% was an A. Her lectures can get a tad boring but overall interesting and one of the better psych professors!

She is the most disengaging teacher. She always has clicker questions on stuff she has never taught us. She is monotone and you there is no logical flow to her slides. Her study guides are like someone just puked up random information and then threw it on a piece of paper. She really needs help with engaging students on a personal level.

Dr. Sereno gives amazing lectures and is always available for office hours. Her knowledge of psychology is extensive. Attendance via iClicker. No lab.

I wish I could give this professor the benefit of the doubt but I can't. Test are super hard, lectures are painfully boring and she doesn't seem to know her material. Every time a student asks a question, she ponders on it for a minute and then says, "Good question, I do not know." It's urking!! To pass exams be prepared to study for a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I thought Prof. Sereno was a great lecturer, she was a clear speaker and her tests were fair but pretty easy if you paid attention in class and went over the slides.

Talks for the entire class time, no engaging activities. Sometimes doesn't even cover material on the exam until the day before. Not sure how this class falls into the psychology category but is more science than anything relevant to the major. Strongly discourage psych majors from taking this course as it will not pertain to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sereno is a wonderful teacher! She teaches the material in a very systematic and clear way. The thing I would say to anyone before taking her class, is that there are 4 exams total. In order to do well on the exams, it is necessary to study the lecture slides until you memorize them. If you are 100% committed, the class is easy and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wow Dr. Soreno is such an amazing professor. She really cares about all her students. I am so inspired by her. Will take her again for sure. Thank you so much

Personally, I really enjoyed PSY 202 more because it deals with social interactions, personality and psychological disorders, but it was really interesting to learn about the anatomy of the brain, neurons, language and sensation/perception in PSY 201, and I thought Professor Sereno gave excellent lectures!

She really needs to be updated on technology. We were often left just hanging out while the professor tried to figure out a way to get a vhs to work or complained about technology. This class was a huge disappointment. For many students this is their only exposure to Psychology. I'm sure a lot of students were no longer interested in the subject.

Professor Sereno knows an incredible amount of material about psychology.  However, she struggles to keep her students engaged and present the material clearly.  I think our first exam had nearly 150 terms we had to learn.  Exams are 70% of your grade, and they are tough.  If you are not passionate about psych, stay away from this class.  PLEASE!

Ok, so Prof Sereno is a great person, smart and very nice. She is there for you if you put the effort to contact her, though her lectures are pretty boring she is trying to make them more entertaining with videos and class engaging activities. Tests can be sort of tough but if you read and pay attention they are very easy. Would recommend.

I would recommend this class if you're a psych major, otherwise it may be a struggle to stay interested. In order to enjoy/get good grade in this class  do these things: Sit in lower section of lecture hall, understand that the material gets easier/more interesting as term progresses, and know that everything on test will be discussed in lecture.

Lectures are not engaging or enjoyable. Tests are extremely difficult, only positive thing is that she curves them, which is the only reason I think I'm going to pass this class. Your grade is based off the exams with only 5% participation and 2% extra credit. Would not recommend.

Lectures often times put me to sleep and they are mandatory for iClicker points...I'd like this class a lot better if I didn't have to attend the lectures but that just isn't realistic. Prepare to be in a room with 500 students, 100 of which won't stop talking, 350 which are on their phones/laptops, and 50 of which are actually paying attention.

This woman is a the worst kind of professor. She only requires books in her classes from a certain publisher. A little digging reveals why ($). Her class is based on iclicker questions and basic literacy. She requires students play guinea pig to psych experiments, attempted to prevent me from graduating when I refused to be an unpaid test subject.

The lectures are pretty boring, but you need to get the iclicker points. A lot of examples she uses are on the midterms including the videos. The mid terms are very fair and everything on the test has been on the powerpoints. The weekly quizzes are very easy points, just read the labs. Not a sure 1st round pick but is a steal in the later rounds.

Absolutely LOVE her. I'm a psych major and transferred here expecting "meh" classes and she made my term. She's organized and clear and helpful and you really learn a lot from the structure she provides. Take her class. She really wants you to do well and learn.
I was really excited to take this class, Margaret ruined Psychology for me. Boring long classes, only need to be there for clicker questions. Not an easy A do not take if your not a Psych major.

The class is very reading based but her lectures were really key to understanding the content. She's kind of brainy but has a good sense of humor and is very good at communicating complex ideas. Studying for tests is essential. The weekly quizzes shouldn't be so many points for 3-4 questions but that's the only thing I could fault.

Sereno really wants her students to learn, but her lecture slides move so fast that it is impossible to get good & complete notes. However, she posts her slides online beforehand, and it is best to take the notes and copy the info before class, and then listen to her speak and read them over during. There are four exams and no final, pretty easy.

I really enjoyed Professor Sereno! She would always listen to students questions even in a 500 person lecture hall and always had a happy personality in class. There are 4 exams (just study the slides and they are pretty easy), Iclicker questions, and online quizzes. Great way to get a science credit! Can be a long class, but really interesting!

Dr. Sereno is extremely intelligent and knows what she is talking about to the "T"! She does unfortunately drone a bit, though this is difficult when talking about psychology to a bunch of people that don't care. Quiz questions resemble each other far too closely, often differing only by a word or two, so it can become a guessing game. Long class.

One of the worst teachers Ive ever had. She knows a lot about psychology, but from a teaching standpoint she is absolutely horrible. She reads off her slides, and goes too quickly for you to take notes. her mono-toned voice puts you to sleep after the first 20minutes. Attendance is required (Iclicker) quizes every week w/ZAPS. 4 Exams, none drop.

This class is pretty easy, but extremely boring. She strictly reads off of her slides, and her tests are based off the slides as well. She curves the tests, but this class almost put me to sleep every time.

Super easy class but feel asleep in probably every lecture. She has clicker questions in class but you don't even need to get them correct to get credit, the tests are easy if you simply review the her PowerPoints she goes over in class that she posts to blackboard. This class is one of the easiest ways to get a science credit.

Such an easy class. I only attended class to take the exams (there are 4 and one score is dropped). She spells it out for you with her study guides -- literally all you need to do is read her study guide and go through her power points from lecture and the exams are very easy to pass.
She knows a lot and would like you to study hard and understand the concepts. Otherwise it is hard to get a good grade. The class was fun and I learned a lot, office hours were were helpful.
Dont listen those who tell that you dont need a textbook! Half of the midterm question not related with her slides at all.  I did not pay to much attention to the textbook and it was  a mistake.
Boring Boring Boring. All she does is read off her slides. Looks very anxious.

I think she may be one of my favorite teacher that I have had here at the U of O. I found her to be extremely helpful especially during office hours. I really struggled in this class, and she took every effort to help me out to prepare for the exams. I would take another class from her and would recommend her as well. very nice and very helpful.

Very nice, she knows a hell of a lot. On the other hand she can be a bit redundant with her lecture. It is true (like others have said) that she can be a bit dry, but its really only boring if you aren't into the material; she does a fine enough job. Plus, the text book is rediculously priced, but you dont need it! everything is on the slides.

She TALKS VERY FAST. I hate it when she goes back and forth, back and forth between slides, you can never take good notes. But she is very helpful during office hours. Great lady, knows what she's talking about, not really that great of a teacher
Class isn't really necessary, since all the test answers will be in her slides. There is some cool material though.
someone needs to tell her that it's a 200 LEVEL CLASS!!!! way to intensive
The tests are easy and as long as you memorize the powerpoints you can get an A
Horribly dull class. All she does is read off her slides (which she posts online) at supersonic speeds. SHE DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO TEACH.

Very boring teacher. Class was pointless since she read off her slides. All slide shows were posted online. Don't bother buying the text book, you wont need it! Only 4 tests throughout the course and no accumlative midterm or final. She scales each individual test and then curves the final grade at the end so the majority of the class receives a B-

The class is extremely boring.  Professor Sereno is very boring and paces while she lectures which makes me really dizzy. It was a waste of money for me to buy the textbook, I read the first assigned reading, & never read anything past that & still did good on the exams.

Yes, this class can be very boring and long, but honestly it is a breeze. Her MC test questions are straight from her Powerpints which she posts online. There are 4 exams of 40 questions, and no final. I study the night before tests and have averaged a 94% on the first three exams. If you put any effort into this class you will get a good grade.
i mean, the classes were pretty boring, but she definitely knows her ****. and all in all it wasnt too hard

not the best class in general, but a good teacher who obviosuly knows a lot. Her notes are very nicely laid out and out onto blackboard VERY helpful for the tests! also she let me take a midterm late because I was really sick, very considerate person!
I had little interest in the class and found it quite dull, but the professor was obviously knowledgable.  She was a competant teacher and made a valient attmept to make the subject interesting.
BORING CLASS.

Dr. Shoemaker is clearly passionate and endlessly knowledgeable about his field. If you respect straight-forward assignments and tests, this is the professor for you. His lectures are packed full of information so expect to take diligent notes, especially as the exams require a lot of attention for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Shoemaker is obviously passionite in the subject and very knowledgeable. However, if there are students in class not participating, this does seem to make him upset, and he will make the tests absurdly niche on purpose. Enjoyable lectures, study a lot for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very smart and interesting prof. Super passionate about his subject, his lectures are super engaging. Graded on only a couple of things. Doesn't use canvas, just his website. Exams are difficult.

Professor Shoemaker is a really knowledgeable guy and his lectures are super interesting, but the class itself is really difficult. There are no study guides for the exams and you are only graded on one essay and 3 exams, attendance barely counts. If you aren't super good at remembering dates and names, good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much reading. So, so much reading. You don't need to do all of it but it does help a lot if you want a good grade. Also pretty difficult to pass if you aren't in class; I struggled to catch up after getting sick. It was manageable, just hard. Lectures were pretty interesting which helped.
Whole class is graded on 2 exams and 1 essay. He offers no study guide. The whole class he just reads of the slides for 2 straight hours.

I loved this professor. He's very straightforward in what he expects and a no bs type of guy. He teaches from a very historical viewpoint of the religions. It's impossible to pass this class without going to lecture and taking really good notes. It's a difficult course for a level 100 and there's a lot of memorization involved, but interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Shoemaker is very knowledgable, but this class is tough for a 100-hundred level; I would not recommend taking for general credit. You do not need to do the readings for class. There are 3 exams, a paper, and discussion boards. Attendance isn't mandatory for lecture, but you need to go to do well! Attendance is mandatory for discussion.

Lectures for the whole class and answers no questions. Graded off of two midterms a final exam with a final essay due the same week as the final exam. There is no homework however you get participation for showing up to your discussion. It is almost impossible to get an A on any of the exams, as his lecture is confusing and story-like.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes very smart, definitly knows his stuff, his lectures are mostly just him showing bullet points then going in detail, so you have to actively listen and show up to class. There are about 4 assignments in the class, 2 midterms, 1 final, 1 final paper, so you gotta be prepared. The class is unforgiving but the teacher himself is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shoemaker is very knowledgeable in what he teaches. This course is pretty lecture heavy and has a decent amount of reading, but as long as you keep up with the readings and go to class you should do fine on the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While this professor tries to make the lectures as engaging as possible, the class will mostly just be getting spoken at by this professor. While attendance is not mandatory, there is no way that you will pass this class if you regularly skip the lectures; this professor does not make any material from lectures available online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class was based on medieval topics like knights and kings, but it's heavily based on just religion in the middle ages. The professor is great, but his lecture slides are really vague and simple, so you actually have to pay attention to the lecture to take good notes. He was always fitted though, I need his sweater collection.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though the lectures were interesting and the content was fairly easy to understand, class is only graded by 3 tests, 1 essay, and participation in discussions. The tests are ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE to pass. Half is based on random info in lecture. I studied my hardest and never received higher than a 67/100 on a test. Disappointed but loved content.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Stephen J. Shoemaker teaches this class the same way every year: 3 tests, and 6 pg paper. His lecture are heavy on speaking rather than slides, so show up take good notes. He has study guides posted from past classes on his personal website where the syllabus is located, so use those for tests. He's a good lecturer who structures content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: lots of assigned reading for hw , mostly irrelevant lectures can be boring but pay attention and take goods notes and you're fine. be prepared to be talked at for 50 min straight
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing Prof.!

I got a B- in the class but that's because I choked on the Matchmaking for the first two tests (terrible test taker). Taking notes is obviously essential to doing well in this class. Truth be told, the better the notes you take, the better you'll do. I'm not really a good example but the truth is, this is an easy A class. As for him, he's decent.
Very interesting class. Exams are easy, multiple choice, matching dates, and 5 short answer questions. Doesn't give study guides so take good notes in class. Easy A

I happened to learn VERY well with this professor. You definitely NEED to go to class to get a good grade, but if you attend his classes and take good notes (he's very thorough in his descriptions) you will do really well! He talks the entire time, but it's all relevant information.

This guy is very knows his stuff! All I know is I have learned a ton from him. I have taken two courses from him and plan to take more. He has two tests and one paper. If you go to lectures it is not hard to get a good grade because he explains everything in such depth. He is passionate and keeps the class fun and relaxed. Makes history fun!

This professor is extremely arrogant and not very intelligent.  His expectations are very unclear and he shows a great deal of favoritism in his class.  I will never take a class from this man again, and regret ever doing so.

I thought he was a great professor!! Extremely knowledgable. From reading these other comments, 5-6yrs old now, I don't find that he exemplified any of those traits, maybe he's matured. :) It was a VERY informative course. He spoke and taught clearly. very animated, makes for an entertaining class as well. Highyly recommend the course.
He was very clear, but it was just a lot of information.  He doesn't give a study guide so you have to know EVERYTHING.  Even though he was clear the class was still very hard.

Professor Shoemaker is awesome! His knowledge of the subject is incredible. I just feel so lucky to have had this class. I don't think I've ever taken a course like his and I feel like my life has been transformed. Wow!!

Awesome teacher and class. If you study and go to class its so easy. Everything is very clearly laid out, and broken up well. He is a specialist in Christianity so his upper div classes are better, but all are good! I was suprised at how knowledgable he was. He may not know everything about Islam, but he knows a ton about his field of Christianity.

thought I didn't care much for the topic, he kept me interested. he's a funny guy. the tests and papers are pretty easy and he seems to grade fairly. the only difficulty I had was understanding and discussing theological ideas but I guess that's my fault for taking an upper division class without any background in this subject.

Agreed: lacks knowledge in Islam and other "smaller" sects.  His tests were more difficult than expected, though his paper is fairly easy - with research.  Must understand in-depth terms from all sources (i.e. both books and lecture) to fully do well on tests.

Occasionally his lectures were offensive.  He doesn't have a very in-depth understanding of Islam.  However, his lectures keep the class interested.  If you aren't good at memorizing dates the tests will be hard, but otherwise you are golden.  Overall, he provided an acceptable overview and fulfilled the purpose of the course.
Outrageously bad course and teaching

Take a class from this guy! He is super smart AND really funny. You'll be laughing for the whole term. He's also really open-minded  and willing to entertain some pretty far out ideas as long as they are logical and backed up by the readings.

Infuriating.  Arrogant.  He taught Islam in the most demeaning way-ignoring most of the tradition, while covering his own new "theories".  On the plus side, his tests and written assignments are straightforward.  In addition, he is relatively amusing.
Very knowledgeable and interested in his work, but rigid in his thinking and may freely rub students the wrong way

Although he has always been professional, there is a definite feeling of favoritism in his classes.  Nothing that seems entirely out of line (and my grade was acceptable) but I never felt heard in class and he has been overtly rude to me outside of class. It seems that he simply feels superior and it shows.
Great professor, great lecuters, very knowledgeable, will go out of his way to help you out.

He was extremely rude to me when i asked him to clarify something he mentioned in lecture. He did not seem to care about what he was teaching, and taught for testing only. Too hard for a 100-level class.
He was alright.  His lectures were clear and concise.
His tests are all Multiple choice. So it is pretty easy. He is a really good prof.

Great prof! i would take another class with him if i needed to. Lectures are a mixture of him making jokes and content. His instructions are pretty vague on purpose. You have a project as final, 2 midterms, pop quizzes, and a NYT journal that ur supposed to write an entry for everyday but i didn't read any assigned text and still got an A
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof cares so much about what he teaches. He's very passionate and a super interesting guy. He provides a very supportive environment. I felt comfortable talking in class and staying after to ask him any questions. Lots of reading, but all interesting stuff. One of the best classes I've taken. Very moving. Just pay attention and show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Shaul is a great person, with lots of lived experience. However, I found the class to be relatively unorganized, and the content to be somewhat confusing or irrelevant. The class is on population and geography and after having taken the class, I still don't know what it means, aside from "it's about everything". Plus, the NYT logs are excessive.

This class was very impactful and I enjoyed it a lot more than I ever thought I would! Shaul is very knowledgeable, and lectures are important to pay attention to. It's an easy class to do well in as long as you pay attention and study, particularly the historical figures mentioned. There is barely any assignments, the exams are most important.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny, engaging lectures which reward participation. Excellent socratic teacher.

Easy Pop quizzes check attendance; tests based on lecture so go to class and pay attention. Long readings but skim or summarize it. Key readings mentioned in lectures. Don't be put off by his personality, go to office hours and speak up! He is very sweet, gave me advice on grad school, and has a lot of whimsy. I'd never taken GEO, give it a chance!
Very interesting class with a very interesting professor. There are weekly readings but they aren't too long. If you put in effort and pay attention an A is very achievable!

One of the best professors Ive had. He is wonderful to listen to and cares deeply towards each of his students and their success. His classes have a decent work load but are beyond worth it. I recommend taking as many classes with him as you can at the University of Oregon.

GEOG 343 is ridiculously easy. Everything we analyze feels like recycled 2014 Tumblr takes made by middle school girls— except it's repackaged for people who never had a breakdown in a flower crown.

I'm looking at you Gen Z iPad babies….

While this professor was an easy A, i would not recommend. His assignment setup is very unclear and confusing. You have to do a NYT article summary everyday which is the only homework, but it is so time consuming and is the smallest portion of your grade… There were three pop quizzes, some take home, some in class, so attendance was necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were arduous and boring but you have to go to class, even though he didn't show up a lot at first. Make sure you read the supplied materials because he often didn't cover them in class, but we were tested on them. Almost all of the graded work was in the last two weeks, which was very frustrating. Didn't take away much from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: one of the weirder professors ive had.. would get mad at students for leaving class early and had lectures that were so incredibly boring. i felt like he didnt care for his students, especially if they didn't try their absolute hardest in the class. i liked the final project but we only had a couple assignments in gradebook so grades matter A LOT.

Cohen's classes are exactly what people are talking about when they say the University of Oregon (and colleges in general) are hiveminds of a certain political ideology. Professor Cohen has said "capitalism has to go" and made other political takes I find inappropriate for a professor. Cohen also had an entire class devoted to talking about himself

more than a teacher, shaul is a great and interesting person to talk to about nearly everything in life. he was my FIG teacher as well as class teacher and while the class I took was very similar to AP Human Geography that I had taken in high school, I still feel like I learned new viewpoints. Encourages lots of discussion and overall is inspiring.

Some things are graded easy but others are graded harshly. Lecture slides did not have much to take notes on, it was difficult to catch up if a class was missed. Have to turn assignments in printed in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded by 3 pop quizzes, 2 midterms, and 1 final project and a NY log. grading instructions were always so unclear and got points marked off when I didn't mention something although it wasn't in the prompt. if you pay attention to the philosphers he talks about in lecture and then read about them, you should be fine on your grades.

Only 5% of our grade was up on Canvas in week 8. Disorganized course, the majority of work was assigned in the last 2 weeks. Assignments weren't graded harshly, but the instructions were unclear. Cohen spent a lot of class time talking about himself (including an entire lecture dedicated to answering personal questions and opening his mail).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: He is the best! Please take his class. Make sure you get a decent grasp on readings for the exams, but don't sweat it over the pop quizzes. Shaul is fascinating and my favorite professor I have taken. I learned to much and actually enjoyed showing up.

Shaul is an awesome professor. His class was easy if you showed up and did the work. There are 3 "pop quizzes" but he usually reminds you about it a class before it will happen. He goes over a lot of themes. Things like world population, running water, lack of food, and basic human rights. Interesting class and a take-home final.

Good professor! While his lectures may sometimes feel long, he has interesting ideas and barely any homework. Really an awesome guy, and has a cool lifestyle. I would recommend if you are interested in the world and how we can do better.

All classes are lectures with periodic questions about the readings. There will be 3 "pop quizzes," I say it in quotations because he will remind you that he gives pop quizzes a class or two before. Can go on tangents but the midterm and pop quizzes will relate to the slides or in the readings. Midterm is a written exam, and the final is a project.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures can be long-winded and he has interesting teaching methods, to say the least. But if you pay attention, his opinions and stories are ones to get you really thinking. Especially if you're taking the CGO FIG (freshmen), you see that his words and actions are rooted in ethics studies. Great guy to talk to!
The lectures can be hard to take notes on but as long as you pay attention you won't really need to. The test is mostly writing and application of concepts from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory because there are 3 "pop" quizzes. You will get full credit as long as you are present and turn anything in. Class is mainly discussions.
