The tests are based the readings assigned on Canvas. Know the readings in order to get a good grade on the midterm. The G.E.'s will grade everything except for the final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Shaul is a nice teacher but the class was set up weirdly. Attendance wasn't mandatory but he did have 3 pop quizzes and you got full credit if you showed up and took them. Final was a take home midterm paper that doesn't really require lecture material, just readings. Final project was a fun project of your choosing though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He acts like he's the smartest human on the planet. He's not great but he's not horrible. Class is easy , but there really wasn't a central theme of the class. There are readings but they're pretty worthless. Pop quizzes and he makes you do a weekly log on NY times articles. A couple of essays as well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Overall, his class was honestly a waste of time and money. His class barely had any direction or cohesiveness; it was all over the place. He would often talk about his personal political beliefs. He would talk very quietly too. Not a hard class per se, but also not a meaningful one. Even now, I still don't know what the class's purpose actually was

Shaul is a laid back and very intelligent professor. He knows a lot and about the world and seems like an interesting person to get to know. He grades reasonably and pretty fairly. He does expect a lot out of his students, but I believe that people can adjust to do so.

Shaul is super funny, but I felt numb in his class most days. The lectures are very weird and there isn't much note taking, which is a bit frustrating when studying for the midterm. He does give out pop quizzes so make sure to show up for class. He uploads the textbook chapters onto canvas. Also, he does not have a super loud voice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had in college. He has made such an impact on my life over the past four years. I've never met a professor with more expectations or more devotion to his students. Not only has he been a mentor but 3 of my favorite classes in college were with him. Too down to earth for the Ivy league he belongs at.
A lot of the class was looking at pictures while he talked about them. The class was interesting and got me interested in human geography, which he said was the point.

Really enjoyed taking this class. I definetley recommend reading the chapters assigned before coming to class because he jumps right into things. Although you can probably pass the class without reading at all because he mentions "key terms" every lecture in his slides and as long as you know those and can describe them you should do pretty well.
Inspiring person, great teacher, knows his stuff. Extremely vague but if you can go with the flow, then he is the teacher for you

I spend time with Professor Cohen multiple times each week and have done so for a while. Very strait forward, VERY opinionated. I have never even imagined reading books as awful as the ones he makes you read. having said that...he will expand your mind if you TAKE GOOD NOTES

Great professor and very smart man. comes off super intimidating at times but he is really a very understanding professor. He does not like to waste time or have you waste it. Don't be late, don't sleep, and don't text. AND DON'T USE LIKE INAPPROPRIATELY. Take his class and remember to keep an open mind.

Sure, he is opinionated. He's also makes concessions to others and is fair in his evaluations. Sure he's a lefty. But he knows his stuff. This guy is brilliant, is genuinely interested in expanding your mind, and has a great sense of humor too. He'll make you feel guilty about destroying the environment with your lifestyle, but maybe you should.

He is a really great teacher who has a lot of interesting ideas. His view on the middle east is very insightful and made me want to visit one day. Although there are only 3 novels to read one is 600 pages long and a bore. I would totally recommend him as a teacher and to take his FIG camels and cowboys

I've heard mixed feelings towards Dr. Cohen. I feel like you either love him or you really dislike him. I happened to LOVE his course. He's extremely intelligent, passionate and knowledgeable in his area of studies. I would and have highly recommended to take a course from Dr. Cohen. Like someone else said, he belongs at an ivy leauge

Shaul is an amazing professor and person. He's knowledgeable, passionate, and ready to challenge his students. He also has a very unique perspective being an Israeli with palestinian family. He is unbiased and just a joy to learn from.
Easily the best professor I've had in college.  Opened my mind to things I had never considered.

Great professor, incredibly interesting, intelligent, and great lecturer.  I'd say he is biased, but come on- you're taking and Population and Environment class at the University of Oregon- what do you really expect!?!  He's honest and frank about the issues facing our world, but readily acknowledges how difficult it is for people to change.
It's an interesting class but exactly what you are studying is very vague.  I'm still not entirely sure what we were supposed to get out of that class.

Interesting class if you are into the region...class is ok. Sometimes its really interesting, sometimes its not. Really interesting person outside of class though. He knows his stuff about the middle east. Read three novels which are kinda boring. Have to see movies outside of class which kinda sucks. Not too bad of a class.
Shaul Cohen: Self-righteous? Yes. Egotistical? Yes. Interesting? Yes.

Love Shaul! His classes are always entertaining and interesting. He is understanding and willing to help with assignments, although sometimes he isn't very clear with what he wants. If you don't understand, ask him about it and he will explain. I recommend taking any of his classes, as they will be interesting and informative!

Cohen is a pretty cool guy but his class it too long. Even 2 days a week, 1 hour 20 mins is too long in his class. The first couple of weeks were interesting and it is a good topic to learn, but at the end I lost interest.  The reading is novels only which is cool. And only 2 tests, book reviews are easy.  Glad I took it, learned lots.
certaintly can't construct a good conversation. expects us to just start talking without raising any questions. very opiniated. thinks he knows more than he does.
Absolutely awsome! He really cares about those students that care about what they're doing.  Extremely helpful and insightful.

cohen is very vague and no one really knows whats going on in his class. but there is no homework, only 2 midterms and an end of the term project that is open to interpretation. very cool guy and a very easy class. just go to lecture. also, no books required just a subscription to the NY Times.
I am minoring in geography because Dr. Cohen is so good.
Tough class really unsure about what you were going to be tested on.  Imperative you attend class and listen and take notes.  Not too much out of class work, book analyses are easy.

Cohen is one of those teachers who you WANT to impress. He is very intelligent and belongs at Harvard so his lectures are WORTH YOUR MONEY. No main textbook, just has you read a couple of Middle-Eastern novels and write a 2-3 page paper. Very good class, great teacher. My advice: SHOW UP, PUT YOUR PEN  TO USE AND WRITE EVERYTHING THAT HE IS SAYING.

Great teacher. He is really passionate about what he is teaching and that shows in his lectures. Very interesting topics. He does a great job making the class interesting but his multiple choice tests are hard...his essay test rock though! Overall good teacher!

Definitely different!  Manages to get 100 people to have interesting discussions, partly by being provocative, but in a good way.  Let's you know what he thinks, or does he?  Readings are sometimes dry, but he brings everything to life and ties it all together.  Makes you look at your values, which ain't always easy.
Boring! He must be a jerk. I didn't like his class although I got a B. The man got issues.
He is a great teacher and really intelligent. His voice is a little mono tone, so it gets boring at times, but if you can handle that you will enjoy his classes

Expects you to think, some want to others don't.  Pretty funny, but don't give him an opportunity to mock.  Clearly  cares about the stuff he teaches and the people in his class.  Smart as a whip, drink your latte before you go in there.  If you want to you'll learn more than in most classes.  Seems like somebody you could hang with after class.
Great teacher.  Very clear and precise.  Very approachable.
Rather biased in opinion and controversial. He certainly captured my interest though.
No Comments

You just have to talk to him and show your interest in the class. He's usually eager to meet with his students, and if you meet with him and you have a question about a paper or test, he will definitely help you out.
class was ok. i am taking his class next term so it wasn't all that bad.  just a little unclear of how the grading is performed
Sense of humor so dry it's hard to percieve.  Gave me an F, the twit.
Awesome professor. Too bad he's stuck with feckless UO students.

This guy is a great professor. Thick accent, but still the most informative and helpful professor I've had here so far. He gave good feedback when asked and is available outside of class almost always. Responds to emails within the hour when awake. Goated man. Only got a grade as low as I did because I showed up to maybe 27/40 lectures. 10/10

Very sweet guy, but not a very good teacher. He has a very thick accent that makes it hard to understand, and he overexplains things. I recognized some topics from AP Calc in high school, but the methods he used were way more complicated than they needed to be, so I essentially taught everything to myself.

prof shen is a very kind person and he definitely cares about his students HOWEVER the class is impossible quite frankly i got As in calc 1 and 2 and i am struggling to pass this class the practice midterms are 100x easier than the actual midterm and lectures are confusing full of proofs you have to be able to teach yourself to take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anyone on here hating on Yefeng is definitely awful at math and expects teachers to do everything for them. Yefeng made Calc 2 easy. Dude is really excited to teach and is also really knowledgable at everything he teaches, and makes challenging concepts such as rotating axis volume integrals easy to understand. Highly recommend him.

The class is easy and is almost impossible to get a bad grade in because so many homeworks and quizzes (and even a midterm) are dropped from the final grade. 

However, The teacher is so bad I stopped going to class after week 2. class is worthless because all he does is read off the slides in an accent so thick its basically mandarin.

Shen has a accent which could make it hard to learn, but is a great explainer overall( good detail). I often dozed off in class and got a B. So if you pay close attention in lecture, you'll for sure get a good grade. Do the homework for points and pay decent attention and you'll be fine.

Terrible. I would not recommend him to any student. STAT243z is supposed to be an intro class to stats, but we jumped into topics like we were supposed to know them already. He seems annoyed when you ask questions and doesn't explain things thoroughly. He mumbles a lot as well, so it is very difficult to understand!!

He gets a point for being a nice guy, but he doesn't logically explain topics or seem to understand the content very well. He has gotten multiple questions wrong on the weekly quizzes and in the lectures. There is also a massive language barrier, and he lacks the vocabulary and pronunciation to explain topics. He makes stats more confusing.

Guy seems like he has no idea how to do statistics, he's gotten problems wrong in class and explains things HORRIBLY. Lectures are in broken english and super disorganized. You will learn more from 5 minutes of youtube than an hour long lecture. Nothing he teaches relates to the homework or quiz's. Do not take this class. You will regret it.
do not take his class

Real nice guy, genuinely cares about helping you pass and is pretty flexible with assignments. He extended deadlines a number of times and removed extremely difficult questions from webwork. The lectures are pretty hard to follow as he is quite disorganized, but he is generous when it comes to grading. Overall not too bad, no complaints.

Yefeng seems like he wants wants to be a good teacher but doesn't know how too. His lectures are extremely disorganized and do not pertain to the weekly quizzes, he also gives very very little time to complete the quizzes. He spends more time rambling and acting confused than he does teaching. If you want to succeed you need YouTube.

I learned the entire course through YouTube. Can't understand his lectures and they didn't pertain to the homework too strongly. His office hours were half in English and halve him talking down to another student in a different language. This class was a nightmare, thank god for the internet.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Shen is very respectful and seems to enjoy teaching, but his lectures are very unclear and disorganized. His lectures consist of 90% proofs in broken English that are unrelated to the homework problems. I learned more from 5 minute YouTube tutorials than I did from attending lectures. That being said, he is a fair grader.

Yefeng is a wonderful person when you go to his office hours but inside the lecture everything was so confusing. He explained how to do one problem but would not teach the process of how to apply it to other problems. The average for one of our midterms was a 58% before the curve and also wont tell you what your class grade is until after final
He just really likes math so if you have any questions he'll be more than happy to answer them, and he actually explains it so you understand and if you don't understand he'll make sure you do

This is the most amazing teacher of all time. He is ridiculously smart and sometimes skips steps because he is so smart. At the beginning of the school year no one thought he knew there name but by the end it was obvious that he knew everyones name. He should be nominated for many math awards. He is by far the most amazing math teacher that I had:)
although he has lots of homework and a little hard,he is wiling to give a high score on your letter grade. you could ask him questions and he would give you a patient guide

Josh is a fantastic professor! He is passionate, caring for his students, and an entertaining lecturer! I even took an 8:00am class that wasn't required, so I could listen to his lecture style. I recommend his classes to everyone I know.  He is truly made to be a teacher and cares for his students.

Great prof. He's passionate about sustainable business, which made the class all the better. There's a fair amount of homework, but still within reason, and it was all informative. The quizzes can be a bit frustrating because he often mixes facts with his own interpretation of the readings, but overall would recommend this class.

He gives u like 3 assignments a day which is absolutely ridiculous and on top of that he grades each of your comments/assignments as if its a final. He needs to be more clear with what he wants from students if hes gonna grade every assignment as if his life depends on it! Dont take this class if you want to have a life outside of school!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: By far the best professor I have had. He is genuinely hilarious and incredibly intelligent. He truly cares about what you learn and constantly engages with students. I would totally recommend taking any of his classes, especially BA 199 . It will make you think differently as a consumer.

This class was unorganized and extremely hard to sit through. He doesn't communicate well with due dates, and barely explains anything. He treats this class like it could be a middle or high school class. This has been my least favorite ed class, and it seems like that is a common pattern among most ed majors/minors
He's a fine professor, class felt useless and repetitive. Claims to be helpful and "for the students" but I did not find this to be true. Overall, if you can avoid it, I would not take this class.

He gets offended when you ask for help despite his awfully confusing grading criteria. It's all over the place during lectures. I tried to come in with an open mind about this professor but have just felt extremely frustrated.

Prof was a super nice person. I wish there was clearer grading criteria (I think our grader was not great) but it was not a challenging class and allowed for redos. He wanted to support and help you wherever you needed it. He takes feedback productively! But sometimes the class felt repetitive.

Maks's did a good job teaching the class. He was good at making sure everyone understood what was going on, and being available for students. He had us work in pairs during class which was helpful. CIS 111 IS NOT EASY! I think he did a good job of explaining things. I enjoyed the bio's as well.  He's definitely improved based on the past reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Completely Unorganized, inflexible, gets offended when you ask for help. Projects are hard as hell and the material as not explained clearly in class. Wastes Class time going on tangents in class and Often forgets to explain information needed for the projects and tests. Not helpful at all during office hours gets offended when you ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had him for CIS 111, and it was overall an okay experience. I found that yes, the class was pretty hard but he was always available for office hours and his GTFs were as well. My biggest pet-peeve with him was that he made his projects so difficult and then often had gave the answers away because he hadn't explained the concepts earlier on.

Absolutely horrible. If you have any background in programming it isn't even worth showing up to class, just treat it as an online class. If you do have the misfortune of needing to go to class you'll have to sit through him talking about his political point of views and his lectures that cover homeworks that have already been finished.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He wastes half of his 50 minute classes talking about useless information like his personal life and repeating "jokes" ad nauseam. He assigns projects for which he hasn't taught much of the material, and gets offended when you ask for help. Your time and money are wasted with him. Avoid if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I have ever had. Literally not worth the effort to wake up and go to class.  Assigns projects and doesn't give the information needed to complete them. Cannot stick to his syllabus. Doesn't have a creative bone in his body just takes projects and slides from another class. Do your self a favor and don't take this class.

Ive taken a few Comp Sci classes and this has been the worst.  Class does not seem useful, though he makes it clear he wants it to be.  Over and over.  Most people stopped showing up.  All of his content is taken from another teacher.  Take the class from him instead.

Lectures are unorganized, repetitive, and often irrelevant to the tests or projects. projects almost exclusively require help from office hours because there are no instructions on how to complete them. The tests are equally unorganized and somewhat unpredictable, made up of almost entirely vague true/false questions that pertain little to lecture.

This guy is the worst! He assigns five projects throughout the term each of them require hours of sitting in office hours, because his lectures and the book do not cover material required for the projects. His midterms are way harder than the class. The class average was a "D" and he still refuses to curve the grade. STAY AWAY!

Super sweet and caring, love her. Some people said they think her lectures are scattered, but I disagree— I followed them pretty easily. The weekly readings are a hit or miss (I vastly prefer her lectures to the readings), but no big essays. I'd always stop by after class and chat with her about the subject of the day.
Middle of the road.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Skowron is extremely fun and truly cares about the students in her class. She brings a lot of personal knowledge and information to the class which is helpful. She also allows you to practice the skills you learn in class on each other in groups. If you attend the lectures and participate in group discussions, you'll have a great time.
Very nice and understanding.

I really wanted to take the developmental psych class and enjoy myself. Skowron made this very hard to do. She requires every chapter you read to have a 1 page assignment (2-4 a week). Lectures were so scattered, has no idea what she is doing. Tests have multiple choice, fill-in the blank, and 10 essay questions. So much work for an elective. NEVER
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is a hard class for sure, but this professor make things easier for students. Slides, notes and practice questions are helpful as well.

Professor Slabin is the most patient  professor I ever met at University of Oregon. He offers extra hours to help students solve problems, and his classes completely and exactly cover the exams he gave. He really cares students. Highly recommend you guys take his classes!

Ulad is a very supportive understanding professor.  Always availalbe to work with me and answer questions.  He has a thick accent, and is a pretty easy going approachable person, some people take that he isn't serious or knowledgeable which is not the case.  He tells you what you need to know, you just have to listen.  He very reasonable!

Because this class is over the summer, it is very intense and fast paced.  In class, the lectures can go by very quickly and cover a lot of material.  I went to Prof. Slabin's office hours often and he always helped me understand the difficult concepts.  He was patient and always available and willing to help.  I highly recommend Prof. Slabin.

Professor Slabin is great! Many people here gave him bad ratings and that is likely because they didn't attend his lecture.  The lectures were perfectly suited for the material on his tests, and if you do the homework/understand it you will do great on the exams.  Also, he has online office hours and is very good at explaining unclear topics.
A Perfect Professor! His class is very helpful, and he is patient and also use skype, youtube and Second Life to help us. I like his class!
Slabin is a great teacher! If you put in the work you will do great! :)

Just a warning to all U of O students who are considering taking a science course during summer term: be prepared to cram 10 weeks work and studying into 4 weeks. I made the mistake of taking the general chem series during the summer and while I aced the labs I failed chem223 along with 60% of the class. There's alot of math involved, but no time.

I guess you kind of have to sympathize with his frustrations. He's been teaching for over 20 years and I'm sure the non-chalant additude of the average american college student is unbecoming compared to his first students in his home country of Belarus. Still I am choosing to avoid professors in the future who speak english as a second language. :)

I loved it when Mr. Slabin became angry when only ten students came to lecture on the final days of class after he had announced that lecture was optional. It was also quite an adventure when students had to constantly correct him on examples during final exam study group. Just so everyone knows: Summer Classes Suck.

Dr.Slabin used the lectures provided by the textbook publisher which featured pictures and phrases right out of the book. For someone like me who reads the entire textbook this turned out to be disasterous. The redundency added to the monotone speeches, broken english and static position through the four hour class put me to sleep almost instantly.

I want to warn people that my opinion of Dr. Slabin may be tainted because I failed (D) his chem223 class but prior to taking his summer series I was a 4.0 student. My ability to learn from Mr. Slabin was complicated firstly by his strong russian accent and secondly by his lectures. I will explain in the next comment.

Since she's only a GTF, it's expected that she's not perfect in her teaching tactics, and can sometimes be unclear. However,I have only had her this term and so far she's been super nice and helpful. She loves it when you participate and really shows that she wants the best for her students. I don't know what these other people are thinking.

Alexandra doesn't have the personality to teach.  Downright rude at tImes. Not appreciative even if you go the extra mile. Just generally comes across as unhappy and wanting to find things wrong instead of focusing on student's efforts and good intentions. Her class was not fun and I love French.  I didn't look forward to going.
Alexandra is friendly, fun and understanding. She explains things very well and is helpful if you have problems in class. The homework is good and the class activities are engaging.

Great professor,  knows what he's talking about (and he should since he got his PhD in Brown). Makes sure students understand the readings. Doesn't go off topic and tries to keep students engaged in conversation. Good at backing up authors' arguments and point he's trying to get across. Interesting class to take, I recommend it.

Great professor! I highly recommend taking his classes. Creates interesting and stimulating conversations, makes sure students understand material before moving to a new topic. Passionate about subjects and really knows his stuff!
Overall I would mostly say slater is organized. His lectures were outlined at the beginning of class. There was little off topic ranting.
Great professor. Really knows a lot about philosophy. Stimulates discussion.

He's a chiller. Good writing teacher who cares about his students and wants the best for them. His lectures kind of get boring sometimes, just cause they're very long, but it's ok that happens with every class. He's not strict on laptops or phones, really, so it's a chill class. Take him if you need writing credit, you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, not a lot of homework just a discussion at the end of the week, Argumentative essay in the middle of the term and research presentation in front of the class at the end. Not too difficult but just have to do research for sources outside of class. Some reading at the beginning of the term.

He is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. Clear instructions, rubric, and feedback. Genuinely cares about his students success and learning. It is evident that he is passionate about what he teaches. If you can take him, please do! Stay on top of readings, assignments, and projects and it will be a smooth ride.

The best man ever truly. He cares so much, he is passionate and just so so sweet. I recommend because how much he cares makes you want to go to class. Not a super hard class, perfect work load tbh. Haven't met someone who doesn't like bennet!
Took some getting used to, and a conversation about what I needed from him, but he warmed up nicely, was a kind guy and made the class enjoyable.

This guy is absolutley awesome PLEASE take him if you get the chance. Had him for WR321, took the class to fufil some requirnments and I am so thankful I did. Makes coming to class fun, assignments can be long but all feel like they actually benefit you. Cannot reccomend this guy enough, best professor I've had at Oregon through three years.
Great dude. Honestly nothing bad to say. Sometimes just went to class to hang out with him. Cool dude and really just wants to make you a better writer, nothing more.
Awesome teacher, probably the best teacher I've had at the UO. A bit homework heavy but he provided a great grading system and had great lectures. highly recommend.
He motivated me so much that I was excited to come to class and write my essays. I am a math major and am only taking this course to graduate, but I would take any class with him as the professor.
This is the best professor I've every had. I wish I had him next term but I don't. Please take his class and laugh at all of his goofy slides and dad jokes. Really smart guy. Thank you, Bennet!

Professor Bennet was such an amazing teacher!!! I can emphasize that enough. He made me think of writing in a whole different way and was just great teaching. really connects with students and cares if you communicate/emailing. two major assignments, an essay and a research project!! if you have to take WR 122 you have to take Professor Bennet!!!!

If you're looking for a teacher for writing credit, especially if you don't care much for english, TAKE BENNET! My favorite teacher I had freshman year. He genuinely cares for his students and only wants us to learn to love English a little more then before. Very easy workload, no busywork. Only a few essays, and provides extensive feedback.

Bennet Smith is by far the best writing professor I have had. He gives great feedback and never talks down to his studnets. He turns seemingly dull lectures about grammer and paragraphs into interesting and engaging discussions. I always felt encouraged to do better after leaving his classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Mr. Smith is probably one of the most amazing writing teachers I've ever had. Genuiley wants you to learn and be good at writing. Wants to work with you to succeed. Forms the class so that you will pass with a good grade if you give effort, yet gives very clear feedback and wants you to be better. Would definitely recommend it.

The class itself was really chill, and wasn't very difficult. And Professor Smith is very enthusiastic about what she teaches, so the lectures were very thorough. Anyways just do the work and listen to what she has to say, and the class will be great.

Every guest speaker that comes in talks about how awesome Hollie is and I fully agree! I'm not in the SOJC myself, but her lectures are so informative and helpful for those looking for a career in some sort of media. If you're into the media careers or if you're in the SOJC, TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!!!!
Professor Smith is great, she's super kind and cares about student careers. The class is really easy and a good foundation for SJOC students. Would recommend!

You can tell Hollie enjoys teaching this course and it makes for lectures that are as engaging as they can be. The course is very much designed for people who want to explore the SOJC, and does a good job at that. There are a lot of guest lecturers, which can be insightful and a good change-of-pace. The coursework itself is very simple and easy.
super light class, mostly graded off of participation and I clickers etc. assignments are quite straight forward and you probably did a version of them in high school.

JCOM101. This class is insanely boring, convinced me to switch my major boring. Hollie doesn't lecture that much because the class is mainly guest speakers who all give the same speech. There is a homework assignment every 2 weeks that is usually relatively easy. Iclicker online is required and is a good portion of the grade. Boring and easy class!
Didn't really listen to her all term, she knows her stuff though. Most of the term is just guest speakers. She's cool but gives off almond mom vibes
Class wasn't the most interesting but had lots of important information. She definitely knows her stuff and wants to share her knowledge. Assignments and tests are super easy.

For an beginner class for Jcom101 it is not bad the downside is when it came the hw some of the assignments took an long time and I had to learn apa style on my own as she had a few assignments using apa. Didn't explain how to use it and I felt when talking to her uncomfortable as the conversations  didn't really bother to build relationships

I took JCOM101 with professor Smith and although her lectures were not the most interesting, the class was really easy. She was always available to help and she laid out the assignments far ahead of time to give us lots of time to prepare. I would recommend this class to anyone.

This course is based around writing a PR publication on a researcher on campus. Holly walks you through the process, and makes it seem way less daunting. She's a wonderful prof. I really enjoyed this course, made super cool connections w/ scientists, and felt super proud of the work I put in by the end of the term

She's super nice & caring! She drops your lowest homework grade (3-4 assignments) as well as your lowest exam grade, so you don't have to take the final if you do well on the midterm! We got the choice of choosing our final project topic & whether we wanted to do a creative piece or paper for it. Overall, super great teacher! 10/10 recommend!

Professor Smith is incredible and did a great job of introducing and explaining media careers. Her class involves many guest speakers, some of which are better than others, but her assignments are very straightforward and engaging. It actually felt like they were worth my time. Highly recommend taking one of her classes!!

Hollie Smith is a great professor. She is kind, understanding, and approachable. The class is easy, though it can be a bit dull due to the focus on guest speakers. Minimal effort is needed to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: i loved professor smith in jcom101! it was my first class in the j-school so i was hesitant, but she exceeded all expectations. you can miss up to 3/4 classes & the homework in her class was actually kinda fun. overall great professor & class.

Awesome professor. Loves what she teaches and is approachable. The entire class is guest speakers and the homework assignments are not difficult. Midterm is incredibly easy, it's an A on a platter. Guest speakers were interesting and had many from different fields of Journalism. Attendance required and you only get 3 absences throughout the term.

Prof Smith is one of the most caring professors I've had at UO. This class was built around writing your own Sci Comm story to be published, so there wasn't any real busy work. Everything felt like a good use of my time and I learned a ton, developed so many good career skills. Highly recommend Prof Smith and this course

Hollie is amazing. It sucks this course is only guest speakers. 4 assignments and 2 exams throughout the term. 1 exam and 1 assignment is dropped at the end, so you do not have to take the final if you do good on midterm. The assignments are usually quizzes that are straight forward on the readings. I would take Hollie for another class if I could
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and understanding professor! She drops one test and one assignment so you don't have to take the final if you score well on the first midterm (which isn't difficult).
Dr Smith is an amazing professor and the class is very laid back.

Super easy class, super understanding professor. She drops one test and one major assignment which takes a lot of stress out of the class. Make sure to do the readings because that's what you'll be quizzed on, not the guest lecturers. Overall, easy class for SOJC majors.
Laid back class, very understanding professor.

Hollie is so amazing and she makes such an easy class so fun. There is guests every week who come lecture so it isn't always her giving out information. She is really sweet and cares about her students success. Without a doubt would have her again.

Prof. Smith always has a smile and is super sweet to all her students. Her class is not difficult at all and this is a very low-stress class. The homework assignments are easy to do and don't take up much time. It's hard not to pass this class with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hollie is probably one of the best profs I've had at UO and I'm a senior so I've had quite a few. She is so kind so you don't feel intimidated to ask her questions. She gives excellent paragraph long feedback on every assignment. She grades very fairly. If you put in the work, she will give you a good grade. Due to COVID class wasn't mandatory too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hollie made this class so fun! It was only 2 credits so pretty easy but we just got to listen to alumni from the SOJC come and talk about their careers and answer questions. There are a few small paper assignments (one page) and overall Hollie is really nice and you learn a lot from listening to the speakers. This class helped me pick my major!

This is the easiest SOJC class you'll ever have to take. Just show up and listen to the lectures from people from all over the work field of PR, advertising, journalism and media studies. You have to write a few questions before each week, and then write a short, easy paper after each week, but that's about it. Hollie was also very sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith is an amazing professor. I was nervous for this class to be online but she structured the class based on student preferences so there were modules instead of weekly Zoom meetings. You work on a PR plan the whole term and Prof. Smith gives amazing feedback and is very accessible to meet with.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Though Caitlin did have a wavery voice, I didn't perceive it as "nervous" -- her lectures were a little boring, but informative and included topical cases. Python is easy and so is stats if you pay attention. Exam looks rough (2 hour mcq) but doable. GEs (besides Nafisul) were helpful and I never felt left behind in this course.

Nervous voice to go along with confusing lectures. Homework, labs, and projects take a couple hours a week if you're not familiar with python. A handful of quizzes and a difficult final. I recommend taking a stats class before you try data science cause it would greatly help your foundation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were not very helpful tbh, but it's clear they were relatively nervous and got better as the term went on. If you already know some python, even just CS 210, this class is a breeze. Homework took me only about an hour a week. Very easy but you're mainly teaching yourself.

The worst professor I have ever had. Should not be employed. Did not understand the content they were teaching. Couldn't talk in front of a class. Can't answer simple questions and just reads straight off a slide. Impossible to get a hold of, never answers emails, and will not be lenient or understanding.

Very bad teacher, do not take a class with them! Only read things off the slides and didn't know anything about the subject! Constantly messed up grading and assignments always had typos or bad instructions.  Very horrible teacher and didn't give back any feedback or help.  Did well because I stopped going to class and taught myself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are so boring. I appreciate the attempt to make them interactive, but it just doesn't really work. If you know a little python or stats, this class is not too hard. If not, you'll have to teach yourself but that's just how CS classes go. HW/labs are most of your grade which is nice, just don't procrastinate. Final is also worth nothing??.
Lectures are super boring and useless.

Insane workload for a 100 level class. Doesn't seem to know much about the material often times lectures are irrelevant. Was left to sort of figure it out on your own. Grading was weird if you didn't do it their way you wouldn't get full credit despite having the correct answer.

She talks really fast and her voice is kind of monotonous, so nothing she says is ever understood. She only reads off the slides which don't actually say anything important, and I have to learn everything outside of class. The quizzes are confusing and include material that isn't covered in class, also there's zero room for error. Do not take her

I feel like im teaching myself python. I don't learn anything in lectures because she goes fast over the hard stuff and slow over the easy stuff. Half of the things on the slides mean nothing. Clearly new to teaching too. 2 asignments a week plus a quiz on stuff she didnt cover every other week
good overall professor
His lectures are very well planned and he's very organized. He is very clear in his explanations. The homework is all online and you get multiple chances to do it. Although his tests are very hard.

Sly's an alright guy, and lectures are pretty well done. But the biggest chunk of the grades, and best chance to do well, is online hw, which he never talks about. Never ties them into lectures, never discusses due dates. I guess this is fair, but it's really not the sign of a good teacher. And can easily cause kids to get unfair grades.

One of my two favorites at the UO, seriously, he is so organized, prepared for class, and he is unbelievably clear. No doubt that if I ever needed extra help that he would be more than willing to talk it through with me. He's awesome, try to take one of his classes!

Awesome teacher. Unbelievably clear... if you pay attention in class! He has all the lecture notes typed out prior, but writes them out in class as to match the students speed. Very funny dude. Econ is not easy, and as a result people have rated him lower. he is a great teacher though.
His office hours are helpful sometimes. His tests were so hard, but homework were all online. I did not like the class and will not recommend it to anyone.
easy class, good at teaching

I didn't like him at all. He made the class harder that it is, he write during the lectures in almost 200 class, with bad & small hand writing, so its hard to keep track of the notes. The exams are unpredictable and hard for Into 201, too much HW loads, I don't recommend him if you have other good option. Rude and unhelpful. Avoid.

Sly is the best teacher I've had at U of O so far! I love that he writes the notes because it makes it easier to follow. The midterm and final are hard but he curves so much and if you do the work and study a decent amount for tests you'll be golden! Sly is actually the coolest

The professor is a good guy.  For being an intro to econ, I have no idea why he makes it harder than it really is.  The midterm and finals are difficult.  If you want an A, you would have to put in a good amount of time to study and know the material.  The homework isn't too bad and it makes up about 40% of the grade.

Sly is awesome. The tests are really hard, but he curves the class to make it fair in the end. He uses creative examples that help to keep the class interesting. Terrible at responding to emails, but he's still a great professor and really easy to understand. Cutest professor I've ever seen, too, so that's a plus.

Sly is an excellent professor. Unlike other professors, during lecture he completes the notes live, as in, handwritten. By doing so he assures that everyone can keep up and the diagrams are clear. Tests are challenging, but he curves the class at the end.

Lectures were not very clear and did not seem to be consistent with the homework assigned. If I had not bought the textbook there is no way I ever would have been able to do the homework. He rarely even gives you the equations you will need to use on the homework assignments.
Nice guy, however, just not that great of a teacher. His lectures were difficult to follow and not that clear.

MAKE SURE YOU GO TO CLASS. class is not mandatory but Sly is SUCH A GOOD PROFESSOR and if you just go to class and listen and take notes it will be very helpful. Homework is easy because you get lots of chances. Tests are really really hard but he does curve it a bit at the end.

Honestly I don't see why people complain about this guy.  ECON 201 was my first economics class in my entire life and he has made it very interesting.  The tests are a little tough but if you study, take notes in class and actually do the homework you're guaranteed to do well.  He answers promptly to emails and always tries to help out.

Horrible professor.  This is an INTRO class, but he says he gives same tests as his 300 level students. Worthless.  The comment below said he curves the grades, so not to worry.  You better worry, because he does NOT curve!  Better yet, drop and take another professor.

I did not like him when I was in his class, but when I attended other econ  classes, I thought he is great. His lectures are clear, and homework is helpful. Although sometimes I do not know what he write, the pictures he draws are so helpful.

Only downside was that he made some of the concepts seem harder than they actually were. However, half of the class was based on homework, so it has to take an effort to fail! I always wanted to go to class on account of how good looking he is. Overall.. Would definitely recommend!

He is one of  the best professors I've had. I took his class because I have to and I had no interest In Econ, now I find it interesting and enjoyable. Homework is 50 % so do it, you get like 9 chances to get it right. Hw is a bit time consuming but very helpful along with going to class. No Friday discussions. I highly recommend him! Plus he's hot!

Energetic guy who keeps his lecture pretty interesting. The homework is really easy and was 50% of the grade which helped out a lot and doesn't take very much time at all, however the midterm and final are pretty damn hard. Be ready to put in a good amount of studying in for those two tests. And you don't use your textbook.
Sly is a cool dude. Very energetic and he makes the class go by smoothly. Uses awesome examples to help clarify subjects. However, his tests are incredibly hard...

Absolute worst professor at the University of Oregon. Doesn't use his blackboard, notes in class are unclear/messy, and was told at the beginning of the course that the tests were the same for his upper division students and that an 'A' grade was unobtainable and that a 66% on the exams were considered good. Work ethic doesn't get you a good grade.

Very helpul and give clear outline of notes. The tests are hard but if you study and pay attention, they are simple. Most of the grade is easy online homework so his class is very easy to pass. Makes econ fun and interesting Highly recommend this guy.

SO energetic in class! He is an amazing professor however, his tests are very difficult. But he openly announces that at the beginning of class. If you work hard and study a lot, the class is not that hard. He also is very willing to help a student understand the information better. He is also soooo good looking!
He is gorgeous. Looks just like Clark Kent (from Superman). Made class relatable and fun!

Good teacher. Used class time very well and used a lot of examples in class lectures in order to make things understandable. Test were a bit hard and studying was a must, but he is very helpful if you need extra help.

One of my favorite teachers so far, 50% of the grade was simply myeconlab homework which is so simple to do.  I also love how hip he his, the glasses, the sweater, and he seems to mention an apple product every class.  He really is a class act.
He will curve your grade at the end of the term. Don't worry

He made his class interesting by providing a lot of examples, but his tests were very difficult. The homework was extremely easy though so it make up for it. He wasn't that helpful when going to his office hours though. Overall, if you put in some effort you should get no less than a B.
I second the comment below mine. I thought the midterms and final were difficult but Sly does a pretty great job of explaining stuff. I thought he was a really high quality lecturer. Take him!

Awesome professor. Assignments on Myeconlab about once a week but they are totally doable if you read the textbook and take notes in class. Although it is easy to get through the homework because of how many time you can do a question, make sure you take the time to learn the material because that's what will earn you an A on the exams.
Good teacher. Somewhat harder than other econ teachers.
Really good teacher, extremely fair exams. If you study, you can get an A. Study for the quizzes and ask questions in discussions and you will do good in the class.
So boring, he goes through his very unorganized notes so fast, he gives good examples. No homework, one midterm one final. His exams are hard. Weekly quizes that are considerably long.
So boring

Good Teacher. Downfall you have to take a lot of notes.Upside no HW. You take weekly quizzes which are not to bad as long as you take notes in class and study a little before each quiz. His midterm and final were medium difficulity but if you study you can easily get a high B or an A

Have to take a LOT of notes, quizzes/exams are somewhat hard if you don't study well, but he uses great, clear, relatable examples that make it easier to understand. Also,  he is extremely good looking so going to class is worthwhile.
Cute,interesting, and he makes up his own ratings on RMP. A triple whammy!

Very basic and straightforward. Makes you take a lot of notes, but quizzes are fair and there is no textbook. Sly keep things interesting by relating economics to his students through different examples. Not to mention, he's pretty easy on the eyes...
Cute and interesting, a double whammy!
No Comments

I have mixed feelings on Dr. Smith. He is smart and knows the content well. However, he is a bit disorganized in terms of grading and doesn't always respond to emails. His grading system on canvas is very confusing and leaves students with more questions than answers. Also a bit inconsistent across grading the ongoing final essay assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First impression was that he didn't know what he was talking about, and that grew to also not knowing how to grade his own assignments. I got confirmation on a revision that the issue was fixed and 'perfect' to include in the final paper and he gave a 0 on that same exact revision no matter him saying it was fixed. Prepare for constant frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: very awkward professor but you can tell he enjoys what he does. uses words that are not synonymous with each other to describe the same thing so it was very hard to understand what he expected for assignments. had an extremely hard time trying to clarify some questions i had. random in class assignments for attendance credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were so boring, still went and listened he had some interesting parts, tests are online during your own time. Final project is easy. Loved this guy.

Snodgrass is very passionate about every topic, but as a business major, it was boring. Only assignments are easy labs, a few online quizzes, and a group presentation + essay. I felt that the group essay was a waste of time and should be converted to an individual one. Easy A without even attending class.

Professor Snodgrass is truly a wonderful teacher. As a freshman this is the first science class I've taken at UO, and it served as a great introduction. FYI the final is a group project, but it's really not bad. Final is the most difficult part, quizzes are super easy. My GE was awesome too, shoutout Mckenzie. :)

the most important part of this class were the labs, talking to peers and GEs made this an easy A. all lectures posted on canvas which make notes easy to take. loved this class and it was super interactive and fun

I would 100% take this class again, for ANTH ive had a hard time in classes and this class was so easy and fun and engaging. small assignments, biweekly quizzes but pretty good if you do the readings. funny in lectures and gives gifts to people who ask questions sometimes
He posts all lectures to canvas ahead of class and the labs are super low-key.

He's so nice and understanding, I've taken two of his classes and they've been great. He does a flipped-lecture format so there are recorded lectures to watch before class and then he goes over them in lecture, which I've liked. He's inclusive and entertaining too

Professor Snodgrass is the best teacher I have had at the university. So far I have taken two classes with him and for both, he has been amazing. He is a very inclusive and understanding teacher and is flexible with deadlines and extensions if needed. He teaches in a way that gives you opportunities to learn the content, not just take a test.

Snodgrass was an amazing professor, he made classes interesting and explained things clearly and thoroughly. You have to watch the lectures on your own time which are about an hour or a little more and the classes are just discussion that aren't mandatory. If you take good notes you'll do great on assignments, lots of extra cred in class if you go.

I took human growth and development (ANTH 369) with Dr.Snodgrass and would 100% take it again. He is very passionate about his work and makes our in-person meetings engaging. There are a few online quizzes and papers you do, which is the bulk of what you're graded on. Honestly, couldn't have asked for a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was great, he lectured in person but also provided recorded lectures on canvas which was great. He curved tests if the mean score was under 80 or so and was super understanding. We did not have a final or midterm, 100% would take him again!
Snodgrass is an amazing professor! His lectures were long but actually super interesting, I would so take another one of his classes.

Snodgrass is awesome and very understanding! Every assignment and test were very easy if you pay attention to lecture videos. He goes over the videos in class and class time is used for discussion and questions. The final was broken down into small parts throughout the course so by the end you were basically done already.

I honestly loved this class and the content was extremely interesting and helpful. This class was based off 4 quizzes that were online, a final group project, and 3 labs. Everything is easy and I honestly didnt spend much time doing the actual class outside of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing class, discussion based not lectures. No exams, but weekly discussion posts. Lecture was amazing because everyone had so much to share and the topics were great! a final essay, participation, discussion posts, and leading class is what your graded on. Prof is so helpful and kind. Classmates were really smart and inspirational. Best class!!!

ANTH 175 with Professor Snodgrass is a great introduction to anthropology as a whole. This year the class was completely online WEB and Prof Snodgrass was so understanding and empathetic towards students. He gave us a group project as the final and canvas quizzes every two weeks- no tests. Also, the lectures are long and important for the quizzes.

Medical Anthropology taught by Prof. Snodgrass is a must take if you are interested in going to any sort of medical field. Slides are posted online, but I always go to class because I enjoy it so much. A few quizzes (open note) and a HARD midterm and final, but if you study a lot you'll do fine. He is the most friendly prof ever. 10/10.

Dr. Snodgrass is fantastic! He's so open and welcoming to discussion, and super interested in our feedback. He organized a study review session where he only took our questions, and there's not a lot of homework. There is one group project and one midterm along with the final, and he gave a fair curve. He's super passionate about the class too.

Liked the professor but the course content was not what I expected. A lot more elementary and review of general biology/anthropology than getting into the specific stuff. I bit disappointed with what I've learned but it was a good class overall and he's a cool guy! He is VERY respectful of answers/questions given by people and loves participation
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Snodgrass is a very good professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches. The lectures do not take attendance, but it is hard to do well on tests if you do not go. That being said this class is very difficult as it is detailed. Studying for midterms and the final is crucial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rachel is not a good instructor. Study guide for the final exam was more like a study suggestion. Very different from the final.
Attendance does not count as attendance points in this class. We need to ask questions to get attendance points. This is unfavorable for those with easy class content and no questions.

Rachel is a great Professor for Math111. She was good with lecture and if something didn't make sense she is easy to ask about it. Her exams were solid with fix-its to gain back some points lost. She is fairly new to teaching and is very understanding. I finished with over 100% in the class and I couldn't have done it with any other Professor.

She clearly has no idea what she's doing, and does not understand a classroom setting. Very childish, disorganized, unprofessional etc. She's sweet, but I felt like I was being babysat more than taught. Also constantly canceled class, sometimes very last minute.

Rachel is a masters student but one of the best math teachers I've ever had. I struggled with math so much throughout high school but I am doing so well in her class due to her great explaining skills, open-minded grading on tests (participation points if she thinks you knew what were doing), extra credit, and long times open for testing.
Unprofessional, anxious, unorganized, doesn't know how to teach, etc.

i took her class a while ago so she was new to teaching, a little frazzled but very caring and sweet will do anything to help you.  Math111 was very easy, obviously with webwork but shes a great way to pass the class.
no comment.
Class itself is not too hard to understand. She is new to teaching and is still getting familiar with how to help other people learn but I was able to get a good grade without an issue.

Amazingly personable for a guy with such massive class size. He's one of those teachers who is actively involved with research and writes his lectures with a focus on that. If you have any interest in the subject you'll get a ton out of it - if not you can probably still pass without too much struggle. Quizzes are multiple choice/open note.

Snodgrass is a good professor who cares about the topics and making sure you understand it, however you have to put in the effort too as it's a difficult course. Take good notes and study for quizzes and tests, and you'll be fine.

Snodgrass is a very respectable teacher. He cares a lot about the topic and it really shows through in his lecture, though I found this class to be pretty hard as a freshmen with no background in the subject. Tests are hard and most of your grade. If your not extremely interested, don't take the class or you will be bored.

Snodgrass is a super enthusiastic professor! You can tell that he is passionate about the subject, and he wants his students to be passionate as well! Lectures include a lot of discussion and they make you think about things you wouldn't of thought about before. Tests are hard, just take the time to study in advance and not cram.

He speaks really conversationally which makes it difficult to know what we'll be tested on, however we have online quizzes every couple of weeks, and if you study those and the online power points, you'll do fine. He's a really nice guy and raised my grade quite a bit at the end of the term.
You have to study A LOT and memorize a lot.
Most approachable teacher I've had. He made the class super interesting and was just all around awesome.

I think that this was an amazing class he did such a good job with keeping it interesting. I would say that it is pretty easy as long as you do all the work and he is really helpful and so are the GTFs.

Dr. Snodgrass did a great job of taking a lot of complex ideas and presenting them in a clear and understandable manner. The class was difficult because it takes a number of concepts you are already familiar with and applies a new perspective. Dr. Snodgrass does a great job of introducing and applying this new perspective in an understandable way.

I really like Snodgrass a lot!  He's a very smart man who is really passionate about teaching and research.  He always knows the answers to random questions asked in class, it's impressive. He's very fair, and his lectures are interesting. This was my first ANTH class, and he made me really excited about the subject. Awesome professor!

Really awesome guy.  One fo the few profs I've had that got excited about lower division classes.  The course material felt repetitive with other anth. major requirements.  But he was constantly sending emails with helpful links to everyone.  Definitely a great prof. who is interested in his students well-being.
Classes have lots of content, a good prof for anth majors or very serious students

PHENOMENAL. Incredible lecturer, crystal-clear explanations, great enthusiasm, incredibly knowledgeable. He's a hard tester but extremely fair and always willing to help you with problems. Highly, highly recommended.
Great teacher, but pretty difficult tests.

I absolutely love Josh. Such a genuine person, so enthusiastic, but not cheesy, and very good at explaining difficult concepts in a simple way. Moves quickly thru lecture, but he also posts all the lecture notes online the night before, which provides you with the opportunity to both read and hear the lecture at the same time. Once again, love him.

I love Josh. He is very enthusiastic about his subject, and excited to see people do well in his class. His courses are generally very difficult, but all you need to do is read over lecture notes, skim the book, and go talk to him in office hours. It does mean a little extra effort on your part, but if you like bioanth, you will love his classes!
There was a lot of info in a little time. Tests had pretty specific information so there is a need to look over your notes carefully and remember dates.
Tests are really fair. Really good guy and very enthusiastic about the subject. Don't need to look through textbook. Posts lecture slides on blackboard before every class.
The class is really hard and not very interesting.

Dr. Snodgrass class is boring... because i didn't want to be in that class. I only took it because of my Fig. He is a GREAT person in general, but his class is a little bit boring. But lecture notes are online, tests are kinda hard, you need to remembeer everything on his lecture slides in order to do well on his tests. he's a awesome person..

This class is truly impossible without a lot of prior knowledge of science. Even if you study a lot, the tests are incomprehensible. I got the impression from my academic advisor that this was an easy science class, but it is anything but. Even if you know the material, the tests are impossible.

he could care less if you understand the material. even if you make the effort and go talk to him in his office. hes only interested in the subject matter he likes, and it all SUCKS! i love anthro and he ruined that!
A clear and well-prepared professor. Definitely suggested for Anthropology. Class is a little difficult, but that simply requires a higher work-ethic.
No Comments

Learned everything on my own. Read the textbook and do flashcards; she is very hard to understand and seems to lack effort when presenting the slides. I was a bit shocked, especially with a course with such complex topics where it could be used in the real world. Instead, it lacks any interest in the financial world.

Professor Wang is a very sweet lady, but she is extremely hard to understand and her lectures consist of just reading off the textbook and not explaining the steps of problems at all. About halfway through the term, I decided I was better off trying to teach myself the material rather than attend class and do outside work during class anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For the love of god do not take a class with her. Can't understand anything

The UO Economics department continues to be a joke. Although very qualified in the field of economics, Professor Wang is hard to understand and blows through material by just reading off the slides that came with the textbook. The tests are very hard while she makes you try memorize 16 different formulas you won't need. Afraid I'm going to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sophie is very intelligent, but not at teaching. Exam prep materials were borderline misleading, with critical typos and did not cover most exam material. Prepare to study directly from slides, and use your own intuition to determine what you will be tested on. Otherwise very friendly but would not recommend this professor for this class.

Dr. Souilmi was extremely unprofessional. There were a number of times I watched her scroll through her phone looking at emails while students were presenting. Her grading system seemed completely arbitrary, and I found her to be quite confrontational in person and over email when discussing grading.

Didn't teach and made students present all the material. She barely seemed to understand it herself and appeared to learn just as much as her students during presentations. Her only qualification is taking the class as a grad student, but she's highly disorganized and unclear on grading. She literally doesn't say anything in class. HORRIBLE prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
For PS 410 MENA Politics
This professor is disorganized, and awful at using the Canvas platform. Class was a waste of time. She put up one week of slides, and then relied on a syllabus that was buried deep into an announcement for people to keep up on readings. Posted final exam details only hours before the last day.

Grading was never consistent and she didn't know when things were assigned. If you ever took PS 111 this is the same class almost identical material but then she wanted 300-level work even though we were getting 100-level content. Instructions were never really clear and her canvas did not have modules making the organization of the course hard.

This class needs to be structured better. The content is relatively easy to understand, but the professor seems not to want to be teaching. The canvas needs to be clearer, and there needs to be more straightforward communication concerning deadlines. She is knowledgeable about the subject but lacks interest in teaching.

Professor doesn't seem prepared to answer peoples questions and does not hold productive conversations about the subject material. Her class seems more focused on being able to regurgitate information rather than actually learning about the material. It seems like she doesn't have enough energy to stand up and even read through her slides.

late to class a lot, got subs instead of canceling class, does not respond to e-mails quickly, stickler on grades which seems silly for an intro to drawing class. I never missed a class and completed every assignment and still got a B+ (89.72%) when I asked about rounding up or completing a little extra credit to get an A she said no.
Sonja is great, super understanding and knowledgable. Class is not too difficult just a few assignments a week nothing too bad. She is a great professor.

Sonja's a great professor, it's clear she's passionate about what she's teaching. Lectures ARE mandatory, and very strict on attendance. GE's grade the Artist Lectures pretty hard, but overall the assignments are easy. Sonja's lectures can come off as boring sometimes, but the content makes it worth it. I recommend taking this course!
She's so boring and hard to pay attention to but its really easy

Professor Dahl is very lenient and honestly the only time you need to show up for lectures is the days when a visiting artist is lecturing as the notes for her lectures are always posted on canvas. The assignments are short and super easy.

This class is very easy. Minimal hw and one very short/easy essay. The lecture slides and artist feature slides are on Canvas, but the artist lectures are not, so you have to show up on those days. I needed another class for my GE requirement, and this was perfect. Little effort is required while still fun and interesting.
Super sweet and understanding teacher, lectures were long but very engaging. Assigns a lot of homework and assignments, it gets a bit tedious but they’re all really easy. Easy A

A lot more homework than expected. Sonja is very organized with super clear instructions and guidelines on Canvas. Everything was accessible online. I never went to class but was still easily able to do homework assignments. She was understanding and allowed late work within a two day period with a small point deduction.

Sonja is a pretty solid professor, although I believe that the class content is difficult to keep interesting. She is a very kind person and clearly tries very hard to keep students engaged and successful. Showing up and doing a bit of reading should earn any student an A+. If you have a tough schedule, this is a solid class option.

Lots of reading assignments and explaining what your feeling is. Sonja is awesome with communication and is willing to accommodate your needs as long as you talk to her. Class can be done hybrid - which i did. Just lots of writing assignments and reflecting about how you feel on artwork. Not my type of class but some art pieces were nice to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really understanding but fair and clearly has a good understanding and passion for the subject. Also has adjusted to the online format really well, and assignments are a little work but they're not hard, they more just want to know your opinions and perceptions.

I took Sonja's class in web format for Fall term 2020. Her teaching style is informative and clear, and you can look forward to the same types of assignments and similar homework loads every week. The extra credit assignment was in place of our regular assignment. Refreshing and inclusive lectures and information. Very cool class.

Kind and passionate about the topics. I dont know a lot about art but I learned a lot from her. Strict about attendance and phones/computers when in-person. Quiz material comes from lectures so be sure to take notes.

Sonja Dahl is the best professor that I had for Art 111 this Spring. If you want to take a fun and creative class with such an amazing teacher, then Art 111 is the class for you. She is very sweet, caring, creative, and the most hardworking person I ever seen. She prepares beautiful and amazing lectures. I highly recommend her!

Professor Dahl is an amazing teacher. She is so caring and understanding of all situations. Granted I took her class online because of COVID but everything was still there. It almost felt like I was in a real class. Lectures were very cool and if you're interested in art I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was boring, seemed easy, but in the end it is only graded by a few things. I got a B+ on my midterm and that was the grade I ended up with, I've checked my canvas and nothing else is graded. Really strange. The short stories are interesting but i would avoid bc it seems like this class could've been an email lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Southworth is so nice! This was an introductory level english class and you could tell she really cared about improving the students ability to analyze articles but the students did not care. We read short stories before each class so it was annoying when people wouldn't read them and be able to participate in discusssion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
There were 3 assignments total on canvas, a 4th was a google doc "discussion board"
GRADES WERE NEVER UPLOADED TO CANVAS. Final grades were submitted only.
Would not take again simply for grading anxiety and disorganization, but I enjoyed Prof Southworth as a person!

This class was a waste of time. Your grade depends on 2 essays, and the instructions for each are pretty vague. Don't bother showing up (unless you enjoy listening to people ramble about the most generic tropes in the text), I promise you won't miss anything. Helen's teaching style is lazy and uninspiring. xoxo

This class really could have been completely online. New readings for every class, have to participate in a google docs, and one major assignment that wasn't even explained that well. I wish I would've taken a different class. The class was twice a week and lasted 80 minutes. Most pointless 80 minutes of my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's the end of the term. I still don't know what grade I've had the whole time because she doesn't use Canvas. This class was a waste of time and money. You can pass it but you won't learn much unfortunately, as she doesn't teach anything worthwhile about the genre or text, just long rambling about random parts of the reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are only 2 papers, no other assignments. I got an A on my first paper with 0 feedback. Then on my 2nd paper idek what grade I got because she doesn't post ANYTHING on canvas but my transcripts say I got a B- in the course. No explanation, no feedback, no comments. Not to mention class is a rambling bore. Never received a B- in a class before

Only 2 essays the whole term. Little to no feedback on both papers. Grade isn't published until the term is over. No use of Canvas. Overall the course is a large discussion of each reading then it is never brought up again. You choose one story for each essay out of the bunch that you read. This structure, or lack thereof, is not for everyone

Unfortunately, you won't know your grade until the end of the term when grades are published. This can make it hard to know what you need to improve on for your next paper. You are only graded by two things: an in class midterm essay and a final essay. Southworth does not use Canvas at all. No powerpoints, modules, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Southworth encourages a environment where students can engage in very open discussion with freedom and possibility of many different interpretations to the same text. Some students dislike the structureless feeling of the course but I enjoy having the opportunity to come up with my own ideas conclusions without being hand held.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Helen Southworth is the queen of my world. She is awesome. So smart. So beautiful. So educated. I actually really love her so much I've had her before and she is so amazing. She lets you talk and talk and talk and she doesn't interrupt like some of these people are saying. She is very encouraging and makes you feel awesome. I love you Helen. XO

The classes were discussion heavy and we only had two assignments the whole term. She takes forever to trade papers. She's nice overall and seems to want to help students, but the classes were disorganized and she didn't guide the discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Southworth was a very caring person. Lots of books to buy for the year and there's little done with them (the last one we talked about for 30 minutes and never brought up again - the book was $25 and not available at the library). Spent a lot of $ on books only to never discuss them. We were graded by 3 assignments (2 papers + final).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, she will kick your butt in English. She grades INCREDIBLY tough, so try and put effort into your papers. That being said, the books she chooses in her classes are great, and I found that if you make an effort to go up to her and re-do your papers, she appreciates the time. :) She just wants you to know how to critically read by the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Southworth no longer teaches in the honors college but just the regulars joes such as myself. I had her for English 208, which is a genre course, a requirement for the English major. We read legit 5 books (autobios) in 10 weeks. Only 2 grades, midterm + final. Spare feedback on either and it appears she's an easy grader but doesn't give A's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I will never take a class with Southworth again. She was so disorganized and dominated every "class" discussion. She was lazy and only had two assignments, the first and second paper. None of the grading criteria was clear, and she was extremely pompous. One of the worst professors I have ever had the misfortune of taking a class with. STAY AWAY!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a fairly easy grader on the final research paper.
