However you read legit a book a week if not more (if you actually do it) and she gives zero feedback on your rough draft of the research paper. It's also super boring and she talks and talks for the entire class even though it's supposed to be a "discussion".
Very helpful, really funny, and kinda hot.

Professor Southworth is great. She led class discussions well, and kept them on track. The books she had us read were well related, and seemed deliberately chosen. Finally, she gave helpful feedback on our papers (if you can read it, that is), and is happy to elaborate if you have questions. She will notice if you haven't read the books.

Professor Southworth knows a lot about the topic and the class was mostly her showing off the books on Virginia Woolf and talking on tangents. That being said, these books gave us an idea of resources we could use for the paper and she was willing to help in any way possible. She is also an extremely easy grader on the final paper.

Southworth's class was my favorite this term; she gets very into the subject and is a positive person.  As a professor, she can be disorganized and go off on tangents, but she means well, is very intelligent, and is friendly and helpful in and out of class.  I highly recommend her classes!

Professor Southworth is very bad at leading a class that should be based around discussion. She interrupts comments with her own elaboration and interpretation that becomes a mini-lecture and by the time she has finished no one else can add to or differ from the point. She attempts to give lectures but is extremely disorganized. She had to be told

She will occasionally fill entire classes with her endless ramblings, which is unfortunate.  Other than that though, she's knowledgeable, insightful, and helpful.  She cares about the students and wants to help them succeed.
Awesome

Hard to give her a bad rating. As long as you do the reading and talk in class (two things I didn't do because the class was too easy) you should be fine. She called me out in class once when I hadn't read, but I probably deserved it. Disregarding my personal grudge over that, she's a good prof.
She is great if you have work ethic, and easy even if you don't.  If you want to learn, just make sure to ask her, because she knows what she is talking about.

Southworth is amazing.  We finished the Odyssey recently and her lectures on the text were great.  The discussions in class were interesting and she is extremely helpful.  I would highly recomend her as a lit professor.
a Virginia Woolf expert -- very knowledgable and fun
No Comments
Professor Southworth is a fantastic teacher. That's all there is to it.

The grading criteria was straightforward: 3 exams (75%, 25% each) and Quiz (25%). The exams were a way more difficult than practice questions and quizzes, but he gave the huge amount of extra credits. Lecture was kinda boring but he seems passionate on teaching students though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can tell he cares about his profession, but we are graded only on tests and quizzes, and the lectures are very heavy. We are only allowed one index card for each exam, which is great, but I think everyone would appreciate a full sheet of paper for a cumulative final exam. I wish he provided more resources to learn the material as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a very nice guy, but myself and a lot of other people struggled with his online class this term. We are only graded on tests and quizzes, and no study guides are provided for the tests because the quizzes are supposed to prepare us. I think his classes are probably a lot better in person, but the online course lacks structure.

Seems super nice and passionate about economics but isn't the best at actually teaching the subject. The test averages were between 50-65 percent so he just inflated everyone's grade. Interesting class but it is overpowered by literally failing everything. There are three tests worth 75 percent of your grade which was also crazy.

Please do not take Econ 202 with Prof Song if you aren't the greatest with economics. Prof Song "doesn't believe in study guides" when your entire grade comprises three exams. His tests don't match the practice quizzes he gives because he "wants students to engage more with the content." It's an online class with hours of lecture—waste of a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely kind guy who wants the best for his students. Curves midterms and the final by a decent margin to benefit the whole class, and keeps students engaged during lectures. Definitely would recommend taking EC202 with him if possible

Solid Profesor. 25% of the grade is weekly quizzes (1 retake), 50% is split between two midterms, and 25% is the final. He gave us 2 extra credit opportunities. Don't buy the textbook.  Discussions are productive and helpful, try not to skip those. The math is simple, but most of the difficulty comes from the graphs so prioritize those to succeed

Super straightforward task. Assigns all the work for the week on Monday. For me, it took about 2-3 hours a week to write down notes and be ready for the weekly quizzes and exams. (All related well to what we were learning about)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super young and nice. He wants you to succeed in this class and multiple times straight up asked students what they need him to do to for us to get a good grade on the exams. He ended up giving us both sides of the note card. There were 4 problem sets throughout the term. However lectures were dull and the final asked overly specific info
Goated professor. Only grades are from exams and quizzes, but he curves exams and gives retakes for quizzes.
Extremely harsh grader. Treats assignments as if they're part of a P.H.D. program. I highly do not recommend them for a GE or Professor.

Professor Miller was one of my favorite professors at UO, and I had them for three classes. They give great feedback on assignments, and overall the classes were very easy. I would definitely take their classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was easily the worst class I have ever taken. Prof Miller assigns ridiculous amounts of work (70-80 pages of reading per week plus lectures plus weekly discussion posts that have to be 500 words, plus the huge project). They are also a really tough grader, super nitpicky about discussion posts. Do NOT take this class. You will regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures did not align with the homework, quizzes, exams, or worksheets. He moves at a very fast pace and often skips over a lot of important steps. Homework was on WebWork and was messy. Often, they were due at 11:59 on Sundays, but other times, he would randomly change the due date to Thursdays or to different time zones and assign more than one.

He is kind and a good person, but his teaching style is hard to follow. He moves quickly, and the daily problems, quizzes, and the second midterm don't match the lectures. He often skips steps, leaving you to figure it out later, which makes learning and performing well difficult.

Let me start off with Prof. Speckman is pretty nice. But other than that, he talks way too fast for a lot of the class to understand. He doesn't slow down to give students the time to understand it, and the weekly quizzes are pretty rough. When asking for help, his advice is usually confusing or he is confused himself. Midterms can tank your grade.
She is very caring but she somtimes gets mad

Luckily, this professor is retired, so this will never be an issue for you. But is important, so that history isn't repeated, that we remember the horrors. I feel like she would have been the weird, old neighbor that invites you over to give you cookies, but when you grow up you realize that she was actually very weird.

This class requires interest, dedication, and hard work. Write on the lecture slides provided and use the book for extra help. Office hours are golden, if you don't understand something, speak up! Ask questions. Use the practice tests. Practice and work hard and this class will change the way you perceive the world and your own body! So COOL!

This course is set-up for people who have a rudimentary understanding of Bio, AP bio level is sufficient, and it is very lecture intensive.  Print out her slides and annotate them during class. Go to office hours. Karen truly cares about educating so if you are struggling seek out her help and you'll do just fine on the exams.
Worse professor at UO. Terrible lectures, ridiculous exams. Avoid, avoid, avoid!

Don't learn just memorize. Memorize the practice problems. Topics are not covered in lecture. The problem with the lab is how it is written, if they would just please use a published resource for the sake of making the labs clear. "This is an honors course" is not an excuse for the lack of instruction for this class. Horrible.

Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible Terrible class. Learned nothing from lectures and information from assigned reading does not match information in lectures. Labs are pointless and inconsistent with what was thought in lecture. Every part of the class was disorganized.  AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS.

Lectures only cover the very basic definitions of the current topic. No examples done in class, no relevant textbook used. The resource for this class is purely a set of problems sets with answers lacking clear explanations.
Worst professor at the University. Condescending, elitist, and only cares about the top students. Should have retired years ago.

This is a tough class. It is at most all schools. If you dont care much about bio and dont have to take it, dont. That said, Karen is a great teacher and youll learn a lot. The lectures cover the basics but the problem sets are the key. Go to office hours for those. She is clear and very helpful, just make the time and you'll be fine.

Tests (most of class grade) do not reflect lectures.  Text is too advanced for 200 level course.  Expectations of sophomore level biology far too high.  You're better off taking 211, you'll learn something and actually pass.

She's a really nice person, but she only teaches the conceptual stuff, and ALL she tests on is calculations. The average on the last midterm was 56%, which clearly shows that the majority of her students DO NOT get the material she's testing on. I HIGHLY recommend taking the 211 series over this one. She's one of the worst teachers I've ever had.

You can learn a tremendous amount from Karen and do well in this class - but not just by taking notes in class and reading the text.  You have to do the optional homework, do the practice exams she gives you, get all frustrated (which you will), then go in to office hours and get your questions sorted out.  Meeting this challenge is very rewarding.

I enjoyed biology until her class. She was unhelpful when students asked questions.  The book was useless because her lectures did not connect.  Her tests were insanely hard.  The average on the final was 99/200.

I can't say anything that hasn't already been said. The class was extremely disorganized, lectures were useless and exams contained hardly any of the information from lecture. TAs were not knowledgeable and the whole experience was frighteningly difficult and unsatisfying. AVOID
The absolute worst professor at the University of Oregon. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!
By far the worst professor I have ever had. Tests contain info from "optional" assignments. The final had nothing to do with the class. Highest score in class: 164/200...no curve...AVOID AT ALL COSTS

She was possiably the worst teacher I have ever had. Made me want to switch majors..She couldnt answer relavent questions, her office hours didnt help, and her test prep sessions were a waste of time. AVOID

No class is impossible. The material is very interesting and Karen is a kind women and good lecturer. Tests are insane and BI251 is much, much harder than Organic Chemistry, though. If you are going to take this class and expect an A, be prepared to study hard and goto office hours weekly. Sometimes it did seem like the entire teaching staff was in

Avoid. Demonstrates no knowledge of course material, is Unable to derive calculations. Tests do not reflect lecture. In fact, GTF's and TA's are more helpful than her. She finds answers by "assuming", yeah very scientific Sprague
Avoid
No Comments
karen is impossibly hard! the tests were way too hard and detailed for the amount of information covered in the class. not to mention the class was extremely boring.
Karen is very patient, knowledgeable, and nice.  I thought she was an unusually good teacher although her tests were very difficult.  The final was absolutely impossible-expect a low class average.

He ran workshops very well, allowing the class to get to work on the parts of each-others' stories that we wanted to talk about, and giving good, specific feedback about what can be addedremovedchanged. Not much patience for students coming to class without having done readings, but the readings he assigns are worth reading in the first place.
I can not imagine how this guy can teach university class. He said:"I was trained, and I know how to grade you." Very hard to get 80% or above. Always knock you down.

He is very challenging in class, but has a mightier than thou attitude. HE expects you to know everything and if you don't then he makes you feel terrible about what you just said. He grades paper like you're in grad school. I like the class because it is challenging, but it sucks that he grades to hard.
Extremely cool guy. Very analytical and challenging.

I took sex, drugs, thinking, and neuropsych with sparks. Absolutely an amazing instructor. My favorite at the UofO hands down. He makes lecture interesting and he is straight hilarious. I look forward to his classes and made sure I took every class he taught. His test are difficult but he goes through a lot of information and goes beyond. Take him

I agree that his lecture powerpoints are vague and the tests very specific.  I also agree he doesn't email back and too tough as an elective.  The information presented was pretty boring. He has a monotone voice. I hated this class pretty much and it is disappointing he teaches the sex class.

His tests were impossible! I studied for 2 days straight and still only got a 76% on the tests. The questions were worded terrible. Sometimes his test questions contradicted the book. Very frustrating. Lectures were interesting.

Amazing person, great teacher, and just a great guy to have a conversation with! His Human Sexuality class is quite difficult and students are required to understand the material very well prior to exams. No course pre reqs - very difficult class for an elective, but interesting and informative nonetheless. It's upper div psych, what'd you expect?

His lectures are extremely interesting. He talks the whole time with an outline on the projector. He loves to philosophically explain abstract talks and is very passionate. His tests though are very difficult. If you go in and talk to him though, you will be better prepared for the exams.

The subject of this class was very interesting, and he kept the lectures interesting during class. However, his exams were impossible to prepare for and were way too difficult for an elective class. He can also be rude toward students' questions at times. I wouldn't recommend taking him if you have other options.

For the quizzes you had to understand the material 110% backwards and forward. Exams were horrible! Multiple choice but poorly worded almost as if to make the question harder. Class will be graded on a curve, but I'm glad I changed it to P/NP. Usually a good professor, but this term this class way to difficult for an elective.

I enjoyed his lectures, but the class in general was very vague. He would give lectures on broad topics, and expect us to know the specifics on exams. Quizzes and exams were very difficult, and the questions were often poorly worded.

Dr Sparks is a clear teacher and a good lecturer, however he will NOT email you back. You have to go into office hours if you ever want to communicate with him. Over all he's a good, interesting and not very hard teacher who I would recommend. I've taken multiple psych classes with him.

Covers very vague and broad topics in class which are interesting but not helpful for the very specific exams. Spent a 90 min session covering the basics of the scientific method when we needed to be studying higher level topics. Grading is very harsh, he doesn't explain what he wants for the essay portion on the exams.

Nice guy but one of the worst professors I've ever had...Very enthusiastic about the topics but almost too enthusiastic.  He assumes students know a lot more than they do and gets off topic very easily.  You never know what information might be tested on.  Lecture notes are very vague (along with study guides) and specific test questions

Nice guy, horrid prof. repeated the same info to boredom, vague lecture info but very specific exam questions. Didn't get grading done quickly and getting hold of him to talk to him is a task. Avoiding classes he teaches in the future.

This class was SO interesting. Learned a ton and didn't mind going to the lectures because he is such a great professor. Really good lectures and interesting topics. Allowed for a lot of in class discussion and helpful dialogue, tests were easy!

This class was super interesting!! His lectures are entertaining and his slide shows are even better. He is a great professor and I went to every single class just because I got a kick out of listening to him talk. He is clearly very knowledgable and passionate about Psychology!
Really funny, slacks a little on putting things up on blackboard, like grades and study guides. Tests are not too bad as long as you read the text. Gets off topic a lot but class is entertaining!
Incredibly interesting lectures, uses stories to enhance material. Super knowledgeable in field. Quite possibly my favorite prof I've had.
Awesome professor, makes class very interesting, uses good examples, funny, and tests aren't too hard.

Spence is a HORRIBLE History Professor. He is smart, but is a horrible lecturer. His lectures do not link to the text we are reading what so ever, and he is hard to follow. He also brings personal opinions into lecture as well and I found that very unprofessional.

Probably the worst professor I've had so far. He's a pretty smart guy but he has no idea how to instruct a class and teach. He just gives his opinions and really doesn't teach that much. His coursework throughout is unorthodox also and very unusual compared to other history courses. Avoid if possible.
EXTREMELY HARD CLASS! I had to work really hard and study a lot. Also theres a lot of online and text book readings

Spence is a knowledgable source, and a terrible instructor. Instead of teaching the Historical events, he gives us his personal interpretation and emphasizes only his personal interests, leaving the class unlearned in basic history.
This teacher ate all my skittles and gave me a robot!
Nice teacher but very hard on essays.
Grades very hard on essays. I am sure you could find someone easier for this ridiculous class.

Awesome teacher. She is very helpful and wants students to be interested in what they are learning. She lets you pick the topics for every discussion and essay you write through out the course. I would recommend her to anyone!
One of the best math teachers I ever had. Very clear and easy with what comes on the quizzes/tests. Take him if you can.

He is a ok teacher, but sometimes he gets off topic. He also messes up at least a few times a class, which can be frustrating when you are coping his notes. But overall he is a good teacher that knows the subject well.

He is very helpful and VERY easy. His tests are straight from lecture with very few surprises. Homework is assigned once a week and a large portion of your grade. Few quizzes and 5% participation. I would strongly recommend taking a class from him if possible.
Awesome!And very fun guy.

Great teacher. Very clear and helpful on homework, quizzes, and tests. Beware though.. his humor is sometimes hard to read. Overall, a good class. Takes a lot of time and effort but he makes it do-able. RECOMMENDED
Enjoyed going to his class. Found him to be friendly and helpful. Would take a class from him again.
David is hilarious! It's pretty entertaining to have his class at 8am. His exams are pretty easy as long as you do the homework. He also has an interesting "philosophy" about teaching.

Professor Sneed is a nice guy, but not a great professor. He makes tons of mistakes both during lecture and on the documents he uploads to canvas which makes it very hard to learn from him. He also never replies to any emails you send him, so don't bother.

There is little to no communication, the Canvas is very disorganized and not kept up to date, making it very frustrating to be in his online class. He won't respond to emails alerting him of issues, won't provide any outside help, or take accountability for messing up. I'd advise against taking his class if possible.
He rarely answers emails.

Professor Sneed for 352 was not bad I will be so honest. The 1st half of the class was completely fine (bonds, leases, pensions) but the second half (tax liabilities and equity) is where it felt very disorganized for me due to his cancelled classes for personal reasons. Watch the Panopto videos posted for the second half. Overall, decent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely a nice guy, sometimes the lectures can feel a bit disorganized because of mistakes made, time spent retrospectively correcting them, followed by the remainder of the lecture moving at a faster pace to catch up, but for me I found his uploaded videos on the topic to be really beneficial for review for anything I may of missed in class.

had a decent experience taking his async 211. lectures were very informative. homework was a bit tedious but fine. lots of study materials. tests were tricky but manageable. good curve for overall grade. however, canvas was disorganized. didn't respond to a few emails. all in all a mixed experience but would take again.

This is the third accounting class I have taken with Sneed. He is a really nice guy, who definitely cares about his students. However, the only way to pass his classes are to teach yourself all the material outside of class. Going to lecture isn't very beneficial, but he does provide a lot of study material that I would use along with his slides.

Joel is the most disorganized teacher I have ever had in my life and he moves so fast during lectures that its nearly impossible to keep up. He also does not set you up for success on exams whatsoever. If you are studying for his tests do NOT use the long answer exam prep questions, they do not show up on the test at all. Just use class notes.

Prof Sneed is a great guy, but his lectures are very confusing/he makes mistakes a lot of mistakes. I found teaching myself the material and watching the videos posted to be more helpful. Quizzes are very hard, exams aren't as bad but still difficult. He's always willing to answer questions, but get ready to put in a lot of work outside of class.

The most unorganized, incompetent professor I've ever dealt with. Avoid if possible. Doesn't know his own lectures, makes 5-10 mistakes per class that students have to call him out on. Learn the material on your own before class, and use class time as review - if you come to class expecting to learn the chapter, you will be lost.

Beat the curve, remember this is a gatekeeper class to the upper division accounting major. I recommend studying cash flows, receivables, and FIFO LIFO changes. Midterm was easier than the final, the final has receivables and a lot of people struggle with those. Watch his Panopto videos and go through problems listed in the videos, it will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inaccessible outside of class, completely disorganized course online during the summer, total lack of clarity in assignments, tests, and the overall course. The online lectures were pretty thorough, though, but that's about it.

This course makes no sense. There are so many ghost links. The assignments are posted randomly and without lecture. Throughout my academic career I've taken nothing but AP and accelerated courses. I have never encountered a course as horrific as this one. No organization, absurdly difficult homework that takes 2-4 hours per assignment (by design).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful professor. Lectures are impossible to follow due to the constant mistakes and unorganization. He gives 0 time to practice the problems in class. He makes the exams so hard that most of the class fails and then curves the class 10%. Does not respond to emails or follow through on promises. He claims to be average but he is way below average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's Terrible, took this class online and it has been the worst experience. He's unreachable, doesn't respond to emails, and didn't even publish the office hour link, theres literally no way of reaching him. He doesn't bother trying to prepare you for tests. DON'T take this class with Professor Sneed your better off being taught by a 2 year old.

I took this class in person last term but dropped mid-term. It felt much easier and the homework was lighter. The online version feels unstructured, little communication, not responsive to emails, unclear grades, and study guides that don't match the tests. I've felt lost most of the time. I'd recommend a different teacher or in-person option.

Worst class management, consistent mistakes in grading, Uploaded practice test day of test 5 minutes before the exam at 8am. Dude is learning with the students at the same time. Homework contains material that were not taught at all in class and no resources. Long midterm. He is confused while teaching which leads to students being confused.

He is a very nice person and is passionate about his job. That being said, he is not good at teaching a class. He just goes through practice problems without explaining the concepts being used. Unless you already have a firm knowledge of the subject or are willing to spend time to teach yourself the course, do not take his class.

I took Joel's class, and overall, it was a good experience. While he can sometimes be slow to reply to emails and a bit disorganized, he always makes time to meet with students in person and assist them with personal issues one-on-one. I liked Mr. Sneed; he was very flexible about scheduling exams on days that worked better for me.

I actually really like the guy. He's funny, but as a teacher he's super disorganized. When we go over practice problems he doesn't even give you a chance to read the problem or try to attempt it. He basically just does all the work and then is like, "You guys understand right?" Also does math wrong way to often for being a teacher. Try to avoid
Absolutely no help or communication, which is super needed from an online class. Homeworks are insane busy work
This teacher is awful. Taking async class, yet constantly getting announcements for the in person version. Sent multiple emails early in term and have yet to hear back. Avoid, avoid, avoid..

Sneed struggles with his organizational skills a lot. If you can get over the disorganization of the canvas page and inconsistency with posting of homework / practice problems, then Sneed is a good teacher. He knows the material well is passionate and cares about students, however this can't overcome how bad his organizational skills are.

I love Joel, as a person, friend, mentor, he truly is one of a kind. Yes, during his lectures he will get problems wrong and go on the occasional tangent. But he always comes with high energy and a willingness to teach. He is always open for criticism or to explain topics. Show up, go talk to him, you will do just fine. Seriously great guy.
Tough class, but the curves help. Lectures are messy, but office hours are useful. Definitely attend class - Unstuck study was a lifesaver for practice problems.

Terrible communicator and will barely respond to emails. Luckily, my GE would respond to emails super quickly. I would say go to lectures, but they aren't super helpful since he doesn't teach concepts well. For every midterm, I had to teach myself everything, but he has GREAT practice materials available, which is a plus.

Lectures weren't mandatory, but labs were. I was able to teach myself most of the content (because I was too lazy to go to class half the time) but following along with examples during lectures definitely did help. It's accounting, so it's an awful class, but I don't think Joel was as bad as people are saying.

I am sure that he is a very nice guy, but honestly makes the class way harder than it needs to be. His class is HEAVY on showing up to lectures, but the lectures aren't even super useful. He does provide study material, but you are basically teaching yourself all the material. Look at other options, IMO.

NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS. Lectures are him going through problems the entire time, not once does he teach. The homework's fine, but he's a tough grader on midterms, which are so different from what he goes through in class. Don't waste your time trying to contact him either, he never answers emails and doesn't even show up for his own office hours.
do not take joel sneed. trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assignments are lengthy and there are a lot of them. Way too much busy work

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! His lectures are so unorganized as is all of the content, he goes ghost if you try to email him for clarification, is inaccessible for office hours so you have zero help, and the tests are very difficult because they're proctored in person in the library for 2 hours. Worst 8 weeks of my life!!!!!!!!!!!

Sneed was perfect for the first part of the term because the material was more math-based. So all he does is walk you through steps with examples and it's fairly easy. After the Midterm the class gets tougher because it's more concept-heavy and he struggles to teach it. Overall he's not a bad teacher, but he has a unique teaching style.
Couldn't assign more work if he wanted to. Bad educator, smart guy.

Horrible. His lectures make no sense. He would constantly contradict himself and you would need to call him out on his problem process for him to do it in a way that would actual work. Nothing he did in the class prepared me for the test and if you pursued him for out of class help it would actively make you more confused then when you started.

Worst professor I've ever had at UO. Don't bother emailing him, I emailed him SEVERAL times and never received a response. Expects you to grasp the material and follow along and makes constant mistakes during lecture. Half the stuff on the midterms isn't even what he explained, looks like a dollar store John Malkovich.
Pretty hard class but curves on the test are nice. Helpful in office hours, but you definately dont want to miss a lecture in this class, even though attendance doesn't count towards the grade.

ACGT 352
Lectures are long and he tries to teach, but once we move to examples there are constant mistakes being made whether its calculations or wrong numbers being written. You could see the confusion on everyone's face because a lot of us didn't know what was going on. The only beneift was how much he curved the course.

Simply awful. He never taught the class, and would instead just do problems in front of us and expected us to absorb the material via osmosis. I once emailed him about a scheduling issue I had, and never heard back from him. Hands down the worst professor I had in my time at UO. I would say avoid him, but there was no other option when I registered

He can't teach. He is a great accountant but he doesn't explain stuff that help people learn accounting. He takes forever to respond to my emails, he doesn't give us time in class to do practice problems, he just goes over them and expects us to remember. I could write a 5-page essay and name it "How Not to Teach, a Letter to Incoming Professors."
Bro cannot teach to save his life. He messed up so many times in class and was so hard to follow
Unreachable when it mattered most for the class. Course work is fine but him being unresponsive really affected my experience with the class.

even asynchronously his recorded lectures were dogshit, watered down regurgitations of the textbook (doesnt state things plainly, b4 examples).also the syllabus module where he talked about the class he filmed while shirtless on a beach in Greece. Take the class but i advise you only use the textbook for everything and dont even bother w/ his vids.
Tests are incredibly difficult and his lectures are basically just him messing up example problems. Class has a pretty nice curve to it though.

Joel Sneed seemed extremely full of himself, while making a lot of mistakes during his own lectures. Everything he told the class was inconsistent, and he seems to think someone's stupid for asking for clarification. If you want to attempt to enjoy managerial accounting, choose another professor.
He is very bad with technology. Also, he made students have to print out the slideshows before class. Most of his lectures involve just going over practice problems with very limited actual teaching.

One of toughest classes at UO, and I reccomend taking this class immediately following 211. Definately a class where you can't miss a lecture or you will fall behind, so dont miss class, despite attendance not being mandatory. There is a curb at the end of the class, and most of the grade is test scores.

Professor Sneed seemed like a nice guy but his lectures were difficult to follow as he didn't use Powerpoint ever and instead relied on using pieces of paper to solve problems in front of the class. All term he claimed there would be a curve at the end of the course but there was not. Lectures are long and painful as he makes errors throughout.

While Professor Sneed is a nice enough guy, his lectures are abysmal. The material itself is not terribly difficult, but I've taken Biochem classes that were less confusing than his lectures. When corrected on the excessive mistakes he makes, he sometimes becomes borderline rude. I have a 99% in the class & still would warn others to not take him.

Joel Sneed is a very caring guy but he is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He does not help you understand the material, he only ever goes over worksheets and is constantly making mistakes. Students have to constantly correct him on mistakes he makes (every single lecture) and it makes it very difficult to learn. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Joel gets a lot of hate, which is not always valid. He definitely goes very fast and the lecture is basically just practice problems, but he does care and wants you to learn. If you go to lecture and work hard the class is very manageable. I liked him, I would 100% take another accounting class if he was teaching it.

Joel is a nice person but is not a good professor and I have no idea how he has such a good rating. All he does the whole "lecture" is go over practice questions, he goes wayyy too fast and he is constantly getting the answers wrong, students are also always correcting him on these problems. Do not take his class if there is another option!!

I honestly didn't take this class but my boy has had joel sneed for 3 terms now and I have seen it take a tremendous toll on his mental health. He has barely gotten out of bed or showered in 6 weeks and he now walks around the house mumbling under his breath "joeeeel sneeeeed". BEWARE OF THE TALE OF JOEL SNEED
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is confusing, makes many mistakes in class. Concepts in class are not explained well. He goes straight into examples without explaining where numbers come from / why. hard to follow along. Must have full attention in class. You must teach yourself the concepts, not very straight forward in class. Avoid this professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but an awful professor. Constantly makes mistakes and doesn't know what he's doing. Very confusing teaching style. You're going to have to teach yourself the material. Absolutely sign up for class encore for this course, it will save you.

Sneed means well but his teaching is confusing and wrong a lot of the time too. He doesn't lecture the material and give formulas, he just starts doing problems in pencil and draws arrows to numbers but makes some mistakes. He's a funny and nice guy but you basically have to teach yourself because his teaching makes the material harder than it is.

No clue how his rating is this high. All he does is solve problems in class on the projector, and it's clear that he hasn't gone over any of them, as he makes mistakes and gets corrected by students multiple times per class. Seems like he tries to trick you on tests, as it's nothing like the practice material. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM.
Bad. Very bad.

Joel was a great professor. Class is pretty hard, and you can't really miss lectures. Mr. sneed is a really nice guy outside of class. Not too much homework at all, and attendance is not counted. Big tests though

Prof Sneed is a good professor, and teaches a good class. The material is hard, so if you miss a lecture, you can easily fall behind. Really funny guy in class, and always available for office hours and lending a hand. Tough class, so make sure you don't miss the lectures.

Professor Sneed has such a messy way of teaching. He also gives so much workload due in a little amount of time. You would have to listen very hard in order to grab some sort of idea on what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Joel is a good lecturer, and is always willing to help. Willing doesn't mean capable though; his "help" is encouragement at its best. The quality of materials is awful, everything that is explained to you is what has to be done, but not how it works and why it happens.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At first, I think his teaching style is confusing to a lot of people. But, give it some time. If you pay attention and come to class, you will come to realize that Professor Sneed is very helpful on exams and homework. The work that you do in class is very similar to exams. Also, he is very helpful in office hours. Would highly recommend his class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Joel really cares about his student's success and you can see that demonstrated in his videos posted online. Definitely recommend seeing him during office hours as you're guaranteed a helpful response to all inquires--as he can be slow on email responses. This is a hard class, but that's expected due to its necessity to the major.
He's willing to help if you go to his office hours. Course is fairly difficult since it's a gatekeeper for the accounting major.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Joel Sneed was a great professor. He always did so many example problems in class which is something I wish more professors would do. It's clear that he cares about his students success. He was always happy to help when I would go in for office hours and wanted to make sure you fully understood the material. His tests were challenging but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking his class! I took his class online, and the class structure was perfectly organized and easy to follow along with. He was always very approachable and helpful with accommodating with my test-taking schedule. He offered me solid career advice, and is one of my favorite professors because he helped me excel in a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Joel is a really nice man. However, his communication skills were remarkably poor in my experience, not once responding to an email I sent him. His lectures are fine, but the material is dense and difficult, and if you lose him at any point you likely won't be able to tune back into the lecture. Rely on your own time to study, with others if u can.
Joel is not a great professor. He made tons of errors in class, didn't understand what he was teaching, and had errors on test problems. Avoid this class if you can.
A great introduction to the intermediate sequence. A lot of studying is required, but Joel really wants to do best by his students and welcomes any and all questions we have, especially before exams.

He's very knowledgeable about accounting, but seems to talk to students like they're all 3rd year accounting majors. "This is really simple stuff" was said a lot when students were frustrated. His notes were easy to follow, but he makes frequent small mistakes which can derail the entire class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He don't even know what is the grading rule for the work. Time arrangement is poor. Heavy work. No feedback before test. Poor test design.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Joel is very accommodating, midway through the term he wanted everyone to give him feedback on what he could do to improve. He's also very helpful in office hours. It's a difficult class, but he's very lenient with giving partial credit on everything, and I learned a ton in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Joel's teaching style. He works through problems in class which keeps me engaged. He's energetic and caring and while the class is very challenging he try's to make things understandable and applied.

Avoid this class if you can. Joel is an extremely nice person, but this class is the most frustrating one I've ever taken. You'll need to be able to teach yourself the material, the lectures and homework definitely don't prepare you for the tests. The curve ended up being an entire letter grade since everyone in the class did so horrible.

Joel means well but is very confusing in his lectures which is not helpful in such a difficult class. The class was curved almost 10% at the end of the terms so don't freak out if you don't do good on the tests. The class is definitely designed to weed out people who plan on being accounting students.

He utilized the online Connect program which was extremely helpful.  HW done online, except first 3 also handed in.  He knows what he's talking about.  Prepares you for exams and reviews every quiz and exam after.  You learn a lot and he cares about his students being successful!  I'll take classes from him anytime I can.

Professor Sneed is one of my favorite professors that I've had this year. He's really helpful and tends to give to a lot of worksheets to help you actually practice what you've learned. My class generally had a somewhat higher average on the midterms and I scored above average on the tests. Definitely take Professor Sneed if you can!
Very nice and easy to understand

The best accounting professor I have had at the university. He is easy to understand and actually cares about the material and the students. It's not the easiest class ever, but he makes it clear what students need to do in order to be successful.

Joel makes consistent mistakes during class. If it was occasionally it would not be an issue, but it is so frequent that often mistakes were not realized until days later after the process had already been made confusing. I had difficulty following when every few minutes we had to jump back to correct errors.

His teaching style is unique. His powerpoint/lectures are not very helpful because he just talks the entire time and does not really engage the class. He also always talks about examples and stories from his life that aren't really relevant and  shows that he's a little bit of a know it all. He also makes many mistakes during class examples.
He is a funny and helpful instructor. Love his classes.

Sneed's an overall alright professor. I wouldn't say he's amazing because he certainly doesn't go out of his way to help out, but he's also alright at explaining the material. He fills in the notes handouts as he goes, so it is easy to follow along. All the exams for all ACTG 211 classes were the same, made by one accounting professor.

Joel knows a lot and goes a little fast in lectures. He gives practice exams before every test and if you do those and know how to do them you will get a B or better in the class. Like all accounting classes, your grade really depends on the effort you put in.

Read the text in advance like he actually assigns and you'll be fine. He goes through his lectures with you with pen and paper so he messes up sometimes but don't worry about that. He is just trying to vibe with you and relate.

Professor Sneed genuinely cares about his students. His lectures can be fast paced, but he is more than willing to answer questions. He is extremely accessible to students and I highly recommend using his office hours.

Though I got a good grade in this class, I still dont like him. His class is extremely unorganized and chaotic. I almost forget everything in this class after the final exam. Not suggest to take his course.

Joel is a great guy and is honest. His tests are very straight forward. People who use the excuse about him being messy need to grow up. His class is easy if you try just like any class. Don't be upset with results you don't get from effort you don't give.
Extremely unorganized and makes countless errors on notes and homework assignments. Very frustrating class.

I’ve never been more frustrated and confused while sitting in a UO class. Sneed used math not taught on Earth. He would round monetary values and give wrong answers. It’s unacceptable that a professor, who is a CPA and has a Ph.D, got so much wrong in class. I would recommend finding a different university that hires competent ACTG 213 professors.

Sneed is a boos, he pretty much wings these classes because you can tell the accounting is so elementary to him at this level. He makes a lot of little math mistakes that the class has to correct him on, but he definitely knows his stuff. Recommend taking him for any actg class

Joel can be extremely confusing sometimes because he makes a good amount of mistakes, or at least he did in my class. It is hard to catch on sometimes because accounting is all numbers. however, joel is very understanding/nice and ended up curving my grade a lot at the end because i told him i needed a certain grade to get into the business school

Great guy, although a little bit unorganized. Everything you need to know for the tests he teaches you through lecture and doing examples. Take Good notes and practice all the time, way more than you think is needed even, and you will be surprised at how well you will do. That is how straight forward his class was.

Prof. Sneed teaches everything himself through lectures and  examples and he then he tests you on that information; which is great. My only critique is that he can be a little all over the place at times. Take GOOD notes and practice, practice, practice and you will do well.

Joel is an amazing teacher, but his style is definitely unique. Come prepared to think quickly and learn through examples, not to blindly copy down PowerPoint slides. He's fun, fair, and very honest/frank about everything, which can be hilarious.

The class was completely unorganized and unstructured, as were his notes. Purchasing the book was a complete waste of time, as it was never used. Very poor at returning e-mails, and the syllabus used was one from a completely different term with different dates. Overall it was an extremely frustrating experience to be in this class.

Good teacher. Teaches through examples in class. If you practice the examples he gives you over and over you will do well on exams! I didn't once use the actg. book... definitely don't need it. Would highly recommend taking actg 213 with Joel.
He realizes he makes mistakes and then he fixes them anyway. It is a good idea to read the book along with attending lectures to fully understand the topics in this course.

Joel is one of the best professors I've had so far. He is very straight forward with his expectations of the class but that just motivates students to work hard. He teaches by doing a ton of example problems in class. I never even touched the book! He moves pretty fast though, so be prepared to go to office hours. Very approachable. Love him!

He brings handouts to all the classes which makes taking helpful notes really easy. Tells you what to study for tests, and posts a lot of practice exams on blackboard. Homework is based on completion for the most part. If you go to class and pay attention you should do pretty well in the class.

Great guy, pretty good teacher. He is very funny and approachable and clearly a family man, but pretty disorganized. I loved that he brought handouts to class and he pretty much tells you exactly what will be on the exams. Not great with blackboard and makes small mistakes frequently. Nonetheless, I'd still recommend him.

Not a fan of his teaching style. He makes multiple mistakes - in each class. It's hard to take him seriously when as a class we have to consistently correct him. He's also very disorganized. His blackboard site is so jumbled. His tests, homework, and practices contain spelling and number errors that are so frustrating. Wouldn't recommend him.
Best teacher ever! He is really smart, patient, and funny.

He's a really nice guy, very approachable and wants to help, but I just couldn't really learn under his style. He makes a lot of mistakes and I personally got more confused listening to his lectures than reading the book. His tests are also very tricky and long, which I didn't like because I was rushing throughout them and made dumb mistakes.
Pay attention and go to class and you will get an A :)

you get what you put in. he gives you everything you need to do well and it's up to you whether or not to use it! i thought he was a great professor, makes mistakes in class which was a tad frustrating but if you make a small mistake on a test he takes off only that point, even if that one mistake caused other mistakes. i think he's fair and helpfu

Sneed is a great Professor. He does make some mistakes in class but he is real. He will tell you everything that is going to be on the test and it's up to you to put in the work. Work hard and you'll get a B
It is a good teacher, but too many homework, quiz, and exam.
I can't believe I paid so much money to take this class.. Unbelievably bad teacher.

Awful teacher.. Constantly making mistakes in his in class examples.  All he does is copy his notes. Goes way to fast on material that is not that easily understood. I wish UO had another accounting 213 teacher to take. This guy should not be teaching.
He likes to throw tricks on the quiz, some of the content on the exam is somewhat incomprehensible. And he goes too fast in the lecture, not recommand

One of the worst professors i've ever had.. He tests you on things he teaches in class but he throws in "tricks" and makes accounting 5 times harder to understand then it already is. I had an awful term with this guy. I wish UO had more choices of teachers for accounting 213 :-(
He's a great professor, he made accounting not that completed easier to understand
One of the best teachers at UO. Accounting still sucks but he makes it at least interesting.

Great Professor! Very entertaining in class and a real genuine guy. He gives you everything you need to succeed. Just use his in class exercises and do not focus completely on his practice Tests he posts. the tests will often consist of problems drawn directly from the In class problems.

Great guy and a great teacher.  Entertaining for an accounting teacher and was on top of the work.  He definitely didn't take any crap from anyone so do what is told and you will do great in the class.
Favorite professor ever! Very helpful,down to earth, wants you to succeed.
Great guy, great personality, he makes accounting as interesting as it can be however he can be pretty un organized at times.

All time favorite prof. Great guy, really puts in the time to help you understand the material. Very approachable. Tests are exactly what he say so if you put in the time there is no reason you shouldn't do good. Definitely recommend him!
He was a great teacher and was very helpful if you did not understand the material.  He wants everyone to succeed.

He is a great teacher.  He sincerely wants you to do good in the class. His approach does have flaws but he has been in the field and knows what is important and wants his students to know it as well.  Great teacher.

He is the worst teacher ever. He complains more in class about how no one does the homework rather than actually teaching the information. Attendance is mandatory which is good because the class is necessary to learn the material rather than the book, however, he talks more about being moral and studious than teaching the new concepts of the week.

A great accounting teacher. yes, attendance is mandatory but i went to every class and didnt have to really study besides doing that. Go to class, do the homework (which doesnt take long) and there really isnt much studying needed to be done. He has a lot of energy and is very engaging. Makes class time worth it.HIghly recommended

He genuinely cares about the class and the students. A great professor, however if you don't do your homework or zone out in class it would be easy to get lost, however that is true with any accounting course...

This teacher seems to care too much about students learning rather than just giving them a free pass. His approach does have flaws, but it's been effective for me. He goes over many problems in class. Seems always willing to help. Sets very clear expectations for exams and provides many practice examples.

Very very helpful teacher. Gives lots of examples in class, tells you exactly what is going to be on the test and sticks to it. No surprises. He drops your lowest quiz score. A little unorganized during class but overall a great guy.

This man is not only incomprehensible, but an idiot.  He can not keep assignments, answer keys, or the text straight.  He can't add correctly.  His class is an overall nuisance.  He is more than unorganized.  I can hardly bare it.

This teacher was completely unorganized and his class was unstructured. In order to enjoy this class, or do well, you must have a stronger background in acounting. His classes were extremely frustrating and there was no book for further clarification.

gives many sample problems, but they're time consuming. He's very helpful, but he talks really fast and goes at a face pace.  His explanations may be confusing.  Really understanding and stays on task.  However, he may be unorganized, but approachable.
Attendance is not mandatory on days Duck student tickets are up for grabs.
Fun guy, smart but very unorganized and scattered, if you prefer classes with structure think about a different instructor
No Comments

While he did make Accounting easy to understand, he was very unorganized. When he tried to do an example in class he usually made up the numbers on the spot and made mistakes so we couldn't follow it. Or the examples didn't match the solutions because they are similar with random numbers changed. But a good class to take for non-accounting majors
Great professor! Dynamic and engaging. I suck at actg and had to take 211 twice. I got an A in his class. Difficult tests but you will pass if you do the work. He does not fail anyone.

This teacher gave me hope in the educational system. The material was delivered by him in a clear and concise manner. Communication was excellent and the testing was directly correlated with the material covered. This professor made a subject I wouldnt have been interested in, interesting because of the care they exuded! Loved this class.

One of the most approachable, caring profs I've had. This class was super easy but interesting, so I recommend him for 301. Super straightforward lectures and quizzes (no final or tests, just 5 quizzes). He didn't respond to emails very fast and wouldn't really tell you why he graded you down, BUT take him nonetheless, he's great!

I am currently a senior (ad major) and Sanjay is one of the most caring and compassionate professors I have ever had. He cares so much about how everyone is doing and is always willing to talk if you need some extra help. Great class, really interesting for someone who isn't a psych major!

My favorite psychology professor so far. He's seriously so nice and understanding (especially in the midst of the pandemic). If you pay attention you will always know what you are supposed to do; he's super organized!

Even though it was not required to go to his lectures, I never wanted to miss one of his due to his gift of teaching and capturing his student's attention. He is hilarious!! He explains concepts in a simple, straight-froward way with a down-to-earth manner. He loves interacting with his students. He would also record his lectures for later use.

One of the best professors I've had at UO. Very funny guy and gives breaks during the long lectures. He really knows his material and is there to help the students. Tests are difficult but as long as you do the InQuisitives and study the vocal you'll do fine. Definitely would take a class with him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is incredibly funny,  lectures are heavy with course material and are often on the midterm. READ THE SYLLABUS it matters. Discussion that is tacked on with the class is high key a waste of time... but besides that very concept heavy! Make sure you read the book and use the inquizitive that coincides with the text.

Great lecturer. Funny and engaging. Uses lots of class participation during lecture, but makes it fun (I usually hate this stuff). Tests were manageable. All around, he's a pleasant guy to learn from!

Sanjay is an excellent Professor! I had his class at 8:30 in the morning and I did not miss one class, he made it fun and engaging. He has so much knowledge about what he teaches and made me want to go to class and pay attention and learn. I wish all psych classes were taught by him!

Professor Srivastava was great. He makes material interesting and entertaining. He's a very likeable and approachable guy. Grading and tests were within what I would consider normal. No textbook. I had a great time in his class when I was able to make it. I would recommend Professor Srivastava to philosophy and psychology majors alike.

Sanjay is a straightforward dude. The class requires some online posts to topics in the posted readings. No textbook lots of primary source readings instead, so you need to go to lectures to get the material. Topics are interesting and class is easy if you score well on tests which are more like quizzes (25 questions), also there are two papers

Sanjay is a good teacher. He knows his stuff in psychology. Cracks jokes from time to time that kept me interested. His quizzes are pretty straight forward and logical, don't take them lightly (40% of your grade, lowest gets dropped). Was pretty approachable. Only complaint: He would say that we would get out 20 minutes early...rarely happened
He was good. Funny, organized, interactive. Work load wasn't to bad. Was nice and helpful.

Great teacher! i was worried by the name that he may not speak clearly but he speaks perfect english, makes jokes to keep attention, and knows the material very well. he chooses his words carefully and makes the class very easy to pass if youre willing to put in any effort. the only thing i didnt like is his grading structure for discussion.

Sanjay is an awesome teacher.  He's really charismatic, he knows the material, and is able to present it in a way that makes it interesting.  It was truly never a boring class.  True, the discussions weren't the greatest, but lectures were great.  I would highly recommend him.
No Comments
he is great. hard to get an A.  but great great great.
Very clear and in to the material.  Had him his first term teaching and after he works out the kinks and gets more comfortable he will be very good.
Kind of interesting and young, but he says um so much it's almost distracting.  And the discussions are a waste of time...
No Comments
Poor speaker, tests are difficult, the discussion sections he sets up arent helpful at all.

Joe's very experienced with CS/DSCI but it doesn't seem like it. His lectures are super boring and he just reads off slides. I was also taking CS210 which had some overlap, so I didn't find it too difficult, but I might have struggled if I hadn't. There is a lot of homework, but the labs are great because the GE's are super nice and helpful.
i took this last year but this was the best structured class I've ever taken here I'm in other cs classes rn and i miss this...

Why teach a 101 course if you don't have the tolerance for questions from students? Long, boring, monotonous lectures with no student interaction. Answers questions from students condescendingly and doesn't have patience for anyone who challenges his teaching in any way. Def an easy course tho if you have any stats or CS background.

I litteraly love how clear the course was. there was so many office hours and the canvas had literally everything needed. the structure was so nice. however, I would not take this class without any prior programming experience because it is pretty harshly graded, and no feedback is given unless you ask

Joe is an incredibly good guy, especially if you take the time to get to know him. He made intro to data science accessible by providing tons of virtual office hours which allowed me to get lots of help on the homework. The lectures are not the most interesting but if you are willing to work hard you will do great in the class!

If you want to take DSCI101, I wouldn't take it with Prof. Sventek. He reads off slides that he didn't make, and isn't great at explaining some topics. I had some prior programming experience, and I still found some programming difficult in this class. However, this class offers excellent office hours, so you're able to use them if you fall behind.

Professor Sventek has an overly harsh and punitive teaching style that is not fit for most students. His deadlines are strict. He also grades quite harshly. The class itself is already quite difficult for someone new to computation, but his teaching style makes it much more difficult. I recommend taking this class when its taught by someone else.

He was just awful. Didnt learn anything from him. I took him in Data science 101 but that wasn't an option to pick. a literal quote he told me was "this is all very simple and intuitive, and I don't know what to say or how to help you, now there are people behind you in office hours so ill have to kick you out". speaks for itself.

His lectures were okay, but he was super clear on his expectations for assignments and quizzes. He was always available to help out and was generally really caring in wanting us to do well in the course. The content was challenging but in a helpful way, and Prof Sventek understood that when he was teaching. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: didnt go to most of the lectures since i found the textbook more useful (it contains the same content, excluding the useful-ish exam review slides he provided). if u were solid in 210/11, the biggest learning curve will come down to working with the aspects of C that make it a lower-level language. prof was generous with curves/extensions/EC imo

His course made no sense and was terribly structured. It's all over the place and has no focus. I didn't learn many new things except lots of C syntax. I shared his book with some engineers and they laughed at it. They called it an outdated and bad technical manual. Random YouTubers are better teachers than him. Tenure is pretty sweet.

I think Dr. Sventek definitely gets a bad reputation. He and his TA's are all very accessible outside of class with ample office hours throughout the week. Most of the code is either given in labs, the textbook, or the lecture slides. Can be a little insensitive to students struggles, but has a fantastic class structure to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly gets a bad rap. A little harsh on ignorance/ having to repeat himself, but cares about students doing well, is very helpful in office hours, and is usually lenient on giving extensions. Learning C is a steep learning curve but the projects don't increase in difficulty that badly after that. If you put in the work you can succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Sventek is a genuinely good person. But he has trouble actually teaching things effectively. See him after class a lot, email him, and talk online. Since it can be hard to know exactly what he wants and what he means sometimes. And like others posted here, learn C before you take 212, it'll save your sanity. Oh and he has cute cats.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: remember that bad teacher you had in high school? well this guy makes them look like teacher of the year. he has no ability to actually teach material. and after going to his office hours a bunch, i realize all he knows is academic code in C. if you know C/C++ before 212 ur good to go. 212 is all mem. management and pointer manipulation in C. fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Thinks he's way smarter than he actually is. And he's an awful writer, but makes references to his own unpublished book and makes you frequently use it. There are good reasons it's not published dude. Packs A LOT into a 10 week course with a new language and OS. LEARN C AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE BEFORE YOU TAKE 212 UNLESS YOU HAVE A LOT OF FREE TIME.

The class is difficult and stressful but looking back on it I learned a lot about the c programming language and the expectations of upper division courses. Joe seems pretty callus but when it came down to it, he was empathetic and willing to adapt to the challenges of remote learning and external stress.

His 212 class is basically a weed-out class. He makes students develop and learn in Unix/C when the classes before were in Python. It's an unnecessary jump and hard for anyone with no C/Unix background. Much of the course also covers way too many data structures and algorithms for a 10-week first-year course. Also grumpy and rude. Avoid if possible

212 is a weeder class and Sventek gets villainized for it. He does have extremely high expectations and little patience if you dont meet them. But behind the gruff exterior, hes a good guy. Ultimately, Sventek wants to make sure youre ready for the rigor of the CIS major. Read the textbook before class, start stuff early, and youll be fine.

If you're reading this, you're probably already registered for CIS212 or DSCI311 and just deciding how stressed out you should be. The best advice I can give is work hard, talk to GEs and TAs when you have questions, get the class over with and forget you ever knew the man. Keep your head up, no matter how rude or irritated he seems, and move on!

Literally should not be teaching. Arrogant, outdated, doesn't even like being asked questions. Teaches the 3rd CIS intro course in C, however the previous 2 intro courses were in Python. Prepare to spend weeks just learning C syntax and the C language versus actual software design and principles. Go to Oregon State instead, the profs are bad here.

I was a bit worried going into Prof. Sventek's class because I've heard he's a bit grumpy, but I think deep down he's a nice guy! I think he has a voice version of rbf where whenever he explains something he sounds annoyed but he's really not and just focusing. Projects are hard, but well-structured and heavily based on textbook (which he wrote!).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Joe Sventek is direct and methodical in his teaching style. He will work with you through problems in office hours. As long as you show up and put in the work, he wants you to do well and will help you. Start every assignment/lab early so you have time to troubleshoot. Material is front-loaded and intense if you are unfamiliar with Python.

I think Joe Sventek gets a bad rap because of his impatience for student's questions during lectures, but he is a solid teacher. His class is very organized; topics learned each work are directly applied to labs. He grades each lab within a week (which is more than I can say for most UO professors) and gives helpful feedback on them. Solid teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: "Good morning everyone, what's that? You don't already know everything, well that's your fault. You should be better... Why would you ask such a stupid question?" If you're not perfect you're dumb. Go to a different school for computer science, they're all like this here . At least there's lots of Office Hours. Need > 100% for A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rude and condescending. Double standards, he messes up all of the time, but if we do, he posts a rant online IN ALL CAPS. Do not take his classes if you are easily offended. He creates a hostile environment. Communication between the teaching staff is bad as well. He marks our projects down for doing things GEs and LAs suggested. Avoid Joes classes

He definitely thinks every student in class is Ralph from the Simpsons, but if you can get past that he's an intelligent prof with a good curriculum. Be sure to read each project prompt thoroughly, he grades far harsher than what you're probably used to from CIS 210 and 211.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a hard teacher, but he's fair. If he screws something up (e.g. releases an assignment a day late) he'll make up for it. He was strict, getting a perfect score on the projects was extremely difficult, but it felt so much more rewarding. The one thing that really sucked with him is that he would always be condecending with questions.

There's a bit of a double standard with Professor Sventek. He expects students to be perfect, but includes typos in his instructions, and errors and bugs in his code. He's also rude when answering questions in class (less so on piazza). I would avoid Professor Sventek if possible, but that's tough when he teaches 212 two terms in a row.

Knows what he is talking about and is clear in his lectures and on expectations for assignments but is not great at teaching. There is a feeling of condescension when he has to answer a question and he is more rude than helpful. He has trouble putting himself in the students shoes and understanding what it is like to be learning the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The grade of a one is not coming out of a place of disrespect. I understand Joe is an incredible computer scientist and is very knowledgable about the subject. Unfortunately, that does not translate into an ability to teach. Joe gets irrationally frustrated when you ask questions he deems "easy to understand". He is also an impossible grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He will mark you down for any tiny inconsistency in homework, even if this includes turning in a rich text format doc, instead of a text format doc. Often he will respond to legitimate student questions by telling them to simply google it. He's the head of the department, and tenured, which gives him immunity for this behavior.

Joe is the head of the CIS department, and it shows in his class. Projects were difficult and worth a relatively low percentage of your overall grade. He isn't the type of professor you can squeak by with, either you know the material or you don't. One of the most challenging classes I've taken so far, but I appreciated being pushed!

Joe is the department head of CIS and that is for a reason. He makes his classes very difficult but understandably. 210 specifically was a weeding out course, i.e. if you can't succeed you likely won't be successful moving on. His tests were impossible and averages were around D- for midterm+final, and he does not curve. Homework was more doable.

I took this class my first term as a freshman and it was a rude awakening to what college classes could be like. The professor had no mercy or sympathy for anyone, not curving the midterm even though the average was a D. He is very knowledgeable but seems to have no patience for people struggling in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sung is an amazing professor who cares about his students and work. Throughout the term he made clear requirements and was always pushing us to ask questions and nudging us in the right direction.

Dude got in a car crash and rolled up to class the day after. Super cool guy. He's definitely new to teaching, but he's got great potential. I wish this class was a tad harder or had more business-prep stuff, but I feel like that's the curriculum rather than Sung. The group project and presentations are where most of your grade is. I recommend!
Honestly best professor for BA453. This class does not overwhelm your schedule and workload it is extremely doable and enjoyable. He ends class early lots of times and assigns almost no homework.
(BA453) The greatest to ever do it. If Sung is a potential candidate as your BA453 professor, take it from me and drop everything else in order to get into one of his sections. No more need be said.

Professor Sung was awesome! None of us knew it was his first time teaching until the last day—he was that smooth & engaging. He made class interactive, encouraged teamwork, & genuinely cared about our success. When we found out, the whole class gave a standing ovation. Highly recommend! Super down to earth & caring. I'd take any class he teaches!

If you're taking BA453, I guarantee you there is no other professor who is better than Professor Sung Park. He didn't assign any assignments that felt like busy work, and the workload was pretty light, but helpful to read for our projects. He has class activities that help you understand concepts, but they're very engaging. TAKE HIS CLASS 10/10

Sung is so awesome. I have heard so many bad things about BA 453 teachers but he truly is so nice and cares about all of his students. He really wants everyone to succeed. I highly recommend his class. Important to note that there is also a Sung Park in the journalism department but they are not the same.
Professor Park is awesome! He is the best option for BA 453.
Dr. Sussman likes to include group activities into every lecture so if you enjoy that then this class is for you. They're very passionate about what they do and clearly care about their students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Sussman is the best! Every time we have class, it is always so engaging and interactive. She works well with students to ensure that everyone can learn in ways that best benefit everyone. All she asks for is respect, and everything else is smooth sailing.

Professor Lim was by far the best Korean professor I've had at UO. She is very clear with her teaching and this is the easiest time I've had learning the content. There are weekly vocab quizzes and a quite a bit of chapter tests, but there are practice tests for all of them and it's easy to feel well prepared.
very nice, caring, and will make you pay attention in class, be sure to be aware of a lot of homework per 2 weeks

Dr. Lim is one of the best profs I've ever had. Participation is encouraged, not forced so discussions are fun (no forced BS comments for participation points). She gives specific advice and compliments on assignments and genuinely cares about the thoughts and opinions of her students. If you're reading this, this is your sign to take her class.
A lot of reading, but P. Lim is so knowledgeable and they were always interesting. Grading is super easy.
Lots of reading homework but super fun and interesting. if you time manage well you'll do great. She's an amazing person and very excited about what she's teaching and the discussions we have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Lim is a wonderful teacher! Initially, I wasn't very thrilled about taking her class, but it proved to be very interesting and definitely worth my time. She is very kind and accessible outside of class. I would definitely recommend taking a class from her! If you work hard, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed professor Lim's class, but it did prove to be difficult to get higher than a B+ on essays. She really makes you work on essays and I felt that at times her suggestions were really just places that she disagreed with your paper. Otherwise the class was engaging and I enjoyed the array of reading we were assigned.

There are readings every week, but the class is extremely laid back. Lim gives everyone a B+ on their essays, which can be frustrating. Overall, Lim is a great person, who is extremely nice and helpful. She also appreciates it if you can make her laugh.

It takes a little bit to get used to the way Professor Lim talks, but she is great to get to know and has a great sense of humor. If she gives the option to sign up for office hours to talk about your paper, do it. It's worth the time. It's  really difficult to get above a B+ on a paper, and meeting with her just might help.
