Professor Lim is a great teacher! She is always available for questions, and is just a very kind person. She really knows her stuff, and seems like a really chill person to get to know. If I was her age, I would want to be her friend.
Pretty good, though her way of speaking just makes me anxious. I always felt a little rushed in her class even though we had plenty of time to do everything. NOT laid back.

Lim can be a bit intimidating at times, but it's because she clearly knows her stuff. She's actually pretty nice, if a little reserved. Class is well structured, 2 papers and a presentation make up most of the grade, but she's a fair grader. I learned a ton from her class, even though I don't have much interest in literature. Overall good teacher.

Professor Lim is wonderful! Her class is organized and she facilitates discussion well. She is an expert in Russian literature, and I would recommend her class to anyone regardless of prior interest in Russian lit.

After the first day of class I left intimidated by the teacher and the class itself, but it turned out to be the academic class I looked forward to most all year. Prof. Lim is kind, considerate, knows exactly what she's talking about, and has got a great sense of humor as well. Recommended.
Great teacher, young but still very knowledgeable about her subject, without going overboard on random tangents. If you speak up in class and go to office hours, should be an excellent class.

Sung is very hard to get help from. He grades insanely hard and knit picks every assignment. Only talks about his achievements during class and then goes over assignments and nothing is ever good enough. Worst teacher I have had at the UO and am flabbergasted he is teaching a 200 level class. He also does not believe in A's at all.

I don't think he is a good professor. The class has A+ grade at 97/100. But he gives everyone 94/100 in every grade as the highest score. So there is no way to get A+. Also I think he is deliberately ambiguous.

(JCOM 241) I've had Park for multiple classes now and I can say he is a massive a-hole. I had a multiple assignments docked 10-15% just because of tiny little mistakes. He doesn't have rubrics for any assignments. He even admitted to barely watching video projects. I learned a decent amount in his class but if you care about your GPA, avoid him.

I enjoyed my photo/video classes with Sung, but he is a tough grader and likes things a particular way. As long as you follow the instructions and you can utilize office hours because he will help you very clearly with what he wants, then you will do great in this class. He allows redos so you have a chance to redo everything which I appreciate.

Please try and avoid this professor if you are taking a beginner level class. He should not be able to teach and give feedback to beginners, as he is extremely subjective and does not comprehend that his class is advertised as for beginners.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sung is an amazing teacher- going to his class each week felt like going on a Gordon Ramsay cooking show but in a good way.. His criticism is bluntly honest, but he cares about your work and your growth as a student more than anyone else in the J school tbh. Super understanding, honest, hilarious, and caring prof.

This class is very intimidating to walk into but was a great experience. Sung starts the class by making it clear that he doesn't mind failing people on their assignments because if you are to fail anywhere, it should be in the classroom, and not the "real world," and will allow full redos. I learned a ton and value the experience.

Park is an expert in his craft but cant seem to effectively teach it to a beginner. A lot of the grades/feedback felt extremely subjective and to his own personal preferences and changed student to student.

Super tough grader, he really makes you work for your A in this class. His feedback is awesome, you can tell he really wants his students to do well. Very responsive to emails, he even holds office hours late at night before assignments are due just in case you have any issues. Definitely take this class with him if you want to go into videography

Sung is a very knowledgable professor though could use some work on his teaching skills. He gave some solid foundational advice about general photography and feel better because of it. Some of the techniques he taught though were hard to understand until I asked the GE or Sung directly. He provided a lot of hands-on experience though which was grea

The basic photo/video class taught me nothing about photography or videography. You just do stupid little assignments every week with your iphone camera and he doesnt really give any feedback. Its clear hes knowledgeable about photography but hes just not good at teaching it. Wouldnt want to take a class with him again.
The class was ineffective in teaching principles essential to professional success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sung cares about helping students reach their full potential. He provides you with great feedback. Be prepared to do your work, don't show up late, and don't expect an A unless you are willing to work for it.

Class consists of nothing but him lecturing about F stops and shutter speeds, then he expects you to go out and produce pictures that meet his ideals. He expects way too much from students with no experience taking pictures and producing videos. He is also impatient when you ask for help. I only took his class because I had too.
He didn't really teach us anything he more so bragged about all of his accomplishments and used those as examples.
Tough. Nitpicky. Perfectionist. But, you will learn.  And he wants that.
Hard class but good teacher. Not the most interesting but he will teach you what you need to know.

he is soooo lame. tells us directions to assignments the DAY BEFORE it is due....mean...lame....boring....does he even prepare his material????? seems like he would be a nice person to know....not professor material

She's downright awful. She doesn't know how to teach and she's so rude. Like that's literally it. She's a horrible teacher and I honestly don't even know what her credentials are because she's so weirdly vague. I'm sure the children she's worked with hated her. -10/10 don't recommend. I honestly feel sorry for her inability to take feedback.
I think that Sunny was great I dont know how she even had a bad rating. I'm currently in her async class, and I love it. There are two tests the whole term that are online and group discussions.

I really like this professor! She's super organized and clear about expectations for assignments. Not a ton of reading/work to do outside of class. She also changed the midterm and final so that they're now taken online due to negative feedback from previous classes about taking it in person.

Save your grade and do not take this class. This is an ONLINE CLASS that takes IN PERSON exams. She is very understanding but her exams are 20 questions with each question being 1% of your grade so good luck. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Never responds to emails.
The class was very organized, but the lectures are all pre-recorded and incredibly boring. If you don't have a strong interest in the topic, you may want to choose something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quiz questions are vague, and missed points feel inevitable regardless of preparation. The grading is the most punishing I've encountered: one missed assignment can crater your grade with no recovery. Material feels outdated. The documentary was the one highlight. Don't miss a single assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why UO keeps professors around to reuse 9-year-old content. Its insane to pay thousands of dollars for a class made up of YouTube lectures. Easy science credit, but soooooo boring. One quiz and one discussion board every week. Way too many lectures and readings, but they're really not even necessary. Skim everything, and you'll pass.

I took three classes of her class and got an A in all of them. The lectures are old, and the GEs grade everything so any grading problems were from them but I didn't have much issue. There's a ton of reading but as long as you skim it and pay attention to the main concepts it isn't as bad, not all of the readings are super relevant.

Spent most of this class reading large bodies of text that didn't make sense. Often was boring, repetitive, and got little to no feedback from the GEs. Grading based on weekly quizzes and bi-weekly worksheets. Made a big dent in your grade if you didn't do well, but barely any feedback was given so you could get better. Extremely irritating.
It's an easy class to fulfill the science requirement. A worksheet and a quiz every week, a simple class, although so does not curves, round, extra credit, or makeovers at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not awful not good. Your grade is entirely dependent on weekly quizzes and a bi-weekly worksheet. Sometimes it feels like the quizzes are impossible to score well on because the questions are so random.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best prof. Made a gen ed class a nightmare, especially with it being so boring and nonrelevant to now. Only had her online class so it wasn't horrible but made you read pages upon pages of text that made little to no sense and ended up making a good dent in your grade if you didn't do well on the worksheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It was ok. Easy for an online course. I readings were a lot to process and sometimes too many were assigned. Worksheets are easy . Quizzes seemed to only be based on youtube lectures and not the readings so the readings seemed like boring busy work. It definitely covers topics that i think are inportant to know just not in an interesting way.

You'll have to do a movie reflection each week which will take a while so don't start late. Weekly quizzes on lecture material, they are long lectures but u need all the info. I suggest using your phone camera to copy and paste onto GD to use for quizzes and watching the lectures a 2nd time before quiz u won't have alot of time to look for answers

Ridiculous amount of work assigned that would only be acceptable if this were the only class you took for a whole term. Hundreds of pages of readings along with lengthy droning lectures. No exams but you're only graded by quizzes and discussion posts which are written like essays. With this class, you can either have free time, or a bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: we had weekly closed-note online quizzes and incredibly long readings, she's understanding and accommodating, the load is very well organized
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The material was interesting however, as this was an online class there were a lot of online lectures every week. The lectures were incredibly difficult to learn from because they were very mundane. The lecture slides consisted of paragraphs of text. There was so much writing, making it hard to learn/take notes.

I found this class super interesting so it was easy for me to get through it. There were way too many reading to even try to read them all, so I quickly stopped actually reading them. However, the class was routinely structured the same so it was very easy to predict the quizzes and it wasn't hard to do them without the readings.
You can pass without doing much of the readings as long as you do the lectures.

ANTH 163 is incredibly lecture-heavy, and you must watch and take notes on the lectures in order to do good on the weekly quizzes and understand the weekly worksheets. It isn't terrible, but it is difficult sometimes to get through the lectures. Michelle is a good teacher, I think it might've just been this specific course that was difficult.

Takes forever to grade assignments, 100+ pages of reading per week, hard quizzes worth a lot of your grade, and repetitive lectures that are structured terribly. If you are looking for a class with an insane amount of workload, take this one. Content was interesting at first but became incredibly redundant and I quickly couldn't care less about it.
Her GEs are incredibly tough graders. Quizzes are based off the lecture heavily, take notes. Boring lectures read off of a script. Quizzes every week and worksheets every other week.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. Grading structure is ridiculously scattered and unorganized. As an ANTH art course, part of formulating a response to the artifacts is being subjective, however she expects the complete opposite. I mean, it is an art course? Lectures/readings are EXTREMELY dense as well.

This class's structure was from a different professor so the recorded lectures weren't even Prof. Sugiyama talking (and they were soo boring). Only one short lecture a week but lots of readings. Midterm and final had multiple choice questions from the readings and some were super detailed. Discussions were easy and movies were fun, overall OK class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Legit copy and pasted a different instructor's canvas. She put in no work and the tests are extremely difficult-questions heavily based on readings (not even the fun readings). Discussion posts are basically essays, with initial post 300-450 words & responses 200-250 words. Only perk: watching a movie every week after week 3.
Don't take anything from this prof. Inconsiderate and is not understanding at all, especially when she makes the mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are incredibly monotone. She is clearly reading off a script during her lectures and it's extremely hard to follow along as she overcomplicates ideas for no apparent reason. Readings are immense. Tests are extremely difficult. Questions on tests you cannot prepare for. Concepts that are taught are not interesting. Overall bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Slides are basically transcripts. Have to simplify them yourself. They tell you to read first then watch the lectures, but reading 80 pages of dense academic work is difficult esp. when you don't know what to look out for. WATCH LECTURES FIRST. THEN READ. THE SYLLABUS IS YOUR HOLY BIBLE. then pray bcs this class is not it b... i'm crying and dying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be prepared to spend a lot of time watching the lectures and taking notes. The weekly quizzes and worksheets are worded weird and she is not the most understanding professor. Don't try to ask her for any help or understanding because she lacks complete empathy and compassion for her students. One of the most condescending professors I have ever had
Such a nice person, she is super passionate and it shows. I took this class online, so we had weekly worksheets and quizzes and they were pretty easy if you paid attention to her lectures.

Professor Sugiyama talks extremely fast. Her lecture slides are filled to the brim and she flys through them like theres no tomorrow. It's impossible to write things down. Quizzes are worded tough and are tricky. Movie worksheets are graded very meticulously. If you put in the effort you can get a good grade, there is not much work. Nice lady.

Sugiyama talks ridiculously fast- after lectures I had to go through the slides again in order to take good notes. You could learn just as well by not going (she posts all powerpoints on canvas). Don't bother doing the assigned readings, she ends up telling you everything you need to know in lecture. Overall a fairly pointless (but not hard) class.

Not hard to pass the class by paying attention to lectures, although the readings were very long. I had an easy A coming, but I missed a deadline. It was a mistake, and usually I have found Professors to be understanding. However, she was not. That's fine, but the obvious attempts to be rude and spiteful when replying were really soul crushing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was super interesting, though the lectures could be a bit dry. I really enjoyed the ethnographic films, though the worksheets were graded pretty harshly. Overall, Id say it was a great class, especially for an online one

I took her online course which incorporated a simple layout: readings, lectures, online responses, and a weekly quiz. The lectures were super interesting but quite lengthy. The online responses were rather easy if you actually put effort into them. And the first few quizzes were easy/average but afterward, they were tricky, at least for me.
This online class requires very little work. Take good notes from the lectures, and do the readings and it will be an easy A. Your grade will reflect the amount of effort you put in

I've taken other online courses before, but this was awful. The quizzes were the worst - poorly written and tricky. She assigns an extensive amount of long, outdated readings and her lectures are boring and move fast. The course was weighted on fact memorization, not content application. I enjoyed the subject, but not the course organization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Yes she is a fast talker & she knows that too but she uploads notes & allows you to take notes any way possible. The Discussions are a decent part of your grade so go, EC is also given out a lot there. Test are easy if you just pay attention to what's being taught. She teaches all reading material and goes over the exact stuff on the test in depth.
Definitely makes you work for it, but has clear expectations and if you follow the syllabus, it is a relatively easy class.
Good Luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sugiyama is knowledgeable & open to providing resources for students. However she talks so fast that it is impossible to take notes. The class layout is clear but every discussion is spent taking a quiz which is worth 1/3 of your grade. Eventually I stopped showing up to lecture & took notes on my own time & was still able to pass all the quizzes.

Lectures are long and very boring, but she never takes attendance. The midterm was hard and she did not prepare us or mention it after it happened. She assigns readings but never mentions them. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COST.

Jessica is very nice as a person, but aggravating as a professor. She is weird about grading, will tell you something looks great, and then give you a B. She is also not very understanding about other obligations. I dropped a full letter because I was absent due to illness twice, and tardy twice.
Jessica is wonderful. Her grading can be a bit confusing and offers better critiques on Canvas than in person, but she is very knowledgeable, kind, and caring. The assignments are fun and rewarding!

While I did like this class &Jessica is nice, I was under the assumption that I'd receive instruction on how to do a lot of the structure &foundations behind a lot of the DWG we have done. For 233 she assumes people have somehow taken other art courses which puts you at a disadvantage. She also grades very harsh &I min. put in 15-20hrs per DWG.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a tough grader for this to be an intro to drawing 1 class. Will walk around and give no feedback other than like "thats so good" and then gives a C as the grade. the better drawers seem to be getting Bs so I dont know if getting an A is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly awful. Only have negative things to say. Doesn't make expectations clear and doesn't even consider time and effort when it comes to grading. I put min 6 hours into every project and still got somewhat low grades. No empathy or understanding when it comes to grade and never give constructive, consistent feedback. Do not take.

For an intro, to drawing class, the professor offered no demonstration or explanation for techniques she expected us to use. I learned more from reading books and from my classmates than from her. I would ask her for advice on a project and she would say something like "That looks fantastic!" and then give a low mark, as well as offer vague advice.

I had Jessica for 115, she is kind and I learned from her class. However, she expects students to already have basic drawing techniques which made it hard for beginners like me. She would praise my sketchbook but give me a C and not say what could be improved, and my classmates had to show me basic skills she did not teach, which was frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is very supportive of artists both young and old. I wish that I could take another class with her.

She pretends like she is supportive and cares but the longer you are in the class, the more it'll become evident that she doesn't give two shits about you. She does NOT want you to succeed.  Single-handedly the worst professor I have ever had. Also, she is such a harsh grader for a beginner art class and has NO empathy. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS

Media History can be really dry, but Swartz taught it well by including modern implications and concepts. He asked big questions and asked us to consider relationships with/in media beyond usage and preference. Clear syllabus and assignment expectations. Made effort to be available to students often. He is the reason I became a media studies major.

Swartz means well, but falls short in his execution. The man's 2 hour long lecture could be covered in 15 minutes at best and he seems to draw out class time for the sake of drawing it out. 6 reflections, beware, you have to sit through class before turning it in. Exams are easy and if you don't like being called on, steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is very straight forward. 20% of grade is summaries which there are ten, but only six are required to be completed. Lectures can be long and kind of boring but, if you miss a day its not a big deal. He's easy to talk to so don't feel scared to ask for help. Exams are not tricky, if you just use the do the study guide. Should be easy A :)

Jeremey is rather pretentious. He likes to add his personal opinion - and seems to think of it as the highest truth. He randomly calls people out in class not only to answer questions but also to read slides, ask their opinion, share an insight, etc. Readings are dense, unclear. Provides only some lecture slides online. Must attend to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I actually look forward to going to his lectures. He makes history interesting. Imagine that.

Sylvan is the sweetest professor I've ever had. He will always notice when you're having a hard time, painting-related or not, and will always ask how you are. He is always very honest, but never too harsh. He pushes us to be better, and will always ask what you think of your work instead of just straight up telling you if he likes it.

I love him, and he's my favorite professor I've ever had. He will be completely upfront and honest with you about his thoughts, but don't be afraid to challenge them if you think you should. A great person to talk to and have deep conversations with, he is always there to listen to what is on your mind.

Sylvan is a great professor if you are passionate about painting/drawing. He is very much a no bullshit guy, and intimidating. He will give an honest critique and wants to see students improve. He assigns a few readings, and sometimes they can go over your head. Your grade is determined by your improvement for the most part; he has a massive curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took artp390 with Sylvan years ago I've had 10+ different teachers in the art department at UO he was the worst. This class is a bad memory, while he has a cheerful and friendly demeanor his limited scope puts a cap on self-expression. This is the only art class I can look back at during my time at UO and say "wow that was not good".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took his 281 class and get ready to only do abstract art. He loves abstract art and only really gives prompt to get you to do that but he can appreciate good craftsmanship and painting technique. He is chill abt leaving class  to get coffee. He will give you good feedback and guidance but make your own decisions. Only grades at the end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Sylvan's 391 class. He didn't grade a single project / assignment the entire term and explains many things about the course vaguely. His class is fun but be aware of your grade throughout the term and ask questions. IT IS VERY IMPORTANT FOR YOU TO PARTICIPATE IN CLASS.

Sylvan is a fantastic painting teacher who is also a successful painter himself. This may sound like an obvious thing to say, however I have had painting classes with bad painting teachers who were not successful painters, it makes a difference. He is not easy, but if you love painting this class is for you. He is good communicator too.

He is excellent as an art professor because he requires you to think for yourself and make your own decisions. He never gives you answers, but guides you in making your own discoveries about art, your work, and yourself as an individual. He helped me to become more confident and concrete in my art practice. Also, an incredibly nice person.

Sylvan is not only an amazing painter in his own right but a fantastic teacher. He promotes individual critical thinking, and pushes students to delve deeper and think more critically as an individual. Sylvan is very generous with his time, energy, as well as very affable. He will however force students to make their own decisions.

It's impossible to keep track of your grade because he never tells you what it is even if you ask. He also supposedly grades "mentally." He is very arrogant and unhelpful even if you try to go to him for guidance regarding expectations, etc.
Professional and gifted. New as an educator but great insights.

He was very unhelpful when both giving advice and explaining expectations, even when I attempted to talk with him personally. He was also very forceful with his opinions, and essentially behaved as if he is always right; when dealing with a highly subjective matter like art, that is simply not okay. The environment of the class was not encouraging.

I took math 112z with Prof. Washburn. Prof. Washburn moves through topics fairly quickly but always takes time to answer any questions. Extremely available for support due to of his endless amounts of office hours plus his quick responses to emails. Will reexplain the simplest concepts repeatedly if needed without making the students feel dumb.

Literally my favorite math teacher of all time! Washburn is amazing, and truly knows what he is talking about, and knows how to explain it, and re-explain it. His class is entertaining, and even if you don't like math, he'll make you want to go to class every day. If I could, I'd take another class with him, no questions asked. Take this class!
Best math teacher iv ever had. Provided a ton of office hours and added extra sometimes before midterms and the final. Very clear in lecture and is great at assisting you when you ask for help.

Professor Washburn's lectures are clear and concise, and he's good at making sure quiz and test questions directly reflect class topics. Very lowkey and understanding, and good at explaining when something is unclear.
Honestly the best math teacher I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class is super easy, just is comprised of a lot of busy work. I feel like a majority of the class work is done in the last 3-4 weeks and everything else is kind of not nearly as important. You can turn late work in whenever, he's super lenient and chill about things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is gives really good feedback and is gives grace and extensions on assignments. There is a good amount of them and at the start of the term there is a lot of reading. But he is really nice and clearly cares about what he is teaching and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Tasker is such a kind and understanding professor! Would definitely recommend taking his classes!

The flaw of WR 122 is that the homework and course material wasn't engaging. However, Dr. Tasker is kind, accessible, and flexible. He offers 48 hour extensions on all homework, and is still very lenient about late work after that. He gives thorough feedback on writing that really shows he cares about your success.
I love him!! He really wants you to do well in his class and focuses on giving you proper feedback. He made this online class really manageable and never felt too overwhelmed with the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class! He wants you to do well, sometimes I felt a bit confused on what he wanted from us but was always open to talking!

Super great prof and genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. He's really understanding of outside workload and gives automatic 2 day extensions for most assignments but if you ask you can increase that. Its important to go to class because his lectures/activities help a lot with assignments but def recommend him as someone that hates writing.

Tom is a really kind teacher that I would highly recommend to anybody taking writing classes. He is understanding and as long as you dedicate time during the week to the class you will be completely fine.
He is my favorite professor I have had here so far, I highly recommend him for writing classes.

Super great class! I took this class ASYNC, and he had weekly modules with guidelines on how to stay on track. Class materials were easy/informative, and lectures were always 8-15 min. All assignments have a 48-hr extension. He was quick to respond and willing to help out. Papers can take time, but should be expected for a 300-level writing class.

Great Prof. He genuinely cares about you succeeding and improving as a student. Very understanding with missing class and late work as long as you communicate. Easy grader with good feedback on essays as well as gives opportunity for extra credit.

He is very kind and engaged but also understands that many kids have large work loads outside of class and doesn't give much busy work. Always gives extensions and accepts late work. Attendance is tracked but not very strict. Overall a great professor and would love to have him again

We usually have homework assignments due every class but they're fairly straightforward, just requiring to read a couple articles and write discussion posts. All essays/writing projects have an automatic 48 hour extension which is super nice! Classes may be boring sometimes but it seems Tasker really cares, and can provide great feedback.

Tom really is a great guy. Every assignment has an automatic 2 day extension and there isn't a ton of massive assignments to do. You will be writing a lot in this class but why else are you taking a writing course. Tom simply wants students to engage, participate, and actually think about the texts given. Great Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you need to take a writing class (which you probably will), make sure to take it with Dr. Tasker. He gives really clear and helpful feedback on your writing and he clearly wants his students to improve and succeed. Dr. Tasker always gives you credit when he can see that you put in effort and he's very willing to give help when you ask for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Coolest professor I've ever had

Tom Tasker, is an amazing professor! His class is well organized, and is actually fun to go to! He is an amazing person, who truly cares for his students. I liked the way every assignment had a 48-hour extension no matter the assignment. 100% choose this professor!

Professor Tasker was an excellent professor and his class was very well structured and had a very nice organization in terms of assignments. You can tell that Professor Tasker truly cares for his student's success, with that said he provides really solid feedback and is very kind in the way he suggests revisions.

Tom's class was really nice. He was super understanding and would take any late work for full credit. We basically just have to practice annotations and write 2 essays throughout the course. He gives very detailed directions and is always willing to answer questions. Honestly a lot easier class than I thought it would be, would suggest.

This class is just not helpful . The sound engine Kyma is completely outdated and you're gonna spend most your time applying to what you know about sound to this outdated application with the teacher who thinks every question has been talked about in the past and you should have a note about it.

This class and teacher is just not good. You're here learning an application made in 1990 with a teacher. It doesn't clearly go over everything and will combat with students when they ask questions. You'll leave this class having spent all your time just trying to apply everything you know about sound to an outdated app.

She was great and the love for the material given was there. Her teaching style is specific in that it's a little more curt, but she was a very supportive teacher and helped me with my assignments and project when I couldn't figure it out myself.

I took MUS447 and my professor was pretty good at lecturing and informing students of course content. There was good communication within the class about deadlines and requirements. What threw me off was how little help was offered to me when I asked questions. It was always "why weren't you paying attention". Also lab hours no help was offered.

This was the most offensive misuse of my time and tuition that I've experienced in college – and that's a very high bar. We didn't get our hollow joke of a syllabus until *week 5.* One day we all wrote down 2 things we wanted to learn about that day and shared in a circle, which took up the whole class, meaning we didn't learn anything!

ok so i took 490 very interesting subjects. An important note for taking her class. Basicly graded by 5 things, pArticipation which includes a lot of reading and then talking in class about it. A mid term essay and a big finals oral recording and then a presentation about final project. if you dont do any one of these youre cooked not harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is extremely slow-paced, disorganized, and became increasingly hard to stay engaged. She is unaware of how to use Canvas, there are few and far between grade opportunities, and even then, the criteria are unclear. We're weeks behind the syllabus and do slim to nothing. Easy pass, but hardly educational, and not worth the thousands.

the course is quite disorganized, the canvas is very confusing and not accessible or accurate. professor is kind and educated but seems burnt out and unable to engage properly/ stay up to date on coursework. She feels very unprepared. Nice lady but very odd class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's lovely! Textbooks were recommended but not required, she reviews readings in class and often goes on tangents but she cares a lot for students and the course material. She also once brought her dog to class
Great professor, great material, I would take this class again right now if I could.

This professor has the least engaging voice of all time. Her class was disorganized, we never discussed the readings we were assigned until long after the date on the syllabus. Not a lot of opportunities for graded assignments and didn't update canvas enough. Unclear grading criteria. Would not recommend.

She is a relatively easy grader as long as you do the assigned readings and were prepared for the discussion section. Sometimes the due dates of assignments and dates of quizzes/tests were unclear/disorganized.
I dreaded coming to this class everyday. The lectures were not engaging at all. I would recommend taking this class from someone else. Her grading style is inconsistent and confusing.

This was my favorite Spanish class I've ever taken, it was amazing!!!! Analisa covered a lot of really interesting and important topics and I feel like she deals well with the many uninterested students that just show up and expect a grade without participating. I wish I could take more of her classes!!!
She is very smart, and a really nice teacher. Sometimes it gets a little boring, but overall, she keeps the course moving along so its not the same thing over and over. I would recommend this course!

This teacher was nice, however very hard to understand. She has a low, monotone voice and it's very hard to keep your attention on what she says for eighty minutes. I could understand our GTF better, a native speaker, than I could this professor. I would not recommend this professor.
No Comments

Taylor Adams was a fantastic professor whose class I took last year. She was kind, great listener, supportive, and gave great feedback. The projects were extremely manageable and a lot of fun, especially the wiki page. I learned a lot about languages and had a great time in this honors course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lives of languages has to be my favorite honors class I've taken so far. It was interesting, and the assignments were very unique. Discussions are a big part of the class, but it's no pressure if you don't want to participate. Prof. Taylor-Adams is very personable and makes lectures fun for everyone. I can't recommend this class enough.

She is one of the best and most patient teachers I've had at UO. She makes me comfortable talking in class and  asking questions, which I normally don't feel comfortable doing. When asking her questions, she gives clear and precise answers so I don't get confused.

Allison is a kind person and passionate about linguistics! She is new to teaching though and this was obvious throughout the class, often class was spent on things that felt unnecessary. The class material built off each other well, though, and there were many chances for discussion. Allison is also very receptive to suggestions from students!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is an awesome teacher! She makes the subject really easy to understand and listens carefully to student's questions and concerns. I don't go to her office hours that much, but when I asked her after class; she was willing to stay a little later and explain a concept to me. Tests are also easy and are related to the lectures and homework!
Was very straightfoward in teaching and all tests were not hard
She is really kind and approachable.

Lectures match exams and homework. Responds quickly to emails. provided pre made lecture notes son we can actually pay attention to the material that was being taught. Went a decent pace through notes and allowed for questions. WISH SHE TAUGHT CALC 251!!!
Great, kind teacher! Clearly goes over all concepts and lectures are pretty in depth. Class material is somewhat difficult but easy to figure out.
Very nice teacher and goes into depth on all concpets
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very helpful during office hours. lectures are easy to understand (sometimes). Easy to communicate with. Attentive with her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures were quite hard to understand, very disorganized, did not feel like I learned a lot in this class.

Professor Teo is strange in a mellow way, which can make class both entertaining and frustrating. I enjoyed our class, but was disappointed with her lectures. I felt she did not analyze poems in a way that really taught me anything. It was all kinda surface level. She is very nice though, and the discussions she fostered were enjoyable.

Not as bad as everyone is making her sound to be real. She can be disorganized and were reading the same book in diff versions, but its easy to follow. I missed many readings and still know whats going on. Yes nothings in grade book, but she's nice and PREGNANT THIS TERM, give her a break. Use her class to study if you must, but work is so minimal.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is quirky and fun, but she does get a little disorganized at times. I have to say that no grades by week 10 is a bit concerning, but as long as you turn in the work, you'll do fine. Antigone and all the versions we had to read were in the course description so nothing she gave the class was unprecedented. She was also very pregnant!
Update week 10 still no grades in the grade book, and she is being very unhelpful answering questions about the final project.

Okay girl is sassy. After not telling students what she expects she gets butt hurt when they dont read her mind.  Also not to be a hater, but we had to read the same story over and over again in different visions, and I'm just not that passionate about Antigone. Nothing is on canvas. There are no grades in week nine. I use this as study hall

She's nice but sooo disorganized. Not really any clear descriptions for the assignments and NO grades in the grade book and it's week 9. I couldn't summarize what I've learned from this class...because I don't think I've gained anything at all. I've never left a review on a professor before but she's prompted me to.

Professor Teo is not fit to be teaching a college class. Her lectures were incredibly disorganized and the point of the class was largely unclear. I had to ask her for an extension on an assignment multiple times after she failed to ever send the rubric and expected me to still meet the deadline. It is Week 8 and I still don't have a single grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was incredibly unorganized. Admitted in the first week of class that she did not want to talk (translates to not wanting to teach). Does not release instructions for assignments until last minute yet expects you to know what to do w/out them. No grades were submitted until after week 9 overall frustrating class don't suggest this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a good teacher and she graded very easily as long as you do the work. However, she didn't even have one grade in the gradebook until week eight and we got very minimal feedback. It was hard to know how you were doing. Additionally, I did not like the way she led discussions in class. Overall, a fine teacher to have a class with.

To be fair, most HC classes are fairly easy, but I did feel that Prof. Teo truly graded on if you put forth effort. I really enjoyed this class and the interesting variety of topics we discussed in it through a poetry lens. Overall it was fairly straight forward and I almost always knew what was expected of me (except for the final?).

I really like Professor Teo as a teacher, she was understanding and supportive. Her lectures were informational, and helped us work through the four readings we had for the class. My only issue is the feedback. Nothing in Canvas was graded all term, besides the syllabus quiz, and none of the essays I submitted were graded or got any feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teo is very supportive and encouraging. She understands when readings or topics can be difficult ( for example, abstract poetry) and creates a supportive environment to discuss the material and make sure students understand and learn from it. Really love this professor and recommend her. She's very welcoming and fun to talk to.

Katie is awesome! I took PS 458 with her last term and am currently taking PS 348 with her now. She is confident, easy-going, and super accessible for questions and feedback. Class discussions are central to her teaching style so even though participation isn't graded it is encouraged. The readings are interesting! She does move through slides fast

I took Professor Temple's PS 348 Women and Politics class and the fact that I made an RMP account just to rave about her probably says everything you need to know. Super friendly, knowledgable, and seems to genuinely enjoy teaching.

Amazing lectures w/ lots of real life examples. Readings are posted on canvas, no textbooks. Grade based on a few papers that weren't difficult. She's helpful, funny, interesting, and accessible. Topics were interesting and class was lots of discussion. Attendance mandatory but can miss a few classes w/out penalty. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Temple facilitated great discussions on the class topic, and it was exciting to talk about our experiences and learn from each other, as well as the history of feminism. Perfect attendance was incentivized and the few assignments were easy and straightforward. Would absolutely take it again!!!

Get ready for boring lectures and vague lesson plans. Much of the time in the class room was centered around discussions with table mates and basically their experiences (or lack of) with prejudice in society. There was almost nothing of educational value that was presented in lecture so don't waste your time going.

This teacher is INCREDIBLE!!! Most entertaining class lecture/discussion-based, but people want to talk. Shes so caring and comforting. No quizzes or tests. Shes a pretty easy grader and created a super comfy environment in the class where attendance wasn't mandatory, but everyone WANTED to go!!! Be blessed by this woman and take her class! AMAZING

Ben is awesomeeee. Go to office hours if you can, he allows catch up on all assignments in week 10. He's sincere and wants you to genuinely pass and understand what is being taught. Be respectful and communicate with him for any alterations ofc though.
Homework and quizzes weekly that are pretty hard and the grades add up. Study and memorize the practice test and you can do good. He only takes attendance once a week.

Ben's a king. His lectures are clear, easy to follow, and well-executed. Says the funniest things with a straight face. Homework can be tough, but only because algebra and arithmetic can be tedious and lengthy. Tests are straightforward; he gives practice tests that model exactly the kinds of problems to expect. Love him more than my own dad.

Amazing guy. He is so helpful, funny, and truly cares about his students. It was hard, but very doable if you put in the work. Choose Ben Tighe if you are looking for a great 251 professor. He sets you up well for calc 2 also.
Didn't take precalc before this class and was worried but turned out fine. Quiz every week but they're easy since we do group work which is very similar to quiz questions.

He's great. He explains really well and he's a good professor to listen to. The workload is fine, and he is very clear on his grading and expectations. My only warning is that all of the lectures are written out (and eventually erased) on the whiteboard, which means notes are vital in this class.
Amazing professor, good lectures, caring and great office hours outside of class. Highly recommend.

Professor Tighe is very kind and has a strong passion for math, but I think that he would be a better Calculus Theory professor. His homework problems are designed for proofs and the class examples are incredibly pedantic. Beware of optimizations.

His class is passable, but getting above a C is VERY difficult. Be ready to put in triple hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are 2 exams, weekly quizzes and online homework. Attendance isn't really mandatory except for one day a week he does group work and takes attendance for the week. He provides quizzes and exams from the previous year which are basically the same as the ones you'll take with different numbers. He's great and definitely cares, I recommend!
Amazing Person, Amazing teacher, makes everything simpler for you.

I took Professor's Tighe's class in the fall. It was my first calc class here at UO, I was very scared, but Professor Tighe was great! There was a lot of homework, and weekly quizzes. But Professor Tighe was always very helpful and accessible, quizzes and exams aligned closely with what is taught in class and practice exams were great! Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super good teacher, lectures were very easy to follow. Webworks were pretty difficult, but he did remove some questions that he thought were too hard. He dropped the lowest 2 webworks and gave +5 points on exams. When I took the course he had very generous grading policies idk about now. Overall nice person and teacher.

Mr. Tighe was an amazing 251 teacher. His humor, kindness, and accessibility allowed me to perform much better than I had anticipated. The Webwork he assigns is quite difficult, and not always on topic, so be prepared to sweat a bit extra on them. Other than that, Tighe was a great prof and cultivated a great class atmosphere.

There are both a lot of readings and its very lecture heavy, it's a law class. Two midterms and a final. Tippet manages to make the subject of Torts both incredibly interesting and understandable. She explained Torts incredibly well with her interesting lectures. She's blunt with her feedback but also kind of vague about it unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the furthest thing from understanding and doesn't care about her students. I dropped after a few weeks because of how insensitive and unaccommodating she is.

Professor Tippett is a Harvard grad and it shows. She's so intelligent and I loved learning from her. Every class requires that you complete the reading prior, and while the readings can be a little mundane, Tippett makes it worthwhile in class. She cold calls, and gives the feeling of an actual law school class. Loved her class, would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, her lectures are so golden. She bring personality to otherwise boring material and it is reading heavy but they're mostly worth it to get through them. Def read them all if you want to understand what the lectures are based on

Overall a great professor. He is very kind and caring, mild mannered, and a metal head of all things! (be ready for 9am metal music xD) Only 4 assignments, all are graded rather harshly. As long as you take your time, you'll be fine! Wicked smart but so much so it can be difficult if you are someone who's struggling with some of the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pack is by far one of the best professors that teaches theory. He always responds to emails fairly quickly and even on weekends (he responded to my Sunday 5am email in 1 hour.) Lecture material can be hard to understand. There are also not many assignments to do so make sure you work hard. Final exam was also wagered out with 80%< attendance.

I didn't have to take a final because he has a policy where if the lecture attendance is 80% or higher the final is canceled. Dr. Pack provides also many examples outside of European music, which is very cool for theory. I've taken many of Dr. Pack's classes including the summer review course, and he is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: available at 5am sometimes responding to emails. fantastic feedback, really cares and makes sure you know the material. two assignments were the majority of the grade, but lots of feedback could be gotten on those and mostly prepared for them. doesnt over-work students. passionate about the material and really knows his stuff. caring/understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He 's a nice person, but not the best teacher. Classes aren't organized. Makes it hard to know what he is trying to teach you. Goes off topic all the time, which makes learning whatever that is needed even harder to take in. Makes learning theory a super boring thing even though with the right person teaching, it could be super interesting.

As long as you're willing to put in the effort, Dr. Pack will do everything in his power to make sure you're up to his standards for passing. Ask him questions and he will explain in detail. You need help at any time of the week and he will meet with you. He truly cares about you and has great analogies that always stick and help you learn.
Super laid back, adorable southern white guy who actually cares if you understand the content of his class. Helpful and super respectful and tells hella dad jokes. Over all a super awesome dude.

If you don't know something well or found him confusing in lecture EMAIL HIM!  His Emails are very clear and extremely helpful.  He can go off topic, but it is because he cares a lot about the music. He also  cares about the well-being of the students.  If you are struggling in other classes he is a good resource to go to.
Yeah music theory is made extra boring with this professor, but it's not like you have a lot of choices. My advice is to definitely always go to the labs, the GTFs make things way easier.

This teacher doesn't stay on topic, is vague about what will be on tests, does not adequately prepare you for those tests, and get's mad when most people fail them. I do not find the labs to be that helpful either, and teach most of the material to myself through the textbook. Nice guy, awful teacher.

The lectures seem to go by very slowly, and consequently very little of the content sinks in until the review in labs. It's a pity, given how fascinating the material can be. On the other hand, he is very approachable, and does not mind reviewing content in class when there is confusion. He tries very hard to make sure everyone succeeds.
Absolutely one of the best professors I've had at UO!

He makes music theory even more boring. His jokes are pathetic, he doesn't teach what we are supposed to learn (goes way off topic), and does not organize his lessons. The class could be passed without even going to his lessons, just read the textbook and ask questions if you have any to the GTFs.

He has the funniest southern humor.  I remember most of the content purely by writing the funny sayings following the lesson.  He tends to go off topic a lot which takes up most of the class time.  In turn, we don't finish our lesson in class and learn everything we need to know in labs.  Thank goodness for GTFs!
Great professor, very, very entertaining lectures.

I love Dr. Williams so much; he is my favorite professor on campus. He is very kind and funny, and goes the extra mile for his students. Please take his class, I promise you, you will love it! His classes are so engaging and fun, and he is just great at his job.

Uses the online textbooks that integrates the homework alongside outside of Canvas, not a fan but what can you do (My only gripe about this man). Show up to class, do the homework, complete the 3 two page Document Analysis, easy work. Works really well with students, just please don't talk in class, he hates it.

Professor Williams is a great teacher; he's very passionate about what he does, and his class is very easy if you take decent notes and do well on the assignments. He's very laid back and often let us out of class 20 minutes early; overall a really chill person.

Timothy Williams is a great teacher. The only problem I had was with one of his GEs, Lee Gray. I would describe Lee Gray as lazy, always in a bad mood, obviously hates his job, he takes his frustration out on his students and he is very awkward and hard to communicate with. Would NOT take his discussion again. The other GEs are great though.
Great professor 10/10
Is not an easy A and requires you to work hard but is an incredible professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This was an online class and everything was very clear on the syllabus and did not change throughout the course so you know what to expect. If you do the readings and watch the lectures you will do well. There are no trick questions on the quizzes and the writing is minimal and fairly graded. Dr. Herrera was very responsive and helpful, he's great!
Literally so easy. Never had homework, and everything was graded easily and fast.

Herrera is the nicest professor ever. His lectures are often discussion focused with lots of docs and videos. His grading structure appears intense, however sets you up for success of the final project. The assignments are engaging and interesting. He is very caring and flexible. Be prepared for emotionally difficult topics.

Rating anth 329- just didn't see it as an option. The class is easy, but his lectures are incredibly boring and impossible to pay attention to. GE is great and very helpful, she should've taught the class honestly. There is an attendance grade so best to show up. Probably won't take his course again

Hybrid class.

He's re-using old lecture videos where he directly reads off the slides, very robotically. Also re-using old email templates. He seems very uninterested in the material.

Quiz questions are copy/pasted from the book word for word. Critical thinking questions are the same way. Everything is open book.

Worst teacher I've had so far.

I enjoyed his class quite a lot. The lectures were short, but the main ideas they introduced would be expanded upon in the readings. The readings were very well chosen imo and I really liked the emphasis on making connections and finding patterns in the assignments. This class has helped me understand a lot of current events.

He doesn't teach anything. Just reads off his slides word for word. It's not a tough class, but all you do is textbook reading. For the essay questions you have to be very precise because he will not give you the point if you don't connect the reading to exactly what he did. Which is crazy because you're interpreting the information.

Very interesting class on pirates and the golden age of piracy. His lectures were incredibly short, averaging only 6-8 minutes long in length. The weekly readings made up for it and were quite lengthy (compelling stuff though!). There were weekly quizzes but it was just short reflections on readings and a final paper. I enjoyed his class!
Great lectures and slides for class each day. Dan keeps the class engaged through discussions and paces each class well. Highly recommend taking any class of his for PS majors/minors.
One of my favorite classes and professors! Highly recommend.

Dan Tichenor will go down as one of my favorite professors. He is really effective at opening up discussions and facilitating progressive conversations. He has clear expectations of assignments and he is very flexible. Offers students unique opportunities to further understanding of concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Has an appreciation for the broader theme of the topics he covers. Makes you instantly comfortable and engaged during lectures.

One of the best professors I've had. Lectures were content-heavy but he made the material very engaging. Midterm and final require that you understand a lot of content but they're not impossible, just prepare for them. Overall an extremely intelligent person and passionate about what he was teaching.

Dan is the type of Professor who is wasted on lower level classes. I first had him for a 100 level PS class, and it was easy to see he had so much more to offer. This course seems to be right in his wheelhouse. He is engaged and energetic during lectures, and gives great clarification to any question he is asked. A thoughtful and amazing professor.

Dan is an easy-going guy who tries to make topics like capitalism, immigration reform, and climate change interesting to all students. Though it may be hard to pay attention in lectures if you don't find these topics interesting, make sure to do the reading for the quizzes and study vocabulary/dates for midterm and final for an A.

Dan is so sweet and tries really hard to make his lectures engaging with a lot of participation. The final and midterm were super easy and we got study guides for both. I had 100% in the class up until the final because I didnt even try to get above a C on the final because I didnt need it. Definitely recommend his class.

He does a good job of making his lectures interesting and collaborative. The reading is sometimes a lot but it's usually worth it. The discussions aren't very fun if you have a new graduate student who grades hard. Just show up and do your best and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tu he or made the lectures really exciting and did a great job presenting super interesting material. Its important to go to discussions and his lectures offer useful info for the tests. Somewhat reading heavy but they are interesting and you can get by with skipping a few here and there

Dan is very smart, however I find him to be a very dry lecturer. He can talk your ear off all class with information but does not make it interesting to help you remember. He also requires a LOT of difficult readings, so if you don't like reading, don't take this class. If you're doing it for the 400-level requirement, there's other better options
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dan does his job. The good: he's articulate, hands out outlines highlighting the most important concepts, exams are fair and challenging, workload is very manageable. The bad: Slides and notes are somewhat disorganized, throws curveballs in (borderline) unethical pop quizzes, grading and feedback are tough. I've had better, but certainly had worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome lecturer and teacher, but overall does a great job of connecting the topics in class to past an future things in the course. Does a great job at breaking down the fundamentals and putting them in tests and finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: PS106 is full of reading and I'm not gonna lie.. its pretty boring if you're not into political science. I worked really hard to get a B. The midterm was devastating and the final was so hard. But, Dan is a really kind professor and shows he cares about his students. If you take the time to talk to him he will remember you and help you out.

Dan is an awesome professor who truly cares about the information he is teaching. He is always open to talking after class and during office hours. The extra credit he provides makes it really easy to pass the class without too much stress. The tests are short answer so you can't guess your way through it. The 10 short papers were annoying though.
One page papers due each week. Two tests. Tests are not multiple choice so you have to know what you're talking about but he is thankfully not a tough grader.

He's a great guy and a very knowledgeable professor. His class is extremely heavy on the reading and requires a lot of studying in order to pass. My roommate and I took this class just because we thought it would be an engaging, somewhat easy course... and oh boy were we wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tichenor is a highly respected and sophisticated professor. This class exposes students to the general climate of u.s. politics today and how to approach the issues with a sociological framework. It will open your eyes to inequality and injustice and how to tackle it with politics. This class is an easy A and entertaining.
Dan is an awesome professor. Very nice and really knows his stuff. Awesome class, very important to keep up on readings, but they're not that bad.

So much reading!! He seems very knowledgable but I can't distinguish what he is talking about gently and what is testable material. He does provide an outline of what we will be going over in class. That is helpful. Good for studying.
Best teacher at UO so far. Very passionate and caring for student success.

Tichenor is an incredibly nice guy, who knows his stuff and actually cares about his students. If you ever have a problem with anything in the course, go to office hours. The GTF's can be tough, but remember that Tichenor's in charge, and he wants to help you out. Great class for an intro, I'm a PS major so I found it a tad basic though
Such a boss. This guy knows his stuff. You will learn a lot and you will want to go to class
Makes you work but it is worth it.
Very nice guy and good professor.

Great lecturer! He assigns non-textbook readings that are very interesting and applicable to the content being covered. If you have any problem he'll take the time to clarify it for you. Great teacher!
He is a great lecturer and very clear. He is also very open. While his quizzes are tricky he always wants to know if his students believe they are fair. He is the best professor I have had.
Great lecturer

Amazing professor. He talks fast, but is incredibly interesting. Great with one on one. Grades all pop quizzes (4 total) on his own. Gets to know the students and is very personable. Highly recommended.

Great professor. He is so smart and so clear, a little fast though and can be tricky on tests. He is really caring about his students and really wants them to learn, so he creates quizzes and exams based on how the class is. Don't be scared to speak up in his class! Discussions can be really intriguing if the students participate.
This guy really knows his stuff! He is an enthusiastic Professor that makes you want to hear/learn more.
Awesome! I did not miss a lecture, so enjoyed the class. He helps a lot outside the class, has many great ideas for inspiration.
The best teacher ever! Great sense of humor and very patient. The class was real fun! Not sure about easy As - I worked hard for this class. He gives clear guidelines and always ready to help.

The nicest teacher I have ever met in any writing class. Super easy going and he is an easy grader if you do what he asks for. He always gives the class extra time to finish our papers if we can't finish the papers in time. The bad thing is he is not teaching WR122 for the following term. Otherwise, I will definitely register for his class.

SOOO nice. nicest teacher ever and so incredibly helpful. Loves to talk and is a corcky little guy. If he sees your trying hard, he will give you an A even if you didnt deserve one. Super nice. Take him. Easy A thats for sure--and i suck at writing!

2/3 projects are group projects, they're all a lot of work. Lectures are really informative, but examples can be a bit repetitive. Tom is a knowledgeable and a good resource. The extra office hours for the final were really useful. The GE can strongly influence your class experience, but I lucked out. There are readings but they mimic the lectures.

Kind and incredibly caring to his students. He understands that construction is hard to get into and is very patient in explaining concepts in Lecture. He also set up extra office hours before the final to help his students with last minute questions!!

Was so sad to see his rating so low, he deserves better! I just had him for my first arch studio and he was beyond caring and compassionate, but helpful and I learned so so much. He guides you through the tough parts to let you have more fun with the artistic and story side of it. Love him!

Love Tom! Took ARCH470 and 491 w/ him, his project guidelines are clear, he tries to make the assignments/lectures fun and entertaining. He loves his students and will absolutely love it if you go to his office hours. He will even help you w/ your studio project if you ask. So so helpful, easy tests too! Open note, free textbook.

Very respected professor who cares for his students. He is always willing to help with projects or offer extra credit. Gives a lot of information during lectures, but you are not expected to know it all. There is no midterm or final exam, and you are only graded on projects and assignments. It is a reasonable workload along with other classes.

Tom is a knowledgeable professor and very lecture heavy. A lot of material was covered over the course, which therefore made the tests difficult. He wants the best for his students; he goes into many lab sections and offers a lot of extra credit so you can always ask questions and put in work to get your grade up.

I took three architecture studios with Tom Hahn in 2017 and 2018. He was my favorite studio instructor at the U of O! He will match your enthusiasm for your project, is very sustainability-focused, and has plenty of real-world experience in climate-responsive design. Plenty of fantastic and universally applicable information on eco-focused design!

If you try to approach him for help or ask questions he immediately gets defensive. He is highly hypocritical with what he teaches.. preaching about sustainability but simultaneously causing a basswood shortage in all craft stores in Eugene. You will find that his classes are an opportunity to stroke his ego... nothing more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams asked detailed questions but it was open book and open note, the drawing part of the final exam was absolutely ridiculous and very detailed, there was a lot of busy work especially the lab reports that were more annoying than anything, but above all Tom is extremely disrespectful and very hard to approach forget asking a question.

I really enjoyed Tom as a professor when I took him in 2019. He was often found in our lab sections and was super easy to talk to. We also were able to reach him (and the GEs) outside of class during studio hours to get help with our structure. His lectures are very dense and he likes Arizona a little too much but overall he's a cool guy :)

Very lecture heavy- expects you to remember every construction detail said in his lecture, so be prepared for oddly specific test questions. He lacks the insight of what architecture means, and has horrible taste in design. Seems like he is trying to compensate for his lack of artistic and architectural design for useless construction information.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He hates when you ask him questions and is extremely condescending. The textbook was the only thing that helped me through the course. I'm not sure why I'm paying thousands of dollars for this college education, only to be taught by a book. Very old school. We're still doing projects he taught in the 80's. That should say something about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Harsh and egotistical. He is difficult to approach for questions because his responses are often condescending. I was lucky enough do well in his class, but I definitely did not have a good experience. His studio critiques go off on a tangent and they aren't very constructive which made the class tougher.

By far the worst teaching experience I ever received; expects all of us to remember every detail mentioned in the lecture, which is impossible due to how fast-paced his lecture is. When asked to slow down during lecture by MULTIPLE students, he disregarded all of them saying, that the information provided is already condensed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took AP Calc in high school and did well, so I already know the material and only needed the class for credit. The lectures are disorganized and only on the board, with no notes or slides. She grades very strictly, even for tiny sign errors. Homework comes twice a week, is long and difficult, and takes hours of self‑teaching

She is amazing. I learned a lot from her and can't believe how well I did. Her lectures are crystal clear, and every assignment (HW, quizzes, review) prepares you for the final so well. It takes me A LOT of time to get work done for this class, but it's WORTH IT. Truly underrated, and the people who hate just don't put effort into the class. LOVE!!

this class was genuinely awful. I dreaded going to class because she would speed through every topic and make the homework so unnecessarily hard. the webwork is nearly impossible to do, and there are 2 of them plus a quiz every week. the final is worth 30% of your grade and is cumulative. she's super nit picky when she grades, she made me hate math

this class was small which means you got a lot of help  when needed. def recommend take this before math111 to freshen up on basic algebra. super understanding and helpful teacher. tests were similar to quizzes material wise.

Gives way too many webworks, quiz every week and two midterms. Moves fast in lectures and the webworks are very long and sometimes unreasonably difficult, even tutors have a hard time. Doesn't think we have other classes, webworks super time consuming and never stop.

Professor assigns absurd amounts of homework that isn't helpful with the specific coursework. I often find myself completing the homework for me to feel as if it wasn't enough as I often must consult the internet, or extensively read to even be able to solve the homework problems. Counterintuitive homework setup that just leads to more stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Thorenson is stern and gave out a lot of homework, but it was all very useful practice. Plenty of opportunity to redeem grades and receive extra credit. Replaces the final/midterm grade with the better score, drops the lowest hw. She prepares students well for exams and is understanding about extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very "teach yourself" class. Be prepared to not understand anything and feel very dumb because of it. She's very willing to help, but there's a lot of help needed. Class is extremely frustrating and difficult for a 101 class.
Super nice, but didn't actually teach anything and seemed like a pointless class as it was just getting packets of problems and quizzes on things she didn't cover.

Honestly a very good prof. Many people describe her as tough and unfair but I do not see where this is coming from. She had incredibly clear lectures, homework was well connected to in class material and she was available all of the time. I loved this class because it was the first math class where homework+tests were similar to in class material
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Thorenson is easily one of the best calculus teachers I've had. Although she moves fast she explains the material well and is easily accessible outside of class. USE THE TEXTBOOK! It's free and has a million practice problems. If you want to do well you HAVE to put in the work outside of class. The homework is awful but tests are manageable.
Class is very fast-paced with weekly quizzes and webwork. Don't skip any lectures or you'll be very behind. Prof can seem cold, but is accessible for help outside of class.

Do not take her class if you do not have prior calculus knowledge and aren't willing to spend hours outside of class teaching yourself the content. Speeds through lectures and it's hard to keep up. 2 WebWorks a week that are crazy hard and take so long. Weekly 20 min quizzes w/ no calculator. Tough grader. Learned more on YouTube than in her class.
omg the web work takes sooooo long.... and the exam is so much to be done in only 50 mins. plus ur not allowed to have a cheat sheet or anything and there's no curve........ sigh....

Do not take this class if you don't have any prior calc 2 knowledge. Its a calc class for people who are already good at integrals. Class goes very fast, and the tests are hard. if you can't score well on tests you are not gonna make it. Professor is tough, but she will try to help. It's just if you can't do the integrals well you'll fail.
not a very helpful teacher.

Never learned anything at her lectures. She moves way too fast, and only solves the problems, never explains the process. Weekly quizzes that were tough with low averages, two midterms and a final, webwork included. Exams were incredibly tough. Was always lost in her lectures. Seemed like she didn't want to be there half of the time. Curve saved me

Jennifer is a great professor! Her lectures are very clear and her handouts are incredibly helpful. If you put in the work, this class will not be difficult. She is truly a gem in the math department.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Long and boring lectures, and she goes very fast, even through difficult concepts. So many homework assignments. I bought Chegg for this class and it saved my life, I recommend doing the same. Thankfully I took calculus in HS so this class acted as a review, but if I was new to calculus, my rating and grade would've been much lower.
