Very tough professor to learn from. Doesn't really teach, just does the problem and keeps moving through the lectures. Tests matter greatly, iclicker questions are also important. There's a slight curve at the end, which saved my grade.

Jennifer's lectures were not interesting, but I don't think it's her fault since business calc is inherently boring. There was a lot of homework, and I spent countless hours putting in work for no reward. I'd recommend making sure you have a good GE, or I'd avoid this professor if possible.

This course is a very demanding and difficult one, but you definitely learn after taking it with Jennifer. She seems intimidating, but really is just a bit shy. She's very accessible through office hours, and will explain any concepts you need. She expects a lot, but if you are willing to put in the work, then you can do very well in this class.

Homework takes a long time and is graded harshly. Her expectations are very high for students, not an easy A. However, she makes no mistakes in class and is very accessible and helpful outside of class hours. You will spend 12+ hours a week on this class, but will learn quality material.

whatever you do do not take a class with this professor unless you want to become severely depressed and rethink your life altogether. my life has become math. there is nothing that brings me joy anymore. hours upon hours of math each day just to get marked down on the tests for the smallest mistakes. can't take it anymore. hardest class ever.

This is probably the hardest class I have ever taken. For a Calculus 1 class that is necessary for a lot of majors, it is made unnecessarily difficult. She spends the whole class writing proofs on the board that nobody in the class understands. Zero class engagement because everyone is scared of her. Tests suck, impossible homework every two days.

the most boring lectures of my life. doesnt explain problems at all. gives you 2 seconds to write things down/answer questions. acts like youre stupid when you ask questions. tests are the hardest thing I've taken in my life. you'll end up teaching everything to yourself on YouTube, and failing (unless youre a math god). good luck.

Haven't completed the course yet but is definitely the hardest teacher I have ever taken in my life. Tests/quizzes amount to 76% of the grade so if you are bad with testing like I am, there's no hope. and its not just me, as almost all of the quiz averages are below 65%, and the midterm averages aren't much better. lectures are monotone/boring

I haven't completed her class yet but it makes me highly frustrated. She moves through the lecture entirely too fast, giving us barely enough time to write down the problem. Same with in class iclicker quizzes so you better be fast. Weekly homework due twice a week plus one quiz every week. Homework sometimes takes hours to complete.
Professor gives good lectures with legible writing but has weekly homework and quizzes so make sure to study and you'll do fine. Generally curves at the end.

If you want to succeed then you need to go to class because the lectures cover a lot of material in a short amount of time, that being said the professor is very willing to work with the students and modify the speed of her lectures to fit the needs of the students best. Quizzes are weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jennifer Thoreson is undoubtedly the best math professor I have ever had. Amazing lectures, clear thought process, able to answer any question very thoroughly, and almost little to no errors. However, this class was extremely tough and unforgiving, and Jennifer is a strict and harsh grader. By far a very hard teacher, but an excellent one at that.

It feels like you’re getting taught by a robot. Her voice is so dry and monotone so paying attention in lecture is already a difficult task. Grades so harshly on the smallest details. No exam or hw solutions and does not curve the class at all with test averages below a 70
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So nitpicky with grading and doesn't really give you much opportunity to practice the material outside of the homework which takes up to 10 hours to complete.

Thorenson would be a great professor for anybody who learns best by reading out of their textbook, as the entire class is spent writing proofs and examples on the board, but is absolutely horrific otherwise. She is very dry and fails to answer questions in class effectively. Take her proofs class, but otherwise, she should be avoided at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class virtually during Covid. The HW was always much harder than the lectures, and the tests were somewhere in between. Doing the HW can be strenuous but it boosts your grade. For tests, no calculators or notes allowed.

In my 2 classes with Jennifer, she's been awesome. She actually is personable. In office hours, she's kind and understanding. I've never felt judged for asking a question. The classes she teaches involve lots of material, so she's focused in lecture. She proves concepts to show you why they are true. If you care as much as she does, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jennifer Thorenson is a decent math teacher. She is a really harsh grader, especially for homework- she assigns hard proof problems. Her tests and quizzes are fair though, and they do represent what she has taught in class well. Be aware that proofs will be on the tests in linear algebra.

Jennifer is actually quite a clear lecturer, but shes a little monotone, so you have to work to stay focused. She also really likes to go through derivations of things, which I think means less time to show how you actually think about problems. Shes good in office hours, though. Start homework early so you have time to go, and youll be fine.

She is definitely a tough grader and wants you to show that you completely understand the concepts inside and out. She is very articulate and descriptive in her lectures providing all the information you need for homework. If you want to pass her tests you HAVE TO STUDY DILIGENTLY. If you do the work, you'll definitely be prepared for higher math.
Overall shes kinda meh. Her tests are pretty insane though. Lots of true/false questions that are almost trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jennifer is hard to approach & can be very cold. She's condescending to students who ask questions. Her lectures are proof-heavy & lack examples. The tests are brutal & her review sheets are way off base. It is clear that she lacks a passion for teaching & is not personable. If you prefer to read out of the book then take her, otherwise avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Jennifer's expectations are very clear but she is also soft spoken and relaxed during lectures which made this class less scary. I am dyslexic, anxious, and I took this class after not having taken math for the past 4 years! I would not have passed if it was taught by some grad student. The HW is just like exams & definitely go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Clear she truly understands the material, lecture not just txbk problems, any questions you have she can explain very well and clear/simply. The hw is exactly the same as lectures, just slight diff. To know the material well enough to do any problem do all the webwork carefully so you understand. Tests are the same difficulty as HW!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doesn't give herself enough credit! she's pretty soft spoken & speaks in a monotone voice which makes it hard to stay engaged in class. She's helpful during office hours, but takes a long time to warm up to. In general a difficult class, but writes fair tests (though they err on the longer side). she replaces the lowest midterm score w/ final!

Great at explaining difficult concepts and does it at a very reasonable (sometimes slower, but helpful) pace. Great examples for homework, which although is hard, really prepares you for her tests. Overall, learned a lot and liked the  class a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jennifer obviously really knows what she's talking about. She speeds through calculus lectures like no tomorrow. The only way to learn the material well is to really do the webwork and go to office hours. She seems boring at first but she's pretty funny and nice. Very open to questions and help but just has a lot to cover in too little time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her tests are ridiculous and the class is not curved in any way. Test averages are C's or lower. Do not recommend.

She wasn't the best math teacher I have had. I feel like she failed to connect/interact with the class when she is teaching. She only gives a few examples and then expects you to understand it. But there is a lot to learn in a short period of time so its kinda understandable.

Worst teacher Ive ever had. She speeds through lectures at a pace most students cant keep up with and gives out countless hours of WebWork each week, sometimes with subjects we barely  covered or with problems that are nearly impossible to solve. Only reason I got a good grade is because I took the class in high school and knew most of the concepts

Professor Thorenson's office hours saved my entire semester grade. I was having a lot of difficulty with many topics and she was willing to work with me outside of her regular office hours to make sure I got enough help. She is not particularly friendly or warm, but her lectures are clear. She explains with examples.
