reviews.comment: Worst class I have taken at the U of O. Assignments were almost comically vague in scope, but docked harshly for silly arbitrary details that were often left out or not emphasized in project descriptions. Sadly the course material and readings on their own are fascinating topics, just handled poorly. Virtually impossible to get an A on anything.

Everything about this class is incredibly vague. I have a higher grade in Calculus and I hate math, think about that for a moment. Half of our lectures were guest speakers over Skype who would rather advertise their Twitter accounts than care enough to teach anything. We were told to write essays on topics when given little details, then punished.

reviews.comment: He assigns quizzes after almost every reading, the readings are incredibly long and the quizzes are usually two or three questions in a minute, and the answers aren't always straight forward. The lectures are just him rambling for usually over 50 minutes and they don't really apply to the midterm or tests that many people failed

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Lectures are 50 minutes of absolute rambling on occasion engaging. Still the majority of all 10 weeks of lectures are bare-bone slides with limited content and Mr.Wilson babbling about god knows what. He said verbatim, "I should be teaching at a Jesuit University Not a public University." I gave my best effort. It was awful.

This was an extremely hard class for it being an 100 level course. Get ready to read a lot just for the quizzes to be two questions long and have a time limit of 60 seconds, and also be expected to buy a new book during week 8. The midterm was hard and the class put me to sleep multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: it's baffling this was a 101 class with how demanding it was. Expect endless reading almost daily, sometimes reading entire books within a week, on top of writing essays, and reading quizzes. He isn't very considerate, giving us a midterm morning after Halloween. Lectures are often rambles, with sparse slides. The midterm average was a 58%. Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are 50 minutes of complete rambling; slides don't cover test topics, so don't rely on them. Professor Wilson is a nice man but not thorough in his teachings of humanities. Topics are hard to follow, with heavy reading for homework. If you want to understand anything, expect 1-2 hours of reading a night. THIS IS NOT AN EASY GEN ED CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Exams in this class are very difficult. Expect him to ramble in class for 50 minutes then an exam on words and ideas that he briefly talks about.

Professor Wilson seemed like honestly a very nice man, but he was very unorganized with his lectures, and if you don't attend class, good luck trying to learn the material. Overall a little boring, he just lectured for the whole 50 minutes but sometimes wouldn't even finish because he would get sidetracked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very forthright about the mindset, persistence, logical brainpower that learning Ancient Greek requires. He held nothing back on that front. But he was incredibly humorous + entertaining in his lectures, encouraged creative translations, and took positively to mistakes. Quite scatterbrained at times but also very clever. Communication is key.

I dropped this class right before the midterm. The lectures were unorganized and had nothing to do with the homework and reading assignments which made it very confusing. Expect to be reading 50-70 pages a day of genesis and the Iliad. Would not recommend this class unless you have previous knowledge of Genesis and the Iliad.

He's a nice and engaged guy, but his lectures for hum 101 were really disorganized and there was very little grading transparency. I've had easier 400 level classes tbh, which felt unwarranted for a 100 level class. He didn't make lecture or study guides, and I didn't really know how to prepare for the exam. His political jokes are awkward, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are actually engaging if you're interested in the humanities, although the content was really difficult to write about if you don't read like I did. Other than that it was an okay class and a good professor

Horrible. So insanely organized. Slides are a mess and he rambles on so much it's hard to distinguish what we should actually learn vs. what are just random opinions of his. Much of what he said I also did not feel like was accurate or true, either. Even our GE agreed that his lectures were a mess and I learned more from my GE than lecture.
In lectures he does not seem to talk in full sentences, made me feel like I was zoning out when I was fully paying attention

Malcom Wilson seems like a nice guy, but I can genuinely say I did not comprehend one word he said in his lectures. It was as if he was speaking a foreign language. Unreasonably long reading assignments, an endless list of vocab terms, and impossible exams. Everyone was lost. If you want an A, good luck. Many people were happy to have passed :/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS TERRIBLE. My friends and I took it to get an easy credit out of the way, most of us barely passed. It was the source of all my anxiety this term. Malcolm's lectures do NOT make any sense. The notes you take won't even help you. Sorry but it's a massive no from me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It has a terrible course structure that is impossible to keep up with. The whole class is reliant on dense and heavy readings, but you will never be told what to read for. He tests you on random items such as terms, locations, or characters. Not even the GEs knew what to study for. It's all random greek and biblical text

I found this class to be very interesting. It may be a little but of a jump into readings especially if youre not familiar with classic readings like the Bible and Greek writings. The Bible lectures dont take up much time though, just about 2 weeks. Overall I really enjoyed this class!

This was one of the worst classes I have ever taken to be honest. He is insanely unorganized and dumps everything on the GEs. You must attend your discussion section every week or you will fail. Textbook is confusing but mandatory, unless you are very familiar with the Bible and Greek Mythology you will be 100% lost in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm writing this after 1 week of class. This class is horrible and if you're not religious you will be completely lost. The first unit is on the Bible and talks to the class like everyone goes to church every Sunday. Instead of converting me to a christian, he's making me feel like I'm in hell.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While the class is interesting, he can ramble on sometimes which would distract me. He is super funny and I can tell he really cares about his students. One thing to mention is there's a lot of readings that are time consuming. Overall it was a helpful class to take.
Wilson is a super funny and laid back professor. Though his class is reading heavy and the essays are a bit tough, the class is well put together. Hes very friendly and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The Canvas class page was poorly organized and so were the lecture slides. It is difficult to understand WHY were talking about something in class because he just starts reiterating the story you read in between classes rather than tell its importance. We have no rubric for our final essay either.

He does not grade essays harshly, but hold student's up to writing and grammar mechanics that he himself does not meet. He teaches Latin and Greek as well, and when he talks in English it sounds as if it is a direct translation from either language (aka it is NOT clear). I'm writing this before my grade is out, but I'll either get a B, B+, or A-.

He seems like a great guy & is really into what he talks about. His lecture style is not my preferred style as he rambles on about topics & uses minimal slides. So unless you're into that, you probably will get lost. And this class really requires you to keep up with all the reading if you want to do well. This was a challenging 100 level class.

He rambles on a lot and it's hard to keep up with what he's talking about you do not like reading classics or old books DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS, the class is solely reading based. He also does not post grades until AFTER FINALS, so you never know what your grade is the entire term.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes were not pop quizzes, just attendance quizzes that you could easily figure out. Very easy to skip this class, so long as you understand main course texts it isn't that difficulty

Doctor Wilson was by far my favorite prof. His class was interesting and well paced. Great knowledge and passion of the subject material. It was a fairly easy course. Do the assignments and you'll pass. Very little homework, mostly reading which could be dry but was always relevant to the lecture which is rare. 10/10

If you are interested in all forms of ancient Greek culture from poetry to theater, gods and otherwise then this is the class for you. The lectures can be dry but Malcolm tries to make things interesting and you can tell he has a passion for what he is teaching , which is rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Malcolm is very passionate about Greek culture and his lectures are great. But we did not have a single grade posted to canvas the entirety of the course. None of us had any idea where we stood, and I received a grade lower than I had expected. You have to read 7 books. There's lots to remember.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is enthusiastic, kind, and passionate about Ancient Greece. If you want to receive an A, you have to work for it, but if you keep up with the readings and attend lecture, there is no reason for you to not receive one. The material is demanding, but is throughly gone over in class. He's an amazing professor.

I think Prof. Wilson is a good professor, but the class was hard and took up a lot of my time. He calls on people to translate, so you should be prepared to avoid embarrassment.  Also, his final is cumulative, so memorize the entire text starting from week 1 to avoid having to basically sight-read.

Malcolm is a cool guy and can be very funny at times. He gives pop quizzes when attendance gets low and discussion attendance is mandatory.His exams can be tough because the class covered so much material.It required a lot and I mean  of reading.Liked Malcolm hated the class.More work than necessary for a class intended to settle an A&L or MC req

one of my favorite teachers at UO. he's interesting and explains things extremely well. has a GREAT lecture voice and makes you get excited about learning! takes time to get to know students and has an overall happy demeanor. the best!

Professor Wilson is THE MAN! He is truly interested in what he is teaching and it shows. He wants to know who his students are and he wants them to enjoy what they are learning. He has a sweet voice and his Greek Culture class is pretty much just listening to him share awesome epics everyday. He's one of my favorite teachers at UO

He learned everyone's name by the end of the second week. Great interaction in class. Took care to explain everything well. Funny and a little goofy. Required lots of reading, but went over what he expected us to understand in class.  Knows his stuff. Some reviewers called him arrogant, but I haven't seen any of that. A good guy.

Wilson is a great professor! Yes, his expectations are high for his students, but I understand that he just wants us to learn a lot! If you read, go to discussion, and study for your exams, you will be just fine! I even slacked a little bit and still ended up with a B-. Not my greatest grade, but you can definitely do it! Take the class!!
Amazing! Loves what he teaches and gives great lectures. If you have a chance, redgister for a disscusion section with Aaron Hienrich, when you take this class.
Gives out very little work, lectures are difficult to follow. Notes are very hard to take
He's a really good teacher.

Very articulate, concise and helpful.  The course is extremely demanding, but his lax teaching style and personable nature made the class a delight.  [and the fact that he has a sexy accent doesn't hurt a bit]  :o)
Self-righteous prick, not interesting and not good at explaining things. I swear he made up words this whole course, terrible...
Prof.Wilson can be tough, particularly his finals, but his classes are always rewarding, and he has a great rapport with his students.

Malcolm is a funny and interesting professor.  He is helpful, funny and random.  If you show up for class, take notes and do the reading all will go well.  This isn't a easy class, but you'll be satisfied with how much you get out of it.
Hard, tons of stuff to remember...but if you learn it, it will help you so much in other classes
He sounds like canadian Frasier... i can barely take it
He knows his****, and is a nice guy

This guy is heartless and I wonder if he has a sole?  I needed to withdraw from his class because I had mono, so I made an appointment to see him, and he refused.  Instead he decided to give me an F, because I had some C's on my transcript.  So now I have a term with all W's, a doctors note, and one big fat F from this guy.  Awesome.  Just stay away, far far away.

Lets put it this way..He SHOULD NOI be teaching a 101 class. WAY too hard on his students and he doesnt exactly work around your scheduel so you can get help. And when you do meet with him, he only asks u questions~HE GIVES NO ANSWERS.

Very hard, but knows his stuff.  Most studnets will never see an A from this prof...but the learning experience is worth it.  I think I have learned more from this prof than any other in a single term.  Made other classes easier for me.
very detailed and yes arrogant. If you are interested in 5th century Hellenistic culture this is the guy to learn from. I took 4 class with him because he was so darn interesting.

The arrogance of this man. He once even told the students that were finishing the term off with a review of the professor that he didn't care what they put because he was tenured "so try and rate me low, - you can't get me in trouble." What a jerk. He thinks every word he speaks some how makes the world better.
Class was super interesting but all he cares about is spelling and memorization! Doesn't care if your working hard, not understanding.

Strict on spelling and wording; have to memorize over 60 trees common name and scientific. Also does not allow for make-ups and isn't very caring when it comes to absences no matter the reason. Lectures are interesting but the quizzes are nearly impossible to get a good grade on due to strict grading and heavy focus on memorization.

Pros: Lectures are interesting. Outside for the 2nd hour of class. 2-3 page readings
Cons: He marks up papers worse than an English prof. Botanical names must be spelled exactly (hyphens, capitalization, etc.) and he tries to trick you on tests. He looks for very specific words in short answer test questions. Also, he does class during review week
Such a harsh grader. You will learn how to write, but still a lot of reading and writing. Would recommend if you really want to learn.

although I thought her class was a little boring i felt that i really learned a lot from her teaching and feel like a stronger writer.

She is an amazing econ professor, she really was engaging to listen to during lectures, and went through examples in class that helped my understanding of the content. The practice midterm was helpful and reflective of what was on the midterm.

Very smart professor but seemed like she had other priorities in her life that made her attention not enough for our class. This would also be visible during her office hours. When asked for further guidance, would say "I don't know why you're just not getting it." I wouldn't recommend it since she's not helpful or gave many in-class examples.

Prof Wong is one of the best professors in the Econ department. Her 311 class is a balance of theory, deriving the mathematical models/graphs, and real world connections (pizza and beer, iykyk). EC311 is definitely a weeder class, but she sets up lots of opportunities for help. I'm an Senior Econ major, and her 311 class was my fav. Highly respect.

Not enough practice problems leading up to tests make it difficult learn how to answer questions presented on tests. She's a very intelligent professor, but I think many would have greatly benefited from examples in class that accurately reflected the types of questions on exams.

I LOVED her!! I think she's an incredible teacher and cares a lot about her students. She taught in a way that worked so well for me; she explained everything about the real world to help students understand better. She's also incredibly brilliant and knows what she is talking about through and through. (Practice test is basically the test too)

reviews.comment: I had a great experience with Professor Wong. If you are planning on taking EC311, be sure to have a strong understanding of the fundamentals of calculus and you should have little problems. Lectures are long but if you're actively following the problems, it's not a bad experience. She genuinely cares about your progress in class, very recommended.

Definitely the most personable econ prof I've ever had. She does explain things fairly quickly, but if you did alright in Math 241, the math is very manageable. The course content altogether is tough, but an A on the curve is certainly obtainable if you put in the work. Her rep is only bad on rmp bc the avg biz student expects to be handed an A.

If you are a business major take any other professor's section tests that are worth most of your grade and study materials are basically useless. She's very smart. Will teach things very quick and it may seem tough, but the tests are much easier than the things she covers in class. So as long as you go to class and participate a bit you'll be good.

Teaches a very hard class but she's a very nice person. Offers extra lab sessions to study and you can earn extra credit. Super smart and professional, but she moves on a very fast pace, so go to office hours often if you want a good grade.

reviews.comment: Prof. Wong is extremely knowledgeable and educated in the subject she teaches. reviews.comment: Great professor. She is fantastic and she does a great job lecturing. You should take a class from her

reviews.comment: Super knowledgeable in her field and great at answering spur of the moment questions. Reviewing slides and papers is vital to doing well in this class.

I can honestly say I gained close to nothing from this class

reviews.comment: Very funny professor , I strong suggest you guys don't take her class , trust me

Wow. I've had my fair share of professors here at the UofO but this one just takes the cake. Homework is worth a big portion of your grade and extremely tough (you almost won't be able to answer anything using her lecture slides) Lectures are not intuitive either; she over-explains everything and doesn't take time to properly clarify the process

Nathan is/was a great professor. He always pushed us to go further and made sure that we understood what we were learning/talking about. We talk a lot in class which at first was a change from previous classes (we talk in small groups about 85% of our class) but it's the best way to talk in Spanish. I feel like I learned a lot from Nathan.

SPAN202 is content-heavy and can be intensive, regardless of the educator. Professor Whalen is patient and attentive to needs, learning gaps, and success in the language—understanding the lifelong process. Participation, attention, and effortful engagement during class time are key to the instructor and vital to success within the course.

Nathan Whalen has been one of the most incredible Spanish teachers I've ever had, his willingness to help his students and engaging lectures made this class enjoyable. While yes, his grading may be tough, he is only trying to make you put the work in to get the outcomes you want (in your grade).

At his ripe age, his haircut is too interesting not to look away from, and quite frankly it was rather distracting. Overall is an unhappy and mean individual. Gets a high off of catching students use google translate. Thinks students will care when its a required course. i hate spanish now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nathan is an amazing lecturer/teacher. He will genuinely give you enhanced perspectives on various subjects and topics. Loved taking Spanish with him.

Great professor with interesting and entertaining lectures. There's a fair but of homework, but nothing crazy. SPAN 301 exams were a bit challenging, but there are several other big grades to offset them. He gives great feedback on all of the work which really helped me feel prepared for the final paper and exam.

Prof. Whalen is great! Short readings that are really interesting are discussed in class in a very easy-going manner. It's important to participate and share your ideas. It's clear he enjoys teaching and it very passionate about Spanish. Very clear expectations, highly suggest!
Just a rude and mean person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If youre bot confident in you Spanish abilities/if u struggle languages he will make you feel worse about it. Taking his class completely turned me off from wanting to learn spanish. Extremely rigid in his grading, wont give u the extra .2 percent needed to pass cuz hes an un empathetic authoritarian.

Made me and multiple other students cry. Is egotistical and plays into an unfair power dynamic. Doesnt care that youre paying thousands for the class. Critiques you heavily in a condescending way. Also assumes ppl give a crap about learning spanish when its a language requirement for many.
Calls on students who do not raise hands, tended to be discouraging if answer was not correct.

Gives out schedule/rubric in beginning of the class and follows it completely, you won't ever be caught off guard. A lot of homework but is usually easy and beneficial for your learning. Nathan is very clear and very knowledgable. Ask questions if you need help and he will answer them. Super cool guy. But be prepared to fully participate

reviews.comment: The curriculum is already set so that part is easy. He is very passionate about what he teaches (though sometimes that gets old.) He really wants you to be 100% involved with the class but everyone has there off days, he doesn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nathan is a great teacher! Very passionate about Spanish and I truly feel he does as much as he can to help everyone succeed. If you put in the effort you will gain a lot from this class. Very important to go to class everyday and participate. I would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nate is a good teacher and clearly wants his students to succeed. I was intimidated by this class initially because I took a term off of Spanish but he grades really easy and catching up was not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I liked him as an individual, but he is a hard person to get to know. He has moments of frustration when we can't speak in Spanish, but he reverts to English half of the time. Makes no sense to me. Honestly, he grades you on a rubric that is handed out the first day, but you'll have to work hard if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Whalen is a professor who cares about your grade but he makes you work for a good grade. I would suggest going to his office hours, he tries to help you and it shows him that you care (helped my grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I've had Whalen for SPAN 305 & 308, and I've really enjoyed it. He's a great teach & very passionate. Plus, you'll hear cool cultural stuff that no other professor will tell you. One thing that does suck is he doesn't post grades to Canvas, so you have to go to his office to find out your grade. But he provides great feedback and is very helpful.

this class has made me really begin to hate my Spanish minor. I have taken several 300 level Spanish classes and none of them have ever offered tests in the way he does. It is so difficult to focus in this class, and I regret taking this class. If you are a first language Spanish learner it will be easy, but other than that it is so HARD!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nathan has been one the best Spanish professors that I have ever had. He made sure that everyone was engaged and participating while also making it fun. He is very straight forward about what he expects from his students and gives good feedback. I will definitely try to take more classes with him in the future.

Ive always loved spanish, but have hated spanish classes up until i took my last spanish class with whalen. the class was so interesting and he was so enthusiastic, making me want to be there and want to participate. my spanish was actually improving just by going to class every day, which is very rare for a UO spanish class. tuition $ well spent.

I love Nathan! He is a bit intimidating at first. If you don't care about Spanish or your grade, find a different prof. If you want to learn and are prepared to work for it, he is great! Passionate about the subject and knowledgable as well.  I was often hesitant to share and was called on a lot, but all my mistakes he corrected quickly but kindly.

In front of the whole class he seems to be engaged in teaching and cares, but go to him during office hours and ask for help, he's not very kind at all. Tried to go over an exam and was blunt with what I did wrong but wouldn't explain what I was doing wrong grammatically and did not want to offer any advice to fix the problem.
He expects everyone to pay attention and participate which was great, considering in other Spanish courses I have taken there had been a lot of awkward long silences. I would take his class again.

Nathan is the only instructor you should take 305 from. He is very passionate and knowledgeable on political change and will be sure you know it too. My Spanish skills improved greatly. However, he is extremely intimidating at times. If you are faint at heart, save yourself the anxiety. Not afraid to randomly call out in class. Would take again.

Easily the worst Spanish teacher I've ever had.  Although he speaks a lot in English as well as Spanish, what he expects from assignments is always extremely confusing and poorly explained, even if you go to office hours and email. Condescending towards his students and treats everyone like middle schoolers instead of adults. Don't expect sympathy.

Whalen is an academic in the strictest since of the word. The man knows his content upside down and expects you to get the majority of it. He is intense in both positive and negative ways. If you are easily intimidated by firm eye contact and a strong personality, don't do this to yourself. If you do the homework and show up you WILL learn a ton.

I loved professor Whalen's classes so much that I took him twice. I especially loved 303 - all we did was study artwork and listen to music. A great class - if you want to improve your Spanish, this is the class for you.

I have enjoyed Spanish for years, but I dread his class. He's incredibly condescending and always responds in a patronizing tone. He says that to learn a language you must be unashamed, yet he consistently makes his students feel ashamed for not understanding or remembering something. He also never responds to emails, so communication is difficult.

Worts spanish teacher I've ever had. He does not answer your question directly, and is definitely not helpful. He makes you feel dumb, and that is one of the worst things when trying to learn a second language.
The worst Spanish teacher I've ever had!! He is very arrogant and his attitude makes him unapproachable.

Nathan is an absolute gem. He gives difficult tests and requires a lot of writing homework, but my Spanish improved by leaps and bounds in his class. His methods are tough but effective, and he's a fabulous guy. Going to his office hours are intimidating but enjoyable and helpful. I can't say enough good things about him. Definitely worth the work.
excellent teacher, you get the worth of your money
Nathan Rocks! My friend and I took him several times throughout college. He's very nice and easy to talk to. He makes himself available outside of class time when needed. I recommend Nathan 100%!

Nathan demands participation, effort and attention from every student — which can lead to his appearance as a tight ass. If you have trouble paying attention, he is not for you. However, he explains everything in a very clear and interesting manner. Have no doubt, if you take this class, you are going to learn Spanish —  or you are going to fail.

The most arrogant professor I have ever had in college. He has no sympathy towards students who may have a harder time learning a language, and grades for fluency, instead of progress and improvement. Very moody and gives quizzes almost every class. Do not take his class.
Nathan is a tough grader, but he makes class fun. He really knows his stuff, and is really willing to help you out. I would for sure take a class with him again.

He is a pretty hard grader for quizzes and tests. Do not sit in the front row if you don't want to be called on. He always calls on people in the front row, or if you look bored to death he will always call on you. Very passionate but talks to you like your stupid sometimes. Good teacher but kind of a dck.

He is a hard grader on quizzes and tests. He also isn't clear on his grading rubrics, and doesn't write down due dates. BUT I really liked him as a teacher!! He was challenging, passionate about the class, and an overall great guy! I really suggest taking one of his classes.

Nathan is a great teacher and highly cultured, he knows his stuff. Highly recommended for students who are willing to throw down some time to actually work at their Spanish - he is always willing to help. Kind of intimidating when it comes to tests/quizzes but in the end he just wants you to succeed. You'll do fine.
He is a really nice guy who makes learning fun

Nathan made the this class fun and re-sparked my interest in Spanish (I was ready to be done with the language after 6 terms). He breaks the language down in a way that makes it interesting and fun to learn. He speaks Spanish 99% of the time but will translate if you need. He's available for help outside of class time too. He is GREAT!
Great teacher, extremely clear. Knows what he wants and communicates it clearly. If you're taking Spanish make sure you take it from this guy.

Like most Spanish teachers who are not native speakers, Nathan has had to do a LOT of studying to master the language and so he expects his students to do the same.  He knows a ton about the Spanish language and culture, and honestly has really inspired me to continue with Spanish.  He is not condescending at all unless you are consistently late.
Nathan is super-knowledgable in language and culture, and is a great teacher. He takes no BS, you actually have to work in his class to do well.

Nathan is a pretty good Spanish teacher. He uses scare tactics to do your homework and study for quizzes and tests, but in the end it helps you. Can seem a little intimidating but in the end just wants you to succeed. Takes his job serious but is pretty funny too. Just do your homework and ACTUALLY study.
Very nice guy.  Easy going. I wouldn't say the class is easy but you will get a lot out of it.

Took Nathan for 201 - 203.  He is the only reason I (an all A's 1st yr student) survived 2nd yr after having withdrawn from my 1st attempt @ 2nd yr a yr prior due to a different horrid prof.  Have to think those w/complaints here expected to have grades handed to them.  Nathan is very compassionate & very knowledgeable.  You get the grade you earn.
Nathan is awesome!

Nathan is a great guy and teacher.  You will learn SO MUCH from his class, but you have to work for it.  Not an easy A class at all, though.  Definitely go to his office hours, because he will treat you better and help you a lot.  He really cares about his students.

It was my first class at the University and the impression I had was that he is harder than most other profs. There were surprise quizes and the grading was very tough on homework. The easiest part of the class was surprisingly the tests. He is approachable and a good teacher but you will get ****ed gradewise if you take his class.
just plain mean! I got a's in all other Spanish classes and he gave me a B-. Very hard and unfair grader. Avoid him if you can

The most caring professor I've had at UO. Tried to push me as a student and keep me interested. He will treat you differently if you go to office hours, so go! He inspired me, one of those professors who cares. But he was a super hard grader and his teaching methods were hard to learn from. He is super approachable and willing to to work w/students
This teacher was really stressful and not helpful. He was, at times, challenging; However, it did not make up for his strategy of teaching which did not progress my spanish in the least.
This is the best class I have taken at UO. Nathan is enthusiastic, very well organized, approachable, and interesting.  I definitely recommend him.

My first term with Nathan was really tough. He is hard-headed and speaks almost entirely in spanish. He has an authentic passion for Spanish and wants to help you as much as he can. My second term with him he seemed a lot more laid back. He's fun, but he stands  firm on his teaching style. Give him a chance.  You might hate him at first, but he's c

Horrible teacher. He was really rude and controlling. Ignored the students in class. If he didn't like a question that you ask he would just skip over you. Horrible, please do not take any  of his classes.

Nathan is very knowledgeable, and has a lot of enthusiasm for the subject. He adds interesting anecdotes about places he has traveled each day in class. Exams are fairly easy. The study materials given out weeks before exams are typically exactly what will be on the test. Nathan can be a bit abrasive and almost rude at times.
The class is great. Professor Whalen is extremely helpful and the classroom has a very relaxed environment. If you keep up on the work from day to day you will not have any problems. :)
When I first saw him, I thought this guy is gonna be chill and nice...not at all!  He does go through the material clearly, but he can be mean and egotistical, and he has no compassion
Organized class...thought nathan would be a chill hippie, but really strict and up tight. Not very helpful, knowledgeable, but not helpful. Almost rude at times.
EGOTISTICAL! Condescending, mean, humiliating, shows no compassion towards students. There is no equality in the classroom. Seems to be mad at the class all the time. Not the slightest bit flexible.
No Comments

Great Professor, excellent in the Spanish/Latino language program. You have to work in this class. Only thing was his sometimes "don't care I'm right your wrong" attitude. It got to me sometimes...but overall a great teach.
Nathan is a great spanish teacher, one of the best I've ever had. He also seems like he's a cool guy, a little on the hippy side, but absolutely my number one spanish teacher pick.
tool and definaetly not hot
nathan is a badass...he brews his own beer, plays lots of instruments, and kinda looks like jesus, which is hot.
Learned much from this long-haired leaping gnome.

Nathan Whalen has a passion for the Spanish language and culture which could be a good thing however he tends to take it too far to the point where it can be intimidating to ask him question, because he has a way of making you feel like you should have known it before asking.
He is a great teacher and a great guy.
No Comments
You can't help but like this friendly, bearded, smoking hippie with the Speedy Gonzalez accent.

I really loved her class, she had great lectures and explained things thoroughly and clearly. Definitely a decent amount of hw in this class, but it prepares you well. Class was challenging but you learn a lot. Overall a very considerate and fun teacher that covered the material in detail while making it easier to understand.

Possibly my favorite instructor to date. Prof. Wong is a very nice person, with a good teaching philosophy and time management. She is also good at explaining chemistry concepts in simple and memorable ways and can be pretty funny. Homework is dense, but great preparation for weekly quizzes and tests, which can be difficult but never surprising.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher with a lot of office hours. There's a lot of homework and things due on Friday's which can be annoying and weekly quizzes that are graded harshly but good explainer for difficult concepts and a lot of available time for feedback.

Incredibly kind professor with a lot of supporting material for the class. Class concepts get hard but she provides a lot of support and is always super helpful. I would 100% take it again and am sad to be leaving her :(
Cathy Wong was a wonderful teacher, very helpful and easy to get a hold of outside of class.
Not a lot to say other than great professor! Class is just a little tough in general.

I couldn't recommend taking a class with Prof. Wong enough! She goes out of her way to show how much she cares about students, including holding more office hours than I've ever seen a professor have and taking feedback from students. She wants her students to succeed and ensures everyone has an opportunity to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I couldn't praise Professor Wong enough! She makes chemistry easy to understand, using metaphors and analogies while mixing it with science to make it all make sense. Homework was manageable though not light. While attendance/participation was part of your grade she had zoom available on days you couldn't make it to in-person lecture!
Professor Wong actually cares about her students success and is a great lecturer. She gives students plenty of resources to be successful in this course.

Best lab professor I've had! There was a lot of work for the course but it was organized well and none of it felt like busy work. She was really caring and wanted to get to know all the students. Lectures were amazing and super clear. The labs were fun and informative as well.

More difficult subject material in comparison to CH 221 and weekly quizzes. However, the lectures are great and made very digestible and understandable. Highly recommend taking this class if you care about becoming proficient in chemistry.

For real the best teacher I've ever had, which I did not expect after being told to be wary of chem professors in college. Lowkey spoiled for all of college now, no professor will ever compare to her. So supportive and actually cares that we know the material and is willing to explain things and encourages questions. LOVE HER!!!!

Cathy was awesome. Very knowledgeable and was excited about teaching us. Going to office hours just to do homework was really helpful; she'll stick with you until you figure out the problem. I would never have guessed it was her first time teaching CH224. There was a lot of homework, but hey, it's an honors class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Assigned so much homework I would get overwhelmed by the pages of descriptions on what to do that week I would shut my laptop. Would always go over time for zoom discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this online course, especially if you're an undergrad. So much work with very little direction, mostly self guided learning. Quizes, reflections, 1000 lectures and readings to do pretty much every week, way more than usual in-person lecture style classes. Prof Wood is sort of supportive- but  expects way too much out of students.

This teacher is not suitable for teaching. Extremely inappropriate and unprofessionalism behavior was displayed in multiple emails. I have never had problems with any professors before her. Cannot express enough how displeased and annoyed I am that she is STILL EMPLOYED AT UO. Should be fired effective immediately.

she was a yapper. would consistently talk until after class was over and had to leave the meeting in the middle of her speaking. no respect for other classes students needed to get to next. took it online so was easy to cheat through it but it was still a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SO SO much work for a beginner-level class. Don't bother taking it unless you're prepared to spend every spare second of your time trying to finish it all. SO overwhelming with the workload. Someone needs to tell Prof Wood this isn't a graduate-level course and making everyone spend 20 hours a week on bio isn't making anyone more interested in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful. I'm someone who hates to leave reviews let alone bad ones but if I can save one soul from suffering through this class it will have been worth it. Find ANY other class to fill your science gen ed. This class should be a 400 level class with the workload you're given. Do yourself a favor and pic a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I think Prof Wood is knowledgeable, but she gives too much homework. The canvas grade is not reflective of your actual grade due to the way she grades work so be sure to understand that. If I could go back and do it again, I would find a different class to satisfy my science gen ed. She gives extra credit, but the class is still hard to follow

She is a very sweet person, but an awful professor. She assigns an inhumane amount of work and barely teaches any of it herself. You're basically asked to teach yourself all the fundamentals of marine biology with the occasional aid of her mind-numbingly boring lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Demands an absurd amount of work to be completed for an intro-level bio class. Boring and horrible do not take unless you're willing to make it your part-time job to learn about the sea

I really liked her as a person! However, especially for online classes, she was awful. The course was really disorganized and due dates/descriptions for assignments were all over the place and sometimes conflicted with each other.
Dull lectures. Didn't learn much I hadn't had in other classes.

If you put work into Michelle's classes, you have the opportunity to learn a huge amount. She is receptive to questions and her class discussions are interesting. She also allows you to focus your learning to what you are interested in within the scope of the class. I would highly recommend her if you are interested in marine sciences.

She's a sweetheart, but her classes aren't for everyone. You get out what you put in. There are multiple assignments in different areas, so if you miss something,or do poorly, it won't kill you. However, the schedule/outline for the class will be vague, so I can be hard to make a schedule, but she'll help you when you need it!
No Comments
one of my favorite classes. Prof actually let us put half the questions on final exam. Highly recommended!

So so passionate and knowledgeable about environmental law! However, if you're not interested in law, don't take the class. Environmental law is so intensive and complex, so it is important to attend and pay attention in her lectures. They can be long and sometimes boring, but she explains the concepts well.

Prof. Wood's lectures are extremely boring. She talks for 2 hours very fast, leaving students to go through hundreds of slides to find what they couldn't write quick enough. Midterms are easy enough if you study for at least 3 hours. She is lenient with late work, which is a god send and something I appreciated. If you lock in, you'll do okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is very passionate about teaching environmental law. She is a very tough grader, though, and can be mean sometimes. She can be nice, but also passive-aggressive. Don't take this class if it isn't for credit.

She is by far the most passionate teacher I have had thus far, and constantly works hard to inspire her students about environmental law and climate change. She loves what she teaches, and it shows in her lectures. She can be a tough grader however. If youre interested in learning about environmental law, take her class!
Professor Wood is extremely caring and passionate . Her lectures are very long and FULL of content. If you're not interested in law then this probably isn't a class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Always almost fell asleep during her two hour long lectures. I wanted to rip my hair out whenever I was there, it was that boring. She's a very caring professor, just not my type of class at all. Be prepared to read 30-40 pages out of the textbook every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is a very good teacher despite the fact she doesn't know how to handle most of her technology used in class. She is a very understandable and approachable person who is an expert and active participant in environmental law. She integrates intersting material and keeps the class updated on new cases and climate summits. Love her!

She is a very good teacher in the sense that everything she says is on the power point, and reading is optional after the first midterm. Before the first midterm, reading is mandatory. Gives a question by question review for the tests.

Key phrase: Global Warming. She spent most of the course discussing global warming & how property rights are obsolete. She is very sweet and she tells you exactly what is on the exam. The only problem is, it is a typing test. Whoever can type the most, gets the best grade.

A great teacher - doesn't hide the ball or focus on theories.  She gives you law in a straightforward manner.  Keep up on readings and go to class - you will learn a lot.  She and Prof. Aoki use the same syllabus; both are great profs.

Prof Wooten is literally the best! He cares so much about his students. The class was an easy A but one of the best taught classes I have ever taken. He tells personal stories and makes it easy to understand hard topics. Taking a class next term just so I can have him again. Take if you need credits but you will end up learning a lot from him.

He is literally an angel and I am taking more of his classes just to see him. I'm not sure about his other classes but this one in particular was insanely easy. Gets you cultural credits with no sweat off your back and a teacher who really cares about you.

Professor Wooten was very nice but often went on long tangents. The class is a very easy A. Like ridiculously easy. Lectures are not mandatory, and he gets a little bit boring. There is a weekly quiz which is 3 questions online, and there is one midterm. Take the class for a passing credit, not to learn something interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally an awful grader, I submitted both my midterm and final with quotes from the various textbooks and knew what I was talking about and still received a 65 and 75. With no feedback as well. the assignments mean nothing because of the weight.

LOVE Wooten. He is actually so sweet and cares so much about his students and the material. His lectures can get a little slow, but he puts in so much effort to make the material make sense and apply to the real world. There were weekly 200-word responses for discussion sections, the midterm and final were open-note, open-book essay questions.

Super nice guy and passionate about what he teaches! Waiting for my final to get graded which was three 300 word responses and a couple multiple choice questions. There are weekly 200 word reflection papers and content from discussions is important to being prepared for the midterm and final! I really enjoyed the lectures and content over the term

Course was read three books, write 3 essays. Lectures went in depth over material w/ daily quizzes on the readings. Simple enough and turned out to be one of the best classes I have ever taken, Wooten gives super interesting lectures that strongly engage the class to participate and inspires deeper levels of analytical thinking. Fantastic overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love Wooten so much! He had amazing, inspiring lectures that had half the kids changing their minor to food studies by the end of the class. He really is an amazing teacher and very understanding. The workload is very doable, and he accommodates extra needs. You will not regret this class for his lectures alone. Also, he handed out snacks a lot!

Very kind professor, grades in this class: 10% weekly discussion participating (10 total meetings), 30% midterm (very easy midterm assignment, like very), 30% weekly attendance quizzes (extremely easy if you're in class, somewhat hard if not), 30% online final. Very passionate and kind, lectures are a bit boring, but this global p. credit is easy.

Prof. Wooten is one of the nicest and most caring professors. He's handed out snacks and treats, told some of his life's stories, is very giving and always has a warm smile. If you go to the lectures you don't really need to do the readings most times and he does have a lot of guest speakers come.

One of the easiest classes seriously. Caring professor and gives free snacks. Lectures themselves were story heavy and would often go on tangents. Very nice guy, but not sure I left with a lot of knowledge, going to class wasn't really that needed. Weekly quizzes were easy and very easy midterm.
Awesome class, lots of free snacks and he's very nice. Good grader and easy midterm.

I took GLBL250 Online Spring 2024 and Wooten was a great professor. His course is straightforward and not confusing to follow. As long as you write well, you will do well in the class. Professor Wooten is also just a friendly and welcoming presence that puts this class at the top of my "insightful and educational yet laidback" classes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He will assign 5 essays for your midterm and final. He assumes that this class is the only class you're taking so good luck even taking another class. Don't even get me started with Garrett the GE. He will take every opportunity to cold call you in class and then push his liberal thoughts down your throat. Take this class as a 4credit term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof Wooten is great and I'm not sure why his rating is so low. 
He doesn't give out homework so you only have assigned readings outside of class. 
He gives take home essay style exams and you have multiple days to complete them. If you participate in class and do all the readings this class is easy and super fun. 10/10 low stress and fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super sweet and nice professor, not sure why his rating is so low. Can be a little rambley but I really didn't mind it

You could tell how excited he was to be back in the classroom and teaching in person. He brought some extraordinary personal experience to this class which made it very interesting. The assignments are very thought provoking and pull on ideas learned from the great readings throughout the class, if you don't mind reading this class rocks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wooten is definitely my favorite professor at UO. It is quite clear that he really cares for the well-being and success of his students, which is rare. He brings an interesting life story and perspective to the classroom. His lectures are great and keep you engaged.

Wooten is such a sweet and caring professor. He is one of my favorite profs since im a global studies major and i have taken a couple of his courses. He definitely knows a lot about the topics and is super passionate about them. He definitely goes off on tangents and this class is centered around books rather than actual material on Africa.

I took Africa Today with Wooten this term. You can tell he's passionate about the subject, which is good but also he's so into it that sometimes we moved slowly during lecture while having to read a lot outside class and take a new test every 2 weeks. He's a nice guy who cares about his students, if you understand the books you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wooten is a nice guy, but do not take his class. It's mind-numbingly boring. He goes on tangents, and practically every one falls asleep. If you are taking an INTL (now GLBL) class just to try it out to see if you'd like the major, don't let this class sway you. Unfortunately, this is the worst INTL class I have ever taken.

The lectures are posted on Canvas and you can save yourself about an hour just reviewing the slides there. Wooten rarely covers content during class and when he does he presents the information as if he were teaching elementary school students. Most people stopped showing up to class because it was literally pointless. You will need the book.

Wooten barely covers the course content during his lectures. Not a single person thought the lectures were worth their time. Additionally, he put incorrect information for dates on his slides which cost me letter grades. He is very unprofessional and won't admit his mistakes when addressed. Condescending towards students. Avoid this professor.

SO BORING literally just talks about his own life and posts all slides so it is not even necessary to show up to class. This class made me sad because I wish I learned something from it. He talks as though students are dumb and spends way too much time explaining the most basic things. Made me feel tired and stupid.
90% of lectures are tangents. Condescending. Will literally never talk about the content. Still a boomer even though hes an ethics professor. Felt like a huge waste of time. Sorry Wooten.

He is very passionate about what he teaches, but he has a tendency to go off on tangents unrelated to what the class is about and likes to over-explain topics and terms that are standard knowledge for college students. You really need to know the material for the tests, but he was chill and let our final be online instead of in class.

His lectures and the class itself were very interesting. The only negative comment I have is that the I didn't feel prepared for questions on the midterm and final. I feel there should have been more preparation on his part. Like give us an actual study guide instead of just telling us to "review the slides."

Seemed like Professor Wooten glossed over a lot of the important parts of global ethics, which is what the class was about. He focused on the positive side of things, which is extremely limited when looking at anything on a global scale. Seemed like he had unrealistic opinions about the topic. The class was saved by the GE leading discussion.

Stephen is the best professor I've had during my undergrad. He is an amazing man who genuinely cares about his students and what he is teaching. This dude loves food, not like some kind of glutton, but he seriously gets giddy when talking about new, unique foods and drinks. Like a jolly, giggly foodie. If you get the chance, study abroad with him!
Although he does not assign a lot of assignments his lectures are amazing which makes the material much easier to grasp! Take this class!

You need the book for discussion. The final and midterm are purely based on the slides though. The final and midterm total 80% of your grade, half and half and the discussion is only 20% so you need to study hard for the midterm. They are essay style questions for the midterm/final. 6 essays questions and write about 5. he' friendly engaging boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great proffessor. Really cares about his students and he's passionate about the class material. Makes coursework exciting and engages the classroom.
Class was very interesting
LOVED this class and Mr. Wooten!!!

OMG SO BORING. He talks about general ideas and concepts ALL THE TIME. It's like a sermon with him preaching. No attendance is required, he basically regurgitates the book in the slides. Essay questions on the tests. Do the discussion section readings as they are always on the test.

Wooten is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. He is passionate about what he teaches and is very friendly and nice. He tells stories and gets involved in good discussions instead of reading off of his slides. This is an extremely interesting class (even if some of the case studies may be a little dull). GREAT professor!!!!

He's a very engaging prof. He talked a lot about his experiences in Africa, which made the class more personal and interesting. His GTF did all the grading, which sucked. If you don't read, the final will be very tough. It was all essay questions based on both required texts.

Professor Wooten is one of my favorite professors outside of class- he's very engaged, caring and interesting to talk to. I loved his class, the only complaint was that he got off-topic a lot. Most of the lectures came from the text, so study one or the other and you'll be fine.

This class wasn't hard, but you have a different lecturer each class so you have to take good notes. Tests are based on lectures. You have to write a 1500 word paper on a book, but it wasn't too bad. It is an interesting course.
His style of lecture is very boring. I often fall asleep. He just talks stuffs off the textbook. Nothing challenging or exciting. Boring class! Not recommended.

Wooten is amazing! Contrary to whatever people have written, he actually cares about his students and our opinions! I chose him as my advisor for these reasons. He is exciting and fun to listen to. His tests are extremely directed at what we discussed in class and he uses the reading simply for reference. No tricks here, a good guy with a big heart

Prof. Wooten is a great professor. I've had him for two classes - INTL 260 and HUM 315. In INTL 260, his lectures are pretty much just from the book and he manages to keep the class engaged by sharing lots of personal anecdotes. Likes to go on tangents. Very approachable in office hours and likes to get to know students personally.
Great teacher! Super nice, interesting, and passionate about the subjects. The class was easy because he kept the students engaged. Highly recomended!

Hes a smart guy, and loves teaching. hes really good at organizing the class, and keeping it on track. but beware this man likes to talk and does NOT stop!! He is also hard to contact outside of class for help. But besides that he was good. I learned  A LOT in his class. very informational. pretty easy grader too, at least for this class.

Excellent teacher. Very passionate about subject. Lectures are directly out of the book, but he does throw in extra facts that will be on the test, so be sure to go to lecture. He is very approachable and will listen to what you have say.

Okay, he is nice and the course materials are okay. But seriously... he is officially the most boring professor in U of O. Everyone who had him agreed that he's boring and his voice is like a sleeping pill. His boring teaching style makes it impossible to stay focused during the class... Oh, and he made no afford to know his students.
I have had him for two different classes, and he is definitely an interesting person to listen to, but he does like to talk a lot!

Wooten was a very interesting speaker. He does like to talk a lot and will pull one of the most random question on test from something he said in the lecture. He asked us a question about his grandmother... Great personality and energy, his GTF's were very helpful. Tests are pretty based on the book and lecture notes.
he's fun and interesting to listen to, I have him again this term from INTL445
Really nice guy, really put me to sleep in class.....

Very, very nice man. Friendly to everyone and enthusiastic about his topic. Extremely interested in students' opinions, and often spends the entire class just listening. I think he's a great guy and I learned a lot.

i liked as a person but is seriously the most boring person...do not get a class in the morning because you WILL fall asleep! and you need to do the readings because the tests ask you questions from them that are really specific!

I enjoyed the class. However it seemed as though he was missing a huge part of the underlying issues surrounding the topics in class. We scratched the surface but didn't fully acknowledge the true problems. He also would have outbursts in class of the way he felt about our class.
extremely nice person, okay prof, tests are "key phrase" things, not much tested on reading only lectures
No Comments

I enjoyed his lecture style. The only complaint is that he grades his quizzes on his catch phrases or certain words not on the concept. He is very patient with students who ask a lot of questions and seemed to take a great interest in his subject. I am not sure I would take another class from him, but I am not interested in his area either.
No Comments
No Comments

Took for 101-201. She is very intimidating in class but a decently kind grader, especially for 101.
KRN has a sharp learning curve, you really need to pay attention the first couple weeks or you'll be lost. Def. need to master the alphabet.
I wish there was a little more lenience on attendance, especially if getting the work done and learning well.

I had Professor Woo for 100 levels and she was an amazing professor. She is very organized and knows how to effectively teach a language. Her assignments are very straightforward and she helps students a ton. She will try her best to support students if they are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lets students speak disrespectfully to her and others in class, play on their electronics, and will then reduce the work load and class material taught when they whine to her about how they can't do it. It isn't really higher education. Talks loudly during tests she is proctoring and does an excessive amount of product placement for Starbucks.
Very nice and great professor. A lot of outside work but an enjoyable class and I felt like I learned a lot

reviews.comment: KRN 102 was harder than 101, but because of the content. Professor Woo is always quick to clarify any questions clearly. In her way, she is funny, although her voice is soft so I recommend sitting at the front and don't fall asleep.

honestly, the worst professor i've ever had. doesn't really understand english and grading system SUCKS! had straight As since middle school before this professor, no amount of studying can help you, sorry. nice guy though
Very bad, I hope he knows it because it's very disappointing. Worst teacher/professor I've ever had.
very strict grader with vague instructions

I took Calc3 with her at JHU. Amazing lectures and great explanations. Midterms are very fair and quizzes are easy. Good computational explanations.

Weekly homework assignments worth 30%, participation worth 10%, final group project worth 10%, midterm take home worth 30%, final take home project worth 20%. reviews.comment: It's like she can't decide if she should baby us or not. The homework's graded by a grader where WAY more lenient than what she graded herself. Overall, Kayla is very nice and I liked the way she structured the lectures. Only 1 midterm and a final, but the exams are graded a LOT harder than the weekly homework. We also had group presentations week 10 which we only had about a week to work on and was also graded harshly. If there were no group projects, I would take her again

Good professor, she isn't the best but tries very hard, she is new to teaching. Grading was harsh, and homework was basically all of the grading for this class. If you are a responsible studious individual you will succeed in this class. She is very kind and is very good at math, she seemed very nice and patient. I would recommend taking her.

She would give us very simple problems in our hw and in class, then give significantly harder questions on tests that honestly felt very unreasonable. She would frequently make mistakes in class that students would have to correct, and felt pretty passive aggressive at times.

I truly wish I could rate her higher, she was kind and had good lectures. But the expectations were insane. Tests were take-home, except she said they would take us 1-2 hours and ended up taking most of the class at least 7. She graded extremely harshly on the tests and the expectations had not been reflected in how the homework was graded.

She never puts grades into canvas, you have to essentially guess your grade. A lot of the male students would sit very close and take up lecture time too

reviews.comment: Hands down the best math teacher I've ever had (not an exaggeration). She's so attentive and caring to any issues you may have, and she'll do her best to help accomodate your needs as best she can. I've never had a teacher as kind as her. If you have the opportunity to take her class you should totally do it, I can't recommend her nearly enough.
very nice and understanding, great lectures

Kayla's lectures are engaging and digestible. Lots of examples and a desire to make concepts that can seem pretty abstract make sense. Two take-home midterms that reflect the work done in homework well. The homework is pretty involved, but really promotes learning. Highly recommend!
Leah was an amazing instructor, and I highly recommend anyone to take one of her yoga classes at least once.

I took PEMB 201 (gentle yoga) this term and she is very understanding and caring. A great yoga teacher, and if you are looking for a yoga class that is relaxing take this class. We only stood up about three times over the term and I really enjoyed it.

Leah is an incredible yoga teacher. She aims to please everyone and will gear her teaching toward the general mood of the class that day. She accepts requests for how she instructs her class during yoga and has a very soothing voice.

I've taken her paddleboard yoga class and vinyasa yoga and she has the most calming voice. She asks people what the vibe is and bases her teaching based on how people are feeling (tired, tense, energetic, etc).

Daily quizzes (5 or so are dropped) are very similar to test material. Lectures are engaging and super interesting. Highly recommend Andrew as he's a great guy AND highly recommend bio calc over regular calc.

reviews.comment: I cannot say enough good things about Andrew. I had him for 246 and 247; he's amazing. The daily quizzes have one or two problems very similar to classwork from the previous day, but he drops 5 or so of them. He's funny, super approachable and incredibly available during office hours. He really wants you to succeed! TAKE HIM IF YOU GET THE CHANCE!!

Andrew is an excellent teacher, especially considering that he is a grad student. His lectures are well prepared and organized. He delivers them with commendable enthusiasm and humor. He's a great teacher and person who wants his students to understand the ideas behind equations. There are daily quizzes and a lot of HW, but it's worth it.

I would definitely take another one of his classes!

reviews.comment: Andrew was a great teacher! He was always willing to help an always thinking of way to help the students. Calc is a hard topic so he was always willing to hold office hours and practice sessions before exams. I recommend him to anyone.

Best math prof. at UO. Clearly explains concepts, and genuinely cares if you understand the material. The exams are just like practice examples and homework, and he gives daily quizzes to make sure youre staying current with the material. Highly recommend him!

Andrew is by my favorite teacher at the university. I took his class over the summer which was fast paced but I just spent went to his office hours multiple days each week and he was more than willing to help. Many times he stayed hours past office hours ended to help myself and other students. Most caring guy ever. I got an A+ because of Andrew.

Nigel is hands down the best teacher I have ever had and the best human I have ever met. No one has had as much of an impact on how I see the world and my interactions as him. Nigel has an aura that makes everyone around him happier about their life. He is caring, smart, wonderful. There are not enough words in the world to describe his impact.

Best teacher I have ever had. Better than any professor. Nigel cares about his work and is very inspirational when teaching. He knows his stuff, and he teaches in a way that reaches out to college students. If I could forever take his classes, I would. Highly recommend him and his classes because I promise you will not be disappointed.
I wish he taught all of my SAPP courses.
AoD Pharmacology is my favorite class so far here at the UO. Nigel makes an almost three hour class fly by.

Nigel is awesome! He really loves what he teaches about and really is a down to earth, cool teacher! Definitely would take another one of his classes! Makes these longs SAAP classes fun and engaging. Love, love, love him

Nigel is one of the absolute best teachers I have ever had. He is incredibly passionate about the topics he teachers and adamant about creating an open and engaging classroom. The assignments and readings in his classes are generally minimal, as his focus is primarily on experiential learning. I have learning more in his classes than most! :)

Nigel is the man! I had to miss his "mandatory" class one time and he let me come up with my own alternative assignment instead. Easy grader, has great personal stories, and just an all around chill guy!
Very fun class and learned a lot. Made me rethink what I wanna do in my future career-wise.
he is a very engaging speaker, and i learned a lot in his classes.

This is the best teacher I've had. Ever. In my life. Period.  He's one of those teachers that you'll remember for ever.  I had him at PCC in Portland for two terms and I wish I had taken him last so I wouldn't be full of woe when I don't get teachers anywhere near are radical as he!
an amazing teacher that everyone should get to know and take a class from.
Nigel Rules!!!
Amazing instructor.  Very helpful and fun

If you are going to take marketing 390 at UO, definately take it with him. You will love the class, super easy, always get out early, and tests arent bad at all as long as you study the notes he gives you! Very interesting class, take it with him!!

Peter was an outstanding teacher. Lectures were engaging, classes were short, and I learned a lot about marketing, and the class increased my interest in the subject. The class stood up and applauded on the last day of class

He is the sweetest soul ever!!! I have him for 462 right now. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to do well. Youchang is awesome. Took him for FIN462. He's fun and always excited to teach. Yes, the material is difficult, but just practice the quizzes and you'll be set for the exams. Great teacher!

Tough course to take but Wu makes it his best effort to try and explain the content. Lectures can be long  but you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. He work's almost every problem in class from homeworks as well as student questions. Solid professor to have.

The material for this class is complicated and tough, but Wu did a solid job teaching it. Most of your grade comes from the bi-weekly review questions and the two exams. Slides were always quite confusing and will go onto 10-15 minute tangents where you can tell the class is no longer paying attention. Towards the end of the term, students stopped showing up and would prefer to teach themselves due to how confusing the classes were.

Game theory is math intensive so Wu is good at giving examples, but I dont think his grading criteria are fair (10% on homework, 40% on midterm, and 50% on final). He's a smart man who means well, but gives the hardest exams. Class averages were in the 60s for both exams we took. Multiple answer multiple choice questions suck, and they're a staple of every test and exam he gives. He makes an easier class more difficult than it needs to be.

the best professor I've ever had

I enjoyed Haotian Wu's class. He is very knowledgeable and approachable. You can tell he wants you to learn the subject matter and will help you if you're having a hard time with it. Nah he was working hard but accounting is one of the most difficult classes that I have to study. Anyway, if you feel confident about your knowledge, go ahead and take him, if don't, you should not take his class.

Tough to understand.
straight out of china. can barely understand him. his english was horrible, but he knew the material really well.
he has a heavy accent and is hard to understand, flies through topics without clear explanation.

Thick accent, calls on students to answer questions and cuts them off to explain the answer before they get a chance to respond. He has a hard time understanding questions students ask. Poor grammar. Definitely would not take his class again. I retook the class with Hansen and got a C+ in it (almost a B-). He is a tough grader and does not teach well at all. I found out he is the only teacher for EC 360 and I need that class so I will have to deal with him again. Avoid taking his EC 311 class.

Joe is one of the best economics professors I have had at the U of O. His lectures are well put together and you really come away with an understanding of the material. This is my favorite teacher so far. He is very helpful and teaches so well, I haven't even opened the book yet. Very clear on everything, teach lecture for first hour session and then some practice problem during the second. If you finish the practice problem earlier, you can leave early. Easy homework. She is very clear and concise when teaching. Come to class and you'll likely get an A.

She is clear and lets you know exactly what will be on exams. Her lectures are informative and you should always go to her class. Her midterm was easy but she didn't prepare you as much for her final.
Best Chinese teacher ever !!!

Signing up, I assumed I would get another Chinese teacher with a tough accent to understand, but Professor Liu turned out to be an incredibly clear and helpful teacher.  The way the class is structured it's very easy to stay on top of things with fairly little effort outside of class. If you go every day and pay attention it should be no problem.
She is a very nice professor. Always willing to help and explain the material. Although the class is boring, she uses examples to make it easier for the students to connect to. Highly recommend her!
Professor Hu really knows her stuff, and is very willing to explain and help students with material. She is enthusiastic about the topic and willing to help students with any difficulty.
Xing is an awesome teacher. Final was a little hard, but as long as you put in a good enough effort and participate in class, it'd be hard for you to get anything less than an A-.
Xing's class is rigorous and offers very useful analytical tools. Awesome class!
She is a nice and excellent teacher. Although the topics in OBA335 were challenging, she explained well and gave us enough examples to understand.  I hope to take her other classes!

Xing is a good teacher. She prepares well and always motivate us to learn. There are some quantitative subjects which are challenging, she provides enough exercises and examples. She is very fair in exams.

Xing was hard to understand and she wasn't able to explain concepts past the definitions in her slides. Her examples are too simple. On the bright side, her exams are fair.

Take this class with anyone else!

Tianyuan (Eddy) does not know hot to give a class a lecture. He makes a moderately difficult class impossible. Eddy basically failed the entire class on the first midterm exam and did nothing about it. Do not recommend.

reviews.comment: Eddy is a nice guy. He was accommodating to fit extra office hours that worked for me. He'll readily stop to answer your question in class and - in case you were curious - he speaks perfect English. All of that is all well and good, but I agree with the 2/08/2017 rater - he's very technical and it's tough to follow along without outside resources.

MATH 341. Eddy's lectures fall into an awkward middle ground sitting between mathematically rigorous and colloquially accessible. Often provides formal proofs using incredibly informal language, which is frustrating for everyone, math major or otherwise.  Nice guy, very knowledgeable,  tends to either over/under-complicate matters.

Took Calculus 3 during my first term at the University, and out of all of my instructors of the term, Tianyuan Xu (Eddy) was easily my favorite out of all the instructors. I think it is worth to take his class, he described things very clear. Anyway he is helpful. The best math teacher in U of O I think.
