best math teacher in UO
Extremely organized teacher, doesn't throw you any surprises on exams. It's an accounting class so it will obviously be hard, however he gives you all the tools you need to succeed in his class.

From all the intermediate accounting classes this one was the "easiest" or should I say the less hard. He has an accent but is not heavy as previous comment said. He is knowledgeable, approachable, and always willing to help.

Xuesong has an accent but it's not thick at all and it's easy to get used to.  He is very invested in making sure each student that puts forth effort understands the material and seems to actually be passionate about making the material relative and uses class time well.  Definitely one of my favorite accounting professors here.

He is very through in his lectures and examples. Tests are pretty straight forward.  He is a bit hard to understand at times because of his accent but you get used to it pretty quick. He is about average, not great but not horrible
Wow. Either he has improved in his communication considerably since the previous comments, or they are just off the mark. No problem understanding his English. Good guy, good teacher.
Hu is a horrible teacher and no one should ever take his class!

Went to the first day of class and could barely understand anything he said. What I could understand made very little sense. cant understand a word he says. try to avoid!

This guy is awful, I had 4 years real world accounting experience when I came into this class and now I have no idea about accounting, confused more about the subject than I ever had been.  This teacher has 0 real accounting experience and he emphasizes topics which have little relevance in the real world.  Book taught teachers are horrible!

Dr. Hu has a somewhat thick Chinese accent, but is still lucid in his lectures. The class is very fast paced, but that is necessary for the course. Dr. Hu is obviously very experienced in the field of accounting and provides a good course for a beginning accounting or business student.
he is a good teacher kind of hard to understand but he makes sure you get his points.

He's plenty smart, but this is his first year actually teaching and has no idea how to actually get the material across so it's understandable, also has an accent still, so he sorta speaks in broken english

Save yourself the money and take classes with literally anyone else, because it couldn't be worse. She does not want to see her students succeed; rather, she seems to feed on their misery.

Shes not as bad as most people make it out to be. She teaches a 2hr class that isnt super interesting, so most people dont go or leave midway through and complain about their grade. Ill admit the lectures are mostly just copies of the textbook, but if you just sit through the lecture and answer one easy question, most of the material is intuitive.

Before I talk about Angela, a brief note on the class: Most of your grade comes from in-class participation, so the class is like dogfighting for extroverts. Easy A+ if you help with group projects.  

As for Angela, she's the second least competent teacher I've had after 5 years at UO. But she's new, so cut some slack while she learns to teach.

She's not the best professor by any means and her lectures are essentially just copy paste from the textbooks. However when she gave instructions for the projects her instructions were clear and it was clear what we had to do. She encourages you to participate and come to class and even if you mis a few its fine and you don't get punished rly.

reviews.comment: Angela is a wonderful instructor. The class is very easy, and the test questions are literally from the textbook, quizzes, and lectures. All you really need to do is show up and participate, and it's an easy B at the minimum. The people who are mainly complaining are the flaky people, and are the ones you don't want to have on your group projects.

I have no idea how she even got a job as a professor. She should not be a college professor by any means. She does not treat students with any respect. She does not care if students have to leave class early for an actual job. She gives half credit for attendance for that even though they are leaving to go to work.

This course wasn't hard by any means, but she made it worse than it needed to be, I heard multiple students get turned down for questions because "we aren't working on that right now". There was a lot of guessing on the grading since each time we would ask it seemed like there was a new version of what was needed. The lower ratings are right.

Overall, just not a good or well-organized course. She seemed abrasive and at times mean. Classes were hardly interesting, and the group projects were never clearly explained in class. Most of the time was spent just sitting there, wondering what was going on.

Not sure how she earned three 5* reviews, the plethora of 1* reviews are far more accurate. Lectures are just copy and paste from the textbook; class activities seem to just waste time. Her feedback is useless, and certain expectations can only be met if you happen to ask the right question.

took BA 316 with her. Group projects are the majority of the grade; if you have a bad group, it is over for you. She is an extremely tough grader. I got a 95% on every test but still ended with a B due to my poor group. Participation matters in class and she will dock your grade if you don't ever raise your hand to ask a question or answer one.

Such a good teacher, she is my favorite "business" teacher by far and I've taken a lot of business classes at UO. You will 100% get an A if you just study for the three tests. Very little homework. Her lectures are not bad and her in-class activities are fun. She does go a little fast but it's manageable. Definitely take her if you can!!

BA316 The other reviews are somewhat harsh, she's not that bad. She goes so fast through the slides & focuses so much on in class activities that are a waste of time. 2 midterms, 1 final, all were made up of prep questions from class, so they were easy As. Take this class with a friend because we have at least 5 in class activities every class

FOR BA316: Angela is a great professor. She focuses on feedback for her teaching and implements positive change quickly. I really enjoyed her class and found the work extremely manageable. Horrible. Cold calls in class, and lectures are basically her re-reading the textbook. She is clueless and not good at teaching. She gives us an exam but doesn't help us prepare for it. When a student asks her questions, she asks other students to answer
does not lecture good at all, mandatory participation that will drop your grade and cold calls in class. only allows 2 absences.

She bragged first class about receiving a teaching award but this entire term has been utter chaos. There is next to no structure to the class and she refuses to lecture. She does class activities that have no relevance to the course then expect you to know everything. The first midterm average was a C and she told us to try harder. Avoid her.

She cannot even manage a classroom for a class where she is supposed to teach about management. The class should not be mandatory if all the teacher will do is sit down and ramble. There was a Kahoot in the class where 1/10th of the class got the answer right. None of the material felt relevant to what was on the tests or the group projects I did.

This guy's funny asf. The class is hard cause it's a finance class with a bunch of math but he cares more about you using the correct equation rather than getting the answer right. I like that and so does everyone else I've talked to about him. If you're honest to god gonna take this class, make sure this guy is your professor. He's just better.

He did a good job of teaching the material and keeping the class engaged, it was just rough material with even rougher tests. If you have to take this class as a requirement, he was a great professor to take it with.

Super chill, always there if you need help. Made what seemed like an intimidating class, actually pretty exciting. Homework is super light. Midterm can be replaced by the final if you do better on it. It is a tough class but he makes it as easy as possible and explains concepts really well. If you have to take this class take it with Yuchi.
Goated prof. Somehow makes boring topics pretty interesting. I was consistently excited to go to class.

Yuchi is pretty goated. He is young and smart, and while his class isn't very hard, it isn't a cake walk either. He grades off of a weekly homework assignment, which is a 10-question Canvas quiz. Also, a Midterm and Final, in which the Final can replace the Midterm score. Concepts get a little confusing as the class goes on but he explains it well.

He has great intentions, however is not prepared in class. He could not solve his own practice midterms, solves his homework incorrectly, and marks us down when we get answers correct About 1/5 of the class is spent by Dante having to learn the material, then trying to teach it to us. He is friendly and genuine, but does not know the material

Had him for Game Theory. I promise this is not an exaggeration: he consistently made errors in class, office hours, slides, quizzes, and homework. Didn't cover methods to complete the homework in class occasionally. Overall, Dante is not simple in his communication or teaching methods. Spent a lot of time outside of class teaching myself content.
Would confuse himself during lectures and ask the class for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Beginning of the term was rough and content felt rushed and hard to understand, but after the mid term the class got much better with content taught at a much more reasonable pace. He said it was his first time teaching the class, which was understandable, so I am sure anyone who takes it from here on out will not find the class to be half bad.

311 is a very hard class so you are going to have to go to office hours and study a lot on your own time if you want a good grade. That being said, he goes by the lecture slides very quickly, but you can tell him to slow down. His entire class is very easily accessible, and there is a lot of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Look, it's his first year of teaching, I believe. The first couple of weeks were rough, but he took our feedback and tried to make changes. Econ 311 is no joke. It's hard. He tried his best and is overall a nice guy. There's one midterm and a final. He uses a wheel to call on people. There is a large curve aswell.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This ec311 class has taken years off of my life. Dante consistently displayed a lack of understanding of the material that he himself is teaching. Horrible lectures and inconsistent teaching styles make it almost impossible to understand lecture. He also takes attendance with a massive random wheel and intimidates students DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ben is awesome! He is always there to help and truly wants the best for his students, I have not had a professor so caring in a long time. The class itself is fine you just need to make sure you actually understand the notes you are taking and the homework you do.

The class is fairly easy. The homework assignments and quizzes follow what you learn in class and are fairly easy. There is many opportunities to work in groups. Tests are a little hard but you get a 1 page cheat sheet and are not too bad if you study. Ben is a good professor and great communicator.
No comment

Ben is a very kind and knowledgable professor. He is very clear in assignment expectations, and does a good job at connecting course work to current events. Very similar structure to other OBA courses with the addition of a fun online simulation
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very eager to get feedback to ensure we are understanding what he is teaching. You can tell he likes his job. Although he doesn't take attendance, it is important to go because you will miss a lot if you don't.
Amazing professor, super respectful and helpful!

Super nice guy that is great at simplifying concepts. Lectures can feel long but that was expected with OBA, though he cuts them short a lot. All assignments are really easy, and you are allowed a whole cheat sheet for the exams. I definitely recommend Ben.

Ben is a great teacher who knows how to simplify complicated concepts. Almost everything he goes over is written/illustrated on his slides which you can go back and review. The midterm/final is easy because it is open note and exactly like the homework problems. Make sure you go to class/read slides and you will be fine. Easy to get a good grade.
Hard to understand but very nice guy, just study a lot and you'll do great.
Not much to say, great professor overall, not much homework, super kind.

I enjoy taking this class with Prof. Yang, he is generous! I got below the mean for midterm and final was on average, he curved, now Im on the range of b+. Study the review slides, especially focusing on the conceptual stuff and understand it. IT WILL SHOW UP ON THE EXAM! The calculation part is hard, so be prepared and practice A LOT!

One of the things I didn't love about this course is you never got to see the correct answers to some of the assignments as well as the midterm. The study guide for the midterm was also very vague. The course had weekly quizzes and assignments, and the grading criteria were clear.

Ben is my favorite OBA professor. He knows his craft very well and will help you feel confident in the material if you put the work in. If you struggle understanding OBA, this class will be difficult, because he assumes you are prepared coming in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are hard to understand but the material was fairly straight forward. The midterm was easy but the final was incredibly difficult. He gave us problems never seen in class or on the homework before. He also gave no practice final or study questions beyond our in class quizzes and hw which barely helped.

Lecture heavy with lots of posted lecture slides, but they are very general and don't show clear step by steps. Doesn't post the answers to example problems which makes reviewing difficult. His final exam was VERY difficult and very abstract from the HW and quizzes. HE DID NOT PREP THE STUDENTS WELL FOR THE FINAL. No review or practice materials!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory. However, if by chance you miss any in class exercise, it will significantly damage your grade. Overall, the materials are not hard, just need to pay attention to details. The final project is a good exercise to test you if can apply what you learn. My suggestion: Choose your teammate carefully and wisely!

Ben's lectures are a bit confusing to listen to, and the directions he gave concerning the Littlefield games that we had to participate in throughout the term were inaccurate and led us to make decisions that cost us a lot and negatively affected our grade. The second half of the term increased in difficulty and his review for the final was no help

Yang is way chill if you go into his office hours. His class is pretty easy and he makes it easier because he will answer literally almost anything you need help on. Get help on the cases and youll be fine in the class.

WHAT AN AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! Keli Yerian is the kindest, and most helpful teacher I have ever had. The class is so interesting, and the textbook is written by students and her. The textbook is also free and extremely interesting to read. The lectures are interesting, and you get to listen to very cool stories and presentations from other professors
i would love to take her classes again but have no room in my schedule

Keli is a very kind caring professor who is very clear and concise on the work due and what you need to pass the class. There is no 
tests for 144 so that is a plus. You can tell Keli is very interested in her work and truly applies herself to her lecture. While the class tends to linger at times and may be a little boring, I would still recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Yerian is the best prof I have had here at the UO. She is the only one of my teachers who takes the time out of their day to learn each of her students name, and her classes are over 100 kids each. She finds a way to make such a large class personal. The class isn't too hard, no tests just projects and it is a very collabrative class.
Dr. Yerian is the best! Take her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Yerian is a passionate, kind, and experienced professor. She is professional while providing activities for students that are fun and engaging. There are guest speakers occasionally, but most days are lectures with activities. As long as you participate in class, you'll be set.
Loved this class, super interesting lecturer, felt inspired to take more Linguistics classes after LING144.
Professor really cares for you. I haven't had a teacher who wants everyone in the class to succeed and meet their true potential this much since 4th grade.
Professor Yerian is awesome. Super nice, fun lectures, and in general just a great professor to learn from. Highly recommend you take a course with her.

Professor Tan is very smart, informative, and kind. However, she had her assistant Robin grade most assignments. This was problematic as Robin was unprofessional and probably the hardest grader I have ever had in my college experience. Frustrating as it was, anyone else who enrolls in this course probably won't have to deal with her.

Epic course. Every lecture was phenomenal: interesting and cohesive. No need to do the readings if you take solid notes and understand conceptual aspects, BUT the readings are integral for the papers. Paper grading criteria abundantly clear, a quality paper will get a 100. Also, get the book used off of amazon, mine was $3.

Tan is a very knowledgeable and respected professor and anyone who is somewhat interested in politics should take this course. However, I think it is important to remember the heavy western-liberal premise of the course itself, and some of the general portrayals of both the past and present of the CCP are sort of misleading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my 2nd course with Tan, she's a really good professor who knows her stuff and gives in depth feedback when you reach out for help. She's a tough grader and a majority of the assignments (quizzes and midterm) are based on the lectures only. Participation matters for your grade, this class is enjoyable but you do have to put the work in.
very good, smart, and fair imo. The class is challenging but if you put in work, it's definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tan is amazing! She's very knowledgeable about the material and tries to answer questions in depth. There are few assignments for this class, so it's important to do well on the work so it doesn't hurt your grade. There is a lot of material covered, but I think if go to lecture, keep your notes organized, and study, you'll be good to go.

This class was really difficult but it's the most I've learned in any of my courses. There aren't a lot of assignments and the material can be tough but as long as you take good notes it's pretty easy to get a good grade. This class takes a lot of time so if you have other time-consuming classes you might want to wait for another term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is very smart and knows what she is talking about. The expectations are clear, but they do not round up no matter how close your grade is to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yeling is a harsh grader. You get little feedback, and there are only about 4 assignments. She doesn't always answer questions clearly. Her final paper prompt is delivered on Friday and turned in the following Monday.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading about trade and globalization which I've never been interested in, but for some reason in this class I was so invested in the readings. The activities she planned for class were so fun and Tan is super caring, relaxed, and smart. I also took Politics of China which was more challenging and history-heavy but nonetheless a good time.

I recommend this class to anyone serious about politics. There are few assignments so things are weighted very heavily, and the rubric isn't exceptionally detailed. I managed without doing too many of the readings but had to compensate by really paying attention to the analytical political-sciency applications of her lectures. great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yeah there was a long essay but it was doable, just keep up with the readings and lectures and you'll do fine. The grading is tough but as long as you diligently do the readings and not skim over them you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
The final is about a 6-8 page double space essay which only gives you 36 hours to finish, and such requirement is not transparent until near-final. It will tell you it's an EXAM at the beginning, I wouldn't say I liked this insufficient transparency of the syllabus. Looks like a fraud for me. 

And, the liberalism premise of the class is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. It helps if you already like ps. There is a lot of readings but you can get by w skimming tbh as long as you retain enough to say smth in class. All in all she's a really understanding teacher that makes lectures engaging. One class presentation but she doesn't grade too hard. There's a weekly writing that's not bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very intriguing class. The lectures don't regurgitate the readings, so it is good to follow both. That said, I managed to get by with only partial readings. The grading is clear and there aren't any group projects. If you want to learn about the history and role of China, this is a great class to take!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a very interesting class, and with so many things happening in the global sphere involving China, this was the perfect time to offer/take this class. The lectures and the readings are each very much their own things. If you focus on one, and neglect the other, you will lose important information and context. Do the reading, go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at the University of Oregon. He's a tough grader sometimes but it's always aimed at making you a better student. He will bend over backwards for any students who need help and seek it out.
One of my favorite teachers thus far. He takes a potentially dry and boring subject, and makes it fun. He always interjects humor into his lectures which keeps them interesting and fresh.
Don't take this teacher.  You might learn SPSS but it's boring and hard.

your grade is made up of four quizzes, the final, and a group project. you can either drop the two lowest quizzes or not take the final. the class was so curved that my 69% got me an A- in the class. he wasn't very helpful but that's just my opinion. if you understood the material, you'll do great. otherwise, it's pretty tough

Optional to take final exam to drop 2 of the quiz scores. 4 "quizzes" overall which are all open note, open book, open internet. Come to class because he does all of the demonstrations in class. Super helpful with questions and very nice. Let us leave 15 minutes early each class if we opted to not have a break in the middle.

Doesnt communicate the content well and his teaching style is poor. Tests are in depth and problems build on each other so if you make any mistake many subsequent questions will be wrong. Tests are LONG, about 90% of the class ran out of time during final. Only positive is the class is heavily curved

awful experience. requires the book for hw but material is explained unlike the book. only positive is the class is curved beyond belief because the whole class suffers due to his lack of getting through to students. would not recommend taking the course, find another professor or take a different class

Professor Ying is a great teacher and can help you create good portfolio work. She is hard to understand sometimes because if her soft voice. If you put in the work you will get a really good grade. She will help you with projects to gain ideas and tell you what she wants, other teachers beat around the bush when it comes to being clear.
she tends to ramble and over explain, but she is great to bounce ideas off of. not a lot of technical knowledge, but can really help conceptually and give you ideas. does more with less.
She talks on and on about the same thing in five different ways. Projects are interesting and benefits portfolios but I have never had to sit through such an awful digital art critique.

Young is a goated proffessor, overall cared about your grade and learning and gave you so much help with learning catagories in german. Never went too fast, everything was posted and just an understanding teacher. Its hard getting a good teacher and good grader these days but mr. Young is that man.

Honestly best professor I've had, and possibly will have. Extremely down to earth, super informal, and a great environment all around. The tests/homework were easy as long as you're actually doing the homework and trying to learn the language. You're graded on your effort in learning, not perfection.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super nice guy and amazing professor! I had him for both German 101 and 102. Loved his class highly recommend

Jeremiah is good. I took his class simply for an arts and letters credit. It was very middle tier. Definitely not bad and he is super passionate about what he teaches. He's invested in his students and his classes are super conversation heavy. Also. SO. MUCH. READING. not too much work though, which I appreciate so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy and easy to root for. But oh my god was there so much reading. I took the outlaw saga class and sagas are already hard to read but 60 pages due every class felt almost impossible. Professor is awesome, but if you arent super passionate about the topic and know you won't read, then i would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jeremiah is a great professor and is passionate about the subject so that makes it enjoyable. Decent amount of reading, but is beneficial to the lecture and group assignments.

Just a genuinely great professor. She is willing to go out of her way to help you with course content you might be struggling with and works very hard to make her course engaging. Absolutely loved taking the 300 level classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. She has everything you would want in a Japanese teacher. The amount she goes above and beyond is genuinely staggering at times. If you mention something in class that she doesn't know, she goes and looks it up on her own time and presents it at a later date. Lots of work but of course there is. It's a five credit language class.

O'brien sensei really cares about her students and their learning. Every lecture is formatted in a way that gets you to practice ideas in mutiple forms. There are a lot of homeworks, quizzes, and small oral performances but every assignment is simpler than it seems and she is always happy to help you. The workload makes sense for the topics.
Best Japanese teacher I have ever had. She is just incredible. Amazing person and teacher.

Super kind!!! My favorite Japanese teacher here by far. 
She is funny and understanding of the difficulty that is learning a new language. She is open to helping outside of class and has a very open demeanor.

O'Brien Sensei was kinda nit picky when it came to grading, and was strict about attendance. I don't think this class was the best for learning about Japanese business and it wasn't too bad. I took it because I needed it for my major and I would take it again if I needed to but it's not my favorite.

Professor O'Brien was incredibly fun to learn from. She is incredibly enthusiastic when teaching and is very flexible with schedules and assignments. Whilst there is a lot of homework, quizzes, writing assignments, and oral performances it is all manageable. The GEs and Professor O'Brien are willing to help you out every step of the way.
Very sweet and understanding teacher, would def recommend. There is a lot of homework but it is relatively easy and it is not serious if you miss a couple assignments.

If you are new to Japanese, she is a great teacher to have, but if you have previous experience, she will hold you to a high standard and hold it over your head. Given that I have previous experience, she would remind me of my experience when I wasn't up to her standard. She may be coming from a good place, but it turned me away from the language.

O'Brien sensei is the best JPN professor! She makes learning Japanese fun & uncomplicated & is enthusiastic so her lectures are always super engaging! You can tell she's passionate about teaching and her positive enrgery is just so contagious (I always looked forward to her class!) As long as you study, attend, and do the homework you'll do great.

O'Brien is a great professor and understands that you won't become fluent just by taking through 300 level Japanese. She is really helpful outside of class and knows how to assist everyone individually in class. The small class sizes she teaches really helps her to have a focus on everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was my first college level Japanese class and I loved it. She's really friendly and cares about her students. I'm signing up for her class again next term.

Amazing professor, wish she was still teaching lower level classes. She goes a bit slower than other professors, speaking and material wise. She is also willing to re-do sections if the class still doesn't understand. Very friendly and extremely helpful! Can't wait to take her classes again!
Very very very nice lady! She respects all your opinions and she love to help students with passion and patience. Love all her classes! Would love to take her classes anytime!
perfect

I. Love. This. Woman. Absolutely adorable and loves what she does. She has so many Japanese classes, but makes each feel like they're her favorite. And I think, deep down (or not so deep), she just finds Americans endlessly amusing.
What a sweet heart.  One of the nicest japanese instructors in the program.

I took O'brien-sensei for 202 and 203 over the summer, she is a great teacher. She's very nice and helpful, though sometimes she teaches a bit fast. We didn't use the textbook, but we did use the workbooks a lot. She made the class enjoyable and was very fair to everyone.
Very likable. Goofy at times but still a good teacher.
art 154

not the worst professor, but far from the best. this was such a hard class to attend as it was extraordinarily boring. I stopped attending after week 8, just did the in-class exercises on my own. she's sweet, just a shame that the subject is god awful, and the amount of FORMULAS that are within the material is mind boggling. Take the guy professor

Nice professor, but the class is mind-numbing. She moves really quickly so its hard to grasp the material. Tests were way harder than the homework and in-class exercises, made it hard to succeed. Would not recommend but unfortunately its a required class.

The entire term, I don't think I ever felt anything other than, "I'm in class right now, I should pay attention." That pretty much sums up this class it's like unflavored pudding. You'll learn a bit, do some homework here and there, study for a test, and do fine. But overall, it suffers from the lack of attention Oregon gives the OBA program

YuanYuan does provide clear slides that are helpful to learn the content from. However, she does move extremely fast and sometimes makes very vague comments that confuse you subtly. The midterm was a 60 minute test with too many multiple choice and written questions to be answered in that time period. Assignments are based on completion.

Exams are hard, and lectures can get pretty confusing. Its hard to pay attention in class because it was so boring. She's nice and open to feedback. Each class has an in-class assignment that you can't make up, so attendance is mandatory.
Easy to understand everything. Slides are clear and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yuanyuan has the most organized and clear class you could ask for. Go to class, participate and do the homework and you'll understand what's happening. I really appreciated her lecture style, but it is fast at times. Most clear exam study guides ive seen in a while. this girl is awesome.
Read to learn the material, it's interesting stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yugen Wang is a very nice guy, who really seems to care about teaching Chinese history. For his CHN150 class, if you do the readings you'll be fine. Tests are very easy, and so is the homework. Not many people go to his lectures (given that it's not mandatory), but I strongly encourage you to go if Chinese history interests you. Very fun guy!

Dr. Wang's Literary Chinese class was great. He did a great job in organizing the course to slowly get us more comfortable with reading Literary Chinese and made sure to include plenty of examples in translating to English and occasionally to modern Chinese as well. Interesting subject and an engaging course. Heard his other courses are great too!

I had Yuruhary for SPAN 202 and she was amazing. She is so caring and funny and willing to work with you if you need any extra support or time on an assignment. There is almost daily HW but it isn't difficult. She grades very fairly on exams and in class essays.

Yuru is amazing! She is super understanding and supportive. She makes learning Spanish fun and not stressful. As long as you put in the effort and do the work for the class you will come out with a good grade. The environment she creates in the classroom is inclusive and comfortable.

Yuruhary was great. The course isn't that difficult if you just pay attention. She occasionally cold calls but makes it simpler to understand. She was also very kind and understanding if you had to makeup an assignment. I would take one of her classes again.
She is an angel. Great fashion, funny lessons, and kind person. Would take her class again.
Great professor. Very funny and sweet. She makes sure you understand the topic before moving on and is very understanding towards her students. Overall would definitely take a class with her again.

She teaches Spanish, which does require a lot of participation- sometimes she will cold call, so prepare for that. Otherwise, I really really enjoyed her class. She is one of the most excellent Spanish teachers I have ever had, and I felt really comfortable participating in this class. She is super friendly and makes classes really fun!

This class required consistent attendance and even that wasn't enough to fully understand lectures. Outside resources are scarce and he was difficult to reach outside of class. Lectures didn't fully prepare students for homework or tests and I often felt blind sighted by the content he chose to test us on. Wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Fang really gets his points across and his in-class projects are among the most interesting I have ever done. I definitely recommend this class !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Great teacher who is interesting and engaged. You must be a studious worker to do well in his classes though, I must add.

Yue is a fun professor but he can be VERY difficult to understand. His accent can make class material very hard to understand and follow. The course isn't too overly difficult but there is a bit of group work and some fairly difficult tests. I would recommend reviewing the MTH242 material before starting this course because it builds on that class.
Professor Braun truly isnt bad herself, but the class was one of the worst courses ive ever taken. The amount of work, especially the final- was so painful and unrewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This has been by far one of the most horrid and unnecessarily difficult classes I have ever taken (and I've taken 400 level global courses). The final is worth the bulk of your grade and it states that "As are rarely ever given," that's not something to flex, is it? The grading criteria for the final and instructions are so unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor himself was not bad. But the TAs on the other hand were horrible. If they disagree with a view point you have, they will give you a zero and ask you to resubmit but with no grade change. I had a B and almost failed because of one assignment. I was very excited to take this class but now very discouraged.
I had her as my FIG leader this year and she was honestly amazing. For our FIG she was vary engaging and accessible. She was understanding and made sure everyone felt heard and understood.
Yvonne is such a sweet person. However, her class was alright. It was definitely interesting, but a lot of reading and writing, so be prepared.

I was disappointed by this course. Although Braun clearly has deep knowledge of the subject, she made herself unavailable & inaccessible to students. There were guest lecturers or groups more often than Braun herself, and she gave weekly reading quizzes and even cancelled the last class before finals. Loved the class, didn't care for her at all.
100% based on essays and papers. unless you're super dedicated or WGS is your major i probably wouldn't suggest this class.

Maybe it's because my WGS 101 class was her first WGS class she's taught, but sometimes Prof Braun was a snore. She is very clear in her lectures and passionate about the subject. But the class is essay based and its IMPOSSIBLE to get an A on those things. Frustrating. Also, I had her mid-GTF strike and she withheld our grades until it was over...
Yvonne is a good professor but lectures in a rather condescending tone. I like the subject matter and appreciate her attempts to be clear but cannot get past being treated like a 10 year old.
Braun puts together a good class. MANY of the lectures feature helpful and interesting guest speakers. However, be prepared to write essays every week and large papers every couple weeks.

During the first 2 or 3 weeks, I found her class very interesting.However, I lost my interest in her lecture and reading assignments weeks later till the end of the term.The contents are repeated in a confusing way.The application of theories in practical contexts are very limited which explains all of the repetition and gradual loss of engagement.

Really nice, but the class is so boring. I felt like I was learning the same stuff over and over again. She's a little biased about women and such. You can kind of get by without reading but in general this class is lame.

Very personable instructor who's clarity of lectures and course information needs to be more defined. She has a way of expressing knowledgeable information in a manner that uses unclear vocabulary (big dictionary words) that looses students ability to understand the lecture. Her grading was always unclear, even after meeting during her office hours

Prof. Braun knows her material that is for sure. The way in which she presents the material, however can be very dry. Some of the material is incredibly dense and abstract as well, especially in the first half of the term when we had to read the text of universal human rights by Donnelly. main textbook used in the honors program at Columbia U fyi
Yvonne is great, she has some really interesting experience with International Development, and she is open to ideas and comments from students. I would definitely recommend her.
Absolutely incredible professor. Highly recommended.

I have taken two of her classes. the first time i hated it. the Okays and Rights drove me insane. it was also a large 300 person lecture. i also took a 100 person lecture and it was much better. but i might have just been more interested, or used to her teaching style. either way she isnt as bad as i first judged her to be.

I'm a soc major.Dont like the class due to her lectures, her respons to emails and word choice on test question. When gtfs are confused on those questions as well,there is a problem. Okay's works the nerves system. Like the lowest exam drop and the structure of final.

I think the first review is a little harsh. The subject material is actually really interesting and she is passionate about it. Once you get past her "okay's" you really do learn a lot and see the world in a different perspective. The gtfs for this class are very relaxed and legit. Not an easy A, but maintainable. You get out what you put in

Worst teacher ever, at the end of every sentence says "Okay?' or "right?...Okay..." its the most annoying thing ever. hard to pay attention. likes to control and be rude towards students. takes lecture as a discussion.. low class attendance because she was so horrible!

Prof Saavedra is personally relatable&lectures very well, but has some dissonances in that she has a no late work policy period for a 200 level class. The final essay question was interesting. She structured the final essay in a way that would be indicative of a 10-12 page essay, but assigned a 3-5 page essay. Reading is on par with a studies class
One of my favorite professors. She is so much fun, and I always looked forward to class. There were a lot of readings, but the content was interesting.

Honestly liked the class until there was clear misinformation which dropped off my interest in the class. Also her emphasis on not summarizing for papers but the essay topics are specific to summarization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Saavedra but she isn't for everyone. She assigns fairly heavy reading loads and might be hard to follow if you're unfamiliar with concepts discussed. But if WGS is something you're passionate about, PLEASE take a class w/ her! Funny, intelligent and kind, even if she's tough, and I've learned more from her than all my other classes combined.

I can tell that this professor is used to 300+ level classes, because she doesn't really explain things at an introductory level even though this is INTRO to queer studies. The assignments/grading also tend to be unclear. 
If you don't answer a question the exact way she would answer, then you're wrong and will probably not get an explanation why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took a 4-week intensive summer course with Dr. Saavedra. She is a really passionate professor and her classes are very valuable but are not an easy A. Expect a heavy amount of reading that you can't really get away with not reading. Class participation is also required, as long as you engage thoroughly with class material/content you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This prof has absolutely no issue cancelling class or extending deadlines for her own personal life, however, she fails to cut her students any slack in return. She will also assign you papers with prompts that are so painfully specific that the goal is to restate her opinions and arguments, which is extremely frustrating. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I see a lot of harsh reviews of Professor Saavedra, but she was my favorite professor at the U of O. She is a harsh grader and assigns a heavy reading load, but she is also available and willing to help if requested. She is super intelligent and passionate about what she teaches and I wish I wasn't graduating so I could take another class from her!

Saavedra is a good and interesting lecturer who runs an overly strict class. Attendance is incredibly mandatory, and good luck trying to get extensions on assignments or excused absences. Readings are interesting but heavy, and you have to write a lot. However, it's an interesting class.

This professor requires attendance even when things may be out of your control you still will be marked absent and with no way of making up your grade. I will not ever be taking a class with her.  I have a whole child and despite covid-19 being strict, he had to miss days and I would face penalties.

Professor Saavedra is a passionate and kind teacher. She is a tough grader and sometimes her assignments do not have enough information, but then the rubric is looking for something very specific. Taking her class remotely was a challenged and the final paper took me about 10 hours to complete, definitely outside the common 1.5 hour expectation.

While Mr Young is a very nice guy, his class is very test-heavy, and I often felt that the lecture material didn't correlate very well with tests. I enjoyed doing the projects, though they were only worth a small portion of the grade.

He makes the exams super weighted; there are 3 all-term plus the final, and those really depend on your grade. Not a bad guy, but his lectures have nothing to do with the projects. My last exam, I got him told me to read chapters 3 and 4 as if I didn't do that 2 weeks straight before. He's not a guy you would want.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
i would rather get run over than take any of his classes again. thank god i transferred out of UO 

just take the equivalent courses at lane CC, much easier to understand and not self harm inducing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Out of the intro CS courses, Michal is probably the best out of the Professors UO puts in these classes, but man the way this class is structured sucks. He's nice, lectures are useful enough, but makes the mini-exams and the final basically the only thing that matters for the grade. Luckily he rarely ever fails students, even for failing grades.

He does not seem to care about the actual learning of his students, making the course incredibly test heavy. Even when students put in extra effort and do well on projects, they will be punished if they do not do well on exams, testing on problems he himself cannot do perfectly. He should not be the only option at UO for these classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I follow along in all of his lectures and read the short chapter pages, I do the labs and the projects. All of that is very easy compared to the tests. 3 mini exams and a final. Worth 50% of the grade. Pencil and paper. He writes up the exam questions to be confusing. His mini exams are about 10 deviations of difficulty more than the other stuff!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything I learned was from myself. Basically your entire grade is exams, which are on paper and graded harsh. The projects didn't really correlate with what you're learning and not worth anything. It's a hard class but not the worst. Just be prepared to put in a lot of work.

He's not the worst, not the best. Almost your entire grade is tests, which aren't really given any partial credit. Projects are worth almost nothing, lectures aren't super helpful. The class isn't hard, but only because it is relatively easy. I wouldn't recommend, but he's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Michal grades hard and 75% of your grade is exams but you get to bring in unlimited notes including past exams, so if you prepare well they aren't too bad. And for weekly projects, if you just go into office hours, there are tons of LAs who are super helpful. CS is hard in general but Michal is funny and does care a lot about the class and students

I wish I had a better experience but your entire grade is dependent on the 3 mini exams and the final. The exams are graded SO harshly, no partial credit which is ridiculous, I got a 25% on the first exam. Projects are long but worth nothing for ur grade. I wish I could go back in time and stop myself from taking his class I'm struggling so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Michal's CS210 and CS211 when i was a freshman, and I'm a CS senior now so hopefully I can share some light on his course. Michal cares A LOT about his students. He'll answer questions any day of the week (including weekends) at almost any time. His class is very hard, but that's CS, it doesn't get easier. Hell make you a good coder.
Great Teacher

Michal was a great. It is not a hard class if you go to lectures, and he has good Learning Assistants/Teaching Assistants. Those who struggled probably did not use their resources. I had virtually no coding background before coming into this class. I can understand how some projects could be confusing, but his TAs/LAs and OHs are very helpful.

I first want to say that Professor Young is such a nice guy, and cares a lot about his teaching. That being said, there are certainly problems with the class. Projects are 10-12 hours long every week and are only worth 15% of your grade. Exams are worth 75% which is too heavy in my opinion. If you're a good student though you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The projects for homework didn't help you learn for the tests which were all awful. Usually around 4 questions each worth 25% and getting partial credit per question is like trying to eat soup with a fork. The amount of self-study you have to do is criminal. Class averages for the tests got to 39%. My only saving grace were the GE's.

Grading curve for 94% being A- adds unnecessary stress but he will usually lower the curve at the end of term. Tests were often difficult and on paper but notes are allowed. Learned a lot from his class, but often required a lot of self-studying and struggling to get through projects & exams. I don't think he's a bad prof. but not amazing either.

I liked the content of this course, as expressed through the projects completed. There is, however, more of a grading focus on the in person, pen and paper tests, than on those projects and that is extremely unfortunate. Overall, this class was fine, if not a little convoluted at times.

Michal is a really good guy, easy to talk to and super easy to reach. If I was rating Michal purely on his character, he'd get a 5. I gave him a 3 because his exams were very terribly graded, you have to write code on paper and what you write is compared to an answer key and you are graded on how close you are to the answer key which is terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall a pretty good professor. It's not too difficult if you put in the work to fully understand the projects. The projects were well thought out and reasonably challenging. There was ample study material for the tests and the course is lenient if you do poorly on a mini quiz or two. I do wish the projects were worth more of the overall grade.

Horrible class, probably the worst class and professor I've ever had in college.  Lectures aren't relevant to the tests, grading is extremely strict and unclear, class made me want to switch majors.

Never take Michal Young if you have the choice! Class might be worth waiting another semester so you don't have to get him.
MY GPA IS COOKED .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I could say good things about him he is a very sweet guy but his teaching style and expectations for the exams are at human prodigy level and it's just insane. Unless you are the 1% that can whip out a code out of nowhere and write perfect code without testing it then this class is for you. If there is any other professor offered TAKE THEM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Michal seems like a really nice guy, but he is a pretty awful lecturer and test writer. All of the exams were 5-6 questions long and the last question was always worth 25% of the exam grade and was always extremely difficult to a point where it was not possible with the material we had covered. The projects were incredibly easy though.

Taking CS 122 first will help a lot. The class is graded mostly by exams which was difficult for me since I'm not a test person. The professor cares a lot about his students & will explain things in great detail for you! He's very nice. Projects are only worth a small portion of your grade but that is how you learn for the exams and your future.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: making a b- at a 84 is dumb to begin with, then he returns the projects really late, pretty much at the end of the term so you wont know if you did bad on your projects till the very end. the only good part is that he lets you bring in unlimited notes for the tests.
Horrible.

I really wish I could rate him higher because he is really a nice guy but the class is just awful. Spend 90% of the class talking about the projects but all together worth 10% of your grade?? Then you're expected to apply that to a PAPER exam worth 50% of your grade. Some concepts weren't even covered beforehand. You're set up to fail I'm sorry.

Paper exams worth 50% of your grade with problems you've never seen before, which he then gets mad when people don't do well on them. It's frustrating because he is genuinely a nice person, but his class is set up horribly.

Grading scale makes no sense, three mini exams given are worth 45% of your grade while weekly projects only contribute to 10%. if you aced all tests and didn't submit any projects you could get an A in this class. Extremely confusing mini exams with problems not covered in lectures. If you are not overly familiar with python, good luck passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded primarily on weekly projects, mini-exams, and final. Learned a good bit, but took a lot of unnecessary time struggling and stressing. Projects aren't bad, but instructions can be very confusing. Exams are very important, but they always have 1-2 very difficult questions that are tricky and barely covered. Gra.-Scale fluctuated, started 93=B+

I have a 100% in canvas for this class. This is not enough for him to consider my grade an A+.
A 94% is a B+.

Seriously? For an introductory course?

He's a good teacher who really knows what he's teaching. Most people are dramatic about the on paper exams, but they're relatively straight forward if you've paid attention and done the projects. The project instructions were hard to understand, and the he docked points for not passing hidden test cases that you can't see when your writing the code

Literally gives paper and pencil exams for a COMPUTER science course. Instructions in projects are so unclear, understanding what he is trying to have you do is harder than the actual material. All the material makes sense to him, but pretty much only him. People in this class were constantly confused and frustrated with Michal.

After having plenty of experience coding, this class was comically easy. Unfortunately after going into the final with a 95%... after my grade wasn't completely entered/ adjusted, I finished with an 89% B-. I assumed that this was a mistake, but apparently not. Wanna learn how to code? Take DSCI. Good material, profs, and real grading systems.

The content was well put together. I liked that he made the textbook and projects himself bc it was easier to understand. His grading scale was super skewed against you. He was available for help after class. The tests were graded harshly, either you knew what you were doing or you didnt to him. He's nice but his grading is not. Graded attendance.

This is definitely a class that expects previous coding experience, but it is not a hard prerequisite. If you have previous experience, this class is fairly easy. He cares about his students and makes plenty of time for office hours after class every day. Definitely a worthwhile class

Our COMPUTER science final was on paper. He made the final based on HIS way of difficultly. A lot of students, including myself were really confused with his grading system. In his class, an 84% is a C. The final 100% screwed me up because I had a 96% and the final really messed my grade up. He doesn't see how hard the students work for his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had 2 written coding exams that completely tanked my grade. The textbook used is one that he has written himself. The projects involve finishing functions that he has already created. The grading scale made no sense at all

In the syllabus the grading scale states "students who receive an 84+ will receive b/b-". There is no indication what differentiates between a b and b-. I ended with an 89, which was apparently a b-. It also doesn't help that Prof. Young is very good at ignoring emails. Class is easy if you've used python before, but if you haven't, good luck.

I overall really liked him, but even though I ended with an 89%, it was counted as a B-. That sucks especially since you need a B- at least to go onto harder CS classes. The in person tests and a couple of the projects were a bit tricky, but I feel pretty good about most of the concepts I have learned. I think he taught things well.

Gave us an in-person paper/pencil midterm AND final for a *computer science* class. Made the grade cutoff 94% for an A- too? I had an A in this class ALL term and because I didn't do too fantastic on a paper comp sci test, I finished with a B (91%). The project instructions were vague and unhelpful. This class tanked my GPA for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The cutoff for a A- in this class is a 94%
Overall best CS professor I've had at UO.
Doesn't really teach anything in his lectures. Easy grading for the most part though :)

Projects were long and dense, but overall his class is super well-organized. His tests are an exact representation of the class content, so if you've been putting in the work, it's a breeze! He's also very active on Slack and replies EXTREMELY fast with thoughtful and thorough advice. It's clear how much he cares about comp sci AND his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor for 461. Considerate, and waits for you to learn at your own pace. Communicate with him at every step to get the best results, because building a compiler can get very hard very fast, and you often feel like scrapping your previous work and starting over from scratch.

Prof Young is also the best teacher for 422. DO NOT take 422 with anyone else. For 461, he literally wrote his own virtual machine for our class use to make it easier on us. He cares about his students more than any other prof. His only downside is that he makes things sound easier than they actually are. Strongly recommend this class to everyone.

I took Michal Young for 211, he is not as bad as everyone makes him seem. 211 is a weedout class, even though he tells you it's not. People go in expecting an easy class like 210, that's not the case. He does care and is very helpful outside of class. I have taken other classes from him, and am writing a review years later after I took 211
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He went out of his way to be accommodating during the time of online learning. The class was really difficult, but he was almost always accessible to ask for help. Told very wonderful corny jokes throughout his lecture. Would 10/10 recommend him for CIS 211.

Michal was the only professor that made online classes bearable! Instructions for projects could be a bit disorganized and confusing, but there was plenty of support available, and he built an environment where asking questions, making mistakes, and learning was very comfortable and fun. Expect some lengthy lectures and challenging projects :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Like poor communication skills, written and verbal? Modifying spaghetti code? And arrogant people who never worked a day in their life outside academia? Well Mr Young is the guy for you! His 211 course is poorly instructed and it's a bad course. Learning things you shouldn't be learning yet and dealing with his crudely written instructions. Enjoy!

I feel like people give him too much credit. There's more to being a good professor than teaching well and giving good individual help. His class is pretty awful. Although I'm aware other CIS professors at UO are much worse, that doesn't make him good.

Lazy grader, didn't grade anything for over a month until the course was over. Projects are just modifying his code. Didn't learn well that way. Object orientation, recursion and assembly/machine level code is what you'll be learning. Python is a bad language to learn computer architecture however. Too much changing of subjects. Not enough focus.

Lots of work. Expects you to not have much else going on in your life with the amount of work assigned. Course should honestly be 8 units at least. A very lazy grader as well. Takes sometimes weeks and weeks before things are graded. And he jumps around into too many different subjects. You spend weeks on assembly and machine level code.

I was super surprised to see his reviews on here! I really liked this professor. He takes the time to help you personally on a project you're turning in a week late, is constantly taking student feedback to make the course better, and is overall one of the only professors I've had who managed to seem engaged with his students despite the class size
Michal is a super sweet guy, very fun to engage with. The projects are quite long, and in many cases also rather difficult, but you learn a LOT from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very sweet, willing to answer questions and give you his full attention, at least during office hours. He does expect a lot from his students but not to an unrealistic point when it comes to tests and projects. I found his lectures to be extremely informative and helpful as well. I'd take another class with him. He certainly knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Michal is an elitist who doesn't care about you at all. He wants to keep you in his class forever and thinks it's perfectly normal that half his students should fail. He is immune from reprisal as other teachers who themselves don't understand what he's talking about rely on him to keep stupid people out of the major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Michal can come off as egotistical and arrogant when students ask questions, but is generally better one on one. Has unrealistic expectations for exams, but if you do all the practice tests, look over the projects, and review the live coding, you should come out alright.

Took a class with Michal as project leader. Has a huge ego and is all theory, no practice. He procrastinates and seems to enjoy boasting about his knowledge than ever applying it or expanding what he knows. Has never worked a day in his life.
Egotistical guy, believes his code speaks for itself and doesn't follow up on explaining past that, don't recommend him whatsoever.

Michael Young has a teaching style and outlook on his courses that is a bit unique compared to other professors. His courses are pretty hard and outside help through office hours is pretty much required, but because of the difficulty he is generous on grading. It worked well for me, learned a TON and ended up with a decent grade.

He believes you can learn all you need to by just reading his code with no detailed explanation. I'd compare his teaching strategy to giving someone a detailed explanation on how to drive a car (there is the gas/brake pedal) and then because you now know so much about cars from driving, you can obviously perform a oil change? The two don't compare
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Didn't grade any assignments until week 6, 1 grade with no feedback, even after email request. Didn't get any other feedback or grades until after final. While discussing grade on a question on final, admitted he read the first page and didn't bother with the rest. Tried to grade all of the assignments for every student on a single Raspberry Pi

I had Professor Young as a lead on a research project, in Compiler Construction, and in Software Methodology.  Overall, I can say that Michal is both an excellent individual, and excellent professor.  I highly recommend taking his classes.

Young is one of the nicest professors you will ever have. The problem is he doesn't teach the material. I found the labs were semi-helpful but in class he didn't teach in a way the masses could understand. The projects were absurdly difficult and many failed. My dad is a programmer and he even got confused on some of the instruction.

The man is a doll--probably the nicest professor I've had. He has a genuine interest in teaching, extremely knowledgeable, and willing to help students succeed. Some of the projects were pretty tough, but he's always available to answer questions, and help you debug. A lot can be gained from this class, but you really have to work for it.
the project is so hard, and at class he didn't teach much

While I can see how people may not agree with his teaching style, it just comes down to knowing how to ask the right questions. He is extremely knowledgeable and I learned a lot from CIS 210 (more than 211 and 212 combined).

I had a very bad experience with Prof. Young. The majority of people in the class didn't understand the material he presented at all, and while he personally knew the material, he wasn't effective at communicating it to anyone else. I wasn't able to complete a single assignment and ended up with a B+...that's just not right.

Michal is very nice and interested in his subject. I didn't find the lectures easy to understand- that has been the case with all of UO's CIS classes. Its like being told to write a paper- they explain the body, thesis, conclusion, but you need to write it in Spanish and they don't teach you the language. Hard if programing doesn't come naturally.

Dr. Young is really clear when explaining complicated concepts. He is really good at detecting and reacting to mystery on students' faces. He reacts by slowing down the lecture, approaching the explanation in a systematic way, including elemental/foundational details, crucial to student understanding, in the course of explaining a piece of code.

Michal is extremely helpful, knowledgeable and approachable. I think his teaching is very clear, but I could see how others might not. CIS 422 is a wonderful course. I loved working on a project with a small team. First half of the term you do an assigned project and you can pick your own project the second half.

I've known him personally for quite a while and he's extremely friendly and willing to help. But this class seems a bit lost on the lectures..maybe it's the nature of software engineering classes. The number of people who regularly show up (or don't show up) tells the story. Group projects are helpful for the inexperienced.

I really enjoyed CRWR 230 with Zack Barrett. I was engaged the whole time, and the class always had fun banter. Zack never fails to make his students feel safe and understood, and his teaching style is fun and engaging. The content of the class is thought-provoking and interesting if poetry is something you enjoy!

amazing teacher! super fun lectures and not too bad of a course load. there is a lot of participation required in this class and you will have to speak about your poem that get written. the smaller class size was helpful for a more inviting atmosphere and is super beneficial! over an amazing class and professor!
The literal best professor I've had period. Lots of reading but so fun so who cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: insane workload chill guy but not an easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took womens and gender studies with her, it was my favorite class of the year! She's a funny, engaging and very kind professor who cares deeply about her students. Her deadlines are lenient, and there's no busywork. All readings are relevant, interesting, and relatively short! No tests! Would reccomend to anyone and everyone.

I had Hannah for both Wr121 and Wr122 and I got an A+ in both. Her classes are fun and easy if you put at least some effort in. If you attend office hours a few times then you are basically guaranteed a good grade in the class.

Hannah is a kind, caring, and very generous GE. She helps you in any way, and is generous on grading and pretty lenient on grades and late work. Her class is easy, at UO every writing class is themed, and my class was Horror, monsters, true crime, and gender identities. If you do not want to write or learn about these things then it's not for you.
Her lectures are boring and even admits that they aren't good. The structure of the course is terrible
Her lectures are really bad and grades are completely dependent on exams.

Lectures: 2/5
Course structure: 1/5
Availability: 3/5
Course difficulty: 5/5
Professor as a person: 4/5

The course is hard, but overall it's still pretty interesting. The structure and grading is really bad along with the majority of the lectures. It's dependent on the GE you have because I can see it being much worse. She chill tho so overall 3/5

Professor Ariola is a good lecturer, but the course is set up so that she has to put in the minimal amount of effort to administer it. There is no graded homework and the answers are only released at class discussions. The justification for this is that the tests will be exactly like the homework, but this is not true!
Absolutely terrible. Worst prof in the dept. She doesn't care about students. Avoid at all costs.

Want ungraded assignments with your whole grade coming from 2 midterms and a final, then this is the class for you. She cannot teach if her life depended on it. Has the TA's do everything for her, I can't believe she is still here. Oh wait, it's cause she's the assistant head of the department. Everything you will learn will be from the TAs
Really a bad teacher, office hours need appointment, hard exams, only give "yes" or "no" answer in piazza. Don't know why she could still be a 4-level instructor, the worst teacher I have ever met.

She's a solid lecturer and speaks very clearly, but her homework assignments will consume your life. The average on her CIS425 final was a 43% - I cannot believe she is allowed to continue structuring her class with this setup.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Ariola genuinely puts in effort to this class. She's a decent lecturer, but unfortunately the course material itself is awfully tough and incomprehensible. I'm expectinghoping for a massive curve in the end though, so there's that.
Speaks clearly and slowly despite her thick Italian accent. Very helpful in office hours. Not very active on message board.

Heavy accent, hard to understand, boring. Material was hard which is alright for a theory course, but some programming assignments seemed too difficult...good news is that you don't have to worry about them if you're good at exams (75% of grade!). Exams are not difficult if you know the "core" stuff and what types of questions she might ask.
Very hard to understand, can't explain concepts more than one way, supplies hershey's kisses to keep you interested in lectures, which are extremely boring.
Also, no an easy class. However, this is an under pinning computer science class.
Difficult material. However, this is a graduate theory course. Get in or get out. She is fair and always willing to work with students who actually demonstrate an interest in learning the material.

Hard to understand and doesn't explain things any better the second time around. Exams are extremely difficult, and assignments seem to have nothing to do with the textbook or material taught in class.
She is very intense. Her accent makes it hard to understand her lectures. Midterms and Final are very difficult.
No Comments

She is my favorite professor of all time. You will write 3 essays, but you will get a lot of time to write each. There are a lot of readings, and you will sometimes get mini quizzes on them, but they are easy. All the readings were AMAZING and relevant; I improved as a writer and person because of them. I 100% recommend you take her.

I definitely loved her teaching. She is very caring and has a way with words when she is grading. She is open to hearing your issues if you need extra time with an assignment, just make sure you contact her two days AT LEAST prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I would take another class from Professor Seyran in a heartbeat. She is so accommodating and wants you to do well. If you show up to class you will get an A. To be fair, I took her comp 1 class so already an easy class, but she is just a kind, caring teacher.
Love her

Very helpful comments on assignments. Grading was pretty confusing, poetry assignments were out of 7 and responses were graded with checks, pluses and minuses. Other than that, very helpful discussion and review sessions
Definitely a pleasure.

Fun and knowledgeable but lectures can be sort of word vomit with no direction although if you read the text and pay attention it can come together. Molecular genetics is definitely hard but Prof Zemper is an above average teacher and if you put in the work you can learn it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Zemper as a person, she's a super nice person who loves being able to help and support her students. However, her class is unorganized and relies almost entirely on you teaching yourself the material from the textbook. I would take her again just because I like her, but not because her class was amazing or anything. It's rough.

Truly a mid class. The content isn't actually that hard but it's given in a very frantic and rushed manner during the lectures. This makes it seem way more confusing than it actually is. The discussion section of the course is a huge waste of everyone's time. It hardly ever reinforces the content learned in the lectures.

I think overall she's a good professor, but it is true that the material is hard to understand if you don't do the readings or actually pay attention in class. That's not her fault, since the material is complex if you haven't taken cell bio/etc. prior. So just pay attention, do the readings, go to class, and ask questions.

Assigns a lot of reading that is not very helpful and then would get mad when it was obvious students didn't do all the readings due to time (obviously) or they didn't understand the material. Lectures are very rushed and not very helpful either, so get ready to do a lot of teaching yourself.

Prof Zemper is an amazing person but her lectures always feel rushed to me. I find that her teaching style is best supplemented with office hours so make sure to leave time for that in your schedule if you have her. She is so incredibly passionate about the material however and it is contagious. The tests arent hard but the problem sets for hw are.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: "Do the readings!" - her, then gives you full score on a quiz because she forgot to post it. Its incredibly clear that she only teaches to continue being paid research $. She's simply a fast pace slide-show reader. Many slides have poor grammar/spelling. She begins lecture 10min late at best and is highly hypocritical about respecting people's time
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She assigns a LOT of reading and prefecture videos. It Is clear that she treats her "A+ students" with a lot more respect. No matter how much work I put into the course and how much I contributed during class, I was still scared to go to office hours. She truly is a kind professor and has the best intentions but sometimes it doesn't feel like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: easy A. exams are not too difficult if you study hard and do the readings. pay attention in lecture and take good notes youll do great. there are graded questions. overall good experience
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly I think it's a bit unfair to see that she got a low rating… Personally I think she is a nice and caring person. She gave me many useful feedback on my mid-term paper and it later got developed to a project.
